nor through the rational intellect of the Sages—
רַק מִצַּד שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל נְבִיאִים בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים,
rather because the people of Israel are prophets and the children of prophets,
שָׁרְשָׁם דָּבוּק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם
whose root is bound to the supernal, concealed Root
וְחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מַמָּשׁ,
being an actual portion of God,
הֵם מְכַוְּונִים מֵעַצְמָם לַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שׁוּם הֶאָרָה גְּלוּיָה כְּלָל
they intuitively direct themselves to perform a practice lacking all overt revelation
וְנֶעְלָם לְגַמְרֵי;
and completely hidden;
רַק מִצַּד דִּיבּוּקָם בַּנֶּעְלָם הֵם מַשִּׂיגִים הַנֶּעְלָם.
solely by virtue of their clinging to the Hidden Realm do they perceive and channel what is hidden.
וְזֶהוּ הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכָח דִּלְעָתִיד,
And this is identical to grasping the direct Presence destined for the future,
שֶׁהוּא בַּהֹוֶה נֶעְלָם לְגַמְרֵי,
which in the present era is entirely concealed,
רַק מִצַּד דִּיבּוּקָם בַּנֶּעְלָם הֵם מַשִּׂיגִים גַּם זֶה.
yet through their cleaving to the Hidden Realm, they perceive this as well.
וְזֶהוּ "דִּמְדַלְּגִי" –
And this accounts for why 'they skip' portions of Hallel:
כִּי מֵחָכְמָה וָאֵילָךְ שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַגִּלּוּי הוֹלֵךְ בְּסֵדֶר,
for from Chokhmah onward, which represents the beginning of structured revelation, light proceeds in ordered succession;
אֲבָל בַּנֶּעְלָם אֵין מְסוּדָּר כַּנּוֹדָע.
whereas in the Primordial Hidden Realm there is no linear order, as is known.
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מְסוּדָּר אָז הוּא בִּשְׁלֵימוּת וְהוּא בְּגִילּוּי,
For when something is sequentially ordered, it stands complete and manifest;
אֲבָל הַנֶּעְלָם הוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
but the Hidden Realm is the unfathomable depth of the primordial root of divine thought,
בִּהְיוֹתוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם עֲדַיִן מִן הַחָכְמָה עַצְמָהּ
while yet concealed even from wisdom itself
וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת,
and not yet in manifest disclosure;
עַל כֵּן הוּא בְּדִילּוּג וְאֵין מְסוּדָּר עֲדַיִן.
therefore it expresses itself through skipping and lacks structured progression.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְדִלְגּוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ד),
And concerning this, Scripture states: 'And His banner / skipping over me was love' (Song of Songs 2:4),
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הָאַהֲבָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for this constitutes the core of the love of Hashem, blessed be He, for the people of Israel,
בַּמֶּה שֶׁהֵם דְּבוּקִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם.
in that they are bonded directly to the Concealed Root.
וְהַגַּם שֶׁהֵן מְדַלְּגִין וְאֵין מְסוּדָּר
And even though they skip and lack systematic order,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ דְּגָלוּי דְּהוּא מְסוּדָּר,
which is the opposite of revealed wisdom that is always structured,
עִם כָּל זֶה דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
nonetheless they remain inseparably attached to Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה טַעַם "בַּמָּה אֲהַבְתָּנוּ וְגוֹמֵר וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְגוֹמֵר" (מַלְאָכִי א, ב),
And this is the meaning of ''In what have You loved us?... Yet I loved Jacob, etc.' (Malachi 1:2),
בְּלִי שׁוּם טַעַם,
without any rationalizing cause,
רַק שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁלִּי וּלְחֶלְקִי.
solely because 'this one is Mine and belongs to My allotted portion.'

sections.en: Divine Kindness and Complete Redemption

items.h: All divine attributes serve the ultimate good of Israel; redemption culminates when even thought and inner consciousness remain bound to Hashem.

Seif 1 — Divine Kindness from Action to Thought
All divine powers serve Israel's good, culminating in redemption when even inner thought remains attached to Hashem.

p: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא לְעוֹלָם גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים,
Hashem, blessed be He, is forever called 'He Who bestows good kindnesses,'
כִּי זֶה כָּל פְּעוּלוֹתָיו
because this is the totality of His actions,
וְכָל אֲצִילוּת מִדּוֹתָיו הָיָה רַק לְצוֹרֶךְ לְהֵיטִיב לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
and the entire emanation of His divine attributes was solely for the purpose of doing good unto Israel,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב (מִזְמוֹר קטז88 Midrash Tehillim 116:3 — "To my voice, my supplications" — the Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Even if all the nations of the world call upon You, leave them and hear my prayer; therefore, "to my voice, my supplications." And so the Holy One, blessed be He, did: "for He has inclined His ear to me." The ears on high are open to hear nothing but my prayer alone, as it is said, "Ears You have dug for me," and it is written, "Incline Your ear to me."):
and as it is written in Shocher Tov (Midrash Tehillim, Psalm 116):
"אָזְנַיִם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה אֵין כְּרוּיוֹת אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ תְּפִלָּתִי,
"The supernal ears are hollowed only to hear my prayer,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי'".
as it is stated: 'Ears You hollowed for me.'"
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה בְּכָל כֹּחוֹת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
And similar to this with all supernal celestial powers,
הוּא רַק לְצָרְכֵינוּ לְהֵיטִיב לָנוּ.
they exist solely for our needs, to bestow good upon us.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִרְאֶה פְּעָמִים לָעַיִן לֹא כֵן,
And when it sometimes appears to human sight to be otherwise,
זֶה אַדְּרַבָּה לְהֵיטִיב בְּטוֹבָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשֵּׂכֶל הָאֱנוֹשִׁי.
this is, on the contrary, meant to bestow a far greater good that transcends human mortal intellect.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט89 Bereshit Rabbah 9:5-7 — In R. Meir's Torah scroll they found written: "And behold, it was very good" — "and behold, death is good." R. Simeon ben Elazar said: "And behold, it was very good" — and behold, sleep is good. And is sleep very good? Rather, because a man sleeps a little he rises and labors much in Torah. R. Nachman bar Shmuel said in the name of R. Shmuel bar Nachman: "Behold, it was good" — this is the good inclination; "and behold, it was very good" — this is the evil inclination. And is the evil inclination very good? Rather, were it not for the evil inclination a man would not build a house, or marry a wife, or beget children, or engage in trade.):
And along the lines of what they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 9):
"'טוֹב מְאֹד' – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע וּמָוֶת וְשֵׁינָה",
"'Very good' – this refers to the evil inclination, death, and sleep,"
דְּכָל אֵלּוּ נִרְאִים לֹא טוֹב לָעַיִן,
for all of these appear negative to the eye,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דְּהוּא טוֹב מְאֹד,
and concerning this it was stated that it is 'very good,'
דְּבָזֶה יֵשׁ עוֹמֶק טוֹב.
for within this resides an unfathomable depth of goodness.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל:
By way of an allegory:
הָאוֹכֵל מַאֲכָל מָתוֹק לַחֵךְ הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הֲנָאַת בָּרֶגַע,
one who consumes food that is sweet to the palate does so merely for momentary gratification,
אֲבָל הָאוֹכֵל מַאֲכָל מָרוֹר
whereas one who consumes bitter food,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁהוּא לְהַבְרִיא גּוּפוֹ,
perforce it is specifically to heal his body,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה אוֹכְלוֹ,
since without this purpose he surely would not consume it;
אִם כֵּן עַל כֵּן הֲנָאָתוֹ מְרוּבָּה יוֹתֵר הַרְבֵּה.
consequently, its ultimate benefit and true gratification are vastly greater.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "מַה גָּדְלוּ מַעֲשֶׂיךָ ה'",
And concerning this it is stated: 'How great are Your deeds, O Hashem!'
פֵּירוּשׁ, "מַעֲשֶׂיךָ" הוּא כָּל עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הַנִּגְלֶה וּפְעוּלוֹת הַנִּגְלִים,
meaning: 'Your deeds' encompasses the entire manifest World of Action (Asiyah) and visible events;
"גָּדְלוּ" הוּא מִדַּת הַגְּדוּלָּה וְהַחֶסֶד לְהֵיטִיב,
'are great' refers to the divine attribute of Greatness and Lovingkindness (Chesed) that dispenses overt good,
וְהַרְבֵּה טוֹבוֹת יֵשׁ בְּנִגְלוֹת הַמַּעֲשִׂים.
and abundant goodness exists within manifest actions.
"וּמְאֹד עָמְקוּ מַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ" הוּא כְּטַעַם "טוֹב מְאֹד" –
'And Your thoughts are exceedingly deep' mirrors the inner essence of 'very good' –
מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו הוּא עוֹלָמוֹת הַנֶּעְלָמִים וּדְבָרִים שֶׁטּוֹבָתָם נֶעְלֶמֶת,
His 'thoughts' encompass the hidden realms and matters whose benevolence is concealed,
דִּלְפִי הָרְאוּת הָיָה טוֹב לְהֵיפֶךְ,
where according to superficial perception it appeared that the opposite would be good,
כְּעִנְיַן צַעֲקַת יִרְמְיָה: "מַדּוּעַ דֶּרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים צָלֵחָה וְגוֹמֵר",
parallel to the outcry of Jeremiah: 'Why does the way of the wicked prosper, etc.,'
דִּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הוּא הַמְשָׁכַת מִדַּת הַגְּדוּלָּה וְהַחֶסֶד דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא בַּמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי.
since superficially it appears to be a bestowal of Hashem's Greatness and Lovingkindness upon an undeserving place.
וְזֶה שֶׁסִּיֵּים גַּם כָּאן: "בִּפְרֹחַ רְשָׁעִים וְגוֹמֵר וְאַתָּה מָרוֹם",
And this explains why Scripture concludes here as well: 'When the wicked spring up, etc., but You are on high (marom)' –
פֵּירוּשׁ, בְּרוּם מַעְלָה וְעוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים דְּהַיְינוּ עוֹלַם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
meaning: in the ultimate height and supernal worlds, namely the World of Thought;
זֶה נִקְרָא "מָרוֹם" שֶׁהוּא מִתְרוֹמֵם מֵהַשָּׂגַת בְּנֵי אָדָם,
this is termed 'marom' because it towers far above the comprehension of mortal men,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מֵהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת וְכִבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא
belonging to the esoteric hidden things and the divine secrets of the Merciful One,
שֶׁאֵין נִגְלֶה שַׁלְוַת הָרְשָׁעִים וְיִסּוּרֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים,
where the worldly peace of the wicked and the suffering of the righteous are not explained to our sight,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ90 Menachot 29b — Moshe said before Him: Master of the Universe, You have shown me his Torah — show me his reward. He said to him: Turn around. He turned around and saw them weighing out his flesh in the market stalls. He said before Him: Master of the Universe — such Torah, and such its reward? He said to him: Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me. Rashi: "In the market stalls" — the place of the butchers. They were weighing out his flesh, as is said in Berakhot 61b, that they raked his flesh with combs of iron. Maharsha: "Turn around" here too means the letters expounded in reverse, from tav to alef, as is set out in the chapter HaBoneh [Shabbat 104a], where the reversed alphabet is expounded first of the measure of the wicked and then of the measure of the righteous, and it is explained there that the righteous receive their punishment in this world in order that their reward in the World to Come be increased. Thus "such Torah, and such its reward?" — the vision itself alludes to the reward that their punishment earns; and He answered that so it did arise in thought, just as you suppose. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Menachos 29b): Moshe now knew that R. Akiva had no portion in the existence of this world, and therefore he asked to be shown his reward in it; "Turn around" meant that he should apprehend the order of existence that would come after him, and in that order he saw them weighing out his flesh. "Be silent, so it arose in thought" means that although by the measure of the Torah it was not fitting that this should be so, nevertheless the order that the Holy One, blessed be He, arranged decreed it. For R. Akiva had no portion at all in the perceptible world — which is why he expounded the crowns of the letters, whose apprehension is remote and separate from it — and so the nations, who have a portion only in the perceptible world and none at all in the separate world, prevailed over him, since they are his very opposite. (מְנָחוֹת כט:):
in the manner of what they stated (Menachot 29b)
בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: "כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה".
concerning Rabbi Akiva: 'So it arose in the Supernal Thought.'
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "מְאֹד עָמְקוּ מַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ",
And regarding this it is stated: 'Your thoughts are exceedingly deep,'
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲמַקִּים שֶׁל טוֹבָה הַנִּקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד".
signifying that within it dwell profound depths of goodness designated as 'very good.'
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂי אָדָם הוּא מַעֲשֵׂי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And all deeds of man are in truth the deeds of Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ",
as it is written: 'For all our deeds You have wrought for us,'
וְזֶה וַדַּאי "מַה גָּדְלוּ",
and this certainly corresponds to 'how great are Your deeds,'
כְּטַעַם "זְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת".
mirroring the concept that 'willful sins are transformed into merits.'
וּמַחְשְׁבוֹת אָדָם וְהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת דְּאִינּוּן מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא,
And human thoughts and secret internal states, which are brain and heart,
הֵם וַדַּאי לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ,
belong certainly unto Hashem our God,
וְהֵם מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and they are ultimately His divine thoughts, blessed be He;
אֵלּוּ "מְאֹד עָמְקוּ",
these are what 'are exceedingly deep,'

כְּעִנְיַן "לֹא יְהַרְהֵר אָדָם בַּיּוֹם וְכוּלֵי91 Ketubot 46a — A man should not entertain such thoughts by day, and so come to impurity at night. Rashi (s.v. "that a man should not entertain thoughts by day"): "For the teaching of R. Pinchas" — it is in tractate Avodah Zarah. "That a man should not entertain thoughts by day and so come to impurity at night" — because next to that verse stands, "If there be among you a man who is not clean by reason of that which happens him by night" (Deuteronomy 23:11)."
as in the matter of: 'A man should not indulge in sinful thoughts by day, etc.,'
(כְּתוּבּוֹת מו.),
(Ketubot 46a),
רְאִיַּת קֶרִי בַּלַּיְלָה הוּא מַעֲשֶׂה
and experiencing nocturnal emission is an involuntary occurrence
שֶׁאָנוּ צוֹוְחִים עַל זֶה: "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
concerning which we cry out: 'For all our deeds You have wrought for us, etc.,'
דְּאָנוּ לֹא רָצִינוּ בָּזֶה כְּלָל.
for we harbored absolutely no conscious desire for this whatsoever.
וְתִיקּוּן עַל זֶה בַּזְּמַן הוּא חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר בַּשָּׁנָה,
And the rectification for this in time is the month of Adar during the cycle of the year,
דִּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה מִמַּה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ פְּעָמִים שְׁנֵי אֲדָרִין,
which, as is evident from the fact that there are sometimes two Adars,
הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁבֶט יוֹסֵף
corresponds to the tribe of Joseph,
שֶׁהוּא פְּעָמִים שֵׁבֶט אֶחָד וּפְעָמִים שְׁנַיִם
which is sometimes reckoned as one single tribe and sometimes as two,

(וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר קְדוּשַּׁת לֵוִי92 Kedushat Levi, Exodus, Tetzaveh 8 — And they correspond to the twelve tribes of Yah, the twelve stones of the breastplate. And the month of Adar corresponds to Joseph, from whom two tribes issued, Ephraim and Manasseh; therefore the month of Adar is the one that is doubled, and there are at times two months of Adar. And therefore Adar's constellation is Fishes, which is the aspect of Joseph, of whom it is written, "and may they multiply like fish in the midst of the earth.").
(and so it is stated in Sefer Kedushat Levi).
גַּם מַזָּלוֹ דָּגִים,
Furthermore, its zodiac sign is Pisces (the fish),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹסֵף: "וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב",
as it is written concerning Joseph: 'And let them grow into a multitude like fish,'
וְהוּא עַל הַפְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
which pertains directly to fruitful reproduction,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ח93 Rosh Hashanah 8a — R. Yochanan said: Both of them expounded a single verse, as it is said, "The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are covered over with grain; they shout for joy, they also sing." R. Meir holds: When are the meadows clothed with flocks? At the time when the valleys are covered over with grain. And when are the valleys covered over with grain? In Adar. They conceive in Adar and give birth in Av, and their New Year is Elul. Rashi: "The meadows are clothed with flocks" is a verse in Psalms: the ewes are "clothed", that is, they conceive; "the valleys are covered over with grain": the sown seed sprouts and is plainly visible; "they shout for joy, they also sing": in Nisan, when harvest time comes and the grain stands on its stalks, the wind blows and they knock against one another, and a sound is heard, so that they seem to be singing. The gestation of small cattle is five months; and "their New Year is Elul" because the division between their new and old [animals] at the renewal of the year falls close to the completion [of their births]. Tosafos (s.v. "the meadows are clothed with flocks"): The Targum renders it "the rams mount the flocks", which is a euphemism [for mating]. Rashi explains it in this way below (11a), on R. Yehoshua's statement that the world was created in Nisan, where it is said that that season is the time when cattle and beasts mate with one another; but here he did not explain it so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): This month corresponds to the power of desire, and its sign is the fish — "let them multiply like fish" — in which lies the power of increase, for the power of "be fruitful and multiply" was first stated of the fish. And it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar," and Israel are likened to a flock, for they too are exceedingly fruitful and multiply. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The month of Adar, whose sign is the fish, corresponds to Joseph, whose blessing is "let them multiply like fish," for in it lies the power of fruitfulness of that blessing, which is in Adar — as it says in Rosh Hashanah, "the flocks conceive in Adar," and Israel are everywhere likened to a flock. It is called Adar from adir, "mighty," denoting strength and might, whose essence is the subduing of the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 5): Therefore it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar" — Israel are likened to a flock, and that is the time of their increase. I have received that this month is therefore auspicious for barren men and women to be remembered, because it is designated for the eradication of Amalek, and every withholding of childbirth among the seed of Israel comes only from the accusation of Amalek..):
as they stated (Rosh Hashanah 8a):
"אֵימַת לָבְשׁוּ כָרִים הַצֹּאן? בַּאֲדָר",
"When are the pastures clothed with flocks? In Adar,"
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ מַשְׁחִית זַרְעוֹ.
which represents the absolute antithesis of wasting the seed.
וּמַתְחִיל אַחַר הַשׁוֹבָבִ״ים,
And it begins right after the period of Shovavim (weeks of spiritual repentance),
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
which is known according to the teaching of the holy Ari, of blessed memory,
שֶׁאָז הוּא גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן עַד פָּרָשַׁת "כִּי תִקְנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי".
that this marks the culmination of rectification extending through parashat 'When you acquire a Hebrew servant.'
וְנִבְרָא בְּאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה,
And Adar was created through the Hebrew letter Kuf, as written in Sefer Yetzirah;
וְיוֹם שִׁשִּׁי שֶׁהוּא בַּיָּמִים גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד מִדַּת יוֹסֵף
and Friday, which among the days of the week likewise corresponds to the attribute of Joseph,
שֶׁהוּא מִדָּה שִׁשִּׁית כַּנּוֹדָע,
being the sixth sefirotic attribute (Yesod) as is known,
נִבְרָא בְּאוֹת רֵי״שׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה,
was created through the letter Reish, as written in Sefer Yetzirah;
וְהֵם אַתְוָון דְּשִׁקְרָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בִּתְחִלַּת הַהַקְדָּמָה.
and together they constitute letters of falsehood (Reish and Kuf of Sheker), as stated in the Zohar at the beginning of the Introduction.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא,
And this is why this physical world is designated 'the World of Falsehood,'
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא – עָלְמָא דִּקְשׁוֹט.
whereas the World to Come is 'the World of Truth.'
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And Hashem, blessed be He, created this world;
הֲרֵי בָּרָא כֹּחַ זֶה הַשִּׁקְרָא,
thus He deliberately brought into being this power of apparent falsehood,
וְהַכֹּל נִבְרָא בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
and everything was fashioned through the letters of the Torah,
וְאוֹתִיּוֹת רֵי״שׁ קוֹ״ף הֵם כֹּחַ זֶה,
and the letters Reish-Kuf embody this force,
כִּי הַשִּׁי״ן הוּא יְסוֹדָא דִּקְשׁוֹט.
since the letter Shin constitutes the enduring foundation of truth.

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים לב, מז94 Deuteronomy 32:47 — For it is no empty thing for you, for it is your life; and through this thing you shall prolong your days upon the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess. Rashi: "For it is not an empty thing for you" — it is not for nothing that you labor in it, for much reward depends upon it, "for it is your life." Another explanation: there is no empty word in the Torah which, if you expound it properly, has no grant of reward attached to it.):
And that is what is meant by the verse (Deuteronomy 32:47):
"כִּי לֹא דָבָר רֵק וְגוֹמֵר",
"'For it is not an empty matter, etc.,'"

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֵּאָה פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה א95 Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 — This accords with what R. Mana said: "For it is not an empty thing from you" — and if it is empty, it is from you, because you do not labor in it. "For it is your life" — when is it your life? At the time when you labor in it. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "This accords with what R. Mana said"): On the verse "for it is not an empty thing from you, for it is your life": the two halves are not a thing and its opposite, and what is added by the word "from you"? He therefore expounds it thus — it is not an empty thing, and if it is empty, that is "from you," it only appears so to you because you do not labor in it. "For it is your life" is a further step beyond that: at the time when you do labor in it, not only will it not be empty for you, it will also be your very life and will endure in your hands.):
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Yerushalmi Peah 1:1):
"וְאִם רֵק – מִכֶּם הוּא, רַק לָמָּה? שֶׁאֵין אַתֶּם יְגֵיעִים".
"'And if it is empty—it is from you; but why? Because you do not exert yourselves.'"
דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא עוֹלַם הַיְגִיעָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְלוּת,
For this world is the realm of toil and strenuous effort,

וּ"מִי שֶׁטָּרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת יֹאכַל בְּשַׁבָּת" (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג96 Avodah Zarah 3a — They said before Him: Master of the Universe, give it to us anew and we will perform it. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: Fools of the world! One who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat; one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat — from where will he eat on Shabbat? Rashi: "On the eve of Shabbat" means in this world. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "and sukkah is its name"): Since the nations claim to be fit for the Torah, which is intellectual and beyond nature, He gave them the commandment that shows a person going out of his nature: leaving his fixed, natural dwelling to sit in the shade of the sukkah. The nations, whose whole conduct is natural, cannot bear this and kick at it; Israel too are somewhat natural, for man is not an angel, and are exempt from the sukkah when it causes them suffering, yet they do not kick, for they desire and love to go beyond nature, only that at such times it is impossible for them. This shows that the Torah, the whole of which is beyond nature, is not fit for the nations at all. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat"): That is, this world is the physical world, which is always in potential, and therefore commandments and good deeds belong to it, for in it things go out from potential into actuality. But in the World to Come a person is already in actuality, and going out into actuality has no place there, since it is not physical; the World to Come is therefore cessation and rest. Hence he said that one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat, the day of action, will eat on Shabbat, the day of rest, on which nothing goes out into actuality — and so the commandments pertain to this world alone. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 25): Shabbat is [the day on which God Himself is one's light, needing no fire of fear]; nevertheless one must toil to cook the food on the eve of Shabbat, for "one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, what will he eat on Shabbat?" and "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward": this light does not come to a person by itself. So too the Shabbat lamp must be lit from the eve of Shabbat, for on Shabbat there is no longer time to arouse fear, the day being entirely love and cleaving to God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): This world is the world of toil, and "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat" refers to the world to come, the day that is entirely Shabbat, where there is no doing even of Torah and mitzvot, as they said, "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward"; and Shabbat is a semblance of the world to come, the time of the Blessed One's rest. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Sukkah): Shabbat alludes to the future, when there will be no labor, but only what a person acquired in this world through his deeds will then be fixed in his heart, according to how much he toiled in this world. Therefore all labors are forbidden on Shabbat in this world, and only what one toiled for on the eve of Shabbat does one eat on Shabbat. Beis Yaakov (Vayeishev 3): All the possession a person acquires for himself in the world of action comes only from performing the mitzvot, and clarity [of understanding] alone does not suffice; by this he acquires the life of the world to come, for this world is like the eve of Shabbat and the world to come like Shabbat, and "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will have what to eat on Shabbat." Tiferes Yosef (Shemini Atzeres 4): A person calls his labor "toil" only where he does not see its purpose; on Shabbat he attains the light of the Blessed One and recognizes that he attained it through the work of the six days. This is "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat": through the toil and labor he expended he attains this light, and so he recognizes retroactively that all the activity of the six weekdays was not futile toil for him either. Sod Yesharim (Sukkos 18): In the future the nations will want to begin from the start, without first entering the gate of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the Blessed One answers that this is impossible: "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat" means that had they first refined themselves to be included in Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, within "every citizen in Israel" [which includes converts], they too could have kept the mitzvah of sukkah. But to begin now without that prior inclusion is impossible, for one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat has nothing to eat on Shabbat, and from where would he gain a share in the mitzvah of sukkah?.),
and 'he who toiled on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath' (Avodah Zarah 3a),
שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דִּקְשׁוֹט.
which is the realm of truth.
וְנִמְצָא גַּם הָעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ דָּבָר רֵק,
Consequently, the eve of Shabbat and this world are likewise not an empty matter at all;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יְגֵיעִים נִרְאֶה דָּבָר רֵק.
only because we fail to exert ourselves does it appear to be an empty thing.
וְעַל זֶה נִקְבַּע פּוּרִים בְּאוֹתוֹ חוֹדֶשׁ,
And regarding this, Purim was established specifically in that month of Adar,
דְּבוֹ חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע,
wherein one is obligated to become intoxicated until he knows not,
לוֹמַר דְּבֶאֱמֶת הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַמּוּלִים אָסוּר בְּעַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
to proclaim that in ultimate truth, one who vows against the circumcised is forbidden even to uncircumcised Jews,

דְּאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרָא אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נְדָרִים לא97 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along.:),
since uncircumcision is attributed by name solely to the pagan idolaters (as they stated in Nedarim 31b),
וְ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית,
and 'your people are all righteous,' faithful guardians of the Covenant,
שֶׁכֻּלָּם נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם יוֹסֵף: "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף".
since they are all titled after Joseph: 'the remnant of Joseph.'
וְהַגַּם שֶׁאֵין נִרְאֶה כֵּן,
And even though externally it may not appear so,
הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
it is merely a superficial appearance,
לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יְגֵיעִים נִרְאֶה דָּבָר רֵק וְעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא;
because we lack exertion it seems an empty thing and a world of falsehood;
אֲבָל "בְּשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים",
yet 'when Hashem brings back the captivity, etc., we were like dreamers,'
שֶׁהַכֹּל חֲלוֹם וְהָאֱמֶת אֵין כֵּן,
realizing that the illusion was merely a dream while reality is not so,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ",
for in truth 'all our deeds You have wrought for us,'
הֲגַם שֶׁאָנוּ לֹא יָדַעְנוּ בֵּין יָמִין לִשְׂמֹאל,
even while we knew not between right and left,

וְהַיְינוּ: "שְׁכֻרַת וְלֹא מִיָּיִן" (יְשַׁעְיָה נא, כא98 Isaiah 51:21 — "Therefore hear now this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine." Rashi: "And drunken, but not with wine" — drunk from something other than wine. Radak: "And drunken, but not with wine" — the meaning is: drunk with troubles, and not with wine. Metzudas Dovid: "Therefore" — since you have already received the recompense of your sin, hear now this. "And drunken" — confused like a drunkard, not from drinking wine but from trouble and grief. Malbim: "Therefore" — since there is none of your sons to save you, "hear now this, you afflicted one," made so by the cup of wrath; "and drunken, but not with wine" — drunk from troubles, by the cup of reeling, that is to say, made drunk by poverty and distress.).
which aligns with: 'Drunken, but not with wine' (Isaiah 51:21).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא נִיצּוּחַ לַעֲמָלֵק
And through this divine awareness comes the definitive triumph over Amalek,
שֶׁהָיָה זוֹרֵק מִילוֹתֵיהֶם כַּיָּדוּעַ,
who used to tauntingly cast upward the circumcised foreskins, as is known,
דְּלָכֵן אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף
which is why Amalek falls solely at the hand of the offspring of Joseph

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג99 Bava Batra 123b — R. Chelbo asked R. Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, "And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph" (Genesis 30:25) — what was different once Joseph was born [that Jacob then asked to return home]? He said to him: Jacob our father saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, as it is stated: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for straw, and they shall kindle in them and consume them" (Obadiah 1:18). Rashbam: "What was different" — why he did not wish to return to his father's house until Joseph was born. Maharsha: By acquiring the birthright and taking the blessing from Esau it was granted to Jacob that he should rule over Esau, who was the elder; and all of this Jacob handed on to Joseph, as is derived from "And I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite" (Genesis 48:22). It is in this way that the seed of Esau was delivered into the hand of Joseph and was not delivered into the hand of his other brothers. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Batra 123b): This matter — that the seed of Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph — is exceedingly deep. Over the seed of Joseph the eye has no power, while Esau's blessing is the opposite of this, as it is said, "and the hands are the hands of Esau" (Genesis 27:22) — for the hands are the most outward of the limbs, the rest being within. The seed of Joseph therefore prevail, because their blessing is from a place and a level over which Esau's eye has no power; whereas the other tribes, whose blessing was from the revealed level, could not overcome the power of Esau, which is itself revealed. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 58): Esau, who belongs only to this world, is called 'aluf', a captain of a thousand (the utmost of this world's blessing), but not the rank of a king who endures forever. Therefore Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, who was "ruler over all the land of Egypt": a ruler, that is, a minister and chief of the same pattern as 'aluf', like Messiah son of Joseph, who is at the rank of ruler and is slain, having no everlasting endurance, which belongs only to David. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The obstinacy of Israel issues from wisdom, through the knowledge that joins wisdom to the powers of action, and is obstinate only for the honor of Heaven; therefore Amalek falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek is the root of obstinacy, his chief claim being against the desires of Israel, as the Sages said on "who happened upon you"; but his obstinacy is against the will of the Blessed One, whereas the obstinacy of Joseph's seed accords with the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Of Amalek it is said, "and he feared not God," and the Sages said that this is why he falls into the hand of the seed of Joseph, of whom it is said, "I fear God." And though "he feared not God" refers to Israel, it means [that it came upon them] through Amalek "who happened upon you," who brought into them imaginings and forces of forgetfulness, whereby they became "faint and weary" and did not fear God. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph because, as the Sages said, "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven": fear of Heaven is the province of man's choice and effort, for love can come into a person's heart of itself, but fear cannot. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eira 1): Before Benjamin's birth Jacob was given tidings of Benjamin, Menashe and Ephraim, who are Amalek's adversaries, as the Gemara says that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek stands against the holiness of the covenant (they would cut off the circumcisions of Israel), while Menashe and Ephraim are Joseph's two tribes, and Benjamin too is the attribute of the Tzaddik; therefore the name E-l Sha-dai, which corresponds to the attribute of the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world, is mentioned there. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 38): On account of Rachel's modesty the Holy One, blessed be He, restored [the birthright] to her, in that every beginning of salvation is aroused through her children. Thus every beginning of salvation is revealed through the children of Rachel, as the Gemara says that Jacob saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. Sod Yesharim (Purim 15): If Israel rely on the strength they possess from their root, Amalek at once stands against them, claiming that he too has strength from the root, being born of Isaac and Rebecca. Therefore the Sages said that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph: the seed of Joseph rely on no strength at all, but clarify wherever there is something to clarify, and where the power of their service does not reach, there the Blessed One will clarify it for good.:),
(as written in Bava Batra 123b),
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר
namely in the month of Adar,
וּבְכֹחַ זֶה שֶׁאָנוּ דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם בְּעֵת הַבִּיסּוּם עַד דְּלָא יָדַע,
and by virtue of this reality where we cling to Hashem, blessed be He, even during the state of intoxication 'until he knows not';
כִּי אֵין אָנוּ צְרִיכִים יְדִיעָה וְהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת שֵׂכֶל כְּלָל,
for we require neither intellectual knowledge nor conscious contemplation,
דְּעֶצֶם שָׁרְשֵׁינוּ דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
since our essential root remains cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְכָל אֲשֶׁר אָנוּ עוֹשִׂים הוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה,
and all that we enact, He is the ultimate Doer,
וְזֶהוּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה.
and this relates to the realm of deed.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
And following this, the month of Nisan,
וּבַיָּמִים יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
and among the days of the week, the holy Sabbath day,
הוּא עַל הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
corresponds to the higher realm of thought,
וְשֶׁגַּם כָּל הִרְהוּרָא דְּיוֹמָא שֶׁלָּנוּ דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
signifying that even all our daytime reflections remain bound to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְשֶׁגַּם עַל מַחְשְׁבוֹת שֶׁלָּנוּ נֶאֱמַר:
and that even regarding our inner thoughts it is proclaimed:

"מְאֹד עָמְקוּ מַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים צב, ו100 Psalms 92:6 — How great are Your works, O Lord; Your thoughts are very deep. Radak: When I contemplate Your works I recognize that they are great, and too high for us to grasp them in their perfection. So too "Your thoughts are very deep" — the reasons of the world were never disclosed even to the wise, who are left with hard questions such as why God created the world at this particular time and not earlier; the answer is that His wisdom so decreed, and we do not know His mind. Metzudas Dovid: "They are deep" — these are deep matters, and they cannot be understood. Malbim: Your ordered works of nature are "great" and plain to every eye, but "Your thoughts are very deep" in that You have hidden Your providential governance, so that a man does not always find it and many suppose that the world simply runs its course by nature. This depth is deliberate: were the wicked punished at once and all governance openly providential, men would be afraid to do evil and there would be no free choice, and so no reward and punishment.),
"'Your thoughts are exceedingly deep' (Psalms 92:6),"
וְזֶהוּ הַגְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁמֵּעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and this constitutes the complete redemption which serves as the foretaste of the World to Come.

sections.en: Love, Fear, Cleaving, and the Patriarchs

items.h: The three Patriarchs root love, fear, and cleaving within every Jewish soul, with Torah and prayer completing their expression in later generations.

Seif 1 — Love, Fear, and Cleaving
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob embody love, fear, and Torah-cleaving - the three fundamental modes of divine service.

p: שְׁלֹשָׁה עַמּוּדֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה הֵם אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה וּדְבֵיקוּת.
The three pillars of divine service are love, fear, and cleaving.
אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה הֵם תְּרֵין גַּדְפִּין וּשְׁתֵּי זְרוֹעוֹת עוֹלָם
Love and fear are the two wings and the two eternal arms,
וְהֵם תְּרֵין אֲבָהָן אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק.
and they correspond to the two Patriarchs, Abraham and Isaac.
וּדְבֵיקוּת הוּא מַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּגוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא,
Cleaving represents one who grasps the very body of the King,
צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, being engraved upon the Throne of Glory;
"אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב"
"truth to Jacob,"
וְאֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
and there is no truth other than Torah

(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ח, יח101 Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 3:8 — Samuel said: "And a host was given over, together with the daily offering, through transgression" (Daniel 8:12) — through the transgression of the Torah. "And it cast truth to the ground" — whenever Israel casts the words of the Torah to the ground, this wicked kingdom decrees and succeeds. What is the reason? "It cast truth to the ground, and it acted and succeeded." And there is no truth but Torah, as you say, "Buy truth and do not sell it, wisdom and instruction and understanding" (Proverbs 23:23). Pnei Moshe (s.v. "through the transgression of the Torah"): When transgressors grow slack and cast the Torah aside, then "a host is given over" against them. And because the verse "they encamped in Rephidim" is likewise expounded to mean that they let their hands go slack from the Torah, and therefore "Amalek came," these verses too are expounded here in the same manner..),
(Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah 3:8, 18a),
וּמַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אָחִיד בְּגוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא,
and one who holds onto Torah holds onto the King's essence;
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is stated: 'And you who cling, etc.,'
דְּכוּלָּם נִקְרְאוּ בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב וְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
for all are called by the name of Jacob and Israel,

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד102 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..)
and 'even though he sinned, he remains Israel' (Sanhedrin 44a),
וְלֹא נִיתַּק מִמִּדַּת דְּבֵיקוּת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת,
and is never truly severed from the attribute of cleaving unto Hashem, blessed be He;

כִּי לֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר עֲרָיוֹת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם סג103 Sanhedrin 63b — Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: Israel knew that idolatry has no substance to it, and they served idols only in order to permit themselves forbidden sexual relations in public. Rashi: "Only to permit themselves forbidden relations in public": because their inclination overpowered them in the matter of forbidden relations, they said, "Let us throw off the whole yoke of the Torah from upon us, and let no one rebuke us over forbidden relations"; but in the matter of idolatry their inclination did not overpower them. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The Sages said that [Israel] served idolatry only to permit forbidden relations, for the root of idolatry is not found in Israel at all; and what is said, "lest there be among you a root," stems only from the inclination to forbidden relations, which exists in Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 9): Although the inclination to idolatry, once it came into action among the nations, spread to Israel as well, the Gemara says that they served idolatry only to permit forbidden relations: among them this inclination found no full expansion within their hearts of its own accord, and they came to idolatry only through being enticed toward desire, until "after they had become attached to it," when this inclination too entered their very hearts. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 3): The root of all the particular forces of evil is the desire for eating, the first entry of evil, from which one comes afterward to every kind of evil; even the inclination to idolatry begins from desire, as it says, "Israel served idolatry only to permit forbidden relations." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Micah, who kicked at the root of Jewishness, was led to his idol by being swept up in a desire for money beyond all bounds, serving no pleasure at all; for all desire for bodily pleasure falls under the desire for forbidden relations, which exists in Israel too, and "they served idolatry only to permit forbidden relations in public." Hence the impurity of zivah, which comes through desire, does not send one out of the camp of Israel, for it is within the bond [of all Israel].:),
for Israel served idolatry solely to permit illicit relations (as written there, 63b),
תַּאֲווֹת וַאֲהָבוֹת רָעוֹת.
namely base desires and corrupted loves.
וְכָל הַחֲטָאִים הֵן בִּתְרֵין גַּדְפִּין,
All sins occur within the two wings,

וַהֲלָכָה: נִשְׁבְּרוּ אֲגַפֶּיהָ כָּשֵׁר (חֻלִּין נו:)104 Chullin 56b — And these are kosher among birds: if the windpipe was pierced or split; if a weasel struck it on the head in a place that does not render it a torn animal; if the crop was pierced; if its innards came out but were not pierced; if its wings were broken; if its legs were broken; if its wing feathers were plucked. Rashi: "The crop" is the pouch in which the food collects. "Its wings" means the bones of the wings; "its legs were broken" means from the knee-joint downward, or even above it, provided the bone did not protrude — for where it protruded we have learned that the bird is a torn animal. "Its wing feathers were plucked" refers to the large plumage covering the whole body, whereas the down is the fine covering next to the flesh, which has no quills. Tosafos (s.v. "but if he jumbled them it is a torn animal"): This falls within the mishna's own category of "perforated," for the reason is that they will in the end be perforated and rot. כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and the halakhah states: 'if its wings are broken, it remains kosher' (Chullin 56b), as is known.
אֲבָל בְּגוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא שָׁם אֵין חֵטְא,
However, within the King's essence there is no sin,
דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
for our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had a bed that was whole,
וְאֵין שׁוּם זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל נִיתַּק מֵעֶצֶם דְּבֵיקוּתוֹ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל,
and no seed of Israel is ever severed from its essential cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He, whatsoever;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "יִפֹּל מִצִּדְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
and concerning this it is stated: 'A thousand shall fall at your side, etc.,'
כִּי זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים,
for God made one corresponding to the other.
שְׁלֹשָׁה כֹּחוֹת הָרַע הֵם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
The three forces of evil are idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed.
וְיָדוּעַ: הָעוֹמֵד לְעוּמַּת חֲבֵירוֹ יָמִין זֶה נֶגֶד שְׂמֹאל זֶה וְכוּלֵי
And it is known: when standing face-to-face with another, one's right faces the other's left, etc.
(עַיֵּין רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רמו עַמּוּד ב).
(see Ra'aya Meheimna, Zohar Part III, 246b).
וְזֶהוּ "יִפֹּל וְגוֹמֵר",
And this explains 'shall fall, etc.':
דְּהַשְּׂמֹאל דְּהַיְינוּ יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִיא מַפֶּלֶת תַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת.
that the left, which is fear of Hashem, blessed be He, fells wicked desires.
וּכְמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב: "כִּי אָמַרְתִּי רַק אֵין יִרְאַת וְגוֹמֵר",
And as explicitly stated in Scripture: 'For I thought: surely there is no fear of God in this place...'
כִּי הַשְּׁקוּעִים בְּתַאֲוָה אֵין יִרְאָה נֶגֶד פְּנֵיהֶם.
for those immersed in lust have no fear set before their eyes.

וּלְכָךְ הַיִּרְאָה הִיא תַּרְעָא לְאָעָלָא וְכוּלֵי (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א, יא עַמּוּד ב105 Zohar, Introduction 13:120-123 — "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord." This verse ought to have read, "The end of wisdom is the fear of the Lord," since the fear of the Lord is the end of wisdom. Rather, it is the beginning, for entering into the grade of supernal Wisdom; as it is written, "Open to me the gates of righteousness" — "This is the gate to the Lord" indeed, for whoever does not enter by this gate never enters at all. So too, the first gate to supernal Wisdom is the fear of the Lord. Therefore fear rests in this place, and this is the gate through which one enters to all the good of the world.),
Therefore fear is the gateway to enter, etc. (Zohar Part I, 11b),
הַיְינוּ הַהַתְחָלָה בְּיַלְדוּת דְּאָז יֵצֶר הַתַּאֲווֹת בּוֹעֵר.
which is the beginning in youth, when the fire of desire burns.
"וְיִפֹּל" – רַק אֶלֶף,
And there falls only a thousand,

כִּי אָמְרוּ106 Sotah 47a — Our Rabbis taught: Let the left hand always push away and the right hand draw near — not as Elisha did, who thrust Gehazi away with both hands. Maharsha (on the parallel sugya, Sanhedrin 107b, to which he refers here): [The baraita] assigns the pushing away to the left hand and the drawing near to the right because everywhere the left alludes to the attribute of judgment and the right to mercy: thus "let the left," which is the attribute of judgment, push away, and let the right, which is mercy, draw near. "Not as Elisha, who thrust Gehazi away with both hands" — that is, he turned even the mercy into anger. (סוֹטָה מז.):
for they taught (Sotah 47a):
"יֵצֶר וְכוּלֵי וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת".
'The left pushes away, and the right draws close.'
אֲבָל "רְבָבָה מִימִינֶךָ"
However, 'ten thousand at your right hand'
עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַגּוֹרֶמֶת אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
occurs through the love of Hashem, blessed be He, which generates love of Israel
וְדוֹחָה רְצִיחָה וָכַעַס וְקִנְאָה וַאֲבִיזְרַיְיהוּ,
and entirely banishes bloodshed, wrath, jealousy, and their offshoots;
וּלְאֵלּוּ הִיא דּוֹחָה לְגַמְרֵי דְּאֵין בָּזֶה קֵירוּב כְּלָל.
and these it rejects utterly, since there is no room to draw them close at all.
"וְיִפֹּל רְבָבָה" – לְשׁוֹן רִיבּוּי מְאֹד,
And 'ten thousand shall fall' denotes tremendous multitude,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֶלֶף הוּא גַּם כֵּן סַךְ רַב דֶּרֶךְ גּוּזְמָא בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת,
whereas a thousand is also a large hyperbolic sum in various places,
אֲבָל הוּא תַּחַת סוּג הַמִּסְפָּר,
yet it still falls under a measurable category of number,
כִּי אֶלֶף הוּא סוֹף הַמִּסְפָּר הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב.
for a thousand is the ultimate highest named number in biblical usage.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רִבּוֹא לְשׁוֹן רִיבּוּי אֵינוֹ בְּסוּג הַמִּסְפָּר,
In contrast, 'myriad' denotes boundless expansion beyond basic counting,
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּלֹא גְּבוּל;
meaning without limitation;
אֲבָל שָׁם הַהַפָּלָה בִּגְבוּל,
yet there, the felling occurs within boundaries,
דִּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְרִיבּוּי בְּלֹא גְּבוּל שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיָמִין אָז הִיא מְקָרֶבֶת,
for when it reaches boundless expansion, which is the realm of the right, it draws near,

כְּטַעַם: "אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ וְכוּלֵי מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ" (סֻכָּה נב107 Sukkah 52b — The school of R. Yishmael taught: If this loathsome one accosts you, drag him to the study hall. If he is stone he will dissolve; if he is iron he will shatter. If he is stone he will dissolve, as it is written, "Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water," and it is written, "Water wears away stones." If he is iron he will shatter, as it is written, "Is not My word like fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that shatters rock?" Rashi: "This loathsome one": the evil inclination. "Come for water": Torah is likened to water, and it is written, "Water wears away stones." "My word like fire": and fire penetrates iron; this is "shatters," for the sparks fly off from it. Tosafos (s.v. "if he is iron he will shatter"): This is puzzling, for the verse implies that the hammer, which is iron, shatters the rock [and is not itself shattered]; some therefore read here, "If he is iron, [fire] penetrates him, as it is said, 'Is not My word like fire,' and fire penetrates iron; if he is rock, he shatters, as it is said, 'like a hammer that shatters rock.'" Rabbeinu Tam upholds the reading of the books and explains "like a hammer that the rock shatters," as in the Midrash of a man who bought a sapphire and tested it on an anvil with a hammer: the anvil split and the hammer broke, but the sapphire did not move from its place. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Koach HaYetzer 1): This comes to make known the virtue of the Torah: the evil inclination is called "loathsome" because it is the deficiency that clings to man, whereas the Torah is perfect and without any deficiency, so that insofar as a man is joined to the Torah the evil inclination does not rule him, and he remains at the level of an angel, as though wholly intellect. "Stone" is the inclination to sexual immorality, which lies in the body — "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh" — for stone, the hardest of things, corresponds to the inclination that clings to inert matter; and "iron," from which the sword and the axe and all instruments of destruction are made, corresponds to the evil inclination in the soul, which is an active power, a power that does evil. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 26): Words of Torah are like fire, burning up every evil desire: "If this loathsome one accosts you" — that is the inclination to forbidden relations and lust — and when one drags him to the study hall he dissolves and shatters. They said "drag him to the study hall," not that he should go and learn by himself, nor "drag him to words of Torah," because although all words of Torah are like fire, there is a strong, blazing fire and a small, weak one, and so are the levels of words of Torah: in the study hall, where Torah is disseminated and the many study together, words of Torah act more, for the power of the fire in them is stronger. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): All sanctifying of the power of desire is only through Torah, as stated: "If this loathsome one accosts you" — this is the power of desire, which is utter loathsomeness, and they said "this" as though pointing with a finger, because it is present in everyone, even the most pious — "drag him to the study hall; if he is stone he will dissolve," as it is written, "Water wears away stones," for words of Torah too are likened to water. He draws all his desire and longing into words of Torah and finds all his delight there, and thereby the heart of stone, which signifies the force of desire, dissolves; and "if he is iron he will shatter" may allude to the inclination to murder, for iron kills. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): "Drag him to the study hall": the ordinary inclination is that of desire, especially since the inclination to idolatry was nullified, and it is the one called "loathsome," for there is no loathsomeness like it. The remedy the Blessed One created for this desire is desire for words of Torah: that they draw all their desire into words of Torah, for which they have great longing, and find in it the fulfillment of their desire. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Noach 3): Suffering repairs the past, and the Oral Torah repairs for the future, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah — that is, the Oral Torah, as stated, "If this loathsome one accosts you, drag him to the study hall," which is the place where new halakhos are innovated. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 223): Words of Torah are like a sword, which kills at close range: even one surrounded and entangled in stray thoughts on every side, if he turns to words of Torah, they kill and nullify them, as stated, "If this loathsome one accosts you" — even if he has already accosted and touched you, drag him to the study hall and he shatters. But the synagogue and prayer do not help at all once he has already accosted and one is entangled in such thoughts.:),
in the spirit of: 'If this disgraceful one confronts you, drag him to the study hall' (Sukkah 52b),
הַיְינוּ לֹא שֶׁתִּדְחֵהוּ, רַק תִּמְשְׁכֵהוּ לְשָׁם.
meaning: do not push him away, but rather draw him in.
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין כְּמוֹ דָּבָר הַמְּתַבֵּל וְעוֹשֶׂה הַבָּאוּשׁ טוֹב וְטַעַם לִשְׁבָח.
For the Torah is a spice, seasoning and transforming what is spoiled into goodness and pleasing flavor.
"וְאֵלֶיךָ" דְּהַיְינוּ לְגוּפָא "לֹא יִגָּשׁ",
And 'unto you'—meaning to your essential core—'it shall not approach,'
דְּשָׁם אֵין שְׁלִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע כְּלָל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
for there the evil inclination holds no sway whatsoever, as noted above,
דַּאֲפִילּוּ כָּל רוּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם לֹא יְזִיזוּ מִגּוּף הַדְּבֵיקוּת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
since all the winds in the world cannot budge the essential cleaving of Israel to their Father in Heaven,
וּ"מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת וְגוֹמֵר".
and 'many waters cannot quench the love, etc.'
וְזֶה טַעַם "תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת בָּהֶם"
And this is the reason why 'the fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars'

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף חֲגִיגָה כז108 Chagigah 27a — R. Abbahu said in the name of R. Elazar: The fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars. This follows a fortiori from the salamander: if the salamander, which is born of fire, is such that one who anoints himself with its blood is untouched by fire, then Torah scholars, whose whole body is fire — as it is written, "Is not My word like fire, says the Lord" — how much more so. Rashi: The salamander is a creature born of fire, formed when a fire is kept burning in one place for seven years continuously, without interruption. Tosafos (s.v. "salamander"): The Arukh: "the weasel and the mouse" (Leviticus 11:29) are rendered by Yonatan as karkushta and salamandra. Maharsha: Because the words of Torah are themselves fire, the bodies of those who learn them become fire, as they said, "A Torah scholar who seethes — it is the Torah within him that makes him seethe." As for Acher, from whose grave smoke rose and over whom the fire of Gehenna did have power, he was worse than other Torah scholars, for, as the Jerusalem Talmud says, he knew his Master and rebelled against Him. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 26): At the end of Chagigah the fire of Torah is likened to the fire of Gehenna — therefore the fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars, and they derived it from the salamander, for it is all one fire — and afterwards the fire of Gehenna is likened there to the fire of the altar, a fire from above that consumes yet does not destroy. It is like the purging of an iron vessel in fire, which expels the absorbed flavors while the vessel itself remains: it burns only the evil absorbed in this world, and in Torah scholars the fire of Torah burns it away in this world. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Although the inclination is stronger in Torah scholars, they said at the end of Chagigah that the fire of Gehenna has no power over them because their whole body is fire; for the fire of Gehenna is the fire of the desires — "your spirit is a fire that shall consume you": the fire of Gehenna is made from the sin itself — and the fire of Torah is a fire that consumes the fire of Gehenna. "Their whole body is fire" means that they leave the category of body altogether, for everywhere fire alludes to something spiritual. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): Gehenna is chiefly for corruptions of the covenant, and for this there is no repair except through Torah; about this they said that the fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars — for they have surely repented, since the light of Torah brings them back to the good and they repair what came before. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Of Israel who engage in Torah it is said at the end of Chagigah that their whole body is fire, as it says, "Is not My word like fire"; and the sinners of Israel too, of whom it is said there that they are full of mitzvos — when they engage in the Torah's mitzvos they are engaged in Torah and cleave to it and become fire, and therefore the fire of Gehenna has no power over them either. This comes through their cleaving to the Blessed One by engaging in His mitzvos, for He is a fire that consumes the fire of Gehenna, which comes from the burning of evil desires. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 15): Reish Lakish's statement about the sinners of Israel is introduced as "said Reish Lakish," not "Reish Lakish said" as one who comes to disagree, implying that the two do not disagree; but then, if the fire of Gehenna has no power even over all the sinners of Israel, why need R. Elazar say it only of Torah scholars, because their body is fire? They said "has no power," not "they do not enter at all," so clearly they do enter, only the fire does not rule over them — yet this cannot mean that they do not feel the burning at all, for then why would they enter? And from Acher, from whose grave smoke rose, we see that it did rule over him even though his whole body was fire. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 144): The essence of a person is not the body but the soul, which is the power that thinks; wherever his thought is fixed, there the whole person is. So one who cleaves to Torah and thinks of it constantly — all his limbs become so, as the Sages said: the fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars, for their whole body is fire, as it says, "Is not My word like fire." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 10): Through R. Yochanan, Acher too entered the Garden of Eden: the smoke and fire of the evil desires that surrounded him were extinguished, and the light of his Torah was revealed, though his deeds were not so. When his daughter said to Rebbi, "Remember his Torah," fire licked at [Rebbi's] bench — that is, the fire of his Torah, for "Is not My word like fire," and Torah scholars' whole body is fire, wherefore the fire of Gehenna has no power over them, as they said at the end of Chagigah..),
(as written at the end of Chagigah 27a),
כְּטַעַם "אֵלֶיךָ לֹא יִגָּשׁ",
in accordance with 'it shall not approach you,'
דְּמַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אָחִיד בְּגוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא.
for whoever holds fast to Torah holds fast to the King's essence.
וְשַׁלְהוֹבָא דְּיִצְרָא בִישָׁא הוּא עַצְמוֹ אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם,
And the flame of the evil inclination is itself the fire of Gehenna,
וּלְגוּפָא לֹא יִגַּשׁ כְּלָל וְאֵין לוֹ שְׁלִיטָה בֶּאֱמֶת.
and it shall not approach the King's core at all, possessing no genuine dominion.

items.h:
Seif 2 — The Patriarchal Roots within Every Soul
The spiritual powers of the Patriarchs are inherited by Israel and await their full expression through prayer.

p: וּמַעֲשֵׂה אָבוֹת סִימָן לַבָּנִים,
And the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children,
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ הַבֵּן מִטִּיפֵּי מוֹחַ שֶׁל הָאָב,
for the root of the son's soul is drawn from the mental essence of the father;

דְּלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב דְּעֵדֻיּוֹת מִשְׁנָה ט109 Mishnah Eduyot 2:9 — He used to say: A father endows his son with beauty, with strength, with wealth, with wisdom, and with length of years, and with the number of the generations before him — and that is the End [of the exile], as it is said, "He calls the generations from the beginning." Even though it is said, "And they shall serve them and afflict them four hundred years," it is also said, "And in the fourth generation they shall return here." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 18): David was chosen both for his own merit and for his father's; the Sages' reading implies that the choice was from the outset one of Jesse's sons, for "a father endows his son" etc. So too many came by the merit of their fathers, and mostly their fathers' merit assists them; only Abraham, the father of the whole world, who had none before him and did not come by his fathers' merit, is therefore called the first of converts. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:143): [Solomon attained this] as an inheritance from his father: since the halakha is that a son inherits his father, it is truly his, and "a father endows his son" etc., for the son is drawn from the father's very essence. He truly has the father's power in him, only with more added, and therefore the father endows the son and not the son the father. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part I 61): This is also why Torah scholars do not have sons who are Torah scholars: a father endows his son with wisdom, even though choice is in man's hand, only through the blessing "Make [the words of Your Torah] pleasant … and our offspring"; and it comes about because they did not recite this blessing. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): Moses did not bequeath his crown to his sons — not on his own account, even though a father endows his son with wisdom, but because the Blessed One did not want it, on account of the generation, which was not worthy and might have erred into thinking that Torah is an inheritance.):
which is why they taught (end of Eduyot 2:9):
"הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
'A father endows his son, etc.,'
וּבִפְרָט אֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
especially the Patriarchs of the world,
אֵין לְךָ נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה כָּלוּל בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת,
there being no soul among Israel that does not contain a root from the three Patriarchs,
דְּלָכֵן נִקְרְאוּ אָבוֹת.
which is why they are called Fathers.
וְאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק אֵין מִטָּתָן שְׁלֵימָה דְּנִמְצָא בָּהֶן פְּסוֹלֶת,
Now, Abraham and Isaac did not have a completely pure bed, as dross emerged from them;
כֵּן מִדַּת אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
similarly, the attributes of love and fear cannot be entirely perfected,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ110 Vayikra Rabbah 14:5 — Even the most pious of the pious cannot be free of some measure of transgression in this matter. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:10): The meaning of "the counsel of the serpent" is learned from Jesse, who is counted among the four who died through it, and of whom the Sages said, on "in iniquity was I formed," "even the most pious of the pious…". In Elijah, who did not die, even the serpent's counsel was rectified, and he, the angel of the covenant, testifies concerning birth that it is not, Heaven forbid, in iniquity, but that all are holy from the womb. Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 12): Death still comes through the counsel of the serpent, that is, the filth the serpent cast [into Eve], and that filth is the desire for lewdness, about which the Sages said of Jesse, one of the four who died through the serpent's counsel, "even the most pious of the pious…". Only Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their filth cease, and then they were truly free of the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 19): The seminal drop is drawn from the brain, but because it comes with the desire of this world, as the Sages said, "even the most pious of the pious…", it imparts impurity; yet the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth the pure from the impure, for a child is formed from it. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 16): The beginning [of a fall] is in matters of desire, where everyone is in any case somewhat lax about complete holiness like that of Jacob our father, who intended only to raise offspring and was aroused only for the sake of the mitzvah and of Heaven; not every person merits this, as the Sages said on "in iniquity," "even the most pious of the pious…". This comes from laxity in the service of the Blessed One and in bringing the holiness of the words of Torah into one's heart, for one whose thought cleaves to the love of Torah will let no desire for anything else enter him. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): On "in iniquity was I formed," with "iniquity" written full, the Midrash says that even the most pious of the pious intends only his own pleasure; this is Jesse, the father of David, and this is the counsel of the serpent, a deficiency in the birth of everyone born of woman, of the offspring of Eve, against which no effort avails, even for the most pious of the pious. Only, as the Sages said, "Who purifies you? The Holy One, blessed be He": the purification from this is His, for He testifies that this desire of Israel is clean and pure. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 5): The impurity of childbirth applies even when a woman bears a righteous one, even the Messiah, and its reason is the Midrash on "Behold, in iniquity was I formed": R. Acha says, "even the most pious of the pious… did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? Surely he intended only his own pleasure." This was said of Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, and the serpent's counsel is what the serpent instilled in man, that he should feel his own pleasure; from this sprang the impurity of the menstruant and the seven-day impurity of childbirth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, was clarified through the birth of David, who applied to himself "Behold, in iniquity was I formed," which the Sages expounded from "iniquity" being written full: "even the most pious of the pious…". As is known from the Arizal, wherever letters of the Divine Name are added they indicate added holiness, and vav is the letter of truth; for desire is called falsehood, being a pleasure of the moment, whereas the desire of Israel, who cleave to the living God, endures as they do, for all their powers cleave to holiness. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 147): Only the Unique One of the world can bring forth the pure from the impure, for in this desire lies the source of the deficiencies that come from the serpent, as the Sages said on "in iniquity" [written full], and that is Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent. Man's root is in truth impure, as it is written, "in iniquity was I formed," yet there is holiness and purity in it as well; Balaam, being of an evil root, did not believe this, for he did not know that there could be holiness here too. (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ יד, ה):
and as they said (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Tazria 14:5):
"אֲפִילּוּ חֲסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי" לְעִנְיַן תַּאֲוָה.
'Even the most pious among the pious, etc.,' regarding bodily desire.

וְכֵן אָמַר (מִשְׁלֵי כז, ד111 Proverbs 27:4 — Wrath is cruel and anger overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy? Rashi: “But who can stand before jealousy” — who can stand before the jealousy of Him who is jealous and vengeful? Metzudas Dovid: Fury brings a man to cruelty, and anger incites him to sweep away and destroy; but before a jealous man, who can stand and endure? For jealousy is harsher still than fury and anger, since the jealous man will choose the evil that falls upon his fellow as well over the good that would come to himself and his fellow alike. Malbim: “Fury” is inward anger, in which a man nurses hatred in his heart, and “anger” is outward anger.
