Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): All [Israel] is one assembly, and a deficiency in part of it is in the whole; this brought about the destruction of the First Temple, until the Men of the Great Assembly arose to repair the assembly by nullifying the inclination for idolatry, and therefore they were called the Great Assembly, for through them the assembly was made great. But the inclination for sexual transgression remained, which causes licentiousness and the casting off of the yoke, and from it derive heresy and the Sadducees. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 5): The shell of idolatry can be repaired completely, from its root, so that it is nullified entirely, as we find with the Men of the Great Assembly, who nullified the inclination for idolatry. But the corruption of Adam, which came about through the serpent in the lust for eating, after which [the serpent] cast filth into Eve, is a blemish that cannot be repaired entirely in this world. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, from the Yerushalmi 16): Seeing the magnitude of the sins, the Men of the Great Assembly said, "We want neither it nor its reward," and nullified the inclination for idolatry. Through subduing that inclination, the opposite of recognizing the Blessed One, [Israel] had attained the revelation of the Shechinah; so once the sin made it necessary to nullify it, prophecy and the Shechinah departed from Israel as a matter of course, for nothing was left through which to attain that revelation, and everything was in concealment. Sod Yesharim (Purim 32): In the days of Ahasuerus the Blessed One handed over to the Men of the Great Assembly the entire conduct [of the world] until the time of the end, as we find that the inclinations for idolatry and for sexual transgression were delivered into their hands. Had they wished, it was within their power to subdue all the forces in the world beneath them and bring them into holiness; but they held themselves back from receiving any good before the time that had arisen in His simple will to grant it to them.",
they said: 'Neither it do we desire, nor its reward,'
פֵּירוּשׁ אַגְרֵיהּ – הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ,
meaning by 'its reward' the corresponding perfection drawn down through it;
כִּי מֵעֵת שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר יִצְרָא דְּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
for from the time the inclination for idolatry was uprooted,
נִסְתַּלְּקָה נְבוּאָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
prophecy departed from Israel.
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר אֵין חִסָּרוֹן בָּזֶה,
For when there is no deficiency in this realm,
אֵין שְׁלֵימוּת לִהְיוֹת הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח דֵּאלֹהֵי אֱמֶת לָעַיִן,
there is no corresponding perfection to perceive the direct Presence of the true God visibly,
רַק בְּהֶעְלֵם
rather only in concealment,
כְּטַעַם "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא"
mirroring the principle 'a sage is superior to a prophet,'
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
which operates via divine inspiration (Ruach HaKodesh),

(עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַמְבַּ״ן בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא יב167 Chiddushei Ramban on Bava Batra 12a — As to what we say, "From the day the Temple was destroyed, although prophecy was taken from the prophets, from the Sages it was not taken" — Rashi explained: although it was taken from prophets who are not Sages. But this may be objected to, for we say in tractate Nedarim (38a) that the Holy One, blessed be He, causes His Presence to rest only upon one who is wise, mighty, and wealthy. Rather, this is what is meant: although the prophecy of the prophets, which is vision and sight, was taken away, the prophecy of the Sages, which comes by way of wisdom, was not taken away; rather they know the truth through the holy spirit that is within them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Korach 14): As the Zohar says, Malchus "is the holy spirit," and this is the aspect of the Oral Torah, as the Ramban wrote: it is concerning this that they said "a sage is preferable to a prophet," for [the sage's wisdom] comes through the holy spirit..)
(see there in Ramban on Bava Batra 12a)
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם.
and this stems from the concealed dimension.

לְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (ז, ח168 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:8 — "This your stature is like a palm tree." R. Chuniya said in the name of R. Dosa bar Tevet: Two inclinations did the Holy One, blessed be He, create in His world — the inclination to idolatry and the inclination to sexual immorality. The inclination to idolatry has already been uprooted; the inclination to immorality still stands. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Whoever is able to withstand immorality, I credit it to him as though he had withstood both of them. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, from the Tanchuma 9): The misleadings of the inclination are in sum two, the inclination for idolatry and the inclination for sexual transgression, as in Shir HaShirim Rabbah: the latter is immersion in all the delights of the lowly world and total forgetting of the Blessed One, the power in man that cleaves to material things, while the inclination for idolatry comes from the power of the soul to cleave to the supernal, and cleaves to foreign supernal powers. For whatever is in the great world is in man: as heaven and earth include all of creation, so these two powers are in man, to use for good or the reverse; with the heavenly he may cleave to the host of heaven to worship them, with the earthly to all the pleasures of the earth, and the other inclinations are secondary to them.):
Because they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (7:8):
דְּאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
that the Holy One, blessed be He, declared:
"הַנִּשְׁמָר מִיֵּצֶר רַע דִּזְנוּת – מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו כְּאִלּוּ נִשְׁמַר מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם".
'Whoever guards himself against the evil inclination of illicit desire is credited as though he guarded against both of them.'
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, הַשְּׁמִירָה מִיִּצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם,
Nonetheless, vigilance against the inclination for idolatry remains in concealment;
לְכָךְ הַהַשָּׂגָה גַּם כֵּן בְּהֶעְלֵם.
therefore the spiritual perception is likewise achieved in concealment.

וְאָמַר בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קב169 Sanhedrin 102b — Rav Ashi broke off his lecture at [the chapter of] the three kings and said: Tomorrow we will open with our colleagues. Manasseh came and appeared to him in his dream. He said to him: You call us your colleague and your father's colleague? From where are you required to begin breaking the loaf for [the blessing] "Who brings forth bread"? He said to him: I do not know. He said to him: You have not learned even from where you must begin breaking the loaf for "Who brings forth bread," and you call us your colleague? He said to him: Teach it to me, and tomorrow I will expound it in your name in my lecture. He said to him: From the place where it has been crusted by the baking. Rashi: Rav Ashi concluded that chapter of his lecture on reaching the three kings and said, "Tomorrow we will open with our colleagues" — we will expound about our colleagues, who were Torah scholars like us and have no share in the World to Come. "From where do you break for 'Who brings forth'" — from which place in the loaf you must break for the blessing; answer: from where the face of the loaf has crusted in the oven — the top, the sides or the edges, but not the middle — so that even if a slice of bread is brought to him he should break and bless from the edge of the loaf and not from its middle. "You would have lifted the hem of your garment" — you would have raised the edge of your robe from between your legs so as to run lightly, and would have run there, because of the inclination to idolatry that then held sway. Maharsha: "We will open with our colleagues" was said on account of Menashe, who according to R. Yehuda has a share in the World to Come because he repented; of Jeroboam and Ahab Rav Ashi would not have said it. Menashe therefore objected to being counted with them as "your colleague" in this world and "your father's colleague" in the World to Come, for they have no share there while he, through his repentance, has one; and his question about where to begin "Who brings forth" hints at the same point: the blessing over bread differs from the other blessings over created things, because after Adam's sin the earth no longer yields bread by its nature, and it is by God's kindness, won through repentance, that He "brings forth bread from the earth." "You would have grasped the hems" recalls "her impurity is in her skirts": you too would have lusted after the impurity of idolatry and run after me, for the inclination to idolatry still existed until the Men of the Great Assembly abolished it. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 102b): Rav Ashi held that the kings strayed after idolatry not because their evil inclination overpowered them but because they were not so wise, and Menashe answered that they were wise, but the inclination overpowered the intellect: a wise sinner who knows that he sins but cannot master his inclination longs for some impediment to stop him, whereas a fool removes any impediment, not knowing how great his sin is — so "you would have grasped the hems of your cloak" in your teeth, lest it hold you back from running after idolatry. As for "from where does one begin 'Who brings forth'": Rav Ashi thought they turned to idolatry because they could not see how multiplicity issues from the One, and Menashe showed that he knew the answer — multiplicity comes by way of a "first," just as bread has its "first," the part crusted in the baking, over which one must bless "Who brings forth bread from the earth." Hence "Since you were so wise" — knowing how the chain of existence proceeds from the One — "why did you worship idols?".):
And it is related in Sanhedrin (102a):
"חַבְרָא קָרֵית לִי, מֵהֵיכָא קָשְׁרוּ הַמּוֹצִיא וְכוּלֵי",
'You call me a colleague? From where do they begin the blessing of HaMotzi, etc.?!'
פֵּירוּשׁ כִּי הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים
the explanation being that the blessing instituted by the Sages
הוּא הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח
is the direct recognition of the divine Presence,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס וְנוֹתֵן דְּבַר מַאֲכָל וַהֲנָאָה זוֹ,
that Hashem, blessed be He, nourishes, sustains, and bestows this food and this pleasure;
וְעַל זֶה מְבָרְכִין "בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה'" בְּנוֹכַח,
and on this account we recite 'Blessed are You, Hashem' in direct address,
אֶלָּא דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַסִּיּוּם בִּלְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר: "הַמּוֹצִיא וְכוּלֵי",
except that the conclusion is nonetheless phrased in the third person: 'Who brings forth, etc.',
וְכֵן כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת,
and so it is with all blessings,
כִּי הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח הוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת.
because the direct perception of the Presence is general, an inheritance from the Patriarchs.
אֲבָל בְּדֶרֶךְ פְּרָט שֶׁיַּכִּיר בְּכָל עִנְיָן הַנּוֹכַח מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, in an individualized, detailed way, such that one perceives in every specific instance the immediate Presence of Hashem, blessed be He,
הַמּוֹרֶה לוֹ בְּאֶצְבַּע לוֹמַר "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
pointing with a finger to say 'this is the way, walk in it, etc.',
כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה בִּימוֹת הַנְּבִיאִים – זֶה נִסְתַּלֵּק.
as existed in the days of the Prophets—this has departed.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁשָּׁאַל: "מֵהֵיכָא קָשְׁרוּ וְכוּלֵי",
And this is what King Menashe challenged: 'From where do they break the bread, etc.',
פֵּירוּשׁ: אִם אַתָּה מַכִּיר בִּפְרָט נְתִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר
meaning: do you recognize in precise detail Hashem's personal bestowal of bread unto all flesh,
וְלָדַעַת מֵהֵיכָן הוּא הַהַתְחָלָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהָכִין לְךָ לֶחֶם וּמָזוֹן
so as to know at what exact point Hashem began preparing bread and nourishment for you,
שֶׁעַל זֶה תְּבָרֵךְ לוֹ בִּפְרָט?
so that over this specific moment you recite the blessing to Him?
וְהָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְרַב אַשִׁי לִסְבּוֹר סְבָרָא זוֹ
Now Rav Ashi could easily have reasoned this logic
"מֵהֵיכָן דְּקָדִים בִּישׁוּלָא" מֵעַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן,
'from wherever the baking crust forms first' by himself as well,
דְּזֶה שֵׂכֶל פָּשׁוּט:
for this is simple common sense:
דְּמֵהֵיכָן שֶׁמַּקְדִּים לֶאֱפוֹת כְּבָר קָדַם לִהְיוֹת מוּכָן לְמַאֲכַל אָדָם.
from wherever it bakes first, it has preceded in becoming ready for human consumption.
רַק כָּל הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁל חַכְמֵי הַתַּלְמוּד
Yet all halakhot of the Sages of the Talmud
לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא מִדְּבָרִים הַמּוּשָּׂגִים בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבָּם
were derived exclusively from matters perceived through the direct revelation of their hearts
וְלֹא מִן הַשֵּׂכֶל לְבַד,
and not from abstract intellectual logic alone,
שֶׁזֶּה אֵין נִקְרָא חָכְמָה כְּלָל בֶּאֱמֶת.
which is not truly titled wisdom at all.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לְבָבוֹ הַכָּרָה זוֹ
And so long as this conscious perception was not openly revealed in his heart
שֶׁהֵיכִי דְּקָדִים בִּישׁוּלָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַקְדִּים לְהָכִין לוֹ הַמָּזוֹן,
that wherever the crust bakes first Hashem precedes in preparing his food,
אָז לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהוֹרוֹת דִּמְבָרֵךְ הַמּוֹצִיא שָׁם;
he was unable to rule halakhically that one must break and bless HaMotzi there;
דְּאֵין דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם
for the words of our Sages and their halakhic rulings are not
כְּמִנְהָגִים הַקְּבוּעִים בְּאֵיזֶה סֵפֶר מוּסָר מִצַּד הַשְׁעָרַת שֵׂכֶל,
like customs recorded in an ethical treatise based on reasoned estimation,
דְּאִם כֵּן, מַה הָיָה הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין הַתַּלְמוּד הַמְּקֻדָּשׁ לִסְפָרִים אֲחֵרִים מֵחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל?
for if so, what distinction would remain between the sacred Talmud and ordinary writings of Jewish scholars?
אֲבָל כָּל הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא רַק מֵהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב
Rather, all of their halakhot derive strictly from the illumination of the heart,
עַד שֶׁנִּפְתַּח הַפֶּה בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לוֹמַר הֲלָכָה זוֹ
until the mouth is irresistibly opened to state this halakhah,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר.
which could not possibly be stated in any other manner.
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַנּוֹכַח דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּפְרָט כָּל דָּבָר,
And that occurs through feeling the immediate Presence of Hashem, blessed be He, in every specific matter,
עַד שֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ בֶּאֱמֶת בִּלְבָבוֹ
until a person truly feels in his heart
אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֶגַע זוֹ שַׁלִּיט בַּכֹּל,
how Hashem at this very moment sovereignly rules all,
וְהוּא אוֹפֶה פִּתּוֹ וּמֵכִין מְזוֹנוֹ,
and He is the One baking his bread and preparing his nourishment,
וְלוּלֵי הוּא לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל,
and without Him he would have nothing to eat;
עַד שֶׁמִּמֵּילָא נִפְתַּח פִּיו לְבָרֵךְ הַמּוֹצִיא בְּדוּכְתֵּי דְּקָדִים בִּישׁוּלָא.
until his mouth opens spontaneously to bless HaMotzi at the exact place where the crust baked first.
עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשָׁה בְּרוּרָה וּמְפוֹרֶשֶׁת בַּלֵּב כָּזוֹ
Through such clear and articulated perception in the heart,
אֶפְשָׁר לְחַדֵּשׁ אוֹתָהּ הֲלָכָה
is it possible to innovate and originate that halakhah,
לִהְיוֹת הֲלָכָה קְבוּעָה אַחַר כָּךְ בַּתַּלְמוּד.
so that it becomes an enduring, codified law in the Talmud.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה אֶחָד שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁ בֵּירוּר אוֹר זֶה עַל בּוּרְיוֹ,
For as is known, whenever one person has clearly perceived this divine light in its full clarity,
כְּבָר נִפְתַּח שַׁעַר אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹר בָּעוֹלָם.
the gate to that light has already been unlocked within the cosmos.
וְהוּא פָּתוּחַ אַחַר כָּךְ לַכֹּל,
And it remains open ever after for all;
דְּזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן עֵסֶק הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁקָּבַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for this is the entire underlying purpose of the generations established by Hashem,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם מִתְקַטְּנִים וְהוֹלְכִים.
even though they progressively diminish in stature.
לְפִי שֶׁכָּל הָאוֹרוֹת שֶׁנִּפְתָּחִים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר עַל יְדֵי אַנְשֵׁי סְגֻלָּה מֵחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Because all spiritual lights opened in every generation by elite scholars of Israel
אֵין נִסְתָּמִים עוֹד,
are never sealed shut again;
וְהֵם פְּתוּחִים לְעוֹלָם
they remain open eternally,
וְנַעֲשִׂים הֲלָכוֹת קְבוּעוֹת לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and become enduring halakhot for all the Jewish people.
וּלְפִיכָךְ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדּוֹרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים קְטַנִּים,
Consequently, even though the later generations are smaller in stature,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לָהֶם מַעֲלָה זוֹ דְּנַנָּס עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָק.
they nonetheless possess the distinct advantage of a dwarf standing upon the shoulders of a giant.
כִּי כְּבָר פְּתוּחִים לִפְנֵיהֶם כָּל שְׁעָרִים שֶׁפָּתְחוּ קַדְמוֹנִים,
For all the gates opened by early masters already stand wide open before them,
וְהֵם מְחַדְּשִׁים וְהוֹלְכִים לִפְתּוֹחַ שְׁעָרִים אֲחֵרִים.
and they proceed forward innovating to open further gates.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם קְטַנִּים מְאֹד,
Even though they themselves are exceedingly small,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם בְּמַעֲמַקִּים יוֹתֵר,
they nevertheless reach into deeper depths,
כִּי הֵם כְּבָר עָבְרוּ שַׁעַר בְּנַפְשָׁם שֶׁנִּפְתַּח לָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
because their souls have already traversed the gate originally opened for earlier sages.
וְכָל הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁהוּא מֵאוֹר הַמֵּאִיר בַּלֵּב לְכָל אֶחָד מֵחַכְמֵי הַתַּלְמוּד בִּפְרָט
And every halakhah emanating from the light illuminating the heart of a Talmudic sage in particular
כְּבָר נִקְבְּעוּ לְאוֹרוֹת וַהֲלָכוֹת קְבוּעוֹת לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
has already become fixed as enduring lights and established rulings for all Israel.
כִּי מִיָּד שֶׁנִּפְתַּח אוֹתוֹ אוֹר לְלֵב חָכָם פְּרָטִי,
For the moment that illumination opens within the heart of an individual sage,
לִבְּבוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְחֻבָּרוֹת כְּלֵב אֶחָד,
the hearts of all Israel are bonded together as one heart,
וּמִיָּד הוּא פָּתוּחַ בְּלֵב כֻּלָּם,
and it instantly becomes open within the heart of each of them,
כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ עַד קַטְנוּת הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת.
each according to his personal measure, down to the humblest levels.

וּכְטַעַם (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כה.)170 Moed Katan 25a — It is written, "The word of the Lord came [hayo haya] to Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest in the land of the Chaldeans" — yet Babylonia is not a place for the Divine Presence to rest. What is meant by "haya"? — That it had already been [before, in the Land of Israel]. Rashi: "Babylonia caused it" — for the Divine Presence does not rest outside the Land. "That it had already been" — that is, it was at that hour alone and no more; and some say that it had already been in the Land of Israel, where the Divine Spirit had rested upon him. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. "What is meant by 'haya'? — that it had already been"): Rashi's second explanation is found in the Midrash [Yalkut] on this matter, and it derives it from the doubled expression "hayo haya, the word of the Lord": "hayo" — that He had spoken with him in the Land; "haya" — that He spoke with him outside the Land. "הָיֹה הָיָה" –
Reflecting the principle (Moed Katan 25a) 'it surely came to pass'—
שֶׁהָיָה כְּבָר בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that because it had already manifested in the Land of Israel,
יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ אַף בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
it could subsequently occur even in the Diaspora,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁפַל הַמַּדְרֵגָה וְהֶעְלֵם אוֹר;
which is a lowly station of concealed light;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹתוֹ אוֹר שֶׁכְּבָר נִפְתַּח אֵין נִסְתָּם עוֹד.
nonetheless, that light which has once been unlocked is never again shut.
"וְזֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר",
'This is the gate of Hashem, the righteous shall enter into it...'
"וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים".
and 'Your people are all righteous.'
וַהֲלָכָה זוֹ דְּ"מֵהֵיכָן קָשְׁרוּ הַמּוֹצִיא",
And this halakhic inquiry of 'from where do they break bread for HaMotzi,'
שֶׁהוּא פְּתִיחַת אוֹר דְּהַכָּרַת נוֹכַח בְּכָל פְּרָט וּפְרָט,
which is the unlocking of the light of direct perception in every single detail,
זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דִּנְבוּאָה.
this is impossible except through the lofty level of prophecy.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ מְנַשֶּׁה "חַבְרָא וְכוּלֵי",
And this is why Menashe challenged him: 'You call me a colleague?!'
דִּכְפִי הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ כָּךְ הָיָה הַשְּׁלֵימוּת גַּם כֵּן
for commensurate with his immense deficiency was his corresponding potential perfection
בְּהַשָּׂגַת נוֹכַח דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע,
in perceiving the Presence of Hashem as though pointing with a finger,
כִּי "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ".
for 'all our deeds You have wrought for us.'
וּבִקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁיֹּאמַר לוֹ וְיִדְרוֹשׁ בִּשְׁמוֹ בַּפִּירְקָא.
And Rav Ashi beseeched him to tell it to him, and promised to teach it in his name during the public discourse.
פֵּירוּשׁ, הָאֲמִירָה אֵינוֹ סִפּוּר דְּבָרִים,
The explanation is: this transmission was not mere storytelling;
רַק שֶׁיָּאִיר לוֹ אוֹר זֶה בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבוֹ,
rather that Menashe radiate this experiential light directly within Rav Ashi's heart;
דְּזֶה הָיָה כָּל לִמּוּדָם תַּלְמִיד מֵרַבּוֹ,
for such was all authentic study of a student from his master,
שֶׁהָרַב הָיָה מְגַלֶּה לוֹ תַּעֲלוּמוֹת לִבּוֹ
wherein the master would unveil the inner chambers of his heart,
וְנִפְתַּח הַלֵּב שֶׁל הַתַּלְמִיד גַּם כֵּן,
and the heart of the disciple would likewise open,
דִּ"דְּבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִן הַלֵּב נִכְנָסִים אֶל הַלֵּב".
for 'words that emerge from the heart enter the heart.'
דְּלָכֵן לֹא נִכְתַּב תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
For this reason the Oral Torah was originally not permitted to be transcribed,
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא לִבּוֹ,
since the Oral Torah resides in the heart,
וּמַה שֶּׁבַּלֵּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִכְתּוֹב,
and what is in the heart cannot be written down;

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לה171 Sanhedrin 35a — Let them try him on the eve of Sabbath and conclude his verdict on Sunday? — They would forget their reasoning. And although two court scribes stand before them and write down the words of those who acquit and the words of those who convict — granted that they write what is spoken by mouth, but what is in the heart is forgotten. Therefore it is not possible. Rashi: "Let them try him on the eve of the Sabbath and conclude on Sunday" — for as long as the verdict is not concluded there is no torment of judgment, since every moment he hopes to be saved, whereas once it is concluded he spends the whole day awaiting death. "They would forget their reasons" — which they had debated and weighed carefully on the first day. "What is in the heart is forgotten" — what is in men's hearts they do not write, and though one remembers the basis of the reasoning, the way he had worked it out is forgotten from his heart, and he cannot compose it to give a proper reason as at first. Sod Yesharim (Parashas Zachor 15): The full warmth of remembrance is on the very day; on the next day the matter has grown old and is no longer called "remember" but "keep," as we find in the Gemara: "Shall we try him on the eve of Shabbat and conclude on Sunday? They will forget their reasoning; though two court scribes stand before them and write the words of those who acquit and those who convict, granted that they write what is said aloud, the heart of men forgets." That is, even though they remember the matter as on that day, the warmth of the remembrance cannot be on the following day as it was on the very day..):
as they stated in Sanhedrin (35a),
וְרַק הַפֶּה קוּלְמוֹס הַלֵּב,
and the mouth alone serves as the quill of the heart,
הוּא יָכוֹל לְהַכְנִיס בְּלֵב חֲבֵירוֹ וְתַלְמִידוֹ גַּם כֵּן.
empowered to instill this inner reality within the heart of his fellow and his disciple as well.
וְזֶה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁיְּגַלֶּה לוֹ אוֹר זֶה בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבוֹ כְּדֶרֶךְ רַב לְתַלְמִיד,
And this is what Rav Ashi asked: that Menashe reveal this illumination within his heart like a master to a student,
וְאָז "יִדְרוֹשׁ בַּפִּירְקָא",
and then he would 'teach it in the public lecture,'
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיְּפַרְסֵם זֶה בְּלִבְּבוֹת כָּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
meaning to spread this illumination into the hearts of all Israel
מֵאַחַר שֶׁיִּפְתַּח זֶה בִּלְבָבוֹ.
once it had been unlocked within his own heart.
וְיִדְרוֹשׁ מִשְּׁמוֹ,
And he promised to teach it in his name,
כִּי הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר זֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְדַּבְּקוּת רוּחֵיהּ בְּרוּחֵיהּ,
because the disclosure of this light occurs through the intertwining of spirit with spirit,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה לְלִבּוֹ דְּרַב אַשִׁי.
for without that communion it could not have been perceived by the heart of Rav Ashi;
כִּי הוּא מֵאוֹר הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁכְּבָר נִסְתַּלֵּק,
since it stems from the prophetic radiance that had already departed,
וְלֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת הֲלָכָה זוֹ רַק בַּחֲלוֹם,
and this halakhah could only be transmitted in a dream,

שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת נז172 Berakhot 57b — Five things are each a sixtieth part, and these are they: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep and a dream. Fire is a sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey, a sixtieth of the manna; Shabbat, a sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep, a sixtieth of death; a dream, a sixtieth of prophecy. Maharsha: "One-sixtieth" is not meant precisely, as Tosafot write in several places. One may also explain it from the law of nullification, where one part in sixty is not nullified but retains something of substance — as we learn from the boiled foreleg [of the nazirite's ram]; so too here he speaks by way of resemblance, that in each of the things enumerated there is some small measure of the substance of that which it resembles. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Gemilus Chasadim 3): Precisely a sixtieth, since [one who shares another's illness] does not receive the essence of the illness; and anything that is not the essence of a thing is one part in sixty of it — as the Sages said, "a dream is a sixtieth of prophecy.":).
which is one-sixtieth of prophecy (as written in Berakhot 57b).
– וְגַם יָרָבְעָם הָיָה לוֹ מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דְּהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח בְּכָל פְּרָט וּפְרָט,
And Jeroboam likewise possessed this elevated level of perceiving the Presence in every detail,
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף
and that is the spiritual rung of Joseph,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "כָּל אֲשֶׁר הוּא עֹשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר",
as I wrote elsewhere on the verse 'All that he did, Hashem made to prosper...'

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה173 Bereshit Rabbah 86:5 — “And the Lord was with Yosef.” He would enter whispering and leave whispering. His master said to him: Mix me a cup of warm water — and it was warm; hot — and it was hot. He said to him: What is this whispering in your mouth? Is it sorcery? He said to him: This is the prayer I pray constantly. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה פו):
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 86 end):
"נִכְנָס וּמְלַחֵשׁ, יוֹצֵא וְכוּלֵי – רָצָה פוֹשְׁרִין וְכוּלֵי".
'He enters whispering prayer, exits whispering prayer; if Potiphar desired lukewarm water, etc.'
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן הָעֵגֶל: "אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר יֵלְכוּ לְפָנֵינוּ",
And this was also the core error of the Golden Calf: 'Make for us gods who shall go before us,'
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּלִיטָה לָעַיִן בְּכָל פְּרָט.
seeking a visible, manifest perception in every practical circumstance.
וּלְכָךְ עֵגֶל רִאשׁוֹן נַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי טַבְלָא דְּ"עֲלֵה שׁוֹר" דַּאֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
Therefore the first Calf was formed through the plate inscribed 'Arise, ox' used for Joseph's coffin,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא יט174 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 19 — Some say it was Micah, who had been pressed into the building [in Egypt] and whom Moses had rescued from among the bricks. He took the tablet on which Moses had written "Rise up, ox" when he brought up Joseph's coffin, and cast it into the furnace among the earrings, and the calf came out bellowing and prancing. They began to say, "This is your god, O Israel." The ministering angels thereupon declared, "They forgot God their savior, who did great things in Egypt.").
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 19).
וְכֵן עֶגְלֵי יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהָיָה מִזַּרְעוֹ,
And so too the calves erected by Jeroboam, who was of his lineage;
כִּי כְּפִי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כֵּן הַחִסָּרוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
for commensurate with the potential perfection is the severity of the flaw, as noted above.
וְהַתְחָלַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ, כְּפִי דּוֹרְשֵׁי הָרְשֻׁמּוֹת,
And the beginning of its rectification, according to the interpreters of esoteric traces,
הָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר הִתְחִיל לְעוֹרֵר אוֹר מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
commenced when he began awakening the light of Mashiach ben Yosef,
שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיָרָבְעָם מֵאֲבִיָּה,
who stems from the seed of Jeroboam through his son Aviyah,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא (בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ בָּלָק דַּף נו175 Zohar Chadash, Balak 124 — And this Messiah is of the tribe of Ephraim, and he comes from the seed of Jeroboam son of Nebat, from his son Abijah, who died in his youth. On the very day that he died a son was born to him, and he was taken from the house of Jeroboam out to the wilderness; and there a hundred and seventy warriors went with him, all of them righteous men of the tribe of Ephraim who had not been found in Jeroboam's sin. And from this son of Abijah comes forth this Messiah.).]
as brought in the Zohar Chadash, Balak 56a.

sections.en: Light Drawn from Darkness

items.h: Israel's light is revealed specifically against the darkness of the nations, showing that divine honor emerges most powerfully from what appears lowest.

Seif 1 — Divine Honor Revealed through Darkness
Israel's light emerges against the nations' darkness, showing how divine honor is revealed from the lowest places.

p: הָאוֹר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשָׁךְ מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
The light for Israel is drawn specifically from the darkness of the idolaters,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי הַחֹשֶׁךְ יְכַסֶּה [אֶרֶץ] וְגוֹמֵר וְעָלַיִךְ יִזְרַח [ה'] וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written (Isaiah 60:2): "For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, etc., but upon you Hashem shall shine, etc.,"
וְאֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ נְקָמָה
and this is not by way of vengeance,
דְּזֶהוּ מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for vengeance is among the affairs of this physical world;
אֲבָל בְּהַגָּעַת הָאֱמֶת, מַה אִיכְפַּת לָהֶם
however, upon the arrival of ultimate Truth, what does it matter to them,
וּמַה הֲנָאָה הוּא זוֹ כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הָאֱמֶת
and what satisfaction could that be when Truth is revealed
וְיִתְוַודַּע דְּאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לָאֵלּוּ עִם אֵלּוּ כְּלָל,
and it becomes known that these have no connection to those whatsoever,
וְאֵין נְקָמָה אֶלָּא בַּדּוֹמִים.
and vengeance applies only between those who are alike.
אֲבָל זוֹ מֵעִנְיַן וְדֶרֶךְ הַהַנְהָגָה שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Rather, this belongs to the fundamental manner of divine order established by Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי הַזְּרִיחָה נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַחֹשֶׁךְ
for the shining of light is inherently drawn out of darkness,
כִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא"
mirroring the very creation of the universe: "first darkness, and then light"

(שַׁבָּת עז176 Shabbat 77b — R. Zeira found Rav Yehudah standing at the entrance of his father-in-law's house and saw that he was in good spirits, such that had he asked him about all the hollows of the world he would have told him. He said to him: Why do the goats walk at the head and the sheep after them? He said to him: It is as at the creation of the world — first darkness and afterward light. Rashi: "All the hollows of the world": that is, the things that happen throughout the space of the world. "First darkness": goats are generally black, and ewes generally white. Maharsha: Although the natural philosophers gave reasons for how each thing is formed, and the Talmud too has a few such ("why is the whole ear hard and the lobe soft"), these reasons are forced in their plain sense, so they must be meant as a parable on matters of Torah: Greece is likened to a goat ("and the he-goat grew exceedingly great", Daniel 8:8) and Israel to a sheep ("Israel is a scattered sheep", Jeremiah 50:17), and he asked why in the Second Temple the goats — the kings of Greece, Alexander of Macedon and those after him — reigned first, and only afterward the sheep, the kings of Israel. He answered that this was already alluded to in the creation of the world: first darkness — "and darkness was upon the face of the deep", which Bereshit Rabbah expounds of Greece, who darkened Israel's eyes — and afterward light, the Hasmonean kingdom, who came to reign through the miracle of the Chanukah lights. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 77b): The goats derive from the power of the attribute of judgment, which is the attribute of night; and night came before day because the attribute of judgment, by the very strength of that attribute, hastens to go forth into actuality. So too the goats walk at the head of the flock because of the swiftness of action they receive from the attribute of judgment — and this is what he answered him: as at the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 1): With respect to night, which is darkness, cessation and darkness come before day, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness...": for one who stands in darkness, darkness comes first and afterward light, and so there were two thousand years of chaos and afterward two thousand of Torah. But for one who stands in the day, day comes first and afterward night, to rest from his toil; and so once the Torah was given there was light for the world, and light comes before darkness. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 61): Esau was the firstborn in birth, which is the emergence into actuality, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness": on the side of the refuse the left is the right and comes first, and the this-world of Esau, in which darkness prevails, comes first. But in formation [yetzirah], which is the hidden world, the thought of creation and the conception of the world, the right comes first. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): The creation of the world was "first darkness and afterward light": first comes the portion of Bereishis, in the knowledge of the vessels, and afterward the attainment of the light of Abraham our father through knowledge, in the manner of "the advantage of light over darkness." Such too is the order of man's attainment of the light of the Blessed One, like the creation of the world: first the six days of work and afterward Shabbos; but for man's own action the light must come first and afterward the making of the vessel. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): This light [of the soul's root] can be attained in this world only through repentance, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light." Thus for certain righteous men, such as King David in the trial of Bathsheba, the Blessed One arranged a deed of the wicked in order to establish the yoke of repentance, for this cannot come about except through a preceding darkness. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): [In the Oral Torah and the innovation of laws not yet clarified] it is impossible to stand at all without a prior stumbling, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," for so is the light attained by created beings: specifically out of darkness and concealment. Therefore Esau was formed before Jacob, being the preceding darkness that leads to the attainment of the light of Torah afterward. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 21): On "Why do the goats go first... as at the creation of the world, first darkness and afterward light," Rashi explains that goats are ordinarily black. So Teves, whose sign is the kid, is the aspect of darkness, and specifically then [the Hasmoneans] brought about their miracle through their self-sacrifice, to shine out of the darkness with greater excellence, as the Zohar says, "there is no light except that which comes out of darkness"; and this is like the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): Since it is of the working of the Blessed One that it be so, "first darkness and afterward light," for the advantage of light is recognized only from darkness, [the forces of evil] therefore begin to act first, and from this the light shines forth, as in "He made darkness His hiding place," for there He is hidden. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Such is the way of the Blessed One in the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light"; and so [the Sages] said that He would create worlds and destroy them, these being the worlds of chaos, until the world of rectification emerged. So it is in everything: all the incarnations of the Messiah that have already been in the world are akin to "creating worlds and destroying them," and specifically through those destructions the world of rectification is built, by raising up the lights of the broken vessels. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 174): Since in natural things the Blessed One established this order, "first darkness and afterward light," it is certainly the essence of His will, as [the Sages said], "In the place where penitents stand...". Although, Heaven forbid, one may not say "I will sin and repent" and do so by choice, it nonetheless happens of itself, for "there is no righteous man on earth..."; and such is the order: "the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light," far beyond one who did not walk in darkness. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): From the standpoint of this world's imagination it seemed at first that everything belonged to Esau, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," as [the Sages] said at the beginning of Berakhos, which is why the evening Shema was placed first. For the Shema, the recognition of [God's] unity, was the essence of the creation of the world, and first one must recognize it out of darkness and concealment, for that was the whole matter of creation. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Shabbos): This is as it is written, "The Lord my God illuminates my darkness": after a person recognizes his sin and is pained over it, he merits that the Blessed One shines for him a rectification for it. Through the darkness, the remorse and pain he felt over the deed, he merits the light that reveals its rectification; and this is "first darkness and afterward light." Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 71): The Blessed One set the light in this world surrounded and encompassed by darkness, to leave man room to distinguish himself, that he remove the darkness and shine even within it. Therefore, when the Blessed One shines His bright light, He will shine it only for one who on his part walked in the light and did His will; He created the darkness only for the sake of one who desires the light, that for his sake He will illuminate the darkness too. Tiferes Yosef (Shavuos 7): It is written, "who forms light and creates darkness," yet at the creation of the world "there was evening and there was morning," first darkness and afterward light, so here too it should have said "creates darkness" first. The explanation: the first light was not yet within creation's capacity to receive, and light that creation cannot receive is called darkness from creation's standpoint; therefore it says "forms light and creates darkness," for from creation's standpoint it begins with day, since in the first evening creation had no grasp at all. Sod Yesharim (Shabbos HaGadol 6): As my father and teacher explained, the whole purpose of the darkness that the Blessed One set first is only that the light afterward be the more explicit; therefore "it was evening" is said first and then "it was morning." So too with Abraham our father: all the concealment he had at first, until he said, "Shall you say the palace has no master?", was the darkness that came first, only so that the Blessed One would afterward shine to him with greater clarity, "I am the master of the palace.":),
(Shabbat 77b),
וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ הוּא יֵצֶר רַע דְּמַחְשִׁיךְ אַנְפֵּי בְּרִיָּיתָא.
and darkness is the evil inclination that darkens the face of creation.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט177 Bereshit Rabbah 9:7 — R. Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in the name of R. Shmuel bar Nachman: "Behold, it was very good" — this is the good inclination; "and behold, it was very good" — this is the evil inclination. But is the evil inclination very good? Astonishing! Rather, were it not for the evil inclination a man would not build a house, nor marry a wife, nor beget children, nor engage in trade. And so Solomon says, "For it is a man's rivalry with his fellow."):
And our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 9):
"'טוֹב מְאֹד' – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע",
"'Very good'—this is the evil inclination,"
כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הַזְּרִיחָה,
because from it the dawn of light is drawn,
כִּי יִתְגַּלֶּה דְּ"הַחֹשֶׁךְ יְכַסֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" רַק לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
for it will be revealed that 'darkness shall cover, etc.' applies only to the idolaters,
אֲבָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין יֵצֶר רַע שׁוֹלֵט בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל,
whereas within Israel the evil inclination holds no true dominion at all,
בַּנְּקוּדָּה הַנִּקְרֵאת בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת לְשָׁם אֵין מַגִּיעַ הַחֵטְא,
since at the inner point truly designated by the name of Israel, sin never reaches;
שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת "אָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי הוּצֵי"
which is exemplified by 'a myrtle standing among thorny hedges'

(סַנְהֶדְרִין מד178 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..),
(Sanhedrin 44a),
פֵּירוּשׁ, "הוּצֵי" הֵם עַמִּים כּוּלָּם כְּקוֹצִים כְּסוּחִים.
meaning the thorns are the idolatrous nations, all of whom are like cut briers.
וּלְכָל אוּמָּה מֵעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יֵשׁ מִין חַשְׁכוּת מְיוּחָד,
And each nation of the idolaters possesses a specific, distinct variety of darkness,
שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעִים כֹּחוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
seventy nations corresponding to seventy faculties within the human soul;
וּמִצַּד הַגּוּף יִשְׂרָאֵל דּוֹמִין לָאוּמּוֹת כְּפִי מַרְאִית עֵין בָּשָׂר,
and from the perspective of the physical body, Israel resembles the nations to the sight of flesh,
מִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ שְׁלִיטַת חַשְׁכוּת זֶה גַּם בָּהֶם לְמַרְאִית עַיִן.
and from this arises the apparent dominion of this darkness within them as well, to outward appearances.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַגָּלוּת, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּאֱמֶת,
And this is the essential purpose of the exile: to clarify that in ultimate truth it is not so,
וְ"הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְגוֹמֵר אֲבָל עָלַיִךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
and that 'darkness shall cover the earth, but upon you Hashem shall shine';
וּבְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא הוּא אֶצְלָם לְבַד,
and 'first darkness' is experienced among the nations alone,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיכָּר יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
and afterward the preeminence of Israel's light emanating out of darkness becomes recognized.
וְתֵיכֶף לְתוֹקֶף הַחֹשֶׁךְ דְּ"יְכַסֶּה וְגוֹמֵר",
And immediately upon the climax of the darkness of 'shall cover the earth,'
מִיָּד נִגְלָה הָאוֹר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
Israel's light is instantly unveiled,
כְּטַעַם: "לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גָּאוֹן",
in the spirit of: 'Pride goes before destruction' (Proverbs 16:18),
שֶׁגְּאוֹן הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא כְּפִי תוֹקֶף הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
for the arrogant pride of the idolaters corresponds directly to the zenith of darkness,
דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְגַּבְּרוּתָם וּשְׁלִיטוּתָם בְּכָל מִינֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּבְכָל מִינֵי רְצִיחָה,
namely their dominance and tyranny across all worldly appetites and all manner of murderous bloodshed,
כְּסַנְחֵרִיב וּנְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר וְהָמָן וְטִיטוּס וְכַדּוֹמֶה – זֶהוּ גְּאוֹנָם.
like Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, Haman, Titus, and their ilk—such is their pride.
וְאָז תֵּיכֶף הַתְחָלַת זְרִיחַת אוֹר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And right then marks the dawn of the illumination of Israel,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ד, יז: וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה א179 Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:4 — An Arab said to a Jew who was plowing: Jew, Jew, unyoke your ox and loosen your plow, for the Temple has been destroyed. The cow lowed a second time. He said to him: Jew, Jew, yoke your ox and fasten your plow, for King Messiah has been born. [The child's mother later said:] I would sooner strangle him, for on the day he was born the Temple was destroyed. He said to her: We are confident that at his feet it was destroyed, and at his feet it will be rebuilt. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "and he made himself a seller of swaddling cloths for infants"): "I would sooner strangle him, the enemy of Israel" — she was speaking of the child himself by euphemism, because on the day he was born the Temple was destroyed. And the man said to her: I am confident that just as it was destroyed on his day, so it is destined to be rebuilt on his day; come and buy for him. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael 26): Because the destruction of the Temple is itself the cause of the Messiah's coming to be — for what is already complete does not come into being — he answered her, "at his feet it was destroyed and at his feet it will be rebuilt." This birth is no bodily birth, for the Sages are not speaking of bodily matters at all; they mean that from that hour the very power of the Messiah is present in the world, which it was not before the Temple was destroyed. That he is nonetheless withheld is from another side altogether: the forces of impurity still prevail in the world, until the Holy One, blessed be He, removes them from it., נז):
just as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4, 17b; Midrash Rabbah Eichah 1:57):
דִּבְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.
that on the Ninth of Av the Messiah was born.
וְהַגָּאוֹן שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא רַק לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר,
And their arrogant pride exists merely prior to ruin,
דְּ"כָל קַרְנֵי רְשָׁעִים אֲגַדֵּעַ, תְּרוֹמַמְנָה [קַרְנוֹת צַדִּיק]" (תְּהִלִּים עה, יא),
for 'all the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted' (Psalms 75:11);
וְ"לִפְנֵי כָבוֹד עֲנָוָה" (מִשְׁלֵי טו, לג),
and 'before honor comes humility' (Proverbs 15:33),
דְּתוֹקֶף אוֹר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא עֲנָוָה.
for the ultimate strength of Israel's light is designated as humility.
כְּטַעַם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
Reflecting the nature of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the greatest in Israel,
גַּדְלוּתוֹ הָיָה: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו [מְאֹד וְגוֹמֵר]" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ג).
whose greatness lay in: 'And the man Moses was exceedingly humble, etc.' (Numbers 12:3).
כִּי גֵּיאוּת הוּא לְבוּשׁוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For exalted majesty (ge'ut) is the outward garment of Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "ה' [מָלָךְ] גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ" (תְּהִלִּים צג, א),
as it is written: 'Hashem reigns, He is robed in majesty' (Psalms 93:1);
פֵּירוּשׁ: עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה וְהַנִּגְלֶה לְעֵין בָּשָׂר וָדָם
meaning: the World of Action and what is visible to the eyes of flesh and blood,
זֶה נִקְרָא לְבוּשׁ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּלְבוּשׁ הַמְכַסֶּה וּמַסְתִּיר הַגּוּף.
this is termed the garment of Hashem, blessed be He, like a garment that conceals and shrouds the body.
וּמִצַּד הַלְּבוּשׁ נִקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "כִּי גָאֹה גָּאָה",
And from the perspective of this outer vestment, Hashem is described as 'exceedingly exalted,'
שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מְלוּכָה וּמֶמְשָׁלָה נִקְרָא גֵּיאוּת,
for in this physical world, sovereignty and ruling power are termed grandeur,
שֶׁהוּא שַׁלִּיט בַּכֹּל – זֶהוּ גֵּיאוּת וּגְדוּלָּה.
since being sovereign over all is viewed as lofty majesty and greatness.
וּכְפִי הָאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה אֶלָּא שִׁפְלוּת,
Yet according to ultimate truth, this is nothing other than lowliness,

כְּטַעַם (הוֹרָיוֹת י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב180 Horayot 10b — [Rabban Gamliel] said to them: Do you suppose that I am giving you authority? It is servitude that I am giving you, as it is said, "And they spoke to him saying: If today you will be a servant to this people [and serve them and answer them and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever]." Rashi: "Servitude I am giving you" — for high office is servitude to a man, since the yoke of the public is laid upon him. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 5): This teaching comes to make known that even when the Blessed One gives a man high office, he should not think in his heart that the office is his own, nor exalt himself in that office and that honour, for it is nothing but servitude to him. The prince, and even the king, has the whole purpose of his kingship in the need of the people; and whatever exists for the sake of something else is subordinate to it and subject to it. Were the purpose of the kingship for the king himself it would be reckoned kingship; but since the kingship is for the need of the people, the king is subordinate and subject to them, and is therefore called a servant.): "עַבְדוּת אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לָכֶם",
in the spirit of (Horayot 10a): 'Servitude am I conferring upon you,'
שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁיּוֹרֵד לִשְׁלוֹט בִּפְחוּתִים וּשְׁפֵלִים הוּא שִׁפְלוּת,
for one who descends to exercise dominion over lowly, base subjects experiences lowering,
שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה רֹאשׁ לַשּׁוּעָלִים.
becoming a head to foxes.

וְלִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם מַכִּירִים הָאֱמֶת (מְגִילָּה לא181 Megillah 31a — R. Yochanan said: Wherever you find the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility. This is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and stated a third time in the Writings. Written in the Torah: "For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords" — and after it, "who executes justice for the orphan and the widow." Repeated in the Prophets: "Thus says the High and Exalted One, who dwells forever, and whose name is holy" — and after it, "and with the contrite and lowly of spirit." Stated a third time in the Writings: "Extol Him who rides upon the heavens, the Lord is His name" — and after it, "father of orphans and judge of widows." Maharsha: “Wherever” is not exact, for in many verses His might is mentioned without His humility following; it means rather: in the Torah, in the Prophets and in the Writings alike. Nor is “might” exact, since the verses cited from the Prophets and the Writings use no term of might; it means wherever the exaltedness of the Holy One, blessed be He, is spoken of, and “might” was chosen because the verse from the Torah contains “the great, the mighty and the awesome God.” The point is that His way is not the way of flesh and blood, where the mighty man keeps the crushed and lowly of spirit — orphans and widows — at a distance; He, on the contrary, draws them near and watches over them all the more. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 1): R. Yochanan means that humility is itself the very greatness, the greatness above all greatness, than which there is none higher; were it not so, His humility would not be found in every place where His greatness is found. For one who possesses humility is bounded and defined by nothing, and this indicates absolute simplicity, and what is absolutely simple is without limit. Therefore “He executes justice for the orphan and the widow” follows upon His greatness: out of that simplicity He is not confined to doing justice for the great rather than the small, but does justice for all alike. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 47): At the Sea the Blessed One appeared as a mighty warrior only because Pharaoh had grown haughty, so He clothed Himself, as it were, in a garment of might against him. When Israel's hearts opened to sing, they grasped this and said, "I will sing to the Lord, for He is exalted" [over the proud] — all His majesty is directed only against the proud, while the truth is "I, the Lord, dwell with the contrite," as the Sages said, "wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility ... to revive the heart of the contrite." Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 4): Holiness denotes God's exaltedness and greatness as a person recognizes it, and the ultimate knowledge of created beings is to know that the Blessed One is set apart and exalted far beyond created intellect. That is why the Sages said, "wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility": in the very place where His greatness and exaltedness is grasped by a creature, there is His humility, to be grasped even by the lowliest creature, for in grasping His exaltedness he grasps the Blessed One. Hence "Holy, holy, holy" concludes "the whole earth is full of His glory" — His glory is grasped throughout the earth and fills all the lowly parts of creation. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 45): The name Shaddai teaches that the Blessed One measures out for each creature its fitting place and watches over the small as over the great: unlike flesh and blood, for whom some things are essential and others secondary and superfluous, for the Blessed One all matters are equal, and there is "enough" [dai] in His divinity for every creature, even the smallest. This flows from the secret of the Most High, that "wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility," and it is hinted in the verse, "He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High abides in the shadow of Shaddai.".):
And for the children of Israel, who recognize the inner truth (Megillah 31a):
"בִּמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עַנְוְותָנוּתוֹ",
"Wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility,"
"אֲנִי אֶת דַּכָּא [וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ] וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, טו).
"I dwell with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit, etc." (Isaiah 57:15).
וְכֵן הֵם דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ,
And so they cling unto Him;
תוֹקֶף אוֹרָם הוּא הָעֲנָוָה,
the supreme force of their light is humility,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כָּל שַׁלְוַות וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
such that through all worldly tranquility and elevated status,
הֵם מַכִּירִים הַשִּׁפְלוּת יוֹתֵר,
they perceive essential lowliness all the more,
כִּי זֶה שִׁפְלוּת גָּדוֹל לִהְיוֹת מִתְנַשֵּׂא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for it is a profound descent to puff oneself up in this transient world.
וְזֶהוּ "לִפְנֵי כָבוֹד [עֲנָוָה]",
And this is 'before honor comes humility,'
דְּאָז יַשִּׂיגוּ לַכָּבוֹד הָאֲמִיתִּי,
for through this they attain authentic, enduring honor,
דְּאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת נִקְרָא כָּבוֹד
which in relation to Hashem, blessed be He, is truly termed kavod (honor),
וְלֹא גָּאוֹן וְגֵיאוּת,
and not ga'on or ge'ut,
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר גַּבְהוּת וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת וְאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שִׁפְלוּת בֶּאֱמֶת;
which imply arrogant height and presumption, being in truth mere lowliness;
רַק נִקְרָא כָּבוֹד כְּטַעַם "כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד",
rather it is termed kavod, as in 'the Throne of Glory (Kissei HaKavod),'
שֶׁהַכָּבוֹד הוּא הֲדוֹם רַגְלָיו,
wherein Glory serves as His footstool,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגוֹת שֶׁלְּמַטָּה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד כַּנִּזְכָּר,
because it is specifically through the lower tiers that divine Honor is revealed, as mentioned,
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ יוֹתֵר.
and this is not the place to elaborate further.

sections.en: Circles, Lines, and Modes of Divine Knowledge

items.h: Divine awareness has a universal, inherited dimension and an individualized, graded dimension, corresponding to encompassing faith and differentiated spiritual attainment.

Seif 1 — Universal Faith and Individual Attainment
Faith surrounds every Jew equally, while differentiated spiritual knowledge unfolds according to each person's unique level.

p: שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הַשָּׂגוֹת אֱלֹהוּת יֵשׁ:
There are two forms of divine comprehension:
אַחַת כְּלָלִית
one is general,
שֶׁהִיא בְּשָׁוֶה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
which is equal across all Israel,
מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים,
inasmuch as they are believers, children of believers,
מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת,
an inheritance from the Patriarchs,
דְּיֵשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ בּוֹרֵא מַשְׁגִּיחַ וְיָכוֹל וְכוּלֵי.
that there is a God Who creates, supervises, possesses omnipotence, etc.
וְהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָעִגּוּלִים
And this constitutes the perception of Circles (Iggulim),
מִצַּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סוֹבֵב כָּל עוֹלָמִים,
stemming from Hashem, blessed be He, encompassing all worlds (Sovev Kol Almin),
דִּבְהֶקֵּף וְעִגּוּל אֵין מַדְרֵגוֹת,
for within a perimeter and circle there are no hierarchical gradations;
וְהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם
and it exists in concealment,
וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ,
rather than within the open revelation of the heart,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב182 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I am asleep with respect to the redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 8): The theme of this month [Adar] is that even in sleep Israel are holy, since they are bound at their root to the Blessed One — as the Midrash says, "I am asleep from the commandments ... but my heart is awake to perform them ... where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? 'God is the rock of my heart.'" From the side of the Blessed One, "the voice of my beloved knocks, open for me": "my heart is awake" means that the Blessed One, the heart of Israel, rouses Israel from their sleep to perform the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): The Congregation of Israel boasts, "I am asleep but my heart is awake," which the Sages expounded as referring to the Holy One, blessed be He — "rock of my heart." Even when they are asleep from the commandments and have no "eyes," as in sleep when the eyes are shut and the heart is sunk in imaginings, since the root of the soul is a portion of God and the depths of the heart cleave to the Blessed One, all the imaginings too cleave to Him; even at the height of immersion in the imaginings of this world, which hide the truth, there remains in him a power of awakening to the Blessed One through the heart's cleaving to the living God. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 68): All the service of the body's limbs, and the commandments performed with them, serve only to set the heart straight; the essential thing is the heart, the dwelling place of the Blessed One, as the Sages said, "the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it says, 'rock of my heart.'" Therefore these [outward acts] are not to be a person's goal in themselves, but only things that lead to the goal, as the Zohar calls the 613 commandments "613 counsels."):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2):
"הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
"The Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: צור לְבָבִי".
as it is stated: 'The rock of my heart.'"
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגַת הַיֹּשֶׁר
And this is attained through the level of Linearity (Yosher),
שֶׁהוּא מְמַלֵּא כָּל עוֹלָמִים,
which fills all worlds (Memaleh Kol Almin),
וְהוּא הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ בְּקֶרֶב לִבָּן,
and He dwells literally amidst the children of Israel, within the midst of their heart;
וְהוּא הַשָּׂגָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ.
and this constitutes perception through the revelation of one's heart.
וּבָזֶה יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת,
And within this realm there are gradations,
כִּי בְּיֹשֶׁר יֵשׁ מַעְלָה וּמַטָּה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל,
for in Linearity there exist above and below, right and left,
וְכָל אַחַת מַדְרֵגָה חֲלוּקָה,
and each represents a distinct degree,
וְאֵין הַשָּׂגַת נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת דּוֹמָה לְנֶפֶשׁ אַחֶרֶת כְּלָל,
and the comprehension of one soul does not resemble that of another soul at all,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין שָׁרְשָׁם בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ
for their roots do not occupy one identical location
בְּקוֹמַת הַיֹּשֶׁר
in the Stature of Linearity,
שֶׁהוּא קוֹמַת הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לַנְּפָשׁוֹת,
which is the stature of the revelation of His light, blessed be He, unto souls,
דְּמִשָּׁם הוּא עֶצֶם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם,
whence emerges the very essence of the souls of Israel and the root of their vitality,
כִּי חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ כְּחֵלֶק מִן הַכֹּל.
for 'Hashem's portion is His people,' as an intrinsic part of the whole.
וּבְכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ נֶאֱמַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים "אֲנִי ה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם",
Throughout the entire Torah it is stated numerous times, 'I am Hashem your God' (in the plural),
וְהוּא הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁבְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל לְכֻלְּכֶם בְּשָׁוֶה.
which is the general perception shared by all of you equally.
אֲבָל בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת פָּתַח: "אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ",
However, in the Ten Commandments He opened: 'I am Hashem your God' (in the singular),
הַיְינוּ לְכָל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא.
meaning to each individual specifically according to what he is.

וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ כֵּן בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב183 Midrash Tehillim 119:21 — Moshe said: “For you are a holy people to the Lord your God.” It is not written here “the Lord our God chose among you,” but “the Lord your God chose you” — even one of you is more beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He, than all the nations. And so Yeshayahu said: “All the nations are as nothing before Him.” (מִזְמוֹר קיט, ח) עַל פָּסוּק "בְּךָ בָּחַר ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" –
And so they expounded in Shocher Tov (Psalm 119:8) on the verse 'Hashem your God chose you' (singular) –
וְלֹא "אֱלֹהֵינוּ", דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר לְכָל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד.
and not 'our God', denoting each individual alone.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן יָדוּעַ שֶׁהֵם בְּקוֹמַת אָדָם
This is because the commandments of the Torah, as is also known, correspond to the human stature
נֶגֶד מָאתַיִם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה אֵבָרִים וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה גִּידִים,
parallel to the 248 limbs and 365 sinews;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא חֲלוּקַּת הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת,
and through the Torah unfolds the differentiation of levels,
וּלְכָךְ פְּתִיחָתָהּ דְּדִבּוּר זֶה שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ
therefore the opening of this utterance, which constitutes the root of the entire Torah,
הוּא בְּהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ הַפְּרָטִית שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט.
is rooted in this individualized perception unique to each person.
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ לַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בַּתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת
And this is the root of human effort in Torah and commandments,
לְהַשִּׂיג הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ.
to attain this specific comprehension aligned with his spiritual root.
דִּלְהַשָּׂגָה הַכְּלָלִית אֵין צָרִיךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
For regarding general comprehension no strenuous effort is required,
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דִּלְעָתִיד יַשִּׂיגוּ מַדְרֵגַת עִגּוּלִים,
and as is known, in the ultimate future all will attain the level of Circles,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרְכוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
meaning they will not require personal exertion,
כִּי הוּא מַדְרֵגַת אוֹר מַקִּיף,
for that is the dimension of Surrounding Light (Ohr Makif),
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַקִּיף מִבַּחוּץ לְקוֹמַת אָדָם,
wherein Hashem, blessed be He, encompasses the stature of man from without,
לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׂכְלוֹ וַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַקִּיפוֹ.
transcending his intellect, service, and exertion, Hashem encompasses him.
וְלֹא אָמַר זֶה בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי,
And He did not phrase this as a direct commandment,
רַק דֶּרֶךְ הוֹדָעָה: "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
merely by way of an announcement: 'I am Hashem your God, etc.,'
וְכָל דִּבּוּר הוּא פּוֹעֵל כֵּן לְעָלְמֵי עַד.
and every divine utterance effects this for all eternity.
דְּדִבְּרוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יֵשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל
For the utterances of the Holy One, blessed be He, contain dynamic operative force,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ: "בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ",
as we find: 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made,'
וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר זֶה דְּ"אָנֹכִי" הוּא הֶאָרַת אוֹר זֶה בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט לְפִי חֶלְקוֹ.
and through this utterance of 'I am' occurs the illumination of this light within each soul individually according to its allotted portion.
וּבִתְחִלַּת הַתּוֹרָה הֶאָרָה זוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And at the beginning of the Torah this illumination emanates directly from Hashem, blessed be He,

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְכִילְתָּא וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּשַׁלַּח184 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Shirah 3:10 — "This is my God." R. Eliezer says: Whence do you say that a maidservant saw at the Sea what Isaiah and Ezekiel did not see? For it is said, "And by the hand of the prophets I was imagined," and "The heavens were opened and I saw visions of God." They gave a parable: to what may the matter be compared? To a king of flesh and blood who entered a city, with a bodyguard about him and mighty men to his right and to his left and his troops before him and behind him, and everyone was asking, "Which one is the king?" — since he is flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself at the Sea, not one of them needed to ask "Which one is He?" Rather, as soon as they saw Him they recognized Him, and they all opened their mouths and said: "This is my God and I will glorify Him, the God of my father and I will exalt Him!" Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): At the splitting of the Red Sea came the revelation of sight — "a maidservant saw at the Sea," etc. — which they afterwards attained as a possession at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:35): Therefore the Sages said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea," etc.: with the complete destruction of Egypt, the hidden root of evil, the hidden root of good was clarified — that the root of things is from the Blessed One alone — and this is the ultimate unity, when it becomes clear to the eye. Then she saw the entire Account of the Chariot of Ezekiel, that is, how the Blessed One rides upon all of creation, which is only a throne and chariot for Him and nothing apart from Him or a thing in its own right. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on completing the Talmud 2): The Talmud opens in Berakhos with Shema, prayer and blessings — speech addressed to the Blessed One and clear recognition of His truth — in the manner of "a maidservant saw at the Sea": when a Jew first begins to draw near to words of Torah, the Blessed One opens a great light for him. Afterwards the light is dimmed, as at Sinai, where after the first utterance the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down dew; for there are depths and light above light, and the Blessed One wishes to raise a person ever higher. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): Holy sight stems from awe, the level of Isaac; its clarification began with Isaac's birth and continued four hundred years until the Exodus, when "a maidservant saw at the Sea," as the Sages said — for then the seeing was completed in full. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bo 3): The distinction made in the plague of pestilence was of the aspect of supernal wonder, as at the splitting of the Red Sea, which depended on Atika [the Ancient One]; and when the Sages said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see," this is the revelation of Atika, of whom it is written, "doing wonders." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 189): Apprehending God through His governance — how the Blessed One "rides" upon His creatures — is called the Account of the Chariot, the level of "knowledge" of Moses our teacher. The generation of the wilderness, called the "generation of knowledge," of whom it is said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see" — that is, the Account of the Chariot — were all prepared for this knowledge, the level of Moses, the leader who encompassed them all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Bava Metzia): At the Exodus Israel attained by sight, as it says, "a maidservant saw at the Sea," and they thought that by this seeing they had acquired the light as a full possession. But afterwards they went three days without finding water — without longing, for "water" is Torah — and recognized that they did not yet have a full possession, until they attained it completely at the giving of the Torah. What a person attains by sight he can later acquire fully through effort, and only what he acquires by his own effort remains his in the World to Come.):
and along the lines of what they stated (Mekhilta and Zohar HaKadosh, Beshalach):
"רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם וְכוּלֵי",
"A maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel the prophet did not see, etc.,"
דְּמַה שֶּׁעֲתִידִין לְהַשִּׂיג בְּסוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
so that what is destined to be attained at the end of all generations through exertion—
דְּ"אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת רוּחִי עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹמֵר" –
as in 'I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh, etc.'—
זֶה הָיָה בַּהַתְחָלָה בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
this occurred initially without any exertion,
וּכְטַעַם "בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי [לֶעָתִיד] אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ מִיָּד וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ".
in the spirit of: 'In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned in the future, I will immediately come unto you and bless you.'
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה דְּכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא רַק לָבוֹא לְמַה שֶּׁמּוּכָן,
For Hashem shows that all human effort is solely to arrive at what is already prepared,

וְ"אֵין אָדָם נוֹגֵעַ בַּמּוּכָן לַחֲבֵירוֹ" (יוֹמָא לח185 Yoma 38b — "And from your own they shall give You." No man touches what is prepared for his fellow, and no kingdom encroaches upon its neighbor even by a hairbreadth. Rashi: "And of your own they will give you": that is, it is not a gift of theirs, but sustenance allotted to you from Heaven. "No kingdom encroaches upon its neighbor": once the time has come for a kingdom to fall and another to arise, it is not delayed even by a hairbreadth; one whose time to fall is at night falls at night, as it is stated, "In that very night Belshazzar was slain" (Daniel 5:30), and one whose time is by day falls by day, as it is stated, "At Tehaphnehes the day shall be darkened" (Ezekiel 30:18). Maharsha (Yoma 38a, s.v. "in disparagement of them"): "Of your own they will give you": whatever was given to them [the House of Garmu and the House of Avtinas] from the Temple treasury was their own, so they did not thereby diminish the honor of the Omnipresent; and "no man touches what is prepared for his fellow": the craftsmen who had been brought [from Alexandria] were unable to touch what was prepared for them; and he concluded that in the same way no kingdom encroaches upon its neighbor. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTzedek 3): If the Holy One, blessed be He, gave each and every hair its own source of nourishment, how much more did He give each person his own: He has ordained for each one what is fitting for him, and no man touches what God has ordained for his fellow; if he does, it is reckoned as robbery. And just as He has ordered the individuals of the species, each receiving what befits him, so He has ordered each generation as a whole, giving it a king and setting it apart by itself, so that no kingdom encroaches upon its neighbor; the two are alike, the one being the order of the individual and the other the order of the generation as a whole. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Every desire for the sake of Heaven needs guarding, lest one desire what does not belong to him — hence the warning "you shall not covet," the last of the Ten Commandments, whose end is bound to their beginning: one who recognizes "I am the Lord your God" does not covet what is not his, for he knows that "from your own they shall give you" and that "no man touches what is prepared for his fellow," since the Lord God guides him.:),
and 'no person touches that which is prepared for his fellow' (Yoma 38b),
וּכְטַעַם "וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי",
and mirroring 'Yet I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated,'
שֶׁאַף אִם יַרְבֶּה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַד אֵין קֵץ
for even if one multiplies effort without end,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְשׁוּם דָּבָר וְשׁוּם מַדְרֵגָה
it is impossible to reach any achievement or spiritual degree
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ מֵאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם,
since in his root he does not stem from that source;
כִּי הוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשָּׂנוּי,
for he is from the root of what is hated,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָשָׂה בָּעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת דָּבָר מַרְאֶה הַהֵיפֶךְ
meaning that Hashem established within the world an entity portraying the opposite,
וְנִדְמֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּאִלּוּ הוּא שָׂנוּי.
which appears in this world as though it were hated.
כִּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא דִּמְיוֹן,
For this world is a realm of illusion,
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה אֶלָּא בְּדִמְיוֹן,
and this matter has grasp solely within illusion,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ, הוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י, וְיַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי עַל פָּסוּק "וַיִּתְרֹצֲצוּ186 Rashi on Genesis 25:22:1 — "And the children struggled within her." Our Rabbis expounded it as an expression of running: when she passed by the doors of Torah of Shem and Ever, Jacob would run and struggle to come out; when she passed the door of idolatry, Esau would struggle to come out. Another explanation: they were struggling with one another and quarreling over the inheritance of the two worlds."):
and as written (Midrash cited in Rashi, and Yalkut Shimoni on the verse 'and the children struggled'):
"וְעֵשָׂו נָטַל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה",
'And Esau took this world,'
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה אֶלָּא בְּדִמְיוֹן לְבַד.
meaning that he holds grasp solely within illusion.
"וְלִהַט אֹתָם הַיּוֹם הַבָּא",
'And the day that comes shall burn them up' (Malachi 3:19),
דִּכְשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הָאֱמֶת
for when ultimate Truth is revealed,
אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ מְצִיאוּת לַדָּבָר הַשָּׂנוּי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
there is no existence possible for whatever is rejected by Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם מַמָּשׁוּת כְּלָל,
and it possesses no actual substance whatsoever,
רַק כַּחֲלוֹם יָעוּף כְּשֶׁמֵּקִיץ וְרֵיקָה נַפְשׁוֹ.
flying away like a dream upon awakening with one's soul left empty.
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל כֻּלָּם דְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת,
In contrast, Israel are all cleaving unto the Truth,
וּכְפִי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת כָּךְ יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ.
and according to each one's spiritual level, so can he attain through his exertion.
וּבְוַדַּאי הֲגַם דְּ"רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי"
And certainly, even though 'a maidservant saw at the Sea, etc.,'
הָיָה מַדְרֵגוֹת,
there existed distinct individual levels,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לִקְרוֹת "שִׁפְחָה" כְּלָל;
for were it not so, the title 'maidservant' would not apply at all;
רַק דְּגַם מַדְרֵגוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר קְטַנִּים וְהַשְּׁפָחוֹת הָיְתָה לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגוֹת יְחֶזְקֵאל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
only that even the lowest ranks and the maidservants were higher than the level of Ezekiel in his exertion in this world.
אֲבָל מַדְרֵגַת יְחֶזְקֵאל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
However, regarding the spiritual level of Ezekiel in the World to Come,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה וְגוֹמֵר".
concerning this it is stated: 'No eye has seen, O God, beside You.'
וְכֵן בְּעֵת שְׁפִיכַת הָרוּחַ לְכָל בָּשָׂר
Likewise, at the time of the outpouring of the spirit upon all flesh
יִהְיֶה כֵּן מַדְרֵגוֹת.
there will similarly be distinct gradations.
וְכֵן בְּעֵת דִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי"
