Similarly, at the time of the divine utterance 'I am,'
הֵאִיר לְכָל אָדָם וּלְכָל נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
it illuminated unto every person and every soul throughout all generations
כְּפִי פְּרָט הַשָּׂגָתָן.
according to the specific measure of their individual comprehension.
וְדִבּוּר זֶה נִצָּב קַיָּים בְּכָל נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
And this utterance stands enduringly within all souls of all generations,
שֶׁהָיוּ כֻּלָּם בְּמַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי.
who were all present at the assembly at Mount Sinai.
וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר שֶׁיּוֹצְאִים לַפּוֹעַל בַּגּוּף בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And in every single generation, as they emerge into physical actuality in this world,
גַּם דִּבּוּר זֶה יוֹצֵא בַּפּוֹעַל בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם
this utterance likewise emerges into actuality within their heart
בְּעֵת הַתְחָלַת פְּנִיָּיתָם לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת.
at the moment they initially turn toward the words of Torah and spiritual exertion.
מֵאִיר לָהֶם אוֹר זֶה דְּ"אָנֹכִי",
This light of 'I am' shines forth to them;
בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מַשִּׂיג אוֹר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ,
without prior exertion he grasps the light of Hashem that belongs to the root of his soul,
כְּאִלּוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרְרוֹ:
as though Hashem were stirring him:
"לְהַשָּׂגַת אוֹר זֶה אַתָּה מוּכָן,
"'For the comprehension of this light you are prepared,
וּבְהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתְךָ תַּשִּׂיגֶנּוּ".
and through your own exertion you shall attain it.'"
וְזֶה טַעַם "אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם" גַּם כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד,
And this is why 'Who brought you out of the land of Egypt' is likewise phrased in the singular,
שֶׁיְּצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם גַּם כֵּן הָיָה לְכָל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט הַשָּׂגַת אֲחֵרוֹת
for the Exodus from Egypt was also experienced by each individual through a unique comprehension,
כְּטַעַם "רָאֲתָה וְכוּלֵי".
mirroring the concept that 'a maidservant saw, etc.'
דְּגָלִיּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ מִקְרֶה,
For the exiles of Israel are never incidental,
וְסִפּוּר מַעֲשֶׂה לֹא הָיָה נִכְתָּב בַּתַּנַּ״ךְ,
and a mere chronicle of history would never have been recorded in the Tanakh,
אֲבָל עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הוּא לִמּוּד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
rather it is perforce an eternal teaching of Torah.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשִׁעְבּוּד אוּמָּה בָּהֶם
And this signifies that subjugation to an empire
הוּא שִׁעְבּוּד אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַגּוֹבֵר בְּאוּמָּה זוֹ.
is subjugation to the spiritual archetype dominating that nation.
וְכֹחַ מִצְרַיִם בִּכְשָׁפִים,
The principal force of Egypt lay in sorcery,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְנָחוֹת פה187 Menachot 85a — Yochana and Mamre said to Moses: Are you bringing straw to Afarayim? He said to them: People say — to a city of vegetables, bring vegetables. Rashi: Yochana and Mamre were the chief sorcerers of Egypt, and they said this to Moshe our teacher when he began to perform the signs before Pharaoh, for they supposed he was doing them by sorcery. "Do you bring straw to Afarayim?" — Afarayim is a place of much grain; do you bring grain there to sell? So too, the land of Egypt is full of sorcery: do you come there to busy yourself with sorcery? And he answered them: to a city where much greenstuff grows, bring your greenstuff to sell, since everyone gathers there to buy — they spoke to him in mockery, and he answered them in their own idiom. Maharsha: The parable may be explained from the verse, "The prophet that has a dream, let him tell a dream, and he that has My word, let him speak My word in truth: what has the straw to do with the wheat?" — which Rashi explains there as: what has falsehood to do with truth. So they were saying: as we here busy ourselves with sorcery, a false thing like this straw, so do you busy yourself. And he answered them with another parable: the greens brought to market to sell are certainly not all alike, some poor and some esteemed — if your greens are falsehood and sorcery and worth nothing, not so mine, for my matter is a true and esteemed thing, and it is from Him, blessed be He. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Menachos 85a): It appears that there were two of them, one for the work of demons and the second for the work of sorcery; and Mamre was the one for the work of sorcery, which "contradicts the heavenly retinue" — for such men rebel [mamrin] against the household above. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 4): The Egyptian exile was a preparation for the Written Torah, which was then itself in exile in Egypt, where its opposing counterpart was the wisdom of Egypt, worked through sorcery — as stated, "Are you bringing straw to Afarayim?", which Rashi explains: Egypt is full of sorcery, and you come there to practice sorcery? Sorcery is the counterpart of Torah from Heaven, for it too is a received wisdom, though through the forces of impurity; and through the Egyptian exile Israel merited the "great wealth," the giving of the Torah..): "תֶּבֶן אַתָּה מַכְנִיס וְכוּלֵי",
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Menachot 85a): "You bring straw to Afarayim, a city of straw?!"

וּפֵירוּשׁ כְּשָׁפִים – שֶׁמַּכְחִישִׁין וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין סז188 Sanhedrin 67b — R. Yochanan said: Why are they called keshafim (acts of sorcery)? Because they contradict the heavenly retinue. Rashi: "If it succeeds for you" — if you succeed in working sorcery on me, do it; "'there is none beside Him' is written" — if the Omnipresent desires me, you will not be able to harm me, and if you are able, it has come from Him, and I accept it. Keshafim is an abbreviation of "they contradict (kachash) the heavenly retinue," for they put to death one on whom it was decreed that he live. "His merits were abundant" — and Heaven exerts itself to save him. Maharsha (Chullin 7b, to which he refers here): The verse means that "there is none else" can be said only of the Holy One, blessed be He: what He decrees, no other powers — the forces of impurity and sorcery — can change; but what is decreed through sorcery, there is still the Holy One, blessed be He, who can change that decree by virtue of merits, as in the case of R. Chanina. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 67b): Sorcery is that which alters the order of the world, and this is what he meant by "they contradict the heavenly retinue." A demon can bring about something new, but it does not contradict the heavenly retinue, for a demon cannot alter the power of the heavenly retinue; only the act of sorcery, which throws the order into confusion, thereby contradicts the heavenly retinue.:),
and the definition of sorcery (keshafim) is that they 'lessen/deny the Heavenly household' (makhkhishin), (Sanhedrin 67b),
הַיְינוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לִפְעוֹל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
namely striving through self-effort to act contrary to the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְשֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּנְהִיג.
and denying that Hashem is the sole Director.
אֲבָל "אֱלֹהֶיךָ" – פֵּירוּשׁ מַנְהִיגְךָ,
However, 'your God' (Elohekha) signifies your personal Guide,
וְהוּא יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
which represents the Exodus from Egypt,
שֶׁהֵאִיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּהוּא לְבַדּוֹ הַמַּנְהִיג
wherein Hashem radiated the reality that He alone is the Guide
בְּפַרְטוּת לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ וְנֶפֶשׁ
specifically for each individual soul,
וְלֹא דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל לְבַד.
and not merely in an overarching, generalized manner.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם189 Sanhedrin 67b — "There is none else besides Him" (Deuteronomy 4:35) — R. Chanina said: even in a matter of sorcery. A certain woman was trying to take dust from beneath R. Chanina's feet [to work sorcery upon him]. He said to her: If you succeed, go and do it — "There is none else besides Him" is written. Rashi: "Even in a matter of sorcery" — it has no power before His decree, for there is no power beside Him. "From beneath his feet" — in order to work sorcery on him; "'there is none else besides Him' is written" — if the Omnipresent desires me, you will not be able to harm me, and if you are able, it has come from Him, and I accept it. Maharsha (Chullin 7b, to which he refers here): The verse means that "there is none else" can be said only of the Holy One, blessed be He: what He decrees, no other powers — the forces of impurity and sorcery — can change; but what is decreed through sorcery, there is still the Holy One, blessed be He, who can change that decree by virtue of merits, as in the case of R. Chanina.)
And as they stated (there),
דְּמִקְרָא זֶה דְּ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ"
that this scriptural declaration of 'there is none else beside Him'
הוּא הִפּוּךְ וְסוֹתֵר לִפְעוּלַת הַכְּשָׁפִים.
is the complete antithesis and nullification of the works of sorcery.
וּכְפִי הַשָּׂגַת כָּל אָדָם זֶה כְּפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ,
And commensurate with each person's grasp of this truth according to his root,
כָּךְ הוּא מַדְרֵגַת יְצִיאָתוֹ מִמִּצְרַיִם,
such is the measure of his personal Exodus from Egypt;
וְכָךְ הָיְתָה הַשָּׂגַת רְאִיָּיתָם עַל הַיָּם
and such was the degree of their perception at the Red Sea,
דְּאָז הָיָה גְּמַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
for then occurred the ultimate completion of the Exodus from Egypt,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוֹת יד, יג190 Exodus 14:13 — And Moses said to the people: Fear not, stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord which He will work for you today; for as you have seen Egypt today, you shall never see them again. Rashi: "For as you have seen Egypt" — what you have seen of them is only for today; today is when you saw them, and you shall not see them again. Ramban: According to our Rabbis this is a negative commandment binding for all generations. The verse is therefore saying: do not fear, stand in your place and see the salvation of the Lord who saves you from their hand today, and do not go back to their servitude — for concerning the Egypt you have seen today the Holy One, blessed be He, further commands you never again of your own will to look upon them, from now and forever.):
as it is stated (Exodus 14:13):
"כִּי אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם הַיּוֹם לֹא [תוֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם]",
"'For as you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall see them no more forever, etc.,'"
דְּיוֹם הַהוּא עֲדַיִן רְאוּם,
for on that very day they still saw them,
וְהָרְאִיָּה אֵינוֹ מִקְרֶה וְסִפּוּר מַעֲשֶׂה,
and this seeing was neither incidental nor a casual chronicle of event,
רַק עֲדַיִן הָיָה לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִרְאוֹתָם
rather they still harbored a residual connection enabling them to see them,
שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִזְדַּכְּכוּ לְגַמְרֵי
because they were not yet completely purified
לְהַשִּׂיג רְאִיָּה דְּיָם
to apprehend the spiritual vision of the Sea,
עַד רֶגַע קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף
until the very instant of the parting of the Red Sea,
דְּהִבְטִיחָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "לֹא תוֹסִיפוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
when the Holy One, blessed be He, promised them: 'You shall not see them again, etc.'
זוֹ הַבְטָחָה דְּכָל מִי שֶׁהוּא מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
This is an enduring guarantee that whoever stems from the holy root and lineage of Israel
לֹא יָבוֹא לוֹ הִרְהוּר וּמַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ כְּלָל בְּלִבּוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
shall never have such a doubt or thought arise in his heart, Heaven forbid,
לוֹמַר: "לֹא יִרְאֶה [יָהּ וְלֹא יָבִין] אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב".
to claim: 'God will not see, neither will the God of Jacob understand.'
דְּכָל מִי שֶׁמִּזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב מַאֲמִין שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה וּמֵבִין וּמַשְׁגִּיחַ בִּפְרָטוּת,
For everyone from the seed of Jacob believes that He perceives, understands, and supervises in precise individual detail,
וְהוּא אֱמוּנָה הַכְּלָלִית,
and this constitutes the universal faith,
וְזֶהוּ "לֹא תוֹסִיפוּ" לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים.
and this explains 'you shall not continue' (lo tosifu) stated in the plural.
וְאָז רָאוּ אַחַר כָּךְ כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט בַּיָּם,
And then they saw subsequently, each one individually at the Sea;
וּמִזֶּה נִצְמַח אַחַר כָּךְ הַשָּׂגָה דְּכָל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and from this sprouted forth the individualized comprehension of each person at the Giving of the Torah
דְּ"אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
in the phrase 'Who brought you out, etc.,'
כְּפִי הַהוֹצָאָה שֶׁהִשַּׂגְתָּ בִּפְרָט נַפְשְׁךָ,
so that according to the measure of liberation you perceived within your specific soul,
כֵּן תַּשִּׂיג "אָנֹכִי" בִּפְרָט כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
so do you apprehend 'I am' (Anokhi) in particular, as mentioned above.
– וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעֵת קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף "ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה",
Therefore Hashem, blessed be He, is titled at the parting of the Red Sea 'Hashem is a man of war,'
דִּכְשָׁפִים מַכְחִישִׁין – הַיְינוּ כְּנִלְחָם שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַכְחִישׁוֹ וּלְבַטְּלוֹ.
for sorcery which 'denies' operates like a combatant seeking to resist and nullify Him.
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "כְּאִישׁ מִלְחָמוֹת יָעִיר [קִנְאָה] וְגוֹמֵר",
And so regarding the future it is said: 'Like a man of wars He will stir up jealousy, etc.',
וְנִקְרָא "כְּאִישׁ" וְלֹא "אִישׁ",
and He is termed 'like a man' (ke-ish) rather than 'a man',
כִּי בִּרְכַּת עֵשָׂו "וְעַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה" גַּם כֵּן מִלְחָמָה וְנִיצּוּחַ לַנִּבְרָאִים וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל
since the blessing of Esau 'and by your sword you shall live' likewise involves war and conflict against creatures and Israel,
וְלֹא לִפְלִיא שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
and not against the Wonder of the supernal Realm.

וּלְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רַשִּׁ"י מַטּוֹת ל"א, ג מִסִּפְרֵי שָׁם, וּפָרָשַׁת בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ פִּסְקָא פד191 Rashi on Numbers 31:3 — "The vengeance of the Lord" — for one who stands against Israel is as though he stands against the Holy One, blessed be He.):
And because they taught (Rashi, Matot 31:3 from the Sifrei there; and Parashat Beha'alotekha, section 84):
"כָּל [הָעוֹמֵד] כְּנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ [עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא]",
'Whoever stands against Israel is as though he stands against the Holy One, blessed be He,'
לָכֵן נִקְרָא "כְּאִישׁ וְכוּלֵי",
therefore He is termed 'like a man, etc.',
הַכָּ״ף הַדִּמְיוֹן הַיְינוּ כִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים: "כְּאִלּוּ"].
the prefix Kaf denoting comparison, corresponding to the rabbinic idiom 'as though'.

sections.en: Opposing Views within Living Torah

items.h: Torah truth can contain opposite positions because both emerge from the Divine source; mature wisdom grasps the unity underlying apparent contradiction.

Seif 1 — Both Are the Words of the Living God
Opposing Torah positions can both be true because they reflect distinct facets of one divine source.

p: בְּכָל חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת דָּבָר מְבוֹרָר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נְטִיָּה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן,
In all novel insights of the Torah, it is impossible for a matter to be elucidated without a leaning this way and that,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֲגִיגָה ג:):
as it is written (Chagigah 3b):
"הַלָּלוּ מְטַמְּאִין וְכוּלֵי",
"These declare impure, etc.,"

"וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" (עֵירוּבִין יג192 Eruvin 13b — R. Abba said in the name of Shmuel: For three years Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel were in dispute, these saying, The halakhah is in accordance with us, and these saying, The halakhah is in accordance with us. A Divine Voice went forth and said: Both these and those are the words of the living God, and the halakhah is in accordance with Beit Hillel. Maharsha: The like of this was said in the first chapter of Chagigah [3b], and it is explained there. Maharal (Derech Chaim 5:16): One might ask why the Heavenly Voice said "these and those are the words of the living God" of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel in particular, when every dispute of sages is likewise such that both sides are "from the mouth of the Master of all deeds." But there is a difference: in other disputes, although everything is from the Blessed One, one of the two opinions stands nearer to Him than the other; whereas with Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel the two are the words of the living God in altogether equal measure, the reasons on the two sides being perfectly balanced, one to permit and one to forbid. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:83): The halakhah follows Beit Hillel because they taught both their own words and those of Beit Shammai: Beit Shammai taught only their own view, holding that the truth is with them alone, since truth is one, whereas Beit Hillel knew that "these and these are the words of the living God" and so taught Beit Shammai's words as well. Hence as soon as the Heavenly voice declared "these and these are the words of the living God," it immediately added that the halakhah follows Beit Hillel, for the one depends on the other — this was the essence of their wisdom and the point on which they differed from Beit Shammai. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 221): Words of Torah are called "words of the living God" in the language of the Sages: "these and these are the words of the living God." Because the Blessed One is called Elohim, Master of all the powers, what is with Him is called "words," speech in particulars: the angels proclaim only the general voice of His will for that day, while each person, through understanding and the heart's perception, grasps the particulars of the words of the living God according to his level — and "these and these are the words of the living God," even though they differ over particulars in the Oral Torah.:).
"and 'both these and those are the words of the living God' (Eruvin 13b)."
פֵּירוּשׁ, "אֱלֹהִים" – בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם הַנִּפְרָדִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם,
The meaning is: 'Elohim' denotes the Master of all differentiated forces in the world,
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
and this is why it is phrased in the plural;
וְכֵן "חַיִּים" לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
and likewise 'Chayyim' (life) is in the plural,
דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא חַיּוּת הַבְּרִיאָה כֻּלָּהּ.
for words of Torah are the vitality of the entire Creation.
וְיֵשׁ חֲלוּקוֹת שֶׁל חַיִּים,
And there are varied allocations of life,

וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "פַּלְגֵי מַיִם לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד וְגוֹמֵר193 Proverbs 21:1 — “A king’s heart is like streams of water in the hand of the Lord; He turns it wherever He wishes.” Metzudas Dovid: Just as channels of water are in a man's hand to divert wherever he wishes by digging trenches, so the heart of a king is in the hand of the Lord, to turn it wherever He wishes. Malbim: Although the heart of a private man is given over to him and the choice is his, the heart of a king is not, since the welfare of the community depends on his choices and if he chooses an evil way he will destroy many; therefore this public heart of his is in the hand of the Lord, and in matters of the community he is without free choice. He is likened to channels of water, which men dig and divert toward the places that need them and away from places they would harm, because that is the public need; so too the king's heart, since from his deeds the affairs of the community flow, whether for chastisement or for kindness, for war or for peace, and God turns it at the very first inclination, as channels of water are diverted at the beginning of their course.",
and concerning this it is stated: 'Like streams of water, the heart of a king is in the hand of Hashem, etc.'

מַאן מַלְכֵי – רַבָּנָן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גִּיטִּין סב194 Gittin 62a — Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda were sitting when Geneiva passed by them. Meanwhile he came over to them and said: Peace upon you, kings, peace upon you, kings. They said to him: From where do you know that the Sages are called kings? He said to them: As it is written, "Through me kings reign." Rashi: "A man of Torah" — a son of Torah. "A contentious man" — one who disputes with the Sages, for he used to vex Mar Ukva, who was head of the court, as stated in the first chapter. Maharsha: The very same incident appears at the end of the chapter "Kol HaGet," where it is not mentioned that he greeted them, because there the Gemara needed only the matter it was dealing with; here, however, the main point for which it is brought is that we double the greeting for Torah scholars, who are called kings. The matter is plain: a king of Israel, and the Torah scholar likewise, makes peace above and below, as they said that whoever occupies himself with Torah for its own sake makes peace in the household above and the household below, as it is stated, "Let him take hold of My strength, let him make peace with Me." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 62a): A king's greeting is doubled, one for himself and one on account of his kingship, since in the king's peace lies the peace of everything; but that reason does not fit a Torah scholar. Rather, one may say it is because the Sages said that Torah scholars increase peace in the world, just as the king increases peace in the world — for were it not for fear of the government, a man would swallow his fellow alive. And so, since Torah scholars increase peace in the world, we double the greeting to them: one for his own peace and one for the peace of the world. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 27): A Torah scholar who can produce novel insights through pilpul — the level of Moses — thereby attains the level of kingship, as stated, "Who are kings? The Rabbis," and of prophecy. Kingship, too, attains true sovereignty from the well and flowing spring that is the source of wisdom, as it says, "Through me kings reign": kingship derives from the Torah, and when it is a flowing spring it never ceases and the reign endures, like that of King David. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): The blessing of Israel, who are called "man," is "subdue it and rule" — to conquer all the earthliness and physicality of this world. The Torah is the template of all creation, and "Who are kings? The Rabbis" — for through their attainment in Torah they rule over all of creation..),
'Who are kings? The Rabbis' (as written in Gittin 62a),

וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תוֹרָה (בָּבָא קַמָּא יז195 Bava Kamma 17a — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: What is meant by "Happy are you that sow beside all waters, that send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey"? Whoever occupies himself with Torah and with acts of kindness merits the inheritance of two tribes. For it is said, "Happy are you that sow" — and sowing means nothing other than charity, as it is said, "Sow for yourselves according to charity, reap according to kindness"; and water means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, "Ho, everyone that thirsts, come for water." Rashi: "That sow" means charity and acts of kindness, as the Gemara goes on to explain. "The inheritance of two tribes" — for this is the implication of the verse: your feet shall be sent forth into the inheritance of the ox and the donkey, that is, of Joseph and of Issachar. Maharsha (s.v. "he merits a canopy like Joseph"): The two inheritances answer to the two merits. The canopy of Joseph is the reward of acts of kindness — worthy children are called an inheritance, "behold, children are an inheritance of the Lord," and Joseph sustained and provided for his brothers in Egypt until they multiplied exceedingly — while the inheritance of Issachar, who was rich in possessions and so able to occupy himself with study, is the reward of Torah..),
and 'water' refers specifically to Torah (Bava Kamma 17a),
וְהֵם נִפְלָגִים לְמַעְיָינוֹת שׁוֹנִים לֶאֱסוֹר וּלְהַתִּיר,
and they divide into distinct springs—to prohibit and to permit;
וְכִסְבוּרִים אָנוּ דְּהוּא בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל חָכָם,
and we might assume that this depends merely upon the sage's own reasoning,
וְאֵינוֹ כֵן,
yet it is not so,
אֶלָּא גַּם זֶה בְּיַד ה'
rather this too is in the hand of Hashem,
שֶׁמֵּאִיר עֵינָיו וּמַטֶּה לְבָבוֹ כְּפִי הַחֵפֶץ וְרָצוֹן אֱלֹהִי לְבַד.
Who illuminates his eyes and bends his heart solely according to the divine will and desire.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
Therefore they are termed 'the words of the living God,'
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֵן דִּבְרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for in truth they are the words of Hashem, blessed be He.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב196 Bava Batra 12a — R. Avdimi of Haifa said: From the day the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages. Is a Sage then not a prophet? This is what he means: even though it was taken from the prophets, from the Sages it was not taken. Rashi: "Prophecy was taken" — this statement is brought here because just above R. Yose said "these are nothing but words of prophecy," calling the words of the Sages prophecy. "Is a Sage then not a prophet?" means: is a Sage not fit to be a prophet? For the Master said that it was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages, which implies that at first the Sages had no prophecy. The answer is: even though it was taken from the prophets — that is, from those prophets who are not Sages — from the Sages it was not taken, and prophets do have a heart of wisdom. Tosafos (s.v. "Is a Sage then not a prophet?"): One might raise the same difficulty against the statement in Sanhedrin that from the day the Temple was destroyed the savor of intercourse was taken and given to transgressors: did transgressors have no such savor before the destruction, since it is derived from "Stolen waters are sweet" (Proverbs 9:17)? The answer is that there too one could resolve it as it is resolved here — it was taken from others but from transgressors it was not taken — and the Gemara simply did not trouble to raise the question in every place. Maharsha: On Rashi's reading — that it was taken from prophets who are not Sages — some object: how was there prophecy among men who were not Sages even before the Temple was destroyed, since we are taught that the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His Presence only on one who is wealthy, mighty and wise, all of it derived from Moses? The difficulty is resolved by the Rosh's explanation there, that "He does not rest His Presence" means that He does not do so permanently. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Batra 12a): A prophet is simply one who knows what is not known to everyone, and whoever knows what is hidden from all is called a prophet — hence the objection, "Is a Sage then not a prophet?", for he too knows what others do not. And what difference is there between the prophet, whose prophecy is told him by the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Sage, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, likewise makes known what is hidden from all? For although the Sage knows it by his own intellect, the intellect does not pass from potentiality to actuality of itself; it is the Holy One, blessed be He, who brings a man's intellect from potentiality to actuality — and since He does, the Sage too is a prophet. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): Although [such an apprehension] is lesser, it has this advantage: through an apprehension that is not openly revealed one can grasp what cannot be grasped by the high apprehension of open revelation, to the point that they said "a Sage is greater than a prophet." This is the holy-spirit apprehension of the Sages, from whom prophecy was not taken, as stated there and as the Ramban writes in his novellae; it is a far smaller level than prophecy, yet it is superior, for through it they can attain higher apprehensions (as the Midrash says on "and his eye saw every precious thing," that things not revealed to Moses were revealed to R. Akiva and his colleagues), since whatever apprehension is smaller in quality is greater in quantity..):
And as they said (Bava Batra 12a):
דּמִן הַחֲכָמִים לֹא נִיטְּלָה נְבוּאָה,
that prophecy was not taken away from the sages,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּנְבוּאָה;
for it truly derives from Hashem, blessed be He, just like prophecy;
רַק הַחִלּוּק דִּנְבוּאָה הוּא "כֹּה אָמַר ה'",
the only distinction being that prophecy declares 'Thus said Hashem,'
הַיְינוּ כָּזֶה מַמָּשׁ
meaning precisely thus,
וְאֵין בּוֹ הַטָּיָה וְחִלּוּק,
admitting no variance or division,
וּשְׁנֵי נְבִיאִים הַמַּכְחִישִׁים זֶה אֶת זֶה הָאֶחָד נְבִיא שֶׁקֶר.
and if two prophets contradict one another, one is a false prophet.
כִּי "נָבִיא" מִלְּשׁוֹן נִיב כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בַּחוּמָשׁ,
For navi (prophet) derives from niv (utterance), as Rashi explains in the Chumash,
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבּוּרוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that denotes the explicit speech of Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַדִּבּוּר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַמָּשׁ בִּגְרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל נָבִיא.
for the actual speech of Hashem resonates in the throat of the prophet.
וְהַדִּבּוּר הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת לַפּוֹעַל,
And speech represents externalized manifestation into actuality,
וּבְהִתְגַּלּוּת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and in manifest reality two opposites cannot coexist in a single subject, as is known,
דְּשֵׂכֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם מַכְחִישׁ זֶה כַּנּוֹדָע מִדִּבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן.
for human intellect denies this, as known from the teachings of the Rambam.
אֲבָל חָכָם הוּא דָּבוּק בְּחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, a sage clings to the supernal wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
which abides within thought in the brain;
שָׁם אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד.
there it is possible for two opposites to coexist within a single subject.
וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא כִּמְעַט מוּכְרָח
Moreover, it is almost necessary,
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה דָּבָר וְהֶפְכּוֹ
according to how Hashem, blessed be He, established all Creation—each thing alongside its opposite,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מִסֵּפֶר יְצִירָה:
as is known from Sefer Yetzirah:
אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה הִיפּוּכוֹ מַמָּשׁ גַּם כֵּן;
there is nothing in existence that does not also possess its exact opposite;
וּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ לָזֶה רְשִׁימוּ בְּחָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and there certainly exists an imprint of this in His wisdom, blessed be He,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן הַמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל.
which constitutes the root of the will bringing things into actualization.
רַק שֶׁבַּפּוֹעַל שְׁנֵי הַהֲפָכִים אֵינָם בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד:
Only in practical manifestation do two opposites not coexist in a single subject:
כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹם אֵינוֹ לַיְלָה וּכְשֶׁהוּא לַיְלָה אֵינוֹ יוֹם,
when it is day it is not night, and when it is night it is not day;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמָּקוֹר, שָׁם כּוּלָּא חַד.
whereas in the primordial Source, everything is utterly one.
וּלְכָךְ כָּל חִידּוּשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה חָכָם,
And for this reason, with any novel insight of Torah that emerges into the world through a sage,
בְּהֶכְרֵחַ יוֹצֵא אָז גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפֶךְ.
its opposite perforce emerges alongside it as well.
וְזֶה טַעַם: "פּוֹטֵר מַיִם רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן" –
And this is the meaning of: 'One who releases water begins strife' (Proverbs 17:14) –
מַיִם הַיְינוּ תוֹרָה,
water signifies Torah;
מִי שֶׁפּוֹתֵחַ אֵיזֶה שַׁעַר וְדָבָר הוּא רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן וּמַחֲלוֹקֶת.
whoever unlocks a gate or new concept inaugurates controversy and dispute.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז.)197 Sanhedrin 7a — There was a certain man who went about saying: Happy is he who hears himself abused and keeps silent — a hundred evils pass him by. Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda: A verse states it, "The beginning of strife is as when one lets out water" — the beginning of a hundred lawsuits. Rashi: "Happy is he who hears and keeps silent" — happy is he who hears himself insulted and is silent, and accustoms himself to it; through his silence a hundred evils that would have come upon him through the quarrel pass him by. "One who lets out water" — one who begins and opens a quarrel, that is the beginning of a hundred lawsuits. מדון ["strife"] is an acronym of מאה דיני ["a hundred lawsuits"]; another version: מדון has the numerical value of a hundred. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaShalom 1): This is alluded to in the open mem [with which the word מחלוקת, "dispute", begins], which is open only a little, and so [strife] keeps on growing, for this is the nature of strife. For privation clings to strife and dispute, just as peace [שלום] is whole [שלם]; and whatever privation clings to, the privation in it keeps increasing — a whole garment is hard to tear, but once it has begun to tear, the tear keeps spreading. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:135): As I heard on "the beginning of a hundred lawsuits" in the first chapter of Sanhedrin: while [a matter] is in the heart it is of the number ten, but in the brain each ten is filled out by ten and becomes a hundred, and strife pertains to the brain.: "רֵישׁ מֵאָה דִּינֵי",
And our Sages of blessed memory taught in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (7a): 'the beginning of a hundred judgments,'
פֵּירוּשׁ כִּי יֵשׁ חֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה,
meaning that there exist fifty gates of understanding (Binah),
וְזֶה טַעַם מֵ"ט פָּנִים טָמֵא וּמֵ"ט פָּנִים טָהוֹר,
and this explains why there are forty-nine aspects to declare impure and forty-nine to declare pure,
כִּי שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים אֵין מוּשָּׂג.
because the fiftieth gate is beyond human comprehension.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּ"פָּנִים" פֵּירוּשׁ גִּלּוּיִים
And this signifies that 'panim' (aspects/faces) denotes outer disclosures,
מַה שֶּׁהֶחָכָם מַרְאֶה פָּנִים מִפְּנֵי מָה אוֹמֵר כֵּן;
wherein the sage demonstrates reasoned grounds explaining why he rules thus;
וְיָדוּעַ מֵ"ט הֵם שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע
and it is known that forty-nine is seven times seven,
נֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁל כֹּחַ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת,
corresponding to the seven structural attributes of the power of manifestation;
וְשַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים נֶגֶד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
while the fiftieth gate corresponds to the intuitive understanding within the heart,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת כְּלָל לַחֲבֵירוֹ הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב מַה שֶּׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בְּלִבּוֹ הַטַּעַם לַדָּבָר,
which is completely impossible to convey to another—the subjective feeling in his heart regarding the true reasoning for the matter,
דְּטַעַם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַסְבִּיר וּלְגַלּוֹת כְּלָל.
for the inner taste and essence can never be fully articulated or revealed.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (לה198 Sanhedrin 35a — Shall we judge him on the eve of Shabbat and conclude the verdict on Sunday? They will forget their reasoning. And though two scribes of the judges stand before them and write down the words of those who acquit and the words of those who convict — granted that they write what was spoken aloud, the heart of men forgets. Therefore it is not possible. Rashi: "Let them try him on the eve of the Sabbath and conclude on Sunday" — for as long as the verdict is not concluded there is no torment of judgment, since every moment he hopes to be saved, whereas once it is concluded he spends the whole day awaiting death. "They would forget their reasons" — which they had debated and weighed carefully on the first day. "What is in the heart is forgotten" — what is in men's hearts they do not write, and though one remembers the basis of the reasoning, the way he had worked it out is forgotten from his heart, and he cannot compose it to give a proper reason as at first. Sod Yesharim (Parashas Zachor 15): The full warmth of remembrance is on the very day; on the next day the matter has grown old and is no longer called "remember" but "keep," as we find in the Gemara: "Shall we try him on the eve of Shabbat and conclude on Sunday? They will forget their reasoning; though two court scribes stand before them and write the words of those who acquit and those who convict, granted that they write what is said aloud, the heart of men forgets." That is, even though they remember the matter as on that day, the warmth of the remembrance cannot be on the following day as it was on the very day..):
And along the lines of what they stated in Sanhedrin (35a):
"לִיבָּא דְּאִינָשֵׁי אִינָשֵׁי",
'The heart of people makes them men,'
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתוֹ בִּכְתָב
such that it cannot be disclosed in writing,
וְכֵן בְּדִבּוּר אִי אֶפְשָׁר,
and likewise in speech it cannot be fully conveyed,
רַק הָרְשִׁימוּ שֶׁבַּלֵּב מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּדִבּוּר
save that the impression within the heart clothes itself in speech,
שֶׁכְּפִי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם שֶׁלּוֹ בַּלֵּב כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר,
so that in proportion to his felt grasp of the rationale in his heart, such is the force of the spoken word,
וְנִיכָּר עַל הַדִּבּוּר הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב,
and the heart's impression is recognizable upon the speech,
אֲבָל אֲמִיתַּת טַעַם שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת.
yet the genuine truth of the taste he perceives cannot be externally unveiled.

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ199 Midrash Tehillim 12 — A seasoned disciple would give forty-nine reasons to declare a thing impure and forty-nine reasons to declare it pure. (בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר יב):
Therefore they stated (in Shocher Tov, Psalms 12):
"תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק הָיָה אוֹמֵר מֵ"ט פָּנִים וְכוּלֵי",
'A distinguished disciple would articulate forty-nine aspects, etc.,'
פֵּירוּשׁ, אוֹמֵר לְגַלּוֹת אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק מֵ"ט פָּנִים.
meaning: through speech to disclose, one can communicate only forty-nine aspects.
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּקִבֵּל תּוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
And so too Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who received the Torah from Heaven,
שֶׁהוּא חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which is the divine wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He,
מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג לִבְנֵי אָדָם לְחַדֵּשׁ מִלְּבָבָם כְּמוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which is beyond human ability to innovate spontaneously from the heart like the Oral Torah,

אֶחָד (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:)200 Rosh Hashanah 21b — Rav and Shmuel. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all of them were given to Moses save one, as it is stated: "You have made him but little less than God." "Kohelet sought to find words of delight" — Kohelet sought to be like Moses. A Divine Voice went forth and said to him: "And that which was written uprightly, words of truth" — "And there has not arisen a prophet again in Israel like Moses." Rashi: Rav and Shmuel are expounding the end of this verse: "refined sevenfold" means seven sevens, which are fifty less one — the gates that were transmitted to Moses; and we learn that fifty were created, since he was made "but little less than God" (a verse from the psalm "What is man that You are mindful of him"). Maharsha: The "words of delight" that Kohelet sought are the gates of intellect and understanding in which the Holy One, blessed be He, delights that man should gain understanding, as it is said: "that he understands and knows Me… for in these I delight" (Jeremiah 9:23). The Divine Voice's "written uprightly" follows the teaching that the "Book of the Upright" is Deuteronomy, of which it is said "and you shall do the upright and the good" (Avodah Zarah 25a): what is written in Deuteronomy — "And there has not arisen a prophet… like Moses" — is words of truth. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 21b): The fiftieth gate corresponds to the Jubilee, which is holy of holies: it is the apprehension of the Holy One, blessed be He, in His own true essence, known to none but Himself, whereas the forty-nine — seven times seven, for the world created in seven days is sevenfold and each of its sevens contains all seven — belong to man, who is in the world. Moses, the seventh righteous man (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehath, Amram, Moses), was fit for the forty-nine, but the fiftieth, which binds and unites all the gates, is beyond one who is in this world, founded as it is on seven. It is called "little" because it is a single gate — little in quantity and great in quality. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 21b, s.v. "but among the kings one did arise"): The Sages expounded the verse because it should have said "Kohelet sought to find delight, to write upright words": "delight" means that he desired to be like the wisest of men, Moses, and "written uprightly" is the answer — though he desired it, so uprightness requires, for no prophet like Moses has arisen again. Nor may one object that if none arose among the prophets, all the more so none could arise among the kings: kingship has a great level of its own, above all the king of Israel — like Solomon, who "sat on the throne of the Lord" (I Chronicles 29:23) and ruled over the upper and the lower beings — to whom an inner level belongs by virtue of kingship. דְּלֹא הִשִּׂיג שַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים,
one gate (Rosh Hashanah 21b) he did not attain, namely the fiftieth gate,
דְּשַׁעַר חֲמִשִּׁים מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא הַרְגָּשָׁתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּלֵּב שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
for the fiftieth gate of the Written Torah is Hashem's own feeling in the supernal Heart,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת
which is impossible to reveal,
וְ"לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא".
and 'the heart does not reveal to the mouth.'
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁמְּחַדְּשִׁים חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, regarding that which the sages of Israel innovate,
מִי שֶׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ, הוּא מַשִּׂיג בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר כָּל הַחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה,
the one who innovates grasps in that specific matter all fifty gates of understanding,
וְהֵן מֵאָה דִּינֵי, חֲמִשִּׁים לְכָל צַד.
and these constitute the hundred judgments—fifty to each side.
וּבְמַחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁהוּא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת שַׁמַּאי וְהִלֵּל,
And in a dispute that is for the sake of Heaven, such as the controversy of Shammai and Hillel,

דְּבֵית הִלֵּל הָיוּ שׁוֹנִין דִּבְרֵיהֶם וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין יג201 Eruvin 13b — Since both these and those are the words of the living God, why did Beit Hillel merit that the halakhah be fixed in accordance with their opinion? Because they were agreeable and forbearing, and they would teach both their own words and the words of Beit Shammai; and not only that, but they would place the words of Beit Shammai before their own. Rashi: "Forbearing" means long-suffering. That they would teach both their own words and the words of Beit Shammai means this: when Beit Shammai brought a proof for their view from a verse and Beit Hillel brought their proof from another verse, Beit Hillel would nonetheless expound Beit Shammai's verse and ask what it comes to teach, and it was not light in their eyes; and that they placed Beit Shammai's words before their own is seen where they said, "the elders of Beit Shammai and the elders of Beit Hillel went," naming Beit Shammai first. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaKaas 1): A man of composure does not depart from rectitude at all but remains in balance, unlike the man without composure, who is carried out of balance altogether; and the halakhah is the way that does not turn to the right or to the left but goes evenly — which is why it is called halakhah, a going straight. Beit Hillel had this measure in all their conduct: they were agreeable and did not take offence even when offended, they taught their opponents' words together with their own and even before their own, and in all of this they were ordered and never went out of the order. And do not say that Beit Shammai were not sages — on the contrary, they were great sages and sharp; but the halakhah, which is the straight path, is with Beit Hillel, because they were men of composure who did not depart from the order and the balance. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:83): The halakhah follows Beit Hillel because they taught both their own words and those of Beit Shammai: Beit Shammai taught only their own view, holding that the truth is with them alone, since truth is one, whereas Beit Hillel knew that "these and these are the words of the living God" and so taught Beit Shammai's words as well. Hence as soon as the Heavenly voice declared "these and these are the words of the living God," it immediately added that the halakhah follows Beit Hillel, for the one depends on the other — this was the essence of their wisdom and the point on which they differed from Beit Shammai.:),
where the House of Hillel would teach their own words alongside the words of the House of Shammai (as written in Eruvin 13b),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מַשִּׂיגִין גַּם דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְהַטְּעִימָה שֶׁל הַהֵיפֶךְ,
this signifies that they grasped the words of the House of Shammai and the experiential taste of the opposing stance as well;
וּכְעִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר שְׁנֵי הַפָּנִים,
mirroring that distinguished disciple who could articulate both perspectives,
כִּי מִצַּד דְּבוּקוּתוֹ בְּחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מַשִּׂיג בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שְׁנֵי הַהֲפָכִים שֶׁבַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה,
for through his attachment to the wisdom of Hashem, blessed be He, he comprehends within that very matter both opposites present in the Supernal Thought,
וְנִמְצָא לְכָל אֶחָד מֵאָה.
resulting in a full hundred for each.

וְזֶה טַעַם הַגְּמָרָא בְּשַׁבָּת (קכט202 Shabbat 129b — Rav proclaimed: A hundred gourds for a zuz, a hundred heads for a zuz, a hundred mustaches for nothing. Rav Yosef said: When we were in the academy of Rav Huna, on a day when the Sages took a break from their studies they would say, Today is a day of mustaches — and I did not know what they were saying. Rashi: "A hundred karei": gourds. "A hundred heads for a zuz": that is, if animal heads are very cheap, buy them, and if not, do not buy them, for they are not healthy to eat. "A hundred sifmei": as in "upon the upper lip" (Leviticus 13:45) — the lips of an animal. "A day when the Rabbis were idle": when the students were lax about coming to the study hall, it was called "a day of lips" — that is, this day is lost to him and there is no benefit in it. Tosafos (s.v. "a hundred heads for a zuz"): By Rashi's explanation it is puzzling what this has to do with [bloodletting] here. Rabbeinu Chananel reads "a hundred horns (קרני) for a zuz" and takes "heads" as human heads: the fixed rate was to shave a hundred heads for a zuz and to let blood with a hundred [cupping] horns for a zuz, but a hundred mustaches were trimmed for nothing, since the trimming came with the fee for shaving and bloodletting, and on a day he trimmed mustaches alone he took nothing. Hence it became a proverb: anyone who toiled and received no wage was said to have had "a day of mustaches." Tosafos (s.v. "the Rabbis were idle"): Their strength had failed, and they were weak and unable to study, as in "two hundred men who were too faint (פגרו) to cross the brook Besor" (I Samuel 30:10).:):
And this is the inner reason of the Gemara in Shabbat (129b):
"מֵאָה קָרֵי בְּזוּזֵי וְכוּלֵי",
"A hundred pumpkins for a zuz, etc.,"
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
and this is not the place to elaborate further.

sections.en: Revelation through Concealment

items.h: Spiritual delight and divine revelation emerge from prior darkness, teaching that the very place of deficiency can become the source of its opposite virtue.

Seif 1 — Delight Born from Concealment
The highest spiritual light and virtue emerge from the very darkness and deficiency that initially obscure them.

p: הַשָּׂגַת הַגִּלּוּי רַק מִתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם,
The attainment of divine revelation comes only out of concealment,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, מז עַמּוּד ב203 Zohar 3:47b — "And I saw that wisdom excels folly" — from folly itself benefit comes to wisdom, for were folly not found in the world, wisdom and its words would not be known, just as benefit comes to light from darkness, for were there no darkness light would not be known. "As light excels darkness" — the benefit of light comes only out of darkness. What perfects white? Black; were there no black, white would not be recognized, and it is by reason of black that white is raised up and honored. R. Yitzchak said: It is like the sweet within the bitter — a man does not know the taste of the sweet until he has tasted the bitter. Who makes this sweet? Say: this bitter one. And so it is written, "God has made the one corresponding to the other."):
along the lines of what they said in the Zohar (Part III, 47b):
"מַאן דְּיָתֵיב בְּצַעֲרָא וְכוּלֵי",
"One who sits in sorrow, etc.,"
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁמּוּרְגָּל בְּתַעֲנוּגִים,
in contrast to one who is accustomed to worldly pleasures;
וְאֵין בַּטּוֹבָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעוֹנֶג.
and in goodness, there is nothing higher than transcendent delight (oneg).
וְעִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא רַק כְּפִי הָעוֹנֶג שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מִזֶּה.
And the essence of spiritual comprehension corresponds solely to the measure of delight one derives from it.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג204 Sanhedrin 93a — The righteous are greater than the ministering angels, as it is stated: "He answered and said: Behold, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods." Rashi: For [the verse] reckons the three righteous men first and the angel last, as it is written: "and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods." Maharsha: The verse says only "four men," including the angel with them; but Rashi's point is that "the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods" implies that the angel is the fourth because they are greater than he: as they walked they went before him, and he came fourth, behind them. Alternatively: we find that the wise are called "gods," as in "the cause of both parties shall come before the gods" [i.e., the judges], whereas the angel is called only "a son of the gods," for he is not as distinguished as the righteous, who are called "gods.".):
And this explains what they taught in Sanhedrin (93a):
"צַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת",
"The righteous are greater than the ministering angels,"
וּמָצִינוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים לְהֵיפֶךְ,
yet we find several times the opposite stated,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַב אַבְרָהָם בֶּן עֶזְרָא דְּוַדַּאי הַשָּׂגַת מַלְאָכִים גְּדוֹלָה,
as Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra wrote that the intellectual apprehension of angels is certainly greater,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן.
and as Maimonides (Rambam) also wrote.
רַק הֵם אֵין לָהֶם עוֹנֶג,
However, they possess no experience of sublime delight,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט205 Shabbat 89a — [Moses said to the ministering angels:] Again, what is written in it? "Honor your father and your mother" — do you have a father and a mother? Again, what is written in it? "You shall not murder," "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not steal" — is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you? At once they conceded to the Holy One, blessed be He. Rashi: "Is there jealousy among you?" — through which you would come to murder. Maharsha: Once it had been shown that even the hidden part of the Torah is within man's reach, through the soul that is bound to the Throne of Glory, Moshe argued that the Torah should be given to him rather than set in heaven, on account of its revealed part — "what is written in it?" Therefore "at once the ministering angels conceded" that it is more fitting to give the Torah to Israel than to set its glory and secret in heaven, since the revealed Torah has no application in heaven. Maharal (Derush al HaTorah 5): Moshe answered each of the first five commandments separately but the later ones in a single reply, because the first five are between man and God — "Honor your father and your mother" among them, for there are three partners in a person, and one who honors his parents is accounted as having honored the Holy One, blessed be He — while the last five are all between man and his fellow. These are joined together, since a sin against people leaves its mark on the one sinned against, whereas of a sin against Heaven it is said, "If you have sinned, what do you effect against Him?" Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 24): Moshe's "what is written in it?" means that although the angels grasp of themselves that there is an order ordained by the Blessed One, the order itself belongs to man alone: the Torah, though created before the world, is arranged according to man's humanity — its commandments correspond to his 248 limbs — and, like the Divine image, which needs a physical body to bear it, it rests upon physical things, the practical commandments, and requires a physical bearer. That was the answer to the angels, and therefore "they conceded.".):
just as our Sages stated in Shabbat (89a):
"כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע בֵּינֵיכֶם?",
"Is there an evil inclination among you?"
דְּהָעוֹנֶג נִמְשָׁךְ רַק מִן הַהֵיפֶךְ.
for sacred delight is drawn exclusively out of its opposite.
וְזֶהוּ יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר כְּשֶׁהוּא מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
And this is the preeminence of light when it emerges from darkness;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּעוֹנֶג הוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשֵּׂכֶל,
for as is known, oneg is the primordial depth that transcends mortal intellect,
כְּטַעַם: "תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'",
in the spirit of: 'You shall delight upon Hashem' (Isaiah 58:14) –
פֵּירוּשׁ, שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַמּוּשָּׂג,
meaning: the Tetragrammaton (Havayah) represents the manifest expansion of that which can be comprehended,
וְהָעוֹנֶג הוּא דְּבֵיקוּת בַּמֶּה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַמּוּשָּׂג.
while delight is the mystical cleaving to that which transcends comprehension.
"וְהָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל" –
'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light' (Isaiah 9:1) –
פֵּירוּשׁ, "גָּדוֹל" הוּא מִמִּדַּת גְּדוּלָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning: 'great' stems from the divine attribute of Gedulah (Lovingkindness/Greatness) of Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין שִׁיעוּר,
signifying infinite expansion without measure,
כִּי הוּא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַשִּׁיעוּר,
because it is completely beyond bounded measure,

כְּעִנְיַן (שַׁבָּת קיח206 Shabbat 118a — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Yose: Whoever delights in the Shabbat is given an inheritance without bounds, as it is stated: "Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father." Rashi: "Without bounds": that is, it has no end. "Then you shall delight": this is written after "and you call the Sabbath a delight." "The heritage of Yaakov" — and not the heritage of Avraham and Yitzchak: "its length and its breadth" means this land and no more, and "these lands" means these and nothing further. Maharsha: The Beit Yosef (Tur, Orach Chayim 242) explains it as measure for measure: as he spends without limit for the Shabbat, so he is given an inheritance without limit. Alternatively, the delight of Shabbat touches the spiritual — the additional soul, through which one merits the day that is wholly Shabbat, which has no bound in space — so its reward too has no bound, and "you shall spread out" (ופרצת) is read here as the breaching of a fence, so that his inheritance has no fence or border. The blessing was given to Yaakov and not to Avraham and Yitzchak because in their merit bounded lands were given to other nations as well (to Lot and to the children of Esav), whereas in the merit of Yaakov, through whom the merit passed down from fathers to sons, this further blessing of an inheritance without bounds was added. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 118a): Delight by its nature has no constraint — one who is hemmed in by distress is not in delight at all — and since the Shabbat, being a day of rest, is the one day fit for delight, one who delights in it is given a portion likewise without constraint: an inheritance with a border is hemmed in by what lies beyond it, while one without a border extends in every direction. Further, holiness is the attribute of Yaakov (hence the blessing corresponding to him is "You are holy"), and the Shabbat is the holiness in the world; the holy, being separate from the physical, has no limit, since only the physical, which has extension, has an end — therefore Yaakov's inheritance, and that of one who delights in the Shabbat, is without bounds. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 3): Scripture says of Shabbat "in all your dwellings" in keeping with the teaching "Whoever delights in the Shabbat is given an inheritance without bounds … like Jacob, of whom it is written, 'And you shall spread out to the west and to the east.'" That is, wherever he goes the holiness of the Land of Israel goes with him; therefore on Shabbat a Jew merits that every place where he stands is holy ground, and in all one's dwellings one can attain the holiness of the Land of Israel, the inheritance from the Patriarchs. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 5): Abraham was given a possession still within boundaries — "all the land which you see," that is, wherever you see the glory of Heaven — because Ishmael issued from him, and had it been given without limit he too would have taken of it without choice; likewise Esau issued from Isaac, so to him it was given with constrictions, "all these lands." But in Jacob there was no dross at all, so it was given to him without any boundaries: "And you shall spread out to the west and to the east." On Shabbat the verse mentions Jacob alone, "the heritage of Jacob your father," because Shabbat alludes to the future, when "the Lord shall be One and His name One," and then it is the inheritance without bounds, the portion of Jacob..):
in the manner of Shabbat (118a):
"הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים".
"Whoever delights in the Sabbath is given a boundless heritage."
כִּי כֹּחַ הָעוֹנֶג הוּא לְמַעְלָה מִקַּו הַמִּדָּה,
For the power of delight is higher than the measuring line,
כִּי לְהַשָּׂגָה יֵשׁ מִדָּה וּגְבוּל,
since cognitive apprehension has measure and boundaries,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְעוֹנֶג.
whereas delight has no boundaries.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת עז207 Shabbat 77b — R. Zeira found Rav Yehudah standing at the entrance of his father-in-law's house and saw that he was in good spirits, such that had he asked him about all the hollows of the world he would have told him. He said to him: Why do the goats walk at the head and the sheep after them? He said to him: It is as at the creation of the world — first darkness and afterward light. Rashi: "All the hollows of the world": that is, the things that happen throughout the space of the world. "First darkness": goats are generally black, and ewes generally white. Maharsha: Although the natural philosophers gave reasons for how each thing is formed, and the Talmud too has a few such ("why is the whole ear hard and the lobe soft"), these reasons are forced in their plain sense, so they must be meant as a parable on matters of Torah: Greece is likened to a goat ("and the he-goat grew exceedingly great", Daniel 8:8) and Israel to a sheep ("Israel is a scattered sheep", Jeremiah 50:17), and he asked why in the Second Temple the goats — the kings of Greece, Alexander of Macedon and those after him — reigned first, and only afterward the sheep, the kings of Israel. He answered that this was already alluded to in the creation of the world: first darkness — "and darkness was upon the face of the deep", which Bereshit Rabbah expounds of Greece, who darkened Israel's eyes — and afterward light, the Hasmonean kingdom, who came to reign through the miracle of the Chanukah lights. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 77b): The goats derive from the power of the attribute of judgment, which is the attribute of night; and night came before day because the attribute of judgment, by the very strength of that attribute, hastens to go forth into actuality. So too the goats walk at the head of the flock because of the swiftness of action they receive from the attribute of judgment — and this is what he answered him: as at the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 1): With respect to night, which is darkness, cessation and darkness come before day, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness...": for one who stands in darkness, darkness comes first and afterward light, and so there were two thousand years of chaos and afterward two thousand of Torah. But for one who stands in the day, day comes first and afterward night, to rest from his toil; and so once the Torah was given there was light for the world, and light comes before darkness. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 61): Esau was the firstborn in birth, which is the emergence into actuality, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness": on the side of the refuse the left is the right and comes first, and the this-world of Esau, in which darkness prevails, comes first. But in formation [yetzirah], which is the hidden world, the thought of creation and the conception of the world, the right comes first. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): The creation of the world was "first darkness and afterward light": first comes the portion of Bereishis, in the knowledge of the vessels, and afterward the attainment of the light of Abraham our father through knowledge, in the manner of "the advantage of light over darkness." Such too is the order of man's attainment of the light of the Blessed One, like the creation of the world: first the six days of work and afterward Shabbos; but for man's own action the light must come first and afterward the making of the vessel. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): This light [of the soul's root] can be attained in this world only through repentance, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light." Thus for certain righteous men, such as King David in the trial of Bathsheba, the Blessed One arranged a deed of the wicked in order to establish the yoke of repentance, for this cannot come about except through a preceding darkness. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): [In the Oral Torah and the innovation of laws not yet clarified] it is impossible to stand at all without a prior stumbling, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," for so is the light attained by created beings: specifically out of darkness and concealment. Therefore Esau was formed before Jacob, being the preceding darkness that leads to the attainment of the light of Torah afterward. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 21): On "Why do the goats go first... as at the creation of the world, first darkness and afterward light," Rashi explains that goats are ordinarily black. So Teves, whose sign is the kid, is the aspect of darkness, and specifically then [the Hasmoneans] brought about their miracle through their self-sacrifice, to shine out of the darkness with greater excellence, as the Zohar says, "there is no light except that which comes out of darkness"; and this is like the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): Since it is of the working of the Blessed One that it be so, "first darkness and afterward light," for the advantage of light is recognized only from darkness, [the forces of evil] therefore begin to act first, and from this the light shines forth, as in "He made darkness His hiding place," for there He is hidden. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Such is the way of the Blessed One in the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light"; and so [the Sages] said that He would create worlds and destroy them, these being the worlds of chaos, until the world of rectification emerged. So it is in everything: all the incarnations of the Messiah that have already been in the world are akin to "creating worlds and destroying them," and specifically through those destructions the world of rectification is built, by raising up the lights of the broken vessels. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 174): Since in natural things the Blessed One established this order, "first darkness and afterward light," it is certainly the essence of His will, as [the Sages said], "In the place where penitents stand...". Although, Heaven forbid, one may not say "I will sin and repent" and do so by choice, it nonetheless happens of itself, for "there is no righteous man on earth..."; and such is the order: "the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light," far beyond one who did not walk in darkness. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): From the standpoint of this world's imagination it seemed at first that everything belonged to Esau, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," as [the Sages] said at the beginning of Berakhos, which is why the evening Shema was placed first. For the Shema, the recognition of [God's] unity, was the essence of the creation of the world, and first one must recognize it out of darkness and concealment, for that was the whole matter of creation. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Shabbos): This is as it is written, "The Lord my God illuminates my darkness": after a person recognizes his sin and is pained over it, he merits that the Blessed One shines for him a rectification for it. Through the darkness, the remorse and pain he felt over the deed, he merits the light that reveals its rectification; and this is "first darkness and afterward light." Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 71): The Blessed One set the light in this world surrounded and encompassed by darkness, to leave man room to distinguish himself, that he remove the darkness and shine even within it. Therefore, when the Blessed One shines His bright light, He will shine it only for one who on his part walked in the light and did His will; He created the darkness only for the sake of one who desires the light, that for his sake He will illuminate the darkness too. Tiferes Yosef (Shavuos 7): It is written, "who forms light and creates darkness," yet at the creation of the world "there was evening and there was morning," first darkness and afterward light, so here too it should have said "creates darkness" first. The explanation: the first light was not yet within creation's capacity to receive, and light that creation cannot receive is called darkness from creation's standpoint; therefore it says "forms light and creates darkness," for from creation's standpoint it begins with day, since in the first evening creation had no grasp at all. Sod Yesharim (Shabbos HaGadol 6): As my father and teacher explained, the whole purpose of the darkness that the Blessed One set first is only that the light afterward be the more explicit; therefore "it was evening" is said first and then "it was morning." So too with Abraham our father: all the concealment he had at first, until he said, "Shall you say the palace has no master?", was the darkness that came first, only so that the Blessed One would afterward shine to him with greater clarity, "I am the master of the palace.":),
And this is the secret of the universe's creation, 'first darkness, etc.' (Shabbat 77b),
דִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הָיָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה
for the creation of the world occurred precisely in this manner
לְהַשִּׂיג מִדַּת הָעוֹנֶג,
in order to attain the divine attribute of delight;
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא.
and this is achievable only through darkness coming first.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ" דַּיְיקָא, "אָז ה' אוֹר לִי",
And as it is written (Micah 7:8): specifically 'though I sit in darkness, then Hashem is a light unto me,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב): "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ",
and as it is written (Psalms 18:12): 'He makes darkness His secret place,'
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִסְתַּתֵּר תּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, conceals Himself within the darkness.
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהַהֶעְלֵם
And in proportion to the intensity of the obscurity and concealment,
כֵּן הוּא תּוֹקֶף הָאוֹר הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ
such is the magnitude of the light hidden within it
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַחַשְׁכוּת.
that one is able to attain through that very darkness.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר", מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא;
And as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:29): 'And from there you shall seek Hashem, etc.'—specifically from there;
וְאוֹמֵר: "עֵת צָרָה וְגוֹמֵר וּמִמֶּנָּה יִוָּשֵׁעַ",
and Scripture states (Jeremiah 30:7): 'It is a time of trouble... but he shall be saved out of it,'
וְהַכָּתוּב אֵין קוֹרֵא צָרָה לַגּוּף לְבַד,
and Scripture does not define trouble as pertaining to the body alone,
רַק מַה שֶּׁבֶּאֱמֶת מֵיצַר גַּם בַּנֶּפֶשׁ
rather that which truly afflicts the soul as well;
מִזֶּה דַּיְיקָא הוּא הַיְשׁוּעָה לַנֶּפֶשׁ.
out of this specific inner distress emerges the ultimate salvation for the soul.
וְכֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר,
And similarly throughout every single generation,
אֵין לְךָ מִי שֶׁטָּעַם מִכָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
you have no one who tasted of all the physical desires of this world like King Solomon, peace be upon him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר קֹהֶלֶת: "עָשִׂיתִי לִי וְגוֹמֵר וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאֲלוּ עֵינַי וְגוֹמֵר" כַּנּוֹדָע,
and as written in the Book of Ecclesiastes (2:4, 10): 'I made for myself, etc., and whatever my eyes desired, etc.,' as is known;
וְאֵין לְךָ גַּם כֵּן לֵב נָקִי מִכָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲוָה כִּלְבָבוֹ,
and likewise you have no heart as utterly cleansed from every form of lust as was his heart,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יָדַיִם סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג208 Mishnah Yadayim 3:5 — R. Akiva said: Heaven forbid — no man in Israel ever disputed that the Song of Songs renders the hands impure, for the whole world is not worth the day on which the Song of Songs was given to Israel; for all the Writings are holy, but the Song of Songs is the holy of holies. And if they disputed, they disputed only about Ecclesiastes.):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated at the end of Yadayim (chapter 3):
עַל סֵפֶר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים.
concerning the Song of Songs, that it is the Holy of Holies.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה וְתַאֲוָה שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדוּשָּׁה
And wherever you find a boundary against immorality and lust, there you find holiness

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כד209 Vayikra Rabbah 24:6 — R. Yehudah ben Pazi said: Why was the section of forbidden relations set beside the section "You shall be holy"? Only to teach you that in every place where you find a fence against sexual immorality, you find holiness. And this accords with R. Yehudah ben Pazi, who said: Whoever fences himself off from sexual immorality is called holy. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shoftim 5): [The Sabbath] also corresponds to the holiness of Joseph; this is what is said, "and He sanctified it": this is holiness, as they said, "wherever you find a fence against sexual immorality you find holiness," and Joseph the Righteous is the chariot of this attribute. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 1): The essence of holiness is the holiness of the covenant, as they said in Vayikra Rabbah, "wherever you find a fence against sexual immorality you find holiness," as R. Yehudah ben Pazi said, "whoever fences himself off from immorality is called holy." The Nazirite too is called holy in the Torah, essentially because he has separated himself from wine, which is a fence against immorality; and included in this are all restraints of bodily desires, which are fences against immorality, and therefore, according to one opinion, one who sits in a fast is called holy. Beis Yaakov (Vayeishev 35): Joseph the Righteous is the light of all Israel, for through guarding the covenant and a person's self-restraint one merits to see the face of the King, the Lord, in His beauty, explicitly before him. And "wherever you find a fence against sexual immorality you find a fence of holiness": the fence against immorality is the aspect of Joseph the Righteous, and the fence of holiness is confidence, strength and joy. Sod Yesharim (Seventh Night of Pesach 29): This is as the Sages said, "wherever you find a fence against sexual immorality, there you find a fence of holiness": the fence of holiness is true life, without any falsehood or levity, whereas for those who are not fenced off from this desire, their life is falsehood and no real life at all, only mere levity. But Israel, because they are fenced off from this desire, have the structure of their bodies ever further strengthened with true life.),
(as written in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashah 24),
דְּזֶה טַעַם קְדוּשָּׁה – פְּרִישׁוּת מִתַּאֲווֹת רַק מוּקְדָּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for this is the very definition of kedushah: separation from base desires to be consecrated solely unto Hashem, blessed be He;
כִּי זֶה הֵיפֶךְ זֶה:
because the one is the complete antithesis of the other:
הַשָּׁקוּעַ בַּתַּאֲווֹת נֶאֱמַר: "לְתַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּשׁ נִפְרָד",
regarding one immersed in lust it is stated: 'He who separates himself seeks his own desire' (Proverbs 18:1),
שֶׁהוּא נִפְרָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
meaning that he becomes separated and alienated from Hashem, blessed be He;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מוּקְדָּשׁ לַשָּׁמַיִם,
in contrast, in kedushah one is consecrated unto Heaven,
כְּמוֹ קִדּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה פֵּירְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין ב:):
just as regarding betrothal (kiddushin) of a woman, our Rabbis explained in Kiddushin (2b):
לְשׁוֹן הֶקְדֵּשׁ, שֶׁשַּׁיָּיכָה לַבַּעַל.
it is an expression of consecration (hekdesh), designating her exclusively to her husband.
וְעִנְיַן שִׁיר הוּא מִצַּד הַחֵשֶׁק,
And the essence of song emerges from intense, passionate longing,
דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא שִׁירֵי עֲגָבִים;
which is why love-ballads are termed shirei agavim;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר כָּלְתָה נַפְשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and when a person's soul yearns away entirely toward Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהוּא חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה לוֹ,
and he is lovesick for Him,
אָז נִפְתַּח פִּיו לְשׁוֹרֵר לְפָנָיו.
then his mouth is opened to sing before Him.
וְאֵין לְךָ שִׁירִים מְעוֹרְרִים אַהֲבָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וְהִתְאַחֲדוּתָם כְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים.
And you have no songs that awaken the love of Israel for their Father in Heaven and their mutual union like the Song of Songs.
וְאַהֲבָה זוֹ הוּא הֵיפֶךְ אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And this sacred love is the direct opposite of worldly love,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים,
therefore it is the Holy of Holies,
שַׁיָּיךְ לְגַמְרֵי לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
belonging entirely to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְנִפְרָשׁ לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and completely separated from all earthly desires,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָהֶם כְּלָל.
having no connection to them whatsoever.
וְכָךְ הוּא הַמִּדָּה:
And this is the operative spiritual principle:
דְּאוֹתוֹ לֵב שֶׁטּוֹעֵם מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ עַד קָצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן
that the very heart which tastes of the darkness down to the outermost edge
וּמְבַקֵּשׁ מִשָּׁם אֶת ה',
and seeks Hashem specifically from that place,
טוֹעֵם הָאוֹר עַד קָצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן,
tastes the divine light up to its ultimate boundary,
עַד שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שֶׁאֵין חֹשֶׁךְ
until he realizes that darkness has no independent reality,
וְ"כָל חֹשֶׁךְ לֹא יַחְשִׁיךְ וְגוֹמֵר לַיְלָה כַּיּוֹם יָאִיר וְגוֹמֵר".
and that 'even darkness darkens not from You, but the night shines as the day' (Psalms 139:12).
וְכֵן בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת:
And similarly across all character traits:
בִּמְקוֹם צָרוּת עַיִן שָׁם הוּא טוֹבַת עַיִן,
in the very place of a stingy, narrow eye, there resides the generous, good eye;
וּבִמְקוֹם רוֹעַ לֵב – לֵב טוֹב.
and in the very place of a hardened, malicious heart resides the good and benevolent heart.

sections.en: Purim, the Lot, and the Erasure of Amalek

items.h: Purim's holiness arises through Haman's own lot, revealing how Amalek's force becomes the instrument of its destruction before renewed Temple building.

Seif 1 — The Lot that Destroys Amalek
Purim transforms Haman's lottery into the mechanism of Amalek's downfall and preparation for renewed redemption.

p: עִנְיַן פּוּרִים עַל שֵׁם הַפּוּר,
The matter of Purim is named after the lot (pur),
דִּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת קָבוּעַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דִּמְקַדֵּשׁ,
for the holiness of Shabbat is established permanently by Hashem, blessed be He, Who sanctifies it,
וּקְדוּשַׁת יוֹם טוֹב וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי,
while the sanctity of the festivals and Rosh Chodesh is sanctified by the Jewish people ('Israel sanctifies the seasons'),
אֲבָל פּוּרִים אוֹתוֹ יוֹם זָכָה בַּגּוֹרָל עַל יְדֵי הָמָן
yet concerning Purim, that very day was selected through the lottery cast by Haman
שֶׁנִּבְחַר לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק,
which was singled out for the obliteration of Amalek,

כִּי "מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא וְכוּלֵי210 Sanhedrin 39b — From the forest itself comes the handle for the axe — that is, a thing is brought down by what issues from it. Rashi: "Abba" is a forest: from the very wood of the forest [a piece] goes into the axe to be its handle, and with it they cut down the forest. So too Obadiah against Edom, and David against Moab, for he descended from Ruth the Moabite. Maharsha (s.v. "Obadiah was an Edomite convert"): That is, the prophecy is all the more borne out because Obadiah was one of their own, testifying against them — as was said above of Balaam. So too with "and he measured them with a line": we do not find that David did such a thing to any other nation he conquered, but because he himself came from Moab, being one of their own he did this to them, so that it would be all the more borne out that they deserved it. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 39b): A person is more apt to act upon himself than upon another, for a thing is close to itself; therefore it was Obadiah who prophesied against Edom, to bring the retribution upon Edom. And this is what R. Yochanan said [of David and Moab], "from it and in it, the axe": retribution usually comes upon a person from within himself, because one is apt to act upon oneself, whereas through others it does not so readily take effect. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 5): R. Akiva, the foundation of the Oral Torah, was a son of converts and came from Esau, in the manner of what the Sages said in Sanhedrin about Obadiah, an Edomite convert who prophesied against Edom, because "from the forest itself [comes the handle for the axe]." That is, because Esau came from Isaac, on which account the Sages call Esau "an apostate Israelite"; and since there was in some respect a connection to Isaac, the beginning of the Israelite lineage, Esau too had some share in it." (סַנְהֶדְרִין לט:),
for 'from the forest itself comes the axe-handle to fell it, etc.' (Sanhedrin 39b),
וְעַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ נִבְחַר
and through Haman himself it was chosen:
עַל פִּי הַגּוֹרָל נָפַל עַל יוֹם זֶה
by means of the lot it fell upon this specific day
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוּכָן לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק
to be prepared for the destruction of Amalek,
וְלָנוּחַ בַּיּוֹם שֶׁאַחֲרָיו וְעָשׂוּ וְגוֹמֵר.
and to rest on the day following it, 'and they made it a day of feasting, etc.'
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הַגּוֹרָל נִרְאֶה מִקְרֶה,
Now seemingly, a lottery appears to be mere blind chance,

רַק הַכָּתוּב מֵעִיד (מִשְׁלֵי טז211 Proverbs 16:33 — The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the Lord. Rashi: "The lot is cast into the lap" — a man casts the lot privately, by himself. "But its every judgment is from the Lord" — to select for each and every one his portion. Metzudas Dovid: Those who cast lots place the slips in the lap or in some other hidden place and draw them out to assign the portions. Scripture says: do not question the lot and say that it came by chance, for while the slips were still cast into the lap, before they were drawn out, the judgment of the matter had already been decreed by the Lord, and each man received the portion God above apportioned to him. Malbim: There are matters that appear to be left to chance and are in fact governed by Providence, for where human choice and effort break off the eye of Providence appears — as when a matter is in doubt between two men and they cast a lot to learn to whom the disputed share belongs.
