Though the lot is cast in the lap, hidden from the human eye and given over to chance, the eye of the Lord's providence rests upon it, and the verdict the lot yields is no accident but "from the Lord" — as with the division of the land, where the lot fell by His providence., לג):
yet Scripture testifies (Proverbs 16:33):
"וּמֵה' כָּל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ",
"'and from Hashem comes its every verdict,'
דְּהַמִּקְרֶה גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
revealing that chance itself is likewise directed by Hashem, blessed be He.
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר נִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק
Through this profound realization occurs the principal defeat of Amalek,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
concerning whom it is stated: 'who happened upon you (karkha / rooted in mikreh - chance),'
וְכֵן בְּהָמָן: "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ",
and likewise regarding Haman: 'all that had happened to him (karahu),'
שֶׁנִּתְלִים בַּמִּקְרֶה;
for they attribute everything to arbitrary chance;
כִּי כְּפִי שָׁרְשָׁם כָּךְ הֵם כָּל עִנְיָנָם,
since according to their essential spiritual root, so unfolds their entire character,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ212 Sanhedrin 90a — And why to such an extent? It was taught: He denied the resurrection of the dead; therefore he shall have no share in the resurrection of the dead — for all the measures of the Holy One, blessed be He, are measure for measure. Maharsha: That this is a grave heresy is certain; rather, "why to such an extent" asks why [the mishnah] placed the denial of the resurrection of the dead before the denial that the Torah is from Heaven and before the heretic. And it answers that [the punishment for] this one is measure for measure more than for the other heresies. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 90a): Because the measures of the Holy One, blessed be He, are measure for measure, it is known that no evil comes from God, only good, and that man brings the evil upon himself by the measure with which he measured. When a loan is repaid with exactly what was lent, the repayment is ascribed not to the one who repays but to the one who lent; so too, because the Holy One, blessed be He, repays measure for measure, [the punishment] is ascribed to the man himself and not to God. Maharal (Derech Chaim 4:16): The Gemara explains the reason: because he denied the resurrection of the dead, he shall have no share in the resurrection of the dead — which shows explicitly that the World to Come is the world that will be after the resurrection. Therefore it says "He denied the resurrection of the dead," and so he shall have no share in the resurrection of the dead, which is the World to Come..):
along the lines of what they stated (Sanhedrin 90a):
"הוּא כָּפַר בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, לְפִיכָךְ אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְכוּלֵי",
'He denied the resurrection of the dead, therefore he has no share in it, etc.,'
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַבְּחִירָה.
and this represents the human perspective of free choice.
וּמִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ:
Yet from the perspective of supernal divine foreknowledge, it is the reverse:
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים
namely, that whoever has no allotted share in the resurrection of the dead
הוּא כּוֹפֵר בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.
ends up denying the resurrection of the dead.
וְכֵן כָּל עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק מִקְרֶה בָּעוֹלָם,
And likewise, the whole phenomenon of Amalek is the manifestation of 'chance' in the universe,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן מִקְרֶה
for Hashem, blessed be He, deliberately created the reality of chance as well,
דְּאֵין דָּבָר חוּץ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since there is nothing outside of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְדָבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this concept also originates from Hashem, blessed be He:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִקְרֶה מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מְסוּדָּר כְּפִי הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁיִּסַּד.
that there should appear as 'chance' whatever is not aligned with the manifest order He established.
וְזֶהוּ עֲמָלֵק,
And this is the archetype of Amalek;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִקְרֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
and because his existence is rooted in chance, as written 'who met you by chance (karkha),'
הוּא תּוֹלֶה הַכֹּל בַּמִּקְרֶה.
he attributes everything to coincidence.
וְאָמַר "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ",
And Scripture says: 'all that happened to him (karahu),'
וְזֶהוּ הָיָה בְּעֵת הַסּוֹף שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהָלַךְ לַאֲבַדּוֹן,
and this was at the time of his ultimate downfall when he was headed for oblivion;
אָז אָמַר "אֲשֶׁר קָרָהוּ"
only then did he say 'all that happened to him,'
שֶׁתָּלָה הַכֹּל בַּמִּקְרֶה,
attributing everything stubbornly to random occurrence,
דְּכָל דָּבָר מִתְבָּרֵר בְּסוֹפוֹ,
for every entity's true nature is clarified at its culmination;
כְּמוֹ בְּבִלְעָם בַּסּוֹף בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דִּשְׁטִים
just as with Balaam at the end in the incident of Shittim,
נִתְגַּלָּה דְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ זְנוּת,
it was unveiled that his essential root was licentiousness,
וְאָז אָמַר: "הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ לְעַמִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
and then he said: 'Behold, I go unto my people, etc.,'

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי בָּלָק, וּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י213 Rashi on Numbers 24:14 — "I go to my people" — from now on I am like the rest of my people, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has withdrawn from him. "Come, I will counsel you" — what you are to do; and what was the counsel? The God of these people hates licentiousness, and so forth, as related in [Sanhedrin] chapter Chelek. Know that it was Balaam who gave this counsel to make them stumble through licentiousness, for it is said, "Behold, these caused the children of Israel, by the counsel of Balaam.")
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Yalkut Shimoni, Balak; and Rashi's commentary)
וְנוֹדַע שֶׁנִּבְאַשׁ.
and it became universally known that he had made himself odious.
דְּבַתְּחִלָּה כָּל דָּבָר רַע הַגָּוֶון הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ,
For initially, in every evil matter the outward guise portrays the reverse,
וְגָוֶון עֲמָלֵק הוּא שֶׁאֵין נִתְלֶה בַּמִּקְרֶה,
and the deceptive guise of Amalek is that he does not seem to hang on chance,
דְּעִנְיַן הַגּוֹרָל מָצִינוּ בַּתּוֹרָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וּבַחֲלוּקַּת הָאָרֶץ,
since the concept of the sacred lottery is found in the Torah on Yom Kippur and in the division of the Land of Israel,
דְּזֶהוּ עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְמוֹךְ עַל גּוֹרָל
where it is the hallmark of Israel to rely upon the lot
לְהַחֲזִיק שֶׁאֵין הַדָּבָר בְּמִקְרֶה.
in order to affirm that nothing occurs by chance.
וְזֶה כָּל תָּקְפּוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו:
And this constitutes the full deceitful strength of Esau:

"פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה214 Bereshit Rabbah 65:1 — “Esau was forty years old” — that is what is written: “The boar out of the wood ravages it” (Psalms 80:14). R. Pinchas in the name of R. Simon: Of all the prophets, only two publicized it [the character of the wicked kingdom] — Moses and Asaph. Moses said: “And the swine, because it parts the hoof”; Asaph said: “The boar out of the wood ravages it.” Why does he liken it to a pig? Because just as this pig, when it lies down, stretches out its hooves as if to say, “I am pure,” so this wicked kingdom robs and plunders, yet appears as though it were setting up the seat of judgment. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 3): No convert is accepted from Amalek, meaning that he cannot convert at all: even if he performs the commandments, and not in deed alone but even accepts in thought and will to be a complete Israelite, he is still called only one who "stretches out its hooves like a pig" to say "pure," for the deepest beginning and root of his thought and will, hidden even from himself, is certainly not so, and it is complete falsehood. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 24): So too Esau "stretches out his hooves like a pig": the pig has a sign of purity in its hooves, and of the two signs, which allude to deed and thought, the hooves correspond to deed; these he stretches out, for "the hunt was in his mouth" but not in his heart, saying "see, I am pure." Yet he is not even half pure; rather, whatever lacks the four signs is entirely impure. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 20): In deed, Esau too "stretches out his hooves like a pig," and Amalek is called "the first of nations" because only his deepest beginning is evil: he can stretch out his hooves through all nine levels that unfold from the deepest beginning of thought, appearing as though he too were good, yet his deepest beginning is utterly evil, and so he is wholly evil. With Israel it is the reverse: even one who has sinned, as the Sages said of Achan that he denied the entire Torah, still has his deepest beginning cleaving to the good, and so he is wholly good. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Toward this the preparation is the exile of Edom, of which the Sages said "it stretches out its hooves like a pig and says, I am pure." For the Giving of the Torah is a clarification over against Egypt, which was openly "flesh of donkeys," whereas Edom's revealed aspect is pure; therefore it came from Esau, born of Isaac, with whom holy flesh begins, and so the Sages called Esau "an apostate Israelite," except that he apostatized and became like a complete gentile. For the clarification always comes through its opposite, since in truth Edom is the one entirely lacking purity by birth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): From this side comes the hold of Esau, who "stretches out his hooves like a pig" (that is, his heel), and of whom the Sages said that he "sets up the tribunal," showing himself as righteous, for there are some light commandments among the nations. And although it is also true that "the kindness of the nations is a sin for them," since all they do is only for self-aggrandizement and to stretch out their hooves, nevertheless, from the standpoint of what is revealed in this world, it is not discernible.),
'displaying his split hooves to appear kosher, etc.' (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 65),
עַד שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לוֹמַר: "אֲנִי חָשַׂפְתִּי אֶת עֵשָׂו, גִּלֵּיתִי מִסְתָּרָיו",
until Hashem, blessed be He, had to declare: 'I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places' (Jeremiah 49:10),
דְּאַחֵר לֹא יוּכַל לְגַלּוֹת זֶה.
for no other could ever expose this.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו, נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו" (עֹבַדְיָה א, ו),
And it is stated: 'How are the things of Esau searched out, how are his hidden treasures sought out!' (Obadiah 1:6),
מַשְׁמָע דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ מַצְפּוּנִים;
implying that he harbors deep, inscrutable concealments;
וְאֵין הַכָּתוּב קוֹרֵא מַצְפּוּן מַה שֶּׁצָּפוּן לְעֵין סְתָם בְּנֵי אָדָם,
and Scripture does not title as 'hidden' that which is merely concealed from ordinary men,
רַק מַה שֶּׁצָּפוּן גַּם מִמַּלְאָכִים וּנְבִיאִים וַחֲכָמִים,
rather that which remains veiled even from angels, prophets, and sages,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מֵאָדָם עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַטְעוֹת עַצְמוֹ,
and it goes without saying from man himself, who can self-deceptively mislead his own consciousness,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת זֶה
so that it is impossible to expose this
אֶלָּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַבָּקִי בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב.
save for Hashem alone, Who is expertly versed in the innermost depths of the heart.
וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
And this is the entire power of Amalek who is termed 'first among the nations' (Numbers 24:20),

וְנֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים כה, יט): "וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר תִּמְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר215 Deuteronomy 25:19 — “You shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; you shall not forget.” Rashi: "You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" — man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, so that the name of Amalek should never again be mentioned even of a beast, to say, "This beast belonged to Amalek." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 3): Therefore the rule not to accept a convert from Amalek was not stated explicitly in the Torah; even though it says "you shall blot out," [that is no proof,] for of the Canaanites too it says "you shall not let any soul live," and nevertheless Joshua sent three proclamations. Rather, concerning this no command or warning applies, for one who cleaves so deeply to the Blessed One at the deepest beginning stands by this of himself and need not be commanded.",
and it is stated (Deuteronomy 25:19): 'And it shall be when Hashem has given you rest, etc., you shall blot out, etc.,'
דְּכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
for regarding all idolaters,
אִלּוּ לֹא הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ מֵהֶם בְּלִבּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
were there no spiritual root of them latent in the hearts of Israel,
לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם.
they would possess no independent existence in the world.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן נִיצּוּחָם:
And this is the secret of their ultimate defeat:
כַּאֲשֶׁר מְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הָרַע שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
whenever one subdues that interior power of evil within the heart,
מִמֵּילָא הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה בַּפּוֹעַל.
he automatically overpowers that physical nation in actuality.
וְכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם רַע נִגְלֶה,
All the other idolaters represent overt, recognizable evil;
וְ"הָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר" – שֶׁכְּבָר יִהְיֶה לוֹ נִיחָא מִזֶּה
and 'it shall be when He gives you rest, etc.' means when a person has achieved respite from this,
שֶׁלֹּא יְבַלְבְּלוּ שׁוּם רַע וְנִדְמֶה בְּעֵינָיו טוֹב,
such that no overt evil agitates him and he appears good in his own eyes,
אָז צָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַזֵּק נֶגֶד עֲמָלֵק
only then must he brace himself to battle Amalek,
שֶׁהוּא נִדְמֶה בְּעֵינָיו טוֹב,
who deceptively seems entirely upright in his eyes,
רַק שֶׁהוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּרַע,
whereas in truth he is the primordial root-depth of evil,
וּבִשְׁאָר הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אֵין מוּרְגָּשׁ רַע כְּלָל.
and throughout the rest of outward manifestation no evil is sensed at all.
וּבוֹ צָרִיךְ "תִּמְחֶה",
And concerning him Scripture demands 'you shall utterly blot out,'
כִּי מַה שֶּׁרַע בַּנִּגְלֶה, הַכֹּל הוּא לְצוֹרֶךְ,
because that which is overtly evil was created for a constructive purpose,
שֶׁאֵין לְךָ רָעָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שִׁימּוּשׁ לְצוֹרֶךְ גַּם כֵּן,
there being no base trait lacking a constructive application,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּבָר זֶה בַּלֵּב.
since otherwise Hashem, blessed be He, would never have created it within the human heart.
וְתַאֲוָה וְכַעַס וְכַדּוֹמֶה
Bodily desire, anger, and the like,
הַכֹּל פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ
all sometimes have legitimate sanctified utility
כְּשֶׁמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנּוֹדָע.
when one directs them according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, as is known.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִקְרֶה
In contrast, Amalek is designated as 'chance' (mikreh)
וְאֵינוֹ מֵעֶצֶם הַבְּרִיאָה,
and does not stem from the fundamental fabric of Creation;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא גַּם דָּבָר זֶה
for Hashem brought forth this phenomenon
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּבָר נִרְאֶה מִקְרֶה
merely so that there exist a reality seemingly ruled by chance,
וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִמְחוֹתוֹ לְגַמְרֵי,
and which must be eradicated completely,
כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ לֹא יִשָּׁאֵר רוֹשֶׁם לְטוֹב כְּלָל.
because from it no remnant of goodness shall ever remain.
כִּי רֵאשִׁית הַכֹּל הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the true Beginning of all existence is Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יֵשׁ חִלּוּקֵי מִדּוֹת שׁוֹנִים,
and across outward manifestation there are differing spiritual attributes;
אֲבָל הַ"רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" הוּא "עֲדֵי אֹבֵד",
but the counterfeit 'first among the nations' is doomed 'unto destruction' (Numbers 24:20),
כִּי "אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן",
for 'I am the First' (Isaiah 44:6),
וְכָל רֵאשִׁית שֶׁחוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא אֶפֶס בֶּאֱמֶת.
and any independent primacy outside of Him is absolute nothingness.

כִּי כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת "קָרוּ לֵיהּ אֱלָהָא דֶּאֱלָהָא" (מְנָחוֹת קי216 Menachot 110a — R. Abba bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav Chisda said — and some say Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: From Tyre to Carthage they recognize Israel and their Father in Heaven; but west of Tyre and east of Carthage they recognize neither Israel nor their Father in Heaven. Rav Shimi bar Chiyya raised an objection to Rav: "From the rising of the sun to its setting My name is great among the nations, and in every place offerings are presented to My name, and a pure meal offering" (Malachi 1:11). He said to him: Shimi, is it you [who asks this]? They call Him the God of gods. Rashi: "They recognize Israel" — they acknowledge them in their former honor and do not lay a heavy yoke upon them; "and their Father in Heaven" — they hold fast to the Holy One, blessed be He, and not to idolatry. "Shimi, is it you?" is said in astonishment: are you, Shimi, a great scholar, the one who raises such a difficulty against me? Some say that Rav never lifted his eyes but always kept them lowered out of modesty [and so did not know who was speaking]. Maharsha: Israel is mentioned first because it is through Israel below that His divinity and His power in the lower world became known — that He is the God of Israel and watches over the earth, which is what "their Father in Heaven" means. But west of Tyre, since they do not recognize Israel, they do not recognize their Father in Heaven as one who watches over this lowly world; they acknowledge Him only as "the God of gods," holding that He gave power and dominion below to the deities beneath Him and does not Himself watch over the lower world. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Menachos 110a): The meaning is that they recognize the Holy One, blessed be He, as the Cause and Israel as that which is caused by Him; that is why it says "Israel and their Father in Heaven." All the nations concede that Israel is the people chosen by the Holy One, blessed be He; but those at the far east and the far west, remote from the settled world, have gone out from the mean to the extreme, and therefore recognize neither the caused, which is Israel, nor the Cause, who is their Father in Heaven — for what befits Israel is the middle, the Land of Israel, which lies at the center of the world. And the answer "they call Him the God of gods" means that they call Him a great god but not the Cause of all; in that respect they do not recognize Him at all, since they have gone out entirely to the extreme. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Corresponding to "to destroy" [in Haman's decree]: that wicked one intended the removal of the Divine Presence from the lower world, which is the destruction of the Congregation of Israel — for without sheep there is no shepherd, no one on earth upon whom to unify His Name — leaving only "the God of heaven," whom they call "the God of gods," as stated at the end of Menachos. This is the essential aim of the evil of "the first of nations" [Amalek]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis 12): The fourth husk is heresy, and corresponding to it is Gog and Magog, who will gather [forces] from all seventy nations and come "against the Lord and against His anointed" — for all the nations, as the Gemara says at the end of Menachos, call Him "the God of gods." He will gather all the nations against the Lord and His anointed, and will arise at the very end, when the Messiah has already come. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Noach): The builders of the Tower wanted fear [of Heaven] to be imprinted in them by nature, so that they would not need [the labor of] service — the opposite of the Temple, where all Israel united and crowned the Lord. This is the matter of the Gemara's statement that they call Him "the God of gods": that they would not need to fear, since nature itself would take on the power of fear; and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed them that a unity contrary to His will cannot endure. Tiferes Yosef (Sukkos 7): From the Blessed One's side even those who transgress His will uphold His glory, as it is written, "From the rising of the sun to its setting My name is great among the nations"; the difference, however, is as the Talmud says, that they call Him "the God of gods." That is, the nations hold that it is not His way to watch over the lower world, so they set up a deity for themselves and worship the cause that seems to them to bestow good on them — and when the good stops they turn insolent and say, "There is no judgment and no Judge"; whereas Israel serve the Blessed One constantly, at every moment..),
For all other nations 'call Him the God of gods' (Menachot 110a),
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַתּוֹלִים בַּמִּקְרֶה וְ"לֵית דִּין וְכוּלֵי".
unlike those who ascribe reality to chance, claiming 'there is neither justice nor Judge, etc.'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה כֻּלּוֹ רַע
And just as within Israel that which appears entirely evil
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֻּלּוֹ טוֹב,
is in internal truth entirely good,
כִּי הֵם מְהַפְּכִין חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא,
for they transmute darkness into radiant light;
כָּךְ בָּאוּמּוֹת הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ:
so too among the nations it is the reverse:
מִי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כֻּלּוֹ טוֹב
he who appears outwardly entirely virtuous
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֻּלּוֹ רַע,
is in internal truth entirely evil,
וְאֵין בּוֹ הַשְׁאָרָה לְטוֹב כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
and contains no lingering trace of goodness whatsoever.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And the subtle root of Amalek within the heart
הַיְינוּ הֶעְדֵּר הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח,
is precisely the absence of immediate perception of the divine Presence,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא217 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 11 — R. Levi said in the name of R. Acha b. R. Chanina: So long as the seed of Amalek exists in the world, neither is the Name complete nor is the Throne complete. Once the seed of Amalek has perished, the Name is complete and the Throne is complete. What is the reason? "The enemy is finished, ruins forever." And what is written after it? "But the Lord sits enthroned forever; He has established His throne for judgment" — behold, the Name is complete and the Throne is complete. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 79): That [Jacob and the angel] raised dust up to the Throne of Glory alludes to "the Throne is not complete until the seed of Amalek is blotted out": the throne alludes to fear [of Heaven], through which desire is conquered, and as a throne is the king's seat, nothing can hold the "sitting" of the Blessed One — that is, apprehend His reality — except the conquest of the desires, for desire is a screen that keeps one from apprehending the spiritual. So when the Throne is complete, Amalek is blotted out and the power of Esau is nullified; and "the Name is not complete" is stated first, alluding to the Torah, which is entirely names of the Holy One, blessed be He. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): So long as the evil inclination is in the world, all influences from above must also come in modesty and concealment because of the accusers, and this is why "the Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete." The first two letters of the Name are the hidden things, the concealed unity that is not revealed — hence "This is My name l'olam" is written [to conceal] — for so long as the seed of Amalek, the root of evil in the world, exists, the attachment of the Congregation of Israel to their Father in Heaven cannot be revealed, since he always finds claims and accusation; and "the Throne is not complete" because "the Master (Aluf) of the world" [the letter alef] is hidden and concealed — the hidden light. Sod Yesharim (Rosh Hashanah 1): As a flame has no hold or existence without its bond to the coal, so the Blessed One, as it were, established that His will should have no completeness without Israel, since only through their service is His will completed — as the Sages said, "the Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete." That is, there will be no completeness without the service of Israel within the boundaries of this world.):
as written (Midrash Tanchuma, end of Parashat Ki Teitzei):
"אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְאֵין הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם עַד וְכוּלֵי".
"'Neither the Name is whole nor the Throne whole until Amalek is eradicated.'"

וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַשֵּׁם הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים נ218 Pesachim 50a — R. Avina raised a contradiction: It is written, "This is My name forever," and it is written, "and this is My memorial for all generations." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am not read as I am written. I am written with yod-heh, and I am read with alef-dalet. Rashi: It is written "This is My name le'alem" — in concealment — and it is written "This is My memorial," which implies reading aloud and not concealment. Alternatively: once it says "This is My name," it is obvious that "this is My memorial" — how else would He be called but by His name? "I am not read as I am written": [the verse] taught two names, the name of writing and the name of reading. Maharsha: "His name one" means the Unique Name, [used] in the World to Come in writing and in reading alike; the rest, he says, is explained in chapter Asarah Yuchasin. There (Kiddushin 71a) he explains that in this world the attribute of judgment rules in partnership with mercy, as at creation, so the Name is written as the name of mercy and read as the name of judgment — Adonai, a "remembrance," which denotes judgment; but the World to Come is entirely mercy, and then the Name will be complete, read as it is written. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 42): He, blessed be He, is ever One in Himself; the difference lies with the recipients, for this world is not conducted according to the truth of His name. The writing of the Name indicates the truth of His essence, while the reading is directed toward man; in this world, where man is physical and material and a screen separates him from God, He is read as Adonai, "Master," for He stands to His world as a master to a servant, who is separate from him. But in the World to Come, when man will be at the level of the angels, removed from physicality, and He will stand joined and connected to His world as a son is joined to his father, He will be written and read alike with the Unique Name. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 15): [Explaining why one who pronounces the Name with its letters has no share in the World to Come:] It is fitting to conceal this Name, the Unique Name, as the Sages expounded "This is My name le'olam" — le'alem ["to conceal"] is written — for the Unique Name has a hidden and concealed level. One who pronounces the Name with its letters departs from that hidden and concealed level, and so has no share in the World to Come, which is itself of a hidden and concealed level. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 2): Because in this world [the glory of Heaven] is not yet acquired in the heart, "in this world I am not read as I am written," and every blessing opens in direct address, "Blessed are You," and then turns to the hidden. The Name Havayah denotes true presence, as a son speaks face to face with his father, while Adonai, "Master of all," is hidden, as a servant is abashed to look at his master's face; when [this recognition] is acquired in the heart, with the complete redemption, He will be called by Havayah as well, but in this world that level is possible only "in writing" — potentially, not in actuality — so in practice one must stand in solemnity, like a servant before his master. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 9): The Name Havayah signifies "He was, is and will be" — One and unique even now, as before the world was created — and this is "This is My name forever": in this world it is not read as it is written. In writing, that is, in thought, [the unity] is revealed in this world too, for Israel arose in [God's] thought, where the unity is, and Israel can sense it in thought; but not in reading and speech, which reveal the world of action, where what appears are separate things. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): As regards this world, "This is My name l'olam" is written [defectively, to conceal], so that it is not read as it is written: the Name Havayah, which signifies the union of all the hidden powers with the revealed ones, all for the Lord alone, is concealed in this world, and though Scripture states explicitly that this is the truth, it is [held] by way of faith and concealment. In the future it will become clear that "Your people are all righteous" even in actual deed — that all our deeds too were for the sake of Heaven — and then it will be read as it is written; but in this world it is not read aloud as something clarified. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chukas 7): In Nishmas, "shall bless Your name, O Lord our God" follows what the Sages said: "This is My name forever" — I am written with yod-heh, that is, the Name Havayah. And "shall glorify and exalt Your remembrance" follows the same Gemara: "This is My remembrance for all generations" — I am read as Adonai, which is the last attribute, Malchus. Beis Yaakov (Vayeira 22): In this world a person must go by way of the Oral Torah, recognizing the glory of Heaven through his own self-restraint. This is the meaning of the Talmud's "Not as I am written am I read": the writing is the Name Havayah and the reading is Adonai, because a person needs fear and clarifications. Sod Yesharim (Night of Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 9): "On that day the Lord shall be One and His name One": seemingly it should have said "the Lord and His name shall be one," since His name pertains to the service of creation; but it is as the Gemara says: "Not as I am written am I read — I am written yod-heh and read alef-dalet, and in the World to Come I am read as I am written." In this world His being written yod-heh indicates that no thought can grasp Him at all, and when a person constrains himself to submit to this and accepts His mastery and lordship upon himself, that is His being read as Adonai; and "on that day," when the Blessed One reveals His great light, the lordship Israel accepted in this world will be their protection, for His name signifies Israel's service, through which they will never be nullified..):
And the wholeness of the Name is as written in Pesachim (50a):
"לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא",
"'Not as I am written am I pronounced,'
בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין בְּלִיטָה זוֹ לָעַיִן לְגַמְרֵי
for in this world this truth is not manifestly prominent to the eye,
אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה הוֹוֶה וְיִהְיֶה וּמְהַוֶּוה הַכֹּל
as to how Hashem, blessed be He, was, is, will be, and continuously animates all,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הוֹרָאַת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה.
which is the precise meaning of the Tetragrammaton (Havayah).
וְהַכִּסֵּא הוּא הַהַשְׁגָּחָה,
And the Throne (Kissei) embodies divine providence,
שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב כְּמֶלֶךְ עַל כִּסֵּא וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה.
enthroned as King upon a seat of judgment Whose sovereignty rules over all.
"וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר" –
And 'it shall be when He gives you rest, etc.' teaches:
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים אֲחֵרִים, תַּאֲווֹת וְכַעַס וְכַדּוֹמֶה הַמַּסְתִּירִים זֶה,
that initially there exist other distractions—passions, anger, and the like—which obscure this;
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ נָקִי
yet even when a person's heart has been cleansed
וַעֲדַיִן אֵין הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח מְאִירָה לוֹ
and nonetheless the conscious awareness of the Presence does not radiate within him,
לִהְיוֹת מַמָּשׁ תָּדִיר כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל
to stand continuously as one situated before an awesome King,
וּמוּרְגָּשׁ לָעַיִן בְּכָל דָּבָר אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיג וּבוֹרֵא וְאֵין בִּלְתּוֹ –
where it is vividly felt in every detail how Hashem directs, creates, and there is none beside Him—
זֶהוּ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק
this subtle void stems from the root of Amalek,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִמְחוֹת בַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב:
which one must eradicate through interior service of the heart:
"וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת יז, יא).
'And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed, etc.' (Exodus 17:11).
וְהוּא קוֹדֶם הַכְנָסַת כָּל דָּבָר קְדוּשָּׁה גְּמוּרָה:
And this eradication must precede the entry of any manifestation of complete holiness:
קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
prior to the Giving of the Torah (at Rephidim),
וְקוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן –
and prior to the construction of the First Temple—
מִיָּד בִּמְלוּכַת שָׁאוּל הָיָה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת
for right at the coronation of Saul there arose an awakening to build the Temple,
וְהֻוצְרַךְ מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק קוֹדֶם עַל יְדֵי שָׁאוּל וְדָוִד.
and the blotting out of Amalek had to occur first through Saul and David.
וְכֵן קוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי –
And so too prior to the building of the Second Temple—
מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק דְּהָמָן.
there occurred the downfall of the Amalekite Haman.
וְכֵן יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
And so shall it unfold in the ultimate future
קוֹדֶם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי
prior to the building of the Third Temple,
שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן.
which shall be built speedily in our days, Amen.

sections.en: Exile of the Shechinah and the Beginning of Redemption

items.h: The Shechinah accompanies Israel even in distance; recognizing that hidden presence marks the first movement from exile toward final redemption.

Seif 1 — The Shechinah within Exile
Recognizing that the Shechinah accompanies Israel in exile becomes itself the beginning of redemption.

p: עִנְיַן גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה,
The matter of the exile of the Shechinah,
פֵּירוּשׁ שְׁכִינָה הוּא מִדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
meaning: Shechinah is the divine attribute of Hashem, blessed be He, wherein He dwells within the hearts of the children of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹךְ [בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל] וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written: "And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, etc.,"
"אֲנִי ה' שֹׁכֵן וְגוֹמֵר",
"'I am Hashem Who dwells, etc.,'"
וְהוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
and this corresponds to the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty),
כְּטַעַם: "וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה",
in the spirit of: "And His kingdom rules over all,"
פֵּירוּשׁ "בַּכֹּל" – הַיְינוּ גַּם מַה שֶּׁהוּא מֶרְחָק רַב
meaning 'over all'—including even that which stands at a vast spiritual distance

"וּבְתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" (יוֹמָא נו219 Yoma 56b — The Sages taught: "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity" — even at a time when they are impure, the Divine Presence is with them. Maharsha (Yoma 57a, s.v. "now you are certainly impure"): [The Sadducee] meant: even if you were once pure, now in exile you have certainly become impure, as it is written, "Her impurity is in her skirts," and He separates Himself from you as one keeps apart from the impurity of a menstruant. [R. Chanina] answered him from what is written of them, "that dwells with them [in the midst of their impurity]," that He does not separate entirely, but as a man keeps apart from his wife while she is a menstruant yet lives with her in one house; so the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells with us even now in exile, as it is said, "I will be with him in distress." Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 4): The Blessed One does not dwell in the midst of their impurity unless the sin was unwitting, and of that it is written, "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity." [Hence the First Temple, whose distinction was that the Divine Presence rested in it,] was destroyed when they defiled the Sanctuary through idolatry, sexual immorality and bloodshed, the three sins that are called impurity. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1): The Divine Presence does not depart even toward evening, in the time of darkness, as it is likewise said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity." For the souls of all Israel are bound and linked together as in a chain, so that the revelation of the Divine light — in concealment, hiddenness and great contraction — is not absent from the heart of any Jew; even the lowest of the low has in him a portion of life, a portion of God from above. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Regarding spiritual holiness it is said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity," and "the Divine Presence never departed from the Western Wall": in concealment it never departed, even in every kind of sinking into evil bitterer than death — "I will fear no evil, for You are with me." We suppose this a deficiency, but in truth it is the strength of completeness and the ultimate clarification: that wherever a person sinks, his heart remains bound to the Blessed One with a bond that cannot be severed. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The Holy One, blessed be He, as it were entered Egypt, the place of impurity, and this was the great miracle and the first of the miracles: the clarification of "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity," from their beginning and root in the Patriarchs, who are truly holy seed with no connection to any impurity, so that it was revealed that impurity has no real existence. Esther is the end: even in the lowest levels, where the nations hold sway, the Blessed One is with them, even in the place of impurity's greatest strength, as when Esther entered the house of Ahasuerus. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Raising the holy sparks out of the matters of this world, by engaging in them for the sake of Heaven, is like a king's son returning from captivity, whose joy exceeds that of one who was always in the palace; of this it is said, "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity" — amid it precisely. Over this that wicked one [Bilaam] was blinded when he spoke of "the fourth of Israel" and said "He who is holy…," for he did not know that there is holiness even in bodily matters. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): So too the souls of Israel outside the Land are like the Tabernacle [dismantled in order to be rebuilt], for the Blessed One dwells with them amid their impurity and His Presence is within the hearts of Israel: wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went into exile with them, and that place became their place. Through the exile they gather in the bit of good among the nations and return it all to holiness, and that place too becomes sanctified with the holiness of the air of the Land of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Even when sin caused Israel to be exiled among the nations, outside even the holiness of the Land, wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went with them — for even "in the lands of their enemies I have not rejected them," and "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity." Nonetheless they are never separated from the root of holiness, and in the end all will be redeemed, even those wholly assimilated among the nations.:),
and 'in the midst of their uncleanness' (Yoma 56b),
אֲפִילּוּ בְּלֵב הַמְשׁוּקָּע מִכָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת וְזוּהֲמָא
even within a heart deeply immersed in all manner of lusts and contamination,
שֶׁהֵם הַנִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב טֻמְאָה,
which are designated in biblical terminology as impurity;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם "חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ",
nonetheless, 'Hashem's portion is His people,'
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא,
and 'even though he has sinned, he remains Israel,'
שָׁרְשׁוֹ דָּבוּק הוּא בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
his essential root remaining bound to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְקָדוֹשׁ שָׁרוּי בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָיו
and the Holy One rests deep within his innermost being
וּבְמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם.
and within the hidden recesses of his heart.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁרָצָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא –
And this is the primary dwelling of the Shechinah in lower realms that the Holy One desired—
הַיְינוּ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
namely, within the hearts of the children of Israel.
אֲבָל בַּגָּלוּת נֶאֱמַר: "לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד ה'",
However, regarding the exile it is stated: 'The king's heart is in the hand of Hashem,' (Proverbs 21:1),
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּחִירָה, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיגָם.
for pagan kings possess no free will, rather Hashem, blessed be He, directs them.
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבָּם לְהַנְהִיג,
Yet it is not said that Hashem dwells within their heart to guide them,
דְּזֶה לֹא נִקְרָא שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הַלֵּב כְּלָל;
for this is not considered being within the heart at all;
וְגַם בַּגָּלוּת אֵין שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and even in exile His divine presence dwells solely within the hearts of the Jewish people,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב, ט220 Shemot Rabbah 2:2 — R. Elazar says: The Shechinah has not departed from within the Sanctuary, as it says, "And My eyes and My heart shall be there," etc. (II Chronicles 7:16). … Rav Acha said: The Shechinah never departs from the Western Wall, as it says, "Behold, He stands behind our wall" (Song of Songs 2:9). [Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:9, named in the text, says on this verse only that the Western Wall will never be destroyed.] Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1): "The Divine Presence never departed from the Western Wall": it is the wall where the light sets — that is, at the wall near sunset, toward evening and the time of darkness, the Divine Presence does not depart. For the souls of all Israel are bound together as in a chain, so that the revelation of the Divine light, in concealment and great contraction, is not absent from the heart of any Jew, even the lowest of the low. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): "The Divine Presence never departed from the Western Wall": the west is called the "back," as in "you shall see My back" — seeing the face was in the Temple, at the time of full revelation, but "from the Western Wall," that is, in concealment, it never departed, even in all the concealments. We suppose this a deficiency, but in truth it is the strength of completeness: that wherever a person sinks, his heart remains bound to the Blessed One with a bond that cannot be severed.):
and as they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:9):
"מֵעוֹלָם לֹא זָזָה שְׁכִינָה וְכוּלֵי".
"'Never did the Shechinah depart from the Western Wall, etc.'"
רַק אֶצְלָם הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ,
Except that with foreign monarchs it is the reverse:
דִּלְבָבָם בְּיָדוֹ,
for their heart is in His hand,
שֶׁאֵין לִבָּם גַּם כֵּן תּוֹךְ לִבָּם,
meaning that even their own heart does not belong to them,
דְּאֵין לִבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָם לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנָם,
their heart not being in their own control to act as they wish,
רַק כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather exclusively according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל, רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם מַה שֶּׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹנָם נִקְרָא בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנָם,
Whereas with Israel, Hashem's will—even that which seems contrary to their outward desire—is fundamentally their true inner will,

כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין221 Mishneh Torah, Divorce 2:20 — One whom the law obligates to divorce his wife and who refuses to divorce — a Jewish court, in every place and at every time, beats him until he says "I consent," and he writes the bill of divorce, and it is valid. We call a man coerced only when he is pressed and forced to do something the Torah does not obligate him to do. But this man, who does not wish to divorce — since he wishes to be of Israel, and wishes to perform all the commandments and to keep far from transgressions, and it is his impulse that has overpowered him, once he has been beaten until his impulse weakened and he said "I consent," he has already divorced of his own will. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 21): This follows the Rambam's reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing'": in the depths of the heart everyone wishes to heed the words of the Sages and only the leaven in the dough holds him back, so once he has been beaten and his inclination has weakened until he also says with his mouth, "I am willing," it suffices. So too, intention not for the sake of Heaven in a Jew comes only from the inclination, which accustoms him to seek his own benefit in everything, whereas the depths of the heart of the children of Israel are solely for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): That the name Israel can never be uprooted from a Jew seems to take away his free choice; this is the mountain held over them at Sinai, that he will be Israel against his will. But when they accepted [the Torah] again in the days of Ahasuerus it was clarified that this is not coercion, for at his root he truly chooses the Blessed One of his own will; as the Rambam wrote on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" even if he is wicked and unwilling to accept the words of the Sages, his true will is not so. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): "All Israel have a share in the World to Come" includes even the wicked of Israel, for all are called righteous, just as all Israel are called circumcised even one who is in fact uncircumcised. One who is wicked in deed is so only because of the evil inclination and not from his heart, as it says, "It is revealed and known before You that our will [is to do Your will]," and as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing.'" Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 3): There was a "great protest" against the Torah [since it was accepted under coercion] until they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus, when the Blessed One clarified that the point of the heart is truly good; consequently there is no "great protest," as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing'": since in truth he wants it, it is not called duress, and so they were already acquired as a people and for eternal life. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Even the wicked and the sinners of Israel have this: although they sin through the incitement of the inclination, the leaven in the dough, in their true will there is this point, that they can abandon all the desires of this world for the will of the Blessed One. That is why "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing'" is effective, as is known from the Rambam's reason; and this is an inheritance from our father Isaac. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): Therefore, although he has sinned, he is still Israel in every respect, for all of it comes only from the leaven in the dough and not from the truth of the point of the heart, as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing,'" which holds even for one who apostatizes from the whole Torah out of spite. This stems from the root of Jewish holiness that was fixed as a lasting acquisition in the heart of all Israel at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from a Jew however many his sins: even when he multiplies sins, it all comes from the leaven in the dough and the subjugation of the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness, as it says, "It is revealed and known before You that our will...," and similarly in the Rambam on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing.'" Therefore [the Sages] compared [the sinner of Israel] to a myrtle standing among reeds: the sins are only in the reeds surrounding the myrtle, while the myrtle itself has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): As is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" what in the heart is unwilling is so only because of the evil inclination. On this it says, "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable [ratzon]," and I received the interpretation that even when one sees that his heart's will is not yet in it, speaking good with the mouth, which is called "the lips of the righteous," helps to teach and to draw the will into the heart as well. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Mishlei 10): "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable [ratzon]": as the Sages said, "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" that is, through his speech he brings the will into his heart as well. What he says with his lips while his heart is not yet clarified helps him to clarify his heart toward the will wholeheartedly: for instance, when anger at his fellow sprouts in his heart, his counsel is first to speak kindly to his fellow even if not wholeheartedly, and by this he gradually brings love into his heart in place of hatred. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 57): When a person shortchanges himself in divine service, this is "the buyer was defrauded," and a buyer defrauded by less than a sixth is like what the Talmud says, "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing'": in truth the depth of the heart of Israel is drawn after the will of the Blessed One, but on the outer garment there are impediments that keep him from serving God, and he is shortchanged by them. Yet this is only less than a sixth, which is wholly waived [and the sale stands].)
as known from the words of Maimonides (end of chapter 2 of the Laws of Divorce)
בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אָנִי".
regarding the rationale for 'they compel him until he says: I am willing.'

וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן טַעַם דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה222 Rosh Hashanah 4a — One who says, “This coin is for charity so that my son may live,” or “so that I may merit the World to Come” — such a man is a wholly righteous person. This applies to Israel; but of a gentile who makes such a condition, since he regrets it afterwards, it is not so. Rashi: "With respect" [literally, "from your burden"]: from the very text with which you came against us to refute us I give you an answer — see what is written in it: "that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons"; you learn that he did it not for the sake of Heaven but for his own benefit. "Such a man is wholly righteous": if he is accustomed to this. "Here, of an Israelite": whose heart is directed to Heaven, and if it goes ill with him in his life he does not complain but ascribes the suffering to his sin; but a gentile, if he is not repaid in kind, complains. Tosafos (s.v. "so that my sons may live"): And what we learned in the first chapter of Avos, "Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward", refers to the nations of the world, who come to regret their earlier [good deeds]. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "so that my sons may live"): The reading [in Tosafot] should be "like the nations of the world", as in Tosafot Yeshanim; for it is unreasonable that the Mishnah [in Avos] speaks only of the nations of the world, since Tzadok and Baitus, who erred in [Antigonos's] words, were Israelites. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 4a): This does not contradict "Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward" (Avos 1:3), which speaks of one who performs a commandment for the sake of the reward of that very commandment, so that the aim of his service is not the Blessed One but himself; this man performs the commandment as it should be, out of love of the Blessed One, only that the aim of his love is that it should go well with him — and since in the end he loves the Blessed One and serves Him as is fitting, he is wholly righteous. As for the distinction between Israel and a gentile: the very being and rank of Israel is righteousness and goodness, so that an Israelite who performs a commandment for his own benefit is wholly righteous, for "righteous" means only one who is drawn along the path of uprightness (to look to nothing but love of the Blessed One is the rank of the pious man, not a condition of the righteous); but the nations are not in their essence of the rank of righteousness, so a gentile is righteous only when his whole intention is for the sake of Heaven. (ד.)
And this is likewise the underlying reason for the words of our Sages at the beginning of the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (4a)
הַחִלּוּק בְּעִנְיַן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְעַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
regarding the distinction in serving not for its own sake and on condition of receiving reward between Israel and idolaters, see there;
דִּבְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת הֵיפֶךְ רְצוֹנָם הָאֲמִיתִּי
for among idolaters, the will of Hashem is genuinely the opposite of their authentic desire,
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which is entirely contrary to the will of Hashem.
רַק דְּהַמְּלָכִים אֵין לִבָּם בִּרְשׁוּתָם,
Only that the monarchs have no dominion over their hearts,
רַק בְּיָדוֹ וּרְשׁוּתוֹ וְכֹחוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which are kept strictly in the hand, domain, and power of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גָּלוּת,
And this condition constitutes exile,
שֶׁגָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לִפְלַטְרִין שֶׁל מְלָכִים מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
wherein His divine presence is exiled into the palaces of pagan kings,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה טו223 Shemot Rabbah 15:5 — R. Shimon said: Great is the love borne to Israel, that the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself in a place of idolatry, in a place of filth, and in a place of impurity, in order to redeem them. A parable: a priest whose teruma fell into a cemetery. He says: What shall I do? To defile myself is impossible; to abandon my teruma is impossible. Better that I defile myself once and then purify myself again, than that I lose my teruma. So too our fathers were the teruma of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "Israel is holy to the Lord" (Jeremiah 2:3); and they were among the graves, as it is said, "for there was no house where there was not one dead" (Exodus 12:30). The Holy One, blessed be He, said: How shall I redeem them? To abandon them is impossible; better that I go down and rescue them. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The whole force of the miracle of Egypt is that they had sunk deeply there, and He entered Egypt, as it were, a place of impurity, as the Sages said, "a parable of a priest: even a thousand impurities I will enter." This was a great miracle and the first of all miracles, the clarification of "I am the Lord who dwells with them in the midst of their impurity," by virtue of their beginning and root in the Patriarchs, who are truly holy seed with no connection to any impurity at all.)
along the lines of what they said in Shemot Rabbah (Parashah 15)
הַמָּשָׁל: "אֲפִילּוּ אֶלֶף טֻמְאוֹת אֲנִי נִכְנָס וְכוּלֵי"
the parable: "Even into a thousand impurities I enter, etc."
עַל פָּסוּק "וְעָבַרְתִּי אֲנִי ה'".
on the verse 'And I, Hashem, will pass through' (Exodus 12:12).
דְּזֶה שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לְהִטָּפֵל בְּלִבּוֹת מְלָכִים דְּאוּמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
For having to occupy Himself with the hearts of pagan kings,
זֶה אֵין דּוֹמֶה כְּלָל לְ"תוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
is completely incomparable to being 'in the midst of the impurities' of the children of Israel;
דְּזוֹ טֻמְאָה קַלָּה לְפִי שָׁעָה
for Israel's is a temporary, light impurity
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ טָהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל ה',
which possesses purification in Hashem, the ritual pool (mikveh) of Israel,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא פה224 Yoma 85b — R. Akiva said: Happy are you, Israel! Before whom are you purified, and who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven, as it is stated, "And I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be pure." And it says, "The Lord is the ritual bath of Israel" — just as a ritual bath purifies the impure, so does the Holy One, blessed be He, purify Israel. Maharsha: Israel in their sins are like those defiled by the dead, who need both sprinkling and immersion: "I will sprinkle pure water upon you" is the sprinkling of the purification waters, and "the ritual bath" is the immersion, so that they attain complete purity when the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives all their sins. The evil inclination is called impure and entices a person toward the impurity of death, so its impurity requires purification of both body and soul; and as sprinkling is done by the pure upon the impure, through another, while immersion one performs oneself before the Pure, so "I will sprinkle" — from the Pure One, the Holy One, blessed be He, upon the impure — purifies the soul, while "and you shall be pure" refers to the impurity of the body. Hence "before whom are you purified" refers to the impurity of the body, and "who purifies you" to that of the soul. Maharal (Derush l'Shabbos Shuvah): R. Akiva explains why Yom Kippur atones only for sins between man and God: "before whom are you purified" — Israel are purified on Yom Kippur because they cleave to Him, as it is written, "But you who cleave to the Lord your God," and there is no higher rank than this; and "who purifies you" — their very cleaving to Him, to whom sin has no relation, removes sin from them. Hence "just as a ritual bath purifies the impure": the ritual bath, to which impurity has no relation, purifies the impure person who cleaves to it wholly without any interposition, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies Israel, who cleave to Him wholly without interposition or separation. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 56): In respect of their true essence Israel belong to God, and in that respect their sin is removed entirely, for He, blessed be He, is a ritual bath of purity from whom there is no separation, and so He purifies Israel, who cleave to Him. A ritual bath [מקוה] is so called because the waters are gathered [נקוים] into it; and to Him, blessed be He, all existence is gathered, so He purifies all that is gathered to Him — and Israel in particular are gathered to Him, therefore He purifies them.:):
as they said (Yoma 85b):
"מִי מְטַהֵרְכֶם? אֲבִיכֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם",
"Who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven,"
כַּאֲשֶׁר דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשָׁם,
for when they cleave unto Him Who is their root,
הֲרֵי זֶה כְּמוֹ הַשָּׁקָה לְמַעְיָין
it is like contact (hashakah) with a flowing natural spring,
דְּמוֹעִיל לְטַהֵר מַיִם טְמֵאִים.
which is halakhically effective to purify contaminated waters.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן טֻמְאַת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הִיא אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה,
In contrast, the impurity of idolaters is the ultimate progenitor of uncleanness (avi avot hatumah),
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם מַדְרֵגוֹת:
and among them are distinct levels:
טֻמְאַת עֲמָלֵק הִיא אֲבִי טֻמְאָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ טָהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶוה כְּלָל,
the impurity of Amalek is a degree of uncleanness that has no purification in a mikveh at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תִּמְחֶה";
as it is written: 'You shall blot out';
וּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת הוּא מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהֲשִׁיבָם לַמַּעְיָין כְּלָל,
and other nations are of a nature that they cannot be restored to the spring at all,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם דְּבֵיקוּת וְהַשָּׁקָה לַמַּעְיָין;
since they possess no inherent connection or confluence with the spring;
רַק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר: "יִשָּׁקֵנִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיהוּ",
only regarding Israel is it stated: 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth' (Song of Songs 1:2),
זֶהוּ הַהַשָּׁקָה לַמַּעְיָין
this being the mystic kiss/confluence (hashakah) to the spring

(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה225 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:5 — Another interpretation: "Let Him kiss me [yishakeni] with the kisses of His mouth" — let Him arm me, let Him purify me, let Him join me to Himself. Another interpretation: "Let Him kiss me with the kisses of His mouth" — let Him purify me, like a man who brings two cisterns into contact with one another and thereby joins them, as it is said, "as the joining of pools [k'mashak gevim]" (Isaiah 33:4). Another interpretation: "Yishakeni" — let Him make me cleave to Him, as it is said, "and the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching [mashikot] one another" (Ezekiel 3:13).).
(and as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah).
וּלְכָךְ, שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם
Therefore, Hashem's dwelling amidst the children of Israel even in the midst of their impurities
אֵינוֹ קָרוּי גָּלוּת כְּאִישׁ נוֹדֵד מִמְּקוֹמוֹ;
is not termed exile in the sense of a man wanderer from his home;
דְּהַגַּם דִּמְקוֹמוֹ מְקוֹם טָהֳרָה "כְּעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר",
for even though His pristine place is pure 'like the very heavens for clearness,'
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
unlike the coarse physical lower world,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִיָּד שֶׁהַלְּבָבוֹת נִדְבָּקִים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
nevertheless the moment Jewish hearts cleave to Hashem, blessed be He,
שָׁבִים גַּם הֵם לִמְקוֹם טָהֳרָה.
they too immediately return to a place of purity.
וְזֶהוּ "טֻמְאֹתָם" דַּיְיקָא –
And this is why Scripture precisely says 'their impurities'—
אֶצְלָם מִצִּידָּם נִקְרָא טֻמְאָה,
meaning from their human perspective it is termed impurity,
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר סְתָם "בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאָה",
yet Scripture does not say generically 'in the midst of impurity,'
דְּמִיָּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן אֵין כָּאן טֻמְאָה.
for the moment Hashem dwells, impurity ceases to exist.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמו226 Shabbat 146a — When the serpent came upon Eve, he injected a contamination into her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai — their contamination ceased; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai — their contamination did not cease. Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi: And what of converts? He said to him: Even though they themselves were not there, their guardian angels were there, as it is written, "with him who stands here with us this day before the Lord our God, and with him who is not here with us this day." Rashi: "When the serpent came upon Eve": when he counseled her to eat from the tree, he came upon her, as it is written, "The serpent beguiled me (השיאני)" — a term of marriage (נשואין). "What of converts": who were not at Mount Sinai — from where did their contamination cease? "Their mazal was there": at Sinai; and all who stood at Mount Sinai were sanctified, purified and healed of every blemish, even the blind and the lame among Israel, as taught in the Sifrei. Maharsha: All the generations yet to come were included in "him who is not here with us this day" (as stated in Shevuot 39a); but of Israel one can say that although their bodies were not there, their souls, bound up in the bond of life, were present, whereas of converts this cannot be said — only that their mazal was there. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 146a): As explained on Sotah 9a, the serpent came upon Eve because he wished to kill Adam and marry Eve; he truly joined himself to her, and through that improper union he cast filth and abomination into her. Because Eve had a union with the serpent, the contamination passed from it to her, so that all the nations bear contamination on account of that union; but Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, were freed of it, for against Eve's union with the serpent stands Israel's union with the Holy One, blessed be He, and this ended the contamination that came of joining with the serpent. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 17): Although the law follows R. Yehudah ben Beseira that words of Torah do not contract impurity, that is only after the giving of the Torah, when "their filth ceased": the root of the impurity of lust, which came through the serpent's coming upon Eve and is therefore found more in women, is not severed by the Torah as a "spice" but ceased through the Torah entirely. Therefore converts too need immersion before accepting the Torah: although their guardian angel stood at Mount Sinai and their filth too ceased thereby, it does not leave the convert at his birth, and while a gentile he is like all the filth-laden nations; only when he converts does it cease, through his acceptance of the Torah, as it did for all Israel at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 1): The main thing is to repair the flaw of the serpent, which began with his enticement through eating, after which he cast filth into Eve, and the filth clung to her offspring. At the giving of the Torah Israel's filth ceased, and they then repaired the whole flaw of the serpent, as it says, "I said, you are gods," for they would not have died; presumably the entire flaw of the serpent that brought death was then repaired..):
And along the lines of what they stated (Shabbat 146a):
"בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן",
"At the time of the Giving of the Torah their defilement ceased,"
וְהוּא לְעוֹלָם בִּמְקוֹם טָהֳרָתוֹ.
and He remains eternally in His place of purity.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַטִּפּוּל בְּלֵב מְלָכִים וְשָׂרִים
In contrast, occupying Himself with the heart of gentile kings and ministers
הוּא נִקְרָא נְדִידָה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, מְקוֹם טָהֳרָה וּנְקִיּוּת מִתַּאֲווֹת וְכָל טִנּוּפֶת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
is termed wandering from His place of purity and detachment from the lusts and filth of this world,
וְלִבָּם מָלֵא בֶּאֱמֶת מִכָּל מִינֵי טֻמְאָה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל –
since their heart is genuinely full of every kind of irremediable impurity as mentioned above—
זֶה נִקְרָא גָּלוּת.
this is what is truly called exile.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֵּירְשׁוּ זֶה הַסּוֹד
And our Sages of blessed memory explained this mystical secret

בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א וְאֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג, י; מִדְרָשׁ אַבָּא גּוּרְיוֹן א, טו227 Esther Rabbah 3:10 — R. Yudan and R. Levi in the name of R. Yochanan: Wherever it is said in this scroll "to King Ahasuerus," Scripture speaks of King Ahasuerus; and wherever it says simply "to the king," it serves both the sacred and the profane. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): The Sages said that wherever "the king" appears without qualification it speaks of the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, by virtue of His clothing Himself in Ahasuerus to bestow [His bounty]. This is the reason for Mordechai's intention to save him from Bigsan and Teresh: even in the height of the darkness he understood the purpose of all that was happening, that Esther's being taken by Ahasuerus was no accident, and that everything was truly by the providence of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 6): The Sages said, "No one knew how to slander like Haman," and the Midrash says that every unqualified "king" speaks of the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He; if so, all his words, "it is not worthwhile for the king to tolerate them" and "I will weigh out into the king's treasuries," were directed on high. He first accused them of their sins, [claiming] that they had already entirely corrupted the whole stature of man. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 2): "No one knew how to slander like Haman" refers not to his slandering and disparaging Israel before Ahasuerus but to his accusing Israel before the Blessed One, saying, "and they do not keep the king's laws," for wherever the Megillah says "the king" without qualification, Scripture speaks of the King of the kings of kings. His accusation concerned Daniel's decree against their bread, wine and daughters: Haman judged that it was not from the law and command of the King, the Holy One, blessed be He, and claimed they did it only out of haughtiness. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): Through Esther's feast Mordechai attained the holiness of the World to Come, going out "in royal apparel," for even in his garment he cleaved wholly to the kingdom of Heaven: every unqualified "king" in Esther speaks of the King of the kings of kings, as they said in the Midrash, and likewise unqualified "royalty," as they said in the Megillah on "And Esther clothed herself in royalty," that the holy spirit clothed her, that is, the kingdom of Heaven.):
in what they taught (Zohar III 109a; Esther Rabbah 3:10; Midrash Abba Gurion 1:15):
"כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר 'הַמֶּלֶךְ' סְתָם בִּמְגִילַּת אֶסְתֵּר – בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר".
"Wherever 'the king' is stated without qualification in the Scroll of Esther, Scripture speaks of the King of kings."
כִּי בְּכָל הַמְּגִילָּה לֹא נִזְכַּר שׁוּם שֵׁם מִשְּׁמוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
For throughout the entire Megillah not a single one of the holy Names of God is explicitly mentioned,

הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה228 Megillah 14a — Why is Hallel not recited on Purim? … R. Nachman said: The reading of the Megillah itself is its Hallel. Rava said: This is well for the miracle of the Exodus, where we may say “Give praise, servants of the Lord” — servants of the Lord and not servants of Pharaoh. But here, what shall we say — “servants of the Lord” and not servants of Achashverosh? We are still the servants of Achashverosh. Rashi: "And not servants of Pharaoh" — for at the Exodus they went out into freedom. "We are still servants of Ahasuerus" — for at Purim they were redeemed from death alone [and not from their servitude]. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. "Its reading is its hallel"): Since the reading of the Megillah is itself the reciting of hallel, the inference "if for deliverance from slavery to freedom we recite song…" teaches that the Megillah is read both by night and by day, just as hallel is recited on Passover by night and by day; earlier the Gemara derived this from verses. Beis Yaakov (Miketz 5): When Joseph came out of prison our father Jacob surely felt something of it, but it was like the salvation of the Second Temple, which came without victory — as the Sages said, "We are still the servants of Achashverosh," for the nations say all day long, "Where is your God?" Tiferes Yosef (Pesachim 8): In Egypt Israel were sunk in exile together with their very understanding, and the Blessed One redeemed us to everlasting freedom, so that never again would Israel's understanding be in exile — of this one may say, "Give praise, servants of the Lord, and not servants of Pharaoh." But in the days of Achashverosh the understanding was not, Heaven forbid, in exile, only the body, and from bodily exile we have not yet fully escaped and are in such an exile still today; therefore there is no place for Hallel, for "we are still the servants of Achashverosh." (מְגִילָּה יד.):
which aligns with what our Sages said (Megillah 14a):
"אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
"'We are still servants of Ahasuerus,'"
וְאֵין כָּאן הִתְגַּלּוּת שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
and there is no overt revelation of Heaven's Name here.
רַק דְּזֶה נִגְלָה דְּלֶב מְלָכִים וְשָׂרִים בְּיַד ה',
Only that this reality was unveiled: that the heart of kings and ministers is in Hashem's hand,
דְּנִתְגַּלָּה סוֹד זֶה שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ גָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם,
revealing the secret that wherever they were exiled, the Shechinah was exiled with them,

שֶׁלְּמָדוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי תַּעֲנִית פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ג229 Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:1 — R. Simeon ben Yochai taught: Wherever Israel was exiled, the Divine Presence was exiled with them. They were exiled to Egypt and the Divine Presence was exiled with them — what is the reason? "Did I not reveal Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt, in the house of Pharaoh?" (I Samuel 2:27). They were exiled to Babylon and the Divine Presence was exiled with them — "For your sake I was sent to Babylon" (Isaiah 43:14). They were exiled to Media and the Divine Presence was exiled with them — "And I will set My throne in Elam" (Jeremiah 49:38); and Elam is nothing other than Media, as you say, "And I was in Shushan the capital, which is in the province of Elam" (Daniel 8:2). Pnei Moshe (on the preceding line, s.v. "My God — from where was He joined to me"): "From where was He joined to me, to hearken to my voice? From Se'ir" — that is Edom, which is Rome; as R. Yehoshua ben Levi said, if a man says to you, "Where is your God now, in the exile?" say to him, "In the great city of Rome." That is to say, wherever Israel was exiled the Divine Presence was exiled with them, as R. Simeon ben Yochai taught. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael 10): I say that the words are to be taken at face value, and that there is more reason for Him to be with Israel in the exile than when they come out of it. For whatever stands in need of guarding receives His providence the more; and Israel in exile are like a sick man who has departed from his nature, since it is not in the nature or the order of the world that one nation should be subject to another. And a second reason: it is the measure of the Holy One, blessed be He, that His Presence is with the crushed, as it is said, "I dwell with the contrite and lowly of spirit" (Isaiah 57:15) — and Israel in exile are crushed, so His Presence is fittingly with them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 12): Even in exile the Blessed One alone is the leader, as it says, "And I will set My throne in Elam and destroy from there king and princes" — "king," this is Vashti — and as they said, "wherever they were exiled, the Divine Presence is with them." The world merely runs its course in concealment, so that it seems the leadership has been handed over to [the nations], but in truth the Blessed One leads, and through this [concealment] Israel suffers. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 4): Faith is implanted in [a Jew] from the day of his birth and persists also at night, that is, in exile, as it says, "I will go down with you to Egypt," from which the Sages learned that "wherever they were exiled, the Divine Presence was exiled with them." For the Divine Presence is the Blessed One's dwelling amid their impurity — hidden in the heart of every Jew even when he is at the farthest remove from the Blessed One — and this holds even in exile. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Blessed One dwells with Israel amid their impurity and His Presence is within their hearts, and wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence was exiled with them and that place became their place. For by gathering up the bit of good among the nations and returning it all to holiness, that place too is sanctified with the holiness of the air of the Land of Israel, so that the whole world will be sanctified with the holiness of the Land of Israel through Israel's having been there in exile.)
which our Sages deduced (Yerushalmi Ta'anit 1:3)

עַל גָּלוּת פָּרַס מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יִרְמְיָה מט, לח230 Jeremiah 49:38 — "And I will set My throne in Elam, and I will destroy from there king and princes, says the Lord." Rashi: "And I will set My throne" — My siege-works. Radak: Since I shall destroy from her king and princes, and they will understand that it is from Me, it is as though I had set My throne there and set a king over her. Our Rabbis explained the verse of the affair of Vashti and of Haman and his sons, all of which God brought about for Israel's good in their exile: "king" is Vashti and "princes" are Haman and his ten sons, and this is "I will set My throne in Elam," for all knew that the deliverance was from the Lord. Metzudas Dovid: "I will set My throne" — that is, none will rule in Elam but I alone, for I will destroy their princes from them and there will be no one left to rule. Malbim: "I will set My throne" — since they will have no king and no princes, I Myself will rule over them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 12): Even in exile the Blessed One alone is the leader, as it says, "And I will set My throne in Elam and destroy from there king and princes" — "king," this is Vashti — and as the Sages said, wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence is with them. The world merely runs its course in concealment, so that it seems the leadership has been handed over to [the nations], but in truth the Blessed One leads.):
concerning the Persian exile from the verse (Jeremiah 49:38):
"וְשַׂמְתִּי כִסְאִי בְעֵילָם, וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
"'And I will set My throne in Elam, and will destroy, etc.,'"

וּמִקְרָא זֶה דְּרָשׁוּהוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִילָּה (י סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)231 Megillah 10b — Rabbah bar Ofran opened his discourse on this passage from here: "And I will set My throne in Elam, and destroy from there king and princes." "King" — this is Vashti; "and princes" — this is Haman and his ten sons. Rashi: "And I will set My throne in Elam" — Shushan the capital was in Elam, as it is written in the book of Daniel, "in Shushan the capital, which is in the province of Elam." Tosafos (s.v. "Rabbah bar Ofran"): The reading is "Ofran" and not "Efron," since "the name of the wicked shall rot" (Prov. 10:7), and they would not call themselves by such names. Maharsha: It would appear that the prophecy in which it is said "Behold, I will break the bow of Elam" was spoken of the destruction of the Persian kingdom by Alexander, after the Second Temple was built; but this verse, "And I will set My throne in Elam," he understands to have been said of the days of the exile, before the Second Temple was built, when the throne of the Holy One, blessed be He, was in Elam — as they said, when they were exiled to Elam the Divine Presence was with them. And since we do not find that any king and princes were destroyed there in war at that time, it must be said of Vashti, who was a queen and a king’s daughter, and of Haman and his sons, who were princes. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Pesichah): This too was a cause of the events of the Megillah: when Israel went into exile and were under the kingdom of Media, the Holy One, blessed be He, was with them there as well, so that His throne is said to be in Elam, where Israel were, just as before they were exiled the throne of His kingship was in Jerusalem. All this is so that He not abandon Israel, for otherwise they would be consumed in their exile under the nations; rather He is with them, and His providence is upon them. This verse is therefore a promise to Israel: because His providence is over Israel not to abandon them, He destroys before them the king and princes who oppress them. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): They were exiled to Elam and the Shechinah was with them, as it says, "And I will set My throne in Elam"; and "I will destroy from there king and princes," which the Sages expounded of Vashti and of Haman and his sons. For even "when they are in the land of their enemies I have not rejected them," and He is the one who sits upon the throne of the kings of the nations, only that the Shechinah is in exile, not revealed so as to clothe itself in the holy garment of the holy kings of Israel, but only in the sackcloth garment of the husk. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 12): In the seven attributes which the Blessed One emanated for the conduct of this world, even in exile it is the Blessed One alone who leads, as it says, "And I will set My throne in Elam and destroy from there king and princes" — "king" is Vashti, etc. — and as they said, wherever they were exiled the Shechinah was with them. The world follows its natural course in concealment, and it appears as if the conduct had been handed over to them, Heaven forfend; but in truth the Blessed One leads, only in concealment, and for this Israel suffers pain. עַל וַשְׁתִּי וְהָמָן.
and this verse was expounded in the first chapter of Megillah (10b) as referring to Vashti and Haman.
דְּאָז נִתְגַּלָּה עִנְיַן גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּלֵב מְלָכִים,
For then was revealed the exile of the Shechinah within the hearts of gentile monarchs,
שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לָקַחַת לְבָבוֹ בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחוֹ לְהִתְנַהֵג רַק כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
wherein He was required to hold the king's heart in His hand so as not to allow him to act except according to Hashem's will.
וּכְעֵין הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
