And this parallels Hashem's governance through His Shechinah within the hearts of the children of Israel,
דְּאֵין מַנִּיחָם לְנַתֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלָל,
whom He never permits to become severed from Him at all,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבְחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם".
as it is written (Ezekiel 20:33): 'And with fury poured out will I rule over you.'

כִּי זֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא פֶּרֶק ט232 Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 9 — From here they said: Even if a man has piled up many transgressions, one above the other, and afterward returns in repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, says: I am with him in mercy, and I accept his repentance. And even if a man stood and reviled and blasphemed toward Heaven and afterward returned in repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, says: I am with him in mercy.):
For what they said (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 9):
"אִם יַגְדִּיל אָדָם עֲבֵירוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
"If a man multiplies transgressions one upon another, etc.,"
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מַנִּיחוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל כָּךְ עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לָשׁוּב עוֹד,
means that Hashem prevents him from sinning to such an extent that he could never repent,
כִּי חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ חֶלְקוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ,
for 'Hashem's portion is His people,' His allotted heritage,

כְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב233 Rosh Hashanah 12b — Or is it not so, but rather even the first tithe is annulled [in the third year]? The verse states: "Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you take from the children of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritance." Scripture likened it to an inheritance: just as an inheritance has no interruption, so too the first tithe has no interruption. Rashi: "Or perhaps even the first tithe is annulled": and "the year of the tithe" speaks of a single tithe, the one the verse goes on to specify — "to the Levite, the stranger, the orphan and the widow" — namely the poor man's tithe, the Levite too being counted among the poor, since he has no portion in the land.:),
like an inheritance that has no end (Rosh Hashanah 12b),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק
and it is impossible to sever;
וְהוּא מַנְהִיג הַלֵּב מַמָּשׁ וְלִבָּם בְּיָדוֹ.
and He guides the heart directly, their heart being in His hand.
וְכָךְ בַּגָּלוּת הֵם לִבְבוֹת מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בְּיָדוֹ מַמָּשׁ
And likewise in exile, the hearts of pagan kings are literally held in His hand
שֶׁלֹּא יַנְהִיג כְּלָל כִּרְצוֹנוֹ,
so that the king cannot govern according to his own malicious will at all;
הֲגַם דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אוֹיֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מֵהָמָן
even though Ahasuerus was an enemy of Israel even more hostile than Haman,

כִּמְשַׁל רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד234 Megillah 14a — A parable of Ahasuerus and Haman: to what may the matter be compared? To two men, one of whom had a mound in the middle of his field and one of whom had a ditch in the middle of his field. The owner of the ditch said: Who will give me that mound for money! The owner of the mound said: Who will give me that ditch for money! In time they met one another. The owner of the ditch said to the owner of the mound: Sell me your mound. He said to him: Take it for nothing — and would that you had taken it sooner! Rashi: That is to say, one may learn from Ahasuerus that he too had it in mind to destroy them. Maharsha: Haman’s offer of ten thousand talents and the king’s reply, “The silver is given to you, the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you,” are precisely the parable: “Sell me your mound,” and the answer, “Take it for nothing.” He likened Ahasuerus to the owner of the mound — the mound standing for Israel, for whom Ahasuerus had no desire — and Haman to the owner of the ditch and pit, who wanted the mound in order to cast it into his pit; and in Haman was fulfilled “he who digs a pit shall fall into it” (Proverbs 26:27). Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:9): Ahasuerus, like the rest of the four kingdoms, was opposed to Israel, and so to him Israel were like a mound in the middle of a man's field, something superfluous that does not belong to him, for Israel have no part in the kingdom of the nations; yet a mound does the owner of the field no harm, and a king — above all one who, like Ahasuerus, reigned over the whole world, his kingship coming to him from the Holy One, blessed be He — exists to sustain all things, so that reason does not allow destruction to come from him. The ditch, however, is a pit, a thing of lack and privation, and to Haman Israel were reckoned a pit. It was Haman who took them out of the domain of Ahasuerus, as Scripture says, "when a man rose up against us" — a man and not a king: for a king is there to sustain existence, whereas a man, on the contrary, seeks to destroy his fellow. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Emor 3): Haman's decree was something that had never entered anyone's mind: oppressors such as Sennacherib and Nebuchadnezzar exiled Israel, but who had ever heard of handing over an entire nation to slaughter for nothing? Even Achashverosh, in whose heart it had arisen, as the Gemara says in the parable of the owner of the mound and the owner of the ditch, could not bring it to his lips until Haman came..) דְּבַעַל הַתֵּל וְהֶחָרִיץ,
as in the Sages' parable (Megillah 14a) of the owner of the mound and the owner of the pit,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּעָלְכָרְחוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּטוֹבָתוֹ הֵיטִיב לָהֶם,
nonetheless, against his will and without good intention, he favored them;
וְגַם זָעַף עַל אֶסְתֵּר וּבָא מַלְאָךְ וְכוּלֵי כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and he also raged at Esther until an angel came, etc., as our Sages expounded

(אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו וְיַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי שָׁם235 Esther Rabbah 9:1 — She came into the inner court, facing the king, and stood before him, and the king was seated on his royal throne in garments of gold and precious stone. He lifted his eyes and saw Esther standing before him, and his wrath blazed up against her exceedingly, because she had broken his law and come before him unsummoned. Esther lifted her eyes and saw the king's face, and behold, his eyes were like burning fire from the fury in his heart; the queen perceived the king's rage and was greatly terrified and her spirit failed her. Then our God saw and had pity on His people, and turned to the distress of the orphan who trusted in Him, and gave her favor before the king, and added beauty to her beauty and splendor to her splendor. And the king rose in alarm from his throne and ran to Esther and embraced her and kissed her.).
(Esther Rabbah 6; Yalkut Shimoni there).
וְהוּא הַכֹּל מַה שֶּׁלְּבָבוֹ בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And this was entirely because his heart was in the hand of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְכָל מָקוֹם "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם – בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
And every unqualified occurrence of 'the king' points to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
הֲגַם דִּמְבוֹאָר בִּפְשַׁט הַכָּתוּב דִּבְאַחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מְדַבֵּר,
even though the plain meaning of the text clearly speaks of Ahasuerus,
כְּמוֹ "יָבוֹא הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן אֶל הַמִּשְׁתֶּה" וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
such as 'Let the king and Haman come to the banquet,' and similar verses,
רַק הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת בְּגָלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה.
only that it refers through the divine enclothement during the exile of the Shechinah.
וְכָל דִּבּוּרֵי אֶסְתֵּר הָיָה אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
And all of Esther's words were secretly addressed to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד: טו236 Megillah 15a — "And it came to pass on the third day, that Esther clothed herself in royalty" — it should have said "in royal garments." R. Elazar said in the name of R. Chanina: this teaches that she clothed herself in the Divine Spirit. It is written here "and she clothed herself," and it is written there, "and the spirit clothed Amasai." Tosafos (s.v. "on the third day"): In the merit of the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings; or in the merit of priests, Levites and Israelites; or in the merit of Moses, Aaron and Miriam; or because it was the third day of the giving of the Torah. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, Megillah 14b, s.v. "and Esther clothed herself in royalty"): "Royalty" is the last of the ten attributes, and from it the Divine Spirit is bestowed upon whoever is worthy of it. The verse brought as proof, "and the spirit clothed Amasai," certainly does not there speak of the Divine Spirit, for no prophecy of his is recorded anywhere; it means rather a spirit of willingness, as the commentators explain, like "and the spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah." It is cited here only because there too Scripture uses the language of "clothing" with regard to a spirit. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 5:1): Scripture does not say "royal garments," since even a commoner can put on royal garments; but of Esther, who was herself queen, it is fitting to say that when she put on royal garments she put on royalty entirely. The explanation of R. Elazar's teaching is that when Esther put on royal garments in this way, she thereby put on the Divine Spirit as well, for the Divine Spirit clothed her, that is, it rested upon her — just as "and the spirit clothed Amasai" means that the spirit rested upon him. So "Esther clothed herself in royalty" means that when she clothed herself in royalty, the Divine Spirit then rested upon her..):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Megillah 14b, 15a):
שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתְהוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
that the Holy Spirit clothed her,
מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ הַנִּקְרָאת מַלְכוּת,
which is this specific sefirotic level called Malchut,
דְּהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָהּ,
which is the revelation of His Shechinah within her heart,
וְכִי רַק הוּא לְבַדּוֹ שׁוֹכֵן בְּכָל קַצְוֵי אֶרֶץ,
perceiving that He alone abides across all ends of the earth,
וְאֵין עוֹד מַמָּשׁ,
and there is literally none else,
שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר מַמָּשִׁי כְּלָל זוּלָתוֹ,
there being no substantial reality at all apart from Him,
רַק הַנְהָגַת מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְבַד.
only the sovereign governance of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, alone.
וְכֵן כָּל הַסִּפּוּרִים בַּמְּגִילָּה, בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם,
And likewise in all the narratives of the Megillah, wherever 'the king' is stated without qualification,
הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין
the insightful person will understand
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה בְּנֵס פּוּרִים,
that this truth was revealed during the miracle of Purim:
שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ סְתָם הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים.
that 'the king' unspecified is the King of kings.
וְשֵׁם זֶה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִתְגַּלָּה בְּפוּרִים,
And this specific title of Hashem was revealed on Purim,
דְּגַם מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לִבָּם בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
demonstrating that even the heart of pagan kings is in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He.
דָּבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לְעֵין כֹּל בְּפוּרִים,
This reality was openly demonstrated before all eyes on Purim,
דְּהַגַּם דַּ"עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
that even though 'we are still servants of Ahasuerus,'

מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָנוּ עַבְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם בְּהִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּת זֶה דִּלְאַחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ237 Ezra 9:9 — “For we are slaves; yet in our bondage our God has not forsaken us, but has extended mercy to us before the kings of Persia.” Rashi: "For we are slaves" — to Darius, king of Persia. "And He extended lovingkindness to us" is the causative form: He inclined His lovingkindness upon us. "A fence" refers to the fence they made about themselves to guard His commandments. Metzudas Dovid: We are still slaves to the kings of Persia, yet even in our servitude He has not forsaken us altogether. "Its ruins" are the ruins of this House [the Temple]; and "a fence" means to be fenced about on every side, so that we should no longer be trampled underfoot by all. Malbim: He explains that we are still servants of the kings of Persia, and that this was therefore no complete redemption, since it came only by permission of those kings and as an act of grace from the Lord: to give us sustenance, to raise up the House of our God, to preserve the building from the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin who had written an accusation against its building, and to give us "a fence." By that fence they could remain set apart from the nations, having their own governor, their own leaders and their own judges, so that they were a distinct people.,
we are nonetheless servants of Hashem even in this outward subservience to Ahasuerus,
(עֶזְרָא ט, ט) "וּבְעַבְדֻתֵנוּ [לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ אֱלֹהֵינוּ] וְגוֹמֵר".
(Ezra 9:9): 'Yet in our servitude our God has not forsaken us, etc.'
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר זֶה הוּא בְּכָל פּוּרִים
And the revelation of this spiritual light returns every Purim
וּבִכְלַל הַחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר,
and throughout the entire month of Adar in general,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה238 Taanit 29b — R. Papa said: Therefore a Jew who has litigation with a gentile should avoid him in the month of Av, when fortune is bad, and should make himself available in Adar, when his fortune is good. Rashi: "Let him go with him" [in Adar, i.e., make himself available]: to their courts. Tosafos (s.v. "R. Papa said: therefore"): That is, because it was said above that "liability is brought about on a day of liability." Maharsha: "In Av, when his fortune is bad... in Adar, when his fortune is good": although they said that Israel is not subject to the constellations, nevertheless merit is brought about on a day of merit and liability on a day of liability, as was said above. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar II 1): Adar corresponds to Joseph, whose power is victory over the nations, and so the Sages said one should "make himself available in Adar, when his fortune is good." One might think Nisan more fitting, since its redemption was greater, whereas of Adar it is said, "We are still the servants of Achashverosh"; but in Nisan the essence of the redemption was to benefit and exalt Israel, while in Adar the essential aim was the slaying of their enemies and the eradication of Amalek — therefore let him present himself in Adar, for that is the time of victory over them. (תַּעֲנִית כט:):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Ta'anit 29b):
"הַאי מַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵי [נָכְרִי] וְכוּלֵי",
"One who has litigation with a gentile, let him seek judgment in Adar, etc.,"
כִּי מִשְׁפְּטֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם,
for the judicial powers of the nations derive from their earthly kingdom,
וְאָז מִתְגַּלֶּה דְּגַם מַלְכוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and during Adar it is revealed that their kingdom is likewise in the hand of Hashem,
הַיְינוּ בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which means in the hands of Israel,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם בֶּאֱמֶת
in whose hearts Hashem truly dwells,
וּמַנְהִיג גַּם כֵּן לִבְבוֹת מַלְכֵי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כִּרְצוֹנָם.
and directs the hearts of pagan kings according to Israel's true desire.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חוֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ,
In contrast to the month of Av which is the exact opposite,
דְּהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַגָּלוּת,
being the starting point of exile,
שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלָה עֲדַיִן דָּבָר זֶה דְּגָלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם;
wherein it was not yet revealed that the Shechinah had been exiled along with them;
שֶׁגִּילּוּי דָּבָר זֶה הוּא אַתְחַלְתָּא דִּגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה.
for the revelation of this reality constitutes the beginning of complete redemption.
וּמִיָּד סָמוּךְ לַאֲדָר הוּא נִיסָן,
And immediately adjacent to Adar is the month of Nisan,

"מִסְמַךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִגְאוּלָּה" (מְגִילָּה ו239 Megillah 6b — Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds: "in each and every year" — just as in each and every year Purim falls in the Adar adjacent to Nisan, so too here. R. Tavi said: The reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is that it is preferable to join one redemption to the other. Rashi: "One redemption to the other" means Purim to Passover. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar II 1): After Adar comes Nisan, corresponding to the tribe of Judah, from whom the Messiah son of David will come to rectify everything. This is the depth of "it is preferable to join one redemption to the other": the month of Adar corresponds to Joseph, whose power is victory over the nations, and afterwards Nisan corresponds to Judah, from whom comes the redeeming Messiah.:),
to 'juxtapose redemption to redemption' (Megillah 6b),
דִּבְנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה.
for in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed in the ultimate, complete redemption.

sections.en: Purim and the Final Divine Attribute

items.h: Purim reveals Malchut, the final divine attribute, showing that even at the lowest level and without conscious knowledge Israel remains attached to Hashem.

Seif 1 — Purim and Malchut at the Lowest Point
Purim reveals that even at the furthest concealment, Israel remains bound to Hashem beneath conscious awareness.

p: נֵס דְּפוּרִים נִקְרָא בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג דְּיוֹמָא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים,
The miracle of Purim is called at the beginning of the third chapter of Yoma (29a) 'the end of all miracles,'
כִּי הוּא נַעֲשָׂה בַּמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה מִמִּדּוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because it was wrought through the final attribute among His attributes, blessed be He.
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת,
For it is known that there are seven divine emotional attributes (sefirot),
וְשֵׁשׁ מִדּוֹת הֵם נֶגְדָּם שִׁשָּׁה זְמַנִּים הַמְּפוֹרָשִׁים בַּתּוֹרָה:
and facing six of these attributes stand the six sacred seasons explicitly articulated in the Torah:
פֶּסַח, שָׁבוּעוֹת וְסֻכּוֹת יָדוּעַ דְּהֵם נֶגֶד תְּלָת אֲבָהָן;
Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot are known to correspond to the three Patriarchs (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet);
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הֵם נֶגֶד תְּרֵין בַּדֵּי עֲרָבָה;
and Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur correspond to the two willow branches (Netzach and Hod);
וַעֲצֶרֶת, שֶׁהוּא רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן "כְּנִישׁוּ", נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַיְסוֹד
and Shemini Atzeret, which is a festival in its own right and translated into Aramaic as kenishu ('assembly'), corresponds to the attribute of Yesod
שֶׁלְּשָׁם מִתְאַסְּפִין כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
into which all supernal attributes gather to channel the divine influx into the attribute of His Sovereignty (Malchut), blessed be He.
וְאֵלּוּ הַשֵּׁשׁ הֵם מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי".
And these six appointed times are those that 'Israel sanctifies.'
אֲבָל הַשְּׁבִיעִית הִיא קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת דִּ"קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא",
However, the seventh is the sanctity of Shabbat, which is inherently 'fixed and enduring,'
דְּנִקְרָא שַׁבָּת עַל שֵׁם הַשְּׁבִיתָה מִכָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעוּלַת אָדָם
for it is termed Shabbat after cessation from all human exertion and mortal initiative,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם מָבוֹא בָּזֶה,
wherein they possess no entry or role;
דְּהוּא שׁוֹכֵן גַּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאוֹתָם,
for He abides even in the midst of their defilements,

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד240 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..),
and 'even though he has sinned, he remains Israel' (Sanhedrin 44a),
כִּי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּת זוּגוֹ דְּשַׁבָּת
because the Congregation of Israel is the destined mate of Shabbat,
וְהֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּמִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתְּקָם כְּלָל.
and they cling unto this attribute such that it is utterly impossible to sever them.

כִּי מִדָּה זוֹ נִקְרָא אֱמוּנָה (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רל עַמּוּד א241 Zohar 3:230a — As He is humble, His Presence is humble; He is kind, and she is kind; He is mighty, and she is mistress over all the nations of the world; He is truth, and she is faith; He is prophet, and she is prophetess; He is righteous, and she is righteous; He is King, and she is Kingship; He is wise, and she is wisdom; He is understanding, and she is His discernment; He is crown, and she is His diadem, "a crown of glory."),
For this attribute is termed Faith (Emunah / Malchut; Zohar Part III, 230a),

וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים (שַׁבָּת צז242 Shabbat 97a — Reish Lakish said: One who suspects the innocent is stricken in his body, for it is written, "But they will not believe me" — and it was revealed before the Holy One, blessed be He, that Israel would believe. He said to him: They are believers, the children of believers, and you in the end will not believe. They are believers, as it is written, "And the people believed"; the children of believers, as it says of Abraham, "And he believed in the Lord." Maharsha: Because Moses suspected Israel of not believing him, the sign given him was one in which he himself was stricken. He was at fault, though he could not know they would believe without a sign, because the Holy One, blessed be He, had already told him "and they will hearken to your voice" — for, as the Midrash says, the elders held a tradition that the redeemer would come with the words "I have surely remembered." Hence they are "children of believers," holding that tradition from their fathers; and "And the people believed" continues "and they heard that the Lord had remembered" — they believed on account of that tradition, not merely because of the signs. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 97a): One who suspects the innocent deserves to be stricken in his body. It is like one who throws a stone at a wall: if the wall is of stone and does not receive the stone, it rebounds upon him, but if the wall is of clay it receives the stone and it does not rebound. So when a person suspects another, if the suspicion is true the other "receives" it and it does not return upon him; but if he suspects the innocent, the suspected one does not receive it, since it is untrue, and the suspicion returns upon the one who suspected. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 22): "I am [the Lord]" was not said in the language of command, since faith cannot be commanded — if one does not believe in the Blessed One, how would he obey His command? — but all the seed of Israel are "believers, the children of believers." One who kicks at faith appears to have left the community of Israel, as if he were not of the seed of Israel; but that is only to outward appearance in this world, the world of falsehood, while the Blessed One keeps truth forever so that none of them is banished. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 45): If Moses' worry was that they would say "the Lord did not appear to you," what proof is there from Abraham, to whom the Lord did appear? Rather, Moses' claim was "by what merit shall I redeem them?" — they would not believe because they felt they had no merit of their own for which to be redeemed — and the Blessed One answered that they are "believers, the children of believers," children of Abraham, who believed in Me that I can send illumination into a person's heart even when he has nothing of his own. This was their faith in Egypt, as it says, "And the people believed.".) מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים,
and Israel are called 'believers, the children of believers' (Shabbat 97a),
וְזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲמִין כְּלָל,
and the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob cannot possibly lack faith entirely,
כִּי זֶהוּ מִצַּד קְדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
because this stems from the sanctity permanently established and enduring from Hashem, blessed be He, within the hearts of the children of Israel.
וּקְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ מִתְגַּלֵּית בְּכָל תּוֹקֶף בְּפוּרִים,
And this sanctity is revealed with ultimate intensity on Purim,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה ז243 Megillah 7b — Rava said: A man is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until he no longer knows the difference between "cursed is Haman" and "blessed is Mordecai." Rashi: "To become intoxicated" means to become drunk with wine. Tosafos (s.v. "that he does not know the difference between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai'"): In the Jerusalem Talmud [the formula runs]: "Cursed is Zeresh, blessed is Esther; cursed are all the wicked, blessed are all the Jews." Maharsha: There is a righteous man who suffers in this world — one not wholly righteous, who receives his punishment here — and a wicked man who prospers here — one not wholly wicked, so that he may be driven out of the World to Come; but the wholly righteous man is granted both tables, as Mordecai was granted all his greatness in this world too, and the wholly wicked man, like Haman of the seed of Amalek and Esau, loses even this world. "Until he does not know" therefore means that he no longer sets his heart to discern the vast distance between "cursed is Haman," who was wholly wicked and lost both worlds, and "blessed is Mordecai," who was wholly righteous and was granted both worlds. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Even in drunkenness "until he does not know," when he has no understanding to act from, the depths of [a Jew's] heart are steeped in love of Israel. This is the whole clarification of Purim — that Israel's sins and their seeming like all the nations are only external: even when one is intoxicated "until he does not know between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai,'" not recognizing openly the difference between Israel and the nations, they bear no likeness at all and are utterly distinct in the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman's eye was evil toward Israel's festivals, for he did not believe there could be any holiness in bodily enjoyment such as eating and drinking. Hence "a person is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until...": precisely through drunkenness with wine, without conscious understanding, the inner holiness of Israel is made clear — that even their enjoyment of food and drink is in holiness — after the manner of "wine enters, the secret comes out.":): "חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע",
where they stated (Megillah 7b): 'A person is obligated to become intoxicated until he knows not,'
דְּהַפֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּשׁוּט בּוֹ הוּא גִּלּוּי דָּבָר זֶה
for the straightforward meaning of this is the revelation of this reality:
דְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִים בֵּין יְמִינָם לִשְׂמֹאלָם.
that the hearts of the children of Israel are truly cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He, even when they know not between their right and their left.

וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר (עֵירוּבִין סה244 Eruvin 65b — R. Ila'i said: In three things a man is known — in his cup, in his purse, and in his anger. And some say: also in his laughter. Rashi: "A man is known" — whether he is a worthy man. "In his cup" — whether his mind stays settled upon him with his wine. "In his purse" — whether he acts in good faith when he deals with people. "In his anger" — that he is not exacting beyond measure. Maharsha: The traits fall in general into three classes: good toward Heaven, good toward one's fellows, and good toward oneself. "In his purse" — whether he deals faithfully with men, that is, good or bad toward his fellows; "in his cup" — whether he remains settled with his wine, which is good toward himself, and not like those of whom it is said, "Who has woe, who has sorrow?"; "in his anger" — if he does not grow angry he is good toward Heaven, whereas of one who grows angry they said that it is as though he worshipped idols. And because these three words are close in sound, he took them as a mnemonic for those three divisions. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): "In three things a person is known — in his cup...": that is, precisely through drunkenness, when understanding is taken from him, the difference between the holiness of Israel and the nations is recognized and made clear, for in Israel there is inner holiness even in this-worldly enjoyments. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 12): The Sages give as the sign by which a person is known "his cup, his purse and his anger," and not the hour when he stands in the synagogue wrapped in a tallis and crowned with tefillin, implying that this is no proof. The main recognition comes when he enters the concealments of this-worldly affairs, dealing with people in the markets and streets; then one can recognize the preciousness in a person — what he is in the depths of his heart.:):
And in three things a person is recognized (Eruvin 65b):
בְּכוֹסוֹ וּבְשִׁכְרוּתוֹ,
in his cup and in his drunkenness,
שֶׁאָז אֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה שְׁלֵימָה לְהַסְתִּיר וּלְהַעֲלִים מַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ.
since at that moment he lacks conscious control to disguise and conceal the depths of his heart.
וְאָז מִתְגַּלֶּה מַה שֶּׁהוּא תּוֹךְ מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב,
And then what resides within the heart's innermost depth is laid bare,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח245 Sanhedrin 38a — R. Chiyya said to him: My teacher, let it not be evil in your eyes. "Wine" is given in seventy [the numerical value of its letters], and "secret" is given in seventy: when wine goes in, the secret comes out. Rashi: "In seventy letters" — that is, by numerical value. Tosafos (s.v. "wine went in, the secret came out"): This is what is said in chapter HaDar (Eruvin 65a): whoever stays settled in his wine has in him the understanding of seventy elders — for in him the secret prevails over the wine, and the wine has no power to draw it out. Maharsha: The "secret" is the secret of intercalating the month: the kingship of the House of David is likened to the moon, which begins to wane after fifteen days, and it waned after fifteen kings, in Zedekiah's time, leaving only a little rule — the Exilarch in Babylonia and the Nasi in the Land of Israel; and as the moon wanes entirely before it is renewed, so when these two have come to an end David's kingship will be renewed. Rebbi was pained that his office would come to an end, and R. Chiyya told him not to take it ill, for with the wine that went in, the "secret" of the intercalation had come out of them — that the kingship of the House of David will be renewed, and with it the greatness of the families of the Nesi'im. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 38a): Wine comes from a place of secrecy, for wine issues from the inner part [of the fruit]; you see from this that wine is from a hidden and concealed place, and therefore "wine" equals "secret" in numerical value. When wine goes in, it cleaves and draws near to the secret, and when it draws near to the secret, the secret is laid bare and comes out. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 20): Further, from that same night: one who reveals mysteries and secrets that ought not to be revealed is punished by being reincarnated, and in his second incarnation he is a drunkard, for "when wine goes in, the secret comes out." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): [The Purim feast reveals each year that all the feasting of Israel is holy:] when wine goes in the secret comes out, and the mysteries in the hearts of Israel are revealed, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it is written, "the Rock of my heart." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): [On the obligation to become intoxicated on Purim:] It is precisely through intoxication with wine, without awareness, that the inner holiness of Israel is made clear — that even their enjoyment of eating and drinking is in holiness — in the manner of "Give the youngsters much wine so that they will say something … when wine goes in, the secret comes out." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 199): "By his cup" corresponds to "with all your heart," as it is written, "Wine and new wine take the heart." The heart is tested when it is unsettled; but if its whole cavity is already filled through and through with true love of the Blessed One, then even when wine goes in, the secret that comes out is the "secret of the Lord" stored within him. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): On Purim, the festival founded on Haman's downfall, one is obliged to become intoxicated so as to be "recognized by his cup," for by it the strength of Israel's holiness is recognized: when wine goes in the secret comes out, and what was hidden in the depths of the heart is revealed — that the holy Israel cleave in the depths of their hearts to the holiness of the Blessed One, "the Rock of their heart and their portion.".): "נִכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד"
as they said (Sanhedrin 38a): 'Wine entered, the secret came out'
וְנִתְגַּלָּה,
and was unveiled,
דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
revealing that the depth of the heart of the children of Israel cleaves to Hashem, blessed be He,
בְּלִי שׁוּם יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת וּכְפִיָּה לִרְצוֹן הַלֵּב,
without any deliberate calculation or forced subjugation of the heart's desire;
רַק נְקוּדַּת הָרָצוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּית הִיא דְּבוּקָה בֶּאֱמֶת מֵעַצְמָהּ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather the authentic, innermost point of will is inherently bonded on its own unto Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל יְדֵי מִדָּה זוֹ נַעֲשָׂה הַנֵּס דְּפוּרִים,
And through this divine attribute was the miracle of Purim wrought,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת",
as it is written (Esther 5:1): 'And Esther clothed herself in royalty (Malchut),'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמָרְדֳּכַי יוֹשֵׁב בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ", "וַיָּשָׁב מָרְדֳּכַי אֶל שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ".
and as written: 'and Mordechai sat in the king's gate,' 'and Mordechai returned to the king's gate.'

וְיָדוּעַ דְּמִדָּה זוֹ נִקְרֵאת "תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא גּוֹ מְהֵימְנוּתָא" (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א, ה עַמּוּד ב; יא עַמּוּד ב246 Zohar 1:11b — "In the beginning God created" — this is the first commandment of all, and this commandment is called the fear of the Lord, which is called "beginning," as it is written, "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord," [and] "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge" — for this thing is called "beginning." And this is the gate through which one enters into faith, and upon this commandment the whole world stands. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 7): [In the Zohar's words that Israel below stand] "to open paths," this is the aspect of fear, which is "the gate for entering into faith" — the arousal from Israel's side, as in "Open for Me one opening of repentance like the eye of a needle, and I will open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter"; this opening is fear, which comes from Israel's side. Sha'ar HaEmunah (Entrance to the Gate 1): The fear of the Lord is the receptacle for receiving the Torah. Faith is the root of fear, and fear is the vessel that holds faith: fear is rooted in a person's believing in the Blessed One, and through his faith in the vastness of His power and exaltedness [he comes to fear Him] — as in the Zohar's introduction, "In the beginning God created: this is the first commandment of all … and this is the gate for entering into faith."),
And it is known that this attribute is termed 'the gate to enter into faith' (Zohar Part I, 5b; 11b),
וְעָלֶיהָ נֶאֱמַר: "זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' וְגוֹמֵר".
and concerning it Scripture declares: 'This is the gate of Hashem, etc.'

וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה טז247 Megillah 16a — And this is what is written: "And Mordecai returned to the king's gate." Rav Sheshet said: He returned to his sackcloth and to his fast. Rashi (s.v. "and to his fast"): It was the third day of the fast, for they had begun to fast on the fourteenth of Nisan; and what Scripture says, "And it came to pass on the third day, that Esther clothed herself in royalty," was the third day from the sending out of the couriers. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): Scripture need not have told us where he returned to, were it not to teach that he returned to his sackcloth, which lay before the king's gate. And although "to the king's gate" earlier means within the gate, here — since one may not enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth — it is proved that "to the king's gate" means no further than the gate. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 6:12): [On the plain sense of the verse:] Mordecai returned to the king's gate and did not come before the king: rather than send for him and tell him that this greatness was his reward for reporting Bigthan and Teresh, the king had Haman take him from the king's gate, so that he would return there of himself — and from this Mordecai knew that the king wanted him not beside him but at the gate, keeping watch there against anyone who would harm the king. It is also possible that Ahasuerus meant him to sit at the king's gate because, for all the good Mordecai had done him, he had sold all the Jews to Haman, Mordecai among them, and had not yet annulled his decree..) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּשָׁב מָרְדֳּכַי" – שֶׁשָּׁב וְכוּלֵי.
And so our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 16a) on the verse 'and Mordechai returned'—that he returned to his sackcloth and fasting.
דִּתְפִלָּה הוּא מִמַּדְרֵגָה זוֹ
For prayer derives from this specific spiritual rung,
כְּטַעַם "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד.
mirroring 'and I am prayer' (Psalms 109:4), which is the rung of David (Malchut).
כִּי "אַתָּה" נִקְרָא שֵׁירוּתָא,
For 'You' (Attah / direct presence) is designated as the beginning,
וְהוּא הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכַח בְּפֶסַח דְּ"רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי".
and that was the open perception of the divine Presence on Passover when 'a maidservant saw, etc.'
וְ"אֲנִי" הוּא מִדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה,
While 'I' (Ani) represents the final attribute,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ
wherein Hashem, blessed be He, abides literally within the hearts of the children of Israel,
עַד שֶׁהַנָּבִיא יוּכַל לוֹמַר בְּפִיו "אֲנִי ה'",
to the extent that the prophet can articulate with his mouth 'I am Hashem,'
כִּי הוּא עַצְמוֹ לְבָבוֹ הוּא מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because he himself, his very heart, serves as the tabernacle of His glory, blessed be He.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ הַתְּפִלָּה,
And from this prayer is drawn forth;
דְּלָכֵן תִּקְּנוּ מִקּוֹדֶם "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וְגוֹמֵר",
which is why they instituted beforehand: 'O Lord, open my lips, etc.,'
וּבְשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת,
specifically using the divine Name of Adonut (Mastery),
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מִדַּת אֲדוֹנוּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
signifying the attribute of His mastership and sovereignty within the lower realms;
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹתֵחַ חַדְרֵי לְבָבוֹ וּפוֹתֵחַ שְׂפָתָיו בִּתְפִלָּה,
for it is impossible to pray unless Hashem unlocks the chambers of one's heart and opens his lips in prayer,
וְלוּלֵי זֶה אֵין מְצִיאוּת לִתְפִלָּה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל.
and without this there is no authentic existence of prayer whatsoever.

דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (סוֹף תִּיקּוּן יג)248 Tikkunei Zohar 29b — Therefore a herald goes forth each day: Whoever slays that serpent which nests in the great mountains, they give him the king's daughter, who is prayer, seated upon the tower of which it is said, "The name of the Lord is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is set on high." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): The "life of the hour" comes from the union of the soul with the body, and that vitality dwells in the heart, the place of toil, for the evil inclination sits at the two openings of the heart; so only "whoever conquers in battle is given the king's daughter, which is prayer." The eternal life of Torah, by contrast, which is in the mind and does not come from the union with the body, is open to all: one who has not conquered [his inclination] should engage in Torah, and not only after the victory. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 208): A person's main war with his inclination is over the imaginings and thoughts of the heart and mind, and of this the Tikkunim say, "whoever conquers in battle is given the king's daughter, which is prayer." For prayer is awareness of [God's] presence, like standing before the King — a standing of heart and mind — and whenever a stray thought befalls a person, at that moment he is not standing before the Blessed One; one who conquers his inclination and leaves imagination and outside thoughts is "given" that the Blessed One is present before his eyes at the time of prayer.: "בְּרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא דָּא צְלוֹתָא",
Therefore it is designated in Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 13): 'The daughter of the King—this is prayer,'
כְּמוֹ בַּת מֶלֶךְ שֶׁאֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ מַנִּיחָהּ לָלֶכֶת לְבַדָּהּ.
like a king's daughter whom the monarch never permits to walk unescorted.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ דְּאָז מִתְפַּלֵּל וְנַעֲנָה.
And this is what is termed 'he directed his heart,' wherein he prays and is answered.
פֵּירוּשׁ "לִבּוֹ" – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
The meaning of 'his heart' is the Holy One, blessed be He,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה249 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness; I am asleep with respect to the redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The Blessed One always dwells in the depths of one's heart, as Shir HaShirim Rabbah says that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel — "the Rock of my heart and my portion" — and on this they expounded "I am asleep but my heart is awake": though a person is sunk in imagination, which is the sleep, the imagination does not reach the depths of the heart, where the point of "the Rock of his heart" is always awake, and through it he can awaken from his slumber and merit the complete redemption. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 7): [The Zohar reads] "Many of those who sleep in the dust shall awaken" with "I am asleep but my heart is awake": when the Blessed One dwells in the heart of Israel, as they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel ("God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever"), death is only like sleep. Even though the flaw that brought death has not been repaired in the world at large, one who merits that his heart be a dwelling for the Shechinah is redeemed completely, and his death is only like sleep followed by awakening. ה, ב) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי עֵר".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2) on the verse 'and my heart is awake.'

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ל250 Berakhot 30a — The Sages taught: … One standing outside the Land should direct his heart toward the Land of Israel, as it is stated: “and they pray to You by way of their land” (I Kings 8:48). One standing in the Land of Israel should direct his heart toward Jerusalem, as it is stated: “and they pray to the Lord by way of the city which You have chosen” (I Kings 8:44). One standing in Jerusalem should direct his heart toward the Temple, as it is stated: “and they pray toward this house” (II Chronicles 6:32). One standing in the Temple should direct his heart toward the Chamber of the Holy of Holies, as it is stated: “and they pray toward this place” (I Kings 8:35). One standing in the Chamber of the Holy of Holies should direct his heart toward the Ark cover. One standing behind the Ark cover should regard himself as though he stood before the Ark cover. Accordingly, one standing in the east turns his face to the west; in the west, he turns his face to the east; in the south, he turns his face to the north; in the north, he turns his face to the south. Thus all Israel direct their hearts toward one place. Rashi (s.v. "behind the Ark cover"): To the west of the Temple courtyard there were eleven cubits of court, from the wall of the Holy of Holies to the western wall of the courtyard; one standing there turns his face eastward, toward the Ark cover. Tosafos (s.v. "one standing outside the Land should direct toward the Land of Israel"): We do not read "his heart" here, for it is his face that is meant, as the latter clause teaches: "one standing in the east turns his face to the west.".): "יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים",
And similarly they stated (Berakhot 30a): 'He shall direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies,'
דְּפֵירוּשׁ הַפָּשׁוּט שֶׁהַלֵּב מְכֻוָּון נֶגֶד קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁשָּׁם שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
where the direct meaning is that his heart is aligned facing the Holy of Holies where His Shechinah rests,
וְאָז הַלֵּב עוֹמֵד מְכֻוָּון וּמְיוּשָּׁר לִתְפִלָּה.
and then the heart stands properly aligned and oriented for prayer.
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן גַּם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם מִתְפַּלְּלִים,
For otherwise, the idolaters also pray,
אֶלָּא דְּהֵם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִתְפִלָּה מִצַּד לְבָבָם
except that they have no intrinsic attachment to prayer by virtue of their heart,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לִשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל.
which possesses no connection to the dwelling of Hashem's Shechinah whatsoever.
וְזֶה הָיָה טָעוּת בִּלְעָם בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת דְּבָלָק,
And this was the tragic error of Balaam in the sacrifices of Balak,
שֶׁחָשַׁב עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה יִפְעַל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
in that he presumed he could effect results from Hashem through prayer,
וְלֹא יָדַע דְּאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת תְּפִלָּה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
not knowing that the capacity for prayer belongs exclusively to Israel.
רַק מִצַּד תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Only through the universal prayer of King Solomon, peace be upon him,
דְּגַם הַגּוֹי כְּשֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אֶל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ יֵעָנֶה,
that even the foreigner when praying toward the Holy Temple would be answered,
נִיתַּן קְצָת כֹּחַ,
was some slight spiritual efficacy granted;

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א וּמִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תְּרוּמָה ט251 Vayikra Rabbah 1:11; Midrash Tanchuma, Terumah 9 — Had the nations of the world known how good the Tent of Meeting was for them, they would have surrounded it with tents and encampments [to guard it]. And in the Tanchuma: Had the nations known how good the Tabernacle and the Temple were for them, they would have surrounded them with tents and encampments to guard them. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): The revelation of the Shechinah [in the Temple], where the Foundation Stone lies, sustains the whole world, even the nations, as the Sages said, "If they knew how good the Temple is for them …," and [so too] the seventy bullocks to atone for them. For when Israel is on its land as one nation, it passes the residue of its bounty to the nations, so that they too have existence, and in drawing from Israel's residue they have some connection with Israel.):
in accordance with what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Vayikra Rabbah 1; Midrash Tanchuma, Terumah 9):
"אִלְמָלֵי הָיוּ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יוֹדְעִין כַּמָּה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ יָפֶה לָהֶם וְכוּלֵי",
"'Had the idolaters known how good the Temple was for them, etc.'"
כִּי זֶה כָּל עִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
for this is the entire purpose of the Holy Temple:
לִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָה קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גָּלוּי לְעֵין כֹּל, אַף לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
that the Shechinah dwell permanently established in this world, manifest to the eyes of all, even the nations of the world.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיָנָיו שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּנְשִׂיאַת נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת,
And this was the overarching design of King Solomon, peace be upon him, in marrying foreign women,
שֶׁהוּא רָצָה שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ כֻּלָּם כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתְךָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד.
desiring that all humanity recognize the power of Your sovereignty as will unfold in the ultimate future.
וְזֶה טַעַם תְּפִלָּתוֹ זוֹ:
And this was the rationale of his prayer:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם לַגּוֹיִם הַכָּרָה בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
that even the gentiles should possess an awareness of the holiness of the Temple,
שֶׁיִּפְנוּ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֵלָיו,
so that they would turn to pray toward it,
עַד שֶׁמִּכֹּחַ הַכָּרָה זוֹ יִהְיֶה לָהֶם קְצָת כֹּחַ בִּתְפִלָּה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲנִים.
such that by virtue of that recognition they would hold some measure of power in prayer to be answered.
וּבְעֵת חוּרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
Yet during the destruction of the Temple,
דְּהַגָּלוּת הוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַכָּרַת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת זֶה,
where exile represents the total loss of that perception among the nations,
מִמֵּילָא אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת תְּפִלָּה כְּלָל, רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
prayer naturally has no connection to them whatever, remaining exclusive to the children of Israel.
וּבְפוּרִים הָיָה גַּם כֵּן קְצָת הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
And on Purim there was likewise a partial disclosure of illumination toward the nations,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written (Esther 8:17): 'And many from among the peoples of the land became Jews, etc.,'
וְאוֹמֵר: "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה [אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשֹׂן] וִיקָר",
and Scripture states: 'For the Jews there was light and gladness, and joy and honor,'

וְדָרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה טז252 Megillah 16b — On "The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor," Rav Yehuda expounded: "Honor" — these are the phylacteries, and so it says: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you." And it is taught in a baraita: R. Eliezer the Great says: These are the phylacteries of the head. Maharsha: Among the commandments there are some that serve as a sign and a testimony for Israel — the Sabbath, of which it says "between Me and you," the phylacteries, of which it says "and it shall be a sign upon your hand," [and circumcision, which is the sign of the covenant] — and it was against these in particular that Haman decreed, because they are the testimony of Israel. "Honor" is the phylacteries, which are the glory of Israel, as the verse says "that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you"; and to this they returned, as it is written, "for the fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them." Maharal (Gevuros Hashem 39): The phylacteries teach that Israel belong to the unique Name, for in them the going out from Egypt is recalled, which He brought about by wonders; therefore "they shall fear you," because of His mighty and awesome deeds. R. Eliezer said specifically "the phylacteries of the head" because the phylacteries of the arm express the binding and cleaving of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, and where there is cleaving there is no fear; but in the phylacteries of the head there is no binding, only that His name is called upon them — and in being called "the God of Israel" He is set apart from them, and on that side there is fear, for it is fitting to fear the God of Israel, to whom belongs might. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:40): In front are the tefillin themselves, of which the Sages said, "'And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you' — these are the tefillin of the head," for it is recognizable to all that the name of the Lord is called upon him. But at the back there is no such clear recognition, only the knot of the tefillin, from which the "smallness" that desires for its own sake draws, so that an accuser can claim that it is truly for himself and not for the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 13): "And honor — these are the tefillin of the head": this shows that Israel are bound at the root, above the grasp of human intellect; hence the Sages were precise to say tefillin "that are in the head" and not "that are on the head," for the meaning is that they are bound in the brain. Against this Amalek accused, and since they merited to wipe out Amalek, they merited the aspect of "honor," which signifies attachment at the root, the aspect of Atika. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Vezos HaBerachah): Tefillin allude to strength and boldness for Israel, as it is written, "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you," and the Gemara says, "These are the tefillin of the head." Therefore [Elisha, "the man of wings,"] was filled with strength and boldness to go out wearing tefillin [despite the decree], trusting that if the quaestor saw him he would fear him, and that he would thereby know he had acted according to the will of the Blessed One. Beis Yaakov (Vayetzei 72): Jacob's dealings with the sheep were a compelling and overcoming of the sitra achra, so as to bring [what it held] into holiness; and, as the Zohar says, the work of the rods is the secret of tefillin, for tefillin allude to triumph, as it is written, "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you," and it is taught: "R. Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin of the head." Sod Yesharim (Purim 1): "And honor — these are the tefillin": in the tefillin of the Master of the world it is written, "For what great nation…," that is, tefillin are a garment for His light — the light of His will is clothed in this mitzvah, and when a person dons them he can attain His light that is clothed in them; and they allude to all the deeds of the mitzvos, in which a person can dig and reveal the light that dwells within them. Amalek denies this, saying that all these things are what the Ancient of Days covered so that there should be concealment, and that it is not His will to reveal the concealment in this world.:): "אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ",
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 16b): 'This refers to the tefillin of the head,'
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם [ה' נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ] וְגוֹמֵר".
fulfilling 'And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of Hashem is called upon you, etc.'
וְהַיְינוּ רְאִיָּה זוֹ דְּשֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And that refers to this external perception—that the Name of Hashem is invoked upon the children of Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי נָפַל פַּחַד הַיְּהוּדִים עֲלֵיהֶם",
as written: 'for the fear of the Jews fell upon them,'
שֶׁלֹּא הִשִּׂיגוּ שׁוּם הַשָּׂגָה מִגִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since they did not achieve any inner comprehension of the revelation of His Shechinah,
דְּזֶה הָיָה אָז בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל
because this was then veiled in profound concealment;
וְאֵין שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִזְכָּר בַּמְּגִילָּה כְּלָל,
and indeed the divine Name of Heaven is not explicitly mentioned anywhere in the Megillah,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת וּפִרְסוּם אֱלֹהוּת לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
there being no overt revelation and publication of divinity to the idolaters,
רַק פִּרְסוּם גַּדְלוּת הַיְּהוּדִים אֵיךְ הֵם מוּשְׁגָּחִים בְּהַנְהָגָה עֶלְיוֹנָה.
only the public demonstration of the Jews' elevated stature, showing how they are miraculously guided by supernal providence.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
For in ultimate truth, the actual dwelling of Hashem's Shechinah is exclusively within the hearts of the Jewish people,
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא "אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and Shabbat is 'a sign between Me and the children of Israel,'
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב מִיתָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נח:).
and an idolater who observes Shabbat is liable to the death penalty (Sanhedrin 58b).
כִּי עִנְיַן הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהֶעְדֵּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַכָּרָה דִּפְעוּלַת אָדָם אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם, רַק הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the essence of resting and renouncing human exertion stems from the realization that mortal effort is nothing, everything being solely from Hashem,
וְזֶה חַיּוּתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and this consciousness is the very life-force of Israel;
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ מִיתָתָן שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
whereas this very concept constitutes the spiritual demise of idolaters,
דְּכָל חַיּוּתָם הוּא מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעוּלַת אָדָם וְהֶעְדֵּר הַהַכָּרָה,
since their entire vitality is predicated upon mortal striving, human initiative, and the absence of divine recognition,
אֲבָל מִיָּד שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה דָּבָר זֶה דְּהַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשֶׁאֵין מָבוֹא לִפְעוּלַת אָדָם – אָז נֶעְדַּר חַיּוּתָם.
so the moment this truth of Hashem's omnipotence is disclosed, demonstrating that human striving has no absolute role, their vitality is annihilated.
וְכֵן הָיָה מִיתַת בְּכוֹרִים דְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל – זוֹ גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
And thus was the death of the Egyptian firstborn brought about through 'great terror'—which denotes the overt revelation of the Shechinah;
וּמִצַּד זֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הֲרִיגַת הַשּׂוֹנְאִים וּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק דְּפוּרִים.
and from this very perspective emerged the destruction of the enemies and the blotting out of Amalek on Purim.
כִּי עִנְיַן עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכְּרֵי כֶסֶף לִשְׁקוֹל אֶל גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
For the meaning of weighing out ten thousand talents of silver into the treasuries of the king—
דְּמֶלֶךְ סְתָם בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְדַבֵּר,
wherein 'the king' unspecified refers to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He—

הַיְינוּ כִּי הָמָן טָעַן "יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד" – יָשְׁנוּ מִן הַמִּצְווֹת כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יג253 Megillah 13b — "There is one people scattered abroad and dispersed" (Esther 3:8). Rava said: There was none who knew how to slander like Haman. He said to him: Come, let us destroy them. He said to him: I fear their God, lest He do to me as He did to those before me. He said to him: "There is" [yeshno] — they have slumbered [yashnu] away from the commandments. He said to him: But there are sages among them. He said to him: They are "one people" [all alike]. Rashi (s.v. “There are Sages among them”): From Haman’s reply we learn that this is how Ahasuerus had answered him. Maharsha: The verse is superfluous, and its expressions are doubled — it need only have written “there is” [yesh] and not “yeshno” — and therefore they expounded that Haman told him they had slumbered away from the commandments: either from the word “change,” that they alter their commandments, or from the word “sleep,” that they sleep away from them. And from the superfluous word “one” they expounded Ahasuerus’s objection, “There are Sages among them” who will shield them by their good deeds — to which Haman answered, “They are one people”: just as the rest of the people do not keep the commandments, so too the Sages among them do not keep them. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:8): As for their expounding "there is" [yeshno] as "they have slumbered from the commandments," it seems that the exposition does not rest chiefly on the word yeshno being a form of "sleep"; rather, the expression "there is a people" itself implies it — that they are nothing but a people, whereas the commandments do not derive from their being a "people" but from the name "Israel," for all the other nations, which are peoples, have no commandments. So he said that these too are merely "a people," like every other people that is called only "a people," since they do not perform the divine commandments. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): Haman — of whom the Sages said that none knew how to slander like him — aimed his accusation against Israel above: he said, "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and of the Rabbis, "They too are one people," that is, he accused Israel's own sanctity, which comes through Torah and mitzvos, saying that all of them, even the Torah scholars, had slumbered from Torah and mitzvos. And against the sanctity that comes from the Blessed One he said that He of whom it is said "the Lord is One" has fallen asleep away from His people. Sod Yesharim (Purim 25): "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and in the Midrash, "[Haman] said: their God is asleep" — as the Arizal wrote, this is like the deep sleep at the beginning of Creation: when a person nullifies himself entirely and surrenders all his selfhood to the Blessed One, He returns to him a sprouting of salvation all the more, and every salvation must be preceded by such nullification. The destruction and exile were such a self-nullification, in which Israel surrendered to the Blessed One all the might they had drawn from the mitzvos dependent on the Land, until they appeared to be sleeping from the mitzvos, and from this the Second Temple sprouted. At that very time, when they appeared to be asleep, Haman said "their God is asleep, they have slumbered from the mitzvos," seeking to accuse Israel, and the Blessed One showed him, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.":).
was that Haman slandered: 'there is (yeshno) one nation'—meaning they have slept (yashnu) from the commandments, as our Sages expounded (Megillah 13b).

רַק בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב254 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I am asleep with respect to charity, but my heart is awake to perform it. I am asleep with respect to the offerings, but my heart is awake for the recitation of Shema and prayer. I am asleep with respect to the Temple, but my heart is awake in the synagogues and the study houses. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 8): The theme of this month [Adar] is that even in sleep Israel are holy, since they are bound at their root to the Blessed One — as the Midrash says, "I am asleep from the commandments ... but my heart is awake to perform them ... where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? 'God is the rock of my heart.'" From the side of the Blessed One, "the voice of my beloved knocks, open for me": "my heart is awake" means that the Blessed One, the heart of Israel, rouses Israel from their sleep to perform the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): The Congregation of Israel boasts, "I am asleep but my heart is awake," which the Sages expounded as referring to the Holy One, blessed be He — "rock of my heart." Even when they are asleep from the commandments and have no "eyes," as in sleep when the eyes are shut and the heart is sunk in imaginings, since the root of the soul is a portion of God and the depths of the heart cleave to the Blessed One, all the imaginings too cleave to Him; even at the height of immersion in the imaginings of this world, which hide the truth, there remains in him a power of awakening to the Blessed One through the heart's cleaving to the living God.):
Yet in truth our Sages stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2):
"אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה מִן הַמִּצְווֹת כו' וְלִבִּי עֵר לַעֲשׂוֹתָן",
'I sleep from the commandments, etc., but my heart is awake to perform them,'

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת יז255 Berakhot 17a — After he had prayed, R. Alexandri would say: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will — and what prevents us? The yeast in the dough and subjection to the kingdoms. May it be Your will to deliver us from their hand, that we may return to perform the statutes of Your will with a whole heart. Rashi: "And what prevents us" — from doing Your will. "The yeast in the dough" — the evil inclination in our heart, which leavens us. Maharsha: He explains it after what Maimonides wrote in the Eight Chapters, that a man must keep to the middle path in his traits and his deeds. The evil inclination drives him to one extreme within what is permitted him — to be arrogant and to indulge in permitted desire — and is therefore likened to the leaven in the dough, which raises the dough and makes it more than its true measure; while subjection to the gentile kingdoms forces him to the opposite extreme, for they do not allow Israel to hold themselves up but abase them utterly and withhold from them every good, even what they need for the service of God. Thus "our will is to do Your will" — to walk the middle path — "and what prevents us?" These two, each pulling toward its own extreme; may it be Your will to subdue them before us and behind us, that is, both extremes, "that we may return" to walk in the middle. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 21): In Israel a thought that is not for its own sake comes only from the [evil] inclination, which accustoms one to seek his own pleasure in everything, but the depths of the hearts of the children of Israel are solely for the sake of Heaven, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." Hence, when there is an actual deed, that suffices to join it to the will in the depths of the heart, and no account is taken of the thought of the "yeast in the dough" that confuses it. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 1): The sign of the covenant testifies that the holy flesh of Israel does not desire evil, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will … and who prevents us …": this depth of will stems from our father Abraham, while the Torah is the spice against the [evil] inclination and the Land of Israel is the opposite of subjugation to the kingdoms. "Our will," the depth of the will, is freedom from the evil inclination and from subjugation; hence no exile came from Abraham's side, and the sufferings come only from the side of the inclination and the subjugation. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): Though Israel sank in exile into the forty-nine gates of impurity, this was a clarification before Him who examines hearts of the difference between the nations' immersion, which stems from the essence of their hearts, and Israel's, which comes only from their being mixed among the nations, whereas in the essence of their hearts "it is revealed and known that our will is to do [Your will]." The essence of Israel's hearts is not immersed in impurity at all, and from this side comes the redemption from the nations. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): Even the wicked of Israel are all righteous, just as all Israel are called circumcised, even one actually uncircumcised; so one who is wicked in deed is so only from the side of the [evil] inclination and not from his heart, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …," and as the Rambam explains the reason for coercing [a husband] until he says "I want." Though he is called wicked for his actual sin, even the sinners of Israel are full of regret, and there is no wicked Jew who does not regret for some moment once the pleasure has passed and the inclination no longer incites him, because of the depth of good in the depths of his heart. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 24): On Atzeres, the time of accepting the yoke of Torah and mitzvos, there is a mitzvah to give pleasure to the body as well, for the yoke is felt mainly by the body, whereas as for the soul, "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." By this we show that although for the body it is a yoke, it nevertheless rejoices in accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, of Torah and of mitzvos. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The holiness of the name Israel at the root of every Jew cannot be uprooted, and even if he multiplies sins it is all from the side of the "yeast in the dough" and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" that surround the root of Judaism, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …" Therefore he is compared to a myrtle standing among reeds: the sins are only in the reeds surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 263): The reason the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to the deed is that in truth "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God" and "the Lord's portion is His people," as it says, "It is revealed and known … and who prevents us …"; but in idolatry, where one denies [God], God forbid, even an evil thought is joined [to the deed]. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the depths of the heart "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will — and who prevents us …": even the hindrances in a heart that inclines to evil lie only in the revealed part of the heart, from the "yeast in the dough" that sits at the openings of the heart and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" — the thorns that surround the rose and clothe it, one from without and the other from within. But it is all only a garment and not the essence, which is the depth of his heart, where his essential vitality cleaves to the Blessed One..): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי",
and as they said (Berakhot 17a): 'It is revealed and known that our true will is to do Your will, but what hinders us? The leaven in the dough,'
כִּי אֲמִיתַּת נְקוּדַּת הָרָצוֹן דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק יֵצֶר הָרָע מְעַכֵּב.
for the true inner point of will is bound to Hashem, blessed be He, only the evil inclination deters.
וְטָעַן הָמָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מְחִיר לָתֵת נֶגֶד הַיְּהוּדִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ זֶה:
And Haman asserted that he had an equivalent price to tender counter to the Jews, claiming that he too possessed this spiritual power;
"כֶּסֶף" פֵּירוּשׁ רָצוֹן וְחֶמְדָּה,
for kesef (silver) signifies yearnful desire and longing (kosef),
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּכֶסֶף דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and as is known, silver is the spiritual rung of Abraham who is the inception of Israel's root,
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה.
and he alleged that he likewise shared this primal root.

וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו "פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי טָהוֹר אֲנִי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה256 Bereshit Rabbah 65:1 — “Esau was forty years old” — that is what is written: “The boar out of the wood ravages it” (Psalms 80:14). R. Pinchas in the name of R. Simon: Of all the prophets, only two publicized it [the character of the wicked kingdom] — Moses and Asaph. Moses said: “And the swine, because it parts the hoof”; Asaph said: “The boar out of the wood ravages it.” Why does he liken it to a pig? Because just as this pig, when it lies down, stretches out its hooves as if to say, “I am pure,” so this wicked kingdom robs and plunders, yet appears as though it were setting up the seat of judgment. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 3): No convert is accepted from Amalek, meaning that he cannot convert at all: even if he performs the commandments, and not in deed alone but even accepts in thought and will to be a complete Israelite, he is still called only one who "stretches out its hooves like a pig" to say "pure," for the deepest beginning and root of his thought and will, hidden even from himself, is certainly not so, and it is complete falsehood. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 24): So too Esau "stretches out his hooves like a pig": the pig has a sign of purity in its hooves, and of the two signs, which allude to deed and thought, the hooves correspond to deed; these he stretches out, for "the hunt was in his mouth" but not in his heart, saying "see, I am pure." Yet he is not even half pure; rather, whatever lacks the four signs is entirely impure. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 20): In deed, Esau too "stretches out his hooves like a pig," and Amalek is called "the first of nations" because only his deepest beginning is evil: he can stretch out his hooves through all nine levels that unfold from the deepest beginning of thought, appearing as though he too were good, yet his deepest beginning is utterly evil, and so he is wholly evil. With Israel it is the reverse: even one who has sinned, as the Sages said of Achan that he denied the entire Torah, still has his deepest beginning cleaving to the good, and so he is wholly good. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Toward this the preparation is the exile of Edom, of which the Sages said "it stretches out its hooves like a pig and says, I am pure." For the Giving of the Torah is a clarification over against Egypt, which was openly "flesh of donkeys," whereas Edom's revealed aspect is pure; therefore it came from Esau, born of Isaac, with whom holy flesh begins, and so the Sages called Esau "an apostate Israelite," except that he apostatized and became like a complete gentile. For the clarification always comes through its opposite, since in truth Edom is the one entirely lacking purity by birth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): From this side comes the hold of Esau, who "stretches out his hooves like a pig" (that is, his heel), and of whom the Sages said that he "sets up the tribunal," showing himself as righteous, for there are some light commandments among the nations. And although it is also true that "the kindness of the nations is a sin for them," since all they do is only for self-aggrandizement and to stretch out their hooves, nevertheless, from the standpoint of what is revealed in this world, it is not discernible.),
And this is the entire deceitful power of Esau 'extending his hooves, etc., claiming: I am pure' (Bereishit Rabbah 65),
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא טָהוֹר כְּמוֹהֶם.
alleging that he was just as unblemished as they.
וַ"עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים" – כִּי אֶלֶף הוּא מִסְפַּר הָרִיבּוּי
And he offered 'ten thousand'—because one thousand is the archetype of multitude,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן עַל פָּסוּק "נָתַתִּי אֶלֶף כֶּסֶף",
as the Ramban wrote on the verse 'I have given a thousand pieces of silver,'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל דָּבָר מִתְחַלֵּק לְעֶשֶׂר
and it is known that every entity is subdivided into ten,
וְנִמְצָא עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים תַּכְלִית רִיבּוּי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
so that ten thousand represents the absolute zenith of expansive perfection.
וַעֲמָלֵק בָּא בְּעֵת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַעֲלָה עֶלְיוֹנָה,
And Amalek attacked specifically when Israel stood at the highest spiritual pinnacle,
הָיָה פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפָיו לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא בְּמַעֲלָה כְּמוֹהֶם,
and his displaying of hooves was designed to assert that he too held a lofty rank equivalent to theirs,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק מד וּפְסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה יב257 Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 44 — R. Zecharyah says: Amalek was the grandson of Esau, and in his grandfather's enmity he came against them to take vengeance upon them. The pillar of cloud encircled the camp of Israel like a city surrounded by a wall, and no foe or enemy could reach them; only whoever required immersion would the cloud cast outside the camp of Israel, which was holy, and Amalek cut down and killed whatever was behind the cloud, as it is said, "and he cut off all the stragglers in your rear."):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 44; Pesikta Rabbati 12):
בָּא בְּכֹחוֹ שֶׁל זְקֵינוֹ וְכוּלֵי
