he arrived boasting in the power of his grandfather (Esau), etc.,
בְּהַשָּׂגָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
in intellect and human exertion;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיְזַנֵּב וְגוֹמֵר",
and as it is written (Deuteronomy 25:18): 'and he cut off the hindmost of you, etc.,'
וְכָל נִיצּוּחַ הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט,
and every spiritual triumph proceeds through strict judicial balance;
וַדַּאי הָיָה הוּא נָקִי בָּזֶה.
and he surely presented himself as blameless in this regard.
וּלְכָךְ מְנַצְּחוֹ הָיָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
Therefore his conqueror was Joshua from the seed of Joseph,
שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר.
who represents the foundational power of holy exertion and overcoming the base inclination.
וְנֶאֱמַר רַק "וַיַּחֲלֹשׁ", וְלֹא נִיצּוּחַ גָּמוּר,
Yet it is merely stated: 'And Joshua weakened (vayachalosh) Amalek,' not a total eradication,
רַק "לְפִי חָרֶב" – בְּפֶה שֶׁל הַחֶרֶב נָגַע בָּהֶם.
rather 'according to the edge of the sword'—touching them at the very mouth (peh) of the sword.
פֵּירוּשׁ: "פֶּה" הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
The explanation is: 'mouth' embodies the outward disclosure of that which is in the heart,
כִּי בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַיָּדַיִם אֵין נִיכָּר הִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב, רַק בַּפֶּה.
for through manual action alone the heart's inner motivation is not fully manifest, only through the mouth.
שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הֵם: בַּתּוֹרָה וּבַמִּצְווֹת;
There are two forms of spiritual exertion: in Torah and in mitzvot;
וּמִצְווֹת יֵשׁ בָּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
and superficial observance of mitzvot exists among idolaters to outward appearance,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י258 Bava Batra 10b — Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to them: Just as a sin-offering atones for Israel, so charity atones for the nations of the world. Ifra Hurmiz, the mother of King Shapur, sent four hundred dinars to R. Ami, and he did not accept them. She sent them to Rava, and he accepted them for the sake of peace with the kingdom. R. Ami heard and was angered. He said: Does he not hold with "When its boughs are withered they shall be broken off; women come and set them alight" (Isaiah 27:11)? And Rava — [he accepted] for the sake of peace with the kingdom. Rashi: "When its boughs are withered they shall be broken off" — when the merit they hold is used up and the sap of their acts of charity has dried out, then they are broken. Maharsha: On this exposition, "Righteousness exalts a nation" is said of the nations of the world as well, for the charity and kindness they perform is reckoned to them in place of the sin-offering of Israel. That is why this exposition does not cite "a nation — these are Israel, as it is written 'And who is like Your people Israel'" as the earlier Sages did.:) עַל פָּסוּק "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bava Batra 10b) on the verse 'when its boughs are withered,'
וּקְרָאוּם "מִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת",
and they designated these 'a few light commandments,'
כִּי הֵם קַלּוֹת מְאֹד לִדְחוֹתָם,
because they are exceedingly flimsy and easily cast aside,
לְפִי שֶׁעִיקַּר כֹּבֶד וִיקַר הַמִּצְוָה הוּא מִצַּד הַכַּוָּנָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב,
since the true weight and preciousness of a mitzvah derive from inward intention and heartfelt desire;
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם קְרוּיִים מִצְווֹת.
yet nevertheless they are termed mitzvot.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
However, Torah holds no connection to idolaters,

וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט259 Sanhedrin 59a — And R. Yochanan said: A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death, as it is stated: "Moses commanded us a Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob" (Deuteronomy 33:4) — an inheritance for us, and not for them. Rashi: "An inheritance" for us and not for them — so [his studying it] involves robbery, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain. Maharsha (on 58b, s.v. "a gentile who rests on the Sabbath"): Why should a gentile be liable to death precisely for these two things — resting on the Sabbath and engaging in Torah — which we are obligated to do? Because the Torah is called "betrothed" (as expounded in Pesachim, reading "inheritance" as "betrothed"): since most people do not engage in it, to them it is like a betrothed woman still in her father's house, while to one who engages in it, it is like a married wife and is called "his Torah." Gentiles have no category of a betrothed woman, so for a gentile, engaging in the Torah is as though he had relations with an Israelite's betrothed, for which he is judged under Israelite law. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 59a): Just as the Sabbath rest, which belongs to one who has reached actual completion, does not belong to the gentiles, so the supernal intellect [of the Torah] is not fitting for them, and they have no relation at all to that level. Therefore he is liable to death, for he has entered a level not fitting for him: when a gentile enters the level of the Torah, a level that is lacking and absent in him, he takes on privation, and so he is liable to death, which is privation. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): It seems to me that what they said in Sanhedrin, too, "A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death," refers to engaging in it in order to understand what is written in it, which is the Oral Torah; for all the words of the Written Torah are closed, and one who engages in it must interpret them, so that one cannot engage in the Written Torah at all without the Oral Torah. This is the "inheritance" and the "betrothed" of the congregation of Jacob alone, to whom the Torah is entirely handed over, whereas the Written Torah by itself was written on the stones in seventy languages..),
and an idolater who studies Torah is liable to death (Sanhedrin 59a),

וְ"הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם – אַל תַּאֲמֵן" (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי ב, ט260 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no Torah." If a man says to you, There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written, "I will destroy the wise out of Edom and understanding out of the mountain of Esau." [If he says,] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, as it is written, "Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it.).
and 'if one says to you: there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it' (Eichah Rabbah 2:9).
וְהָמָן הָיָה בְּעֵת שֵׁינָה מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
Now Haman attacked during a period of Israel's dormancy from active exertion;
וְ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" גַּם הוּא טַעֲנָתוֹ מִצַּד דְּגַם הוּא דָּבוּק בִּרְצוֹנוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and corresponding to 'one opposite the other,' his argument was framed claiming that he too was bound in his true desire to Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ כֵּן הוּא מִפְּנֵי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and that whatever fell short in him was solely due to the external evil inclination.
וְעַל זֶה נִתְחַיֵּיב מִטַּעַם עַכּוּ"ם שֶׁשָּׁבַת;
And on this premise he incurred guilt under the principle of an idolater who observes Shabbat;
כִּי דְּבֵיקוּת בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for essential cleaving without dependent exertion belongs exclusively to the children of Israel,
וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶם רַק שְׂכַר מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
whereas idolaters receive reward merely for superficial, light commandments, as mentioned above.
וְנִתְגַּלָּה בְּפוּרִים דְּ"נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא אֲשֶׁר וְגוֹמֵר",
And on Purim it was unveiled that 'it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over those who hated them,' (Esther 9:1),
שֶׁלִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ כֹּחַ, הֲגַם דִּישֵׁנִים מִמִּצְווֹת, דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
revealing that the children of Israel possess the intrinsic power that even when asleep from mitzvot, they remain cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ "סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים" –
And this is the secret of 'the end of all miracles'—
הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּבֵיקוּת זֶה שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה בְּפוּרִים,
the revelation of this ultimate cleaving which is unveiled on Purim,
דְּגַם אִם נִשְׁתַּקַּע כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקַּע עַד דְּלָא יָדַע לְגַמְרֵי,
that even if one has sunk as deeply as he may have sunk, reaching 'until he knows not' entirely,
וְתִינוֹק שֶׁנִּטְמַע בֵּין הָעַמִּים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יְדִיעַת בֵּית רַבּוֹ גַּם כֵּן –
and even a child captured among the nations who possesses no knowledge of his master's house—
אַף הוּא דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
he too remains completely bound unto Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה דָּבוּק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
for 'the end of action is bonded within the initial thought,'
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּ"נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן".
as is known: 'their end is wedged in their beginning.'

sections.en: Four Heavenly Gifts and Human Attainment

items.h: Wisdom, joy, success, and wealth reflect distinct heavenly gifts, clarifying what lies in human action and what depends upon divine assistance.

Seif 1 — Wisdom, Joy, Success, and Wealth
Heavenly gifts illuminate the boundary between human effort, revealed action, and the hidden assistance of Hashem.

p: אַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי עִנְיָנִים שֶׁל מַעֲלוֹת וַהֲנָאוֹת וּמַתָּנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם הֵם.
Four varieties of virtues, delights, and gifts belonging to man that are favorable gifts bestowed upon him from Heaven exist.
שְׁלֹשָׁה הֵם בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ,
Three reside within the person himself,
וְהֵם: חָכְמָה בַּמּוֹחַ,
and they are: wisdom in the brain,
וְשִׂמְחָה בַּלֵּב,
and joy in the heart,
וְהַצְלָחָה בִּכְלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בַּפּוֹעֵל, "כָּל אֲשֶׁר הוּא עֹשֶׂה ה' מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ".
and success in practical execution, 'all that he does Hashem makes to prosper in his hand.'

וְהֵם הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר261 Jeremiah 9:22-23 — “Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the mighty man glory in his might, nor the rich man glory in his riches. But let him that glories glory in this — that he understands and knows Me, that I am the Lord who exercises kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these things I delight, says the Lord.” Rashi: "Let not the wise man boast" — do not boast, saying, "We are wise"; you have rejected My words, so what wisdom have you? If you have understood and known Me, then you may boast of your wisdom. Radak: If there are wise men among you, let them not boast of their wisdom, for it will not avail them, since they did not know the Lord and did not walk in His ways; and so too the mighty, whose strength will not save them from death or from captivity, and the rich, whose wealth will not redeem them from the sword. He named these three because it is the way of the world that a man escapes by his cunning, or by his strength, or by ransoming himself with his money — and the prophet tells them that by these three they will not be saved. Metzudas Dovid: Let not the wise man boast, for he cannot save himself by his wisdom, nor the mighty man by his might, nor can the rich man redeem himself with his wealth; there is nothing in these to boast of, since no benefit will come to them from them. "But in this let him that boasts boast" — in understanding and knowing Me, that I am the Lord and there is none besides Me, and that I am the one who does kindness to those who love Me and keep My commandments, judgment to exact payment from the wicked, and righteousness to receive those who return. Malbim: Let no man boast of wisdom, might or wealth, for none of them will help him if the Lord has decreed evil against him. But a man may boast of them when he uses them as instruments for a worthy end — his wisdom "to understand and know Me, that I am the Lord," and his might and his wealth "to do kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth," doing justice for the oppressed by his might and kindness and charity by his wealth — "for in these I delight," these being the end I seek.",
And these correspond to the three concerning which Scripture states: 'Let not the wise man glory, etc.,'

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נִדָּה טז262 Niddah 16b — R. Chanina bar Pappa expounded: The angel appointed over conception is named Night. He takes the drop and sets it before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says before Him: Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop? Mighty or weak? Wise or foolish? Rich or poor? But "wicked or righteous" he does not say — in accordance with R. Chanina, who said: All is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, as it is stated: "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear Him." Rashi: “Everything is in the hands of Heaven” — all a man's qualities and all that befalls him come upon him by the decree of the King, except this one. “But to fear” — this alone He asks of you, because everything else is in His hand and this is in yours. Tosafos (s.v. “the angel appointed over conception”): But over birth no angel is appointed, as is said at the beginning of Ta'anit: three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He — of a woman in childbirth, of rain, and of the resurrection of the dead. Even those three keys are at times handed over to an agent for a time, for Elijah held the key of rain and revived the dead, and so did Elisha and many righteous men; and even Beri, who is the prince of rain, acts only by the permission of the Holy One, blessed be He. Tosafos (s.v. “everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven”): In “Elu Na'arot” it is said that everything is in the hands of Heaven except cold and heat. Here the statement concerns a man's nature and his traits, while there it concerns the things that befall him, such as illnesses and calamities, all of which are decreed upon him and against which he cannot guard himself — except cold and heat, against which he can guard himself. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “this drop, what shall become of it — mighty or weak, wise [or foolish]”): This is the meaning of the verse “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom”: what is compelled is neither praised nor blamed, and therefore these three — wisdom, might and wealth — which are compelled by the decree from the hour of a man's formation, are no ground for glorying. “But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me” — for that is the thing which depends upon his choice. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 16b): He is called Night because the gestation takes place in the woman's belly, “like the bones in the womb of her that is with child,” and the child is there in darkness. Therefore the angel appointed over gestation is called Night, since in the belly it is always night and never day. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part I 4): "If you have learned much Torah, do not claim credit for yourself" [as if] you were better than others, "for that is why you were created," as stated in Niddah: "wise or foolish." And so the early authorities explained "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom … but let him who glories glory in this," in keeping with what is said there: "righteous or wicked he does not say." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The Sages said that "children, life and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal," for these three comprise all of a man's needs in this world, and this is decreed at the beginning of his formation: "wise or foolish" — and "wisdom gives life to those who possess it," so from it life is drawn; "mighty or weak" — from this come children, "like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth"; "rich or poor" is the flow of sustenance. But "righteous or wicked," which is a matter of merit, he did not say. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The Sages said "You created righteous, You created wicked," yet they said "righteous or wicked he does not say"; but in truth "a gourd is known by its shoot," and one can recognize even in children that some are formed from the outset with a good nature, to walk in innocence and uprightness, and some the opposite, and this falls under "wise or foolish," for the intent is not human wisdom but the wisdom of truth, to conduct oneself as is fitting. This has nothing to do with the choice between righteous and wicked: even one created righteous has an inclination that overpowers him every day, and the choice is his, and one created wicked likewise has the choice to subdue the inclination of heart he was born with and return to the Blessed One.:):
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Niddah 16b):
דְּנִגְזַר בִּשְׁעַת יְצִירָה: "טִיפָּה זוֹ חָכָם אוֹ טִפֵּשׁ, וְעָשִׁיר אוֹ עָנִי" –
that at the moment of conception it is decreed: 'Shall this drop become wise or foolish, wealthy or impoverished?'—
הַיְינוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזּוֹ עִיקַּר עֲשִׁירוּת,
meaning the joy within the heart, which is the very essence of true wealth,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד)263 Pirkei Avot 4:1 — Ben Zoma said: Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion, as it is stated: "When you eat the labor of your hands, you are happy and it is well with you" (Psalms 128:2) — "you are happy" in this world, "and it is well with you" in the World to Come. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): The "rich" [on whom prophecy rests] is rich in deeds, and "Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion" means that the perfection of deeds is in the hand of the Omnipresent, and "poor or rich" is pronounced at the beginning of formation; therefore one should not seek great things but be content with what God has apportioned him. It says "rejoices" because joy is drawn from wisdom; and the Gemara's wording, "one who has satisfaction of spirit in his wealth," speaks of the spirit, which is in the heart, the seat of choice, and therefore it says "in his wealth," whereas regarding wisdom it says "in his portion," which God apportioned him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 6): In this world there is no satiety, as it is written, "He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver"; but "sated with favor" [said of Naftali] means that the Blessed One bestows favor [ratzon] upon him, and thereby he is sated. So the Sifrei teaches that Naftali was happy with his portion, and the Gemara says, "Who is rich? Whoever has satisfaction in his wealth," which Rashi explains as one happy with his portion, in the language of the Mishnah in Avos, "Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): [David called himself poor though he was very rich, for] the intent is not physical poverty: the Sages already said, "Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion," and there is a poor man who rejoices in his portion, delights in it and lacks nothing, and this is the trait of the pious of Israel such as King David, to whom poverty does not apply at all. But the wicked, even when they are rich, are not at ease, for "one who has a maneh wants two hundred," and they are very poor. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Anthology, Jeremiah 9; from Tiferes Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Chagigah 5): The verse "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, let not the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches" is not speaking of matters of this world; rather, "Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination," and "Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion," that is, whose soul is content with it, and the wise is one whose heart is illuminated by the light of Torah. Yet a person should not glory in this or take any power to himself from it: the one who rejoices in his portion should recognize well that this power is illuminated to him by the Blessed One.: "אֵיזֶהוּ עָשִׁיר? הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ",
as they stated (Avot 4:1): 'Who is wealthy? He who rejoices in his portion,'
וְאִם יַרְבֶּה כַּחוֹל כֶּסֶף וְאֵין לוֹ שִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב, הוּא קָרוּי עָנִי,
and if a person amasses silver like the sand yet lacks gladness of heart, he is termed poor;

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח דִּתְרוּמוֹת264 Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:4 — R. Yochanan said: I have been robbed by the men of Kanya. He went up to the study hall, and R. Simeon ben Lakish put a question to him and he did not answer; he put it to him again and he did not answer. He said to him: What is this? He said to him: All the limbs depend upon the heart, and the heart depends upon the purse. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "I have been robbed by the men of Kanya"): "The men of Kanya" was the name of the brigands who plundered and robbed R. Yochanan of what was his. He entered the study hall, and Reish Lakish put a matter of law to him and he did not answer, and asked him again and he did not answer; he said to him, Why are you sunk in such distress? — and he answered, All the limbs depend upon the heart, and the heart upon the purse; and then he told him, I have been robbed by these men of Kanya, and they have taken all my money. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Ahavas Hashem 1): When a man loses his money his understanding is thereby taken from him, as they said: a man's heart is bound up with his purse — for a man's understanding is drawn after his money, since it is his money that gives him his continuance. This is why Scripture says "with all your might," that is, with all your money: even if He takes your money from you, and that is for you the loss of understanding, [you are to love Him still].):
and likewise they said (Yerushalmi Terumot 8:12):
"לִבָּא בְּכִיסָא תַּלְיָא",
'The heart depends upon the purse,'
דְּשַׁלְוַות הַלֵּב תָּלוּי בַּעֲשִׁירוּת.
meaning the tranquility of the heart depends upon wealth.
"וְגִבּוֹר אוֹ חַלָּשׁ" –
'And mighty or weak'—
הַיְינוּ שַׁלְוַות כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, דְּהַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּפּוֹעַל.
this refers to the ease of the instruments of action, since might is expressed through physical deed.
וְאָמַר: "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר",
And Scripture states: 'Let not the wise man glory, etc.,'
דְּהַכֹּל בִּגְזֵירָה;
for all these three are preordained by divine decree;
"כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל וְגוֹמֵר" –
'but let him that glories glory in this, etc.'—
הַיְינוּ צַדִּיק אוֹ רָשָׁע דְּלָא קָאָמַר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם).
referring to righteousness or wickedness, which the angel does not declare (as noted there in Niddah).
וְאֵינוֹ דָּבָר מְחוּדָּשׁ,
Nor is this an isolated novelty;
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה "הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדוֹעַ אוֹתִי":
rather, Scripture means to say regarding these three: 'that he understands and knows Me'—
הֶחָכָם בְּחָכְמָתוֹ מַכִּיר וְיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that the wise man in his wisdom recognizes and knows that his wisdom originates from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְכֵן כֻּלָּם –
and likewise across all three virtues—
אָז יוּכַל לְהִתְהַלֵּל.
only then can he legitimately glory.
כִּי בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע,
For in each of these facets there exists a righteous manifestation and a wicked one,
דְּאֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה כּוֹלְלִים כָּל קוֹמַת אָדָם:
since these three encompass the entire stature of man:
בְּחָכְמָה יֵשׁ חָכָם בַּתּוֹרָה וְיֵשׁ חָכָם לְהָרַע;
in wisdom there is one wise in Torah, and there is one wise to do evil;
וְכֵן בְּשִׂמְחַת הַלֵּב יֵשׁ שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה וְעָשִׁיר בְּדַעַת,
and likewise in joy of the heart there is the joy of a mitzvah and being rich in spiritual understanding,
וְשִׂמְחָה שֶׁל הוֹלֵלוּת וְתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁמְּמַלֵּא כָּל חֲמוּדוֹתָיו בְּעָשְׁרוֹ;
and there is the joy of frivolity and base lusts wherein one indulges all earthly desires with his wealth;
וְכֵן בִּגְבוּרָה יֵשׁ הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ,
and so too in might there is he who conquers his evil inclination,
וְיֵשׁ גְּבוּרַת כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה.
and there is the destructive might of wrath and murder.
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה כְּתָרִים,
And these correspond to the three crowns,

"וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם265 Pirkei Avot 4:13 — R. Shimon says: There are three crowns — the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood and the crown of kingship; and the crown of a good name rises above them all." (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה יג):
'and the crown of a good name surpasses them all' (Avot 4:13):
דְּשֵׁם טוֹב הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִיד עָלָיו שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם,
for a good name represents that which Hashem, blessed be He, testifies regarding him that his intention is directed purely toward Heaven,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "רְאוּ קָרָאתִי בְשֵׁם וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written (Exodus 31:2): 'See, I have called by name, etc.,'

שֶׁלָּמְדוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (נה266 Berakhot 55a — R. Yochanan said: Three things the Holy One, blessed be He, proclaims Himself, and these are they: famine, plenty, and a good leader. Famine — as it is written, "For the Lord has called for a famine." Plenty — as it is written, "And I will call for the corn and will increase it." A good leader — as it is written, "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: See, I have called by name Bezalel." Maharsha: "Calling" in its literal sense, as in "And the Lord called to Moses," cannot be said of something that does not hear, such as the famine or the grain; and as for Bezalel, since we do not find that he was a prophet or that the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with him, "See, I have called by name" cannot be literal either. They therefore explained it in the sense of a proclamation, as in "a voice says: Proclaim" and "a voice proclaims in the wilderness" — the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself proclaims, so that the matter should stand firm and not be changed. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 4): [Explaining why the Holy One, blessed be He, weeps over a leader who lords it over the community:] Nothing is as close to the Blessed Name as the Torah, and likewise the leader who must guide the community, for he is the emissary of the Blessed Name; therefore they said in Tractate Berakhos that the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself proclaims the leader who guides the community. From this you see that the governance of one who is leader over the community belongs to the Blessed Name Himself, who governs all creatures, and the leader who governs is His emissary..):
which they deduced in the chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 55a):
מִזֶּה דְּפַרְנָס טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְמַנֶּה.
from this, that a worthy leader is personally appointed by the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְשֵׁם טוֹב וְכָבוֹד הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְמַנֶּה,
And a good name and honor represent that which Hashem, blessed be He, assigns,
שֶׁהוּא מֵעִיד שֶׁרָאוּי לְכָבוֹד כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא:
wherein He bears witness that each individual is deserving of honor according to what he is:
יֵשׁ מְכֻבָּד מִצַּד חָכְמָתוֹ
there is one honored on account of his wisdom,
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד עָשְׁרוֹ וְהוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת,
and there is one honored on account of his wealth, which is the crown of kingship,
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד גְּבוּרָתוֹ וְהוּא כֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה.
and there is one honored on account of his spiritual might, which is the crown of priesthood and divine service.
וְהַכָּבוֹד הוּא הַמַּעֲלָה וּמַתָּנָה הָרְבִיעִית,
And honor is the fourth virtue and gift,
וְהִיא אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ,
and it does not originate from within the person himself,
רַק מִצַּד הַזּוּלַת שֶׁחוֹלְקִין לוֹ כָּבוֹד.
rather from others who accord him honor.
וְכָל כָּבוֹד הוּא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ מִצַּד אֶחָד מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה מַעֲלוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר אוֹ מִצַּד כֻּלָּם,
And all honor necessarily stems from one of the three aforementioned virtues or from all of them together;
וְזֶהוּ "עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם",
and this is why it 'surpasses them all'—
כִּי אֵינָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ רַק עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם,
because it does not stand independently but rests directly upon them,
וְהוּא עוֹלֶה עֲלֵיהֶם כִּי זוּלַת זֶה אֵין הֵם מַעֲלוֹת כְּלָל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and it surpasses them, for without this divine honor they are not true virtues at all, as noted above.
וְהֵם תְּלָת אֲבָהָן,
And these three correspond to the three Patriarchs,
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֶגֶל רְבִיעִי שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה
and King David, peace be upon him, is the fourth leg of the divine Chariot
כִּי הוּא זָכָה לְשֵׁם טוֹב,
for he merited the crown of a good name,
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר מִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
which is the primary essence of the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty),

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם נח267 Berakhot 58a — The Sages taught: One who sees the Sages of Israel says, "Blessed... Who has shared of His wisdom with those who fear Him"; the sages of the nations of the world, he says, "Blessed... Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood." One who sees the kings of Israel says, "Blessed... Who has shared of His glory with those who fear Him"; the kings of the nations of the world, he says, "Blessed... Who has given of His glory to flesh and blood." Maharsha: Of the Sages of Israel he says "Who has shared of His wisdom," for they are the portion of His inheritance, and it is as though He shares with them His own wisdom, which is the wisdom of the Torah; He calls them "those who fear Him" in accordance with the teaching that one whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures. But to the sages of the nations He does not share the wisdom of the Torah; He gives them only a worldly wisdom. So too with glory: of the kings of Israel he says "Who has shared of His glory," which is the true glory, since "there is no glory but Torah," and that He shared with those who fear Him; whereas to the kings of the nations He gives a worldly glory. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 14): The difference between the two blessings is that the language of "giving" implies that what is given is not of the very substance of the wisdom that belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He. Of the nations one says "Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood," for it is insofar as they are flesh and blood, material, that He bestowed wisdom upon them, and this is not of the truth of God's wisdom, which is separate and divine; but upon Israel He bestowed the supernal, divine wisdom..):
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Berakhot 58a):
שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עַל הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר.
that over a monarch we recite the blessing: 'Who has imparted of His glory, etc.'
אֲבָל כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת שֶׁמִּצַּד עַצְמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, מִצַּד הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
However, the crown of royalty that originates from within the person himself, from the joy in the heart,
זֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
this is the spiritual rung of our father Jacob, peace be upon him.
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּפוּרִים: "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשֹׂן וִיקָר",
And this was manifest on Purim: 'For the Jews there was light and gladness, and joy and honor' (Esther 8:16);
הֵם כָּל אַרְבָּעָה כְּתָרִים הַלָּלוּ:
these represent all four of these crowns:

"אוֹרָה" – זוֹ תוֹרָה (מְגִילָּה טז:)268 Megillah 16b — "The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor." Rav Yehuda said: "Light" — this is Torah, and so it says: "For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light." "Gladness" — this is the festival, and so it says: "And you shall rejoice on your festival." "Joy" — this is circumcision, and so it says: "I rejoice over Your word." "Honor" — these are the phylacteries, and so it says: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you." And it is taught in a baraita: R. Eliezer the Great says: These are the phylacteries of the head. Rashi: "Light — this is Torah": Haman had decreed against them that they should not occupy themselves with Torah, and he had decreed against all of these as well; now they took the festivals upon themselves once more. "I rejoice over Your word" is circumcision, which was given with a "saying" and not with a "speaking" — "And God said to Abraham: And you shall keep My covenant"; and we find that David rejoiced over it, for when he was in the bathhouse and saw himself without Torah and without commandments, as soon as he looked at his circumcision he rejoiced. Maharsha: By the plain sense the verse should have read "there was light" [in the masculine], as in "there was light in their dwellings"; since it says "there was orah" in the feminine, they expounded it of the Torah, which is everywhere spoken of in the feminine. Certain commandments serve as a sign and a testimony for Israel — the Sabbath, the phylacteries [and circumcision] — and Haman decreed against these in particular because they are Israel's testimony, so that when his decree was annulled these testimonies returned to their former state. "Gladness" is the festival, which is a day of rest, and they turned from mourning to a festival; "joy" is circumcision, to which they returned, as "many of the peoples of the land became Jews"; and "honor" is the phylacteries, the glory of Israel, to which they returned, as "the fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them." Maharal (Gevuros Hashem 39): R. Eliezer said specifically "the phylacteries of the head" because the phylacteries of the arm express the binding and cleaving of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, and where there is cleaving there is no fear. But in the phylacteries of the head there is no binding, only that His name is called upon them — and in being called "the God of Israel" He is set apart from them, and on that side there is fear, for it is fitting to fear the God of Israel, to whom belongs might. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Through the outpouring of wrath upon Haman — for "it is a joy to the righteous to do justice" — [Esther] drew down for the Jews "light and gladness": "light — this is Torah," the Oral Torah, which is a great light emerging from within the darkness; and "gladness" is the joy of the righteous in the Lord, their stronghold in a time of trouble, when the trouble, the dross of the judgments, is turned into strength and might. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 4): "The Jews had light" — this is the illumination of the yesod of Abba, which is called Torah; and "gladness — this is the festival," the sanctity of the times, which Israel sanctify: by virtue of Purim, the clothing of His wisdom in the Written Torah within the Congregation of Israel, the festival that Israel sanctify becomes holy like the Sabbath, which is fixed and established and sanctified by the Blessed One, for all is one; and from the sanctity of Purim comes an addition of joy to every festival. "And joy — this is circumcision": the sanctity of the yesod, in guarding the covenant. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): Israel is sanctified with three sanctities, rooted in "You shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy": their own, through the awakening from below; the sanctity rooted in the Patriarchs; and the sanctity from above, from the Blessed One; and after the miracle all three were revealed. "Light — this is Torah" and "gladness — this is the festival" revealed Israel's own sanctity, for they engaged in Torah and mitzvos and "accepted it anew in the days of Ahasuerus," and the festival is the sanctity of time, which Israel sanctify — for although they did not accept Purim as a festival with a prohibition of labor, its joy and mitzvos fall at a time fixed by the month, which Israel sanctify. "Joy — this is circumcision" revealed the sanctity that comes from the Patriarchs, and "honor — these are the tefillin" revealed Israel's sanctity from the side of the Blessed One, for they are bound at the root. Sod Yesharim (Purim 1): On this day the Blessed One revealed openly to Israel the light of all the things that Amalek denies. "Gladness — this is the festival": the festivals are called "the face of the Lord," for just as a face attests to all the limbs of the body, so at the time of a festival one can recognize all that the Blessed One seeks of a person, since in those days there is a straight path for every individual soul that seeks the Lord to reach what is sought of it; and Amalek denies this, saying that in this world there can be no straight path to recognizing the light of His will. בְּמִקְרָא מְגִילָּה
"'Light'—this is Torah (Megillah 16b), embodied in the public reading of the Megillah,
דְּנִקְרֵאת אֱמֶת כַּאֲמִיתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה,
which is termed Truth like the ultimate veracity of the Torah,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם269 Megillah 16b — "Words of peace and truth." R. Tanchum said, and some say R. Assi said: This teaches that it requires ruled lines, like the truth of the Torah [a Torah scroll]. Rashi: "Like the truth of the Torah" — like a Torah scroll itself; the requirement of ruled lines is a law given to Moses at Sinai. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 9:30): Ruled lines signify the complete straightness of the book written with them, and this befits the Torah alone, for the Torah is complete straightness and never departs from it — whereas the Prophets, which tell of the kindness God, blessed be He, does beyond the line of strict law, need no ruling. But in the Megillah, Haman sought to destroy Israel entirely, and God would certainly not allow them to be destroyed, since they have the Torah on which the world stands; Haman's downfall was therefore sheer straightness, a peace in which there is truth. Hence it needs ruled lines "like the truth of the Torah," for there is no truth greater than the Torah, all of whose words are truth and straightness. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 32): No Divine Name is written anywhere in the Megillah, for the Name of Heaven was not revealed to the eye; nevertheless it "requires ruled lines like the truth of the Torah," for the Torah too was given scroll by scroll, the meaning of megillah being the revelation of words of wisdom. The Torah issues from the yesod of Abba, the influx of wisdom, while the Megillah is the yesod of Abba entering the Nukva and emerging from it — the Blessed One's wisdom entering the hearts of Israel and revealed from within the hearts of the Sages of Israel.):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (there):
שֶׁאָז יֵשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת חָכְמַת אֱמֶת בְּמוֹחַ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that then occurs the disclosure of true wisdom within the intellect of the children of Israel.
"וְשִׂמְחָה" – זוֹ יוֹם טוֹב,
"'Gladness'—this is Yom Tov (the festival),"

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (שָׁם ה270 Megillah 5b — Rabbah son of Rava said: Even if you say that he planted on his own day of Purim — they accepted upon themselves eulogy and fasting, but labor they did not accept upon themselves. For at first it is written, "gladness and feasting and a festival day," and at the end it is written, "to make them days of feasting and gladness," while "a festival day" is not written. Rashi: Our reading is “Even if you say it was on his own day”: Rabbi planted on the very day on which his townsmen read the Megillah. As for your difficulty from “a festival day,” on which labor is forbidden — the verse “gladness and feasting and a festival day” is written at the outset, before they accepted the days upon themselves; but when they accepted them they accepted only gladness and feasting, so as to forbid eulogy and fasting, while “a festival day” they did not accept upon themselves. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): "Gladness — this is a festival day" is also the holiness of the festival, the holiness of time, which Israel sanctifies; and although "a festival day," as regards the prohibition of labor, "they did not accept upon themselves," as stated in Megillah 5b, nevertheless the joy and the mitzvos practiced on Purim fall at a fixed time of the month, which Israel sanctifies, since they intercalate the months.:):
yet our Rabbis of blessed memory noted (Megillah 5b):
"יוֹם טוֹב לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ",
"'The prohibition of labor on Yom Tov they did not accept upon themselves,'
וְלָכֵן פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י עַל יָמִים טוֹבִים אֲחֵרִים,
and therefore Rashi explained that this refers to the reaffirmation of other biblical festivals;
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת:
and both interpretations are truth:
כִּי יוֹם טוֹב בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב אֵינוֹ רָצָה לוֹמַר הַשִּׂמְחָה בַּלֵּב בִּלְבַד,
for 'Yom Tov' in biblical terminology does not signify joy in the heart alone,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ "שִׂמְחָה וְגוֹמֵר",
for Scripture explicitly enumerates 'gladness, etc.',
וְיוֹם טוֹב עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּיוֹם טוֹב אֵינוֹ עַל הַשִּׂמְחָה לְבַד, רַק עַל מְנִיעַת עֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה.
and Yom Tov perforce does not denote gladness alone, but the active cessation of performing creative labor.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים יוֹם טוֹב הַיְינוּ עַל הַשִּׂמְחָה בִּלְבַד,
In contrast, in rabbinic idiom, 'Yom Tov' refers directly to pure rejoicing,

כְּמוֹ (שַׁבָּת קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א, וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)271 Shabbat 119a — Abaye said: May [reward] come to me, for when I see a young scholar who has completed his tractate, I make a festive day for the Rabbis. Rashi: "Who has completed his tractate": who has studied it through. "I make a festive day for the Rabbis": for the students — he was head of the academy. Maharsha: He speaks first of "a young scholar" and then of a festive day "for the Rabbis": when he saw even one student — surely one of few — who had learned a whole tractate thoroughly, he made a festive day for all the Rabbis, as though he saw that all of them had learned thoroughly to the end. A support for such a feast is the Midrash that a feast is made at the completion of the Torah; hence it is called a siyum ("completion"), since it requires that he have completed the tractate. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 118b): On the whole series of sayings "May [reward] come to me": all these sages mean that a person should be careful and zealous in at least one mitzvah, for through it he acquires a supernal reward — since a person stands at half merits and half liabilities, everything hangs on the one mitzvah that tips the balance. Each says "May [reward] come to me" because he fulfilled this particular mitzvah properly, so that it is performed in the world as it ought to be, and that is a reward in itself. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 9): On "I make a good day for the Rabbis" (Shabbat 119a; Kiddushin 31a), which Rashi explains as a feast: its meaning is that through the joy of a mitzvah in the feast, for completing a tractate, or for hearing that the halacha follows R. Yehuda and later that it does not, they had the power to bring holiness into the meal, so that whoever ate would sense the light "that it was good." This is what "good day" signifies: "day" is light, as in "And God called the light day," and "good" as in "And God saw the light, that it was good.": "עֲבִידְנָא יוֹמָא טָבָא לְרַבָּנַן",
as in (Shabbat 119a and other sources): 'I will make a festive day for the Rabbis,'
דְּוַדַּאי אֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה.
where it certainly does not imply an abstention from work.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַכָּתוּב הוּא דָּבָר הַמְּפוֹרָשׁ לַכֹּל,
And this is because Scripture deals with that which is explicit to all,
וְיוֹם טוֹב מְפוֹרָשׁ הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִגְלֶה עַל כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה;
and an explicit Yom Tov means that sanctity is visibly enacted upon the instruments of practical action;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ,
whereas the words of the Sages in the Oral Torah pertain to that which is unwritten,
יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְפוֹרָשׁ.
so their Yom Tov is that which is internal rather than explicitly visible.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תְּחִלָּה "וְיוֹם טוֹב",
And this explains why the Megillah initially wrote 'and a Yom Tov,'
רַק דְּלָא קַבִּילוּ,
only that they did not accept the cessation of labor,
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא עָלָה אֶל לְבָבָם דָּבָר רֵיק שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְקַבֵּל
and certainly there did not enter their holy thoughts an empty suggestion unworthy of acceptance,
וְגַם לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְהַזְכִּיר זֶה בַּמְּגִילָּה.
nor would it have been fitting to record such a failure in the sacred Megillah;
רַק דְּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא יוֹם טוֹב מִצַּד הַחֲכָמִים,
rather in internal truth it truly is a Yom Tov from the perspective of the Sages,
דְּאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם רֹאשׁ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the Men of the Great Assembly are the leaders of Israel's sages as is known,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם וְהַחָכְמָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹם טוֹב בְּשִׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
meaning from the perspective of concealment and wisdom, it possesses the essential root of Yom Tov in internal heartfelt joy.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי בְּפֵירוּשׁ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, from the perspective of overt, visible revelation to all Israel,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין סו.)272 Kiddushin 66a — Elazar ben Po'ira said to King Yannai: If you heed my counsel, crush them. [Yannai] said: But what will become of the Torah? [He replied:] It lies rolled up in a corner — whoever wishes to study, let him come and study. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Immediately heresy was injected into him, for he should have said: That is well for the Written Torah, but what of the Oral Torah? Rashi: "Crush them" means: kill them. "But what will become of the Torah?" — perhaps it will be forgotten; and he answered him that the Torah scroll lies rolled up with the commandments in it, so they will not be forgotten. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): In this too Elazar misled the king, for the king himself surely needs the crown of Torah, and by this counsel he would be leaving it to others. And Rav Nachman said that heresy was immediately injected into him, because even on the terms of that deception the answer holds only for the Written Torah — but what of the Oral Torah, of which others too would then know nothing? עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב: "כְּתוּבָה וּמוּנַּחַת",
along the lines of what they said (Kiddushin 66a) regarding the Written Torah: 'it is written and lying open,'
דְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב נִגְלֶה לַכֹּל וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לַחֲכָמִים,
meaning that what is explicitly written is manifest to everyone without requiring sages,
וְלִהְיוֹת יוֹם טוֹב מְגוּלֶּה לַכֹּל – זֶה לֹא הָיָה;
and to be an overtly evident Yom Tov to all—this was not appropriate;
כִּי נֵס דְּפוּרִים הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם מְלוּבָּשׁ בְּדַרְכֵי הַטֶּבַע,
because the miracle of Purim occurred in hiddenness, enclothed in the natural order,
רַק שֶׁהַחֲכָמִים וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ שֶׁהוּא נֵס גָּמוּר וּגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה,
such that only the sages and insightful thinkers understand that it was a total miracle and complete redemption,
אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה בְּגִילּוּי גָּמוּר לְעֵין כָּל בָּשָׂר.
yet it was not overtly revealed before the eyes of all flesh.
וּלְכָךְ יוֹם טוֹב זֶה נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "שִׂמְחָה".
Therefore, this unique Yom Tov is designated in biblical phrasing as 'simchah' (gladness).
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן קִיּוּם יָמִים טוֹבִים הָאֲחֵרִים כְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י,
And this also accounts for the reaffirmation of the other festivals as Rashi explained,
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר בִּזְמַנּוֹ אָז הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
for each matter in its appointed season is in manifest revelation,
וּמִקּוֹדֶם הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם מוֹשֵׁךְ אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה,
while beforehand it draws down that holiness in concealment,
כְּמוֹ בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִשַּׁבָּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
just as during the six working days vitality is drawn from the permanently established sanctity of Shabbat.
וּבְכָל הֶחֳדָשִׁים מִיּוֹם טוֹב הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי, דְּהַיְינוּ עוֹנֶג וְשִׂמְחָה,
And across all months, the sanctity sanctified by Israel is drawn from Yom Tov—namely divine delight and joy;
וּבְיוֹם טוֹב הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ
and on Yom Tov itself it is explicit,
וּבְכָל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כָּל שִׂמְחָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מִקְּדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב.
whereas throughout the year all joy experienced by man is drawn directly from the sanctity of Yom Tov.
וּבְפוּרִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה דְּהַמְשָׁכַת הַשִּׂמְחָה מִיּוֹם טוֹב,
And on Purim occurs the overt revelation of this drawing forth of joy from Yom Tov,
וְהוּא קִיּוּם יָמִים טוֹבִים אֲחֵרִים.
and that is the spiritual fulfillment of the other festivals.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ,
And this is actualized through sending portions one to his fellow,
דְּזֶהוּ דֶּרֶךְ שִׂמְחָה וְשַׁלְוַות הַלֵּב.
which is the authentic way of joy and inner peace of the heart.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שִׂמְחַת אֱמֶת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ לוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן לְהַהֲנוֹת מֵחֶלְקוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים,
And this is the core of authentic joy: when one possesses a generous eye to give pleasure to others from his own allotted portion,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן צַר עַיִן אֵין קָרוּי עָשִׁיר כְּלָל,
whereas a stingy, narrow-eyed person is not termed rich at all,
כִּי אֵין שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעֵינוֹ צָרָה בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים.
since he does not rejoice in his portion because his eye is grudging toward what belongs to others.
"וְשָׂשׂוֹן" – זוֹ מִילָה,
"'And joy (sason)'—this is circumcision (milah),"
הוּא הַהַצְלָחָה בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר,
which represents success in practical action through subduing the evil inclination;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִצְוַת הַמִּילָה שֶׁעָלֶיהָ אָמַר דָּוִד: "שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
and this is the root of the commandment of circumcision, concerning which David proclaimed: 'I rejoice at Your word, etc.' (Psalms 119:162),
שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה קְרוּיָה אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
for uncircumcision is designated solely by the name of idolaters,

אֲבָל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְרוּיִים נִימּוֹלִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נְדָרִים לא273 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along.:)
while all of Israel are termed circumcised (as written in Nedarim 31b),
כִּי כֻּלָּם גִּבּוֹרֵי כֹּחַ עוֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ;
for all are mighty warriors executing His command;
כִּי גַּם רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם רַק מַרְשִׁיעִים כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since even the sinners of Israel only do wickedness in accordance with Hashem's mysterious plan,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר לֶעָתִיד [אַחַר תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה]
as will be clarified in the ultimate future (after repentance out of love),

שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲטָאִים כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פט274 Shabbat 89b — "If your sins be as scarlet" — why the plural form, when the singular would be expected? R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins be like these years, which are ordered and come one after another from the six days of creation until now, "they shall be white as snow." Rashi: "It should have said ka-shani" [in the singular] — parallel to "as snow," for it does not say "as snows." Maharsha: "Like these years that are ordered" refers to the multitude of sin — as many as the years, presumably the years that have run in order since the six days of creation. One cannot read ka-shanim as "like two years," the minimal plural, for what novelty would there be in two sins? We say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah that He removes the first [sin] first, so for two sins "they shall be white as snow" would not be needed. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 89b): Sin is open to atonement because it is committed by accident, and the accidental does not annul what a person is in essence; but sins committed in great number and constantly are no longer accidental, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, says that even if your sins are ordered and fixed like these years, they shall be white as snow. Nothing is more fixed and ordered than the years, which have run so since the six days of creation, yet even they will cease, since the world is physical and will end in destruction; so too Israel's sins, though fixed on the side of the physical, can be removed, because Israel's essential level is not physical. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 19): The holiness of Tisha B'Av in the future, when it becomes a festival, will not come from Israel's sanctifying it, for on the contrary they sinned and made it a day of calamity, but only because in the future "your sins will be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," as stated in Shabbos 89b: then "they shall be white as snow" and be turned into merits, through this, that such was the will of the Blessed One from the six days of creation. Thus the essence of its holiness is only that this was the Blessed One's will at the beginning of creation, a holiness fixed and abiding like the holiness of Shabbos, except that it is revealed only in the future, after the rectification. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): "The scarlet [shanim] shall be white as snow" means that the scarlet of holiness, too, will be whitened, after they lift their eyes to the Blessed One, as stated in Shabbos there; and the sins will be "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, like merits; and afterwards they will rise still further, to the supernal whiteness, which is Wisdom, above Understanding. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 17): The deed itself is ordered and set so, as "Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of creation," and in truth this will be clarified in the future regarding all the sins of Israel, when they are refined and whitened, as the Sages said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow." That is, since the true will of the Blessed One was so, it is like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): In the future this will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel, as the Sages said in Shabbos 89b on the verse "If your sins be": "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation" — it will be clarified that it was ordered from the true will of the Blessed One that it be so, and if so, in this too they did the will of the Blessed One, and it was all like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Naso 2): Such was the intent in the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," as the Zohar says, there is no light but that which comes out of darkness; and then "the Lord will not count iniquity to him," since it will be clarified that this was created only so that it be "very good." As they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow," that is, they will be as merits. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): From the side of the hidden things that will be revealed in the future there was no sin at all, and of this they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, from the side of the "hidden things of the Merciful One," then "they shall be white as snow" entirely, for there is no sin at all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei 31): Snow alludes to fear, and so the Gemara says, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation until now, they shall be white as snow": "years" alludes to cycles and order, that is, if there is an accusation, Heaven forbid, and it seems that a person sinned deliberately and in [recurring] cycles, the Blessed One will illuminate that this deed came only out of fear of the Blessed One, and this is "white as snow.":),
that sins will be like these solar years that are prearranged and set since the six days of Creation (as written in Shabbat 89b);
כָּךְ הַחֲטָאִים הַכֹּל מְסוּדָּר מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
so too the transgressions were all orchestrated from the six days of Creation as Hashem willed that Israel undergo.

וְכֵן כָּל עֲבֵירוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עֲבֵירוֹת לִשְׁמָהּ הַגְּדוֹלוֹת מִמִּצְוֹת שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נָזִיר כג275 Nazir 23b — Ulla said: Tamar acted licentiously and Zimri acted licentiously. Tamar acted licentiously — kings and prophets came forth from her. Zimri acted licentiously — many tens of thousands of Israel fell on his account. R. Nachman bar Yitzchak said: A transgression for its own sake is greater than a commandment not for its own sake. Rashi (s.v. "Tamar acted licentiously"): But she intended it for the sake of a commandment, to raise up seed, as it is written, "for she saw that Shelah had grown"; whereas Zimri intended it for the sake of transgression. "Kings and prophets came forth from her" — kings from David, and prophets from Isaiah. Rashi (s.v. "greater is a transgression for its own sake"): That is to say, one done for the sake of a commandment. Tosafos (s.v. "Tamar acted licentiously"): But she intended it for the sake of Heaven, as it is written, "for she saw that Shelah had grown." Kings came forth from her, as is written at the end of Ruth, "And these are the generations of Peretz ... unto Jesse"; and prophets, for the Master said that Amotz and Amatzyah were brothers — Amatzyah the king being of David's line — and it is an established tradition that wherever Scripture names a prophet's father in a prophecy, the father too was a prophet. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Nazir 23b): In Tamar's licentiousness her whole intent was to draw near to Israel, the holy seed; Zimri's intent was to remove himself far off and to cleave to the nations. Therefore from Tamar kings came forth, while through Zimri many tens of thousands of Israel fell. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): Esther's going [to the king], though outwardly it seemed the very opposite, since this time it was of her own will, was in truth [a case of] "a transgression for its own sake is greater than a commandment not for its own sake"; nor did she derive benefit from the transgression, since "all their good [is evil for the righteous]." It thus became for her a garment of commandment and holiness, and a means of attaining the holy spirit that comes through complete cleaving to His kingship.:),
And so all sins of Israel are 'transgressions for Heaven's sake' that are greater than mitzvot performed not for Heaven's sake (Nazir 23b),
הַיְינוּ מִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂים הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ,
referring to the sparse, light mitzvot observed by idolaters which are not for Heaven's sake,
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת לִשְׁמָהּ שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for it is impossible for theirs to be for Heaven's sake, since it is not the divine will,
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַפֶּה: "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה".
Hashem anticipating: 'when its boughs wither they will be broken.'
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
However, Israel cling unto the Name of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and all their deeds are intrinsically for the sake of Heaven, only that this remains hidden in this world.
וְעַל זֶה הִיא שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִצְוַת הַמִּילָה,
And upon this rests the root of the commandment of circumcision,
שֶׁהוּא הַכָּרָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַהוֹלָדָה שֶׁהֵם רְשׁוּמִים לִשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
which is the recognition at the very source of procreation that they are inscribed unto the Name of the Holy One in their root;

וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "אִמְרָתֶךָ" – אֲמִירָה בִּלְחִישָׁה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פח עַמּוּד ב; חֵלֶק א, רלד עַמּוּד ב276 Zohar 3:88b — "Speak to the priests" — R. Yitzchak said: "Speak to the priests" — in a whisper. Just as all the acts of the priests are done in a whisper, so their speech is in a whisper. "Speak... and say to them" — once and twice, to warn them concerning their holiness, that they not become defiled.)
and therefore it is called 'Your word' (imratekha)—speech in a whisper (as written in Zohar III 88b, and I 234b)
שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת.
which is not in outward disclosure.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַשָּׂשׂוֹן,
And over this specifically is the sason (joy),
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הוֹרָאַת הַמִּלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ:
which means the significance of the word sason in the Holy Tongue:
הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה.
the active manifestation of the joy of the heart breaking forth into actual deed.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה דְּקַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ אַחַר הַשִּׂמְחָה,
And this occurs through the feast that they accepted upon themselves following gladness,
דְּ"חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי וְכוּלֵי",
namely that 'a person is obligated to become intoxicated, etc.,'
וְהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה לַפּוֹעַל,
which is the actualization of joy into physical reality,
דְּגַם דְּלָא יָדְעֵי בֵּין וְכוּלֵי – הֵם דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם.
demonstrating that even when they know not between good and evil, they remain bound to Hashem in all their actions.
"וִיקָר" – הַיְינוּ כֶּתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב וְכָבוֹד,
"'And honor (yakar)'—this is the crown of a good name and glory,
אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ,
referring to the tefillin of the head,
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל וְגוֹמֵר",
fulfilling: 'And all the peoples of the earth shall see, etc.',
דִּתְפִלִּין אֵינוֹ מִצְוָה בְּעֶצֶם הָאָדָם רַק לְבוּשׁ הַמַּלְבִּישׁ לָאָדָם,
for tefillin is not a mitzvah within the person's essence, but an outer garment adorning man;
וְכֵן הַכָּבוֹד הוּא לְבוּשׁ מִבַּחוּץ.
and likewise honor is an outward vestment from without.
רַק לְבוּשׁ יָקָר דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַתְּפִלִּין,
Only that the precious, honorable garment of Israel is the tefillin,
דְּהַיְינוּ כִּי שֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עֲלֵיהֶם.
signifying that the Name of Hashem is invoked upon them.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה בְּפוּרִים,
And this disclosure occurred on Purim,
כִּי "נָפַל פַּחַד וְגוֹמֵר",
for 'the fear of the Jews fell upon them, etc.,'
עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת מַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים,
through the mitzvah of gifts to the poor (matanot la'evyonim),
כִּי "מַתַּן אָדָם יַרְחִיב לוֹ, וְלִפְנֵי גְדֹלִים יַנְחֶנּוּ",
for 'a man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men' (Proverbs 18:16);
גְּדוֹלִים הַיְינוּ בַּחָכְמָה,
and 'great men' refers to those great in wisdom,
וּ"בְצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף",
for 'in the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of silver' (Ecclesiastes 7:12),
כִּי עִיקַּר הַכָּבוֹד מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
since true honor derives from wisdom,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ" –
as it is written: 'The wise shall inherit honor' (Proverbs 3:35)—
כְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת,
like an unending, perpetual inheritance,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פה277 Bava Metzia 85a — R. Parnach said in the name of R. Yochanan: Whoever is a Torah scholar, and his son is a Torah scholar, and his son's son is a Torah scholar — the Torah never again ceases from his offspring, as it is stated, "And as for Me, this is My covenant... they shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, said the Lord, from now and forever." What is meant by "said the Lord"? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am your guarantor in this matter. Rashi: "Nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, said the Lord, from now and forever" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said thus: I am guarantor from now on that it shall never depart. Maharsha: The Mishnah in Avot says "prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you," which is addressed precisely to the son of a Torah scholar: only if he rouses himself to study can he fill his fathers' place. A guarantor everywhere stands for the borrower; here the borrower is the man himself, who is bound to labor at Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is guarantor that his labor will be repaid — that he will reach the standing of his fathers. And this is wherein the scholar's grandson has the advantage over the son of an unlearned man, for whom too everything depends on study: the Torah he learns "circles back to its lodging place," returning to assist him until he fills his fathers' place, for their house is her lodging. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Thirteen Principles of Conduct 10): One who is righteous, his seed too is not forsaken, and he is a Torah scholar. Although Torah scholars are not commonly found to have sons who are Torah scholars, that means [sons who are] exceptionally great; and [the Torah] returns to their seed's seed, so that whoever is a Torah scholar, and his son, and his son's son, is assured that it will not cease. If he sees that it is ceasing, let him marry the daughter of a Torah scholar, and "through the scent of water it will bud.".):
as they said (Bava Metzia 85a):
"כָּל שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וּבְנוֹ וְכוּלֵי אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת",
'Whoever is a Torah scholar, and his son, etc., it never ceases from his seed,'
וּפֵירוּשׁ הוּא וּבְנוֹ וּבֶן בְּנוֹ –
and the meaning of he, his son, and his grandson is:
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהִיא חָכְמָתוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
namely when his wisdom is in ultimate perfection,

כִּי הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵדֻיּוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב278 Mishnah Eduyot 2:9 — He used to say: A father endows his son with beauty, with strength, with wealth, with wisdom, and with length of years, and with the number of the generations before him — and that is the appointed End, as it is said, "calling the generations from the beginning." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 18): David was chosen both for his own merit and for his father's; the Sages' reading implies that the choice was from the outset one of Jesse's sons, for "a father endows his son" etc. So too many came by the merit of their fathers, and mostly their fathers' merit assists them; only Abraham, the father of the whole world, who had none before him and did not come by his fathers' merit, is therefore called the first of converts. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:143): [Solomon attained this] as an inheritance from his father: since the halakha is that a son inherits his father, it is truly his, and "a father endows his son" etc., for the son is drawn from the father's very essence. He truly has the father's power in him, only with more added, and therefore the father endows the son and not the son the father. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part I 61): This is also why Torah scholars do not have sons who are Torah scholars: a father endows his son with wisdom, even though choice is in man's hand, only through the blessing "Make [the words of Your Torah] pleasant … and our offspring"; and it comes about because they did not recite this blessing. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): Moses did not bequeath his crown to his sons — not on his own account, even though a father endows his son with wisdom, but because the Blessed One did not want it, on account of the generation, which was not worthy and might have erred into thinking that Torah is an inheritance.),
for a father endows his son with wisdom (Eduyot 2:9),
כִּי הַבֵּן נִמְשָׁךְ מִטִּיפֵּי מוֹחוֹ.
because the son is drawn from the essence of his father's mind.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַחָכְמָה רַק מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְאֵינוֹ בְּמַעֲמַקָּיו בֶּאֱמֶת, רַק חָכָם לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
And when wisdom is merely from the lip outward and not in his authentic depths, being wise only to appearance,
אֵינוֹ חָכָם בִּשְׁלֵימוּת וְאֵין בְּנוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
he is not truly wise, and his son will not be a Torah scholar.

וְזֶה טַעַם "שֶׁלֹּא בֵּרְכוּ בַּתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נְדָרִים פא279 Nedarim 81a — Ravina said [why Torah scholars do not commonly have sons who are Torah scholars]: Because they do not first recite a blessing over the Torah. For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: What is meant by that which is written, "Who is the wise man that may understand this... for what reason is the land perished"? This matter was put to the Sages and to the prophets, and they could not explain it, until the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself explained it, as it is written: "And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken My Torah which I set before them, and have not hearkened to My voice, nor walked therein." Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: ["Nor walked therein" means] that they did not first recite a blessing over the Torah. Rashi: "They did not first recite a blessing" — when they rise early for Torah study; and scholars who are the sons of scholars, because they are diligent in Torah and accustomed to it, are not careful to recite the blessing when they begin, and so the blessing "may we and our offspring be learners of Torah" is not fulfilled in them. "It was put to the Sages" — as it is written, "Who is the wise man"; and to the prophets, as it is written, "and to whom the mouth of the Lord has spoken, that he may declare it." Tosafos (s.v. "they do not first recite a blessing over the Torah"): When they rise early to study Torah they do not recite the blessings "to engage in words of Torah," "make pleasant," and "who chose us." Maharsha: It may further be explained in the light of what they said in the chapter Bnei HaIr, that any Torah scholar before whom an ignorant priest recites the blessing over the Torah is liable to death — that is, the scholars themselves were not first to bless over the Torah, but let an ignorant priest bless before them. This is what is expounded here from "nor walked therein," for whoever sees a scholar abased before an ignoramus says that there is no satisfaction in Torah; and it is then measure for measure that the sons of scholars are not commonly scholars. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Nedarim 81a): Heaven forbid that they did not bless over the Torah at all; they certainly recited the blessing with the mouth and also with the heart. Rather, they did not bless the Holy One for the giving of the Torah as it deserved, for one must bless for each thing according to the blessing the Holy One has given, and for the greatness of the good and the blessing that is the Torah which He gave Israel they did not bless with a whole heart, since that is not possible; so although they blessed with the mouth, they did not bless with the intention of heart that the blessing over the Torah deserves. Accordingly they were not cleaving to the Torah as they should, and therefore no Torah scholars issue from them. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): "Why is it not common for Torah scholars to have sons who are Torah scholars" — that the offspring should come from the side of wisdom, since they are exceedingly wise and the wisdom in their minds is great by the Blessed One, who created them so? But "they did not bless the Torah first": every blessing is the recognition of the Name of Heaven before one's eyes, knowing who commanded thus and who decreed thus, which is the fear in the heart. When the blessing precedes the Torah, which is wisdom, then the offspring too is a Torah scholar from the side of wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, From Tanchuma): The sage, who is occupied with Torah, needs the warning "I am [the Lord]" to remember it, for out of immersion in Torah one can also come to forget the Blessed One; this is what is alluded to in "they did not bless the Torah first," that is, they did not know that there is a Giver of the Torah. The blessing beforehand is the recognition that "I am the Lord," that everything is from Him and from His hand He gave you the Torah and the wisdom..),
And this explains why 'they did not recite a blessing over the Torah first' (Nedarim 81a),
כִּי הַבְּרָכָה לְפָנֶיהָ הוּא הַכָּרָה דְּהַחָכְמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for the blessing beforehand is the conscious recognition that wisdom comes from Hashem, blessed be He,
וּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דִּמְיוֹן וְחָכְמָה לְמַרְאִית עַיִן לְבַד וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת.
and without this, it is merely illusion and superficial wisdom, not truth.
וְיֵשׁ מִמַּעֲמַקִּים תְּרֵין עוּמְקִין דְּאִינּוּן נִסְתָּרוֹת מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא,
And out of the depths there are two depths: the concealments of brain and heart,
וְעוֹמֶק הַשֵּׁנִי נִגְלָה בְּבֶן הַבֵּן;
and the second depth is revealed in the grandson;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַחָכְמָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בְּכָל מַעֲמַקָּיו, שׁוּב אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶקֶת, וְהַכָּבוֹד לוֹ לְנַחֲלָה.
and when wisdom is complete throughout all his depths, it never ceases, and honor becomes his enduring heritage.
כִּי כְּבוֹד ה' נִקְרָא הַמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה הַמּוּשֶּׂגֶת לִבְרִיּוֹתָיו
For the glory of Hashem is designated as the final attribute (Malchut) comprehended by His creatures,
שֶׁהֵם מַשִּׂיגִים אֲדוֹנוּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ
