wherein they perceive His Mastership and Sovereignty,
שֶׁמִּצַּד זֶה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד מִן הַזּוּלַת כַּנּוֹדָע.
from which vantage point honor is accorded by others, as is known.
וּמִדָּה זוֹ עִיקָּרָהּ הוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת,
And this attribute is essentially the crown of royalty,
וְלָכֵן עַל מְלָכִים אוֹמְרִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ" –
and therefore over kings among Israel we recite: 'Who has imparted of His glory'—
שֶׁמַּלְכוּתָם חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל,
because their kingdom is an actual portion of God from Above;
וּבְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת: "שֶׁנָּתַן מִכְּבוֹדוֹ" –
and over idolaters: 'Who has given of His glory'—
כִּי הֵם בָּשָׂר וָדָם וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לֶאֱלֹהוּת כְּחֵלֶק מִן הַכֹּל וְנִקְרָא נְתִינָה,
for they are flesh and blood and have no intrinsic connection to Godliness as a portion of the Whole, hence it is termed a mere external gift;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מִכְּבוֹדוֹ
yet nonetheless it derives from His glory,

כִּי "לֶב מְלָכִים וְגוֹמֵר280 Proverbs 21:1 — “A king’s heart is like streams of water in the hand of the Lord; He turns it wherever He wishes.” Metzudas Dovid: Just as channels of water are in a man's hand to divert wherever he wishes by digging trenches, so the heart of a king is in the hand of the Lord, to turn it wherever He wishes. Malbim: Although the heart of a private man is given over to him and the choice is his, the heart of a king is not, since the welfare of the community depends on his choices and if he chooses an evil way he will destroy many; therefore this public heart of his is in the hand of the Lord, and in matters of the community he is without free choice. He is likened to channels of water, which men dig and divert toward the places that need them and away from places they would harm, because that is the public need; so too the king's heart, since from his deeds the affairs of the community flow, whether for chastisement or for kindness, for war or for peace, and God turns it at the very first inclination, as channels of water are diverted at the beginning of their course. הַכֹּל בְּיַד ה'" כְּמִקּוֹדֶם,
because 'the heart of kings, etc., is all in the hand of Hashem' as mentioned above,
וּכְבוֹדוֹ הוּא הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט.
and His divine glory is what expands forth.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ",
Nevertheless it is stated: 'By me kings reign' (Proverbs 8:15),

וּ"מַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גִּיטִּין סב281 Gittin 62a — Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda were sitting when Geneiva passed by them. Meanwhile he came over to them and said: Peace upon you, kings, peace upon you, kings. They said to him: From where do you know that the Sages are called kings? He said to them: As it is written, "Through me kings reign." Rashi: "A man of Torah" — a son of Torah. "A contentious man" — one who disputes with the Sages, for he used to vex Mar Ukva, who was head of the court, as stated in the first chapter. Maharsha: The very same incident appears at the end of the chapter "Kol HaGet," where it is not mentioned that he greeted them, because there the Gemara needed only the matter it was dealing with; here, however, the main point for which it is brought is that we double the greeting for Torah scholars, who are called kings. The matter is plain: a king of Israel, and the Torah scholar likewise, makes peace above and below, as they said that whoever occupies himself with Torah for its own sake makes peace in the household above and the household below, as it is stated, "Let him take hold of My strength, let him make peace with Me." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 62a): A king's greeting is doubled, one for himself and one on account of his kingship, since in the king's peace lies the peace of everything; but that reason does not fit a Torah scholar. Rather, one may say it is because the Sages said that Torah scholars increase peace in the world, just as the king increases peace in the world — for were it not for fear of the government, a man would swallow his fellow alive. And so, since Torah scholars increase peace in the world, we double the greeting to them: one for his own peace and one for the peace of the world. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 27): A Torah scholar who can produce novel insights through pilpul — the level of Moses — thereby attains the level of kingship, as stated, "Who are kings? The Rabbis," and of prophecy. Kingship, too, attains true sovereignty from the well and flowing spring that is the source of wisdom, as it says, "Through me kings reign": kingship derives from the Torah, and when it is a flowing spring it never ceases and the reign endures, like that of King David. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): The blessing of Israel, who are called "man," is "subdue it and rule" — to conquer all the earthliness and physicality of this world. The Torah is the template of all creation, and "Who are kings? The Rabbis" — for through their attainment in Torah they rule over all of creation..),
and 'Who are kings? The Rabbis' (as written in Gittin 62a),
הַיְינוּ חַכְמֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning the masters of the Oral Torah,
דְּמַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ, וְחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה.
for Malchut is the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah, and lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah).
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין "שֶׁחָלַק" וְ"שֶׁנָּתַן" מֵחָכְמָתוֹ,
And this also explains why we recite the blessings 'Who has imparted' and 'Who has given' of His wisdom,
וְאֵין מְבָרְכִים גַּם כֵּן עַל גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר;
whereas we do not recite an analogous blessing over a mighty man or a rich man;

וּמָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן תֹּאַר עָשִׁיר עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה)282 Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 1 — Blessed is the Omnipresent, blessed is He, who discerns at the outset what will be at the end, who declares the end from the beginning and from of old what has been done, who knows what has been done and what is destined to be done, who looks toward good and does not look toward evil, who is rich and rejoices in His portion; and by His wisdom and by His understanding He created His world and established it, and afterward created man within it. וְכַמָּה פְּעָמִים: "עָשִׁיר וְשָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְכוּלֵי",

and we also find the designation 'rich' attributed to Hashem, blessed be He, in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah) and several other places: 'rich and rejoicing in His portion, etc.';
אֲבָל מִדּוֹת אֵלּוּ בְּעֶצֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד מִדּוֹתָיו
yet these attributes within the essence of Hashem from the perspective of His higher sefirotic attributes
הֵם מִן הַמִּדּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא מִמִּדַּת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט לִשְׁכּוֹן בְּדָרֵי מַטָּה.
are among the primary attributes, not belonging to the attribute of His glory that expands to dwell among earthly dwellers.
וְהָעוֹשֶׁר וְהַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת עוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה בְּמִדַּת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
And wealth and might in the lower realm stem from the enclothement of supernal wealth and might within the attribute of His glory,
הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּכָל הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ לִכְבוֹדוֹ בָּרָא,
which expands throughout all Creation which He created entirely for His glory,
וְאֵין לִקְרוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק וּנְתִינָה מֵעָשְׁרוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ מַמָּשׁ
and this cannot strictly be termed an imparting or gift of His actual wealth and might,
דְּזֶהוּ לְאֵין קֵץ,
for those are infinite,
וְעוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה דְּבָשָׂר וָדָם הוּא בִּגְבוּל
while the wealth and might of flesh and blood are bounded,
שֶׁהָעוֹשֶׁר יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּךְ וְכָךְ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר,
wherein the rich man has a quantified amount and cannot possess without limit,
וְכֵן בִּגְבוּרָה לַגִּבּוֹר הַיּוֹתֵר עָצוּם יֵשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁיְּנַצְּחֶנּוּ וְשֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַעֲמוֹד בּוֹ,
and so too in might, for the most mighty warrior there exists a force that can overcome him which he cannot withstand,
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין לִקְרוֹתוֹ עָשְׁרוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ.
and if so, it cannot be called His absolute wealth and might.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמָה וְכָבוֹד הוּא מִצַּד מִדָּה תַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁהִיא הַנּוֹתֶנֶת גְּבוּל וְקִצְבָּה לַנִּבְרָאִים,
In contrast, wisdom and honor stem from the lowest attribute (Malchut) which establishes boundaries and measure for creations,
וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן בְּלִי גְּבוּל בְּעֶצֶם שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא מִמִּדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and it is likewise inherently limitless in its essence, being an attribute of Hashem;
וְכֵן הַחָכְמָה וְהַכָּבוֹד שֶׁל בְּרִיּוֹת הֵם בְּלֹא גְּבוּל בְּעֶצֶם
and similarly the wisdom and honor of human beings are inherently boundless in their pure essence,
רַק מוּגְבָּלִים מִצַּד הָאָדָם,
being limited only from the side of the mortal recipient,
כִּי הֵם חֵלֶק מֵחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה וְכָבוֹד הָעֶלְיוֹן.
because they are an actual portion of the lower supernal Wisdom and Supernal Honor.
וְכָל מְלוּכַת מְלָכִים בַּפּוֹעַל הֵם עַל יְדֵי חָכְמַת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And all reigning of kings in practical governance operates through the wisdom of the Oral Torah,

וְזֶה נִקְרָא רָאוּי לַמַּלְכוּת כְּהָאוֹמֵר כֵּן עַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ283 Megillah 11a — “Who reigned” — Rav said: That he reigned of his own accord. Some say this to his credit, and some say it to his discredit. Some say it to his credit — that there was no man as fit for kingship as he. And some say it to his discredit — that he was not fit for kingship at all, but he gave out abundant money and so rose to it. Rashi: "That he reigned of his own accord" — that he was not of the royal line. Maharsha: Rav expounds the participle "who reigned" because otherwise Scripture should have written simply "this is Ahasuerus who was king from Hodu"; the opening of the verse, "And it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus," already shows that it speaks in the past tense, so the unusual form is there to be expounded. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 1:1): By the plain sense Scripture should have said "who reigned" in the past tense rather than the present participle, which implies that he reigns now; therefore the Gemara explained "who reigned of his own accord": when a king is the son of a king there is no departure from the order [of things], and no further departure follows from him, but his reigning of his own accord was a departure, and every alteration brings another in its train — therefore in his days came about the affair of Haman, an utter departure from the order of the world, to destroy an entire nation. According to the one who says it to his credit, Scripture is not speaking of the wicked man's virtue; rather "who reigned" is joined to "from India to Cush", explaining that he was so highly regarded that he reigned of his own accord and therefore ruled from India to Cush; according to the one who says it to his discredit, the word is joined to "He is Ahasuerus" and speaks of his disgrace. (מְגִילָּה יא.),
and this is what qualifies one as 'fit for kingship,' like the sage who stated this concerning Ahasuerus (Megillah 11a),

כִּי גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא חָכָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם טז.)284 Megillah 16a — "And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to all his friends." It calls them "his friends" and it calls them "his wise men." R. Yochanan said: Whoever says a word of wisdom, even among the nations of the world, is called a wise man. Maharsha: The "word of wisdom" for which they earned the name of wise men is a word of the wisdom of the Torah, namely what the verse goes on to say: "If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews" — if he descends from the other tribes you can prevail over him, but if from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim or Manasseh you cannot. For that Mordecai was a Jew they already knew, since it had been published throughout the provinces; until now they had supposed he came from one of the other tribes and that Haman could prevail over him, and only when they saw the beginning of Haman's fall did they take fright and say that he might be of those tribes for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, "stirs up His might." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): As stated in Megillah, one who says a word of wisdom among the nations is called a wise man — learned from Haman's "wise men," who grasped the truth that he would fall before the seed of the Jews. For this is the whole wisdom of the nations: to grasp the superiority of Israel, that they cannot prevail against them; but to grasp the wisdom of truth, the wisdom of the Torah — the apprehension of His truth — is impossible for them, for "He has not done so for any nation." בְּחַכְמָיו דְּהָמָן.
for among the nations of the world one can also be termed wise, as our Sages noted (there, 16a) regarding 'the wise men of Haman.'
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ עִנְיַן חָכְמָה מְיוּחָד שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ רָאוּי לְכָבוֹד,
And a monarch possesses a unique dimension of administrative wisdom on account of which he is deserving of honor;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְהָאוֹמֵר "מָמוֹנָא יַתִּירָא דִּיהֵיב וְקָם" כְּבוֹדוֹ מִצַּד הָעוֹשֶׁר דְּ"בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר",

in contrast to the authority who states that 'he gave excessive money and rose to power,' where his honor derived from wealth as in 'in the shadow of money is the shadow of wisdom,' (Ecclesiastes 7:12),
כִּי כָבוֹד מִצַּד עוֹשֶׁר וּגְבוּרָה אֵינוֹ כָּבוֹד שֶׁל אֱמֶת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יִכּוֹן לָעַד
for honor derived from wealth and physical power is not authentic honor that endures forever,
כִּי הוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וְיֵשׁ לוֹ הֶפְסֵק.
because it is bounded and subject to cessation.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמָה אֵין גְּבוּל כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא דָּבוּק בְּחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
In contrast, wisdom has no boundary when cleaving to Supernal Wisdom,
כְּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מִצַּד דִּיבּוּקָם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
like the Davidic dynasty through their adherence to the Oral Torah;
רַק "בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר" דְּעַל יְדֵי "מַתָּן יַרְחִיב" מִתְרַחֵב לוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיּוּכַל לֵילֵךְ לִפְנֵי הַחֲכָמִים, מִמֵּילָא גַּם כְּבוֹדוֹ כֵּן.
only that 'in the shadow, etc.' shows that through 'a gift makes room' the path broadens for him to walk before the wise, and consequently his honor is similarly established.
וְהָיוּ שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד בַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
And these two opposites were combined within a single subject in Ahasuerus,
כִּי "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
for 'both these and those are the words of the living God,'
דְּזֶה עִנְיַן פּוּרִים וְ"נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא וְגוֹמֵר"
for this is the very essence of Purim and 'it was reversed to the opposite, etc.,'
שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד,
that two opposites coexist in a single subject,
וּמִצַּד הַסּוֹף כְּבוֹדוֹ מִצַּד חָכְמָה וּמִצַּד הַהַתְחָלָה מִצַּד עוֹשֶׁר.
and from the perspective of the end his honor stemmed from wisdom, while from the beginning it stemmed from wealth.

וְהַמֶּלֶךְ סְתָם הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א285 Zohar 3:109a — R. Shimon said: But we find "courts" in the verse "And she stood in the inner court of the king's house, opposite the king's house" (Esther 5:1). And in every place where "the king" is said without qualification, this is the Holy One, blessed be He. "And she stood" — "standing" means nothing other than prayer. "Opposite the king's house" — opposite the Temple, for all Israel must offer their prayer toward that place and be facing the Temple. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): For one who understands, the whole Megillah is the story of the "slumber" of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, from beginning to end. It begins from the feast of Shushan, for from there begins "the king" without qualification rather than "King Ahasuerus," meaning the King of kings of kings who clothed Himself [in him], and the hundred and eighty days before it were the preparation for receiving that clothing of the King of kings of kings. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 13): Haman said, "To whom would the king desire [to do honor]?" — and it is known from the Sages that "the king" without qualification speaks of the King of kings of kings: he thought that he was esteemed by the Blessed One as well, since not for nothing had He made him great and delivered Israel into his hand to destroy them, because they had grown lax in (lit. “slept from”) the commandments, and he imagined that He had chosen him in their stead. It became a mockery afterward, when he heard the king's words that it was Mordechai the Jew in whom he delighted, and that he himself would be a servant before him.)
And 'the king' unspecified is the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He (as written in Zohar III 109a),
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָתוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה מִתְלַבֶּשֶׁת בּוֹ בְּסוֹד גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה
which is the revelation of His Shechinah enclothed within him in the mystery of the exile of the Shechinah,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יוֹנְקִים בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן, הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים.
from which the children of Israel drew sustenance at that time, which likewise operated through two opposites.
וּשְׁנֵי מִינֵי כָבוֹד:
And there are two categories of honor:
אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ – הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
these are the tefillin of the head—pertaining to wisdom residing in the brain,
דְּזֶהוּ לַאֲחֵרִים לְאוֹת;
which serves as a sign unto others;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תְּפִלִּין שֶׁל יָד שֶׁהוּא מַעֲלוֹת הַלֵּב וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, זֶהוּ רַק "לְךָ לְאוֹת",
in contrast to the tefillin of the arm which embodies the virtues of the heart and the faculties of action, being solely 'a sign unto you,'
דְּאֵין מִצִּדָּם כָּבוֹד מִצַּד הַתְּפִלִּין דְּהַיְינוּ הַדְּבֵיקוּת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for from their side there is no outward honor generated by the tefillin—namely inner cleaving to Hashem—
רַק מִצַּד מַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים, הַיְינוּ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּזוּלָתוֹ, זֶה גּוֹרֵם לוֹ כָּבוֹד,
save through gifts to the poor, meaning the deficiency present in another is what causes honor to be reflected upon him;
כִּי הֶחָכָם מְכֻבָּד גַּם בֵּין חֲכָמִים,
for the wise man is honored even among fellow sages,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִהְיוּ גְּדוֹלִים מִמֶּנּוּ מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אִם הוּא חָכָם בֶּאֱמֶת יוּכַל לוֹמַר דְּבַר חָכְמָה בֵּין חֲכָמִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ שֶׁהוּא חָכָם,
and even if they are greater than he, if he is genuinely wise he can articulate a profound insight among great scholars such that they recognize his wisdom,
כִּי אֵין שִׁיעוּר לַחָכְמָה וְהוּא יוּכַל לְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה עַל לִבָּם.
for wisdom has no limit and he can innovate something that never occurred to them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּגְבוּרָה וְעוֹשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא בִּגְבוּל,
In contrast to might and wealth which are bounded,
מִי שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹתוֹ אֵין לוֹ כָּבוֹד נֶגְדּוֹ,
where one who equals him accords him no deferential honor,
רַק הַכָּבוֹד מִצַּד אֶבְיוֹנִים וּפְחוּתִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
the honor stemming solely from the indigent and those lower than he.
וּבְפוּרִים נִמְשָׁכִים כָּל אַרְבָּעָה מַתָּנוֹת אֵלּוּ מִלְּמַעְלָה לַיְּהוּדִים,
And on Purim all four of these heavenly gifts are drawn down from Above unto the Jews,
וַחֲכָמִים קָבְעוּ נֶגְדָּם אַרְבַּע מִצְווֹת שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
and the Sages instituted facing them four mitzvot so that they merit this through their active exertion,
וְיִהְיֶה נִקְרָא עַל שְׁמָם דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים".
and it be credited to their name under the principle that 'Israel sanctifies the seasons.'
וְהַשָּׂגַת קְדוּשַּׁת הַיְקָר דִּתְפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
And the attainment of the sanctity of precious honor (yakar) of the head-tefillin through wisdom,
הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא בְּמַתַּן אָדָם דְּ"בְּצֵל וְגוֹמֵר"
its active human exertion is through man's charity in 'in the shadow of money,' etc.,

וְ"לִפְנֵי גְדוֹלִים286 Proverbs 18:16 — “A man’s gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.” Rashi: Take it in its plain sense. Its midrashic reading speaks of those who give charity, for charity widens a man's portion in the world to come, and in this life too it "leads him before the great," who say of him that he is a man of standing. Metzudas Dovid: A man whose affairs require him to go before the great — the gift he gives widens the way for him and leads him before them. Malbim: There is a difference between the generous man and "a man of gifts": the latter is in the habit of giving presents even to the rich and the great. Though it seems that he is scattering his money for nothing, at times it makes room for him, for it leads him before the great, and when he is in straits they remember his gifts and exert themselves on his behalf." שֶׁהוּא הוֹלֵךְ קוֹדֶם,
and 'before great men' where he walks forward beforehand,
דַּהֲלִיכַת אָדָם הַיְינוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
for a man's walking represents his initiative and exertion;
וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עִיקָּר בָּזֶה,
and exertion is primary in this,
דְּעִיקַּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דִּפְעוּלַת אָדָם הוּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
since the foundational sphere of human action and effort is in physical deed,
דְּבָזֶה יַד אָדָם שׁוֹלֶטֶת,
for in deed man's hand holds active sway,
וְהוּא מֵהַנִּגְלוֹת שֶׁ"לָּנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ".
belonging to the revealed things that are 'unto us and unto our children' (Deuteronomy 29:28).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַחָכְמָה עִיקָּרָהּ בַּמּוֹחַ וְלֵב
In contrast, wisdom has its essential core in the brain and heart,
מֵהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁ"לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ",
belonging to the concealed things that are 'unto Hashem our God,'
וְרַק מִפִּיו יִתֵּן חָכְמָה בְּעֵזֶר אֱלֹהִי.
and solely from His mouth does He bestow wisdom through divine assistance.

sections.en: Divine Mitzvot, Purim, and Boundless Cleaving

items.h: Hashem Himself fulfills mitzvot in the supernal sense; Purim expresses this reciprocal bond and the total inversion required to erase Amalek.

Seif 1 — Hashem's Mitzvot and Purim's Reciprocal Bond
The supernal fulfillment of mitzvot reveals the mutual bond of Hashem and Israel that ultimately overturns Amalek.

p: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גַּם כֵּן מְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְווֹת,
The Holy One, blessed be He, likewise fulfills the commandments,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל287 Shemot Rabbah 30:9 — It once happened that Rabban Gamliel, R. Yehoshua, R. Elazar ben Azaryah and R. Akiva went to Rome and expounded there: The ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, are not like those of flesh and blood, who issues a decree and tells others to carry it out while he himself does nothing. A certain heretic was there, and after they had gone out he said to them: Your words are nothing but falsehood. Did you not say that God speaks and Himself performs? Why then does He not keep the Sabbath? They said to him: Wicked one, is a man not permitted to carry within his own courtyard on the Sabbath? He said to them: Yes. They said to him: The upper and lower worlds are the courtyard of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "The whole earth is full of His glory."):
as it is written in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30):
מֶלֶךְ גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה וְהוּא וְכוּלֵי,
a mortal king issues a decree and he, etc.,
לָמָּה אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי,
why does He not observe Shabbat, etc.,
וְהֵשִׁיבוּ דְּהוּא חֲצֵירוֹ;
and they responded that the whole universe is His personal domain;

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ו288 Berakhot 6a — R. Avin bar Rav Adda said that R. Yitzchak said: Whence do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons phylacteries? For it is said, "The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength." "By His right hand" — this is the Torah, as it is said, "From His right hand, a fiery law for them"; "and by the arm of His strength" — these are the phylacteries, as it is said, "The Lord will give strength to His people." Maharsha: Others have written a hidden mystery here, but I see the matter as close to its plain sense: the substance of the mitzvah of phylacteries is that we should cleave to Him, and by donning them we cause His Presence to rest upon us through His Name; and correspondingly the Holy One, blessed be He, has a cleaving and a singling-out with Israel, as it is said, "I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine" — and this is why phylacteries are called "glory." He brings "the Lord has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength" to show that He swore by two attributes, kindness and might: "by His right hand — this is the Torah," for the right is the attribute of kindness, as it is said of the Torah, "a Torah of kindness is on her tongue"; "and by the arm of His strength — these are the phylacteries" of the left arm, which is the attribute of might and strength, for through donning them a man causes the Divine Presence to rest upon him before the nations, so that they fear His might, as it is written, "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you." Maharal (Gevuros Hashem 44): Any perfection that goes out to another — as when we say that the Holy One bestowed being upon all that exists — is a higher level and a greater perfection than a perfection that does not go out to another. Therefore they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons phylacteries: that splendor and perfection of His which goes out to another is what is called "phylacteries," for phylacteries are bound to the one who wears them and are not his own essence, and such an added elevation is called "glory." He wears them upon the head because wisdom is in the head — the glory He has in that all existing things are ordered by His wisdom — and upon the arm in that He is glorified through the deeds He performs in them, which is ascribed to the arm, as it is written, "and with Your outstretched arm." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:40): The matter of tefillin is the binding of the Jew's entire being — his thoughts, will and deeds — to the Lord alone, through the depth of his hidden thought; and then, measure for measure, the Blessed One also binds Himself to him, which is the sense of "Whence do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin?".):
and similarly they stated (Berakhot 6a):
מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִלִּין?
From where do we derive that the Holy One, blessed be He, dons tefillin?
וְעוֹד טוּבָא.
and many further teachings.
וְכֵן מִצְוֹת חֲכָמִים,
And so too concerning the rabbinic commandments,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְתִגְזַר אֹמֶר וְיָקָם"
regarding this Scripture states (Job 22:28): 'You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established,'

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה ג289 Pesikta Rabbati 3 — Let a man not say: I will not keep the commandments of the elders, since they are not from the Torah. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: No, My son; rather, whatever they decree upon you, keep it, as it is said, "According to the Torah which they shall teach you." And why? Because they decree even upon Me, as it is said, "You shall decree a thing and it shall be established for you." You may know this from Jacob: when he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, "he set Ephraim before Manasseh" — he put the younger before the elder, and his decree was upheld, for at the offerings of the princes the tribe of Ephraim offered first. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): "You shall decree a thing and it shall be established": the righteous man decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills, for he becomes the deciding voice in the court on high, and the law follows him in his decrees against the decree of the supernal judgment — since all judgments in all the upper worlds are according to the Torah, and the Torah has already been handed over to those below, so that as the Sages decide in this world, so is the decision in all the upper worlds. The fulfilled decree of the righteous means that he declares that this is how the judgment ought to be — that is what is called a decree — and therefore it is fulfilled.):
(as written in Pesikta Rabbati, Parashah 3):

צַדִּיק גּוֹזֵר וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים (תַּעֲנִית כג290 Taanit 23a — Our Rabbis taught: What did the members of the Chamber of Hewn Stone send to Choni the Circle-Drawer? "You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine upon your ways." "You shall decree a thing" — you decreed below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills your word above. "And light shall shine upon your ways" — a generation that was dark, you lit up with your prayer. Rashi: "The Chamber of Hewn Stone": the Sanhedrin. "A generation that was dark": from the great distress, because the rains had not fallen. Maharsha: They drew four [distinct] things from verses that seem to speak of one matter, because they were recounting all his deeds in the order told above: at first, when they had seen no rain at all, it was a dark generation, and "you lit it up with your prayer" when they saw the rains begin..).
a righteous person decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills (Ta'anit 23a).
וְגַם הוּא מְקַיֵּים מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת בְּפוּרִים:
And He also fulfills the sending of portions (mishloach manot) on Purim:
"אִישׁ" – הַיְינוּ "ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה",
"'A man'—this is 'Hashem is a man of war' (Exodus 15:3),"

"לְרֵעֵהוּ" – הַיְינוּ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּהָרוֹאֶה (נד291 Berakhot 54b — “Stones of elgavish” — what are “stones of elgavish”? It was taught: stones that stopped on account of a man (al gav ish) and came down on account of a man. They stopped on account of a man — this is Moshe, as it is written, “And the man Moshe was very humble”; they came down on account of a man — this is Yehoshua, as it is written, “Take you Yehoshua son of Nun, a man in whom there is spirit.” Rashi: "They stopped" — in the air. "And no rain reached the earth" — it did not come down to the ground but stood in the air. Maharsha: "Stones of elgavish" is a phrase from Ezekiel, said of the war of Gog and Magog, while the stones spoken of here are those of the descent of Beit Choron in the days of Joshua; the Gemara therefore explains that Ezekiel too calls them by this name because they stood on account of a man and came down on account of a man, some in Joshua's day and the rest destined to come down in the days of Gog and Magog. The point is that the messengers of the Omnipresent long to carry out the errand on which they were sent, to take God's vengeance upon His enemies; so when Moses' prayer suspended these stones, their mission was not annulled but held in reserve, and they stood waiting to fulfill it against God's enemies in Joshua's time and in the days of Gog and Magog.:)
"'to his friend'—this is in accordance with what our Sages expounded in HaRoeh (Berakhot 54b)
עַל גַּב אִישׁ זֶה מֹשֶׁה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה".
regarding 'on the back of a man'—this refers to Moses, as it is said 'And the man Moses' (Numbers 12:3).
וְיָדוּעַ דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם נִקְרָא מֹשֶׁה בְּכָל חַכְמֵי כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
And it is known that the essential root of a Torah scholar is designated as Moses across all sages of all generations,
כַּנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as is well known according to the teaching of the holy Ari, of blessed memory,

עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קא: וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת292 Shabbat 101b — The mishna teaches: Boats tied to one another — one may carry from this one to that one. Is that not obvious? Rava said: It was necessary only to permit the small skiff between them. Rav Safra said to him: Moses, is what you say correct? We learned in the mishna, "One may carry from this one to that one"! Rashi: ["Is that not obvious"] — that one may carry. The Mishnah's "one may carry" was needed only to permit carrying from one boat to the other by way of a small skiff lying between the two large ones: although it is not itself tied, it is permitted through the tying of the two outer boats, and we are not concerned that it may slip out from between them so that he carries through the airspace of a karmelit. "Moses" — that is, our master, who is in his generation as Moses was in his; "is what you say correct?" is said in astonishment, for "from this one to that one" implies that no other boat intervenes for the one carrying to pass into. Tosafos (s.v. "Is that not obvious"): At this stage the Gemara supposes that both boats belong to one person, and therefore asks "Is that not obvious?"; when they are not tied one may not carry between them, by a decree lest the object fall into the water and he carry from a private domain into a karmelit and come to bring it back. Although above (97a) no such decree was made concerning two houses, with boats, which are not fixed in place, there is more reason to decree lest the object fall. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "Is that not obvious"): Tosafot mean that he may be unable to reach the fallen object by hand from inside the boat, and would take a long reed and extend it out of the boat over the water to reach it; he would then have carried the reed from a private domain into a karmelit, and would come to bring the object and the reed back from the karmelit into the private domain. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Just as Moses our teacher is the root of all the wisdom of all the sages of Israel in every generation, as is known regarding the Gemara's expression "Moses, is what you say correct?", so Balaam is the root of all the wisdom of all the sages of the nations in every generation. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 3): Moses our teacher merited the fig tree, which is the source of wisdom, so that the Torah is called by his name; for, as is known from the Arizal's explanation of the Sages' expression "Moses, is what you say correct?", the power of Torah and wisdom in all the souls of Israel is the soul of Moses our teacher. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): "Judah is my lawgiver" — the root of the "lawgiver," as Moses our teacher is called, who is the root of the Torah scholars of Israel, as is known from the mystery of the expression found in several places in the Gemara, "Moses, is what you say correct?"; so too Judah is the root of the Torah scholars of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 6): It is known from the Arizal's explanation of the Sages' expression "Moses, is what you say correct?" that Moses is the root of the da'as [understanding] in all the Torah scholars of Israel in every generation, for the soul of Moses is the one that encompasses the Torah as a whole. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Shekalim 1): Moses our teacher is the inwardness of all the souls of Israel, the da'as [understanding] in the souls of Israel in every generation; therefore the Gemara says, regarding words of Torah, "Moses, is what you say correct?" — in astonishment: where is your da'as? And there are leaders of a generation whose souls include that entire generation, like Moses, with their root in Moses, as the Arizal wrote on this expression: the great one of the generation is called by that name because he is a spark of Moses himself, reincarnated in every generation. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 77): [On "Even were he like Joshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter":] the speaker deliberately said "like Joshua son of Nun" and not "like Moses," because Moses is the root of the Torah, and with the crown of Torah there is no concern for lineage; had he been "like Moses" — that is, a great Torah scholar of the generation, who is "like Moses," as the Sages said, "Moses, is what you say correct?" — he would have given her.):
on the statement of our Sages (Shabbat 101b and other places):
"מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ".
'Moses, you have spoken well!'
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי מָנוֹת לְאָדָם אֶחָד,
And these are two portions given to one person,
הַיְינוּ כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא אָדָם אֶחָד
meaning that all the Torah scholars in Israel are considered collectively as one person,
רֵעֵהוּ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
the companion of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁכֵּן קוֹרְאוֹ: "לְמַעַן אַחַי וְרֵעָי",
for so He addresses them: 'For the sake of My brothers and companions' (Psalms 122:8),

וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כז293 Shemot Rabbah 27:1 — "Do not forsake your friend and your father's friend" (Proverbs 27:10). "Your friend" — this is the Holy One, blessed be He, as you say, "For the sake of my brothers and my friends." "And your father's friend" — this is Abraham, as it is said, "the seed of Abraham My beloved." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 1): The Blessed One fulfills the mitzvah of "sending portions each man to his friend," for in these days, when the unification of the Divine Name is accomplished, Israel are called friends of the Holy One, blessed be He — "for the sake of my brothers and my friends"; and Rashi (Shabbat 31a) explained "what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow" as referring to the Blessed One, on the basis of the verse "your friend and your father's friend do not forsake." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): The Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel "my brothers and my friends": the brotherhood is from the side of Jacob, and the friendship from the side of Isaac, who is called "friend," as they expounded "your friend and your father's friend," which refers to Isaac, who is called simply "your father," as they said in Shabbat on "for You are our father." This is more than [being] a lover: an added closeness, face to face and eye to eye, as is the way of friends; and it is attained through love of Israel, by which they are one unique nation.)
and our Sages expounded (Shemot Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 27)
עַל פָּסוּק "רֵעֲךָ וְרֵעַ אָבִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" – זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
on the verse 'Your companion and your father's companion, etc.' (Proverbs 27:10)—this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
וּפֵירוּשׁ "אָבִיךָ" – הַחָכְמָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and the meaning of 'your father' is Wisdom, as is known.
וּשְׁתֵּי מָנוֹת הַיְינוּ דְּיֵשׁ שְׁתֵּי חָכְמוֹת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה:
And 'two portions' signifies that there exist two dimensions of wisdom and Torah teachings:
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהֵם חָכְמָה עִלָּאָה – מַה שֶּׁמּוּרְגָּשׁ שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which correspond to Supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah)—that which is distinctly felt to originate from Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי לְהַשִּׂיג דָּבָר זֶה,
since it is impossible for mortal human intellect to attain this on its own;
וְחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה – מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה דְּשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי מַשִּׂיגוֹ,
and Lower Wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah)—that which appears as though human intellect comprehends it,
וְהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
yet in ultimate truth it too emanates entirely from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְהֵם הַשְּׁתֵּי מָנוֹת שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים בְּפוּרִים:
And these are the two portions attained on Purim:
הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת בַּלֵּב מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּגִילּוּי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
novel renewal in the heart from words of Torah that are overtly revealed from Hashem,
וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם וְנִרְאֶה כְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הַלֵּב.
and that which is in hiddenness and appears merely as an internal innovation of the human heart.
וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים הוּא הַתָּאֵב לְכָל דָּבָר וּמִלּוּי הַחֵשֶׁק וְרָצוֹן,
And 'gifts to the poor' (matanot la'evyonim) addresses one who hungers for something, fulfilling the yearning and desire,
וְהֵם שְׁנֵי אֶבְיוֹנִים,
and these are two distinct categories of the needy:
דְּיֵשׁ בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת:
for there are masters of Torah and masters of mitzvot;
"אוֹהֵב תוֹרָה לֹא יִשְׂבַּע", וְכֵן "אוֹהֵב מִצְווֹת לֹא וְכוּלֵי"
'he who loves Torah shall never be satisfied,' and likewise 'he who loves mitzvot shall never, etc.,'

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וָאֶתְחַנַּן עַל פָּסוּק "אֹהֵב כֶּסֶף וְגוֹמֵר294 Devarim Rabbah 2:26 — "Then Moses set apart" (Deut. 4:41). This is what Scripture says: "He who loves silver will not be sated with silver" (Eccl. 5:9). Do we not already know that a man never fills his soul? What then is "with silver"? The Rabbis said: These are the Torah scholars, who love words of Torah, which are likened to silver, as it is said, "To acquire understanding is to be chosen above silver." Rav Nachman said: One who loves Torah is never sated with Torah. And what is "and he who loves abundance, without increase"? One who yearns and clamors after Torah yet raises up no disciples. Another interpretation of "He who loves silver": R. Yitzchak said — one who loves the commandments is never sated with the commandments. How so? You find two of the world's great men, David and Moses, who were not sated."),
(as written in Midrash Rabbah, Va'etchanan on the verse 'He who loves silver, etc.'),
וְהוּא אֶבְיוֹן לַדָּבָר הַהוּא,
and he is spiritually destitute and longing for that thing,
וּמִלּוּי הַחֵשֶׁק נִרְאֶה מַתָּנָה אַחַת.
and the fulfillment of this intense desire appears as one gift.
וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת הוּא כָּבוֹד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹלֵק לָאָדָם,
And mishloach manot represents honor that Hashem, blessed be He, imparts unto man,
כְּעִנְיַן "וַיְהִי יַעְבֵּץ נִכְבָּד מֵאֶחָיו" עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
in the manner of 'And Ya'betz was more honorable than his brothers' (I Chronicles 4:9) through words of Torah

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לח295 Shemot Rabbah 38:5 — "The wise shall inherit honor" (Proverbs 3:35) — honor is nothing other than Torah. Know this: what is said at the beginning of Chronicles? "Adam, Seth, Enosh," and so all of them; and you do not find honor written of any one of them until you reach Yabetz, as it is said, "And Yabetz was more honored than his brothers." Why is honor written of him? Because he toiled in Torah. Hence, "the wise shall inherit honor." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 5): This is hinted in the Tanchuma: thirty-six generations from Adam to Yabetz, and honor is written of none of them except Yabetz — "And Yabetz was more honored than his brothers." That is, he was the first in the world to learn Torah through toil, restoring by his dialectic the laws forgotten during the mourning for Moses, which is why he was called Yabetz, for he counseled and spread Torah in Israel; this is the root of the Oral Torah, which requires great toil to be engraved upon the heart of stone.).
(as written in Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 38).
וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים הוּא עוֹשֶׁר שֶׁנּוֹתֵן לָאֶבְיוֹן לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ:
And gifts to the poor represents wealth that He bestows upon the indigent to make him complete:
הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם מִתְעַשֵּׁר בְּדַעַת,
the Torah scholar becomes enriched with divine perception (da'at),
וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת בְּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
and the masters of mitzvot are enriched with good deeds.
וְזֶהוּ הַנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן,
And this accounts for the placing of Esther over the house of Haman,
כִּי לְהָמָן הָיוּ שְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ,
for Haman possessed both of these outward assets,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וּמִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא מַטּוֹת296 Bamidbar Rabbah 22:7 — Our Rabbis taught: Two wise men arose in the world, one from Israel and one from the nations — Ahithophel from Israel and Balaam from the nations of the world — and both were lost from the world. So too two mighty men arose in the world, one from Israel and one from the nations — Samson from Israel and Goliath from the nations of the world — and both were lost from the world. So too two rich men arose in the world, one from Israel and one from the nations — Korah from Israel and Haman from the nations of the world — and both were lost from the world. Why? Because their gift was not from the Holy One, blessed be He; rather, they snatched it for themselves.):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Midrash Rabbah and Midrash Tanchuma, Matot):
שְׁנֵי עֲשִׁירִים הָיוּ בָּעוֹלָם, הָמָן בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
two exceedingly rich men existed in the world, Haman among the nations of the world.
וּכְבוֹדוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב: "גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר", "לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר וְגוֹמֵר",
And his honor is explicitly stated in Scripture: 'the king promoted Haman, etc.,' and 'whom the king delights to honor, etc.,'
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמֶלֶךְ סְתָם בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
and it is known that 'the king' unspecified refers to the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
כִּי הָיָה חָלַק לוֹ כָּבוֹד וְעוֹשֶׁר מִלְּמַעְלָה,
because He had apportioned unto him honor and wealth from Above,
וְזָכוּ לָזֶה מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר וְנִצְּחוּהוּ.
and Mordechai and Esther merited this and conquered him.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "נָתַן הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר אֶת בֵּית הָמָן וְגוֹמֵר",
And it is stated: 'King Ahasuerus gave, etc., the house of Haman, etc.,' (Esther 8:1),
וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ: "וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר הִנֵּה בֵית הָמָן נָתַתִּי וְגוֹמֵר".
and likewise afterward: 'And King Ahasuerus said, etc., Behold, the house of Haman I have given, etc.' (Esther 8:7).
וְנִרְאֶה כִּי "הַמֶּלֶךְ" לְבַד הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים,
And it appears that 'the king' alone represents the King of kings,
וַ"אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" לְבַד הוּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ,
and 'Ahasuerus' alone denotes Ahasuerus from his own wicked perspective,

כְּמוֹ "וַיְהִי בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" – הוּא אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּרִשְׁעוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ (מְגִילָּה יא297 Megillah 11a — "He is Ahasuerus" (Esther 1:1) — he was in his wickedness from his beginning to his end. "He is Esau" (Genesis 36:43) — he was in his wickedness from his beginning to his end. "They are Dathan and Abiram" (Numbers 26:9) — they were in their wickedness from their beginning to their end. "He is King Ahaz" (II Chronicles 28:22) — he was in his wickedness from his beginning to his end. Maharsha: He began with "He is Ahasuerus," which is the paradigm for them all, since in his case it is stated most explicitly — "in the beginning of his reign they wrote an accusation" — and the verse means: as he was wicked at the outset, over the building of the Temple, so he was at the end, in the affair of Haman. So too Dathan and Abiram were in their wickedness at the outset, while still in Egypt, when Moses said, "Wicked one, why do you strike your fellow?", and so they were at the end, in the affair of Korah; and Esau at the outset, when he sold the birthright as a lad of fifteen, and at the end, when he contested Jacob’s burial; and of Ahaz the verse reads, "And in the time of his distress he trespassed yet more against the Lord — he is King Ahaz," that is, he had already been wicked at the outset and added to it at the end. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 1:1): Our Rabbis mean that all the good that Ahasuerus did for Esther, for Mordecai and for Israel was entirely from the Holy One, blessed be He, who brought it about, for he himself was wicked from his beginning to his end. This is stated at the very beginning of the Megillah to make known that everything done in the Megillah was from the Holy One, blessed be He..),
as in 'And it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus'—he is Ahasuerus in his malice from beginning to end (Megillah 11a),

וְצָוְוחוּ "וַוי" בְּיָמָיו (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה)298 Esther Rabbah, Petichta 9 — Another interpretation of "that a flattering man not reign, a snare of the people" (Job 34:30): this is Ahasuerus, who was a flatterer, for he killed his wife on account of his friend, and another time killed his friend on account of his wife. ... When the beloved children provoke their Father in Heaven by their deeds, He sets over them a flattering king to exact punishment from them; and who is this? Ahasuerus. And when all saw this, they began to cry out "Woe!" — "And it came to pass [va-yehi] in the days of Ahasuerus.", זֶהוּ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ;
and they cried out 'woe' (vay) in his days (Midrash Rabbah), reflecting his personal nature;
אֲבָל "הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ" יֵשׁ בּוֹ הַרְכָּבָה פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְגַם מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ.
however, 'the king Ahasuerus' contains a synthesis of Hashem's sovereign operation enclothed together with his own self.
וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ זֶה בְּכָל הַמְּגִילָּה.
And insightful scholars will comprehend this across the entire Megillah.
וְכֵן בַּנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן וַדַּאי הוּא פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And so regarding the placing over the house of Haman, it is certainly the divine work of Hashem as mentioned above,
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מִצַּד אֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ,
yet nonetheless it does not operate from the perspective of ultimate, absolute truth,
דְּזֶה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק בִּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת,
for taking over a fallen entity applies only to other nations,
דְּעַל יְדֵי נִיצּוּחַ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם קוֹלְטִים הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם שַׁיָּיךְ דְּהֵם לָקְחוּ אַרְצָם,
where through Israel's victory they absorb the latent goodness within them, which is why they rightfully inherited their land,
וְנִקְרָא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם "אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן" –
and the Land of Israel is still termed 'the Land of Canaan'—
שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל לָקְחוּ חֶלְקָם וְקָלְטוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם.
meaning that Israel claimed their allotted portion and extracted the sparks of good within them.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תִּמְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
In contrast to Amalek concerning whom it is stated: 'You shall utterly blot out, etc.,'

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח299 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Amalek 2 — "From under the heavens" — that Amalek shall have neither offspring nor descendant under the whole expanse of the heavens; that they should not say, "This camel belonged to Amalek, this palm tree belonged to Amalek, this ewe belonged to Amalek." Therefore Scripture says, "From under the heavens" — that Amalek shall have neither offspring nor descendant under the whole expanse of the heavens.):
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Mekhilta, end of Parashat Beshalach):
שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ: "שׁוֹר זֶה שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק",
so that people never say: 'this ox belonged to Amalek,'
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בָּהֶם קְלִיטַת הַחֵלֶק כְּלָל,
meaning that no extraction or absorption of any spiritual portion is applicable to them whatsoever,
רַק נִיצּוּחָם הוּא אַבְדָנָם מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
rather their defeat means their absolute, total obliteration.
וְאֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ נְתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן?
How then can an inheritance or appointment over the house of Haman be relevant,
כִּי בְּאַבְדָנוֹ אֵין כָּאן עוֹד בֵּית הָמָן שֶׁיִּרְשׁוּ מֵהֶם וְלֹא קָלְטוּ מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם!
since in his annihilation there is no longer any 'house of Haman' to inherit, nor did they absorb anything from him!
רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִמְחָה זֵכֶר שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר כֵּן,
Rather, in this physical world, as long as the memory of Amalek has not yet been fully blotted out, it is fitting to speak thus;
כִּי מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן הֵם גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה,
for from the perspective of worldly illusion, they too appear part of the fabric of Creation,
אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ יֵשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן אֵיזֶה צוֹרֶךְ בְּרִיאָה
and if so, perforce they must also serve some purpose in Creation,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יוּכְלוּ לִקְלוֹט שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה גַּם כֵּן.
and Israel could seemingly extract this root as well.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת אֵינָם מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה כְּלָל,
Yet from the perspective of ultimate truth, they are not part of Creation at all,
שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ רַק כְּדֵי לְמַחוֹתָם מִן הָעוֹלָם.
having been created solely in order to be erased from the world.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַפּוּרִים דַּעֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מְגִילָּה ה300 Megillah 5b — Rabbah son of Rava said: Even if you say that he planted on his own day of Purim — they accepted upon themselves eulogy and fasting, but labor they did not accept upon themselves. For at first it is written, "gladness and feasting and a festival day," and at the end it is written, "to make them days of feasting and gladness," while "a festival day" is not written. Rashi: Our reading is “Even if you say it was on his own day”: Rabbi planted on the very day on which his townsmen read the Megillah. As for your difficulty from “a festival day,” on which labor is forbidden — the verse “gladness and feasting and a festival day” is written at the outset, before they accepted the days upon themselves; but when they accepted them they accepted only gladness and feasting, so as to forbid eulogy and fasting, while “a festival day” they did not accept upon themselves. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): "Gladness — this is a festival day" is also the holiness of the festival, the holiness of time, which Israel sanctifies; and although "a festival day," as regards the prohibition of labor, "they did not accept upon themselves," as stated in Megillah 5b, nevertheless the joy and the mitzvos practiced on Purim fall at a fixed time of the month, which Israel sanctifies, since they intercalate the months.:),
And this explains the essence of Purim, that they did not accept upon themselves the prohibition of creative labor (Megillah 5b),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for in truth, cessation from labor originates directly from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְשׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
requiring no human striving whatsoever,
וְשַׁיָּיךְ רַק מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
and is applicable only from the vantage of Hashem and the fixed, enduring sanctity of Shabbat.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יוֹם טוֹב דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי" הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת;
In contrast, Yom Tov which 'Israel sanctifies' operates through active effort;
רַק טַעַם בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה מִשּׁוּם דִּבְיוֹם טוֹב נִיתּוֹסַף קְדוּשָׁה מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת עַל יְדֵי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי,
and the rationale for the cessation of labor there is because on Yom Tov a renewed sanctity is added through Israel sanctifying it,
וְאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה מִשְׁתָּרֶשֶׁת בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת
and that added sanctity takes root in the pristine sanctity of Shabbat—
דְּהַיְינוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹנֵק מִזֶּה,
namely the sanctity of Hashem Who is the Root of all from which all existence suckles—
וְנַעֲשֵׂית מֵהוֹסָפַת קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
and through that addition of holiness it likewise becomes a fixed and permanent sanctity.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּפוּרִים אֵין הוֹסָפַת דָּבָר,
In contrast, on Purim there is no addition of anything new,
רַק שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אוֹר זֶה דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ הוֹסָפַת דָּבָר
save that this supreme light is revealed: that there is no need for any addition,
דְּאֵין כָּאן תּוֹסֶפֶת כִּי דְּבוּקִים בָּעִיקָּר.
there being no supplement here because they are bound essentially to the Core.
וְזֶה טַעַם "כָּל הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת בְּטֵלִים וִימֵי הַפּוּרִים לֹא יִהְיוּ בְּטֵלִים"
And this is the inner reason why 'all festivals will be annulled, yet the days of Purim will never be annulled'

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ מִשְׁלֵי פָּרָשָׁה ט301 Midrash Mishlei 9 — "She has also set her table" (Prov. 9:2) — she set a table for herself in this world and in the world to come. And what is this? The good name she acquired for herself in this world and in the world to come. For all the festivals are destined to be nullified, but the days of Purim will never be nullified, as it is said, "And these days of Purim shall not pass from among the Jews" (Esther 9:28). R. Elazar said: The Day of Atonement, too, will never be nullified, as it is said, "And this shall be for you an everlasting statute, to atone for the children of Israel from all their sins once a year." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The festivals will be nullified — so that one will no longer say "as the Lord lives, who brought out" — because each marks a going out from some particular immersion in evil, and the holiness of each, revealed through its particular miracle, is nullified when a greater holiness is revealed, like a candle in daylight; but Purim is not a going out from a particular immersion — it is the going out from the general root of evil, Amalek, "the first of the nations," and it clarifies the root of Israel: that even when they are in every evil, it is not truly so. Every redemption is a going out from evil to good, but Purim shows that even while in evil they are not evil at all; and this holiness is not nullified by a greater holiness, for all the others come from the side of virtue, whereas the virtue of the days of Purim comes from the side of lack, and the greater the lack, the greater the virtue.),
(as written in Midrash Mishlei, Parashah 9),
כִּי כָּל מוֹעֵד עַל יְדֵי נֵס וִישׁוּעָה נִתְחַדֵּשׁ הוֹסָפָה,
for every other festival brought an added novelty through an historical miracle and deliverance,
וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִהְיֶה ה' לְאוֹר יוֹמָם וְאֵין כָּאן הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת;
whereas in the World to Come Hashem Himself will be their everlasting light, leaving no place for separate novelty;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים הוּא גַּם כֵּן אוֹר זֶה.
unlike the days of Purim which embody this exact primordial light.
וּמִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה.
And from the perspective of Israel sanctifying it, a cessation of labor does not apply.
וְנִמְצָא בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין כָּאן הוֹסָפָה,
Consequently, in truth there is no supplement here,
רַק מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ הוֹסָפָה
only that from the vantage of this physical world there appears to be an addition,
דְּזֶה עַצְמוֹ הוֹסָפָה שֶׁנִּיתּוֹסַף הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ דְּאֵין הוֹסָפָה כְּלָל.
since it is itself a magnificent addition that this sublime perception was added: that no addition is needed at all!
וְזֶהוּ הַנְּתִינָה עַל בֵּית הָמָן,
And this explains the appointment over the house of Haman,
דְּנִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ
for the triumph over Amalek is achieved through this very realization:
שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שֶׁאֵין הוֹסָפָה כְּלָל,
attaining the awareness that there is no addition whatsoever,
הִיפּוּךְ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הוֹמֶה וּמְהַמֶּה
the exact antithesis of Amalek who roars and agitates,
וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹתִיּוֹת "עֲלַק" – הִיא עֲלוּקָה דְּצָוְוחַת "הַב הַב".
containing the letters of alak
(ע-ל-ק
)—the insatiable leech (alukah) crying 'give, give!'
וְנִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַהֵיפוּךְ
And the defeat of Amalek occurs through complete inversion
וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי הַקְּלִיטָה מִמֶּנּוּ;
and not through extracting or elevating anything from him;
וְהַהֵיפוּךְ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת דְּבֵיקוּת זֶה לְגַמְרֵי
and this inversion is the attainment of total cleaving,
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ חַד בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ,
perceiving that the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are utterly one in ultimate truth,
וְהֵם נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים,
and they constitute a boundless heritage,
וּבְמַה שֶּׁאֵין גְּבוּל אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ תּוֹסֶפֶת.
and within that which has no boundary, no addition can ever apply.

sections.en: Shushan Purim, Walls, and Inner Restraint

items.h: Walled cities symbolize spiritual containment; Purim and Shushan Purim reveal disciplined desire, purified anger, and bodily longing directed wholly toward Heaven.

Seif 1 — Walls, Restraint, and Shushan Purim
The walled city symbolizes disciplined desire, while Purim purifies anger and bodily longing for Heaven's sake.

p: עִנְיַן שׁוּשַׁן פּוּרִים,
The matter of Shushan Purim,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עִיר פְּרוּצָה אֵין חוֹמָה אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵין מַעְצָר לְרוּחוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, כח).
is in accordance with what is written (Proverbs 25:28): "Like a breached city without a wall is a man whose spirit has no restraint."

וְכֵן בַּפָּשׁוּט אָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת קי302 Ketubot 110b — R. Yose bar Chanina said: From where do we know that dwelling in walled cities is hard? As it is said: "And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem" (Nehemiah 11:2). Rashi (s.v. "dwelling in walled cities is hard"): Because everyone settles there and they are pressed together, and the houses are built close to one another so that there is no air; whereas in a town there are gardens and orchards adjoining the houses, and their air is good.:):
And so in its plain sense they stated (Ketubot 110b):
"יְשִׁיבַת כְּרַכִּים קָשָׁה",
"Dwelling in walled metropolises is difficult,"
שֶׁהַמָּקוֹם דָּחוּק
because the space is cramped,
וְצָרִיךְ לַעֲצוֹר עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּהַרְחָבָה.
and one must constrict oneself not to expand broadly.
וְלֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "פְּרָזוֹת תֵּשֵׁב יְרוּשָׁלַיִם",
And concerning the ultimate future it is said (Zechariah 2:8): "Jerusalem shall be inhabited as open villages (perazot),"
כִּי יִהְיֶה בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר
for there will then be the annulment of the evil inclination,
וְלֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ עֲצִירַת רוּחַ
and they will not require restraint of spirit,
וְיוּכְלוּ לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט כְּכָל אַוַּת נַפְשָׁם.
and will be able to expand in accordance with all their soul's longing.
כִּי רַק מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הוּא הַצּוֹרֶךְ לְצַמְצֵם וְלַעֲצוֹר עַצְמוֹ.
For solely on account of the inclination is there the necessity to constrict and restrain oneself.

וְהָנֵי דִּכְרַכִּים "מִיגַנְיָא טְפֵי וּמְכַסְיָא" (מְגִילָּה ה:)303 Megillah 5b — With regard to the sale of houses in walled cities he had no doubt. Where he was in doubt was with regard to the reading of the Megillah: what are the unwalled towns and what are the walled cities of which Scripture speaks concerning the reading of the Megillah? Is it because these are exposed and those are not exposed — and this city too is exposed; or perhaps because these are sheltered and those are not sheltered — and this city too is sheltered? On that account he was in doubt. Rashi: “Where he was in doubt was with regard to the reading of the Megillah” — for there no wall is specified; Scripture writes only of unwalled towns and of those that are not unwalled, and he was in doubt whether “unwalled” denotes a place that lies exposed or denotes a city that is easily taken. מֵעֲמָלֵק
And those in walled cities are "more shielded and hidden" (Megillah 5b) from Amalek,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כָּל כָּךְ טַעֲנָה נֶגְדָּם.
who possesses less of an adversarial claim against them.
כִּי עִיקַּר הִתְעוֹרְרוּת עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל יְדֵי טַעֲנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
For the primary awakening of Amalek occurs through a claim lodged against Israel,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא "וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק" פָּרָשָׁה א304 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Amalek 1 — Others say: "Rephidim" means nothing other than slackness of hands. Because they let their hands go slack from words of Torah, the enemy came upon them; for the enemy comes only on account of a slackening of the hands from Torah, as it is said, "And it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, that he forsook the Torah of the Lord, and all Israel with him." And what was the punishment for this? "And it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had trespassed against the Lord."):
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Mekhilta, "Vayavo Amalek," Parashah 1):
בִּרְפִידִים – מִיָּד "וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק",
at Rephidim (where their hands slackened from Torah) immediately "Amalek came,"
שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ וּמִתְעוֹרֵר לָבוֹא,
for he senses this lapse and is stirred to attack;
כִּי מִשָּׁם הוּא יְנִיקַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֵשָׂו,
because from there derives the vitality of Esau's root,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה ו.)305 Megillah 6a — Caesarea and Jerusalem: if a man says to you that both are destroyed, do not believe him; that both are settled, do not believe him; that Caesarea is destroyed and Jerusalem settled, or that Jerusalem is destroyed and Caesarea settled — believe him. As it is said, "I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste": if this one is full, that one is laid waste; if that one is full, this one is laid waste. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: From here — "and one people shall be stronger than the other people." Rashi: “I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste” — the opening of the verse is “because Tyre said concerning Jerusalem”; that is, now I shall be filled from her ruin. Maharsha: Of the first two alternatives “do not believe him” is said of each one separately, whereas “believe him” is said of the remaining two together and only once. Had “believe him” likewise been said of each separately, one might have understood that only one of them is to be believed — either that Jerusalem is always settled and Caesarea laid waste, or always the reverse; in truth both are to be believed, for at times Caesarea is settled and Jerusalem laid waste, and at times the opposite. So too “one people shall be stronger than the other people,” where Scripture leaves unstated which of them prevails — meaning that each prevails over the other, now this one and now that. Maharal (Gevuros Hashem, ch. 64): There are nations whose prosperity cannot be found while Israel prospers, and when Israel prospers those nations do not. This is the meaning of “I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste” — Tyre was filled only from the ruin of Jerusalem; and so in time to come Jerusalem will be built and established when the city of Edom is in its turn laid waste. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 35): Abraham was full of holy desire and love, while Lot was full of lewdness; therefore "the land could not bear them to dwell together," for when this one rises that one falls — so much so that the Sages said it of Caesarea and Jerusalem. Only after Lot parted from him was Abraham assured of the holiness of the Land. עַל פָּסוּק "אִמָּלְאָה הָחֳרָבָה",
as our Sages taught (Megillah 6a) on the verse (Ezekiel 26:2) "I shall be filled from the ruined one,"

וּכְשֶׁזֶּה קָם זֶה וְכוּלֵי (רַשִּׁ"י תּוֹלְדוֹת כה, כג306 Rashi on Genesis 25:23 — "And the one people shall be stronger than the other people" — they shall not be equal in greatness; when this one rises, the other falls. And so it says, "I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste" (Ezek. 26:2) — Tyre was filled only from the ruin of Jerusalem.).
and 'when this one rises, the other falls, etc.' (Rashi, Genesis 25:23).
וְעַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה נְפִילָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִתְגַּדֵּל;
And through any spiritual fall, Heaven forbid, within the souls of Israel, he magnifies himself;
וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר הַהֲנָאָה מִסְּעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע – "גִּדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר".
and immediately following their illicit pleasure from that wicked one's banquet—"King Ahasuerus promoted Haman, etc."

וְאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג:)307 Bava Batra 123b — R. Chelbo asked R. Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, "And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph" (Genesis 30:25) — what was different once Joseph was born [that Jacob then asked to return home]? He said to him: Jacob our father saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, as it is stated: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for straw, and they shall kindle in them and consume them" (Obadiah 1:18). Rashbam: "What was different" — why he did not wish to return to his father's house until Joseph was born. Maharsha: By acquiring the birthright and taking the blessing from Esau it was granted to Jacob that he should rule over Esau, who was the elder; and all of this Jacob handed on to Joseph, as is derived from "And I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite" (Genesis 48:22). It is in this way that the seed of Esau was delivered into the hand of Joseph and was not delivered into the hand of his other brothers. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Batra 123b): This matter — that the seed of Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph — is exceedingly deep. Over the seed of Joseph the eye has no power, while Esau's blessing is the opposite of this, as it is said, "and the hands are the hands of Esau" (Genesis 27:22) — for the hands are the most outward of the limbs, the rest being within. The seed of Joseph therefore prevail, because their blessing is from a place and a level over which Esau's eye has no power; whereas the other tribes, whose blessing was from the revealed level, could not overcome the power of Esau, which is itself revealed. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 58): Esau, who belongs only to this world, is called 'aluf', a captain of a thousand (the utmost of this world's blessing), but not the rank of a king who endures forever. Therefore Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, who was "ruler over all the land of Egypt": a ruler, that is, a minister and chief of the same pattern as 'aluf', like Messiah son of Joseph, who is at the rank of ruler and is slain, having no everlasting endurance, which belongs only to David. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The obstinacy of Israel issues from wisdom, through the knowledge that joins wisdom to the powers of action, and is obstinate only for the honor of Heaven; therefore Amalek falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek is the root of obstinacy, his chief claim being against the desires of Israel, as the Sages said on "who happened upon you"; but his obstinacy is against the will of the Blessed One, whereas the obstinacy of Joseph's seed accords with the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Of Amalek it is said, "and he feared not God," and the Sages said that this is why he falls into the hand of the seed of Joseph, of whom it is said, "I fear God." And though "he feared not God" refers to Israel, it means [that it came upon them] through Amalek "who happened upon you," who brought into them imaginings and forces of forgetfulness, whereby they became "faint and weary" and did not fear God. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph because, as the Sages said, "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven": fear of Heaven is the province of man's choice and effort, for love can come into a person's heart of itself, but fear cannot. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eira 1): Before Benjamin's birth Jacob was given tidings of Benjamin, Menashe and Ephraim, who are Amalek's adversaries, as the Gemara says that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek stands against the holiness of the covenant (they would cut off the circumcisions of Israel), while Menashe and Ephraim are Joseph's two tribes, and Benjamin too is the attribute of the Tzaddik; therefore the name E-l Sha-dai, which corresponds to the attribute of the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world, is mentioned there. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 38): On account of Rachel's modesty the Holy One, blessed be He, restored [the birthright] to her, in that every beginning of salvation is aroused through her children. Thus every beginning of salvation is revealed through the children of Rachel, as the Gemara says that Jacob saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. Sod Yesharim (Purim 15): If Israel rely on the strength they possess from their root, Amalek at once stands against them, claiming that he too has strength from the root, being born of Isaac and Rebecca. Therefore the Sages said that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph: the seed of Joseph rely on no strength at all, but clarify wherever there is something to clarify, and where the power of their service does not reach, there the Blessed One will clarify it for good. דְּאֵין נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
And they taught (Bava Batra 123b) that Amalek falls only by the hand of the offspring of Joseph,
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף הוּא הַצִּמְצוּם וַעֲצִירָה מִתַּאֲווֹת.
for the essential root of Joseph is constriction and restraint against bodily desires.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּיֵשׁ שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים: דְּכַעַס וְתַאֲוָה, שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים,
And it is known that there are two core inclinations: anger and lust, which are two opposites,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מַכּוֹת י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)308 Makkot 10a — As it is written, "Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with blood" (Hos. 6:8). What is "tracked with blood"? R. Elazar said: They would lie in ambush to kill people. And why are those on this side and on that side set far apart, while the middle ones are close together? Abaye said: In Shechem too murderers are common, as it is written, "And as bands of robbers lie in wait for a man, so is the company of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem" (Hos. 6:9). What is "the company of priests"? R. Elazar said: They would band together to kill people, like those priests who band together to divide the priestly gifts at the threshing floors. Rashi: "They would lie in ambush" — they would lie in wait for them. Hebron and Kadesh lie far from the borders of the land, two quarters of its length in, so that one who kills at the edge of the border must flee a quarter of the length of the land; the middle city is close, for one who kills between Hebron and Shechem, or between Shechem and Kadesh, is near a city of refuge on either side. Maharsha: Even so, murderers were not as common in Shechem as they were in Gilead; for if they were, the original difficulty would return to its place — three cities beyond the Jordan and three in the Land of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 250): When Jacob saw Esau "faint" from murder — that he had an intense desire for it — he absorbed the power of holiness within it, and it was given to the seed of Rachel, and to Joseph in particular, as stated, "In Gilead and Shechem murderers are common" — that is, inadvertent ones, which is why cities of refuge are needed. Meaning, among them is the good that is in murder, as I heard on "your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Mount Gilead": "hair" means anger and murder, and "from Mount Gilead" is the good [in it]. דִּבְגִלְעָד וּשְׁכֶם שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים,
and as written (Makkot 10a) that murderers were prevalent in Gilead and Shechem,
שֶׁהֵם מְקוֹמוֹת דְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף
which are the tribal territories of the seed of Joseph,
דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ עֲצִירַת תַּאֲוָה.
where mastery and restraint over physical desire prevailed.
וְכֵן עִיקַּר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִתְחִיל מִיָּרָבְעָם,
And likewise, the primary sin of idolatry began with Jeroboam (from Joseph);
כִּי בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הֵם קוֹרְאִים שְׁנֵי יְצָרִים: דִּזְנוּת וְדַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
for in the idioms of our Sages they are titled two inclinations: licentiousness and idolatry;
רַק אַחַר שֶׁבִּיטְּלוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵין מְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶלָּא בְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה,
only that after they abolished the inclination for idolatry, it operates solely through anger and murder,
אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הוּא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
yet its fundamental root is idolatry,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת309 Shabbat 105b — One who tears his garments in anger, or breaks his vessels in anger, or scatters his money in anger — let him be in your eyes as one who worships idols. For such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it says to him do this, and tomorrow it says to him do that, until at last it says to him worship idols — and he goes and worships. Rashi: [The Gemara cites this baraita to show that tearing in anger] is not a constructive act, for he thereby teaches and accustoms his inclination to come upon him. Maharsha: [The evil inclination] works by craft to bring a person from a minor transgression to a major one, as is expounded on the verse "who draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with a cart rope"; and one who tears his garments [in anger] is certainly also committing a transgression, for he violates [the prohibition] "You shall not destroy." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 105b): One who does something in anger to another, and not to himself, is regarded as accomplishing something for himself; but one who destroys his own garments commits utter ruin and is regarded as if he worships idols, for idolatry is destruction, as it is written, "lest you act destructively" (Deuteronomy 4:16), and one who goes after idolatry is utterly destroyed. The evil inclination, too, entices a person to his own destruction; hence, when a person follows it and heeds it to destroy and ruin, tomorrow it will entice him wholly after idolatry, which is destruction. (קה:): "הַשּׁוֹבֵר כְּלִי בַּחֲמָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי עַד וְכוּלֵי",
as written in Shabbat (105b): "One who smashes a vessel in his wrath, etc., is like one who serves idols,"
כִּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן הֵיפֶךְ מִזְּנוּת.
for idolatry is likewise the metaphysical opposite of licentiousness.

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין כא:)310 Eruvin 21b — "Come, my beloved, let us go out into the field" (Song of Songs 7:12) — the Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, do not judge me like the inhabitants of the large cities, among whom there is robbery and forbidden relations and vain oaths and false oaths. "Let us go out into the field" — come and I will show You Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah out of hardship. Rashi: "Large cities" are places of markets and of great settlement, where peddlers and merchants are constantly to be found; robbery and forbidden relations are therefore common in them. "The field" — countrymen and tillers of the soil, who nevertheless occupy themselves with Torah out of hardship. Maharsha: This verse belongs with the exposition given just above, "The mandrakes yield a fragrance — these are the young men of Israel who never tasted the taste of sin," for the verse that follows continues the same subject, as it concludes here, "there I will give you my loves — I will show You my glory and my greatness, the praise of my sons and daughters." Those are the young men and the daughters of Israel spoken of above, who never came to any matter of sin. בִּכְרַכִּים מָצוּי גָּזֵל וַעֲרָיוֹת,
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Eruvin 21b) that in metropolises robbery and illicit relations are common,
הַיְינוּ דְּתַאֲווֹת מָצוּי בִּכְרַכִּים יוֹתֵר;
meaning that lust is more prevalent in metropolises;
דְּ"מַעְצָר לְרוּחוֹ" רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּכַעַס, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "רוּחוֹ" בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב,
for "restraint over his spirit" signifies control over anger, which is called "his spirit" in biblical language,
דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה צָרִיךְ הֶקֵּף חוֹמָה וְהַגְדָּרָה לְגַמְרֵי,
whereas idolatry requires an absolute encompassing wall and hermetic containment;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּתַאֲווֹת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מז.)311 Sotah 47a — The Sages taught: The left hand should always push away and the right hand draw near — not like Elisha, who pushed Gehazi away with both his hands. It is taught: R. Shimon ben Elazar says: With the evil inclination, with a child, and with a wife, the left hand should push away and the right hand draw near. Maharsha (on the parallel sugya, Sanhedrin 107b, to which he refers here): [The baraita] assigns the pushing away to the left hand and the drawing near to the right because everywhere the left alludes to the attribute of judgment and the right to mercy: thus "let the left," which is the attribute of judgment, push away, and let the right, which is mercy, draw near. "Not as Elisha, who thrust Gehazi away with both hands" — that is, he turned even the mercy into anger.
