"the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, but he did not know"): Moses' words, 'your sons died only to sanctify the Name,' cannot mean that they died without sin, for there is no sanctification or glory of the Omnipresent in that — far be it from Him to execute judgment without justice; rather, it is His glory to exact punishment from the righteous in this world for the few transgressions in their hands, and thereby He is exalted, sanctified and feared: if so with the righteous, how much more with the wicked. The meaning, then, is that they did not die on account of this sin [as such], but because "round about Him it storms mightily" (Psalms 50:3) [— He is exacting with those near Him], and through them His Name is sanctified and feared. This is why Moses said, 'I had thought it would be through me or through you,' we being the nearer; but when he saw their death he said that they were the more honored, and that it was of them He had hinted "sanctified by My glory" — by My honored ones — to exact punishment from them for light transgressions. Maharal (Derech Chaim 3:2): Of Aaron it is written "And Aaron was silent": he accepted the attribute [of justice] of the Blessed Name in silence, and at once received a reward, as the Sages expounded (Torat Kohanim) from the next section, "And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them" — to Elazar and Itamar — because they had been alike in silence and accepted the decree of the Omnipresent with love. For whoever accepts the decree of the Blessed Name is fit for recompense, since he takes the yoke upon himself; every yoke is the essence of service, and all service stands to be recompensed — so the acceptance of the decree is fit above all to receive a reward. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 18): Since man is physical, what he is to know must be made clear to him in a manner fitting a physical being; so, that all might know the sanctity of the Tabernacle, He said "and it shall be sanctified by My glory" — 'by My honored ones,' Nadav and Avihu, who would commit a sin and the House be sanctified through them. For He, blessed be He, who dwells in this House is separate from all beings, and that is the sanctity of the House; and this is shown in that even with the righteous He does not unite and has no joining with them. Were He joined to beings, He would surely be joined to those who love Him and are honored by Him, and then He would not execute judgment upon them; the judgment He executes upon the righteous shows that He, blessed be He, is entirely separate even from those who love Him.:)
Except that at that moment the transcendent light of the Mikdash also began to radiate (Zevachim 115b):
"וְנִקְדַּשׁ בִּכְבֹדִי" – בִּמְכֻבָּדַי,
"'and it shall be sanctified by My glory'—through My honored ones,"

דְּ"כָל הַמְכַבֵּד וְכוּלֵי331 Avot d'Rabbi Natan 27:1 — R. Yose says: Whoever honours the Torah is himself honoured by others, as it is said, “For those who honour Me I shall honour, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed.”" (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כז);
for "whoever honors the Torah, etc." (Avot DeRabbi Natan, beginning of Chapter 27);
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם גָּרְמוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר זֶה דְּמִדַּת הַכָּבוֹד וְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְיִרְאָה,
and since they caused the manifestation of this light of Glory, reverent etiquette, and awe,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְאֶת מִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ" שֶׁזֶּה שַׁיָּיךְ לְשֵׁם "מִקְדָּשׁ",
and as it is written: "and you shall revere My sanctuary," which pertains directly to the title Mikdash,
עַל כֵּן הֵם קְרוּיִים "מְכֻבָּדַי" שֶׁהֵם מְכֻבָּדִים אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
therefore they are designated "My honored ones," being precious and honored before Hashem, blessed be He,
וְלָכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִתְכַּבֵּד עַל יָדָם.
and therefore Hashem was glorified through them.

וְכֵן בֵּית עֵלִי, אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת נה332 Shabbat 55b — R. Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R. Yonatan: Whoever says that the sons of Eli sinned is simply mistaken, as it is said, "And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the Ark of the Covenant of God, priests to the Lord." Then how do I uphold "who lay with the women"? Since they delayed their bird-offerings, so that the women did not return to their husbands, Scripture accounts it to them as though they had lain with them. Rashi: "Whoever says that the sons of Eli sinned" — with a married woman — "is simply mistaken"; in contempt for the sacred offerings, however, they did sin. "Since they delayed their bird-offerings": they would refuse to offer any sacrifice except grudgingly, as it is written, "Even before they burned the fat…" (I Samuel 2:15); so when women after a flux or after childbirth came from elsewhere to Shiloh to offer their pairs of birds, they delayed offering them, and the women, unable to rely on them to offer them, stayed there and did not return to their husbands until they saw their offerings brought and were pure for sacred things and for entering the Temple court. Therefore Scripture accounts it to them as though they had lain with them, for they kept them from procreation. Tosafos (s.v. "whoever says that the sons of Eli sinned is simply mistaken"): That is, in what is written, "who lay with the women", they did not sin; but they did treat the sacred offerings with contempt, as it is written, "Even before they burned the fat…" (I Samuel 2:15). Maharsha: The verse "And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there, priests to the Lord" would be superfluous, with no purpose in its place, were it not for this exposition, which equates the two: just as Phinehas did not sin, so Hophni did not sin. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 55b): Taking a woman away from her husband is itself accounted as lying with her, for lying with a woman is nothing other than taking her to oneself. With men as great as Hophni and Phinehas, "priests to the Lord" — and all the more since they did this to all the women of Israel, and above all when the women had brought their offerings to be purified for their husbands — they took the women from their husbands, and keeping the wives with themselves is accounted as lying and union with them.:)
And likewise regarding the house of Eli, our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shabbat 55b)
חֶטְאָם הָעִיקָּר בְּבִזָּיוֹן קָדָשִׁים,
that their sin was essentially in showing contempt for sacred offerings,
דַּ"אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכְּבוּן וְגוֹמֵר" הַיְינוּ שֶׁשִּׁיהוּ קִנֵּיהֶם,
for "that they lay with the women, etc." meant that they delayed their sacrificial bird-offerings,
דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד בִּזָּיוֹן קָדָשִׁים;
which also stemmed from contempt toward holy offerings;
זֶה הוֹלִיד קְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם בְּתֹקֶף,
yet this very failure ultimately birthed the transcendent holiness of the Mikdash, which is the powerful manifestation of Heaven's glory,
כִּי חֶטְאָם נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "חַטַּאת הַנְּעָרִים וְגוֹמֵר",
for their sin is termed in Scripture: "the sin of the young men, etc.",
וְ"חַטָּאת" הַיְינוּ שׁוֹגֵג,
and chattat signifies unintentional error,
וְ"נְעָרִים" מַשְׁמָע דְּהוּא מַעֲשֵׂה נַעֲרוּת לְבַד.
and "young men" implies that it was merely an act of youthful impetuosity.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בְּנַעֲרוּת יֵשׁ לָאָדָם תֹּקֶף אַהֲבָה וְשִׂמְחָה, כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי דַּרְכּוֹ וְעִנְיָנָיו,
That is to say: in youth a person possesses intense love and joy, each according to his path and pursuits,
וְהָעוֹבֵד ה' בְּנַעֲרוּת, עֲבוֹדָתוֹ בְּשִׂמְחָה יְתֵירָה,
and one who serves Hashem in his youth conducts his divine service with overflowing joy,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א פָּסוּק א)333 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1:10 — He wrote three books: Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs. Which of them did he write first? R. Yonatan said: He said Song of Songs first, then Proverbs, and then Ecclesiastes. R. Yonatan derived it from the way of the world: when a man is young he utters words of song; when he has grown, he utters words of proverbs; when he grows old, he speaks of vanities. דְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ
as they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1) that Solomon recited the Song of Songs in his youth

(וְעַיֵּין זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, לט עַמּוּד א334 Zohar 2:39a — It was taught: His names were all named after wisdom, and therefore he composed three books — Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes, and Proverbs — all of them to complete wisdom. Song of Songs corresponds to lovingkindness, Ecclesiastes corresponds to judgment, Proverbs corresponds to mercy, all in order to complete wisdom. And everything he did, he did in order to display wisdom, corresponding to the supernal rung; and yet he said, "in the days of my vanity," "vanity of vanities.").
(and see Zohar II, 39a).
וְכֵן בִּכְלַל הָעוֹלָם: אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הַהַתְחָלָה וְהָיָה בְּתֹקֶף אַהֲבָה,
And so it was in the history of the world: our father Abraham, peace be upon him, was the starting point, operating with the intensity of love,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹלַד יִצְחָק וּבָא הַיִּרְאָה.
and afterward Isaac was born and awe arrived.
וּבִשְׁבִיל תֹּקֶף אַהֲבָתָם וּדְבֵיקוּתָם, זֶה מוֹלִיד מִיעוּט יִרְאָה וְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
And because of the overpowering force of their love and cleaving, this breeds a diminishment of awe and reverent etiquette,
עַד שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּבִזָּיוֹן קָדָשִׁים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
until it looks like contempt for holy matters, Heaven forbid.
וְקִבְּלוּ עָנְשָׁם דּוּגְמַת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא,
And they received their retribution just like Nadav and Avihu,
וְנִגְרַם שְׁבִיַּת אָרוֹן שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת חוּרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
which caused the capture of the Ark, which prefigured the destruction of the Holy Temple.

וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁאָמַר לְאֶבְיָתָר: "עֲנָתֹת לֵךְ עַל שָׂדֶיךָ" (מְלָכִים-א ב, כו335 I Kings 2:26 — And to Abiathar the priest the king said: "Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you are a man deserving of death; but on this day I will not put you to death, because you carried the Ark of the Lord God before David my father, and because you suffered in all that my father suffered." Rashi: "To Anathoth" — he was from there. "For you are a man deserving of death" — because you rebelled against my father's kingship in siding with Adonijah, to make him king without his knowledge. "For you carried the ark" — when my father fled before Absalom, and you were afflicted with him in that trouble, as it is said, "the people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness" [II Samuel 17:29]. Radak: "Anathoth" — [go] to Anathoth, for he was from there, and Anathoth belonged to the priests. "A man of death" — one who rebels against the kingship is liable to death, and Abiathar rebelled against David in siding with Adonijah, knowing that David meant to crown Solomon; and even had he not known, it was rebellion to crown a king in David's lifetime without his leave. "You were afflicted" — for he went with David when he fled from Saul and when he fled from Absalom, and the hardship of the road was theirs. Metzudas Dovid: He said this to Abiathar on seeing that he still persisted in his rebellion, in counselling Adonijah to ask for Abishag. "To Anathoth" — go to your own place, Anathoth, which was a city of priests; "for you are a man deserving of death" — for having been party to the conspiracy to crown Adonijah without my father the king's knowledge, and therefore you shall no longer sit here and see my face.),
And this is the reason Solomon said to Evyatar: "Go to Anatot, unto your own fields" (I Kings 2:26),

כִּי יָדוּעַ בְּמִדְרָשׁ אֵיכָה (פְּתִיחְתָּא א)336 Eikhah Rabbah, Petichta 1 — "Layish" (Isaiah 10:30) — and if not, "layish": the lion will come up against you. This is the wicked Nebuchadnezzar, of whom it is written, "The lion has gone up from his thicket" (Jeremiah 4:7). "Destitute" — destitute of righteous men, destitute of prophecy, destitute of commandments and good deeds. "Anathoth" — and if not, "Anathoth": that man of Anathoth will come and prophesy concerning you, as it is written, "The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, of the priests who were in Anathoth" (Jeremiah 1:1). And when the punishment came, he lamented over them: "How [eikhah]...": "וְאִם לָאו עֲנָתוֹת, הָא יִרְמְיָה עֲנָתוֹת וְכוּלֵי337 Isaiah 10:30; Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 1 — “Cry aloud, O daughter of Gallim; hearken, O Laishah; O poor Anathoth!” And they expounded this verse in Eichah Rabbah: “Hearken” — hearken to My commandments, hearken to words of Torah, hearken to the words of prophecy, hearken to righteousness and good deeds; and if not — “Anathoth,” I shall come and prophesy against you the words of the son of Chilkiyahu, who was of Anathoth. Since calamity was to come upon them, He lamented over them: Eichah!",
for it is known in Midrash Eichah (Petichta 1): "and if not Anatot, behold Jeremiah is of Anatot, etc.",
דַּעֲנָתוֹת רוֹמֵז לְחוּרְבָּן,
showing that Anatot alludes to destruction,
הַיְינוּ דִּלְךָ יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחוּרְבָּן עִנְיַן מִקְדָּשׁ וּבִזָּיוֹן קָדָשִׁים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
meaning: you bear a connection to the destruction of the sanctuary and contempt for holy things, Heaven forbid.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח.)338 Rosh Hashanah 18a — "And therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be expiated by sacrifice or offering forever." Rava said: By sacrifice and offering it is not expiated, but it is expiated by Torah. Abaye said: By sacrifice and offering it is not expiated, but it is expiated by Torah and acts of kindness. Maharsha (on the parallel sugya, Yevamot 105a, to which he refers here): These are the three pillars of the world, as we learned: "The world stands on three things — on Torah, on the [Temple] service, and on acts of kindness" (Avot 1:2). Since they sinned through the service, as it is said, "Why do you kick at My sacrifice and at My offering?" (I Samuel 2:29), and an accuser cannot become an advocate, [it is not expiated by that]; but by the other two pillars, Torah and acts of kindness, it is expiated. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 18a): It is known that acts of kindness atone more than sacrifices, and so does the Torah, for acts of kindness stand above the sacrifices; therefore there is atonement through Torah and acts of kindness, for by them one cleaves to kindness and to Torah. [The house of Eli] sinned through sacrifice and offerings, as Scripture records, and the verse says that through sacrifice and offerings, by which they sinned, it shall not be expiated — but through something that stands above sacrifice and burnt offering it is expiated. דְּמִתְכַּפֵּר עֲווֹן בֵּית עֵלִי בַּתּוֹרָה,
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Rosh Hashanah 18a) that the iniquity of the house of Eli is atoned through Torah,
דְּרַק בְּזֶבַח וּמִנְחָה אֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר;
for solely through sacrifice and meal-offering is it not atoned;
דְּתוֹרָה הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּידְהוּ, שֶׁהֵם בִּזּוּ עִנְיַן יִרְאָה וּבָחֲרוּ בִּתְקִיפוּת וְעֹז דְּתוֹרָה.
since Torah was their personal spiritual realm, as they dismissed external awe and chose the passionate strength and boldness of Torah.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה כְּעִנְיַן חַבְרוּתָא כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא,
And because this conduct was akin to treating Heaven with excessive peer-like familiarity,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אִם יִתְכַּפֵּר וְגוֹמֵר",
concerning this it was said: "if the iniquity of Eli's house shall be atoned, etc.",
דְּקָרְבָּנוֹת דּוּגְמַת תְּפִלָּה צָרִיךְ יִרְאָה לִהְיוֹת הָעִיקָּר,
for with sacrifices, which parallel prayer, awe must be the primary foundation,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתּוֹרָה שִׂמְחָה הָעִיקָּר, רַק יִרְאָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ.
unlike in Torah where joy is primary, provided only that one's fear of sin precedes his wisdom.
וּבַכֹּהֲנִים נֶאֱמַר: "וָאֶתְּנֵם לוֹ מוֹרָא וְגוֹמֵר" (מַלְאָכִי ב, ה),
And regarding priests it is stated: "and I gave them to him for fear, etc." (Malachi 2:5),
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקָּר לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
this being the essential requirement for a High Priest;
לְכָךְ נִדְחוּ נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וּבֵית עֵלִי מִכְּהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה.
therefore Nadav, Avihu, and the house of Eli were removed from the High Priesthood.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַדְּרַבָּה, "וְנִקְדַּשׁ בִּכְבֹדִי",
Nevertheless through this, on the contrary, "and it shall be sanctified by My glory" was fulfilled,
נִגְרַם אוֹר זֶה דְּיִרְאָה;
bringing about this transcendent illumination of awe;

וְהוּא כְּטַעַם (בְּרָכוֹת ח.)339 Berakhot 8a — R. Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla: Since the day the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world but the four cubits of halakhah alone. And Abaye said: At first I would study in my house and pray in the synagogue; but once I heard this teaching of R. Chiyya bar Ami in the name of Ulla, I would pray only where I study. R. Ami and R. Asi, although they had thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, would pray only between the pillars, where they studied. Rashi: "Between the pillars" — for the study house was built upon them, above. Maharsha: While the Temple stood there was the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from which decided halakhah went forth by the Sanhedrin, and with them the Divine Presence surely dwelt. Now that the Temple is destroyed, those four cubits of halakhah which every Torah scholar fixes as the place of his study in the Talmud stand in its stead, so that the Divine Presence is with him there. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael 70): The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in the corporeal world, for the corporeal is removed from Him; what is His is the four cubits of halakhah. It is called halakhah because, as one who walks a road does not swerve to right or left, so a ruling of halakhah does not swerve from the point of truth. Just as He chose the Temple, which is fit for holiness because it stands at the centre — and the centre has no distance about it, distance belonging to the corporeal — so halakhah is wholly simple intellect, with no relation to the corporeal, and therefore the place where halakhah is belongs to Him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): Torah is "voice", the male, and prayer, said in a whisper, is "speech", the female; and just as "a woman who seeds first bears a male" and the females are made dependent on the males, so it says "they would pray only where they studied", and in Megillah the reverse, "they would study only where they prayed": for through the voice of Torah one merits prayer, and through prayer one begets the voice of Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): The word "voice" is joined to Jacob because the voice of the Oral Torah is the essential root of Jacob, and the voice of prayer is drawn from it, as with R. Ami and R. Asi, who would pray only between the pillars where they studied. For [the Sages] instituted that one first say "O Lord, open my lips", since one can pray only when the Blessed One opens his lips, and this opening comes through the Oral Torah.: "לָא הֲוֵי מְצַלֵּי אֶלָּא בֵּינֵי עַמּוּדֵי דַּהֲווֹ גָּרְסֵי",
and this mirrors the practice (Berakhot 8a): "he would pray only between the pillars where he studied,"
דְּעִיקַּר תֹּקֶף הַתְּפִלָּה כַּאֲשֶׁר הִיא בָּאָה מִתּוֹךְ דְּבַר תּוֹרָה הַקּוֹדֵם לָהּ.
for the ultimate power of prayer manifests when it emerges directly out of the words of Torah that preceded it.

sections.en: Spiritual Ascent, Descent, and Rosh Chodesh

items.h: The waxing and waning moon mirrors human rise and fall, teaching that deficiency itself is divinely created and can become the basis of renewal.

Seif 1 — The Waning Moon and Spiritual Renewal
Human ascent and descent mirror the moon, teaching that acknowledged deficiency is itself the basis of renewal.

p: הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ עוֹמֵד תָּמִיד בְּסֵדֶר וּמַצָּב אֶחָד,
Man does not remain constantly in a single order and status,
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ תָּדִיר עֲלִיּוֹת וִירִידוֹת
and he constantly experiences spiritual ascents and descents,
כַּנּוֹדָע לְכָל הַשָּׂם דְּרָכָיו.
as is known to all who examine their ways.
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה עִנְיַן מִיעוּט הַיָּרֵחַ,
And this reflects what Hashem, blessed be He, established within Creation concerning the diminution of the moon;
דְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁמֶשׁ וְיָרֵחַ הֵם רוֹמְזִים לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ,
for it is known that the sun and moon allude to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
דְּיָרֵחַ רוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין אוֹרָן מִן הַחַמָּה,
the moon alluding to the Congregation of Israel who receive their light from the sun,
"שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה'",
"'For a sun and a shield is Hashem'" (Psalms 84:12),
וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ מִלּוּי וְחִסָּרוֹן בְּכָל חוֹדֶשׁ.
and the moon undergoes waxing and waning each month.
וְהֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים בַּשָּׁנָה נֶגֶד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים,
And these are twelve months in the year corresponding to the twelve tribes,

כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיְחִי טו340 Midrash Tanchuma, Vayechi 15 — "All these are the twelve tribes of Israel." Elsewhere it is written, "Twelve princes shall he beget." These tribes correspond to the order of the world: twelve hours in the day and twelve hours in the night, and so too the constellations and the months, and the twelve stones of the ephod. Therefore, "All these are the twelve tribes of Israel."),
as is known from our Sages of blessed memory (Midrash Tanchuma, Vayechi 15);
הַיְינוּ דִּבְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ מַעֲלָה וְחִסָּרוֹן מְיוּחָד שֶׁאֵין בְּשֵׁבֶט אַחֵר,
meaning that within each tribe exists a distinct virtue and unique deficiency not present in any other tribe,
וּלְפִיכָךְ הֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִינֵי מִלּוּיִם וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִינֵי חֶסְרוֹנוֹת.
and therefore they constitute twelve types of fullness and twelve types of deficiencies.
וְאֵלּוּ הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת הוּא מַה שֶּׁמִּתּוֹלָדָה,
And these deficiencies are intrinsic from the very inception of creation,
כְּעִנְיַן "בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר רָע",
like the concept of "I created the evil inclination" (Kiddushin 30b),
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא הַחִסָּרוֹן וּמִלּוּיוֹ.
in that Hashem, blessed be He, created deficiency alongside its fulfillment.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן "הָבִיאוּ עָלַי כַּפָּרָה עַל שֶׁמִּעַטְתִּי הַיָּרֵחַ" (שְׁבוּעוֹת ט341 Shevuot 9a — Reish Lakish said: Why is the goat of the New Moon different, that of it alone is it said, "for the Lord" (Numbers 28:15)? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let this goat be an atonement for Me, for having diminished the moon. Rashi: "Bring atonement" — to appease the moon. Tosafos (s.v. "this goat shall be an atonement for Me"): The Arukh explains: this goat is an atonement for Israel, and "for Me" [means that it is] upon Me to fix a time for this atonement, and I fixed it on the New Moon to appease the moon. Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, Chullin 60b): [The moon in this passage alludes to the Community of Israel, who diminish themselves in this world.] Seeing that her mind was not at ease at having no dominion at all in this world, He said that the goat of the New Moon would be [an atonement]: the goat [sa'ir] is Edom, the accuser of Israel, whose strength is to be sapped on the New Moon, so that Israel too would at times have dominion in this world — like the moon, which at one time grows from the beginning of the month and at another wanes at its end. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shevuos 9a): Many are astonished at "Bring atonement for Me" only because the expression is used of one who sinned and brings atonement for his sin, which cannot apply to the Blessed One; but every removal and clearing-away is called kapparah. The moon had a grievance against the work of the Lord — though sun and moon are the two rulers of the world, she alone of all the heavenly host wanes every month until no light is left — and since it is the way of the Blessed One to give an elevation in place of the lowliness that befell a thing, so that all is equal, He gave her in exchange the New Moon offering, which neither the sun nor any of the heavenly host has; "Bring atonement for Me" means that this offering clears the grievance away from the Blessed One. So too chatat means nothing but deficiency, and "a sin-offering for the Lord" is written of this offering alone to say that it makes good the deficiency in the work of the Lord [namely, the diminishing of the moon]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 1): The Zohar says that those who bear the moon's defect together with it will be renewed with it, and these are called "sufferings of love," for the light of the lesser love was impaired, pushed away from the great love; and this is the secret of "Let it be an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon." Beis Yaakov (Mikeitz 16): The New Moon offering is a sin-offering "for the Lord," as the Gemara says, "Bring an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon" — that is, [for the question] why the Blessed One did not put light into the soul so that it could stand up to and overcome the concealment found in the body. Yet man too is liable for this, since he assisted somewhat in the matter. Tiferes Yosef (Pesachim 6): All the concealment and absence seen in the world stems from the diminishing of the moon, as in "Bring an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon," which alludes that it is only from the side of human perception that the Blessed One set a concealment of light in this world, so that man by his service would break through the apparent concealment and darkness to reach the light, and have room to distinguish himself..),
And this is the essence of "Bring an atonement upon Me for having diminished the moon" (Shevuot 9a),
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבְּכָל שֵׁבֶט הוּא בְּתוֹלָדָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the root of the deficiency in each tribe was placed within created nature by Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁבָּרָא הָאָדָם בַּעַל חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הַשְׁלָמָה;
Who created man as an inherently deficient creature requiring completion;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמּוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה,
and this is the root of Israel who count their calendar by the moon,
שֶׁהֵם בַּעַל חִסָּרוֹן וּמְקוּיָּים הַשְׁלָמָתָן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
being subjects of deficiency whose completion is sustained directly from Hashem, blessed be He.
אֲבָל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מוֹנִין לַחַמָּה
However, the nations of the world count by the sun,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן,
appearing to possess no internal lack,
לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הַשְׁלָמָה,
because they have no transcendent divine completion;
נִדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁאֵין חֲסֵרִים כְּלוּם,
it seems to them that they lack nothing at all,
עַד שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב אֶדַּמֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" לְדַמּוֹת לַחַמָּה.
until they boast (Isaiah 14:14): "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will be like the Most High, etc.," seeking to resemble the unvarying sun.
וְזֶה כָּל חֵשֶׁק אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם:
And this is the entire desire of the nations of the world:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם כָּל מַאֲוַויִּים שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְדָבָר, אֲפִילּוּ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
that they possess all their wishes so as not to need anything, not even Hashem, blessed be He;
אֲבָל חֵשֶׁק בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא שֶׁיִּצְטָרְכוּ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
whereas the yearning of the children of Israel is specifically to be in need of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהוּא יִהְיֶה הַמַּשְׁלִימָם,
that He alone should be their Completer,
וְאֵין חֲפֵצִים כְּלָל שְׁלֵימוּת בְּלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
desiring no completion whatsoever apart from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן יָרֵחַ שֶׁכָּל אוֹרָהּ מֵהַחַמָּה,
And this is the nature of the moon whose entire light derives from the sun,
וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ חִסָּרוֹן וּמִלּוּי בְּהַשָּׂגַת אוֹרָהּ עַל הָאָרֶץ,
exhibiting waxing and waning in the perception of its radiance upon the earth;
כִּי כְּשֶׁסְּמוּכָה לַחַמָּה פָּנֶיהָ הַמְּאִירִים לְמַעְלָה וְאֵין נִרְגָּשׁ עַל הָאָרֶץ,
for when it is adjacent to the sun, its illuminated hemisphere faces upward and is not felt on earth,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ לָהּ אוֹר.
even though in truth it possesses light all along.
וְכֵן חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל:
And likewise is the deficiency at the root of Israel:
הַיְינוּ בַּנִּגְלֶה בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּגּוּף נִרְאֶה כְּחִסָּרוֹן,
namely in manifest reality, while enclothed in the physical body, it appears as a defect,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין חִסָּרוֹן כְּלָל.
yet in ultimate truth there is no deficiency whatsoever.
וְכֵן יֵשׁ פְּעָמִים לַקּוּת לַלְּבָנָה,
Similarly, an eclipse sometimes occurs to the moon,
וְהוּא בִּשְׁבִיל אֶרֶץ הַמַּפְסֶקֶת בֵּינָהּ לַחַמָּה,
and this is on account of the earth interposing between it and the sun;
וְהוּא הַגּוּף הַמַּעֲכִיר וּמַאֲפִיל מֵאוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that represents the coarse physical body which obstructs and obscures the light of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא זְמַן מוּעָט וְחוֹזֵר וּמֵאִיר.
lasting only a brief moment before it returns to shine forth.
וְכַפָּרָה עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ עִנְיַן מִיעוּט הַיָּרֵחַ הוּא בַּשָּׂעִיר דְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ,
And the atonement for the primal root of the moon's diminution is through the male goat of Rosh Chodesh,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "עָלַי כַּפָּרָה",
and this is termed "an atonement upon Me,"

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה342 Midrash Tehillim 1:20 — R. Eliezer of Modiin said: In time to come all the ministering princes of the nations of the world will come and accuse Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying before Him: Master of the Universe, how are Israel different from the other nations? These are idolaters and these are idolaters; these are shedders of blood and these are shedders of blood; these are immoral and these are immoral — why should these go down to Gehinnom and these not go down? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: If so, let every nation go down to Gehinnom with its god and be tested, and let Israel too go and be tested. Israel answer and say before the Holy One, blessed be He: You are our hope and You are our trust; we have no security but You — if it be Your will, go before us first. And the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them: Fear not, for all of you wear a second garment, and this is the covenant of circumcision, as it is said, “She fears not the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet”; and even so, I go with you, as it is said, “For all the peoples walk each in the name of his god, and we shall walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.” (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר א וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ב, א)
along the lines of what our Sages expounded (Shocher Tov, Psalm 1; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:1)
עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי בָאֵשׁ ה' נִשְׁפָּט",
on the verse (Isaiah 66:16): "For by fire will Hashem execute judgment,"
שֶׁיֹּאמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "תָּבוֹא כָּל אוּמָּה וֵאלֹהֶיהָ".
wherein the Holy One, blessed be He, declares: "Let every nation and its deity come forward."
פֵּירוּשׁ, דְּגַם הַבְלֵי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
The explanation is: even the false deities of the idolaters,
הֲגַם דְּהוּא הֶבֶל,
even though they are empty vanity,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם עוֹבְדִים לָזֶה, עַל כֵּן זֶהוּ שָׁרְשָׁם;
nonetheless, since they worship them, these constitute their cosmic root;
וְאִלּוּ הָיָה דְּבַר הֶבֶל מַמָּשׁ, לֹא הָיוּ מִצְווֹת נֶגֶד זֶה,
and had it been sheer nonexistence, there would not have been specific commandments counteracting it,
כְּמוֹ קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח בְּמִצְרַיִם,
such as the Paschal offering in Egypt,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, מא עַמּוּד ב)343 Zohar 2:41b — What is written? “And you shall not break a bone in it” — to show contempt for it and for all the deities of the Egyptians. For the bones were cast in the marketplace, and dogs came and dragged them from place to place, and this was harder for them than anything, since the bones are the framework of the body; and Israel cast them into the marketplace in a manner of contempt. Therefore it is written, “And you shall not break a bone in it” — you shall not break them, but the dogs would come and break them. דְּזֶה הָיָה בִּיעוּר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם טָלֶה, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
of which they stated in the Zohar (Part II, 41b) that this constituted the eradication of their idolatry, the lamb, see there;
וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּלָל, לֹא הָיָה עֵסֶק לְדַבֵּר מִזֶּה,
and regarding something that has no spiritual reality, there would be no reason to speak of it,
כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיְּצַוֶּוה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעִנְיָן זֶה מִצְוָה הַמִּתְנַגֶּדֶת.
much less that Hashem, blessed be He, would command a specific opposed mitzvah concerning it.
אֲבָל וַדַּאי שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִצְרַיִם אָז, בְּעֵת שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים לָהֶם,
Rather, surely the root of Egypt at that time, when Israel was subjugated to them—
וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן וְהֵם שִׁעְבְּדוּ בָּהֶם –
and the children of Israel were compared to sheep while they enslaved them—
וַדַּאי הָיוּ גַּם הֵם מוּשְׁרָשִׁים בָּזֶה שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְשַׁעְבְּדָם;
was that they too were spiritually rooted in this faculty so as to hold dominion over them;
וּלְכָךְ אָז הָיוּ עוֹבְדִים לַצֹּאן,
and on that account they then worshipped sheep,
כַּיָּדוּעַ עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל הַקַּדְמוֹנִים,
as is known regarding the idolatrous concepts of the ancients,
שֶׁהָיוּ מַחְשִׁיבִים כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁרוֹאִים שֶׁמַּצְלִיחַ הַרְבֵּה
who attributed divinity to whatever they saw succeeding greatly
וְשֶׁכָּל עִיקַּר הַצְלָחָתָם וּפַרְנָסָתָם מִמֶּנּוּ וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
and from which their primary prosperity and sustenance flowed, and the like.
וְהָיָה אָז עִיקַּר הַצְלָחָתָם בַּצֹּאן,
And their primary prosperity was then through sheep,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֻלִּין פד:)344 Chullin 84b — One who wishes to become wealthy should occupy himself with small livestock. R. Chisda said: What is meant by "and the flocks [ashterot] of your sheep"? That they enrich [me'ashrot] their owners. Tosafos (s.v. "one who wishes to become wealthy should occupy himself with small livestock"): If you ask: we say in Pesachim (50b) that one who occupies himself with small livestock sees no sign of blessing. Rabbeinu Tam answers that there it speaks of settled country, and the reason is the evil eye, whereas here it speaks of woodland, where the eye has no power over them. Maharsha: Rashi cites this exposition in his commentary on the portion of Ekev, and the Re'em wrote on the portion of Ki Tavo that even on this reading "ashterot" would derive from the sense of strength and not from the sense of wealth; but from our sugya it does not appear so. דְּנִקְרָא עַשְׁתְּרוֹת – שֶׁמְּעַשְׁרוֹת;
as our Sages taught (Chullin 84b) that flock is called ashterot because it enriches (measherot);
וּבְוַדַּאי הָיָה אָז שָׁם עוֹשֶׁר מְרוּבֶּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּבְטְחוּ לָצֵאת בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל.
and certainly vast wealth existed there then, for Israel had been promised to depart with great wealth.
וְהָיָה אָז הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גָּדוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהִתְעַשֵּׁר,
And an intense worldly drive was then awakened to exert effort to become rich,
וּלְפִיכָךְ עָסְקוּ בַּצֹּאן שֶׁהֵם מְעַשְׁרוֹת בַּעֲלֵיהֶן;
and therefore they occupied themselves with sheep which enrich their owners;
אֲבָל הֵן עַצְמָן אֵינָם כָּךְ,
yet the sheep themselves are not so,
רַק שֶׁזֶּה יֵשׁ לָהֶם שֶׁנִּמְשָׁכִים אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה,
possessing merely this quality of being drawn after the shepherd,
לְכָךְ נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם.
which is why Israel was likened unto them.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת רוֹצִים שֶׁגַּם אֱלוֹהַּ שֶׁלָּהֶם יִהְיֶה בִּרְשׁוּתָם כַּנִּזְכָּר,
And since the idolaters desire that even their god be subordinate within their domain as mentioned,
וּבִפְרָט בַּמִּשְׁתַּדְּלִים עוֹשֶׁר וּרְכוּשׁ, דְּ"אוֹהֵב כֶּסֶף לֹא יִשְׂבַּע",
especially among those pursuing wealth, for "he that loves silver shall not be satisfied," (Ecclesiastes 5:9),
וְחָפֵץ שֶׁגַּם הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ יִהְיֶה שֶׁלּוֹ;
wishing that the very source of abundance be owned by him;
וּלְפִיכָךְ עָבְדוּ לַצֹּאן שֶׁנִּמְשָׁכִים אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה,
they therefore worshipped sheep that are led after the shepherd,
לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם אֱלוֹהַּ שֶׁלָּהֶם הַמְּעַשְׁרָם הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְנִכְנָע לָהֶם.
alleging that even their god who enriches them is drawn after them and subservient to them.
וְהָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה,
And this dynamic was also present in Egypt,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּסּוֹף שֶׁהֶעֱשִׁירוּ בַּעֲלֵיהֶם – הַיְינוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, "וַיְנַצְּלוּ אֶת מִצְרַיִם",
and as occurred in the end when they enriched their rightful masters—namely Israel, "and they despoiled Egypt"—
וְנִמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
and the Egyptians were drawn after the shepherd at the splitting of the Red Sea,
הָלְכוּ אַחַר יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתוֹךְ הַיָּם וְנִטְבְּעוּ,
marching after Israel into the midst of the sea and drowning,
שֶׁאֶצְלָם הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּוחָם הוּא הַמּוֹרִידָם לִשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית.
so that their own primal power became the very force driving them down into the lowest netherworld.
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַהַמְשָׁכָה אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה שֶׁלָּהֶם,
For the root of that impulse of being drawn after their shepherd,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּוחָם וְהוּא עִנְיַן כֹּחַ הַצֹּאן כַּנִּזְכָּר,
which was their foundational strength, mirroring the archetype of the flock as mentioned,
הֵם עָשׂוּ כֹּחַ זֶה לֶאֱלוֹהַּ;
they made this faculty itself into an idol;
כִּי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת עוֹבְדִים לְכֹחַ אֶחָד מֵהַכֹּחוֹת,
for the idolaters worship a single localized power,
כָּל אוּמָּה לְכֹחַ שֶׁלָּהּ,
each nation unto its specific force,
וְלֹא לֵאלֹהֵי עוֹלָם בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כּוּלָּם,
and not unto the God of the universe Who is Master of all forces,
רַק לְכֹחַ נִפְרָד הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לָהֶם.
rather unto a detached power belonging to them.
וְכֹוחָם לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר רוֹעֶה – דְּהַיְינוּ אֱלוֹהַּ הַמַּנְהִיג –
And their capacity of being drawn after a shepherd—meaning a governing deity—
הֵם עָשׂוּ כֹּחַ זֶה אֱלוֹהַּ,
they turned that capacity itself into a god,
וְנִמְצָא נִמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר עַצְמָם וְלִבָּבָם.
so that they were ultimately following their own egos and hearts.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּטָלֶה שֶׁהוּא נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הָאָדָם,
And this was the idolatrous worship of the lamb which follows man,
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר רוֹעֶה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶם,
meaning they followed a shepherd who followed them,
וְזֶה הוֹרִידָם לַיָּם,
and this dragged them into the sea,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כג)345 Shemot Rabbah 23:14 — The waves of the sea appeared like mares, and the wicked Egyptians like lustful stallions, and they ran after them until they sank in the sea, as it is said, "the horse and its rider He cast into the sea." The Egyptian would say to his horse: Yesterday I was drawing you along to give you water and you would not come after me, and now you come to drown me in the sea? And the horse would answer him: "Ramah va-yam" — see what is in the sea [re'eh mah ba-yam]; the Exalted One of the world I see in the sea. עַל פָּסוּק "סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ" –
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shemot Rabbah 23 end) on the verse "the horse and his rider":
דְּהַסּוּס מָשַׁךְ רוֹכְבוֹ.
that the horse dragged its rider.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח,
And this is the inner purpose of the Passover sacrifice,
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לְהַקְרִיב צֹאן,
wherein Hashem, blessed be He, commanded to sacrifice flock,
דִּבְשְׁבִיל כֹּוחָם זֶה מָשְׁלוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן.
because through this archetype they had dominated Israel who are likened to sheep.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מַקְרִיבִין כֹּחַ זֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Yet in truth, Israel dedicate this faculty unto Hashem, blessed be He,
וְלִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁכִים אַחֲרָיו כַּצֹּאן.
to be drawn after Him like sheep.

וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, מא עַמּוּד ב)346 Zohar 2:41b — What is written? “And you shall not break a bone in it” — to show contempt for it and for all the deities of the Egyptians. For the bones were cast in the marketplace, and dogs came and dragged them from place to place, and this was harder for them than anything, since the bones are the framework of the body; and Israel cast them into the marketplace in a manner of contempt. Therefore it is written, “And you shall not break a bone in it” — you shall not break them, but the dogs would come and break them. דַּחֲזוֹ גַּרְמֵי רְמָאן בְּשׁוּקָא וְכוּלֵי,
And they stated in the Zohar (Part II, 41b) that the Egyptians saw the bones cast out in the street, etc.,
וְהָיָה בִּיטּוּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
which was the nullification of their idolatry.
פֵּירוּשׁ: הָעֶצֶם הוּא עִיקַּר חֹזֶק הַבַּעַל חַי
The explanation is: the bone forms the structural strength of an animal,
וְאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בּוֹ מִלּוּי וְחִסָּרוֹן מִצַּד הַמִּרְעֶה,
undergoing neither fattening nor wasting on account of grazing,
וְאֵין בּוֹ טַעַם כְּלָל;
and having no taste at all;
אֲבָל הַבָּשָׂר יֵשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם לַחֵךְ,
whereas the meat possesses culinary flavor to the palate,
וּבְמִרְעֶה טוֹב הוּא נִשְׁמָן,
becoming fat with good pasture,
וּבְכָחוּשׁ נִרְזֶה וְאֵין בּוֹ חֹזֶק.
and lean and weak in poor grazing.
וְכֵן כֹּחַ מִצְרַיִם: לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ אַחַר רוֹעֶה הַמְּעַשְׁרָם עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְרוֹעֶה,
Such was the power of Egypt: to follow a provider who enriches them to the point of not needing any shepherd,
וְהוּא בַּמָּשָׁל עַצְמוֹת הַצֹּאן,
which parallels the dry bones of the flock;
דְּוַדַּאי בָּזֶה יֵשׁ חֹזֶק יוֹתֵר לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן,
for in that state there appears to be greater strength to the eye,
בְּשַׁלְוָה כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁאֵין חִסָּרוֹן כְּלוּם,
enjoying such static tranquility that there is no perceived deficiency,
וְדוֹמֶה לַחַמָּה;
resembling the constant sun;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין בּוֹ טַעַם כְּלָל,
yet in truth it has no flavor whatever,
וּ"רְמָאן בְּשׁוּקָא" וּכְלָבִים גּוֹרְרָם,
cast out in the street for dogs to drag,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָאָדָם כְּלָל
being entirely unworthy for man,
וְלֹא בָּזֶה בָּחַר ה' לְצוּרַת הָאָדָם.
and not for this did Hashem choose human form.
וְזֶהוּ בִּיטּוּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
And this is the nullification of idolatry:
דְּהַיְינוּ כֹּחַ זֶה דְּמִצְרַיִם נִתְבָּרֵר דְּאֵינוֹ כְּלוּם,
namely, this illusion of Egypt was proven to be nothing,
רַק כֹּחַ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה תָּמִיד,
leaving only Israel's spiritual capacity to be drawn after the Shepherd constantly,
וְשֶׁלֹּא יֶחְסַר דָּבָר זֶה לְעוֹלָם, שֶׁ"ה' רֹעִי";
and that this truth never be lacking, that "Hashem is my shepherd" (Psalms 23:1);
כִּי אֵין חֲפֵצִים כְּלָל בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר,
for they desire nothing else,
רַק שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ תָּדִיר מִיָּדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
save to receive continuously from the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He,
וְיִהְיוּ צְרִיכִין לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו
and to be dependent upon following Him;
אִם טוֹב וְאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּמִלּוּי וּבְחִסָּרוֹן,
whether in times of good or Heaven forbid otherwise, in fullness or in lack,
לְעוֹלָם רוֹצִים לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ אַחַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
they forever yearn to be drawn after Hashem, blessed be He.
דָּבָר זֶה הוּא הָרָאוּי לְצוּרַת אָדָם וְלִהְיוֹת "חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ",
This consciousness alone is worthy of the human form and of being "Hashem's portion is His people,"
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד
for they possess no autonomous, separate power,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם מְצַפִּים לְיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל כֹּחוֹתָם.
since they perpetually look toward the hand of Hashem with all their faculties.
וְכָל אוּמָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד,
Each gentile nation possesses an isolated, specific force,
וְזֶהוּ תֵּרֵד כָּל אוּמָּה וֵאלֹהֶיהָ:
and this is why every nation and its deity descends:
הַכֹּחַ שֶׁלָּהּ יֵלֵךְ לַאֲבַדּוֹן
its specific force will perish,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מִמֶּנּוּ הַשְׁאָרָה לֶעָתִיד בִּשְׁחִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע;
leaving no remnant in the future upon the slaughter of the evil inclination;
כִּי כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָאוּמּוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת מִכֹּחוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
for all powers of the nations derive from faculties of the evil inclination in the heart;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ כְּלוּם,
whereas Israel possess this transcendent power—that they claim no independent strength,
רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם,
only that which Hashem, blessed be He, channels into them;
וְכֹחַ זֶה הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי הֵם "חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ".
and this power is truly divine, for they are "the lot of His inheritance."
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיָדוּעַ דִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם הוּא בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת,
And this connects to the principle that the creation of the world occurred through the awakening of the attribute of Malchut,
דְּ"אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם",
for "there is no king without a nation,"
וּמִדָּה זוֹ צְרִיכָה לְזוּלַת לְהַשְׁלִימָהּ,
and this attribute requires an external other to complete it,
דְּאֵין נִקְרָא בְּשֵׁם מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הָעָם.
since one is titled king solely by virtue of a people.
וּמִדָּה זוֹ הִיא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע,
And this attribute is the celestial root of the Congregation of Israel as is known,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִזֶּה הוּא גַּם כֵּן נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם הָעָם,
meaning that from this source emanate the souls of Israel who constitute that nation,
וּצְרִיכִין לְהַשְׁלָמָה לַרוֹעֶה שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁהוּא הַמֶּלֶךְ – דְּהַיְינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא;
requiring completion from their Shepherd Who is the King—namely the Holy One, blessed be He;
וּמַלְכוּת שֶׁל הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא בְּעַם שֶׁלּוֹ, דְּהַיְינוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and the sovereignty of the King is manifested within His people, the Congregation of Israel.
וּמִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה דִּצְרִיכִין הַשְׁלָמָה, נוֹבֵעַ הַתְחָלַת הַחִסָּרוֹן,
And from this root of needing completion springs the origin of lack,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּאִים בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל מִינֵי חֶסְרוֹנוֹת,
whence expand all varieties of human shortcomings,
עַד שֶׁיֵּשׁ טַעֲנָה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גַּם נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל.
until there arise accusations to superficial sight even against Israel.
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת כָּל הַחֲטָאִים דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל סְדוּרִים וּבָאִים מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית;
Except that in truth, all sins of Israel are preordained and structured from the six days of Creation;
הַיְינוּ דְּכָךְ הַסֵּדֶר בִּבְרִיאַת יִשְׂרָאֵל: לִהְיוֹת חִסָּרוֹן וּמִלּוּי,
meaning such was the primordial design in creating Israel: to experience deficiency and fulfillment,
שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי חִסָּרוֹן מְקַבְּלִים הַשְׁלָמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
so that by virtue of being creatures of lack, they receive their wholeness from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ עַם שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְמֶלֶךְ.
And through this divine kingship is realized, when a people exists in need of a king.

וְזֶהוּ "כִּי בָאֵשׁ ה' וְגוֹמֵר", כִּבְיָכוֹל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים שָׁם347 Midrash Tehillim 1:18 — He says to them: If so, let every nation go down, and its god with it, as it is said, "For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god" (Micah 4:5). R. Reuven said in the name of R. Chanina: Were the verse not written, it would be impossible to say it — "For with fire the Lord will be judged" (Isaiah 66:16). It is not written here "the Lord judges," but "is judged.").
And this explains: "For by fire will Hashem execute judgment, etc.," as though the Holy One enters judgment with Himself (Shocher Tov, Psalms 1);
פֵּירוּשׁ, דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ הִיא הַגּוֹרֶמֶת הַחִסָּרוֹן,
meaning that the attribute of His Malchut is what brought about the deficiency,
וְהִיא כֹּחַ הַחִסָּרוֹן דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
being the source of lack within Israel,
"וְהַמִּשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהִים הוּא".
"and the judgment is God's" (Deuteronomy 1:17).
וְזֶהוּ "כַּפָּרָה עָלַי" דְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ:
And this is the meaning of "an atonement upon Me" on Rosh Chodesh:
לְתַקֵּן הַחִסָּרוֹן בַּלֵּב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא,
to rectify the deficiency of heart present in every Jewish soul according to its state,
עַל יְדֵי בֵּירוּר דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פָּעַל כָּל זֹאת;
through the clarification that Hashem, blessed be He, orchestrated all of this;
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא הַפּוֹעֵל, אִם כֵּן הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה,
and since He is the Prime Mover, all is necessarily for good,
דְּאֵין דָּבָר רַע יוֹצֵא מִלְּמַעְלָה.
for no evil emanates from Above.
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ מִלּוּי הַחִסָּרוֹן עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה זוֹ
And consequently, the lack is filled through this very awareness,
שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהַחִסָּרוֹן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
recognizing that the deficiency itself was authored by Hashem, blessed be He.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן קְדוּשַּׁת רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה מִדֵּי חֹדֶשׁ [בְּחָדְשׁוֹ וּמִדֵּי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ] וְגוֹמֵר348 Isaiah 66:23 — “And it shall come to pass, that from one New Moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh shall come to bow down before Me, says the Lord.” Radak: "From one new moon to another" is like "month by month," and the word "as often as" indicates that the thing continues without interruption. He mentions two intervals, the nearer for those who are near and the more distant for those who are far off, according to how far their lands are from Jerusalem. "All flesh" means all men, even the other nations. Metzudas Dovid: Whenever it is the new moon — and "in its month" means on the new moon itself, the set time not being allowed to pass — and likewise "from one Sabbath to another." "All flesh shall come" means all men, even the other nations, "to bow before Me" in the Temple. Malbim: In every month and on every Sabbath fresh men will come from among the nations to bow before Me, to receive the true faith and to cast away their idols.",
And this is the sanctity of Rosh Chodesh of which it is stated: "And it shall come to pass that from one New Moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, etc." (Isaiah 66:23);
דְּשַׁבָּת הוּא הַהַשְׁלָמָה: "בָּא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה"
for Shabbat represents completion: "when Shabbat arrives, rest arrives"

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ הוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י בְּרֵאשִׁית פָּסוּק "וַיְכַל", וּמְגִילָּה ט349 Rashi on Genesis 2:2 — "And God finished on the seventh day" — R. Shimon says: Flesh and blood, who does not know his times and his moments, must add from the profane to the holy; but the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows His times and His moments, entered into it by a hairsbreadth, so that it appeared as though He completed the work on that very day. Another explanation: What was the world lacking? Rest. Shabbat came — rest came; the work was thereby ended and completed..),
(Midrash quoted in Rashi, Genesis 2:2; Megillah 9a),
וְאֵין חָסֵר כְּלוּם;
and nothing is lacking;
וְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ הוּא הַחִסָּרוֹן,
while Rosh Chodesh embodies the conscious deficiency,
וּמַכִּיר דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and one acknowledges that both states stem from Hashem, blessed be He;
"יָבוֹא כָל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹמֵר".
"all flesh shall come to prostrate before Me, etc."
וּלְכָךְ קְדוּשַּׁת רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ לַנָּשִׁים בְּיִחוּד,
Therefore the sanctity of Rosh Chodesh belongs especially to women,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (פֶּרֶק מה350 Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 45:4 — The women heard and would not accept upon themselves to give their earrings to their husbands; rather they said to them: "You wish to make a detestable abomination that has no power to save?" They did not listen to them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the women their reward in this world and in the world to come. And what reward did He give them? In this world, that they keep the New Moons, as it is said, "who satisfies you with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's" (Psalms 103:5).);
as is written in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (Chapter 45);
הַיְינוּ דְּהַכָּרָה דְּחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְמִלּוּי,
namely, that the acute awareness of deficiency needing fulfillment
זֶהוּ סִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ.
is the mystical realm of the feminine (Nukva), as is known.

sections.en: Torah's Greatness and Prayer's Need

items.h: Torah measures stature through attained wisdom, while prayer draws power from deficiency; in the future these opposite hierarchies will be revealed as one.

Seif 1 — The Greatness of Torah and the Poverty of Prayer
Torah grows through attained wisdom, while prayer grows through felt need; ultimately these opposites are united.

p: בַּתּוֹרָה הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הֵם כְּפִי הַמַּעֲלוֹת,
In Torah, levels correspond to virtues,
שֶׁכָּל הַמְעֻלֶּה בְּחָכְמָתוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵחֲבֵירוֹ הוּא הַגָּדוֹל.
for whoever is superior in wisdom to his peer is the greater.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּתְפִלָּה, אַדְּרַבָּה, הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הֵם כְּפִי הַחִסָּרוֹן,
In contrast, regarding prayer, on the contrary, levels correspond to deficiency,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, כג עַמּוּד ב351 Zohar 1:23b — And David, because of the exile, said, "hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness"; because he saw the Shekhinah desolate and dry, he took her suffering upon himself. Afterward, when he saw that Israel would return in joy, he instituted ten kinds of song, and at the end of them all he said, "A prayer of the poor man when he is faint" (Psalms 102:1) — and this is the prayer that wraps up all the prayers that come before it, so that they do not enter until his own prayer enters. Therefore the poor man precedes them all.):
and as written in the Zohar (Part I, 23b):
"תְּפִלָּה לֶעָנִי דִּמְעַטְּפָא כָּל צְלוֹתִין",
"A prayer of the afflicted man envelops all prayers,"

וּכְמִשְׁלֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי דְּעֶבֶד וְשַׂר352 Berakhot 34b — Again, it happened that R. Chanina ben Dosa went to study Torah with R. Yochanan ben Zakkai, and the son of R. Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill. He said to him: Chanina my son, pray for mercy for him, that he may live. He put his head between his knees and prayed for mercy for him, and he lived. R. Yochanan ben Zakkai said: Had ben Zakkai pressed his head between his knees all day long, no heed would have been paid to him. His wife said to him: Is Chanina then greater than you? He said to her: No — but he is like a servant before the king, and I am like a nobleman before the king. Rashi: "Like a servant" — a member of the household, who comes in and goes out without permission. "Like a nobleman before the king" — who is not accustomed to come before him. Maharsha: Another man's prayer sometimes avails more than one's own, as they said, "a prisoner cannot free himself from prison" — which is why Yitzchak prayed for Rivkah, and "the Lord granted his prayer," his and not hers; and this is why R. Yochanan ben Zakkai, like Rabban Gamliel above, turned to R. Chanina to pray for mercy. When he said, "Had ben Zakkai pressed his head between his knees all day long," he spoke out of his own humility, and to his wife, who did not know his real reason, he answered according to her understanding with this parable. He is like a servant, who is always near the king in his house — so R. Chanina was constantly in the house of the Lord, praying before Him over whatever befell men — whereas R. Yochanan ben Zakkai was like a nobleman who is not at home in the palace, for he was occupied with the needs of the community as head of the court of his generation and had no leisure to be always praying for others. (בְּרָכוֹת לד:).
and like the parable of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai comparing the servant and the minister (Berakhot 34b).
כִּי כָּל מִי שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר חָסֵר וְנִצְרָךְ בְּיוֹתֵר
For whoever is more deficient and destitute
הוּא יָכוֹל לִפְעוֹל בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ יוֹתֵר,
is able to accomplish more through his prayer,
כִּי תְּפִלָּתוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵעוּמְקָא דְלִבָּא.
because his prayer emerges from a deeper recess of the heart.
וְעִיקַּר הַתְּפִלָּה הוּא מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן
And the essence of prayer stems from deficiency
וּמְבַקֵּשׁ הַשְׁלָמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
as one seeks completion from Hashem, blessed be He;
וְאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין שׁוּם חִלּוּק בֵּין גָּדוֹל לְקָטָן,
and before Hashem there is no distinction between great and small,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר אָסָא בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (ב יד, י353 II Chronicles 14:10 — And Asa called to the Lord his God and said: "Lord, there is none beside You to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, O Lord our God, for we rely upon You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O Lord, You are our God; let no mortal prevail against You." Rashi: "There is none with You to help" — that is: though we are few and they are as numerous as the sand of the sea, and we have no strength before them, it is with You to help, whether the many or the powerless; it is known that You have power to help, and therefore "help us, Lord our God, for on You we lean." "Let no man prevail with You" — let not that man, our enemy, hold back the hands of Your people against You so as to defeat us, lest he say, "We have defeated their God." Radak: "Let no man prevail with You" — the word means "rule," as in "heir to the throne" [Judges 18:7]; that is, let them have no dominion against You. Or it means: let him not muster strength. Metzudas Dovid: "There is none with You to help" — with You there is no difference in helping, whether a numerous people or one who has no strength at all. "And in Your name" — trusting in Your name. "Let no man prevail with You" — let no man muster strength against You, to hold back Your power from prevailing. Malbim: "There is none with You to help" — a man's help is a limited power, so it is easier for him to help one who already has much, since then only a little need be added to what the helped one has, and harder to help one with no strength at all, where he must do everything himself. But Your power is without limit and needs nothing from the one You help; there is none joined with You in helping, and so it makes no difference to You whether the one helped is a great multitude or has no strength — therefore help us, both because we lean on You and because in Your name we have come against this multitude.):
just as Asa proclaimed in Chronicles (II 14:10):
"אֵין עִמְּךָ לַעְזוֹר בֵּין רַב לְאֵין כֹּחַ",
"'It is nothing for You to help, whether with many or with them that have no power,'
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ בְּכֹחַ בָּשָׂר,
and surely he did not intend this merely in its literal sense of physical strength,
רַק רַב בְּמַעֲלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה אֱלֹהִית;
rather one great in Torah virtue and divine holiness;
וְ"אֵיזֶהוּ גִּבּוֹר? הַכּוֹבֵשׁ וְכוּלֵי",
and "who is mighty? He who subdues his inclination, etc.",
וְאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
and the Torah emanates from the side of Gevurah (Might; Zohar III 80b end),
כִּי זֶה עִיקַּר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה
for this is the core of Torah wisdom:
כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי הַחָכְמָה,
when one behaves according to wisdom,
דְּזֶהוּ שֵׁם "תּוֹרָה" – שֶׁמּוֹרָה דֶּרֶךְ אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג.
which is the meaning of the name Torah: that it teaches the path of proper conduct.
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁלֹּא עָצַר כֹּחַ לְהִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה,
However, one who could not muster strength to conduct himself according to Torah wisdom,
הֲרֵי הוּא חֲסַר מַעֲלַת הַתּוֹרָה.
lacks the stature of Torah.
וּכְפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחִסָּרוֹן,
And commensurate with the depth of the lack,
אִם הוּא מַכִּיר חֶסְרוֹנוֹ וּמְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעַזְרֵנוּ עַל זֶה,
if he acknowledges his deficiency and implores Hashem to assist him in this,
הֲרֵי הוּא דָּבוּק עַל יְדֵי זֶה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
he is bound through this unto Hashem, blessed be He,

כְּטַעַם "אֲנִי אֶת דַּכָּא" (סוֹטָה ה354 Sotah 5a — "[I dwell in the high and holy place,] and also with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit" (Isaiah 57:15). Rav Huna and Rav Chisda: one said, the contrite one is with Me; and one said, I am with the contrite one. And it stands to reason like the one who said, I am with the contrite one, for the Holy One, blessed be He, passed over all the mountains and hills and rested His Presence upon Mount Sinai, and He did not raise Mount Sinai up to Himself. Rashi: "The contrite one is with Me" — I raise him up until he dwells beside Me, and this is [the sense of the verse] "I dwell [on high] … with the contrite." "I am with the contrite one" — I lower My Presence to be beside him. Maharsha: The practical lesson [of the view that 'I am with the contrite one'] is that even a distinguished person should lower himself toward one beneath him, and not say that this is beneath his dignity, for there is no honor greater than the honor of Heaven. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sotah 5a): According to the one who says "the contrite one is with Me," the Holy One, blessed be He, raises up the contrite: just as arrogance inclines toward the material, humility is a separate [transcendent] level, as Moses possessed it, so it is fitting that the humble man be elevated to God and be with Him. According to the one who says "I am with the contrite one," God rests His Presence upon what is crushed and lowly, because the lowly are simple — as the Sages hinted that the essence of the Divine Presence was [originally] among the lower beings. [It stands to reason like the latter,] for when God joins Himself to the contrite one the union is according to His power and is complete, whereas when the contrite one is with God the union is not as full. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 1): On either view the contrite one, as the effect, is joined to God, the Cause: according to "I am with the contrite one" the Cause turns toward the effect, which is prepared to receive His glory, and according to "the contrite one is with Me" the effect is raised to be with the Cause. It stands to reason like "I am with the contrite one," for one who comes to another is wholly with him, since the other receives him entirely, whereas one who comes to the great cannot be joined with him so fully. God comes to the humble man to be with him — passing over all the high mountains to rest His Presence on Mount Sinai — because the humble man possesses something of his Maker's own attribute, and like things are found together..),
mirroring "I dwell with the contrite" (Sotah 5a),
דִּבְמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ.
for in the place of His greatness, there you find His humility.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּסוֹד "רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק"
The explanation, as known from the mystical secret of running and returning like lightning
הַנִּרְאֶה לְצוֹפֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה,
seen by the visionaries of the Divine Chariot,
שֶׁבִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהֵם הוֹלְכִים שָׁם הֵם שָׁבִים;
is that to the place they go, there they return;
הַיְינוּ בִּמְקוֹם כְּלוֹת הָאוֹר
meaning that where light reaches its final vanishing point,
שָׁם הוּא חוֹזֵר וְנַעֲשֶׂה הַסּוֹף הַתְחָלָה וְחוֹזֵר חָלִילָה,
there it turns back, the end becoming the beginning in a continuous cycle,
לִהְיוֹת סוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין מִתְדַּבֵּק בִּתְחִלַּת וְעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית
so that the end of all levels binds directly to the origin and depth of the Beginning,
וְנִקְרָא רֹאשׁ כָּל דַּרְגִּין,
being called the head of all levels;
כִּי רֵאשִׁית הַכֹּל הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for the Beginning of all is Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר בּוֹ הוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הַנִּבְרָאִים.
and absolute cleaving to Him is the primordial depth of the unfolding of creations.
וְהוֹלֵךְ סֵדֶר הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת עַד תַּכְלִית הַמַּטָּה,
And this cascading order descends to the ultimate bottom,
שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בְּכָל מִינֵי חִסָּרוֹן הַמַּרְחִיקִים מִדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר.
which is immersion in all deficiencies that estrange one from complete cleaving.
רַק מַאן דְּאִיהוּ מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ,
Yet one who stems from the holy root and stock of Israel whose portion is Hashem,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּשְׁכַּח לְגַמְרֵי;
cannot forget Him entirely;
אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹק שֶׁנִּשְׁבָּה לְבֵין הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
even an infant captured among idolaters,
מִיָּד שֶׁנִּתְוַודַּע לוֹ בְּשִׂכְלוֹ מֵעִנְיַן אֱלֹהֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם,
as soon as his intellect awakens to the God of Heaven,
הוּא מַתְחִיל לִנְהוֹת וְלִצְעוֹק מֵעוּמְקָא דְלִבָּא כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּתוֹ.
begins to pine and cry out from the depths of his heart in proportion to the depth of his sunken state.
וּתְפִלָּה הוּא לְשׁוֹן דְּבֵיקוּת,
And tefillah signifies cleaving,
דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִלַּת "תָּפֵל" בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ;
for that is the root of the word tafel (attaching) in the Holy Tongue;
הַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי,
meaning that through this one is fully bound,

וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה "מַאן דְּאִיהוּ זְעֵיר אִיהוּ רַב" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קכב עַמּוּד ב355 Zohar 1:122b — Tosefta: Happy is the one who makes himself small in this world — how great and exalted he is in that world! And thus did the head of the academy open: One who is small, he is great; and one who is great, he is small. As it is written, "And the life of Sarah was a hundred years and twenty years and seven years": a hundred, which is a large number, is written with "year," the smaller form — He diminished it; seven, which is a small number, He increased and enlarged, as it is written "years." Come and see: the Holy One, blessed be He, raises up only the one who lowers himself, and lowers only the one who raises himself.).
and consequently through this "he who is small is great" (Zohar I 122b).
וְדָוִד הוּא הַקָּטָן, הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And David is the small one, the final level (Malchut) as is known,
וְהוּא נְעִים זְמִירוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, תַּכְלִית כֹּחַ הַפֶּה בִּתְפִלָּה, כְּטַעַם "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה".
being the sweet singer of Israel, the pinnacle of the mouth in prayer, as in "and I am prayer."
הוּא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ "תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ" – שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַכֹּל.
He is the king of Israel of whom it is said "you shall set over you"—standing above all.
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ נִקְרָא "מָרוֹם וְקָדוֹשׁ",
And the Holy One in the place of His greatness is called "high and holy,"
שֶׁהוּא מְרוֹמָם מִכָּל חֶסְרוֹנוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנִבְדָּל מֵהֶם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם הִתְחַבְּרוּת לָזֶה.
elevated above all mundane deficiencies and removed from them, having no association with them.
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע,
And over this matter the eye of Balaam the wicked was blinded,

אָמַר: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר וְקָדוֹשׁ וְכוּלֵי356 Niddah 31a — And it was over this matter that the eye of Bilam the wicked was blinded. He said: He who is pure and holy, and whose ministers are pure and holy — shall He look upon such a thing? Immediately his eye was blinded. Tosafos (s.v. “whose eye is shut”): “Shut” [shetum] is a term of uncovering and opening, as the Targum renders it “who sees well,” and so it is used in the language of the Mishna in tractate Avoda Zara. Here the Gemara infers that his eye was blinded from the fact that “whose eye is shut” is written in the singular; and what is written elsewhere, “and whose eyes are open,” refers to how he was at first. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “and on account of this the eye of Balaam was blinded”): This is not explicit in that verse, and one must also consider how it can be said that his eye was blinded “immediately,” when several of Balaam's prophecies intervene. It seems that they relied on the exposition of the preceding verse, “And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel dwelling tribe by tribe” — that he sought to cast an evil eye upon them and diminish them, once he had seen that the Holy One, blessed be He, counts their couplings. Because he wished to set his eye upon them for evil, one eye was at once blinded, as is written thereafter “whose eye is shut”; and since “eye” is written in the singular, whereas above it says “he lifted up his eyes,” we learn that one of the two was blinded. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 31a): The Holy One, blessed be He, counts their couplings because the seed of Israel is drawn from an inward power, and there is no shame of nakedness in it — for nothing is called nakedness except where there is uncovering, as it is written “the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover”; but what is inward is no nakedness at all. Balaam said that this was a thing of nakedness, and he entered that lofty apprehension improperly; and this came to him because he himself was a man of lewdness, for in itself the act does not depart from holiness, and it was only because he was such a man that it was a wonder to him. Because he entered to gaze upon what it was not fitting for him to gaze upon, his eye was blinded. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): As the Sages said, "Sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you," so that this laughter be in holiness; and over this matter the eye of that wicked one was blinded, who said, "He who is holy and whose ministers are holy — shall He gaze upon such a thing?" For one whose mind is [rooted in] scheming and the harlot cannot understand that holiness could have any connection with this at all. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): Impurity everywhere denotes desire, and the purification from it is that the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies — as the Sages said on the verse "and numbered the stock [rova] of Israel," "Over this matter the eye of that wicked one was blinded": the Holy One, blessed be He, testifies that this desire of Israel is clean and pure, and they are called "holy flesh," whereas the Egyptians, their opposite, are called in Scripture "the flesh of donkeys." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman's eye was evil in this, for he did not believe that any holiness is found in bodily pleasures such as eating and drinking. So too the Sages said, "Over this matter the eye of the wicked Bilam was blinded: he said, He who is pure and holy and whose ministers are pure and holy — shall He gaze upon such a thing?" — that is, he did not believe that holiness could exist in this matter, since, as is known, this desire too derives from the blemish of the serpent, who cast filth into Eve. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Over this matter the eye of that wicked one, who said "and numbered the stock [rova] of Israel," was blinded: he saw that all their desires too are in holiness and beloved to the Blessed One, and so he gave counsel to make them stumble with the daughters of Midian. For only among the children of Israel, where he and she alike are of holy seed and cleave to holiness, are all their deeds "the work of the righteous for life"; but when one cleaves to the daughter of a foreign god, who is from the side of death, her offspring is like her, and this is not called "the stock of Israel" at all. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 147): Bilam, being of an evil root, did not believe in this and said, "He who is pure and holy…," for he did not know at all that there could be holiness in this too, "a pure thing out of an impure." Bilam's root was lacking, with no good or purity in it, and therefore he could not understand this; only the children of Israel, who cleave to the One Unique in the world, [understand it]. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): Through this the eye of that wicked one was blinded, who said, "He who is holy and whose ministers are holy — shall He gaze upon this secret?" For the nations, who have no connection to the words of Torah, regard the sense of touch as an utter disgrace, as the Greek philosopher said, and holiness for them lies only in complete separation, since they cannot attain holiness in bodily matters, which for them are full of filth and lewdness. Not so Jacob our father, who said "Give me my wife" — something even the most frivolous would not say — and felt no disgrace in it, for he intended only to raise offspring. (נִדָּה לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א),
for he said: the Holy One, Who is pure and holy, etc. (Niddah 31a end),
כִּי הוּא מְדַמֶּה כִּי גַּם יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם מְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּעוֹנֶג עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהֵם הֵיפֶךְ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה, הֵם נִפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
imagining that when Israel are immersed in worldly pleasures contrary to holiness, they are severed from Hashem;
וְזֶה הָיָה עֲצָתוֹ בְּשִׁטִּים.
and this was his scheme at Shittim.

אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "שֹׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא נו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב357 Yoma 56b — "That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity" (Leviticus 16:16) — even at a time when they are impure, the Divine Presence is among them. Maharsha (Yoma 57a, s.v. "now you are certainly impure"): [The Sadducee] meant: even if you were once pure, now in exile you have certainly become impure, as it is written, "Her impurity is in her skirts," and He separates Himself from you as one keeps apart from the impurity of a menstruant. [R. Chanina] answered him from what is written of them, "that dwells with them [in the midst of their impurity]," that He does not separate entirely, but as a man keeps apart from his wife while she is a menstruant yet lives with her in one house; so the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells with us even now in exile, as it is said, "I will be with him in distress." Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 4): The Blessed One does not dwell in the midst of their impurity unless the sin was unwitting, and of that it is written, "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity." [Hence the First Temple, whose distinction was that the Divine Presence rested in it,] was destroyed when they defiled the Sanctuary through idolatry, sexual immorality and bloodshed, the three sins that are called impurity. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1): The Divine Presence does not depart even toward evening, in the time of darkness, as it is likewise said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity." For the souls of all Israel are bound and linked together as in a chain, so that the revelation of the Divine light — in concealment, hiddenness and great contraction — is not absent from the heart of any Jew; even the lowest of the low has in him a portion of life, a portion of God from above. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Regarding spiritual holiness it is said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity," and "the Divine Presence never departed from the Western Wall": in concealment it never departed, even in every kind of sinking into evil bitterer than death — "I will fear no evil, for You are with me." We suppose this a deficiency, but in truth it is the strength of completeness and the ultimate clarification: that wherever a person sinks, his heart remains bound to the Blessed One with a bond that cannot be severed. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The Holy One, blessed be He, as it were entered Egypt, the place of impurity, and this was the great miracle and the first of the miracles: the clarification of "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity," from their beginning and root in the Patriarchs, who are truly holy seed with no connection to any impurity, so that it was revealed that impurity has no real existence. Esther is the end: even in the lowest levels, where the nations hold sway, the Blessed One is with them, even in the place of impurity's greatest strength, as when Esther entered the house of Ahasuerus. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Raising the holy sparks out of the matters of this world, by engaging in them for the sake of Heaven, is like a king's son returning from captivity, whose joy exceeds that of one who was always in the palace; of this it is said, "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity" — amid it precisely. Over this that wicked one [Bilaam] was blinded when he spoke of "the fourth of Israel" and said "He who is holy…," for he did not know that there is holiness even in bodily matters. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): So too the souls of Israel outside the Land are like the Tabernacle [dismantled in order to be rebuilt], for the Blessed One dwells with them amid their impurity and His Presence is within the hearts of Israel: wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went into exile with them, and that place became their place. Through the exile they gather in the bit of good among the nations and return it all to holiness, and that place too becomes sanctified with the holiness of the air of the Land of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Even when sin caused Israel to be exiled among the nations, outside even the holiness of the Land, wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went with them — for even "in the lands of their enemies I have not rejected them," and "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity." Nonetheless they are never separated from the root of holiness, and in the end all will be redeemed, even those wholly assimilated among the nations.),
Yet in truth Hashem "dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness" (Yoma 56b end),
כִּי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the Congregation of Israel represents the level of prayer as is known,
דְּזֶה כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
this being the root of Israel:

שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד358 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh.
