Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..) וְזוֹכֵר בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that even if he sinned as he did, he remains Israel (Sanhedrin 44a) and remembers Hashem,
וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה וּצְעָקָה בַּלֵּב תָּדִיר בִּתְפִלָּה
and the transgressors of Israel are filled with remorse and interior outcry in prayer

[וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא "גַּנָּבָא אַפּוּם מַחְתַּרְתָּא וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת סג359 Berakhot 63a — Bar Kappara expounded: Which is the brief passage upon which all the essentials of the Torah depend? "In all your ways know Him, and He will make your paths straight." Rava said: Even for a matter of transgression. [The reading of Ein Yaakov continues: Rav Pappa said — this is what people say: the thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One.] Rashi (s.v. "in all your ways"): "In all your ways" — even to commit a transgression. "Know Him" — give thought to whether it is required for a mitzvah, as with Elijah on Mount Carmel, and [if so] transgress it. Maharsha: He did not say "remember Him" but "know Him" — a true knowledge of His existence, and that He is able and watches over all your ways, to give good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked. And it concludes, "and He will make your paths straight," after the manner of what they said: in the way a man wishes to go, he is led, and one who comes to purify himself is assisted. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 34): As it is written, "In all your ways know Him," and the Sages said, "even for a matter of transgression" — then "He will straighten [your paths]." That is, one should give himself over to the Blessed One even to the point of losing his entire share in the World to Come when such is the will of the Blessed One — as I heard concerning the trial of the Binding — and then "He will straighten": the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself straightens you and separates the evil from you without toil. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 19): On "In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths," Rava said, "even for a matter of transgression," and the reading of Ein Yaakov is: "Rav Pappa said, this is what people say: the thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One." That is, even though he commits an explicit transgression of "You shall not steal," since he does not forget the Blessed One and believes in Him at the moment of the act, calling upon the Merciful One, of this it is said "and He will straighten your paths": the Blessed One will straighten his paths, so that "the banished one is not banished from Him," and he will have a rectification. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Beshalach): "Encamp opposite it by the sea": it is written, "In all your ways know Him" — even for a matter of transgression; and this is the meaning of "encamp opposite it": even though you perform deeds like those of the Egyptians, nevertheless the deeds of Israel are good, for the Israelite nation, the portion of the Blessed One, cleaves to simple life without any garment and draws from that source of life alone. All these powers, when among Israel, are full of holiness even though they resemble those of Egypt, for the Blessed One testifies about them that in the heart of Israel there is nothing but love of the Blessed One. Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Berakhos 7): [By placing "I am" before "You shall have no other gods," the Blessed One showed that] even one who has, Heaven forbid, stumbled in a deed that is not good is not barred from repentance and can perform mitzvos though he is not yet cleansed of "turning from evil." This is what the dictum "In all your ways know Him," on which all the essentials of the Torah depend, teaches; and as Rava concludes, "even for a matter of transgression" — that is, a person should not despair after stumbling in sin, for repentance is never withheld from him..)].
and what is more, "the thief at the opening of the breach invokes God, etc." (Berakhot 63a).
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אַדְּרַבָּה, לֹא זָכוּ לְשׁוּם מַעֲלָה אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי חִסָּרוֹן הַקּוֹדֵם,
And Israel, on the contrary, attained virtues only through a preceding lack,
וּמַעֲשֵׂה שִׁטִּים הָיָה הֲכָנָה לִכְנִיסַת הָאָרֶץ,
and the sin of Shittim was preparation for entering the Land;
דְּהַיְינוּ לִזְכּוֹת לָאָרֶץ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה וְהַפְרָדָה לְגַמְרֵי מֵאֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים
namely, to merit the Holy Land and achieve complete separation from the lands of the nations
הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַצְּעָקָה וַחֲרָטָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בְּשִׁטִּים עַל חִבּוּרָם לִבְנוֹת הָעַמִּים.
came through the outcry and remorse they experienced at Shittim over joining with foreign women.
דִּבְכָל עִנְיַן מַעֲלָה יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר עַד הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית,
For in every virtue there are gradations in that area up to cleaving to the depth of the Beginning,
וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים אָז לִדְבּוֹק בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לָזֶה לִהְיוֹת נִפְרָדִים מִגּוֹיִם לְגַמְרֵי בְּאֶרֶץ מְיוּחֶדֶת.
and they then needed to cleave to the depth of the Beginning relevant to this to become separated from gentiles in a designated Land.
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה מִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה,
And it was impossible to merit this from the vantage of ascent alone,
דְּמִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מַעְלָה מַעְלָה עַד עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית הָאֲמִיתִּי, שׁוּב אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לָאָרֶץ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל.
for when ascending through virtue to the true depth of the Beginning, one loses all connection to physical land in this world.
רַק מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן, שֶׁשָּׁבוּ תַּחְתּוֹנִים לְמַעְלָה עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵיקוּת דִּתְפִלָּה,
Only through deficiency, whereby the fallen lower realms return Above through the cleaving of prayer,
עֲזָרָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָזֶה לְהִפָּרֵד מִגּוֹיִם לְגַמְרֵי.
did Hashem assist them in separating completely from the nations.
וְעִנְיָן זֶה הוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ,
And this matter is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
דְּהַיְינוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּקִרְבָּם.
namely the Congregation of Israel within whom the Holy One dwells.
וְזֶה עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ: "וְאֶל זֶה אַבִּיט אֶל עָנִי וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is His humility: "but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor, etc." (Isaiah 66:2),

רַק "שֶׁחָרֵד עַל דְּבָרִי360 Isaiah 66:2 — “But to this one will I look: to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at My word.” Rashi: "All these" — the heavens and the earth — "My hand has made"; it was for this that I confined My Presence among you while you were obedient to Me, for such is My way, to look to one who is poor and crushed in spirit and who hastens to do My bidding. But now I have no desire for you, for he who slaughters the ox has struck down its owner and robbed him of it. Radak: Do not think, because I said "the heaven is My throne and the earth My footstool," that they are as ancient as I am; rather I alone am the Ancient One, and I made all these anew. And though I am exalted above all, I look to the lowly and the humble and to those who tremble at My word to keep My commandments, even though they bring no offering — for one who does not sin needs no offering, while those who bring offerings and whose deeds are evil find their offering unacceptable. Metzudas Dovid: Even the heavens and the earth are not as ancient as I am, for My hand made them and only afterwards did they come to be. "And to this I will look" — although I am exalted above all that is exalted, I still look and attend to the lowly: to the poor, to one whose spirit is broken by sorrow and grief, and to one who trembles at My word to do it — but not to those who bring offerings while their heart is far from Me. Malbim: That they should build Him a house to dwell in would imply that He lacks something and asks His own creatures to supply it; but how can that be said of the Lord, when "all these My hand has made" — both their first making and the continuance of their kinds are through Me alone. "And to this I will look, to the poor and contrite of spirit" — one poor in his outward state and broken in his inward state, who nonetheless trembles at My word to obey Me. This was the whole purpose of the Sanctuary and the offerings, that it is a satisfaction before Me that I spoke and My will was done; the offering itself is not what is sought, but the doing of My will and the submission a man shows before Me in obeying My word.".
provided only that he "trembles at My word."
וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הוּא גְּדוּלָּתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא קָדוֹשׁ וּמְרוֹמָם.
And the Holy One represents His greatness, being transcendent and holy.
וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַגּוֹיִם לְהָבִין כְּלָל,
And this dynamic is impossible for the nations to comprehend,
אֵיךְ דְּגַם שֶׁ"הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהַלָּלוּ וְכוּלֵי"
how "these are idolaters and those are, etc.",
וּמְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּכָל מִינֵי חֶסְרוֹנוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and immersed in all types of mundane deficiencies,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
yet despite this, remain bound to Hashem;
וּכְשֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִסְתַּכֵּל וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּדָבָר זֶה,
and when they attempt to gaze and contemplate this,
נִסְמָא עֵינֵיהֶם וְכֹחַ רְאִיָּיתָם מִפְּנֵי תֹּקֶף הַבְּהִירוּת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִגֶּדֶר כֹּחַ הַשָּׂגָתָם שֶׁהוּא מְעַוֵּור.
their eyes and vision are blinded by the blinding intensity of the light transcending their capacity.
כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין לָהֶם רְאִיָּה לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתָם,
For Israel possess no vision detached above their actual reach,
שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁהַשָּׂגָתָם פְּחוּתָה וַחֲסֵרָה יוֹתֵר, הֵם דְּבוּקִים וּמִתְעַלִּים יוֹתֵר;
since the lower and more broken their perception is, the more closely they cleave and ascend;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נְבִיאֵי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
unlike the prophets of the idolaters
הֵם כְּפִי מַעֲלָתָם בִּפְרִישׁוּת מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
who perceive only according to their ascetic detachment from worldly affairs,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר רוֹצֶה לִידַּבֵּק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אָז הוּא מְשׁוּקָּע בֶּאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
so that when one desires worldly attachment, he is genuinely submerged in this world,
כִּי תְּפִלָּה הוּא רָזָא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
for prayer is the exclusive mystery of the Congregation of Israel,
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁחֲסֵרִים, הֵם חֲסֵרִים בֶּאֱמֶת וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה כְּלָל.
and whatever the nations lack, they lack in absolute reality, being unable to bridge it.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת (בְּרָכוֹת ז361 Berakhot 7a — And R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Yosei: Moses asked three things of the Holy One, blessed be He, and He granted them to him. He asked that the Divine Presence rest upon Israel, and He granted it to him, as it is said, "Is it not in that You go with us?" He asked that the Divine Presence not rest upon the nations of the world, and He granted it to him, as it is said, "So that we are distinguished, I and Your people." Rashi: "Three things Moses asked and He granted them to him" — for at the end of his request it is written, "This thing also that you have spoken I will do" (Exodus 33:17). Maharsha: Rashi's proof, "This thing also that you have spoken I will do," fits these two requests, which are drawn from the verse standing immediately before it. But to the request "Show me now Your ways" He had already replied, "My presence will go and I will give you rest," which He then explains with "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious" — to the one fit for grace; and R. Meir disagrees and holds that this last request was not granted him at all. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): It was Moses our teacher who asked that the Divine Presence not rest upon the nations of the world, and it was granted to him — that is, not immediately but only after his death, for Bilam came afterwards, at the end of [Moses'] days; and so the Gemara in Bava Basra says that once Moses died, no more prophets arose among the nations. For the Blessed One loves justice, and by the justice governing this world each thing must have its counterpart, so that as long as Moses was among Israel, with their attainment of the knowledge above human intellect, the like had to exist among the nations. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Moses our teacher took in from Midian the good within its power of division and strife, to arouse strife between the nations and our Father in Heaven — as they said, he asked that the Divine Presence not rest upon the nations of the world — and he brought down destruction and hatred upon them, so that even should a gentile wish to mend his deeds completely he cannot, for even the pious of the nations have not the slightest connection to the holiness of Israel unless they convert and take the name of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): From Berakhos it is evident that it was Moses our teacher who asked that the Divine Presence not rest upon the nations of the world, and it was granted to him; yet Bava Basra says that once Moses died no more prophets arose among the nations — it was granted only after his death, since Bilam prophesied afterwards, at the end of his days — and this must be said of prophecy alone, not of the holy spirit. One may explain that Moses' request concerned the resting of the Divine Presence in the revelation of words of Torah, like the prophecy of Bilam, which is written in the Torah, and [that of] Job; and in any case prophecy did rest after Abraham on those not of his seed at all, so that Moses had to pray for this, Abraham having received no promise of it. Tiferes Yosef (Shavuos 1): From the side of the Blessed One [the bestowal] is like "rain for all, for the righteous and for the wicked"; it is man who must limit the bestowal so that it goes only to those who do His will — as Moses our teacher asked, "So that we are distinguished, I and Your people," and as the Talmud says, he asked that the Divine Presence rest only upon Israel..),
And this is why Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, requested that the Shechinah not rest upon idolaters (Berakhot 7a),
וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ גַּם עַל תְּפִלַּת הַגּוֹי שֶׁיֵּעָנוּ,
while King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed that the prayer of the foreigner also be answered,
וְגַם לֶעָתִיד בִּמְשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד נֶאֱמַר: "אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה וְגוֹמֵר".
and concerning the future Messianic era it is said: "I will turn to the peoples a pure language, etc." (Zephaniah 3:9).
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה,
For Moses represents the level of Wisdom (Chokhmah),

וְכָל הָאוֹמֵר דְּבַר חָכְמָה גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא חָכָם (מְגִילָּה טז362 Megillah 16a — "And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to all his friends." It calls them "his friends" and it calls them "his wise men." R. Yochanan said: Whoever says a word of wisdom, even among the nations of the world, is called a wise man. Maharsha: The "word of wisdom" for which they earned the name of wise men is a word of the wisdom of the Torah, namely what the verse goes on to say: "If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews" — if he descends from the other tribes you can prevail over him, but if from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim or Manasseh you cannot. For that Mordecai was a Jew they already knew, since it had been published throughout the provinces; until now they had supposed he came from one of the other tribes and that Haman could prevail over him, and only when they saw the beginning of Haman's fall did they take fright and say that he might be of those tribes for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, "stirs up His might." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): As stated in Megillah, one who says a word of wisdom among the nations is called a wise man — learned from Haman's "wise men," who grasped the truth that he would fall before the seed of the Jews. For this is the whole wisdom of the nations: to grasp the superiority of Israel, that they cannot prevail against them; but to grasp the wisdom of truth, the wisdom of the Torah — the apprehension of His truth — is impossible for them, for "He has not done so for any nation.".),
and whoever speaks wisdom even among the nations is called wise (Megillah 16a),

דְּ"יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בַּגּוֹיִם – תַּאֲמִין" (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה ב, ט363 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." If a man says to you: There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written, "And I will destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau." [If he says:] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, as it is written, "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Although the sages of the nations may originate wisdom in matters of the service of the Blessed One, it is not reckoned as Oral Torah — only what the Sages of Israel originate. And this is "He shone forth from Seir to them": human wisdom, which is chiefly in Seir, as the Sages said, "There is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'"; and this shone forth to Israel, to be theirs alone, for nothing is called wisdom but the wisdom of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 17): "You have taken gifts among men [ba-adam]" — these are the spoils taken from Esau, the power of "we will do"; for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom,'" that is, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, to rectify the excess of anger, while might is used only to conquer the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it.),
for "if one tells you there is wisdom among the nations, believe it" (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 2:9),
דְּיֵשׁ גַּם בָּהֶם גָּוֶון מֵחָכְמָה;
there existing among them an outward facet of wisdom;
רַק דְּלֵב אֵין,
only that the heart is lacking,

דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא "צוּר לְבָבָם" דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב364 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse, as it is written: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 8): The theme of this month [Adar] is that even in sleep Israel are holy, since they are bound at their root to the Blessed One — as the Midrash says, "I am asleep from the commandments ... but my heart is awake to perform them ... where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? 'God is the rock of my heart.'" From the side of the Blessed One, "the voice of my beloved knocks, open for me": "my heart is awake" means that the Blessed One, the heart of Israel, rouses Israel from their sleep to perform the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): The Congregation of Israel boasts, "I am asleep but my heart is awake," which the Sages expounded as referring to the Holy One, blessed be He — "rock of my heart." Even when they are asleep from the commandments and have no "eyes," as in sleep when the eyes are shut and the heart is sunk in imaginings, since the root of the soul is a portion of God and the depths of the heart cleave to the Blessed One, all the imaginings too cleave to Him; even at the height of immersion in the imaginings of this world, which hide the truth, there remains in him a power of awakening to the Blessed One through the heart's cleaving to the living God. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 68): All the service of the body's limbs, and the commandments performed with them, serve only to set the heart straight; the essential thing is the heart, the dwelling place of the Blessed One, as the Sages said, "the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it says, 'rock of my heart.'" Therefore these [outward acts] are not to be a person's goal in themselves, but only things that lead to the goal, as the Zohar calls the 613 commandments "613 counsels.").
for the Holy One is called "the rock of the heart" of Israel (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2).
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לִטְעוֹת,
Yet from the perspective of wisdom one could err;

וּמִי שֶׁרָאָה בִּלְעָם בְּיָמָיו, וַדַּאי הֲגַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה סוֹף עַמּוּד א)365 Sanhedrin 105a — R. Yochanan said: Balaam was lame in one leg, as it is stated, "and he went limping [shefi]"; Samson in both his legs, as it is stated, "a horned snake [shefifon] upon the path." Balaam was blind in one eye, as it is stated, "whose eye is closed." He practiced divination with his membrum. It was stated: Mar Zutra said, he practiced divination with his membrum; Mar son of Ravina said, he had relations with his donkey. The one who says he practiced divination with his membrum — as we have said; and the one who says he had relations with his donkey — it is written here, "he crouched, he lay down," and it is written there, "between her legs." Rashi: Shefi ["limping"] is as in "the hip whose bone has slipped [shaf] from its place," and shefifon implies two. "Whose eye is shetum" means open, as in "its opening [shetumo] is noticeable": one eye was open, implying that the other was closed (some explain shetum as satum, "closed," but that is not correct); "divining with his membrum" is like one who raises [the dead] by his membrum. [On "he crouched, he lay down":] just as the crouching there, which involves falling, denotes intercourse, so the crouching here, where "falling" is written, denotes intercourse — that he had relations with his beast. Maharsha: Shefi is from shufi, the hip bone. It teaches Balaam's evil heart toward Israel: he was lame in one leg, perhaps as a punishment for going to curse them, as it says, "and [the donkey] crushed Balaam's foot," and even so he did not hold back from saying "I will go; perhaps the Lord will come to meet me," though he went limping; his blindness in one eye was likewise a punishment for wishing to curse Israel, as the Midrash has it. Of Samson it teaches that although he was lame in both legs, he performed his mighty deeds against the Philistines. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 105a): He divined from the side of his form, for the membrum signifies the form of "man" [ish], and Balaam divined from the very essence of his human form; the one who holds this likens Balaam, in his power of impurity, to Moses — as they said, "in Israel none arose [like Moses], but among the nations one did" — for Moses is called "the man Moses" on account of the eminence of his form. Mar son of Ravina, who says he had relations with his she-donkey, holds that the power of impurity that rested upon him came from his joining himself to matter [chomer], the donkey [chamor], through an abominable act. He likens Balaam to Abraham, of whom it is said "and he saddled his donkey" — except that Abraham's was a male, which he rode while remaining separate from it, whereas Balaam's was a she-donkey, to which he was joined. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 57): Both statements mean that Balaam cleaved to lewdness, harlotry and impurity. According to the one master, he used that shameful organ for spiritual matters, which is a great indecency and disgrace; according to the other, he had relations with his she-donkey, which is a great disgrace — to join oneself to a beast. דְּבָא עַל אֲתוֹנוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
and whoever observed Balaam in his day—even though our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 105a end) that he acted perversely with his donkey, etc.—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְמַרְאֵה עֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהוּא אָדָם גָּדוֹל,
nonetheless to human sight one could have presumed he was a great man,
וְהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְדַבֵּר דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת שֶׁנִּכְתְּבוּ בַּתּוֹרָה.
possessing the capacity to utter truths recorded in the Torah.
וּלְכָךְ הוּצְרַךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה וְכוּלֵי,
Therefore Moses had to pray that the Shechinah not rest upon them,

דּבֶאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה שָׁם)366 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah" (Lamentations 2:9). If a man should say to you, There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written: "And I will destroy the wise men out of Edom, and discernment out of the mount of Esau" (Obadiah 1:8). [If he should say,] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, for it is written: "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it.: "יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם – אַל תַּאֲמִין",
for in truth they taught: "if one tells you there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it,"
דְּהִיא "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב" לְבַד.
as it is the exclusive heritage of the congregation of Jacob.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא לד367 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34 — R. Yehudah bar Shalom said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "Write these words," Moses asked that the Mishnah too be put in writing. But the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the nations of the world were destined to translate the Torah and read it in Greek, and to say, "We are Israel." Until now the scales are balanced. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the nations: You say that you are My children — I do not know; only those who hold My mysteries are My children. And which are they? This is the Mishnah, which was given orally, and from which everything is to be expounded. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): After prophecy departed, the sages of the Oral Torah began, and the Sages said, "He has set me in dark places — this is the Talmud of Babylonia"; but this is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says in Tanchuma, "Those who hold My mysteries are Israel." For it is written, "He made darkness His hiding place" — there are His hidden things; and though it is darkness and the hiding of the Face, the darkness is cast by the shadow of His hand, shielding us by way of concealment, as one must make shade to protect against the blazing sun. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:86): The Blessed One teaches human beings to exert effort, which is why the Torah began for Israel as the Written Torah; He wishes a person to arrive at His mysteries — as in the Midrash, "He who holds My mysteries…" — and to understand what He indicates to him with the compass. This is the essential effort: to come to the Oral Torah, which is the recognition that everything is from the Blessed One, the "finding" that comes after toil. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): The novel insights of Torah belong to the Oral Torah, whereas in the Written Torah, which is written and set down [before all], there are no novel insights; therefore the nations claim on the strength of the Written Torah, "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers, "He who holds My mysteries…," for the Oral Torah exists only in the hearts of the children of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Edom claims that they are the good and the pure by birth; therefore Haman's decree was a preparation for the Oral Torah, as the Midrash says: because the nations are destined to say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "He who holds My mysteries…" — for it is the Oral Torah that clarifies this. The Oral Torah is what springs from the heart of Israel, the hearts of the children of Israel being its originators, so that it is theirs alone, and this is the testimony that they, and no others, are the masters of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Just as there is wisdom among the nations but no Torah among the nations, so it says in Tanchuma, "He who holds My mysteries…": the Oral Torah was given over only to Israel. The nations, even if they study Torah and innovate in it by their wisdom, speak vanity and not Torah at all, for they innovate from their own wisdom, whereas the Torah is the wisdom of the Blessed One; but the sages of Israel bless over the Torah first and know that the Blessed One is the Giver of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 3): The essence of the Torah is the Oral Torah, which reveals the hidden things of the Written Torah, as it says in Shemos Rabbah that the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek… "He who holds My mysteries…." This is an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob alone: the Torah is handed over to them according to what they clarify through their dialectic and their wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): They said in Tanchuma that the Oral Torah was given because the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek and say "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say, "He who holds My mysteries…." That is, the nations too have a connection to the Written Torah, which is why it was revealed in writing to all who come into the world; but the Oral Torah is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, which cannot be revealed in writing at all, only "the secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him" — the Congregation of Israel, who look to the Blessed One from the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): All the innovation of the Oral Torah comes through the unions and complete cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is His mysteries, as they said in Tanchuma at the end of Ki Sisa: because the nations of the world are destined to translate the Torah and say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "He who holds My mysteries…." This is the telling of secrets, which is for Jacob alone — and "telling" does not mean in writing — so "He tells [His words to Jacob]" means the Oral Torah, the handing over of the words of Torah of which it is said "He has not done so for any nation"; whereas the Written Torah alone was written on the stones in seventy languages.):
And in the manner our Sages taught in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34):
"עֲתִידִים אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר: אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי, מִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי וְכוּלֵי".
"The nations will claim: We are Israel; but God says: My mystery (the Oral Torah) proves who is Mine."
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה:
And this is the essence of the resting of the Shechinah:
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיגוּ מֵחָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
that they never comprehend the wisdom of the Oral Torah.
וּבִלְעָם הִשִּׂיג דְּבָרִים שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרוּ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
For Balaam grasped only concepts articulated in the Written Torah;
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא רָזָא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
since the Oral Torah is the mystery of the Congregation of Israel,
הַנּוֹבֵעַ רַק מִלִּבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
flowing exclusively from the hearts of the Jewish people;
דְּתוֹרָה עִיקָּרוֹ לְשׁוֹן הוֹרָאַת דֶּרֶךְ לְהַשִּׂיג יִחוּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְהִדָּבֵק בּוֹ.
for Torah essentially means showing the way to attain the unity of Hashem and cleave unto Him.
וְהֵם אַדְּרַבָּה, כָּל חָכְמָתָם הוּא מְאַבְּדָם;
Whereas with the nations, on the contrary, their wisdom destroys them;
וְהֲגַם דְּמַשִּׂיגִים הָאֱמֶת כְּעִנְיַן בִּלְעָם וְכֵן חֲכָמָיו דְּהָמָן,
and even when grasping truth like Balaam or Haman's advisors,
עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִפָּרֵד מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ.
nonetheless, it is impossible for the gentile to detach from his spiritual root.
אֲבָל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד שֶׁהֵם דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה,
However, regarding the Davidic dynasty representing the level of prayer,
שָׁם אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לְבֶן נֵכָר כְּלָל,
a foreigner possesses no point of contact whatsoever,
דְּעִיקַּר תְּפִלָּה בַּלֵּב וְזֶה אֵינוֹ אֶצְלָם,
for the core of prayer is in the heart, which is absent in them,
כִּי בָּזֶה הֵם נִפְרָדִים בֶּאֱמֶת.
since in this they are truly severed.
לָכֵן בִּקֵּשׁ אַדְּרַבָּה,
Therefore Solomon specifically prayed,
דְּהֲגַם דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת בֶּאֱמֶת –
that even though they cannot attain an authentic inner connection—
דְּזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּעֹמֶק הַלֵּב בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which comes through cleaving to Hashem in the depths of the heart, the unique root of Israel,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְהַפְּכוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְשׁוּב אֵינָם קְרוּיִם בְּנֵי נֵכָר וְעַמִּים כְּלָל,
meaning that they would have to convert to Israel, no longer being foreigners or separate nations,
דְּעִנְיַן בֶּן נֵכָר הַיְינוּ שֶׁעֹמֶק לִבּוֹ אֵין דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ –
since a foreigner is defined as one whose heart's depth is not bound to Hashem—
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ עַל כָּל פָּנִים קְדוּשַּׁת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
yet nonetheless Solomon asked that they at least recognize the sanctity of the Temple and Israel.
וְזֶהוּ "שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה" – מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ,
And this is a "pure language (safah)"—from the lips outward,
הֲגַם דְּאֵין בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב,
even though not penetrating the inner heart,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי זֶה יַכִּירוּ מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן,
nonetheless through this they will recognize Israel's stature,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לוֹמַר עַל יְדֵי זֶה "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל" כְּלָל.
making it impossible for them to claim "we are Israel."
וְאָז "וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם",
And then "I will destroy the wise men out of Edom" (Obadiah 1:8),

דְּהוֹכִיחוּ מִזֶּה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה שָׁם)368 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah" (Lamentations 2:9). If a man should say to you, There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written: "And I will destroy the wise men out of Edom, and discernment out of the mount of Esau" (Obadiah 1:8). [If he should say,] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, for it is written: "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Although the sages of the nations may originate wisdom in matters of the service of the Blessed One, it is not reckoned as Oral Torah — only what the Sages of Israel originate. And this is "He shone forth from Seir to them": human wisdom, which is chiefly in Seir, as the Sages said, "There is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'"; and this shone forth to Israel, to be theirs alone, for nothing is called wisdom but the wisdom of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 17): "You have taken gifts among men [ba-adam]" — these are the spoils taken from Esau, the power of "we will do"; for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom,'" that is, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, to rectify the excess of anger, while might is used only to conquer the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it. דּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ.
from which our Sages proved that in this world worldly wisdom does exist.
דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה זֶה לִשְׁנֵי דְבָרִים נִפְרָדִים,
For in this world these appear as two divided concepts,
וּבֶאֱמֶת מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא הֵם תְּרֵין רֵיעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין,
yet in truth the brain and heart are two companions that never part,
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה כּוּלָּא חַד,
and likewise Torah and prayer are entirely one,

וּבִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה תְּפִלָּה (בְּרָכוֹת ח., מְגִילָּה כט369 Berakhot 8a — Rav Chisda said: What is meant by "The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob"? The Lord loves the gates distinguished in halakhah more than synagogues and study houses. And this accords with what R. Chiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla: From the day the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world but the four cubits of halakhah alone. And Abaye said: At first I would study in my house and pray in the synagogue; once I heard this teaching of R. Chiyya bar Ami in the name of Ulla, I would pray only where I study. R. Ami and R. Asi, though they had thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, would pray only between the pillars where they studied. Rashi: "Distinguished" — from tziyyun, a mark set up, and the assembling of a congregation. "Between the pillars" — for the study house was built upon them, above. Maharsha: In a synagogue all sorts are found, small and great alike, and in their study houses some learn Scripture and some Mishnah, and the decided halakhah that issues from the Talmud does not come into their hands; "gates distinguished in halakhah" therefore means the place where each Torah scholar fixes a place for his study in the Talmud, which brings him a decided ruling. "Gates" here is like "in your gates," which the Targum renders "at the door of your court" — a fixed place from which instruction goes out to the townsfolk; and "dwellings" are the synagogues and study houses, which stand in place of the Tabernacle, the Divine Presence dwelling in them in exile. While the Temple stood there was the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from which decided halakhah went forth by the Sanhedrin, and the Divine Presence surely dwelt with them; now that it is destroyed, those four cubits of halakhah stand in its stead. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael 70): The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in the corporeal world, for the corporeal is removed from Him; what is His is the four cubits of halakhah. It is called halakhah because, as one who walks a road does not swerve to right or left, so a ruling of halakhah does not swerve from the point of truth. Just as He chose the Temple, which is fit for holiness because it stands at the centre — and the centre has no distance about it, distance belonging to the corporeal — so halakhah is wholly simple intellect, with no relation to the corporeal, and therefore the place where halakhah is belongs to Him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): Torah is "voice", the male, and prayer, said in a whisper, is "speech", the female; and just as "a woman who seeds first bears a male" and the females are made dependent on the males, so it says "they would pray only where they studied", and in Megillah the reverse, "they would study only where they prayed": for through the voice of Torah one merits prayer, and through prayer one begets the voice of Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): The word "voice" is joined to Jacob because the voice of the Oral Torah is the essential root of Jacob, and the voice of prayer is drawn from it, as with R. Ami and R. Asi, who would pray only between the pillars where they studied. For [the Sages] instituted that one first say "O Lord, open my lips", since one can pray only when the Blessed One opens his lips, and this opening comes through the Oral Torah..);
and in the place of Torah there is prayer (Berakhot 8a, Megillah 29a);
רַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן נִרְאֶה כִּדְבָרִים נִפְרָדִים וַהֲפָכִים מַמָּשׁ,
only to superficial sight do they seem separate and opposite,
דְּתוֹרָה הַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת, וְהַשָּׁלֵם אֵינוֹ חָסֵר.
for Torah denotes perfection, and the whole lacks nothing.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד,
Yet with Hashem it is possible for two opposites to coexist in one subject,
וּבִמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ.
and in the place of His greatness is His humility.

וְכֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל: "כָּל הַגָּדוֹל [מֵחֲבֵירוֹ] יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל [הֵימֶנּוּ]" (סֻכָּה נב370 Sukkah 52a — Abaye said: Had it been the one who hates me [meaning himself], he would not have been able to restrain himself. He went and leaned against the doorpost in distress. A certain elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his. Rashi (s.v. "had it been the one who hates me"): Had my enemy been alone with the woman, he could not have restrained himself from sinning; and he was speaking of himself. Rashi (s.v. "he leaned"): He leaned against the bolt of the door, like a man who is brooding and in distress. Rashi (s.v. "the way is long, and the company pleasant"): It is a long way between our two places, and we cannot go on together any further; had we been able to go by one road, our company would have been pleasant. Rashi (s.v. "when they were parting from one another"): They were from two towns, and when they reached a fork in the road he turned one way and she the other. Maharsha (on "for he has done greatly"): The verse concludes "for he has done greatly," meaning that he provokes the great more, as Abaye concludes. Alternatively, "he has done greatly" means that he has made himself great in relation to the righteous, [appearing to them] as a mountain, as was said above that at first he resembles a spider's thread and in the end cart-ropes; and "among Torah scholars more than all of them" is then a statement in its own right, as in the incident of Abaye. Maharsha (s.v. "the way is long"): It may also be explained as referring to the past: we have come a long way, but the company was pleasant, so that because of the company the way did not seem so long to us. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Koach HaYetzer 2): The evil inclination provokes the Torah scholar more than all, although he is complete, being a man of intellect: for the intellect a man possesses [in this world] is never in its completeness but is held with deficiency, so that the Torah scholar and Israel lack the completeness fitting for them, whereas other men and other nations, who have only the small level, cannot be called so deficient. Therefore the evil inclination provokes them more and more, and whoever has a higher level must guard himself against the evil inclination. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 48): After Israel received the Torah and reached a supreme level, the evil inclination provoked them to sin, in the manner of "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": because they had reached a supreme level that the rest of creation had not reached, the evil inclination, which is Satan, seeks to cast them down from their level. For privation clings more to a man who has a supreme level, one not fitting for every man, than it clings to the low level that is found in all. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 19): Just as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his" (and that elder, who was Elijah according to some commentators in Tosafos, a view I have received as primary, was revealed to Abaye through his anguish to tell him this and console him), so too, when someone's inclination is greater than his fellow's, this is a sign that he is also greater than him in the holy sparks within him, for God has made one opposite the other in each person, and the choice is in his hands. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 6): Such an abundance of light would bring great hardship to those who walk in the way of God, for the same reason as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": with a greater abundance of the light of the Blessed One, the evil in that same place grows stronger too, because so much light lies within it, for evil always surrounds the good. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Since the Blessed One does not deal tyrannically with His creatures, and even one created righteous must choose against an inclination that overpowers him daily, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his". Therefore the inclination appears to the righteous like a mountain, for its assault on them is enormous, matching the great power of good innate in them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 8): The Sages said that the evil inclination provokes Torah scholars more than all and that "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"; why should this be? The inclination is longing, and the purpose of its creation is to be the delight of Torah; so the one who is greater, in whom the delight of Torah is sunk more deeply, has, since "God has made the one opposite the other," a stronger desire toward the opposite as well, while one who does not magnify the delight of Torah in himself has no strong desire for the opposite either. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 2): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for the virtue is drawn together with the deficiency: as great and precious wealth needs more guarding than a small thing, being more liable to harm because more people strive after it, so in the soul, the greater its stature, that is, the more divine power it holds (and the will toward the opposite is also a divine power), the greater in it is this power of inclination as well, and it needs guarding. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for as the strength of the virtue, so is the strength of the deficiency, from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, where evil stands opposite the good and corresponds to it. Hence Dan, the lowest of the tribes in virtue, is lower in his deficiency as well, and the inclination is not as strong in him. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 134): When a person reaches a higher level, by the measure of that level he has not yet begun to repent, and his sin returns in full force; of this it is said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", for the sin is the deficiency in a person, and so is the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Where the strength of the virtue lies, there lies the strength of the deficiency, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": as is known, in Adam's sin the "man of Belial" ruled over the holy man limb for limb, God having made the one opposite the other, so that corresponding to the holiness of each limb and power is the dominion of the "man of Belial" in enticing to evil. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Mishlei 19): "The desire of a man is his kindness": the desire found in a person's heart is also a kindness from the Blessed One, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", and if he brings the power of his longing and desire into holiness, his stature grows all the more. Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 4): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for "God has made the one opposite the other": the power of good against the power of its opposite. Yet every person has the power of good to overcome his inclination, and through this he rises, gathering wealth in holiness little by little, which is the whole purpose of man's creation in this world. Sod Yesharim (Seventh Night of Pesach 16): The vessel [of longing] that a person attains in old age was already in him on the day he was born, only that each time he clarifies himself further, the vessel grows larger in him too, as the Sages said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"..),
And so it is with Israel: "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater" (Sukkah 52a),
וְהוּא חָסֵר בְּיוֹתֵר,
meaning he feels more deeply deficient,
וּכְפִי גּוֹדֶל חָכְמָתוֹ כָּךְ הוּא מַכִּיר בְּיוֹתֵר חֶסְרוֹנוֹ.
and according to his wisdom, so does he recognize his deficiency.
וְלֶעָתִיד יְבוֹרַר זֶה לָעַיִן,
And in the future this will be clearly demonstrated,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "עֹד תַּעֲבֹרְנָה הַצֹּאן עַל יְדֵי מוֹנֶה" –
and it is said: "the flocks shall pass again under the hands of him that counts them" (Jeremiah 33:13)—
מַשְׁמָע אֶחָד;
implying a single counter;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נֶאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר פֻּקַּד עַל פִּי מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן",
unlike in this world where it is said: "who were numbered by Moses and Aaron,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר רֵישׁ בַּמִּדְבָּר דְּיֵשׁ חַיָּילִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְחַיָּילִין דְּמַשְׁכְּנָא.
as written in the Zohar (beginning of Bamidbar) that there are legions of the Torah and legions of the Mishkan.
דִּכְמוֹ דְּשִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא אוֹתִיּוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה,
For just as there are 600,000 letters in the Torah,
וְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק מְיוּחָד בַּתּוֹרָה,
and every soul of Israel possesses a specific share in the Torah,
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ הַדָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
which derives from intellectual wisdom in the brain cleaving to Hashem;
כָּךְ יֵשׁ לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל חֵלֶק פְּרָטִי בַּמִּשְׁכָּן וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
so does every soul of Israel possess an individual part in the Mishkan and Temple
מִצַּד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַדָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
stemming from devotion of the heart cleaving to Hashem.
וְחִבּוּר הַמּוֹחִין דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
And the joining of the intellects of Israel forms the letters of the Torah,
וְחִבּוּר עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מְלֶאכֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן.
while the joining of the heart's service forms the craftsmanship of the Mishkan.
וְהַמִּנְיָן נִקְרָא "שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ",
And the census is termed "raise the head" (take the sum),
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת מְיוּחָד,
for each person holds a unique elevation,
דְּכָל חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה אוֹ בַּמִּשְׁכָּן הוּא נִצְרָךְ,
every share in the Torah or Mishkan being vital,
שֶׁאִם יֶחְסַר יִפָּסֵל,
such that if one part is missing the whole is invalidated,
וְנִמְצָא כָּל אֶחָד מְנוּשָּׂא בְּעִנְיָן מְיוּחָד.
and thus each individual is elevated in a unique aspect.
וְהָיָה הַמִּנְיָן עַל פִּי מֹשֶׁה – דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה,
And the counting was conducted by Moses—the level of Wisdom,
וְאַהֲרֹן – דַּרְגָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה,
and Aaron—the level of Service;
וְהֵם לִכְאוֹרָה שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים,
which are seemingly two opposites,
וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּמְנוּ יַחַד כְּסֵדֶר אֶחָד?
and how could they count together in one single order?
וְכָל אֶחָד מָנָה כְּסֵדֶר תְּפִיסָתוֹ בְּמַעֲלַת וּמַדְרֵגַת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת,
For each counted according to his perspective on the stature of the souls,
וְנִמְצָא עֶלְיוֹנִים שֶׁל זֶה לְמַטָּה אֵצֶל זֶה.
so that those deemed highest by one were lowest to the other.
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שׁוּשְׁבִינָא דְּמַלְכָּא – הַיְינוּ דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ,
For Moses our teacher was the attendant of the King—namely the Holy One in His greatness,
שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי הַמַּעֲלָה וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה וְהוּא עָלָה לַמָּרוֹם;
which corresponds to virtue and holiness as he ascended on High;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַהֲרֹן שׁוּשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא
whereas Aaron was the attendant of the Queen,
לְיַפּוֹת כָּל מִינֵי חֶסְרוֹנוֹת
sent to elevate all deficiencies
וְלִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּבֵית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע,
bringing the Shechinah into the lower realms into the Holy of Holies reflecting the heart of Israel,
וְהַמַּעֲלָה לְעֶרְכּוֹ הוּא כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחִסָּרוֹן.
with stature in his assessment measured by the depth of deficiency.
וְכֵן הַמִּשְׁכָּן הוּא לְתִיקּוּן הָעֵגֶל,
And the Mishkan served to rectify the Golden Calf,
וַדַּאי כָּל מִי שֶׁהָיָה מַרְגִּישׁ חֶסְרוֹנוֹ וְחֶטְאוֹ יוֹתֵר, הִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּתִיקּוּנוֹ יוֹתֵר,
and whoever felt his sin more acutely exerted himself more in its rectification;
וְנִמְצָא חַיָּילִין דְּמַשְׁכְּנָא לְמַרְאֵה עַיִן מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ בְּהֵיפֶךְ הַסֵּדֶר מֵחַיָּילִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
so that the legions of the Mishkan appeared arranged in reverse order from the legions of the Torah.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת כּוּלָּא חַד,
Yet in truth all is one,
רַק שֶׁאֵצֶל כָּל אֶחָד הָיָה בְּלִיטָה בְּדָבָר מְיוּחָד,
with each person merely having a prominent quality in a specific area,
וּכְסֵדֶר אֶחָד פּוּקַּד עַל פִּי שְׁנֵיהֶם,
and in a single unified order they were numbered by both,

דְּ"כָל הַגָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי" (סֻכָּה נב371 Sukkah 52a — Abaye said: Had it been the one who hates me [meaning himself], he would not have been able to restrain himself. He went and leaned against the doorpost in distress. A certain elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his. Rashi (s.v. "had it been the one who hates me"): Had my enemy been alone with the woman, he could not have restrained himself from sinning; and he was speaking of himself. Rashi (s.v. "he leaned"): He leaned against the bolt of the door, like a man who is brooding and in distress. Rashi (s.v. "the way is long, and the company pleasant"): It is a long way between our two places, and we cannot go on together any further; had we been able to go by one road, our company would have been pleasant. Rashi (s.v. "when they were parting from one another"): They were from two towns, and when they reached a fork in the road he turned one way and she the other. Maharsha (on "for he has done greatly"): The verse concludes "for he has done greatly," meaning that he provokes the great more, as Abaye concludes. Alternatively, "he has done greatly" means that he has made himself great in relation to the righteous, [appearing to them] as a mountain, as was said above that at first he resembles a spider's thread and in the end cart-ropes; and "among Torah scholars more than all of them" is then a statement in its own right, as in the incident of Abaye. Maharsha (s.v. "the way is long"): It may also be explained as referring to the past: we have come a long way, but the company was pleasant, so that because of the company the way did not seem so long to us. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Koach HaYetzer 2): The evil inclination provokes the Torah scholar more than all, although he is complete, being a man of intellect: for the intellect a man possesses [in this world] is never in its completeness but is held with deficiency, so that the Torah scholar and Israel lack the completeness fitting for them, whereas other men and other nations, who have only the small level, cannot be called so deficient. Therefore the evil inclination provokes them more and more, and whoever has a higher level must guard himself against the evil inclination. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 48): After Israel received the Torah and reached a supreme level, the evil inclination provoked them to sin, in the manner of "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": because they had reached a supreme level that the rest of creation had not reached, the evil inclination, which is Satan, seeks to cast them down from their level. For privation clings more to a man who has a supreme level, one not fitting for every man, than it clings to the low level that is found in all. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 19): Just as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his" (and that elder, who was Elijah according to some commentators in Tosafos, a view I have received as primary, was revealed to Abaye through his anguish to tell him this and console him), so too, when someone's inclination is greater than his fellow's, this is a sign that he is also greater than him in the holy sparks within him, for God has made one opposite the other in each person, and the choice is in his hands. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 6): Such an abundance of light would bring great hardship to those who walk in the way of God, for the same reason as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": with a greater abundance of the light of the Blessed One, the evil in that same place grows stronger too, because so much light lies within it, for evil always surrounds the good. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Since the Blessed One does not deal tyrannically with His creatures, and even one created righteous must choose against an inclination that overpowers him daily, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his". Therefore the inclination appears to the righteous like a mountain, for its assault on them is enormous, matching the great power of good innate in them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 8): The Sages said that the evil inclination provokes Torah scholars more than all and that "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"; why should this be? The inclination is longing, and the purpose of its creation is to be the delight of Torah; so the one who is greater, in whom the delight of Torah is sunk more deeply, has, since "God has made the one opposite the other," a stronger desire toward the opposite as well, while one who does not magnify the delight of Torah in himself has no strong desire for the opposite either. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 2): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for the virtue is drawn together with the deficiency: as great and precious wealth needs more guarding than a small thing, being more liable to harm because more people strive after it, so in the soul, the greater its stature, that is, the more divine power it holds (and the will toward the opposite is also a divine power), the greater in it is this power of inclination as well, and it needs guarding. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for as the strength of the virtue, so is the strength of the deficiency, from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, where evil stands opposite the good and corresponds to it. Hence Dan, the lowest of the tribes in virtue, is lower in his deficiency as well, and the inclination is not as strong in him. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 134): When a person reaches a higher level, by the measure of that level he has not yet begun to repent, and his sin returns in full force; of this it is said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", for the sin is the deficiency in a person, and so is the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Where the strength of the virtue lies, there lies the strength of the deficiency, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": as is known, in Adam's sin the "man of Belial" ruled over the holy man limb for limb, God having made the one opposite the other, so that corresponding to the holiness of each limb and power is the dominion of the "man of Belial" in enticing to evil. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Mishlei 19): "The desire of a man is his kindness": the desire found in a person's heart is also a kindness from the Blessed One, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", and if he brings the power of his longing and desire into holiness, his stature grows all the more. Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 4): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for "God has made the one opposite the other": the power of good against the power of its opposite. Yet every person has the power of good to overcome his inclination, and through this he rises, gathering wealth in holiness little by little, which is the whole purpose of man's creation in this world. Sod Yesharim (Seventh Night of Pesach 16): The vessel [of longing] that a person attains in old age was already in him on the day he was born, only that each time he clarifies himself further, the vessel grows larger in him too, as the Sages said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"..);
for "whoever is greater has a greater inclination" (Sukkah 52a);
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה נִרְאֶה לָעַיִן עִנְיָנִים נִפְרָדִים וְנֶחְלְקוּ לְמוֹנִים נִפְרָדִים.
though to the physical eye they appeared as distinct matters requiring two separate counters.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה מוֹנֶה אֶחָד,
In contrast, in the future there will be a single counter;

דּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה "לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא וְכוּלֵי" (פְּסָחִים נ372 Pesachim 50a — "On that day the Lord shall be One and His name one." What is meant by "one"? Is His name then not one now? R. Nachman bar Yitzchak said: The World to Come is not like this world. In this world [the Name] is written with yod-heh and read with alef-dalet; but in the World to Come it is all one — read with yod-heh and written with yod-heh. Maharsha: "His name one": that is, the Unique Name, [used] in the World to Come in writing and in reading alike; the rest, he says, is explained in chapter Asarah Yuchasin. There (Kiddushin 71a) he explains that in this world the attribute of judgment rules in partnership with mercy, as at creation, so the Name is written as the name of mercy and read as the name of judgment — Adonai, a "remembrance," which denotes judgment; but the World to Come is entirely mercy, and then the Name will be complete, read as it is written. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 42): "On that day the Lord shall be One" does not, Heaven forbid, refer to Him in Himself, for He is ever One, but to the recipients: the beings of this world receive from Him both good and ill, and what they receive is not from the truth of His name. The writing of the Name indicates the truth of His essence, while the reading is directed toward man; in this world, where man is physical and a screen separates him from God, He is read as Adonai, "Master," for He stands to His world as a master to a servant, who is separate from him. But in the World to Come, when man will be at the level of the angels, removed from physicality, and He will stand joined and connected to His world as a son is joined to his father, He will be written and read alike with the Unique Name. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 2): Because in this world [the glory of Heaven] is not yet acquired in the heart, "in this world I am not read as I am written," and every blessing opens in direct address, "Blessed are You," and then turns to the hidden. The Name Havayah denotes true presence, as a son speaks face to face with his father, while Adonai, "Master of all," is hidden, as a servant is abashed to look at his master's face; when [this recognition] is acquired in the heart, with the complete redemption, He will be called by Havayah as well, but in this world that level is possible only "in writing" — potentially, not in actuality — so in practice one must stand in solemnity, like a servant before his master. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): He is not called by this Name because Israel cannot yet grasp in their hearts the joining of all four letters — the unity of mind, heart, faculties and completed deed, all for the Lord alone; this was revealed only to the High Priest in the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur, whereas for Israel at large in this world, "This is My name l'olam." Though it is written — Israel knows it through wisdom — it is not read in speech, which would bring this light out into actual revelation, for it will be revealed in actuality only in the future, when there will be no exile and no sin at all, sin arising from the concealment of this light. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): As regards this world, "This is My name l'olam" is written [defectively, to conceal], so that it is not read as it is written: the Name Havayah, which signifies the union of all the hidden powers with the revealed ones, all for the Lord alone, is concealed in this world, and though Scripture states explicitly that this is the truth, it is [held] by way of faith and concealment. In the future it will become clear that "Your people are all righteous" even in actual deed — that all our deeds too were for the sake of Heaven — and then it will be read as it is written; but in this world it is not read aloud as something clarified. Sod Yesharim (Night of Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 9): "On that day the Lord shall be One and His name One": seemingly it should have said "the Lord and His name shall be one," since His name pertains to the service of creation; but it is as the Gemara says: "Not as I am written am I read — I am written yod-heh and read alef-dalet, and in the World to Come I am read as I am written." In this world His being written yod-heh indicates that no thought can grasp Him at all, and when a person constrains himself to submit to this and accepts His mastery and lordship upon himself, that is His being read as Adonai; and "on that day," when the Blessed One reveals His great light, the lordship Israel accepted in this world will be their protection, for His name signifies Israel's service, through which they will never be nullified..),
for in this world "not as I am written am I pronounced" (Pesachim 50a),
דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה – הַיְינוּ מְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ,
for the Tetragrammaton represents the place of His greatness,
זֶה הוּא בִּכְתָב – הַיְינוּ מְפוֹרָשׁ לָעַיִן שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִיחַ הַמּוֹחַ;
which is written down, manifest to the eye which serves the intellect;
אֲבָל לֹא לַפֶּה שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִיחַ הַלֵּב,
yet not uttered by the mouth which serves the heart,
כִּי עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וּמָלֵא חֶסְרוֹנוֹת,
for the heart is deceitful and full of deficiencies,
וְהַהַרְגָּשָׁה מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן כְּעֶבֶד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
causing one to feel deficient like a servant before the King,
וְהַקְּרִיאָה בְּשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת.
and the oral pronunciation is through the Name of Adonut.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר זֶה לָעַיִן דִּמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ וְעַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ חַד,
In contrast, in the future it will be demonstrated that His greatness and humility are one,
שֶׁיָּשׁוּב הַסּוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל דַּרְגִּין,
the end of all levels returning to be the head of all levels,
כְּטַעַם "נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר",
mirroring "a woman shall encompass a man" (Jeremiah 31:21),
אָז יִהְיֶה נִקְרָא וְנִכְתָּב בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
and then He will be both written and pronounced with the Tetragrammaton,
דְּיִהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת זְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת כָּל מִינֵי חִסָּרוֹן מִלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי.
there being the slaughter of the inclination and total removal of every deficiency from the heart.

sections.en: Shabbat and the Surrender of Human Agency

items.h: Shabbat teaches that human labor is not autonomous; by ceasing from work, a person recognizes Hashem as the true source of every weekday action.

Seif 1 — Shabbat and the Illusion of Human Control
Ceasing labor on Shabbat reveals that Hashem, not human autonomy, is the true actor behind weekday work.

p: עִנְיַן עֲלִיַּת הָעוֹלָמוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עַד שֶׁבַּעֲשִׂיָּה אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא שֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת לְבַד וְלֹא הַשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,

The matter of the ascent of the worlds on Shabbat, to the extent that in the World of Asiyah (Action) there remain only the seven lower sefirot alone without the three supernal ones, as is known from the teaching of the holy Ari, of blessed memory,
הוּא בַּפָּשׁוּט כִּי עִנְיַן אִיסּוּר מְלָאכָה בְּשַׁבָּת: "כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת וְגוֹמֵר",
is simply because the rationale of the prohibition of creative labor on Shabbat—"because on it He rested, etc."—
הַיְינוּ דְּהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לָדַעַת בְּכָל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו וּמַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁלֹּא הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל,
is that a person must realize regarding all his actions and deeds that he himself is not the autonomous prime mover,
רַק הַכֹּל בְּכֹחַ עֶלְיוֹן וְכָל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
rather everything occurs through supernal power, all his actions deriving from Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּעִנְיַן "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ".
mirroring the verse (Isaiah 26:12): "for all our works You have also wrought for us."
וּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ לִפְעוֹל כְּלוּם,
And without this divine empowerment he has no capacity to accomplish anything whatsoever,
רַק עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
save through the operative creative power of Hashem, blessed be He,
הַנִּמְשָׁךְ בּוֹ מִכֹּחַ עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת דְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
channeled into him from the potency of the Ten Utterances of Creation,
שֶׁהֵם נִצָּבִים חַיִּים וְקַיָּימִים לְעוֹלָם,
which stand active, living, and enduring eternally,
כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה כָּל דָּבָר בְּיוֹמוֹ כְּפִי פְּעֻלַּת הַדְּבָרִים בִּימֵי בְרֵאשִׁית.
directing the forces of action—every matter upon its specific weekday in accordance with the works of the Six Days of Creation.
וְכָךְ כָּל פְּעֻלָּה הַשַּׁיָּיכֶת לְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם מַצְלַחַת בְּיוֹתֵר,
And thus every undertaking corresponding to that specific day is most successful;
עַיֵּין שִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת בְּ"מַזַּל יוֹם גּוֹרֵם".
see the end of Shabbat (156a) regarding the principle "the constellation of the day is the determining cause."
וּבֶאֱמֶת "ה' יִתֶּן אֹמֶר הַמְבַשְּׂרוֹת צָבָא רָב",
And in truth (Psalms 68:12): "Hashem gives the word; the women who publish the tidings are a great host,"
וְכָל נִיצוֹץ מִתְפַּשֵּׁט לְכַמָּה גְּוָונִין
and every supernal spark radiates into multifaceted dimensions,
עַד שֶׁכָּל מִינֵי פְּעֻלּוֹת נִמְשָׁכִים מִכֹּחַ אוֹתָהּ פְּעֻלָּה.
until all variations of action are drawn down through the potency of that initial divine deed.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, הַכֹּל מִכֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Yet nevertheless, everything originates from the operative creative power of Hashem, blessed be He;

וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲבֵירוֹת נֶאֱמַר: "בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" – אֲפִילּוּ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה (בְּרָכוֹת סג373 Berakhot 63a — Bar Kappara expounded: Which is the brief passage upon which all the essentials of the Torah depend? "In all your ways know Him, and He will make your paths straight." Rava said: Even for a matter of transgression. Rashi (s.v. "in all your ways"): "In all your ways" — even to commit a transgression. "Know Him" — give thought to whether it is required for a mitzvah, as with Elijah on Mount Carmel, and [if so] transgress it. Maharsha: He did not say "remember Him" but "know Him" — a true knowledge of His existence, and that He is able and watches over all your ways, to give good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked. And it concludes, "and He will make your paths straight," after the manner of what they said: in the way a man wishes to go, he is led, and one who comes to purify himself is assisted. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 34): As it is written, "In all your ways know Him," and the Sages said, "even for a matter of transgression" — then "He will straighten [your paths]." That is, one should give himself over to the Blessed One even to the point of losing his entire share in the World to Come when such is the will of the Blessed One — as I heard concerning the trial of the Binding — and then "He will straighten": the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself straightens you and separates the evil from you without toil. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 19): On "In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths," Rava said, "even for a matter of transgression," and the reading of Ein Yaakov is: "Rav Pappa said, this is what people say: the thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One." That is, even though he commits an explicit transgression of "You shall not steal," since he does not forget the Blessed One and believes in Him at the moment of the act, calling upon the Merciful One, of this it is said "and He will straighten your paths": the Blessed One will straighten his paths, so that "the banished one is not banished from Him," and he will have a rectification. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Beshalach): "Encamp opposite it by the sea": it is written, "In all your ways know Him" — even for a matter of transgression; and this is the meaning of "encamp opposite it": even though you perform deeds like those of the Egyptians, nevertheless the deeds of Israel are good, for the Israelite nation, the portion of the Blessed One, cleaves to simple life without any garment and draws from that source of life alone. All these powers, when among Israel, are full of holiness even though they resemble those of Egypt, for the Blessed One testifies about them that in the heart of Israel there is nothing but love of the Blessed One. Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Berakhos 7): [By placing "I am" before "You shall have no other gods," the Blessed One showed that] even one who has, Heaven forbid, stumbled in a deed that is not good is not barred from repentance and can perform mitzvos though he is not yet cleansed of "turning from evil." This is what the dictum "In all your ways know Him," on which all the essentials of the Torah depend, teaches; and as Rava concludes, "even for a matter of transgression" — that is, a person should not despair after stumbling in sin, for repentance is never withheld from him..),
and even concerning transgressions it was stated: "'In all your ways acknowledge Him'—even regarding a matter of transgression" (Berakhot 63a),
וְאַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה דִּ"זְדוֹנוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת", אַף הוּא מִפְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and following total repentance out of love whereby "willful sins become transformed into merits," that too is seen to stem from the ultimate operation of Hashem,
רַק הוּא כְּעִנְיַן דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּוֵּין אוֹ מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ;
only that it resembles an unintentional consequence or an action not required for its intrinsic purpose;
וּ"זְדוֹנוֹת כִּשְׁגָגוֹת" הַיְינוּ כְּמִתְעַסֵּק בְּעָלְמָא.
whereas the level where "willful sins become like unintentional errors" resembles one who acted with mere casual detachment (mit'asek).
וּבְשַׁבָּת, דְּאֵין כֹּחַ פְּעֻלָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם כְּלָל שֶׁ"בּוֹ שָׁבַת וְכוּלֵי",
And on Shabbat, when no operative creative power of Hashem operates in that day at all, "for on it He rested, etc.",
הָעוֹשֶׂה בוֹ מְלָאכָה הֲרֵי זֶה דּוֹמֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְקוֹצֵץ בִּנְטִיעוֹת,
whoever performs creative labor upon it is comparable, Heaven forbid, to one who uproots saplings;

דְּאָמְרוּ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (סוֹף תִּיקּוּן סט סוֹף דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "קָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְאָמַר וַתּוֹסֶף לָלֶדֶת וְגוֹמֵר374 Tikkunei Zohar 117b — The essence of the four letters and of the ten letters [of the Name] is Malkhut, which is comprised of all ten sefirot, and in it everything must be included; for whoever takes Malkhut without the nine sefirot cuts among the plantings, and whoever takes the nine sefirot without Malkhut denies the fundamental principle."):
as stated in the Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 69):
דְּהַיְינוּ מַאן דְּנָטַל מַלְכוּת בְּלָא תְּשַׁע סְפִירוֹת,
namely, one who takes Malchut (action) without the preceding nine sefirot;
פֵּירוּשׁ: כֹּחַ פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם בְּלֹא הַכָּרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל,
the explanation being: presuming human action operates without recognizing that Hashem is the true Prime Mover,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּשַׁבָּת,
which is completely impossible on Shabbat,
וְעַל כֵּן אָז חוֹשֵׁב דְּהוּא הַפּוֹעֵל בְּכֹחוֹ וְעֹצֶם יָדוֹ וְזֶה כְּפִירָה;
