and therefore he presumes at that moment that he acts via his own independent might and the strength of his hand, which is heresy;

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין סט375 Eruvin 69a-b — Rav Huna said: Who is an Israelite apostate? One who desecrates the Sabbath in public. Rav Nachman said to him: In accordance with whose opinion? If in accordance with R. Meir, who said that one suspect in a single matter is suspect with regard to the entire Torah, then any one of the prohibitions of the Torah should equally [make him an apostate]; and if in accordance with the Rabbis, who said that one suspect in a single matter is not suspect with regard to the entire Torah, [he is not one] until he is an apostate with regard to idolatry. Rav Ashi said: This tanna holds that the Sabbath is as grave for him as idolatry — hence idolatry and the Sabbath are equivalent to one another. Rashi (s.v. "Rav Ashi said"): In fact, the apostate of whom Rav Huna spoke is regarded as an apostate in every respect, and Rav Huna holds like the Rabbis; it is this tanna who holds the Sabbath to be as weighty as idolatry. Rashi (s.v. "except for one who is an apostate to pour libations or to desecrate the Sabbath"): For he is like an apostate to the entire Torah, who is excluded by [the verse's] "of you" — and not all of you. Rashi (s.v. "until he is an apostate with regard to idolatry"): For such a one is certainly suspect in every matter, as the master said: idolatry is so grave that whoever acknowledges it is as one who denies the entire Torah, as it is written, "And if you err and do not perform all these commandments" — and that verse speaks of idolatry. Rashi (s.v. "who is an Israelite apostate"): That is, one whom we regard as an apostate in every respect. Tosafos (s.v. "if in accordance with R. Meir"): So it is taught explicitly in Bekhorot: one suspected in a single matter is suspected regarding the entire Torah — the words of R. Meir. Tosafot note the difficulty that in Sanhedrin the Gemara implies that, according to Rava, R. Meir said this only of a plotting witness in monetary cases, whose offense is wrong both toward Heaven and toward people; and they answer that even according to Rava, one suspected in a matter that is wrong toward Heaven but not toward people is suspect regarding the entire Torah in matters of that same kind, even from a lighter prohibition to a graver one. Maharsha (Chidushei Halachot, Eruvin 69a): What is said in this sugya, that R. Meir holds that one suspect in a single matter is suspect regarding the entire Torah, applies to Torah prohibitions, but not to rabbinic ones such as carrying without an eruv. Alternatively, even though such a person is called suspect regarding the entire Torah, he is nevertheless not an apostate, and he may renounce his domain like any Israelite.:): מוּמָר לְחַלֵּל שַׁבָּתוֹת – מוּמָר לְכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ.
and therefore they taught (Eruvin 69b): an apostate regarding Sabbath desecration is an apostate regarding the entire Torah.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, וַדַּאי אִם לֹא הָיָה כֹּחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לַנִּבְרָא לִפְעוֹל כְּלוּם,
And nonetheless, certainly without divine empowerment from Hashem, it would be impossible for any created being to act at all,
וְאָנוּ רוֹאִים עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְרִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל פּוֹעֲלִים בְּשַׁבָּת;
and yet we see idolaters and the wicked of Israel executing labor on Shabbat;
רַק דִּבְשַׁבָּת "מְלֶאכֶת מַחֲשֶׁבֶת אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה",
only that regarding Shabbat, "the Torah prohibited intentional, constructive craft (melekhet machashevet),"
דְּהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא בִּרְצוֹן הָעוֹשֶׂה, וּבִרְצוֹן אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹעֵל כְּלוּם.
meaning that which is conducted through the conscious desire of the actor, whereas through direct will Hashem initiates no worldly work on Shabbat.
אֲבָל פְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁנֶּגֶד רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם נִמְשָׁכִים דֶּרֶךְ אֲחוֹרַיִים,
However, actions running contrary to His revealed will are drawn down through the indirect, posterior channels (achorayim),
וְהֵם דּוּגְמַת דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין וּמְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ,
resembling unintentional acts and labor not needed for its own intrinsic purpose,
כְּמוֹ מוֹצִיא כִּלְאַחַר יָדוֹ שֶׁמּוּתָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה;
like carrying out in an awkward, backhanded manner (ki-le'achar yado), which is biblically permitted;
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁכֹּחַ פְּעֻלַּת נִבְרָאִים בְּשַׁבָּת הוּא פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה;
meaning from the perspective of Hashem, the active agency of creatures on Shabbat reflects His divine workings in this indirect mode;
וְאָסוּר מִדְּרַבָּנָן, דַּחֲכָמִים הֵם הוֹסִיפוּ בֵּירוּרִים לוֹמַר דִּפְעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשַׁבָּת הַיְינוּ מִתְעַסֵּק בְּעָלְמָא, וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי.
yet rabbinically prohibited, for the Sages added safeguards to indicate that Hashem's operation on Shabbat is merely akin to a detached actor (mit'asek), which aligns with what I wrote.
אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה וְגוֹמֵר",
However, regarding the World to Come, "eye has not seen, etc.",
וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת,
and the World to Come is an eternal day that is entirely Shabbat,
וְהָעֵסֶק שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ עִם הַנִּבְרָאִים אֵינוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגַת בְּרִיָּה;
and Hashem's engagement in it with creations is completely beyond the comprehension of any creature;
רַק מִצַּד הַתְּפִיסָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּחָכְמָה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה דְּאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשׁוּם פְּעֻלָּה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שָׁם,
only that from the vantage point of perception in this world with mortal wisdom, it appears that no action or striving could apply there,
גַּם בִּמְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין,
even regarding labor not needed for its own sake or unintentional acts;
מֵאַחַר דְּאָז יִהְיֶה "ה' אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד" בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר, אִם כֵּן מַה מָּקוֹם לִפְעֻלָּה וּמַעֲשֶׂה?
for since at that time "Hashem shall be One and His Name One" in absolute unity, what possible room remains for human action and deed?
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר: רַק מְלֶאכֶת מַחֲשֶׁבֶת אָסוּר,
Nevertheless Hashem declares: solely intentional craft is prohibited,
דְּזוּלַת זֶה יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת פְּעֻלָּה;
implying that outside of this conscious craft there remains a place for spiritual action;
וְזֶה אֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג לְשֵׂכֶל חֲכָמִים כְּלָל,
and this is not graspable by the intellect of the Sages at all,
דְּ"עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה וְגוֹמֵר" הַיְינוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג אֶפְשָׁרוּת זֶה כְּלָל,
for "eye has not seen, etc." means it is impossible to conceptualize this potentiality,
וּלְכָךְ הֵם הֶחְמִירוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין וּמְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ.
and therefore they instituted stringencies regarding unintentional acts and labor not needed for its own purpose.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם פָּטוּר מִמִּיתָה,
And nonetheless one is biblically exempt from execution for such acts,
דְּגוּף וָנֶפֶשׁ הַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for body and soul mirror the divine union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as is known;
וְאִיסּוּר תּוֹרָה הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and biblical prohibition derives from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאִיסּוּרִין דְּרַבָּנָן הוּא מִצַּד כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וּשְׁכִינַת עֻזּוֹ שֶׁהוֹפִיעָה בְּלֵב חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
while rabbinic prohibitions stem from the Congregation of Israel and His Shechinah radiating within the hearts of the Sages of Israel;
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַגּוּף, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָדוּן בּוֹ עַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
and that operates from the perspective of the body, making it impossible to pass judgment of spiritual execution upon the soul.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת לַגּוּף,
And in the World to Come, where bodily limitation will have no hold,

אָז "כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב אֲנִי נִקְרָא" (פְּסָחִים נ376 Pesachim 50a — R. Nachman bar Yitzchak said: The World to Come is not like this world. In this world [the Name] is written with yod-heh and read with alef-dalet; but in the World to Come it is all one — read with yod-heh and written with yod-heh. Rashi: It is written "This is My name le'alem" — in concealment — and it is written "This is My memorial," which implies reading aloud and not concealment. Alternatively: once it says "This is My name," it is obvious that "this is My memorial" — how else would He be called but by His name? "I am not read as I am written": [the verse] taught two names, the name of writing and the name of reading. Maharsha: "His name one" means the Unique Name, [used] in the World to Come in writing and in reading alike; the rest, he says, is explained in chapter Asarah Yuchasin. There (Kiddushin 71a) he explains that in this world the attribute of judgment rules in partnership with mercy, as at creation, so the Name is written as the name of mercy and read as the name of judgment — Adonai, a "remembrance," which denotes judgment; but the World to Come is entirely mercy, and then the Name will be complete, read as it is written. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 42): He, blessed be He, is ever One in Himself; the difference lies with the recipients, for this world is not conducted according to the truth of His name. The writing of the Name indicates the truth of His essence, while the reading is directed toward man; in this world, where man is physical and material and a screen separates him from God, He is read as Adonai, "Master," for He stands to His world as a master to a servant, who is separate from him. But in the World to Come, when man will be at the level of the angels, removed from physicality, and He will stand joined and connected to His world as a son is joined to his father, He will be written and read alike with the Unique Name. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 15): [Explaining why one who pronounces the Name with its letters has no share in the World to Come:] It is fitting to conceal this Name, the Unique Name, as the Sages expounded "This is My name le'olam" — le'alem ["to conceal"] is written — for the Unique Name has a hidden and concealed level. One who pronounces the Name with its letters departs from that hidden and concealed level, and so has no share in the World to Come, which is itself of a hidden and concealed level. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 2): Because in this world [the glory of Heaven] is not yet acquired in the heart, "in this world I am not read as I am written," and every blessing opens in direct address, "Blessed are You," and then turns to the hidden. The Name Havayah denotes true presence, as a son speaks face to face with his father, while Adonai, "Master of all," is hidden, as a servant is abashed to look at his master's face; when [this recognition] is acquired in the heart, with the complete redemption, He will be called by Havayah as well, but in this world that level is possible only "in writing" — potentially, not in actuality — so in practice one must stand in solemnity, like a servant before his master. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): He is not called by this Name because Israel cannot yet grasp in their hearts the joining of all four letters — the unity of mind, heart, faculties and completed deed, all for the Lord alone; this was revealed only to the High Priest in the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur, whereas for Israel at large in this world, "This is My name l'olam." Though it is written — Israel knows it through wisdom — it is not read in speech, which would bring this light out into actual revelation, for it will be revealed in actuality only in the future, when there will be no exile and no sin at all, sin arising from the concealment of this light. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): As regards this world, "This is My name l'olam" is written [defectively, to conceal], so that it is not read as it is written: the Name Havayah, which signifies the union of all the hidden powers with the revealed ones, all for the Lord alone, is concealed in this world, and though Scripture states explicitly that this is the truth, it is [held] by way of faith and concealment. In the future it will become clear that "Your people are all righteous" even in actual deed — that all our deeds too were for the sake of Heaven — and then it will be read as it is written; but in this world it is not read aloud as something clarified. Sod Yesharim (Night of Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 9): "On that day the Lord shall be One and His name One": seemingly it should have said "the Lord and His name shall be one," since His name pertains to the service of creation; but it is as the Gemara says: "Not as I am written am I read — I am written yod-heh and read alef-dalet, and in the World to Come I am read as I am written." In this world His being written yod-heh indicates that no thought can grasp Him at all, and when a person constrains himself to submit to this and accepts His mastery and lordship upon himself, that is His being read as Adonai; and "on that day," when the Blessed One reveals His great light, the lordship Israel accepted in this world will be their protection, for His name signifies Israel's service, through which they will never be nullified..),
then "as I am written, so am I pronounced" (Pesachim 50a),
דְּשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת הָרוֹמֵז לַשְּׁכִינָה לֹא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ אָז;
for the Name of Adonut (Mastership) alluding to the Shechinah will not be utilized then;
וּמִשֵּׁם זֶה הוּא כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה וַעֲבוֹדַת עֶבֶד שֶׁהוּא בַּגּוּף דִּבַעֲשִׂיָּה,
and from that Name derives the faculty of physical action and the labor of a servant which resides in the bodily World of Asiyah;
וְאָז יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת.
and then will be an eternal day that is entirely Shabbat.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יִהְיֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת לְכָל הַתּוֹרָה וְגַם כָּל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים יִהְיוּ קַיָּימִים,
And nevertheless connection to the entire Torah will remain, and all words of the Sages will endure,
דְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה הִיא מִסֵּדֶר הַבְּרִיאָה לֹא יִתְבַּטֵּל,
for the World of Asiyah is part of the divine order of Creation and will not be annihilated;
רַק יִהְיֶה עֲלִיַּת עוֹלָמוֹת;
rather, an elevation of worlds will occur;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת בְּלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת –
meaning seven lower sefirot without the three supernal ones—
פֵּירוּשׁ: כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה וְהַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהָרָצוֹן,
meaning: faculties of practical action stripped of the three supernal ones which represent thought and conscious intention,
דְּהַיְינוּ מְלֶאכֶת מַחֲשֶׁבֶת אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר.
signifying that intentional, designing craft was prohibited by the Torah, as mentioned.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּעָשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר וּבַיּוֹם וְגוֹמֵר",
Therefore Scripture states (Exodus 35:2): "Six days shall work be done (te'aseh)... and on the day, etc.",
אָמַר "תֵּעָשֶׂה" הַתָּי״ו צְרוּיָה,
saying te'aseh with the letter Tav punctuated with a tzere,
דְּנִדְרָשׁ בְּכָל מָקוֹם בְּכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא שֶׁמֵּעַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית;
which is expounded in every such instance to indicate that work is done on its own;
הַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר עַצְמוֹ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת,
meaning that through the holiness of Shabbat wherein a person refrains from work,
זֶה מֵעִיד עַל עַצְמוֹ דְּכָל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
he bears witness concerning himself that all his actions derive from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְשֶׁהֵם נַעֲשִׂים מֵעַצְמָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּכֹחוֹ וְעֹצֶם יָדוֹ כְּלָל,
and that they unfold as though by themselves without his own independent power or the might of his hand,

כְּטַעַם "וְזֶה יִכְתֹּב יָדוֹ לַה377 Isaiah 44:5 — “One shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Yaakov; and another shall subscribe with his hand to the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel.” Rashi: "This one will say, I am the Lord's" — these are the wholly righteous; "and this one will call himself by the name of Jacob" — these are the young children of the wicked. "This one will inscribe his hand to the Lord" — these are the penitents; "and by the name of Israel he will call himself" — these are the converts from among the idolaters. So it is taught in Avot de-Rabbi Nathan [36:1]. Radak: Those who remain in Israel will all be holy, and all will be called as belonging to the Lord and as of the seed of Jacob, as it is said, "He that is left in Zion and he that remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy" [Isaiah 4:3]. "He will inscribe his hand to the Lord" — he will say it with his mouth and write it with his hand, that he belongs to the Lord; and "he will call himself" — he will name himself by the name of Israel, not mentioning his own name but saying, "I am an Israelite." Metzudas Dovid: The righteous among them will say that they have always belonged to the Lord and believed in Him; the young children of the wicked will not incline after their wicked fathers' opinion but will call themselves by the name of Jacob, to be righteous as he was. The penitents will bind themselves to return to the Lord like a man who binds himself by his own signature; and those who call themselves by the name of Israel are the converts who will be added to them. Malbim: The divine abundance and the knowledge of God will so increase that the degrees within that knowledge will be many. One will say, "I am the Lord's" — gentiles who come to recognize God and, though they do not take on His Torah, declare that they belong to the Lord and not to a foreign god; another will call himself by the name of Jacob — the mass of the people of Jacob's seed, who keep their lineage so as to guard their fathers' faith; and another will inscribe his hand to the Lord — the righteous who walk before God continually, giving themselves over like one who writes himself a bond of service, and such a man is called by the name of Israel, for he is governed above nature.'",
mirroring (Isaiah 44:5): "and another shall subscribe with his hand unto Hashem,"

שֶׁהוּא כִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא קַמָּא פה378 Bava Kamma 85a — Rather, we assess how much a man would be willing to take to have his hand — a hand already made over in writing to the government [for amputation] — severed with a sword rather than with a drug. They said: here too, he would not take money and bring pain upon himself. Rather, we assess how much a man would be willing to give to have his hand, already made over in writing to the government, severed with a drug rather than with a sword. Rashi: "Between a drug and a sword" — how much would he be willing to take to have his hand, already made over in writing to the king, severed with a sword, when it might be severed with a drug and with no pain at all. "He would not take" — no money in the world would he take to bring pain upon himself by having it cut off; and here the deed has already been done. "How much a man would be willing to give" — to the king's agent, who is to sever his hand, already made over to the government, with a sword, so that the agent will sever it with a drug instead..): "יָדוֹ כְּתוּבָה לַמַּלְכוּת",
which parallels the Talmudic idiom (Bava Kamma 85a): "his hand is inscribed unto the government,"
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכֹחַ יָדוֹ וּפְעֻלָּתוֹ בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning that the strength of his hand and his deeds are placed in the hand of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁאָמַר בִּפְסוּק "זָכוֹר" גַּם כֵּן: "שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תַּעֲבֹד וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is the rationale why in the verse of 'Remember' (Exodus 20:9) it is likewise stated: "Six days you shall labor, etc.",
דְּעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת דַּוְוקָא הוּא שֶׁהוּתְּרָה מְלֶאכֶת שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים,
for specifically through Sabbath observance is the work of the six weekdays permitted,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין הוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה וְהַפּוֹעֵל כְּלָל.
since he understands that he is not the autonomous creator or prime mover whatsoever.

sections.en: Jacob's Eternal Promise and the Seven Blessings

items.h: Hashem's promise to Jacob extends to every Jew, with seven blessings mapping the soul's journey from inherited holiness through repentance and renewed closeness.

Seif 1 — The Eternal Promise to Jacob
Hashem's promise to Jacob remains active in every Jew, guiding the heart toward eventual complete repentance.

p: הַבְטָחַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
The promise of Hashem, blessed be He, unto our father Jacob, peace be upon him:

"הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵךְ379 Genesis 28:13-15 — “And behold, the Lord stood over him and said: I am the Lord, God of Avraham your father and God of Yitzchak. The land on which you lie, to you will I give it and to your seed. And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south; and through you shall all the families of the earth be blessed, and through your seed. And behold, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not forsake you until I have done what I have spoken of to you.” Rashi: "Standing over him" — to guard him. "The land upon which you lie": the Holy One, blessed be He, folded the whole Land of Israel beneath him, intimating to him that it would be as easy for his descendants to conquer as the four cubits a man occupies when he lies down. "I am with you" was said to him because he was afraid of Esau and of Laban. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 1): Already when Jacob left his father, at sixty-three, the Holy One, blessed be He, promised him "and you shall spread out…," and this came through His promise "I am with you and will guard you wherever you go": he was promised that He would guard him from all evil and he would not stray after the evil inclination, and through this, as a matter of course, "you shall spread out." For victory over the evil inclination is also victory over the nations, since each nation has its own particular evil power, and together they make up all the powers of evil of the evil inclination. Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 39): "And behold, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go, and I will bring you back": this is the blessing with which He blessed him, a blessing for exile — for "Anochi" ["I"] includes "I" and "He," the upper world and the lower world, [meaning] that man too can act through his service, as the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "You should have helped Me"; that is, the Blessed One desires and gives room for man's service and deeds, that man should serve Him and bless Him. "And I will bring you back to the land" — that is, I will bring this into holiness through it.",
"'Behold, I am with you, and will keep you wherever you go' (Genesis 28:15),"
לֹא הָיְתָה הַבְטָחַת שָׁעָה,
was not merely a temporary promise for that moment,
רַק הַבְטָחָה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד לְכָל אֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנֶּה,
rather an eternal promise for all time unto everyone who is designated by the name of Jacob and Israel;
שֶׁהֵם נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא
in that they are called after the name of the primordial ancestor Israel (Yisrael Sava),
לֹא דֶּרֶךְ כִּינּוּי הַשֵּׁם לְבַד,
not by way of an external titular appellation alone,
רַק הֵם בֶּאֱמֶת כְּעֶצֶם מֵעַצְמוֹ וּבָשָׂר מִבְּשָׂרוֹ.
rather they are in ultimate truth like bone of his bone and flesh of his flesh.
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For the essential soul-root of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.
encompasses all the souls of Israel throughout all the generations.
וְרַק בְּנַפְשׁוֹת הַגֵּרִים נֶאֱמַר: "שֶׁבְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנּוּ" –
And only regarding the souls of converts is it stated (Isaiah 44:5): "and surname himself by the name of Israel"—
לְשׁוֹן כִּינּוּי וְלֹא שֵׁם הָעֶצֶם.
being phrasing of an earned title, rather than an essential name.
אֲבָל בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא שֵׁם הָעֶצֶם מַמָּשׁ,
However, among the native children of Israel, it is the actual substantive name itself,
דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא מֵת,
for our father Jacob, peace be upon him, never died,

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה380 Taanit 5b — R. Yochanan said: Yaakov our father did not die. He said to him: Was it then for nothing that they eulogized him and embalmed him and buried him? He said to him: I expound a verse — “And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov, says the Lord, and be not dismayed, O Israel, for behold I save you from afar and your seed from the land of their captivity.” Scripture likens him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive. Rashi: "Did not die": rather, he lives forever. "For nothing": was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized and the embalmers embalmed, as it is written of him, "and they embalmed … and they eulogized" (Genesis 50)? "Just as his seed is alive": when He gathers Israel from the land of their captivity, it is the living He gathers, for they are in captivity, and the dead are not in captivity; "so too is he alive": for He will bring him into the exile so as to redeem his children before his eyes, as we find in Egypt — "And Israel saw" (Exodus 14:31), expounded as Israel the Elder; and as for the embalming, it seemed to them that he had died, but he was alive. Tosafos (s.v. "Yaakov our father did not die"): So too it is implied by Scripture, for it is written of him "and he expired" and not "and he died," as is explained in Sotah (13a) in connection with the episode of Chushim. Maharsha: [The questioner] did not object from Scripture's mention of his death, for death is not stated of him, only "and he expired," as Tosafot write; and Rashi's explanation, that it only seemed to the embalmers that he had died, is forced, the crux of the answer being missing from the text. I have heard it explained that "Yaakov did not die" can mean either that he did not die even in body, or that he did not die in soul, like other righteous men, though in body he died: the questioner took it in the first sense and objected from the eulogies and the embalming, and the answer is that it was meant of the soul — and Yaakov is singled out because only he can be likened to his seed, unlike Avraham and Yitzchak, whose seed included Yishmael and Esav. Alternatively: the dead outside the Land do not live [as those within it], for the Land of Israel is called "the land of the living," so Avraham and Yitzchak, who died in the Land, are alive even in death, while one might argue that Yaakov, who died abroad, is not; hence he taught that Yaakov too is alive, as though he had died in the Land, deriving it from "I save you from afar" — that is, from Egypt, alive, as though he had died in the Land. Maharal (Derech Chaim 5:4): One might ask: Yaakov's good, which signifies the end of Israel, ought to have been very great, yet at the end Yaakov's good was but slight, unlike the destiny of Israel, which is to be eternal. For this reason they said, "Yaakov our father did not die": he abides in an eternal good that will never be removed, signifying that the good of Israel will be eternal. And since the World to Come will be wholly spiritual, this is what the Sages' saying that Yaakov did not die signifies — for without doubt Yaakov's life now is spiritual, not like this life, which is natural. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 50): Whatever ceases has an end; but where there are three, the middle one between them has no end at all, and what has no end does not cease. So it is with what they said in Taanit, "Yaakov our father did not die": this is because he was the third of the patriarchs, and the third is not bounded by an end; therefore he is alive and did not receive an end. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 3): The tribes are the whole of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in whom the very essence of Yaakov's soul spreads forth; to this they alluded with "just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive" — that is, the totality of the souls of Israel in each generation is itself the stature of Yaakov's soul as it spreads forth in that generation. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Motzei Yom Kippur 4): The abiding of the Torah of truth in the heart was realized chiefly in Yaakov, because he was the root of the life of holiness, as the Sages said, "Yaakov our father did not die"; through this one can be purified even from the impurity of the dead, cleaving to the root of the life of holiness and entering the camp of the Shechinah. Even though this is not perceptible in this world, Yaakov's own aspect is not perceptible in this world either, as the Gemara says, "Was it for nothing that they embalmed him?" until he answered, "I expound a verse … just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): Yaakov our father is the complete man who was in this world, whose bed was whole and who did not die, for "just as his seed is alive…," as they said: that is, the stature of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in each and every generation is itself the stature of Yaakov our father, only particularized and divided into many individual souls. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Anthology, Isaiah 26; from Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 3): Every one of the seed of Israel will be shown, at the resurrection of the dead, not to have died but to have been as one asleep, as the Gemara expounds, "He likens him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." And there is no half-analogy: as He likens Yaakov to his seed, so He likens his seed to him, so that all the seed of Yaakov will be clarified at the level of "Yaakov did not die," and when one awakens from his sleep he will remember all the words of Torah. (תַּעֲנִית ה:):
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Ta'anit 5b):
"מַקִּישׁ הוּא לְזַרְעוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
"Scripture likens him to his seed, etc.,"
פֵּירוּשׁ דְּזֶהוּ חַיּוּתוֹ עַל יְדֵי זַרְעוֹ.
meaning that this is his living vitality—manifested through his offspring.

וְזֶהוּ הַתֵּירוּץ עַל "וְכִי בִּכְדִי חָנְטוּ חָנְטַיָּא וְכוּלֵי" (שָׁם381 Taanit 5b — R. Yochanan said: Yaakov our father did not die. He said to him: Was it then for nothing that they eulogized him and embalmed him and buried him? I have heard it explained that "Yaakov did not die" can mean either that he did not die even in body, or that he did not die in soul, like other righteous men, though in body he died: the questioner took it in the first sense and objected from the eulogies and the embalming, and the answer is that it was meant of the soul — and Yaakov is singled out because only he can be likened to his seed, unlike Avraham and Yitzchak, whose seed included Yishmael and Esav. Alternatively: the dead outside the Land do not live [as those within it], for the Land of Israel is called "the land of the living," so Avraham and Yitzchak, who died in the Land, are alive even in death, while one might argue that Yaakov, who died abroad, is not; hence he taught that Yaakov too is alive, as though he had died in the Land, deriving it from "I save you from afar" — that is, from Egypt, alive, as though he had died in the Land. Maharal (Derech Chaim 5:4): One might ask: Yaakov's good, which signifies the end of Israel, ought to have been very great, yet at the end Yaakov's good was but slight, unlike the destiny of Israel, which is to be eternal. For this reason they said, "Yaakov our father did not die": he abides in an eternal good that will never be removed, signifying that the good of Israel will be eternal. And since the World to Come will be wholly spiritual, this is what the Sages' saying that Yaakov did not die signifies — for without doubt Yaakov's life now is spiritual, not like this life, which is natural. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 50): Whatever ceases has an end; but where there are three, the middle one between them has no end at all, and what has no end does not cease. So it is with what they said in Taanit, "Yaakov our father did not die": this is because he was the third of the patriarchs, and the third is not bounded by an end; therefore he is alive and did not receive an end. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 3): The tribes are the whole of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in whom the very essence of Yaakov's soul spreads forth; to this they alluded with "just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive" — that is, the totality of the souls of Israel in each generation is itself the stature of Yaakov's soul as it spreads forth in that generation. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Motzei Yom Kippur 4): The abiding of the Torah of truth in the heart was realized chiefly in Yaakov, because he was the root of the life of holiness, as the Sages said, "Yaakov our father did not die"; through this one can be purified even from the impurity of the dead, cleaving to the root of the life of holiness and entering the camp of the Shechinah. Even though this is not perceptible in this world, Yaakov's own aspect is not perceptible in this world either, as the Gemara says, "Was it for nothing that they embalmed him?" until he answered, "I expound a verse … just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): Yaakov our father is the complete man who was in this world, whose bed was whole and who did not die, for "just as his seed is alive…," as they said: that is, the stature of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in each and every generation is itself the stature of Yaakov our father, only particularized and divided into many individual souls. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Anthology, Isaiah 26; from Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 3): Every one of the seed of Israel will be shown, at the resurrection of the dead, not to have died but to have been as one asleep, as the Gemara expounds, "He likens him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." And there is no half-analogy: as He likens Yaakov to his seed, so He likens his seed to him, so that all the seed of Yaakov will be clarified at the level of "Yaakov did not die," and when one awakens from his sleep he will remember all the words of Torah.),
And this resolves the Talmudic challenge: "Was it for naught that the embalmers embalmed him, etc.?" (there),
דִּלְכָאוֹרָה לֹא מְשַׁנֵּי כְּלוּם;
which seemingly changes nothing;
רַק הַכַּוָּנָה דְּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא מֵת,
rather the intention is that the reason he did not die
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי חַיּוּת זַרְעוֹ,
is through the living vitality of his seed,
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בָּהֶם,
which is literally the primal root of his own vitality expanding through them,
וַהֲרֵי עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא עַצְמוֹ לֹא מֵת;
and behold, through this, he himself did not die;
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ חַי וְקַיָּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּגּוּף
and the root of his soul is living and enduring in this world within physical bodies
בִּכְלָלוּת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר,
among the totality of the souls of Israel in that generation,
שֶׁכְּלָלוּתָם אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְבַד,
whose collective sum is nothing other than the soul of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, alone,
הַמִּתְחַלֶּקֶת לְשִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נִיצוֹצוֹת,
which subdivides into 600,000 sparks,

דְּאֵין דּוֹר פָּחוֹת מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רעג עַמּוּד א382 Zohar 3:273a — From the moment you [Moses] were gathered from the world, you are like the sun that shines in every generation: for when the sun is gathered in at night, it shines in the moon and in six hundred thousand stars. So are you, who shine in six hundred thousand in every generation. And this is what Kohelet hinted at, "A generation goes and a generation comes" (Ecclesiastes 1:4); and the Sages explained: no generation has fewer than six hundred thousand. And they further explained: the generation that goes is the one that comes, to fulfill "That which was is that which shall be." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:131): They said, "No generation has fewer than six hundred thousand," because the Torah is the root of the world, and it is known that the six hundred thousand letters of the Torah are the root of the six hundred thousand souls of Israel; necessarily it is so in every generation, since the existence of the whole world in every generation is only by virtue of the Torah.).
for no generation has fewer than 600,000 souls (Zohar Part III, 273a).
וְהֵם מִכְּלַל קוֹמַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
And they constitute the full spiritual stature of our father Jacob, peace be upon him:
יֵשׁ רָאשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעֵינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּשְׁאָר אֵיבָרִים.
there are the heads of Israel, the eyes of Israel, and the other bodily limbs.
וְצוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
And the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, is engraved upon the Throne of Glory

(מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה בַּמִּדְבָּר רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ד383 Bamidbar Rabbah 4:1 — "Since you were precious in My eyes, you were honored" (Isaiah 43:4). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Jacob: Jacob, you are exceedingly precious in My eyes, for, as it were, I have fixed your image upon My throne, and by your name the angels praise Me and say, "Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel, from eternity to eternity" (Psalms 41:14). Hence, "since you were precious in My eyes, you were honored."),
(Midrash Rabbah, Bamidbar, beginning of Parashah 4),
הַיְינוּ כְּפִי צוּרָתוֹ בְּכָל דּוֹר כָּךְ הוּא חֲקוּקָה,
meaning according to his collective stature in each specific generation, so is it engraved,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּנְשָׁמָתִין אִתְגְּזָרוּן מִכֻּרְסְיָא;
as is known that souls are hewn directly from the celestial Throne;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לְפַרְסֵם כְּבוֹדוֹ,
for Hashem, blessed be He, desired to broadcast and magnify His glory,
וּפִרְסוּם כָּבוֹד אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ הֶעְלֵם.
and the publication of glory occurs only where prior concealment exists.
וְזֶהוּ בִּבְרוּאֵי מַטָּה,
And this takes place within earthly creatures below;
וּלְכָךְ בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּגוּפוֹת
and therefore Hashem created human beings within physical bodies
מְלֵאִים מִכָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת וַחֲמָדוֹת שֶׁבְּהֵיפֶךְ מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
filled with all varieties of lusts and desires that run contrary to the will of Hashem, blessed be He,

וְ"כָל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ" (סֻכָּה נב384 Sukkah 52a — Abaye said: Had it been the one who hates me [meaning himself], he would not have been able to restrain himself. He went and leaned against the doorpost in distress. A certain elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his. Rashi (s.v. "had it been the one who hates me"): Had my enemy been alone with the woman, he could not have restrained himself from sinning; and he was speaking of himself. Rashi (s.v. "he leaned"): He leaned against the bolt of the door, like a man who is brooding and in distress. Rashi (s.v. "the way is long, and the company pleasant"): It is a long way between our two places, and we cannot go on together any further; had we been able to go by one road, our company would have been pleasant. Rashi (s.v. "when they were parting from one another"): They were from two towns, and when they reached a fork in the road he turned one way and she the other. Maharsha (on "for he has done greatly"): The verse concludes "for he has done greatly," meaning that he provokes the great more, as Abaye concludes. Alternatively, "he has done greatly" means that he has made himself great in relation to the righteous, [appearing to them] as a mountain, as was said above that at first he resembles a spider's thread and in the end cart-ropes; and "among Torah scholars more than all of them" is then a statement in its own right, as in the incident of Abaye. Maharsha (s.v. "the way is long"): It may also be explained as referring to the past: we have come a long way, but the company was pleasant, so that because of the company the way did not seem so long to us. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Koach HaYetzer 2): The evil inclination provokes the Torah scholar more than all, although he is complete, being a man of intellect: for the intellect a man possesses [in this world] is never in its completeness but is held with deficiency, so that the Torah scholar and Israel lack the completeness fitting for them, whereas other men and other nations, who have only the small level, cannot be called so deficient. Therefore the evil inclination provokes them more and more, and whoever has a higher level must guard himself against the evil inclination. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 48): After Israel received the Torah and reached a supreme level, the evil inclination provoked them to sin, in the manner of "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": because they had reached a supreme level that the rest of creation had not reached, the evil inclination, which is Satan, seeks to cast them down from their level. For privation clings more to a man who has a supreme level, one not fitting for every man, than it clings to the low level that is found in all. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 19): Just as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his" (and that elder, who was Elijah according to some commentators in Tosafos, a view I have received as primary, was revealed to Abaye through his anguish to tell him this and console him), so too, when someone's inclination is greater than his fellow's, this is a sign that he is also greater than him in the holy sparks within him, for God has made one opposite the other in each person, and the choice is in his hands. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 6): Such an abundance of light would bring great hardship to those who walk in the way of God, for the same reason as "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": with a greater abundance of the light of the Blessed One, the evil in that same place grows stronger too, because so much light lies within it, for evil always surrounds the good. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Since the Blessed One does not deal tyrannically with His creatures, and even one created righteous must choose against an inclination that overpowers him daily, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his". Therefore the inclination appears to the righteous like a mountain, for its assault on them is enormous, matching the great power of good innate in them. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 8): The Sages said that the evil inclination provokes Torah scholars more than all and that "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"; why should this be? The inclination is longing, and the purpose of its creation is to be the delight of Torah; so the one who is greater, in whom the delight of Torah is sunk more deeply, has, since "God has made the one opposite the other," a stronger desire toward the opposite as well, while one who does not magnify the delight of Torah in himself has no strong desire for the opposite either. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 2): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for the virtue is drawn together with the deficiency: as great and precious wealth needs more guarding than a small thing, being more liable to harm because more people strive after it, so in the soul, the greater its stature, that is, the more divine power it holds (and the will toward the opposite is also a divine power), the greater in it is this power of inclination as well, and it needs guarding. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for as the strength of the virtue, so is the strength of the deficiency, from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, where evil stands opposite the good and corresponds to it. Hence Dan, the lowest of the tribes in virtue, is lower in his deficiency as well, and the inclination is not as strong in him. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 134): When a person reaches a higher level, by the measure of that level he has not yet begun to repent, and his sin returns in full force; of this it is said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", for the sin is the deficiency in a person, and so is the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Where the strength of the virtue lies, there lies the strength of the deficiency, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his": as is known, in Adam's sin the "man of Belial" ruled over the holy man limb for limb, God having made the one opposite the other, so that corresponding to the holiness of each limb and power is the dominion of the "man of Belial" in enticing to evil. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Mishlei 19): "The desire of a man is his kindness": the desire found in a person's heart is also a kindness from the Blessed One, for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his", and if he brings the power of his longing and desire into holiness, his stature grows all the more. Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 4): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his," for "God has made the one opposite the other": the power of good against the power of its opposite. Yet every person has the power of good to overcome his inclination, and through this he rises, gathering wealth in holiness little by little, which is the whole purpose of man's creation in this world. Sod Yesharim (Seventh Night of Pesach 16): The vessel [of longing] that a person attains in old age was already in him on the day he was born, only that each time he clarifies himself further, the vessel grows larger in him too, as the Sages said, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his"..),
and "whoever is greater than his fellow, his evil inclination is greater than he" (Sukkah 52a);
וְהַהֶיקֵּשׁ בְּהֵיפֶךְ:
and the reverse deduction is equally true:
שֶׁכָּל שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל, כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן שָׁמַיִם – הוּא הַגָּדוֹל.
that whoever possesses a greater inclination, when he fulfills the will of Heaven—he is the truly great one.
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר מִי שֶׁהוּא מְשׁוּקָּע בְּתַכְלִית תֹּקֶף עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For when one who is submerged in the absolute intensity of worldly affairs
וְתַאֲווֹתָיו הַמַּשְׁכִּיחִים לְגַמְרֵי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and its appetites which cause total forgetfulness of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְהוּא מִתְחַזֵּק וְנִזְכָּר לְהַכִּיר אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ,
nevertheless strengthens himself and remembers to recognize his Creator,
הֲרֵי זֶה קִילּוּס עָצוּם יוֹתֵר.
this brings forth a far more immense, cosmic praise.
וְזֶה תַּכְלִית כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה: "כֹּל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" – לְקִילּוּסוֹ
And this is the ultimate purpose of all Creation: "Hashem made everything for His own purpose" (Proverbs 16:4)—meaning for His praise

(שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב רֵישׁ מִזְמוֹר יט385 Midrash Tehillim 19:1 — "For the leader. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God." This is what Scripture says: "The Lord has made everything for His own sake" (Proverbs 16:4) — for His praise, as it is said, "Sing to the Lord with thanksgiving" (Psalms 147:7). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 2): The aim of the whole Torah is to come to a complete apprehension that there is a Creator, Ruler and Overseer, which was the purpose of the creation of the world: "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. All 613 commandments are counsels for reaching this, for the Torah is called truth, being counsels for reaching a clear apprehension in the heart, so manifest that it needs no faith. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 6): Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created for His glory, He created to reveal the glory of His kingship and His Presence among the lower beings, and "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. The building of the Tabernacle and the Temple is man's work of building a place for His Presence after the sin, when the Presence is not revealed everywhere, in the pattern of the Blessed One's work in creation; had man not sinned, the whole world would have been a Tabernacle and a Sanctuary. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): The angels cry, "Where is the place of His glory?", but man grasps the Throne of Glory, for "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise; the purpose of creation is the revelation of His glory, and its purpose is man. For the chief revelation of glory is when a person with free choice, whose body inclines toward impurity, nevertheless subdues his inclination and desires for the sake of Heaven's honor, which the angels, who have no evil inclination, cannot attain at all.).
(Shocher Tov, beginning of Psalm 19).
וְנַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּיוֹתֵר מִנַּפְשׁוֹת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
And the souls of the children of Israel are plunged into deeper struggles than the souls of the nations of the world,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (שָׁם386 Sukkah 52a — The Rabbis taught: "And I will remove the northerner far from you" (Joel 2:20) — this is the evil inclination, which lies hidden and stands in the heart of man. "And I will drive him into a land barren and desolate" — to a place where there are no men for him to provoke. "With his face toward the eastern sea" — for he set his eyes upon the First Temple and destroyed it, and killed the Torah scholars in it. "And his end toward the western sea" — for he set his eyes upon the Second Temple and destroyed it, and killed the Torah scholars in it. "And his stench shall rise and his foul odor come up" — for he leaves the nations of the world and provokes the enemies of Israel [that is, Israel themselves]. "For he has done great things" — Abaye said: and among the scholars more than among all of them. Rashi (s.v. "and his stench shall rise and his foul odor come up"): And because he raised a stench and a foul smell, in that he left the nations and provoked Israel. Rashi (s.v. "his face toward the eastern sea"): The First Temple, which was like a sea, for everyone gathered there, as all the rivers go to the sea. Maharsha (s.v. "a land barren and desolate"): This is his slaying and nullification in the time to come: in this world we find that he comes "from roaming the earth and walking about in it" to provoke men, but [then] he will be driven to a place where men are not found for him to provoke. Maharsha (s.v. "for he leaves the nations of the world"): Therefore he is driven away from before Him, blessed be He. And the verse concludes "for he has done great things," meaning that he provokes the great more, as Abaye concludes; alternatively, he has made himself great in relation to the righteous, [appearing to them] as a mountain, and Abaye's "and among the scholars more than all of them" is a statement in its own right, as in the incident of Abaye. Maharsha (s.v. "his face"): The verse recalls the evil he had already done in this world. It likens the Temple to the sea because Israel, while settled [in their land], were fruitful like the fish of the sea and "many as the sand of the sea," and it says that this is what caused "his stench to rise and his foul odor to come up." Maharsha (s.v. "which lies hidden and stands in his heart"): That is, he stands there always and does not budge from him, so as to be able to make him sin, as below: "A man's inclination overcomes him every day." Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 2): He leaves the nations and provokes Israel, and the Torah scholars most of all, because whoever has a level greater than other men's is as though he has gone beyond the order and the measure, and a power attaches itself to him that stands ready to nullify that level; so it clings to Israel, who inherited the supreme level, and still more to Torah scholars, in whom intellect cannot be found in its completeness but only with deficiency. "And I will drive him into a land barren and desolate" means that in the time to come the world will be complete, and deficiency will remain only in what is fit to be deficient, like a desolate land, but not where human beings are, for whom completeness is fitting.)
as they stated in Sukkah (there)
דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע הִנִּיחַ כָּל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְנִטְפַּל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל;
that the evil inclination left all the nations of the world aside and fastened specifically onto Israel;

וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בֹּא387 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Pischa 1 — Jonah said: I will go outside the Land, to a place where the Divine Presence is not revealed — for the nations are close to repentance, so as not to bring guilt upon Israel. They offered a parable: to what may this be compared? To a priest's slave who fled from his master and said, I will go to the cemetery, a place my master cannot follow me. His master said to him: I have agents like you. So too the Omnipresent said to Jonah: I have many messengers like you, as it is stated, "And the Lord cast a great wind into the sea" (Jonah 1:4).):
and as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Mekhilta, beginning of Parashat Bo):
אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קְרוֹבֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל;
the nations of the world are near to repentance, which is not the case with Israel;

וְכַיּוֹצֵא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת סג388 Yevamot 63a — R. Elazar bar Avina said: Calamity comes upon the world only on account of Israel, as it is stated: "I have cut off nations, their corners are desolate; I have laid waste their streets" (Zephaniah 3:6), and it is written: "I said: Surely you will fear Me, you will accept correction" (Zephaniah 3:7). Rashi: "On account of Israel": to make them afraid, so that they will repent. Maharsha: For just before this [the prophet] recounts the abominations of Jerusalem — "Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city; she did not listen to the voice" — and then breaks off with the matter of "I have cut off nations, their corners are desolate": that is, on account of their abominations and your iniquity I have cut off the idolaters, so that you will fear Me. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 63a): It cannot be that the Blessed Name brings calamities upon the nations for their own sin, for only good comes from Him: calamity sent to destroy the nations would be evil, and it cannot be meant to return them to the good, since the nations, when suffering comes upon them, only grow more corrupt, reviling and blaspheming, whereas Israel in their distress call upon the Lord. Why then does calamity come? All of it is so that Israel may learn discipline and return to the good; and so everything that comes from the Blessed Name, even calamity, is good — for suffering atones for iniquity and removes sin, which has no application to the nations..):
and along the lines of what they taught (Yevamot 63a):
אֵין פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּא לָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל;
calamity comes to the world solely on account of Israel;
וְיָדוּעַ דְּפוּרְעָנוּת הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַחֵטְא,
and it is known that calamity is intrinsically the sin itself,

כְּטַעַם (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז389 Bava Batra 16a — Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, "And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord." He is the evil inclination, for it is written there, "Only evil all the day," and it is written here, "Only against himself do not put forth your hand." He is the angel of death, as it is written, "Only spare his life" — evidently his life rests in his hand. Rashi: "Evidently his life rests in his hand" — it lies with Satan to take the soul, and God warned him not to take it. Maharsha: Our texts misquote the verse: it reads "only [akh] spare his life," not "only [rak]." The verbal analogy holds nonetheless, since "only [akh]" and "only [rak]" are alike terms of limitation. The hint in it is this: "only evil all the day" — let a man limit his evil inclination and master it, and then "only spare his life" — the Holy One, blessed be He, will limit the power of the angel of death, that he not rule over his soul. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil..): "הוּא יֵצֶר רָע וְכוּלֵי" שֶׁמִּתְהַפֵּךְ בִּגְוָונָיו.
mirroring (Bava Batra 16a): "he is the evil inclination, he is Satan, he is the angel of death," shifting his various guises.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And the root of this deep immersion intensifies within Israel,
כִּי הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁעִיקָּרָם רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for regarding the idolaters whose essence belongs strictly to this physical world,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם קוֹצִים כְּסוּחִים, אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ הִתְגַּבְּרוּת,
who are in truth cut thorns, no dynamic struggle applies;
דְּכָל הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הוּא נֶגֶד הַהֵיפֶךְ,
for all overcoming exists only against an opposing force,
וּכְפִי תֹּקֶף הַהֵיפֶךְ כָּךְ הוּא תֹּקֶף הַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת.
and commensurate with the strength of the opposition is the power of overcoming.
וְזֶה כָּל מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל:
And this is the supreme virtue of Israel:
שֶׁגַּם בְּכָל תֹּקֶף הִתְגַּבְּרוּת שִׁיקּוּעָם,
that even amid the full force of their deep immersion,
וְגַם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה וְהִרְהוּרִים
and even the willful transgressors of Israel are filled with remorse and spiritual longings
שֶׁהֵם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ כְּפִי שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשָׁם;
that are directed toward Heaven in ultimate truth according to the root of their souls;
וְעַל יְדֵי פֶּתַח קָטָן זֶה כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט הֵם מִתְעַלִּים לְגַמְרֵי.
and through this tiny opening like the eye of a needle, they become completely elevated.
וּלְפִיכָךְ הֵם קְרוּיִים "כִּסֵּא כְּבוֹדוֹ",
Therefore they are termed "the Throne of His Glory,"
וְהוּא עוֹלָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּלְאָכִים,
which is a realm high above the ministering angels;
כִּי הַכְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם נִשְׁעָן דַּוְוקָא עַל אֵלּוּ שֶׁמֵּהֶם עוֹלֶה הַכָּבוֹד.
because the glory of Heaven rests specifically upon those from whom that glory ascends out of darkness.
וְזֶהוּ צוּרַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִדַּת אֱמֶת,
And this is the form of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is titled the attribute of Truth;
וְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא",
and this physical world is termed "the World of Falsehood,"
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא – "עָלְמָא דִּקְשׁוֹט".
whereas the World to Come is "the World of Truth."
וְזֶהוּ: "שַׁבָּת – אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And this explains: "Shabbat is a sign between Me and the children of Israel" (Exodus 31:17),
דְּשַׁבָּת רוֹמֵז לְיוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא;
for Shabbat alludes to the eternal day that is entirely Shabbat and the World to Come;
וְהַכָּרַת נְקוּדַּת אֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and recognizing the core point of truth within this world
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּנַפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד;
is found exclusively within Jewish souls alone;
וְנִקְרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "הַשֹּׁמֵר אֱמֶת לְעוֹלָם",
and the Holy One is called "He Who keeps truth forever" (Psalms 146:6),
וְכֵן "שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל" עַל שֵׁם הַבְטָחָתוֹ: "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר";
and likewise "the Guardian of Israel" (Psalms 121:4) based on His promise: "and I will keep you, etc.";
הַיְינוּ נְקוּדַּת הָאֱמֶת הַנִּקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל,
meaning that this point of truth named Israel,
זֶה יִשְׁמוֹר לְעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע בָּהּ קִלְקוּל,
He will protect eternally so that no fatal corruption ever befalls it,

כְּטַעַם (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד390 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..): "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל".
mirroring (Sanhedrin 44a): "even though he has sinned, he remains Israel."
וְזֶהוּ "בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵךְ" –
And this is "wherever you go":

מִלַּת "בְּכֹל" יֵשׁ לִדְרוֹשׁ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּהָרוֹאֶה (סג391 Berakhot 63a — Bar Kappara expounded: Which is the brief passage upon which all the essentials of the Torah depend? "In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths." Rava said: Even for a matter of transgression. Rashi (s.v. "in all your ways"): "In all your ways" — even to commit a transgression. "Know Him" — give thought to whether it is required for a mitzvah, as with Elijah on Mount Carmel, and [if so] transgress it. Maharsha: He did not say "remember Him" but "know Him" — a true knowledge of His existence, and that He is able and watches over all your ways, to give good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked. And it concludes, "and He will make your paths straight," after the manner of what they said: in the way a man wishes to go, he is led, and one who comes to purify himself is assisted. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 34): As it is written, "In all your ways know Him," and the Sages said, "even for a matter of transgression" — then "He will straighten [your paths]." That is, one should give himself over to the Blessed One even to the point of losing his entire share in the World to Come when such is the will of the Blessed One — as I heard concerning the trial of the Binding — and then "He will straighten": the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself straightens you and separates the evil from you without toil. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 19): On "In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths," Rava said, "even for a matter of transgression," and the reading of Ein Yaakov is: "Rav Pappa said, this is what people say: the thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One." That is, even though he commits an explicit transgression of "You shall not steal," since he does not forget the Blessed One and believes in Him at the moment of the act, calling upon the Merciful One, of this it is said "and He will straighten your paths": the Blessed One will straighten his paths, so that "the banished one is not banished from Him," and he will have a rectification. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Beshalach): "Encamp opposite it by the sea": it is written, "In all your ways know Him" — even for a matter of transgression; and this is the meaning of "encamp opposite it": even though you perform deeds like those of the Egyptians, nevertheless the deeds of Israel are good, for the Israelite nation, the portion of the Blessed One, cleaves to simple life without any garment and draws from that source of life alone. All these powers, when among Israel, are full of holiness even though they resemble those of Egypt, for the Blessed One testifies about them that in the heart of Israel there is nothing but love of the Blessed One. Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Berakhos 7): [By placing "I am" before "You shall have no other gods," the Blessed One showed that] even one who has, Heaven forbid, stumbled in a deed that is not good is not barred from repentance and can perform mitzvos though he is not yet cleansed of "turning from evil." This is what the dictum "In all your ways know Him," on which all the essentials of the Torah depend, teaches; and as Rava concludes, "even for a matter of transgression" — that is, a person should not despair after stumbling in sin, for repentance is never withheld from him..)
the word "in all / wherever (bekhol)" is to be expounded as they taught in HaRoeh (Berakhot 63a)
עַל "בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" – אֲפִילּוּ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה;
on the verse "in all your ways acknowledge Him"—even regarding a transgression;
דְּגַם כְּשֶׁחוֹטֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמְרוֹ
in that even when a Jew sins, the Holy One guards him
שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַחֲטוֹא כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁיֹּאבַד שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
so that he can never sin to such a degree that the name of Israel is lost, Heaven forbid,
וּנְקוּדַּת הָאֱמֶת מִמֶּנּוּ;
and the inner spark of truth erased from him;
לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁקָע בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי – זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל.
to become entirely lost and submerged in this world is utterly impossible.
וְיֵדַע אָדָם שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הִגְדִּיל עֲבֵירוֹת עַד אֵין קֵץ,
And a person should know that even if he multiplied sins without end,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִיתַּק מִנְּקוּדַּת הָאֱמֶת וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל אַף זִיז כָּל שֶׁהִיא.
he was nonetheless not severed from the point of truth and the root of Israel even by the slightest fraction.
וּלְפִיכָךְ אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
And therefore, nothing can ever stand in the way of repentance.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר תֵּיכֶף אַחַר הַבְטָחַת "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר":
And that which Scripture stated immediately following the promise of "and I will keep you, etc.":
"וַהֲשִׁבֹתִיךָ אֶל [הָאֲדָמָה הַזֹּאת] וְגוֹמֵר",
"'and I will bring you back unto this land, etc.,'"
הוּא רָזָא דִּתְשׁוּבָה,
is the mystical secret of repentance (teshuvah / hashivakha),
שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִתְשׁוּבָה בֶּאֱמֶת;
that through this divine guarantee he will ultimately merit true repentance;
כִּי סוֹף הַכֹּל אֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל נִגְאָלִים אֶלָּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
for in the end, Israel are redeemed solely through repentance,
וְהֵם יְנַצְּחוּ בְּבַקָּשָׁתָם "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ [ה'] אֵלֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
and they will triumph in their plea: "Turn us back unto You, Hashem, etc." (Lamentations 5:21),

שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם הָאִתְעָרוּתָא לִתְשׁוּבָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ392 Eichah Rabbah 5:21 — The Assembly of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, it depends upon You — “Return us, O Lord, to You, and we shall return.” And He said to them: It depends upon you — “Return to Me, and I shall return to you.” (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה סוֹף אֵיכָה).
that the initial awakening to repent will likewise be granted from Hashem, blessed be He (Midrash Rabbah, end of Eichah).
וְכֵן לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בִּפְרָט,
And likewise for each individual soul of Israel specifically,
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ לִזְכּוֹת לִשְׁלֵימוּתוֹ
the Holy One, blessed be He, assists him to merit his personal completion
וּלְהַשִּׂיג לִטְעוֹם מִבִּרְכוֹתָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר וַהֲשִׁבֹתִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר";
and to taste the blessings of our father Jacob: "and I will keep you... and I will bring you back, etc.";
וְהֵם הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים בַּלֵּב מֵעַצְמָם.
these being the thoughts of repentance that spontaneously fall into the heart on their own.
וּפְעָמִים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין אֵיזֶה סִבּוֹת הַמְּעוֹרְרִים לִתְשׁוּבָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
And at times Hashem orchestrates outer circumstances that stimulate repentance and the like,
בְּאֹפֶן שֶׁסּוֹף כָּל סוֹף "דִּידַן נָצַח",
in such a manner that ultimately "ours is the victory,"
לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצִּידּוֹ הַפּוֹתֵחַ גַּם כֵּן הַפֶּתַח כְּחֻדּוֹ שֶׁל מַחַט בַּלֵּב
wherein Hashem, from His side, likewise opens the opening like the eye of a needle in the heart
לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה בֶּאֱמֶת וּבְלֵב שָׁלֵם.
unto total repentance in genuine truth and with a whole heart.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Seven Blessings and the Path of Return
Jacob's seven blessings map the soul's sanctification from embodied holiness to the higher closeness of teshuvah.

p: וְהֵם שֶׁבַע בְּרָכוֹת שָׁם בַּכָּתוּב נֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת.
And these are seven blessings there in the text (Genesis 28:13–15) corresponding to the seven sefirotic attributes.
נְתִינַת הָאָרֶץ הוּא בִּרְכַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
The giving of the Land is the blessing of our father Abraham, peace be upon him (Chesed),
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִהְיֶה אֶרֶץ נִקְרָא "אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל",
meaning that the earthly domain is designated as "the Land of Israel",
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַגּוּף קָדוֹשׁ וּבְיָדוֹ.
the meaning being that the physical body itself becomes holy and under one's dominion.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַכְּנִיסָה דְּשֵׁם יְהוּדִי,
And this marks the initial entrance into the name and identity of a Jew,
לִהְיוֹת אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ מְקוֹם מִשְׁכָּן לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
that his personal four cubits become an indwelling sanctuary for Hashem, blessed be He.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְהָיָה זַרְעֲךָ" – הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
And afterward, "and your seed shall be as the dust of the earth" represents the expansive multiplication,
וְהוּא מִמִּדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה,
and this derives from the attribute of Gevurah,

כַּנּוֹדָע מִמִּזְמוֹר: "אַשְׁרֵי כָּל יְרֵא ה' וְגוֹמֵר393 Psalms 128:3-4 — “Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine in the recesses of your house; your children like olive shoots around your table. Behold, thus shall the man be blessed who fears the Lord.” Rashi: “As a fruitful vine” — her children will be many. “In the recesses of your house” — because marital relations are conducted in private. “Your sons like olive shoots” — just as olive trees take no grafting, so will there be no disqualification among your sons. Radak: He likens her to a vine because there is no tree that men plant inside a house except the vine, which some plant in the recesses of their house and then lead out through an opening to the sun, so that its root is within and its branches without; so the wife is to be modest in the recesses of the house and not go out, while the sons go out for their work and for the needs of the house, like the branches of the vine. And he likens the sons to olives because the olive tree takes no grafting from another tree and its shoots are true sons of their father: so there will be no suspicion of illegitimacy in the sons of such a woman, since their mother is modest; and with such qualities and such practices is the man who fears the Lord blessed. Metzudas Dovid: She will be like a vine that bears fruit and stands at the rear of the house, close by, so that it can be tended, dunged and watered in its season, and its fruit is therefore abundant and good — so your wife will bear you many and goodly children. “Like olive shoots” — which keep their beauty all the year round; so the look of your sons’ faces will never grow dim, and they will be around your table and not seated at the table of others. Malbim: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine in bearing children, and like a vine planted in the recesses of your house which, though it stands at the rear, raises its branches and tendrils to the roof and shelters the whole house from there — so she is modest, dwelling within the tent at the rear of the house, and yet guards and shelters the household as a whole. Your sons are like olive shoots, which take no grafting and yield oil for light: so they will be true seed, shining with the light of knowledge, and seated around your table. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 18): By rectifying himself for the moment through hearing the shofar [on Rosh Hashanah], a person draws down the flow of "children, life and sustenance": children through fear [of Heaven], as it says, "Happy is the man who fears the Lord … his seed shall be mighty in the land," and it says, "Happy is everyone who fears the Lord … your wife [shall be as a fruitful vine]."",
as is known from the psalm: "Praiseworthy is everyone who fears Hashem, etc." (Psalms 128:1),
וְ"הַלְלוּיָהּ, אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר".
and "Hallelujah, praiseworthy is the man who fears Hashem, etc. his seed shall be mighty upon earth" (Psalms 112:1–2).
וּבִרְכַּת "וּפָרַצְתָּ" הוּא נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And the blessing of "and you shall spread abroad (u-faratzta)" is the heritage of our father Jacob, peace be upon him (Tiferet),
נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים,
a boundless, unrestricted heritage,
שֶׁיִּפְרוֹץ הַמֵּיצַר וְהַגְּבוּל;
bursting through all confinement and limitation;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשׁוֹת וְהַהַבְדָּלָה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַגְּבוּל,
and this is attained through sacred devotions and separation from this world which is a world of boundaries,
וְנִדְבָּק בַּמֶּה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַגְּבוּל.
cleaving unto that which transcends every boundary.
"וְנִבְרֲכוּ וְגוֹמֵר" הוּא נִיצּוּחַ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
"And in you shall be blessed all the families of the earth, etc." represents the triumph over the idolaters,
דְּמַלְאָךְ רָע יַעֲנֶה "אָמֵן" בְּעָלְכָרְחוֹ,
wherein the evil angel is compelled to respond "Amen" against his will;

זֶהוּ נֶגֶד הַנֵּצַח (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת נח394 Berakhot 58a — R. Sheila expounded: "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness" — this is the work of creation; "and the might" — this is the exodus from Egypt; "and the glory" — this is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua; "and the victory" — this is the downfall of Rome; "and the majesty" — this is the battle of the valleys of Arnon; "for all that is in heaven and on earth" — this is the war of Sisera; "Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom" — this is the war of Amalek; "and You are exalted" — this is the war of Gog and Magog. Rashi: "Yours is the kingdom — this is the war of Amalek": for concerning it a throne of kingship is written, "The hand upon the throne of the Lord" — that is, through the Lord's war against Amalek His throne will be exalted. "And You are exalted": since a term of exaltation is used, it refers to Gog, "the chief prince of Meshekh and Tubal." Maharsha: By this exposition the items do not stand in their historical order, for the downfall of Rome is placed before the war of the valleys of Arnon and the war of Sisera; Scripture arranged them rather according to their attributes, the seven lower attributes in their order, as the masters of Kabbalah have written. R. Sheila came to expound the emanation of these seven, in each of which He acted according to its own measure: "the greatness" is the attribute of kindness, by which the work of creation came into being, as it is said, "the world is built by kindness"; by "the might" He acted in the exodus from Egypt through the plagues He brought upon the Egyptians; and by "the glory" the sun and the moon stood still for Joshua, which was to Joshua's name and glory in all the world. Maharal (Gevuros Hashem, Third Introduction): Scripture names just these things in order to say that everything is His — that all the differences of existence and all the differing powers belong to Him; and the things that are opposed and divided one from another are, first of all, the six directions of the world, the four winds with above and below, and a seventh, the center, which stands over against them all.
