"Yours, O Lord, is the greatness — this is the work of creation" corresponds to the east, for from the east the sun rises and renews the work of creation each day; "and the might — this is the exodus from Egypt" to the west, where the sun sets and the undoing of existing things belongs, for as He brought the world into being by ten utterances, so He undid Egypt by ten plagues. "And the glory — this is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua" corresponds to the middle, for nothing rules over sun and moon except what is separate from matter, and everything separate is glorious, since the turbidity of the corporeal has been removed from it..).
this corresponds to the attribute of Netzach (Eternity/Victory; as written in Berakhot 58a).
"וְאָנֹכִי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ" הוּא נֶגֶד הַהוֹד,
"And behold, I will be with you" corresponds to the attribute of Hod,
דְּשָׁם הַיִּחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ כַּנּוֹדָע:
for there takes place the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as is known:
אִיהוּ בְּנֵצַח וְאִיהִי בְּהוֹד,
He is rooted in Netzach and She in Hod;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נָחִיתָ כַצֹּאן עַמֶּךָ בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן",
and as it is written (Psalms 77:21): "You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron",
וּבְדַרְגָּא דְּאַהֲרֹן "יָבֹא אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ" לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים,
and through the priestly rung of Aaron one enters "into the holy place" into the innermost Holy of Holies,
דְּהַיְינוּ "אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ" מַמָּשׁ.
which is the literal manifestation of "I am with you."
"וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" הוּא נֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד,
"And I will keep you, etc." corresponds to the attribute of Yesod,
בָּהּ דְּנִקְרָא "הִילּוּךְ",
wherein lies the faculty termed "walking" (hilukh),

כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (עד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)395 Yoma 74b — R. Zeira said: What is the verse? "Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire" (Ecclesiastes 6:9). Reish Lakish said: The sight of the eyes with a woman is better than the act itself, as it is stated, "Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire." עַל פָּסוּק "מַהֲלַךְ נֶפֶשׁ396 Yoma 74b — Reish Lakish said: Better is the sight of the eyes upon a woman than the act itself, as it is said, “Better is the sight of the eyes than the going of the soul.”",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Yoma (74b end) on the verse "the journey of the soul",

וּבִבְרָכוֹת (יא397 Berakhot 11a — As it is taught: "When you sit in your house" — excluding one occupied with a commandment; "and when you walk on the way" — excluding a bridegroom. From here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt [from reciting the Shema], and one who marries a widow is obligated. Rashi: Although a bridegroom too is engaged in a commandment, a second verse is needed to exempt him: the exclusion drawn from "in your house" removes only one busy with the actual work of a commandment, where there is real occupation, whereas the bridegroom's is an occupation of the mind alone — he is thinking about the consummation of the marriage — and without the extra verse he would not have been excluded. Hence "one who marries a virgin is exempt," for his mind is taken up with the thought of the marital act that is a commandment..) עַל פָּסוּק "וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ",
and in Berakhot (11a) on the verse "and when you walk by the way",
וְשָׁם צָרִיךְ שִׁימּוּר,
and there spiritual vigilance and safeguarding are essential;

כַּנּוֹדָע דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ)398 Vayikra Rabbah 14:5 — "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity" (Psalms 51:7). R. Acha said: Even were one the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he should not have one aspect of iniquity. David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? Surely he intended only his own pleasure. Know that this is so, for after they have satisfied their need, this one turns his face this way and that one turns her face that way, and it is You who bring in every single drop that is in him. And this is what David said, "For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord will gather me in" (Psalms 27:10). Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:10): The meaning of "the counsel of the serpent" is learned from Jesse, who is counted among the four who died through it, and of whom the Sages said, on "in iniquity was I formed," "even the most pious of the pious…". In Elijah, who did not die, even the serpent's counsel was rectified, and he, the angel of the covenant, testifies concerning birth that it is not, Heaven forbid, in iniquity, but that all are holy from the womb. Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 12): Death still comes through the counsel of the serpent, that is, the filth the serpent cast [into Eve], and that filth is the desire for lewdness, about which the Sages said of Jesse, one of the four who died through the serpent's counsel, "even the most pious of the pious…". Only Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their filth cease, and then they were truly free of the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 19): The seminal drop is drawn from the brain, but because it comes with the desire of this world, as the Sages said, "even the most pious of the pious…", it imparts impurity; yet the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth the pure from the impure, for a child is formed from it. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 16): The beginning [of a fall] is in matters of desire, where everyone is in any case somewhat lax about complete holiness like that of Jacob our father, who intended only to raise offspring and was aroused only for the sake of the mitzvah and of Heaven; not every person merits this, as the Sages said on "in iniquity," "even the most pious of the pious…". This comes from laxity in the service of the Blessed One and in bringing the holiness of the words of Torah into one's heart, for one whose thought cleaves to the love of Torah will let no desire for anything else enter him. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): On "in iniquity was I formed," with "iniquity" written full, the Midrash says that even the most pious of the pious intends only his own pleasure; this is Jesse, the father of David, and this is the counsel of the serpent, a deficiency in the birth of everyone born of woman, of the offspring of Eve, against which no effort avails, even for the most pious of the pious. Only, as the Sages said, "Who purifies you? The Holy One, blessed be He": the purification from this is His, for He testifies that this desire of Israel is clean and pure. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 5): The impurity of childbirth applies even when a woman bears a righteous one, even the Messiah, and its reason is the Midrash on "Behold, in iniquity was I formed": R. Acha says, "even the most pious of the pious… did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? Surely he intended only his own pleasure." This was said of Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, and the serpent's counsel is what the serpent instilled in man, that he should feel his own pleasure; from this sprang the impurity of the menstruant and the seven-day impurity of childbirth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, was clarified through the birth of David, who applied to himself "Behold, in iniquity was I formed," which the Sages expounded from "iniquity" being written full: "even the most pious of the pious…". As is known from the Arizal, wherever letters of the Divine Name are added they indicate added holiness, and vav is the letter of truth; for desire is called falsehood, being a pleasure of the moment, whereas the desire of Israel, who cleave to the living God, endures as they do, for all their powers cleave to holiness. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 147): Only the Unique One of the world can bring forth the pure from the impure, for in this desire lies the source of the deficiencies that come from the serpent, as the Sages said on "in iniquity" [written full], and that is Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent. Man's root is in truth impure, as it is written, "in iniquity was I formed," yet there is holiness and purity in it as well; Balaam, being of an evil root, did not believe this, for he did not know that there could be holiness here too.:
as known from the words of our Sages (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Tazria):
"אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי",
"Even the most pious among the pious cannot escape a trace of sinful thought, etc.",
וְאָמְרוּ זֶה עַל יִשַׁי;
and they applied this even unto Jesse;
וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה דְּזֶהוּ "עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ"
and it appears from this that this is "the counsel of the primordial Serpent"

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת נה399 Shabbat 55b — Four died through the counsel of the serpent [and not through any sin of their own], and these are they: Benjamin son of Jacob, Amram father of Moses, Jesse father of David, and Chileab son of David. Rashi: "Through the counsel [be'etyo] of the serpent": through the counsel of the serpent, who enticed Eve, and not through any other sin, for they did not sin. "Etyo" is as in "counsel and discretion" (Daniel 2:14). Tosafos (s.v. "four died through the counsel of the serpent"): And as for what is written, "For there is not a righteous man upon earth who does good and sins not" (Ecclesiastes 7:20) — that speaks of the majority of people. Maharsha: Rashi takes "etyo" in the sense of counsel, while the Aruch offers also the sense of a pen, as in "the pen [et] of a scribe". Besides Tosafot's answer, one may say that even one who has some slight sin is not deserving of death for it. And if one asks whether these four were then greater than Moses and Aaron, who died through their sin: they were not of such stature [as to be judged as exactingly], and they did not sin either. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 55b): These four did not incline from uprightness at all, and each is named by his father or his son because that tie is the cause of it: Benjamin's soul was bound up with Jacob, who is called Jeshurun ["the upright one"], so that the offspring that came from Jacob was upright and without sin — as the Temple shows, which stood in his portion, at the center of the world, inclining to no side. Moses and David could have some sin, since so exalted a rank cannot be wholly free of deficiency, but the father who brought each of them into the world had to be wholly righteous, for had he strayed from uprightness such an offspring could not have come from him; and David, like Jacob, had a son joined to him who was without sin and died only through the counsel of the serpent.:) בְּיִשַׁי דְּלֹא הָיָה בּוֹ חֵטְא400 Vayikra Rabbah 14:5; Shabbat 55b — R. Acha said: Even the most pious of the pious cannot be free of some measure of transgression in this matter. David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the worlds, did my father Yishai intend to bring me into being? Surely he intended only his own pleasure. And in Shabbat 55b: Four died through the counsel of the serpent — Binyamin son of Yaakov, Amram father of Moshe, Yishai father of David, and Kilav son of David.,
concerning which our Sages stated (Shabbat 55b) that Jesse possessed no actual sin,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "עָווֹן מָלֵא",
and this is termed an inevitable, systemic "full iniquity",
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דִּלְזֶה כִּיוְּונוּ דְּהוּא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם לְהִינָּצֵל כְּלָל.
perforce showing that their intention was the instigation of the Serpent from which it is not within mortal power to escape entirely.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל וְגוֹמֵר",
And concerning this it was promised: "and I will keep you in all wherever you go, etc.",
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּכָל עִנְיָן לֹא תוּכַל לְהִינָּתֵק כְּלָל מִמֶּנִּי.
guaranteeing that in any circumstance you can never become utterly severed from Me.
וּבִכְלַל זֶה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁלֹּא יִתְעָרְבוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ בְּעַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת,
And within this promise is also included that the holy seed shall never intermingle, Heaven forbid, among the pagan nations,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק יח401 Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 18 — They offered a parable: a king sat upon his throne with golden vessels set before him bearing figs and grapes, pomegranates and nuts, dates and dried figs, apples and citrons; he sat and sorted them, setting each kind by itself, and while he turned aside the wind came and mixed them together again. And so the Sages taught in the Mishnah: Ten genealogical classes came up from Babylonia. Had the Holy One, blessed be He, withdrawn His hand from Israel for two or three generations one after another, these ten would have become intermingled with one another and they would have been like the rest of the nations. Why, then, do you not acknowledge and bless and praise your Father in heaven, who has held you with His two hands upon His two arms and has guarded you from coming to disqualification?):
and as written in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (Chapter 18):
דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמֵר הָעֲשָׂרָה יוּחֲסִין שֶׁלֹּא יִתְעָרְבוּ וְכוּלֵי.
that the Holy One, blessed be He, preserves the genealogies of Israel from assimilation, etc.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וַהֲשִׁבֹתִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" הוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת
And afterward, "and I will bring you back, etc." represents the ultimate completion (Malchut),
וּמִדַּת "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה הַנָּעוּץ בִּתְחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה",
and the attribute of "the end of action wedged within the initial thought",
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה,
which is the royal level of David who established the yoke of repentance;
דְּהַגַּם שֶׁהָלַךְ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ וְנִשְׁקַע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁקַע,
in that even though a person wandered wherever he wandered and sank wherever he sank,
יוּכַל לָשׁוּב לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ וְלִמְקוֹמוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה בַּמַּדְרֵגָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה,
he is capable of returning to his primal root and to his place in holiness at the highest degree,
כַּנּוֹדָע לְצוֹפֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה דְּכָל אוֹר נִרְאֶה כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק:
as known to the visionaries of the Divine Chariot, that all light is perceived like the appearance of lightning:
לִמְקוֹם שֶׁהוֹלְכִים – מִשָּׁם שָׁבִים.
to the place they travel—thence they return.
הוּא כְּטַעַם "מִשָּׁם יִקָּחֲךָ" – דַּוְוקָא מִשָּׁם;
This mirrors the principle (Deuteronomy 30:4): "from thence will He fetch you"—specifically from there;
וּמִתַּכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת הוּא מִתְקָרֵב לְגַמְרֵי לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and out of the absolute nadir of lowliness, he draws close in complete intimacy unto Hashem, blessed be He.

וְכַנּוֹדָע דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה402 Berakhot 34b — R. Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R. Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only concerning penitents; but as for the wholly righteous — “no eye has seen, O God, but Yours.” And this differs from R. Abbahu, who said: In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous do not stand, as it is said, “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near” — to the far first, and then to the near. And R. Yochanan said: “Far” means one who was far from transgression from the outset; “near” means one who was near to transgression and has now distanced himself from it. Rashi: "They prophesied only" — [all their promises of] the good things and the consolations. "No eye has seen" — it was never seen and never revealed to any prophet. And "far" [in R. Yochanan's reading] is one who was far from transgression all his days, that is, righteous from the outset. Maharsha: In penitents the bodily, material power once prevailed, and so they will have only a bodily and material reward, such as the prophets were able to foretell; not so the wholly righteous, who will merit a great spiritual reward, of which "no eye has seen." And since all three of these statements were said by R. Chiya bar Abba in the name of R. Yochanan, they must not contradict one another. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTeshuvah 4): "All the prophets prophesied only concerning penitents" — for the prophets are men in a body, and it is impossible that they should behold in their prophecy the level of the righteous man who is wholly separated [from matter], the level that will be his in the time to come. They prophesied only of the level of penitents, whose soul had been sunk in matter when they sinned; and though they have turned back, their soul does not attain a wholly separated level. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): This is the "very good" within the evil inclination, for "in the place where penitents stand the wholly righteous do not stand": through the sin, when one afterwards merits repentance, he reaches a greater level. The penitent is not helped to re-enter by the gate through which he went out, resolving henceforth to behave like a wholly righteous man as if he had never sinned and restraining himself because the thing is forbidden, for the inclination has already overpowered him there; he must raise himself to the upper gate, of doing nothing that is not for the satisfaction and fulfillment of the will of the Blessed One, and this is the gate through which penitents come, a higher place than the lower gate that is open to the righteous. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 8): R. Yochanan said that all the prophets prophesied only about penitents, but of the wholly righteous "no eye has seen," and R. Abbahu said that in the place where penitents stand the wholly righteous do not stand; one may say that these and those are the words of the living God and they do not disagree, but it depends on the quality of the repentance: through repentance out of fear of punishment deliberate sins become like unwitting ones, whereas through repentance out of love they become like merits. The one who repents out of love, the Blessed One shines upon him and repairs the deed itself so that it becomes a merit, and therefore he is superior to a wholly righteous man, for he has new merits that one righteous from the outset has no power to attain, as in "there is no light except that which comes out of darkness." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): Repentance is above [human wisdom, the Torah and prophecy], and none of them can fathom its depth, as they said, "in the place where penitents stand the wholly righteous cannot stand": the place of the wholly righteous is what is due them according to their deeds, which follow the Torah, prophecy and wisdom without leaving their bounds, "this you shall do and this not," "thus far shall you come and no further." But the penitent has already breached the fence of the world as bounded by the Torah, the prophets and the sages, and sunk where he sank; and when he returns to God and repairs the past with the clear recognition that "You are with me" and that wherever he may be there is nothing besides Him, he merits the inheritance of Jacob, an inheritance without bounds. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 164): In people's minds the penitent is not like a wholly righteous man, still less are the sins he committed reckoned as merits, even though one believes the Sages' words that deliberate sins become merits and that "in the place where penitents stand [the wholly righteous do not stand]"; this is because repentance is called the "hidden world," and its preciousness and beauty are not revealed to people. [In a bracketed note he adds that] the dissenting view concerns the perception of the prophets: the one master derives his view from the verse "to the far and to the near," which is in the Prophets, while in the other's view it is not so from the standpoint of prophecy, since of the wholly righteous it is said "no eye has seen," which is from the standpoint of the Blessed One alone. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Sanhedrin): As explained in Likutei HaShas, they do not disagree, and these and those are the words of the living God; their dispute is alluded to in the Mishnah, "The blood of the sin-offering precedes the blood of the burnt-offering because it atones; the limbs of the burnt-offering precede the sacrificial parts of the sin-offering because it is wholly consumed." The sin-offering is the penitent and its blood is the cry from the depth of the heart: the penitent's cry is greater, for he cries out because it seems to him that, God forbid, he has no remedy without the salvation of the Blessed One, and so his cry rises to the place where the righteous do not stand; but in the limbs of the burnt-offering, that is, the performance of the commandments, the wholly righteous take precedence, for their body is greatly refined and cleaves to the Blessed One, never separated for a moment. (בְּרָכוֹת לד:) עַל פָּסוּק "לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב",
And as known from the teachings of our Sages (Berakhot 34b) on the verse (Isaiah 57:19): "Peace to him that is far off and to him that is near",
דִּ"לְקָרוֹב" הַיְינוּ בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה;
that "to the near" points to the penitent (ba'al teshuvah);
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים נִקְרָא בַּכָּתוּב "קָרוֹב",
and in any event he is termed by Scripture "near",
דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ קוּרְבָא יוֹתֵר כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְ"מִשָּׁם יִקָּחֲךָ" וְנַעֲשָׂה מִשָּׁם הַהַתְחָלָה,
for he attains an even closer intimacy once he arrives at "from thence will He fetch you" and makes that very place his new beginning,
אָז מִמֵּילָא הוּא קוֹדֵם בַּמַּדְרֵגָה לְצַדִּיק גָּמוּר.
so that he automatically precedes in spiritual rank even the perfectly righteous.

sections.en: Mind, Heart, and the Rule of the Sages

items.h: The mind and heart guide the person, while the sages channel divine judgment into Israel; simple faith ultimately joins revealed truth within the heart.

Seif 1 — Mind, Heart, and the Eyes of Israel
The sages join intellect, faith, and heart, directing divine judgment toward inward clarification and salvation.

p: הָאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי מַנְהִיגִים: הַמּוֹחַ וְהַלֵּב.
A person has two leaders: the mind and the heart.
זֶה בְּשִׂכְלִיּוֹת וְעֵצוֹת דֶּרֶךְ חָכְמָה,
This one in intellectual matters and counsels by way of wisdom,
וְזֶה בְּכֹחוֹת הַנַּפְשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁכֻּלָּם מֵהַלֵּב,
and that one in the powers of the soul, all of which stem from the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים",
as it is written: "For from it are the issues of life",
כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַחִיּוּנִיִּים שֶׁבַּגּוּף יוֹצְאִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
all the vital faculties in the body proceed from it.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי..." וְגוֹמֵר,
And regarding this it is said: "Do not explore after..." and so forth,
עַיִן — פֵּירוּשׁ: הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
eye—meaning: the wisdom in the mind,
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין וְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים "עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה"
and as is known, the Sanhedrin and the sages of Israel are called "the eyes of the congregation"

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ד וּבְבָבָא בַּתְרָא ד403 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:1:2; Bava Batra 4a — "Your eyes are doves" — your eyes are the Sanhedrin, who are the eyes of the congregation, as it is written, "if it was done unwittingly, hidden from the eyes of the congregation" (Numbers 15:24). There are two hundred and forty-eight limbs in a man, and none of them goes or comes except after the eyes; so too Israel can do nothing without their Sanhedrin. And in Bava Batra, [Bava ben Buta said to Herod:] He who blinded the eye of the world — as it is written of the Sages, "if it was hidden from the eyes of the congregation" — let him go and occupy himself with the eye of the world, as it is written, "Behold, I will profane My Sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes" (Ezekiel 24:21). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 10): So too with the Sages of Israel, who are called the heads of the generation and "the eyes of the congregation": just as a community is reckoned as that very generation and "a community does not die," so the court, being the eyes of the generation, does not die, and it is as though it were that same court. And since they are the eyes of the Congregation of Israel — just as the Congregation of Israel is one and one generation bears the sins of another, so the eyes of the Congregation of Israel in this generation bear the sin of its eyes in another generation, for it is all one. עַמּוּד א).
(as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, beginning of parashah 4, and in Bava Batra 4a).
וְהַיְנוּ דְּצָרִיךְ לֵידַע שֶׁהוּא לֹא יוּכַל לַעֲזֹר לוֹ בְּעֵצוֹתָיו וּבְכֹחוֹתָיו כְּלוּם,
And the meaning is that a person must know that on his own he cannot help himself at all through his counsels and faculties,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אַל יִתְהַלֵּל..." וְגוֹמֵר "כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת..." וְגוֹמֵר404 Jeremiah 9:22-23 — “Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the mighty man glory in his might, nor the rich man glory in his riches. But let him that glories glory in this — that he understands and knows Me, that I am the Lord who exercises kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these things I delight, says the Lord.” Rashi: "Let not the wise man boast" — do not boast, saying, "We are wise"; you have rejected My words, so what wisdom have you? If you have understood and known Me, then you may boast of your wisdom. Radak: If there are wise men among you, let them not boast of their wisdom, for it will not avail them, since they did not know the Lord and did not walk in His ways; and so too the mighty, whose strength will not save them from death or from captivity, and the rich, whose wealth will not redeem them from the sword. He named these three because it is the way of the world that a man escapes by his cunning, or by his strength, or by ransoming himself with his money — and the prophet tells them that by these three they will not be saved. Metzudas Dovid: Let not the wise man boast, for he cannot save himself by his wisdom, nor the mighty man by his might, nor can the rich man redeem himself with his wealth; there is nothing in these to boast of, since no benefit will come to them from them. "But in this let him that boasts boast" — in understanding and knowing Me, that I am the Lord and there is none besides Me, and that I am the one who does kindness to those who love Me and keep My commandments, judgment to exact payment from the wicked, and righteousness to receive those who return. Malbim: Let no man boast of wisdom, might or wealth, for none of them will help him if the Lord has decreed evil against him. But a man may boast of them when he uses them as instruments for a worthy end — his wisdom "to understand and know Me, that I am the Lord," and his might and his wealth "to do kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth," doing justice for the oppressed by his might and kindness and charity by his wealth — "for in these I delight," these being the end I seek.,
and as it is written: "Let not the wise man glory..." and so forth, "but only in this..." and so forth;
פֵּירוּשׁ: הַשְׂכֵּל הוּא הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
meaning: "haskeil" (understanding) is the intellect in the brain,
וְיָדֹעַ הוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
and "yado'a" (knowing) is the felt awareness in the heart,
שְׁנֵיהֶם יִהְיוּ רַק בְּעִנְיַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
both must be directed solely toward the Blessed Name,
שֶׁיַּשְׂכִּיל בְּשִׂכְלוֹ וְיַרְגִּישׁ בְּלִבּוֹ דְּאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ.
that he understand in his intellect and feel in his heart that there is none besides Him.
וְחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, וּגְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
And his wisdom in the mind, and his might in the heart,
וְעָשְׁרוֹ וּרְכוּשׁוֹ שֶׁהַמּוֹחַ וְהַלֵּב מִתְלַבֵּשׁ —
and his wealth and possessions, in which the mind and heart clothe themselves—

כְּטַעַם: "לִבָּא בְּכִיסָא תַּלְיָא" (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח דִּתְרוּמוֹת)405 Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:4 — R. Yochanan said: I have been robbed by the men of Kanya. He went up to the study hall, and R. Simeon ben Lakish put a question to him and he did not answer; he put it to him again and he did not answer. He said to him: What is this? He said to him: All the limbs depend upon the heart, and the heart depends upon the purse. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "I have been robbed by the men of Kanya"): "The men of Kanya" was the name of the brigands who plundered and robbed R. Yochanan of what was his. He entered the study hall, and Reish Lakish put a matter of law to him and he did not answer, and asked him again and he did not answer; he said to him, Why are you sunk in such distress? — and he answered, All the limbs depend upon the heart, and the heart upon the purse; and then he told him, I have been robbed by these men of Kanya, and they have taken all my money. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Ahavas Hashem 1): When a man loses his money his understanding is thereby taken from him, as they said: a man's heart is bound up with his purse — for a man's understanding is drawn after his money, since it is his money that gives him his continuance. This is why Scripture says "with all your might," that is, with all your money: even if He takes your money from you, and that is for you the loss of understanding, [you are to love Him still].,
in the sense of: "the heart depends upon the purse" (Jerusalem Talmud, end of Terumot ch. 8),
וְהָרְכוּשׁ הוּא לְבוּשׁ מִבַּחוּץ הַמַּלְבִּישִׁים חָכְמָה וּבִינָה שֶׁבְּמוֹחָא וְלִבָּא,
and possessions are an external garment clothing the wisdom and understanding in the mind and heart—
יַשְׂכִּיל וְיַרְגִּישׁ דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
if he understands and feels that all is from the Blessed Name,
אָז יוּכַל לְהִתְהַלֵּל בָּהֶם לֵאמֹר: רְאוּ מַתַּת ה' לְהִתְפָּאֵר.
then he can glory in them, saying: "Behold Hashem's gift in which to glory."

וְ"כֹל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" — לְקִלּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב רֵישׁ מִזְמוֹר יט)406 Midrash Tehillim 19:1 — "For the leader. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God." This is what Scripture says: "The Lord has made everything for His own sake" (Proverbs 16:4) — for His praise, as it is said, "Sing to the Lord with thanksgiving" (Psalms 147:7). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 2): The aim of the whole Torah is to come to a complete apprehension that there is a Creator, Ruler and Overseer, which was the purpose of the creation of the world: "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. All 613 commandments are counsels for reaching this, for the Torah is called truth, being counsels for reaching a clear apprehension in the heart, so manifest that it needs no faith. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 6): Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created for His glory, He created to reveal the glory of His kingship and His Presence among the lower beings, and "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. The building of the Tabernacle and the Temple is man's work of building a place for His Presence after the sin, when the Presence is not revealed everywhere, in the pattern of the Blessed One's work in creation; had man not sinned, the whole world would have been a Tabernacle and a Sanctuary. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): The angels cry, "Where is the place of His glory?", but man grasps the Throne of Glory, for "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise; the purpose of creation is the revelation of His glory, and its purpose is man. For the chief revelation of glory is when a person with free choice, whose body inclines toward impurity, nevertheless subdues his inclination and desires for the sake of Heaven's honor, which the angels, who have no evil inclination, cannot attain at all.,
And "Hashem made everything for His purpose"—for His praise (Shocher Tov, beginning of Psalm 19),
וְהוּא קִלּוּס הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and this is the praise of the Blessed Name.
וְזֶה כְּלָל גָּדוֹל בְּכָל דָּבָר:
And this is a major foundational principle in every matter:
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עֵצוֹת בְּחָכְמָתוֹ אוֹ בְּכֹחוֹתָיו לְהֵעָזֵר,
whenever one must seek counsels in his wisdom or in his faculties to find help,
יַשְׂכִּיל וְיֵדַע מִקּוֹדֶם
he must understand and know beforehand
דְּאֵין חָכְמָה וְאֵין עֵצָה וּתְבוּנָה,
that there is no wisdom and no counsel and no understanding,
וְלֹא שׁוּם כֹּחַ וְתַחְבּוּלָה בְּיַד הָאָדָם לְהֵעָזֵר,
nor any power or device in man's hand to help himself,
אִם לֹא מִיָּדוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
unless it comes from the hand of the Blessed Name.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים" וְגוֹמֵר407 Psalms 121 — “A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to the mountains — from where will my help come? My help is from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth. He will not let your foot falter; your Guardian does not slumber. Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps. The Lord is your Guardian; the Lord is your shade at your right hand. By day the sun shall not strike you, nor the moon by night. The Lord shall guard you from all evil; He shall guard your soul. The Lord shall guard your going out and your coming in, from now and forever.” Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 2): This explains R. Shmuel bar Nachman's opening, "I lift my eyes to the mountains" — "to the parents, to my teachers…": Yaakov was surely not distressed over the good of this world but over the accusation of the evil inclination [in what it adds of its own], against which words of Torah do not avail, so that even the Torah he had learned from his teachers Shem and Ever had not helped him — "from where will my help come?" Hence the Midrash: "I will not give up hope in my Creator, but 'my help is from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth'" — He bears with and has mercy on all souls, from the loftiest, called heaven, to the lowest level, called earth. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Vayeitzei): When Yaakov left Be'er Sheva with no bread to eat and had to go to Lavan and tend sheep for his livelihood, he was greatly dejected, for he looked [to his parents] and saw himself very small beside his fathers, who never needed to look to the matters of this world and were always occupied with divine service and the Work of the Chariot, while he had to occupy himself with such small things. Then he said, "I will not give up hope in my Creator": though they were engaged in great things and I see myself in small things, there is service of the Blessed One in this too, for He is the Maker of all. Tiferes Yosef (Tzav 1): His father explained that from the side of the Blessed One there is truly no break in His light, even to the smallest garment; only from man's lowly perception does it seem that where the garment is remote His light cannot dwell. This is the meaning of "I lift my eyes to the parents, to my teachers and makers…": once a person removes from himself all his own interests, he recognizes clearly that nothing is, God forbid, devoid of His light. Sod Yesharim (Purim 11): The salvation of the Blessed One need not come from another place: in the very place that seems bad to a person's perception, there the Blessed One can show him all the good, in the manner of the verse, "I lift my eyes to the mountains — from where will my help come? My help is from the Lord": once a person comes to [recognize] that his help is from the Lord, he finds in his heart all the help, right there with him.,
And as it is written: "I lift up my eyes to the mountains..." and so forth,
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח):
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 68):
הַהוֹרִים — לִמְאַלְּפַנַי וּלְמַעְבְּדַנַי,
"The mountains (heharim) are the parents (hahorim)—those who instruct me and produce me";
פֵּירוּשׁ: הַמּוֹחַ הוּא הָרַב הַמְלַמֵּד חָכְמָה לָאָדָם,
meaning: the mind is the master who teaches wisdom to man,
וְהַלֵּב הוּא הָאָב הַמּוֹלִיד כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה,
and the heart is the father that generates the powers of action,
וּמֵאַיִן יָבוֹא עֶזְרִי מֵהֶם?
and whence can my help come from them?
רַק "עֶזְרִי מֵעִם ה'..." וְגוֹמֵר.
Only: "My help comes from Hashem..." and so forth.
שָׁמַיִם רוֹמֵז לִשְׁלֵמוּת הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וְזַכּוּתָהּ,
Heaven alludes to the perfection and purity of wisdom in the mind,
כַּאֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶה "כְּעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר",
when it is "like the very essence of heaven for purity",
וָאָרֶץ — לִשְׁלֵמוּת כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה,
and earth alludes to the perfection of the power of action,
שֶׁ"הָאָרֶץ לְעוֹלָם עֹמֶדֶת" וּבְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵמוּת כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה.
for "the earth stands forever" and embodies ultimate endurance in action.
וְזֹאת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה כֹּחוֹת הַלָּלוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּתָם,
And the Blessed Name establishes these powers in their fullness;
מִמֶּנּוּ עֶזְרִי בְּכֹחוֹת הַלָּלוּ.
from Him is my help in these very faculties.
וּמִמֵּילָא "אַל יִתֵּן..." וְגוֹמֵר,
Consequently: "He will not suffer..." and so forth,
גַּם רַגְלְךָ — שֶׁהוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר פְּחוּתָה שֶׁבְּךָ — גַּם כֵּן "לֹא יִמּוֹט",
even your foot—which is the lowest rung in you—likewise "shall not falter",
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "עֹשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ",
for the Blessed Name is the "Maker of heaven and earth",
הַיְנוּ נְפָשׁוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת בְּמַעֲלָה וּנְפָשׁוֹת קְטַנּוֹת הַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ,
meaning exalted souls and lowly souls are all from Him,
וְאִלּוּ רָצָה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה מֵהָרֶגֶל רֹאשׁ,
and had He willed, He could have made the head from the foot,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה רֶגֶל,
only that He willed that this be a foot,
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין לוֹ נַפְקָא מִנַּהּ בֵּין רֶגֶל לְרֹאשׁ,
and if so, before Him there is no difference between foot and head,
וְאַף בְּתַכְלִית שִׁפְלוּתְךָ הוּא עִמְּךָ.
and even at the very depth of your lowliness He is with you.
וְאָמַר: "אַל יִתֵּן..." וְגוֹמֵר "אַל יָנוּם..." וְגוֹמֵר,
And Scripture says: "He will not suffer..." and "He will not slumber...",
כִּי בְּכֹחוֹת הַשֵּׂכֶל יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת טָעוּת,
for in the faculties of intellect error can occur,
בְּאֹפֶן שֶׁכָּל הַהַנְהָגָה בְּטָעוּת,
in such a way that one's entire conduct is led astray,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "אַל יִתֵּן..." וְגוֹמֵר,
and concerning this it says: "He will not suffer...",
שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחַ לְךָ לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּטָעוּת וְלִטְעוֹת בְּשִׂכְלְךָ,
that He will not permit you to conduct yourself in error and stumble in your intellect,
וּלְזֶה צָרִיךְ עֵזֶר בַּהַתְחָלָה.
and for this one needs divine aid right at the start.
וּבְכֹחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת כִּשָּׁלוֹן אוֹ עֲיֵפוּת וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
And in the faculties of action there can be failure, weariness, or the like,
וְצָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה וּזְרִיזוּת עַד גְּמַר הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל,
requiring protection and alacrity until actual completion in deed,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "אַל יָנוּם..." וְגוֹמֵר.
and regarding this it says: "He will not slumber...".
הַיְנוּ דְּהַגַּם שֶׁהָאָדָם כְּמִתְנַמְנֵם,
That is: even though a person may be like one dozing,
וּבְעֵת הַתְּנוּמָה לֵב אֵין, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and at the time of slumber the active heart is absent, as is known,
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לִהְיוֹת נִצָּב קַיָּם עַל עָמְדוֹ,
for it is impossible for a person always to remain firmly on his spiritual station;
וּבְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעֻלָּה הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת בַּלֵּב בַּהַתְחָלָה חָזָק,
and in every undertaking and action the awakening in the heart is strong at the beginning,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְחַלֵּשׁ,
and afterward weakens;
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה: "גּוֹל אֶל ה' מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וְיִכֹּנוּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶיךָ",
and the counsel for this is: "Commit your works to Hashem, and your thoughts will be established",
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ מִתְנַמְנֵם,
because the Blessed Name does not slumber.
וְהוּא כְּטַעַם "אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר",
And this is like: "I sleep, but my heart is awake",
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה,
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Shir HaShirim Rabbah,
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי..." וְגוֹמֵר,
as it is stated: "The rock of my heart..." and so forth,
וְהוּא עֵר לָתֵת חַיּוּת בִּפְעֻלּוֹתָיו שֶׁפּוֹעֵל כְּמִתְנַמְנֵם.
and He is awake to supply vitality to the deeds a person performs while dozing.
וּתְנוּמָה הִיא קַלָּה, דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְעָנֵי
Slumber is light, such that if they call him he answers

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסָחִים קכ408 Pesachim 120b — What are the circumstances of dozing? Rav Ashi said: Asleep and not asleep, awake and not awake — such that when they call him he answers, but he cannot return a reasoned reply, and when they remind him of a thing he recalls it. Rashbam: ["A reasoned reply":] in a matter that requires reasoning — for instance, when they ask him, "Where did you put this vessel?" [he cannot answer]; but when they remind him, "You put it in such-and-such a place," he remembers and says yes or no. עַמּוּד ב).
(as written in Pesachim 120b).
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁאָמַר "שֹׁמְרֶךָ" לְיָחִיד בִּפְרָט, דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְעָנֵי,
Therefore, when Scripture says "your Guardian" to an individual in particular, he answers when called,
שֶׁכְּשֶׁמְּעוֹרְרִים וּמַזְכִּירִים אוֹתוֹ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמְרוֹ מִדְכַּר וְיָדַע מִזֶּה וּמַרְגִּישׁ,
for when one awakens him and reminds him that the Blessed Name guards him, he recalls and knows this and feels it,
אֶלָּא דְּלָא יָדַע לְאַהֲדוֹרֵי סְבָרָא,
only that he cannot return a coherent reasoned reply,
פֵּירוּשׁ: לְהִתְעוֹרֵר בְּמַיִין נוּקְבִין כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
meaning: to awaken feminine waters (mayin nukvin) opposite it,
הַיְנוּ בְּחֵשֶׁק וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא מִפְּאַת הַתְּנוּמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
namely in longing and an awakening from below, due to the dozing in the heart—
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "אַל יָנוּם" לְבַד.
regarding this it says: "He will not slumber" alone.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר עוֹד יוֹתֵר:
And afterward Scripture states even more:
דְּהִנֵּה אֱמֶת נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר כִּי "לֹא יָנוּם..." וְגוֹמֵר,
that it is truly firm that "He shall neither slumber nor sleep...",
בִּכְלַל "שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל" בִּכְלָלוּת,
encompassing the "Guardian of Israel" as a collective whole;
וְהַיְנוּ בְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְלָא עָנֵי,
and this refers to deep sleep when they call him and he does not answer,
שֶׁאֵין מַרְגִּישׁ כְּלָל שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמְרוֹ וּמַנְהִיגוֹ,
when he has no felt awareness at all that the Blessed Name guards and guides him,
שֶׁיִּצְדַּק לוֹמַר "שֹׁמְרֶךָ",
such that it could personally be said "your Guardian";
עִם כָּל זֶה, גַּם בְּעֵת שֵׁינָה כָּזוֹ,
nevertheless, even in such deep sleep,
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "לֹא יִישָׁן" וְלִבּוֹ עֵר.
the Holy One, blessed be He, "shall not sleep," and his true heart remains awake.
וְלָכֵן הִקְדִּים "יָנוּם",
Therefore Scripture mentioned "slumber" first;
הֲגַם דְּגַבֵּי שֶׁאֵין נָם — תְּנוּמָה קוֹדֶמֶת,
even though for one who does not sleep, slumber naturally comes first,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁאֵין יָשֵׁן,
and all the more so he does not fall into deep sleep,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַר הַכַּוָּנָה כְּלַפֵּי הַנִּשְׁמָרִים:
nevertheless, the primary focus is directed toward the ones being guarded:
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נְקֻדַּת עֹמֶק לִבָּם בֶּאֱמֶת,
for the Blessed Name is the innermost core of their heart in truth,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵן מִתְנַמְנְמִים, אָז שַׁיָּךְ עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְשׁוֹן "לֹא יָנוּם",
and when they are dozing, the phrase "He will not slumber" applies to the Blessed Name;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵן אַחַר כָּךְ יְשֵׁנִים,
and when they are subsequently in deep sleep,
שַׁיָּךְ לוֹמַר עַל צוּר לְבָבָם דְּ"לֹא יִישָׁן",
it applies to the Rock of their heart that "He will not sleep",
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא "שֹׁמְרֶךָ" וְ"צִלְּךָ עַל יַד יְמִינֶךָ",
because He is "your Guardian" and "your shadow at your right hand"—
פֵּירוּשׁ: לְמַעְלָה מִמִּדַּת חַסְדְּךָ וְטוּבְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה חָפֵץ לְהֵיטִיב לְךָ,
meaning: far beyond the measure of your own kindness and good with which you desire to benefit yourself,
הוּא רוֹצֶה בְּטוֹבָתְךָ עוֹד יוֹתֵר.
He desires your good even more.
"יוֹמָם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ..." וְגוֹמֵר,
“The sun by day…” and so forth,
שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק לְךָ רוֹב טוֹבָה וְלֹא רוֹב וְכוּלֵי,
that an excess of good shall not harm you, nor an excess of... and so forth,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת מז סוֹף עַמּוּד א)409 Yevamot 47a — And just as they inform him of the punishment for the commandments, so they inform him of their reward. They say to him: Know that the World to Come is made only for the righteous, and that Israel at the present time are unable to bear either too much good or too much punishment. Rashi: "Not too much good": because the evil inclination pursues them, as we say in Tractate Sukkah (52b), and perhaps they would grow haughty over it and sin. Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, on "so they inform him of their reward"): That is, the righteous have a portion in both worlds: their principal reward, in the World to Come, is for the righteous alone, and they also have a portion in this world, except that in this world they cannot receive either too much punishment or too much good, as Rashi explains; the wicked man, by contrast, receives much good in this world in order to drive him out of the World to Come entirely. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 15): One must ask why they cannot receive too much good at the present time: what prevents it? The explanation is that if Israel received much good in this world, Israel's level would be a physical one; but it is not so, for Israel cleave to the divine level that is not physical, and so they cannot receive too much good in the physical world. Likewise they cannot receive too much punishment, because of that divine level, which will not abandon them entirely so that they be cast off and forsaken, since they are prepared for the World to Come, and in this world a man must prepare himself for the World to Come; therefore they must be kept in existence in this world.:
and as our Sages of blessed memory said (Yevamot 47b):
יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל רוֹב וְכוּלֵי.
Israel in this world cannot receive an excess of... and so forth.
כִּי "ה' יִשְׁמָרְךָ..." וְכוּלֵי "צֵאתְךָ וּבוֹאֶךָ",
For "Hashem will guard..." etc. "your going out and your coming in",
הַיְנוּ יְרִידָה וַעֲלִיָּה,
meaning descent and ascent,
וּפָתַח בְּ"יוֹמָם" וְאַחֲרָיו "לַיְלָה" — הַיְרִידָה וַחֲשֵׁכוּת,
and Scripture begins with "by day" followed by "by night"—the descent and darkness,
וְאָז נִקְרָא "יוֹצֵא" וְחוֹזֵר וּ"בָא".
and then one is termed "going out" and returning and "coming in".
וּבְכָל עֲלִיּוֹת וִירִידוֹת וַעֲלִיּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם בְּכָל מֶשֶׁךְ יְמֵי חַיָּיו,
And in all ascents, descents, and renewed ascents that a person experiences throughout his days,
הַכְּלוּלִים בִּכְלַל "מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם"
which are all encompassed within "from now and forevermore"
[עוֹלָמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹבֵל הַגָּדוֹל],
(the world of the Great Jubilee),
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמֵר נַפְשׁוֹ לְבִלְתִּי יִמּוֹט וְיִכָּשֵׁל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
the Holy One, blessed be He, guards his soul so that it will not falter and stumble, Heaven forbid,
אַחַר שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר בַּהַתְחָלָה "מֵאַיִן יָבוֹא עֶזְרִי",
once he recognizes at the outset: "whence shall my help come",

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה410 Sukkah 52a-b — R. Yitzchak said: A man’s evil inclination overcomes him every day, as it is said, “only evil all the day.” R. Shimon ben Lakish said: A man’s evil inclination overcomes him every day and seeks to kill him, as it is said, “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to slay him”; and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not withstand it. Rashi (s.v. "the Lord will not leave him in his hand"): It is written immediately after ["The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to slay him"]. Maharsha (s.v. "a man's inclination overcomes him"): In the first chapter of Kiddushin [30b] the reading [of R. Yitzchak's statement] is "renews itself upon him." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 48): The evil inclination in man is the deficiency and privation that clings to existing things, and this privation seeks to deprive man of existence and diminish him entirely, were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, who upholds existing things and sustains them, and therefore does not let the power of privation prevail. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 8): Of himself Jacob said "the God who has shepherded me," for he had nothing through his own effort, only what the Blessed One illumines for him; and he said "From where will my help come? My help is from the Lord." Fear that comes from a person's own side, when he takes to heart that the King of kings stands over him, may not endure, for "a man's inclination overcomes him every day" and renews itself against him every day; but the trait of Jacob, upon whom fear falls from the side of the Blessed One, endures forever. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 8): When a person breaks his heart and repents, the book of his sentence is torn; yet he still needs the help of the Blessed One to complete every level of repentance fully, so that his inclination, which overcomes him every day, will not hold him back, as they said, "were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not withstand it." This concerns the future, of which it is said "I will heal." (סֻכָּה נב עַמּוּד ב):
as our Sages of blessed memory said (Sukkah 52b):
יִצְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
"A person's evil inclination renews itself every day... and were it not that the Holy One helps him...",
אָז הַמִּשְׁפָּט בַּעֲבוּר הַכָּרָה זוֹ,
then the divine judgment, on account of this very recognition—
הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל בִּתְנוּמָה וְשֵׁינָה,
even when he is in profound concealment, in dozing and deep sleep,
רַק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֱמוּנָה לְבַד, שֶׁלֹּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ,
clinging only by way of simple faith without the active revelation of his heart—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִדַּת לַיְלָה בְּיוֹם מְחֻבָּר יַחַד,
nevertheless, the attribute of night is joined together with day,
לִהְיוֹת אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה דְּבוּקִים,
so that truth and faith cleave together,
לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הָאֱמֶת וְהַבֵּרוּר שֶׁבַּלֵּב גַּם כֵּן בַּסּוֹף עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
to bring about the revelation of truth and the clarification in the heart at the end at all events,
וּמִמֵּילָא הַמִּשְׁפָּט תֵּיכֶף לְעָזְרוֹ לְגַמְרֵי.
and automatically the divine decree acts immediately to help him completely.

sections.en: Remembering and Erasing Amalek

items.h: Amalek thrives on forgetfulness and spiritual slackening; remembrance restores Torah strength and ultimately uproots the deepest roots of vanity and corrupt imagination.

Seif 1 — Erasing Amalek from Memory and Imagination
Remembering Amalek strengthens Torah and uproots first overt corruption, then the hidden fantasies from which it grows.

p: עִנְיַן מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּצְטַוֵּוינוּ עַל זֶה בְּ"לֹא תִשְׁכָּח411 Deuteronomy 25:17-19 — “Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, as you came out of Egypt — how he met you on the way and cut down all the stragglers at your rear, when you were faint and weary, and he did not fear God. Therefore, when the Lord your God grants you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; you shall not forget.” Rashi: "Remember what Amalek did to you" — if you falsify weights and measures, be anxious about the provocation of the enemy, as it is said, "A false balance is an abomination to the Lord," and immediately after it, "When insolence comes, then comes disgrace." "Who happened upon you on the way" — an expression of chance; another explanation, an expression of cold, for he cooled you and made you lukewarm before the nations after your boiling heat. "You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" — man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, so that the name of Amalek should not be mentioned even of a beast, to say, "This beast belonged to Amalek." Ramban: The correct interpretation is that you are not to forget what Amalek did to us until we blot out his remembrance from under the heavens, and that we are to relate it to our children and to our generations, saying to them: "Thus did that wicked one do to us, and therefore we have been commanded to blot out his name."",
The matter of blotting out Amalek, which we were commanded with "do not forget" (Deuteronomy 25:19),
נִלְמָד מִזֶּה שֶׁהַדָּבָר נָקֵל לָבוֹא לִידֵי שִׁכְחָה.
we learn from this that the matter is prone to easily slip into forgetfulness.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר עֲמָלֵק,
For this is the very essence of Amalek,
שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי רִפּוּי יָדַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
who attacks due to the slackening of hands from words of Torah,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו412 Sanhedrin 106a — What is the meaning of the word "Rephidim"? R. Eliezer says: Rephidim was the name of the place. R. Yehoshua says: That they slackened [rippu] themselves from words of Torah, as it is said, "The fathers do not turn to their children, from feebleness [rifyon] of hands." Rashi: [The Gemara] cites Rephidim because R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua disputed the meaning of "Shittim" just above, and they disputed Rephidim in the same manner. "The fathers do not turn to their children" — to do them good — "from feebleness of hands" in Torah and commandments; so too "Rephidim" is feebleness of hands: because they slackened their hands from the Torah, Amalek came upon them. Maharsha: "They slackened themselves from words of Torah" means that they desecrated the Sabbath, which is equivalent to the entire Torah, as is evident in [Shabbat, chapter] Kol Kitvei; R. Yehoshua too agrees that this was the place's name, in accordance with the plain sense of the verse, but holds that it was so called on account of "slackness of hands." Rashi's explanation that in the prooftext too the feebleness of hands is from Torah is forced, for that verse is said of the downfall of the Philistines, and what has Torah to do with them? Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 106a): They dispute Rephidim just as they dispute Shittim: R. Eliezer, who says that was its name, holds that since man is a bodily being he is prone to sin of himself, while R. Yehoshua holds that a person comes to sin only because he turns away from the words of Torah. At Rephidim the sin was not of the body, like the harlotry at Shittim, but of the intellect — saying "Is the Lord among us?" — and according to R. Yehoshua they came to that sinful thought through turning away from the Torah, which is of the intellect. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:65): A salvation that begins in the heart in smallness draws some error along with it: so before the giving of the Torah there was at Marah a slight opening of the light of words of Torah, and through it they came to error and to slackness of hands from words of Torah at Rephidim. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 10): In the wilderness, when the time had come for the revelation of the Written Torah, Amalek attacked Israel to cancel their acceptance of it. This was at Rephidim, so named because they slackened themselves from words of Torah, and it was Amalek who cast that slackness of hands from words of Torah upon them, because he knew that through the giving of the Torah he would be entirely nullified..) עַל רְפִידִים,
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin 106a) concerning Rephidim (from rifui yadayim),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כָּל הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים וְגוֹמֵר עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ וְגוֹמֵר" –
and as it is written: "all that were feeble behind you, etc., faint and weary, etc."—
פֵּירוּשׁ, בְּלֹא כֹּחַ לְהִתְאַמֵּץ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
meaning lacking the strength to exert oneself vigorously in words of Torah.
כְּשֶׁבָּא לִידֵי רִשּׁוּל,
When one falls into laxity,
אָז תֵּיכֶף גּוֹבֵר כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק בַּלֵּב,
then immediately the power of Amalek overpowers within the heart,
שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which is the force that causes forgetfulness of the truth of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּמַגְבִּיר כָּל מִינֵי דִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים שֶׁל הֶבֶל וְשֶׁל דִּמְיוֹן שֶׁהֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת.
and inflates all manner of vain fantasies and illusory musings that run directly contrary to Truth.
וְדָבָר זֶה נִרְאֶה בְּחוּשׁ,
And this phenomenon is perceived empirically through the senses:
שֶׁתֵּיכֶף עַל יְדֵי רִפּוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גּוֹבֵר הַדִּמְיוֹן בַּלֵּב,
that immediately upon slackening from words of Torah, illusion surges in the heart,
וְלָמַדְנוּ מִזֶּה שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק,
and we deduce from this that such is the quintessential root of Amalek,
שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לָבוֹא תֵּיכֶף בְּרִפּוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
whose modus operandi is to strike instantaneously upon the slackening from words of Torah.
וְנִקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
And he is called "the first among nations" (Numbers 24:20),
כִּי כָּל שִׁבְעַת עֲמָמִין הֵם שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
for all seven Canaanite nations embody the seven negative emotional traits manifest within one's outward heart at least,
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לָהֶם הַכָּרָה גַּם כֵּן בַּנִּגְלֶה בְּפָנָיו,
and consequently they also possess recognizable expression visibly upon one's countenance,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "הַכָּרַת פְּנֵיהֶם עָנְתָה בָּם",
in accordance with what Scripture states: "The look of their countenance witnesses against them" (Isaiah 3:9),
שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁהוּא כְּבָר בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ הָרוֹשֶׁם נִיכָּר בַּפָּנִים,
for that which is already overtly active in the heart leaves an imprint discernible upon the face,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ, צ"ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב וְעוֹד בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת.
as written in the Zohar, end of Parashat Lech Lecha, 96b end, and in several other places.
אֲבָל הָ"רֵאשִׁית" הוּא מַה שֶּׁאֵין בּוֹ גִּילּוּי,
However, the "first/beginning" is that which has no outward manifestation,
וְהֵם הַהִרְהוּרִים וְהַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת
and these are the subconscious musings and fantasies
שֶׁהֵם אֵינָם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב כְּלָל,
which do not emerge into the overt conscious heart at all,
רַק שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ בָּא וְנִמְשָׁךְ לִרְצוֹנוֹת רָעוֹת דְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב.
save that through them one is subsequently drawn toward the corrupted desires of the seven traits manifest in the conscious heart.
אֲבָל הָרֵאשִׁית הוּא הַדִּמְיוֹן,
Yet the foundational beginning is illusion itself,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּקְרָא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא".
which is the entire fountainhead of evil in this physical realm, termed "the World of Falsehood."
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בְּשׁוּב [ה' אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן הָיִינוּ] כְּחֹלְמִים",
And it is stated (Psalms 126:1): "When Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers,"
חֲלוֹם הוּא דִּמְיוֹן שֶׁקֶר,
for a dream is a false illusion,
שֶׁכֵּן כָּל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and such is this entire earthly existence.
וְצָרִיךְ כֹּחַ וְהִתְאַמְּצוּת,
And one requires fortitude and vigorous exertion,
וְהָעִיקָּר לִזְכּוֹר תָּמִיד מִזֶּה וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁכּוֹחַ,
and the essential task is to remember this perpetually and not forget,
כִּי זֶה כָּל כֹּחַ הַדִּמְיוֹן – לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ,
for the entire power of illusion is to induce forgetfulness,
וְצָרִיךְ לִזְכּוֹר שֶׁיִּתְאַמֵּץ נֶגֶד זֶה.
and one must actively remember so as to exert himself against it.

וְזֶהוּ "מִלְחָמָה לַה' וְגוֹמֵר413 Exodus 17:16 — “And he said: For a hand is on the throne of the Lord — the Lord shall have war with Amalek from generation to generation.” Rashi: "For a hand is upon the throne of the Lord" — the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, was raised to swear by His throne that He would have war and enmity with Amalek forever. And since the word for "throne" is written short and the Divine Name is split in half, He swore that neither His Name nor His throne is complete until the name of Amalek is wholly blotted out. Ramban: He cites Rashi's reading, and then gives as the plain sense the explanation of others: when a hand is upon the Lord's throne — that is, when a king of Israel sits upon the throne of the Lord — there shall be war for the Lord against Amalek. This is a hint to Saul, the first king, and "from generation to generation" means that every king of Israel is bound to fight them until they are blotted out.",
And this is "Hashem has a war with Amalek from generation to generation" (Exodus 17:16);
שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הוּא מִדַּת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
the Four-Letter Name (Havayah) embodies the attribute of Truth belonging to Jacob,
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן,
which is the absolute antithesis of illusion,
רַק הַהַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה לְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים בַּאֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
being the crystal-clear perception granted to all creations regarding His ultimate reality, blessed be He.
וְזֶה הַשֵּׁם הוּא נִלְחָם בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר עִם שׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל הַדִּמְיוֹן לְכַלּוֹתוֹ מִן הַלֵּב,
And this divine Name wages battle across every generation against the root of illusion to eradicate it from the heart,

כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְכוּלֵי (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא414 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 11 — R. Levi said in the name of R. Acha bar Chanina: So long as the seed of Amalek is in the world, neither the Name is whole nor the throne is whole; once the seed of Amalek has perished, the Name is whole and the throne is whole. What is the proof? "The enemy is finished, in ruins forever" (Psalms 9:7); and what is written after it? "But the Lord sits enthroned forever, He has established His throne for judgment" (Psalms 9:8) — behold, the Name is whole and the throne is whole. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 79): That [Jacob and the angel] raised dust up to the Throne of Glory alludes to "the Throne is not complete until the seed of Amalek is blotted out": the throne alludes to fear [of Heaven], through which desire is conquered, and as a throne is the king's seat, nothing can hold the "sitting" of the Blessed One — that is, apprehend His reality — except the conquest of the desires, for desire is a screen that keeps one from apprehending the spiritual. So when the Throne is complete, Amalek is blotted out and the power of Esau is nullified; and "the Name is not complete" is stated first, alluding to the Torah, which is entirely names of the Holy One, blessed be He. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): So long as the evil inclination is in the world, all influences from above must also come in modesty and concealment because of the accusers, and this is why "the Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete." The first two letters of the Name are the hidden things, the concealed unity that is not revealed — hence "This is My name l'olam" is written [to conceal] — for so long as the seed of Amalek, the root of evil in the world, exists, the attachment of the Congregation of Israel to their Father in Heaven cannot be revealed, since he always finds claims and accusation; and "the Throne is not complete" because "the Master (Aluf) of the world" [the letter alef] is hidden and concealed — the hidden light. Sod Yesharim (Rosh Hashanah 1): As a flame has no hold or existence without its bond to the coal, so the Blessed One, as it were, established that His will should have no completeness without Israel, since only through their service is His will completed — as the Sages said, "the Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete." That is, there will be no completeness without the service of Israel within the boundaries of this world.).
for the Name is not complete nor the Throne complete until Amalek is erased (Midrash Tanchuma, end of Parashat Ki Teitzei).
פֵּירוּשׁ, כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּשְׁלֵימוּת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה מוֹרֶה לִשְׁלֵימוּת כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת
The explanation is: as is known, the wholeness of the Name Havayah signifies the perfection of all the sefirotic attributes

מֵרֹאשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עַד סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רנח סוֹף עַמּוּד א415 Zohar 3:258a — The tefillin of the Master of the world — that is Keter. And what is the Keter of the Master of the world? It is YHVH: yud is Chokhmah, heh is Binah, vav is Tiferet, which comprises the six sefirot, heh is Malkhut. And therefore, "Who is like Your people Israel," "For what great nation is there that has God near to it, as the Lord our God is whenever we call upon Him" — the four are all inscribed in the kaf of Keter, which is comprised of ten sefirot from above downward and of ten sefirot from below upward.).
from the zenith of Thought to the culmination of Deed (Zohar Part III, 258a end).
וּשְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת רוֹמְזוֹת עַל שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
And the first two letters (Yud-Hei) allude to the three supernal sefirot (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah),
וְשָׁם אֵין שְׁלִיטָה לַעֲמָלֵק,
and there Amalek possesses no dominion whatsoever,
שֶׁהוּא רַק "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
for he is merely "the first among nations",
שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת דְּרַע וְאֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת לְשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת דְּטוֹב.
through whose agency the seven corrupt traits are drawn down while suppressing the revelation of the seven holy traits.
אֲבָל הָרֵאשִׁית דְּטוֹב שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלָם –
However, the primordial Source of goodness, which is transcendent and concealed—
וּבַנֶּעְלָם בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹב, וְאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לִשְׁלוֹט כְּלָל
within that concealed realm it is intrinsically good, leaving him no room to hold sway at all,
רַק מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא הַנִּגְלֶה;
save from the perspective of this physical world which constitutes manifest reality;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַנֶּעְלָם הֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ אֵין רַע כְּלָל.
whereas from the perspective of the hidden realm, in ultimate reality there is no evil at all.
וְכָל שְׁלִיטַת הָרַע הוּא מִצַּד הַגָּלוּי וְלֹא מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם,
And the entire dominion of evil operates exclusively on the plane of the manifest, not within the transcendent concealment,
וְלָכֵן שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת הַמּוֹרוֹת עַל הַגָּלוּי אֵין נִשְׁלֶמֶת.
and therefore the final two letters (Vav-Hei) that denote the manifest realm remain uncompleted until his defeat.

וְ"אֵין נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף" (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג416 Bava Batra 123b — R. Chelbo asked R. Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, "And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph" (Genesis 30:25) — what was different once Joseph was born [that Jacob then asked to return home]? He said to him: Jacob our father saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, as it is stated: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for straw, and they shall kindle in them and consume them" (Obadiah 1:18). Rashbam: "What was different" — why he did not wish to return to his father's house until Joseph was born. Maharsha: By acquiring the birthright and taking the blessing from Esau it was granted to Jacob that he should rule over Esau, who was the elder; and all of this Jacob handed on to Joseph, as is derived from "And I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite" (Genesis 48:22). It is in this way that the seed of Esau was delivered into the hand of Joseph and was not delivered into the hand of his other brothers. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Batra 123b): This matter — that the seed of Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph — is exceedingly deep. Over the seed of Joseph the eye has no power, while Esau's blessing is the opposite of this, as it is said, "and the hands are the hands of Esau" (Genesis 27:22) — for the hands are the most outward of the limbs, the rest being within. The seed of Joseph therefore prevail, because their blessing is from a place and a level over which Esau's eye has no power; whereas the other tribes, whose blessing was from the revealed level, could not overcome the power of Esau, which is itself revealed. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 58): Esau, who belongs only to this world, is called 'aluf', a captain of a thousand (the utmost of this world's blessing), but not the rank of a king who endures forever. Therefore Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, who was "ruler over all the land of Egypt": a ruler, that is, a minister and chief of the same pattern as 'aluf', like Messiah son of Joseph, who is at the rank of ruler and is slain, having no everlasting endurance, which belongs only to David. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The obstinacy of Israel issues from wisdom, through the knowledge that joins wisdom to the powers of action, and is obstinate only for the honor of Heaven; therefore Amalek falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek is the root of obstinacy, his chief claim being against the desires of Israel, as the Sages said on "who happened upon you"; but his obstinacy is against the will of the Blessed One, whereas the obstinacy of Joseph's seed accords with the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Of Amalek it is said, "and he feared not God," and the Sages said that this is why he falls into the hand of the seed of Joseph, of whom it is said, "I fear God." And though "he feared not God" refers to Israel, it means [that it came upon them] through Amalek "who happened upon you," who brought into them imaginings and forces of forgetfulness, whereby they became "faint and weary" and did not fear God. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph because, as the Sages said, "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven": fear of Heaven is the province of man's choice and effort, for love can come into a person's heart of itself, but fear cannot. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eira 1): Before Benjamin's birth Jacob was given tidings of Benjamin, Menashe and Ephraim, who are Amalek's adversaries, as the Gemara says that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek stands against the holiness of the covenant (they would cut off the circumcisions of Israel), while Menashe and Ephraim are Joseph's two tribes, and Benjamin too is the attribute of the Tzaddik; therefore the name E-l Sha-dai, which corresponds to the attribute of the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world, is mentioned there. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 38): On account of Rachel's modesty the Holy One, blessed be He, restored [the birthright] to her, in that every beginning of salvation is aroused through her children. Thus every beginning of salvation is revealed through the children of Rachel, as the Gemara says that Jacob saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. Sod Yesharim (Purim 15): If Israel rely on the strength they possess from their root, Amalek at once stands against them, claiming that he too has strength from the root, being born of Isaac and Rebecca. Therefore the Sages said that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph: the seed of Joseph rely on no strength at all, but clarify wherever there is something to clarify, and where the power of their service does not reach, there the Blessed One will clarify it for good.:),
And "Amalek falls only by the hand of the offspring of Joseph" (Bava Batra 123b),
שֶׁחֲלוֹמוֹתָיו הָיָה אֱמֶת,
for Joseph's dreams were pure truth,
דְּגַם דִּמְיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ אֵינוֹ כּוֹזֵב;
in that even his imaginative faculty was never deceptive;
וְהַגַּם שֶׁהוּא דִּמְיוֹן מֵהִרְהוּרָא דְּלִבָּא,
and even though a dream is an imaginative projection stemming from the musings of the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ אֶחָיו: "הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
as his brothers challenged him: "Will you indeed reign over us, etc." (Genesis 37:8),

רַק שֶׁדְּיוֹקְנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל אָבִיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פד417 Bereshit Rabbah 84:8 — "And Israel loved Joseph." R. Yehudah and R. Nechemiah: R. Yehudah says, because the radiance of his features resembled his own. R. Nechemiah said, because all the laws that Shem and Ever transmitted to Jacob, he transmitted to him.).
except that his countenance bore the likeness of his father's image (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 84).
וְהַחֲלוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנֶּאֱמָר בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And the first dream recorded in the Torah belongs to our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אֱמֶת שֶׁהֵיפֶךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן,
who is the primal root of Truth, the antithesis of illusion;
אֶצְלוֹ שַׁיָּיךְ לְסַפֵּר מִדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ, כִּי גַּם דִּמְיוֹנוֹ הוּא רַק אֱמֶת,
with him it is fitting to speak of his imaginative realm, for even his imagination was absolute truth,
שֶׁכֵּן בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ: "וְהִנֵּה ה' נִצָּב עָלָיו וְגוֹמֵר" – שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה.
for so it was in his dream: "and behold, Hashem stood above him, etc."—the Name Havayah.
וְהַחֲלוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי בְּיוֹסֵף,
And the second set of dreams belongs to Joseph,
וְהוּא רַק דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ;
and he reflects only the likeness of his father's image;
כִּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל דִּמְיוֹנוֹתָיו גַּם כֵּן רַק בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד,
for with our father Jacob, peace be upon him, all his imaginations were likewise occupied solely with the ultimate reality of Hashem alone,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל הִרְהוּרָיו;
this forming the entirety of his inner musings;
אֲבָל יוֹסֵף דִּמְיוֹנוֹתָיו כְּכָל דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם,
whereas with Joseph, his dreams resembled the ordinary imaginative faculty of human beings,
אֲשֶׁר רוּבָּם בְּהִשְׂתָּרְרוּת וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת,
most of which dwell upon dominion, lordship, and self-elevation,
שֶׁבָּזֶה נִמְשָׁךְ כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדִּמְיוֹן
whereby the entire root of worldly illusion is drawn forth,
שֶׁבָּא מִכֹּחַ שְׁבִירָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמַּחֲשֶׁבֶת "אֲנָא אֶמְלוֹךְ" כַּנּוֹדָע.
emanating from the cosmic Shattering of the Vessels (Shevirat HaKelim) originating from the primordial thought "I will reign", as is known.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ: "הֲמָלֹךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is what his brothers said to him: "Will you indeed reign, etc.",
וְתַרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס: "אַתְּ מְדַמֵּי וְגוֹמֵר";
which Onkelos translates into Aramaic: "Do you imagine that you will rule over us..."
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיוּ דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שָׁוְא, שֶׁהֲרֵי הָיָה כָּךְ.
yet in truth these were not vain illusions, for behold, it literally unfolded as envisioned.
וְזֶהוּ נִיצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק:
And this is the defeat of Amalek:
לֹא עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטָה עַל הַדִּמְיוֹן לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְדַמֶּה וִיהַרְהֵר רַק אֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ –
not through completely obliterating the imagination such that one never imagines anything outside of Hashem's pure truth—
שֶׁזֶּה מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא מֵת,
for that is the sublime level of Jacob our father who never died,
שֶׁאֵין עוֹד מָקוֹם לְמִיתָה כְּלָל מֵאַחַר שֶׁדָּבוּק בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַחַיִּים,
there being no remaining place for death once a soul is cleaved unto the Truth of Life,
וּלְזֶה אָנוּ מְחַכִּים שֶׁ"יְבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת",
and for this we await in the ultimate future when "death will be swallowed up forever",
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק לְגַמְרֵי מִן הָעוֹלָם.
which will transpire when the eradication of Amalek from the universe is complete.
אֲבָל כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא בָּעוֹלָם, נִיצּוּחוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת יוֹסֵף –
However, as long as Amalek still exists in the world, his subjugation is achieved through the attribute of Joseph—
שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת אֱמֶת,
namely, that the imaginative faculties are themselves transformed into truth;
כִּי כָּךְ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁדְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת,
for such is the primal root of Israel who are bound to truth,
וְכָל דִּמְיוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם אֱמֶת;
that all their underlying imaginations are fundamentally aligned with truth;

שֶׁגַּם בְּ"דְּלָא יָדְעֵי בֵּין וְכוּלֵי" (מְגִילָּה ז418 Megillah 7b — Rava said: A man is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until he no longer knows the difference between "cursed is Haman" and "blessed is Mordecai." Rashi: "To become intoxicated" means to become drunk with wine. Tosafos (s.v. "that he does not know the difference between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai'"): In the Jerusalem Talmud [the formula runs]: "Cursed is Zeresh, blessed is Esther; cursed are all the wicked, blessed are all the Jews." Maharsha: There is a righteous man who suffers in this world — one not wholly righteous, who receives his punishment here — and a wicked man who prospers here — one not wholly wicked, so that he may be driven out of the World to Come; but the wholly righteous man is granted both tables, as Mordecai was granted all his greatness in this world too, and the wholly wicked man, like Haman of the seed of Amalek and Esau, loses even this world. "Until he does not know" therefore means that he no longer sets his heart to discern the vast distance between "cursed is Haman," who was wholly wicked and lost both worlds, and "blessed is Mordecai," who was wholly righteous and was granted both worlds. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Even in drunkenness "until he does not know," when he has no understanding to act from, the depths of [a Jew's] heart are steeped in love of Israel. This is the whole clarification of Purim — that Israel's sins and their seeming like all the nations are only external: even when one is intoxicated "until he does not know between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai,'" not recognizing openly the difference between Israel and the nations, they bear no likeness at all and are utterly distinct in the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman's eye was evil toward Israel's festivals, for he did not believe there could be any holiness in bodily enjoyment such as eating and drinking. Hence "a person is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until...": precisely through drunkenness with wine, without conscious understanding, the inner holiness of Israel is made clear — that even their enjoyment of food and drink is in holiness — after the manner of "wine enters, the secret comes out.":),
so that even in the state of "until he knows not between blessed be Mordechai and cursed be Haman" (Megillah 7b),
שֶׁבְּשִׁכְרוּת כָּזוֹ הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁרָחוֹק מֵאֱמֶת לְגַמְרֵי,
wherein during such intoxication one enters the absolute climax of illusion seemingly severed entirely from truth,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)419 Yoma 75a — R. Ami and R. Asi differed. One said: Whoever fixes his eye on his cup — all the forbidden unions seem to him like level ground. And one said: Whoever fixes his eye on his cup — the whole world seems to him like level ground. Rashi: "His eye on his cup": one who loves drunkenness. "The whole world seems to him like level ground": the property of others seems to him permitted. Maharsha: [All the forbidden unions seem level to him] because drinking wine leads to licentiousness, as it is written, "Harlotry and wine and new wine take away the heart" (Hosea 4:11). As for "the whole world," Rashi's "the property of others" means that once he has consumed his own money he seeks to feed his habit with the money of others; and it seems that on this view one should read "whoever sets his eyes on his purse [כיסו]," which is how the verse is written, with a yod — that is, one whose eye is grudging toward his own purse comes to covet the money of others.: "בְּשִׁכּוֹר כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ דּוֹמֶה עָלָיו כְּמִישׁוֹר",
as our Sages stated (Yoma 75a): "to a drunkard the entire world seems like a smooth plain",
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָז מִתְבָּרְרִים שֶׁהֵם אֵין כָּךְ;
yet Israel are then revealed to be fundamentally distinct from this degradation;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה420 Megillah 12b — Rava said: The seventh day was the Sabbath — for when Israel eat and drink, they begin with words of Torah and words of praise; but the nations of the world, when they eat and drink, begin with nothing but words of frivolity.
