for during the feast it is possible to illuminate that trapped holy spark—
הַיְינוּ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַבְּרִיאָה בְּעִנְיַן הַבְּחִירָה וְכֹחַ הָאֶפְשָׁרוּת –
namely Hashem's pristine will at the beginning of Creation regarding free choice and potentiality—
אוֹתוֹ נְקוּדַּת הָרָצוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה יִסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ,
so that this hidden point of divine will departs from him,
וּמִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה נִמְחֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם.
whereby he is automatically blotted out from the world.
וְהָרְפוּאָה שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַמַּכָּה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁתֵּה אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן "עַד דְּלָא יָדְעֵי",
And the remedy preceding the blow operated through the feast of the gentiles likewise 'until they knew not,'
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִסְתַּבֵּב הָרֵאשִׁית לָרֵאשִׁית –
whereby the primordial Beginning turned upon this beginning—
הַיְינוּ סִבָּה לִקְלִיטָה זוֹ דְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁבַּעֲמָלֵק.
generating the catalyst to extract this depth of the Beginning embedded in Amalek.

וְהֵם שְׁנֵי מִינֵי מִשְׁתָּאוֹת: לְכָל הַשָּׂרִים, וְלִבְנֵי שׁוּשָׁן471 Esther 1:3-5 — “In the third year of his reign he made a feast for all his officers and servants, the army of Persia and Media, the nobles and officers of the provinces being before him — when he displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the splendid honour of his greatness for many days, a hundred and eighty days. And when these days were completed, the king made a seven-day feast for all the people present in Shushan the capital, from the greatest to the least, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace.” Rashi: The "partemim" are governors, in the Persian tongue; "many days" means that he made the banquet for them all that time. "Garden" [ginnat] is a place sown with vegetables, and "pavilion" [bitan] is a place planted with trees. Malbim: The banquet was contrived to establish his kingship as unlimited rather than limited: by seating his own officers, servants and the army of Persia and Media ahead of "the nobles and the governors of the provinces" — who had been rulers only "before him," that is, before he conquered them — he showed that he held the throne by his sword and not by their choice. So too he displayed the treasure of the kingdom for a hundred and eighty days as though it were his private wealth and not the realm's, and then feasted all the people of Shushan "from great to small" to show that great and small alike were merely his servants.;
And these correspond to the two feasts: for all the princes, and for the residents of Shushan;
הוּא נֶגֶד שְׁנֵי יְמֵי פוּרִים.
parallel to the two days of Purim.
הָאֶחָד: "בְּהַרְאֹתוֹ אֶת עֹשֶׁר וְגוֹמֵר וְאֶת יְקָר וְגוֹמֵר",
The first: 'when he showed the riches, etc., and the honor (yeqar), etc.',
כִּי "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְגוֹמֵר וִיקָר", דְּכָךְ מַגִּיעַ בְּפוּרִים.
mirroring 'for the Jews there was light... and honor,' for such is attained on Purim.

וְיָדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט עַמּוּד א472 Zohar 3:109a — R. Shimon said: But we find "court" said of that which is written, "And she stood in the inner court of the king's house, opposite the king's house" (Esther 5:1) — and everywhere that "the king" is said without qualification, this is the Holy One, blessed be He. "And she stood" — standing means nothing other than prayer. "Opposite the king's house" — opposite the Temple, for all Israel must offer their prayer toward that place and face the Temple. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): For one who understands, the whole Megillah is the story of the "slumber" of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, from beginning to end. It begins from the feast of Shushan, for from there begins "the king" without qualification rather than "King Ahasuerus," meaning the King of kings of kings who clothed Himself [in him], and the hundred and eighty days before it were the preparation for receiving that clothing of the King of kings of kings. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 13): Haman said, "To whom would the king desire [to do honor]?" — and it is known from the Sages that "the king" without qualification speaks of the King of kings of kings: he thought that he was esteemed by the Blessed One as well, since not for nothing had He made him great and delivered Israel into his hand to destroy them, because they had grown lax in (lit. “slept from”) the commandments, and he imagined that He had chosen him in their stead. It became a mockery afterward, when he heard the king's words that it was Mordechai the Jew in whom he delighted, and that he himself would be a servant before him.):
And known is the teaching of our Sages (Zohar III 109a):
כָּל מָקוֹם "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם – בְּמַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם מְדַבֵּר;
wherever 'the king' is stated without qualification, Scripture speaks of the King of the Universe;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה עָשְׁרוֹ וִיקָרוֹ בְּמִשְׁתֶּה זוֹ,
and Hashem revealed His wealth and precious honor in that feast,

דְּזֶה עִיקַּר הַיְקָר שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה טז473 Megillah 16b — On "The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor," Rav Yehuda expounded: "Honor" — these are the phylacteries, and so it says: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you." And it is taught in a baraita: R. Eliezer the Great says: These are the phylacteries of the head. Maharsha: Among the commandments there are some that serve as a sign and a testimony for Israel — the Sabbath, of which it says "between Me and you," the phylacteries, of which it says "and it shall be a sign upon your hand," [and circumcision, which is the sign of the covenant] — and it was against these in particular that Haman decreed, because they are the testimony of Israel. "Honor" is the phylacteries, which are the glory of Israel, as the verse says "that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you"; and to this they returned, as it is written, "for the fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them." Maharal (Gevuros Hashem 39): The phylacteries teach that Israel belong to the unique Name, for in them the going out from Egypt is recalled, which He brought about by wonders; therefore "they shall fear you," because of His mighty and awesome deeds. R. Eliezer said specifically "the phylacteries of the head" because the phylacteries of the arm express the binding and cleaving of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, and where there is cleaving there is no fear; but in the phylacteries of the head there is no binding, only that His name is called upon them — and in being called "the God of Israel" He is set apart from them, and on that side there is fear, for it is fitting to fear the God of Israel, to whom belongs might. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:40): In front are the tefillin themselves, of which the Sages said, "'And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you' — these are the tefillin of the head," for it is recognizable to all that the name of the Lord is called upon him. But at the back there is no such clear recognition, only the knot of the tefillin, from which the "smallness" that desires for its own sake draws, so that an accuser can claim that it is truly for himself and not for the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 13): "And honor — these are the tefillin of the head": this shows that Israel are bound at the root, above the grasp of human intellect; hence the Sages were precise to say tefillin "that are in the head" and not "that are on the head," for the meaning is that they are bound in the brain. Against this Amalek accused, and since they merited to wipe out Amalek, they merited the aspect of "honor," which signifies attachment at the root, the aspect of Atika. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Vezos HaBerachah): Tefillin allude to strength and boldness for Israel, as it is written, "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you," and the Gemara says, "These are the tefillin of the head." Therefore [Elisha, "the man of wings,"] was filled with strength and boldness to go out wearing tefillin [despite the decree], trusting that if the quaestor saw him he would fear him, and that he would thereby know he had acted according to the will of the Blessed One. Beis Yaakov (Vayetzei 72): Jacob's dealings with the sheep were a compelling and overcoming of the sitra achra, so as to bring [what it held] into holiness; and, as the Zohar says, the work of the rods is the secret of tefillin, for tefillin allude to triumph, as it is written, "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you," and it is taught: "R. Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin of the head." Sod Yesharim (Purim 1): "And honor — these are the tefillin": in the tefillin of the Master of the world it is written, "For what great nation…," that is, tefillin are a garment for His light — the light of His will is clothed in this mitzvah, and when a person dons them he can attain His light that is clothed in them; and they allude to all the deeds of the mitzvos, in which a person can dig and reveal the light that dwells within them. Amalek denies this, saying that all these things are what the Ancient of Days covered so that there should be concealment, and that it is not His will to reveal the concealment in this world.:): "תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ",
this being the essence of honor which our Sages expounded (Megillah 16b): 'the tefillin of the head,'
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַמּוֹחַ שֶׁדָּבוּק בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית, זֶה דָּבָר יָקָר,
meaning that which transcends the brain cleaving to the depth of the Beginning, this being most precious,
כִּי כָּל נֶעְלָם הוּא יָקָר;
for all that is concealed is precious;
הֲגַם שֶׁבַּנִּגְלֶה הָיָה רָשָׁע זֶה עוֹשֶׂה מַרְזֵיחִין.
even though openly this wicked one was conducting corrupt revelry.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה474 Esther Rabbah 1:10 — “In those days” — this is one of the places where the ministering angels brought their petitions before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying before Him: Master of the Universe, the Temple lies in ruins, and this wicked man sits and holds his feasts? He said to them: Set days against days. This is what is written: “In those days I saw in Yehudah men treading winepresses on the Sabbath.” (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֶסְתֵּר פָּרָשָׁה א עַל פָּסוּק "בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם"):
And our Sages expounded (Esther Rabbah 1 on the verse 'in those days'):
"תְּנוּ יָמִים כְּנֶגֶד יָמִים",
'render days corresponding to days,'
"בַּיָּמִים הָהֵמָּה וְגוֹמֵר דּוֹרְכִים גִּתּוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת" –
referencing Nehemiah 13:15: 'in those days saw I in Judah some treading winepresses on the Sabbath'—
פֵּירוּשׁ, עוֹשִׂים יַיִן שֶׁלֹּא כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ מִשְׁתֵּה יַיִן זֶה.
meaning they produced wine contrary to Hashem's will, whence this drinking feast was drawn forth.
וְהֵם חִלְּלוּ שַׁבָּת שֶׁרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת,
And they desecrated Shabbat wherein Hashem's will is to rest,
דִּקְדוּשַׁת הַיּוֹם נִקְרָא הֶעְדֵּר מְלָאכָה,
for the holiness of the day is defined by cessation from creative labor,
כִּי הַיּוֹם וְהַזְּמַן עִיקָּר לִהְיוֹת "יֵצֵא אָדָם לְפָעֳלוֹ וְגוֹמֵר", וְהַיּוֹם לִמְלָאכָה, וּבָזֶה הוּא כָּל הַגְבָּלַת הַזְּמַן;
since weekday time is designated for 'man goes forth unto his work,' being bounded by time;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שַׁבָּת דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ מְלָאכָה, לֹא נֶאֱמַר "וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר",
whereas on Shabbat where labor does not apply, 'there was evening and there was morning' is omitted,
כִּי הוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְסֵדֶר זְמַנִּים.
being an inkling of the World to Come which transcends temporal order.
וְגַם יוֹם טוֹב הוּא דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי", לִהְיוֹת הַיּוֹם קָדוֹשׁ כְּעֵין שַׁבָּת;
Festivals likewise operate through 'Israel sanctifies,' rendering the day holy like Shabbat;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן פּוּרִים, יוֹם טוֹב לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ,
unlike Purim, where they did not accept the cessation of labor of Yom Tov,
דְּאֵין קְדוּשַׁת הַיּוֹם לֵיאָסֵר בִּמְלָאכָה;
there being no sanctity bound to the prohibition of work;
כִּי מִן הַדַּעַת וְאֵילָךְ הֵם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁהֵם נִקְרָאִים מִדּוֹת שֶׁהֵם בַּעֲלֵי גְּבוּל
for from Da'at downward extend the seven sefirot, termed 'measures' because they possess boundaries
וְהֵם שִׁבְעָה יָמִים וּבָהֶם שַׁיָּיךְ קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם;
corresponding to the seven days wherein the sanctity of a day applies;
אֲבָל בְּרֵאשִׁית, שָׁם אֵין נִקְרָאִים יָמִים כִּי אֵינָם תַּחַת הַגְּבוּל.
whereas in the Beginning they are not called 'days,' transcending all limitation.
וְכֵן כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם בְּיִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו עַל סֵדֶר נָכוֹן וּבִגְבוּל וְקֶצֶב לְכָל דָּבָר כָּרָאוּי;
Likewise, when a person is in settled consciousness, all his actions follow proper order with boundaries and measured limits;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּשִׁכְרוּת אֵינוֹ תַּחַת הַגְּבוּל, יוּכַל לְפַזֵּר יוֹתֵר מִיְּכֹלֶת אָדָם וְכַיּוֹצֵא, כִּי אֵינוֹ תַּחַת הַסֵּדֶר.
unlike in intoxication where he is unbounded, distributing charity beyond normal mortal ability, standing above structured order.
וְזֶהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת פּוּרִים: לְמַעְלָה מִסֵּדֶר זְמַנִּים וְיָמִים,
And this is the sanctity of Purim: soaring above the order of times and days,
וְאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ יוֹם טוֹב וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם כְּלָל;
where the standard restriction of a festival does not apply;
וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְקַן מַה שֶּׁחִלְּלוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם,
and automatically that which desecrated the sanctity of the day was rectified,
כִּי זֶה הַחִלּוּל הוּא רַק מִצַּד סֵדֶר הַזְּמַנִּים, וְיֵשׁ יוֹם מִיָּמִים דְּמָארֵי צָבֵי בֵּיהּ;
for desecration exists only relative to the temporal framework, where one specific day is favored by the Master;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא לְמַעְלָה מִסֵּדֶר יָמִים.
unlike when one ascends above the temporal order of days.
וְזֶהוּ "תְּנוּ יָמִים כְּנֶגֶד יָמִים" –
And this is 'render days corresponding to days'—
לְעוֹרֵר מִשְׁתֵּה מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁתֵּה הָאֻמּוֹת;
awakening the feast of the King of the Universe through the feast of the nations;
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂהוּ בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין, כָּךְ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת קְלִיטָתוֹ לְטוֹב.
for this matter, just as its action unfolded unintentionally, so is its extraction for good awakened.
וְהַתְחָלַת הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת עַל כָּל פָּנִים הוּא בָּא מִדַּעַת אָדָם,
And the beginning of the awakening at least originates in human consciousness,
כְּמוֹ מִשְׁתֵּה פוּרִים שֶׁהָאָדָם רוֹצֶה לִשְׁתּוֹת לְקַיֵּים מִצְוַת חֲכָמִים;
like the Purim feast where a person intentionally sets out to drink to fulfill the rabbinic mitzvah;
הֲגַם דְּאַחַר כָּךְ לֹא יָדַע בֵּין וְכוּלֵי, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהַתְחָלָה הוּא בְּדַעַת.
so even though afterward he knows not, the initiation occurs with conscious intent.
וְזֶהוּ אַחַר הַהֲרִיגָה בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר וּמָחוּ עֲמָלֵק בַּפּוֹעַל.
And this took place following the battle on the thirteenth, blotting out Amalek in actual deed.
אֲבָל הָרְפוּאָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַמַּכָּה,
However, regarding the remedy that preceded the affliction,
בָּא הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת דְּמִשְׁתֵּה מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁתֵּה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וַעֲשִׂיַּת מַרְזֵיחִין דְּרֶשַׁע;
the awakening of the feast of the King of the Universe arrived via the feast of Ahasuerus and the revelry of the wicked;
וּמִזֶּה נִתְקַן דְּרִיכוֹת גִּתּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְנַעֲשָׂה מִזְּדוֹנוֹת זְכִיּוֹת,
and through this the treading of winepresses on Shabbat was rectified, deliberate sins turning into merits,
לִהְיוֹת אוֹתָן גִּתּוֹת יַיִן לְמִשְׁתֵּה מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
transforming those presses into wine for the feast of the King of the Universe.
וְנִמְצָא הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת – הַיְינוּ הַתְחָלַת הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי הֲרִיגַת וַשְׁתִּי – בָּא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁתֵּה אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עַצְמָן,
Thus the initial awakening—the beginning of rectification through the execution of Vashti—came through the feast of the nations themselves,
וּכְעִנְיַן גִּיּוּרֵי עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא דַּוְוקָא עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן
paralleling the spontaneous conversion of Amalek's descendants which occurs solely by their own initiative,
וְלִהְיוֹת בָּא מִמֵּילָא וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי כַּוָּנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
emerging automatically without the conscious agency of Israel.
וּמִשְׁתֵּה שׁוּשָׁן הוּא נֶגֶד שׁוּשַׁן פּוּרִים,
And the feast of Shushan corresponds to Shushan Purim,
וּבָהּ הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן שֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן, לְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְעוֹרֵר הַמִּשְׁתֶּה דְּמַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לְמַעְלָה.
and in it the Jews of Shushan were likewise present, since the supernal feast of the King of the Universe had already been stirred Above.
וּמִשְׁתֵּה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֵלּוּ כְּבָר הָיָה הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן הָרְפוּאָה שֶׁנִּבְנֵית בְּשִׁבְעָה יָמִים,
And this seven-day feast was already the beginning of the structure of the remedy built in seven days,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ קֶצֶב שֶׁקָּצַב לְכָל דָּבָר, בִּנְיַן קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה צָרִיךְ שִׁבְעָה יָמִים;
which is the set measure: the erection of a complete stature requires seven days;
וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי "כְּטוֹב לֵב וְגוֹמֵר", אָז הוּא נִשְׁלָם,
and on the seventh day 'when the heart of the king was merry with wine,' it was completed,
וּלְכָךְ אָז נִתְעוֹרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּשְׁתֶּה.
and therefore Israel were then stirred to be present at the feast as well.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַגָּוֶון הָיָה חֵטְא שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ וְכוּלֵי,
Yet nonetheless its outward guise was a sin in that they derived pleasure, etc.,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין הַתִּיקּוּן מִצַּד הַדַּעַת רַק מִצַּד הַלֹּא-דַּעַת;
for the rectification operates not through conscious Da'at but through non-Da'at;
וְרַק עַכְשָׁיו נִגְלָה הַדָּבָר לִהְיוֹת מִצְוָה בַּפּוֹעַל לִבְסוֹמֵי וְהַהַתְחָלָה בְּדַעַת,
and only now is the matter revealed to be an active mitzvah to become intoxicated, beginning with Da'at,
כִּי כְּבָר נִתְקַן הַהַתְחָלָה אָז בִּימֵי מָרְדֳּכָי.
because that beginning was already rectified back in the days of Mordechai.
אֲבָל אָז שֶׁהָיָה הַהַתְחָלָה, הָיָה גָּוֶון חֵטְא,
However, then when it was the initial stage, it bore the guise of sin,
וְהֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים,
and they acted merely for outward appearance,
כִּי רַק בַּגָּוֶון נֶהֱנוּ מִסְּעוּדַת הָרָשָׁע,
for only outwardly did they enjoy the banquet of the wicked one,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת נֶהֱנוּ מִסְּעוּדַת מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
whereas in inner truth they were delighting in the banquet of the King of the Universe.
כִּי מִשְׁתֶּה זוֹ הִיא מִשְׁתֵּה מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
For this feast is the feast of the King of the Universe,
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי בְּכָל הַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁלְּמַטָּה יֵשׁ גָּוֶון זֶה לְמַעְלָה אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן,
for certainly regarding all mitzvot below there is a corresponding dimension Above with Hashem as well,
כְּטַעַם: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנִּיחַ תְּפִלִּין, וְכֵן כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת;
mirroring the teaching: Hashem dons tefillin, and so with all commandments;
וְכָךְ סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים וַדַּאי יֵשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ,
and so the festive meal of Purim certainly possesses a celestial root,
וְהַתְחָלַת אוֹתָהּ מִצְוָה הוּא מֵאוֹתוֹ זְמַן.
and the inception of that mitzvah dates from that very time.
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה יָדְעוּ דְּהַתְחָלַת נֵס דְּפוּרִים וְהַתְחָלַת סִפּוּר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא מִמִּשְׁתֵּה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
And the Men of the Great Assembly knew that the inception of the Purim miracle and the opening of the Megillah's chronicle begins with the feast of Ahasuerus,
כִּי אָז הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַמִּצְוָה וּקְדוּשַּׁת מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה דְּפוּרִים.
for then was the beginning of the mitzvah and the sanctity of feasting and joy of Purim.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁעִיקָּרוֹ בְּלֹא דַּעַת,
Only because its essence is rooted in non-Da'at,
נִגְלָה מִקּוֹדֶם לַפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּנַפְשׁוֹת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
it was first manifested in action in this world within the souls of the nations,
כְּכָל קְלִיפָּה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַפְּרִי;
just as every husk precedes the fruit;
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הַמִּשְׁתֶּה הוּא מִשְׁתֵּה מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
yet the true core of the feast is the feast of the King of the Universe.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה475 Esther Rabbah 2:5 — Rav Chanina bar Atal said: Jews were present at that feast. That wicked man said to them: Can your God do more for you than this? They said to him: “No eye has seen a god beside You” — if He were to make for us a feast like this one, we would say to Him: We have already eaten at the table of Achashverosh. (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֶסְתֵּר פָּרָשָׁה ב עַל פָּסוּק "וּבִמְלֹאת הַיָּמִים"):
And this is what our Sages expounded (Esther Rabbah 2 on the verse 'and when these days were fulfilled'):
שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: אִם יִהְיֶה סְעוּדָה דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא כָּךְ?
that he asked: will the banquet of the Future Era be like this?
וְאָמַר לוֹ: "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה וְגוֹמֵר",
And he answered him: 'eye has not seen, etc.'
כְּבָר אֲכַלְנוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ;
we already consumed it in the days of Ahasuerus;
הַיְינוּ דִּסְעוּדָה זוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה מֵעֵין סְעוּדָה דִּלְעָתִיד מִצַּד שֶׁהִיא סְעוּדָתוֹ דְּמַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
meaning that this meal was truly an inkling of the Future Banquet inasmuch as it was the banquet of the King of the Universe.
רַק אָז יִהְיֶה "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה" –
Only that in the future it will be 'eye (ayin) has not seen'—
פֵּירוּשׁ, "עַיִן" – גָּוֶון, כְּמוֹ "כְּעֵין הַבְּדֹלַח",
the definition of ayin being color/appearance, like 'the appearance (ke-ein) of bdellium,'
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם גָּוֶון אַחֵר בִּסְעוּדָה זוֹ רַק "אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתְךָ",
meaning that there will be no alien hue at that banquet, solely 'God beside You,'
"צַדִּיקִים יוֹשְׁבִין וְכוּלֵי וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו וְכוּלֵי", וְלֹא שׁוּם גָּוֶון אַחֵר;
'righteous sit and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah,' without any other color;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הָיָה גָּוֶון אַחֵר,
unlike in the days of Ahasuerus where an alien guise cloaked it,
דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁעֲמָלֵק בָּעוֹלָם אֵין הַשֵּׁם וְהַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם וְהוּא בִּלְבוּשׁ.
for as long as Amalek exists in the world, neither the Name nor the Throne is complete, remaining enclothed in outer garments.
וְכָל סִפּוּר הַכְּתוּבִים וּדְרָשׁוֹת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִשְׁתֶּה זוֹ
And the entire biblical narrative and rabbinic homilies regarding this feast
הוּא מִצַּד מִשְׁתֵּה "הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם – בְּמַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
are framed from the perspective of 'the king' unspecified—Scripture speaking of the King of the Universe,
אֵיךְ הֵם חַדְרֵי סְעוּדָה שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
revealing the inner banquet chambers of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאֵין לְהַאֲרִיךְ כָּעֵת יוֹתֵר לְפָרֵשׁ כָּל פְּרָטֵי הַדְּבָרִים.
and I will not elaborate further here on all the details of these matters.

sections.en: Israel among the Nations

items.h: Exile places Israel like a rose among thorns; through the seven spiritual powers, their inner distinction from the nations is clarified even amid outward similarity.

Seif 1 — The Rose among the Thorns
Exile clarifies Israel's inner difference from the nations through the seven powers that structure both soul and world.

p: כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת הֵם אָז בְּרִחוּק מִן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
When Israel are among the nations they are then in a state of distance from Hashem, blessed be He,

וְאָז נִמְשְׁלוּ כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים476 Song of Songs 2:2 — “As a lily among the thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters.” Rashi: The thorns pierce the lily, yet it goes on standing in its beauty and its redness. "So is my beloved among the daughters" — they entice her to run after them and stray after other gods as they do, and she stands firm in her faith. Metzudas Dovid: The beloved sends word to her: it is true that you are like a lily, and I will add to your praise — set against all the other maidens you are like a lily standing among thorns, which no one can come near to handle and spoil its form. So too you, for all the beauty in you that inflames men's hearts to pursue your love, let no one draw near you; the lesson is that though all the idolaters entice Israel to walk in their ways and join them, she will not consent and will not listen to them. Malbim: The beloved answers: among the daughters of Jerusalem you are like a lily among thorns, for the stalk on which the lily grows is full of thorns, and if it mingles with them they pierce it and ruin it, so it must carry its head above them and not mix with them. So must you take care that the daughters of Jerusalem do not entice you to the love of Solomon..
and then they are likened to a rose among thorns.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה477 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:3 — “Hedged about with lilies” — these are words of Torah, which are as tender as lilies. R. Levi said: It is the way of the world that a man marries a wife at thirty or at forty, and after he has spent what he has he comes to be intimate with her; and she says to him, I have seen something red — and he at once separates from her. Who caused him not to approach her? Was there a wall of iron between them? Was there a pillar of iron between them? Did a serpent bite him, or a scorpion sting him, that he should not approach her? Words of Torah, tender as a lily — for it is said of her, “And to a woman in the impurity of her separation you shall not approach.” (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ז, ג) עַל פָּסוּק "סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים":
As our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:3) on the verse "hedged about with roses" (Song of Songs 7:3):
"כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה אֲדֻמָּה וְכוּלֵי",
"Like a red rose, etc.,"
שֶׁזֶּה רוֹמֵז עַל עֵת נִדּוּת וּזְמַן הָרִחוּק דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבַּעְלָהּ.
that this alludes to the period of menstrual separation and the time of distance of the Congregation of Israel from her Husband.
וְהַיְינוּ בְּעֵת הַחֵטְא, דְּאָז נִקְרָאִים גַּם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת "בָּנוֹת" לְמַרְאִית עַיִן, בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַשֶּׁפַע הוֹלֵךְ לָהֶם.
And that is during the time of sin, when even the idolaters appear to outward sight as "daughters," divine abundance flowing unto them in this world.
אֶלָּא דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם "אַתְּ רַעְיָתִי",
Yet nevertheless "you are My beloved",

וּמִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה דְּ"סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים478 Sanhedrin 37a — A certain heretic said to Rav Kahana: You say that a woman in the state of niddah may be secluded with her husband — is it possible to place fire against tow and have it not blaze? He said to him: The Torah has testified concerning us, “hedged about with lilies” — that even a hedge of lilies they do not breach. Rashi (s.v. "blaze"): Catch hold and burn. Rashi (s.v. "hedged about with lilies"): Fenced about with lilies — that is, at a light warning and a slight separation they hold back from transgression and need no fence of stones to divide them: even when they are not far from the transgression, and only a fence of lilies stands between them, they do not break through it. Tosafos (s.v. "the Torah testified concerning us, 'hedged about with lilies'"): The verse is expounded of menstrual blood: as soon as she says, "I saw blood like a red lily," he separates from her. As for how a verse from the Writings can permit seclusion, which the Torah forbids: the Torah forbade only [seclusion with] one like his mother, who can never become permitted, whereas a niddah will in the end become pure — though where he has not yet had relations with her, even a niddah is forbidden in seclusion (Ketubot 4a). Maharsha: A hedge of lilies is named because a person is drawn to uproot and breach that very hedge to enjoy the lilies' fragrance. The heretic would not have accepted this answer unless the verse itself spoke of menstruation, so it appears that the whole verse speaks of it, close to its plain sense: "your navel" is the source of her blood, whose regular period comes monthly like the moon, "a round goblet"; "your belly is a heap of wheat" is the pain of pregnancy and childbirth, decreed on account of the wheat that Eve ate; and in these days of niddah and childbirth she is "hedged about with lilies." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 37a): Israel were given the Torah above all the nations and are fit for it, because they are close to accepting statute and fence; therefore even a hedge of lilies they do not breach. Not so the other nations, who are creatures of matter, and matter is subject to change, so they do not keep statute and fence, whereas Israel are likened to form; the reverse of this is at times for ill, for Israel are a stiff-necked people, far from repentance, since they stand firm and do not change their deeds, while the nations, bound to changeable matter, are closer to repentance." (סַנְהֶדְרִין לז.),
and a man is secluded with his menstruant wife through the hedge of roses (Sanhedrin 37a),
וְלָכֵן "אֲנִי ה' הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם"
and therefore "I am Hashem Who dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness"

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא נו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב וְסִפְרֵי סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת מַסְעֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם479 Yoma 56b — "That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity" (Leviticus 16:16) — even when they are impure, the Divine Presence rests among them. [And in the Sifrei, at the end of Masei:] "In whose midst I dwell" (Numbers 35:34) — beloved are Israel, for even though they are impure the Divine Presence is among them. R. Natan says: Beloved are Israel, for wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went with them. Maharsha (Yoma 57a, s.v. "now you are certainly impure"): [The Sadducee] meant: even if you were once pure, now in exile you have certainly become impure, as it is written, "Her impurity is in her skirts," and He separates Himself from you as one keeps apart from the impurity of a menstruant. [R. Chanina] answered him from what is written of them, "that dwells with them [in the midst of their impurity]," that He does not separate entirely, but as a man keeps apart from his wife while she is a menstruant yet lives with her in one house; so the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells with us even now in exile, as it is said, "I will be with him in distress." Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 4): The Blessed One does not dwell in the midst of their impurity unless the sin was unwitting, and of that it is written, "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity." [Hence the First Temple, whose distinction was that the Divine Presence rested in it,] was destroyed when they defiled the Sanctuary through idolatry, sexual immorality and bloodshed, the three sins that are called impurity. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1): The Divine Presence does not depart even toward evening, in the time of darkness, as it is likewise said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity." For the souls of all Israel are bound and linked together as in a chain, so that the revelation of the Divine light — in concealment, hiddenness and great contraction — is not absent from the heart of any Jew; even the lowest of the low has in him a portion of life, a portion of God from above. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Regarding spiritual holiness it is said, "who dwells with them amid their impurity," and "the Divine Presence never departed from the Western Wall": in concealment it never departed, even in every kind of sinking into evil bitterer than death — "I will fear no evil, for You are with me." We suppose this a deficiency, but in truth it is the strength of completeness and the ultimate clarification: that wherever a person sinks, his heart remains bound to the Blessed One with a bond that cannot be severed. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The Holy One, blessed be He, as it were entered Egypt, the place of impurity, and this was the great miracle and the first of the miracles: the clarification of "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity," from their beginning and root in the Patriarchs, who are truly holy seed with no connection to any impurity, so that it was revealed that impurity has no real existence. Esther is the end: even in the lowest levels, where the nations hold sway, the Blessed One is with them, even in the place of impurity's greatest strength, as when Esther entered the house of Ahasuerus. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Raising the holy sparks out of the matters of this world, by engaging in them for the sake of Heaven, is like a king's son returning from captivity, whose joy exceeds that of one who was always in the palace; of this it is said, "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity" — amid it precisely. Over this that wicked one [Bilaam] was blinded when he spoke of "the fourth of Israel" and said "He who is holy…," for he did not know that there is holiness even in bodily matters. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): So too the souls of Israel outside the Land are like the Tabernacle [dismantled in order to be rebuilt], for the Blessed One dwells with them amid their impurity and His Presence is within the hearts of Israel: wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went into exile with them, and that place became their place. Through the exile they gather in the bit of good among the nations and return it all to holiness, and that place too becomes sanctified with the holiness of the air of the Land of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Even when sin caused Israel to be exiled among the nations, outside even the holiness of the Land, wherever they were exiled the Divine Presence went with them — for even "in the lands of their enemies I have not rejected them," and "I am the Lord who dwells with them amid their impurity." Nonetheless they are never separated from the root of holiness, and in the end all will be redeemed, even those wholly assimilated among the nations.);
(as written in Yoma 56b end, and Sifrei end of Parashat Masei, see there);
רַק "אִתָּם" וְלֹא "בְּקִרְבָּם", דְּהַיְינוּ קֵירוּב בָּשָׂר;
only "with them" and not "within them," which denotes physical intimacy;
אֲבָל "אִתָּם" רָצָה לוֹמַר יִחוּד, זֶהוּ מִצַּד שׁוֹשַׁנָּה, הִיא רַעְיָתִי וַחֲבֶרְתִּי לִהְיוֹת יַחַד.
however "with them" denotes mystical union, stemming from the rose: she is My beloved and companion to dwell together.
וְזֶהוּ כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, דּוּגְמַת דַּם נִדּוּת בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא מִתּוֹלָדָה וְטֶבַע הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן.
And this applies to all the sins of Israel, mirroring menstrual blood in a woman which is of nature and the fabric of Creation so to be.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנִדָּה (לא480 Niddah 31b — It is taught: R. Meir would say: Why did the Torah say that a menstruating woman is [forbidden] for seven days? Because her husband grows accustomed to her and becomes weary of her. Therefore the Torah said: Let her be impure seven days, so that she will be as beloved to her husband as at the hour she entered the wedding canopy. Rashi: “A menstruant for seven” — this does not refer to a woman after childbirth. “Because he grows accustomed to her” — [being with her] whenever he wishes; “and becomes weary of her” — she becomes repugnant to him. The Torah therefore said that whenever she sees blood she shall be impure for seven days, so that he not grow accustomed to her and she become dear to him. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “why did the Torah say that a menstruant is for seven”): One day would have sufficed in her days of menstruation, as in the days of ziva, where one who sees blood for a single day need only watch a day against a day; and to this the answer is given, “so that she will be beloved to her husband.” It is for this reason that a menstruant, whose impurity is the beginning of impurity, requires seven days, which is not so with ziva, where she has already become impure.:): שֶׁהוּא כְּדֵי לְחַבְּבָהּ עַל בַּעְלָהּ,
And our Sages of blessed memory stated in Niddah (31b): that it exists in order to make her beloved unto her husband,
וְכָךְ בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּל הַחֲטָאִים וִימֵי הָרִחוּק.
and so it is with the Congregation of Israel regarding all sins and days of distance.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט481 Shabbat 89b — "Though your sins be like scarlet [ka-shanim]" — it should have said ka-shani, in the singular. R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years [shanim] that have come in order from the six days of Creation until now, they shall become white as snow. Rashi: "It should have said ka-shani" [in the singular] — parallel to "as snow," for it does not say "as snows." Maharsha: "Like these years that are ordered" refers to the multitude of sin — as many as the years, presumably the years that have run in order since the six days of creation. One cannot read ka-shanim as "like two years," the minimal plural, for what novelty would there be in two sins? We say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah that He removes the first [sin] first, so for two sins "they shall be white as snow" would not be needed. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 89b): Sin is open to atonement because it is committed by accident, and the accidental does not annul what a person is in essence; but sins committed in great number and constantly are no longer accidental, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, says that even if your sins are ordered and fixed like these years, they shall be white as snow. Nothing is more fixed and ordered than the years, which have run so since the six days of creation, yet even they will cease, since the world is physical and will end in destruction; so too Israel's sins, though fixed on the side of the physical, can be removed, because Israel's essential level is not physical. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 19): The holiness of Tisha B'Av in the future, when it becomes a festival, will not come from Israel's sanctifying it, for on the contrary they sinned and made it a day of calamity, but only because in the future "your sins will be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," as stated in Shabbos 89b: then "they shall be white as snow" and be turned into merits, through this, that such was the will of the Blessed One from the six days of creation. Thus the essence of its holiness is only that this was the Blessed One's will at the beginning of creation, a holiness fixed and abiding like the holiness of Shabbos, except that it is revealed only in the future, after the rectification. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): "The scarlet [shanim] shall be white as snow" means that the scarlet of holiness, too, will be whitened, after they lift their eyes to the Blessed One, as stated in Shabbos there; and the sins will be "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, like merits; and afterwards they will rise still further, to the supernal whiteness, which is Wisdom, above Understanding. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 17): The deed itself is ordered and set so, as "Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of creation," and in truth this will be clarified in the future regarding all the sins of Israel, when they are refined and whitened, as the Sages said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow." That is, since the true will of the Blessed One was so, it is like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): In the future this will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel, as the Sages said in Shabbos 89b on the verse "If your sins be": "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation" — it will be clarified that it was ordered from the true will of the Blessed One that it be so, and if so, in this too they did the will of the Blessed One, and it was all like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Naso 2): Such was the intent in the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," as the Zohar says, there is no light but that which comes out of darkness; and then "the Lord will not count iniquity to him," since it will be clarified that this was created only so that it be "very good." As they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow," that is, they will be as merits. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): From the side of the hidden things that will be revealed in the future there was no sin at all, and of this they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, from the side of the "hidden things of the Merciful One," then "they shall be white as snow" entirely, for there is no sin at all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei 31): Snow alludes to fear, and so the Gemara says, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation until now, they shall be white as snow": "years" alludes to cycles and order, that is, if there is an accusation, Heaven forbid, and it seems that a person sinned deliberately and in [recurring] cycles, the Blessed One will illuminate that this deed came only out of fear of the Blessed One, and this is "white as snow.":): "כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית",
And this explains what they said in Shabbat (89b): "Like these solar years that are prearranged and arrive from the six days of Creation,"
כִּי הֵם מְסוּדָּר בְּסֵדֶר הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּךְ.
because they are set in the cosmic design of Creation to be so.
וְהַתְחָלַת הַזֹּהַר הוּא מִפָּסוּק זֶה עַל פָּסוּק "בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא וְגוֹמֵר", יְעֻיַּין שָׁם.
And the opening of the Zohar begins from this verse upon "In the beginning God created, etc.", see there.
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה עַל עִנְיָן זֶה,
For the inception of Creation was for this purpose:
כִּי לִהְיוֹת רַק צַדִּיקִים עוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ הֲרֵי כְּבָר יֵשׁ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת,
for to have only the righteous executing His will, there already exist the ministering angels;
וְתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה הָאָדָם הַמּוּכָן לַחֵטְא,
and the purpose of Creation was man who is prone to sin,
רַק הַמְכֻוָּון הוּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם בַּחֲטָאִים גַּם כֵּן כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה,
save that the target of design is the Congregation of Israel, who amidst their sins are likewise like a rose,
שֶׁהוּא עֵשֶׂב גָּדֵל בֵּין הַחוֹחִים אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא נָאֶה וּבַעַל רֵיחַ טוֹב.
which is a plant growing among thorns, yet beautiful and fragrant with sweet aroma.

וְכָךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו" – רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו (סַנְהֶדְרִין לז482 Sanhedrin 37a — R. Zeira said: From here — "And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him" (Genesis 27:27): do not read "his garments [begadav]" but "his traitors [bogedav]." Tosafos (s.v. "and he smelled the smell of his garments"): "Smell" is a term that belongs to menstrual blood, as we say at the end of chapter Kol HaYad (Niddah 20b): a certain woman brought blood before R. Elazar; he smelled it and said, "This is blood of desire." Maharsha: Jacob was certainly perfectly righteous, but he was now wearing the garments of the wicked Esau, which Esau had coveted from the wicked Nimrod, and how many bloodstains from the murders of these wicked men were on them; yet when Jacob came before his father even these garments gave off a good fragrance, as it is said, "and he smelled the smell of his garments," for the fragrance of the Garden of Eden entered with him. This is a sign for his children, that even the traitors among them give off a fragrance through the commandments, as with the bloodstains of niddah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 37a): The garments allude to the empty ones: garments are secondary to the man, and so the empty ones are not the essence of "man" — for the righteous are always likened to man, and Israel, being more righteous than the nations, are called "man" (Yevamot 61a); therefore the wicked are likened to garments, which are not the man himself and are far from him. The good deed that the empty ones do for the sake of Heaven is called "smell" because smell reaches from far away, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, smells the commandments of the empty ones, who are far from Him; further, smell is associated with the attribute of judgment, and the empty ones, who subdue their inclination with great strength and wage war against it, belong to that attribute. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Esau's heart was full of crookedness, and only through the dimming of his eyes could Isaac think well of him; through that same dimming he afterwards did not recognize Jacob either, but he smelled "the smell of his traitors," for even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and there is no room at all to accuse him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:57): Jacob's service was chiefly in intention for the sake of Heaven, and the "garments" of deed began only with Laban, where he began to beget the souls of Israel, who are themselves the commandments of the Torah; hence it says then that [Rebecca] dressed him in Esau's garments. Therefore the Sages read "the smell of his garments" as "the smell of his traitors," meaning, as they said, that even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate: they too have a garment of the deed of the mitzvot. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 10): In Israel the evil stems from the vessels themselves, not from what is drawn out of them, and in the essence of the vessels there is no evil at all; therefore "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": they too give off a good fragrance, as it says, "the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot." As the Sages said of the myrtle, fragrance without taste, so in Israel there are those who have mitzvot but not Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The penitent breaks through every bound and in a single moment can rise from the utmost darkness to great light, which is the good name that spreads from one end of the world to the other; and of this it is said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": once they have returned from [their betrayals], theirs is the chief good fragrance, smelled throughout the whole world. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 5): When Isaac asked, "Are you my son Esau?", he meant that in the smell of his garments he sensed deeds, for which he called him "Esau" [as one who does the will of his Maker]; and the Midrash indeed reads "his garments" as "his traitors." To this Jacob answered "I am": I am the one who performs the deeds of the mitzvot, and what you sensed is the fragrance of Jacob's traitors, for the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and they too give off a good fragrance. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Even when Israel sins, it is like a myrtle standing among reeds, for the essence of a Jew's heart always gives off a good fragrance like the myrtle, as the Sages said on "he smelled the smell of his garments": "the smell of his traitors." The sins are only like thorns surrounding the rose, which prick it for the moment, and in the future this will be made clear in all Israel, when "the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the seed of Jacob none is cast off, for just as evening and morning make one day, so His praise rises from the wicked as from the righteous: even the empty ones of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and the sinners of Israel are full of remorse. Of this the Sages said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors," and Bereishis Rabbah applies it to the likes of Yakim of Tzeroros, who in a brief moment preceded Yose ben Yoezer, a perfect tzaddik who had toiled all his days, to the World to Come; for the penitent attains this in a single moment..), שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם רֵיחַ טוֹב.
And so with Israel: "and he smelled the fragrance of his garments" (Genesis 27:27)—the fragrance of his traitors (Sanhedrin 37a), in that they possess a sweet aroma.
וְאָמַר: "רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
And Isaac said: "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field, etc.",

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית כט483 Taanit 29b — "And he said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed" — R. Yehuda son of R. Shmuel bar Sheilat said in the name of Rav: Like the smell of a field of apples. Tosafos (s.v. "of apples"): Some explain: “apples” — like the fragrance of etrogim. Maharsha: Tosafot's explanation [that the “apples” are like the fragrance of etrogim] accords with the Targum, which renders “as an apple tree among the trees of the forest” as “as etrogim among the trees”; perhaps they explained it so because the Midrashim say that the fragrance of the Garden of Eden that entered with Jacob came from the garments — the garments of Adam, which had been in the Garden of Eden, passed to Nimrod, and were then seized by Esau — and since the tree from which Adam ate was an etrog, the garments had taken on the fragrance of the etrog of the Garden of Eden. Bereshit Rabbah, however, implies that the fragrance did not come through Esau's garments, but that in Jacob's merit the fragrance of the Garden of Eden entered with him, just as, conversely, Gehinnom entered with Esau through his wickedness. Maharal (Gevuros Hashem, ch. 43): The apple has an exceedingly esteemed fragrance, as it is written, “like the smell of the field which the Lord has blessed,” which our Sages said is a field of apples; and fragrance is related to the attribute of judgment, as it is written, “They shall put incense before You” [literally, “in Your nostril,” the seat of wrath]. [He adduces this to explain why the women in Egypt gave birth “under the apple tree” (Sotah 11b): their births were bound entirely to the attribute of judgment, from which birth proceeds.] Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 10): On Shabbos, when all Israel are free for Torah alone, Israel are likened to apples as they were at Sinai and are called "the field of holy apples"; this is "a field which the Lord has blessed" — a field of apples. Therefore on the night after Shabbos we recite the verses "And may God give you," that they may merit to be occupied with Torah on the weekdays as well. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Toldos): "Field" alludes to expansiveness in desires; therefore Esau was called "a man of the field," for he spread himself into every kind of craving and evil lust. But our father Jacob had expansiveness in holiness, and this is "as the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed" — namely, "the field of holy apples." Beis Yaakov (Toldos 42): "A field of apples": the apple denotes life in joy and the shining of the countenance, and "a field of apples" indicates that a person is prepared on his part to receive the light of the Blessed One's countenance in an abundance of joyous life. When a person is not prepared to receive the flow, it is called "the field of Anathoth" [from poverty]; but the light of the countenance, when one can receive it, is called "the field of holy apples." Sod Yesharim (Yom Kippur 1): Wisdom is like a spice that perfumes all refuse so that it takes on a good scent, as with our father Jacob: he came to receive the blessings from Isaac wearing the skins of goat-kids, whose smell is foul, yet when he entered Isaac said, "See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed," for the scent of the Garden of Eden entered with him. So for one who receives from the root of wisdom, everything is turned to good.:): שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים, וַחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין.
and our Sages of blessed memory said (Ta'anit 29b): an apple orchard, the field of holy apples.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי סִיּוּם הַמִּקְרָא "כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן וְגוֹמֵר" קָאֵי גַּם כֵּן אַעֵת הָרִחוּק,
The explanation is: the conclusion of the verse "As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my Beloved among the sons" (Song of Songs 2:3) applies likewise to the season of estrangement,
שֶׁכִּבְיָכוֹל בֵּין עֲצֵי הַיַּעַר, הַיְינוּ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, מִצַּד הַמְכֻוָּון שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּהֶם.
wherein as it were He is among the trees of the wood, namely the idolaters, from the vantage point of Hashem's intention in them.
כִּי מִצַּד עַצְמָן קְרָאָם "חוֹחִים", שֶׁהֵם עֲשָׂבִים גְּרוּעִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם קִיּוּם רַק לְשָׁעָה;
For on their own accord Scripture termed them "thorns," which are inferior weeds possessing mere transient survival;
אֲבָל אִילָנוֹת הֵם הַמִּתְקַיְּימִים מִשָּׁנָה לְשָׁנָה, וְזֶה רוֹמֵז נֶגֶד כַּוָּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְרִיאָתָם וּבְהַשְׁפִּיעוֹ לָהֶם, שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר הַמִּתְקַיֵּים.
whereas trees are those that endure from year to year, and this alludes to Hashem's divine intent in creating them and sustaining them, which is an enduring design.
וְזֶהוּ "כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים", הַיְינוּ הָאַהֲבָה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת לִי לָאַהֲבָה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת לָהֶם;
And this is "so is my Beloved among the sons," meaning the love drawn unto Me compared to the love drawn unto them;

דְּמִמַּה שֶּׁאָנוּ רוֹאִים שֶׁנִּבְרָאִים וּמוּשְׁפָּעִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּטוּב הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, הֲרֵי אָנוּ רוֹאִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּין הַמְשָׁכַת כֹּחוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּגְלִים כֹּחַ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת גַּם כֵּן,
for from what we observe of their being created and endowed with goodness in this world, we see that among the manifest emanations of His power there is a channel sustaining the idolaters as well,
רַק שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת עֲצֵי הַיַּעַר, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן צֹרֶךְ לַבְּרִיאָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֵצִים לְבִשּׁוּל וַאֲפִיָּה וְתִיקּוּן הַמַּאֲכָלִים;
only that it is like trees of the forest, which also serve a cosmic purpose so there be wood for cooking, baking, and preparing food;
אֲבָל עֲצֵי הַמַּאֲכָל מֵהֶם הַמַּאֲכָל עַצְמוֹ הַנִּכְנָס לַחֵךְ.
whereas from fruit trees comes the sustenance itself which enters the palate.
כָּךְ הוּא צֹרֶךְ הָאֻמּוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
Such is the utility of the nations in this world.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּבְעֵת הָרִחוּק נִרְאֶה כִּי הֵם הָעִיקָּר,
And nonetheless, in this world and during the time of distance, it appears as though they are the primary essence,

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ484 Bereshit Rabbah 83:5 — The straw, the stubble and the chaff were disputing with one another. This one said: For my sake the field was sown; and that one said: For my sake the field was sown. Said the wheat to them: Wait until the threshing-floor comes, and we shall know for whose sake the field was sown. When they came to the threshing-floor, the owner went out to winnow it; the chaff was scattered to the wind, he took the straw and cast it to the ground, he took the stubble and burned it, he took the wheat and made of it a heap — and all who saw it kissed it. So too the nations of the world: these say, For our sake the world was created, and these say, For our sake the world was created. Israel say to them: Wait until the day comes, and we shall know for whose sake the world was created. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּשְׁלַח): הַחִטָּה וְהַתֶּבֶן וְהַמּוֹץ מִדַּיְּינִים מִי הָעִיקָּר, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and along the lines of what they stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, end of Parashat Vayishlach): the wheat, straw, and chaff dispute which of them is the primary product, see there.

וְלָכֵן הִמְשִׁיל לְתַפּוּחַ, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה485 Song of Songs 2:3 — “As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. In his shade I delighted and sat, and his fruit was sweet to my palate.” Rashi: An apple tree standing among barren trees is dearer than all of them, for its fruit is good in taste and in fragrance; "so is my beloved among the sons" — among the young men. The comparison is that the Holy One, blessed be He, is chosen out of all the gods, and therefore "in his shade I delighted and sat." Metzudas Dovid: Now she sends words of praise to her beloved: set against the other young men you are in my eyes like an apple tree among the barren trees of the forest, for although the apple tree's shade is the least of them all, it is better than all of them because it bears fruit — and therefore I desired its shade and sat beneath it, since its fruit was sweet to my palate. The lesson is that the Assembly of Israel says: though the pleasure of sin and of the idolaters comes quickly in this world, like the shade of a tree that benefits a man the moment he sits beneath it, I nonetheless withdrew my hand from sin and clung to You, for the fruit of the reward in the World to Come is sweeter to me, late though it comes. Malbim: The beloved replies: among the sons you are like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, which hide it by their height and their many branches; yet it is recognized among them by two things — by its fragrance, for which "in his shade I delighted and sat," to enjoy its good scent, and by its fruit, which is "sweet to my palate." (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב, ג): תַּפּוּחַ זֶה אֵין לוֹ צֵל וְהַכֹּל בּוֹרְחִין בִּשְׁעַת הַשָּׁרָב וְכוּלֵי486 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:3 — “As an apple tree among the trees of the wood.” Rav Huna and R. Acha said in the name of R. Yose ben Zimra: Just as this apple tree — all flee from it at the hour of the heat, because it gives no shade to sit in — so did the nations of the world flee from sitting in the shade of the Holy One, blessed be He, on the day of the giving of the Torah. One might think Israel did so too; therefore Scripture says, “In his shade I delighted and sat” — I delighted in Him and sat. I am the one who delighted in Him, and not the nations.;

Therefore Scripture likened Him unto an apple tree, and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:3): this apple tree provides little shade and everyone flees from it in scorching heat, etc.;
וְהַיְינוּ דַּעֲצֵי יַעַר יֵשׁ לָהֶם צֵל וְנִרְאֶה דְּהֵם צֹרֶךְ יוֹתֵר;
meaning the forest trees cast dense shade and appear of greater necessity;
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים: "בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר", אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ צֵל כָּל כָּךְ, "וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק וְגוֹמֵר",
yet nevertheless Israel declare: "in His shade I delighted, etc.", even though it has sparse shade, "and His fruit was sweet, etc.",
וַאֲנִי מֵבִין וְיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁמִּזֶּה הָעֵץ עָתִיד לִצְמוֹחַ פֵּירוֹת מְתוּקִים לַחֵךְ מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִשְּׁאָר עֲצֵי יַעַר, וְלָכֵן חִמַּדְתִּי צִלּוֹ גַּם בִּשְׁעַת הַשָּׁרָב.
and I discern that from this tree sweet fruit is destined to blossom for the palate, which is not so with other forest trees, and therefore I desired its shade even in scorching heat.
וְזֶה טַעַם בִּרְכַּת יִצְחָק בְּרֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַעֲלָאַת הָרֵיחַ שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת שׁוֹשַׁנָּה, שֶׁהִיא מִין עֵשֶׂב שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִיּוּם,

And this is the rationale of Isaac's blessing regarding the scent of his traitors, which stems from elevating their fragrant scent, resembling the rose, which is an herb with transient physical existence,
וּבִרְכָתוֹ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ ה'", שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר הַמִּתְקַיֵּים, וְגַם כֵּן מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם בֵּין עֲצֵי הַיַּעַר – זֶהוּ שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים.
and its blessing emanates from Hashem as stated "which Hashem has blessed," an enduring entity, and likewise from its concealment among the forest trees—this is the apple field.
וְזֶה סוֹד סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא סְעוּדָתָא דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין,
And this is the mystery of the Friday night meal, the feast of the holy apple field,
שֶׁאָז זְמַן זִיוּוּג קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה,
for then is the union of the Holy One and His Shechinah from the aspect of this world resembling night,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא "אֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי",
corresponding to our father Abraham, peace be upon him, the first of converts, yet who is nonetheless titled "Eitan the Ezrachi (native)",
רַק שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אָז בְּהֶעְלֵם, דְּלֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן לִהְיוֹת "כָּל רֹאֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּם כִּי הֵם זֶרַע וְגוֹמֵר".
save that the name of Israel was then concealed, not yet having reached "all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed, etc."
וּמִמֶּנּוּ יָצָא יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁאֵין נִקְרָא כְּלָל "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר".
And from him issued Ishmael who is not categorized as an apostate Israelite at all.
וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא גָּוֶון הַהִתְדַּמּוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים, וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא גַּם כֵּן עִיקַּר הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּינֵיהֶם.
And from his aspect arises the apparent outward resemblance of Israel to the nations, and from his aspect also stems the fundamental distinction between them.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן שַׁבָּת: קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, בְּלִי שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת פְּעֻלָּתָם מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי",
And this is the essence of Shabbat: the sanctity of Israel which is fixed and enduring, without any self-exertion or human agency of "Israel sanctifies the seasons",
רַק "אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם" – בְּלִי שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלָּכֶם.
only "a sign between Me and you to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you"—without any striving of your own.
וְהַתְחָלָה הוּא גַּם מִצַּד הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהָעֵירוּב בָּעַמִּים, הוּא "כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר";
And the beginning emerges from darkness and mingling among the nations, being "as an apple tree among the forest trees";
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוֹלֵךְ וָאוֹר עַד נְכוֹן הַיּוֹם, אָז הִיא סְעוּדָתָא דְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
and afterward it shines brighter until midday, then being the daytime feast of the Ancient Holy One (Atika Kadisha),
שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשֵּׂכֶל הַסָּתוּם וְנֶעְלָם מֵעֵין אָדָם עַצְמוֹ.
which represents that which transcends hidden intellect, concealed from the eye of man himself.
כִּי מִצַּד אַבְרָהָם הוּא הַבֵּירוּר כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל דּוֹמִים לָעַמִּים, כְּטַעַם "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי" בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
For from the aspect of Abraham comes the clarification when Israel resemble the nations, reflecting "a nation from the midst of a nation" in the Egyptian exile corresponding to our father Abraham.
אֲבָל מִצַּד יִצְחָק הַבֵּירוּר לְהֵיפֶךְ: כַּאֲשֶׁר עַמִּים רוֹצִים לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, from the aspect of Isaac the clarification is the reverse: when the nations seek to mimic and resemble Israel,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה)487 Bereshit Rabbah 65:1 — “Esau was forty years old” — that is what is written: “The boar out of the wood ravages it” (Psalms 80:14). R. Pinchas in the name of R. Simon: Of all the prophets, only two publicized it [the character of the wicked kingdom] — Moses and Asaph. Moses said: “And the swine, because it parts the hoof”; Asaph said: “The boar out of the wood ravages it.” Why does he liken it to a pig? Because just as this pig, when it lies down, stretches out its hooves as if to say, “I am pure,” so this wicked kingdom robs and plunders, yet appears as though it were setting up the seat of judgment. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 3): No convert is accepted from Amalek, meaning that he cannot convert at all: even if he performs the commandments, and not in deed alone but even accepts in thought and will to be a complete Israelite, he is still called only one who "stretches out its hooves like a pig" to say "pure," for the deepest beginning and root of his thought and will, hidden even from himself, is certainly not so, and it is complete falsehood. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 24): So too Esau "stretches out his hooves like a pig": the pig has a sign of purity in its hooves, and of the two signs, which allude to deed and thought, the hooves correspond to deed; these he stretches out, for "the hunt was in his mouth" but not in his heart, saying "see, I am pure." Yet he is not even half pure; rather, whatever lacks the four signs is entirely impure. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 20): In deed, Esau too "stretches out his hooves like a pig," and Amalek is called "the first of nations" because only his deepest beginning is evil: he can stretch out his hooves through all nine levels that unfold from the deepest beginning of thought, appearing as though he too were good, yet his deepest beginning is utterly evil, and so he is wholly evil. With Israel it is the reverse: even one who has sinned, as the Sages said of Achan that he denied the entire Torah, still has his deepest beginning cleaving to the good, and so he is wholly good. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Toward this the preparation is the exile of Edom, of which the Sages said "it stretches out its hooves like a pig and says, I am pure." For the Giving of the Torah is a clarification over against Egypt, which was openly "flesh of donkeys," whereas Edom's revealed aspect is pure; therefore it came from Esau, born of Isaac, with whom holy flesh begins, and so the Sages called Esau "an apostate Israelite," except that he apostatized and became like a complete gentile. For the clarification always comes through its opposite, since in truth Edom is the one entirely lacking purity by birth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): From this side comes the hold of Esau, who "stretches out his hooves like a pig" (that is, his heel), and of whom the Sages said that he "sets up the tribunal," showing himself as righteous, for there are some light commandments among the nations. And although it is also true that "the kindness of the nations is a sin for them," since all they do is only for self-aggrandizement and to stretch out their hooves, nevertheless, from the standpoint of what is revealed in this world, it is not discernible. בְּעֵשָׂו פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו כַּחֲזִיר וְאוֹמֵר: "רְאוּ שֶׁאֲנִי טָהוֹר",
as written (Bereishit Rabbah 65) of Esau displaying split hooves like a swine, saying: "See that I am kosher",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּצֵאתָם מִבָּבֶל בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, דְּכוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ כָּשֵׁר הָיָה, עַד שֶׁכִּפְשַׁט הַכָּתוּב נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "מְשִׁיחוֹ";
and as occurred upon their departure from Babylon in the Second Temple era, for Cyrus was an upright monarch, even termed "His anointed" in the plain sense of Scripture;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה רֵישׁ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בָּזֶה הַחִלּוּק:
yet our Sages stated at the beginning of Rosh Hashanah (4a) concerning this distinction:

בֵּין עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הָעוֹשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ הוּא רָשָׁע בָּזֶה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲרֵי זֶה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר488 Rosh Hashanah 4a — R. Yitzchak said to him: My teacher, with respect — it is enough for them that they offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons. This is proof that Koresh was wicked, for he gave offerings only that they should pray for him and his sons. But is one who acts so not doing well? Was it not taught: One who says, “This coin is for charity so that my son may live,” or “so that I may merit the World to Come” — such a man is wholly righteous? There is no difficulty: there, of an Israelite (Rashi — for his heart is to Heaven, and if it goes ill with him in his life he does not complain, but ascribes the suffering to his own sin); here, of a gentile (who, if he is not repaid in kind, complains). Rashi: "With respect" [literally, "from your burden"]: from the very text with which you came against us to refute us I give you an answer — see what is written in it: "that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons"; you learn that he did it not for the sake of Heaven but for his own benefit. "Such a man is wholly righteous": if he is accustomed to this. "Here, of an Israelite": whose heart is directed to Heaven, and if it goes ill with him in his life he does not complain but ascribes the suffering to his sin; but a gentile, if he is not repaid in kind, complains. Tosafos (s.v. "so that my sons may live"): And what we learned in the first chapter of Avos, "Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward", refers to the nations of the world, who come to regret their earlier [good deeds]. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "so that my sons may live"): The reading [in Tosafot] should be "like the nations of the world", as in Tosafot Yeshanim; for it is unreasonable that the Mishnah [in Avos] speaks only of the nations of the world, since Tzadok and Baitus, who erred in [Antigonos's] words, were Israelites. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 4a): This does not contradict "Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward" (Avos 1:3), which speaks of one who performs a commandment for the sake of the reward of that very commandment, so that the aim of his service is not the Blessed One but himself; this man performs the commandment as it should be, out of love of the Blessed One, only that the aim of his love is that it should go well with him — and since in the end he loves the Blessed One and serves Him as is fitting, he is wholly righteous. As for the distinction between Israel and a gentile: the very being and rank of Israel is righteousness and goodness, so that an Israelite who performs a commandment for his own benefit is wholly righteous, for "righteous" means only one who is drawn along the path of uprightness (to look to nothing but love of the Blessed One is the rank of the pious man, not a condition of the righteous); but the nations are not in their essence of the rank of righteousness, so a gentile is righteous only when his whole intention is for the sake of Heaven..
an idolater acting not for its own sake is deemed wicked in this, whereas an Israelite acting similarly is deemed completely righteous.
וְזֶה הַהֶבְדֵּל הוּא מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּחֲשָׁבָה הַגְּלוּיָה לָאָדָם,
And this difference stems from the primordial root of Thought transcending the conscious thought of man,
שֶׁשָּׁם שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמַחְשַׁבְתָּם "עַל מְנָת שֶׁיִּחְיֶה בְּנִי אוֹ שֶׁאֶהְיֶה בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא";
where both outwardly share the motive "on condition that my child live or that I merit the World to Come";
רַק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם מֵהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שָׁם הוּא הַחִלּוּק דִּקְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
save that in the hidden root of Thought lies the distinction of Israel's holiness.

כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וּמוּשְׁרָשִׁים בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְכָל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.
For Israel arose in primordial Thought and are rooted in Hashem's Divine Thought, all their inner inclinations originating from Hashem, which is not so with the idolaters.
וְזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק בֵּין הַהֶבְדֵּל הָרִאשׁוֹן, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁעַת רִחוּק וְטֻמְאָה, אֶלָּא דִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָךְ,
And this is the distinction between the first mode of separation, when Israel are in a state of distance and uncleanness, yet such is Hashem's mysterious will,
וְיֵשׁ טַעֲנָה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: "הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי", "מֵאַחַר שֶׁאַתָּה מְרוּצֶּה בְּרִחוּק, מַה לְּךָ בְּרִחוּק שֶׁלָּנוּ?"
and the nations lodge the argument: "these are idolaters and those are idolaters, etc., since You tolerate distance, what differentiates our distance?"
וּלְכָךְ אָז גַּם הֵם נִקְרָאִים "בָּנוֹת" וּ"בָנִים", שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם קְצָת הִדַּמּוּת;
And therefore then they too are termed "daughters" and "sons", bearing partial resemblance;

וְהַהֶבְדֵּל רַק דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם רִחוּק הֶעָתִיד לְהִתְקָרֵב, וְכִדְבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א489 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6:3 — Israel further say to the nations of the world: We will tell you what we are like — like a king's son who went out to the wilderness outside the city, and the sun beat down upon his head and his face darkened. He entered the city, and with a little water and a little bathing in the bathhouse his body whitened and he returned to his former beauty. So it is with us: if the sun of idolatry has tanned us, you are tanned from your mother's womb, for while you were still in your mother's womb you served idols.) עַל פָּסוּק "שֶׁשְּׁזָפַתְנִי הַשָּׁמֶשׁ":

and the difference is that Israel represent a temporary distance destined to draw near, as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1) on the verse "because the sun has tanned me" (Song of Songs 1:6):
"וּבְרִיחוּץ מוּעָט אֲנִי חוֹזֵר, אֲבָל אַתֶּם שְׁזוּפִים מִמְּעֵי אִמְּכֶם".
"with a slight washing I return to my radiant purity, but you are dark from your mother's womb."
וְהַהֶבְדֵּל הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת עַצְמָן, דְּהַיְינוּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, דִּבּוּר וּמַחֲשָׁבָה הַנִּגְלִים,
And this distinction manifests within the lower dimensions themselves, namely within revealed action, speech, and thought,
רַק שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּהוֹוֶה, רַק מִצַּד חוּשׁ הָרֵיחַ עַל הֶעָתִיד,
save that it is not visible in the present, but perceived through scent regarding the future,
שֶׁהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, וּבְרֶגַע קַל יוּכְלוּ לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ, וְהַלָּלוּ לֹא יִתְהַפְּכוּ לְעוֹלָם, דְּשָׁרְשָׁם כָּךְ.
in that Israel lapsed into idolatry merely temporarily and can instantly invert to holiness, while the nations will never invert, such being their inherent root.
וְזֶהוּ "כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה" דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין, דְּחוּשׁ הָרֵיחַ הוּא מַה שֶּׁמֵּרִיחַ מֵרָחוֹק כַּאֲשֶׁר עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס לַחֵךְ.
And this is "like the smell of a field" of the holy apple orchard, for scent is that which detects from afar before entering the palate.

וּלְכָךְ אַבְרָהָם קְרָאוֹ "הַר490 Midrash Tehillim 81:2 — A parable of a king who had three friends, and who wished to build himself a palace. He brought the first and said: I wish to build a palace. He said: Remember, I was a mountain at first. He called the second and said: I wish to build myself a palace. He said: Remember, I was a field at first. He called the third and said: I wish to build myself a palace. He said: Remember, I was a palace at first. He said to him: By your life, I shall build it and call it by your name. So Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov all loved the Holy One, blessed be He. Avraham called the Temple a mountain, as it is said, “On the mountain the Lord shall be seen.” Yitzchak called it a field, as it is said, “See, the fragrance of my son is as the fragrance of a field.” Yaakov called it a house, before it was built, as it is said, “This is none other than the house of God.” The Holy One said to him: By your life, you called it a house before it was built — and I shall call it by your name, as it is said, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Yaakov.”", שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵין שָׁם שׁוּם הַתְחָלָה מֵהֲוָיָה דְּמָקוֹם מְיוּשָּׁב וּבָנוּי,
Therefore Abraham called the Temple site "a mountain," where there is not yet any beginning of a settled, built habitation,

אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר מְקוֹמוֹ נִיכָּר וּמְסוּיָּם בָּעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מָה הָרִים הַלָּלוּ מְסוּיָּמִים וְכוּלֵי491 Bereshit Rabbah 44:7 — “Fear not, Avram.” Of whom was he afraid? R. Berechiah said: He was afraid of Shem. This is what is written: “The islands saw and feared, the ends of the earth trembled.” Just as these islands are marked out in the sea, so were Avraham and Shem marked out in the world. And they feared — this one feared that one, and that one feared this one. This one feared, saying: Perhaps he bears it in his heart against me that I killed his sons; and that one feared, saying: Perhaps Avraham bears it in his heart against me that I raised up wicked men.".
yet its location is distinctly demarcated and prominent in the world, as written: "just as these mountains are prominently marked, etc."
אֲבָל יִצְחָק קְרָאוֹ "שָׂדֶה", שֶׁכְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה הַתְחָלַת הֲכָנָה לְיִשּׁוּב שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
However, Isaac called it "a field," marking the beginning of preparation for Hashem's Shechinah to dwell below.
אֶלָּא דַּעֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ בַּיִת מְיוּחָד, רַק כְּשָׂדֶה הַמֻּפְקָר לַכֹּל, וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם טוֹעֲנִים: "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל".
Except that it was not yet a designated house, but like an open field ownerless to all, and the nations contend: "we are Israel."
וּבָזֶה אֵין בֵּירוּר מִצַּד מַדְרֵגַת תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת אַף בְּרִחוּק זְמַן, כִּי גַּם הֵם פּוֹשְׁטִים טְלָפַיִם בַּמֶּה שֶׁנִּגְלֶה לִהְיוֹת מְצוּיָּנִים בְּמִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְכַשְׁרוּת.
And in this there is no resolution from lower rungs even in the distance of time, for they too display split hooves outwardly, feigning good character and virtue.
אֲבָל הַבֵּירוּר מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַסָּתוּם וְנֶעְלָם: דְּיִצְחָק כְּבָר הוּא מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עוֹד לָאֻמּוֹת כְּלָל.
Rather, clarification emerges from the concealed supernal root: for Isaac was already an Israelite consecrated from the womb, bearing no essential connection to the nations whatsoever.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֲרֵי יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ עֵשָׂו, וּבֵירוּרוֹ מִצַּד הַנֶּעְלָם דִּשְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה כָּל רַע עַד שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת כְּלָל;
Yet outwardly in this world Esau issued from him, and his clarification comes through the hidden dimension of the left arm pushing away all evil until detached;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת, וְנִקְרָאִים "בָּנוֹת" וּ"בָנִים" מִצַּד חֶשְׁכַּת לַיְלָה וּ"בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא",
unlike the right arm drawing near, and they are termed "daughters" and "sons" amidst the dark night of "first darkness and then light",

דְּאוֹר תּוֹרָה, דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)492 Zohar 3:80b — Purity is found in the Torah, as it is written, "The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever" (Psalms 19:10). He said to him: It is written "the fear of the Lord," and not "the Torah." He said to him: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Might. He said to him: And does it issue from there? It issues from here, as it is written, "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord" (Psalms 111:10), and it is written, "The fear of the Lord is pure." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 21): There was still lacking one more Sabbath, that of the attribute of Gevurah, which is the essential one for the Giving of the Torah, since "the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah." As long as they had not received the Torah and brought it down to earth, the revelation of the supernal holiness of that attribute's Sabbath, namely its inclusion within the attribute of Chesed, so that "from His right hand [went] a fiery law for them," was not yet within their reach; that came about on the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah., שֶׁמִּשָּׁם "יִהְיוּ עַמִּים מִשְׂרְפוֹת וְגוֹמֵר" "וְלִהַט אֹתָם וְגוֹמֵר".
wherein the light of Torah emanates from the side of Gevurah (Zohar III 80b end), whence "the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, etc." and "it shall burn them up, etc."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִיא סְעוּדָתָא דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין, נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים,
And afterward comes the third Sabbath feast of Ze'eir Anpin, the boundless heritage of Jacob,
כִּי "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁאֵין עוֹד רַע כְּלָל לִהְיוֹת צָרִיךְ מְצָרִים וּגְבוּלִים "עַד פֹּה תָבוֹא" וְלִהְיוֹת סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
