Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 28): Isaac thought to bless Esau because he reasoned that the Blessed One can shine even within darkness, and if the Holy One, blessed be He, consented to Esau's deeds they would be very exalted; but the Holy One, blessed be He, did not consent, for He had already sealed the name of Jacob, as it is written, "for in Isaac shall seed be called to you.".),
for "in Isaac shall seed be called unto you" (Genesis 21:12)—and not all of Isaac (excluding Esau; Nedarim 31a),
וְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְבַד הֵם זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק.
and Jacob's seed alone constitute the true seed of Abraham and Isaac.
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בָּהֶם נוֹטֶה לַקְּצוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק כֻּלָּהּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, כְּדֶרֶךְ אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, דְּכוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת.
For whatever leans within them toward the traits of Abraham or Isaac is entirely sanctified in holiness, being wholly seed of truth.
וְדַרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב עַצְמוֹ הוּא "וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו" – הַיְינוּ הַטַּלִּית שֶׁל מִצְוָה,
And the spiritual rung of Jacob himself is "and he smelled the fragrance of his garments" (Genesis 27:27)—referring to the tallit of mitzvah,

וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין לז519 Sanhedrin 37a — R. Zeira said: From here — "And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him" (Genesis 27:27): do not read "his garments [begadav]" but "his traitors [bogedav]." Tosafos (s.v. "and he smelled the smell of his garments"): "Smell" is a term that belongs to menstrual blood, as we say at the end of chapter Kol HaYad (Niddah 20b): a certain woman brought blood before R. Elazar; he smelled it and said, "This is blood of desire." Maharsha: Jacob was certainly perfectly righteous, but he was now wearing the garments of the wicked Esau, which Esau had coveted from the wicked Nimrod, and how many bloodstains from the murders of these wicked men were on them; yet when Jacob came before his father even these garments gave off a good fragrance, as it is said, "and he smelled the smell of his garments," for the fragrance of the Garden of Eden entered with him. This is a sign for his children, that even the traitors among them give off a fragrance through the commandments, as with the bloodstains of niddah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 37a): The garments allude to the empty ones: garments are secondary to the man, and so the empty ones are not the essence of "man" — for the righteous are always likened to man, and Israel, being more righteous than the nations, are called "man" (Yevamot 61a); therefore the wicked are likened to garments, which are not the man himself and are far from him. The good deed that the empty ones do for the sake of Heaven is called "smell" because smell reaches from far away, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, smells the commandments of the empty ones, who are far from Him; further, smell is associated with the attribute of judgment, and the empty ones, who subdue their inclination with great strength and wage war against it, belong to that attribute. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Esau's heart was full of crookedness, and only through the dimming of his eyes could Isaac think well of him; through that same dimming he afterwards did not recognize Jacob either, but he smelled "the smell of his traitors," for even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and there is no room at all to accuse him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:57): Jacob's service was chiefly in intention for the sake of Heaven, and the "garments" of deed began only with Laban, where he began to beget the souls of Israel, who are themselves the commandments of the Torah; hence it says then that [Rebecca] dressed him in Esau's garments. Therefore the Sages read "the smell of his garments" as "the smell of his traitors," meaning, as they said, that even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate: they too have a garment of the deed of the mitzvot. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 10): In Israel the evil stems from the vessels themselves, not from what is drawn out of them, and in the essence of the vessels there is no evil at all; therefore "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": they too give off a good fragrance, as it says, "the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot." As the Sages said of the myrtle, fragrance without taste, so in Israel there are those who have mitzvot but not Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The penitent breaks through every bound and in a single moment can rise from the utmost darkness to great light, which is the good name that spreads from one end of the world to the other; and of this it is said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": once they have returned from [their betrayals], theirs is the chief good fragrance, smelled throughout the whole world. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 5): When Isaac asked, "Are you my son Esau?", he meant that in the smell of his garments he sensed deeds, for which he called him "Esau" [as one who does the will of his Maker]; and the Midrash indeed reads "his garments" as "his traitors." To this Jacob answered "I am": I am the one who performs the deeds of the mitzvot, and what you sensed is the fragrance of Jacob's traitors, for the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and they too give off a good fragrance. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Even when Israel sins, it is like a myrtle standing among reeds, for the essence of a Jew's heart always gives off a good fragrance like the myrtle, as the Sages said on "he smelled the smell of his garments": "the smell of his traitors." The sins are only like thorns surrounding the rose, which prick it for the moment, and in the future this will be made clear in all Israel, when "the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the seed of Jacob none is cast off, for just as evening and morning make one day, so His praise rises from the wicked as from the righteous: even the empty ones of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and the sinners of Israel are full of remorse. Of this the Sages said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors," and Bereishis Rabbah applies it to the likes of Yakim of Tzeroros, who in a brief moment preceded Yose ben Yoezer, a perfect tzaddik who had toiled all his days, to the World to Come; for the penitent attains this in a single moment..): "רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו",
which our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 37a): the fragrance of his traitors,
כִּי הַטַּלִּית מְכַסָּה הַמּוּמִין וְהַחֲטָאִים, אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַכִּיר.
for the tallit conceals blemishes and lapses, yet Hashem nonetheless knows all.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ אֱמֶת, אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בּוֹ כִּסּוּי לַדִּמְיוֹן,
However, with our father Jacob who is entirely truth, no superficial cover for illusion applies,
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם,
save that in profound reality it remains transcendent and concealed,
דִּ"יְבֻקַּשׁ אֶת עֲוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר כִּי אֶסְלַח וְגוֹמֵר",
as in: "the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none... for I will pardon, etc." (Jeremiah 50:20),

זֶהוּ רַק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁחֲטָאֵיהֶם "כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת פט520 Shabbat 89b — "If your sins be as scarlet" — why the plural form, when the singular would be expected? R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins be like these years, which are ordered and come one after another from the six days of creation until now, "they shall be white as snow." Rashi: "It should have said ka-shani" [in the singular] — parallel to "as snow," for it does not say "as snows." Maharsha: "Like these years that are ordered" refers to the multitude of sin — as many as the years, presumably the years that have run in order since the six days of creation. One cannot read ka-shanim as "like two years," the minimal plural, for what novelty would there be in two sins? We say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah that He removes the first [sin] first, so for two sins "they shall be white as snow" would not be needed. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 89b): Sin is open to atonement because it is committed by accident, and the accidental does not annul what a person is in essence; but sins committed in great number and constantly are no longer accidental, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, says that even if your sins are ordered and fixed like these years, they shall be white as snow. Nothing is more fixed and ordered than the years, which have run so since the six days of creation, yet even they will cease, since the world is physical and will end in destruction; so too Israel's sins, though fixed on the side of the physical, can be removed, because Israel's essential level is not physical. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 19): The holiness of Tisha B'Av in the future, when it becomes a festival, will not come from Israel's sanctifying it, for on the contrary they sinned and made it a day of calamity, but only because in the future "your sins will be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," as stated in Shabbos 89b: then "they shall be white as snow" and be turned into merits, through this, that such was the will of the Blessed One from the six days of creation. Thus the essence of its holiness is only that this was the Blessed One's will at the beginning of creation, a holiness fixed and abiding like the holiness of Shabbos, except that it is revealed only in the future, after the rectification. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): "The scarlet [shanim] shall be white as snow" means that the scarlet of holiness, too, will be whitened, after they lift their eyes to the Blessed One, as stated in Shabbos there; and the sins will be "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, like merits; and afterwards they will rise still further, to the supernal whiteness, which is Wisdom, above Understanding. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 17): The deed itself is ordered and set so, as "Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of creation," and in truth this will be clarified in the future regarding all the sins of Israel, when they are refined and whitened, as the Sages said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow." That is, since the true will of the Blessed One was so, it is like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): In the future this will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel, as the Sages said in Shabbos 89b on the verse "If your sins be": "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation" — it will be clarified that it was ordered from the true will of the Blessed One that it be so, and if so, in this too they did the will of the Blessed One, and it was all like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Naso 2): Such was the intent in the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," as the Zohar says, there is no light but that which comes out of darkness; and then "the Lord will not count iniquity to him," since it will be clarified that this was created only so that it be "very good." As they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow," that is, they will be as merits. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): From the side of the hidden things that will be revealed in the future there was no sin at all, and of this they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, from the side of the "hidden things of the Merciful One," then "they shall be white as snow" entirely, for there is no sin at all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei 31): Snow alludes to fear, and so the Gemara says, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation until now, they shall be white as snow": "years" alludes to cycles and order, that is, if there is an accusation, Heaven forbid, and it seems that a person sinned deliberately and in [recurring] cycles, the Blessed One will illuminate that this deed came only out of fear of the Blessed One, and this is "white as snow.":),
this holding true uniquely of Israel whose sins are preordained like the solar years (Shabbat 89b),
וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם רֵיחַ טוֹב מֵרָחוֹק שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית.
possessing sweet fragrance from afar, being prearranged from the six days of Creation.
וּלְכָךְ אַחַר לְבִישַׁת הַתְּפִלִּין שֶׁהוּא הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר,
Therefore, following the donning of tefillin which represents absolute Divine Union,

כִּסּוּי הַטַּלִּית הוּא רַק כְּעִנְיַן "תַּלְמִיד חָכָם מַאֲפִיל בְּטַלִּיתוֹ" (שַׁבָּת פו521 Shabbat 86a — Rav Huna said: Israel are holy, and do not have relations with their wives by day. But Rava said: If the house was dark, it is permitted. And Rava said, and some say Rav Papa: A Torah scholar darkens [the room] with his cloak, and it is permitted. Rashi: "As Rav Huna said": that they do not have relations by day, as it is written, "He who despises his ways shall die" (Proverbs 19:16), for modesty is required, that they not look. "A Torah scholar": since he is modest and will not look, it is enough for him to darken [the room] with his cloak. Tosafos (s.v. "Israel are holy"): That is, even without [Moses' instruction] they would have abstained [that morning], for it is expounded, "He who despises his ways shall die" — this is one who has relations by day; and moreover, [Scripture] had called them holy: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" (Exodus 19:6). Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 17a): Relations at night are within modesty, but by day they go out of modesty. The Torah scholar is a being of intellect, not one drawn after the material, and for him the shamefulness of this union attaches only through sight — for the eye is a faculty separate [from matter], as it is written, "that He see no unseemly thing in you" (Deuteronomy 23:15) — so when he darkens with his cloak and sees nothing unseemly it is permitted; whereas the ignorant man, who is drawn wholly after the material, is forbidden by day and permitted only at night, when the light, which resembles the intellect, is absent. Moreover, with the scholar the union itself reaches the level of the intellect, which is why it is called "knowing", and so no prohibition of daytime rests on him, save that he must darken so that his eye is not joined to what is truly unseemly; with the ignorant man it is not called "knowing" at all, and so it is forbidden..),
the enwrapment of the tallit is like a Torah scholar obscuring with his tallit (Shabbat 86a),
כָּרָאוּי לְיִחוּד גָּמוּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּהֶעְלֵם עַיִן וּבִצְנִיעוּת.
as is fitting for intimate sacred union to take place in privacy and modesty.
וְהַכִּסּוּי הוּא רַק עַל תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה וְחִבָּה,
And this covering serves purely to envelop intense love and affection,
וְלֹא עַל הָרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
and not to conceal evil, Heaven forbid,
כִּי אֵין שָׁם רַע כְּלָל, דְּ"מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
since there is no evil there at all, his bed being whole as noted above.
וְזֶהוּ הַהֲכָנָה לִתְפִלָּה – דַּרְגָּא דַּאֲבָהָן,
And this is the preparation for prayer—the rung of the Patriarchs,

כַּיָּדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא522 Bava Metzia 85b — Eliyahu used to frequent the academy of Rebbi. One day it was the New Moon, and he was late and did not come. He said to him: Why was the master late? He said to him: Until I had roused Avraham and washed his hands and he prayed, and I laid him down again; and likewise Yitzchak, and likewise Yaakov. — And let the master rouse them together! — He said: They would pray with too much force and bring the Mashiach before his time. He said to him: And is there anyone like them in this world? He said to him: There are R. Chiya and his sons. Rebbi decreed a fast, and they brought R. Chiya and his sons down. He said: “Who makes the wind blow” — and the wind blew; he said: “Who brings down the rain” — and the rain came. When he was about to say “Who revives the dead,” the world shook. They said in heaven: Who has revealed the secret in the world? They said: Eliyahu. They brought Eliyahu and struck him with sixty fiery lashes. He came, appeared to them as a fiery bear, entered among them and scattered them. Rashi: "They would pray with too much force" — they would multiply prayer, "and bring the Mashiach before his time"; that is why I am not permitted to raise them together. "And is there anyone like them" — whose prayer would be heard as theirs would. "Lashes" — blows of flogging. Tosafos (s.v. "and let the master rouse them together"): Let him stand all three of them together before the ark — as is expounded in the Midrash, that on a public fast three descend before the ark, as it is written "and Moses' hands were heavy... and Aaron and Hur." Tosafos (s.v. "when he came to say 'Who revives the dead'"): Why did the world shake only then, since "Who revives the dead" is said in that same blessing before "Who makes the wind blow"? Rabbeinu Tam answered that the resurrection of the dead comes about only through dew; and one may also answer that at "Who makes the wind blow" and "Who brings down the rain" the wind blew and the rain came because those words are the very substance of the petition for wind and rain, whereas the substance of the resurrection lies in the blessing's closing formula. Maharsha: The New Moon, the day on which the moon is renewed, hints at the renewal of Israel's kingship in time to come, and is therefore a day fit for pressing such a prayer — which is why, had they prayed together on that day, they would have brought the Mashiach before his time. When he came to say "Who revives the dead" and the world shook, this was perhaps the very beginning of the resurrection, as we find of the dead whom Ezekiel revived, "and there was a noise as I prophesied, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together." The fiery bear is the heavenly prince of Persia, called Dubiel, who came in and scattered them — to say that the Messiah's time had not yet come and that Israel were still given over to the rule of Persia. (פה:) דְּאֵלִיָּהוּ מָשֵׁי לַאֲבָהָן לְהַעֲמִידָן לִתְפִלָּה, דַּאֲבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם.
as known from what they taught in Bava Metzia (85b) that Elijah washes the Patriarchs to arouse them for prayer, for the Patriarchs instituted them.
וְיָדוּעַ פֵּירוּשׁ "אָבוֹת" שֶׁזָּכְרוּ בְּכָל מָקוֹם:
And known is the meaning of "Patriarchs" mentioned everywhere:
הַיְינוּ הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
meaning their spiritual potencies present within every Jewish soul,
שֶׁהוּא זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּלוּל כָּל שְׁלֹשֶׁת כֹּחוֹתֵיהֶם,
being the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob encompassing all three of their powers,
וְצָרִיךְ לְעוֹרְרָן בְּלִבּוֹ.
which one must awaken within his heart.

sections.en: The Shofar as Awakening and Remembrance

items.h: The shofar awakens Israel from spiritual sleep and arouses divine remembrance, preparing both personal Torah growth and the future awakening of the Great Shofar.

Seif 1 — Awakening through the Shofar
The shofar awakens human remembrance of Hashem and elicits a corresponding divine remembrance from Above.

p: עִנְיַן תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר שֶׁכָּתַב רַמְבַּ"ם (פֶּרֶק ג מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה הֲלָכָה ד523 Mishneh Torah, Repentance 3:4 — Although the sounding of the shofar on Rosh HaShanah is a decree of Scripture, there is an allusion in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep, and you who slumber, rouse yourselves from your slumber; examine your deeds, return in repentance, and remember your Creator. Those who forget the truth amid the vanities of the times, and who go astray all their year in emptiness and vanity that neither profits nor saves — look to your souls, better your ways and your deeds, and let each of you abandon his evil way and his thought that is not good.): "כְּלוֹמַר עוּרוּ יְשֵׁנִים מִתַּרְדֶּמַתְכֶם",
The matter of the blowing of the shofar concerning which Maimonides wrote (Repentance 3:4): "namely: 'Awake, sleepers, from your slumber!'"

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז524 Rosh Hashanah 16a — The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Recite before Me on Rosh HaShana Kingships, Remembrances, and Shofarot — Kingships, so that you crown Me as king over you; Remembrances, so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar. Tosafos (s.v. "with a ram's shofar"): In chapter Ra'uhu Beit Din (26a) the Mishnah records that R. Yosei validates even a cow's horn; but we hold in accordance with R. Yehuda that one sounds with bent rams' horns, as the Gemara rules there (26b). Maharsha (s.v. "recite before Me Kingships"): The Sifrei derives them from the verse "And you shall sound… and they shall be to you for a remembrance… I am the Lord your God" (Numbers 10:10): "you shall sound" — these are Shofarot; "for a remembrance" — these are Remembrances; "I am the Lord your God" — this is Kingships. The intent of Kingships, Remembrances and Shofarot is explained in the chapter "How is the order of fasts" [Taanit, ch. 2]. Maharsha (s.v. "why do we sound a ram's horn"): The Ran explains that [R. Abbahu] asks this about the mere custom of sounding with a ram's horn; but it seems to me that he asks it on the Mishnah in chapter Ra'uhu Beit Din, "R. Yehuda says: On Rosh Hashanah one sounds with [the horns] of males," which is the accepted halachah. This follows the Midrash that Rashi cites on the Torah, that the yovel is a ram's horn (for in Arabic a ram is called yovla), since we derive the shofar of Rosh Hashanah below [in chapter 2] from the shofar of the Jubilee. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a, s.v. "Kingships, Remembrances, Shofarot"): Kingships: the Blessed One is King, and as King He comes to judge; therefore Remembrances follow, for remembrance is not judgment — on the contrary, it recalls what was forgotten, and since He remembers everything, reaching what is deep and inward, He remembers Israel for good, and by this they are saved from the attribute of judgment. And this is "by the shofar," for the tekia signifies elevation, and all elevation is mercy, as the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 29): when Israel take up their shofars and sound them, the Holy One, blessed be He, rises from the throne of judgment and sits upon the throne of mercy. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a, s.v. "with a ram's shofar"): Rosh Hashanah is the day of judgment, and when they sound a ram's horn it is as though the judgment had already been carried out, for He remembers the binding of Yitzchak, who was bound before the Holy One, blessed be He, as though judgment had been executed upon him. "I shall account it to you" because the father is the root of the son: when the father, the root of the lineage, was bound, the branch resembles him, for Israel too give themselves over to the honor of the Blessed One. In sum, the ram signifies binding and submission to the attribute of judgment, and by giving over our souls to the Blessed One we are saved from the Accuser — which is also why [the shofars] must be bent. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 13): Rosh HaShanah is the Day of Remembrance, for when a person remembers the Blessed One, the Blessed One remembers the person; this too is the matter of the shofar, of which the Sages said, "so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good — with what? With the shofar." Rambam wrote that the shofar hints, "Awake, sleepers, from your slumber … remember your Creator," for it was their way to rouse the people by sounding the shofar; and it is all one — their remembering the Blessed One and their remembrance rising before Him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 3): The holiness of Rosh HaShanah, the Day of Remembrance — "so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good, and with what? With the shofar" — is present on the Sabbath to a greater degree; therefore when Rosh HaShanah falls on the Sabbath there is no need to raise our remembrance before Him for good through the act of the shofar, for [the Sabbath] is in itself a day of remembrance. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Rosh HaShanah): In Remembrances the benefit is explicit, but what is the benefit in reciting Kingships? Though a person imagines that the yoke of Heaven's kingship is servitude, in truth it is the true freedom from every servitude in the world, for where the Blessed One dwells no evil draws near, and one who crowns the Blessed One over himself is entirely free; so the Blessed One counsels Israel that in the days of Rosh HaShanah the word "King" be habitual on their lips, a safeguard from all evil. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh HaShanah 15): "Recite before Me Kingships... so that you crown Me": since the Blessed One desires Israel's crowning of Him, a person is obligated to crown Him over himself in every detail. "Remembrances, so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good" — but what has remembrance to do with the Blessed One, when there is no forgetting before His Throne of Glory? Rather it is from the human side, for a person has many distractions and must fix in himself that none will divert him, and "with what? With the shofar" — only through the shofar can he fix this recognition, for the shofar indicates that a person stations himself in the inner voice. Sod Yesharim (Rosh HaShanah 17): "Recite before Me Remembrances" — that you always bring yourselves near before Me and do not stand far off, behind; as much as a person fixes in his heart the awareness that he always stands before the Blessed One and is watched over every moment, so does the Blessed One truly watch over him. "With what? With the shofar" — a person fixes such awareness by contracting his own desires so as to want only the simple will of the Blessed One, and this contraction is called shofar..): "שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה זִכְרוֹנֵיכֶם לְפָנַי לְטוֹבָה, וּבַמֶּה? בַּשּׁוֹפָר" –
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Rosh Hashanah 16a): "that your remembrance may ascend before Me for good; and through what? Through the shofar"—
הַכֹּל אֶחָד.
are both one single concept.
כִּי "ה' צִלְּךָ", כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם מִתְעוֹרֵר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ וְזוֹכֵר בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For "Hashem is your shadow": when a person awakens from his slumber and remembers Hashem, blessed be He,
אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זוֹכֵר אוֹתוֹ
then Hashem remembers him
כְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁהוּא זוֹכֵר בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
in that exact manner that the person remembers Hashem:
אֵיךְ הוּא "מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ" וְהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ וְצָרִיךְ לְעָבְדוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
how "the whole earth is full of His glory," that all is His, and that one must serve Him, and the like;
כָּל חַד לְפוּם אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ כָּךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
each person according to his own spiritual awakening, so does Hashem respond opposite him,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו525 Berakhot 6a — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: You have made Me a single entity in the world, and I will make you a single entity in the world. You have made Me a single entity in the world, as it is said, "Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One"; and I will make you a single entity in the world, as it is said, "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the earth." Maharsha: As the Gemara brings, the Holy One, blessed be He, takes praise and glory in Israel and Israel take glory and praise in the Lord, as it is written, "You have affirmed the Lord this day," and "and the Lord has affirmed you this day." And "affirmed" has the sense of a single entity — see Rashi in Chagigah 3a — a praise unique to the two of them alike: "the Lord is One" and "Israel is one nation in the earth." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): On the Sabbath, when Moses attains his level and returns the crowns to Israel, we say "You are One and Your name is One" and "Who is like Your people Israel... great glory," in keeping with "You have made Me a single entity in the world, and I will make you a single entity in the world... 'And who is like Your people Israel'" — and this is the "great glory.".): "אַתֶּם עֲשִׂיתוּנִי חֲטִיבָה וְכוּלֵי, אַף אֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם".
along the lines of what they taught (Berakhot 6a): "You made Me a unique entity, etc., so I will make you a unique entity in the world."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם שׁוֹכֵחַ,
In contrast, when one forgets, Heaven forbid,
הֲגַם כִּי אֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִּסֵּא כְּבוֹדוֹ,
even though there is no forgetfulness before the Throne of His Glory,
הַזִּכָּרוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מִצַּד הַשִּׁכְחָה, שֶׁזּוֹכֵר כִּבְיָכוֹל שֶׁבָּזֶה הוּא שׁוֹכֵחַ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה.
His remembrance reflects that forgetfulness, as He recalls, as it were, that the person is currently forgetful, Heaven forbid, measure for measure.
וְלָכֵן יָהֵיב עֵיטָא בַּשּׁוֹפָר לְעוֹרְרֵינוּ.
Therefore He gave us counsel through the shofar to awaken us.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם עַמּוּד ב526 Rosh Hashanah 16b — Why do they sound a tekia and a terua while seated, and then sound a tekia and a terua while standing [in the Amida]? In order to confound the Satan. And R. Yitzchak said: Any year in which the shofar is not sounded at its beginning will suffer misfortune at its end. What is the reason? Because the Satan was not confounded. Rashi (s.v. "to confound"): That he not bring accusation: when he hears that Israel cherish the commandments, his words are stopped up. Tosafos (s.v. "and they sound… while standing"): One may ask: does one not thereby transgress "you shall not add"? [For one cannot say that, having already fulfilled the obligation, it is no longer its time, since regarding the priestly blessing (28b) we say that its time has not passed, for were another congregation to come along he would bless them again.] The answer is that "you shall not add" does not apply to performing a single commandment twice — as a priest who blesses the same congregation again, or one who takes the lulav and takes it again, and likewise one who sounds and sounds again. Tosafos (s.v. "that is not sounded at its beginning"): The Halachot Gedolot explains: not where [Rosh Hashanah] happens to fall on Shabbat, but where some mishap occurred [that prevented the sounding]. Tosafos (s.v. "to confound the Satan"): The Aruch explains, as found in the Jerusalem Talmud: it is written "He will swallow up death forever" (Isaiah 25:8), and it is written "And it shall come to pass on that day that a great shofar shall be sounded" (Isaiah 27:13). When [the Satan] hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed and yet not alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: "Surely this is the shofar of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,' and my time to be swallowed up has come" — and he is confounded and has no leisure to bring accusation. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a–b): The Satan is privation and the shofar is the good that removes privation — hence "one who sees a shofar in a dream should anticipate redemption" (Berakhot 56b), which includes redemption from the Satan — for the tekia on Rosh Hashanah is elevation, and the Accuser cannot reach that place of elevation. They sound twice, seated and standing, because the first sounding only sets up opposition to him, while overcoming requires a second force that prevails and removes him entirely; this is why the Jerusalem Talmud says that at the first sounding he is alarmed and not alarmed, and at the second he is certain. In sum, the Satan accuses only through the attribute of judgment, which rules on Rosh Hashanah, and the soundings signify that attribute's elevation into mercy, whereupon it has no accuser. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh HaShanah 13): Tosafos cites the Yerushalmi that when [the Satan] hears the shofar the first time he is alarmed yet not alarmed, and when he hears it a second time he says, "Surely this is the shofar of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,'" and is confounded; but did he not know that the shofar is the mitzvah of the day, and that blowing again while standing is likewise an enactment of the Sages — why is he confounded by this mitzvah specifically? The first hearing, though also an awakening, can afterwards lapse, so he is not so alarmed; but the second, the blasts of the words of the Scribes, of the aspect of the Oral Torah, rouses the "great shofar," the awakening fixed in the depths of the heart, and thereby his time has come to be swallowed up and confounded, and in his preoccupation he has no leisure to prosecute.) שֶׁהוּא לְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן,
And our Sages stated (Rosh Hashanah 16b) that the shofar serves to confound Satan,

וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז527 Bava Batra 16a — Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, "And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord." He is the evil inclination, for it is written there, "Only evil all the day," and it is written here, "Only against himself do not put forth your hand." He is the angel of death, as it is written, "Only spare his life" — evidently his life rests in his hand. Rashi: "Evidently his life rests in his hand" — it lies with Satan to take the soul, and God warned him not to take it. Maharsha: Our texts misquote the verse: it reads "only [akh] spare his life," not "only [rak]." The verbal analogy holds nonetheless, since "only [akh]" and "only [rak]" are alike terms of limitation. The hint in it is this: "only evil all the day" — let a man limit his evil inclination and master it, and then "only spare his life" — the Holy One, blessed be He, will limit the power of the angel of death, that he not rule over his soul. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil..): "הוּא שָׂטָן, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע",
and this is identical, as they taught (Bava Batra 16a): "He is Satan, he is the evil inclination";
וְעִיקַּר יֵצֶר הָרָע אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַהַשְׁקָעָה בַּדִּמְיוֹן,
and the primary work of the evil inclination is nothing other than immersion in illusion,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחוֹ לִזְכּוֹר וְלָשׂוּם אֶל לְבָבוֹ עַל מָה נִבְרָא בָּעוֹלָם וּלְהִתְעוֹרֵר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ.
which prevents a person from remembering and taking to heart why he was created in this world and from awakening from his slumber.

וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וְגוֹמֵר הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר וְהַנִּדָּחִים וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ כז, יג528 Isaiah 27:13 — “And it shall come to pass on that day that a great shofar shall be sounded, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those who were cast away in the land of Egypt shall come, and they shall bow down to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.” Rashi: “Those who were lost in the land of Assyria” — because they were scattered to a distant land, beyond the river Sambatyon, he calls them “lost.” Radak: They will be gathered as though a great shofar had been sounded to make its voice heard in all the world, and they will come from every quarter. “Those who were lost” are the tribes whom the king of Assyria exiled beyond the river, who were there as though lost, never to come out again; whereas Judah and Benjamin, who returned from the Babylonian exile after seventy years and were afterward exiled a second time, are the ones cast away, driven to every quarter and scattered. Metzudas Dovid: “A great shofar shall be sounded” — a figure of speech: all will gather and come as though a great shofar had been sounded to make its voice heard in all the world. He calls them “lost” because they had not returned to their land from the time they were exiled there. “On the holy mountain in Jerusalem” — on Mount Moriah, which stands in Jerusalem, the place of the Temple. Malbim: “A great shofar shall be sounded” — and the general ingathering will take place. He calls those in the land of Assyria “lost,” for their place and their very existence were forgotten until the end; those in the land of Egypt are only “cast away.” Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 10): Since Israel was sunk in the husk of Egypt like a fetus in its mother's womb, Moses had to grow up in Pharaoh's house without anything of its evil clinging to him, and thereby he was fit to bring Israel out of Egypt though they were sunk in it. Likewise the Messiah, who will need to bring out even "the lost in the land of Assyria and the cast away" though they are sunk, must be "dwelling with them in the province." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Samson's whole effort in his life was to bring back the souls utterly cast away, assimilated among the nations, who have almost no hope of returning to the source of their holiness all the days of this world — until "a great shofar is sounded," when all impurity will be burned away and even "the lost in the land of Assyria and the cast away" will come; and he thought that in his days the time of the End had already arrived and that he could raise them up. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Korach): The verse puts "the lost" before "the cast away," though "lost" implies lost entirely and "cast away" only for a time, because the lost is one whose body appears clean and whose lack lies only in the root of his soul, barely discernible, as with Korah; he is entirely lost for now since, pure in his own eyes, he cannot come upon his lack, but in the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals to him the difference between himself and Moses, he will turn in one moment from darkness to light. The cast away is one whose body is distant and sunk in the evil inclination, and it is very hard for him to purify his body and abandon his ways and desires, so he will be delayed; therefore the lost precedes the cast away in repentance. Beis Yaakov (Chayei Sarah 4): In truth the Blessed One will clarify all the souls of Israel in the future, so that none of Israel, even one who served idols, will remain cast away from Him, as it is written, "and those lost in the land of Assyria and those cast away in the land of Egypt shall come"; but now, in this world, where the tree of doubt rules, a person must clarify himself with all his strength and not put himself into doubt by relying on the Blessed One to clarify him in the future. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh HaShanah 17): From the perspective of this world's grasp, reason requires that the cast away return to his place before the lost, since the lost seems, Heaven forbid, entirely lost — but that is from the side of the small shofar. From the side of the great shofar the Blessed One will show that among Israel no one was ever lost: a thing is truly lost only where its owner no longer seeks it, having despaired, but in the future the Blessed One will show that the owner was still seeking his loss, that is, there was never, Heaven forbid, despair among Israel, and Israel always had hope toward the Blessed One. Sod Yesharim (Rosh HaShanah 1): The lack called Assyria is the excessive firmness that says a person has no power of action, for all is in Heaven's hands, even the fear of Heaven, and one who holds this view is called "lost"; the "cast away" is one who says "the Lord has forsaken the land," the character of Egypt, which was "like the garden of the Lord" and did not need the Blessed One at all. From the side of the small shofar the lost is utterly lost, for his flaw touches the Divine will, above human grasp, that a person reach the supernal light only through service; but when the great shofar is sounded and the root called Atika shines, it will be seen that truly all is in Heaven's hands, and Assyria's lack will be mended at once, whereas the cast away will need more clarification of his coarse deeds — therefore it says first "the lost in the land of Assyria" and afterwards "the cast away in the land of Egypt."),
And concerning this it is said: "In that day... those perishing in the land of Assyria and those outcasts, etc." (Isaiah 27:13),
שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בַּדִּמְיוֹן:
which represent two distinct forms of immersion in illusion:
הָאֶחָד – שֶׁמַּשְׁקִיעַ עַצְמוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת תְּדִירָה בְּעִסְקֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
The first: one who submerges himself in relentless worldly striving,
כְּגוֹן לִקְבּוֹץ מָמוֹן וְכַיּוֹצֵא שְׁאָר תַּאֲווֹת אוֹ רְדִיפַת שְׂרָרָה וְכָבוֹד אוֹ נִיצּוּחַ וְקִנְאָה,
such as amassing wealth, pursuing physical pleasures, authority, honor, triumph, or envy,
עַד שֶׁלִּבּוֹ מוּטְרָד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִזְכּוֹר אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל,
until his heart is so agitated that it is impossible for him to remember Hashem at all;
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "אוֹבֵד" חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ.
and this person is called "perishing / lost," Heaven forbid, when reaching absolute immersion.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן אַשּׁוּר, שֶׁהָרֹאשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם סַנְחֵרִיב,
And this is the nature of Assyria whose leader was Sennacherib,
שֶׁבִּלְבֵּל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עֲצוּמָה כָּל יָמָיו,
who threw the entire world into turmoil through colossal aggressive exertion all his days,
וְלֹא לְיוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי.
bearing no resemblance to one sitting idly asleep.
וְהֲגַם דְּזֶה גָּרַע יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁהוּא כְּאוֹבֵד לְגַמְרֵי,
And although this state is worse to the point of being entirely lost,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא שָׁקוּעַ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּטְרָדוֹת וְלֹא בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל בַּטָּלָה,
since he is submerged in frenetic exertion and anxieties rather than passive fantasies,

וְתַכְלִית הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ הַזֶּה הֵם עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת טז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב529 Yevamot 16b — Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said: A gentile who betrothed a Jewish woman nowadays — we are concerned that the betrothal may be valid, lest he be of the ten tribes. But [is it not the rule that] whatever is separated is presumed to have separated from the majority? [The concern applies only to one who comes] from their settled dwelling places. Rashi: "Lest he be of the ten tribes": who married gentile women; and [Rav Asi] holds that the child a gentile woman bears to an Israelite is a mamzer, and we are concerned for the betrothal of a mamzer. "From their settled dwelling places": where the ten tribes are settled — and whatever is fixed in its place is treated as half-and-half. And where are they settled? As it is written, "And he placed them in Chalach and in Chavor." Tosafos (s.v. "a gentile who betrothed nowadays"): Rashi explains that [Rav Asi] holds the child a gentile woman bears to an Israelite to be a mamzer. This is difficult, since several Mishnayot show that such a child is attributed only to her — though not so difficult, for those Mishnayot hold that the child of a gentile or a slave with a Jewish woman is fit, and likewise in the reverse case, whereas Rav Asi may hold with R. Akiva that such a child is a mamzer; but it seems that Rav Asi's reason is on account of the daughters [of the ten tribes, who bore children to gentiles], and that he does not accept that the daughters of that generation became barren. Tosafos (s.v. "from their settled dwelling places"): That is, in their own place the majority are of the ten tribes — and not as Rashi explained, because whatever is fixed is treated as half-and-half; for if he went to her, [the rule] "whatever separates, separates from the majority" applies, as stated at the end of the first chapter of Ketubot (15a). Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "a gentile who betrothed nowadays"): Tosafot's proof does not compel their explanation. Rashi understood from the Gemara's objection after Shmuel's statement — "But there are the daughters!" — that Shmuel, in replying "Your son from an Israelite woman is called your son…", was answering only that they cannot be disqualified on account of an Israelite man who had relations with a gentile woman, since that was the ground on which Rav Asi disqualified them; on Tosafot's explanation, that Rav Asi too disqualified them because of the daughters, it requires study what Shmuel was answering him with "your son from an Israelite woman." Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 34): One cannot say that [the ten tribes] intermingled with the gentiles and that the dispute whether they will return concerns those assimilated among the nations, for this sugya shows that we have no such concern: [as it concludes,] when a gentile betroths nowadays we are not concerned for his betrothal lest he be of the ten tribes, since it is a tradition that the daughters of that generation became barren — their wombs split and did not receive the seed — so that there is no concern that any remained of the ten tribes. Hence the view that the ten tribes are destined to return must mean that they will return together with the other exiles, among whom they now are, having first been exiled to Africa or to the mountains of Selug and afterwards moved from there to be among the other exiles.):
the epitome of this immersion being the Ten Lost Tribes, of whom our Sages taught (Yevamot 16b end):
שֶׁנִּטְמְעוּ בָּעַמִּים בְּגָלוּת אַשּׁוּר עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ בְּעַצְמָם אִם הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
that they assimilated among the nations in the Assyrian exile until they did not even know if they were Israelites.
כִּי כָּךְ הוּא גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עַד שֶׁמַּשְׁכִּיחַ לְגַמְרֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
For so immense is the power of immersion in this world, that it induces complete forgetfulness of one's Jewish root, Heaven forbid.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא כַּאֲבֵידָה הַמִּתְבַּקֶּשֶׁת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי מַכּוֹת,
Yet nonetheless, it is like a lost object being actively sought, as taught at the end of Makkot (24b),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין כָּאן יֵאוּשׁ בְּעָלִים, דַּעֲדַיִן בְּעָלָיו מְבַקְשִׁים אוֹתָהּ;
meaning there is no despair of recovery by the Owner, for its Master still seeks it;

כִּי הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ סִימָן, דְּ"כָל רֹאֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּם וְגוֹמֵר530 Isaiah 61:9 — “And their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples; all who see them shall recognize them, that they are the seed the Lord has blessed.” Radak: When they travel in the lands of the nations, for pleasure or for trade, they will be recognized by their great honour even though they have no need to go. Walking in free and embroidered garments, people will say of them, "These are the children of Israel, these are the seed the Lord has blessed." Metzudas Dovid: The seed of Israel will be recognized by their distinction, and the children who come from them will be known among the peoples — the verse repeats the matter in different words. Whoever sees them will recognize in them that they are the seed blessed by the Lord. Malbim: Their seed will be known among the nations for renown and praise — not only the grown children but the little ones too, and not only among the lesser nations but among the important peoples as well. All who see them will say of them that these are the seed the Lord has blessed, for they will be marked out by a holy splendour. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Even a Jew who apostatized is "Israel though he sinned," for the body of a Jew is set apart from birth from the body of a gentile, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to recognize, as holy flesh; and at the end of days this will be clarified, that "all who see them shall recognize them" — as some of the nations testified in times of forced conversion that they had toiled in vain even with those who converted, for on investigation it became clear to them that their heart was still toward Heaven.",
for it is an object possessing an identifying mark: "all that see them shall acknowledge them, etc." (Isaiah 61:9),
וְיֵשׁ כָּאן סִימָן הַנִּיכָּר לִבְעָלָיו שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
bearing an identifiable sign recognizable to its Owner, Who is Hashem, blessed be He.
רַק שֶׁבִּהְיוֹתוֹ מוּבְלָע בֵּין הָעַמִּים אֵינוֹ נִמְצָא כִּבְיָכוֹל בְּיָדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּסְתִּיר.
Only that while swallowed among the nations, it is not visibly manifest in His hand, as it were, due to this obscuring world.
אֲבָל "בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא", שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ יוֹם הַזֶּה, יִהְיֶה שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל הַמְּעוֹרֵר גַּם אֵלֶּה.
However, "in that day," which is the spiritual antithesis of this day, the Great Shofar will sound, awakening even these.
וְאֵלֶּה יַקְדִּימוּ לָבוֹא, כִּי הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ שֶׁלָּהֶם מִצַּד כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
And these will arrive first, because their immersion stemmed from the drive of active striving;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יִתְעוֹרְרוּ וְיַהַפְכוּ כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִרְדּוֹף אַחֲרֵי ה', מִצַּד הָרְדִיפָה שֶׁלָּהֶם יַקְדִּימוּ בְּבִיאָתָם.
and once awakened, turning that intense striving toward pursuing Hashem, that very drive will cause them to arrive first.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "הַנִּדָּחִים" – וְהֵם הָעַצְלָנִים הַשְּׁקוּעִים בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל תֹּהוּ וְשֶׁל שָׁוְא וְשֶׁל הֶבֶל.
And afterward come "the outcasts"—the indolent submerged in vain, empty fantasies.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנִּקְרָא "עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ",
And this is the nature of Egypt, designated "the nakedness of the land" (Genesis 42:9),
כִּי עִנְיַן אֶרֶץ הוּא כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, כְּעִנְיַן "מֶלֶךְ לְשָׂדֶה נֶעֱבָד" בַּעֲבוֹדַת הָאֲדָמָה,
for "earth/land" represents the realm of physical exertion, as in "a king is served by the field" through agricultural labor,
שֶׁזֶּה עִיקַּר עֲבוֹדַת וִיגִיעַת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
which is the primary toil of man in this world from an earthly perspective;
שֶׁכֵּן נִמְשַׁל גַּם כֵּן עֲבוֹדַת אֱמֶת דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּגַן עֵדֶן, שֶׁהִנִּיחוֹ "לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ",
just as the authentic spiritual work of Adam in Eden was framed: placing him "to work it and to guard it",

וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)531 Zohar 1:27a — In like manner the Holy One, blessed be He, does to a man, who is created from the four elements: when he repents and occupies himself with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, takes him from there, and of them it is said, "and from there it parted" (Genesis 2:10). He separates his soul from their desire and sets him in His garden, which is the Divine Presence — "to work it" with the positive commandments, and "to guard it" with the negative commandments.: בְּמִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
which our Sages expounded (Zohar I 27a): referring to positive and negative commandments.
וְ"עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ" הַיְינוּ גְּנוּת עִנְיַן הָאָרֶץ שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ עֲבוֹדָה, כִּי נִילוּס עוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה;
And "the nakedness of the land" is the degradation of land requiring no labor, because the Nile rises and waters it passively;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל: "אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ דֹּרֵשׁ וְגוֹמֵר", "לִמְטַר הַשָּׁמַיִם וְגוֹמֵר532 Deuteronomy 11:11-12 — “But the land to which you cross over to possess is a land of hills and valleys; from the rain of heaven it drinks water — a land which the Lord your God seeks out; the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the year’s end.” Rashi: "A land of hills and valleys" — the hill country is better than the plain, for in a plain a field that takes a kor of seed yields only a kor, whereas a hill whose summit takes a kor yields five: four from its four slopes and one on its summit. "A land which the Lord your God cares for" — does He not care for all lands? Rather He cares for that land alone, and through the care He bestows upon it He cares for all the other lands with it; His eyes are always upon it to see what it requires, and at the beginning of the year it is decreed what shall be until the year's end.",
unlike the Land of Israel: "a land which Hashem cares for... drinketh water of the rain of heaven",
וְצָרִיךְ עֲבוֹדָה וּתְפִלָּה וְיִחוּל לַה', וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשְׁקִיעַ עַצְמוֹ בְּשַׁלְוָה כָּל כָּךְ.
requiring toil, prayer, and hopeful reliance upon Hashem, making it impossible to sink into passive complacency.
וְזֶה עִיקַּר קְדוּשַׁת הָאָרֶץ: שֶׁלֹּא לְהַשְׁקִיעַ בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל שַׁלְוָה, רַק לֵידַע שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, וְ"אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד".
And this is the core sanctity of the Land: not sinking into illusions of static tranquility, but knowing that effort is needed, for "man is born to toil."
וּקְדוּשַׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ – לֵידַע שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲמַל מְלָאכָה וּלְהַשְׁקִיעַ בַּעֲבוֹדַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּזֵיתוֹ וְכַרְמוֹ, רַק בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And the sanctity of the Temple is to know not to toil in secular crafts or worldly agriculture, but solely in the service of Hashem.
וְ"עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ" נִקְרָא הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, רַק הוֹזִים שׁוֹכְבִים.
And "the nakedness of the land" denotes immersion in worldliness devoid of active labor, being mere passive dreamers lying down.
וְתַכְלִית שִׁיקּוּעַ בָּזֶה נִקְרָא "נִדָּח",
And the absolute depths of this condition is termed "an outcast",
שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹבֵד, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ שָׁקוּעַ בְּדָבָר אַחֵר וּמוּבְלָע בֵּין הָעַמִּים;
who is not completely lost, for he is not consumed by alien conquests nor swallowed among the gentiles;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא נִדָּח מִידִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
yet he is nonetheless banished from the conscious knowledge of Hashem.
וְהַנִּדָּחִים הַגְּמוּרִים הֵם הַמּוּמָרִים,
And the absolute outcasts are apostates,
שֶׁהֲגַם שֶׁאֵינָם שְׁכוּחִים מֵעִיקָּרָם כְּתִינוֹק שֶׁנִּשְׁבָּה לְבֵין הָעַמִּים וְנִטְמַע עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
who, although not fundamentally oblivious like an infant captured and raised among gentiles who never knew the name of Israel,
אֲבָל אֵלּוּ יָדְעוּ שֶׁהֵם יִשְׂרְאֵלִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּדְּחוּ.
these individuals consciously knew they were Israelites, yet willingly cast themselves out.
וְזֶה בָּא רַק מֵרוֹב בַּקָּשַׁת הַשַּׁלְוָה, וְלֹא לִהְיוֹת בְּשִׁעְבּוּד וּבַעֲבוֹדָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And this arose solely from an excessive pursuit of worldly comfort, wishing to escape the persecution and burdens of Jewish identity.

וְזֶה כֹּחַ אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כג)533 Vayikra Rabbah 23:2 — R. Elazar expounded the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt. Just as a lily set among thorns is hard for its owner to pluck, so was the redemption of Israel hard for the Holy One, blessed be He, to accomplish. That is what is written: "Or has any god ventured to come and take him a nation from the midst of a nation." These worshipped idols and those worshipped idols; these grew locks of hair and those grew locks of hair; these wore forbidden mixtures and those wore forbidden mixtures. If so, the attribute of justice would never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3): On "until Your people pass over, O Lord" [Berakhos 4a]: at the first entry [into the Land], "these worshipped idols…", and it was only because they are "Your people, O Lord," as a father has compassion on his son even though he does not walk in a good way; their acceptance of the Torah, too, was under compulsion. Not so the second entry, when they accepted it again willingly in the days of Ahasuerus. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): The exile of Egypt was an entry into their gates of impurity, as is known, and as the Sages said on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation": "these worshipped idols…". Yet they "acted only for appearance's sake": they were idol worshippers only in their outer garment, not inwardly. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): The redemption of Nisan is what the Blessed One Himself arouses, which is why it is called Nisan, from nes [miracle]: when Israel repent, the salvation comes by right, and only a complete miracle in all the worlds is called a miracle — like the Exodus, when He brought out "a nation from the midst of a nation," as the Sages said, "these [worshipped idols]…," and as it is written, "and you were naked and bare." Only the Blessed One, in His abundant mercy and kindness, sent them a sudden flow of light. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): The Egyptian exile was a preparation for the giving of the Torah, which is a gift — and a gift is what does not come by way of obligation and reward, that is, not through any arousal from below at all, as the Sages said on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation": "these worshipped idols…". Therefore the Torah is everywhere called a gift, [given] without any effort. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 1): Unlike a convert, who must first draw himself near, Israel the Blessed One draws near from His own side — as it was at the Exodus, when He took them "a nation from the midst of a nation" although they were enveloped in the shell of Egypt like a fetus in its mother's womb, as stated in the Pesikta and the Midrash, "these and those…". So too in the future, "as in the days of your going out of the land of Egypt I will show him wonders": the awakening will come from the side of the Blessed One. עַל "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי": "הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי";
And this is the spiritual force of Egypt, as our Sages expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 23) on "a nation from the midst of a nation": "these were idolaters, etc.";
הֲגַם שֶׁהָיוּ מְצוּיָּינִים שָׁם וְלֹא שִׁנּוּ אֶת שְׁמָם וּלְשׁוֹנָם וְשָׁמְרוּ יִחוּסָם וְלֹא נִטְמְעוּ בֵּינֵיהֶם לִהְיוֹת אוֹבְדִים,
for even though they were distinguished there, not changing their names, language, or pedigree, and avoiding assimilation,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרְאוּ "נִדָּחִים".
they were nonetheless termed "outcasts."
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחַ: "כִּי לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח" (שְׁמוּאֵל-ב יד, יד),
And Hashem promised: "that neither doth God take away life, but deviseth means that he that is banished be not an outcast from Him" (II Samuel 14:14),
כִּי יִתְעוֹרְרוּ לְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁיַּשְׁמִיעַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִלְבָבָם,
for they will be awakened by the blast of the Great Shofar that Hashem will sound into their hearts,
הֲגַם שֶׁיִּתְאַחֲרוּ מֵהָאוֹבְדִים מִצַּד הָעַצְלוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם וּצְרִיכִים לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יְתֵירָה;
even though they will arrive after the actively lost on account of their ingrained sluggishness, requiring extra exertion;
אֲבָל סוֹף יָבוֹאוּ כֻּלָּם לְהַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
yet ultimately all will arrive at the Holy Mountain in Jerusalem,
דְּשָׁם הוּא הֵיפֶךְ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי דִּמְיוֹנוֹת הָאֵלֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
where the absolute antithesis of both these illusions reigns, as mentioned above.

items.h:
Seif 2 — From the Human Shofar to the Great Shofar
Each Rosh Hashanah blast begins the awakening that will culminate in divine arousal and yearlong Torah labor.

p: וּבְכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הַשּׁוֹפָר הוּא מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם שֶׁאָנוּ תּוֹקְעִים בַּשּׁוֹפָר,
And on every Rosh Hashanah the shofar blast is generated through human initiative, as we actively blow the shofar,
וְלָכֵן אֵין נִקְרָא "שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל",
and therefore it is not termed "the Great Shofar",
דְּ"גָּדוֹל" רָצָה לוֹמַר הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט עַד אֵין קֵץ וְתַכְלִית.
for "great" denotes that which expands without boundary or end.
וְזֶהוּ "בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִתָּקַע" – מֵעַצְמוֹ,
And that is "in that day it shall be blown"—sounding on its own,
וְלֹא פֵּירֵשׁ מִי הַתּוֹקֵעַ,
Scripture not specifying who the blower is;
כִּי אָנוּ טוֹעֲנִים "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
for in exile we cry: "Turn us back unto You, Hashem, etc.",

וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר "שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה סוֹף אֵיכָה534 Eikhah Rabbah 5:21 — "Return us to You, O Lord, and we shall return" (Lamentations 5:21). The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, it is Yours — return us! He said to them: It is yours, as it is stated, "Return to Me and I will return to you, says the Lord" (Malachi 3:7). She said before Him: Master of the universe, it is Yours, as it is stated, "Return us, O God of our salvation" (Psalms 85:5). Therefore it says, "Return us to You, O Lord, and we shall return." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): Tishrei, the time of repentance in the Ten Days of Repentance, is Israel's returning to the Blessed One from their own side and by their own effort; as is known, we claim, "Return us to You and we shall return," while the Blessed One claims, "Return to Me and I will return to you." And our side prevailed, according to the view that "in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed," for the redemption of Nisan is what the Blessed One arouses. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 1): [In the future] the awakening will come from the side of the Blessed One, as we ask, "Return us, O Lord, to You, and we shall return"; and although the Blessed One says, "Return to Me and I will return to you," as the Midrash states at the end of Eikhah — meaning that He wants Israel to be awakened from below, from their own side, "listen, and your soul shall live" — nevertheless, from His own side the Blessed One draws Israel near first.);
while Hashem responds: "Return unto Me, etc." (as written in Midrash Rabbah, end of Eichah);
וּבַיּוֹם הַהוּא שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר הָאֱמֶת דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ חַד,
yet on that future day when the absolute truth is revealed that the Holy One and Israel are entirely one,
לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלָל לִקְרוֹא הָאִתְעָרוּתָא עַל שֵׁם אֶחָד בְּיִחוּד, כְּאִלּוּ יֵשׁ מְעוֹרֵר וּמִתְעוֹרֵר,
it will be inappropriate to attribute the awakening to one party alone, as though there were an external Awakener and an awakened recipient,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כּוּלָּא חַד.
for in ultimate reality all is unified as one.
וְאֵין שָׁם מָבוֹא לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, וְלֹא לְבַקָּשַׁת "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ",
And there is no entryway for separate human effort, nor for the plea of "Turn us back",
שֶׁזֶּה מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא;
which is human striving imploring an awakening from Above;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעַצְמוֹ הוּא דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִתָּקַע מֵעַצְמוֹ,
rather in truth Israel's intrinsic holiness is bound to Hashem and the shofar sounds of itself,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא גָּדוֹל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת.
and therefore it is "great" in boundless expansion.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, דְּצָרִיךְ לְמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי אָדָם לִתְקוֹעַ,
In contrast, on every Rosh Hashanah, requiring human action to sound the blast,
אֵינוֹ בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת גָּמוּר לָאוֹבְדִים וְנִדָּחִים גְּמוּרִים לָבוֹא לְגַמְרֵי לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת וְגוֹמֵר,
it does not expand completely to reach the absolute lost and outcasts to bring them fully to prostrate, etc.,
רַק הוּא כְּפוּם אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
operating only in proportion to the awakening from below.
וּמִי שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר וּמְקַיֵּים מִצְוַת ה',
And whoever hears the sound of the shofar and fulfills the commandment of Hashem,
הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר מִשִּׁיקּוּעוֹ בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
is aroused from his immersion in worldly illusions,
וּמִמֵּילָא הַשָּׂטָן מִתְעַרְבֵּב,
and consequently Satan is confounded,
כִּי עִיקַּר הַשְׂטָנָתוֹ הוּא הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בַּדִּמְיוֹנוֹת.
for the core of his prosecution is human immersion in illusions.
וְזֶה כָּל "הָאָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד" – לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה,
And this is the meaning of "man is born to toil"—to the toil of Torah,
לְהוֹצִיא עַצְמוֹ מִדִּמְיוֹן שָׁוְא וּלְדַבֵּק בְּתוֹרַת אֱמֶת.
to extract oneself from vain illusion and cleave to the Torah of Truth.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם מִתְעוֹרֵר בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאוֹם מִכָּל מִינֵי דִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְזוֹכֵר בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And when a person awakens suddenly from all forms of illusion and remembers Hashem,
הַשָּׂטָן מִתְעַרְבֵּב וּמִתְבַּלְבֵּל כֹּחַ הַהַשְׂטָנָה.
Satan is confounded and his accusatory power is thrown into confusion.
הֲגַם דְּאֵין כֹּוחוֹ כְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל לִהְיוֹת בִּיאָה גְּמוּרָה לְהַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
Even though this annual blast lacks the potency of the Great Shofar to effect complete arrival at the Holy Mountain—
דְּהַיְינוּ יְצִיאָה גְּמוּרָה מִן הַדִּמְיוֹן לַחֲלוּטִין שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּב עוֹד –
namely, a total and absolute departure from illusion never to return—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּלְבּוּל וְעִרְבּוּב לַהַשְׂטָנָה יֵשׁ;
nonetheless, a potent confusion and disruption of the prosecution is achieved;
וּמִמֵּילָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ חֶסֶד וְזוֹכֵר הַבְּרִית.
and Hashem, Who delights in lovingkindness, remembers the Covenant.

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז535 Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 16b:1:2 — "In order to confuse the Satan." The Arukh explained, as it appears in the Jerusalem Talmud: It is written "He will swallow up death forever," and it is written "And it shall come to pass on that day that a great shofar shall be sounded." When he hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed and not alarmed; but when he hears it a second time he says: This is surely the shofar of "a great shofar shall be sounded," and the time has come for him to be swallowed up — and he is thrown into confusion and has no leisure to act as accuser.:)
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Yerushalmi, cited in Tosafot, Rosh Hashanah 16b)
דְּהוּא חוֹשֵׁב דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל;
that Satan imagines that this is the Great Shofar;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּחוֹשֵׁב דְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת זוֹ תֵּלֵךְ וְתִתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּלֵּב לִהְיוֹת יָתֵד קָבוּעַ שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּט.
meaning he fears that this awakening will expand permanently in the heart as an immovable tent-peg.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַחִלּוּק שֶׁבֵּין שׁוֹפָר לְשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַקּוֹל;
And this is the primary distinction between the annual shofar and the Great Shofar: in the enduring expansion of the sound;
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לֹא נֶעֱקַר מִן הַלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי, כָּל הָאִתְעָרוּתָא הוּא לְפִי שָׁעָה לְבַד,
yet in this world, where the evil inclination has not been uprooted entirely from the heart, every awakening is temporary,

שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר רָע (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב536 Avodah Zarah 4b — And this is what R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: David was not fit for that deed, and Israel were not fit for that deed. David was not fit for that deed, as it is written: "and my heart is slain within me" [Psalms 109:22]. And Israel were not fit for that deed, as it is written: "Would that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments." Why then did they do it? Rashi: "That deed" is the affair of Bathsheba. "And my heart is slain within me" — the evil inclination is slain within me, and it has no power to rule within me. Maharsha: "They were not fit for that deed" means that they were fit to be saved by the Holy One, blessed be He, from so great a sin; for although all is in Heaven's hands save the fear of Heaven, still "in the way a man wishes to go he is led," and Torah too protects a man from sin (Sotah 21a) — and for the same reason David was fit to be saved from sin. This is why the verses are brought: "Would that they had such a heart as this always" shows that their will and their heart were to fear the Lord, and "my heart is slain within me" shows that David's was to do the will of his Father in Heaven. Hence the question, why then did they do it and were not saved from committing the sin. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 4b): The Blessed One did not decree that they should sin; His decree was only that repentance should exist in the world, for so long as repentance was absent from it the world was reckoned greatly deficient. Of themselves, then, Israel were not fit to sin, nor was David; but it was fitting that there be two in the world who are a beginning and a root, after whom the world would be drawn of itself in repentance — Israel who went out of Egypt, the beginning of the nation, and David, the first king, the beginning of individual men. And Israel, being the collective, sinned with idolatry, a sin of the intellect to which collectives are close, while David, being an individual, sinned with Bathsheba, a deed of the body.) בְּתַעֲנִית,
for so long as one's heart is not hollowed within him like King David who slew the evil inclination (Avodah Zarah 4b) through fasting,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִנָּתֵק כְּלָל.
it is impossible to remain perpetually established in his service without ever slipping.
וְזֶה כָּל עֵסֶק הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה: לִהְיוֹת "רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב",
And this is man's entire life's work in this world: to experience "running and returning" (ratzo va-shov),
וּלְהִתְחַזֵּק לְהִתְעוֹרֵר עַצְמוֹ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם.
and to summon strength to awaken himself from his slumber each time anew.
וְתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה הָיְתָה עַל כָּךְ: שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ יֵצֶר הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ, וְהוּא יִתְגַּבֵּר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ.
And the ultimate purpose of Creation was precisely this: that he possess an inclination that induces forgetfulness, and that he conquer it.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן "הָעֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ" דְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי הַפָּלַת תַּרְדֵּמָה,
And this is the secret of woman being "a helper opposite him," created through casting a deep sleep,
שֶׁהוּא הַבִּיטּוּל לְצוּרַת אָדָם, דִּבְשֵׁינָה כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה גּוֹבֵר,
which is the temporary suspension of conscious human form, where imagination dominates;

וְלָכֵן הוּא "אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בְּמִיתָה" (בְּרָכוֹת נז537 Berakhot 57b — Five things are each a sixtieth part, and these are they: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep and a dream. Fire is a sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey, a sixtieth of the manna; Shabbat, a sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep, a sixtieth of death; a dream, a sixtieth of prophecy. Maharsha: "One-sixtieth" is not meant precisely, as Tosafot write in several places. One may also explain it from the law of nullification, where one part in sixty is not nullified but retains something of substance — as we learn from the boiled foreleg [of the nazirite's ram]; so too here he speaks by way of resemblance, that in each of the things enumerated there is some small measure of the substance of that which it resembles. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Gemilus Chasadim 3): Precisely a sixtieth, since [one who shares another's illness] does not receive the essence of the illness; and anything that is not the essence of a thing is one part in sixty of it — as the Sages said, "a dream is a sixtieth of prophecy." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 18): The first stage of the falling is sleep, "and [the Lord God] cast a deep sleep" [upon Adam], as Bereishis Rabbah expounds on that verse; it is "one-sixtieth of death," for in it wisdom and understanding depart, as do all the attributes man possessed at the start of creation, when "God made man upright" and fit to dwell in the Garden of Eden.:);
and is therefore "one-sixtieth of death" (Berakhot 57b);
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִפִּיל זֶה עָלָיו,
and Hashem cast this upon him,
שֶׁכָּךְ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ: לִהְיוֹת הָאָדָם יָשֵׁן וּמִתְעוֹרֵר,
for Hashem established in His world that man sleep and awaken,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְ"עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ" בְּקִיּוּם הַמִּין בְּנִצְחִיּוּת וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
and through this he merits "a helper opposite him" in preserving the species eternally,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בַּדִּמְיוֹן גַּם כֵּן,
which is impossible without a measure of immersion in imagination as well,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט538 Yoma 69b — They said: Since it is a time of favor, let us pray also concerning the inclination to sexual transgression. They prayed, and it was delivered into their hands. [The prophet] said to them: See that if you kill this one, the world is finished. They imprisoned it for three days, and they sought a day-old egg throughout all the Land of Israel and none was to be found. They said: What shall we do? If we kill it, the world is finished; if we pray for half, they do not grant halves in heaven. They put out its eyes and let it go, and this availed, that a man is no longer aroused toward his close relatives. Rashi: "The world is finished": the world would come to an end, for there would be no procreation. "A day-old egg": an egg laid that same day; for the heat had ceased from [the hens'] innards, and even the eggs the hen had already conceived did not ripen within her. "For half": that it should hold sway over a man to be drawn to his wife and not to another. "They put out its eyes": they blinded its eyes with kohl. Maharsha (s.v. "let us pray concerning the inclination to transgression"): They sought to kill it, that is, to annul its power entirely, until they said that it cannot be annulled completely, in the manner of the saying about the evil inclination, "let the left hand push away and the right hand draw near." Nevertheless they annulled it somewhat, so that a man is not aroused more toward his relatives [than toward others]; but certainly nowadays too one is aroused toward relatives as toward others, as is said concerning seclusion with one's daughter. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaLashon 6): The sin of sexual immorality stems from the body and comes from the inclination for sexual immorality; and in Tractate Yoma and in Tractate Sanhedrin they said that there are two inclinations, the inclination for sexual immorality and the inclination for idolatry. These two evil inclinations correspond to the body and the soul: from the side of the body a man inclines to sexual immorality, which he desires, and from the side of the soul he inclines to idolatry. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:28): Of the inclination for sexual transgression [it is said], "a day-old egg was not to be found," which the early authorities explained as [referring to] prayer. This accords with what I wrote above from the Midrash HaNe'elam, that "desire for Torah was not to be found"; for prayer too requires desire and longing, and the root of that inclination in the hearts of Israel is only desire for Torah and longing for the salvation of God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): All [Israel] is one assembly, and a deficiency in part of it is in the whole; this brought about the destruction of the First Temple, until the Men of the Great Assembly arose to repair the assembly by nullifying the inclination for idolatry, and therefore they were called the Great Assembly, for through them the assembly was made great. But the inclination for sexual transgression remained, which causes licentiousness and the casting off of the yoke, and from it derive heresy and the Sadducees. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Megillah): At that time were the Men of the Great Assembly, who vanquished the inclination for idolatry; the inclination for sexual transgression too was in their hands and they wished to nullify it, only that this was not yet the will of the Blessed One, for He wished more precious souls to be born of Israel, and therefore He extended the time. Hence at that time it was close to the light of the Blessed One being revealed explicitly, without any garment. Sod Yesharim (Purim 32): In the days of Ahasuerus the Blessed One handed over to the Men of the Great Assembly the entire conduct [of the world] until the time of the end, as we find that the inclinations for idolatry and for sexual transgression were delivered into their hands. Had they wished, it was within their power to subdue all the forces in the world beneath them and bring them into holiness; but they held themselves back from receiving any good before the time that had arisen in His simple will to grant it to them.:): כְּשֶׁבִּיטְּלוּ יֵצֶר הָרָע דַּעֲרָיוֹת, לֹא אִשְׁתֲּכַח בֵּיעֲתָא.
as they taught in Yoma (69b): when they nullified the urge for licentiousness, not even a fresh egg could be found.
וְיִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת הוּא הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּדִמְיוֹן שֶׁל בַּטָּלָה דּוּגְמַת הַשֵּׁינָה.
And the urge for illicit desire is immersion in passive fantasy akin to sleep.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא יִתְבַּטֵּל לְגַמְרֵי גַּם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
And this will not be extinguished entirely even in the Future to Come,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קלז עַמּוּד א) דְּאִקְרֵי לָבָן דְּאִתְלַבַּן,
as written in the Zohar (I 137a) that it is called Laban because it is whitened and refined,
דְּאִי לָאו הָכִי חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא לָא אִשְׁתֲּכַח,
for were it not so, passionate desire for Torah would not exist,
כִּי יִהְיוּ כְּמַלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע, וְלֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לָהֶם מִטַּעַם זֶה.
since they would resemble angels who have no evil inclination, to whom Torah was not given for this reason.
כִּי עִיקַּר חֵשֶׁק הַתּוֹרָה מִצַּד הַמִּלּוּי לַחִסָּרוֹן,
For the core yearning for Torah arises from filling a deficiency,
שֶׁהִיא תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר רָע, וְהַיְינוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת וְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת הֲבָלִים.
Torah serving as the spice counteracting the inclination—namely lust and immersion in vain fantasies.
עַל זֶה הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין: לִהְיוֹת כָּל דִּמְיוֹנוֹתָיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
Against this the Torah is a purifying spice: channeling all one's imaginative powers into words of Torah,
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁכֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה יוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט גַּם כֵּן בְּמַחְשֶׁבֶת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
as is known that the imagination can also expand through thoughts of Torah
הַבָּאִים מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה, עַד שֶׁגַּם הַדִּמְיוֹן כֻּלּוֹ תּוֹרָה וֶאֱמֶת.
until even the imaginative faculty becomes entirely Torah and Truth.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁהוּא עֲבוֹדָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת זָרָה,
In contrast to the impulse for idolatry, which is alien divine service and corrupt striving;
זֶה צָרִיךְ לַעֲקוֹר לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ אֵל וְכֹחַ זָר, וּלְאַכְפַּיָּא וּלְבַטְּלוֹ לְגַמְרֵי.
this must be uprooted entirely so that no foreign god or power resides within, subjugating and annulling it completely.
כִּי יֵצֶר זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד בְּרִיאַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּסַּד בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
For this inclination was not part of Hashem's intrinsic blueprint of Creation,
רַק בָּא מִצַּד הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ.
but entered through the seduction of the Serpent.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִזְהִיר עַל זֶה מֵאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלֹּא כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And Hashem warned against this through the Tree of Knowledge, which represents striving contrary to divine will.

רַק בִּבְרִיאַת הָאִשָּׁה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יז, ו)539 Bereshit Rabbah 17:6 — R. Chanina son of Rav Idi said: From the beginning of the book until here no samekh is written; once she was created, Satan was created with her. And if a person should say to you, "It is the one that encircles [hasovev]," say to him: those verses speak of the rivers.: נֶאֱמַר סמֶ"ךְ, שֶׁבָּא שָׂטָן עִמָּהּ;
