Yet regarding the creation of woman our Sages noted (Bereishit Rabbah 17:6): the letter Samekh appears (va-yisgor), indicating that Satan was created with her;
הוּא הַהַשְׂטָנָה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁינָה וְהַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּדִמְיוֹן שָׁוְא שֶׁזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה תֵּיכֶף.
this being the temptation stemming from sleep and immersion in empty illusion which occurred immediately.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אֵינוֹ מִתְעוֹרֵר מִזֶּה, אָז הִיא הַגּוֹרֶמֶת לַאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
And when one does not awaken from this, it leads to the eating from the Tree of Knowledge, which is the urge for idolatry.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁינָה רַק כְּרֶגַע כְּפִי צֹרֶךְ הַסִּכְלוּת מוּעָט
However, when sleep is momentary, limited to that brief touch of folly

שֶׁהָיָה בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִהְיוֹת "יָקָר מֵחָכְמָה וּמִכָּבוֹד540 Ecclesiastes 10:1 — “Dead flies cause the perfumer’s ointment to stink and ferment; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honour.” Rashi: "Dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink and bubble" — in the winter season flies have no strength and are near death, yet if one falls into the perfumer's oil and mingles with the spices it makes it putrid and raises a froth in which bubbles appear, and this is the sense of "bubble": a trifling thing has spoiled a precious one. So too a little foolishness outweighs wisdom and honor: a man whose merits and transgressions are evenly balanced who then commits one transgression has tipped the scale against himself, and that small foolishness weighs more than all the wisdom and honor he had. Metzudas Dovid: "Dead flies" — each dead fly that falls into perfumer's oil of strong fragrance makes the oil stink, and the stench does not cease, for the fly makes it bubble forth like a flowing spring; thus a trifling thing has spoiled a precious one. "Outweighs wisdom" — so a man who is precious and esteemed for the wisdom and honor found in him: if a little foolishness is also found in him, that foolishness destroys his esteem." (קֹהֶלֶת י, א) וּמִתְעוֹרֵר תֵּיכֶף,
which Hashem willed so that wisdom is cherished out of brief obscurity, and one awakens instantly,
אָז הוּא "הָעֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ",
then she is "a helper opposite him",
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר.
representing the assistance the Holy One provides to help man conquer the base urge.
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּרָא הַיֵּצֶר, הֲרֵי עַל כָּרְחֲךָ לְכָךְ בְּרָאוֹ: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְגַּבֵּר הָאָדָם נֶגְדּוֹ וְלֹא לְהִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ.
For since the Holy One created the evil inclination, He created it so that man might conquer it rather than succumb.
וְנִמְצָא מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּרָאוֹ הוּא עַצְמוֹ הָעֵזֶר שֶׁלּוֹ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדּוֹ, שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי לְכָךְ נִבְרָא.
Thus the fact that the Holy One created it is itself man's helper to overcome it, as God assists him, for this was its sole purpose.

וּבְכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא זֵכֶר לְיוֹם בְּרִיאַת אָדָם, דְּלָכֵן "כָּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם עוֹבְרִים וְכוּלֵי, סִפְרֵי חַיִּים וְסִפְרֵי מֵתִים וְכוּלֵי541 Rosh Hashanah 16a; 32b — At four seasons the world is judged: on Pesach concerning the grain; on Shavuot concerning the fruit of the tree; on Rosh Hashanah all who come into the world pass before Him like sheep, as it is said, “He who fashions their hearts together, who discerns all their deeds”; and on the Festival they are judged concerning water. And in Rosh Hashanah 32b: R. Abbahu said — the ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, why do Israel not sing before You on Rosh Hashanah and on Yom Kippur? He said to them: Is it possible that the King sits upon the throne of judgment, with the books of the living and the books of the dead open before Him, and Israel sing songs? Rashi: "At four seasons" — of the year, the world is judged. "Like benei maron" and the verse "He who fashions their hearts together" are explained in the Gemara [18a]. Tosafos (s.v. "on Pesach concerning the grain"): From the account in chapter Mi She-meito (Berakhot 18b) of the pious man whose wife provoked him on the eve of Rosh Hashanah, it appears that it was on Rosh Hashanah that he heard two spirits telling each other what they had heard from behind the curtain: that whoever sows at the first rainfall, hail will strike it. Perhaps in heaven on Rosh Hashanah they were recalling the judgment decreed on Pesach; or else [that account] follows R. Yehuda, who says that all are judged on Rosh Hashanah and the sentence concerning grain is [sealed] on Pesach. Maharsha (32b, s.v. "why do Israel not sing before You"): It is explained in chapter Ein Ne'erachin [Arakhin 10b] that it would have been fitting to say song on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, since they are called "appointed times" and are sanctified by the prohibition of labor, were it not for this reason: "Is it possible that the King sits upon the throne of judgment…" Maharsha (s.v. "on Pesach"): The Ran derives the judgment of Rosh Hashanah from "at the covering [of the moon] for our festival day… for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment of the God of Jacob" (Psalms 81:4–5); but our sugya implies that [the Mishnah] relies also on "Remembrances, so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good" — something needed on the day of judgment, which is why it is called "a remembrance of terua," for the remembrance of all who come into the world comes before Him. That all are judged on Rosh Hashanah means every individual in every matter, as we say on Rosh Hashanah, "who by hunger and who by thirst"; whereas at each of the other three seasons the world as a whole is judged on one of the three things named. Maharsha (s.v. "pass"): For the other three seasons the Mishnah uses the term "judged," but here it changes to "pass [before Him]." According to the conclusion below, that the Mishnah follows [the school of] R. Yishmael, whereby man's sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur and the Mishnah speaks of the beginning of judgment, this is well: since it is not sealed on Rosh Hashanah, it uses only the term "pass." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a): Rosh Hashanah is the head of the year, its root and essence, and man too is the beginning and essence of creation, comprising all of it, and is called "the head of the dust of the world" [Proverbs 8:26]; therefore it is fitting that man be judged on Rosh Hashanah, this day, the essence of the whole year, being his in particular. And the four seasons correspond to the four elements by which the world is conducted: on Pesach the grain, the growth of the earth; on Shavuot the fruit of the tree, which grows by the air; and on Rosh Hashanah all who come into the world, corresponding to fire, for the soul of man is the natural heat of the heart.".
And on every Rosh Hashanah, commemorating the creation of Adam, all creatures pass before Him for judgment in books of life and books of death.
כִּי בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם הוּא בַּמַּאֲמָר "נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם",
For the creation of man occurred through the utterance "Let us make man",

וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ח)542 Bereshit Rabbah 8:5 — R. Simon said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create the first man, the ministering angels formed themselves into factions and groups; some said, Let him not be created, and some said, Let him be created. That is what is written, "Kindness and truth have met, righteousness and peace have kissed." Kindness said, Let him be created, for he performs acts of kindness; Truth said, Let him not be created, for he is all falsehood; Righteousness said, Let him be created, for he performs righteous deeds; Peace said, Let him not be created, for he is all strife. R. Huna, the elder of Sepphoris, said: While the ministering angels were disputing with one another and occupied with one another, the Holy One, blessed be He, created him. He said to them: Why are you disputing? Man is already made. שֶׁאָמַר לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת,
which our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 8) that He spoke to the ministering angels,
וְנַעֲשׂוּ כִּתּוֹת כִּתּוֹת וְכוּלֵי, אָמַר לָהֶם: "עַד שֶׁאַתֶּם מִדַּיְּינִים כְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה אָדָם".
and they split into factions, until God said: "While you are debating, man has already been made."
פֵּירוּשׁ: מַלְאָכִים הֵם הַכֹּחוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁכֻּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בָּאָדָם,
The meaning is: angels are the diverse cosmic forces established by Hashem, all encompassed within man,
שֶׁהוּא בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם,
who is created in the image of God, Master of all forces,
וּכְפִי מִסְפַּר הַכֹּחוֹת הֵם מִסְפַּר הַמַּלְאָכִים.
and commensurate with the number of forces is the number of angels.
וּ"מִדַּיְּינִים" הַיְינוּ כָּל כֹּחַ נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיָנוֹ אֵיךְ הוּא בָּאָדָם, אִם לְטָב וְכוּלֵי,
And "debating" means that each force was revealed and evaluated as to how it functions within man, whether for good, etc.,
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה אָדָם.
and automatically through this contemplation man was already formed.
כִּי עֲשִׂיָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת בְּכָל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹתָיו,
For Hashem's creation of man unfolds through His profound contemplation of all human faculties,
דְּזֶהוּ בַּמַּאֲמָר נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם.
which is the principle that the universe was created through Divine Speech.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)543 Shabbat 119b — R. Elazar said: From where do we know that speech is like action? For it is stated: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of His mouth" [Psalms 33:6]. Rashi: [Read not "were finished" but] "they finished": the Holy One, blessed be He, and this person, who recounts the praise of the Omnipresent and the praise of the Shabbat. Maharsha: One who says "And [the heavens and the earth] were finished" bears witness to the work of Creation, and so becomes a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, for without his testimony His work would not be known. And just as the making was by utterance alone — hence the proof "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made" — so his testimony is by utterance, and it is as though he became a partner through utterance. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 119b): Israel alone are the essential creation of the Holy One, blessed be He — the creation of the nations is secondary, following upon it — and an essential effect testifies to its cause; so when Israel say "And [the heavens and the earth] were finished," the effect bearing witness to the Cause who made all, it is as though they became partners with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of Creation. Alternatively, in its plain sense: unlike His other acts in the world, which are carried out through intermediaries, heaven and earth were made by His word alone — hence the proof that speech is called action, "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made" — and so one who says "And they were finished" at its proper time, when sanctifying the day, joins his speech to the speech by which the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world. דְּדִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
And as written in Shabbat (119b) that the speech of Hashem is equivalent to actual deed,
וְדִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא עוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים,
and Hashem's speech constitutes the angelic realm,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה בָּלָק)544 Bamidbar Rabbah 20:18 — "And the Lord put a word in Balaam's mouth" [Numbers 23:5] — He twisted his mouth and bridled it, like a man driving a nail into a board. R. Elazar says: an angel was doing the speaking. עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּשֶׂם ה' דָּבָר בְּפִי בִלְעָם" – מַלְאָךְ.
as our Sages expounded (Bamidbar Rabbah, Balak) on "and Hashem placed a word in Balaam's mouth"—an angel.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם מִדַּיְּינִים וּמְבָרְרִים כֹּחוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם פְּרָטֵי כֹּחוֹת הָאָדָם,
And through this process of clarifying these forces, which are the components of human nature,
מִמֵּילָא נַעֲשָׂה אָדָם בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת הָהֵם,
man was formed within the World of Asiyah, encompassing all these traits,
וְהוּא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל צֶאֱצָאָיו,
this being Adam the first man who contained all his descendants,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מ)545 Shemot Rabbah 40:3 — While Adam the first man still lay as a shapeless mass, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him every righteous man destined to arise from him: some suspended from Adam’s head, some from his hair, some from his forehead, some from his eyes, and some from his other limbs. Know this: when Job sought to argue with the Holy One, blessed be He, He answered him, “Where [eifo] were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?” R. Shimon ben Lakish said: He said to him — Job, tell Me where your measure [eifah] was suspended: from his head, from his forehead, or from which of his limbs? If you know where your measure was, you may argue with Me. דְּכֻלָּם תְּלוּיִים בְּאֵיפַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
as written in Shemot Rabbah (40) that all souls hung within the stature of Adam.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, סִפְרֵי חַיִּים וְסִפְרֵי מֵתִים,
This means that all souls, whether inscribed in the book of the living or the dead,
אֵינָם אֶלָּא קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה הַכְּלוּלָה מִכָּל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִים בִּפְרָט בִּפְרָטֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
constitute a single complete stature, subdivided into varied individual souls.
וְכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִתְעוֹרֵר זֶה,
And on every Rosh Hashanah this cosmic evaluation is reawakened,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן קְדוּשַׁת הַזְּמַנִּים דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי":
as is known that in the sanctification of the festivals by Israel,
עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בָּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא הָרָאוּי לַזְּמַן הַהוּא בְּזֶה שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה.
through awakening from below there descends an awakening from Above reflecting that original cosmic event.
וּבְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת בְּכֹחוֹת אָדָם, מִמֵּילָא "כָּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם עוֹבְרִים וְכוּלֵי כֻּלָּן בִּסְקִירָה אַחַת",
And through this reawakened contemplation of human faculties, all humankind passes before Him in a single glance,
דְּהַיְינוּ בַּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת דְּ"נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם".
which is the pristine divine gaze of "Let us make man."
וּמִצַּד הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת בְּכֹחוֹתָיו בָּא כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁינָה גַּם כֵּן וְהַפָּלַת הַתַּרְדֵּמָה,
And alongside this evaluation of his faculties arises the power of sleep and slumber,
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה סוֹד הַדּוּרְמִיטָא דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
and as is known through the teachings of the holy Ari regarding the mystery of the slumber of Ze'eir Anpin on Rosh Hashanah,
שֶׁהַשּׁוֹפָר בָּא לְעוֹרֵר זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין מִשְּׁנָתוֹ.
wherein the shofar serves to awaken Ze'eir Anpin from his slumber.
וּבֵיאוּר זֶה: כַּיָּדוּעַ דַּאֲצִילוּת הוּא מַה שֶּׁהֶאֱצִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאוֹר כְּבוֹדוֹ הַבִּלְתִּי בַּעַל תַּכְלִית לְהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם.
And the explanation of this: the World of Atzilut is what Hashem emanated from His infinite light for human comprehension.
וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מַשִּׂיג מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד מִדּוֹתָיו הַמְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת בָּעוֹלָם,
Namely, what man grasps of Hashem's truth through His active attributes in the world,
זֶה נִקְרָא "עוֹלַם הָאֲצִילוּת" שֶׁנֶּאֱצַל מֵאֲמִיתָּתוֹ הַבִּלְתִּי מוּשָּׂג לִהְיוֹת מוּשָּׂג,
this is termed Atzilut, emanated from His unknowable Essence to become graspable,
וְהוּא מַמָּשׁ כְּקוֹמַת הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא הַמַּשִּׂיג: כְּפִי כֹּחוֹת הַשָּׂגוֹתָיו כָּךְ הוּא מִדַּת הַהַשָּׂגָה.
mirroring the stature of man who perceives: according to his capacity, so is the measure of divine apprehension.
וְזֶהוּ זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין דַּאֲצִילוּת שֶׁהוּא צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
And this is Ze'eir Anpin of Atzilut, the celestial form of Jacob engraved on the Throne of Glory,
שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם הַמַּשִּׂיגִים;
which embodies the collective of Israel who perceive;
וּכְפִי מִדַּת הַשָּׂגָתָם הוּא הוּא עַצְמוֹ מִדַּת הַהַשָּׂגָה הַנֶּאֱצֶלֶת.
and in proportion to their spiritual comprehension is the manifested emanation.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵם בְּשֵׁינָה וְהֶעְדֵּר הַהַשָּׂגָה,
And when they are asleep and devoid of divine perception,
הֲרֵי נִקְרָא דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין יָשֵׁן כִּבְיָכוֹל, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַמַּשִּׂיג אֲמִיתָּתוֹ.
Ze'eir Anpin is described as sleeping, as it were, since there is no mortal grasping His truth.
וְעִיקַּר עוֹלַם אֲצִילוּת הוּא הַהַשָּׂגָה מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמּוּשָּׂג לִבְנֵי אָדָם;
For the primary function of Atzilut is divine illumination grasped by human beings;
וְלָכֵן הַפָּלַת תַּרְדֵּמָה דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נִקְרָא שֵׁינַת זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין.
therefore the slumber cast upon Adam is termed the sleep of Ze'eir Anpin.
וְזֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר בְּכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה עִנְיַן בְּרִיאַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
And on every Rosh Hashanah the creation of the evil inclination is reawakened,

שֶׁמִּזֶּה: "וַיָּבוֹא גַם הַשָּׂטָן בְּתוֹכָם לְהִתְיַצֵּב" (אִיּוֹב א, ו546 Job 1:6 — Now it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, that the Adversary also came among them. Rashi: "And it came to pass on the day" — that day was the New Year, the day of the sounding of the horn, and the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the Adversary to bring the merit and the guilt of all creatures; this is the meaning of "from roaming the earth." "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord" — to contend with Him, for "standing" is used only of judgment, as it is said, "the Lord stands up to plead"; "and the Adversary also came among them" — to accuse the creatures. Metzudas Dovid: "And it came to pass on the day" means the day appointed for the angels above, those who plead merit and those who plead guilt, to come before the Omnipresent — the day of the New Year, which is the day of judgment. "The sons of God" are those who plead merit, and "the Adversary also" came to plead guilt and to accuse the creatures. Malbim: "The sons of God" are the powers set within the whole of creation, His children and the work of His hands, and they "came to stand before the Lord" in that He brings all existence into being, the world's continuance being a continual creation. The Adversary is the power of privation, the source of evil, corruption, sin and every loss; Scripture therefore does not say that he came to stand together with them, but only that he "came among them," for he has no root in being, only in privation.);
whence: "and Satan came also among them to present himself" (Job 1:6);
הוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
this being the evil inclination that Hashem established in His world;
בִּכְלַל הַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הָאָדָם יֵשׁ גַּם כֹּחַ זֶה דְּשֵׁינָה,
within the spectrum of angels that constitute the human faculties exists this power of sleep,
וְיוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן, שֶׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת, וּמִזֶּה בָּא הַהַשְׂטָנָה.
the idle person being likened to a sleeper, sunken in illusion, whence accusation arises.
וְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר מְעוֹרֵר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ,
And the voice of the shofar awakens him from his slumber,
הַיְינוּ קוֹלוֹת דְּקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
echoing the shofar blasts sounded prior to the Giving of the Torah;
דְּבָרָא תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין, וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לַתּוֹרָה הָיָה בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר הַמְּעוֹרֵר מִשֵּׁינַת מִצְרַיִם הַקּוֹדֶמֶת.
for He created the Torah as a purifying spice, and this awakening to Torah came through the shofar blast that roused Israel from the Egyptian slumber.
וְכֵן כָּל שׁוֹפָר שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין בְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה כֻּלָּהּ,
And so every shofar blown on Rosh Hashanah is the inception of an awakening to engage in Torah as a spiritual remedy throughout the year,
כָּל חַד לְפוּם דַּרְגָּא דִּילֵיהּ;
each person according to his individual rung;
עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת שְׁמִיעַת קוֹל שׁוֹפָר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא זוֹכֶה לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ בְּכָל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כֻּלָּהּ וּלְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בַּתּוֹרָה.
through the commandment of hearing the shofar on Rosh Hashanah, one merits to be aroused from spiritual slumber across all the days of the year and to labor in Torah.

sections.en: Malchiyot, Zikhronot, Shofrot, and the Patriarchs

items.h: The structure of Rosh Hashanah prayer and shofar sounds reflects the three Patriarchs and unifies kingship, remembrance, and spiritual awakening.

Seif 1 — Three Patriarchs in the Rosh Hashanah Service
Malchiyot, Zikhronot, Shofrot, and the shofar's triple patterns channel the three patriarchal powers into one heart.

p: עִנְיַן מַלְכִיּוֹת, זִכְרוֹנוֹת, שׁוֹפָרוֹת – הֵם נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲבָהָן.
The matter of Malchiyot (Kingship), Zikhronot (Remembrances), and Shofrot (Shofar blasts) corresponds to the three Patriarchs.
וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה קוֹלוֹת דִּתְרוּעָה, וּפְשׁוּטָה לְפָנֶיהָ וּפְשׁוּטָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
And likewise the three sounds of the teruah, with a plain blast (tekiah) before it and a plain blast after it.
וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי תְּרוּעוֹת: גְּנוֹחֵי וִילוֹלֵי, וּגְנוֹחֵי לְבַד וִילוֹלֵי לְבַד.
And likewise the three forms of teruot: groaning and wailing (shevarim-teruah), groaning alone (shevarim), and wailing alone (teruah).
וְכֵן הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה סְדָרִים שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ: תְּקִיעוֹת דִּמְיוּשָׁב, וּדְבִלְחַשׁ, וּדְחַזָּרַת הַשְּׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר
And so too the three instituted orders: the sitting blasts, the silent Amidah blasts, and the Reader's repetition blasts,
[וְעֶשֶׂר אַחֲרוֹנוֹת הֵם נֶגֶד מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם],
and the final ten blasts correspond to the attribute of King David, peace be upon him,
כִּי בְּהִתְיַיחֵד אֲבָהָן יַחַד כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מִכֻּלָּם,
for when the Patriarchs unite together, each one is subsumed within all of them,
וְכֵן הוֹלֵךְ הִתְכַּלְלוּת זֶה בְּכָל פְּרָט לִהְיוֹת כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מֵהַכֹּל.
and this inter-inclusion proceeds through every individual detail so that each reflects the whole.
וּכְלַל הַיּוֹם נִקְרָא "יוֹם תְּרוּעָה" וְלֹא "יוֹם תְּקִיעָה",
And the day as a whole is titled "a day of teruah" (blowing/breaking) and not "a day of tekiah",
דְּעִיקַּר מִצְוַת הַיּוֹם בִּתְרוּעָה,
because the primary commandment of the day consists of the broken teruah blast,
וְהַתְּקִיעוֹת נִקְרָא רַק "לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ".
and the plain tekiot are merely defined as "before it and after it."

כִּי יוֹם זֶה נִקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר רֵישׁ תִּיקּוּן מא)547 Tikkunei Zohar 81a — "In the beginning [Bereshit]" — there is Tishrei; and this is the second arm, the second day, of which it is said: "He made darkness His hiding place" [Psalms 18:12]. "יוֹמָא תִּנְיָנָא",
For this day is called in the Zohar (Tikkunei Zohar, beginning of Tikkun 41) "the second day" (Gevurah),

וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב548 Rosh Hashanah 32b — R. Abbahu said: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, why do Israel not sing song before You on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur? He said to them: Is it possible — the King sits upon the throne of judgment, and the books of the living and the books of the dead are open before Him, and Israel are to sing song? Maharsha: Song [that is, Hallel] would properly have been said on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur, since they are called "appointed seasons" and are hallowed by the prohibition of work, were it not for this reason: "Is it possible — the King sits upon the throne of judgment…" (as explained in Arakhin 10b).:) "יוֹם הַדִּין",
and in the words of our Sages (Rosh Hashanah 32b) "the Day of Judgment",
דְּמֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא מִשְׁפָּט;
wherein the King sits upon the throne of judgment;
וּמִצַּד הִסְתַּעֲפוּת מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט, יָדוּעַ דְּנִמְשָׁךְ הַפְּסֹלֶת: עֵשָׂו אִישׁ שָׂעִיר, גְּבַר שֵׁדִין הַמּוּכָן לְשׁוֹדֵד, רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.
and from the branching outward of strict judgment, it is known that the dross issues forth: Esau the hairy man, a demonic warrior poised to pillage, Heaven preserve us.
וְהַתְּרוּעָה הוּא שְׁבִירָה, מִלְּשׁוֹן "תְּרֹעֵם בְּשֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל" (תְּהִלִּים ב, ט),
And the teruah signifies breaking, related to "You shall break them with a rod of iron" (Psalms 2:9),
לְנַפֵּץ וּלְשַׁבֵּר חַרְבּוֹ דְּעֵשָׂו.
to shatter and crush the sword of Esau.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַשּׁוֹפָר, שֶׁהוּא קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב,
And this is the core of the shofar, which is the voice of Jacob,

וּבִזְמַן שֶׁ"הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב" אֵין וְכוּלֵי549 Bereshit Rabbah 65:20 — “The voice is the voice of Yaakov, but the hands are the hands of Esav.” When the voice of Yaakov is heard in the houses of prayer and study, the hands of Esav have no power; and when his voice is not heard, the hands of Esav prevail. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סה),
and whenever "the voice is the voice of Jacob," the hands of Esau have no dominion (Bereishit Rabbah 65),
כִּי כֹּוחוֹ בְּפִיו לְשַׁבֵּר כָּל הַמַּסָכִים וְהַמְקַטְרְגִים עַל יְדֵי קוֹל תּוֹרָה וְקוֹל תְּפִלָּה
for his power lies in his mouth to tear down all partitions and accusers through the sound of Torah and the sound of prayer,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּשִׂמְחָה.
which must be conducted with sacred joy.
וְזֶהוּ פְּשׁוּטָה לְפָנֶיהָ וּפְשׁוּטָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ,
And this is the straight blast before it and the straight blast after it,
דִּתְקִיעָה הוּא לְשִׂמְחָה,
for the plain tekiah signifies joy,
דַּרְגָּא דֶּ"אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" – הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה,
the level of "truth to Jacob" (Tiferet)—namely the Torah,
וְאַבְרָהָם הוּא הַמַּתְחִיל בִּתְפִלָּה וְתִקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית.
and Abraham is the initiator of prayer, instituting the morning prayer (Shacharit).
וְכֵן יָדוּעַ דְּ"אַבָּא יָסַד בְּרַתָּא", שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה
And so too it is known that "the Father founded the Daughter (Malchut)," which is the level of prayer,
הִתְחִיל מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִתְחַבֵּר עִם לוֹט
beginning from our father Abraham, peace be upon him, who associated with Lot,

כְּטַעַם (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נ)550 Bereshit Rabbah 50:10 — "And your two daughters who are found here" — R. Toviah bar R. Yitzchak said: Two finds, Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite. R. Yitzchak said: "I have found David My servant" — where did I find him? In Sodom. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 2): Abraham our father, who chose exile, is the foundation of faith, and with him began the revelation of the trait of King David, as it is said, "Where did I find him? In Sodom" — for there faith was in exile. With the overturning of Sodom Abraham drew the holy sparks out from there and took in the foundation of faith ("and he believed in the Lord"), to root it in his descendants after him.: "הֵיכָן מְצָאתִיו? בִּסְדוֹם", כַּנּוֹדָע.
mirroring: "Where did I find David? In Sodom" (Bereishit Rabbah 50), as is known.
וּבֵינְתַיִם הוּא קוֹל הַתְּשׁוּבָה מֵעוּמְקָא דְלִבָּא
And in between lies the sound of repentance emerging from the depth of the heart,
שֶׁהוּא בִּמְרִירוּת הַלֵּב:
which unfolds in profound bitterness of soul:
"גְּנוֹחֵי גָּנַח" וְ"יִלוֹלֵי יָלֵיל" עַל כֹּבֶד הָעֲווֹנוֹת,
groaning and wailing over the oppressive weight of iniquities,
בַּאֲנָחָה הַשּׁוֹבֶרֶת כָּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הַבָּאָה מִצַּד הַדְּאָגָה וְהַפַּחַד,
with a sigh that shatters a man's entire body stemming from anxiety and dread,
וְזֶהוּ תְּשׁוּבָה מִיִּרְאָה.
and this constitutes repentance out of fear.
וְהַיְלָלָה בִּבְכִי כְּבֵן הַמִּתְגַּעְגֵּעַ לִפְנֵי אָבִיו הוּא תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה.
And wailing in weeping like a child pining before his father is repentance out of love.
וּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִיא תְּשׁוּבָה הַבָּאָה מִצַּד הַרְגָּשַׁת הַכְּאֵב וְהַצַּעַר
And the attribute of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, is repentance born of feeling the anguish and pain
אֵיךְ "רַע וָמָר עָזְבֵךְ אֶת ה'",
of how "evil and bitter is your forsaking of Hashem" (Jeremiah 2:19),
וּמְעוֹרֵר רַחֲמִים רַבִּים בְּקִרְבּוֹ עַל נַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁנִּתְרַחֲקָה בַּעֲווֹנוֹתֶיהָ מֵאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים.
arousing abundant compassion within himself over his soul that was distanced by its sins from the light of the King of Life.
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
And this is Jacob's rung whose form is engraved on the Throne of Glory,
שֶׁהוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
which is absolute cleaving unto the living God,
לִהְיוֹת "אַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים וְגוֹמֵר" – דְּבוּקִים מַמָּשׁ,
to realize "you that cleave unto Hashem"—cleaving literally,
וְרוֹצֶה לַחֲזוֹר לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ וְלִמְקוֹם דְּבֵיקוּתוֹ.
yearning to return to his root and the locus of his divine attachment.
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה הוּא: בְּרֵישָׁא גָּנַח וַהֲדַר יָלֵיל,
And repentance along this path proceeds: first groaning and then wailing,
כְּדֶרֶךְ הַחוֹלִים עַל צַעַר גּוּפָם,
in the manner of the sick over their bodily affliction,
שֶׁבָּרִאשׁוֹנָה מַרְגִּישׁ פַּחַד הַמַּחֲלָה וּמִתְאַנֵּחַ,
who initially feels the dread of disease and sighs,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַזְכִּיר אַהֲבַת עַצְמוֹ וּמְיַלֵּל עַל צַעֲרוֹ.
and subsequently recalls self-love and wails over his pain.
וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי תְּשׁוּבוֹת הַלָּלוּ מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא הֵם:
And these three categories of repentance ascending from below to Above are:
בַּתְּחִלָּה מְרַחֵם עַל עַצְמוֹ, וְזֶה קַל לְכָל אָדָם לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ;
first a person pities himself, which is easy for anyone to arouse naturally from within;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַתְחִיל לְהַרְגִּישׁ פַּחַד ה' וַהֲדַר גְּאוֹנוֹ וּמִתְאַנֵּחַ עַל יְדֵי כֵן עַל חֲטָאָיו;
afterward he begins to perceive the awe of Hashem and His majesty, groaning over his sins on account of this;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבוֹכֶה לְפָנָיו עַל מַה שֶּׁכְּבָר עָבַר וְאַיִן.
and ultimately he attains pure love of Hashem, blessed be He, weeping before Him over what has past and is lost.

וּלְפִי שֶׁמִּצַּד מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה551 Jerusalem Talmud Makkot 2:6 — They asked Wisdom: The sinner — what is his punishment? She said to them: “Evil pursues sinners.” They asked Prophecy: The sinner — what is his punishment? She said to them: “The soul that sins, it shall die.” They asked the Holy One, blessed be He: The sinner — what is his punishment? He said to them: Let him repent, and it shall be atoned for him. This is what is written: “Therefore He instructs sinners in the way” — He instructs sinners in the way to repent. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "They asked Wisdom"): This is said by way of an analogy: from the side of wisdom and from the side of prophecy the sinner had no remedy at all, and it is the Holy One, blessed be He, who acts beyond the strict line of the law and receives him in repentance. More than that — to anyone who wishes to return He shows the way to make a complete and proper repentance; and this too is included in the exposition above, "why is He good... and why is He upright," that is, the added measure by which He both accepts repentance and teaches its way. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTeshuvah 1): Wisdom answers "Evil pursues sinners" because sin is a deficiency, and it is not fitting that a deficiency exist in the world, so the evil that is in the world pursues the sinner to destroy him from it; prophecy, which comes from above, where no evil descends, therefore says outright "the soul that sins, it shall die." The Torah, whose whole office is the rectification of man, answers that he should bring a guilt offering and be atoned for, since that is the sinner's rectification. But the Holy One, blessed be He, says "let him repent," for the sinner whose heart is broken and crushed over his sin is received by Him on that very account — this is His own measure, since the vessels He uses are broken vessels. (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי מַכּוֹת פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ו):
And because from the perspective of strict Justice our Sages stated (Yerushalmi Makkot 2:6):
אָמַר לַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, אָמַר לַנְּבוּאָה וְכוּלֵי, דְּאֵין מָקוֹם לִתְשׁוּבָה,
it asked of Torah, etc., it asked of Prophecy, etc., which said that there is no room for repentance,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבַע בְּתוֹרָתוֹ לִהְיוֹת מְקַבֵּל שָׁבִים.
only Hashem established within His Torah to receive the penitent.
וְלָכֵן הוּצְרְכוּ שְׁנֵי קוֹלוֹת לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ בִּתְקִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה,
Therefore two blasts were required, before and after, as a tekiah of joy,
לְעוֹרֵר שִׂמְחַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִקְרַאת בָּנָיו בְּמִדַּת חַסְדּוֹ וּמִדַּת רַחֲמָיו,
to awaken Hashem's joy toward His children in His attribute of Chesed and Rachamim,
לִשְׁמוֹעַ בְּקוֹל תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד שֶׁלָּהֶם וּבְקוֹל תְּפִלָּה דְּרַחֲמֵי נִינְהוּ,
to hearken unto the voice of their Torah of lovingkindness and their prayer of mercy,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם קְרוּיִים בָּנָיו,
whereby they are designated His children;
וְזֶה בְּטֶבַע הַבְּרִיאָה לִהְיוֹת הָאָב מְרַחֵם עַל בְּנוֹ וּמְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
and such is the fabric of Creation: that a father has compassion on his child and accepts his return.
וְלִהְיוֹת עִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הִיא עֲזִיבַת הַחֵטְא אַלְהַבָּא,
And since the essence of repentance is forsaking the sin for the future,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁיָּעִיד עָלָיו הַבּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּב לְכִסְלוֹ;
as Maimonides wrote in Hilchot Teshuvah: that the Knower of Secrets testifies he will not return to his folly;
וּבַעֲווֹנוֹתֵינוּ הַכָּתוּב צוֹוֵחַ: "מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְחַסְדְּכֶם כַּעֲנַן בֹּקֶר וְגוֹמֵר" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ו, ד),
and in our sins Scripture laments: "What shall I do unto you... for your goodness is as a morning cloud, etc." (Hosea 6:4),
וְכָל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה אֲבָל הוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה,
and all the sinners of Israel are filled with remorse, yet it lasts but an hour;
וְכֵן קוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מְעוֹרֵר לְשָׁעָה,
and so too the blast of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah arouses for the moment,
וְאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא
and is not identical to the Great Shofar of the Future Era
שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִתְעַקֵּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ הָאוֹבְדִים וְגוֹמֵר;
through which the evil inclination will be uprooted entirely until the perishing return;
כִּי יִהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת כָּל כָּךְ קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימֶת וְלֹא חֲרָטַת שָׁעָה,
for that future awakening will be permanently established and not transient remorse,
רַק עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ לְהַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ – קְדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
leading them straight to the Holy Mountain in an immutable, eternal holiness.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְפִי שָׁעָה בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, מֵעֵין שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל דִּלְעָתִיד;
In contrast, on every annual Rosh Hashanah there occurs a temporary awakening in complete repentance, an inkling of the Future Great Shofar;
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ עֲדַיִן כְּיָתֵד הַתְּקוּעָה בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן.
yet it is not yet like a nail firmly fixed in a steadfast place.

וְלָכֵן תּוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין כְּשֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין, וְתוֹקְעִין וְכוּלֵי (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב552 Rosh Hashanah 16b — Why do they sound the shofar blasts while they are seated, and sound the shofar blasts again while they are standing? In order to confuse the Satan. Rashi (s.v. "to confound"): That he not bring accusation: when he hears that Israel cherish the commandments, his words are stopped up. Tosafos (s.v. "and they sound… while standing"): One may ask: does one not thereby transgress "you shall not add"? [For one cannot say that, having already fulfilled the obligation, it is no longer its time, since regarding the priestly blessing (28b) we say that its time has not passed, for were another congregation to come along he would bless them again.] The answer is that "you shall not add" does not apply to performing a single commandment twice — as a priest who blesses the same congregation again, or one who takes the lulav and takes it again, and likewise one who sounds and sounds again. Tosafos (s.v. "that is not sounded at its beginning"): The Halachot Gedolot explains: not where [Rosh Hashanah] happens to fall on Shabbat, but where some mishap occurred [that prevented the sounding]. Tosafos (s.v. "to confound the Satan"): The Aruch explains, as found in the Jerusalem Talmud: it is written "He will swallow up death forever" (Isaiah 25:8), and it is written "And it shall come to pass on that day that a great shofar shall be sounded" (Isaiah 27:13). When [the Satan] hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed and yet not alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: "Surely this is the shofar of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,' and my time to be swallowed up has come" — and he is confounded and has no leisure to bring accusation. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a–b): The Satan is privation and the shofar is the good that removes privation — hence "one who sees a shofar in a dream should anticipate redemption" (Berakhot 56b), which includes redemption from the Satan — for the tekia on Rosh Hashanah is elevation, and the Accuser cannot reach that place of elevation. They sound twice, seated and standing, because the first sounding only sets up opposition to him, while overcoming requires a second force that prevails and removes him entirely; this is why the Jerusalem Talmud says that at the first sounding he is alarmed and not alarmed, and at the second he is certain. In sum, the Satan accuses only through the attribute of judgment, which rules on Rosh Hashanah, and the soundings signify that attribute's elevation into mercy, whereupon it has no accuser. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh HaShanah 13): Tosafos cites the Yerushalmi that when [the Satan] hears the shofar the first time he is alarmed yet not alarmed, and when he hears it a second time he says, "Surely this is the shofar of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,'" and is confounded; but did he not know that the shofar is the mitzvah of the day, and that blowing again while standing is likewise an enactment of the Sages — why is he confounded by this mitzvah specifically? The first hearing, though also an awakening, can afterwards lapse, so he is not so alarmed; but the second, the blasts of the words of the Scribes, of the aspect of the Oral Torah, rouses the "great shofar," the awakening fixed in the depths of the heart, and thereby his time has come to be swallowed up and confounded, and in his preoccupation he has no leisure to prosecute.) לְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן,
Therefore we blow and sound the teruah sitting, and blow again standing (Rosh Hashanah 16b) to confound Satan,
וּבַתּוֹסָפוֹת בְּשֵׁם הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי: דְּקַמַּיְיתָא בְּהִיל וְלָא בְּהִיל, וּבַתְרַיְיתָא אָמַר: "הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי אָתֵי מְשִׁיחָא".
and in Tosafot citing the Yerushalmi: at the first sound he is alarmed yet not alarmed, and at the second he cries: 'Now surely the Messiah has arrived!'
וְתָמוּהַּ: וְכִי אֵין יוֹדֵעַ מִצְוַת שׁוֹפָר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, וְגַם תַּקָּנַת חֲכָמִים לִתְקוֹעַ מְיוּשָּׁב וּמְעוּמָּד?
And this is astonishing: does Satan not know the annual mitzvah of shofar on Rosh Hashanah, and the rabbinic decree to blow sitting and standing?
וְגַם מַה טַּעַם נִבְהָל בַּשְּׁנִיָּה יוֹתֵר?
And why is he more alarmed by the second series?
וְלֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר "יִתָּקַע", מַשְׁמָע רַק פַּעַם אַחַת!
And regarding the future it states "a blast shall be sounded," implying only once!
אֲבָל הַכַּוָּנָה: "בְּהִיל וְלָא בְּהִיל", דְּאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִקְבַּע בַּלֵּב דּוּגְמַת שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל דִּלְעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת קַיָּים כָּךְ,
Rather, the meaning of 'alarmed yet not alarmed' is that Satan cannot discern whether this resolution is permanently rooted like the Great Shofar to endure forever,
דְּדָבָר זֶה תָּלוּי בְּעֵדוּת בּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת, וְהוּא מְסוּפָּק בְּקִטְרוּגוֹ.
for this depends entirely on the testimony of the Knower of Secrets, leaving Satan doubtful in his prosecution.
כִּי תְּקִיעוֹת דִּמְיוּשָׁב כְּנֶגֶד מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב בְּכִסֵּא מִשְׁפָּט, דְּדַיָּינִים בִּישִׁיבָה,
For the sitting blasts correspond to the King sitting on the throne of judgment, judges adjudicating while seated,
וְלָכֵן הוּא שֶׁלֹּא בִּתְפִלָּה דְּרַחֲמֵי.
and therefore they occur outside of the Amidah prayer of mercy.
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט, הַדָּבָר שָׁקוּל אִם הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה זֶה הוּא בַּחֲרָטָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּב לְכִסְלָה.
And from the vantage point of strict justice, it remains hanging in the balance whether this thought of repentance is an absolute turnaround never to lapse.
וְלָכֵן תּוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין כְּשֶׁהֵן עוֹמְדִין,
Therefore we blow and sound the teruah again while standing,
דְּדַיָּינִין בִּישִׁיבָה וּבַעֲלֵי דִּינִים בַּעֲמִידָה;
for the judges sit while the litigants stand;

"אֵין עֲמִידָה אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה" (בְּרָכוֹת ו553 Berakhot 6b — And our father Abraham — whence do we know that he fixed a place [for his prayer]? For it is written, "And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood"; and "standing" means nothing other than prayer, as it is said, "And Pinchas stood and prayed." Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAvodah 4): Abraham fixed a place for his prayer, and his cleaving to the Blessed One was therefore fixed and not incidental, as it is written, "to the place where he had stood." For that reason the Blessed One was with him continually and fixedly, with no removal at all, and he was joined to the Divine Presence; and when he went out to war the Divine Presence fought his enemies and was always his help — all because he fixed a place for his prayer, that is, because his prayer, which is his cleaving to Him, was fixed and not incidental, and what is fixed is never removed, unlike the incidental, which does not endure.:),
"and standing denotes nothing other than prayer" (Berakhot 6b),
כִּי מִדַּת הַדִּין הוּא מִצַּד הַדַּיָּן, אֲבָל הַבַּעַל דִּין מְבַקֵּשׁ לְעוֹרֵר מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְהָרַחֲמִים לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין.
for strict judgment is the stance of the Judge, while the litigant seeks to awaken lovingkindness and mercy beyond the letter of the law.
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין "אֵין לַדַּיָּן אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁעֵינָיו רוֹאוֹת",
And under strict justice "a judge possesses only what his eyes behold",
וַהֲרֵי עֵינֵינוּ רוֹאוֹת שֶׁבַּעֲווֹנוֹתֵינוּ עָבְרוּ כַּמָּה רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְלֹא נוֹשַׁעְנוּ,
and our eyes see that through our sins many an annual judgment has passed without full redemption,
וַעֲדַיִן לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל הָעוֹקֵר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי, רַק הַכֹּל לְפִי שָׁעָה.
not yet having heard the Great Shofar that eradicates the evil inclination permanently, everything remaining temporary.

אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר שְׁלַח (קסח רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)554 Zohar 3:169a — These are voices of distress, and they go and roam through the air, and travel from one end of the world to the other, and enter into the clefts and hollows of the dust and are hidden there. And when a man raises a voice, they are aroused toward that voice. The voice of the serpent is not aroused by the voice of a man. How, then, is it aroused? By a blow. When a man strikes a blow, the voice of the serpent that lay hidden is aroused toward that voice, and not toward any other voice. A voice is aroused after a voice, a kind after its own kind. דְּ"קָלָא מְעוֹרֵר קָלָא",
Yet in truth they taught in the Zohar (Shelach 168a) that "a sound awakens a sound",
וּלְעוֹלָם בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יֵשׁ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִקּוֹל שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל.
and within the annual shofar of Rosh Hashanah there is an essential resonance drawn from the Great Shofar.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיְּבוּטַּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, נֶאֱמַר: "בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְגוֹמֵר יְבֻקַּשׁ עֲוֺן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
Namely, in the future when the evil inclination is nullified, it is said: "In those days... the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none" (Jeremiah 50:20),
דְּגַם עֲבֵירוֹת דִּלְעָבָר אֵינָם בִּמְצִיאוּת,
meaning that past transgressions will cease to exist in reality,

וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת555 Shabbat 89b — “Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though they be red as crimson, they shall be as wool.” It says “as scarlet [ka-shanim, plural]” — should it not have said ka-shani, in the singular? R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel — even if your sins are as many as those years which have come in ordered succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall be white as snow. Rashi: "It should have said ka-shani" [in the singular] — parallel to "as snow," for it does not say "as snows." Maharsha: "Like these years that are ordered" refers to the multitude of sin — as many as the years, presumably the years that have run in order since the six days of creation. One cannot read ka-shanim as "like two years," the minimal plural, for what novelty would there be in two sins? We say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah that He removes the first [sin] first, so for two sins "they shall be white as snow" would not be needed. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 89b): Sin is open to atonement because it is committed by accident, and the accidental does not annul what a person is in essence; but sins committed in great number and constantly are no longer accidental, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, says that even if your sins are ordered and fixed like these years, they shall be white as snow. Nothing is more fixed and ordered than the years, which have run so since the six days of creation, yet even they will cease, since the world is physical and will end in destruction; so too Israel's sins, though fixed on the side of the physical, can be removed, because Israel's essential level is not physical. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 19): The holiness of Tisha B'Av in the future, when it becomes a festival, will not come from Israel's sanctifying it, for on the contrary they sinned and made it a day of calamity, but only because in the future "your sins will be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," as stated in Shabbos 89b: then "they shall be white as snow" and be turned into merits, through this, that such was the will of the Blessed One from the six days of creation. Thus the essence of its holiness is only that this was the Blessed One's will at the beginning of creation, a holiness fixed and abiding like the holiness of Shabbos, except that it is revealed only in the future, after the rectification. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): "The scarlet [shanim] shall be white as snow" means that the scarlet of holiness, too, will be whitened, after they lift their eyes to the Blessed One, as stated in Shabbos there; and the sins will be "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, like merits; and afterwards they will rise still further, to the supernal whiteness, which is Wisdom, above Understanding. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 17): The deed itself is ordered and set so, as "Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of creation," and in truth this will be clarified in the future regarding all the sins of Israel, when they are refined and whitened, as the Sages said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow." That is, since the true will of the Blessed One was so, it is like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): In the future this will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel, as the Sages said in Shabbos 89b on the verse "If your sins be": "like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation" — it will be clarified that it was ordered from the true will of the Blessed One that it be so, and if so, in this too they did the will of the Blessed One, and it was all like a transgression for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Naso 2): Such was the intent in the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," as the Zohar says, there is no light but that which comes out of darkness; and then "the Lord will not count iniquity to him," since it will be clarified that this was created only so that it be "very good." As they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation, they shall be white as snow," that is, they will be as merits. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): From the side of the hidden things that will be revealed in the future there was no sin at all, and of this they said, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation," that is, from the side of the "hidden things of the Merciful One," then "they shall be white as snow" entirely, for there is no sin at all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei 31): Snow alludes to fear, and so the Gemara says, "If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of creation until now, they shall be white as snow": "years" alludes to cycles and order, that is, if there is an accusation, Heaven forbid, and it seems that a person sinned deliberately and in [recurring] cycles, the Blessed One will illuminate that this deed came only out of fear of the Blessed One, and this is "white as snow." (פט:): דְּ"יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת וְכוּלֵי";
mirroring Shabbat (89b): that sins will be like the solar years that are prearranged and set;
וְכֵיוָון שֶׁמְּסוּדָּר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִהְיוֹת כֵּן, הֲרֵי אֵינוֹ חֵטְא, כֵּיוָון שֶׁזֶּה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and once revealed as an ordained trial from Hashem, it is no longer counted a rebellion, being sublimated within His plan.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עִלָּאָה, דַּרְגָּא דְּבִינָה, שֶׁהוּא בְּסוֹד יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים – "תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ" כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And this is attained through Higher Teshuvah, the rung of Binah, the secret of Yom Kippur—the Gate of Freedom, as is known.
וְכֵיוָון שֶׁהַדָּבָר תָּלוּי בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת, דְּתַמָּן "לֵב מֵבִין",
And since this depends upon the perception of the Knower of Secrets, wherein resides the understanding heart (Binah),
כִּי יְדִיעַת הֶעָתִיד הוּא מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן –
for foreknowledge of the future derives from Binah of the heart which transcends time—
שֶׁהֵם שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים וְשַׁבָּת כַּנּוֹדָע, שֶׁבָּהֶם הַחִלּוּק דְּעָבָר וְעָתִיד;
temporal division of past and future existing only within the seven lower days;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן הֶעָתִיד יָדוּעַ כֶּעָבָר.
whereas above time the future is already known like the past.
וּלְכָךְ בּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת יוֹדֵעַ הֶעָתִיד מִצַּד לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן,
Therefore the Knower of Hearts perceives the future from above time,
וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא "יוֹם הַהוּא" – דְּהַיְינוּ הַנֶּעְלָם, וְלֹא "הַזֶּה" שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁתַּחַת הַזְּמַן.
and from that plane it is "that day"—the concealed future, and not "this day" of worldly time.
וּמִתְעוֹרֵר תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר דְּ"יוֹם הַהוּא",
And the shofar blast of "that day" is reawakened,
שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן הוּא "שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל" בְּמִדַּת הַגְּדוּלָּה –
which, transcending time, is the "Great Shofar" in the attribute of Gedulah (Chesed)—
דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק, רַק הוֹלֵךְ וְגָדֵל תָּמִיד, הוֹלֵךְ וָאוֹר יוֹתֵר.
meaning a ceaseless expansion that ever grows and shines brighter.

וּבֶאֱמֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ה פָּסוּק ב)556 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I am asleep with respect to the redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 8): The theme of this month [Adar] is that even in sleep Israel are holy, since they are bound at their root to the Blessed One — as the Midrash says, "I am asleep from the commandments ... but my heart is awake to perform them ... where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? 'God is the rock of my heart.'" From the side of the Blessed One, "the voice of my beloved knocks, open for me": "my heart is awake" means that the Blessed One, the heart of Israel, rouses Israel from their sleep to perform the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): The Congregation of Israel boasts, "I am asleep but my heart is awake," which the Sages expounded as referring to the Holy One, blessed be He — "rock of my heart." Even when they are asleep from the commandments and have no "eyes," as in sleep when the eyes are shut and the heart is sunk in imaginings, since the root of the soul is a portion of God and the depths of the heart cleave to the Blessed One, all the imaginings too cleave to Him; even at the height of immersion in the imaginings of this world, which hide the truth, there remains in him a power of awakening to the Blessed One through the heart's cleaving to the living God. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 68): All the service of the body's limbs, and the commandments performed with them, serve only to set the heart straight; the essential thing is the heart, the dwelling place of the Blessed One, as the Sages said, "the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it says, 'rock of my heart.'" Therefore these [outward acts] are not to be a person's goal in themselves, but only things that lead to the goal, as the Zohar calls the 613 commandments "613 counsels." עַל פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי עֵר",
And in truth Hashem is the essential heart of Israel, as our Sages expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2) on "and my heart is awake",
רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נִגְלֶה זֶה.
only that to outward appearances in this world this remains concealed.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר מִצְוַת הַתְּפִלָּה, שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ רַבִּים: וַהֲרֵי אֵין שִׁינּוּי אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ!
And this addresses the fundamental dilemma of prayer raised by many: behold, there is no change in Hashem!
רַק הַתְּפִלָּה הוּא הַכָּרַת אָדָם דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Rather, prayer is man's internal recognition that everything originates from Hashem,
וּלְכָךְ פּוֹתְחִין "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח", שֶׁמַּכִּיר דְּגַם הַתְּפִלָּה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which is why we begin: "O Lord, open my lips," acknowledging that prayer itself is endowed by Hashem.
וְהַכָּרָה זוֹ הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמַלְכָּא מְשִׁיחָא,
And this consciousness is the spiritual level of King Messiah,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל עַצְמוֹ: "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד).
as known from what King David said of himself: "and I am prayer" (Psalms 109:4).
כִּי זֶה כָּל עִיקַּר חִלּוּק בֵּין עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא", שֶׁאֵין נִגְלֶה הָאֱמֶת דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלֶעָתִיד יִתְגַּלֶּה זֶה.
For this is the primary distinction between this world which is a world of falsehood where divine truth is obscured, and the future where it will be revealed.
וּבְעֵת תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהָאָדָם מַכִּיר זֶה, הֲרֵי מִתְעוֹרֵר מִדָּה זוֹ,
And during prayer when a person internalizes this, that transcendent attribute is stirred,
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ אֲחִיזָה לְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר זֶה עִם קוֹל שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל.
and automatically this annual shofar blast bonds with the Great Shofar.
וְאָמַר: "הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי אָתֵי וְכוּלֵי",
And Satan cries: "Now surely the Messiah comes, etc.",
דְּנִפְשַׁט הַסָּפֵק שֶׁכְּבָר יֵשׁ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִשּׁוֹפָרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בְּכָל שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בַּעֲמִידָה.
the doubt being resolved since an awakening of the Messianic shofar is genuinely present in every standing shofar blast.
וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁנֵי גְּוָונִים:
And these two series function in two distinct modes:
בְּלַחַשׁ הוּא כָּל יָחִיד לְבַדּוֹ מִצַּד מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם – "דְּאֶחָד קְרָאתִיו",
in the silent prayer it is each individual alone reflecting Abraham—"one I called him",
וְכָךְ דֶּרֶךְ עוֹשֵׂי חֶסֶד בַּחֲשַׁאי;
this being the way of performers of Chesed, acting in secret;
כִּי חֶסֶד הוּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַדִּין לְגַמְרֵי וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּפִרְסוּם מִפְּנֵי הַמְקַטְרְגִים.
for Chesed transcends strict law entirely and cannot be broadcast before the accusers.
אֲבָל תְּפִלַּת שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
However, the public repetition by the Reader reflects the attribute of Jacob,
שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכֻּלָּם נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ וְהוּא הַכּוֹלְלָם;
who is the universal representative of all Israel who bear his name and whom he encompasses;
וְכָךְ הוּא מִדָּתוֹ: דַּרְגָּא דַּ"ה' אֶחָד" שֶׁהוּא יִחוּד דְּצִבּוּר – דְּהַיְינוּ רִיבּוּי הַמִּתְאַחֵד;
and such is his attribute: the rung of "Hashem is One," the communal unity of plurality joined together;
וְהוּא מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים שֶׁהוּא חֶסֶד שֶׁבַּמִּשְׁפָּט,
which is the attribute of Mercy—lovingkindness synthesized within justice,
שֶׁכָּךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט: לִהְיוֹת מְרַחֵם עַל בָּנָיו וְלַעֲשׂוֹת עִמָּהֶם חֶסֶד.
for true justice dictates that a Father shows compassion unto His children and does kindness with them.
וְזֶהוּ בְּקוֹל וּבְפִרְסוּם,
And this is proclaimed aloud and publicly,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁכָּךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט אֵין כָּאן שׁוּם מוֹרָא קִטְרוּג
for since this is rooted in lawful mercy, there is no fear of accusation,

וְלֹא בּוּשָׁה כְּ"מַאן דְּאָכֵיל דְּלָאו דִּילֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי" (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי עָרְלָה פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ג557 Jerusalem Talmud Orlah 1:3 — How does one know [from which vine the sunken shoot draws its life]? R. Bivai in the name of R. Ḥanina: If the leaves are turned toward the young vine, it is clear that it lives by the strength of the old one; and if the leaves are turned toward the old vine, it is clear that it lives by the strength of the young one. R. Yudan bar Ḥanin said: The sign is that one who eats from what belongs to another is ashamed to look at him. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "How does one know"): The leaves meant are those of the young vine: if they are turned toward the young vine itself, that is, away from the old one, it is certain that it lives by the strength of the old, and that is just why it turns its face away from it; and if they are turned toward the old vine, it is known that it lives by its own strength. This is what R. Yudan bar Ḥanin's sign means — one who eats from what belongs to his fellow is ashamed to look him in the face, and so turns his face the other way. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 12): In truth "all our deeds You have wrought for us," and everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, which is in the heart alone; only, the Blessed One wanted us to exert ourselves so that [our deeds] be called by our name and we come [to the good] by our own wages — for "one who eats what is not his…" — just as the Sages instituted for a wife that her handiwork is in exchange for her sustenance. Beis Yaakov (Vayigash 12): This is what the Sages intended in saying it is "more comfortable for a person" [not to have been created], rather than "better": for in truth it is better for him to have been created, since while the soul is in the world of souls the life in its hand is very constricted — "bread of shame," as stated in the Yerushalmi, "one who eats what is not his is ashamed to look at him." A person cannot reach the place of his root that befits him unless he passes through this world and is tested. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 16): On Pesach the salvation came without any service on man's part, as it is written, "and you were naked and bare" — naked of commandments. Yet in truth Israel is not at ease with this, as stated in the Yerushalmi, "one who eats what is not his is ashamed to look at him"; therefore the Blessed One afterwards set it that a person should clarify himself, so that the service be called the toil of his own hands — and this is "bring the Omer before Me on Pesach.") רַק בְּתוֹרַת חֶסֶד;
nor any shame of eating unearned bread of shame (Yerushalmi Orlah 1:3), but receiving in dignified grace;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֵּן הָאוֹכֵל אֵצֶל אָבִיו, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן חֶסֶד,
unlike a child dining at his father's table, where, although it is a gift of kindness,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם חֶסֶד זֶה הוּא מִצַּד חוֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ וְאֵין מִתְבַּיֵּישׁ כְּלָל.
this kindness is grounded in the legitimate order established by Hashem in His world, bearing no shame at all.
וְכֵן הִתְעוֹרְרוּת דְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת אֵלּוּ הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁנֵי פָּנִים הַלָּלוּ:
And so too the resonance of the Great Shofar in these blasts operates in these two dimensions:
בַּחֲשַׁאי – כְּאִלּוּ לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא,
silently—as though the heart does not reveal it to the mouth,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט;
Hashem inclining toward pure unmerited Chesed beyond law;
וּמִמֵּילָא בְּעֵירוּב מִדַּת חֶסֶד בְּמִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט מִתְגַּלֶּה תֵּיכֶף מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים שֶׁהוּא בְּגָלוּי וּבְפִרְסוּם.
and automatically, through weaving Chesed into Justice, the attribute of Mercy emerges openly and publicly.
כִּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם דֹּפִי,
For our father Jacob's bed is whole without any blemish,
וְהַקִּטְרוּג מְעוּרְבָּב לְגַמְרֵי.
and all angelic accusation is utterly confounded.
וְנִכְתָּבִים וְנֶחְתָּמִים לְאַלְתַּר לְחַיִּים,
And they are inscribed and sealed immediately for life,
הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה: בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי,
which encompasses all three blessings: children, life, and sustenance;

כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּנִים חָשׁוּב כְּמֵת (נְדָרִים סד558 Nedarim 64b — R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: Any man who has no children is accounted as dead, as it is stated: "Give me children, or else I am dead." And it was taught: Four are accounted as dead — a pauper, a leper, a blind man, and one who has no children. Rashi: "He has set me in dark places, as those long dead" — when a man is set in darkness and does not see, he is accounted as dead. Tosafos (s.v. "four are accounted as dead"): The practical consequence is that one should ask for mercy on their behalf. Maharsha: "Or else I am dead" cannot be taken to mean that she would die of the grief of having no children, for then Scripture should have written "I shall die"; rather metah is an adjective — "I am called dead," because I have no children. And in all the cases reckoned here, "accounted as dead" means that their life is no life. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Nedarim 64b): A man is not reckoned to have existence unless he inclines to no extreme, for one who inclines to an extreme is subject to death, and these four all incline to an extreme, to privation. By way of the plain sense they correspond to the parts of which man is composed — body, soul, the divine image, and the sustenance the Holy One gives him for his time in this world: the leper, to whom leprosy cleaves, is as one who has no body, and one who has no body is accounted dead; one who lacks sight lacks what depends upon the soul; and one who has no children — whom he would beget in his likeness and image — has no likeness and image, as they said, "One who does not engage in procreation is as though he diminished the [divine] likeness." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): There is "the groan of the prisoner": one who is only imprisoned and held back, in the manner of "for the Lord had fast closed up [every womb]" and "the Lord has held me back from bearing," who has the power in the root but is restrained. Of this it says, "to hear the groan of the prisoner, to release those doomed to death [literally, children of death]" — the opening of the prison and restraint of "those doomed to death," for one who has no children is accounted as dead, as the Sages said.:) וְהוּא בִּכְלַל חַיִּים;
for one without children is counted as dead (Nedarim 64b), children belonging to the rubric of life;

וְכֵן מְזוֹנֵי הוּא קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ח559 Taanit 8b — R. Shmuel bar Nachmani said to them: Let us pray for mercy concerning the famine, for when the Merciful One grants plenty, it is to the living that He grants it, as it is written, “You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor.” Rashi: "Let us pray for mercy concerning the famine": so that plenty will come, and the plague will cease of itself. "For when the Merciful One grants plenty, it is to the living that He grants it": to the living and not to the dead, for He does not bring plenty in order to kill people, but so that they may live. "And satisfy every living thing with favor": He grants plenty to living people. Beis Yaakov (Miketz 4): At the beginning of creation man's needs and sustenance were created first and then life; from then on the Blessed One bestows life first, and it grows and strengthens in abundance until one has all one's needs and sustenance — which are only the extension of life. This is the meaning of "when the Merciful One grants plenty, it is to the living that He grants it": if the Blessed One bestows sustenance on the world, we know that He has surely bestowed life before it, for life precedes sustenance; and Pharaoh's dream alludes to this, first of cows, alluding to life, then of ears of grain, alluding to sustenance.:): דְּכִי יָהֵיב רַחֲמָנָא שׂוֹבַע – לְחַיֵּי הוּא דְּיָהֵיב;
and sustenance sustains life, as written (Ta'anit 8b): when the Merciful One gives satiety, He gives it for life;
וְנֶגְדָּם הֵם שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת:
and corresponding to them are the three central blessings of the day:
"מַלְכִיּוֹת" – כְּדֵי שֶׁתַּמְלִיכוּנִי;
"Malchiyot"—in order that you crown Me King;
קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם,
the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven being the level of Abraham,

דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)560 Berakhot 7b — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: From the day the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, there was no man who called the Holy One, blessed be He, "Lord," until Abraham came and called Him "Lord," as it is stated: "And he said: Lord God, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?" [Genesis 15:8]. Rashi: "Lord God" — it is written with alef-dalet, the Name that denotes lordship. Tosafos (s.v. "there was no man who called Him 'Lord'"): One might object from "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem" (Genesis 9:26); but there the Name is not the one spelled alef-dalet, which is the language of lordship. And why does the Gemara not cite "Lord God, what will You give me" (Genesis 15:2), which stands earlier in the text? Because the passages were not related in order, and there is no earlier or later in the Torah: the Covenant between the Pieces in fact preceded the section beginning "After these things" by three years, so "whereby shall I know" is the earlier verse. Maharsha: As Tosafot wrote, this concerns the Name of lordship spelled alef-dalet: before him men called Him only by the Name that indicates His existence, whereas Abraham went further and called Him "Lord," which indicates His mastery and His power to alter decrees and the order of the heavens, as that very passage about Abraham sets out. That is also why Daniel was answered only for Abraham's sake — because Abraham was the head of faith, who made His mastery and His power in the world known to all. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 6:11): Abraham was the one who accepted His lordship and called Him "Lord"; and since the Lord is "Lord of the earth" [the name by which He governs the world in its natural order], He gave the land to Abraham for accepting His lordship. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 19): Until Abraham the Holy One, blessed be He, had no joining or bond with the world, for material nature interposed and separated between Him and the world; therefore Abraham called Him "Lord," for a lord is joined to that over which he is lord and is not separate from it. This is also why circumcision was commanded to Abraham: the foreskin is the separation and covering between the Blessed One, who is the Cause, and man. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 15): Israel called the Blessed One by this Name [of lordship] when they accepted the yoke of His kingship. For although Abraham too called Him "Lord," as the Sages said, "No man called the Holy One, blessed be He, 'Lord' until Abraham came and called Him 'Lord,'" the souls he had made in Haran abandoned his covenant after his death; this Name was revealed and recognized in its fullness only after Israel came and accepted the yoke of His kingship, a complete nation recognizing His lordship and kingship, which was the main purpose of the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 247): The "glory" is the radiance, that is, the evident recognition of His lordship and of His kingship that rules over all: just as a king is recognized by his kingship even by those who have not seen him, so is man's recognition [of God] from the whole of creation, as with Abraham our father, who saw the palace in flames, and as the Sages said, "No man called [Him] 'Lord' until Abraham came." The Name of lordship denotes this glory and radiance. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 1): Abraham our father crowned the Blessed One over the whole world, made Him Lord of all the earth and made His Name familiar in every mouth, as the Talmud says: "No man called the Holy One, blessed be He, 'Lord' until Abraham came and called Him 'Lord.'" Therefore Abraham himself is also called "lord" (as it is written of him, "The Lord said to my lord: Sit at My right hand"), and the Blessed One gave him possession of the whole world.: "לֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא 'אָדוֹן' עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵי",
as our Sages stated (Berakhot 7b): "No man called the Holy One 'Master' until Abraham came, etc.",
שֶׁהוּא הִמְלִיךְ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל כָּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם;
he being the first to crown the Holy One over all inhabitants of the earth;

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)561 Bereshit Rabbah 12:9 — R. Yehoshua ben Korchah said: "When they were created [behibare'am]" — read it "through Abraham [be'Avraham]," by the merit of Abraham. R. Azarya said concerning this teaching of R. Yehoshua ben Korchah: "You alone are the Lord; You made the heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is upon it, and all that is in them." And for what was all this labor? For the sake of: "You are the Lord God, who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and set his name Abraham.": "בְּהִבָּרְאָם" – בְּאַבְרָהָם,
which is why they expounded: "be-hibare'am (when they were created)"—be-Avraham (for the sake of Abraham),
שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ,
for whose sake the world was created to manifest His Kingship,
דְּ"אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם", וְהַיְינוּ עַם הַמַּכִּירִין כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ.
since "there is no king without a people"—a nation that recognizes His royal potency.
וְזֶה הִתְחִיל מֵאַבְרָהָם,
And this began with Abraham,
וְלָכֵן הוּבְטַח בִּנְתִינַת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, כִּי אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא אֶרֶץ;
which is why he was promised the Land, corresponding to Malchut, for there is no king without territory;
וְעַל זֶה צָוַוח: "מַה תִּתֶּן לִי וְאָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ עֲרִירִי",
and over this he cried out: "What will You give me, seeing I go childless" (Genesis 15:2),
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם,
for since there is no king without a nation,
אִם כֵּן מִצַּד מִדַּת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת קַבָּלַת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ,
then from the awakening of the acceptance of His Kingship in his soul,
צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּבָנִים שֶׁיָּחוּל עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
there must be the procreation of children upon whom the Name of His Kingship may rest.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר בַּקָּשַׁת הַבָּנִים דְּאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי:
And this is the core desire for offspring of an Israelite:
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים הָרְאוּיִים לָחוּל עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
that he bear children worthy of carrying the Name of Heaven,
וּמְקַבְּלִים עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם, שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ: "יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵיהּ רַבָּא וְכוּלֵי";
accepting the yoke of His sovereignty, proclaiming: "May His great Name be magnified and sanctified, etc.";
כִּי אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה בְּכָךְ: לִפְרוֹת וְלִרְבּוֹת וּלְהַעֲמִיד עַם מְקַבְּלֵי עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם.
for there is no king without a people, and Hashem desires this: to be fruitful and multiply and establish a nation bearing His yoke.
וּמִצַּד "שֶׁתַּמְלִיכוּנִי עֲלֵיכֶם", שֶׁהִיא מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה,
And through "crowning Me over you," which is the trait of Awe,
כְּטַעַם "אִם אֲדוֹנִים אָנִי אַיֵּה מוֹרָאִי" (מַלְאָכִי א, ו),
mirroring: "if I be a master, where is My fear?" (Malachi 1:6),
זוֹכֶה לְבָנִים,
one merits children,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי כֵן יְבֹרַךְ גָּבֶר יְרֵא ה'" (תְּהִלִּים קכח, ד),
as written: "Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth Hashem" (Psalms 128:4),
וְאוֹמֵר: "אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר גִּבּוֹר בָּאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה זַרְעוֹ".
and Scripture states: "Praiseworthy is the man who fears Hashem... his seed shall be mighty upon earth" (Psalms 112:1–2).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד דְּאַבְרָהָם – "אֶחָד קְרָאתִיו",
Unlike the isolated quality of Abraham's Chesed—"one I called him",
כִּי מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד הוּא לִהְיוֹת הָאָדָם כְּ"אֶחָד מִמֶּנּוּ", אֶחָד כִּיחִידוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלִהְיוֹת חַי לְעוֹלָם;
for pure Chesed seeks for man to be singular like his Maker, living eternally as an individual;
רַק מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט נִגְזַר הֶעְדֵּר הַקִּיּוּם בָּאִישׁ וְהוּצְרַךְ לְקִיּוּם בַּמִּין.
yet under Justice individual mortality was decreed, necessitating continuation through species and offspring.
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה וְכֹחַ גַּבְרָא בָּא הַהוֹלָדָה,
And through Gevurah and masculine potency procreation is enabled,
וְנִמְצָא לֵידַת יִצְחָק עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת יִצְחָק.
so that the birth of Isaac emerged through the awakening of Isaac's attribute of Gevurah.
וְזֶה טַעַם: "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק וְגוֹמֵר אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק",
And this explains: "These are the generations of Isaac... Abraham begot Isaac" (Genesis 25:19),
וּבֶאֱמֶת אַבְרָהָם הַמּוֹלִיד;
for in truth Abraham was the progenitor;
כִּי הֲגַם דְּהַיִּרְאָה הוּא מִדַּת יִצְחָק,
because although awe is Isaac's trait,
הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַיִּרְאָה בָּעוֹלָם – שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, "שֶׁתַּמְלִיכוּנִי עֲלֵיכֶם" – זֶה עוֹרֵר אַבְרָהָם.
the awakening of awe through the yoke of Kingship was ignited in the world by Abraham.
וּלְכָךְ הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן לַעֲקָרִים שֶׁנִּפְקְדוּ.
Therefore he was the first of the barren to be remembered with children.
וּלְעוֹלָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּאֵיזֶה דָּבָר הוּא הַמֵּבִיא עִנְיָן זֶה בָּעוֹלָם,
And always the first in any spiritual channel is the one who introduces it into the universe,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה פְּקִידָה לְמִי שֶׁלֹּא הוֹלִיד שֶׁיּוֹלִיד,
opening divine conception for those unable to bear;
דְּאַחַר כָּךְ אֵינוֹ עוֹד חִידּוּשׁ, וְהַחִידּוּשׁ הוּא אֵצֶל הָרִאשׁוֹן,
for afterward it is no longer a novelty, the breakthrough belonging to the first
שֶׁאָז נִתְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר זֶה עַל יְדֵי הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת שֵׁם "אָדוֹן" עַל יָדוֹ.
when this channel was hewn through the revelation of the Name Adon (Master).
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הָאֲדֹנוּת הוּא הַהוֹלָדָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא שֶׁהִיא "רֹאשׁ לַשּׁוּעָלִים",
And from the attribute of Adonut comes childbearing from the feminine dimension (Nukva), "head of the foxes",
דִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָאִשָּׁה בְּבָנִים,
the woman's completion being children,

דִּבְלָאו הָכִי: "חֲבָל לְדוֹר דְּאִתְּתָא דְּבַרְיָתָא" (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר כב562 Midrash Tehillim 22:16 — R. Berekhiah said: There are four sayings, three concerning a man and one concerning a woman. Dark is the living one who has need of the dead; dark is the strong man who has need of the weak; dark is the light that has need of the blind. And one concerning a woman, such as Deborah: dark is the generation that a woman leads — "and Deborah, a woman, a prophetess" (Judges 4:4).);
for otherwise: "woe to the generation led by a woman" (Shocher Tov, Psalm 22);
רַק הָאֵם מְנַהֶגֶת אֶת בָּנֶיהָ וְהִיא רֹאשׁ לָהֶם מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם בָּנֶיהָ.
yet a mother guides her children and is their head as her offspring.
וְכֵן כָּל מִדַּת הָאֲדֹנוּת הוּא מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֲבָדִים נִקְרָא "אָדוֹן",
And so the title Adon is defined by having servants,
וּ"מֶלֶךְ" כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עָם,
and "King" by having a nation,
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה – לְהַעֲמִיד בָּנִים הַנִּקְרָאִים "עַם ה'".
and from this aspect arises the mission to raise children who constitute the people of Hashem.
וּלְעוֹלָם פְּקִידַת הַלֵּידָה לְמִי שֶׁלֹּא הוֹלִיד הוּא רַק בְּעִנְיָן זֶה:
And the miraculous remembrance of the barren is granted solely for this end:
בִּכְדֵי לְהַעֲמִיד זֶרַע שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְרָא עָלָיו שֵׁם ה' וּמַלְכוּתוֹ,
to establish seed upon whom the Name of Hashem and His Kingship rest,
כְּעִנְיַן שִׁמְשׁוֹן וּשְׁמוּאֵל, שֶׁאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ בָּהֶם.
as with Samson and Samuel, where there is no need to elaborate here.
וּלְכָךְ "מַלְכִיּוֹת" הוּא נֶגֶד בָּנֵי.
Therefore, Malchiyot corresponds to children (banei).
"וְזִכְרוֹנוֹת" – "שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה זִכְרוֹנֵיכֶם לְפָנַי" בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים, הוּא נֶגֶד חַיֵּי;
"Zikhronot"—"that your remembrance may ascend before Me" in the light of the King's countenance, corresponds to life (chayei);
כִּי "עִמְּךָ מְקוֹר חַיִּים בְּאוֹרְךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים לו, י),
for "with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light" (Psalms 36:10),
הַיְינוּ בְּאוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ,
meaning in the light of the King's countenance,
כַּאֲשֶׁר עוֹלֶה לְזִכָּרוֹן לְפָנָיו שָׁם הָאוֹר וְהַחַיִּים מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק,
when one ascends in remembrance before Him where light and life dwell from the side of Isaac,
שֶׁאֲפָרוֹ צָבוּר לְפָנָיו כִּבְיָכוֹל.
whose binding ashes are piled before Him, as it were.

וְהוּא דְּ"מַחֲוֵי לְהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (פט563 Shabbat 89b — [Isaac says before Him:] And if You should say that they are all upon me — I already offered up my life before You. They begin and say: "For You are our father." Isaac says to them: Before you praise me, praise the Holy One, blessed be He — and Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, with their own eyes. Immediately they lift their eyes to heaven and say: "You, O Lord, are our Father; our Redeemer from of old is Your name" [Isaiah 63:16]. Rashi: "For you are our father" — they said this facing Yitzchak, and he told them: Point toward the Holy One, blessed be He, for He is your father. Maharsha: Yitzchak divides the sins: those between Israel and the Omnipresent the Holy One, blessed be He, is to bear, and those between them and other people, which require appeasement, he will bear; "and if You say all are upon me" — that all are between them and other people — "I offered my life before You," and so can bear them all. Therefore they say to Yitzchak, "For you are our father," since he bears all their sins by the merit of having offered himself; but Yitzchak points them to the Holy One, blessed be He, for all their sins may be between them and Him, and at once they say, "You, O Lord, are our Father," that He atone for His Name's sake.
