Even so the man does not come to transgress, for "your temples are like a pomegranate split open" — even the empty ones among you, etc.; and "behind your veil" means that beyond this they restrain themselves further so as not to come to transgression — that a man with a discharge may not eat together with a woman with a discharge, and other such distancings. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 37a): This is because Israel are, in themselves, fit for the Torah, and therefore even the empty ones among them are full of commandments like a pomegranate. For what a thing is by its own nature carries great strength: just as the pomegranate is full [of seeds] by the very essence of its creation, so the empty ones are full of commandments by the very essence of theirs. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Esau's heart was full of crookedness, and only through the dimming of his eyes could Isaac think well of him; through that same dimming he afterwards did not recognize Jacob either, but he smelled "the smell of his traitors," for even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and there is no room at all to accuse him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:57): Jacob's service was chiefly in intention for the sake of Heaven, and the "garments" of deed began only with Laban, where he began to beget the souls of Israel, who are themselves the commandments of the Torah; hence it says then that [Rebecca] dressed him in Esau's garments. Therefore the Sages read "the smell of his garments" as "the smell of his traitors," meaning, as they said, that even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate: they too have a garment of the deed of the mitzvot. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 9): Even [Acher] belongs to the secret of the broken vessels, which were also placed in the Ark; thus "R. Meir found a pomegranate," as it is written, "your temples are like a slice of pomegranate," "even the empty ones among you…": one from whom the light has been emptied resembles a pomegranate. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 5): When Jacob donned Esau's garments to receive the blessings, Isaac smelled in him "the smell of his traitors," which come from the mixture of good and evil; but in Israel it is the reverse: the evil is only on the exterior, in the garment, while the interior is good, for even the empty ones and the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate. And scent is something the soul enjoys, which comes from the interior. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the seed of Jacob none is cast off, for just as evening and morning make one day, so His praise rises from the wicked as from the righteous: even the empty ones of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and the sinners of Israel are full of remorse. Of this the Sages said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors," and Bereishis Rabbah applies it to the likes of Yakim of Tzeroros, who in a brief moment preceded Yose ben Yoezer, a perfect tzaddik who had toiled all his days, to the World to Come; for the penitent attains this in a single moment. עַמּוּד א),
and even the transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvot (Sanhedrin 37a),
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם אַף שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ הֲרֵי זֶה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר וְנִקְרָא שֶׁטָּרַח,
and all their deeds, even if not for Heaven's sake, render them completely righteous and count as having toiled,

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּגֵרִים אֵין מְקַבְּלִין הַמִּתְגַּיֵּר לְשֵׁם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר (יְבָמוֹת כד583 Yevamot 24b — A man who converted for the sake of a woman, a woman who converted for the sake of a man, and likewise one who converted for the sake of the king's table or to be among Solomon's servants — they are not converts; these are the words of R. Nechemya. But it was stated concerning this: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said in the name of Rav, the law follows the one who says that they are all converts. If so, let them be accepted at the outset as well! Because of Rav Assi, who said: "Put away from you a crooked mouth, and perverse lips put far from you." Rashi: "Solomon's servants": they were men of authority. "If so": that she is a proper convert, let him marry her "at the outset as well"; why then does [the Mishnah] teach that he may not marry her? "Because of Rav Assi": the reason of the Mishnah is that it is written, "Put away from you a crooked mouth, and perverse lips put far from you," for [by marrying her] they would come to confirm the earlier rumor. Tosafos (s.v. "because of Rav Assi: 'Put away from you a crooked mouth'"): The Ri said that where a man is suspected concerning an unmarried woman, there is no need to be stringent and bar him from marrying her on account of "perverse lips"; on the contrary, it is a commandment to marry her, for of a violated woman it is written, "and she shall be his wife" (Deuteronomy 22:29). Tosafos (s.v. "if so, at the outset as well"): Granted, if you say she is not a full convert, it is well that he may not marry her at the outset, since she is a doubtful convert, for perhaps she converted for the sake of a man, while after the fact she is not taken from him, since one need not be so stringent on account of this concern [but if she is a full convert, why not at the outset?]. Tosafos (s.v. "the law follows the one who says that they are all converts"): [R. Nechemya's list also included converts out of fear of lions.] These lion converts are not comparable to the Samaritans, of whom one view holds that they are [invalid] lion converts, for there they went on worshipping their own gods, as is written in the Book of Kings; and the one who holds that the Samaritans are true converts holds that they later converted fully. Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, on "Put away from you a crooked mouth"): [The Mishnah's word] "suspected" implies that even if he himself knows the charge is untrue, he may nevertheless not marry her because of the suspicion, lest people say that he has already sinned with her; and this is "Put away from you a crooked mouth": a crooked thing, one that is not true. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "if so, at the outset as well"): That is, she is a doubtful convert only with regard to marrying the man suspected with her, and therefore he may not marry her at the outset; but if she does not marry him she is a full convert, and another man may marry her at the outset, as the questioner himself inferred at the start: "she is, at any rate, a convert." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): The love of Torah is revealed most in converts: Israel were brought out of bondage and drawn near by the Holy One, blessed be He, but the convert left the tranquility of this world and the license he had among the nations to follow his desire, and came of his own will to fence himself in and cleave to Israel, afflicted, lowly and downtrodden in this world. For only "in your poverty shall he fall to you," and converts were not accepted in the days of David and Solomon, nor one who converts out of love for some thing; only for love of the Torah does he draw near and enter under the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. עַמּוּד ב),
whereas regarding converts we do not accept one who converts for the sake of any ulterior motive (Yevamot 24b),
שֶׁאֵין זֶה הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אֶצְלָם.
as this does not constitute worthy exertion for them.
וְקִיּוּמָם לֶעָתִיד יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת הוּא רַק מִצַּד חִבּוּרָם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And their endurance in the future day that is wholly Shabbat is solely through their connection to Israel,

דְּכָל הַנִּטְפָּל לְעוֹשֵׂי מִצְוָה וְכוּלֵי (מַכּוֹת ה584 Makkot 5b — R. Akiva says: The third witness did not come to be lenient with him, but to be stringent with him and to make his law like that of the others. And if Scripture punished one who attaches himself to transgressors as it punishes the transgressors themselves, all the more so will He pay reward to one who attaches himself to those who perform a commandment, as He rewards those who perform the commandment. Rashi: R. Akiva did not need to teach us this, for we know of ourselves that two witnesses can render three conspiring witnesses, since two are competent for every testimony; rather, he comes to be stringent with the third. You might have said that, since the testimony would have stood without him, the law of conspiring witnesses is not applied to him — so Scripture teaches that he too is one of those who establish the matter. And "all the more so": for we find that the measure of good is greater than the measure of punishment, since of the measure of good it says, "keeping mercy unto the thousandth generation," and of the measure of punishment, "upon the third and upon the fourth generation." Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTzedek 3): Whatever is joined and attached to a thing is reckoned as belonging to it; therefore, when a man attaches himself to evil he is of one matter with it, and when he attaches himself to good, that good too belongs to him. This is why Scripture punished the one who attaches himself to transgressors as it punishes the transgressors themselves, and all the more so pays reward to the one who attaches himself to those who perform a commandment, as it rewards those who perform it. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 4): Even complete preparations for a commandment, though not part of the commandment itself, at least bear the name of a commandment, since they are a preparation for it: for even "one who attaches himself to those who perform a commandment is like one who performs the commandment," as the Mishnah teaches, and likewise a thing attached to the act of a commandment is like a commandment in bringing holiness into his heart. This is the receipt of reward, for "the reward of a commandment is a commandment": through the awakening of holiness in the heart he is moved to add further commandments. עַמּוּד ב),
for 'whoever attaches himself to performers of a mitzvah, etc.' (Makkot 5b),

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת מז585 Yevamot 47b — Why [do they say all this to him]? So that if he is going to withdraw, let him withdraw. For R. Chelbo said: Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab, as it is written: "And the stranger shall join himself with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob" (Isaiah 14:1). Rashi: "If he withdraws": so as not to convert. "Let him withdraw": and we do not mind. "Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab": the term "scab" [is used] because they hold on to their former deeds and Israel learn from them, or rely on them in matters of prohibition and permission. Tosafos (s.v. "converts are as hard for Israel as a scab"): Because they are not expert in the fine points of the commandments, and Israel learn from their deeds; in Tractate Niddah (13b) Rashi gives another explanation, that all Israel are guarantors for one another, but this is difficult, for chapter Elu Ne'emarin (Sotah 37b) implies that they were not guarantors for the converts, since the guarantorship of the mixed multitude is not counted there. One may further say that converts are hard for Israel because they intermingle with them, and the Divine Presence rests only on the families of Israel of established lineage; and some explain that it is because Israel were warned especially concerning converts and cannot guard themselves against wronging them. Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, on Tosafot s.v. "converts are hard"): Tosafot's further answer, that [converts are hard] because they intermingle with Israel, is implied in chapter Asarah Yuchasin, for it is in that connection that [R. Chelbo's saying] is cited there; and some explain there further that they are hard because they cause Israel's sins to be recalled. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 47b): As a scab is something appended to a person, and such an addition nullifies the person's form […] and makes a change in him, so too when converts are added to Israel, who are called "man," Israel go out of their bounds […], and there comes upon them what would not have come had they stood by themselves within their bounds. When there are converts among Israel, an addition and a change is made upon Israel, which brings foreign matters upon them, as a scab does on a person; and this is the sense of the expression "converts are hard for Israel." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 1): Once [a gentile] comes to convert he has an Israelite disposition, and when he has converted he becomes subordinate to the Israelite nation and is like it; nevertheless they said, "Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab," for a scab's temperament is not good, and it spoils the flesh that has a good temperament. עַמּוּד ב) דְּקָשִׁים כְּסַפַּחַת,
and therefore they stated (Yevamot 47b) that converts are as difficult as a scab,

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁבוּעוֹת ו586 Shevuot 6b — The Sages taught: A se'et — se'et means nothing other than raised, and so it says, "upon all the high mountains and upon all the raised-up hills" (Isaiah 2:14). A sappachat — sappachat means nothing other than something secondary [appended to another], and so it says, "Attach me [sefacheni], please, to one of the priestly divisions, to eat a morsel of bread" (I Samuel 2:36). Rashi: "Deep" and "raised" — this is not meant literally, but that [the mark] looks deep [or raised]. "Attach me [sefacheni]" — gather me in. עַמּוּד ב): "אֵין סַפַּחַת אֶלָּא טְפֵלָה וְכוּלֵי".
and our Sages of blessed memory said (Shevuot 6b): 'sapachat means nothing other than an attached secondary appendage.'
דְּהַטָּפֵל עַל כָּרְחוֹ אֵינוֹ כְּמוֹ הָעִקָּר דְּאָז הָיָה עִקָּר,
For the secondary appendage perforce is not identical to the primary essence, otherwise it would be the primary;
וְלָכֵן מִצַּד חִבּוּרוֹ לְהָעִקָּר הוּא נֶגַע לוֹ,
and therefore, through its attachment to the core, it becomes a defect to it,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִתְחַבֵּר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת כָּמוֹהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ כֵּן,
for it joins it as though it were identical, which is not so,
וְהוּא נִטְפָּל וְנֶחְשָׁב כְּמוֹ הָעִקָּר וְיוּכְלוּ לַחְשֹׁב שֶׁגַּם הָעִקָּר כֵּן,
and being attached it is reckoned like the primary so people might think the primary is likewise flawed,
וְזֶה חִסָּרוֹן לָעִקָּר שֶׁמִּתְדַּמֶּה לַטָּפֵל.
which diminishes the primary by being likened to the secondary.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת קג סוֹף עַמּוּד א)587 Yevamot 103a — R. Yochanan said: That wicked man had intercourse seven times on that day, as it is stated: "At her feet he sank, he fell, he lay; at her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell down dead." But she derived pleasure from a transgression! R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: Every benefit of the wicked is an evil to the righteous. Rashi: "He sank, he fell, he lay": seven [such verbs] are written in the verse. "Is an evil": for the righteous hate the wicked, and the soul of a righteous person loathes the pleasure that comes from them; hence it is not [counted as] pleasure. Tosafos (s.v. "But she derived pleasure from a transgression"): The objection is not that she should have given up her life rather than submit, for she was passive ["the ground of the world"], as is said of Esther; moreover, he was not forcing her — on the contrary, she coaxed him in order to sap his strength and save Israel. Rather, it asks why Scripture praises her so highly ("Blessed above women shall she be"), which Nazir 23b and Horayot 10b explain by saying that a transgression for its own sake is greater than a commandment not for its own sake — greater, that is, than the Matriarchs, who derived pleasure from intercourse, whereas Yael did not. And the answer is that she certainly derived no pleasure, for the benefit of the wicked is an evil to the righteous. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 103a): The righteous man and the wicked man are two opposites, and benefit and good cannot pass from one opposite to the other; therefore good cannot come to the righteous from the wicked, and whatever good does come to him comes to his harm. The wicked man is considered by the righteous to be altogether evil, and so even the good of the wicked is counted as evil by the righteous, for from evil no good goes forth. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 3): What stands opposite is the very reverse: the joy that stands opposite true joy is a joy of revelry, which lasts only for the moment and ends in sorrow. And for those who are not people of illusion, clinging to illusion and to what is momentary, it is sorrow even at that very time, as it is written, "All the good of the wicked is evil for the righteous." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): Mordechai and his colleagues, the great Sanhedrin of that generation, who were also at [Ahasuerus's] feast, joined it only for appearance's sake, and even that eating was in truth accounted like sacrifices; for they did not truly benefit at all from that wicked man's feast, since "all the good of the wicked is evil for the righteous." As the Sages said in Nazir, it is for this reason that Yael derived no pleasure from the transgression, and it was accounted for her like the mitzvah-union of the holy Matriarchs.: "כָּל טוֹבָתָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים רָעָה לַצַּדִּיקִים",
And in the manner that they said (Yevamot 103b end): 'All favors of the wicked are evil for the righteous,'
גַּבֵּי יָעֵל שֶׁהֵטִיל זֻהֲמָא,
concerning Yael upon whom Sisera cast defilement,
וְנוֹדַע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
and it is known according to the teaching of the Arizal, of blessed memory,
דִּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל סִיסְרָא לָמְדוּ תוֹרָה,
that descendants of Sisera learned Torah,
הַיְנוּ מִיָּעֵל שֶׁנִּתְעַבְּרָה אָז.
stemming from Yael who conceived at that time.
וְזֶהוּ טוֹבָתָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים:
And this is the favor of the wicked:
הַיְנוּ הַטּוֹב הַגָּמוּר שֶׁקָּלְטָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
namely, the complete good she absorbed from him,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם קָלְטָה גַּם כֵּן זֻהֲמָא.
nonetheless, she absorbed defilement as well.
דְּזֶהוּ עִקַּר חֶסְרוֹן דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת:
For this is the primary defect of the idolaters:
שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי לֹא פָּסְקָה זֻהֲמָתָן.
having not stood at Mount Sinai, their defilement never ceased.
הַיְנוּ דִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַדְרִיכָם,
Meaning that the hour of the Giving of the Torah was when Hashem willed to teach Torah to His people Israel and instruct them,
שֶׁהוּא הַגִּלּוּי דְּכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם בַּתּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים גַּם כֵּן הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which is the revelation that all human exertion in Torah and good deeds is likewise entirely from Hashem.
זֶהוּ פְּסִיקַת זֻהֲמָא דְּנָחָשׁ,
This is the cessation of the defilement of the serpent,

שֶׁהוּא: "וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר588 Genesis 3:1-5 — “Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And it said to the woman: Did God really say you may not eat from any tree of the garden? … And the serpent said to the woman: You shall surely not die; for God knows that on the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you shall be like God, knowing good and evil.” Rashi: "Now the serpent was cunning": Scripture is teaching with what design the serpent sprang upon them — he saw them naked and desired Eve. "You shall surely not die": he pushed her until she touched the tree, and then said to her that just as there is no death in touching it, so there is no death in eating it. "For God knows" — every craftsman hates his fellow craftsmen; He Himself ate of this tree and created the world, and therefore "you shall be as God," creators of worlds.",
which is: 'and you shall be like gods, etc.,'
בַּעַל כֹּחַ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
imagining oneself an independent power,
לִהְיוֹת מִתְכַּוֵּן לְגַרְמֵהּ לָדַעַת וּלְהַרְגִּישׁ בְּטוֹב וָרָע וְלַעֲשׂוֹת הַטּוֹב.
acting for one's own self-interest to know and discern good and evil and to do good.
אֲבָל רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת בַּעַל כֹּחַ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל,
Yet the will of Hashem, blessed be He, is that one possess no independent power whatsoever,
רַק לִמְסֹר הַכֹּל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather surrender everything completely to Hashem.
וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ אוֹתָהּ זֻהֲמָא,
And Amalek, who is titled 'the first of the nations,' is the root of that very defilement,
שֶׁיָּדַע כָּל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת הַפְכִיִּים
in that he knew all varieties of opposing powers
וְרוֹצֶה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לִבְחֹר בַּטּוֹב וּבָעֲיָא לְאִגַּיּוֹרֵי.
and seeks through his own exertion to choose the good, desiring to convert.
רַק כַּוָּנָתָהּ: "מוּטָב שֶׁאֶהְיֶה וְכוּלֵי",
Only that Timna's intent was: 'It is better that I be a maidservant, etc.,'
שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר טוֹב לְפִיכָךְ רָצְתָה בּוֹ.
meaning because this is an advantageous thing she therefore chose it.

וְכָל גֵּר, כְּשֶׁמּוֹדִיעִים לוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּווּיִים וְכוּלֵי (יְבָמוֹת מז589 Yevamot 47a — Our Rabbis taught: When one comes to convert at the present time, they say to him: What did you see that you came to convert? Do you not know that Israel at the present time are afflicted, driven about, harried, and torn, and that sufferings come upon them? If he says: I know, and I am not worthy — they accept him at once. Rashi: "Harried": lowly and overturned, as in "overturning a cup" (Shabbat 66b), the overturning of a vessel. "And I am not worthy": I am not fit to share in their distress, and would that I might merit it. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 15): This world is not fitting for Israel, and their principal portion is not in the physical world; rather, Israel's entire stature and level lies in their being separate from the physical, so how could one imagine that they would inherit the physical world? Because Israel's portion is not this world, they are pursued in this world: Israel are afflicted, harried and torn in this world because this world is not fitting for them, and they have opposition in this world. עַמּוּד א),
And with any convert, when they inform him that Israel at this time is afflicted, etc. (Yevamot 47a),
דַּי שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּכִּיר לִמְאֹס בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֲרֵי כְּבָר בִּטֵּל כֹּחוֹ,
it suffices that when he comes to despise this world he has already nullified his independent power,
שֶׁכֹּחַ כָּל אֻמָּה הוּא הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.
for the power of every nation is its submergence in this world in that specific matter.
אֲבָל תִּמְנַע הִיא מַמְזֶרֶת מֵאֱלִיפַז,
However, Timna was born of an illicit union from Eliphaz,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רַשִׁ"י וַיֵּצֵא כט, יא)590 Rashi on Genesis 29:11 — "And he wept" — ... Another explanation: because he had come empty-handed. He said: Eliezer, my grandfather's servant, had rings and bracelets and delicacies in his hands, and I have nothing in mine. This was because Eliphaz son of Esau had pursued him at his father's command to kill him and had overtaken him; but because Eliphaz had been raised in Isaac's lap, he drew back his hand. He said to him: What shall I do about my father's command? Jacob said to him: Take what I have — and a poor man is accounted as dead. דְּגָדַל בְּחֵיק יִצְחָק
concerning whom our Sages said (Rashi, Vayeitzei 29:11) that he grew up in the lap of Isaac,
וְהָיָה מִנְּבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
and was among the prophets of the nations of the world,

וְאֵין הַנְּבוּאָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל חָכָם גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר (שַׁבָּת צב591 Shabbat 92a — Perhaps Moses was different, for the Master said: The Divine Presence rests only upon one who is wise, mighty, wealthy, and of tall stature. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 92a): This matter is self-evident: it is not fitting for the Divine Presence to rest upon anything deficient; therefore all of these [qualities] are required, so that the person be whole, and then it is possible for the Divine Presence to rest upon him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): "Prophecy rests only upon one who is wise, mighty and wealthy" means completeness in the three faculties of man. Wise in the brain; mighty in the strength of the heart, as in "Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination," which comes through the fear of Heaven that restrains his spirit, the inclination dwelling in the heart; and wealthy in deeds, as in "Who is wealthy? One who is happy with his portion," for the completeness of deeds is in the hand of the Omnipresent, so one should not seek great things but be content with what the Lord has allotted him. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part I 8): The essence of man is the soul, the body is his possession, lesser possessions are his money and property, and lesser still his friends and companions, and all of them require completeness: this is "Who is wise … mighty … wealthy … honored," the completeness of the four parts of man. But of prophecy the Sages said "upon one who is wise, mighty and wealthy," the completeness of the three, for [completeness] between a man and his fellow does not apply to a prophet, who is set apart from them; the early authorities placed him as an intermediate between man and angel. Rav Tzadok (Sefer HaZichronos 16): Purification of the heart alone is the main condition of prophecy, while wisdom is an ancillary matter: from the Sages' words, "Prophecy rests only upon one who is wise etc.," it is evident that wisdom is not what brings about prophecy but only an ancillary condition for the prophet, like might and wealth. The essence of prophecy, seeing the truth as it is with the eye of the intellect, comes only through purity of the heart. Beis Yaakov (Chayei Sarah 38): A person must guard the vessels of the body so that they are healthy and strong, and then he will grow wise and succeed in words of Torah, as the Talmud says, "The Divine Presence rests only upon one who is wise, mighty and wealthy"; for the Blessed One so ordained that through these vessels a person can receive words of Torah. For if a human soul is reincarnated in a beast or an animal, the human soul too is considered like a beast and has no stature. עַמּוּד א),
and prophecy rests only upon the wise, mighty, and wealthy (Shabbat 92a),
דְּהַיְנוּ שְׁלֵמוּת בְּג׳ רָאשֵׁי הַכֹּחוֹת נֶגֶד ג׳ אֲבָהָן:
meaning perfection across three cardinal forces corresponding to the three Patriarchs:
חָכְמָה – הֵיפֶךְ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת דִּזְנוּת;
wisdom is the opposite of the spirit of folly that leads to licentiousness;
וּגְבוּרָה – בִּכְבִישַׁת כָּל מִינֵי יְצָרִים הֵיפֶךְ רְצִיחָה הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאֵין מַעְצוֹר לְרוּחוֹ;
and might consists of conquering all base inclinations, the opposite of bloodshed arising from lack of restraint;
וַעֲשִׁירוּת – בְּדַעַת שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ רִבּוֹנוֹ הִפּוּךְ עֲנִיּוּת הַמַּעֲבִיר עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ,
and wealth is in spiritual knowledge of his Master, the opposite of poverty that causes one to transgress his Creator's will,
שֶׁהֵם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
which correspond to idolatry, forbidden unions, and bloodshed.
דְּהַשְׁרָאַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁנָּקִי מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ בְּתַכְלִית,
For the resting of the Holy Spirit is impossible except upon one thoroughly cleansed of these three,
וּמִסְּתָמָא גַּם כָּל שִׁבְעַת נְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כֵּן.
and presumably all seven gentile prophets were likewise so.
רַק הֵם גָּדְלוּ בְּחֵיק אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
Only that they grew up in the bosom of the nations,
שֶׁהִגִּיעוּ לָזֶה מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַצְמוֹ,
attaining this through the very submergence in this world itself,
כְּכָל חַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁמְּבִינִים שֶׁאֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים רָעִים מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
like all secular sages who grasp that these are destructive from a worldly perspective;
וְהוּא גָּדַל בְּחֵיק יִצְחָק,
whereas Eliphaz grew up in the lap of Isaac,

דֻּגְמַת עֵשָׂו דְּנִקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר (קִדּוּשִׁין יח592 Kiddushin 18a — Rav Chiya bar Avin said that R. Yochanan said: By Torah law a gentile inherits from his father, as it is written, "For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance" (Deuteronomy 2:5). But perhaps an apostate Jew is different? Rather, [derive it] from here: "For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance" (Deuteronomy 2:9). Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Isaac taught Torah only to his sons, and even among them there was one who was unworthy, except that he is called an "apostate Israelite" in Kiddushin, for he had a root of Jewishness from birth — his head is buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Isaac's bosom — and therefore he too had some hold on words of Torah; yet in the end he too was waste. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 4): [Isaac, the first to be circumcised at eight days, was the one in whom holiness began to take root in all his offspring;] and his wish to draw Esau near was because Esau had free choice, being called an "apostate Israelite," so that the matter stood in the balance whether he could enter into the holiness of Israel. עַמּוּד א),
mirroring Esau who was designated an apostate Israelite (Kiddushin 18a),
שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יִצְחָק כְּבָר יֵשׁ שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for in the seed of Isaac there already exists the name Israel,
שֶׁהוּא: "כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר",
which is: 'for you have striven with God, etc.,'
שַׂר עַל כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת.
ruling as prince over all forces.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא הֵמִיר זֶה וְנִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּכֹחַ רְצִיחָה,
Only that Esau exchanged this and sank into the power of murder,
וֶאֱלִיפַז לֹא נִשְׁתַּקַּע כָּמוֹהוּ,
while Eliphaz did not sink like him;
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא זֶרַע עֵשָׂו שֶׁמַּחֲלִיף כֹּחַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַל הַכֹּחוֹת לְכֹחַ הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת,
nonetheless he is the seed of Esau, swapping mastery over natural drives for submergence in self-sufficiency,
וְהוּא לֹא רָצָה לְהִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ בְּכֹחַ מְיֻחָד,
and he refused to sink into any specific base passion,
אֲבָל נִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּכֹחַ זֶה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַל כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת.
yet he became submerged in the very pride of his self-mastery over all powers.
כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹסְרִים גַּם כֹּחַ זֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For Israel surrenders even this power to Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַיְנוּ כֹּחַ הַיְדִיעָה דְּטוֹב וָרָע וְלִבְחֹר בַּטּוֹב אַף זֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning the knowledge of good and evil and the capacity to choose good derives likewise from Hashem.
אֲבָל הוּא חוֹשֵׁב דְּכֹחַ זֶה שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא,
Eliphaz, however, deemed this choosing power to be his own;
וְנִמְצָא עֲדַיִן הֵמִיר עִקַּר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל
and thus he still betrayed the essence of the name Israel,
שֶׁהוּא לִמְסֹר כָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְהַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ מְיֻחָד,
which is to surrender all faculties to Hashem and recognize that one possesses no autonomous power,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא שַׂר עַל כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת,
and through this alone is he master over all forces,
וְהַיְנוּ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם.
namely through Hashem Who is the Master of all forces.
אֲבָל הוּא נִקְרָא אֱלִיפַז,
He, however, was named Eliphaz,
פֵּרוּשׁ שֶׁהַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ הֵם נֶחְמָדִים מִפָּז,
meaning that his faculties were to him more precious than fine gold,
זֶהוּ עִקָּרוֹ שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כֹּחוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ וְהֵם נֶחְמָדִים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת לְשׁוּם כֹּחַ.
this being his core identity: priding himself that he has self-contained forces that are precious and free from subservience to base drives.
וְזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת רֵאשִׁית הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת דְּנָחָשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
And this in truth is the primordial submergence of the serpent as I wrote elsewhere,

שֶׁיְּסוֹדוֹ לְהַסִּית לִבְחֹר בְּכֹחַ הַבְּחִירָה593 Poked Akarim §5, s.v. “also in the blotting out of Amalek,” p. 31 col. 2; Yisrael Kedoshim §9, para. 13 — In Poked Akarim: Amalek — “the first of the nations,” the beginning of the spread of every kind of evil — has no particular power of evil at all; he is the root of evil, for his whole power is that he is the opposite of good, and his whole desire is to destroy the name of Israel from the world, Heaven forfend, which would be the world’s return to chaos and the complete reversal of creation. That he was created at all is because the Blessed One wished that a side of evil should exist, in order to give good reward to the righteous who overcome it; so the essence of its existence is that it should have no existence. “God made man upright” (Ecclesiastes 7:29), and He wished them to overcome it at once: had Adam not sinned but overcome the serpent, the root of evil would have been consumed at the very beginning of creation, and the use of choice at that one moment alone would have been enough. In Yisrael Kedoshim: At the beginning of creation “God made man upright,” wholly on the side of holiness — which is why He placed him in the Garden of Eden — and the power of evil was outside him: this is the serpent, the “one set against the other”; as man comprises all the powers of holiness, so it comprises all the powers of impurity. In man He placed only the power of choice — whether to be enticed by the serpent. Once the serpent brought its filth upon Eve and caused them to be enticed into eating of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, the powers of evil entered into man’s heart, so that he himself became filled with both powers, good and evil, at the two openings of his heart..
whose foundational temptation was to entice one to glorify self-willed agency.

וְזֶה גָּרַם שֶׁבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת שֵׂעִיר הַחֹרִי (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב594 Midrash Tanchuma, Vayeshev 1:4 — So too He occupied Himself with the genealogy of the sons of Esau, "And these are the generations of Esau," to make known their degeneracy; for you find that they were children of licentiousness. Thus it says: "The sons of Eliphaz: Teman and Omar, Zephi and Gatam, Kenaz and Timna and Amalek," and it says: "And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz" — this teaches that he married his own daughter. How so? He had come to the wife of Seir, and she conceived and bore him Timna; and he married her as one marrying the daughter of Seir, when in truth she was his own daughter.) יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ,
This led him to cohabit with the wife of Seir the Horite (Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Parashat Vayeishev), dwellers of the land,

דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פה595 Shabbat 85a — R. Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R. Yonatan: What is meant by "These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land"? Does the rest of the world, then, inhabit the sky? Rather, they were expert in the settlement of the land, for they would say: this reed's length of ground is for olives, this reed's length for vines, this reed's length for figs. And "Horite" — that they would smell out the land. Rashi: "This reed's length": the measuring reed with which land is measured. "For olives": fit for growing olives, and this for figs — they knew how to tell the land apart, from one reed's length to the next, by its smell and its taste, where it was for olives and where for figs; and so they were certainly expert in how far [plants] draw nourishment [from the soil]. "That they would smell": rearrange the letters of the word ["Horite"] and expound it [as "smell"]. Maharsha: Elsewhere Scripture speaks of "the inhabitant of the land" where it names a particular land, but here it says "the inhabitants of the land" without specifying which, implying the earth, the lower world, as a whole — hence the question whether the rest of the world inhabits the sky. "Horite — that they would smell" is expounded by transposing letters (as keves and kesev, "lamb", or simlah and salmah, "garment"), which is why Rashi in his Torah commentary preferred the simpler derivation from "free men". And they expounded "the Horite" rather than taking it as the name of a lineage, since Scripture gives such names the definite article ("the Reubenite", "the Hivite") only when they have been mentioned before, and "the Horite" had not been. עַמּוּד א): "בְּקִיאִין בְּיִשּׁוּבָהּ וְכוּלֵי",
of whom our Sages said (Shabbat 85a): 'they were experts in cultivating the earth, etc.,'
הַיְנוּ תַּכְלִית הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
representing the ultimate worldly enterprise;
וְהוּא בָּחַר בַּטּוֹב וְהוֹלִיד תִּמְנַע דְּבָעֲיָא לְאִגַּיּוֹרֵי,
and exercising his moral agency, he sired Timna who desired to convert,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּטוֹב דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כְּשֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִתְגַּיֵּר.
which is the apex of gentile self-driven pursuit of good when wishing to convert.
אֶלָּא דְּאֶצְלָהּ שֶׁבָּאָה מֵאֱלִיפַז שֶׁכֹּחוֹ לִמְשֹׁל עַל כָּל כֹּחוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
Except that with her, descending from Eliphaz whose nature was self-reliant mastery over worldly drives,
אֵין זֶה בִּטּוּל הַכֹּחַ מַה שֶּׁמּוֹאֶסֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּבוֹחֶרֶת בַּטּוֹב,
her despising this world and choosing the good was not true self-nullification;
וּלְכָךְ לֹא קִבְּלוּהָ,
and therefore they did not accept her,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים גֵּרִים לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
just as converts will not be accepted in the Messianic era,
דִּכְשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁזֶּה טוֹב לְכָךְ בּוֹחֵר בּוֹ.
for when one sees that it is advantageous, he chooses it.
וְכֵן הִיא הָיָה לָהּ הַכָּרָה זוֹ מֵאֱלִיפַז דְּזֶה טוֹב.
And she likewise possessed this inherited awareness from Eliphaz that this was good.
וְעִקַּר יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִבְחֹר זֶה כְּלָל,
Yet the essential core of Israel is not choosing independently at all,
רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן וְלִמְסֹר הַכֹּל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather receiving what Hashem bestows and surrendering everything to Hashem.
וְכֹחַ זֶה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this power is the root of the name Israel,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַגֵּר הוּא בָּא מִכֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּבְחִירָה בַּטּוֹב,
whereas the convert arrives through personal exertion and moral choice,
וְהִיא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם בְּחֵשֶׁק דְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְטוֹב,
and she represented the pinnacle of gentiles in active yearning for good,
וְזֶה אֵין נִקְלָט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
and this cannot be assimilated into Israel's core;
כִּי הַתַּכְלִית אֵינוֹ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְטוֹב
for the ultimate purpose is not moral striving,
שֶׁזֶּה הַתַּכְלִית מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which is merely the goal from the vantage point of this world,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and this is called 'the first of nations,' being the finite peak of this world.
אֲבָל תַּכְלִית הַכֹּל הוּא הַהַכָּרָה הַגְּמוּרָה דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
However, the ultimate purpose of all is the absolute recognition that everything originates from Hashem.
וְתִמְנַע שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁהּ מִצַּד אַחֵר מִגּוֹיִם בָּעֲיָא לְאִגַּיּוֹרֵי
And Timna, whose root was distinct from other nations, sought conversion,
וְהִכִּירָה מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְרָצְתָה לְהִטָּפֵל לָהֶם,
and recognized the superiority of Israel and wished to attach herself to them;

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט596 Sanhedrin 99b — As for "And Lotan's sister was Timna" — what is this? Timna was a royal princess, as it is written, "chief Lotan," "chief Timna," and every chief is royalty without a crown. She wished to convert. She came to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and they did not accept her. She went and became a concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, saying: Better that I be a maidservant to this nation than a noblewoman of another nation. From her came Amalek, who afflicted Israel. What is the reason? Because they should not have pushed her away. Rashi: "Royalty without a crown" — a great prince, only not crowned; and since Timna was the sister of a chief, she was certainly a king's daughter. "Better to be a maidservant to this nation" — to the children of Abraham and Isaac, who fear Heaven, rather than a mistress to another nation; therefore she became a concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, who was of the seed of Isaac. "To push her away" — from beneath the wings of the Shechinah, for they ought to have converted her. Maharsha: They derived this exposition from Scripture's taking care to state that Amalek's mother was Timna, who bore him to Eliphaz — "And Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz" — whereas for Eliphaz's other sons, Teman, Omar, Zepho and the rest, it does not mention who their mother was. They expounded that because Abraham [Isaac and Jacob] did not accept her, she had to become a concubine to Eliphaz, saying, "Better to be a maidservant," and for this they were punished in that Amalek, who afflicted Israel, was born of her. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 99b): Abraham, Isaac and Jacob did not accept Timna because, owing to her importance and royalty, she would not enter conversion as is fitting: one is a convert only when he joins himself wholly to those to whom he converts, and while the Patriarchs humbled themselves before God, blessed be He, Timna, being royal, would not regard herself as a convert. Once pushed away she was distanced all the more, for whatever is pushed away is pushed away entirely: had she not come to convert there would have been no distancing, but since she came to convert and was rejected by the Patriarchs, who are the very beginning, this was the utmost distancing, leaving no share or connection at all. Therefore Amalek came forth from her, for no nation could be as opposed to Israel as Amalek was except one born of such distancing. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Among the nations, those with a greater connection to holiness are the worse, and Amalek has more connection to holiness than all the nations: besides issuing from two patriarchs and matriarchs, his mother Timna went around to the doors of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to convert, and they did not accept her, for they sensed the force of impurity of "the first of the nations" destined to come from her. Yet she still yearned to convert and went around their doors — surely because of a holy spark stirring within her. עַמּוּד ב) דְּלֹא הָיָה לָהֶם לְרַחֲקָהּ,
and regarding this they said in Sanhedrin (99b) that they ought not to have pushed her away,

וְהַיְנוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כד597 Avodah Zarah 24a — The colleagues of R. Eliezer answered him from the verse "All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister to you; they shall come up with acceptance upon My altar." R. Eliezer said to them: In the time to come they will all be converts who attach themselves of their own accord. Rav Yosef said: What is the verse? "For then will I turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord." Rashi: "Converts who attach themselves of their own accord" — they drag themselves along to convert on their own initiative, even though [the court] does not accept them. And [Abaye objects that] "that they may all call upon the name of the Lord" shows only that they will withdraw from idolatry, not that they will withdraw from bestiality. Maharsha: Since converts will not be accepted in the time to come, the nations will not be able to serve Him with all His commandments as Israel does, but only with that one portion of the Torah which they are able to keep — and the prohibition of bestiality belongs to that portion, since the descendants of Noah were already commanded concerning it. "For then will I turn to the peoples a pure language": at the beginning of the settlement of the world all men had one language, the holy tongue, and when the generation of the dispersion rebelled He confounded it for them; the verse promises that when the nations return to serve the Lord that pure language, the holy tongue, will be restored to them, for no other tongue is "pure speech" beside it. עַמּוּד א):
analogous to what is written in Avodah Zarah (24a):
בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ כֻּלָּם נַעֲשִׂים גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים,
in the Messianic era they all become dragged-along converts,
דְּרַק אֵין מְקַבְּלִים אֲבָל גַּם אֵין מְרַחֲקִים.
where they are neither officially accepted nor cast out.
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי הַגַּם דְּאָמְרוּ "אַל תִּהְיוּ כַּעֲבָדִים וְכוּלֵי",
For even though they taught: 'Do not be like servants who serve for reward, etc.,'

מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ598 Pesachim 50b — Rava raised a contradiction: It is written, "For Your mercy is great unto the heavens," and it is written, "For Your mercy is great above the heavens." How so? The one speaks of those who act for its own sake, and the other of those who act not for its own sake. And this accords with what R. Yehuda said that Rav said: A person should always occupy himself with Torah and with the commandments even not for their own sake, for out of [doing them] not for their own sake he comes to [do them] for their own sake. Rashi (s.v. "those who act for its own sake"): For those who act for its own sake [His kindness is] "above the heavens"; for those who act not for its own sake, "up to the heavens" — for he is at any rate performing a commandment, as Rav Yehuda [taught]. Tosafos (s.v. "and here, those who act not for its own sake, as Rav Yehuda"): This is puzzling, for he himself said in the second chapter of Berakhot (17a): "Whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake, it would have been better for him not to have been created." R. Yitzchak [the Ri] answers that there it speaks of one who studies in order to be haughty, to taunt and to best his fellows in halachah, and not in order to practice; but here it speaks of one like "the lowly one who profits" mentioned above, who does no work all week nor on the eve of the Sabbath — one who intends nothing bad but acts out of laziness — and even so, His kindness is great up to the heavens. Maharsha (s.v. "and it is written: For great above the heavens"): One who acts not for its own sake — that is, for some lower end, though without intending evil, as Tosafot wrote — has his kindness in this world reach only the lower world, "up to the heavens"; but one who acts for its own sake, whose aim reaches above, has his kindness even in this world come from above, "above the heavens." Both verses end "and Your truth unto the skies," for both, those who act for its own sake and those who do not, will merit the reward of the World to Come. Maharal (Derech Chaim 4:5): [Against Tosafot's question from "it would have been better for him not to have been created":] I do not see the difficulty, for the meaning is that if he does not study not for its own sake, he will not study for its own sake either. One who studies not for its own sake is certainly not good, and it would be better for him not to have been created — yet that is better than not studying at all, for of one who does not study at all this is true all the more. So this is what he says: even if he does not study for its own sake he should study nonetheless, for out of not for its own sake he comes to for its own sake. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Ahavas Hashem 2): Although of one who acts not for its own sake it is said that it would have been better for him not to have been created, he nonetheless has great reward — though certainly the essence is to do the commandment out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for that is the essence of the deed. A commandment not for its own sake has something that a transgression for its own sake lacks: from a transgression for its own sake one will not come to a commandment for its own sake, but from a commandment not for its own sake one does come to a commandment for its own sake, for the deed is one and the same. עַמּוּד ב): "לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסֹק אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְכוּלֵי599 Pirkei Avot 1:3; Pesachim 50b — Antigonus of Sokho received from Shimon the Righteous. He used to say: Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward; rather be like servants who serve the master not in order to receive a reward — and let the fear of Heaven be upon you. And in Pesachim 50b: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav — a man should always occupy himself with Torah and the commandments even if not for their own sake, for out of doing so not for their own sake he comes to do so for their own sake.",
nonetheless they stated (Pesachim 50b): 'A person should always engage in Torah even not for its own sake, etc.,'
דִּבְאֱמֶת לִשְׁמָהּ אִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְמִידוּת,
for unadulterated purity of motive is impossible continuously;
וַאֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹכֵב עֲלֵיהֶם מַמָּשׁ
yet the Patriarchs were the Chariot upon whom Hashem rested literally,
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לִשְׁמָהּ רִחֲקוּ זֶה לְגַמְרֵי.
and their deeds being purely for Heaven's sake, they pushed her away completely.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם רְאוּיִים לַעֲבָדִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
In truth, such souls are fit to be servants to Israel,
שֶׁהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת נִקְרָא עַבְדוּת
for human exertion is termed servitude,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין רְאוּיִים לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כְּלָל
and Israel's essence transcends exertion,
דְּעִקָּרָם לְיוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת,
for their core belongs to the day that is wholly Shabbat,
וְהֵם עֲבָדִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת.
while they serve as laborers through exertion.
וְ"יַעֲסֹק וְכוּלֵי" הַיְנוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת זֶה רָאוּי גַּם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.
And engaging in study with ulterior motives is appropriate within this realm of exertion.
רַק הָאָבוֹת רִחֲקוּ זֶה לְגַמְרֵי,
Only that the Patriarchs pushed this away completely;
וְהִיא אָמְרָה: "מוּטָב שֶׁאֶהְיֶה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
and she pleaded: 'It is better that I be a maidservant, etc.,' as mentioned above,
דְּזֶה עֲבָדִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל רַק שֶׁהֵם רִחֲקוּהָ.
which is the role of servants to Israel, only that they rejected her.
חָזַר וּבָא עָלֶיהָ אֱלִיפַז,
Eliphaz then took her again,
הַיְנוּ כֹּחַ הַבְּחִירָה בַּטּוֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
representing the power of choosing good through self-agency as mentioned above,
וְנוֹלַד עֲמָלֵק דְּצִעֲרִינְהוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and from them Amalek was born who tormented Israel,
שֶׁהוּא לֹא רָצָה עוֹד לְהִתְגַּיֵּר,
in that he no longer sought to convert,
רַק בָּא לְזַנֵּב הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא זָרִיז וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל יוֹתֵר מֵהֶם,
coming rather to strike the stragglers, asserting that he was more zealous and dedicated than they,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הָמָן בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכָּר
just as Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver,
שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (מְגִלָּה טז עַמּוּד א) נֶגֶד הַשְּׁקָלִים.
which Tosafot (Megillah 16a) explain were meant to counterbalance the shekels.
וְהַיְנוּ דְּמִנִּדְבוֹת לִבְבוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּשְּׁקָלִים נִבְנָה מִשְׁכָּן לִשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹכָם.
For from the generous donations of Israel's shekels the Sanctuary was built for the Shechinah to dwell among them;
וְאָמַר שֶׁהוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ נְדִיבוּת כְּמוֹ כֻּלָּם בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּתַכְלִית תֹּקֶף מַעֲלָתָם.
and Haman claimed he possessed generosity matching all of them at their spiritual zenith.

וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק: "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ600 Deuteronomy 25:17-19 — “Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, as you came out of Egypt — how he met you on the way and cut down all the stragglers at your rear, when you were faint and weary, and he did not fear God. Therefore, when the Lord your God grants you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; you shall not forget.” Rashi: "Remember what Amalek did to you" — if you falsify weights and measures, be anxious about the provocation of the enemy, as it is said, "A false balance is an abomination to the Lord," and immediately after it, "When insolence comes, then comes disgrace." "Who happened upon you on the way" — an expression of chance; another explanation, an expression of cold, for he cooled you and made you lukewarm before the nations after your boiling heat. "You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" — man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, so that the name of Amalek should not be mentioned even of a beast, to say, "This beast belonged to Amalek." Ramban: The correct interpretation is that you are not to forget what Amalek did to us until we blot out his remembrance from under the heavens, and that we are to relate it to our children and to our generations, saying to them: "Thus did that wicked one do to us, and therefore we have been commanded to blot out his name."",
And this is the essence of Amalek: 'who met you by the way,'
כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ,
for all effort in this world is called 'a way,'

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה כא601 Sotah 21a — The Torah is compared to light, to tell you: just as light protects forever, so too the Torah protects forever. And it says: "When you walk, it shall lead you; when you lie down, it shall watch over you; and when you awake, it shall talk with you" (Proverbs 6:22). "When you walk, it shall lead you" — this is in this world. "When you lie down, it shall watch over you" — this is death. "And when you awake, it shall talk with you" — this is in the world to come. Rashi: "It shall talk with you" — it will plead your merit on your behalf. Maharsha: This verse, which immediately precedes "For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light," also speaks of the Torah and teaches that it protects forever: in this world "it shall lead you" — in the sense of giving you rest from all troubles; when you lie in the grave "it shall watch over you" against the beating of the grave; and in the World to Come "it shall talk with you," pleading on your behalf against the judgment of Gehinnom. As for Tosafot's difficulty — that by the Gemara's conclusion a mitzva too protects forever — a mitzva protects forever only in this world, whereas the Torah protects even in the World to Come from the judgment of Gehinnom, as the verse "and when you awake it shall talk with you" shows. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sotah 21a): The Torah is intellectual, and whatever is intellectual does not fall under time; therefore it protects forever, as befits that which is beyond time and has no change, whereas the mitzva, like everything physical, falls under time and comes to an end, and so protects only for the moment. And since light signifies complete existence — without light nothing has existence, which is why a blind man is considered as though dead — one who holds fast to the Torah, which is complete light, cannot be abandoned by it to nonexistence: in this world, where a man is a "walker" who has no rest and may do something that brings him to ruin, it leads him; after death, the time of dissolution, it guards him from loss and gives him existence; and in the time to come, when he returns to life, it gives him speech, which is life — "it shall talk with you." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 10): Death stems from the first corruption of Adam, and its repair is through occupation with words of Torah, of which it is said: "When you walk it shall lead you" — this is this world; "when you lie down it shall watch over you" — this is death; "and when you awake it shall talk with you" — in the time to come. For then, at the resurrection of the dead, the clarification will be complete, [showing] that death was only like sleep in this world, as the Sages called death "when he lay down to sleep," and the dew of Torah revives him. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): The world is full of turmoil and has no rest; therefore they said, "When you walk it shall lead you" — in this world, for this world is the time of walking, since "man is born to toil." But there are those whose toil is with knowledge and skill in deed, and whose walking is in holiness. The angels are called "standing," for they remain on the one level at which they were created, but man walks constantly from level to level and has no rest, like the righteous mentioned above — and this is truly the ultimate rest. Beis Yaakov (Vayeishev 5): One who has no words of Torah has none of the good itself, for through words of Torah a person is awakened to all good things, as they expounded: "When you walk it shall lead you" — in this world; "when you lie down it shall watch over you" — this is death; "and when you awake it shall talk with you" — in the time to come. In the time to come the Blessed One will fill the treasuries of Israel and reveal to their eyes the light hidden in the performance of the mitzvos, and then they will see that all the knowledge, intentions and lights Israel had in this world were like a dream compared to its interpretation. עַמּוּד א) עַל פָּסוּק "בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Sotah 21a) on the verse 'when you walk.'
וּבְצֵאתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם הַיְנוּ מֵעַבְדוּת הָאֻמּוֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם
And their departure from Egypt was an exodus from gentile servitude and their striving,
לֵילֵךְ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
to walk in the guidance of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ הַנִּצּוּחַ נֶגֶד כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָאֻמּוֹת
And this represents the triumph over all powers of the nations,
דְּהַיְנוּ: "בְּהָנִיחַ מִכָּל אוֹיְבֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
meaning: 'when He grants you rest from all your enemies, etc.,'
אָז בָּא עֲמָלֵק כְּשֶׁרָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
then Amalek comes when their hands slacken from words of Torah,
וְהוּא "עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ" בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
and he finds them 'faint and weary' through human striving,
"וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים" –
and 'fearing not God' –
הַיְנוּ בַּהַיְדִיעָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּעַל כֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם וְאֵין נַפְקָא מִנַּהּ בֵּין רִפְיוֹן לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת.
meaning lacking the awareness that Hashem is Master of all forces, with no essential difference between human weakness and exertion.
אֲבָל עֲמָלֵק טוֹעֵן שֶׁהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עִקָּר,
Amalek, however, claims that exertion is primary,
וְגַם הוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּכָל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם לְטוֹב,
boasting that he exerts all forces toward good,
דְּזֶה רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם וְתַכְלִית הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is the peak of the nations and the culmination of this world.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֻּלּוֹ עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּם לָעַד
Yet in truth, this world is entirely a World of Falsehood that cannot endure,
שֶׁאֵין זֶה הַתַּכְלִית הָאֲמִתִּי,
as this is not the true divine objective;

וְלָכֵן אַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אֹבֵד602 Numbers 24:20 — “And he saw Amalek and took up his parable and said: Amalek is the first of the nations, but his end shall be destruction forever.” Rashi: "And he saw Amalek" — he looked upon the retribution destined for Amalek. "Amalek was the first of the nations" — he was the first of them all to make war against Israel, "and his end is to perish" at their hands, as it is said, "You shall blot out the memory of Amalek." Ramban: It is possible that "and he saw" is meant literally, for Balaam stood on the top of Peor that looks out over the wasteland and looked toward the land of Amalek, who dwelt in that hill country. He said that Amalek is now "the first of the nations" in the sense of foremost among them, for they were mighty men and valiant in war; and yet "his end shall be to perish" more than all of them, as it is said, "I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.",
therefore 'his end shall be destruction,'
כִּי הוּא מְשֻׁקָּע בְּכֹחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לַחְשֹׁב שֶׁזֶּה כֹּחוֹ וְעֹצֶם יָדוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בַּטּוֹב
because he is submerged in exertion, fancying that by his own strength and might he achieves righteousness,
וְחוֹשֵׁב דְּזֶהוּ עִקַּר הַמְּכֻוָּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and imagining that this is the primary intent of Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר בָּאָדָם בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר
And this is what awakens in man 'when He gives you rest, etc.':
כְּשֶׁעוֹסֵק בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת צָרִיךְ לָדַעַת שֶׁגַּם זֶה הַכֹּחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
while engaging in effort, one must know that even this capacity is from Hashem;
זֶהוּ מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק דְּאֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא קַיָּם,
this is the blotting out of Amalek, for the Name is not complete as long as he exists,
דְּהַיְנוּ שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת הַמּוֹרוֹת עַל דָּבָר זֶה
namely the final two letters (Vav-Hei) pointing to this truth:

שֶׁכָּל כֹּחַ אָדָם בְּכֹחַ וּבְפֹעַל גַּם כֵּן הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר603 Machshavot Charutz §5, s.v. “and the root of Amalek” — The root of Amalek, it seems to me, is the power of immersion in the illusions of this world. He is “the first of the nations” — that is, the root of every kind of nation, for each nation is immersed in some particular kind of evil, which is its root and the source of all its power in this world. … Israel cleave to the Blessed One, Master of all powers, and are immersed in no power at all, for immersion comes from separating a power from the Creator, blessed be He, to make it a thing apart; and Amalek is the root of this power of separation. … Therefore the Name and the Throne are not whole as long as the seed of Amalek is in the world. It is known that of the four letters of the Name, the first two are the hidden things — brain and heart — and the last two allude to the power of action and its completion; these are “the revealed things, which belong to us and to our children” (Deuteronomy 29:28), and in them lies man’s power of effort in this world, whereas the hidden powers come from the Blessed One. … Amalek’s whole desire is to separate the hidden from the revealed entirely, for he wishes to make this world a world separate from the Blessed One … and this is the severing of the last two letters, the powers of action of this world, from the Name altogether..
that all human faculties, in potential and in act, derive entirely from Hashem as I wrote elsewhere.
וְכֵן שְׁלֵמוּת הַכִּסֵּא הַיְנוּ הַהַשְׁגָּחָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
Likewise, the wholeness of the Throne signifies divine providence in the lower realms.
וְנִצּוּחוֹ הָיָה: "כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ",
And his defeat occurred: 'when Moses held up his hand,'
דְּהַיְנוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַמְּיֻחָס לַיָּדַיִם,
denoting exertion associated with hands;

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כט604 Rosh Hashanah 29a — "And it came to pass, when Moses raised his hand, that Israel prevailed" — and did the hands of Moses make war, or break war? Rather, it comes to tell you: so long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed; and if not, they fell. Maharsha: The Mishnah brings this exposition after the ruling that one who hears the shofar fulfills his obligation only if he directed his heart, citing in the same vein a verse that makes everything depend on the heart's intention. Amalek came because Israel's heart had not been toward Heaven — of the manna, "How long do you refuse"; at Mei Merivah, "Is the Lord among us?" — so the Holy One, blessed be He, showed them through Moses' prayer, his hands spread toward heaven, that it all hung on their intention: when they looked upward and directed their hearts to Heaven, as Moses raised his hands, they prevailed, and when their intention was not toward Heaven, Moses' hands too grew slack and Israel fell. That is why Moses, although one who prays usually stands in a low place ("Out of the depths I called You"), went up to the top of the hill: so that Israel in their battle would see his hands and direct their hearts to Heaven accordingly. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 13): The Sages said, "Did the hands of Moses [make war]…? Rather, so long as Israel [looked upward]…" — yet the difficulty remains that, if so, Scripture should not have made it depend on Moses' hands. But in truth Israel at their level then — just out of the defilement of Egypt, not yet having received the Torah or been fully purified through the forty-nine days of the Counting — had no strength against the stirring of Amalek, which weighs down the hearts of Israel with the force of the evil inclination, except through the help of Moses, the leader and heart of the generation, who can instill a spirit of arousal toward good in the hearts of his generation. So when Moses overcame the heaviness that had come into his hands, he also brought the hearts of Israel to gather strength to look upward and subject their hearts to [their Father in Heaven]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Masei 2): [When Israel grew cold and failed to prepare themselves, the Blessed One, as it were, was included with them,] along the lines of "And it came to pass, when Moses raised his hand, that Israel prevailed" and the Gemara's "so long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven." That is, Moses our teacher instilled in the hearts of Israel that they subject their hearts to their Father in Heaven, but without an arousal from below there was no arousal from above. Sod Yesharim (Purim 6): ["So long as Israel looked upward"] means that when Israel look toward the point that is above their grasp, they nullify all their understanding before that point; whereas when the nations look toward this point above their grasp, they say that they are of necessary existence. But Israel understand well that there is no necessary existence, Heaven forbid, and know that all is only the simple Will. עַמּוּד א): "וְכִי יָדָיו וְכוּלֵי",
and our Sages of blessed memory asked (Rosh Hashanah 29a): 'Did the hands of Moses make war, etc.?',
דִּבְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אֵין נִצּוּחַ לוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֵר שֶׁגַּם הוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל,
for through mere human exertion there is no defeat of him, since he claims he too exerts himself,
רַק כְּשֶׁמְּכַוֵּן לִבּוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
rather only when directing his heart above, etc.,
שֶׁעוֹסֵק בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּמְיַחֵד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
wherein one engages in effort yet dedicates his striving wholly to Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ בִּשְׁעַת מִלְחָמָה: "דְּמִלְחָמָה לַה' בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר",
And this is during warfare: 'Hashem has a war with Amalek from generation to generation,'
שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה מִדַּת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
the Name Havayah being the attribute of truth unto Jacob,
הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא הָיָה הֹוֶה וְיִהְיֶה עַכְשָׁו כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ,
the awareness that He was, is, and will be, now just as before the world was created, with none besides Him;
בְּכָל דּוֹר הוּא הוֹלֵךְ וּמִתְגַּלֶּה יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לְגַמְרֵי נִקְרָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּכְתַּב.
and in each generation this becomes increasingly manifest until fully unveiled, pronounced as written.
וְזֶהוּ הַמִּלְחָמָה בַּעֲמָלֵק:
And this is the war with Amalek:
כָּל מַה שֶּׁזֶּה נִתְגַּלָּה יוֹתֵר בְּנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
the more this truth is revealed within the souls of Israel,
הוֹלֵךְ וְנִמְחֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק.
the more the root of Amalek is blotted out.
וְהַנִּיחָא אַחַר הַמִּלְחָמָה הוּא פּוּרִים,
And the rest following this war is Purim,
שֶׁהוּא יוֹם דְּנוֹחַ מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם.
which is the day of rest from their enemies.
וְזֶה דֻּגְמַת שַׁבָּת שֶׁנִּקְרָא יוֹם מְנוּחָה,
And this mirrors Shabbat which is termed a day of rest,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אַחַר מִלְחָמָה, רַק אַחַר עֲבוֹדָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
except that it does not follow war, but labor and striving,
וּמְנוּחָתוֹ הוּא שְׁבִיתָה.
and its rest is cessation of work.
אֲבָל מְנוּחַת מִלְחָמָה הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב (רַשִׁ"י) בְּלֶחֶם וָיַיִן דְּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק,
However, rest after battle is as Rashi wrote concerning Melchizedek's bread and wine,
שֶׁכֵּן נוֹתְנִין לִיגֵיעֵי מִלְחָמָה לִסְעֹד הַלֵּב.
that such is served to those exhausted by war to sustain the heart.
כִּי מִלְחָמָה הוּא טִרְדַּת הַלֵּב וְלֹא אֶבְרֵי הַפְּעֻלָּה בִּלְבָד.
For warfare is an agitation of the heart, not merely of the limbs of action.
וּבְיִחוּד מִלְחֶמֶת עֲמָלֵק,
And especially the war with Amalek,
עִקַּר נִצּוּחוֹ בְּבִטּוּל כָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו כְּעִנְיַן "אֵלֶיךָ ה' נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" בִּמְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ.
its victory lies in nullifying all one's faculties, as in 'To You, Hashem, I lift up my soul' in self-sacrifice.
וּבָא אַחַר כָּךְ מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה סַעֲדָא דְּלִבָּא,
Afterward comes feasting and gladness to sustain the heart,
וְ"חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע",
and 'one is obligated to become intoxicated until he knows not,'
כִּי הַדַּעַת הוּא הַמְּחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
for conscious knowledge (Da'at) unites Wisdom and Understanding,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כֹּחוֹת הַלֵּב עִם הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning the emotional faculties of the heart with the cognitive awareness that all is from Hashem.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין צָרִיךְ לָזֶה כְּלָל,
Yet in truth, the root of Israel requires none of this conscious synthesis at all;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשַּׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כְּלָל,
and just as Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come requiring no exertion,
הֵיפֶךְ כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת שֶׁשְּׁלֵמוּתָם רַק עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת.
the antithesis of all nations whose perfection depends on exertion.
כָּךְ פּוּרִים הֵיפֶךְ עֲמָלֵק
So Purim is the antithesis of Amalek,
שֶׁחֶסְרוֹנוֹ מִפְּנֵי חֶסְרוֹן הַדַּעַת דְּכֹחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
whose defect arises from his lack of knowledge that the very power of exertion is from Hashem.
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, גַּם דְּלָא יָדְעֵי זֶה,
However Israel, even when they know it not,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֶצֶם דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ כְּלוּם בֶּאֱמֶת.
nonetheless the root of Israel is essentially clinging to Hashem, needing nothing in truth.

וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִכָּר: בְּכוֹסוֹ (עֵרוּבִין סה605 Eruvin 65b — R. Ila'i said: In three things a man is known — in his cup, in his purse, and in his anger. And some say: also in his laughter. Rashi: "A man is known" — whether he is a worthy man. "In his cup" — whether his mind stays settled upon him with his wine. "In his purse" — whether he acts in good faith when he deals with people. "In his anger" — that he is not exacting beyond measure. Maharsha: The traits fall in general into three classes: good toward Heaven, good toward one's fellows, and good toward oneself. "In his purse" — whether he deals faithfully with men, that is, good or bad toward his fellows; "in his cup" — whether he remains settled with his wine, which is good toward himself, and not like those of whom it is said, "Who has woe, who has sorrow?"; "in his anger" — if he does not grow angry he is good toward Heaven, whereas of one who grows angry they said that it is as though he worshipped idols. And because these three words are close in sound, he took them as a mnemonic for those three divisions. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): "In three things a person is known — in his cup...": that is, precisely through drunkenness, when understanding is taken from him, the difference between the holiness of Israel and the nations is recognized and made clear, for in Israel there is inner holiness even in this-worldly enjoyments. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 12): The Sages give as the sign by which a person is known "his cup, his purse and his anger," and not the hour when he stands in the synagogue wrapped in a tallis and crowned with tefillin, implying that this is no proof. The main recognition comes when he enters the concealments of this-worldly affairs, dealing with people in the markets and streets; then one can recognize the preciousness in a person — what he is in the depths of his heart. עַמּוּד ב).
And in three things a person is revealed: in his cup (Eruvin 65b).
וּבְעֵת הַבִּסּוּם אָז הַמֵּבִין יוּכַל לְהַכִּיר הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין עֲמָלֵק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And during intoxication, the discerning person can distinguish the chasm between Amalek and Israel:
דְּאֵלּוּ: "כָּל רֹאֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּם כִּי הֵם זֶרַע בֵּרַךְ ה'".
for regarding Israel: 'all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which Hashem has blessed.'

sections.en: Amalek as Inner Accuser

items.h: The nations' spiritual forces appear within the heart as forms of the evil inclination; Purim intoxication exposes Israel's deeper holiness beneath conscious distinctions.

Seif 1 — Amalek within the Heart
Amalek is the primal inner accuser, while Purim intoxication reveals a Jewish holiness deeper than conscious moral calculation.

p: כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת הֵם מְקַטְרְגִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
All the nations act as accusers against Israel,

וְהוּא שָׂטָן הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז606 Bava Batra 16a — Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, "And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord." He is the evil inclination, for it is written there, "Only evil all the day," and it is written here, "Only against himself do not put forth your hand." He is the angel of death, as it is written, "Only spare his life" — evidently his life rests in his hand. Rashi: "Evidently his life rests in his hand" — it lies with Satan to take the soul, and God warned him not to take it. Maharsha: Our texts misquote the verse: it reads "only [akh] spare his life," not "only [rak]." The verbal analogy holds nonetheless, since "only [akh]" and "only [rak]" are alike terms of limitation. The hint in it is this: "only evil all the day" — let a man limit his evil inclination and master it, and then "only spare his life" — the Holy One, blessed be He, will limit the power of the angel of death, that he not rule over his soul. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil. עַמּוּד א),
and 'he is Satan, he is the evil inclination' (Bava Batra 16a),
הֵם הַמַּסִּיתִים בַּלֵּב גַּם כֵּן,
they being the instigators within the heart as well;
הַיְנוּ כֹּחַ וְשַׂר שֶׁל כָּל אֻמָּה הוּא עַצְמוֹ אֶחָד מִכֹּחוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
meaning the spiritual force and prince of each nation is itself one of the powers of the evil inclination within the heart.
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
And Amalek is 'the first of the nations' (Numbers 24:20),
הַסָּתָתוֹ הוּא לְרֵאשִׁית הָרָע,
his instigation being toward the primal source of evil,
וְהַתְחָלַת הָרָע אֵינוֹ מַסִּית לֵילֵךְ בַּפֹּעַל לַחֲטֹא,
and the inception of evil does not entice one to deliberately set out to sin,
דְּזֶה וַדַּאי לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה,
for this a person surely would not do;
רַק שֶׁמִּזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו הַדָּבָר,
rather, an opportunity merely presents itself before him,

וְאָז "עַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי" (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה נָשׂא פָּרָשָׁה י607 Bamidbar Rabbah 10:2 — "And you shall not go astray after your heart and after your eyes" [Numbers 15:39] — the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 16): The Sages' words "the eye sees, the heart desires, and the organs of action complete [the deed]" describe three levels. Wisdom is the stage still at "the eye sees" alone, momentary and not yet spread through to the end, unlike prophecy, which has passed through all the levels and is fully possessed; yet wisdom is superior, in the manner of "better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the soul" (Ecclesiastes 6:9). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 1): A thought that reaches the root of wisdom in the brain is joined to the understanding in the heart, so that it is at once felt in the heart and gives birth to the powers of action, as in "the eye sees, the heart desires, and the organs of action complete [the deed]"; for we find seeing associated with wisdom, as it is written, "my heart has seen much wisdom" (Ecclesiastes 1:16). Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Tetzaveh): The kapores corresponds to the heart and the menorah to the eyes, and these alone were of pure gold [without a core of acacia wood], because in them a person must be clean of any self-interest in this world, since "the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin: the eye sees and the heart desires." The eye should be stripped of all worldly desire and serve only as an instrument for the soul, like clear glass through which the soul looks at each thing and judges whether to accept it; but when the eye itself craves the delights of this world, it is no longer the soul's instrument but acts on its own and covets, and the soul cannot sort the good from the bad.).
and then 'the eye sees and the heart covets, etc.' (Midrash Rabbah, Nasso, Parashah 10).
וְזֶהוּ "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ" (דְּבָרִים כה, יח) –
And this is 'who happened upon you on the way' (Deuteronomy 25:18) –
שֶׁבָּא בְּמִקְרֶה וְהִזְדַּמְּנוּת לֹא בְּכִוּוּן,
for he comes through chance and incidental encounter, not by deliberate design,
רַק בִּהְיוֹתוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּטִרְדָּא,
rather while one is on the road, preoccupied,
אַגַּב אָרְחֵיהּ נִזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו דָּבָר.
incidentally along his way an illicit matter presents itself before him.
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַסָּתַת הַיֵּצֶר,
And concerning such an occurrence is the initial incitement of the evil inclination,
וְעַל זֶה הָעֵצָה צִיצִית:
and for this the remedy is tzitzit:
"וּזְכַרְתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
'and you shall remember, etc., and that you go not about, etc.' (Numbers 15:39),
שֶׁהוּא רוֹמֵז לְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם כַּיָּדוּעַ,
which alludes to the fear of Heaven as is known,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִזְכִירָה.
and through this one arrives at mindful remembrance.
וְזֶהוּ הָעִקָּר:
And this is the essential point:
שֶׁכְּשֶׁיִּזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו אֵיזֶה דָּבָר
that when an opportunity presents itself before him,
יִזְכֹּר מִיָּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָסַר דָּבָר זֶה.
he immediately recall that Hashem, blessed be He, prohibited this matter.
וְעִקַּר תְּפִיסַת הַיֵּצֶר הוּא עַל יְדֵי הִזְדַּמְּנוּת,
For the primary grasp of the evil inclination occurs through sudden opportunity,
וְיִצְרוֹ מַשְׁכִּיחוֹ כְּרֶגַע הָאִסּוּר
and his inclination momentarily causes him to forget the prohibition
עַד שֶׁהַלֵּב חוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי.
until the heart covets, etc.
וְעַל יְדֵי רִפּוּי יָדַיִם שֶׁהוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַזְּרִיזוּת,
And through slackness of hands, which is the absence of alacrity,
"וְעַצְלָה תַּפִּיל תַּרְדֵּמָה" (מִשְׁלֵי יט, טו)
and 'slothfulness casts into a deep sleep' (Proverbs 19:15),
שֶׁהוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַדַּעַת וְהַזִּכָּרוֹן לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן,
which is the lack of conscious understanding and memory to reflect,
כִּי בְּשֵׁינָה כָּל מַה שֶּׁהַלֵּב חוֹמֵד כְּלֵי מַעֲשֶׂה גּוֹמְרִים כַּיָּדוּעַ.
for during sleep whatever the heart covets the limbs of action execute, as is known.
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר עֲמָלֵק,
Through this state Amalek is aroused;
וְזֶהוּ "זָכוֹר וְגוֹמֵר",
and this is 'Remember, etc.' (Deuteronomy 25:17),
דְּהָעֵצָה לָזֶה זְכִירָה:
the counsel for this being remembrance:
"בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר" –
namely 'when He gives you rest, etc.' –
שֶׁלֹּא יִרְצֶה לֵילֵךְ וּלְהַרְשִׁיעַ,
even when one has no desire to actively pursue wickedness,
צָרִיךְ לִזְכֹּר מְאֹד מֵחֵטְא הַבָּא בְּהִזְדַּמְּנוּת כִּלְאַחַר יָד.
he must remain exceedingly mindful of sin arriving incidentally as if offhand.
"וְאַתָּה עָיֵף" – דְּהַיְנוּ עַצְלוּת שֶׁהוּא גּוֹרֵם שִׁכְחָה,
'And you were faint' – this denotes sluggishness which causes forgetfulness;
"וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים" – הַמְּעוֹרֵר הַזְּכִירָה כַּנִּזְכָּר.
and 'fearing not God' – which is what awakens remembrance, as mentioned.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן קְרִיעַת כְּנַף דִּמְעִיל דְּשָׁאוּל עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא קִיֵּם מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק,
And this is the significance of the tearing of the corner of Saul's robe because he failed to fulfill the blotting out of Amalek,
