Yose: A time set for good. “And on the day I reckon, I shall reckon their sin upon them” — it was taught in the name of R. Yose: A time set for punishment. “And Rechavam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king” — it was taught in the name of R. Yose: A place set for punishment. At Shechem they afflicted Dinah; at Shechem his brothers sold Yosef; at Shechem the kingdom of the house of David was divided. Rashi: "And on the day I reckon" — the Ninth of Av, which in each year of the forty years they spent in the wilderness was a day set for punishment: on it the spies returned, and on it the Temple was destroyed the first and the second time. "At Shechem his brothers sold Yosef" — as it is written, "Are not your brothers pasturing in Shechem?"; Dothan, named in the verse, is a village near Shechem and is called by its name; alternatively, following its midrashic reading, that they sat in judgment on him to kill him. Maharsha: "And on the day I reckon": Rashi's explanation implies that this refers to the episode of the spies, but the verse is written about the episode of the Calf, so it is better explained of the Seventeenth of Tammuz, as at the end of Taanit: five things befell our fathers on the Seventeenth of Tammuz — the tablets were broken, the daily offering ceased, the city was breached, and the Torah was burned. As for "a time set": God, blessed be He, brings good and evil upon the world in a manner close to nature, so that when He brings a man good as his reward He brings it at a time set for good, according to the constellation of that time, and so conversely with punishment; and likewise "a place set" is according to the constellation that rules in that place. (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב עַמּוּד א) דְּיֵשׁ עֵת רָצוֹן,
and as our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 102a), that there is an 'acceptable time',
וְכֵן בְּהִפּוּךְ יֵשׁ עֵת מוּכָן וְכוּלֵי,
and conversely there is a time prepared for calamity, etc.;
וְזֶהוּ דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל,
and this applies in an overarching manner,
וּבִפְרָט מִסְּתָמָא אֵין שׁוּם רֶגַע דּוֹמָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ כְּמוֹ בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת.
and in detail, presumably no two moments are alike, just as with souls.
וּבְכָל רֶגַע הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עִנְיָן מְיֻחָד בָּעוֹלָם,
And at each moment a unique spiritual influence radiates throughout the universe,
וְכָל אֶחָד מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ לְטָב אוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
and each individual utilizes it according to his personal will, for good or otherwise.

וַחֲלֻקַּת הַשָּׁנָה בִּכְלָל לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיְחִי טו636 Midrash Tanchuma, Vayechi 15 — "All these are the twelve tribes of Israel." Elsewhere it is written, "Twelve princes shall he beget." These tribes correspond to the order of the world: twelve hours in the day and twelve hours in the night, and so too the constellations and the months, and the twelve stones of the ephod. Therefore, "All these are the twelve tribes of Israel.") נֶגֶד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים,
And the division of the year in general into twelve months, which our Sages of blessed memory taught (Midrash Tanchuma, Vayechi 15) corresponds to the twelve tribes,
שֶׁהֵם צֶאֱצָאֵי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל בַּתּוֹרָה לְשֶׁמֶשׁ,
who are the descendants of Jacob who is allegorized in the Torah to the sun;
וְכָךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר הַקָּפוֹת הַיָּרֵחַ
and likewise the twelve months are the twelve orbits of the moon
לְהַשְׁלִים מִדַּת שָׁנָה שֶׁהוּא הֶקֵּף אֶחָד שֶׁל הַחַמָּה.
to complete the full measure of a year, which is one complete revolution of the sun.
וְהָעִנְיָן, כִּי "שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה'" הוּא שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הָרוֹמֵז לְמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב,
And the deeper meaning is: 'For a sun and a shield is Hashem' (Psalms 84:12) refers to the Name Havayah which alludes to the attribute of Jacob,
הוּא דֻּגְמַת שֶׁמֶשׁ הַמֵּאִיר לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
which resembles the sun that radiates light unto the entire world.
וּמִצִּדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַהֶאָרָה תָּמִיד שָׁוָה,
And from His vantage point, blessed be He, the illumination is perpetually uniform,

"שִׁמְשָׁא אַכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נִיחָא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין לט637 Sanhedrin 39a — The emperor said to Rabban Gamliel: You say that wherever there are ten, the Divine Presence rests. How many Divine Presences are there? Rabban Gamliel summoned the emperor's servant and struck him on the neck. He said to him: Why did you let the sun into the emperor's house? He said to him: The sun rests upon the whole world. He said to him: And if the sun, which is one of a thousand thousand myriads of attendants who stand before the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon the whole world, the Divine Presence of the Holy One, blessed be He, how much more so. Rashi: Rabban Gamliel summoned the servant of the heretic [i.e., the emperor] and struck him on his neck; and the reply, "The sun rests upon the whole world," was the heretic's own. Maharsha: This is explained by what I wrote on the aggadot of the Elders of Athens [Bekhorot 8b]: the Holy One, blessed be He, has no bound of place, as it is said, "the whole earth is full of His glory," and "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" — for He is the place of the world, and the world is not His place. The heretic, who believes in corporeality, will not accept this, and the emperor inclined to that belief; hence he asked how many Divine Presences there must be in so many places, if it rests wherever there are ten. So Rabban Gamliel brought him an analogy and a proof from the sun, which is a body and a single simple element and yet rests upon the whole world: all the more does the Divine Presence, which is not a body, rest upon the whole world, bounded by no place. עַמּוּד א),
'the sun shines comfortably for the whole world' (Sanhedrin 39a),
וּבְכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד שָׁוָה,
and on every day it is consistently even,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּבְקַו הַשָּׁוֶה שָׁם תָּמִיד יוֹם וְלַיְלָה שָׁוִים,
for as is known, on the Equator day and night are perpetually equal,
וְשִׁנּוּיֵי הַזְּמַנִּים הוּא מִצַּד חִלּוּקֵי הַמְּקוֹמוֹת.
and the seasonal fluctuations in daylight arise solely from the varied terrestrial locations.
וְכָךְ: "עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר" לְעִנְיַן הַשָּׂגַת הֶאָרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And similarly: 'God made man upright' (Ecclesiastes 7:29) with respect to apprehending His divine radiance,
רַק שֶׁהֵמָּה בִּקְשׁוּ חֶשְׁבֹּנוֹת רַבִּים,
except that they sought out many calculations,
מִזֶּה בָּא שִׁנּוּי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כְּעִנְיַן שִׁנּוּי עִתֵּי הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַמְּקַבְּלִים.
and from this generated the divergence of souls, parallel to the shifting seasons of the year which stem from the receiving vessels.
וְ"אֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה" –
And 'there is no man who does not have his hour' (Avot 4:3) –
הַיְנוּ דַּחֲלֻקַּת הַזְּמַנִּים הוּא כְּנֶגֶד חֲלֻקַּת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת,
signifies that the differentiation of times corresponds directly to the differentiation of souls;
מִסְּתָמָא כָּל שָׁעָה יְדוּעָה הוּא נֶגֶד נֶפֶשׁ יְדוּעָה.
presumably, each specific hour aligns with a specific, corresponding soul.
וּלְפִי שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְּאָדָם אֶחָד,
And because the entire cosmos is structured like one single human organism,
לְפִיכָךְ כָּל אֶחָד מַרְגִּישׁ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת.
consequently each individual soul likewise senses the faculties of all other souls.
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּנּוּת הַזְּמַנִּים
And this operates through the variation of times,
שֶׁבְּכָל רֶגַע מְשַׁמֵּשׁ כֹּחַ אַחֵר שֶׁל נֶפֶשׁ אַחֵר.
wherein in every single moment a different faculty belonging to another soul holds sway.
וּבְאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלּוֹ, שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בָּעוֹלָם,
And during that specific designated hour belonging uniquely to him, when his internal attribute functions within the universe,
אִם יִזְכֶּה לְכַוֵּן הַשָּׁעָה
if he merits to align himself with that precise hour
לִהְיוֹת עָסוּק וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל אָז בְּהַשָּׂגַת הֶאָרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
so as to be engaged and striving at that time in grasping Hashem's light, blessed be He,
יוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת וּלְהַצְלִיחַ אָז דְּקַיְמָא לֵיהּ שַׁעְתָּא,
he can ascend and flourish at that auspicious moment when 'the hour stands in his favor',
בֵּין בְּהַצְלָחָה רוּחָנִיּוּת שֶׁל אוֹרוֹ וַאֲמִתּוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
both in spiritual triumph of His divine light and truth in apprehending Him,
וּבֵין הַצְלָחָה גּוּפָנִית בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
and in bodily success in worldly affairs such as elevated status and the like.
כִּי בְּאוֹתָהּ רֶגַע הוּא רֹאשׁ הַהַנְהָגָה בָּעוֹלָם,
For at that singular instant he stands at the head of cosmic governance,
וְזֶהוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ פְּרָט בְּכָל רֶגַע.
and this operates individually in each distinct moment.
וּבִכְלָל יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲלוּקִים לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים
And in general, Israel is divided into twelve tribes,

שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם הוּא עִנְיָן מְיֻחָד עַיֵּין [בְּהוֹרָיוֹת (ה638 Horayot 5b — And R. Yehuda and R. Shimon — from where do they derive that a single tribe is called a congregation? They said: As it is written, "And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem" (II Chronicles 20:5). Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected: From where? Perhaps Jerusalem is different, since it belonged to Benjamin as well. Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: As it is written, "Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you a congregation of peoples" (Genesis 48:4) — who was born to him at that time? Benjamin. Learn from this that the Merciful One said: Another congregation is now being born to you. Rashi: From the words "the congregation of Judah" it emerges that a single tribe is called a congregation. Rav Acha bar Yaakov objects that Judah proves nothing, since the tribe of Benjamin was with it in Jerusalem, so that it would be two tribes and not one that are called a congregation; and the promise Jacob reports was spoken to him when "God appeared to Jacob again on his coming from Paddan-aram… and God said to him: I am God Almighty, be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a congregation of nations shall come from you" (Genesis 35:9-11). "Who was born to him at that time" means: who was about to be born at that moment — Benjamin; learn from this that the Merciful One was saying to him, another congregation is now being born to you. Tosafos (s.v. "Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you"): It is puzzling that [the Gemara] passes over the verse in which the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself said to Jacob, "A nation and a congregation of nations shall come from you" (Genesis 35:11), and cites instead Jacob's later report of it to Joseph. Maharsha (Chidushei Halachot, on Rashi s.v. "eleven tribes"): Rashi explained Rav Kahana's retort as resting on the premise that two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, are called a congregation; but this is not compelling, since R. Meir holds that two tribes are not called a congregation. It would have been simpler to explain that eleven tribes are certainly called a congregation in the view of all, even R. Meir, since a majority counts as the whole. עַמּוּד ב)],
each of which represents a distinct, autonomous character; see Horayot (5b),
וְהֵם כָּךְ קְבִיעֵי וְקַיְמָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת,
and they are so permanently fixed and established that it is impossible for them to be altered,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קטו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)639 Bava Batra 115b — How so? The inheritance is traced back and back, up to Reuben. But let it say: up to Jacob! Abaye said: It is a received tradition that a tribe is never wiped out. Rashbam: Abaye's answer means: if the search went back as far as Jacob, one tribe would be found wiped out from Israel, and it is a received tradition that a tribe is never wiped out; the proof of this is in Malachi, "For I the Lord have not changed, and you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed" (Malachi 3:6). "Up to Reuben" is not precise — he named Reuben only because he is the first of the tribes. Maharsha: He explains the verse Rashbam cites as proof. Pharaoh's decree, "Every son that is born you shall cast into the river," was an attempt to kill the males and so to blot out the names of their fathers' tribes, and he chose water because the Holy One, blessed be He, had sworn twice not to bring another flood upon the world — and to that the verse answers, "I the Lord have not changed," I hold to that oath; "and you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed" — the males, who are the names of the fathers, were not destroyed, as it is said, "But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied" (Exodus 1:12). Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Emor 11): The twelve loaves of the showbread correspond to the twelve tribes, and "from the children of Israel, an everlasting covenant" is the covenant of the first ones, of the tribes, for "it is a received tradition that a tribe is never wiped out." That is, just as the covenant of the whole of Israel is forever, so each and every tribe has a holiness of its own, which will never be wiped out, and the holiness will always remain. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 252): All the seed of Israel equally possess success in deed, because the upper and lower unification of the heart of Jacob and his sons is fixed in every one of Israel, for "it is a received tradition that a tribe is never wiped out" — that is, the heart of his sons in [that] unification. So every one of Israel has fixed within him the unification of "Hear O Israel" and "Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever," even though he does not sense it at all in the open awareness of his mind and heart.: "גְּמִירֵי דְּלָא כָּלֶה שִׁבְטָא",
just as they taught (Bava Batra 115b): 'it is received as tradition that a tribe is never utterly eradicated',
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הוּא הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
for each tribe constitutes an entire, complete cycle in its own right,
דֻּגְמַת חֹדֶשׁ הַלְּבָנָה מִצַּד קַבָּלַת הָאוֹר שֶׁל חַמָּה,
mirroring the lunar month in its reception of the light of the sun,
וְהֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר צֵרוּפֵי הֲוָיָ"ה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and they correspond to the twelve permutations of the Tetragrammaton (Havayah) as is known.
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַכִּירִים שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֹוֶה וּמְהַוֶּה הַכֹּל וְאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ
That is: all Israel acknowledge that Hashem, blessed be He, is, animates all, and there is none else besides Him,
מֵרֹאשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁהוּא יוּ"ד דְּשֵׁם
from the inception of Thought, which is the letter Yud of the Name,
עַד סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה.
unto the culmination of Action, which is the final Hei.
אַךְ בְּאֵיכוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה הַזּוֹ יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים:
Yet regarding the quality and nature of this spiritual perception there exist variations:
יֵשׁ מִי שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
there is one who apprehends it through the faculty of intellectual wisdom,
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
and there is one who attains it through the emotional feeling of the heart, and the like.
וְהֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר צֵרוּפִים בְּחִלּוּף סֵדֶר הָאוֹתִיּוֹת
And these manifest as twelve divine permutations through the reordering of the letters,
הַמּוֹרוֹת עַל חֲלוֹף סֵדֶר הַהַשָּׂגָה,
which signify the varied pathways of spiritual comprehension,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל שֵׁבֶט דֶּרֶךְ וְסֵדֶר מְיֻחָד בְּקַבָּלַת אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם,
in that each tribe possesses a distinct avenue and sequence in receiving His light, which is a complete cycle,
דְּהַיְנוּ הַשָּׂגָה דְּכָל אַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּאַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם.
meaning an integrated comprehension of all four tiers corresponding to the four letters of the Name.
רַק שֶׁהַסֵּדֶר מְשֻׁנֶּה בְּכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי שִׁנּוּי קַבָּלָתוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגַת אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Only that the sequence differs within each tribe according to its reception in grasping His ultimate truth,
דֻּגְמַת חָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם דּוֹמֶה לַחֲבֵירוֹ.
resembling the months of the moon, each of which in its own right constitutes a full, complete cycle comparable to its fellow.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גֹּדֶל הַלֵּילוֹת שֶׁמְּשַׁמֶּשֶׁת הַלְּבָנָה מִשְׁתַּנִּים
Nonetheless, the duration of the nights in which the moon serves changes
כְּפִי שִׁנּוּיֵי עֲמִידַת הַחַמָּה בְּמַהֲלָכָהּ הַשְּׁנָתִי,
in accordance with the variations in the position of the sun during its annual path,
שֶׁגַּם הִיא שִׁנּוּיָהּ תָּלוּי מִצַּד הַמְּקַבְּלִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר.
which itself is an apparent shift dependent upon the terrestrial recipients, as has been explained.
וְנִיסָן אַתְוָון כְּסִדְרָן,
And in the month of Nisan the divine letters are aligned in their direct order (Y-H-V-H),
שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ הוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַמַּעֲלֶךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם:
for during that month the spiritual perception descends directly from Hashem, Who raised you from Egypt:
"בְּנִיסָן נִגְאֲלוּ וּבְנִיסָן עֲתִידִין וְכוּלֵי",
'In Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed, etc.,'

שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בָּזֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה ([רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יא רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א640 Rosh Hashanah 11a — R. Eliezer says: ...on Rosh HaShana the bondage of our forefathers in Egypt ceased; in Nisan they were redeemed; and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. R. Yehoshua says: In Nisan the world was created; in Nisan the Patriarchs were born; in Nisan the Patriarchs died; on Passover Isaac was born; on Rosh HaShana Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah were remembered; on Rosh HaShana Joseph came out of prison; on Rosh HaShana the bondage of our forefathers in Egypt ceased; in Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed. Rashi: "The Patriarchs were born": Avraham and Yaakov. "Sarah [, Rachel and Chanah] were remembered": their remembrance came up [before Him] for good, and pregnancy was decreed for them. "The servitude of our fathers ceased": six months before their redemption the bondage stopped. Tosafos (s.v. "on Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers in Egypt ceased"): R. Yehoshua too agrees with this, according to most texts; and although the plagues began in Nisan — for the judgment of the Egyptians lasted twelve months, as we learned in Eduyos — the servitude nevertheless did not cease until Tishrei. Maharsha (s.v. "in Tishrei the world was created"): Yitzchak, who is the attribute of judgment, was born on Pesach, when the attribute of judgment prevailed over the Egyptians in the plague of the firstborn, and Israel were redeemed in it through that harsh judgment upon the Egyptians. But "in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed", because in the future complete mercy will come to Israel, as it is written, "with great mercy will I gather you"; and it is derived from "a great shofar will be sounded", for the sounding of the shofar signifies mercy, as in "Your right hand is extended". Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a): On Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers ceased because in this month the Blessed One reigns as King of Israel — He is then called "the King" — so that they no longer served another king; and because this month is set apart for holiness, the Sabbatical and Jubilee years, holy in their cessation from labor, beginning in it, so that when Tishrei came, labor ceased from our fathers in Egypt. The redemption itself was in Nisan, for Nisan, the first of the months, rises to the place of redemption, which is why miracles beyond nature are renewed in it, and according to R. Yehoshua they will be redeemed in it at the end as well. R. Eliezer holds that the first redemption was fittingly in Nisan, the beginning of redemption, but that at the end of days they will be redeemed in the month whose rank is that of completion, when the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted over all existence — for redemption means Israel's ascent to a place where there is no servitude.]),
wherein Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehudah disputed (Rosh Hashanah 11a),

וּלְטַעֲמַיְהוּ אָזְלֵי בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (צז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב641 Sanhedrin 97b — This is a dispute of tannaim. R. Eliezer says: If Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. R. Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent they are not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, will set over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel will repent, and He will restore them to the good. Maharsha: R. Eliezer's "if Israel repent" means a willed repentance, of their own accord, whereas R. Yehoshua holds that when the time of redemption comes, the Holy One, blessed be He, sets over them a king whose decrees are harsh and restores them to the good so that they repent — a compelled repentance. He rejects Rashi's reading that in R. Yehoshua's view they are redeemed without any repentance at all, for if so, why would R. Yehoshua speak of a king like Haman who restores them to the good? Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 97b): R. Eliezer does not mean that without repentance there will be no redemption and the matter will remain in doubt, for there is no doubt about the redemption of Israel; rather, exile is an accidental thing — in itself, for by the order of the world the Israelite nation ought to be in its land and not under the dominion of others, and if exile depends on sin, sin too is not essential but accidental, and what is accidental has no permanence — and God, blessed be He, will remove from them the sickness of the soul as He removes sickness of the body, as it is written, "And the Lord will circumcise your heart," so that it is impossible that they will not repent. R. Yehoshua did not hold that it depends specifically on Israel's repentance, as though the redemption lay in Israel's hands: Israel must indeed repent and then they will be redeemed, but if God, blessed be He, wishes to redeem Israel and they do not repent, He sets over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's and restores them to the good. In the end, according to all, it is impossible that the exile be permanent. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 37): Answering Abraham's "Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it," He said "Know surely" and told him of the [subjugation to the] kingdoms, for the Land is merited through sufferings, which sweeten the flesh, the bodily part of man that corresponds to deeds. Only through this is there hope for the complete end, as they said, "He sets up a king as harsh as Haman," and then there will be an inheritance and possession without interruption. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Of the future redemption it is said, "As in the days of your going out of Egypt I will show him wonders": when it comes "in its time" and they are not worthy, then even though the Holy One, blessed be He, will set up a king as harsh as Haman so that they repent, that repentance comes from an arousal from Above, and on this the nations have a claim, that had He aroused them from Above they too would have been aroused. Such a redemption "in its time," like the Exodus, comes from an arousal from Above: a sudden redemption without prior merit or effort, whose light is not yet grasped in this world before it appears. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): The King of the world, as it were, removed the ring of His rule and handed it to Haman, holiness clothing itself in Haman's sackcloth, since Israel were asleep to the commandments and could be roused only in this way, while the true intent was the reverse: to exalt Israel and destroy Haman, the seed of Amalek and all Israel's enemies. So too in the future, if, Heaven forbid, they should need a king as harsh as Haman, the Blessed One will clothe Himself within him, for "the king's heart is in the hand of the Lord," and through that clothing in the garment of Esau [Israel's enemies] will be wiped out from the world.):
and they follow their established reasoning in the chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 97b end):

דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סוֹבֵר: "אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי642 Rosh Hashanah 10b; Sanhedrin 97b — It was taught: R. Eliezer says — in Tishrei the world was created, in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born, in Tishrei the Patriarchs died, on Pesach Yitzchak was born, on Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel and Chanah were remembered, on Rosh Hashanah Yosef went out from prison, on Rosh Hashanah our fathers’ servitude in Egypt ceased, in Nisan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. R. Yehoshua says — in Nisan the world was created, in Nisan the Patriarchs were born, in Nisan the Patriarchs died … in Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed. And in Sanhedrin 97b: R. Eliezer says — if Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. R. Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, are they not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, will set over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman’s, and Israel will repent and be restored to the good. Rashi: "R. Eliezer says [in Tishrei the world was created …]": he derives it from verses below. "The Patriarchs were born": Avraham and Yaakov. "Sarah [, Rachel and Chanah] were remembered": their remembrance came up [before Him] for good, and pregnancy was decreed for them. "The servitude of our fathers ceased": six months before their redemption the bondage stopped. Tosafos (s.v. "on Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers in Egypt ceased"): R. Yehoshua too agrees with this, according to most texts; and although the plagues began in Nisan — for the judgment of the Egyptians lasted twelve months, as we learned in Eduyos — the servitude nevertheless did not cease until Tishrei. Maharsha: It emerges that Rosh Hashanah was fixed on the first of Tishrei because the world — that is, man — was created on it, and on it man came to judgment, for he sinned; Adam repented, and the Holy One, blessed be He, who created the world with mercy, forgave him. Therefore on that day the Patriarchs Avraham and Yaakov were born, corresponding to the attributes of kindness and mercy, as a sign for their children that He will deal with them in mercy in the judgment of this day; but Yitzchak, who is the attribute of judgment, was born on Pesach, when the attribute of judgment prevailed over the Egyptians in the plague of the firstborn and Israel were redeemed through that harsh judgment. "In Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed", because in the future complete mercy will come to Israel, as it is written, "with great mercy will I gather you"; and it is derived from "a great shofar will be sounded", for the sounding of the shofar signifies mercy, as in "Your right hand is extended". Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 97b): Rashi explained that according to R. Yehoshua they are redeemed without any repentance at all — but then why would R. Yehoshua speak of a king who "returns them to the good"? Rather, R. Eliezer's "if Israel repent" means a voluntary repentance, of their own accord, while R. Yehoshua answers that when the time of redemption comes the Holy One, blessed be He, sets over them a king like Haman and returns them to the good — a repentance compelled by suffering. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a): The dispute over Nisan and Tishrei is very deep, for these are the two principal months: Nisan is the beginning of the months, holy as the firstborn is holy, while Tishrei is the seventh, set apart and holy as the seventh is always chosen — the Sabbath among days, the Sabbatical year among years — and so it is the "head" of the whole year. R. Eliezer holds that the world was created in Tishrei because the world exists for the sake of its end, its completion, and Tishrei, the seventh, is the month of the world's completion, whereas R. Yehoshua follows the beginning, and Nisan, the beginning of all, befits the beginning that is the creation of the world. So too with the redemption: according to R. Yehoshua, as they were redeemed in Nisan, the month that rises to the place of redemption, so they will be redeemed in Nisan; R. Eliezer holds that the first redemption was in Nisan because Israel had not yet reached the wholly separate divine level, but the final redemption, on a higher divine level, will be in Tishrei, when the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted over all existence. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 97b): R. Eliezer does not mean that the redemption is in doubt, for there is no doubt about Israel's redemption: exile departs from the order of the world, and the sin on which it depends is not of Israel's essence but accidental, and what is accidental cannot endure — so it is impossible that they will not repent. R. Yehoshua holds that the redemption does not hang on Israel's repentance, as though it were in Israel's hands: if the Blessed One wishes to redeem them and they have not repented, He sets over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's and returns them to the good; in the end, according to both, the exile cannot endure forever.",
for Rabbi Eliezer holds: 'If Israel repents, they are redeemed, etc.,'
וְהַיְנוּ בְּתִשְׁרֵי מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין שֶׁהוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
which aligns with Tishrei, from the aspect of strict Justice that operates solely through human awakening from below (itaruta d'letata).
וּלְכָךְ תִּשְׁרֵי אַתְוָון לְמַפְרֵעַ מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָא,
Therefore, in Tishrei the letters proceed retroactively from below upward,
וְהַצֵּרוּף שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ יָדוּעַ מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהוּא צֵרוּף וְהִֽיָּ"הּ,
and the permutation of that month is known from the holy Arizal to be V-H-Y-H,
בָּנִים קוֹדְמִין לָאָבוֹת,
where sons precede fathers (the lower letters Vav-Hei preceding the supernal Yud-Hei),
דְּהַיְנוּ הָעִקָּר: "שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי וְאָשׁוּבָה וְגוֹמֵר" (מַלְאָכִי ג, ז),
meaning the primary premise: 'Return unto Me, and I will return unto you' (Malachi 3:7);
וְהֵם יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
and these are days of active repentance and exertion,

וְנִקְרָא "הָאֵיתָנִים" דִּתְקִיפֵי בְּמִצְוֹת (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם643 Rosh Hashanah 11a — R. Eliezer says: From where that the Patriarchs were born in Tishrei? For it is said, "And all the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the feast in the month of the mighty [eitanim]" — the month in which the mighty ones of the world were born. And the other [R. Yehoshua], who holds that the Patriarchs were born in Nisan — is it not written, "in the month of the mighty"? There it means that the month is mighty in commandments. Rashi: "And it says: Hear, O mountains, the controversy of the Lord, and you mighty ones [eitanim]": so the mighty ones are the mountains; and we find the Patriarchs called mountains, as it is said, "skipping upon the mountains" — He skipped over the appointed end for the sake of the "mountains". "Mighty in commandments": shofar, Yom Kippur, sukkah, lulav, the willow and the water libation. Maharsha: "The month in which the mighty ones of the world were born": that is, the strong ones of the world, upon whose merit the world stands, as he adduces, "and you mighty ones, foundations of the earth"; and therefore they were born in this month, in which, according to R. Eliezer, the world was created. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a): R. Eliezer holds that the Patriarchs, who are holy and godly, were fittingly born in Tishrei, for all divine things belong in Tishrei, the month set apart for everything holy. "The Patriarchs" means the Patriarchs as a whole — Avraham, who is the head, and Yaakov, who is the end — and when the head and the end are born in Tishrei, Yitzchak is included with them as though he too had been born in Tishrei.).
and Tishrei is termed the month of Eitanim because they are robust and mighty in mitzvot (Rosh Hashanah ibid.).
וְכָל תְּקִיפוּת הוּא מִי שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
And all spiritual force is found in one who attains it through his own active exertion,
דְּזֶה נִקְרָא לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁבָּא בִּזְרוֹעַ,
which in rabbinic idiom is termed 'coming by forceful arm,'

וּבְסוֹף פֶּרֶק ב' דִּבְרָכוֹת (יז644 Berakhot 17b — "Hear Me, stubborn-hearted, who are far from charity." Rav and Shmuel — and some say R. Yochanan and R. Elazar. One said: The whole world is sustained by charity, while they are sustained by force. And one said: The whole world is sustained by their merit, while they are not sustained even by their own merit. Rashi: "The whole world is sustained by charity" — by the charity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and not by any merit of their own; "while they are sustained by force" — by the merit that is in their hand. The verse is speaking of the righteous, and calls them "far from" the charity of the Holy One, blessed be He. Tosafos (s.v. "while they are sustained by force"): Accordingly one should emend the text of the shofar-service piyyut [for New Year] to read "and they, by force, came before You," and not "they did not come before You." Maharsha: "Stubborn" [abir] is a term of strength, as is "force" [zeroa], and we find this idiom used of men of standing — "the mightiest of the herdsmen," and "like the mightiest among the mighty" (Rosh HaShanah 25b). And the one who expounds the verse of the wicked likewise takes it from the language of strength, that is, hardness of heart, as in "the stout-hearted are despoiled." עַמּוּד ב): שֶׁרָחוֹק מִצְּדָקָה.
and at the end of the second chapter of Berakhot (17b): that it is 'far from gratuitous charity'.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נִיסָן נִקְרָא כֵּן עַל שֵׁם הַנִּסִּים שֶׁבּוֹ,
In contrast, Nisan is named after the overt miracles within it,
וְכָל נֵס הוּא חוּץ לְדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע שֶׁהוּא הַהַנְהָגָה שֶׁמִּצַּד שׁוּרַת הַמִּשְׁפָּט וְחֹק הַקָּבוּעַ,
and every miracle transcends the natural order, which is the governance rooted in strict judicial measure and fixed law;
רַק הַכֹּל בִּצְדָקָה וּבִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
rather, everything flows through pure charity and the unconditional will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא לְבַד בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת תַּחְתּוֹנִים.
and divine initiative from Above alone (itaruta d'le'eila), without human exertion from below.
וְזֶהוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעֲמֵיהּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם סְבִירָא לֵיהּ: בְּנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל.
And this is Rabbi Yehudah following his reasoning in Sanhedrin who holds: In Nisan they are destined to be redeemed.
וְהַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד הִיא אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם כְּסִדְרָן,
And the perception descending purely from Hashem alone features the letters of the Name in their direct order (Y-H-V-H),
שֶׁהַסֵּדֶר הַכָּתוּב הוּא הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁקָּבַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
for the written scriptural order is the natural flow established by Hashem in His world,
שֶׁכָּךְ מִדַּת הַשְׁפָּעָתוֹ הַשָּׂגָתוֹ,
for such is the descending measure of His bestowal and revelation,
שֶׁזֶּה סֵדֶר מַהֲלָךְ הָרָאוּי שֶׁבְּכָל עִנְיָן מֵרֹאשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עַד סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
which is the proper linear progression across all existence from the origin of Thought to the culmination of Action, as is known.
וּכְפִי סֵדֶר שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה פְּשׁוּטוֹת בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה שֶׁבָּהֶם בְּרִיאַת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים,
And according to the sequence of the twelve simple letters in Sefer Yetzirah through which the twelve months were created,
נִיסָן הוּא בְּאוֹת הֵ"א,
Nisan was created with the letter Hei,
וְהוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל כַּיָּדוּעַ
which represents a receptive vessel as is known,
וּכְלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה כָּל מִינֵי נִסִּים וְנִפְלָאוֹת.
and an expansive vessel holding blessings of all varieties of miracles and wonders.
וְתִשְׁרֵי בְּאוֹת לָמֶ"ד,
And Tishrei was created with the letter Lamed,
כִּי מַזָּלוֹ מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁהוּא הַמַּתְקְלָא,
for its astrological sign is Libra (the Scales), which is the cosmic balance,
דְּמִצַּד הַמִּשְׁפָּט יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשְׁקָל לְהַכְרִיעַ לְאֵיזֶה כַּף.
wherein through judicial measure there is weight to tip toward one pan or the other.
וְאוֹת לָמֶ"ד הִיא הַמֹּאזְנַיִם,
And the letter Lamed is the Scales;

דְּגַגָּהּ נִקְרָא "מִגְדָּל הַפּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר" כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק ([סַנְהֶדְרִין קו645 Rashi on Sanhedrin 106b:11:3 — "On the tower that flies in the air" — the upper stroke above the letter lamed: why is it bent downward. So R. Moses the Elder explained, by received tradition. Another reading: "the tower that flies in the air" refers to one who enters the land of the nations in a chest, a box, or a cupboard — whether he becomes impure or not. Another reading: three hundred laws concerning "the tower that flies in the air" — to work magic so as to suspend a tower in the air. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): It is known that lamed is called "the tower that flies in the air" (Sanhedrin 106b, following Rashi's first explanation there, from received tradition). The Tikkunei Zohar, which calls lamed the supernal Mother, "a tower of strength," appears to read "The name of the Lord is a tower of strength" as referring to that flying tower, the letter lamed: the tower itself is the Mother, and the Daughter, the Congregation of Israel, who is called "poor," dwells in it. Every yesod [foundation] is called such a tower, and this is why the letter lamed was "made king over union," which is in the yesod. עַמּוּד ב]),
its elevated roof being termed 'a tower soaring in the air' as Rashi explains in Sanhedrin (106b),
"וְרַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת" רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.
while its descendancy corresponds to 'her feet go down to death' (Proverbs 5:5), Heaven forbid.
וּלְכָךְ הַגַּג הוּא כְּפוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר,
Therefore its roof hovers like a soaring tower in the air,

וְהֵן הֵם תְּלָת מְאָה בַּעְיָא דִּבְעוֹ וְכוּלֵי (חֲגִיגָה טו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב עַיֵּין שָׁם646 Chagigah 15b — "Where is he who counted the towers?" (Isaiah 33:18) — for they would teach three hundred laws concerning a tower floating in the air. And R. Ami said: Doeg and Ahithophel asked three hundred questions about a tower floating in the air. Yet we learned: three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come. What, then, will become of us? He said to him: Sharp-witted one, there was mud in their hearts. Rashi: "A tower floating in the air": some explain that they would expound the height of the letter lamed and derive all this from it; others, the tower of the generation of the dispersion. But it seems to me that the reading is "a tower open to the air" — these are laws of tent impurity concerning a wooden closet that stands in a doorway whose opening faces a field or a courtyard, which is open air. "Four commoners" — Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel and Gehazi, listed in chapter Chelek. "There was mud in their hearts" — they were wicked men from the first. Maharsha: He refers the reader to Sanhedrin (chapter Chelek), where the counting of all the letters of the Torah, the weighing of its light and weighty matters, and the teaching of three hundred laws concerning a tower floating in the air are set out. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 106b): [On the parallel passage in Sanhedrin:] It seems that this means man's intellect, which rises upward and is called "a tower floating in the air": although man is the bearer of his intellect, the intellect does not stand in him mixed with him, and since it is not mixed with him, it stands in the air. Alternatively, "a tower floating in the air" denotes the intellectual matters that are not mixed with physicality — things wholly separate from matter, which rise upward and float in the air.),
and these are the three hundred theological dilemmas they raised (Chagigah 15b end, see there),
כִּי יָדוּעַ דְּשָׁם דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּאוֹתוֹ מִגְדָּל
for it is known that there resides the spiritual level of David, who sits within that tower
וּמַכְרִיעַ הַכֹּל לְכַף זְכוּת,
and tips everything toward the scale of merit,
שֶׁהוּא הַגֶּבֶר הֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲלֶה הַכֹּל לְמַעְלָה.
being the man who established the yoke of repentance, elevating all back upward.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא פּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר,
And in this physical world it hovers in the air;
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא "בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח" אֵין לוֹ אֲחִיזָה חֲזָקָה עֲדַיִן.
so long as death has not been 'swallowed up forever,' it has no absolute, firm grasp as yet.
וְהֵם תְּלָת בַּעְיָא בִּתְלָת עָלְמִין: בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה,
And these correspond to three inquiries across the three lower worlds: Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
דְּשָׁם הוּא רֹאשׁ לַשּׁוּעָלִים וְנִקְרָא מֶלֶךְ.
where he stands as a leader among foxes and is designated as king.
וּבַעְיָא הוּא הֲטָלַת הַסָּפֵק
And an inquiry represents the injection of doubt,

וּשְׁאֵלַת: "הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ מִיתָתוֹ בַּמֶּה647 Sanhedrin 107a — Rava expounded: What is meant by “But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered; the lowly gathered against me and I did not know; they tore and were not silent”? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that if they were to tear my flesh, my blood would not flow. And more than that — when they are engaged in the four modes of court-imposed death they interrupt their study and say to me: David, one who comes upon a married woman — by what death is he put to death? I said to them: One who comes upon a married woman is put to death by strangling, and he has a portion in the World to Come. But one who shames his fellow in public has no portion in the World to Come. Rashi: "The lowly gathered against me" — the maimed (as in "Pharaoh Necho"), who would mock me while I was as one who does not know; another explanation: "and I did not know" — I would not know when they mocked; that is, that sin came upon me suddenly, and I did not know that it would give them an opening to shame me. Rashi reads: "When they are engaged in the court-imposed deaths, they say: One who comes upon a married woman — his death is…" Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, Bava Metzia 59a): By this exposition, "at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered" refers to David's having sinned through a doubt: "the smitten" are those slain in the war with Ammon, among whom Uriah was killed, "and I did not know" that he had been killed with them, for I took his wife before he was killed, so that she was retroactively only a doubtful married woman. One who comes upon a married woman has a portion in the World to Come only through his death by strangling, since the court's execution is his atonement; but if he is not tried by a court, one who comes upon a woman who is certainly married is no better than one who shames his fellow, for both descend [to Gehinnom] and do not ascend. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Bava Metzia 59a): Although David had come upon a woman who was certainly married, he knew in himself that he suffered when they shamed him in this way; hence David could rightly say that one who comes upon a married woman is put to death by strangling and has a portion in the World to Come, and here there is no doubt. For the sin of a married woman does not reach so far that he is lost from the World to Come, which was created with the yud of His great Name; but the image of God in which man was created is of the level of the World to Come, and therefore one who shames his fellow in public has no portion in the World to Come at all.?" ([סַנְהֶדְרִין קז עַמּוּד א]),
and the Talmudic challenge: 'One who violates a married woman, what is his death?' (Sanhedrin 107a),
שֶׁהָא הַהוֹרָדָה לְ"רַגְלֶיהָ וְגוֹמֵר".
which represents the terrifying descent of 'her feet go down, etc.'
כִּי הָאֲוִיר הוּא מְקוֹם הַסָּפֵק,
For the open air is the domain of doubt;
דְּדָבָר הַמְּבֹרָר הוּא כְּאִלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ מַצָּב חָזָק,
for that which is clearly clarified possesses a firm foundation,
וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא סָפֵק נִקְרָא תָּלוּי בְּרִפְיוֹן דְּהַיְנוּ בָּאֲוִיר.
whereas that which is doubtful is termed suspended in instability, namely in thin air.
וּמִצַּד הָנָךְ תְּלָת עָלְמִין הַדָּבָר בְּרִפְיוֹן,
And from the perspective of those three lower worlds the matter hangs in instability,
אֲבָל הַהִתְחַזְּקוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר וְהָאֲחִיזָה בַּאֲצִילוּת קָדְשׁוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
yet the enduring strength derives from absolute Divine Unity and the bond to the supernal realm of Atzilut, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהֵשִׁיב לָהֶם: "מִיתָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא",
And this is why David replied to them: 'His execution is by strangulation, but he has a share in the World to Come,'
דִּבְאוֹת יוּ"ד נִבְרָא עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
for through the letter Yud was the World to Come created.
וְהַמֵּבִין יָבִין, כִּי לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי אוֹת לָמֶ"ד וְהֵ"א רוֹמְזִים לְעִנְיָן אֶחָד,
And the discerning will understand that according to what I have written, the letters Lamed and Hei allude to one underlying concept,
רַק הַהֵ"א רוֹמֶזֶת מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ לִכְלִי קִבּוּל,
except that Hei alludes through its broad shape to a receptive vessel,
וְאוֹת לָמֶ"ד מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהִיא בְּמִשְׁקֹלֶת לְמַעְלָה וּלְמַטָּה.
and the letter Lamed through its vertical extension reaching both upward and downward.
וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה פְּשׁוּטוֹת רוֹמְזִים לָעִנְיָן הַהוּא עַצְמוֹ,
And in truth, all twelve simple letters allude to this very theme,
כִּי כֻּלָּם נֶגֶד חָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה,
for they all correspond to the lunar months,
רַק כָּל אֶחָד מוֹרֶה עִנְיָן מְיֻחָד שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה.
only that each reflects a unique facet of this divine reality.
וֶאֱלוּל בְּאוֹת יוּ"ד שֶׁהוּא עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י עַל "אָז יָשִׁיר",
And the month of Elul was created through the letter Yud, which designates Thought as Rashi explains on 'Then sang Moses' (Exodus 15:1),
כִּי מַזָּלוֹ בְּתוּלָה,
for its astrological sign is Virgo (the Virgin),
דְּמַשְׁמָעוּתוֹ דָּבָר חָדָשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נָגְעוּ בָּהּ עֲדַיִן,
which signifies something completely pristine and untouched,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּנִדָּה (ח648 Niddah 8b — Rav Kahana said that it was taught: There are three virgins — a virgin woman, virgin ground, and a virgin sycamore. A virgin woman: so long as she has not had intercourse; the practical difference concerns [her fitness] for a High Priest, or her marriage contract of two hundred. Virgin ground: so long as it has not been worked; the practical difference concerns the rough valley [where the heifer's neck is broken], or buying and selling. A virgin sycamore: so long as it has not been felled; the practical difference concerns buying and selling, or felling it in the Sabbatical year. Rashi: "For a High Priest" — who is commanded to marry a virgin; "for her marriage contract of two hundred" — since once she has had intercourse she is no longer called a virgin and her marriage contract is a hundred. "For buying and selling" [of virgin ground] — if a man said to him, "I am selling you virgin ground," he must give him ground that has never been worked, since it yields abundant and rich produce. "So long as it has not been felled" — it is the custom to fell a sycamore so that its trunk will thicken and put out many branches at the cut, and it is then called the stump of a sycamore; and as to buying and selling, a purchaser prefers a virgin sycamore, which is young, so that he may fell it and it will thicken. עַמּוּד ב): ג' בְּתוּלוֹת.
as written in the first chapter of Niddah (8b): three categories of virgin.
כִּי שְׁלִיטַת יְדֵי הָאָדָם הוּא מֵהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְאֵילָךְ שֶׁשָּׁם מוּרְגָּשׁ לָאָדָם,
For human dominion begins from the feeling of the heart downward where emotion is palpably experienced,
וּמִשֶּׁשָּׁלְטָה הַרְגָּשַׁת אָדָם אֵינוֹ בְּתוּלָה.
and once human emotional sensation dominates, it is no longer a virgin.
אֲבָל הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁשָּׁם אֵין שְׁלִיטַת הַרְגָּשָׁה זֶה תָּמִיד כִּבְתוּלָה,
However, Thought, which is entirely free from the dominance of physical sensation, remains perpetually like a virgin;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "וְתִירוֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵב בְּתֻלוֹת" (זְכַרְיָה ט, יז),
and concerning this Scripture states: 'and new wine shall make the maidens flourish' (Zechariah 9:17),
כִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן בְּכָל יוֹם כַּחֲדָשִׁים,
for words of Torah are likewise fresh each day as if newly given,

רַק שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל הַהוֹגֶה מוֹצֵא טַעַם649 Eruvin 54a — R. Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R. Yochanan: What is meant by “He who tends a fig tree shall eat its fruit”? Why are words of Torah likened to a fig? Just as with a fig, whenever a man handles it he finds figs in it, so too with words of Torah — whenever a man meditates on them he finds savour in them. R. Shmuel bar Nachmani said: What is meant by “a loving hind and a graceful doe”? Why are words of Torah likened to a hind? To tell you: just as with a hind, her mate finds her as dear at every hour as at the first hour, so too words of Torah are as dear to those who study them at every hour as at the first hour. Rashi: "Whenever he handles it he finds figs in it" — for figs do not all ripen at once, but a few today and a few tomorrow, so that at every hour some of them are fit to eat. Maharsha: This is why the matter is made to depend upon guarding the fig: other trees, which ripen all at once, need no watching except at the season of their ripening, but the fig, which ripens a little at a time, needs watching every day lest men pick from it. As for the hind: whatever a man is much accustomed to he wearies of, and sometimes it even becomes loathsome to him; words of Torah are not so, but are beloved at every hour as at the first. (עֵרוּבִין נד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב),
only that nonetheless whoever meditates upon them finds fresh flavor (Eruvin 54b),
אֶלָּא שֶׁטּוֹעֵם טַעַם בְּתוּלָה כְּאִלּוּ הוּא דָּבָר חָדָשׁ שֶׁלֹּא טָעַם עֲדַיִן מֵעוֹלָם,
experiencing the pristine flavor of a virgin as though it were a novelty he had never before tasted;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ טַעַם,
yet nevertheless he experiences a definite taste,
וְנִמְצָא בִּשְׁעָתוֹ הוּא "מְנוֹבֵב" –
and so at that precise moment it is menovev –
פֵּרוּשׁ מֵרִיק כְּמוֹ "נְבוּב לֻחֹת" שֶׁמּוֹצִיא הַבְּתוּלוֹת,
meaning hollowed out and emptied, like 'hollow with planks' (Exodus 27:8), discharging the pristine virginity,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזֵר לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ וְלִטְעֹם טַעַם בְּתוּלָה.
only that afterward it renews itself afresh to taste of virgin purity again.
אֲבָל בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם הוּא כְּבוֹעֵל בְּתוּלָה דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל.
Yet during the actual experience, the sensation of taste is allegorically akin to intimacy with a virgin.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי תִּירוֹשׁ,
And this unfolds through new wine (tirosh),
דְּיַיִן מְפַקֵּחַ הַלֵּב שֶׁבּוֹ הַהַרְגָּשָׁה,
for wine enlivens the heart wherein resides emotion;

כִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִמְשְׁלוּ לְמַיִם וּלְיַיִן וּלְחָלָב ([תַּעֲנִית ז650 Taanit 7a — R. Oshaya said: Why were words of Torah likened to these three liquids — to water, to wine, and to milk? For it is written, “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water,” and it is written, “Come, buy and eat; come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.” To tell you: just as these three liquids keep only in the humblest of vessels, so too words of Torah endure only in one whose mind is lowly. Rashi: "These three liquids": water, wine and milk — this is the Torah, for which one gives nothing [— "without money and without price" —] and yet knows it and learns it. "In the humblest of vessels": in earthenware vessels. Tosafos (s.v. "so too words of Torah"): So too we say in Eruvin (55a) on "It is not in heaven … neither is it beyond the sea" (Deuteronomy 30:12–13): you will not find the Torah in one who raises himself as high as the heavens, whose mind is haughty, nor among merchants who travel overseas. Maharsha: Above, with respect to "just as water leaves a high place" [and flows to a low one], wine and milk too, if poured on the ground, leave a high place; but it is not their way to be poured on the ground as water is, nor can one speak of wine and milk leaving a high place as one can of springs and rivers. Here, however, with respect to the humblest of vessels, it is apt to liken the Torah to all three liquids. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 2): These liquids are altered very easily, and so they need the humblest of vessels: an earthenware vessel, on account of its simplicity, does not act upon the liquid, whereas silver and gold, which are not simple as the humblest of vessels is simple, change it. So too the Torah endures only in one whose mind is lowly, for when his mind is lowly he has the quality of simplicity, and if his mind is not lowly the Torah, which is of the intellect, will not endure with him. And the Torah is likened to these three liquids — wine, milk and water — because it is compounded of three qualities, and for this reason the Torah is called "threefold." עַמּוּד א]):
for words of Torah are compared to water, wine, and milk (Ta'anit 7a):
מַיִם הוּא הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ שֶׁהוּא בִּפְשִׁיטוּת בְּלֹא הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב עֲדַיִן,
water is intellectual perception in the brain which exists in simplicity without emotional sensation in the heart,
וְזֶה חִנָּם לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם וְהֶפְקֵר שֶׁאֵין יַד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם מַשֶּׂגֶת לְשָׁם;
and this is free and ownerless to all humanity, beyond the reach of human exertion;
וְיַיִן הוּא הַהֶרְגֵּשׁ שֶׁבַּלֵּב;
wine is the inward sensation of the heart;
וְחָלָב הוּא הַהוֹצָאָה לַפּוֹעַל לְהָנִיק לַאֲחֵרִים.
and milk is bringing it into fruition to nurse and nourish others.
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי, אוֹ רָאִיתִי בְּאֵיזֶה חִבּוּר:
And I heard, or read in some treatise:
"תִּירֹשׁ" אוֹתִיּוֹת תִּשְׁרֵי, הוּא מְנוֹבֵב וּמַפְרִיחַ "בְּתֻלוֹת" הוּא אֱלוּל.
'Tirosh' possesses the letters of Tishrei, which causes to flourish 'the virgins'—which is Elul.
וְהַדְּבָרִים מְכֻוָּנִים עִם מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי:
And these words harmonize perfectly with what I have written:
דְּתִשְׁרֵי הוּא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְהַהֲכָנָה שֶׁלּוֹ;
that Tishrei represents exertion through awakening from below and the preparation and feeling of the heart;
אֱלוּל הוּא בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה בְּלֹא הַרְגָּשָׁה.
while Elul is in pure Thought without emotional feeling.
וּלְכָךְ בֶּאֱלוּל גַּם כֵּן תּוֹקְעִין שׁוֹפָר שֶׁהוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
Therefore during Elul we likewise sound the shofar to awaken arousal from below.
אַךְ הַחִלּוּק:
Yet the distinction is:
בְּתִשְׁרֵי הוּא מִצְוַת ה' כִּי "ה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב",
in Tishrei it is a biblical commandment of Hashem, for 'Hashem sees into the heart';
וְאַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לֹא שַׁיָּךְ צִוּוּי דְּשָׁם הוּא בְּיַד ה',
whereas upon thought an explicit commandment does not apply, for thought is in Hashem's hand,
וּפְעֻלַּת הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל צַד הַהֶרְגֵּל לְבַד,
and man's activity therein operates purely through habituation;
וּלְכָךְ תְּקִיעוֹת דְּאָז מִצַּד מִנְהָג.
hence the sounding of the shofar in Elul stems from custom (minhag).
כִּי עִקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בָּא רַק מִצַּד הַהֶרְגֵּל וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁל מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים מְלֻמָּדָה
For the primary sanctity of thought comes solely through habituation and exertion of rote performance,
שֶׁאֵין פּוֹעֵל כְּלוּם בַּלֵּב מוֹעִיל בְּיוֹתֵר לַמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
which, while stirring nothing in the heart, is exceedingly advantageous for the mind.
דְּמֵהַרְגָּשָׁה שֶׁבַּלֵּב בָּא לְהִתְלַהֲבוּת עַד שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלוּם,
For emotional feeling in the heart leads to burning excitation until one cannot function,
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׂכֶל בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה אֵין מִתְלַהֵב,
whereas through rational recognition in thought one does not burn with excitement,
וְהוּא פּוֹעֵל כָּרָאוּי בְּיִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת,
and acts properly with calm composure;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מִנְהָג וְהֶרְגֵּל,
only that it proceeds by way of habit and custom,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ בַּלֵּב
since he lacks emotional feeling in the heart,
שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא עֲשִׂיַּת הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which is the true locus of performing Hashem's commandments,

כְּטַעַם (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה, ב)651 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 8): The theme of this month [Adar] is that even in sleep Israel are holy, since they are bound at their root to the Blessed One — as the Midrash says, "I am asleep from the commandments ... but my heart is awake to perform them ... where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel? 'God is the rock of my heart.'" From the side of the Blessed One, "the voice of my beloved knocks, open for me": "my heart is awake" means that the Blessed One, the heart of Israel, rouses Israel from their sleep to perform the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): The Congregation of Israel boasts, "I am asleep but my heart is awake," which the Sages expounded as referring to the Holy One, blessed be He — "rock of my heart." Even when they are asleep from the commandments and have no "eyes," as in sleep when the eyes are shut and the heart is sunk in imaginings, since the root of the soul is a portion of God and the depths of the heart cleave to the Blessed One, all the imaginings too cleave to Him; even at the height of immersion in the imaginings of this world, which hide the truth, there remains in him a power of awakening to the Blessed One through the heart's cleaving to the living God. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 68): All the service of the body's limbs, and the commandments performed with them, serve only to set the heart straight; the essential thing is the heart, the dwelling place of the Blessed One, as the Sages said, "the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it says, 'rock of my heart.'" Therefore these [outward acts] are not to be a person's goal in themselves, but only things that lead to the goal, as the Zohar calls the 613 commandments "613 counsels.": הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
mirroring (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): Hashem, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel.
וְלָכֵן הַצֵּרוּף שֶׁל אֱלוּל הוּא סוֹפֵי תֵּבוֹת שֶׁל "וּצְדָקָה תִּהְיֶה לָּנוּ כִּי" (דְּבָרִים ו, כה),
Therefore the divine permutation of Elul forms the acronym of the final letters of 'u-tz'dakah tihyeh lanu ki' (Deuteronomy 6:25),
וְהַיְנוּ מְקַבְּלִים קוֹדֶם לַמַּשְׁפִּיעִים וּבֵן קוֹדֵם לָאָב,
representing recipients preceding benefactors, and the son preceding the father;
דְּהַתַּכְלִית לְעוֹלָם הוּא בַּסּוֹף,
for the ultimate objective is always realized at the end,
וּבֶאֱלוּל הַתַּכְלִית הוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהוּא הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלּוֹ.
and in Elul the ultimate objective is Thought, which stands as its final deed.
וּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בַּפֹּעַל שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהֶרְגֵּל שֶׁלֹּא בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה,
And its initial thought is physical action done through habit without conscious intent,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה:
which represents the unfathomable depth of the primordial thought:
מַה שֶּׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קְצָת כְּמִתְעַסֵּק בְּלֹא הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת מַחֲשָׁבָה גְּמוּרָה.
that which a person performs almost casually without full conscious contemplation.

items.h:
Seif 2 — The Tribes, Months, and Diagonal Boundaries
The twelve tribes and months express differentiated channels through which intellect, heart, and action reach practical fruition.

p: וְסִדְרָן שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים נֶגֶד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים,
And regarding the order of the twelve tribes corresponding to the twelve months,
יֵשׁ כַּמָּה דֵּעוֹת בִּמְפָרְשֵׁי סֵפֶר יְצִירָה,
there are several opinions among the commentators of Sefer Yetzirah,
וַאֲנִי קִבַּלְתִּי סִדְרָן:
and I received their order as follows:
לֵוִי, יוֹסֵף, יְהוּדָה, רְאוּבֵן, שִׁמְעוֹן, זְבוּלֻן, יִשָּׂשכָר, בִּנְיָמִין, אָשֵׁר, דָּן, גָּד, נַפְתָּלִי.
Levi, Joseph, Judah, Reuben, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Benjamin, Asher, Dan, Gad, Naphtali. –
וְעוֹד שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה כִּי הֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר גְּבוּלֵי אֲלַכְסוֹן,
And I further heard concerning that which is written in Sefer Yetzirah, that they are the twelve diagonal boundaries,
וְהַיְנוּ בְּשִׁשָּׁה עֲמָקִים הַמְּנוּיִים בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
meaning that within the six cosmic depths enumerated in Sefer Yetzirah
יֵשׁ שְׁתֵּי נְקֻדּוֹת אֲלַכְסוֹנִיּוֹת שֶׁבִּשְׁתֵּי קְצָווֹת הַנּוֹכְחִיּוֹת שֶׁהֵם זֶה נֶגֶד זֶה,
there are two diagonal points at the two opposing poles that stand face to face;
וְכָךְ בַּשְּׁבָטִים הֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֲלוּקִים לְשִׁשָּׁה,
and likewise the twelve tribes are divided into six pairs,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ אַחֵר שֶׁהוּא אֲלַכְסוֹנִי לוֹ,
where each one has a counterpart that is diagonal to it,
דְּהַיְנוּ מִתְנַגֵּד נֶגְדּוֹ וּמַמָּשׁ עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
meaning opposing it and literally standing counter to it,
דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ הֵיפֶךְ מִדַּת זֶה.
namely that its character is the exact antithesis of the other's character.
וְסִדְרָן: בְּעֹמֶק רוֹם – יְהוּדָה וְיִשָּׂשכָר,
And their configuration is: in the Depth of Height—Judah and Issachar,
שֶׁנֶּגְדָּן בָּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַפְּשׁוּטוֹת לָמֶ"ד, זַיִ"ן;
corresponding to them among the simple letters being Lamed and Zayin;
וּבְעֹמֶק תַּחַת – בִּנְיָמִין וּרְאוּבֵן, שֶׁהֵם נוּ"ן, חֵי"ת;
and in the Depth of Below—Benjamin and Reuben, who are Nun and Chet;
וּבְעֹמֶק מַעֲרָב – אָשֵׁר וְיוֹסֵף, שֶׁהֵם סָמֶ"ךְ, וָא"ו;
and in the Depth of West—Asher and Joseph, who are Samekh and Vav;
וּבְעֹמֶק מִזְרָח – לֵוִי וְדָן, שֶׁהֵם עַיִ"ן, הֵ"א;
and in the Depth of East—Levi and Dan, who are Ayin and Hei;
וּבְעֹמֶק דָּרוֹם – גָּד וּזְבוּלֻן, שֶׁהֵם צָדִ"י, יוּ"ד;
and in the Depth of South—Gad and Zebulun, who are Tzadi and Yud;
וּבְעֹמֶק צָפוֹן – שִׁמְעוֹן וְנַפְתָּלִי, שֶׁהֵם קוּ"ף, טֵי"ת;
and in the Depth of North—Simeon and Naphtali, who are Kuf and Tet;
וְהֵם חָדְשֵׁי הַקַּיִץ כְּנֶגֶד חָדְשֵׁי הַחֹרֶף].
and these represent the summer months set opposite the winter months.
וּלְפִי זֶה אֱלוּל וְתִשְׁרֵי הֵם נֶגֶד זְבוּלֻן וְיִשָּׂשכָר,
And according to this, Elul and Tishrei correspond to Zebulun and Issachar;

וְלֵיכָּא צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּמוֹרֵי אֶלָּא מִלֵּוִי וְיִשָּׂשכָר (יוֹמָא כו652 Yoma 26a — Rava said: You will not find a young scholar who renders decisions unless he comes from the tribe of Levi or from the tribe of Issachar. Levi — as it is written: "They shall teach Jacob Your ordinances" (Deuteronomy 33:10). Issachar — as it is written: "And of the sons of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel should do" (I Chronicles 12:33). Rashi: "Who renders decisions": who issues halachic rulings in Israel. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 11): Issachar stands in holiness against the shell of Ishmael. Of Issachar it is written, "who had understanding," and the Sages said that no young scholar who renders decisions is found except from the tribe of Issachar: this is engagement in Torah, which is Issachar's portion. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 1): In Yoma: "You will not find a young scholar who renders decisions except from Levi or from Issachar." That is, in every legal ruling there are doubts and sides equally balanced either way, and the Sages said that though these forbid and those permit, "these and those are the words of the living God," all given from one Shepherd; for souls differ, and each Sage ruled according to the level of his soul, as he saw fit for its rectification and healing. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Beha'aloscha): The Gemara says that no young scholar who renders decisions is found except from Levi or Issachar, and that Judah, though "Judah is My lawgiver," is excluded with regard to "bringing the law out in accordance with the halachah." Heaven forbid to say that Judah, from whom the Messiah will come, cannot do so; rather, what is called "according to the halachah" for all the other tribes is not yet so called for Judah (one who denies an entire claim is exempt by legal presumption, but before Judah it is not yet clear that he is exempt, for perhaps he truly owes), and therefore the Messiah from Judah will "smell and judge," sensing the depth of the truth. עַמּוּד א),
and 'there is no Torah scholar who issues halakhic rulings except from Levi and Issachar' (Yoma 26a),
שֶׁהֵם הַיּוֹדְעִים לְהַנְהִיג הָעוֹלָם.
for they are the ones equipped to govern the world.
וְכֵן הֵם חָדְשֵׁי נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי,
And similarly situated are the months of Nisan and Tishrei,
דְּרַק בָּזֶה אוֹ בָּזֶה בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם,
for solely in one or the other of these did the creation of the world occur,
דְּאֵין רָאוּי לְהַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא שְׁנֵי סְדָרִים הַלָּלוּ:
there being no order fitting for governing the world other than these two modalities:
דְּהַיְנוּ אוֹ מִצַּד עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
namely, either from the perspective of Hashem's direct supernal assistance,
וְהֵם בְּנֵי לֵוִי הַנִּלְוִים אֶל ה' בְּמַחֲנֵה שְׁכִינָה;
and these are the children of Levi who attach themselves to Hashem within the camp of the Shechinah;
אוֹ מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת אָדָם,
or from the perspective of human awakening from below,
וְהֵם בְּנֵי יִשָּׂשכָר יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה,
and these are the sons of Issachar who have understanding,
שֶׁהוּא הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב, דִּ"לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב" (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ו, י).
which is the deep perception of the heart, as in 'and understand with their heart, and return' (Isaiah 6:10).
וּשְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים אֵלּוּ הָיוּ מְכִינִים לְמָזוֹן לְכָל הַחֹרֶף וְקַיִץ
And these two months were those that prepared nourishment for the entire winter and summer,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת לה653 Berakhot 35b — Rava said to the Sages: I beg of you, in the days of Nisan and in the days of Tishrei do not appear before me, so that you not be troubled about your sustenance the whole year. Rashi: "In the days of Nisan" — the days of the harvest. "In the days of Tishrei" — the treading of the winepresses and the olive presses. Maharsha: From here there is some support for Rashi's explanation in Bava Kamma 113a, that the court does not appoint a date [for litigants to appear] in the days of Nisan or in the days of Tishrei, since these are the season of reaping and of vintage. Maharal (Derech Chaim 6:4): Rava's words imply that a man may interrupt his Torah study for the sake of his livelihood, whereas the Mishnah "this is the way of Torah: bread with salt shall you eat" implies that even if he has nothing but bread he should not neglect the Torah — and the Gemara in Taanit (21a) likewise implies that one may not neglect the Torah for the life of the hour. One must therefore distinguish: where the interruption has a fixed limit, such as a month or two, he should interrupt his study; but where it has no limit, he certainly may not. עַמּוּד ב),
as written in Berakhot (35b),
וּמִסְּתָמָא כֵּן לִמְזוֹן הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
and presumably the same applies to the spiritual sustenance of the soul,
כִּי הַנְהָגַת כָּל הַשָּׁנָה מְקַבְּלִים מִשְּׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים אֵלּוּ.
for the spiritual guidance of the entire year is received from these two months.

וּ"זְבוּלֻן בְּצֵאתְךָ" מַסְפִּיק לְיִשָּׂשכָר654 Bereshit Rabbah 72:5 — Yissachar was ninth among the tribes, yet he brought his offering second to the king. This is what is written: “On the second day Netanel son of Tzuar, prince of Yissachar, brought.” Why? Because he was a man of Torah. And from where did all this praise come to him? From Zevulun, who engaged in commerce and fed Yissachar, who was a man of Torah — as it is written, “Zevulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas.” And when Moshe came to bless the tribes, he gave the blessing of Zevulun precedence over the blessing of Yissachar: “Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar in your tents.” Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Afterwards the light of Zevulun is revealed, in the sense of "in the shade of wisdom, in the shade of money"; nevertheless [Moses] put "Zevulun, in your going out" before "Yissachar, in your tents," for this is a greater level: that even when he goes out into the affairs of this world, his heart should cleave to the living God and King of the world.,
And 'Zebulun, in your going out' provides material support for Issachar,
"וּבְצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יב),
and 'in the shadow of wisdom is the shadow of silver' (Ecclesiastes 7:12);
כֵּן הוּא אֱלוּל לְתִשְׁרֵי,
just so is the relationship of Elul to Tishrei:
שֶׁהַהַרְגָּשָׁה בְּתִשְׁרֵי בַּלֵּב הוּא כְּפִי הַהֲכָנָה בֶּאֱלוּל בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ וְשֵׂכֶל,
for the emotional feeling in the heart during Tishrei corresponds to the preparation in Elul within thought in the brain and intellect,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק רְכוּשׁ הַצָּרִיךְ לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לֵב,
which is merely the requisite spiritual capital needed by one with an engaged heart,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּהַרְחָבַת הַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי הַרְחֵב דַּעַת הַשֵּׂכֶל,
so that he may contemplate with expansive heart through the broad consciousness of the intellect;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְנוֹבֵב וּמַפְרִיחַ הַשֵּׂכֶל כַּאֲשֶׁר מַרְגִּישׁ בַּלֵּב,
and through this, the intellect flourishes and blossoms when felt within the heart,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לְהוֹלָדָה לַפֹּעַל שֶׁזֶּהוּ הוֹצָאַת פֶּרַח.
as is known that through this it arrives at practical fruition, which is the bringing forth of a blossom.

sections.en: The Complete Stature of Israel in Every Generation

items.h: Each generation forms one spiritual body rooted in Jacob; true self-sacrifice comes through surrendering individual prominence to divine kingship and collective unity.

Seif 1 — One Spiritual Body in Every Generation
Israel forms a complete collective stature, and self-sacrifice means surrendering individual prominence before divine kingship.

p: בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר יֵשׁ קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה מִדְּמוּת אָדָם הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא,
In every single generation there exists a complete stature reflecting the likeness of Adam seated upon the Throne,
שֶׁהוּא דְּמוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
which is the image of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, engraved upon the Throne of Glory,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית ה655 Taanit 5b — R. Yochanan said: Yaakov our father did not die. He said to him: Was it then for nothing that they eulogized him and embalmed him and buried him? He said to him: I expound a verse — “And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov, says the Lord, and be not dismayed, O Israel, for behold I save you from afar and your seed from the land of their captivity.” Scripture likens him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive. Rashi: "Did not die": rather, he lives forever. "For nothing": was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized and the embalmers embalmed, as it is written of him, "and they embalmed … and they eulogized" (Genesis 50)? "Just as his seed is alive": when He gathers Israel from the land of their captivity, it is the living He gathers, for they are in captivity, and the dead are not in captivity; "so too is he alive": for He will bring him into the exile so as to redeem his children before his eyes, as we find in Egypt — "And Israel saw" (Exodus 14:31), expounded as Israel the Elder; and as for the embalming, it seemed to them that he had died, but he was alive. Tosafos (s.v. "Yaakov our father did not die"): So too it is implied by Scripture, for it is written of him "and he expired" and not "and he died," as is explained in Sotah (13a) in connection with the episode of Chushim. Maharsha: [The questioner] did not object from Scripture's mention of his death, for death is not stated of him, only "and he expired," as Tosafot write; and Rashi's explanation, that it only seemed to the embalmers that he had died, is forced, the crux of the answer being missing from the text. I have heard it explained that "Yaakov did not die" can mean either that he did not die even in body, or that he did not die in soul, like other righteous men, though in body he died: the questioner took it in the first sense and objected from the eulogies and the embalming, and the answer is that it was meant of the soul — and Yaakov is singled out because only he can be likened to his seed, unlike Avraham and Yitzchak, whose seed included Yishmael and Esav. Alternatively: the dead outside the Land do not live [as those within it], for the Land of Israel is called "the land of the living," so Avraham and Yitzchak, who died in the Land, are alive even in death, while one might argue that Yaakov, who died abroad, is not; hence he taught that Yaakov too is alive, as though he had died in the Land, deriving it from "I save you from afar" — that is, from Egypt, alive, as though he had died in the Land. Maharal (Derech Chaim 5:4): One might ask: Yaakov's good, which signifies the end of Israel, ought to have been very great, yet at the end Yaakov's good was but slight, unlike the destiny of Israel, which is to be eternal. For this reason they said, "Yaakov our father did not die": he abides in an eternal good that will never be removed, signifying that the good of Israel will be eternal. And since the World to Come will be wholly spiritual, this is what the Sages' saying that Yaakov did not die signifies — for without doubt Yaakov's life now is spiritual, not like this life, which is natural. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 50): Whatever ceases has an end; but where there are three, the middle one between them has no end at all, and what has no end does not cease. So it is with what they said in Taanit, "Yaakov our father did not die": this is because he was the third of the patriarchs, and the third is not bounded by an end; therefore he is alive and did not receive an end. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 3): The tribes are the whole of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in whom the very essence of Yaakov's soul spreads forth; to this they alluded with "just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive" — that is, the totality of the souls of Israel in each generation is itself the stature of Yaakov's soul as it spreads forth in that generation. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Motzei Yom Kippur 4): The abiding of the Torah of truth in the heart was realized chiefly in Yaakov, because he was the root of the life of holiness, as the Sages said, "Yaakov our father did not die"; through this one can be purified even from the impurity of the dead, cleaving to the root of the life of holiness and entering the camp of the Shechinah. Even though this is not perceptible in this world, Yaakov's own aspect is not perceptible in this world either, as the Gemara says, "Was it for nothing that they embalmed him?" until he answered, "I expound a verse … just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): Yaakov our father is the complete man who was in this world, whose bed was whole and who did not die, for "just as his seed is alive…," as they said: that is, the stature of the Congregation of Israel, the seed of Yaakov our father, in each and every generation is itself the stature of Yaakov our father, only particularized and divided into many individual souls. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Anthology, Isaiah 26; from Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 3): Every one of the seed of Israel will be shown, at the resurrection of the dead, not to have died but to have been as one asleep, as the Gemara expounds, "He likens him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive." And there is no half-analogy: as He likens Yaakov to his seed, so He likens his seed to him, so that all the seed of Yaakov will be clarified at the level of "Yaakov did not die," and when one awakens from his sleep he will remember all the words of Torah. עַמּוּד ב): "מַה זַּרְעוֹ בַּחַיִּים אַף הוּא בַּחַיִּים".
concerning which our Sages of blessed memory taught (Ta'anit 5b): 'Just as his seed is alive, so too is he alive.'
פֵּרוּשׁ: שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ עַצְמוּת נַפְשׁוֹ מִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל דּוֹר בְּחַיֵּי גוּפָנִים מַמָּשׁ,
The meaning: the very essence of his soul expands in each generation within literal physical bodily life,
כִּי זַרְעוֹ הֵם נִמְשָׁכִים מִטִּפֵּי מוֹחוֹ וְחֵלֶק מֵחַיּוּתוֹ,
for his descendants are drawn from the mental drops of his brain and a portion of his vitality,
וְכָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ בָּהֶם חֵלֶק מֵעַצְמִיּוּת חַיּוּתוֹ.
and within all the seed of Jacob there is an inherent share of his essential vitality.

וְהַגַּם דִּכְשֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם הֵם מַתִּישִׁין כֹּחַ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כִּבְיָכוֹל (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה פֶּרֶק א פָּסוּק ו656 Eikhah Rabbah 1:33 — "And they went without strength before the pursuer." R. Azariah said in the name of R. Yehuda son of R. Simon: When Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, they add strength to the might above, as it says, "Through God we shall do valiantly"; and when Israel do not do the will of the Omnipresent, they, as it were, weaken the great power above, as it is written, "You weakened the Rock that bore you." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on completing the Talmud 5): A deficiency can touch the mind only through its link below to the heart, when it turns downward and not to its cause, for the arousal from below begets the arousal from above, and likewise the desire in the heart begets the thought in the mind; and this is [the meaning of] "You weakened the Rock that bore you," that they weaken the power of the heavenly household. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): By all opinions, addition of strength and weakening of strength certainly apply to the angels as well, as the Sages said on the verse "You weakened the Rock that bore you" that they weaken the power of the heavenly household, and on "Ascribe strength to God" that they add strength to the heavenly household. So Abraham our father, through his meal and the commandment of hospitality, added strength to the heavenly household and "sustained their hearts." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 2): All the supernal forces of holiness depend on man, as it is said on "You weakened the Rock that bore you" that they weaken the power of the heavenly household, and at the Destruction the wings of the Chayos and the heavenly household were diminished: for they too are part of the whole creation, which is all for the sake of man, the likeness upon the Throne who rides upon all of creation.),
And even though when Israel fails to do the will of the Omnipresent they enfeeble the supernal power above, as it were (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 1:6),
הַיְנוּ שֶׁצוּרַת אָדָם זֶה כִּבְיָכוֹל הוּא תַּשׁ כֹּחַ,
meaning that this Form of Adam becomes, as it were, diminished in strength;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְעוֹלָם הוּא צוּרַת אָדָם שְׁלֵמָה, רַק הַחִלּוּק בְּעִנְיַן כֹּחַ.
nonetheless, it remains eternally an intact, complete Form of Adam, the only variation lying in its manifest strength.
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ צוּרַת אָדָם הוּא מִצַּד שֹׁרֶשׁ עֹמֶק הַלֵּב דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And that is because the root of this Form of Adam stems from the essential depth of the heart of Israel
שֶׁהוּא דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲפִלּוּ בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which clings to Hashem, blessed be He, even among the transgressors of Israel,

וּכְטַעַם (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה, ב657 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:1 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. R.
