And through conscious remembrance, man actively effects the attainment of this light within the heart.
וְזֶה כָּל עִקַּר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת –
And thus man's entire primary exertion regarding the sanctity of Shabbat –
הוּא רַק בַּזְּכִירָה.
is confined solely to remembrance.
וְזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה הוּא עֲמָלֵק,
And corresponding opposite to this stands Amalek,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
who is designated the "first among nations,"
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּמָא בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
embodying the root of evil that is fixed and enduring without effort,

כְּטַעַם (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:)708 Kiddushin 30b — The Sages taught: "And you shall place [vesamtem] these words of Mine upon your heart" — read it as sam tam, a perfect remedy; the Torah is likened to an elixir of life. A parable: a man struck his son a great blow and laid a bandage upon the wound, and said to him, My son, so long as this bandage is on your wound, eat what you please and drink what you please and bathe as you please, and have no fear; but if you remove it, the wound will fester. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created the Torah as its antidote; if you occupy yourselves with Torah you will not be delivered into its hand. Rashi (s.v. "a perfect remedy"): "A perfect remedy" means a complete one, lacking nothing needed for the cure. "What you please" — whatever your mind is drawn to, even honey and every kind of sweet thing, which are bad for a wound. Maharsha: In a homiletic vein the baraita speaks of an elixir of life in place of sam tam, for the opposite of tam, "whole", is met, "dead" — that the drug upon his wound would otherwise be a deadly one, since the evil inclination is the angel of death. In the analogue: so long as you occupy yourselves with Torah, which is the bandage over the wound that is the evil inclination, you may take pleasure in this world and will not come to sin, for the Torah shields a man as the bandage shields the wound from festering; but to leave off Torah is to remove the bandage, and then it is impossible not to come to sin, as in "an ignoramus cannot be pious" — he does not know wherein he will stumble. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kiddushin 30b): The Torah is likened to an elixir of life and prevails over the inclination because nothing of privation pertains to the Torah: the intellect is complete in actuality, and the Torah above all is a rank over which privation has no dominion. Therefore the Torah does not let the evil inclination gain the upper hand, for the evil inclination is privation, and privation cleaves to matter; once a man follows the intellect of the Torah, the evil inclination that is the privation cleaving to matter does not overcome him, and in this sense the Torah is the antidote to the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:19): As the Midrash HaNe'lam says, even in the future the evil inclination will not be nullified, for without it there would be no delight in Torah; and on this they said, "I created the evil inclination, I created Torah as its spice", literally like a spice that seasons a food until it becomes "very good", as the Sages said of "very good": this is the evil inclination. For one places all his longing and desire and the natural passion of his body into desire for words of Torah, in which there is truly great desire to know the depth of its wisdom; and then the evil inclination becomes a good inclination, "inclination" meaning desire in one's mind and heart. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): Prayer, "the service of the heart", requires toil to direct one's heart, like a servant before the king; whereas Torah, like a minister, requires no toil to direct the heart, for through delving deeply into words of Torah the heart straightens of itself, in the sense of "I created Torah as its spice", since mind and heart are inseparable companions, and through the wisdom in the heart the heart too is aroused. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 9): The creation of evil is not written explicitly in the account of creation because in truth the Holy One, blessed be He, created nothing evil in the world: even the evil inclination was not created for evil, as it says, "I created the evil inclination, I created Torah as a spice against it"; it is only you who make it evil. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 97): The rectification of mazal is occupation with Torah, as it says, "I created the evil inclination, I created Torah as its spice." A spice is to sweeten the food, that is, to turn the evil into "very good", as the Sages said that ["very good"] is the evil inclination, which is sweetened through words of Torah.: "בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע",
in line with the teaching (Kiddushin 30b): "I created the evil inclination,"
וְיָצָא לַפּוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי עֲמָלֵק.
and it was actualized into historical reality through Amalek.
כִּי הָאָבוֹת, שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ "אֲבָהָן דְּעָלְמָא",
For the Patriarchs, who are termed the "Fathers of the World,"
שֶׁמּוֹלִידִים הָעוֹלָם בִּשְׁלֵמוּת,
who birth the world into spiritual completion,
כָּל אֶחָד הִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּתִקּוּנוֹ בְּדָבָר מְיֻחָד.
each labored in his personal rectification in a unique dimension.
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר יֵשׁ לוֹ רֹאשׁ, תּוֹךְ, וְסוֹף,
For every complete entity has a beginning, a middle, and an end,
וְהַתּוֹךְ הוּא הַמְּכֻוָּן מֵהַדָּבָר וְהָעִקָּר,
and the middle is the intended core purpose and the primary essence,
וְהַסּוֹף נִקְרָא מַה שֶּׁמַּגְבִּילוֹ וּמַבְדִּילוֹ מֵהַזּוּלַת.
and the end is designated as that which bounds it and demarcates it from the outside.
וְהַהַתְחָלָה נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַפּוֹעֵל בִּתְחִלַּת הַפְּעֻלָּה,
And the beginning is defined by the initiator at the inception of the action;
דְּאַחַר הַפְּעֻלָּה, הֲרֵי שְׁנֵי הַקְּצָווֹת שָׁוִים לִהְיוֹת נִקְרָאִים סוֹף וְקָצֶה,
for after the act is finished, both polar extremes appear equally as an outer boundary,
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד פְּעֻלַּת הַפּוֹעֵל נִכָּר רֹאשׁ וְסוֹף,
yet from the perspective of the initiator, beginning and end are distinct:
וְהָרֹאשׁ הוּא הַמַּגִּיד פְּעֻלַּת הַפּוֹעֵל,
the beginning announces the initiator's purpose,
וְהַסּוֹף הוּא הַמַּבְדִּיל וּמְבָרֵר זֶה מֵאַחֵר.
and the end separates and clarifies this entity from another.
וְהֵן הֵם בִּנְיַן תְּלָת אֲבָהָן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And these form the edifice of the three Patriarchs in the completion of this world:
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן הַמַּכְרִיז וּמְפַרְסֵם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם,
and Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was the first to proclaim and publicize Hashem's divinity across the world—
שֶׁהוּא הַבּוֹרֵא וְשֶׁאֵין בִּירָה בְּלֹא מַנְהִיג,
that He is the Creator and that no palace exists without a master,
וּמְבָרֵר הַהַתְחָלָה.
thus clarifying the true Beginning.
וְכֵן הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
So too is the beginning of the Torah: "I am Hashem your God, etc.,"
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהוּא הַרְחָקַת הָרָע,
for it is impossible to arrive at "You shall have no other gods, etc."—the rejection of evil—
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" הַקּוֹדֶמֶת.
except through the prior recognition of "I am, etc."
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה בְּפִרְסוּם זֶה דְּ"אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
And Abraham's entire spiritual exertion was dedicated to making this "I am" universally known,
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְ"קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה",
and it is the spiritual root of positive action ("arise and do"),
דְּהַיְנוּ לְהַכְנִיס כָּל תַּאֲווֹת וַחֲמָדוֹת הַקְּבוּעִים בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּוֹ.
which means subordinating all natural human desires and yearnings exclusively unto Hashem alone.
וְהָאַהֲבָה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה,
And love is the root of positive commandments,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב709 Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:5 — Act out of love and act out of fear. Act out of love — for if you come to hate, know that you are one who loves, and one who loves does not hate. Act out of fear — for if you come to kick, know that you are one who fears, and one who fears does not kick. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "Act out of love and act out of fear"): Even though you do a thing out of love of God, set the fear of His exaltedness before your face as well; or else: act out of love in the positive commandments, and act out of fear, that you take care to keep away from what is forbidden. "If you come to hate" — to hate the Torah and the commandment and cast it behind your back. "If you come to kick" — to transgress a prohibition. (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ט, הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת סוֹטָה כב:):
as it is written (Yerushalmi Berakhot 9, cited in Tosafot Sotah 22b):
"דַּע שֶׁאַתָּה אוֹהֵב וְכוּלֵי שֶׁאַתָּה יָרֵא וְכוּלֵי",
"Know that you love, etc., that you fear, etc.,"
שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
for fear is the root of negative commandments,
דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ,
corresponding to the spiritual rung of Isaac—the mighty warrior who subdues his inclination,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
for this was the central essence of his exertion:
לְבָרֵר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
to clarify "You shall have no other gods, etc.,"
כָּל מִינֵי פְּסֹלֶת וּבֵרוּרֵי הָרָע מִן הַטּוֹב,
sifting out all manner of dross and purging evil from good,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ גְּבוּל הַקִּיצוֹן מִן הָעוֹלָם הַמַּבְדִּילוֹ מִן הַזּוּלַת.
which is the outer boundary separating holiness from the outside world.
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק לְמִי שֶׁהוֹרָתוֹ וְלֵדָתוֹ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה,
And this is accessible only to one whose conception and birth occurred in holiness,
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" כְּבָר קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם בְּלִבּוֹ יָתֵד שֶׁלֹּא תִמּוֹט.
and within whose heart the foundation of "I am" is already firmly anchored like an immovable peg.
וְעִם כָּל זֶה, צָרִיךְ אַחַר כָּךְ לְאַזְהָרַת "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
Even so, the subsequent warning of "You shall have no other gods, etc." remains necessary;
שֶׁאַף מִי שֶׁהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן, מַאֲמִין בֶּן מַאֲמִין,
for even one who is Jewish from birth, a believer descending from believers,
עִם כָּל זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לָרָע לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בּוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כָּל כָּךְ,
evil can still overwhelm him, Heaven forbid, to such a degree

עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לוֹ: "לֵךְ עֲבֹד וְכוּלֵי710 Niddah 13b — R. Ami said: Such a man is called a transgressor, for this is the craft of the evil inclination — today it says to him do this, and tomorrow it says to him do that, until at last it says to him go and worship idols; and he goes and worships. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “for this is the craft of the evil inclination”): This accords with what is said in the chapter “HeChalil”: at first the evil inclination is like a thread, and at the end it is like a cart rope, as it is stated: “Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with a cart rope” — that is, those who draw and drag the evil inclination upon themselves deliberately. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaPerishus 3): One who brings the evil inclination upon himself is wholly evil; had the inclination merely ruled over him without his having incited it, he would not be reckoned wholly evil. And according to the reading that he is called an apostate — an apostate is one who cleaves to idolatry, and the evil inclination itself is reckoned as idolatry; therefore one who incites the inclination against himself is called an apostate, for in the end it brings him to cleave to idolatry entirely.",
that it will tell him: "Go serve idols, etc.",
וְעַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לְנַתֵּק שָׁרְשׁוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן,
to the point that he might sever his spiritual root, Heaven forbid, as well,

כְּעִנְיַן עֵשָׂו דְּנִקְרָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (יח.)711 Kiddushin 18a — Rav Chiya bar Avin said that R. Yochanan said: By Torah law a gentile inherits from his father, as it is written, "For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance" (Deuteronomy 2:5). But perhaps an apostate Jew is different? Rather, [derive it] from here: "For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance" (Deuteronomy 2:9). Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Isaac taught Torah only to his sons, and even among them there was one who was unworthy, except that he is called an "apostate Israelite" in Kiddushin, for he had a root of Jewishness from birth — his head is buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Isaac's bosom — and therefore he too had some hold on words of Torah; yet in the end he too was waste. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 4): [Isaac, the first to be circumcised at eight days, was the one in whom holiness began to take root in all his offspring;] and his wish to draw Esau near was because Esau had free choice, being called an "apostate Israelite," so that the matter stood in the balance whether he could enter into the holiness of Israel. "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר",
as occurred with Esau, who is termed in Kiddushin (18a) an "apostate Jew,"
וְעִם כָּל זֶה נַעֲשָׂה לְאֻמָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
and yet nevertheless became a separate, estranged nation.
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בָּזֶה,
And Isaac's entire spiritual striving was directed toward this:
לְהוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה,
to father Jacob, whose bed is spiritually whole,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְנַתֵּק שָׁרְשׁוֹ כְּלָל בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן,
such that it would be impossible for him to sever his root in any manner whatsoever,

דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא, יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד712 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious..).
for "even though he has sinned, he remains Israel" (Sanhedrin 44a).
וּבֵרוּר הַפְּסֹלֶת שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם הָיָה עַל יְדֵי לוֹט בְּעַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב וְעַל יְדֵי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
And the expelling of dross through Abraham occurred via Lot in Ammon and Moab and through Ishmael,
שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁהֵם הַמַּשְׁכִּיחִים הַכָּרַת אֱלֹהוּת.
who are the root of base desires that cause man to forget divine awareness.
וְהֵם נִפְרְדוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
And they were separated from him,
וְנִשְׁאַר הוּא לְבַדּוֹ לֵאלֹהֵינוּ,
leaving Abraham alone consecrated unto our God,
שֶׁכָּל צֶאֱצָאָיו יֵשׁ בָּהֶם הַכָּרָה זוֹ קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּמָא,
such that all of his true descendants possess this awareness permanently fixed and enduring,
כִּי כְּבָר שׁוֹרֶשׁ זוֹ תָּקוּעַ בְּלִבָּם מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
because this root was firmly embedded within their hearts from Abraham, peace be upon him,
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת מִזֶּה בְּלֵדָה.
for it is impossible for them to change from this at birth.
וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים
And this was Abraham's central ambition, having been the first of converts,
וְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהוֹצִיא שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם,
and he labored to bring forth the name of Israel into the world,
רָצָה לוֹמַר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נוֹצָר בְּרִיָּה שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ מִתְּחִלַּת יְצִירָתוֹ הוּא כָּךְ,
meaning: that there be formed a created being whose root is naturally holy from its first inception,
לֹא שֶׁמִּתְגַּיֵּר אַחַר כָּךְ.
rather than one who converts afterward.
וְזֶהוּ יִצְחָק שֶׁנִּמּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה;
And this was Isaac, who was circumcised on the eighth day;
וְגַם עֵשָׂו מִצַּד תְּחִלַּת לֵדָתוֹ שֶׁהָיָה זֶרַע יִצְחָק נִקְרָא "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר",
and even Esau, from the perspective of his birth as Isaac's seed, was called an "apostate Jew,"
אַךְ עֲדַיִן הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת אַחַר הַלֵּדָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עֵשָׂו.
yet it was still possible for him to degenerate after birth, as indeed occurred with Esau.
וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יִצְחָק בְּהַרְחָקַת כָּל מִינֵי רָע,
And this was Isaac's entire struggle in banishing all manner of evil,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת.
until degeneration would no longer be possible.
וְהוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁרַק בּוֹ נִקְרָא לוֹ זָרַע,
And he fathered Jacob, through whom alone his lineage is called,
כִּי הוּא הָיָה כֵּן עָנָף הַדּוֹמֶה לַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
for he was truly a branch that mirrored the root,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עֵשָׂו הוּא זְמוֹרַת זָר שֶׁיָּצָא מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּהַרְחָקַת הָרָע.
whereas Esau was an alien offshoot produced through the exertion of repelling evil.
כִּי גַּם עֵשָׂו מַרְחִיק הָרָע, דְּפוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו כַּחֲזִיר,
For even Esau pretended to repel evil, showing off his split hooves like a swine,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה713 Vayikra Rabbah 13:5 — Why is the kingdom of Edom likened to a pig? Because when the pig lies down it stretches out its hooves as if to say, See, I am pure. So too the kingdom of Edom boasts and robs and plunders, while it appears to be setting up a judgment seat. (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יג):
as our Sages of blessed memory noted (Vayikra Rabbah 13):
שֶׁמַּצִּיעַ הַבִּימָה וְדָן נוֹאֲפִים וְגַנָּבִים וּמְכַשְּׁפִים,
setting up public tribunals to judge adulterers, thieves, and sorcerers,
וְהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ עָשָׂה בַּלַּיְלָה הַכֹּל.
while committing all those very crimes himself at night.
דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁרַק בְּעֵינֵי הַבְּרִיּוֹת רוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּחֲזִיקוּהוּ לְטוֹב.
Meaning that he only sought to be regarded as righteous in the eyes of society.
דְּיֵשׁ רַע לַשָּׁמַיִם, וְרַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת, וְרַע לְעַצְמוֹ,
For there exists evil toward Heaven, evil toward fellow men, and evil toward oneself,

וְהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין אָדָם נִצּוֹל בְּכָל יוֹם (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד714 Bava Batra 164b — Rav Amram said in the name of Rav: There are three transgressions from which a person is not spared on any day: sinful thought, deliberation in prayer, and malicious speech. Rashbam: Deliberation in prayer: some explain that after a man has prayed he reckons in his heart that the Holy One, blessed be He, will now pay him his reward, supply his needs and hear his prayer, because he prayed with concentration. Tosafos (s.v. "deliberation in prayer"): One might explain that the fault is looking for one's prayer to be answered, as in Berakhot, where such deliberation brings a man to heartache and is listed among the things that call his sins to mind — which would match sinful thought and malicious speech, neither of them a mitzvah. Tosafot rejects this: many people never look for their prayer to be answered, since they do not concentrate that much, so why should no man escape it on any day? Rather the transgression is the want of deliberation — failing to pray with concentration — and from this no man is spared on any day, for nobody is able to concentrate properly in his prayer. Maharsha: If no man can escape these three, in what sense are they transgressions at all, and why does Rav say "no man [adam]"? Man is called adam after ash, blood and bile: because he is moulded of dust and ash he cannot fix his mind in prayer; because he has blood, its heat brings him to sinful thought; and because he has bile, he comes to malicious speech and evil traits. But one who so conducts himself as to resemble an angel of the Lord can indeed be saved from all three — and it is for that reason that they are properly called transgressions.:):
and these parallel the three things from which no man escapes daily (Bava Batra 164b):
הִרְהוּר עֲבֵרָה הוּא רַע לְעַצְמוֹ,
sinful thoughts are harmful to oneself,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כט715 Yoma 29a — Thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression itself; and your mnemonic is the odor of roasting meat. Rashi: "Thoughts of transgression": desire for women is harder, in wasting a man's flesh, than the act itself. "The odor of meat": one who smells roasting meat finds its odor very hard to bear, for he craves it. Maharsha: Besides Rashi's explanation, that the thought of transgression is harder on a man's body than the act itself, since he does not satisfy his desire, it may be explained from what is said in Horayos and Nazir of Lot and his two daughters: they intended [the act] for the sake of a mitzvah, "the righteous walk in them," while Lot intended it for the sake of transgression, "but transgressors stumble in them"; and even a thought with no transgression, as when one intended to take up pork and lamb came into his hand, requires forgiveness and atonement. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaPerishus 2): Rashi's explanation is difficult, for then it should have said "thoughts of a woman"; rather, there is no transgression of unchastity without the thought of it, and although the transgression comes from both together, the thought within it is harsher than the physical act, so that thought alone, even without the deed, is also a grave sin. Or it may be taken literally: not as regards liability to death or lashes, which attach to the act itself, but as regards cleaving to abomination and unchastity, thoughts of transgression are harsher, for the force of thought is very strong, like the odor of meat, since it comes through the mind, which is of the intellect, whereas the deed is a material act. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 4): In the brain, the seat of wisdom, there is no room for evil at all, as "the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to the deed"; not so "thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression," for musing [hirhur] is in the heart, while thought [machshavah] is in the brain. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 19): In thought there is no "transgression for the sake of Heaven" — "It is a time to act for the Lord" is written only of deed — and therefore they said "thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression": in this world, so long as the evil inclination from which the evil thought comes is present, such thoughts cannot be rectified by being turned into merits and holiness. Only one who reaches the level at which it is revealed to him that the inclination itself is from the Blessed One, which nullifies it entirely, has even his evil thoughts turned to good; until then the remedy is to remain "poor and destitute" and not to slake the thirst of his desires at all..): "הִרְהוּרֵי עֲבֵרָה קָשִׁין מֵעֲבֵרָה", פֵּרֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: לְהַכְחִישׁ הַגּוּף;
as stated (Yoma 29a): "Sinful thoughts drain the body more than the sin itself";
וְכֵן כָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת הוּא רַע לְעַצְמוֹ,
and similarly all physical lusts harm oneself,

"מְלָא כְּרֵיסֵיהּ זָנֵי בִּישֵׁי" (בְּרָכוֹת לב716 Berakhot 32a — Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Sheshet: This is what people say — a full belly breeds evil, as it is stated: “According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled and their heart was lifted up; therefore have they forgotten Me” (Hosea 13:6). Rav Nachman said: From here — “and your heart be lifted up, and you forget the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 8:14). And the Rabbis say: From here — “and he shall eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and turn to other gods” (Deuteronomy 31:20). Rashi: "A full belly breeds evil" — the filling of the belly is one of the kinds of evil sins; "zanei" [kinds], for the Aramaic rendering of "after its kind" is "lizanohi." Maharsha: He brings all these verses to correspond to the three parables he had just cited. "According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled and their heart was lifted up," and "and your heart be lifted up and you forget the Lord your God," correspond to the lion, who does not roar over a basket of straw but over a basket of meat; "and he shall eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and turn to other gods" corresponds to the son whom his father bathed and anointed and fed and then set at the door of a brothel; and "and Jeshurun grew fat and kicked" corresponds to the cow that was fed lupines and began to kick its owner. Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 2): The desire for eating and the desire for intercourse are sisters, and the one leads to the other, as it says, "a full belly breeds evil". Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): The beginning of all evil comes through the desire for eating — through it came the first sin and the first enticement of the evil inclination, in eating from the Tree of Knowledge — as the Gemara derives from verses that "a full belly breeds evil"; and above all through drinking. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 3): Of the manna it says, "He afflicted you and let you hunger and fed you the manna," for "a full belly breeds evil"; but the manna brought no filling of the belly, only restricted eating to keep the soul alive, like the eating of a poor man who has not enough to be sated and stays hungry. This was the preparation for receiving the Torah, which was given to the eaters of the manna, for such is the way of Torah — "bread with salt shall you eat" — and not for those who pursue their desires. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 15): Eating in the way of Torah — bread with salt and water by measure — is to keep the body healthy and sustain life alone, not to fill one's desire, for from that come all illnesses, of body and of soul alike, as they said, "a full belly breeds evil"; and from this came the beginning of all sins, the enticement of the inclination, and the death brought upon the world through the desire for eating. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 1): All restraints of bodily desires are a fence against sexual immorality — hence, according to one view, one who fasts is called holy — and restraint of the desire for eating above all, as they said, "a full belly breeds evil"..);
"a belly filled with rich food breeds malice" (Berakhot 32a);
וַאֲבַק לָשׁוֹן הָרָע הוּא רַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת;
and the dust of slanderous speech is evil toward fellow creatures;
וְעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה הוּא רַע לַשָּׁמַיִם.
and calculating expectation in prayer is evil toward Heaven.
וְנֶגְדָּם הֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת:
And corresponding opposite these are the three Patriarchs:
מִדַּת חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם הוּא טוֹב לַבְּרִיּוֹת;
the attribute of Lovingkindness in Abraham is good toward fellow creatures;
וּמִדַּת גְּבוּרָה דִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר הוּא טוֹב לְעַצְמוֹ;
the attribute of Strength through self-mastery in Isaac is good toward oneself;
וֶאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
and the Truth of Jacob, whose countenance is engraved upon the Throne of Glory,
שֶׁחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֱמֶת, הוּא טוֹב לַשָּׁמַיִם.
the seal of Hashem being Truth, is good toward Heaven.
וְעֵשָׂו, כְּבָר בּוֹ הָיָה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּאַבְרָהָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And Esau already carried within him the initial root of Abraham as mentioned above,
זֶה נִקְרָא פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם;
which is why this is termed the displaying of split hooves;
כִּי סִימָנֵי טָהֳרָה דְּנֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִי הֵם טוֹב לְעַצְמוֹ וְטוֹב לַבְּרִיּוֹת,
for the kosher signs of animal nature reflect being good to oneself and good to others,
שֶׁזֶּה מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית גַּם כֵּן;
which operates from the perspective of the animal soul as well;
וְהֵם מַעֲלֵה גֵּרָה, שֶׁהוּא טְחִינַת הַמַּאֲכָל הֵיטֵב,
and these are: chewing the cud, which is grinding one's food thoroughly,
לֹא לִבְלֹעַ הַכֹּל כְּדֶרֶךְ הַגַּרְגְּרָנִים, וְהוּא עֲצִירַת הַתַּאֲווֹת;
rather than gluttonously gulping everything, signifying the restraint of lusts;
וּשְׁסִיעַת הַטְּלָפַיִם, שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִרְמֹס בְּרַגְלָיו מַה שֶּׁתַּחְתָּיו כִּקְלוּטֵי הַפַּרְסוֹת,
and split hooves, ensuring that it cannot trample what lies beneath it like solid-hoofed beasts,
וְלֹא לִדְרֹס מַה שֶּׁלְּפָנָיו כְּבַעֲלֵי הַצִּפָּרְנַיִם.
or claw and tear prey like carnivores.
וְהַיּוֹתֵר מְשֻׁקָּץ וּמְטֻנָּף בְּמַאֲכָלוֹ הוּא הַחֲזִיר,
Yet the filthiest and most abominable in its food habits is the swine;
כִּי כֵּן מִי שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא בֶּאֱמֶת וּפַרְסוֹתָיו שְׁסוּעוֹת,
for so it is with one who is inwardly impure yet splits his hooves,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹמֵס וְדוֹרֵס זוּלַת וּמַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ טוֹב לַבְּרִיּוֹת,
refraining from outward harm and presenting himself as benevolent to society—
אֵין לְךָ מְשֻׁקָּץ וּמְטֻנָּף לְעַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ.
there is no one more internally abominable and degenerate toward himself than he.
כִּי אֵין שְׁסִיעַת הַפַּרְסוֹת סִימַן טָהֳרָה
For split hooves are not a valid sign of purity
רַק לְמִי שֶׁהוּא מַעֲלֵה גֵּרָה גַּם כֵּן,
except when accompanied by chewing the cud as well,
וְכֵן הָיָה עֵשָׂו.
and such was Esau. –
וְכֵן הַהוּא גַּבְרָא שֶׁהָיָה גִּלְגּוּלוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר,
And so was that man who was his reincarnation, as written in the Zohar,
נִדּוֹן בְּצוֹאָה רוֹתַחַת,
punished with boiling excrement;
וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּרָע, מַלְעִיג עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים,
his root being steeped in evil, mocking the words of the Sages,
כִּי זֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל טִנּוּף הַתַּאֲווֹת,
for the root of all defilement of lust,
שֶׁהוּא הַהַשְׁכָּחָה מִן הָאֱמֶת,
which causes truth to be forgotten,
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי לֵיצָנוּת וְהַלְעָגָה מִדִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים]
stems from cynicism and derision of the words of the Living God
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ עֲדַיִן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַרְחָקַת הָרָע דְּיִצְחָק.
because Esau did not yet possess Isaac's internal root of truly banishing evil.
כִּי כָּל נֶפֶשׁ, מַה שֶּׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בּוֹ, שֶׁלְּכָךְ נוֹצַר לְהוֹצִיא דָּבָר זֶה בָּעוֹלָם,
For regarding any soul, the specific spiritual mission for which it was created to bring forth in the world,
הֲרֵי כָּל יָמָיו הַקְּצוּבִים לוֹ הוּא מַה שֶּׁקָּצַב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זְמַן לְבֵרוּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת זֶה,
his entire allotted lifespan represents the time Hashem designated to clarify this effort,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִגְלֶה זֶה בּוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
and this realization cannot become fully disclosed within the person himself,
שֶׁכָּל יָמָיו עוֹדֶנּוּ עָסוּק בַּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, רַק נִגְלֶה בִּבְנוֹ.
for all his days he is actively laboring in this toil, but is revealed only in his son.
וְעַד לֵדַת יַעֲקֹב וְעֵשָׂו, הָיָה יִצְחָק עָסוּק בְּהַרְחָקַת כָּל מִינֵי רָע הַנִּגְלֶה שֶׁמַּכִּירִים שֶׁהוּא רָע;
And until the birth of Jacob and Esau, Isaac was engaged in purging all overt evil that is recognized as evil;

אֲבָל יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן הָאוֹמְרִים לָרַע טוֹב וְכוּלֵי717 Isaiah 5:20 — “Woe to those who call evil good and good evil; who present darkness as light and light as darkness; who present bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter.” Rashi: "Who call evil good" — they praise idolatry, and it seems evil in their eyes to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, who is good. "Who put darkness for light" — of a thing that is destined to bring darkness upon them they say that it will give them light, and of the sin that is destined to bring bitter punishment upon them they say that it will be sweet for them; while the sweet service of the Holy One, blessed be He, they call bitter. Radak: Of their own evil deeds they say that they are good, and of occupying oneself with Torah and wisdom they say that it is evil and a weariness of the flesh. They are as though they put darkness for light: since they do not distinguish with the mind what is good and what is evil, they are like men who cannot distinguish by the senses, whose sight and taste deceive them. Metzudas Dovid: "Evil" — of the worship of the idols of Canaan they would say that it was good; "and good" — that is the service of the Omnipresent. "Who put darkness" and so forth — the matter is repeated twice and three times, as is the way of eloquent speech, and to show that they did so continually. Malbim: He says three things corresponding to the three powers of discernment in man: the intellect, which distinguishes true good from true evil, as a commandment from a sin; the imagination, which distinguishes the useful from the useless, as light from darkness; and the feeling soul, which distinguishes the pleasant from the unpleasant, as honey from wormwood. As in sicknesses of the body a man tastes the bitter as sweet and the sweet as bitter, or in an illness of the eyes takes light for darkness and darkness for light, so it is found in sicknesses of the soul, that evil becomes good to them and good evil.,
yet there are also those who label evil as good, etc.,
שֶׁכְּפִי מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה לַעַיִן יוּכְלוּ לְדַמּוֹת שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ.
who appear virtuous to the casual eye while inwardly being the exact reverse.
וְזֶה הָיָה הַנִּסָּיוֹן דְּיִצְחָק בַּבֵּרוּר שֶׁבֵּין יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו,
And this was Isaac's test in distinguishing Jacob from Esau,
שֶׁעֵשָׂו הָיָה נִדְמֶה לְטוֹב יוֹתֵר מִיַּעֲקֹב בְּעֵינֵי יִצְחָק.
for Esau seemed more righteous than Jacob in Isaac's eyes.
וּבָזֶה הָיָה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יִצְחָק אַחַר כָּךְ,
And this became the entire focus of Isaac's subsequent effort:
לְבָרֵר הַכָּרַת זֶה, לְהַרְחִיק גַּם הַנֶּעְלָם דְּרָע,
to clarify this perception, banishing concealed evil as well,
שֶׁבָּזֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ שֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל", דְּהַיְנוּ עֹמֶק טוֹב,
for this reveals the root of the name "Israel"—an absolute depth of goodness—
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ מֵעֵשָׂו:
which is the exact antithesis of Esau:
דְּהַגַּם שֶׁנִּגְלֵהוּ טוֹב, עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא רָע,
for though Esau appears good on the surface, he is nonetheless evil within,
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם דְּנִגְלֵהוּ רָע, עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא טוֹב.
whereas in Israel, though an individual may appear flawed externally, he is nonetheless good within.
וְזֶה כָּל יְגִיעַת יִצְחָק, לְהוֹצִיא נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן;
And this was Isaac's entire toil: to bring forth a soul embodying this reality;
וּלְכָךְ: "וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו",
and therefore Scripture says: "He smelled the fragrance of his garments,"

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין לז.)718 Sanhedrin 37a — R. Zeira said: From here — "And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him" (Genesis 27:27): do not read "his garments [begadav]" but "his traitors [bogedav]." Tosafos (s.v. "and he smelled the smell of his garments"): "Smell" is a term that belongs to menstrual blood, as we say at the end of chapter Kol HaYad (Niddah 20b): a certain woman brought blood before R. Elazar; he smelled it and said, "This is blood of desire." Maharsha: Jacob was certainly perfectly righteous, but he was now wearing the garments of the wicked Esau, which Esau had coveted from the wicked Nimrod, and how many bloodstains from the murders of these wicked men were on them; yet when Jacob came before his father even these garments gave off a good fragrance, as it is said, "and he smelled the smell of his garments," for the fragrance of the Garden of Eden entered with him. This is a sign for his children, that even the traitors among them give off a fragrance through the commandments, as with the bloodstains of niddah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 37a): The garments allude to the empty ones: garments are secondary to the man, and so the empty ones are not the essence of "man" — for the righteous are always likened to man, and Israel, being more righteous than the nations, are called "man" (Yevamot 61a); therefore the wicked are likened to garments, which are not the man himself and are far from him. The good deed that the empty ones do for the sake of Heaven is called "smell" because smell reaches from far away, and so the Holy One, blessed be He, smells the commandments of the empty ones, who are far from Him; further, smell is associated with the attribute of judgment, and the empty ones, who subdue their inclination with great strength and wage war against it, belong to that attribute. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Esau's heart was full of crookedness, and only through the dimming of his eyes could Isaac think well of him; through that same dimming he afterwards did not recognize Jacob either, but he smelled "the smell of his traitors," for even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and there is no room at all to accuse him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:57): Jacob's service was chiefly in intention for the sake of Heaven, and the "garments" of deed began only with Laban, where he began to beget the souls of Israel, who are themselves the commandments of the Torah; hence it says then that [Rebecca] dressed him in Esau's garments. Therefore the Sages read "the smell of his garments" as "the smell of his traitors," meaning, as they said, that even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate: they too have a garment of the deed of the mitzvot. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 10): In Israel the evil stems from the vessels themselves, not from what is drawn out of them, and in the essence of the vessels there is no evil at all; therefore "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": they too give off a good fragrance, as it says, "the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot." As the Sages said of the myrtle, fragrance without taste, so in Israel there are those who have mitzvot but not Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The penitent breaks through every bound and in a single moment can rise from the utmost darkness to great light, which is the good name that spreads from one end of the world to the other; and of this it is said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors": once they have returned from [their betrayals], theirs is the chief good fragrance, smelled throughout the whole world. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 5): When Isaac asked, "Are you my son Esau?", he meant that in the smell of his garments he sensed deeds, for which he called him "Esau" [as one who does the will of his Maker]; and the Midrash indeed reads "his garments" as "his traitors." To this Jacob answered "I am": I am the one who performs the deeds of the mitzvot, and what you sensed is the fragrance of Jacob's traitors, for the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and they too give off a good fragrance. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Even when Israel sins, it is like a myrtle standing among reeds, for the essence of a Jew's heart always gives off a good fragrance like the myrtle, as the Sages said on "he smelled the smell of his garments": "the smell of his traitors." The sins are only like thorns surrounding the rose, which prick it for the moment, and in the future this will be made clear in all Israel, when "the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the seed of Jacob none is cast off, for just as evening and morning make one day, so His praise rises from the wicked as from the righteous: even the empty ones of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate, and the sinners of Israel are full of remorse. Of this the Sages said, "he smelled the smell of his garments — the smell of his traitors," and Bereishis Rabbah applies it to the likes of Yakim of Tzeroros, who in a brief moment preceded Yose ben Yoezer, a perfect tzaddik who had toiled all his days, to the World to Come; for the penitent attains this in a single moment.: רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו, וַיְבָרֲכֵהוּ וְגוֹמֵר,
which our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 37a): "the fragrance of his betrayers," whereupon he blessed him,
דְּהַכָּרַת הַשְּׁלֵמוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו דַּוְקָא, שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה.
for the realization of perfection is verified precisely through the inner spark of the betrayers, proving his bed is whole.
וְכָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתַּקֵּן הוּא מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית,
And all root-evil that cannot be rectified stems from the animal soul,
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹלַד כְּבָר בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית מְתֻקֶּנֶת לְגַמְרֵי בִּשְׁנֵי סִימָנֵי טָהֳרָה,
whereas Jacob our father was born with his animal soul fully refined through both kosher signs,
וְאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם פְּסֹלֶת עוֹד בְּטֻמְאָה.
bearing no further dross of impurity.
רַק עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת: טָהֳרָה וּקְדֻשָּׁה;
Yet there remain two higher spiritual rungs: Purity and Holiness;
וְטָהֳרָה יֵשׁ בְּכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה וְיֵשׁ טְהוֹרִים,
and purity applies to all created things that can contract defilement, as well as to pure entities,
וְכֵן יֵשׁ בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים טְהוֹרִים וּטְמֵאִים;
and similarly exists among animals that are pure or impure;
אֲבָל קְדֻשָּׁה הוּא רַק בָּאָדָם,
but holiness exists exclusively within the human realm,
וְכֵן כָּל הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת שֶׁל נִבְרָאִים דְּחָיְלָא קְדֻשָּׁה עֲלַיְהוּ, הוּא מִצַּד הָאָדָם שֶׁמַּקְדִּישׁוֹ,
and all holiness that rests upon other creations is imparted through man who sanctifies it,
רַק בְּכוֹר דִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם.
except for the firstborn animal whose holiness is innate from the womb.
וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this was Jacob's entire exertion:
אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹלַד שָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּהַכָּרָה דְּ"אָנֹכִי" וְהַרְחָקָה דְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
after having been born rooted in the affirmation of "I am" and the rejection of false gods,
עֲדַיִן הָעוֹלָם חָסֵר שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא הַהֲשָׁבָה הַכֹּל לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ,
the world still lacked Shabbat—the returning of all existence to its root—
דְּעַדַיִן הַנִּבְרָא הוּא נִפְרָד מֵהַבּוֹרֵא.
since creation still appeared separate from the Creator.
וְזֶה מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא", הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
This arises from this world being a "world of falsehood," opposite the Truth of Jacob,
שֶׁהָאֱמֶת הוּא שֶׁאֵין שָׁם דָּבָר נִפְרָד כְּלָל.
which recognizes that nothing is truly separate from Him at all.
וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשָּׁה,
And this is the meaning of holiness:
שֶׁהַהֶקְדֵּשׁ הוּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה שַׁיָּךְ לַקֹּדֶשׁ,
that consecration denotes an object belonging exclusively to the Sanctuary,
וּכְקִדּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא שַׁיָּכָה לַבַּעַל.
like marriage (kiddushin) wherein a woman belongs solely to her husband.
וְעִקַּר קִדּוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן הַזְמָנָה וַהֲכָנָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And the primary meaning of kiddush is designation and preparation as mentioned above,
כִּי כָּל עִקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם הוּא רַק הַהֲכָנָה וְהַזְמָנָה שֶׁמֵּכִין עַצְמוֹ לְכָךְ,
for man's entire spiritual involvement in the holiness of Shabbat consists merely of readying himself
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שַׁיָּךְ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
to belong unto Hashem, blessed be He, Who is holy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ, כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אָנִי",
as it is written: "You shall be holy, for I am holy,"
וּמִצַּד הַהֲכָנָה לְקַבֵּל קְדֻשָּׁה:
and from this readiness to receive holiness:
"וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם" – הוּא הֲכָנָה לִהְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה "וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים".
"Sanctify yourselves" serves as the preparation to become "and you shall be holy."
וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יַעֲקֹב,
And this was Jacob's entire exertion:
לִהְיוֹת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה גַּם כֵּן מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן,
that holiness be established innately from birth,
דְּהַיְנוּ מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית גַּם כֵּן, כִּקְדֻשַּׁת בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה.
meaning: encompassing the animal soul as well, like the sanctification of a firstborn animal.
וְזָכָה לְכָךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And he merited this, as Scripture states: "My firstborn son is Israel,"
שֶׁקְּרִיאַת הַשֵּׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל" הַמּוֹרֶה עַל נִצּוּחַ הַמַּלְאָכִים הוּא מִצַּד הַזֶּה,
and the conferring of the name "Israel," denoting triumph over the angels, stems from this attainment;
שֶׁהַמַּלְאָכִים הֵם קְדוֹשִׁים וּמֻבְדָּלִים מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for the angels are holy and detached from all affairs of this world,
וּלְכָךְ הֵם עִרְעֲרוּ עַל בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and on that account protested the creation of man who is immersed in physicality.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה719 Bereshit Rabbah 8:5 — When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create the first man, the ministering angels formed themselves into parties. Kindness said: Let him be created, for he performs acts of kindness. Truth said: Let him not be created, for he is all falsehood. Righteousness said: Let him be created, for he does righteous deeds. Peace said: Let him not be created, for he is all strife. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took Truth and cast it to the earth. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ח):
And our Sages of blessed memory noted (Bereishit Rabbah 8):
מֶה עָשָׂה? הִשְׁלִיךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה וְכוּלֵי,
What did He do? He cast Truth to the earth, etc.,
הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which is the trait of our father Jacob, peace be upon him;
כִּי אֵין שַׁיָּךְ אֱמֶת אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ שֶׁקֶר,
for truth is meaningful only when contrasting falsehood,

כַּיָּדוּעַ חִלּוּק רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי, הוּבָא בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק וְרֹא"שׁ סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג דִּשְׁבוּעוֹת)720 Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 3:8 — A vain oath is one who swears to alter what is known to men; a false oath is one who swears to substitute one thing for another... Hezekiah said: One who swears that two are two is flogged for a vain oath. R. Menachem in the name of Reish Lakish: One who sees rain falling and says, "Lord, send down much rain," is flogged for a vain oath. R. Chuniya and R. Ya'akov son of R. Bun in the name of R. Shmuel bar Nachman: There were twenty-four town councils in the South, and all of them were destroyed on account of a vain oath that was true, as it is written, "In vain have I smitten your children" (Jeremiah 2:30). Pnei Moshe (s.v. "to alter what is known to men"): As we learned in the Mishnah: [swearing] of a man that he is a woman. And a false oath is where he swears to substitute something that is not known to everyone — for example, "I ate," and it turns out that he did not eat. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "one who sees rain falling"): One who swears concerning two that they are two — that is a vain oath, and he is flogged. One who sees the rain coming down and says "Kyrie" — "Lord" — is using a form of oath, that much rain should come down ("poly" is "much" and "brechson" is "rain" in Greek); and this is so even though it is a vain oath that is true, as in R. Chuniya's teaching [that follows]. "Boulai" means towns, and "in vain" means on account of matters of a vain oath. בֵּין שָׁוְא לְשֶׁקֶר,
as is known from the Sages' distinction between an oath in vain and an oath of falsehood,
דְּגַם הַנִּשְׁבָּע עַל עֵץ שֶׁהוּא עֵץ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁקֶר, נִקְרָא שָׁוְא.
that swearing that wood is wood, though not a lie, is considered an oath in vain.
וְלָכֵן רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא",
Therefore, only in this world which is a "world of falsehood,"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ דִּמְיוֹן הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת,
where an illusion opposite to truth exists,
שַׁיָּךְ הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת;
is authentic recognition of truth applicable;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין שָׁם שֶׁקֶר,
whereas among the angels where no falsehood exists,
הָאוֹמֵר אֱמֶת הוּא כְּאוֹמֵר עַל עֵץ שֶׁהוּא עֵץ, שֶׁאֵין זֶה קָרוּי אֱמֶת כְּלָל.
one who utters truth is like one declaring that wood is wood, which is not called moral truth at all.
וְנִמְצָא מִצַּד שְׁלֵמוּת מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא נִצּוּחַ הַמַּלְאָכִים.
It follows that from the perfection of Jacob's truth emerges the triumph over the angels.
וְכָל שֶׁקֶר הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה לְעוֹלַם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
And the core falsehood of this world is the perspective of the realm of human effort,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ נִבְרָאִים נִפְרָדִים הַמִּשְׁתַּדְּלִים לַעֲבֹד לַבּוֹרֵא,
that there exist separate created beings striving to serve the Creator—
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן חֲפִירַת הַבְּאֵרוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, שֶׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לִמְצוֹא הַמַּעְיָן.
which was the inner meaning of the digging of the wells by Abraham and Isaac, striving to uncover the hidden spring.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא חָפַר עוֹד בְּאֵר,
Jacob our father, however, did not dig another well,
רַק גָּלַל הָאֶבֶן מֵעַל פִּי הַבְּאֵר,
he simply rolled the stone away from atop the well mouth,
שֶׁכְּבָר הָיוּ הַמַּעְיָנוֹת גְּלוּיִם מֵהָאָבוֹת:
for the springs had already been uncovered by his forebears:
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאֱמוּנָה קָבוּעַ מֵאַבְרָהָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "וְהֶאֱמִן בַּה' וְגוֹמֵר",
the root of faith was fixed by Abraham, of whom it was said: "And he believed in Hashem, etc.",
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעֲבוֹדָה מִיִּצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה עוֹלָה תְּמִימָה, כָּל גּוּפוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ מָסוּר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the root of divine service by Isaac, who was an unblemished offering, body and soul surrendered to Hashem.
וְעַדַיִן יֵשׁ בְּכָל זֹאת הֶעְלֵם,
Yet concealment still lingers in all this,
דְּאַף דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים וְעוֹסְקִים בְּתוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת,
for even though Israel are believers, children of believers, and engaged in Torah and commandments,

דַּאֲפִלּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן (סוֹף חֲגִיגָה721 Chagigah 27a — Reish Lakish said: The fire of Gehenna has no power over the sinners of Israel. This follows a fortiori from the golden altar: if the golden altar, which has upon it no more than the thickness of a golden dinar, and for many years the fire had no power over it — then the sinners of Israel, who are as full of commandments as a pomegranate is of seeds, as it is written, "Your temples [rakatekh] are like a pomegranate split open" (Song of Songs 4:3) — read not rakatekh but reikanin shebakh, "the empty ones among you" — how much more so. Rashi: "No more than the thickness of a gold dinar" — a slight thing, and yet its gold was not diminished, for a miracle was performed with it. Tosafos (s.v. "the fire of Gehenna has no power over the sinners of Israel"): This cannot be said of the sinners of Israel in their bodies, for it is taught in Rosh Hashanah that for them Gehenna is consumed but they are not consumed; it speaks rather of those who are transgressors only in part. Tosafos (s.v. "which has upon it no more than the thickness of a dinar"): In the Tanchuma: Moses wondered at this, that the wood could not but be burned; and the Omnipresent said to him, Such is My way with the fire of above — fire consumes fire and yet does not destroy it, as it is written, "and the bush was not consumed" (Exodus 3:2). Maharsha: From the Tosafot it appears that the point is this: the altar's coating was no thicker than a gold dinar, and even so the wood beneath it was not burned, for the thin gold shielded it. In like manner the sinners of Israel are full of commandments, as it is written, "like a pomegranate split open"; and these commandments, which are likened to gold, as it is said, "more desirable than gold," shield them so that the fire of Gehenna has no power over them. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 26): At the end of Chagigah the fire of Torah is likened to the fire of Gehenna — therefore the fire of Gehenna has no power over Torah scholars, and they derived it from the salamander, for it is all one fire — and afterwards the fire of Gehenna is likened there to the fire of the altar, a fire from above that consumes yet does not destroy. It is like the purging of an iron vessel in fire, which expels the absorbed flavors while the vessel itself remains: it burns only the evil absorbed in this world, and in Torah scholars the fire of Torah burns it away in this world. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): Opposite [jealousy], which is the doing of evil, stands in the good the doing of good, and this is in the camp of Israel, as the Sages said, "even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate" — for "mitzvah" unqualified in the words of the Sages is charity, that is, doing good to one's fellow. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Of Israel who engage in Torah it is said at the end of Chagigah that their whole body is fire, as it says, "Is not My word like fire"; and the sinners of Israel too, of whom it is said there that they are full of mitzvos — when they engage in the Torah's mitzvos they are engaged in Torah and cleave to it and become fire, and therefore the fire of Gehenna has no power over them either. This comes through their cleaving to the Blessed One by engaging in His mitzvos, for He is a fire that consumes the fire of Gehenna, which comes from the burning of evil desires. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 15): Reish Lakish's statement about the sinners of Israel is introduced as "said Reish Lakish," not "Reish Lakish said" as one who comes to disagree, implying that the two do not disagree; but then, if the fire of Gehenna has no power even over all the sinners of Israel, why need R. Elazar say it only of Torah scholars, because their body is fire? They said "has no power," not "they do not enter at all," so clearly they do enter, only the fire does not rule over them — yet this cannot mean that they do not feel the burning at all, for then why would they enter? And from Acher, from whose grave smoke rose, we see that it did rule over him even though his whole body was fire. כז.),
such that even sinners among Israel are full of good deeds like a pomegranate (Chagigah 27a),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי לַלֵּב בַּפּוֹעַל.
nonetheless it is not overtly apparent to the conscious heart in actuality.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְבֹרָר לוֹ כֵּן לָעִנְיָן,
This is the attribute of Truth: that this awareness become clarified for a person,
כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא לְנִסָּיוֹן הָאֱמוּנָה,
such that when put to the test of faith,
עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ לֵב הָאֶבֶן הַסּוֹתֵם עַל פִּי הַבְּאֵר וְצָרִיךְ לְגָלְלוֹ.
there remains a heart of stone obstructing the well's mouth which one must roll away.
שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מְבֹרָר לָעַיִן אֵיךְ "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר",
For when it becomes vividly clear how "I am Hashem" governs all,

וְשֶׁכָּל פָּעַל לְמַעֲנֵהוּ לְקִלּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב רֵישׁ מִזְמוֹר יט722 Midrash Tehillim 19:1 — "For the leader. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God." This is what Scripture says: "The Lord has made everything for His own sake" (Proverbs 16:4) — for His praise, as it is said, "Sing to the Lord with thanksgiving" (Psalms 147:7). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 2): The aim of the whole Torah is to come to a complete apprehension that there is a Creator, Ruler and Overseer, which was the purpose of the creation of the world: "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. All 613 commandments are counsels for reaching this, for the Torah is called truth, being counsels for reaching a clear apprehension in the heart, so manifest that it needs no faith. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 6): Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created for His glory, He created to reveal the glory of His kingship and His Presence among the lower beings, and "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. The building of the Tabernacle and the Temple is man's work of building a place for His Presence after the sin, when the Presence is not revealed everywhere, in the pattern of the Blessed One's work in creation; had man not sinned, the whole world would have been a Tabernacle and a Sanctuary. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): The angels cry, "Where is the place of His glory?", but man grasps the Throne of Glory, for "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise; the purpose of creation is the revelation of His glory, and its purpose is man. For the chief revelation of glory is when a person with free choice, whose body inclines toward impurity, nevertheless subdues his inclination and desires for the sake of Heaven's honor, which the angels, who have no evil inclination, cannot attain at all.),
and that everything was fashioned for His glory and praise (Shocher Tov 19),
מִמֵּילָא מַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ.
one automatically recognizes that there is none else beside Him.
וּמִתְגַּלֶּה קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁמֵּעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And the holiness of Shabbat—a semblance of the World to Come—is revealed,
שֶׁבָּא מְנוּחָה דְּאֵין הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת פּוֹעֵל כְּלוּם,
bringing rest from the illusion that human effort independently accomplishes anything,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂהוּ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
since even one's deeds and strivings originate entirely from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶהוּ גְּלִילַת הָאֶבֶן מֵעַל פִּי הַבְּאֵר,
And this is the rolling away of the stone from atop the well mouth,
שֶׁפִּי הַמַּעְיָן הַנּוֹבֵעַ הוּא הַגִּלּוּי הַגָּמוּר לָעַיִן.
for the flowing mouth of the spring represents the complete revelation before our eyes.
וּגְלִילָה זוֹ מוֹרָשָׁה הִיא בְּיָדֵינוּ מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this rolling away of the stone is an inheritance in our possession from Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מֻשְׁרָשׁ בְּכֹחוֹ מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן
that every single Jew has rooted within his strength from birth
כֹּחַ גִּלּוּי זֶה שֶׁל הָאֱמֶת לְלִבּוֹ.
this capacity to reveal the inner truth to his heart.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט723 Sanhedrin 99b — As for "And Lotan's sister was Timna" — what is this? Timna was a royal princess, as it is written, "chief Lotan," "chief Timna," and every chief is royalty without a crown. She wished to convert. She came to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and they did not accept her. She went and became a concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, saying: Better that I be a maidservant to this nation than a noblewoman of another nation. From her came Amalek, who afflicted Israel. What is the reason? Because they should not have pushed her away. Rashi: "Royalty without a crown" — a great prince, only not crowned; and since Timna was the sister of a chief, she was certainly a king's daughter. "Better to be a maidservant to this nation" — to the children of Abraham and Isaac, who fear Heaven, rather than a mistress to another nation; therefore she became a concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, who was of the seed of Isaac. "To push her away" — from beneath the wings of the Shechinah, for they ought to have converted her. Maharsha: They derived this exposition from Scripture's taking care to state that Amalek's mother was Timna, who bore him to Eliphaz — "And Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz" — whereas for Eliphaz's other sons, Teman, Omar, Zepho and the rest, it does not mention who their mother was. They expounded that because Abraham [Isaac and Jacob] did not accept her, she had to become a concubine to Eliphaz, saying, "Better to be a maidservant," and for this they were punished in that Amalek, who afflicted Israel, was born of her. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 99b): Abraham, Isaac and Jacob did not accept Timna because, owing to her importance and royalty, she would not enter conversion as is fitting: one is a convert only when he joins himself wholly to those to whom he converts, and while the Patriarchs humbled themselves before God, blessed be He, Timna, being royal, would not regard herself as a convert. Once pushed away she was distanced all the more, for whatever is pushed away is pushed away entirely: had she not come to convert there would have been no distancing, but since she came to convert and was rejected by the Patriarchs, who are the very beginning, this was the utmost distancing, leaving no share or connection at all. Therefore Amalek came forth from her, for no nation could be as opposed to Israel as Amalek was except one born of such distancing. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Among the nations, those with a greater connection to holiness are the worse, and Amalek has more connection to holiness than all the nations: besides issuing from two patriarchs and matriarchs, his mother Timna went around to the doors of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to convert, and they did not accept her, for they sensed the force of impurity of "the first of the nations" destined to come from her. Yet she still yearned to convert and went around their doors — surely because of a holy spark stirring within her.:):
And our Sages of blessed memory taught (Sanhedrin 99b):
שֶׁרָצְתָה לִדָּבֵק בּוֹ תִּמְנָע וְהִרְחִיקָהּ;
that Timna wished to attach herself to him, yet he pushed her away;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
because through the realization that everything originates from Hashem, blessed be He,
הִנֵּה יוּכַל לָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ וּלְפְרִיקַת עֹל
a person can be led through this to flippancy and cast off all discipline
(וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר בְּרִית מְנוּחָה:
(and along the lines of what is written in Sefer Berit Menuchah:
עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַיֵּן שָׁם),
through an ungrounded awareness of Israel's lofty stature, see there),
וְיַחֲשֹׁב אָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה כָּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת וְגַם זֶה הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה זוֹ
and a person will imagine he may commit all abominations, claiming that this too is from Hashem through this distortion, –
וְזֶה כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַטַּאת יָרָבְעָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
and this was the underlying core of Jeroboam's sin as I wrote elsewhere,

רַק שֶׁהוּא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְיֵשׁ לוֹ תִּקּוּן אֵצֶל דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת (שָׁם קד724 Sanhedrin 104b — Those who expound hidden meanings would say: All of them [who were listed as having no share in the World to Come] do enter the World to Come, as it is stated: "Gilead is Mine and Manasseh is Mine, and Ephraim is the stronghold of My head; Judah is My scepter" (Psalms 60:9). "Gilead is Mine" — this is Ahab, who fell at Ramoth-gilead. "Manasseh" — in its plain sense. "Ephraim is the stronghold of My head" — this is Jeroboam, who came from Ephraim. "Judah is My scepter" — this is Ahithophel. Rashi: "The expounders of hidden meanings" are expounders of verses, as it is written, "that which is inscribed [ha-rashum] in the writing of truth" (Daniel 10:21); they would say that all of them have a share, even Manasseh, Jeroboam and Ahab. "Gilead is Mine and Manasseh is Mine" — it is upon Me to bear their iniquity so that they may merit [the World to Come]; "Manasseh" in its plain sense is Manasseh son of Hezekiah. Ahithophel [is "Judah"] because he was of the tribe of Judah like David, who called him "my familiar friend," that is, my kinsman. Maharsha: Ahab's fall and death at Ramoth-gilead was itself his atonement, by which he merits the World to Come; and Manasseh alone is named "in its plain sense" because the others are designated by other names, their own names having been names of wickedness all their lives, whereas Manasseh repented in his lifetime and his own name, now in repentance, brings him to the World to Come. Jeroboam is "the stronghold of My head" because he was the first of all the kings of Israel and was made king at the word of the prophet, so he is not fit to be among those who go down to Gehinnom. "Judah is My lawgiver" is spoken by David: Ahithophel was David's teacher — "my lawgiver" — and through David his disciple he merited the World to Come, just as R. Meir, his disciple, brought Acher to the World to Come. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 2): The world was created with measure and limit, with room for choice between good and evil and for reward and punishment, whereas the World to Come has no choice; therefore the dorshei reshumos said that all of them come to the World to Come, for the World to Come is truly without limit, as it is written, "and I will feed you the heritage of Jacob your father," a heritage without boundaries. This world is not so: it is bounded, with time and with deeds good and evil. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): There are many levels of what is called "having no share": such a soul still has existence and is not wholly annihilated like the souls of the nations, enduring forever through its attachment to its root in the living God, only it has no share of its own; and this apart from the dorshei reshumos saying that all of them have a share in the World to Come. Though they said it of the particular souls listed in the Mishnah, from the particular one learns about the whole, for these seven marked individuals correspond to seven kinds of corruption through which one's share in the World to Come can be lost. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): This is the exposition of the dorshei reshumos ["expounders of hidden meanings"] that all of them have a share in the World to Come, all who are of the seed of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, except Balaam: "reshumos" denotes the level of chochmah above binah, binah being the World to Come and the heart, where feeling lies; chochmah in the mind is not felt, only its impression (reshimu) is felt in the heart. From the standpoint of the attainment of chochmah there is no dross at all in the seed of Jacob, and even things that have no remedy through repentance, which alludes to the World to Come, are rectified by the opening of the gate of chochmah, which is above the level of repentance.:)],
save that he is of Israel and retains rectification according to the interpreters of esoteric traces (Sanhedrin 104b),
וְזֶהוּ בִּיאַת תִּמְנָע לְהִתְדַּבֵּק וְהִרְחִיקָהּ.
and this was Timna's approach seeking to cling unto him, which he rebuffed.
וְנִשֵּׂאת לֶאֱלִיפַז שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן עֵשָׂו וְגָדַל בְּחֵיקוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק,
She then married Elifaz who was Esau's son and raised in Isaac's household,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (הוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י וַיֵּצֵא כט, יא725 Rashi on Genesis 29:11 — "And he wept" — because he foresaw by the holy spirit that she would not be buried with him. Another explanation: because he came empty-handed. He said: Eliezer, my grandfather's servant, had in his hands rings and bracelets and delicacies, and I have nothing in my hand. This was because Eliphaz son of Esau had pursued him at his father's command to kill him and had overtaken him; but because Eliphaz had been raised in Isaac's lap, he withheld his hand. He said to him: What shall I do about my father's command? Jacob said to him: Take what I have, for a poor man is accounted as dead.),
as our Sages of blessed memory taught (cited in Rashi, Vayeitzei 29:11),
וְהָיָה בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכָּרַת "אָנֹכִי" וְהַרְחָקַת "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת וְלִמּוּד מִיִּצְחָק.
and he likewise possessed the root of "I am" and the rejection of false gods inherited from the Patriarchs and learned from Isaac.
וּבָזֶה הָיָה מְעֻלֶּה מֵעֵשָׂו, שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לַהֲרֹג אֶת יַעֲקֹב,
In this he was superior to Esau, refusing to murder Jacob,
כִּי הוּא הָיָה מַכִּיר בַּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת זֶה גַּם כֵּן, לָדַעַת שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר נִפְרָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for he recognized this principle as well, knowing that nothing is detached from Hashem, blessed be He.
רַק הוּא שָׁרְשׁוֹ מֵעֵשָׂו שֶׁכְּבָר הֵמִיר דָּתוֹ וְנִתַּק שָׁרְשׁוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת מִן הַטּוֹב,
Only that his root stemmed from Esau, who had already severed his root in truth from the good,
רַק דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם;
maintaining it purely through the hypocritical display of split hooves;
וְכָךְ הוּא בַּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַהַכָּרָה דְּ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ",
and so it was with his grasp of "there is none else beside Him" –
אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת, רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם.
it was not grounded in truth, but merely along the line of displaying split hooves.
וְלֹא כְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁנָּשָׂא רָחֵל וְלֵאָה,
And not like Jacob, who married Rachel and Leah,
אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶם אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל.
who together built the house of Israel.
שֶׁכָּל אָדָם, זִוּוּגוֹ הוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהוֹצִיא כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לַפּוֹעַל,
For every person's marriage partner is ordained by Hashem to bring his spiritual toil into actualization,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בִּנְיַן בַּיִת",
and this is called "building a house,"

וְנִקְרָא "אִשְׁתּוֹ – בֵּיתוֹ" (רֵישׁ יוֹמָא726 Yoma 2a — R. Yehuda says: They would designate another wife for him as well, lest his wife die, as it is stated, "And he shall make atonement for himself and for his house" (Leviticus 16:6) — "his house," that is his wife. They said to him: If so, there is no end to the matter. Rashi: "And for his house": this is written concerning the Day of Atonement, in [the portion] Acharei Mos. "If so": if you are concerned about death. "There is no end to the matter": lest this one too die. Tosafos (s.v. "And the Sages say: If so, there is no end to the matter"): If one must be concerned about the death of one [wife], one must be concerned even about the death of two or three. Although Yevamot 26b implies that we are concerned about the death of one but not of two, here the concern over so short a period arises only from the special gravity of atonement — or, alternatively, because the atonement of all Israel depends on it, unlike the mere loss of the levirate commandment there — and so it would have to extend even to two or three; there would be no end to the matter, and hence no enactment can be made for this concern. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos): On Tosafot's remark that [the concern over the High Priest's disqualification] is a mere apprehension, since presumably many fit [priests] would be found: it is somewhat difficult, for if it is only a mere apprehension because another priest fit for the service would be found on the Day of Atonement even without having been set apart seven days beforehand, then designating another wife is likewise only a mere apprehension, since many priests with wives, fit for the service, would be found. Why then do they say that the atonement of Israel depends on this more than in the case of impurity? This can be resolved. ב.),
and it is taught: "his wife is his home" (Yoma 2a),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִבְנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ בַּיִת קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
for through this an enduring, eternal home is constructed from him.
וְהִיא הָ"עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ" לְהוֹצִיא בְּגִלּוּי כֹּחַ הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבָּאִישׁ.
And she serves as the "helpmate opposite him" to unveil the latent spiritual potential within the man.
וְתִמְנָע הָיְתָה פִּילֶגֶשׁ לֶאֱלִיפַז,
Now Timna was a concubine to Elifaz,
שֶׁעִנְיַן הַפִּילֶגֶשׁ הוּא שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ בְּמַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת,
and the essence of a concubine is that he came upon her in hidden secrecy,
כִּי לֹא נָאֶה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּגִלּוּי.
because it was improper for her to be his wife openly.
וְכֵן עִנְיַן תִּמְנָע,
And so too is the essence of Timna:
שֶׁהוּא עֲשִׂיַּת כָּל הַנִּמְנָע מִצַּד הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵה',
which is the committing of all forbidden things under the premise that everything is from God,
זֶהוּ הֵיפֶךְ דֶּאֱלִיפַז שֶׁגָּדַל בְּחֵיקוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק, הַיְנוּ בְּעִנְיַן הַרְחָקַת הָרָע,
this being the antithesis of Elifaz who was raised in Isaac's bosom of repelling evil,
וְאֵין רְאוּיָה לְשִׁמּוּשׁוֹ כְּלָל מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי שֶׁלּוֹ.
rendering her completely unfitting for him from the vantage point of his manifest character.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת בְּמַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת וּבְהֶעְלֵם הָיָה גַּם הוּא כֵּן דַּרְגָּא דְּעֵשָׂו,
Yet in truth, in secrecy and concealment he too mirrored the level of Esau,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו",
concerning whom Scripture says: "His secret places were uncovered,"
כִּי בְּמַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת שָׁקוּעַ בְּכָל מִינֵי הָרָע.
for in secret he was genuinely immersed in all manner of evil.
וּלְכָךְ הָיְתָה לוֹ פִּילֶגֶשׁ,
Therefore she was his concubine,
שֶׁלָּקַח דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל הַהַכָּרָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְפַרְסֵם בָּעוֹלָם פְּעֻלַּת כָּל מִינֵי רָע.
in that he seized this theological concept of Hashem's omnipotence to justify the practice of all evil in the world.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה727 Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu Zuta 2; Shelah, Sha'ar HaOtiyot — From here they said: Even if a man has in his hand neither Scripture nor Mishnah, but he sits and reads all day — “the sister of Lotan was Timna” — he has the reward of Torah in his hand. And the Shelah writes, in the eighth principle, that Moshe our teacher wrote and engraved from the mouth of the Blessed Name, from Bereshit onward, before the eyes of all Israel; the whole of it Moshe wrote from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He. There is no difference between the verse “I am the Lord your God” and “and Timna was a concubine,” or the like — rather all of it is alike, and it is all the speech of the Lord and His utterance, all its verses and all its words. (תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ, סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב,
And this explains what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 2,
וְעַיֵּן שְׁלָ"ה שַׁעַר הָאוֹתִיּוֹת אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה הָעִקָּר הַשְּׁמִינִי):
and see the Shelah, Sha'ar HaOtiyot, Emet Ve'Emunah):
שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ פָּסוּק "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל",
that her genealogy is recorded alongside truths as momentous as the verse "Shema Yisrael,"
וְיָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁזֶּהוּ שָׁרְשׁוֹ,
and from him emerged Amalek, whose essential root
דְּהַיְנוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע הַנִּפְעָל בָּעוֹלָם מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹעֵל הַכֹּל וְהוּא בָּרָא זֶה.
is the manifestation of evil justified by the claim that Hashem orchestrates all and created this.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה אֶלָּא לִמְחוֹת,
And this corruption has no remedy other than to be blotted out;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת "מִפִּי עֶלְיוֹן לֹא תֵצֵא הָרָעוֹת",
for in truth, "from the mouth of the Most High evil does not proceed,"
רַק בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם.
rather solely through human choice and striving.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם זֶה אֱמֶת שֶׁגַּם עֲמָלֵק מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה,
Yet it is nonetheless true that Amalek forms part of creation,
וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּבְּרִיאָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ לָרָע,
meaning that there exists in creation an innate root for evil,
וְהוּא אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת שֶׁהֻזְהַר אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁהוּא רַק הַיְדִיעָה בָּרָע.
namely the eating of the Tree of Knowledge concerning which Adam was warned, which was the experiential knowledge of evil.
זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
This is the root of evil that Hashem willed:
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לָדַעַת בָּרָע גַּם כֵּן;
that there should exist creatures capable of knowing evil as well;
וְאַף זֶה לֹא נִבְרְאוּ שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ בָּרָע,
and even so, they were not created to know evil inherently,
רַק כְּשֶׁיֹּאכַל מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת יֵדַע בָּרָע גַּם כֵּן,
only that if he ate from the Tree of Knowledge he would know evil too,
וְהֻזְהַר שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכֹל וְשֶׁלֹּא לֵידַע בָּרָע גַּם כֵּן.
and he was warned not to eat and not to know evil as well.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַבְּחִירָה נִתַּן בְּיָדוֹ לֶאֱכֹל, וְאַחַר כָּךְ לֵידַע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרָע בַּפּוֹעַל.
Nonetheless, free choice was placed in his hands to eat, consequently to know, and subsequently to commit evil in deed.
וְהֵם הַמְשָׁכַת כָּל מִינֵי רָע דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
And these form the extension of all evil of the idolatrous nations,
דִּשְׂאֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת הַכֹּל אֶחָד,
the leaven in the dough and the subjugation to empires being all one,
הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מִצַּד רֵאשִׁית הַבְּחִירָה.
drawn down from the inception of human free choice.
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא רֵאשִׁית דְּרָע דִּקְבִיעַ וְקַיָּמָא מֵהַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה בְּכֹחַ הַבְּחִירָה,
And Amalek is the primordial root of evil fixed and enduring from the beginning of creation through the power of choice,
וְאֵין בְּכֹחַ יַד אָדָם לְבַעֲרוֹ,
and it is beyond the power of mortal hands to eradicate him,

רַק: "מִלְחָמָה לַה' וְגוֹמֵר728 Exodus 17:16 — “And he said: For a hand is on the throne of the Lord — the Lord shall have war with Amalek from generation to generation.” Rashi: "For a hand is upon the throne of the Lord" — the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, was raised to swear by His throne that He would have war and enmity with Amalek forever. And since the word for "throne" is written short and the Divine Name is split in half, He swore that neither His Name nor His throne is complete until the name of Amalek is wholly blotted out.
