Ramban: He cites Rashi's reading, and then gives as the plain sense the explanation of others: when a hand is upon the Lord's throne — that is, when a king of Israel sits upon the throne of the Lord — there shall be war for the Lord against Amalek. This is a hint to Saul, the first king, and "from generation to generation" means that every king of Israel is bound to fight them until they are blotted out.",
save through: "Hashem has a war with Amalek, etc.,"
וְרַק: "וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר, אָז תִּמְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
and only: "and it shall be when Hashem has given you rest... then you shall blot out the memory, etc.,"
שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה הַנִּיחָא מִכָּל מִינֵי רָע,
for when rest is achieved from all other forms of evil,
שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ לִקְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא בַּפּוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ,
such that they attain the sanctity of Shabbat as an actual foretaste of the World to Come in tangible reality,
אָז יוּכְלוּ לִמְחוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דְּקָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם,
only then will they be able to blot out that entrenched, enduring root of evil
עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּמָא.
through the fixed and enduring supernal holiness.
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין הַכֹּחַ אֶלָּא בַּזְּכִירָה;
In this world, however, power over it exists solely through remembrance;
הַיְנוּ דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַרְחִיק כְּלָל,
meaning that the root of Amalek, which is the root of evil, cannot be repelled at all
אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַזְּכִירָה "אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה",
except through remembering "what he did" –
דְּהַיְנוּ מַה שֶּׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁזֶּה רַע בַּפּוֹעַל.
namely what flowed from him, which represents evil in practical action.
וְשָׁם הָאָדָם הָעוֹבֵד אֶת ה' יָכוֹל לְנַצֵּחַ וּלְהִתְרַחֵק מִזֶּה.
And there the servant of Hashem can triumph and separate himself from it.
אֲבָל בְּהִרְהוּר בְּעָלְמָא הָעוֹלֶה בַּלֵּב בְּדֶרֶךְ מִקְרֶה,
However, regarding an involuntary passing thought that enters the heart by chance,
כְּטַעַם עֲמָלֵק "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
mirroring Amalek "who met you by chance (karkha)",
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָדָם לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהִתְרַחֵק מִזֶּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא מֵעַצְמוֹ בָּא לוֹ.
it is impossible for a person to exert himself to prevent it, since it arises on its own.
רַק מִמֵּילָא, עַל יְדֵי הַהֲכָנָה וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כָּל הַיּוֹם תָּמִיד בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
Rather, spontaneously, through continuous daily preparation and immersion in words of Torah,
בַּהַהוּא הֲנָאָה וְנַחַת רוּחַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
through the pleasure and contentment produced on High from him,
אֵין שׁוּם הִרְהוּר רָע קָרֵב אֵלָיו מֵעַצְמוֹ,
no evil thought will approach him of its own accord,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לֹא תְאֻנֶּה וְגוֹמֵר כִּי מַלְאָכָיו וְגוֹמֵר729 Psalms 91:10-11 — “No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent. For He will charge His angels for you, to guard you in all your ways.” Rashi: “Shall befall” (te’unneh) — shall not happen, and similarly “and God caused it to come to his hand” (Exodus 21:13). Radak: “No evil shall befall you” — it will not present itself in your tents, neither to you nor to your wife nor to your children. “For He will command His angels for you, to guard you” — for your sake He will command His angels to guard you wherever you go. Metzudas Dovid: “No evil shall befall you” — then no evil will present itself to you; “nor shall any plague come near your tent” repeats the matter in other words. Malbim: He adds that if a man should wish to bring some evil upon you, the evil itself will not consent to befall you; and so with natural evils — though the plague be in your tent it will not come near you, as though the evil and the plague themselves did not wish to touch you or to harm you. And the angels whom the Lord commands to guard you in all your ways will bear you upon their hands and not let you pass over the ground on your feet, for they fear lest your foot strike a stone even with a slight knock, since they are charged with guarding you.".
as it is written: "No evil shall befall you... for He will command His angels regarding you."
הֵם הַמַּלְאָכִים הַנּוֹצָרִים מֵהַמִּצְוֹת,
These are the angels created from the commandments,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּצֵא ג730 Midrash Tanchuma, Vayetzei 3 — R. Meir said: If a man performs one commandment, one angel is assigned to him; if he performs two commandments, two angels are assigned to him; if he performs many commandments, many angels are assigned to him, as it is said, "For He will charge His angels concerning you, to guard you [in all your ways]." And why? To guard him from the harmful spirits, as it is said, "A thousand may fall at your side."):
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Vayeitzei 3):
שֶׁהֵם עִנְיַן הַנַּחַת רוּחַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁאָמַר וְנַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ,
that they embody the divine contentment Hashem experiences when His will is executed;
נִמְצָא אוֹתָהּ מִצְוָה נַעֲשֵׂית אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִנְיַן נַחַת שֶׁרוּחוֹ שׁוֹאֵב מִפְּעֻלַּת אָדָם.
so that the mitzvah becomes a source of pleasure Hashem's spirit draws from mortal action.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "מַלְאָךְ", עַל דֶּרֶךְ "עֹשֶׂה מַלְאָכָיו רוּחוֹת",
And this is termed an "angel," in the manner of "He makes winds/spirits His messengers,"
שֶׁהָרוּחַ הוּא הָאֶמְצָעִי בֵּין הַשָּׁמַיִם לָאָרֶץ.
for the spirit acts as the intermediary between heaven and earth.
וְהַמְשָׁכַת אוֹתוֹ רוּחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹשֵׁךְ מֵאָרֶץ לַשָּׁמַיִם, זֶה נִקְרָא עוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים;
And the channeling of that spirit which Hashem draws from earth to heaven is called the angelic realm;
כִּי נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם הוּא הַנִּכְנֶסֶת לְמַעְלָה מַּעְלָה בִּנְשִׁימַת רוּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for the soul of man ascends into the ultimate heights of His divine breath,
אֲבָל הַמַּלְאָכִים הֵם אֶמְצָעִיִּים,
whereas angels remain intermediaries,
וּמִזֶּה הוּא הִתְהַוּוּת הַמַּלְאָכִים עַל יְדֵי הַמִּצְוֹת לִשְׁמֹר הָאָדָם,
and from this comes the creation of guardian angels through mitzvot to protect the person,
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר.
and this is not the place to elaborate further.

וּכְשֶׁנּוֹפֵל בַּלֵּב אֵיזֶה הִרְהוּר, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא תָתוּרוּ731 Numbers 15:39 — “And it shall be for you as fringes, and you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not stray after your heart and after your eyes, which lead you astray.” Rashi: "And you shall remember all the commandments of the Lord" — the numerical value of "fringe" is six hundred, and with the eight threads and the five knots you have six hundred and thirteen. "And you shall not go about after your own heart" is like "from scouting the land": the heart and the eyes are the spies of the body, procuring its transgressions for it — the eye sees, the heart desires, and the body commits the transgression. Ramban: He said "and you shall not go about after your own heart" to warn men not to go astray through it. This is what our Rabbis expounded: "after your own heart" — this is heresy; "after which you go astray" — this is idolatry; that is, a man should not be led by the blue thread into any thought of heresy or of idolatry, but it shall all be for you "for fringes, that you may look upon it and remember." And they said further, "after your own eyes" — this is immorality.",
And when an unbidden thought falls into the heart, regarding this it is said: "Do not stray,"
שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר דְּסוֹפוֹ כָּל מִינֵי רָע.
that he must remember that its outcome is ruinous.

וְהִמְשִׁילוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנְחוּמָא (תֵּצֵא ז) מִתַּמְחוּי מָלֵא וְתַמְחוּי רֵיקָן732 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 7 — To what may the matter be compared? To a king who made a feast and invited guests. A platter full of every good thing was brought before him. He said: Remember so-and-so, my friend. He set the platter aside and said: Remember so-and-so, my enemy. They said to him: This one you remembered and that one you remembered? He said to them: For this one I set aside a platter full of every good thing, and for that one I set aside an empty platter. So too the Sabbath, of which it is written “Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy” — to honour it with food and drink and with clean garments; and of Amalek it is written “Remember what Amalek did to you” — over what do you remember him? Over an empty table, as it is said, “You shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens.”;
And our Rabbis of blessed memory in Tanchuma (Ki Teitzei 7) illustrated this with the parable of a full bowl and an empty bowl;
כִּי קִיּוּם הַחִיּוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַמָּזוֹן,
for the sustenance of life proceeds through food,
וּמְזוֹן הַנֶּפֶשׁ הוּא הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת,
and the sustenance of the soul is Torah and mitzvot,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב, כד)733 Kohelet Rabbah 2:24 — "There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink." R. Tanchuma said in the name of R. Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak: Every instance of eating and drinking stated in this scroll — the verse speaks of Torah and good deeds. R. Yona said: The paradigm for them all is "and it shall accompany him in his toil" (Ecclesiastes 8:15) — in his world, in this world; "the days of his life" — to the grave. And is there food and drink in the grave, that it accompanies a man to his grave? Rather, these are Torah and good deeds. דְּנִקְרָא שָׁם אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה.
as stated in Kohelet Rabbah (2:24) where it is termed eating and drinking.
וּזְכִירַת עֲמָלֵק הוּא עַל תַּמְחוּי רֵיקָן מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת;
And the remembrance of Amalek applies to a bowl empty of spiritual exertion;
דְּעַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת, אֵין הִרְהוּר רָע קָרֵב אֵלָיו כְּלָל.
for through active immersion in Torah and mitzvot, no evil thought approaches a person at all.
רַק כְּשֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב עַל תַּמְחוּי רֵיקָן,
Only when he sits before an empty bowl,
אָז צָרִיךְ לִזְכֹּר מֵעֲמָלֵק,
must he then remember Amalek,
לְהִזָּהֵר מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁאֵין בְּיָדוֹ לְהִתְרַחֵק רַק עַל יְדֵי הַזְּכִירָה שֶׁזֶּה רָע.
to guard against that root of evil which he can repel solely by remembering that it is destructive.
אֲבָל זְכִירַת שַׁבָּת,
However, the remembrance of Shabbat,
שֶׁגַּם כֵּן אֵין בְּיָדוֹ לְקַבֵּל אוֹתָהּ קְדֻשָּׁה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת רַק בַּזְּכִירָה,
whose holiness one likewise cannot produce through exertion but solely through remembrance,
אֲבָל הוּא עַל תַּמְחוּי מָלֵא, שֶׁכְּבָר טָרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
takes place over a full bowl, having already toiled on Friday.
וְאַחַר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, הוּא הַזְּכִירָה בִּקְדֻשָּׁה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ אֵלָיו כָּל מִינֵי קְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה,
And following that exertion, remembrance channels supernal sanctity downward,
דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
reflecting the level of our father Jacob, peace be upon him.
אֲבָל בְּיָשְׁבוֹ עַל תַּמְחוּי רֵיקָן,
Yet when sitting before an empty bowl,
צָרִיךְ לְהִזָּהֵר בִּזְכִירַת עֲמָלֵק עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּהַרְחָקַת הָרָע בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
one must be careful to invoke the remembrance of Amalek at least to repel evil at its root.
וּלְכָךְ קוֹרִין פָּרָשַׁת "זָכוֹר" בְּשַׁבָּת נוֹסָף אַזְכִּירָה דְּפוּרִים,
Therefore Parashat Zachor is read on Shabbat in addition to the remembrance of Purim,
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם מוֹשֵׁךְ חֲבֵרוֹ כַּמּוּבָן מִתּוֹךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי.
because each remembrance reinforces the other as understood from what I have written.
וּבָזֶה שְׁנֵי הַזְּכִירוֹת מִתְחַזְּקִים לְהִקָּבַע בַּלֵּב יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן.
And through this both remembrances are strengthened to be fixed within the heart like a peg in a steadfast place.

sections.en: Life, Sustenance, Children, and Mazal

items.h: The three fundamental human needs are governed by exact justice as expressed through the soul's supernal root; prayer can reach that level and reshape its flow.

Seif 1 — Children, Life, Sustenance, and Mazal
Exact judgment governs the three basic human needs through the soul's supernal root known as mazal.

p: צוֹרֶךְ הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם יָדוּעַ שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים:
Man's fundamental needs in this world are known to be three things:
חַיִּים, וְקִיּוּם הַחַיִּים דְּהַיְנוּ מְזוֹנֵי,
life, the preservation of life—namely sustenance (mezonei)—
וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה לְדוֹרוֹת דְּהַיְנוּ בָּנֵי.
and continuity across generations—namely children (banei).

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח734 Moed Katan 28a — Rava said: Length of life, children, and sustenance do not depend on merit but on fortune. For Rabbah and R. Chisda were both righteous sages: this one would pray and rain would come, and that one would pray and rain would come. R. Chisda lived ninety-two years, Rabbah lived forty. In R. Chisda's house there were sixty wedding feasts; in Rabbah's house, sixty bereavements. Tosafos (s.v. "rather, it depends upon fortune"): They asked in Tosafot: but we said at the end of Shabbat that "Israel is not subject to a constellation"! One may answer that sometimes a man's lot is changed, as in the cases there, and sometimes it is not changed — as is said in Taanit concerning R. Elazar ben Pedat, to whom it was said: Would it please you that I destroy the world, so that perhaps you might be created anew at an hour of sustenance? Tosafos (s.v. "sixty wedding feasts"): Some explain that the number is not meant exactly. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. "it depends upon fortune"): Tosafot's answer — and in Tosafot at Shabbat it is more explicit — is that "Israel is not subject to a constellation" means that by great merit one's fortune is changed. And so it is proved from our own passage, for Rava asked for Rav Huna's wisdom and Rav Chisda's wealth, which are matters fixed by the decree at birth, since the angel sets up the drop and asks whether it shall be wise or foolish, rich or poor; perforce one must say that by an abundance of pleading for mercy from Heaven, as Rava did, the decree and the constellation under which a man was born can be annulled. Maharal (Derech Chaim 4:9): If we see one who is not a wholly righteous man, and he is a poor Torah scholar, this too has its cause: his ill fortune brings it about, for "life, children and sustenance do not depend upon merit." And even of a wholly righteous man one may say the same, that his ill fortune is the cause — as we find with R. Elazar ben Pedat in Taanit, whose fortune was so exceedingly bad that he had no sustenance at all. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:98): Although children, life and sustenance "do not depend on merit but on mazal" — one's hidden root — the whole Torah is full of reward and punishment in these three, for through merit the mazal changes, as one's deeds incline the hidden root. Yet sometimes both men are completely righteous, as with Rabbah and R. Chisda — which Rosh Hashanah attributes to Rabbah's descent from the house of Eli — and in truth this is what is called mazal: a hidden root drawn from one's forebears, though he himself did nothing. Effort still helped, but because of his mazal Rabbah needed more effort, while less sufficed for R. Chisda. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Children, life and sustenance comprise all of a person's needs in this world, where there is no reward for a commandment, and so they are decreed at the beginning of formation — "wise or foolish, strong or weak, rich or poor" — whereas "righteous or wicked," which is merit, is not. Yet the Torah promises all three as reward, for insofar as they bear on Torah and the commandments — long life to multiply Torah, children to serve God, a ready livelihood — they certainly depend on merit, which can change the mazal; what depends on mazal, decreed at formation, is given even where it does not aid the service of God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): Children, life and sustenance, which "do not depend on merit but on mazal," cannot be attained through prayer; hence they said that sustenance and matching a couple are as hard as the splitting of the Sea. Although we petition for sustenance in every prayer, that is for one born in an hour of sustenance or who prays at a time of favor; but for one not so born, like R. Elazar ben Pedas, it depends on the supernal mazal in Atika, and prayer no longer avails — only Torah and calling to Him in truth, which is above mazal. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 6): The root of all blessings is life, children and sustenance, which "do not depend on merit but on mazal"; the Zohar teaches that this is the attribute of Atika, which is "upon the Lord," as in "Hannah prayed upon the Lord" and "cast your burden upon the Lord" — the tip of the yod above the letters of the Name, alluding to Ayin [Nothingness]. When one merits the primordial light, the dew of Atika, one merits these three. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 1): The souls of converts too were at Mount Sinai, as the Sages said, "their mazal was there" — and mazal is a person's root, as I have written elsewhere on "a person has a mazal" and on children, life and sustenance, which "depend on mazal." Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 45): Of sustenance the Sages said that it "does not depend on merit" — that is, not on the service a person performs with knowledge and clarity when his mind is clear and settled — "but on mazal": holiness must be engraved in his heart so permanently that it does not budge even when his knowledge and clarity are diminished. This is called mazal because service flows from him of itself, even without his awareness; sustenance must be drawn from a place above merit, from the supernal will called mazal..):
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Moed Katan 28a):
"דְּלָאו בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִלְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָא מִלְּתָא",
"the matter depends not on merit, but rather on mazal,"
וְלִכְאוֹרָה זֶה נֶגֶד הַמְּבֹאָר בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת,
and seemingly this contradicts what is explained in the Torah and in the words of our Sages in numerous places,
דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
that everything is governed by exact justice,
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אָדָם נִדּוֹן עַל כָּל זֶה,
and on Rosh Hashanah a person is judged regarding all of these,
וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלֶּה.
and we pray every single day continually for these three necessities.

וְהַגַּם דִּ"שְׂכַר מִצְוָה בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא" (קִדּוּשִׁין לט735 Kiddushin 39b — Rava said: Whose opinion is this? It is R. Yaakov's, who says: There is no reward for a commandment in this world. As it is taught: R. Yaakov says: There is not a single commandment written in the Torah whose reward is stated alongside it that is not dependent upon the resurrection of the dead. A man's father said to him, Climb the tower and fetch me fledglings; he climbed the tower, sent away the mother and took the young, and on his way back he fell and died. Where is the goodness of this one's days, and where is the length of this one's days? Rather, "that it may go well with you" — in the world that is wholly good; "that your days may be long" — in the world that is wholly long. Rashi (s.v. "that is not dependent upon the resurrection of the dead"): The reward stated alongside the commandment is not paid out here at all; it is stated in this way to make known to you that there is no giving of reward except in the world to come. Tosafos (s.v. "the mishna refers to a case where they make him a good day and a bad day"): Rashi's reading is difficult, for Rava's "Whose opinion is this? R. Yaakov's" implies that until now the mishna had not been established according to R. Yaakov, whereas on Rashi's explanation Abaye too had established both the mishna and the baraita according to him. Rabbeinu Tam therefore explains that both the good day and the bad day are in this world — sometimes a good day is made for the wicked man so that he may receive the reward of his commandments here, and a bad day for the righteous man so that his sins may be scoured away here — and this is not like R. Yaakov, who holds that there is no reward for a commandment in this world at all. Maharsha: Do not object from all the promises of the Torah, which can only be understood of this world. R. Yaakov concedes that the merit of the community and its good deeds bring upon it in this world too all the blessings and good things named in the Torah, and the reverse for the community's sin; he spoke only of the individual, whose reward, when his merits are many, is wholly in the world to come, since here evil is done to him in order to give him merit there — and conversely one whose sins are many is given good here in order to drive him from the world to come. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kiddushin 39b): Because the reward that belongs to the commandments is so great, their reward is not in this world; and one cannot say that He pays part of the reward of a commandment in this world and part in the world to come, for there is no payment by halves — hence there is no reward for a commandment in this world. R. Yaakov concedes that a wicked man does receive payment for a commandment he performed, since his reward is not so great; and because it is not great it can be discharged here, for a great reward cannot be given in this world, as they said, "one hour of contentment in the world to come is better than all the life of this world." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 25): Every commandment has its own reward, in the world to come and also in this world through its fruits: only the reward of the commandment itself "is not in this world," but a reward of fruits exists for every commandment, each in its own way — like "tithe so that you become rich," or children for sending away the mother bird. The Mishnah's "things whose fruits a person eats [in this world]" means only that for these one is assured of eating the fruits here, whereas for other commandments the fruits too may remain for the world to come. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 4): Sins have a limit, as this world has a limit, but the commandments have none; therefore "there is no reward for a commandment in this world," since this world is bounded and the reward of the commandments has no bound. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 7): The world to come is the cessation of activity, where the righteous enjoy the radiance of the Presence, and Shabbos is a taste of it; though "there is no reward for a commandment in this world," it is for this reason that Shabbos is called a "good gift." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 13): Life does not depend on merit but on mazal because "there is no reward for commandments in this world"; but that is only the reward of a commandment done out of obligation, whereas what one does beyond the letter of the law the Holy One, blessed be He, repays in one's lifetime. That is why [the Gemara] lists acts of piety as the cause of long life. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 171): "There is no reward for a commandment in this world" because the Holy One, blessed be He, gives a full load, and this world cannot receive that abundance of good at all; so here only sins are repaid, unless one merits tasting the fruit of his deeds or of commandments that bear fruit. Hence a time, place or soul "prepared for calamity" [pur'aniyos] is prepared for repayment [pera'on]: there the abundance of the repayment becomes calamity, as in the breaking of the vessels through excess of light. Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 6): Because "there is no reward for a commandment in this world," Israel holds only the markers [tziyunim] of the good, while the essence of the good is with the nations; in the future both will be joined together with Israel, as the Blessed One returns the essence to the place of the markers — hence the blessing "Who returns His Presence to Zion [Tziyon].":),
And even though "there is no reward for a mitzvah in this world" (Kiddushin 39b),
הַיְנוּ דִּ"סְבִיבָיו נִשְׂעֲרָה מְאֹד",
signifying that "around Him it storms exceedingly,"
וּמְשַׁלֵּם הָעֹנֶשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהַשָּׂכָר שָׁמוּר לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כַּיָּדוּעַ;
so that retribution is exacted in this world while reward is preserved for the World to Come, as is known;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט כְּפִי הַזְּכוּת.
nevertheless, it proceeds through strict justice according to merit.

וְגַם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה736 Shabbat 156a — It was stated: R. Chanina says — there is a constellation that makes one wise and a constellation that makes one rich, and there is a constellation for Israel. R. Yochanan said: There is no constellation governing Israel. And R. Yochanan follows his own reasoning, for R. Yochanan said: From where do we know that there is no constellation governing Israel? For it is said, “Thus says the Lord: Learn not the way of the nations, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven, for the nations are dismayed at them” — the nations are dismayed, but not Israel. Rashi: "A constellation makes one wise" — wisdom accords with the constellation, as it said [above] that one born under the sun will be bright and wise; "and there is a constellation for Israel" — for prayer and charity do not change the constellation. "There is no constellation governing Israel" — for through prayer and merit one's constellation is changed for the better. Tosafos (s.v. "there is no constellation governing Israel"): As for Rava's statement at the end of Moed Katan (28a), that children, life and sustenance depend not on merit but on the constellation: [the constellation] is nonetheless changed through great merit, though at times it is not changed; as it says in Yevamot, chapter HaCholetz (50a), "If he merits, they add to him; if he does not merit, they reduce for him." Maharsha: Tosafot wrote that through great merit [the constellation] is changed; but then, according to R. Chanina, who says there is a constellation for Israel, even great merit would not change it — yet all the Torah's promises, the blessings "if you hearken" and the curses "if you do not hearken," imply no such thing, but make [Israel's lot] depend on their merit or guilt. One may answer that the Torah's promises were said of the community of Israel, and the merit of the many certainly does not depend on the constellation at all; they dispute here only concerning the individual, R. Chanina holding that a constellation makes that individual wise or rich, and R. Yochanan that there is no constellation for Israel even for an individual — for he expounds "the nations are dismayed," but not Israel, even a single Israelite. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 156a): [R. Yochanan] means that the constellation can be outweighed through mitzvos, even without any prayer — for that prayer avails is obvious, since the Blessed One does as He wishes in heaven and on earth. The community of Israel has in itself a supernal, separate level, as does the individual when he performs a divine mitzvah, and this stands above the constellation. This does not mean that the constellation has no hold on them at all — when it stands strongly against Israel they need great merit to outweigh it, as in Egypt, where it portended evil and the Blessed Name turned it to good for the merit of the forefathers — but that they are not wholly under the constellation as the other nations are. (שַׁבָּת קנו.): "אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל",
Furthermore, our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shabbat 156a): "There is no mazal for Israel,"
וְזֶה הִקְשׁוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
and this was raised as a difficulty by the Tosafot, see there.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַךְ מַזָּלָא אֵינוֹ מִמַּזְּלוֹת הָרָקִיעַ שֶׁהָאִצְטַגְנִינִים יוֹדְעִים,
However, in truth this mazal does not refer to the celestial constellations known to astrologers,

שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שָׁם)737 Shabbat 156a — It was stated: R. Chanina says: A constellation makes one wise, a constellation makes one wealthy, and Israel is subject to a constellation. R. Yochanan says: Israel is not subject to a constellation. And R. Yochanan follows his own reasoning, for R. Yochanan said: From where do we know that Israel is not subject to a constellation? As it is stated, "Thus said the Lord: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of heaven, for the nations are dismayed by them" — they are dismayed, but Israel is not. Rashi: "A constellation makes one wise" — wisdom accords with the constellation, as it said [above] that one born under the sun will be bright and wise; "and there is a constellation for Israel" — for prayer and charity do not change the constellation. "There is no constellation governing Israel" — for through prayer and merit one's constellation is changed for the better. Tosafos (s.v. "there is no constellation governing Israel"): As for Rava's statement at the end of Moed Katan (28a), that children, life and sustenance depend not on merit but on the constellation: [the constellation] is nonetheless changed through great merit, though at times it is not changed; as it says in Yevamot, chapter HaCholetz (50a), "If he merits, they add to him; if he does not merit, they reduce for him." Maharsha: Tosafot wrote that through great merit [the constellation] is changed; but then, according to R. Chanina, who says there is a constellation for Israel, even great merit would not change it — yet all the Torah's promises, the blessings "if you hearken" and the curses "if you do not hearken," imply no such thing, but make [Israel's lot] depend on their merit or guilt. One may answer that the Torah's promises were said of the community of Israel, and the merit of the many certainly does not depend on the constellation at all; they dispute here only concerning the individual, R. Chanina holding that a constellation makes that individual wise or rich, and R. Yochanan that there is no constellation for Israel even for an individual — for he expounds "the nations are dismayed," but not Israel, even a single Israelite. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 156a): [R. Yochanan] means that the constellation can be outweighed through mitzvos, even without any prayer — for that prayer avails is obvious, since the Blessed One does as He wishes in heaven and on earth. The community of Israel has in itself a supernal, separate level, as does the individual when he performs a divine mitzvah, and this stands above the constellation. This does not mean that the constellation has no hold on them at all — when it stands strongly against Israel they need great merit to outweigh it, as in Egypt, where it portended evil and the Blessed Name turned it to good for the merit of the forefathers — but that they are not wholly under the constellation as the other nations are. דְּ"אֵין מַזָּל וְכוּלֵי" עַל יְדִיעָתָם מִצַּד מַעֲרֶכֶת הַמַּזָּלוֹת,
concerning which they said (there) that "there is no mazal, etc.," negating astrological influence,
כִּי אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט עֶלְיוֹן יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ כְּפִי כִּשְׁרוֹן נַפְשׁוֹתָם.
for with the children of Israel everything is governed by supernal divine judgment according to the fitness of their souls.

אֲבָל מַזָּלָא זֶה הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בָּבָא קַמָּא (ב:) וּבְשַׁבָּת (נג738 Shabbat 53b — And is there such a thing as an amulet proven effective for a person and not proven effective for an animal? Yes: a person, who has a mazal, is aided by it; an animal, which has no mazal, is not aided by it. Rashi: "Mazal": his angel, who intercedes on his behalf. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos): This implies that an amulet proven for an animal is all the more effective for a person, who has a mazal; but then the Gemara's next question — "if so, what is 'this is a stringency with an animal'?" — is difficult, for that would itself be a stringency with an animal. He suggests, with some strain, that the Talmud takes it as settled that an amulet proven for an animal is likewise not thereby proven for a person. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:90): "A person has a mazal," which Rashi explains as the interceding angel, means his hidden root, from which he is wholly drawn; on it depend children, life and sustenance, the three general powers of the soul, and not on merit and deeds — so the main task is to rectify the root until it cleaves to the Lord even in its hidden aspects. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 1): The souls of converts too were at Mount Sinai, as the Sages said, "their mazal was there" — and mazal is a person's root, as I have written elsewhere on "a person has a mazal" and on children, life and sustenance, which "depend on mazal.":):
Rather, this mazal is what they stated at the beginning of Bava Kamma (2b) and in Shabbat (53b):

"אָדָם דְּאִית לֵיהּ מַזָּלָא739 Bava Kamma 2b — Why is it written of a person “if it gores” (Exodus 21:28), and of an animal “if it hurts” (Exodus 21:35)? A person, who has fortune — of him it is written “if it gores”; an animal, which has no fortune — of it is written “if it hurts.” Rashi: "A person, who has fortune" — who has the sense to guard his own body. "Of him it is written 'if it gores'" — because the ox certainly intended to do harm and came at him with force, whereas "hurts" would imply only that it found him standing and shoved him with its horns. Another reading: because he has fortune he is not easily killed by a shove, which is only a slight thrust of the horn, but only by goring — with force, with intent, and with the horn driven into the body. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bo 2): So we find: "A person, who has a mazal — 'if it gores' is written; an animal, which has no mazal — 'if it strikes [yigof]' is written," meaning a mere blow to the body, since, as Rashi there explains, the word derives from guf, "body." Hence the [first] seven plagues, whose purpose was to bring out from the seven lower [attributes] of the husk, which have the form of a body, are called "all My plagues [magefotai]," a term of "body," for through them the holy body of Israel was drawn out of the impure body of Egypt.",
"a human being who possesses a mazal,"
פֵּרֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ.
which Rashi explained: a guardian, advocating angel (malach meilitz).
וְהִנֵּה זֶה וַדַּאי מִצַּד הַזְּכוּת,
Now, this advocacy certainly stems from merit,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת740 Shabbat 32a — A man should never stand in a place of danger and say that a miracle will be performed for him — lest no miracle be performed for him; and if a miracle is performed for him, it is deducted from his merits. Rashi: "Deducted": that is, diminished. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 32a): When a miracle is performed for a man he goes out of the natural order, and so it is deducted from his merits, which are not natural at all but are kept for him for the World to Come, which is above nature. When the Blessed One deals with a man above nature and performs a miracle for him, He deducts it from those merits, for the man is then consuming in this world what was due to him in the World to Come. (לב.) עַל פָּסוּק "אִם יֵשׁ עָלָיו מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ וְגוֹמֵר",
as they expounded in Shabbat (32a) on the verse: "If there be for him an advocating angel, etc.,"
וְהוּא פָּשׁוּט גַּם כֵּן, כִּי אֵין מְלִיצָה וְלִמּוּד סַנֵּגוֹרְיָא אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁבָּאִים בְּמִשְׁפָּט.
and this is also straightforward, for there is no defense advocacy except when undergoing judgment.
וְאָמְנָם שׁוֹרֶשׁ עִנְיַן מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
Yet the primal root of this advocating angel belonging to each member of Israel,
וַאֲפִלּוּ לְתִינוֹק בֶּן יוֹמוֹ, כִּדְמוּכָח מֵהָא דְּרֵישׁ בָּבָא קַמָּא,
even unto a day-old infant, as proven from the opening of Bava Kamma,
אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ אֵינוֹ מַלְאָךְ הַנּוֹצָר עַל יְדֵי עֲשִׂיַּת הַמִּצְווֹת.
perforce cannot be an angel created via the performance of mitzvot.
רַק דְּעֶצֶם נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם, שֶׁהִיא חֲצוּבָה מִכִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים,
Rather, man's essential soul, being hewn from the Throne of Glory which transcends the angelic realm,
הִנֵּה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִכָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו,
contains elements from all the worlds situated beneath it;
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁכָּל עוֹלָם עֶלְיוֹן הוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּחְתָּיו,
for as is known, every higher world encompasses all that lies beneath it,
שֶׁהֲרֵי מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא מִתְפַּשֵּׁט וְיוֹצֵא.
since from it lower reality expands and emanates.

וּכְדִשְׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג741 Chagigah 13a — Above them are the holy creatures. The feet of the creatures are equal to all of them [the firmaments together]; the ankles of the creatures are equal to all of them; the shins of the creatures are equal to all of them; and so the knees, the thighs, the bodies, the necks, the heads, and the horns of the creatures — each is equal to all of them. Above them is the Throne of Glory: the feet of the Throne of Glory are equal to all of them, and the Throne of Glory is equal to all of them; and the King, the living and enduring God, high and exalted, dwells above them. Rashi: "The feet of the creatures" — the thickness of their hooves; the ankles are the joints above them; the shin is the bone sold together with the foot; the knee is the thigh bone adjoining the shin; and the thigh is the hip bone set into the loins. Tosafos (s.v. "and the feet of the creatures are equal to all of them"): Some emend the Kedushah composed by the Kalir — "and the creatures, foursquare beneath the Throne, the sole of a foot, five hundred and fifteen" — striking out the "and," since by the reckoning here the seven firmaments and the eight spaces between them come to fifteen times five hundred. But they struck it out needlessly, for the Kalir framed his words after the Jerusalem Talmud, where a single foot is said to be greater still; and it was his way in many places to leave the reckoning of our Talmud in order to hold to that of the Jerusalem Talmud. Maharsha: The eight spaces must be counted thus: one from the earth to the firmament, then seven firmaments with six spaces between them, which is fourteen, and the sole of the foot, five hundred, counted as a fifteenth — fifteen times five hundred in all. But since our passage says that the feet of the creatures are equal to all of them, meaning to all the five hundreds already counted, the sole of the foot cannot be the same as "the feet of the creatures." And "the horns of the creatures" spoken of here must be the horns of the ox of the Chariot, since horns do not apply to the others..):
And as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Chagigah 13a):
"רַגְלֵי הַחַיּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד כֻּלָּן, קַרְסֻלֵּי וְכוּלֵי",
"the feet of the Chayyot equal all of them, the ankles, etc.,"
וְכֵן כָּל מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה הוּא כְּנֶגֶד כֻּלָּן שֶׁלְּמַטָּה.
and likewise whatever is above outweighs all that is beneath it.

וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח:)742 Sanhedrin 38b — Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create man, He created one company of ministering angels. He said to them: Is it your will that we make man in our image? They said before Him: Master of the Universe, what are his deeds? He said to them: Such and such are his deeds. They said before Him: "What is man that You are mindful of him, and the son of man that You think of him?" He stretched out His little finger among them and burned them. Maharsha: This is explained by what the Midrash Rabbah says: when the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create man, the angels divided into factions — Kindness said, "Let him be created, for he performs acts of kindness"; Truth said, "Let him not be created, for he is all falsehood"; Righteousness said, "Let him be created, for he does righteous deeds"; Peace said, "Let him not be created, for he is all strife" — and the two factions here are those of Truth and of Peace. "Such and such are his deeds" means acts of kindness and righteousness, and they answered, "What is man [enosh]" — he is all falsehood, like the idolatrous generation of Enosh — "and the son of man [ben adam]" — he is all strife, like Cain, who quarreled with his brother Abel and killed him. His "finger" is the attribute with which He created the world ("Your heavens, the work of Your fingers"), namely kindness, as it is said, "the world is built by kindness"; with it He "burned" the factions, that is, He prevailed over them with the attribute of kindness to create the world — and kindness is the third faction, which consented to the world's creation. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 38b): The first and second factions depart from the balanced middle and so lack the simplicity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and are not close to Him; they therefore accused man, since from the side of the wicked man does not merit to be created — hence "What is man that You are mindful of him?" "He stretched out His little finger among them and burned them": when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to annul a creation He does it with the slightest thing, a small touch — merely touching and drawing near to them burns them — as in "he did not touch me even with his little finger" (Shabbat 13a); for whatever has come into being, even a being separate from matter, is subject to annulment. Alternatively, the little finger stands for man, the smallest beside the angels on high: as a hand without its little finger is lacking, so the world is incomplete without man, and therefore it was the little finger that opposed them and burned them.: מַה שֶּׁאָמַר "נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם", שֶׁאָמַר לַמַּלְאָכִים,
And as they stated (Sanhedrin 38b): when Hashem said "Let us make man," He addressed the angels;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לָהֶם "נַעֲשֶׂה",
and since the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them "Let us make,"

אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ח)743 Bereshit Rabbah 8:8 — R. Shmuel bar Nachman said in the name of R. Yonatan: When Moses was writing the Torah, he would write the work of each day; when he reached this verse, "And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness," he said before Him: Master of the worlds, why do You give an opening to the heretics? He said to him: Write, and whoever wishes to err will err. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Moses, this man whom I have created — do I not raise up from him both great and small? Should a great man come to take permission from one smaller than himself and say, Why must I take permission from one smaller than I? — they will say to him, Learn from your Creator, who created the upper and the lower worlds, and yet when He came to create man He took counsel with the ministering angels. שֶׁזֶּה לִמּוּד דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ לִמָּלֵךְ וְכוּלֵי744 Rashi, Genesis 1:26 — Even though they did not assist Him in forming man, and there is here an opening for the heretics to assert their claim, Scripture did not refrain from writing it — to teach the way of courtesy and the trait of humility: that the greater should consult and take permission from the lesser.,
even though our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 8) that this teaches proper conduct to consult others, etc.,
וַדַּאי לֹא נִכְתַּב דְּבַר שֶׁקֶר,
Scripture certainly did not record a falsehood;
רַק שֶׁהָרוֹצֶה לִטְעוֹת יִטְעֶה לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהָאֲמִירָה הוּא כְּאִלּוּ צָרִיךְ לְשִׁתּוּפָם,
only that one wishing to err may err, thinking that the statement implies He required their partnership,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה אֶלָּא לִמּוּד דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.
whereas in truth it is simply a lesson in humility and derech eretz.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת, אֲמִירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם", עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא נִתַּן בּוֹ כֹּחַ מִכָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
Yet in absolute truth, Hashem's utterance "Let us make man" spontaneously instilled within him potency from all the worlds;
וְזֶהוּ עִקָּר "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ", שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and this is the primary meaning of "in our image"—encompassing all cosmic realms, as is known.
וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁבּוֹ שַׁיָּךְ זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה;
And the evil inclination stems from this physical world wherein merit and culpability apply;

אֲבָל בַּמַּלְאָכִים אֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פט745 Shabbat 89a — [Moses said to the ministering angels:] Again, what is written in it? "Honor your father and your mother" — do you have a father and a mother? Again, what is written in it? "You shall not murder," "You shall not commit adultery," "You shall not steal" — is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you? At once they conceded to the Holy One, blessed be He. Rashi: "Is there jealousy among you?" — through which you would come to murder. Maharsha: Once it had been shown that even the hidden part of the Torah is within man's reach, through the soul that is bound to the Throne of Glory, Moshe argued that the Torah should be given to him rather than set in heaven, on account of its revealed part — "what is written in it?" Therefore "at once the ministering angels conceded" that it is more fitting to give the Torah to Israel than to set its glory and secret in heaven, since the revealed Torah has no application in heaven. Maharal (Derush al HaTorah 5): Moshe answered each of the first five commandments separately but the later ones in a single reply, because the first five are between man and God — "Honor your father and your mother" among them, for there are three partners in a person, and one who honors his parents is accounted as having honored the Holy One, blessed be He — while the last five are all between man and his fellow. These are joined together, since a sin against people leaves its mark on the one sinned against, whereas of a sin against Heaven it is said, "If you have sinned, what do you effect against Him?" Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 24): Moshe's "what is written in it?" means that although the angels grasp of themselves that there is an order ordained by the Blessed One, the order itself belongs to man alone: the Torah, though created before the world, is arranged according to man's humanity — its commandments correspond to his 248 limbs — and, like the Divine image, which needs a physical body to bear it, it rests upon physical things, the practical commandments, and requires a physical bearer. That was the answer to the angels, and therefore "they conceded.".),
whereas among angels there is no evil inclination, as our Sages stated (Shabbat 89a),
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לָהֶם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֲמִירַת שִׁירָה.
yet they nevertheless engage in spiritual exertion, which is the chanting of celestial song.
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהֶם, גַּם זֶה אֵין שַׁיָּךְ,
However, in the realm above them, even exertion is inapplicable,

רַק קַבָּלַת הֶאָרָה כְּטַעַם (בְּרָכוֹת יז.)746 Berakhot 17a — Rav was wont to say: The World to Come is not like this world. In the World to Come there is no eating and no drinking, no procreation and no commerce, no envy and no hatred and no rivalry. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads and take delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “And they beheld God, and they ate and drank” (Exodus 24:11). Rashi: "And they ate and drank" — they were sated by the radiance of the Divine Presence as though they had eaten and drunk. Maharsha: He derives the point from the redundancy and the change of wording in the verse: Scripture had already said "and they saw the God of Israel," and then says again "and they beheld God" — and "beholding" generally denotes an intellectual vision, a prophecy. They beheld and took delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence as though they had eaten and drunk; for at the giving of the Torah they were in the likeness of the World to Come, their crowns upon their heads, as it is said [in Shabbat 88a] that every Israelite received two crowns, and they were removed from bodily things, as it is said of Moses that he did not eat for forty days. Maharal (Derech Chaim on Avot 3:16): The meaning is that in the World to Come a man needs no completing, unlike this world, in which a man must receive his completion; there he will be complete on a higher level. He will therefore need no eating and drinking to complete himself, nor procreation — for offspring are a man's completion — nor commerce, by which a man supplies what he lacks; and there will be no envy or hatred, since these are themselves a defect. And "the righteous sit": the World to Come is not a thing of motion as this world is, and sitting signifies that a man is already complete in actuality and no longer moving toward his completion. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 4): Seeking to be a son of the World to Come purely for one's own sake is no different from seeking a reward in this world; but the essence of the World to Come, that "they delight in the radiance of the Shechinah," is not self-benefit. One can merit this even in this world — the "one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world" that is better than all the World to Come — when the reward of a mitzvah brings one to repentance, love and cleaving; for such a reward one may hope, and serving for it is wholly for its own sake, out of love. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 7): Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come, and the World to Come is the absence of the action of "today to do them" — only "the righteous [sit] … and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah" — and Shabbat holds a semblance of this, which is why, though there is no reward for mitzvos in this world, Shabbat is called "a good gift." In this world one employs the powers of action, whereas the World to Come is the heart alone. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): From within this world, which is likened to night, they will merit the light of the World to Come, which is wholly day with no darkness or evil — the light of the world of Atzilus, the light of the seven days of creation hidden away for the righteous — when they sit "with their crowns on their heads," that is, their attachment to their root in the Blessed One, "and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah," that is, the upper Shechinah. This is the first heh of the Name, alluding to the understanding in the heart, the secret of the World to Come, where the attachment of the hearts of Israel to their source is revealed. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 1): With the creation of man "tohu and bohu" were set aside, for a person can raise his actions without limit and reach a lofty place, as stated: "In the World to Come there is no eating and no drinking … rather the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah." Through the act of the mitzvah of shofar one arouses the "great shofar," which shows that Israel raise all their actions up to the "upper sun," to the place where the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah, and through the shofar one can reach with one's actions and service to the light of the Infinite.: "צַדִּיקִין יוֹשְׁבִים וְכוּלֵי וְנֶהֱנִים וְכוּלֵי",
there being only the reception of divine radiance, as in: "the righteous sit crowned, delighting, etc." (Berakhot 17a),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם לְמַעְלָה מָּעְלָה.
which represents the root of man's soul in the ultimate heights.
וּמִצַּד שָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים הוּא הַמַּלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ, דְּהַיְנוּ כֹּחַ נַפְשׁוֹ עַצְמָהּ,
And from the perspective of its root in the angelic realm, that root is the advocating angel—namely the spiritual power of his own soul;
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא "מַזָּלָא", שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁנָּפַל לְגוֹרָלוֹ בַּתּוֹלָדָה,
therefore it is termed "mazal," representing the soul's root allotted to his portion at birth,

שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (נִדָּה טז:)747 Niddah 16b — R. Chanina bar Pappa expounded: The angel appointed over conception is named Night. He takes the drop and sets it before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says before Him: Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop? Mighty or weak? Wise or foolish? Rich or poor? Rashi: “Everything is in the hands of Heaven” — all a man's qualities and all that befalls him come upon him by the decree of the King, except this one. “But to fear” — this alone He asks of you, because everything else is in His hand and this is in yours. Tosafos (s.v. “the angel appointed over conception”): But over birth no angel is appointed, as is said at the beginning of Ta'anit: three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He — of a woman in childbirth, of rain, and of the resurrection of the dead. Even those three keys are at times handed over to an agent for a time, for Elijah held the key of rain and revived the dead, and so did Elisha and many righteous men; and even Beri, who is the prince of rain, acts only by the permission of the Holy One, blessed be He. Tosafos (s.v. “everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven”): In “Elu Na'arot” it is said that everything is in the hands of Heaven except cold and heat. Here the statement concerns a man's nature and his traits, while there it concerns the things that befall him, such as illnesses and calamities, all of which are decreed upon him and against which he cannot guard himself — except cold and heat, against which he can guard himself. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “this drop, what shall become of it — mighty or weak, wise [or foolish]”): This is the meaning of the verse “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom”: what is compelled is neither praised nor blamed, and therefore these three — wisdom, might and wealth — which are compelled by the decree from the hour of a man's formation, are no ground for glorying. “But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me” — for that is the thing which depends upon his choice. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 16b): He is called Night because the gestation takes place in the woman's belly, “like the bones in the womb of her that is with child,” and the child is there in darkness. Therefore the angel appointed over gestation is called Night, since in the belly it is always night and never day. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The Sages said that "children, life and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal," for these three comprise all of a man's needs in this world, and this is decreed at the beginning of his formation: "wise or foolish" — and "wisdom gives life to those who possess it," so from it life is drawn; "mighty or weak" — from this come children, "like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth"; "rich or poor" is the flow of sustenance. But "righteous or wicked," which is a matter of merit, he did not say.: "טִפָּה זוֹ מַה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי",
concerning which they taught (Niddah 16b): "This drop, what shall become of it, etc.,"
רָצָה לוֹמַר: אֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ יֻשְׁפַּע בָּהּ.
meaning: which specific soul shall be channeled into it.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מ748 Shemot Rabbah 40:3 — While Adam the first man still lay a shapeless mass, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him every righteous man destined to arise from him: one is suspended from Adam's head, one from his hair, one from his forehead, one from his eyes, one from his nose, one from his mouth, one from his ear, one from his earlobe. Know this: when Job sought to argue with the Holy One, blessed be He, He answered him, "Where [eifo] were you when I founded the earth?" R. Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him — Job, tell Me from what place your measure [eifah] was suspended, from his head or from his forehead or from which of his limbs; if you know where your measure was, you may argue with Me.),
And as written in Shemot Rabbah (Parashah 40),
דְּכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מֵאֵיפַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן:
that all souls derive from the stature of Adam the First:
יֵשׁ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ וְיֵשׁ בְּרַגְלוֹ,
some stem from his head and some from his foot,
וּלְכָל אֶחָד כֹּחַ מְיֻחָד.
and each possesses a designated spiritual power.

וּמְלִיצַת הַמַּלְאָךְ, לְפִי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵרוֹת "מַתִּישִׁין כֹּחַ פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה" (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה פֶּרֶק א, פָּסוּק ו749 Eikhah Rabbah 1:33 — R. Yehuda son of R. Simon said in the name of R. Levi son of R. Tarfon: When Israel do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, they add strength to the might above, as it says, "And now, let the power of the Lord be great"; and when they do not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, they, as it were, weaken the great power above — and they themselves also go "without strength before the pursuer." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on completing the Talmud 5): A deficiency can touch the mind only through its link below to the heart, when it turns downward and not to its cause, for the arousal from below begets the arousal from above, and likewise the desire in the heart begets the thought in the mind; and this is [the meaning of] "You weakened the Rock that bore you," that they weaken the power of the heavenly household. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): By all opinions, addition of strength and weakening of strength certainly apply to the angels as well, as the Sages said on the verse "You weakened the Rock that bore you" that they weaken the power of the heavenly household, and on "Ascribe strength to God" that they add strength to the heavenly household. So Abraham our father, through his meal and the commandment of hospitality, added strength to the heavenly household and "sustained their hearts." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 2): All the supernal forces of holiness depend on man, as it is said on "You weakened the Rock that bore you" that they weaken the power of the heavenly household, and at the Destruction the wings of the Chayos and the heavenly household were diminished: for they too are part of the whole creation, which is all for the sake of man, the likeness upon the Throne who rides upon all of creation.),
And the angel's advocacy functions because through sins "they weaken the power of the Heavenly Host" (Eichah Rabbah 1:6);
וְאַף דְּשָׁם בְּעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים אֵין זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה,
and even though in the angelic world there is no intrinsic merit or guilt,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַזְּכוּת וְחוֹבָה שֶׁלְּמַטָּה כֵּן הוּא כֹּחַ הַשִּׁירָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּמַלְאָכִים,
nevertheless, corresponding to merit and guilt below, so is the power of the angels' song and striving,
רָצָה לוֹמַר מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם עֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
meaning because they are the essential celestial root for the souls of Israel.
וְכֹחַ הַמְּלִיצָה הוּא כְּפִי כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשִׂים,
And the potency of advocacy corresponds directly to the force of one's actions,
כִּי אֵין בְּחִירָה וְרָצוֹן בַּמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת מֵלִיץ וּלְהַגִּיד כָּךְ;
for there is no independent free choice in angels to elect to advocate and speak thus;
רַק שֶׁהוּא מִמֵּילָא,
rather it occurs automatically,
שֶׁכְּשֶׁהָאָדָם זַכַּאי, הֲרֵי כֹּחַ הַמַּלְאָכִי שֶׁבּוֹ לְמַעְלָה בְּעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים הוּא מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ.
that when man acts righteously, the angelic facet of his soul above in the angelic world becomes an advocating angel.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ בְּעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא מְקַבֶּלֶת אוֹרָהּ כָּרָאוּי לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לָרוּחַ וְלַנֶּפֶשׁ,
And the root of his soul in the World of the Throne receives its divine illumination to channel downward unto Ruach and Nefesh,

כְּטַעַם750 Yoma 39a — Our Rabbis taught: “And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy.” If a man sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him greatly; if he sanctifies himself below, they sanctify him from above; if he sanctifies himself in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come. Rashi: "And you shall sanctify yourselves": a little; "and you shall be holy": greatly. One who comes to purify himself is assisted. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTzedek 2): [Just as with defilement a man's own act counts as little, since he is a creature of body, yet he is defiled greatly on the side of the soul, from above,] so too with purity and holiness: if a man sanctifies himself a little (for man's deeds are deeds of the body, and that is only a little) they sanctify him greatly from above. And if a man sanctifies himself in this world, they sanctify him in the World to Come, which is the supreme holiness above all; understand, then, how when a man sanctifies himself in holiness, they sanctify him with a supreme holiness. (יוֹמָא לט.): "מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ מִלְּמַעְלָה".
mirroring the principle: "they sanctify him from Above" (Yoma 39a).
וְנִמְצָא כְּפִי זֶה: הַכֹּל תָּלוּי בִּזְכוּתָא,
Thus according to this perspective, everything depends entirely on merit, –
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַבְּחִירָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and this reflects the vantage point of free choice in this world,
וּמִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה דֶּאֱמֶת, הַכֹּל תָּלוּי בְּמַזָּלָא, וּבֶאֱמֶת כֻּלָּא חַד],
while from the vantage point of ultimate Divine Foreknowledge, everything depends on mazal, and in truth all is one,
וְאָמְנָם עִם כָּל זֶה, בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ רְשָׁעִים שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֲלֵיהֶם כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַצַּדִּיקִים, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and yet with all this, in this world there are wicked people who receive what seems fitting for the righteous, and vice versa.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה751 Berakhot 7b — R. Yitzchak said: If you see a wicked man upon whom the hour is smiling, do not contend with him, as it is said, “His ways prosper at all times.” And more than that — he prevails in judgment, as it is said, “Your judgments are far above him.” And more than that — he sees his foes fall, as it is said, “As for all his adversaries, he snorts at them.” Rashi: "His ways prosper" — yachilu means they succeed, as in "therefore his prosperity shall not endure" (Job 20:21). "Your judgments are far above him" — Your judgments are removed far away from him; and "he snorts at them" means that with his very breath he drives them off like straw. Maharsha: His prosperity is certainly only for an hour, as that psalm itself says, "for they shall soon wither like grass" and "yet a little while and the wicked is no more" — it is the fortune of the hour that does it for him. And "his ways prosper at all times" likewise means all that time in which his fortune prospers him; it is from the words "at all times" that R. Yitzchak inferred that a man must beware of him, in law and in provocation alike, for as long as his ways prosper through the fortune of the hour. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaShalom 3): They came to teach that contention is a very ugly trait, but that it is not ugly everywhere, for strife with the wicked and with those who forsake the Torah is good. When the matter is one of Heaven, then he should contend with the wicked man — when the hour is not smiling upon him. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Thirteen Principles of Conduct 12): One upon whom the hour smiles prevails in the judgment of Heaven, being judged as righteous for the time being. So too in human judgment, pleading for mercy is effective even before a court and a Sanhedrin, for through it he may prevail in judgment: not that they will pervert the judgment, but that their eyes will be opened to find merit, since in every matter there is a scale of merit and a scale of guilt. And now that there is no Sanhedrin, Heavenly judgment, the judgment of the four death penalties and other punishments have still not ceased, and through mercy he prevails in judgment and goes free. (בְּרָכוֹת ז:) עַל רָשָׁע שֶׁהַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ:
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Berakhot 7b) concerning a wicked person for whom the hour prospers:
"מָרוֹם מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ מִנֶּגְדּוֹ",
"Your judgments are on high, out of his sight,"
וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר זֶה, וַהֲלֹא כָּל מִשְׁפָּטָיו אֱמֶת?
and how is this possible, when all His judgments are Truth?
רַק דְּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה,
Rather, in truth there is no person who does not contain both merit and culpability,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אֲפִלּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת",
and as they said: "even the transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvot,"
וְ"אָדָם אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר וְגוֹמֵר".
and "there is no righteous man upon earth who does good and sins not."
וְעִנְיַן שִׁקּוּל הַזְּכִיּוֹת וְהָעֲבֵרוֹת
And the weighing of merits against transgressions
כְּבָר כָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהֵם שְׁקוּלִים רַק בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
was already articulated by Maimonides in Hilchot Teshuvah: they are weighed solely in Hashem's knowledge;
וְיַצִּיב פִּתְגָם, כִּי אֵין בָּזֶה יְדִיעָה כְּלָל;
and the matter is solid, for man has no comprehension of this calculation whatsoever;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת: "זֶה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה",
even though our Sages noted in various passages: "this mitzvah is greater than that one,"
הוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל כְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה,
that applies generally according to the Torah's legal framework,
אֲבָל מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּפִי פְּרָטֵי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, אֵין שׁוּם נֶפֶשׁ דּוֹמָה לַחֲבֵרוֹ.
whereas supernal judgment regarding individual souls treats no two souls alike.
וְזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק דְּמַזָּלָא שֶׁאֵין תָּלוּי בִּזְכוּתָא,
And this is the distinction of mazal not depending on generic merit:
דְּהַגַּם דְּתַרְוַיְהוּ צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים וְשָׁוִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם,
that even if both individuals are complete tzaddikim identical in their deeds,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵצֶל זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ אוֹתוֹ מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ עַל יְדֵי זְכִיּוֹת יְדוּעוֹת
nevertheless, in this one the power of that advocating angel is aroused by specific merits
לְהַזִּיל עָלָיו שֶׁפַע בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי מִמַּזָּלוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹן,
to pour down upon him an influx of children, life, and sustenance from his supernal mazal,
וְלֹא אֵצֶל זֶה,
while in that one it is not;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשָׂה גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָן זְכִיּוֹת,
and even though he performed those exact same merits,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּהִשָּׁפְטוֹ כְּפִי שׁוֹרֶשׁ מַזָּלוֹ יִהְיֶה נִדּוֹן בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר.
nevertheless, when judged according to the unique root of his mazal, he is evaluated differently.
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ בָּרְשָׁעִים: יֵשׁ דְּ"מָרוֹם מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ",
And likewise conversely among the wicked: there are instances of "Your judgments are on high,"
שֶׁאֵין כֹּחַ בְּמִדַּת מִשְׁפָּט לְדוּנוֹ עַל רִשְׁעָתוֹ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הַמְּשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ
where strict justice lacks the immediate mandate to punish him during that hour when fortune smiles upon him,
מִצַּד אֵיזֶה זְכוּת הַמַּרְעִישׁ כְּנֶגְדָּם וּמְחַפֶּה עַל הַכֹּל לְפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַשָּׁעָה.
owing to some extraordinary merit that clamors on his behalf and shields everything for that hour's judgment.
וְהַדְּבָרִים אֲרֻכִּים בְּדֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵם כִּבְשׁוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
And these matters are vast concerning the supernal pathways of judgment, touching the deep secrets of the cosmos.
וְהַכְּלָל: דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
And the guiding rule is: everything proceeds by exact justice,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה תָּלוּי בְּמַזָּלָא,
and with all that, it remains dependent upon mazal—
דְּהַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁל זְכִיּוֹת וְחוֹבוֹת לְעִנְיַן הַמְשָׁכַת בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה תָּלוּי בְּמַזָּלָא.
for the judicial evaluation of merits and debts regarding the drawing down of children, life, and sustenance in this world is determined by the soul's mazal.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Prayer above Mazal
Prayer reaches beyond the soul's fixed root, while Purim's mitzvot draw Torah, life, sustenance, and continuity into the world.

p: וְעִנְיַן הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ו:)752 Berakhot 6b — One of the Sages said to Rav Beivai bar Abaye, and some say Rav Beivai said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: What is "when vileness is exalted among the sons of men"? He said to him: These are matters that stand at the summit of the world, and men treat them lightly. Rashi: "When vileness is exalted" — this is the end of the verse cited above ["The wicked walk round about"]. "Matters that stand at the summit of the world" — such as prayer, which ascends on high. Maharsha: It is evident that this refers back to the opening of the verse: one who prays around the synagogue, that is, outside it, is called wicked, because he treats prayer lightly — and prayer is among "the matters that stand at the summit of the world." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Tehillim 34): Although in human eyes the deed seems to be the main thing, the chief guarding is truly of the mouth and tongue, for everything is clarified through the tongue — as the Baal Shem Tov explained the Gemara's "things that stand at the height of the world": it is words [spoken words] that stand at the height of the world. As the holy Zohar says, "once he has brought a word out of his mouth, that word becomes a voice, splits the airs and firmaments, and rises on high."
As for prayer, concerning which our Sages of blessed memory said (Berakhot 6b)
שֶׁהוּא מִדְּבָרִים הָעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
that it is among the matters standing at the height of the world,
הַיְינוּ בִּמְקוֹם הַמַּזָּלָא שֶׁהוּא מְרוֹמָם מֵעִנְיַן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר.
this means at the level of mazala, the soul's supernal root, which transcends the affairs of this world, as mentioned.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא פּוֹעֶלֶת שִׁינּוּיִים בְּמַזָּלָא,
Prayer brings about changes in mazala;
וְזֶה כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ עִנְיַן הַתְּפִלָּה,
and this is the entire foundation of prayer:
כִּי הַמַּזָּלָא הוּא הַמְקַבֵּל וְנֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה,
mazala receives and delights in the radiance of the Divine Presence,
וְהַתְּפִלָּה הוּא לְהַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
whereas prayer is addressed to the One who bestows that abundance, blessed be His Name.
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַהַשְׁפָּעָה מִלְמַעְלָה
According to the strength of the abundance bestowed from above,
כֵּן הוּא הַהִשְׁתַּנּוּת בִּבְנֵי חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי נֶגֶד הַמַּזָּל.
so are the changes in children, life, and sustenance, contrary to what one's mazal would otherwise determine.
וְאַף דְּתָלֵי בְּמַזָּלָא,
Although these depend on mazala,
הַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁמִּתְרַבֶּה הַשֶּׁפַע
this means that through prayer, which increases the abundance,
הֲרֵי מִמֵּילָא מַזָּלוֹ עַצְמוֹ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ זֶה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ מִקּוֹדֶם.
his own mazal consequently bestows upon him what he previously lacked.
וְאוּלָם גַּם זֶה עֲדַיִין תָּלוּי בְּמַזָּלָא,
Yet even this still depends on mazala,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא מִקֵּץ ט)753 Midrash Tanchuma, Miketz 9 — R. Yose bar Chalafta says: There are set times for prayer, as it is said, "But as for me, may my prayer to You, O Lord, be at a favorable time." When is a favorable time? When the congregation is praying. עִתִּים הֵם לִתְפִלָּה,
as they said (Midrash Tanchuma, Miketz 9): there are appointed times for prayer.
וְאֵין לְךָ שֶׁהִרְבָּה בִּתְפִלָּה יוֹתֵר מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְלֹא נַעֲנָה,
No one prayed more than Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, yet his request was not granted.
כִּי גַּם קַבָּלַת הַשֶּׁפַע הוּא רַק כְּפִי הָרָאוּי לְפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ וְחֶלְקוֹ מִמַּעַל,
For receiving the abundance, too, is limited to what is fitting for one's root and portion above;
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַבֵּל יוֹתֵר כְּלָל פְּעָמִים.
and sometimes a person cannot receive anything further at all.
וְגַם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה מִשְׁפָּטִים שׁוֹנִים.
In this, too, there are many differing judgments.
וְאוּלָם הַתּוֹרָה עוֹד לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה,
Torah, however, stands higher still:

דְּמַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אָחִיד בְּכוֹלָּא (זוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קֹרַח)754 Zohar 3:176a — R. Abba opened: "More desirable than gold, than much fine gold, and sweeter than honey and the drippings of the comb" (Psalms 19:11). How exalted are the words of the Torah, how precious they are, longed for above and longed for by all — for they are the Holy Name; and whoever labors in the Torah labors in the Holy Name, and is delivered from all — delivered in this world and delivered in the world to come. Come and see: whoever labors in the Torah takes hold of the Tree of Life, and once he takes hold of it he takes hold of everything, as it is written, "It is a tree of life to those who grasp it." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): Of the three pillars of the world, Torah is the middle line, for "whoever takes hold of the Torah takes hold of everything," while acts of kindness are from Abraham's side and service from Isaac's. One who has kindness alone may still produce dross, as Ishmael came from Abraham, and one who has service alone may produce the dross of idolatry; but the seed of Jacob, who holds the middle line, is a complete bed with no dross at all.,
whoever holds fast to Torah holds fast to everything (the holy Zohar, beginning of Parashat Korach).
כִּי הוּא מִדַּת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים,
For it is the attribute of truth given to Yaakov, an inheritance without boundaries,
כְּטַעַם אֲרוּכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ כּוּלֵּי,
as expressed by, 'Its measure is longer than the earth,' and so forth;
וְאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ אֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל.
and the limitation 'he cannot receive' does not apply.
וְהַתְּפִלָּה הוּא רַק כֹּחַ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה כְּפִי מִדַּת הַמְקַבֵּל שֶׁהוּא הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל.
Prayer draws forth abundance only according to the measure of its recipient, the person praying.
אֲבָל זְכוּת הַתּוֹרָה אֵינוֹ בָּא בִּתְפִלָּה עַל רִבּוּי הַהַשְׁפָּעָה,
But the merit of Torah does not operate through a prayer for increased abundance;
רַק שֶׁהִיא מִמֵּילָא מִתְרַבִּית עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
rather, that abundance increases of itself through Torah,
שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קַבָּלַת הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
for there lies the root from which all the souls of Israel receive abundance.
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּשָׁרְשָׁם בַּתּוֹרָה,
As is known, their root is in Torah:
דְּשִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא אוֹתִיּוֹת נֶגֶד שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע.
six hundred thousand letters correspond to six hundred thousand souls, as is known.
וְהַגַּם דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין כָּל אוֹת דּוֹמָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ,
Although each letter differs from the next,
וְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק יָדוּעַ בַּתּוֹרָה,
and each person has a particular portion in Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד חֶלְקוֹ אֵין לוֹ גְּבוּל לוֹמַר שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִמְנָע כְּלָל.
nevertheless, within that portion he has no limit that would make any matter altogether unattainable.
כִּי כָּל חֵלֶק עַצְמוֹ כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְעִיקַּר שָׁרְשׁוֹ וּדְבֵיקוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל,
For when any particular part reaches its essential root and its attachment to the whole,
הֲרֵי מִתְדַּמֶּה לַכֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ גְּבוּל כְּלָל,
it becomes like the whole, which has no boundary at all;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הִתְאַחֲדוּת הַחֵלֶק בַּכֹּל.
and through Torah the part becomes united with the whole.
וְזֶה סוֹד חָמֵשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת הַיְדוּעוֹת בְּשֵׁם נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה חַיָּה יְחִידָה,
This is the secret of the five levels of soul known as nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, and yechidah.
וִיחִידָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְאַחֵד לְגַמְרֵי בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ;
Yechidah means becoming completely united with Him, blessed be He;
זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
this is possible only through Torah,
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּה חַד.
for Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel are all one.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לָזֶה מִמֵּילָא אָחִיד בְּכוֹלָּא,
Whoever merits this consequently holds fast to everything,
שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר נִמְנָע מִמֶּנּוּ.
so that nothing is beyond his reach.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִמְשִׁילוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ קֹהֶלֶת)755 Kohelet Rabbah 1:1 — R. Simon said in the name of R. Shimon ben Chalafta: This may be compared to a courtier who was raised in the palace of kings. The king said to him: Ask what I shall give you. That courtier said: If I ask for silver and gold or fine pearls, he will give them to me; garments, he will give me. Rather, I will ask for his daughter, and everything will be given me together with his daughter. So too, "at Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said: Ask what I shall give you." Solomon said: If I ask for silver and gold and pearls, He will give them to me; rather, I will ask for wisdom, and everything is included in it.
As our Rabbis of blessed memory illustrated (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Kohelet),
בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ הַחָכְמָה וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכֹּל נָתוּן לוֹ,
King Shlomo, peace be upon him, asked for wisdom and thereby received everything,
לְנוֹשֵׂא בַּת מֶלֶךְ.
like one who marries a king's daughter.
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה מְאוֹרָסָה לִקְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב,
For Torah is betrothed to the congregation of Yaakov;
וּבְאִישׁוּת נֶאֱמַר וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד שֶׁהֵם חַד,
and of marriage it is said, 'They shall become one flesh'—they are one.
וּבְרָא כַּרְעָא דַאֲבוּהּ,
A child is like a limb of the father;
וְנִמְצָא הֵם חַד גַּם עִם הָאָב,
thus they are also one with the father.
וְזֶהוּ כּוּלָּא חַד הַנִּזְכָּר.
This is the 'all are one' mentioned above.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי,
This is what He has not done for any other nation.
דְּאַף שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְדָבָר טוֹב וּקְדוּשָּׁה,
For although they have no intrinsic connection to goodness and holiness,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הִתְקָרְבוּתָם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
nevertheless, through their drawing close to Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים וַעֲבָדִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
as in the future, when there will be converts who attach themselves and servants to Israel,
יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחִיזָה בִּקְצָת מַה שֶּׁיּוֹנְקִים מֵהֶם,
they have some attachment through what they draw from them,
וְעַד מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּפִלָּה,
even reaching the level of prayer,
עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through the prayer of King Shlomo, peace be upon him,
דְּגַם עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ יַעֲנֵם.
that He should answer even idolaters who pray toward the Temple.
אֲבָל לַתּוֹרָה אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת כְּלָל,
But they have no connection at all to Torah,
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין שָׁרְשָׁם בֶּאֱמֶת מִלְּמַעְלָה,
since their root is not truly from above,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד עֶצֶם הַכַּוָּנָה בַּבְּרִיאָה רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
meaning from the essential intention of Creation, but only from its outward extension.

דְּלָכֵן אֵין קְרוּיִם אָדָם (יְבָמוֹת סא.)756 Yevamot 61a — The graves of gentiles do not convey impurity by a tent, for it is stated: "And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are man" (Ezekiel 34:31) — you are called man, and the gentiles are not called man. Rashi: "Do not convey impurity": to one who overshadows them. "You are called adam": and with regard to the impurity of a tent it is written, "When a man [adam] dies in a tent" (Numbers 19:14). Tosafos (s.v. "and gentiles are not called adam"): It is difficult: in Avodah Zarah 3a and Sanhedrin 59a we expound that a gentile who occupies himself with Torah is like a High Priest, from "which a man [ha-adam] shall do and live by them" — it does not say "priests, Levites and Israelites" but "the man." Rabbeinu Tam explains that there is a difference between "adam" and "ha-adam": gentiles are included in "ha-adam," and all the verses the Gemara adduces here read "adam." R. Meshullam used to say that Israel alone are called "adam" specifically where Scripture speaks of calamity, since it did not wish to name Israel explicitly in that context. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 1): What distinguishes man from all other living creatures is that he has a divine soul, and those who have a divine soul are prepared for divine things such as prophecy and the holy spirit — which is found only in the people whom the Blessed Name chose.
