Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil.: הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת.
This is the meaning of the statement (Bava Batra 16a): he is the evil inclination; he is the Angel of Death.
וְעִקַּר הַחֵטְא נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים — שֶׁיֵּשׁ דֶּרֶךְ מְיֻחָד לַצַּדִּיק לֵאמֹר: "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ".
The very possibility of sin extends from the fact that the Blessed One created a path of the righteous—a defined path about which one can say, 'This is the way; walk in it.'
וּמִמֵּילָא, כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה הוּא חוֹטֵא, וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים גַּם כֵּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִבְּדָהּ מִפָּנָיו.
Consequently, one who does not walk that path becomes a sinner, and there is therefore also a possible 'way of the wicked'—except that He destroys it from before Him.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה)903 Bereshit Rabbah 8:4 — R. Berekhiah said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create the first man, He saw that righteous and wicked would issue from him. He said: If I create him, wicked men will issue from him; and if I do not create him, how are the righteous to issue from him? What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He removed the way of the wicked from before His presence, joined to Himself the attribute of mercy, and created him. This is what is written: "For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish" — He made it perish from before His presence, joined the attribute of mercy, and created him. עַל פָּסוּק "וְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים תֹּאבֵד".
As our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 5) on the verse, 'the way of the wicked shall perish.'

כִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה שֶׁיֵּלְכוּ רַק בְּדֶרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים, אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת הַהֵפֶךְ, צָרִיךְ לְ"נֵר מִצְוָה וְתוֹרָה אוֹר" לִהְיוֹת לִמְאוֹרוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל בְּדַרְכּוֹ.

The Blessed One's will is that people walk only in the path of the righteous; nevertheless, because the opposite path is possible, 'a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light' is required as a luminary so that a person not stumble on his way.
וּמִצַּד שֶׁהָאוֹר מְבָרֵר שֶׁזֶּה טוֹב, מִמֵּילָא נִגְלֶה גַּם כֵּן הַהֵפֶךְ.
Precisely because the light clarifies that this is good, its opposite is thereby revealed as well.

כִּי כֵן כָּל מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה בְּעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה — זֶה טוֹב וְזֶה רַע — וְהוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, דְּמִתַּמָּן פָּסוּל וְכָשֵׁר וְכוּלֵי, כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א)904 Zohar 1:27a — Another interpretation of "And a river goes out of Eden": Above, in the Tree of Life, there are certainly no alien shells, as it is written, "evil shall not sojourn with You." But in the tree below there are alien shells, and it is planted in the garden of Eden of the Lesser Countenance. Its shells are, from this side, good, and from that side, evil — and this is forbidden and permitted, fit and unfit, impure and pure. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): Had Adam not sinned, the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, which stands right beside the Tree of Life — for in truth it is all one — would also have been turned into the Tree of Life and the evil wholly consumed from the world; but through his sin even the Tree of Life of the Torah was turned to be "from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, fit and unfit, impure and pure," as stated in the Tikkunim. It seems to me that these correspond to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah: had Adam not sinned, everything would have been in writing, with no need for an Oral Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 2): "Haman — where is he alluded to in the Torah? 'Is it from the tree [ha-min ha-etz]'" [Chullin 139b] means that through Haman they merited the light of the Oral Torah; this is alluded to in "the tree," following what the holy Zohar says, that there is Torah from the side of the Tree of Life, namely the Written Torah, and Torah from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, which is forbidden and permitted, impurity and purity. The tree Haman made fifty cubits high corresponded to the fifty gates of understanding in the Oral Torah, which is from the side of the Tree of Knowledge..

So too, all the Torah's positive and negative commandments establish: this is good and this is evil. This belongs to the aspect of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, from which come the categories of invalid and valid, etc., as is known from the Zohar (Part I, 27a).
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַיְדִיעָה וְאוֹר הַדַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הַמֵּאִיר בַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
Through knowledge and the light of da'at—the level of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him—which illuminates the soul,
נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד טֶבַע הַבְּרִיאָה הַנּוֹתֶנֶת גְּבוּל לְכָל דָּבָר, שֶׁיּוּכַל לָצֵאת מֵהַגְּבוּל וְלָדַעַת רַע גַּם כֵּן.
the very nature of Creation, which sets a boundary for each thing, also makes it possible to cross the boundary and thereby know evil.
וְעַל זֶה צָרִיךְ הָאוֹר, שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יְבָרֵר אֹכֶל מִפְּסֹלֶת וְנִפְרָד הַפְּסֹלֶת וְהָרַע מִן הַטּוֹב.
For this one needs the light, through which food is separated from refuse and the waste and evil are separated from the good.
וְהַפְרָדָתוֹ — זֶהוּ תַכְלִית עָנְשׁוֹ, כִּי כָל חִיּוּתוֹ הוּא רַק דִּבּוּקוֹ לַטּוֹב.
That very separation is the essence of evil's punishment, because all of its vitality exists only through its attachment to the good.
וּכְמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חִיּוּת, הוּא לָהוּט אַחַר הָרַע וְנֶהֱנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ.
Thus in this world, while vitality remains within a person, he can be passionately drawn after evil and derive pleasure from it.

וְיָדוּעַ דְּ"אַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם", וְכָל חִיּוּת וְהַרְגָּשַׁת דָּבָר הוּא רַק מִכֹּחַ נִיצוֹץ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמְחַיֵּהוּ וְנוֹתֵן בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַרְגָּשָׁה לַהֲנָאוֹת וּלְכָל דִּבְרֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן.

It is known that 'You give life to them all.' Every vitality and every capacity to feel exists only through the Divine spark that gives a thing life and grants it the power to experience pleasure and all other phenomena of this world.
וְנִמְצָא, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָרַע מְחֻבָּר לַטּוֹב, שֶׁהוּא הַנִּיצוֹץ הַנּוֹתֵן בּוֹ חִיּוּת וְכֹחַ וְהַרְגָּשָׁה, אֵינוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ בְּרָעָתוֹ, וְאָז הוּא נִקְרָא חֵטְא.
As long as evil remains attached to the good—the spark that gives it life, power, and sensation—it does not fully experience its own evil; in that state it is called sin.
אֲבָל הָעֹנֶשׁ הוּא הַפְרָדַת הַטּוֹב, וְנִשְׁאָר הָרַע לְבַדּוֹ; מִמֵּילָא אָבְדוּ הֲנָאוֹתָיו וְהַרְגָּשׁוֹתָיו לֵאמֹר לָרַע טוֹב, וְנַעֲשָׂה רַע גָּמוּר.
Punishment is the separation of the good, leaving the evil by itself. It thereby loses the pleasures and sensations through which it called evil good, and it becomes revealed as unmitigated evil.
וּכְמוֹ בְּמִיתַת הָאָדָם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַכְלִית עֹנֶשׁ הַנִּכָּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁכְּשֶׁנִּפְרָד חִיּוּתוֹ נִשְׁאָר הַחֹמֶר עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה.
This is like human death, the most visible form of punishment in this world: when life departs, the material body remains as dust of the earth.
וְכֵן דִּין דְּלֶעָתִיד עַל יְדֵי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ הַמֵּאִיר לַצַּדִּיקִים; וּרְשָׁעִים אֵין יְכוֹלִים לִסְבֹּל, וּבָזֶה נִדּוֹנִים.
So too will judgment occur in the future through the sun that shines for the righteous; the wicked cannot endure it, and by this they are judged.
כִּי כַאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ תֹּקֶף אוֹר, הוּא קוֹלֵט הַטּוֹב אֵלָיו, וְהָרַע נִפְרָד לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִסְבֹּל תֹּקֶף אוֹר הַזֶּה.
When an overwhelming light arrives, it gathers the good into itself, while evil separates away because it cannot bear the intensity of that light.

וְגַם הַמִּיתָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ, פִּסְקָה קג)905 Sifrei Bamidbar 103 — R. Dosa says: What is the meaning of "for no man shall see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20)? While he is alive he does not see, but he does see at the hour of death. And so it says: "Before Him shall bow all who go down to the dust, and he who cannot keep his own soul alive" (Psalms 22:30). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): When it is revealed that everything comes from the root in the Blessed One, the screen that sins made between Israel and their Father in heaven is removed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is shown to them before their eyes, even though "no man shall see Me and live" — for the Sages said that "at the hour of their death they see," since then the screen of this world is removed. So too, with the revelation of [Isaac's plea] "half upon You," the screen of this world will be removed.: הָא בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתָן רוֹאִין, וְאֵין הַגּוּף סוֹבְלוֹ, וְנִפְרָד עַל יְדֵי זֶה.

Death itself follows this pattern, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Sifrei Beha'alotekha, piska 103): at the moment of death they see, but the body cannot bear the vision, and therefore it separates.
וְכָל מִינֵי שִׁקּוּעַ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת — הַכֹּל בָּא מִצַּד אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ שֶׁל אוֹר הַנּוֹתֵן חִיּוּת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, עַד שֶׁמִּתְאַוִּים לוֹ.
Every form of immersion in this world found among the idolatrous nations derives from some spark of light that gives vitality to that thing and thereby makes it desirable.

וְזֶה נִמְשָׁךְ מִיּוֹם רְבִיעִי, אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְרָא דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים הַכָּלוּל בִּתְלָת אֲבָהָן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וּמַתְחִיל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם וּלְהָאִיר לְתַלְמִידֵיהֶם: "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ יֵלְכוּ בוֹ".

This extends from the fourth day, after the path of the righteous—contained within the three Patriarchs, as explained above—has been created and begins to spread outward to their descendants and illuminate their students: 'This is the way; walk in it.'
כֵּיוָן שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הַגְדָּרָה, הֲרֵי נַעֲשָׂה מָקוֹם לִמְצִיאוּת הַהֵפֶךְ.
Once a boundary and definition are necessary, room is thereby made for the existence of the opposite.
וּמִזֶּה הוּא כָּל חִיּוּת עִנְיָנִים הַחָמְרִיִּים, מֵאַחַר שֶׁעָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת עִנְיָן זֶה, מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ חִיּוּת לְאוֹתוֹ מְצִיאוּת.
This is the source of the vitality in all material matters: since the possibility of such an existence entered the Divine plan, that existence necessarily possesses some vitality.
רַק הַחִיּוּת הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַנִּצּוּחַ, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁלֹּא יֵלְכוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה וְשֶׁיְּנַצְּחוּהוּ.
But that vitality exists from the standpoint of the attribute of victory: the Blessed One desired that people not follow that path, but overcome it.

וּ"גְדוֹלָה נְקָמָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת" (בְּרָכוֹת לג.)906 Berakhot 33a — R. Ami said: Great is knowledge, for it was set between two letters [that is, between two Names of God], as it is stated: “For a God of knowledge is the Lord” (I Samuel 2:3). Rav Acha Karchina’a objected: If so, great is vengeance, for it too was set between two letters, as it is stated: “A God of vengeance is the Lord” (Psalms 94:1)! He said to him: Yes — in its own place it is indeed great. And this is what Ulla said: Why these two [mentions of] vengeance? One for good and one for evil. Rashi: "Between two letters" means between two mentions of the Divine Name. "In its own place it is indeed great" — in a place where vengeance is called for, it is a great thing. The two vengeances: one for evil, to take vengeance upon the nations who did not accept the Torah; and one for good, as is said in Bava Kamma — "He shined forth from Mount Paran," that He then declared their property ownerless to Israel. Maharsha: Knowledge is the highest of the three attributes — wisdom, understanding, and knowledge — and it is the holy spirit; and the Gemara says "between two letters" rather than between two words of the Name, because the letters of the Name are not like the letters of any other word that signify some thing, but rather one who knows how to combine the permutations of His Names is himself possessed of knowledge and the holy spirit, as Bezalel knew how to combine the letters with which heaven and earth were created. The two Names standing to the right and to the left of "knowledge" and of "Temple" are the Names of mercy and of might, and one who knows how to join them knows how to join the letters by which heaven and earth were created. The objection from vengeance is that vengeance has in it only strict judgment and might, and no joining of mercy with it; and the answer, "in its own place it is great," is that the vengeance taken upon the nations is itself mercy toward Israel — one for good and one for evil — and that is the joining of the two Names. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 14): Knowledge was set between two letters of the Name because one who possesses knowledge cleaves wholly to Him, blessed be He. Had knowledge been set beside a single Name, that too would have indicated cleaving to Him, but not complete cleaving — only cleaving in some respect; set between two Names, the cleaving through knowledge is complete. And as the Temple, which is likewise set between two letters of the Name, raises the world from its material rank to the divine rank that is separate from matter, so through knowledge a man goes out from the material rank to the divine rank. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Shemini): Knowledge and the Temple always encompass the will of God, which is why they were "set between two letters"; vengeance was not, for it is not good at all times: a person must aim the time, the person and the place so that it accords with the will of the Blessed One, as Pinchas had to [with Zimri], since "zealots may strike him" applies only at the moment of the act. Thus a person must at times have the power of vengeance, provided he aims at the moment that is God's will, and be able to leap away from that trait at once, so that no anger or hatred remains in his heart afterward., שֶׁהֵם הַחֶסֶד וְהָרַחֲמִים, רֹאשׁ וְסוֹף דַּאֲבָהָן, שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים.

Thus 'great is vengeance, for it was placed between two Divine Names' (Berakhot 33a): these correspond to kindness and compassion, the beginning and end of the Patriarchal configuration, which together encompass the path of the righteous.
וּבֵינֵיהֶם יוֹצֵאת הַנְּקָמָה לְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים.
Between them emerges vengeance upon the way of the wicked.
וּמִצַּד יוֹם זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ קִלּוּסָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים עַל יְדֵי יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ, וְהַקִּלּוּס גַּם מִדֶּרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים.
From this day comes the praise of the righteous through the superiority of light over darkness, and praise emerges even from the way of the wicked.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז)907 Shemot Rabbah 7:4 — R. Levi said: This is like a king who had an orchard, and he planted in it barren trees and fruit trees. His servants said to him: What pleasure have you from these barren trees? He said to them: Just as I have need of fruit trees, so I have need of barren trees — for were it not for the barren trees, from what would I make my bathhouses and my furnaces? Therefore it says, "to the children of Israel and to Pharaoh": just as the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, rises to Him from the Garden of Eden from the mouths of the righteous, so it rises from Gehinnom from the mouths of the wicked. דְּכָךְ קִלּוּסוֹ עוֹלֶה מִגֵּיהִנֹּם,
As our Sages of blessed memory said (Shemot Rabbah, parashah 7), His praise rises even from Gehinnom,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא, בְּשַׁלַּח ז)908 Midrash Tanchuma, Beshalach 7 — "And I will be honored through Pharaoh" (Exodus 14:4). This tells that when the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts punishment from the nations, His name is magnified in the world, as it is stated: "And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those of them that escape to the nations... that have not heard My fame, nor seen My glory; and they shall declare My glory among the nations" (Isaiah 66:19). דִּכְשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה דִּין בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת נַעֲשֶׂה יִרְאוּי וּמִתְרוֹמֵם.
and as they taught (Midrash Tanchuma, Beshalach 7), when He executes judgment upon the idolatrous nations He becomes feared and exalted.

items.h:
Seif 4 — The Fifth Day: Life within Materiality
Animate life shows divine vitality entering lower matter and strengthening even those who begin from spiritual weakness.

p: וְיוֹם חֲמִישִׁי, שֶׁבָּרָא עוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים לְשַׁבֵּחַ לִשְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת מְצִיאוּת חִיּוּת בְּחֳמָרִים עֲפָרִיִּים.
On the fifth day He created birds and fish to praise His Name; this was the beginning of animate life within earthly material.
כִּי עַד הֵנָּה נִבְרָא חִיּוּת רוּחָנִי, וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן אוֹר דְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּמְאוֹרוֹת דְּיוֹם רְבִיעִי.
Until then the vitality that had been created was spiritual; this is the meaning of the light of the first day and the luminaries of the fourth day.

שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַהֲלִיכָה בְּדֶרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים לָאָבוֹת וְלַבָּנִים — רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לַחְפֹּר בְּעִמְקֵי לְבָבוֹ וּמוֹחוֹ עַל יְדֵי "תּוֹרָה אוֹר", אוֹ מִי שֶׁכְּבָר עִמְקֵי לִבּוֹ טוֹב מִתּוֹלָדָה וְדַי לוֹ בְּהִתְנַהֲגוּת דְּ"נֵר מִצְוָה".

This marks the beginning of walking in the path of the righteous, for fathers and children: either one must dig into the depths of heart and mind through 'Torah is light,' or one's inner heart is already good by nature and the guidance of 'a mitzvah is a lamp' is sufficient.
וְכָל זֶה מֵאִיר רַק לְמִי שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מוּאָר, וּלְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה.
All of this light shines only for one who is fit to be illuminated; toward the idolatrous nations, hatred descended at Sinai.

אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא כֵן, וְעַל זֶה גַּם כֵּן נָתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵצוֹת לְכַפֵּר וּלְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם בְּדַרְגָּא דְּאַהֲרֹן, שֶׁהוּא הַמְכַפֵּר בַּקָּרְבָּנוֹת.
But in truth there are also Jews who are not yet on that level; for them too the Blessed One provided means of atonement and repair through the level of Aaron, who brings atonement by the offerings.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מִסֵּפֶר יוֹסִיפוֹן, שֶׁהָיוּ קוֹרְאִין לַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל: "הַמְכַפֵּר בַּעֲדֵנוּ".
As is known from Sefer Yosippon, they called the High Priest 'the one who atones on our behalf.'
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַהוֹדָאָה בְּוִדּוּי דְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי כָל קָרְבָּן, וּ"מוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם".
This operates through the attribute of acknowledgment: verbal confession precedes every offering, and 'one who confesses and abandons will be shown mercy.'
וְזֶהוּ הוֹד מֶלֶךְ — הוֹדוֹ וְהוּא הֲדָרוֹ, שֶׁמּוֹחֵל וְסוֹלֵחַ.
This is royal hod: His glory and splendor are manifest in His forgiving and pardoning.
וְדָבָר זֶה, לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ אוֹר וְחִיּוּת גַּם לַחֳמָרִים גַּשְׁמִיִּים שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִים לְקַבֵּל חִיּוּת, נִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּיוֹם חֲמִישִׁי.
This new capacity—to extend light and vitality even into coarse material that appears unworthy of receiving life—was introduced on the fifth day.
וְזֶהוּ עִקַּר הַשֶּׁבַח לִשְׁמוֹ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר הַפַּיְטָן: "וְאָבִיתָ תְהִלָּה" וְכוּלֵי, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
This is the deepest praise of His Name, in the sense expressed by the liturgical poet, 'You desired praise,' etc., as is known.
דְּזֶה תַכְלִית כַּוָּנַת הַבְּרִיאָה: שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ גַּם הַמְּקוֹמוֹת הַנִּרְאִים מְרֻחָקִים בְּיוֹתֵר.
For this is the ultimate intention of Creation: that even the places that appear most distant should recognize the power of His kingship.

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "הַרְנִינוּ" וְגוֹמֵר — דְּרִנָּנָה בְּרַמְשָׁא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, רכט, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)909 Zohar 1:229b — And with all this, a man must serve before the Holy One, blessed be He, in joy, and show joy in his service. And these two — gladness and song — correspond to those two: two prayers, and two offerings each day corresponding to these two, which are gladness and song. Gladness in the morning, and song in the evening; and therefore, "the one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at dusk" (Numbers 28:4)..
Regarding this they said, 'Sing aloud,' etc.—for song is at evening (Zohar I, 229b).
הַיְנוּ, כְּשֶׁמֵּאִיר בִּמְקוֹם אֹפֶל גַּם כֵּן, מִזֶּה נִמְשֶׁכֶת רִנָּה, שֶׁהוּא הֶגְיוֹן רֹב עָם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הוֹד וַהֲדַרַת מֶלֶךְ.
When light shines even in a place of darkness, this produces rinah—a many-voiced murmur of the multitude—from which the glory and splendor of the King emerge.

כְּמוֹ לְשׁוֹן רִנָּה בַּתַּלְמוּד (יְבָמוֹת לד:)910 Yevamot 34b — When Ravin came he said in the name of R. Yochanan: Any woman who waited ten years after her husband [died] and then married will no longer bear children. Rav Nachman said: They taught this only where she had no intention of marrying, but if she did intend to marry, she conceives. Rava said to the daughter of Rav Chisda: The Sages are murmuring about you. She said to him: My mind was set on you. Rashi: "To the daughter of Rav Chisda": Rava's wife. "About you": that you waited ten years after your first husband, who was Rami bar Chama [and yet bore children]. Tosafos (s.v. "my mind was set on you"): Rabbeinu Tam said: this was because of the incident in the first chapter of Bava Batra (12b), where the daughter of Rav Chisda said, "I want both of them," and she was waiting for her prophecy to be fulfilled; since Rava had another wife, she was late in marrying him, and even so she was waiting for him. עַל לָזוּת שְׂפָתַיִם, שֶׁהַכֹּל מְרַנְּנִין אַחֲרָיו; דְּדִבּוּר הַרְבֵּה בְּנֵי אָדָם נִקְרָא רִנָּה.
This resembles the Talmudic use of rinah (Yevamot 34b) for public rumor, when everyone talks about a person; the speech of many people together is called rinah.
וּלְפִי שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים בְּכָל דּוֹר הֵם מוּעָטִים, אֵין שָׁם רִנָּה רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמְשָׁכַת חִיּוּת וְאוֹר בִּכְלָלוּת הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, גַּם הַיּוֹתֵר פְּחוּתִים בָּהֶם.
Because the righteous in every generation are few, there can be no many-voiced rinah unless vitality and light are extended to the entire Israelite nation, including even its lowest members.
וְזֶהוּ "עֻזֵּנוּ": כִּי מֵעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת עָתִיד לִפָּרַע, אֲבָל לָנוּ הוּא עֹז וּמָעוֹז בְּיוֹם צָרָה.
This is the meaning of 'our strength': He will exact punishment from the idolatrous nations, but for us He is strength and a stronghold in a day of trouble.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקַּר הוֹרָאַת מִלַּת "עֹז" — מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְאַמְּצוֹ, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהוּא בְּהֵפֶךְ מִזֶּה, אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֹז לוֹ.
The word oz, strength, especially implies strengthening one who needs to be fortified—one who is presently in the opposite condition—yet the Blessed One becomes his strength.
כִּי אוֹר חִיּוּתוֹ שׁוֹפֵעַ גַּם בַּפָּחוּת שֶׁבַּפְּחוּתִים.
For the light of His vitality flows even into the lowest of the low.

items.h:
Seif 5 — The Sixth Day and Shabbat: Unity and Completion
Creation's scattered powers become one, preparing Shabbat as the exclusive union of Hashem and Israel.

p: וְיוֹם שִׁשִּׁי, שֶׁגָּמַר מְלַאכְתּוֹ וּמָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם.
On the sixth day He completed His work and reigned over them.
הַיְנוּ הִתְאַחֲדוּת וְהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת כָּל הַפְּרָטִים לְאֶחָד.
This means the unification and binding together of all the particulars into one.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשְּׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הֵם אָפְנֵי הַהַשָּׂגוֹת וְקִלּוּסִים דְּדֶרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים — שְׁנֵי קְצָווֹת וְיוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי הַמְאַחֵד —
Just as the first three days represent the modes of apprehension and praise belonging to the path of the righteous—two extremes and the third day that unites them—
כָּךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים אֵלּוּ הַקִּלּוּסִים דְּדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים: שְׁנֵי קְצָווֹת.
so these latter three days express the praises emerging from the path of the wicked, likewise through two extremes.
הָאֶחָד מִצַּד הָאוֹר הַשּׁוֹפֵעַ לַצַּדִּיקִים, שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ הַנְּקָמָה לָרְשָׁעִים, וְהוּא הַיָּמִין דּוֹחָה.
The first is the light that flows to the righteous, whose very intensity brings punishment upon the wicked; this is the right hand pushing away.
וְהַשֵּׁנִי הוּא הַשְּׂמֹאל מְקָרֶבֶת גַּם לַיֵּצֶר וְלָרְשָׁעִים, לִהְיוֹת גַּם בָּהֶם נִמְצָא דָּבָר טוֹב.
The second is the left hand that draws near even the inclination and the wicked, because some element of good is found within them too.
וְהָאֶמְצָעִי מְאַחֵד וּמְקַשֵּׁר הַכֹּל, שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת "אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ".
The middle path unites and binds everything, for in truth 'there is nothing besides Him.'
וְזֶהוּ תַכְלִית גְּמַר מְלַאכְתּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הַמּוֹלֵךְ בֵּין עַל הַצַּדִּיקִים בֵּין עַל הָרְשָׁעִים.
This is the ultimate completion of His work: He reigns both over the righteous and over the wicked.
וְ"צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם" — שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ נִשְׁעָן עָלָיו, וְעַל יָדוֹ הַכֹּל אֶחָד.
'The righteous one is the foundation of the world': he is the foundation upon which the whole rests, and through him everything becomes one.
כִּי בֶאֱמֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בַּעַל אֵבָרִים רַבִּים.
In truth, the entire world is like one person composed of many limbs.
וְכֵן "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" — אַף הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁבָּהֶם, שֶׁצְּרִיכִים לְכַפָּרָה וּתְשׁוּבָה, זֶהוּ מִצַּד פְּרָטִיּוּתָם; אֲבָל מִצַּד הִתְאַחֲדוּתָם עִם הַכּוֹלֵל, כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים.

So too, 'Your people are all righteous.' Even those among them who are wicked and require atonement and repentance are so only from the standpoint of their individual state; from the standpoint of their union with the collective, they are all righteous.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (כְּרִיתוֹת ו:)911 Keritot 6b — Rav Chana bar Bizna said in the name of R. Simeon the Pious: Any fast that does not include some of the transgressors of Israel is not a fast — for galbanum's odor is foul, and yet Scripture numbered it among the spices of the incense. Abaye said: [It is derived] from here — "and has founded His bundle upon the earth" (Amos 9:6). Rashi (s.v. "and His bundle"): "And His bundle" — the word implies that only when they are all together is it "founded upon the earth." Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): He was precise to say "and Scripture numbered it among the spices" rather than "and it is burned with them": the point is that the transgressor is counted with them in their fast and does not separate himself from them. And from the hint one may learn further: as there were eleven kinds of spice, ten of good odor and one, galbanum, of foul odor, so the transgressor may be joined to them where there is a holy congregation of ten without him, but he is not to be counted as one of the ten. A remembrance of this is "I will not destroy for the sake of the ten" (Genesis 18:32) — for fewer than ten [Abraham] did not pray. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTeshuvah 7): The incense belongs to the attribute of judgment, as it is written, "they shall put incense before You" (Deuteronomy 33:10); and therefore it is made of spices, which have fragrance, for fragrance belongs to the attribute of judgment. A fast likewise belongs to the attribute of judgment, and therefore there must be among them transgressors who overcome the force of their evil inclination in joining them in the fast — and this too is called "fragrance." Galbanum was numbered by Scripture among the spices of the incense precisely because its power is greater than that of all the other spices.: כָּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי, מֵחֶלְבְּנָה, שֶׁגַּם הֵם צְרִיכִים לְתוֹךְ הַקְּטֹרֶת, שֶׁהוּא קִשּׁוּרָא דְּכֹלָּא.

As our Sages of blessed memory taught (Keritot 6b), every fast that does not include the sinners of Israel, etc., is deficient, as learned from the galbanum; they too must be included in the incense, which is the bond of all.
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם צוֹרֶךְ לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לִקְרוֹתָם צַדִּיקִים, שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Since they have a necessary place within the Blessed One's will, they may in this collective sense be called righteous, for a righteous one is one who carries out the Divine will.
וְזֶהוּ גְּמַר מְלַאכְתּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא מוֹלֵךְ עַל הַכֹּל, וְהִיא בִּבְרִיאַת הָאָדָם בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים, הַשַּׁלִּיט עַל הַכֹּל.
This is the completion of His work: He reigns over all, expressed through the creation of man in the lower world, who is granted rule over all.
וְהוּא הַ"צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם", הַמְקַשֵּׁר כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Man, in this role, is the 'righteous one, foundation of the world,' connecting all created beings to the Blessed One.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה: "הַשֵּׁם מָלָךְ, גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ", שֶׁהַמְּלוּכָה הוּא לְבוּשׁ שֶׁל גֵּאוּת, דְּהַמֶּלֶךְ מִתְגָּאֶה עַל עֲבָדָיו.
Through this comes the verse, 'The Lord reigns; He is clothed in majesty.' Kingship is a garment of exaltedness, for a king must stand above his servants.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ912 Kiddushin 32b — Rav Ashi said: A king who waives the honour due him — his honour is not waived, as it is said, “You shall surely set a king over you” — that his awe be upon you. Maharsha: One might have argued from R. Tzadok's words about the honour of the Omnipresent that a king's waiver should all the more be effective. But the world is God's own and the kingship is His, so He may waive His honour, as was said above of a Nasi and of a teacher; whereas the kingship of a king of flesh and blood is not his own — it is only a likeness of the kingship of Heaven, and it is from Heaven that he is set up, as it is written, "for kingship is the Lord's" — and a king of flesh and blood cannot waive the honour of the kingship of Heaven. (קִדּוּשִׁין לב:): שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ, וּמֶלֶךְ שֶׁמָּחַל וְכוּלֵי, כִּי לוּלֵי כֵן אֵין שֵׁם מְלוּכָה.
As they taught (Kiddushin 32b): 'His awe must be upon you,' and a king who waives his honor, etc.; without this there is no concept of kingship.

וְזֶהוּ בְּרִיאַת יוֹם שִׁשִּׁי — אָדָם הַמִּתְגָּאֶה עַל הַכֹּל (חֲגִיגָה יג:)913 Chagigah 13b — Reish Lakish said: What is meant by "I will sing to the Lord, for He is highly exalted"? Song to Him who is exalted above the exalted. For the Master said: The king among the beasts is the lion, the king among the domestic animals is the ox, the king among the birds is the eagle, and man is exalted over them; and the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted over all of them and over the whole world. Rashi: "The king among the beasts is the lion" and the rest — these four are on the Throne, and He is above them. Maharsha: By the sense of the passage man too is included in "highly exalted," since he is exalted over the exalted ones, the lion, the ox and the eagle. That the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted over them all rests on the close of the verse, "the horse and his rider He has thrown into the sea": man is exalted in riding upon the horse, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted over him, to cast the rider too — that is, man — into the sea. Maharal (Gevuros Hashem 47): The excellences are divided into four — wisdom, strength, wealth and honour, the four of which Ben Zoma spoke — and the Blessed One apportioned them among His creatures: wisdom to man, strength to the lion, wealth to the ox (for wealth is not silver and gold but the firmness and endurance it gives a man, and the ox has more endurance than any other living thing), and honour to the eagle, for honour is elevation, and no creature is more elevated than the eagle, whose way is in the heavens. No single creature is fitted to have more than one of these degrees; man is exalted over them all because his exaltation is that of intellect, which stands above the other excellences, and He, blessed be He, is exalted over all — this is "for He is highly exalted," meaning that nothing goes forth from Him that is not under His dominion. — כִּי זֶהוּ תַכְלִית כָּל מִינֵי הַקִּלּוּסִים, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִים הַמַּכִּירִים בּוֹרֵא.

This is the creation of the sixth day: man, who rises above all other earthly creatures (Chagigah 13b). This is the goal of every form of praise—that there be created beings who recognize the Creator.
כִּי אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם, וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עִנְיַן מְלוּכָה וּמֶמְשָׁלָה.
For there is no king without a people; Creation therefore allows kingship and sovereignty to be manifest.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יָצָא אָדָם תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה, שֶׁבּוֹ קָבוּעַ חֵשֶׁק זֶה גַּם כֵּן.
From this standpoint man emerged as the purpose of Creation, and this impulse toward rule is embedded within him as well.
כַּיָּדוּעַ, שֶׁזֶּה שֹׁרֶשׁ הַבְדָּלַת הָאָדָם מִן הַבְּהֵמָה, שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה, רוֹמֵז עַל בַּקָּשַׁת מֶמְשָׁלָה וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת, הֵפֶךְ כְּפִיפַת הָרֹאשׁ.
As is known, this is part of man's distinction from the animal: he walks erect, symbolizing a drive toward authority and elevation, the opposite of bending the head.
רַק הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת זוֹ עַל צַד הָרָאוּי הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּיהוֹשָׁפָט: "וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי הַשֵּׁם".
Yet this elevation, when proper, is like what is said of Jehoshaphat: 'his heart was elevated in the ways of the Lord.'
שֶׁבָּזֶה יִהְיֶה גֵּאוּתוֹ מִצַּד עִלָּתוֹ, שֶׁיִּבְזֶה בְּעֵינָיו לְהִתְעַסֵּק בְּעִנְיָנִים חָמְרִיִּים וְגַשְׁמִיִּים, בְּשׂוּמוֹ אֶל לִבּוֹ כִּי "חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עַמּוֹ".
His pride should derive from his higher Source: worldly and material preoccupations become small in his eyes when he takes to heart that 'the Lord's portion is His people.'
שֶׁנָּפוּחַ בְּקִרְבּוֹ חֵלֶק מֵעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּמִצַּד אוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק הָאָדָם מֶלֶךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וְרוֹדֶה בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים.
A portion from the Blessed One's own Divine vitality, as it were, has been breathed into him; by virtue of that portion, man is king among the lower beings and rules over the animals.
לֹא מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל, רַק מִצַּד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשּׁוֹפֵעַ בּוֹ.
This is not because of man's independent self at all, but because the Blessed One's kingship flows through him.
וְזֶהוּ גְּמַר מְלַאכְתּוֹ בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם — לִהְיוֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
This is the completion of His work in creating the world: that His kingship be manifest in the lower realm.

וְ"לֵב מְלָכִים אֵין חֵקֶר", שֶׁכָּל עִסְקֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם עָלָיו914 Shabbat 11a — Rava bar Mechasya said in the name of Rav Chama bar Gurya in the name of Rav: If all the seas were ink, and the marshes quills, and the heavens parchment, and all men scribes, they would not suffice to write down the empty space of government. What verse teaches this? Rav Mesharshya said: “The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.” Rashi: "The empty space of government": the depth of their heart, for [a ruler] must have a heart for many provinces, for the fixed tax, for many wars and for many judgments — and all in one day. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 11a): The king is set apart from the people and so has a separate, non-physical level not found in the rest of the people; and the heart is set apart from the body as the king is set apart from the people — hence "the heart of kings is unsearchable," for what is physical is bounded, but what is separate [from matter] has no bound. Therefore they said, "If all the seas were ink…": all these are physical things, which have an end and a limit, whereas the empty space of government has none. In its plain sense: how deep the empty space of government is cannot be written, for the heart of government is separate [from matter], and what is separate has no bound. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): In strength and wealth the king is forbidden excess, so King Solomon asked not for these but only for abundant wisdom, about which the Torah gave no warning; for "the heart of kings is unsearchable," and they need breadth of heart without limit or measure. This is the wisdom of Solomon, who asked for "a listening heart" and was given it as a gift of God, without limit. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Haazinu): People's hearts have different traits: one whose heart is drawn to pride is called "the heavens for height," and one drawn to sadness, "the earth for depth"; and "the heart of kings is unsearchable": a Torah scholar is called a king, and he must always guard himself from both of these. Beis Yaakov (Noach 6): "The heart of kings is unsearchable": how far the word of God branches out, and how far one must clarify the honor of His kingship in this world, has no limit, for even in the most remote garments one who looks deeply will find the honor of Heaven. This is what the Sages expounded, "if all the seas were ink... they would not suffice to write the empty space of government": the great void of the world that appears to a person's eyes as a place empty of the honor of Heaven; a person must bring the honor of Heaven into this place too, ascribing the lack to himself, for it appears empty only because of his own deficiency.; וְכֵן מִצַּד מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מוֹשֵׁל בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה הַנִּבְרָאִים.
'The heart of kings is unsearchable,' for all human affairs rest upon the king; similarly, through the Blessed One's attribute of kingship He rules over every action of created beings.

וְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דּוֹמֶה לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.)915 Avodah Zarah 3a — They said before Him: Master of the Universe, give it to us anew and we will perform it. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: Fools of the world! One who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat; one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat — from where will he eat on Shabbat? Rashi: "On the eve of Shabbat" means in this world. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "and sukkah is its name"): Since the nations claim to be fit for the Torah, which is intellectual and beyond nature, He gave them the commandment that shows a person going out of his nature: leaving his fixed, natural dwelling to sit in the shade of the sukkah. The nations, whose whole conduct is natural, cannot bear this and kick at it; Israel too are somewhat natural, for man is not an angel, and are exempt from the sukkah when it causes them suffering, yet they do not kick, for they desire and love to go beyond nature, only that at such times it is impossible for them. This shows that the Torah, the whole of which is beyond nature, is not fit for the nations at all. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat"): That is, this world is the physical world, which is always in potential, and therefore commandments and good deeds belong to it, for in it things go out from potential into actuality. But in the World to Come a person is already in actuality, and going out into actuality has no place there, since it is not physical; the World to Come is therefore cessation and rest. Hence he said that one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat, the day of action, will eat on Shabbat, the day of rest, on which nothing goes out into actuality — and so the commandments pertain to this world alone. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 25): Shabbat is [the day on which God Himself is one's light, needing no fire of fear]; nevertheless one must toil to cook the food on the eve of Shabbat, for "one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, what will he eat on Shabbat?" and "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward": this light does not come to a person by itself. So too the Shabbat lamp must be lit from the eve of Shabbat, for on Shabbat there is no longer time to arouse fear, the day being entirely love and cleaving to God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): This world is the world of toil, and "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat" refers to the world to come, the day that is entirely Shabbat, where there is no doing even of Torah and mitzvot, as they said, "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward"; and Shabbat is a semblance of the world to come, the time of the Blessed One's rest. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Sukkah): Shabbat alludes to the future, when there will be no labor, but only what a person acquired in this world through his deeds will then be fixed in his heart, according to how much he toiled in this world. Therefore all labors are forbidden on Shabbat in this world, and only what one toiled for on the eve of Shabbat does one eat on Shabbat. Beis Yaakov (Vayeishev 3): All the possession a person acquires for himself in the world of action comes only from performing the mitzvot, and clarity [of understanding] alone does not suffice; by this he acquires the life of the world to come, for this world is like the eve of Shabbat and the world to come like Shabbat, and "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will have what to eat on Shabbat." Tiferes Yosef (Shemini Atzeres 4): A person calls his labor "toil" only where he does not see its purpose; on Shabbat he attains the light of the Blessed One and recognizes that he attained it through the work of the six days. This is "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat": through the toil and labor he expended he attains this light, and so he recognizes retroactively that all the activity of the six weekdays was not futile toil for him either. Sod Yesharim (Sukkos 18): In the future the nations will want to begin from the start, without first entering the gate of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the Blessed One answers that this is impossible: "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat" means that had they first refined themselves to be included in Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, within "every citizen in Israel" [which includes converts], they too could have kept the mitzvah of sukkah. But to begin now without that prior inclusion is impossible, for one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat has nothing to eat on Shabbat, and from where would he gain a share in the mitzvah of sukkah?, שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא כָּל הַטֹּרַח וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דִּבְנֵי אָדָם לְהָכִין לְשַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
This world resembles the eve of Shabbat (Avodah Zarah 3a): it contains all of man's toil and effort in preparation for Shabbat, the seventh day.
עַל שֵׁם "שֶׁשָּׁבַת" — שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה וְגוֹמְרָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְנַפֵּשׁ מִיגִיעָתוֹ וּמֵשִׁיב רוּחוֹ אֵלָיו, וְאָז הוּא עִקַּר מְנוּחָתוֹ.
It is called Shabbat because 'He ceased': like a person who completes his labor and afterward refreshes himself from his exertion, recovering his spirit; that is when his true rest begins.
וְכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הֵם הַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁפָּעַל הַשֵּׁם לְמַעֲנֵהוּ לְקִלּוּסוֹ.
All six weekdays are the actions the Lord performed for His sake and His praise.

וְכֵן כָּל פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִזְכֹּר שֶׁהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ כֹּחַ לִפְעֹל מִצַּד מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה — כָּל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו גַּם כֵּן לְקִלּוּסוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
So too, every human action in this world can become His praise when a person remembers that the Blessed One grants him the power to act through His kingship, which rules over all.
וְקִלּוּס שֶׁל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא: "טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם" — הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַקִּלּוּס לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא דָּבָר טוֹב, וְאַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְכָךְ.
The praise of the Sabbath day is 'It is good to give thanks to the Lord': praising the Blessed One is itself a good, and fortunate is one who merits it.
וְהַנִּבְרָאִים מְקַלְּסִים אוֹתוֹ עַל זֶה עַצְמוֹ, מַה שֶּׁזָּכוּ לְקַלְּסוֹ.
Created beings praise Him for this very thing: that they merited the privilege of praising Him.
זֶה הוּא הַנַּיְחָא שֶׁל כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה וְכָל הַקִּלּוּסִים — כַּאֲשֶׁר הַנִּבְרָאִים מַגִּיעִים גַּם כֵּן לְנַיְחָא,
This is the repose of all Creation and all its praises: the creatures themselves also arrive at repose,
הַיְנוּ שֶׁאֵין זֶה אֶצְלָם בְּגֶדֶר עַבְדוּת וְשִׁעְבּוּד לְקַלֵּס, רַק שֶׁמְּקַלְּסִים בְּמַה שֶּׁזָּכוּ לְעָבְדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְקַלְּסוֹ.
meaning that praise is no longer experienced merely as servitude and obligation; rather, they praise Him for the very privilege of serving and praising Him.
וְזֶהוּ עִקַּר אוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
This is the essential meaning of Shabbat as the sign between Me and the children of Israel.
כִּי הָאֻמּוֹת, הַגַּם שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרוּ מִצְוֹת, הוּא מִצַּד הַהֶכְרֵחַ וְאַהֲבַת שָׂכָר וְיִרְאַת עֹנֶשׁ.
The nations, even when they observe commandments, do so from compulsion, desire for reward, and fear of punishment.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה: מִיָּד מְבַעֲטִין וְכוּלֵי916 Avodah Zarah 3a — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: I have one easy commandment, and sukkah is its name — go and perform it. At once each went and made a sukkah on his roof; and the Holy One, blessed be He, made the sun blaze upon them as at the summer solstice, and each of them kicked his sukkah and went out. Rashi: "On the top of his roof" — because they made most use of their roofs, which were not sloped. "Made the sun blaze [makdir]" is an expression of piercing: it bores through with the force of great heat, as in "one may cut through [makdirin] the hills" (Eruvin 58a). "In the season of Tammuz" — which runs on and extends a full three months, until the day of the Tishrei equinox. Maharsha: Every sukkah is made for shade, to shield from the sun, and one may make its covering as thick as one likes and it is still valid; so He blazed the sun upon them until the covering's leaves withered. That is the force of "made blaze [makdir]" — that holes opened in the covering, and the sun tormented them through them. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "and sukkah is its name"): Since the nations claim to be fit for the Torah, which is intellectual and beyond nature, He gave them the commandment that shows a person going out of his nature: leaving his fixed, natural dwelling to sit in the shade of the sukkah. The nations, whose whole conduct is natural, cannot bear this and kick at it; Israel too are somewhat natural, for man is not an angel, and are exempt from the sukkah when it causes them suffering, yet they do not kick, for they desire and love to go beyond nature, only that at such times it is impossible for them. This shows that the Torah, the whole of which is beyond nature, is not fit for the nations at all. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a, s.v. "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat"): That is, this world is the physical world, which is always in potential, and therefore commandments and good deeds belong to it, for in it things go out from potential into actuality. But in the World to Come a person is already in actuality, and going out into actuality has no place there, since it is not physical; the World to Come is therefore cessation and rest. Hence he said that one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat, the day of action, will eat on Shabbat, the day of rest, on which nothing goes out into actuality — and so the commandments pertain to this world alone. Sod Yesharim (Shabbos Chol HaMoed Sukkos 39): The mitzvah of sukkah completes the final clarification, that Israel are always bound to the Root while the nations are wholly cut off from it: Israel accept the Blessed One's command with no ulterior motive, in utter simplicity, desiring only to follow His will, whereas the nations, even when they accept His command, want it to give them power to bend His conduct to what is right in their own eyes. So when the Blessed One shows them that He leads them beyond their grasp and they cannot bend His conduct to their liking, they kick [their sukkah]; Israel, by contrast, nullify themselves before a conduct they cannot grasp and make of it a surrounding light, a sukkah sheltering over them., וּבְרֵישׁ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דִּבְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם "עַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס" נִקְרָא רָשָׁע.

As they taught at the beginning of Avodah Zarah, they immediately kick it away, etc.; and at the beginning of Rosh Hashanah, serving 'on condition of receiving reward' is characterized as wicked when describing the nations.
לְפִי שֶׁהֵם מְבַעֲטִין כְּשֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעֵם הַשָּׂכָר, כְּעֶבֶד הָעוֹבֵד אֶת רַבּוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ לֹא יִתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ.
For when the reward does not come, they rebel, like a servant who works for his master and afterward is not paid.
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּנִים לַהַשֵּׁם אֱלֹהֵיכֶם, וְאֵין מְבַקְּשִׁים שָׂכָר יוֹתֵר מִזֶּה שֶׁזָּכוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
The children of Israel, however, are children of the Lord your God; they seek no reward greater than the privilege of fulfilling the Blessed One's will.
וְהַנַּיְחָא שֶׁלָּהֶם — שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נַיְחָא מֵהֶם — זֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
Their repose consists in the very fact that the Blessed One has satisfaction from them; this is the sanctity of the Sabbath day.
שֶׁהוּא "אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל": שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ נַיְחָא מֵהֶם גַּם כֵּן רַק מִמַּה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם נַיְחָא.
It is 'a sign between Me and the children of Israel': the Blessed One's satisfaction from them comes precisely through their own repose in Him.
דְּזֶהוּ הַשַּׁבָּת דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהַנִּבְרָאִים מְקַלְּסִים בּוֹ "טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם" — שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם נַיְחָא מִזֶּה.
This is, as it were, the Sabbath of the Holy One, blessed be He: the creatures sing on it, 'It is good to give thanks to the Lord,' because they themselves find rest and delight in that praise.
וּמִי שֶׁטָּרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הוּא שֶׁיֹּאכַל בְּשַׁבָּת: כְּפִי טָרְחוֹ בְּקִלּוּסִין לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כָּךְ הוּא הַשַּׁבָּת — הַהֲנָאָה אַחַר כָּךְ מִקִּלּוּסִין אֵלּוּ.
He who labored on the eve of Shabbat is the one who will eat on Shabbat: in proportion to his toil in praising the Blessed One comes his Sabbath—the enjoyment that follows from those praises.
וּכְפִי הַשָּׂגַת הַהֲנָאָה דִּשְׁבִיתָה דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, כָּךְ הוֹלְכִים הַקִּלּוּסִין וְהַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ.
And in proportion to one's attainment of the delight of Sabbath rest, so proceed the praises and actions of the six weekdays that follow.

וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הָאָדָם, שֶׁקָּדַם אֶצְלוֹ שַׁבָּת לִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה (שַׁבָּת סט:)917 Shabbat 69b — Rav Huna said: If one was walking on the road or in the wilderness and does not know when Shabbat falls, he counts six days and observes one. Chiya bar Rav says: He observes one day and then counts six. In what do they differ? One holds that it follows the creation of the world, and the other holds that it follows Adam the first man. Rashi: "He counts six": from the day he realized that he had forgotten, and he observes the seventh. "He observes one day and counts six": not the day on which he realized it, for he may already have done work on it, but the following day; and on the days he does not observe he likewise does no work beyond what he needs for that day's sustenance, as is explained below. "Like the creation of the world": the weekdays were counted first; "like Adam the first man": who was created on the eve of Shabbat, so that the first day of his count was Shabbat..
This is from the human perspective, for whom Shabbat precedes the working days in the weekly cycle (Shabbat 69b).
דְּמִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹנֶה שִׁשָּׁה דְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַדֵּשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי דְּנַיְחָא, שֶׁהַנַּיְחָא דְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מִצַּד הַנִּבְרָאִים.
From the Divine perspective, however, six days of activity are counted first, followed by the sanctified seventh day of repose; His seventh-day repose comes from the creatures.
אֲבָל הָאָדָם, הַנַּיְחָא שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ נִמְשָׁכִים מִצַּד הַנַּיְחָא דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּפְעֻלּוֹתָיו.
Man's repose, by contrast, comes from the Blessed One, and man's subsequent actions flow from the Divine satisfaction present in His own works.
וְזֶהוּ "וַיְבָרֶךְ... וַיְקַדֵּשׁ". הַבְּרָכָה שַׁיָּךְ בְּאֵיזוֹ פְּעֻלָּה שֶׁהִיא מִתְבָּרֶכֶת; אֲבָל בִּשְׁבִיתָה וְהֶעְדֵּר פְּעֻלָּה, עַל מַה תָּחוּל בְּרָכָה?
This explains 'and He blessed... and He sanctified.' Blessing normally applies to an activity that can increase; but in cessation and the absence of activity, upon what can blessing take effect?
רַק לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל כֹּחוֹת פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם, מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהֵם קִלּוּסִין לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, נִמְשָׁכִים מִיּוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וּמְקַבְּלִים בִּרְכָתוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ.
In truth, all human powers of action, insofar as they become praises of the Blessed One, are drawn from the Sabbath day and receive their blessing from it.
וְזֶהוּ "בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן", שֶׁיָּרַד בְּיוֹם שִׁשִּׁי כִּפְלַיִם.
This is 'He blessed it with the manna': on the sixth day a double portion descended.
וְזֶה הַבְּרָכָה הָיְתָה בְּיוֹם שִׁשִּׁי, לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת; רַק שֶׁזֶּה הוּא הַטֹּרַח שֶׁבְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת כְּדֵי לֶאֱכֹל בְּשַׁבָּת.
That blessing was physically present on the sixth day, not on Shabbat; yet it was precisely the labor of the eve of Shabbat undertaken in order to eat on Shabbat.
וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּנֵי אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא טֹרַח זֶה לְהָכִין לְיוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת.
All human activity in this world is such labor, preparing for the day that is entirely Shabbat.
וּבִרְכַּת הֲכָנָה זוֹ לְצוֹרֶךְ הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הַבְּרָכָה לְטֹרַח דְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
The blessing of this preparation for Shabbat is itself rooted in the seventh day, from which blessing flows backward, as it were, into the labor of the eve of Shabbat.
וְהַקִּדּוּשׁ הוּא הָאֲכִילָה וְהַהֲנָאָה דְּשַׁבָּת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הֲנָאַת הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהַמְּנוּחָה מֵהַפְּעֻלָּה.
The sanctification, by contrast, is the eating and enjoyment of Shabbat itself—the pleasure of cessation and rest from activity.
וְזֶהוּ "קִדְּשׁוֹ בַּמָּן", כִּי לְעוֹלָם הַשֶּׁפַע חִיּוּת שֶׁל צֹרֶךְ קִיּוּם הַנִּבְרָאִים יוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וְלֹא פָסֵיק אֲפִלּוּ רֶגַע.
This is 'He sanctified it with the manna,' for the influx of vitality necessary to sustain creation constantly descends from Heaven and never ceases even for a moment.
דְּאָז הָיָה נִפְסָק, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, חִיּוּת הַכֹּל; וְזֶהוּ הַנִּרְמָז בַּמָּן, לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם.
If it ceased, Heaven forbid, the vitality of everything would cease; this continuing heavenly sustenance is symbolized by the manna, bread from Heaven.
וְיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי הוּא הַנַּיְחָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵחִיּוּת זֶה שֶׁמְּחַלֵּק לַנִּבְרָאִים.
The seventh day is the repose and satisfaction the Blessed One has from this vitality that He distributes to created beings.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ בְּרָכָה בְּחִיּוּת זֶה.
From this arises blessing within that vitality.
וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה — פֵּירוּשׁ הַבְדָּלָה — שֶׁחִיּוּת זֶה נִבְדָּל וְנִתְרוֹמֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִכָּלֵל בִּמְקוֹרוֹ, וּמוֹשֵׁךְ כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים מְקַבְּלֵי הַחִיּוּת.
Sanctity means separation and elevation: this vitality becomes elevated to be included in its Source, drawing upward all created beings who receive that vitality.
וְזֶהוּ הֶעְדֵּר הַיְרִידָה בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה מַעֲלֶה הַכֹּל לְמַעְלָה לִכָּלֵל בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים יִתְבָּרַךְ.
This is why there was no descent of manna on the seventh day: on the contrary, the day raises everything upward to be included in the Blessed Source of life.
וְזֶהוּ אַחַר שֶׁנּוֹתֵן בְּרָכָה בַּחִיּוּת, שֶׁיּוּכַל הָאָדָם לִטְרֹחַ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וִימֵי הַפְּעֻלָּה וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
First He grants blessing within vitality so that man can labor on the eve of Shabbat and throughout the days of action and effort in Divine service.
אַחַר כָּךְ קִדְּשׁוֹ בְּהֶעְדֵּר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, רַק לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
Afterward He sanctified it through the absence of effort, leaving only cleaving to the Lord, the living God.
וְהַדְּבֵקוּת הוּא "אוֹת בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם", שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק "אַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים" וְגוֹמֵר, וְ"לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי".
This cleaving is the 'sign between Me and you,' for it belongs specifically to 'you who cleave,' etc.; 'He has not done so for every nation.'
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּב וְכוּלֵי — דְּמִי יַכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ בֵּין לָבִיא וּלְבִיאָה בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּזְקָקִים זֶה לָזֶה, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה הוּא לְהִזְדַּקֵּק.

Thus an idolater who observes a Sabbath incurs liability, etc.; who would place his head between a lion and lioness at the moment of their intimate union, all the more so trying to insert himself into that bond?
וְעַל יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת נֶאֱמַר: "הַשֵּׁם בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ" וְגוֹמֵר.
And of the day that is entirely Shabbat it is said: 'The Lord alone will guide him,' etc.

sections.en: Love, Fear, and the True Will of Israel

items.h: Love and fear can be distorted into opposite vices; Purim uncovers the deeper Jewish will that remains directed toward Hashem beneath confusion and intoxication.

Seif 1 — Love, Fear, and Their Distorted Shadows
Holy love and fear strengthen service, while their fallen forms produce laziness, anxiety, and bodily desire.

p: הָאַהֲבָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֶנֶת תְּקוּפוֹת בַּלֵּב לִהְיוֹת קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה,
Love of the Blessed One gives firmness to the heart, moving a person to rise and act,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר הוּא עוֹשֶׂה.
for the Lord is with him in all that he does.
וְהַיִּרְאָה בְּהֵפֶךְ מִזֶּה: בְּכָל דָּבָר הוּא מִתְיָרֵא אוּלַי לֹא יָשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Fear operates in the opposite direction: in every matter he is apprehensive that perhaps it is not upright in the eyes of the Blessed One,
וְהוּא לְעוֹלָם שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה.
and so his stance is always one of refraining from action.
וּבִפְסוֹלְתָן הוּא לְהֵפֶךְ.
In their waste-products, however, the pattern is reversed.
מִפְּסוֹלֶת הָאַהֲבָה בָּא הַשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּתַאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת, הַמַּפִּילוֹת עַצְלָה וַעֲיֵפוּת בַּגּוּף.
From the waste-product of love comes immersion in bodily desires, which brings laziness and weariness upon the body.
וּמִפְּסוֹלֶת הַיִּרְאָה בָּא רְצִיחָה וְכַעַס, הַנּוֹתֵן תְּקִיפוּת בַּלֵּב לַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשִׂים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵעָשׂוּ.
From the waste-product of fear come bloodshed and anger, which give the heart a forcefulness to commit deeds that ought not be done.
וְכֵן בַּנְּפִילָה, כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם נוֹפֵל מֵאַהֲבָה, שֶׁהִיא שֹׁרֶשׁ לְמִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה,
So too in spiritual decline: when a person falls from love, which is the root of the positive commandments,
הוּא מְרַפֶּה יָדָיו וּמִתְעַצֵּל בַּעֲשִׂיַּת הַמִּצְווֹת.
his hands grow weak and he becomes sluggish in performing the mitzvot.
וּכְשֶׁנּוֹפֵל מִמִּדַּת הַיִּרְאָה, שֹׁרֶשׁ לְמִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, בָּא לַעֲבֵרוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
And when he falls from the attribute of fear, the root of the negative commandments, he comes to transgression, Heaven forbid.
וּפֶסַח הוּא תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
Passover is the intensity of love, corresponding to Abraham, as is known,
בִּפְרָט בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, דְּאָמְרוּ: "עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ",
especially at the splitting of the Sea, when they said, 'The Lord is my strength and song,'
שֶׁנִּתְּנָה תְּקִיפוּת בְּלִבָּם, דְּעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה "עָזִּי" בֵּיהּ,
for strength was placed within their hearts; this is what the word 'my strength' signifies there.
דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה.
For the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as the Sages of blessed memory taught in Shir HaShirim Rabbah.
וּבַתְּחִלָּה בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה — הַתְּקִיפוּת בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בִּלְבַד.
At first the Children of Israel went out with an uplifted hand: the forcefulness was manifest only externally.
וְעַל יְדֵי קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף נִתְּנָה הַתְּקִיפוּת בִּפְנִימִיּוּתָם.
Through the splitting of the Sea, that strength was implanted within their inner being.
וּכְשֶׁנָּסְעוּ מִזֶּה, כִּי אַחַר כָּל מַדְרֵגָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת נְסִיעָה וּנְפִילָה,
When they journeyed away from this, since after every level there must be a departure and a fall,
כַּיָּדוּעַ עַל פָּסוּק: "שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם",
as is known regarding the verse, 'A righteous man falls seven times and rises,'
הָיוּ הַנְּפִילוֹת בְּעִנְיָן זֶה עַד שֶׁבָּאוּ לִרְפִידִים — רִפְיוֹן יָדַיִם.
their declines occurred precisely in this area, until they came to Rephidim—signifying a weakening of the hands.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְאַתָּה עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ".
And it is written: 'And you were weary and exhausted.'
עֲיֵפוּת הִיא עַצְלוּת וּבַטָּלָה,
Weariness means laziness and inactivity,
"וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים",
while 'and he did not fear God'
כִּי הָעֵצָה לָזֶה — לְהִתְגַּבֵּר אָז בְּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים, שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לְחֵטְא,
teaches that the counsel for this state is at least to strengthen oneself then in the attribute of fear, so that one not come to sin,
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה עַצְלוּתוֹ מִצַּד מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם שֶׁעָלָיו, וְלֹא מִצַּד קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ.
and that even his restraint should come from the awe of Heaven upon him, rather than from frivolity.
וְאָז יַשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן לִזְרִיזוּת וּתְקִיפוּת לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם.
Then he will also attain alacrity and strength for the sake of Heaven.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ כֵן, אָז "וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק",
But when this is not so, then 'Amalek came.'

שֶׁהוּא כֶּלֶב דִּקְלִפָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, בְּשַׁלַּח (סה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)918 Zohar 2:65a — R. Abba said: When they couple together, the people of the world cannot stand before them, and of this it is written, "You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together" (Deuteronomy 22:10) — "together," precisely. And we have learned that a man should give no place to evil kinds, for by a man's deed there is aroused what should not be aroused. And when they couple together, out of their fierceness comes forth the one called "dog," and this one is the most insolent of them all, as it is written, "But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog whet his tongue" (Exodus 11:7). The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You said, "Is the Lord in our midst or not?" — behold, I hand you over to the dog. Immediately, "And Amalek came.",
He is the dog of the husk, as stated in the Zohar, Beshalach (65a, beginning of the page),
שֶׁהוּא תְּקִיפוּת שֶׁל חֻצְפָּה, דְּהַכְּלָבִים עַזֵּי נֶפֶשׁ וְלֹא יָשׁוּבוּ מִפְּנֵי כֹל.
representing the forcefulness of brazenness; dogs are fierce of spirit and do not turn back before anything.
אַף שֶׁרָאָה קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף וּתְקִיפוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, חֻצְפָּתוֹ מְסַיֵּם שֶׁיָּעִיז עִם כָּל זֶה לְהִלָּחֵם.
Though he had seen the splitting of the Sea and Israel's strength, his brazenness culminated in daring nonetheless to wage war.
וְהוּא תַּמְצִית הָרַע שֶׁבְּעֵשָׂו בִּרְצִיחָה, מִפְּסוֹלֶת הַיִּרְאָה.
This is the concentrated evil of Esau expressed in bloodshed, arising from the waste-product of fear.
וּבִרְצִיחָה יֵשׁ עֲדַיִן אֵיזֶה חֵלֶק לְטוֹב — מִי שֶׁבְּמִצְוַת הַתּוֹרָה לְהָרְגוֹ.
Yet even killing contains some possible element of good, when the Torah commands that a person be put to death.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה919 Bereshit Rabbah 63:8 — “Ruddy” — R. Abba bar Kahana said: as though a shedder of blood. And when Shmuel saw that David was ruddy, as it is written, “And he sent and brought him, and he was ruddy,” he was afraid and said: This one too is a shedder of blood, like Esav. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “with fair eyes” — Esav kills of his own mind, but this one kills by the ruling of the Sanhedrin. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 5): King David too was "ruddy," his hands sharp and keen to subdue those who ought to be subdued, yet "with fair eyes," doing nothing except by the decision of the Sanhedrin; he comprised both opposites, and through this he had the power to transform [evil into good]. This is the perfection of kingship, the rose that has red and white, each in its proper place, for kingship is the moon, which has nothing of its own; so David did nothing of his own mind, only what the Blessed One illumined his eyes with by the light of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 175): The trait of kingship, however, is precisely the opposite [of the care never to cause anyone pain, even for a mitzvah]: the Sages said of King David that his hands were "sharp and keen to rule the world with them," and that he was "ruddy" like Esau, only "with fair eyes," by the decision of the Sanhedrin, and therefore he merited kingship. Saul was removed because he became merciful to the cruel, for the trait of kingship is the harsh attribute of judgment. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג): "אַדְמוֹנִי עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם" — אֵינוֹ הוֹרֵג אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין.
As the Sages of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 63) concerning 'ruddy, with beautiful eyes': he kills only by authorization of the Sanhedrin.
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁבְּכָל שִׁבְעִים אֻמּוֹת, בְּכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ מִדָּה רָעָה מְיֻחֶדֶת שֶׁהִיא כֹּחָן בְּיִחוּד.
It is known that among the seventy nations, each possesses a distinctive negative trait that is its particular power.
וְאוֹתָהּ מִדָּה נְטוּעָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן, כִּי לוּלֵי כֵן לֹא הָיָה מְצִיאוּת לְאוֹתָהּ אֻמָּה כְּלָל,
That same trait is also planted within Israel, for otherwise that nation could have no existence at all,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בָּהּ כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ.
but Israel employs it in the manner in which the Blessed One wills that it be used.
אֲבָל כֹּחַ הַחֻצְפָּה כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא,
The power of brazenness toward Heaven, however,

אַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה920 Sanhedrin 105a — Rav Nachman said: Insolence avails even against Heaven. At first it is written, “You shall not go with them,” and in the end it is written, “Arise, go with them.” Rashi: His brazenness in telling Balak's messengers "lodge here tonight" availed him: at first the Holy One, blessed be He, told him "you shall not go," and afterward He said "go." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 105a): The Blessed Name gives a person according to his will; therefore, when a person makes himself strong against the Blessed Name, He lets him do as he wills in the matter in which he is insolent. Just as when a person strengthens himself in prayer the Blessed Name does his will, so with insolence: whoever is insolent is brazen and makes himself strong, and therefore the Blessed Name does his will. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaBushah 2): Insolence is so great in power that it avails even against Heaven: although it is a disgraceful and exceedingly evil trait, the strength and force of this trait avail even against Heaven, for He, blessed be He, who does the will of His creatures, does the insolent one's will because of his strength and force. (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.) דְּמַהַנְיָא מִבִּלְעָם, שֶׁהוּא וַעֲמָלֵק חַד כַּיָּדוּעַ,
though the Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 105a) that brazenness helped Balaam—and he and Amalek are one in this respect, as is known—
הַיְנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מְצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְהִתְקַיֵּם לְפִי שָׁעָה, אֲבָל לֹא עַל הָאֱמֶת.
means only that such a power can exist in this world temporarily, but not in ultimate truth.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּבִלְעָם, דְּחֻצְפָּתוֹ הוֹעִילָה לְהַרְשׁוֹתוֹ לֵילֵךְ,
So it was with Balaam: his brazenness succeeded in obtaining permission to go,
אֲבָל סוֹף כָּל סוֹף הֲלִיכָתוֹ לֹא הוֹעִילָה כְּלוּם, וְאַדְּרַבָּה הָיְתָה לְרָעָתוֹ, וּבֵרְכָן בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ.
but in the end his journey accomplished nothing; on the contrary, it harmed him, and against his will he blessed Israel.
וְנִמְצָא, הֲגַם דִּלְשָׁעָה הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁהוֹעִיל בְּחֻצְפָּתוֹ, אֵין זֶה אֱמֶת כְּלָל,
Thus, although for the moment he thought his brazenness had succeeded, that was not true at all,
כִּי אֵין לְדָבָר זֶה מְצִיאוּת עַל דֶּרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת כְּלָל.
for such a thing has no true existence whatsoever.
וּמַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִן לְכֹחַ זֶה, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִמְחָה זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק,
The reason this power still has some existence in this world, so long as the memory of Amalek has not been erased,

הַיְנוּ כִּי מָצִינוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:)921 Moed Katan 16b — "The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: he that rules over men must be righteous, ruling in the fear of God." What does it mean? R. Abbahu said, this is what it means: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me — I rule over man; and who rules over Me? The righteous man, for I decree a decree and he annuls it. Rashi: "The Rock of Israel" — I rule over man; who rules over Me? The righteous man rules over Me and annuls it. Maharsha: The end of the verse reads "in the fear of God," and it may be explained accordingly: who rules over Me? The righteous — by means of the fear of God, along the lines of what they said, "all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven"; this one decree is not in the hands of Heaven, and in it the righteous man rules over Me. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Ahavas Re'a 2): "My children have defeated Me" [Bava Metzia 59b] is of a piece with this saying, that the righteous man rules by the fear of God: the righteous man, by his petition, annuls the decree, until the Holy One, blessed be He, does his will. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 252): Afterwards Scripture says "you shall take My terumah," meaning that the desire of the Blessed One too is in their hands, in the manner of "the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous man annuls," and like "My sons have defeated Me" — of which the Sages said: at first it is "the Torah of the Lord" and in the end "his Torah," for it is in his hand; what he desires, the Blessed One desires too. גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר וְהַצַּדִּיק מְבַטֵּל.
is that we find even within Israel (Moed Katan 16b): the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous person annuls the decree.
זֶה לִכְאוֹרָה כְּעֵין חֻצְפָּה כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא,
Superficially, this resembles a kind of brazenness toward Heaven,

בִּפְרָט אוֹתָן שֶׁהֵטִיחוּ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה922 Berakhot 31b — R. Elazar said: Chana spoke insolently toward Heaven, as it is said, “And Chana prayed upon the Lord” — this teaches that she cast words upward. And R. Elazar said: Eliyahu spoke insolently toward Heaven, as it is said, “And You have turned their heart backward.” R. Shmuel bar R. Yitzchak said: From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, relented and acknowledged to Eliyahu? For it is written, “and whom I have afflicted.” Rashi: "And Chana prayed upon the Lord" — so it is actually written in Scripture, and we do not have the reading here, "Do not read ["to the Lord" but "upon the Lord"]." That the Holy One, blessed be He, relented and acknowledged to Eliyahu — He acknowledged his words at a later time, through the prophecy of other prophets. Maharsha: That she cast words upward — as she said above, "If You will look, well; and if not, You will see," or in what she said, "These breasts that You have set upon my heart, to what purpose?"; and "cast" in our passage means one who speaks a word of contention toward Heaven. As for "and whom I have afflicted," its plain sense would be the affliction of exile; but evil is not to be ascribed to the Holy One, blessed be He, for "out of the mouth of the Most High evil does not proceed," and therefore they expounded it of His having created the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 15): When Elijah said "and You have turned their heart backward" (of which the Sages said that he "cast words upward," and that the Holy One, blessed be He, relented and acknowledged him, as it is written, "and whom I have afflicted"), the hidden light from Atika [the Ancient One] was revealed to them, by which "though your sins be like scarlet, they shall be white as snow." When one merits the revelation of this light through repentance out of love, deliberate sins become like merits; so Elijah said "You have turned their heart backward," for once he had gathered them they all returned to the Blessed One and proclaimed "the Lord, He is God," a light akin to that of the Giving of the Torah. (בְּרָכוֹת לא, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב).
especially those righteous people who spoke forcefully toward Heaven (Berakhot 31b, end of the page).
אֶלָּא דְּעַל הָאֱמֶת לֹא שַׁיָּךְ כְּלָל חֻצְפָּה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
In truth, however, brazenness does not properly apply to Israel at all,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹשֵׁק וּמִתְגַּעְגֵּעַ לָזֶה שֶׁיְּנַצְּחוּהוּ בָּנָיו.
for the Blessed One desires and yearns for His children to prevail over Him, as it were.
וְעַל זֶה סָמְכוּ אוֹתָן צַדִּיקִים שֶׁהֵטִיחוּ דְּבָרִים,
This is what those righteous people relied upon when they spoke so forcefully,
דְּרַק לְגָוֶן וּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הוּא הַטָּחַת דְּבָרִים,
for only in outward appearance does it look like defiant speech.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הֲרֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹמֵד וּמִתְאַוֶּה: מָתַי יָבוֹא צַדִּיק הָרָאוּי לְבַטֵּל גְּזֵרוֹתָיו, לְנַצְּחוֹ בְּכָל אֹפֶן שֶׁיּוּכַל.
In truth, the Blessed One longs for the worthy righteous person who will come and annul His decrees, prevailing over Him by every means available.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהוּא חֻצְפָּה הֵפֶךְ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָאֲמִתִּי.
Among the nations, by contrast, brazenness is genuinely opposed to the true will of the Blessed One.
וְנִמְצָא, חֻצְפָּה כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא בֶּאֱמֶת, דֶּרֶךְ חֻצְפָּה — מַה שֶּׁהוּא נֶגֶד אֲמִתּוּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ —
Thus actual brazenness toward Heaven—brazenness in the literal sense, acting against the true will of the Blessed One—
זֶה אֵין בּוֹ מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל לְטוֹב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָטוּעַ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל.
has no positive counterpart whatsoever that could be planted in the heart of Israel.

וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בַּעֲמָלֵק: "תִּמְחֶה", וְאֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּר מִמֶּנּוּ (מְכִילְתָּא, סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח)923 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Amalek 2:50 — R. Eliezer says: The Omnipresent swore by His throne — if one from any of the nations of the world comes to convert, Israel shall receive him; but from the house of Amalek they shall not receive him. As it is said, "And David said to the lad who told him: From where are you? And he said: I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite" (II Samuel 1:13). And David recalled at that hour what had been said to Moses: if one from any of the nations of the world comes to convert, Israel shall receive him, but from the house of Amalek they shall not receive him. Therefore it is said, "And David said to him: Your blood is upon your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you" (II Samuel 1:16). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Among the nations, those with more connection to holiness are the worse and hold a greater force of impurity, so that one must keep further from them; and Amalek has more connection to holiness than any nation — sprung from two of the patriarchs and matriarchs, his mother Timna having gone round the doors of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob seeking to convert, and his father Eliphaz raised in Isaac's lap. Therefore he was distanced more than all the nations, his name to be blotted out from under the heavens, and the Mekhilta says that no convert is accepted from Amalek. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): I have explained elsewhere that in my view it is clear that [the descendants of Haman who studied Torah] came through one of the seed of Amalek coming upon a Jewish woman, since converts are not accepted from Amalek; rather, it happened through a woman taken captive among them, or otherwise by force. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Apart from [a child born to a Jewish woman forced by one of Haman's seed], no convert is accepted from Amalek, as the Mekhilta says, for once the name Amalek has come upon them in actuality there is no trace of the moisture of holiness in them: his whole root is the evil latent and hidden, to be drawn into action, and were there room to turn him to good he would not be evil at all. A nation whose root of evil lies in outward action can be transformed, but Amalek himself cannot be transformed at all, for the essence does not change, only its outward extension. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 2): In Egypt the task was to extract the holy sparks, and many of the mixed multitude were fit to cleave to Israel; not so Amalek, for the Mekhilta says that the Blessed One swore that no convert would be accepted from Amalek, and likewise the command was to destroy "from ox to sheep." As for "of Haman's descendants studied Torah in Bnei Brak," though converts are not accepted from Amalek, it seems that Rav Shmuel bar Shilat descended from one of them who came upon a Jewish woman, and so issued from Haman unintentionally. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Of Amalek it is written "you shall blot out," and the Sages said in the Mekhilta that converts are not accepted from Amalek; yet "of Haman's descendants taught children in Jerusalem," so it must have come about through a gentile of his descendants coming upon a Jewish woman, for the offspring is fit and is a Jew, though he is also called the son of the gentile. Absorbing anything from Amalek is possible only in this way, by force and without intent. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 264): Every evil trait includes some good, since it is also set within Israel, and from its good side come the pious of the nations; but the only good in mockery is the mocking of idolatry, which belongs to this world alone. In the future, when the evil inclination is abolished and there is no place for idolatry, there is no place for mockery at all — no remnant of it in the World to Come and no turning into "a clear language," only "you shall blot out" — as the Sages said in the Mekhilta, that no convert is accepted from Amalek. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 10): Hence the Mekhilta says that converts are not accepted from Amalek, for he is the root of evil in which there is no good; even when he comes to convert and says he wishes to be good, it is only a "spreading out of the hooves" [the pig's display of a false sign of purity], which is the root of Esau.,
Therefore it is said of Amalek, 'You shall erase,' and a convert from Amalek is not accepted (Mekhilta, end of Parashat Beshalach),
כִּי הוּא נִקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם", שֶׁכָּל הַגּוֹיִם עִנְיָנָם לַעֲשׂוֹת הֵפֶךְ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for Amalek is called 'the first of the nations': the common characteristic of the nations is to act contrary to the will of the Blessed One.
אֶלָּא שֶׁכָּל אֻמָּה הוּא בְּאֵיזֶה עִנְיָן פְּרָטִי,
Each nation expresses this in some particular area,
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית וְהַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל דָּבָר זֶה — לְהַחְצִיף לַעֲשׂוֹת הֵפֶךְ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
whereas Amalek is the first and root of the entire phenomenon: brazenly acting against the will of the Blessed One.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ כְּלָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
This trait does not exist at all in Israel,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת יז.)924 Berakhot 17a — After he had prayed, R. Alexandri would say: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will — and what prevents us? The yeast in the dough and subjection to the kingdoms. May it be Your will to deliver us from their hand, that we may return to perform the statutes of Your will with a whole heart. Rashi: "And what prevents us" — from doing Your will. "The yeast in the dough" — the evil inclination in our heart, which leavens us. Maharsha: He explains it after what Maimonides wrote in the Eight Chapters, that a man must keep to the middle path in his traits and his deeds.
