The evil inclination drives him to one extreme within what is permitted him — to be arrogant and to indulge in permitted desire — and is therefore likened to the leaven in the dough, which raises the dough and makes it more than its true measure; while subjection to the gentile kingdoms forces him to the opposite extreme, for they do not allow Israel to hold themselves up but abase them utterly and withhold from them every good, even what they need for the service of God. Thus "our will is to do Your will" — to walk the middle path — "and what prevents us?" These two, each pulling toward its own extreme; may it be Your will to subdue them before us and behind us, that is, both extremes, "that we may return" to walk in the middle. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 21): In Israel a thought that is not for its own sake comes only from the [evil] inclination, which accustoms one to seek his own pleasure in everything, but the depths of the hearts of the children of Israel are solely for the sake of Heaven, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." Hence, when there is an actual deed, that suffices to join it to the will in the depths of the heart, and no account is taken of the thought of the "yeast in the dough" that confuses it. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 1): The sign of the covenant testifies that the holy flesh of Israel does not desire evil, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will … and who prevents us …": this depth of will stems from our father Abraham, while the Torah is the spice against the [evil] inclination and the Land of Israel is the opposite of subjugation to the kingdoms. "Our will," the depth of the will, is freedom from the evil inclination and from subjugation; hence no exile came from Abraham's side, and the sufferings come only from the side of the inclination and the subjugation. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): Though Israel sank in exile into the forty-nine gates of impurity, this was a clarification before Him who examines hearts of the difference between the nations' immersion, which stems from the essence of their hearts, and Israel's, which comes only from their being mixed among the nations, whereas in the essence of their hearts "it is revealed and known that our will is to do [Your will]." The essence of Israel's hearts is not immersed in impurity at all, and from this side comes the redemption from the nations. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): Even the wicked of Israel are all righteous, just as all Israel are called circumcised, even one actually uncircumcised; so one who is wicked in deed is so only from the side of the [evil] inclination and not from his heart, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …," and as the Rambam explains the reason for coercing [a husband] until he says "I want." Though he is called wicked for his actual sin, even the sinners of Israel are full of regret, and there is no wicked Jew who does not regret for some moment once the pleasure has passed and the inclination no longer incites him, because of the depth of good in the depths of his heart. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 24): On Atzeres, the time of accepting the yoke of Torah and mitzvos, there is a mitzvah to give pleasure to the body as well, for the yoke is felt mainly by the body, whereas as for the soul, "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." By this we show that although for the body it is a yoke, it nevertheless rejoices in accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, of Torah and of mitzvos. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The holiness of the name Israel at the root of every Jew cannot be uprooted, and even if he multiplies sins it is all from the side of the "yeast in the dough" and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" that surround the root of Judaism, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …" Therefore he is compared to a myrtle standing among reeds: the sins are only in the reeds surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 263): The reason the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to the deed is that in truth "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God" and "the Lord's portion is His people," as it says, "It is revealed and known … and who prevents us …"; but in idolatry, where one denies [God], God forbid, even an evil thought is joined [to the deed]. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the depths of the heart "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will — and who prevents us …": even the hindrances in a heart that inclines to evil lie only in the revealed part of the heart, from the "yeast in the dough" that sits at the openings of the heart and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" — the thorns that surround the rose and clothe it, one from without and the other from within. But it is all only a garment and not the essence, which is the depth of his heart, where his essential vitality cleaves to the Blessed One.: "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ" וְכוּלֵי,
as the Sages of blessed memory taught (Berakhot 17a): 'It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will,' etc.,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּרוּשִׁין)925 Mishneh Torah, Divorce 2:20 — One whom the law requires to divorce his wife and who does not wish to divorce her — a Jewish court, in every place and in every time, beats him until he says "I consent," and he writes the bill of divorce, and it is a valid bill of divorce. And why is this bill of divorce not void, seeing that he is coerced? Because we call a man coerced only when he is pressed and forced to do something the Torah does not obligate him to do. But one whose evil inclination has overpowered him to nullify a commandment or to commit a transgression, and who was beaten until he did what he is obligated to do — he is not coerced by another; rather, he coerced himself by his own evil thinking. Therefore this man, who does not wish to divorce — since he wishes to be of Israel and wishes to perform all the commandments and to keep far from the transgressions, and it is his inclination that has overpowered him — once he has been beaten until his inclination is weakened and he says "I consent," he has already divorced willingly. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 21): This follows the Rambam's reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing'": in the depths of the heart everyone wishes to heed the words of the Sages and only the leaven in the dough holds him back, so once he has been beaten and his inclination has weakened until he also says with his mouth, "I am willing," it suffices. So too, intention not for the sake of Heaven in a Jew comes only from the inclination, which accustoms him to seek his own benefit in everything, whereas the depths of the heart of the children of Israel are solely for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): That the name Israel can never be uprooted from a Jew seems to take away his free choice; this is the mountain held over them at Sinai, that he will be Israel against his will. But when they accepted [the Torah] again in the days of Ahasuerus it was clarified that this is not coercion, for at his root he truly chooses the Blessed One of his own will; as the Rambam wrote on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" even if he is wicked and unwilling to accept the words of the Sages, his true will is not so. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): "All Israel have a share in the World to Come" includes even the wicked of Israel, for all are called righteous, just as all Israel are called circumcised even one who is in fact uncircumcised. One who is wicked in deed is so only because of the evil inclination and not from his heart, as it says, "It is revealed and known before You that our will [is to do Your will]," and as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing.'" Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 3): There was a "great protest" against the Torah [since it was accepted under coercion] until they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus, when the Blessed One clarified that the point of the heart is truly good; consequently there is no "great protest," as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing'": since in truth he wants it, it is not called duress, and so they were already acquired as a people and for eternal life. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Even the wicked and the sinners of Israel have this: although they sin through the incitement of the inclination, the leaven in the dough, in their true will there is this point, that they can abandon all the desires of this world for the will of the Blessed One. That is why "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing'" is effective, as is known from the Rambam's reason; and this is an inheritance from our father Isaac. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): Therefore, although he has sinned, he is still Israel in every respect, for all of it comes only from the leaven in the dough and not from the truth of the point of the heart, as is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing,'" which holds even for one who apostatizes from the whole Torah out of spite. This stems from the root of Jewish holiness that was fixed as a lasting acquisition in the heart of all Israel at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from a Jew however many his sins: even when he multiplies sins, it all comes from the leaven in the dough and the subjugation of the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness, as it says, "It is revealed and known before You that our will...," and similarly in the Rambam on the reason for "they coerce until he says, 'I am willing.'" Therefore [the Sages] compared [the sinner of Israel] to a myrtle standing among reeds: the sins are only in the reeds surrounding the myrtle, while the myrtle itself has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): As is known from the Rambam's words on the reason for "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" what in the heart is unwilling is so only because of the evil inclination. On this it says, "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable [ratzon]," and I received the interpretation that even when one sees that his heart's will is not yet in it, speaking good with the mouth, which is called "the lips of the righteous," helps to teach and to draw the will into the heart as well. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Mishlei 10): "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable [ratzon]": as the Sages said, "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing,'" that is, through his speech he brings the will into his heart as well. What he says with his lips while his heart is not yet clarified helps him to clarify his heart toward the will wholeheartedly: for instance, when anger at his fellow sprouts in his heart, his counsel is first to speak kindly to his fellow even if not wholeheartedly, and by this he gradually brings love into his heart in place of hatred. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 57): When a person shortchanges himself in divine service, this is "the buyer was defrauded," and a buyer defrauded by less than a sixth is like what the Talmud says, "they coerce him until he says, 'I am willing'": in truth the depth of the heart of Israel is drawn after the will of the Blessed One, but on the outer garment there are impediments that keep him from serving God, and he is shortchanged by them. Yet this is only less than a sixth, which is wholly waived [and the sale stands]., בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אֲנִי",
and as Maimonides wrote (end of chapter 2 of the Laws of Divorce) in explaining the rule, 'We compel him until he says: I desire it,'
דְּגַם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲמִתּוּת רְצוֹנָם הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁנּוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because even the sinners of Israel, in the truth of their will, do not desire to deviate from the will of the Blessed One.
רַק הֲסָתַת הַיֵּצֶר, שֶׁהוּא הַחוֹחַ הַמַּקִּיף הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה, גּוֹרֵם לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה לְהִדַּמּוֹת לַגּוֹיִם,
Only the incitement of the evil inclination—the thorn surrounding the rose—causes this distortion to spread into action and resemble the nations,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קְלִיטַת הַגֵּרִים.
and through this occurs the gathering in of converts.
אֲבָל מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק אֵין שָׁם דֻּגְמָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
But the root of Amalek has no corresponding form within Israel whatsoever.
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה בָּא בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ" וְכוּלֵי,
Yet the Sages of blessed memory formulated this as: 'It is revealed and known before You that our will...'
דְּרַק לְפָנָיו הוּא גָּלוּי, אֲבָל לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הֲרֵי יֵשׁ כַּמָּה מוּמָרִים לְהַכְעִיס.
For this truth is fully revealed only before Him; to outward appearance there are indeed Jews who apostatize deliberately to provoke.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ926 Sanhedrin 103b — Amon transgressed with his mother, as it is said, “for he, Amon, multiplied guilt.” R. Yochanan and R. Elazar — one said that he burned the Torah, and one said that he transgressed with his mother. His mother said to him: Do you have any pleasure from the place you came out of? He said to her: I do this only in order to provoke my Creator. Rashi (s.v. "from the place you came out of"): A person is sated with the place from which he emerged, and has no desire for the pleasure of that place. Maharsha: Because Scripture says of Amon that he "multiplied guilt" — that is, he added to the sins of his fathers Ahaz and Manasseh — they said that in forbidden relations too he multiplied guilt, having relations with his mother, which could only have been done to provoke. Perhaps they also inferred it from his very name, Amon, as from immo [his mother], just as Moab is from me-av [from the father]. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 103b): They dispute which is called "great guilt": an intellectual sin, such as burning the Torah — as if to say that he has no share in the Torah of Moses — or having relations with his mother, a bodily abomination. For there is no intellectual sin greater than burning the Torah, and no bodily abomination greater than that of one who has relations with his mother. (סַנְהֶדְרִין קג:): "כְּלוּם כַּוָּנָתוֹ אֶלָּא לְהַכְעִיס אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ".
As they said (Sanhedrin 103b): 'Is his intention anything other than to provoke his Creator?'

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז)927 Kohelet Rabbah 7:8 — [Elisha ben Avuya said to R. Meir:] I was riding on a horse and strolling behind the Temple on a Day of Atonement that fell on a Sabbath, and I heard a divine voice chirping and saying, "Return, wayward children," "Return to Me and I will return to you" — except for Elisha ben Avuya, who knew My power and rebelled against Me. בְּאַחֵר: שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ רִבּוֹנוֹ וּמִתְכַּוֵּן וְכוּלֵי.
And similarly they said (Kohelet Rabbah, parashah 7) concerning Acher: that he knows his Master and intends, etc.
שֶׁזֶּה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן כְּאִלּוּ רְצוֹנוֹ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת וְכוּלֵי, אֲבָל הוּא לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בִּלְבַד.
This makes it appear as though his will itself were not to do God's will, but that appearance is only superficial.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גַּם כֵּן בַּטּוֹב מַה שֶּׁצַּדִּיק מְבַטֵּל, כַּנִּזְכָּר.
The same kind of outward appearance exists on the side of good when a righteous person annuls a Divine decree, as explained above.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת זֶה לְמַרְאֵה עֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
Nevertheless, since such an appearance exists before human eyes in this world,
נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם כֵּן מִזֶּה מְצִיאוּת לַעֲמָלֵק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
it thereby supplies Amalek with a corresponding apparent existence in this world.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק" רַק "מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם",
Therefore the 'memory of Amalek' exists only 'from beneath the heavens.'
דִּלְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׁמַיִם אֵין שׁוּם זֵכֶר וְרֹשֶׁם מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלָל, וְאֵין לוֹ שַׂר לְמַעְלָה כְּכָל הָאֻמּוֹת.
Above the heavens there is no memory or trace of him at all, and he has no celestial minister as do the other nations.
וְגַם תַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם אֵין לוֹ מְצִיאוּת גָּמוּר, רַק זֵכֶר בִּלְבַד.
Even beneath the heavens he has no complete existence, only a residual memory.
וְצָרִיךְ לִמְחוֹת הַזֵּכֶר הַהוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוֹחִין וּמְקַנְּחִין צְלוֹחִית מֵאָבָק שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַמְכַסֶּה בְּהִירוּת הַכְּלִי.
That memory must be erased, like wiping dust from a flask when the dust obscures the vessel's clarity.
כָּךְ זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק הוּא הַמְכַסֶּה בְּהִירוּת כְּלִי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל —
So the memory of Amalek obscures the clarity of Israel's vessel—
מַה שֶּׁבֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנָם לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
namely, the truth that their will is to do His blessed will.
וְזֶהוּ "וַיְזַנֵּב כָּל הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים",
This is the meaning of 'he cut down all the stragglers.'
שֶׁהַנֶּחֱשָׁל הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם בְּעַצְלוּת וְשִׁכְחָה מֵהַכָּרַת שְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
A straggler is a person who has sunk into laziness and forgetfulness of the recognition of His blessed Name,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם מִדָּבָר זֶה שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי,
and thereby this truth—'our will is...'—becomes hidden from him.
וְאָז בָּא זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהַשִּׁכְחָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
Then the memory of Amalek enters, drawing its existence from Israel's forgetfulness.
וְעֵיטָא דְּאוֹרַיְתָא לָזֶה הוּא הַזְּכִירָה,
The Torah's counsel for this is remembrance:
שֶׁיָּשִׂים הָאָדָם אֶל לִבּוֹ לִמְחוֹת זֵכֶר זֶה מֵהָעוֹלָם,
a person must place upon his heart the task of erasing this memory from the world,
הַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר וְיָשִׂים אֶל לִבּוֹ דָּבָר זֶה — שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי,
meaning by remembering and internalizing this very truth—that our will is to do God's will,
וְשֶׁאֵין רוֹצֶה כְּלָל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן,
and that one does not truly desire anything contrary to the will of the Blessed One in any way,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֱמֶת בְּלִי סָפֵק בְּכָל לְבָבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
for this is unquestionably true within every Jewish heart.
וְהַזְּכִירָה בְּדָבָר זֶה מִמֵּילָא מוֹחָה הַהֵפֶךְ וְהַשִּׁכְחָה.
Remembering this truth automatically erases its opposite—the state of forgetfulness.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Adar and the Root Will of a Jew
At the year's lowest edge, Purim intoxication reveals that the essential Jewish will remains solely to serve Hashem.

p: וּזְמַנּוֹ בַּאֲדָר, שֶׁהוּא אַחֲרִית הַשָּׁנָה לַחֳדָשִׁים,
Its appointed time is in Adar, the end of the year when counted by months,
שֶׁהוּא שָׁנָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁמּוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה וּמוֹנִין לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁבּוֹ נַעֲשׂוּ אֻמָּה מְיֻחֶדֶת.
which is Israel's year: Israel counts by the moon and counts from the Exodus from Egypt, when they became a distinct nation.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּעוֹלָם, שָׁנָה, נֶפֶשׁ — הַכֹּל אֶחָד, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה.
It is known that world, year, and soul are parallel structures; each constitutes a complete configuration.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּקוֹמַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ יֵשׁ רֹאשׁ וְזָנָב,
Just as the structure of the soul has a head and a tail,
וּשְׁלִיטַת עֲמָלֵק — "וַיְזַנֵּב" וְגוֹמֵר — הַיְנוּ בַּמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁבָּהֶם.
Amalek's dominion—'he cut down the stragglers,' etc.—takes hold at the lowest level within them.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּיוֹצֵא מִכְּלַל הָאֻמָּה שֶׁרְצוֹנָם וְכוּלֵי.
This is the final level, where a person may appear, Heaven forbid, to have left the collective nation whose essential will is God's will.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא, תֵּצֵא י)928 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 10 — "And he cut off the tail of all who lagged behind you" (Deuteronomy 25:18) — he struck them a blow upon the tail. This accords with what R. Chanina bar Shikla said: What did the house of Amalek do? They would cut off the circumcised flesh of the Israelites and fling it heavenward, saying: This is what You chose — take for Yourself what You chose. שֶׁחָתַךְ עָרְלָתָם.
The Sages of blessed memory said (Midrash Tanchuma, Tetzei 10) that Amalek cut off their foreskins.
וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר יֵשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת חֵלֶק שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְחָתְכוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ,
This signifies that in that organ there is indeed a portion that must be cut away,
כִּי אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת לִהְיוֹת בְּגוּף יִשְׂרְאֵלִי, שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שְׁמָם,
for it has no proper place in a Jewish body; indeed, 'foreskin' is characteristically associated with the nations.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם נוֹצַר עִמּוֹ, וְהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְכָרְתוֹ.
Nevertheless, it is created together with the person, and he must cut it away.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא)929 Bereshit Rabbah 11:6 — A philosopher asked R. Hoshaya: If circumcision is so precious, why was it not given to Adam the first man? He said to him: Why does that man shave the corner of his head and leave the corner of his beard? He said to him: Because it grew with him in his time of folly. He said to him: If so, let him blind his eye and cut off his hands and break his legs, since they too grew with him in his time of folly. He said to him: Have we come to such arguments? He said to him: To send you away empty-handed is impossible. Rather, everything created in the six days of creation requires further work: mustard and lupines require sweetening, wheat requires grinding. Even man requires perfecting. דְּכָל דָּבָר צְרִיכִין תִּקּוּן,
The Sages of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11) that everything requires human completion,
שֶׁכָּךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הָאָדָם, שֶׁהוּא הַפּוֹעֵל דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי,
for the Blessed One desired that this rectification be attributed to man, who actively brings into deed the truth of 'our will is...'
וְלֹא שֶׁהוּא בַּטֶּבַע כָּךְ.
rather than having it exist automatically by nature.
וַעֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בְּחִירָה לָאָדָם, וְיֵשׁ מוּמָר לַעֲרֵלוּת.
A person therefore still possesses free choice, and a Jew can even abandon circumcision.

אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נְדָרִים לא:)930 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along. דְּגַם עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלַל מוּלִים,
Nevertheless, the Sages of blessed memory taught (Nedarim 31b) that even uncircumcised Jews are included in the category of the circumcised.
אַךְ לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הֲרֵי נִרְאֶה עָרֵל,
Yet to outward appearance he looks uncircumcised,
וּמִזֶּה יֵשׁ אֲחִיזָה לַעֲמָלֵק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן.
and from this Amalek obtains an apparent foothold.

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג:)931 Bava Batra 123b — R. Chelbo asked R. Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, "And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph" (Genesis 30:25) — what was different once Joseph was born [that Jacob then asked to return home]? He said to him: Jacob our father saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, as it is stated: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for straw, and they shall kindle in them and consume them" (Obadiah 1:18). Rashbam: "What was different" — why he did not wish to return to his father's house until Joseph was born. Maharsha: By acquiring the birthright and taking the blessing from Esau it was granted to Jacob that he should rule over Esau, who was the elder; and all of this Jacob handed on to Joseph, as is derived from "And I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite" (Genesis 48:22). It is in this way that the seed of Esau was delivered into the hand of Joseph and was not delivered into the hand of his other brothers. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Batra 123b): This matter — that the seed of Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph — is exceedingly deep. Over the seed of Joseph the eye has no power, while Esau's blessing is the opposite of this, as it is said, "and the hands are the hands of Esau" (Genesis 27:22) — for the hands are the most outward of the limbs, the rest being within. The seed of Joseph therefore prevail, because their blessing is from a place and a level over which Esau's eye has no power; whereas the other tribes, whose blessing was from the revealed level, could not overcome the power of Esau, which is itself revealed. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 58): Esau, who belongs only to this world, is called 'aluf', a captain of a thousand (the utmost of this world's blessing), but not the rank of a king who endures forever. Therefore Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph, who was "ruler over all the land of Egypt": a ruler, that is, a minister and chief of the same pattern as 'aluf', like Messiah son of Joseph, who is at the rank of ruler and is slain, having no everlasting endurance, which belongs only to David. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The obstinacy of Israel issues from wisdom, through the knowledge that joins wisdom to the powers of action, and is obstinate only for the honor of Heaven; therefore Amalek falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek is the root of obstinacy, his chief claim being against the desires of Israel, as the Sages said on "who happened upon you"; but his obstinacy is against the will of the Blessed One, whereas the obstinacy of Joseph's seed accords with the will of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Of Amalek it is said, "and he feared not God," and the Sages said that this is why he falls into the hand of the seed of Joseph, of whom it is said, "I fear God." And though "he feared not God" refers to Israel, it means [that it came upon them] through Amalek "who happened upon you," who brought into them imaginings and forces of forgetfulness, whereby they became "faint and weary" and did not fear God. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Esau falls only into the hand of the seed of Joseph because, as the Sages said, "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven": fear of Heaven is the province of man's choice and effort, for love can come into a person's heart of itself, but fear cannot. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eira 1): Before Benjamin's birth Jacob was given tidings of Benjamin, Menashe and Ephraim, who are Amalek's adversaries, as the Gemara says that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. For Amalek stands against the holiness of the covenant (they would cut off the circumcisions of Israel), while Menashe and Ephraim are Joseph's two tribes, and Benjamin too is the attribute of the Tzaddik; therefore the name E-l Sha-dai, which corresponds to the attribute of the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world, is mentioned there. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 38): On account of Rachel's modesty the Holy One, blessed be He, restored [the birthright] to her, in that every beginning of salvation is aroused through her children. Thus every beginning of salvation is revealed through the children of Rachel, as the Gemara says that Jacob saw that the seed of Esau would be delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph. Sod Yesharim (Purim 15): If Israel rely on the strength they possess from their root, Amalek at once stands against them, claiming that he too has strength from the root, being born of Isaac and Rebecca. Therefore the Sages said that the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph: the seed of Joseph rely on no strength at all, but clarify wherever there is something to clarify, and where the power of their service does not reach, there the Blessed One will clarify it for good. דְּאֵין נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
Therefore they said (Bava Batra 123b) that Amalek falls only into the hands of the descendants of Joseph,
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אוֹת בְּרִית הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְהוּא שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית,
for Joseph corresponds to the sign of the holy covenant, as is known, and he guards the covenant,
שֶׁגַּם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אֵין שׁוּם טַעֲנָה נֶגְדּוֹ.
so that even from outward appearance no claim can be raised against him.
וְיָדוּעַ: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים כְּנֶגֶד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים,
It is known that the twelve months correspond to the twelve tribes,
וַאֲדָר כְּנֶגֶד יוֹסֵף, דְּלָכֵן יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי אֲדָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁיּוֹסֵף נֶחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם.
and Adar corresponds to Joseph; hence there can be two Adars, just as Joseph was divided into two tribes.
וּבְחֹדֶשׁ זֶה כֹּחַ פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
In this month the power of procreation is manifest,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ח.)932 Rosh Hashanah 8a — R. Meir holds: When are the meadows clothed with flocks? At the time when the valleys are covered over with grain. And when are the valleys covered over with grain? In Adar. They conceive in Adar and give birth in Av, and their New Year is Elul. Rava said: All agree that "the meadows are clothed with flocks" at the time when "the valleys are covered over with grain," in Adar. Rashi: "The meadows are clothed with flocks" is a verse in Psalms: the ewes are "clothed", that is, they conceive; "the valleys are covered over with grain": the sown seed sprouts and is plainly visible; "they shout for joy, they also sing": in Nisan, when harvest time comes and the grain stands on its stalks, the wind blows and they knock against one another, and a sound is heard, so that they seem to be singing. The gestation of small cattle is five months; and "their New Year is Elul" because the division between their new and old [animals] at the renewal of the year falls close to the completion [of their births]. Tosafos (s.v. "the meadows are clothed with flocks"): The Targum renders it "the rams mount the flocks", which is a euphemism [for mating]. Rashi explains it in this way below (11a), on R. Yehoshua's statement that the world was created in Nisan, where it is said that that season is the time when cattle and beasts mate with one another; but here he did not explain it so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): This month corresponds to the power of desire, and its sign is the fish — "let them multiply like fish" — in which lies the power of increase, for the power of "be fruitful and multiply" was first stated of the fish. And it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar," and Israel are likened to a flock, for they too are exceedingly fruitful and multiply. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The month of Adar, whose sign is the fish, corresponds to Joseph, whose blessing is "let them multiply like fish," for in it lies the power of fruitfulness of that blessing, which is in Adar — as it says in Rosh Hashanah, "the flocks conceive in Adar," and Israel are everywhere likened to a flock. It is called Adar from adir, "mighty," denoting strength and might, whose essence is the subduing of the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 5): Therefore it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar" — Israel are likened to a flock, and that is the time of their increase. I have received that this month is therefore auspicious for barren men and women to be remembered, because it is designated for the eradication of Amalek, and every withholding of childbirth among the seed of Israel comes only from the accusation of Amalek.: אֵימָתַי לָבְשׁוּ כָרִים? הַצֹּאן מִתְעַבְּרוֹת בַּאֲדָר וְכוּלֵי,
as they said (Rosh Hashanah 8a): When do the sheep become clothed with fleece? The flock conceives in Adar, etc.
וּמַזָּלוֹ דָּגִים עַל שֵׁם "וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב".
Its zodiac sign is Pisces, corresponding to the blessing, 'May they multiply like fish.'
וּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַדַּעַת, כְּטַעַם "וְהָאָדָם יָדַע".
Procreation extends from da'at, knowledge, in the sense of the verse, 'And the man knew.'
עַל כֵּן בּוֹ נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא סוֹד הַדַּעַת,
Therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who embodies the mystery of da'at, was born in this month,
וּמֵת גַּם כֵּן בּוֹ, וְנִסְתְּמוּ מַעְיְנוֹת הַחָכְמָה.
and he also died in it, whereupon the wellsprings of wisdom were stopped up.
סְתִימָה הִיא אֹטֶם וְעָרְלָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמְּצִיאוּת עָרְלַת הַגּוּף בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
Closure is blockage and orlah, extending from the existence of bodily foreskin in this world.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הִפִּיל הָמָן פּוּר עַל חֹדֶשׁ זֶה, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁבּוֹ יִהְיֶה נִצְחוֹנוֹ.
From this aspect Haman cast the lot upon this month, thinking that in it he would achieve his victory.
וְנַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא: דְּרַק בְּאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ הוּא מַפַּלְתּוֹ בְּיַד זַרְעָא דְיוֹסֵף, שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶגֶד אוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ.
But the opposite occurred: specifically in that month came his downfall at the hands of Joseph's descendants, who correspond to that month.
כִּי בֶאֱמֶת "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" — שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית,
For in truth, 'Your people are all righteous'—guardians of the covenant,

כְּהוֹרָאַת מִלַּת "צַדִּיק" עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַסּוֹד (זֹהַר, חֵלֶק א, נט:)933 Zohar 1:59b — "These are the generations of Noach." R. Chiya opened: "And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which I glory" (Isaiah 60:21). Come and see: all Israel have a portion in the World to Come. Why? Because they keep the covenant upon which the world stands, as it is said, "Were it not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the statutes of heaven and earth" (Jeremiah 33:25). And moreover, for this they are called righteous. From here we learn: whoever keeps this covenant upon which the world stands is called righteous. Whence do we know it? From Joseph: because he kept the covenant of the world, he merited to be called righteous. And therefore, "And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.",
as the word tzaddik signifies according to the mystical teaching (Zohar, Part I, 59b),
וּכְפִשְׁטֵיהּ, שֶׁהוּא עֲשִׂיַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and in its plain sense as well: doing the will of the Blessed One.
וְכֵן "עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם" — גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי.
Likewise, 'Your people are all...' means that it is revealed and known that our will is to do His will.
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, דְּמַה שֶּׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי נִמְשָׁךְ מִשְּׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית,
The two ideas are one, for this underlying will flows from guarding the covenant,
וּמִבְּרִית הַחָתוּם בִּבְשָׂרֵנוּ, שֶׁמִּקְּטַנּוּתוֹ וְעַד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת וְרָצוֹן כְּלָל, נוֹשֵׂא חוֹתָמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
and from the covenant sealed in our flesh: from infancy, before a person possesses knowledge or conscious will, he already bears God's seal upon his body.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָעֶבֶד נִרְצָע לְסִימַן עַבְדוּת עוֹלָם,
Just as a slave's ear is pierced as a sign of permanent servitude,
כָּךְ זֶה סִימָן שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹ מְשֻׁעְבָּד לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם בְּזוּלַת רְצוֹנוֹ.
so circumcision is a sign that the entire body is bound in service to the Blessed One even apart from one's conscious will.
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר: אַף שֶׁכְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה מִפְּעֻלּוֹתָיו וּרְצוֹנוֹ אֵין כֵּן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֲמִתּוּת רְצוֹנוֹ הוּא כָּךְ.
That is: even when his actions and expressed will appear otherwise, the truth of his innermost will remains so.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּפוּרִים חַיָּב לְבַסּוּמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע,
Therefore on Purim one is obligated to become intoxicated until he does not know,
כִּי אָז אָדָם נִכָּר בְּכוֹסוֹ, שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה רַק כְּפִי כֹּחַ הַנָּטוּעַ בּוֹ, וְאֵין מַעְצוֹר לְרוּחוֹ,
for then a person is revealed through his cup: he acts only according to the power implanted within him, with no restraint upon his spirit,
לַעֲשׂוֹת גַּם מַה שֶּׁנֶּגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
even potentially doing what runs contrary to the will of the Blessed One,

כְּעִנְיַן (מְגִלָּה ז:)934 Megillah 7b — Rabba and R. Zeira held the Purim feast together. They became intoxicated. Rabba arose and slaughtered R. Zeira. The next day he begged for mercy and revived him. The following year Rabba said to him: Let the Master come and let us hold the Purim feast together. He said to him: A miracle does not happen at every hour. Rashi: "They became intoxicated" — they became drunk [with wine]. Maharsha (s.v. "Rabba arose and slaughtered R. Zeira"): It is astonishing to take this according to its plain sense. Rather, he "slaughtered" him in that he plied him with wine and forced him to drink far too much, until he fell ill and was near death — and the term "slaughter" is used because the drinking of wine is spoken of in terms of the throat, the place of slaughter, as in "he fills the throats of the Sages with wine." And "he begged for mercy and revived him" means that he prayed that he should not die of that illness, until he was healed and lived; both Scripture and the Talmud use "live" in the sense of recovery. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Even when [Jews] outwardly appear to do the opposite, as in "Rabba arose and slaughtered R. Zeira," it was no murder at all but only in appearance, for he prayed for mercy and revived him. The story was not written in the Gemara for nothing, but to show that even what appears in Israel as its opposite, like outright murder, is only external and not real; indeed his essential intent was the reverse — love of companions and feasting together.: קָם רַבָּה וְשַׁחְטֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא,
as in the incident (Megillah 7b) where Rabbah arose and slaughtered Rabbi Zeira,
כִּי הוּא הָיָה נָטוּעַ בּוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף שַׁבָּת: "מַר נַמֵּי עָנֵישׁ וְקָטֵיל".
for this force was present within him, as stated at the end of Shabbat: 'The Master too punishes and kills.'
וְכָל כֹּחוֹת רָעִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם נְטוּעִים גַּם כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כַּנִּזְכָּר,
All the negative powers found among the idolatrous nations are likewise planted within Israel, as explained above,
רַק שֶׁהֵם מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בָּהֶם לְטוֹבָה, וּבָזֶה מִתְבָּרְרִים אוֹתָם הַכֹּחוֹת.
but Israel employs them for good, and thereby those powers themselves are clarified and rectified.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַמַּנְהִיג לַגּוּף.
This is accomplished through the soul that governs the body.
אֲבָל בְּעֵת שִׁכְרוּת, שֶׁהַגּוּף פּוֹעֵל בְּלֹא הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת מֵהַנֶּפֶשׁ,
But in a state of intoxication, when the body acts without reflective direction from the soul,
כְּשִׁכְרוּתוֹ שֶׁל לוֹט, נִדּוֹן כְּשׁוֹטֶה שֶׁפָּטוּר מִכְּלוּם,
like Lot in his drunkenness, a person is regarded like one lacking sound mind and is exempt from responsibility,
שֶׁאָז יוּכַל לִפְעוֹל כָּל עִנְיְנֵי פְּעֻלּוֹת הַשַּׁיָּכִים לַכֹּחַ הַהוּא.
for then the body can express whatever actions belong to the power embedded within it.
וְאָז הוּא הַבֵּירוּר שֶׁכֹּחַ דַּעֲמָלֵק לֹא נִמְצָא נָטוּעַ בְּגוּפוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
At that point it becomes clarified that the power of Amalek is not planted in Jewish bodies at all.
וְאַף דְּלָא יָדַע בֵּין "אָרוּר" וְכוּלֵי,
And even though he does not know the difference between 'cursed...' and so forth,
פֵּירוּשׁ: מָרְדֳּכַי, שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הַיְּהוּדִי", שֶׁכָּפַר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
the meaning is this: Mordechai, who is called 'the Jew,' rejected idolatry,
הַיְנוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning that he refused to do anything contrary to the will of the Blessed One,
וּבָזֶה הָיָה הוּא הַמְיֻחָד בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר.
and in this he was unique in that generation.
וְהָמָן מַמָּשׁ בְּהֵפֶךְ — רָצָה לַעֲקוֹר כָּל הָאֻמָּה הָעוֹשִׂים רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Haman was precisely the opposite: he sought to uproot the entire nation that does the will of the Blessed One.
וּכְשֶׁהוּא שִׁכּוֹר כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מַעֲלַת זֶה וְחֶסְרוֹן זֶה,
When a Jew becomes so intoxicated that he no longer consciously knows the virtue of the one and the deficiency of the other,
שֶׁאָז נִתְגַּלָּה שֹׁרֶשׁ עַצְמוּתוֹ,
the root of his essential being is revealed.
אָז יוּכְלוּ לְהַכִּיר הַמְּבִינִים אֲמִתּוּת רְצוֹן אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, שֶׁהוּא רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Those who understand can then recognize the true will of a Jew: it is solely to do His blessed will.

sections.en: Teshuvah and the Great Shofar

items.h: The Ten Days of Repentance and the shofar awaken both human return and a corresponding awakening from Above, culminating in the fixed holiness of Yom Kippur.

Seif 1 — The Ten Days: Return when He Is Near
These days gather Israel's collective cry, awakening even distant souls toward repentance and the future Great Shofar.

p: עִנְיַן עֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְשׁוּבָה, אַף דְּצָרִיךְ אָדָם לִהְיוֹת כָּל יָמָיו בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
The matter of the Ten Days of Repentance: although a person must live all his days in repentance,
רַק אָז נִקְרָא "בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ" וּ"בִּהְיוֹתוֹ קָרוֹב", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י״ח עַמּוּד א.
only then is it called "when He may be found" and "when He is near," as they said in Rosh Hashanah 18a.

וְזֶה שַׁיָּךְ בִּתְפִלָּה, דְּעֵת רָצוֹן מִילְתָא הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבְרָכוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד א935 Berakhot 7b — R. Yitzchak said to Rav Nachman: Why does the master not come to the synagogue to pray? He said: I am unable. He said: Let the master gather ten and pray with them. He said: It is too much trouble for me. … He said to him: This is what R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon bar Yochai — what is meant by “And as for me, may my prayer to You, O Lord, be at a time of favour”? When is a time of favour? At the hour when the congregation prays. Rashi: "I am unable" — my strength has failed. "A time of favour" — it follows that there is an hour which is one of favour. Maharsha: Since the law is that one who has a fixed study hall in his own house should pray there, even without ten — as R. Ami and R. Asi did, though they had thirteen synagogues — we must say that R. Yitzchak knew of Rav Nachman that he had no fixed study hall in his house. As for the verse, that the prayer of the congregation is the more acceptable needs no proof at all; it is brought here to teach that even an individual's prayer in his own house is the more acceptable at the hour when the congregation prays — "and as for me," alone, "may my prayer to You, O Lord, be at a time of favour," that is, at the congregation's time of favour. Maharal (Derech Chaim 2:4): From this it is plain that the will of the Blessed One is in the congregation in particular. The matter is a deep one: there is no accuser against a congregation in so far as it is a congregation, for they possess the power of the whole, and on the side of the whole there is no sin — sin belongs to particulars, and to the whole neither sin nor accusation attaches. The prayer of the congregation in the synagogue is offered from the side of the congregation, and therefore it is an hour of favour.;
This distinction applies to prayer, for an auspicious time is significant, as they said in Berakhot 8a;
אֲבָל תְּשׁוּבָה, כָּל יוֹמָא זִמְנֵיהּ,
but as for repentance, every day is its proper time,
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחַ לְקַבֵּל שָׁבִים לְעוֹלָם, וְעַד יוֹם מוֹתוֹ מְחַכֶּה לוֹ;
for the Blessed One promised to accept those who return at all times, and He waits for a person until the day of his death;
אִם יָשׁוּב — מִיָּד מְקַבְּלוֹ.
if he returns, He accepts him immediately.
רַק שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁנִּכְתָּם עֲוֹנוֹ לְפָנָיו,
Only, they said there in Rosh Hashanah that there are cases in which a person's sin becomes indelibly sealed before Him,
וּמְפָרֵשׁ לָהּ עַל יְדֵי חֲתִימַת גְּזַר דִּין.
and this is explained there in terms of the sealing of the decree.
הָעִנְיָן: "חַטָּאִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה",
The idea is contained in the verse, "Evil pursues sinners,"

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז936 Bava Batra 16a — Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, "And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord." He is the evil inclination, for it is written there, "Only evil all the day," and it is written here, "Only against himself do not put forth your hand." He is the angel of death, as it is written, "Only spare his life" — evidently his life rests in his hand. Rashi: "Evidently his life rests in his hand" — it lies with Satan to take the soul, and God warned him not to take it. Maharsha: Our texts misquote the verse: it reads "only [akh] spare his life," not "only [rak]." The verbal analogy holds nonetheless, since "only [akh]" and "only [rak]" are alike terms of limitation. The hint in it is this: "only evil all the day" — let a man limit his evil inclination and master it, and then "only spare his life" — the Holy One, blessed be He, will limit the power of the angel of death, that he not rule over his soul. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil. עַמּוּד א: "הוּא שָׂטָן, הוּא..." וְכוּלֵי937 Bava Batra 16a — It was taught in a baraita: He descends and leads astray, then ascends and provokes wrath; he obtains permission and takes the soul. Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death. Rashi: He descends below and leads people astray into sin; he ascends above and by his accusation provokes the wrath of the King; and he receives permission from Him to kill the sinner, once permission has been granted, as it is written, "you moved Me against him." Maharsha: The baraita sets the three out in order: as the evil inclination he descends and leads a man astray from the good way to the evil; as Satan he then ascends and accuses him before the Lord and provokes wrath; and as the angel of death he takes permission and takes his soul. It does not say that he descends again to take the soul, because the soul, even during a man's life, cleaves to the upper world through what it apprehends, and it is there that the angel of death severs it from the body. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 168): Sins, judgments and sufferings are all one thing, as the Sages said, "He descends and seduces, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul." And since they said that no angel performs two missions — an angel being the name for the power of a thing — it is all one matter: in the world of the Throne, where the King sits on the throne of judgment, it is called judgments; in the world of the angels, sins; and below, sufferings. Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil.,
in the sense of the teaching in Bava Batra 16a, "He is the Satan, he is..." and so forth;
דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיֶּאֱרַע לָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּעִנְיְנֵי בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי,
for whatever befalls a person in this world in the matters of children, life, and sustenance
מְפֹרָשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי מַעֲשָׂיו.
is set forth in the Torah as corresponding to his deeds.

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי" וְגוֹמֵר938 Leviticus 26:3-4 — “If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do them, then I shall give your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its produce and the tree of the field shall give its fruit.” Rashi: "If you walk in My statutes" cannot mean the fulfilling of the commandments, since Scripture goes on to say "and keep My commandments and do them"; it means rather that you should toil in the Torah — and toil in it with the intention of keeping and fulfilling it. "I will give your rains in their season" means at an hour when men do not usually go out on the road, such as the nights of the Sabbath. Ramban: He put the matter of the rains first because, when they come in their season as is fitting, the air is clear and good and the springs and rivers are good, and this is a cause of health in men's bodies, while all the produce increases and is blessed through them, as He says, "and the land shall yield her produce and the tree of the field shall yield its fruit." With this men do not fall sick, and there is none miscarrying or barren among them or among their cattle, and they live out their days — for when bodies are large and healthy they endure as in the days of Adam; and so this is the greatest of the blessings., וְכֵן הַרְבֵּה,
Thus Scripture says, "If you walk in My statutes..." and there are many passages of this kind.
וְעַל הָרֹב גָּלוּי לְבַעֲלֵי עֵינַיִם טְהוֹרוֹת הַסִּבּוֹת הַפְּרָטִיּוֹת שֶׁל כָּל דְּבַר מִקְרֶה שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע לָאָדָם.
For the most part, to those whose eyes are pure, the particular causes of each event that befalls a person are discernible.
אִם לְטוֹב — הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב דְּהָיָה רָגִיל בּוֹ,
If the event is for good, it comes through some good practice to which he had been accustomed;
וְהַהֵפֶךְ בְּהֵפֶךְ — נַעֲשֶׂה סִבָּה טִבְעִית לִפְעֹל לוֹ אֵיזֶה רָעָה.
and the reverse is likewise true: a contrary deed becomes a natural cause that brings some evil upon him.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל, מִי שֶׁאֵין מַשָּׂאוֹ וּמַתָּנוֹ בֶּאֱמוּנָה, נִגְרָם לוֹ אֵיזֶה הֶפְסֵד בְּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה;
For example, one who does not conduct his business dealings faithfully may thereby suffer some loss in business;
וּבְשִׁקּוּעַ בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה יָבוֹא לְאֵיזוֹ מַחֲלָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה גַּסָּה;
immersion in the desire for food can lead to illness, meaning through coarse or excessive eating;
וּמִשִּׁקּוּעַ בְּנִיאוּף — קַשְׁתּוֹ נִנְעֶרֶת, רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן,
and from immersion in sexual immorality, his "bow" may be emptied, may the Merciful One save us,
שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹלִיד כְּלָל, אוֹ לְהוֹלִיד בָּנִים חַלָּשִׁים שֶׁאֵינָם מִתְקַיְּמִים, וְכַדּוֹמֶה לָזֶה.
so that he cannot father children at all, or fathers weak children who do not survive, and similar consequences.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא גְּזַר דִּין, רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן.
This is what is called a decree of judgment, may the Merciful One save us.
וְעִנְיַן "נִכְתָּם" הַיְנוּ כְּכֶתֶם הָעוֹבֵר מֵעֵבֶר לְעֵבֶר בְּחֹזֶק שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּבֵּס.
The meaning of "indelibly stained" is like a stain that penetrates through and through with such force that it cannot be washed out.
הַיְנוּ כִּי בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ עֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵגוֹת, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
For in every matter there are ten levels, as is known;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ סֵדֶר הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת שֶׁל כָּל דָּבָר לִהְיוֹת קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה.
this is the ordered structure through which each thing becomes a complete configuration.

"וְעֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם" וְגוֹמֵר939 Ecclesiastes 8:9 — “All this I have seen, and I applied my heart to every deed done under the sun — a time when one man rules over another to his own hurt.” Rashi: "All this I saw" refers to what was said above; and I also gave my heart to all the deeds of men. I saw a time when one man ruled over his fellow and prevailed against him, and in the end it turned to his own hurt: Amalek prevailed over Israel, and his end was "his latter end shall be that he perish forever" — and so too Pharaoh, Nebuchadnezzar and Sennacherib. Metzudas Dovid: "All this" — the work that is done, spoken of below — I saw with my own eyes and set my heart upon it to understand it; "under the sun" means in this world. And I saw and understood that there is a time when men rule one over another to do one another harm, because the power is given into the hand of him who wishes to injure his fellow.,
Thus, when "man rules" and so forth,
שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה דְּאָדָם רַע,
so that a complete configuration of an evil person has been formed,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְעוֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית, שֶׁכָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו וּרְצוֹנוֹתָיו שְׁקוּעִים בְּכָךְ,
meaning that he has reached all the way to the depth of the first point, until all his thoughts and desires are immersed in that evil,
עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁמַן לְבָבוֹ וְאָזְנָיו מִלָּשׁוּב כְּלָל — זֶה נִקְרָא "נִכְתָּם",
until his heart and ears have become dulled against returning at all - this is called being indelibly stained,
דְּאֵין כִּבּוּס מוֹעִיל.
so that ordinary cleansing no longer helps.
כִּי כִבּוּס הוּא עַל יְדֵי דְּבָרִים הַמַּעֲבִירִים הַכֶּתֶם,
For washing works through things that remove the stain,
וְהֵם דְּבָרִים הַמְכַפְּרִים וּמְקַנְּחִים, כְּעִנְיַן תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה.
namely, means that atone and cleanse, such as Torah and prayer.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהִיא הֲשָׁבַת הַדָּבָר לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה קֹדֶם הַחֵטְא,
Repentance, by contrast, restores the thing to the state in which it stood before the sin,
וּכְאִלּוּ אֵין כָּאן כֶּתֶם כְּלָל — זֶה מוֹעִיל לְעוֹלָם.
so that it is as though no stain existed at all; this remains effective in every circumstance.
אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַתְּשׁוּבָה,
There are, however, twenty-four things that obstruct repentance,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ רַבֵּנוּ יִצְחָק אַלְפָסִי וְרַבֵּנוּ אָשֵׁר בְּסוֹף יוֹמָא940 Rif Yoma 6a:4 — Twenty-four things hold back repentance, and these are they: talebearing and evil speech; an irascible man; one given to evil thoughts; one who associates with a wicked man; one who habitually joins a meal that does not suffice for its host; one who gazes at forbidden women; one who shares with a thief; one who says "I will sin and repent"; one who honors himself through his fellow's disgrace; one who separates from the community; one who despises his parents; one who despises his teachers; one who curses the public; one who prevents the public from performing a commandment; one who turns his fellow from a good way to an evil way; one who makes use of a poor man's pledge; one who accepts a bribe in order to pervert others in judgment; one who finds a lost object and does not return it to its owner; one who sees his son going out to evil ways and does not restrain him; one who eats the plunder of the poor, orphans and widows; one who disputes the words of the Sages; one who suspects the innocent; one who hates reproof; and one who mocks the commandments. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): Even the twenty-four things that hold back repentance do not prevent its acceptance altogether, as the Rambam said, for in truth nothing stands before repentance. And although by the law of the Torah it ought not to be accepted, this is the greatness of repentance, that it breaks through the fence of the Torah's law..
as cited by Rabbeinu Yitzchak Alfasi and Rabbeinu Asher at the end of tractate Yoma.
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר הָעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה אִם שָׁב,
Certainly, nothing can stand before repentance once a person actually returns;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם מְעַכְּבִין בְּיָדוֹ מִלָּשׁוּב כְּלָל.
rather, these things obstruct him from coming to repentance in the first place.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּן הַמֵּצַר צָעַק לִבּוֹ אֶל הַשֵּׁם בִּתְפִלָּה לְהוֹשִׁיעוֹ מִצָּרָתוֹ הַנִּגְרֶמֶת לוֹ עַל יְדֵי חֶטְאוֹ,
Even though from within his distress his heart may cry out to the Lord in prayer to save him from the trouble brought about by his sin,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין גּוֹמֵר בְּלִבּוֹ לָשׁוּב בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל.
he still does not reach a genuine inner resolve to repent.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְתָּם עֲוֹנוֹ, שֶׁעַל זֶה הֵם כְּלַל הָעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים,
This is because his sin has become deeply stained; this is the common principle underlying the twenty-four obstructing factors.
כְּמוֹ "בַּעַל מַחֲשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת",
One example is a person habitually possessed by evil thoughts,
דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהָרַע גָּבַר בְּכָל כֹּחוֹתָיו עַד שֹׁרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
meaning that evil has gained mastery over all his faculties, all the way to the root of thought,
עַד שֶׁהוּא מְחַשֵּׁב בָּרַע תָּדִיר, רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן, וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ.
until he thinks continually about evil, may the Merciful One save us, and does not abandon it.
וְכֵן כֻּלָּם הֵם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי מַדְרֵגוֹת שֶׁל עֲוֹנוֹת הַנִּכְתָּמִים,
So too, all of them are twenty-four types of levels of sins that have become deeply stained,

שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶגֶד עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה "שָׁבְקֵי לְהוּ" דְּבְתַעֲנִית ה׳, סוֹף עַמּוּד א; עַיֵּן שָׁם941 Taanit 5a-b — Rav Nachman said to R. Yitzchak: What is the meaning of the verse, “For My people have done two evils”? Were there only two? There were twenty-four! He said to him: This is what R. Yochanan said — [it is] one that is equivalent to two. And which is it? Idolatry, as it is written: “For My people have done two evils — they have forsaken Me, the source of living waters, to hew out for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns.” Rashi: “He left out twenty-four?” — asked in astonishment, for in the portion of Ezekiel twenty-four transgressions are enumerated which they committed. Rashi: ["He left out twenty-four?"] — asked in astonishment: in the portion "Will you judge" (Ezekiel 22) twenty-four transgressions that they committed are enumerated; another explanation: that they transgressed the twenty-four books [of Scripture]. ["That is equivalent to two"] — as the Gemara goes on to explain from the Kittim and the Kedarites: [Israel] did worse than both, and did not learn from them; for the Kittim and Kedarites, though what they revere is inferior, would not exchange it, whereas My people exchanged Me for another — and not only that, but for "what does not profit." Maharsha (on 5b, s.v. "and which is it? idolatry"): On the gravity of idolatry it has already been said that it is equivalent to the whole Torah; here the point is that it counts as two transgressions, for it contains two evils. Rashi derives this from the Kittim and the Kedarites, but then the Gemara need not have cited "For My people have done two evils," the very verse in question; rather, it cites it because the two evils are spelled out in its continuation: "they have forsaken Me, the source of living waters," and moreover they hew out for themselves "cisterns, cisterns" — doubled and in the plural, for they desired many gods, as it says, "according to the number of your cities are your gods" (Jeremiah 2:28) — and these are "broken," that is, all of them utterly worthless. Maharsha (s.v. "were there only two?"): [He left out] twenty-two: see Rashi. One may further explain: did they commit only two transgressions? Did He leave out the twenty-two — that is, that they transgressed the entire Torah, which was given in twenty-two letters? Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 2): A person chooses as his deity what he imagines to be his own portion: one nation thinks itself of the portion of fire, and so each nation chose as its deity what it thinks to be its portion; and though they know there is a more important power that prevails over the power that is their portion, since they think they belong to that power they do not exchange it. But Israel, who are the portion of God — and He rules over all — exchanged His glory for "what does not profit," which is not Israel's portion at all. Hence two evils: they are the portion of God alone, and they exchanged Him for what does not profit.,
corresponding to the twenty-four cases of "they left them" mentioned in Taanit 5a, at the end of the page; see there,
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹם בֵּאוּרָם.
and this is not the place to explain them.
רַק בִּכְלָל, כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יֵדַע נִגְעֵי לְבָבוֹ —
In general, every person who knows the afflictions of his own heart,
אֵיזוֹ עֲבֵרָה שֶׁמְּלַפַּפְתּוֹ וְהוֹלֶכֶת עִמּוֹ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁקָּשֶׁה לוֹ לָשׁוּב הֵימֶנָּה,
and knows of a particular transgression that wraps itself around him and accompanies him - meaning that it is difficult for him to return from it -
וַדַּאי הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְתָּם מֵעֲוֹנוֹ, וְהוּא עָנָף אֶחָד מֵאוֹתָן עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים.
this is certainly because the sin has become deeply impressed within him, and it is a branch of one of those twenty-four matters.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהִתְאַמֵּץ עַל זֶה בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְשׁוּבָה,
He must therefore exert himself specifically over this during the Ten Days of Repentance,
שֶׁאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מָצוּי וְקָרוֹב, עַד שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר הַמְעַכֵּב, דְּהַיְנוּ הַמֶּרְחָק.
for then the Blessed One is "found" and "near," so that the barrier - namely, distance - is absent.
כִּי עִכּוּב הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא הָרִחוּק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the obstruction of repentance is distance from the Blessed One,
וְזֶה אֵינוֹ כְּלָל בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְשׁוּבָה.
and during the Ten Days of Repentance that distance is not present in the same way at all.
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי אֱמֶת, גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי;
The truth is that "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will; and what prevents us...?" and so forth.
וְאַף בָּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַתְּשׁוּבָה — מִי מְעַכֵּב?
Even in the case of the twenty-four things that obstruct repentance, what is truly doing the obstructing?
רַק הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה, שֶׁמַּעֲלֶה חִמּוּצִים קָשִׁים לַמֹּחַ וְלַלֵּב,
Only the leaven in the dough, which produces severe fermentations in the mind and heart;
לֹא מִגּוּפָהּ שֶׁל עִסָּה עַצְמָהּ כְּלָל, כִּי רְצוֹנוֹ לָשׁוּב לְפָנָיו בֶּאֱמֶת.
it does not arise from the substance of the dough itself, for the person's essential will is genuinely to return before Him.
וְעַל זֶה תּוֹקְעִין שׁוֹפָר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם אֶחָד מִימֵי תְשׁוּבָה, לְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן,
For this reason the shofar is sounded on Rosh Hashanah, one of the days of repentance, in order to confound the Satan,
וְהוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע, כַּנִּזְכָּר, דְּהַכֹּל אֶחָד.
who is the evil inclination, as stated above; the two are one.
כִּי עִנְיַן קוֹל שׁוֹפָר הוּא צַעֲקַת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the sound of the shofar is the cry of the heart of the Children of Israel to the Blessed One.
וְהוּא קוֹל בְּעָלְמָא, בְּלֹא חִתּוּךְ דִּבּוּר בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת,
It is a simple, unarticulated sound, without speech divided into letters,
רַק כְּמַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל הֶמְיָה לְבַד מִתּוֹךְ הַמֵּצַר.
like one who can only emit a groan from within the narrow place of distress.
וְהַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְתָּם הֶעָוֹן, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקֵּעַ בְּכָל מַעֲמַקֵּי הָרַע,
This corresponds to the state in which the sin has become deeply stained - that is, a person has sunk into all the depths of evil -
עַד שֶׁאֵין שְׂפָתָיו נִפְתָּחוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה,
until his lips can no longer open in prayer to the Blessed One concerning that matter,
אֲפִלּוּ מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ בִּלְבַד גַּם כֵּן.
not even externally, as mere lip-service.
וְהַדִּבּוּר הוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה מֵעֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵגוֹת,
Speech is the final level among the ten levels
הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מֵעוֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה עַד עוֹמֶק אַחֲרִית דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת — פֶּה, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
that extend from the depth of the first point of thought to the depth of the final point, the attribute of Malkhut - the mouth - as is known.

וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַיְפַתּוּהוּ בְּפִיהֶם" וְגוֹמֵר, "וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר" וְגוֹמֵר942 Taanit 8a — Shmuel appointed an interpreter before him and expounded: “And they enticed Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue; their heart was not steadfast with Him, nor were they faithful in His covenant” — and even so, “He, being merciful, forgives iniquity.” Rashi: "Their heart was not steadfast with Him": with the Holy One, blessed be He. "And even so": it is written immediately afterward, "And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity," and He hears their prayer; so how can you say that their prayer is heard only if one places his soul in his palm, that is, that his soul is directed along with his palm? Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 8): When Adam heard from Cain that he had repented and reached a compromise, he said, "Such is the power of repentance": it avails even through verbal confession alone, though one has not yet forsaken [the sin] as is fitting, in the manner of what is said, "They enticed Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue," and even so, "He, being merciful, forgives iniquity." For Israel's inner will is truly to do the will of the Blessed One completely, and on Shabbos, when this becomes clear, even confession of the mouth avails, since the Blessed One afterwards clarifies that it truly came from the will of the heart. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): Among Israel even this [goodness of the mouth alone] is good, as they said: "They enticed Him with their mouth... and their heart was not [steadfast]...," and even so, "He, being merciful, forgives." For what the heart does not want stems only from the evil inclination, and even when one sees that his heart's will is not yet in it, good speech of the mouth, called "the lips of the righteous," avails to teach and draw the will into the heart as well. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 57): "They enticed Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue" is service only from the lips outward, and even so "He, being merciful, forgives iniquity," for the Blessed One, who examines hearts, knows the depth of Israel's heart, that it stirs only with good. This is like overcharging by less than a sixth, which is waived entirely. Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Ta'anis 7): The Gemara's answer, "here of an individual, here of the community," means that an individual standing in prayer before the Blessed One must pray from the depth of the heart with great self-sacrifice; but in communal prayer, where one takes upon himself "You shall love your fellow as yourself," one must give room to one's fellow even if he clarifies himself only in the outer garment and not from the depth of the heart. This is "They enticed Him with their mouth... and their heart was not steadfast with Him": he too must be given a place, for the Blessed One commanded the mitzvah of the parapet, to give a place to every single creature.,
It is written, "They enticed Him with their mouths..." and nevertheless, "He, being merciful, forgives..."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית ח׳ עַמּוּד א,
as the Sages explain in Taanit 8a.
שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִקְרָא נִכְתָּם עָוֹן כְּשֶׁהוּא מְפַתֶּה בַּפֶּה עַל כָּל פָּנִים, מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ,
So long as a person can at least "entice" with his mouth, even if only externally, the sin is not yet called fully indelible,
כִּי זֶה מְהַנֵּי בְּאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי,
for even this has efficacy in a Jew,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן לְעִנְיַן "כּוֹפִין עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אֲנִי",
as Maimonides wrote regarding the rule that "we compel him until he says, 'I want to,'"
דְּלָא מַשְׁגְּחִינַן בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּלִבּוֹ נֶגֶד הַתּוֹרָה.
for we do not treat the contrary impulse in his heart as his true will when it opposes the Torah.
וְזֶהוּ וִדּוּי דְּבָרִים הַמּוֹעִיל לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה,
This is the power of verbal confession, which helps the penitent;
אַף דְּעִקָּרָהּ בַּלֵּב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶה פּוֹעֵל כַּפָּרָה מְעַט,
although repentance is principally in the heart, verbal confession nevertheless produces some measure of atonement,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא יֻכְנַס גַּם כֵּן מְעַט מְעַט לַלֵּב,
and through it the matter can gradually penetrate into the heart as well,
וּכְטַעַם: "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן".
in the spirit of the verse, "The lips of the righteous know favor."
אֲבָל הַמִּשְׁתַּקֵּעַ עַד הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָעֲשִׂירִית,
But one who has sunk as far as the tenth level,
שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר אֵין בּוֹ לָשׁוּב עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן כְּלָל, כִּי נַעֲשָׂה אֶצְלוֹ כְּהֶתֵּר לְגַמְרֵי,
so that even the power of speech is no longer available to him to repent of that particular sin, because it has become entirely permitted in his own eyes,
וְאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כֹּחַ הַשְׁמָעַת קוֹל פָּשׁוּט לְבַד,
retains only the ability to utter a simple, undifferentiated sound,
בְּדֶרֶךְ כְּלָל: "שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ" עַל כָּל פָּנִים.
to express at least the general truth: "Our will is to do Your will."
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כַּאֲשֶׁר יַרְגִּישׁ חֶרְדַּת הַדִּין, מִיָּד צוֹעֵק לִבּוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Every Jew, when he feels the dread of judgment, immediately experiences a cry of the heart toward the Blessed One.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹתֵר, אִם יַעַבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם צָרוֹת רַבּוֹת וְרָעוֹת,
It is well known that even the most sinful Jews, if many severe troubles pass over them,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, יַתְחִילוּ לִצְעֹק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
will begin to cry out to the Blessed One.
וְזֶה מֵעִיד עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם הַנֶּעְלָם,
This testifies to the hidden root in the depths of their heart,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר מִמִּשְׁנָתֵנוּ בְּפֶרֶק י״ז דְּכֵלִים בְּכֶלֶב הַיָּם943 Mishnah Kelim 17:13 — Everything that is in the sea is pure, except the sea-dog, because it flees to dry land — these are the words of R. Akiva. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Thirteen Principles and Guidelines §2): The place to which a person flees in his time of distress shows that it is his root. And if he flees to words of Torah, it is known that his root is from the Torah, even though by birth he is not so. [Source:] Kelim ch. 17, mishnah 13: "Everything in the sea is pure except the sea-dog, because it flees to dry land"; see there in Bartenura.,
as I wrote elsewhere from the Mishnah in chapter 17 of Kelim concerning the sea-dog,
דְּלַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהָאָדָם בּוֹרֵחַ בְּעֵת צָרָתוֹ וְצַעַר הַמַּגִּיעַ עַד הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהוּא בּוֹרֵחַ לְהַצִּיל נַפְשׁוֹ —
that the place to which a person flees when his distress reaches his very soul, when he runs there to save his life,
מִשָּׁם הוּא שָׁרְשׁוֹ.
that is the place of his root.

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ט״ז944 Rosh Hashanah 16a — The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Recite before Me on Rosh HaShana Kingships, Remembrances, and Shofarot — Kingships, so that you crown Me as king over you; Remembrances, so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar. Tosafos (s.v. "with a ram's shofar"): In chapter Ra'uhu Beit Din (26a) the Mishnah records that R. Yosei validates even a cow's horn; but we hold in accordance with R. Yehuda that one sounds with bent rams' horns, as the Gemara rules there (26b). Maharsha (s.v. "recite before Me Kingships"): The Sifrei derives them from the verse "And you shall sound… and they shall be to you for a remembrance… I am the Lord your God" (Numbers 10:10): "you shall sound" — these are Shofarot; "for a remembrance" — these are Remembrances; "I am the Lord your God" — this is Kingships. The intent of Kingships, Remembrances and Shofarot is explained in the chapter "How is the order of fasts" [Taanit, ch. 2]. Maharsha (s.v. "why do we sound a ram's horn"): The Ran explains that [R. Abbahu] asks this about the mere custom of sounding with a ram's horn; but it seems to me that he asks it on the Mishnah in chapter Ra'uhu Beit Din, "R. Yehuda says: On Rosh Hashanah one sounds with [the horns] of males," which is the accepted halachah. This follows the Midrash that Rashi cites on the Torah, that the yovel is a ram's horn (for in Arabic a ram is called yovla), since we derive the shofar of Rosh Hashanah below [in chapter 2] from the shofar of the Jubilee. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a, s.v. "Kingships, Remembrances, Shofarot"): Kingships: the Blessed One is King, and as King He comes to judge; therefore Remembrances follow, for remembrance is not judgment — on the contrary, it recalls what was forgotten, and since He remembers everything, reaching what is deep and inward, He remembers Israel for good, and by this they are saved from the attribute of judgment. And this is "by the shofar," for the tekia signifies elevation, and all elevation is mercy, as the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 29): when Israel take up their shofars and sound them, the Holy One, blessed be He, rises from the throne of judgment and sits upon the throne of mercy.
