It teaches that Israel enter into judgment first — in accordance with Rav Chisda, who said: A king and the community — the king enters into judgment first, as it is said, “the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people.” Rashi: "A king and the community": when the Holy One, blessed be He, judges them, the king enters first. "The judgment of His servant": Solomon says this [of himself]. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 8b): "A judgment for the God of Yaakov" includes the nations, for the God of Yaakov is the God of all: Yaakov's inheritance extends without boundary or limit up to the level that is the cause of all, as it is said, "the portion of Yaakov is the Former of all." The king enters into judgment first — not first in time, for the Blessed One understands all their deeds together, but first in rank — because as king he is set apart from the people and nearer to the Blessed One, and those who are higher come first in judgment, according to their nearness; so too Israel, who are set apart from the nations, more inward and nearer to the Blessed One, and are called kings ("a kingdom of priests"), enter into judgment first, for it is not fitting that Israel should stand outside, and since their judgment is separate and they are not included with the nations, the anger against the rest of creation does not reach them. וְהַיְינוּ לְעִנְיַן הַהַעֲבֵרָה דְּהַסְּקִירָה הוּא כְּאֶחָד.

On Rosh Hashanah, however, all who enter the world pass before Him like bnei maron and are surveyed in a single glance, including the nations; Israel merely passes first, as the Gemara teaches, while the Divine survey itself encompasses all as one.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין מוּבָן לְפִי זֶה מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִיפּוּשׁ חָרוֹן אַף וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּבִּשְׁעַת הַהַעֲבֵרָה כְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה הַמִּשְׁפָּט וְהֶחָרוֹן וְלֹא מִצַּד הַסְּקִירָה.

At first glance, this makes difficult the Gemara’s reason that Israel is judged first “before the Divine anger increases.” It must therefore be that during the individual passing the judgment and anger are already aroused, rather than through the single all-encompassing survey.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת חֲטָאִים תִּרְדֹּף רָעָה וְהָרָע הוּא עַצְמוֹ הֶחָרוֹן וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.)962 Bava Batra 16a — It was taught in a baraita: He descends and leads astray, ascends and stirs up wrath, takes permission and takes the soul. Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. Rashi: He descends below and leads people astray into sin; he ascends above and by his accusation provokes the wrath of the King; and he receives permission from Him to kill the sinner, once permission has been granted, as it is written, "you moved Me against him." Maharsha: The baraita sets the three out in order: as the evil inclination he descends and leads a man astray from the good way to the evil; as Satan he then ascends and accuses him before the Lord and provokes wrath; and as the angel of death he takes permission and takes his soul. It does not say that he descends again to take the soul, because the soul, even during a man's life, cleaves to the upper world through what it apprehends, and it is there that the angel of death severs it from the body. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 168): Sins, judgments and sufferings are all one thing, as the Sages said, "He descends and seduces, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul." And since they said that no angel performs two missions — an angel being the name for the power of a thing — it is all one matter: in the world of the Throne, where the King sits on the throne of judgment, it is called judgments; in the world of the angels, sins; and below, sufferings. Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil. עוֹלֶה וּמְקַטְרֵג יוֹרֵד וְכוּלֵי הַקִטְרוּג הוּא הֶחָרוֹן וּנְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט הַנַעֲשָׂה וְהוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵי וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא מִשְׁפָּט אֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל חֹק שֶׁהוּא לִישָּׁנָא דִּמְזוֹנֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בֵּיצָה טז.)963 Beitzah 16a — A man's entire sustenance is allotted to him from Rosh HaShanah to Yom Kippur, except for what he spends on Sabbaths, on Festivals, and on his sons' study of Torah: if he spends less, less is allotted him; if he spends more, more is added. R. Abbahu said: What is the verse? "Sound the horn at the new moon, at the concealing, for our festal day" — which festival is it on which the moon is concealed? You must say: this is Rosh HaShanah. And it is written, "For it is a statute [chok] for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob." How do we know that "chok" is a term for food? For it is written, "And they ate their allotment [chukam] which Pharaoh gave them." Rashi: "A man's entire sustenance" — all that he is destined to earn in the year and live from is fixed for him: such and such shall he earn this year; and he must take care not to spend lavishly, for they will not add to his earnings for food beyond what was apportioned him. "Except for what he spends on Sabbaths" — for that they did not fix what he should earn or from where it should come to him, but according to what he is accustomed to spend it is provided for him, whether at once or later. "Which festival is it on which the moon is concealed" — on which the moon is not visible to anyone, but only at dawn to those who dwell in the east and at dusk to those who dwell in the west, whereas on the other festivals the moon has already partly filled out and is visible everywhere. Tosafos: Rabbeinu Yitzchak explained that all three are derived from verses cited above: what one spends on the Sabbath, from "Borrow on My account and I will repay"; and his sons' study of Torah, from "the joy of the Lord" — and joy is Torah, as it is written "the precepts of the Lord are upright, rejoicing the heart." Maharsha: Even according to the view that on Passover the world is judged with regard to grain, that concerns the grain of the world at large, whether the crop will prosper; but each individual's sustenance, whether it will come to him in plenty or not, is judged from Rosh HaShanah until Yom Kippur, as is said here. The proof for "chok" as a term for food is taken from the end of the verse, "and they ate their allotment," and not from "for the priests had an allotment from Pharaoh" — since that could mean a fixed sum of money from which they bought whatever they needed, whereas "they ate their allotment" shows that the allotment itself was food. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 105a): Explaining why the decree against the house of Eli could be atoned for through Torah, he writes that the Torah, being intellectual, stands above the decree, "as we explained concerning 'a man's sustenance is allotted to him from Rosh HaShanah' (Beitzah 16a), that the Torah is not subject to the decree, for it stands above the decree" [which is why the expenses of his sons' Torah study are outside the yearly allotment]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 10): From "For it is a statute for Israel" the Sages expounded that all of a man's sustenance is allotted to him from Rosh HaShanah; "man" without qualification means Israel, who are called "man," and "statute" is a term for food. That is, the Blessed One allots to each one of Israel as much sustenance as will benefit him for the service of the Blessed One, and this is the "allotted bread" that King Solomon requested, even though his daily meal was very large. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 1): On "Which festival is it on which the moon is concealed? It is Rosh HaShanah," [the author's] father explained that "at the concealing" alludes to the fact that a person does not see his actions joined all the way up to the Supernal Sun: he sees only that "according to the effort is the reward," but not their connection up to the infinite light. Therefore the commandment of this day is to sound the shofar, which arouses the Great Shofar, signifying that Israel raises all its actions up to the Supernal Sun, to the place where the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence. דְּכָל מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם קְצוּבִים אָז.

For in truth, “evil pursues sinners”: the evil itself becomes the wrath. As the Sages said, Satan ascends and prosecutes and then descends; the prosecution itself is the wrath, while the taking of the soul is the judgment that follows, and all of it is the evil inclination itself. Therefore, with the nations it is called judgment, whereas for Israel it is called a statute—chok, a term also used for sustenance—for all of a person’s sustenance is apportioned at that time.

וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אֶצְלָם דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵחֵלֶק אָז כָּל מִינֵי שֶׁפַע וְטוֹבָה לָהֶם כִּי הֵם יוֹדְעִים לַהֲפֹךְ כּוּרְסְיָא דְּדִּינָא לְרַחֲמֵי כַּנּוֹדָע בְּזוֹהַר וְנִרְמַז בַּגְּמָרָא ט"ז א' שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה זִכְרוֹנֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי לְטוֹבָה בַּמֶּה בַּשּׁוֹפָר כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם אוֹמְרִים מַלְכִיּוֹת לְהַמְלִיכוֹ הֲרֵי נַעֲשָׂה הַשְׁלָמַת הַבְּרִיאָה.

This is the essential character of Rosh Hashanah for Israel: the blessed Hashem then distributes to them every form of bounty and good, for they know how to transform the throne of judgment into a throne of mercy. This is alluded to in the teaching, “that your remembrance rise before Me for good—and through what? Through the shofar”; by reciting Malchiyot and crowning Him King, they bring the purpose of Creation to completion.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זִכְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁהוּא הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא מַשְׁגִּיחַ בַּהוֹוֶה וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשְׁכָה הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ לְטוֹבָה כֵּיוָן שֶׁהֵם מַכִּירִים שֶׁהוּא הַמַשְׁגִּיחַ.

Afterward come Zikhronot: the recognition that He is actively overseeing the present. Through this recognition His providence is drawn toward them for good, because they acknowledge that He alone is the One who oversees.

וְזֶה תַּכְלִית כָּל כַּוָּנַת הַהַשְׁגָּחָה לְהַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ מַשְׁגִּיחַ רַק לְפִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ טְעָנוֹת גַּם עֲלֵיהֶם דְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה מְלֻכְלָכִים וְכוּלֵי עַל כֵּן אָמַר בַּמֶּה רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ וְזְכוּת כֵּיוָן דְּנִקְרָא אָז מֶלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט עַל זֶה אָמַר בַּשּׁוֹפָר דְּהוּא מְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא ט"ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב וּבַתּוֹסָפוֹת בְּשֵׁם הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּיָרֵא שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹפָר דִּלְעָתִיד.

This recognition is the entire purpose of providence. Yet there are claims against Israel as well, for throughout the year they become soiled by sin; therefore the Gemara asks, “through what?”—meaning, through what power and merit can this remembrance rise when He is then called the King of judgment? The answer is: through the shofar, which confounds Satan. The Yerushalmi cited by Tosafot explains that Satan is afraid that this may be the shofar of the future redemption.

הָעִנְיָן כִּי גְּאוּלָּה דִּלְעָתִיד הוּא בַּזְּמַן בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֵּין לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא י"א רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א' וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָז נִשְׁלָם תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה וְהַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא מִאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד כִּי לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ אָז אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.

The matter is that the future redemption takes place at the time associated with the world’s creation, according to either opinion of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, because then the purpose of Creation will be completed. The beginning of Creation itself came solely through an awakening from Above, from the blessed Hashem, since no awakening from below could yet exist.
אֲבָל כַּוָּנַת הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא לָתֵת מָקוֹם לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
Yet the very intention of Creation was to create room for an awakening from below.

וְכָל הַגְּאֻלּוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים כְּמוֹ בְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא שִׁירָה חֲדָשָׁה לְשׁוֹן נוּקְבָא וְיֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיהָ גָּלוּת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מְכִילְתָּא פָּרָשַׁת הַשִּׁירָה פָּרָשָׁה א)964 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Shirah 1:10 — The tenth is for the time to come, as it is said: "Sing to the Lord a new song, His praise from the end of the earth," and it says: "Sing to the Lord a new song, His praise in the assembly of the faithful." All the songs of the past are called by a feminine term: just as a female gives birth, so the deliverances of the past had servitude after them. But the deliverance to come is called by a masculine term, as it is said: "Ask now and see, does a male give birth?" Just as a male does not give birth, so the deliverance to come has no servitude after it, as it is said: "Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation." כִּי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא אֵינוֹ דָּבָר הַמִּתְקַיֵּים בִּתְמִידוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא תַּחַת הַזְּמַן וְשִׁינּוּי כ"ח עִתִּים.

All earlier redemptions came through an awakening from below—through Israel, who sanctify the times. Thus in Egypt redemption followed Israel’s cry. Such redemption is called a “new song” in the feminine form and can be followed by another exile, because an awakening from below cannot remain permanently fixed in this world, which is subject to time and to the changing twenty-eight periods.

אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא הוּא שִׁיר חָדָשׁ לְשׁוֹן זֵכֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיַּרְא כִּי אֵין אִישׁ וְגוֹמֵר וַתּוֹשַׁע לוֹ זְרוֹעוֹ וְגוֹמֵר965 Isaiah 59:16 — “And He saw that there was no man, and He was astonished that there was no intercessor; so His own arm brought salvation for Him, and His righteousness sustained Him.” Rashi: "And He saw that there was no man" — now, when He relents of the evil against His people, He sees that there is no righteous man to stand in the breach. "And He was astonished" — He kept silent, to see whether there was any to intercede for them, and there was none interceding; the word denotes a man who stands mute and bewildered in his astonishment. "So His own arm brought Him salvation" — that He should take vengeance on His enemies, "and His righteousness sustained Him" — moving Him and strengthening His hands for that vengeance, even though we are not worthy to be saved. Radak: "And He saw that there was no man" — this is said of Israel as a whole: that they would not return in complete repentance nor entreat God with a whole heart until they saw the first signs of the redemption. "Man" here means the community as a whole, for it cannot be that there are no righteous and good men in Israel, but only that all Israel cannot be redeemed by their merit. "His own arm brought Him salvation" — for He has no helper or supporter with Him but His own power and His own righteousness alone. Metzudas Dovid: When He sees that there is among them no man fit and worthy for them to be redeemed by his merit, and stands in astonishment, observing that there is none among them to intercede and pray for the redemption — then the arm of the Lord brings Him salvation, to bring the redemption without merit and without an intercessor. "And His righteousness" — the attribute of charity sustains Him to act beyond the strict line of the law. Malbim: A salvation wrought for Israel's own merit comes about in one of two ways: by the merit of the people's deeds, which Scripture calls a "helper," since such merit helps Him to act; or by the prayer of a righteous man, which it calls a "supporter," since that is not full help but only a measure of support. Here God sees that there is no "man" — none found worthy by his deeds to be a helper — and He is the more astonished that there is not even one righteous man to pray for the community and be some support. He was therefore constrained to work the salvation by His own power, not by the deeds of those below: "His own arm brought Him salvation," and what sustained Him was the supernal righteousness alone. כְּבְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם.

But in the future it will be a “new song” in the masculine form, as it is written, “He saw that there was no man... and His own arm brought salvation for Him”—a redemption resembling the original act of Creation.

וְאָז יִתָּקַע בַּשּׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל וְבְּאוֹ וְגוֹמֵר הַיְינוּ דְּיִתְעוֹרְרוּ גַּם הֵם לָבוֹא וְלְהִתְקָרֵב לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְעוֹרְרֵם מִשְּׁנָתָם בְּתַרְדֵּמַת הַבְלֵי עוֹלָם.

Then “a great shofar will be sounded, and those who were lost will come,” meaning that even they will awaken to come and draw near to the blessed Hashem because He Himself will rouse them from their sleep in the stupor of this world’s vanities.

וְאָמְנָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּל עִסְקֵנוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וּבְעוֹבָדָא דִּלְתַתָּא אִתְעָרֵר עוֹבָדָא דִּלְעֵילָא וְאָנוּ מַזְכִּירִין וּמְעוֹרְרִין עִנְיַן תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר זֶה דִּלְעָתִיד דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ טוֹעֲנִין הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ אֵלֶיךָ וְנָשׁוּבָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה סוֹף אֵיכָה966 Eikhah Rabbah 5:21 — "Return us to You, O Lord, and we shall return." The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, it is Yours — return us. He said to them: It is yours, as it is stated, "Return to Me and I will return to you, says the Lord." She said before Him: Master of the universe, it is Yours, as it is stated, "Return us, O God of our salvation." Therefore it is said, "Return us to You, O Lord, and we shall return." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): Tishrei, the time of repentance in the Ten Days of Repentance, is Israel's returning to the Blessed One from their own side and by their own effort; as is known, we claim, "Return us to You and we shall return," while the Blessed One claims, "Return to Me and I will return to you." And our side prevailed, according to the view that "in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed," for the redemption of Nisan is what the Blessed One arouses. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 1): [In the future] the awakening will come from the side of the Blessed One, as we ask, "Return us, O Lord, to You, and we shall return"; and although the Blessed One says, "Return to Me and I will return to you," as the Midrash states at the end of Eikhah — meaning that He wants Israel to be awakened from below, from their own side, "listen, and your soul shall live" — nevertheless, from His own side the Blessed One draws Israel near first.).

In this world, however, our entire avodah is through awakening from below; an action below arouses a corresponding action above. We therefore invoke and awaken the future shofar even now, declaring that ultimately everything comes from Him, as we plead, “Return us to You, and we shall return.”

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט וְגַם תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר דִּלְעָתִיד הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְבֹרָר בְּכָל מָשַׁךְ הַגָּלוּת דְּכָל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָם בְּעֶצֶם רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.)967 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious. אָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי הוּצֵי וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ עַל שֶׁשְּׁזָפַתְנִי הַשָּׁמֶשׁ.

For in truth everything occurs through judgment, and even the future shofar is founded upon judgment: throughout the exile the blessed Hashem clarifies that Israel’s sins are not intrinsic to their essence, but resemble “a myrtle standing among thorns,” as the Sages taught, and the darkness caused only by “the sun having gazed upon me.”

וּבְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת קַל מִלְּמַעְלָה הֵם רָצִים לִקְרָאתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָרוּצָה וְמִשַׁיָּכָה הוּא לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ וְהָרִיצָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ וְחָפֵץ מְאֹד בְּכָךְ.

With only the slightest awakening from Above they run toward Him, as it is written, “Draw me; after You we will run.” Drawing is needed for one who is not yet moving willingly, while running expresses one who now desires to go with all his heart.
וְהָא וְהָא אִיתֵיהּ כִּי מִקּוֹדֶם עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה נַעֲשָׂה כֹּבֶד וְצָרִיךְ מִשַׁיָּכָה וְאַחַר הַמִשַׁיָּכָה תֵּיכֶף נָרוּץ מֵעַצְמֵנוּ.
Both are true: at first the “leaven in the dough” weighs a person down and he requires that Divine drawing; but once he is drawn, we immediately run of our own accord.

מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הֵם נִקְרָאִים הַפּוֹשְׁעִים דְּפָשְׁעֵי וְאָזְלֵי וַאֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם הַנַעֲשִׂים גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים דְּאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כָּל אֶחָד מִבְּעט בְּסֻכָּתוֹ וְכוּלֵי כִּי הֲגַם שֶׁנִּמְשָׁכִים הוּא בַּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּמַה לָהֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת.

The nations are different. They are called “those who rebel and continue rebelling”; even those who attach themselves as dragged-along converts are described at the beginning of Avodah Zarah as each kicking his sukkah. Even when they are drawn, it is against their will, because they see no alternative.
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם לֹא יָבוֹאוּ לְקוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר כִּי הַדִּבּוּר הוּא הַגִּילּוּי מַה שֶׁבַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה דּוּגְמַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
Therefore they will not come merely at the sound of the shofar. Speech is the revealed expression of thought, analogous to action.

וּמַה שֶׁבְּגִלּוּי לְכָל גַּם מַלְאָךְ רַע וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עוֹנִין אָמֵן בַּעַל כָּרְחָם אֲבָל הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּגִילּוּי רַק יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁהֵם רוֹצִים לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ אַחַר מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשָׂה לְנִשְׁמָע.

Whatever is openly revealed is such that even an evil angel and the nations are forced to answer Amen. But the level of hidden thought belongs specifically to Israel: Israel arose in the Divine thought because they desire to be drawn after the blessed Hashem’s thought itself, as shown when they placed “we will do” before “we will hear.”

וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם טָעֲנוּ עַל זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת968 Shabbat 88a-b — A certain heretic saw Rava sitting absorbed in his studies, his fingers beneath his feet so that he crushed them until blood flowed. He said to him: You rash people, who put your mouths before your ears — you still persist in your rashness! First you should have listened; if it was within your power, accept it, and if not, do not accept it. He said to him: We, who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, “The integrity of the upright shall guide them”; but of those who walk in perversity it is written, “and the crookedness of the treacherous shall destroy them.” Rashi: ["His fingers":] the fingers of his hands. ["And he was pressing them":] he was crushing them under his legs and did not notice, from his absorption. ["A rash people":] hasty. ["Who put your mouths before your ears":] before you had heard how hard it is and whether you could stand up to it, you took it upon yourselves to fulfill it. ["We, who walk in wholeheartedness":] we walked with Him in simplicity of heart, as those who act out of love, and relied on Him not to burden us with something we could not withstand. Maharsha: ["The integrity of the upright shall guide them":] Besides Rashi's explanation, one may explain it in the manner of "In the way a person wishes to go, he is led" and "One who comes to purify himself is helped": the upright, who wish to walk the straight path even though it is hard for them to do, are guided with help from Heaven; and conversely, "the crookedness of the treacherous," who walk a crooked and not a straight path, "shall destroy them," for "one who comes to defile himself, [the way] is opened for him." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 29): The heretic held that this was out of order — by right a person should first hear a thing and afterwards know to do it — and so he said that Israel's putting "we will do" before "we will hear" came from their rashness, that they are disorderly in their actions. Rava answered him that the matter is the reverse of what he thought: it is the ways of those who walk in guile that depart from order, but Israel walk in their integrity, and the action of whoever is wholehearted never departs from the proper order — and by the proper order the doing should come first, for that is what man was created for. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 8): The garment for attaining the truth of the Torah is wholeheartedness, to be wholehearted with the Lord, for "the integrity of the upright shall guide them," as they said in Perek R. Akiva: "We who walk in wholeheartedness..." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei): To be easily enticed toward the good is a fine trait for which Israel were praised: they are drawn after the Blessed One with great haste, without deliberation or delay, as the heretic said to Rava, "Rash people, who put your mouths before your ears." Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 20): Rava's reply to the Sadducee who called Israel "rash people, who put your mouths before your ears" and said they should first have listened to see whether they were able, namely "We who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, 'The integrity of the upright shall guide them,'" means that we are wholehearted in the will of the Blessed One, [confident] that He will surely help us to complete it for the good; and this is what is called "whose strength is in You." Sod Yesharim (Seventh Day of Pesach 14): At times a person must set aside his human form [of reasoning] to fulfill the will of the Blessed One, like a horse ridden by its master, as in the heretic's charge against Rava and Rava's reply: Israel, who at their root cleave to knowledge, are taught by that knowledge that at times they should set aside their power of choice to fulfill the will of the Blessed One. But the nations, who branch from the supernal princes that stand in awe without knowledge, have no bond with their prince and act without knowledge or choice, like a horse of the Other Side; and even when they sometimes yield before the Blessed One, it is only so as to spread out afterwards with great force, as Balaam did. (פח סוֹף עַמּוּד א) בְּרֵישָׁא אִיבַּעְיָא לְכוּ וְכוּלֵי אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל רוֹצִים לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ אַחַר מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא שְׁמִיעָה וְיְדִיעָה כְּלָל מַה יִרְצֶה.

The nations objected precisely to this, as the Sages taught at Sinai: “first you should have listened.” Israel, however, desire to be drawn after the Divine thought even before hearing or knowing what He will ask of them.
וְזֶהוּ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא קוֹל פָּשׁוּט בְּלֹא הַוְדַעַת מַה הָרָצוֹן בּוֹ מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּדִבּוּר שׁוֹמֵעַ מַה מְדַבֵּר.

This is the meaning of the shofar sound at the giving of the Torah: it is a simple sound that does not reveal the content of the Divine will. Speech, by contrast, allows the hearer to know what is being said.
וְהַשּׁוֹפָר הוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר לָבוֹא בְּלֹא יְדִיעָה כְּלָל עַל מַה וְלָמָּה.
The shofar therefore awakens a person to come without first knowing exactly toward what, or why.
וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לֹא יִרְצוּ בָּזֶה רַק בְּרֵישָׁא לִשְׁמוֹעַ אִם הוּא כִּרְצוֹנָם.
The nations do not desire this; they first wish to hear whether the command accords with their own will.

וְרַק הָאוֹבְדִים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲגַם שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בַּמֶּה שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקְּעוּ עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא יִתְעוֹרְרוּ לָשׁוּב גַּם דְּלָא יָדְעֵי כְּלָל עַד כְּמַה תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבוֹדָה כִּי נַפְשָׁם קְשׁוּרָה בְּעֶצֶם לָרוּץ אַחַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

But the lost members of Israel, however deeply they have sunk, can be awakened by an awakening from Above to return even without knowing how demanding the service will be, because their souls are intrinsically bound to run after the blessed Hashem.

וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא הֲרַת עוֹלָם שֶׁהָעוֹלָם בְּהֵרָיוֹן וְבְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וְעֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ לְדִּבּוּר וְבְּדָבָר הַשֵּׁם שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ הוּא הַגְּמַר מַעֲשֶׂה וְעַל כֵּן תּוֹקְעִין בַּשּׁוֹפָר.

Thus on Rosh Hashanah, which is called “the conception of the world,” the world is still in pregnancy and in thought and has not yet reached speech; “by the word of Hashem the heavens were made” describes the completion in action. Therefore we sound the shofar.

וְיִסֵּד הַפַּיְטָן בַּשּׁוֹפָר אֲפַתֶּנּוּ וְיָדוּעַ דְּפִתּוּי הוּא מַה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּךְ עַל צַד הָרָאוּי וּכְשֶׁהַפִּתּוּי בְּדִבּוּר הַנִּגְלֶה נֶאֱמַר וַיְפַתּוּהוּ בְּפִיהֶם וְגוֹמֵר וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר וְגוֹמֵר כִּי מִצַּד הַדִּבּוּר הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה יֵשׁ טְעָנוֹת וְצָרִיךְ לְמִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים לְכַפֵּר אֲבָל הַפִּתּוּי דְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר שֶׁהוּא קוֹל פָּשׁוּט בְּלֹא גִּילּוּי הָרָצוֹן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַיוֹדֵעַ מַחְשְׁבוֹת.

This is why the liturgical poet composed the phrase, “With the shofar I will entice Him.” Enticement ordinarily means presenting something in a way that does not fully accord with its revealed state. When the enticement is through revealed speech, Scripture says, “They enticed Him with their mouths... yet He, being merciful, forgave iniquity,” because on the revealed plane of action there are accusations and the attribute of mercy is needed to cleanse them. But the “enticement” of the shofar is a simple sound that does not reveal the will in this world; it is addressed only to the blessed Hashem, Who knows thoughts.
כִּי כָּל קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּסִימָן לָדַעַת מִי שֶׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ הַסִּימָן וְאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה לְאַחַר כְּלָל.
Every shofar sound is therefore like a private sign whose meaning is known only to one who knows the sign; it is not revealed to an outsider at all.
וְעַל כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לֹא יִתְעוֹרְרוּ לְשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל כִּי הֵם אֵין מַכִּירִים הַסִּימָן דְּאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ זֶה רַק מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל הַתּוֹקֵעַ.
For this reason the nations will not awaken to the Great Shofar, because they do not recognize its sign. Only one who knows the thought of the one sounding it can recognize what the sign means.

וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב)969 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2 — "I am asleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2). The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I am asleep with respect to the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness; I am asleep with respect to the offerings, but my heart is awake for the recitation of Shema and prayer; I am asleep with respect to the redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Israel? From this verse: "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Psalms 73:26). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The Blessed One always dwells in the depths of one's heart, as Shir HaShirim Rabbah says that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel — "the Rock of my heart and my portion" — and on this they expounded "I am asleep but my heart is awake": though a person is sunk in imagination, which is the sleep, the imagination does not reach the depths of the heart, where the point of "the Rock of his heart" is always awake, and through it he can awaken from his slumber and merit the complete redemption. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 7): [The Zohar reads] "Many of those who sleep in the dust shall awaken" with "I am asleep but my heart is awake": when the Blessed One dwells in the heart of Israel, as they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel ("God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever"), death is only like sleep. Even though the flaw that brought death has not been repaired in the world at large, one who merits that his heart be a dwelling for the Shechinah is redeemed completely, and his death is only like sleep followed by awakening. דְּבִּפְנִימִיּוּת דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ עַל כֵּן הֵם מִתְעוֹרְרִים לְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר שֶׁלּוֹ וְכֵן הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר לְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר שֶׁלָּנוּ.
The blessed Hashem is called “the heart of Israel.” Because inwardly Israel are bound to Him, they awaken to the sound of His shofar, and correspondingly He is aroused by the sound of ours.

וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּנִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשֶׁיִקָּרֵא זֶה נִקְרָא פִּתּוּי כְּאִלּוּ בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין כֵּן אֲבָל מִצַּד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן כִּי פְּנִימִיּוּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת דְּבוּקָה בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵין שָׁם דָּבָר הַחוֹצֵץ כְּלָל רַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן מִקּוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה וְלֶעָתִיד יְבֻקַּשׁ עֲוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ וְלֹא צְרִיכִין כַּפָּרָה כְּלָל שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן קִנּוּחַ כִּי בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַפְּנִימִיּוּת אֵין חֵטְא.

In this world, which is called the world of falsehood, this is described as “enticement,” as though the claim were not fully true. But from the perspective of primordial thought it is entirely true: the innermost thought of Israel is genuinely bound to Him, with nothing separating at all; the obstruction exists only in outward appearance, like thorns surrounding a rose. In the future, “the iniquity of Israel will be sought and will not be found,” and no cleansing will be required, for when the inward essence is revealed there is no sin.
וְכֵן בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אֵין לְהַזְכִּיר חֵטְא וַעֲוֹן כִּי כָּל עִנְיַן שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת שׁוֹפָר זֶה דִּלְעָתִיד דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ קִטְרוּג וַעֲוֹן כְּלָל.

Therefore on Rosh Hashanah we do not mention sin and iniquity, because the entire shofar service of Rosh Hashanah awakens the future Great Shofar, before which accusation and sin have no standing at all.

וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִגְּרוֹן הָאָדָם גּוּף הַקּוֹל רַק הֶבֶל לְבַד וְאוֹתוֹ הֶבֶל מְקַשְׁקֵשׁ בַּשּׁוֹפָר וּמַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל כִּי גַּם קוֹל הוּא גִּלּוּי מַה עַל כָּל פָּנִים דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל.

This also explains the nature of the shofar’s sound. The actual voice does not emerge directly from the human throat; only breath emerges, and that breath reverberates within the shofar and produces a sound. Even “sound” already represents some degree of outward manifestation.
וְגַם זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם רַק מִצַּד דָּבָר אַחַר הַמְקַבְּלוֹ דְּהוּא הָעוֹלָם.
And even this manifested sound is not produced by the person alone, but through the other object that receives his breath—an image of the created world itself.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאָדָם הוּא רַק הַהֶבֶל לְבַד שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְגָּשׁ כְּלָל בְּשׁוּם חוּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּמַאן דְּנָפַח מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח וּמִפְּנִימִיּוּתוֹ וּבוֹ קָבוּעַ כָּל פְּנִימִיּוּת הָאָדָם.

From the person himself there is only breath, which is not perceptible by any ordinary sense in this world. “One who blows, blows from within himself”: the breath issues from his innermost being, in which the entire inward essence of the person is rooted.
וְעִיקַּר הַמִּצְוָה הוּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ קוֹל זֶה כִּי כָּל כַּוָּנוֹתֵינוּ הוּא לְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא.
The primary commandment is therefore to hear this sound, for our entire intention through it is to awaken an awakening from Above.

items.h:
Seif 2 — The Shofar that Awakens Above and Below
The human shofar echoes the future Great Shofar, awakening Israel while deepening awe before the King.

p: וְלִהְיוֹת קוֹל שׁוֹפָר זֶה שֶׁאָנוּ עוֹשִׂים עַל פִּי מִצְוַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא עַצְמוֹ קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמְּעוֹרֵר אוֹתָנוּ מִתַּרְדֵּמָתֵנוּ כִּלְעָתִיד וְכַנּוֹדָע דִּבְרֵי רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן (פֶּרֶק ג מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה הֲלָכָה דְּ)970 Mishneh Torah, Repentance 3:4 — Although the sounding of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, there is a hint in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep; you slumberers, rouse yourselves from your slumber; search your deeds, return in repentance, and remember your Creator — you who forget the truth amid the vanities of the age and stray all your years after emptiness that neither profits nor saves. Look to your souls, better your ways and your doings, and let each of you forsake his evil way and his thought that is not good. בְּטַעַם שׁוֹפָר כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ עוּרוּ וְכוּלֵי971 Rambam, Hilchot Teshuvah 3:4 — Although the sounding of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, there is an allusion in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep; you slumberers, rouse yourselves from your slumber. Examine your deeds, return in repentance and remember your Creator — you who forget the truth amid the vanities of the time, and who go astray all your years after emptiness and vanity that neither profits nor saves. Look to your souls and better your ways and your deeds; let each of you abandon his evil way and his thought which is not good. וְדִבְרֵי הָאֱלֹקִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַסּוֹד שֶׁהוּא מְעוֹרֵר יְשֵׁנִים בָּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים וְהָא וְהָא אִיתֵיהּ כַּמּוּבָן דְּהַכֹּל אֶחָד.

This shofar sound that we produce in fulfillment of the blessed Hashem’s command is itself a manifestation of the Divine shofar that awakens us from our slumber, just as it will in the future. This is the plain meaning of Maimonides’ teaching, “Awake, sleepers,” and also the deeper teaching of the Ari that the shofar awakens sleepers in the supernal worlds; the two are one.
וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד וַיִּקַץ כְּיָשֵׁן הַשֵּׁם וְגוֹמֵר וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתָּקַע בַּשּׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל לְעוֹרֵר יְשֵׁנִים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּכוּלָּא חַד כַּנּוֹדָע.
So too in the future, “Hashem will awaken as one who slept,” and through this the Great Shofar will be sounded to awaken the sleeping souls of Israel; all of these are one reality.

וְעַל כֵּן תּוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין כְּשֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין וְכְּשֶׁעוֹמְדִין972 Rosh Hashanah 16a-b — Why do they sound a tekia and a terua while seated, and then sound a tekia and a terua while standing [in the Amida]? In order to confound the Satan. And R. Yitzchak said: Any year in which the shofar is not sounded at its beginning will suffer misfortune at its end. What is the reason? Because the Satan was not confounded. Rashi (s.v. "to confound"): That he not bring accusation: when he hears that Israel cherish the commandments, his words are stopped up. Tosafos (s.v. "and they sound… while standing"): One may ask: does one not thereby transgress "you shall not add"? [For one cannot say that, having already fulfilled the obligation, it is no longer its time, since regarding the priestly blessing (28b) we say that its time has not passed, for were another congregation to come along he would bless them again.] The answer is that "you shall not add" does not apply to performing a single commandment twice — as a priest who blesses the same congregation again, or one who takes the lulav and takes it again, and likewise one who sounds and sounds again. Tosafos (s.v. "that is not sounded at its beginning"): The Halachot Gedolot explains: not where [Rosh Hashanah] happens to fall on Shabbat, but where some mishap occurred [that prevented the sounding]. Tosafos (s.v. "to confound the Satan"): The Aruch explains, as found in the Jerusalem Talmud: it is written "He will swallow up death forever" (Isaiah 25:8), and it is written "And it shall come to pass on that day that a great shofar shall be sounded" (Isaiah 27:13). When [the Satan] hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed and yet not alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: "Surely this is the shofar of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,' and my time to be swallowed up has come" — and he is confounded and has no leisure to bring accusation. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a–b): The Satan is privation and the shofar is the good that removes privation — hence "one who sees a shofar in a dream should anticipate redemption" (Berakhot 56b), which includes redemption from the Satan — for the tekia on Rosh Hashanah is elevation, and the Accuser cannot reach that place of elevation. They sound twice, seated and standing, because the first sounding only sets up opposition to him, while overcoming requires a second force that prevails and removes him entirely; this is why the Jerusalem Talmud says that at the first sounding he is alarmed and not alarmed, and at the second he is certain. In sum, the Satan accuses only through the attribute of judgment, which rules on Rosh Hashanah, and the soundings signify that attribute's elevation into mercy, whereupon it has no accuser..
Therefore we sound the tekiah and teruah both while sitting and while standing.

וְכְּשֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין הוּא מִצְוָה דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּמְבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ וְאָז בְּהִיל וְלֹא בְּהִיל דְּעִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה הוּא מַה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר אוֹתָנוּ וְיָהֵיב עֵיטִין אֵיךְ לְהִתְקָרֵב לוֹ.

The blasts sounded while sitting are the Torah commandment, over which the blessing is recited, and at that point Satan is “alarmed and yet not fully alarmed.” Torah itself is the way in which the blessed Hashem awakens us and gives us counsel how to draw near to Him.
וְזֶה עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן מָסַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּיָדָם לְהוֹסִיף גַּם כֵּן מִצְוַת.
Yet He has also entrusted to Israel the ability to add additional commandments.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא לד)973 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34 — R. Yehudah bar Shalom said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "Write these words," Moses asked that the Mishnah too be put in writing. But the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the nations of the world were destined to translate the Torah and read it in Greek, and to say, "We are Israel." Until now the scales are balanced. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the nations: You say that you are My children — I do not know; only those who hold My mysteries are My children. And which are they? This is the Mishnah, which was given orally, and from which everything is to be expounded. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): After prophecy departed, the sages of the Oral Torah began, and the Sages said, "He has set me in dark places — this is the Talmud of Babylonia"; but this is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says in Tanchuma, "Those who hold My mysteries are Israel." For it is written, "He made darkness His hiding place" — there are His hidden things; and though it is darkness and the hiding of the Face, the darkness is cast by the shadow of His hand, shielding us by way of concealment, as one must make shade to protect against the blazing sun. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:86): The Blessed One teaches human beings to exert effort, which is why the Torah began for Israel as the Written Torah; He wishes a person to arrive at His mysteries — as in the Midrash, "He who holds My mysteries…" — and to understand what He indicates to him with the compass. This is the essential effort: to come to the Oral Torah, which is the recognition that everything is from the Blessed One, the "finding" that comes after toil. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): The novel insights of Torah belong to the Oral Torah, whereas in the Written Torah, which is written and set down [before all], there are no novel insights; therefore the nations claim on the strength of the Written Torah, "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers, "He who holds My mysteries…," for the Oral Torah exists only in the hearts of the children of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Edom claims that they are the good and the pure by birth; therefore Haman's decree was a preparation for the Oral Torah, as the Midrash says: because the nations are destined to say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "He who holds My mysteries…" — for it is the Oral Torah that clarifies this. The Oral Torah is what springs from the heart of Israel, the hearts of the children of Israel being its originators, so that it is theirs alone, and this is the testimony that they, and no others, are the masters of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Just as there is wisdom among the nations but no Torah among the nations, so it says in Tanchuma, "He who holds My mysteries…": the Oral Torah was given over only to Israel. The nations, even if they study Torah and innovate in it by their wisdom, speak vanity and not Torah at all, for they innovate from their own wisdom, whereas the Torah is the wisdom of the Blessed One; but the sages of Israel bless over the Torah first and know that the Blessed One is the Giver of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 3): The essence of the Torah is the Oral Torah, which reveals the hidden things of the Written Torah, as it says in Shemos Rabbah that the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek… "He who holds My mysteries…." This is an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob alone: the Torah is handed over to them according to what they clarify through their dialectic and their wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): They said in Tanchuma that the Oral Torah was given because the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek and say "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say, "He who holds My mysteries…." That is, the nations too have a connection to the Written Torah, which is why it was revealed in writing to all who come into the world; but the Oral Torah is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, which cannot be revealed in writing at all, only "the secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him" — the Congregation of Israel, who look to the Blessed One from the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): All the innovation of the Oral Torah comes through the unions and complete cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is His mysteries, as they said in Tanchuma at the end of Ki Sisa: because the nations of the world are destined to translate the Torah and say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "He who holds My mysteries…." This is the telling of secrets, which is for Jacob alone — and "telling" does not mean in writing — so "He tells [His words to Jacob]" means the Oral Torah, the handing over of the words of Torah of which it is said "He has not done so for any nation"; whereas the Written Torah alone was written on the stones in seventy languages. דְּעַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב יוּכְלוּ אוּמּוֹת לוֹמַר אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי מַה דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנְּחָא הוּא גִּלּוּי לְכָל.
The Sages therefore taught that regarding the Written Torah the nations could claim, “We too are Israel,” because what is written and laid before everyone is openly accessible to all.

אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלּוֹ מַה שֶׁבְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת בִּכְתָב כְּלָל רַק עַל יְדֵי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּדּוֹר דּוֹר שֶׁחוֹשְׁבִים מִצַּד דְּבֵיקוּת מַחְשַׁבְתָּם בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.

The Oral Torah, however, consists of His hidden mysteries—the content of His Divine thought—which can never be fully revealed in writing. It is revealed only through the sages of Israel in every generation, who think and apprehend from the attachment of their own thought to Him.
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּלָל כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דְּהוּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא אֶפְשָׁר לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לַחְשׁוֹב אִם יְעוֹרְרוּם יַעֲשׂוּ גַּם הֵם.
This is something the nations cannot possess. Regarding the Written Torah, which is an awakening from Above, they can imagine that if they were awakened they too would obey.
אֲבָל בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא מוֹלִיד אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְחֵשֶׁק בָּהֶם כְּנוּקְבָא לְגַבֵּי דְּכְּוְרֹא דְּאַחַר מָשְׁכֵנִי נָרוּצָה.

But among Israel, the awakening from Above itself generates an awakening from below and a desire for Him, like the feminine responding to the masculine: after “Draw me” immediately comes “we will run.”
וְאָנוּ מוֹסִיפִים עוֹד מִצְוַת וּגְדָרִים דְּרַבָּנָן הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מָשָׁל תּוֹרָה מִצַּד גּוֹדֶל הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּנוּ.
We therefore add many rabbinic commandments and protective boundaries beyond what is explicit in the Torah, out of the greatness of our desire for Him.
וְכָל מַה שֶׁמּוֹסִיפִים הוּא גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה שְׁלֵימָה.
Everything that Israel adds in this manner is itself complete Torah.

כִּי הוּא מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְמִמִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת הַהוֹסָפָה נַעֲשָׂה רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק דְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁנִתְעוֹרְרוּ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְתַקְּנִים לְתַקֵּן זֶה.

For it accords with His will and with His hidden mysteries; the addition comes specifically through the intensity of the awakening from below that stirred the sages of Israel to institute that ordinance.
וְבְּחֵשֶׁק זֶה נִדְבְּקוּ בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנַעֲשָׂה כִּבְיָכוֹל כּוּלָּא חַד.
Through this desire they became attached to Him, until, as it were, all became one.

וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (גִּיטִּין ס:)974 Gittin 60b — R. Yoḥanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant with Israel only for the sake of the words that are oral, as it is stated: "For on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel." Maharsha: The word "for" indicates that the verse is giving the reason for "Write you these words": since what is oral is prone to be forgotten unless there is a written record, and many matters are drawn out of hints in the written text. Hence it says: write these words down, because it is upon the oral words that I cut a covenant with you, and their memory cannot be brought to mind except through the Written Torah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 60b): The Torah is the covenant between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel: Israel possess the Torah, which is from the Lord, and His decrees that He decreed upon man, and this itself is the bond between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel who receive His decrees. But the bond that Israel have with the Torah exists only through the words that are oral, for through the Oral Torah we understand the true meaning of the Torah, and only then does a man have attachment to the Torah. Further, the Oral Torah is with the recipient himself and not in writing, and therefore it is through it that the Holy One, blessed be He, cut the covenant — for every covenant is the joining of two together. עַל פָּסוּק עַל פִּי וְגוֹמֵר כָּרַתִּי בְּרִית דְּעַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא עִיקַּר הַבְּרִית.
This is why the Sages expounded the verse “according to the mouth... I have made a covenant”: the principal covenant is specifically through the Oral Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּבָתְרַיְתָא שֶׁהוּא תְּקִיעוֹת דְּרַבָּנָן דְּנִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ דְּהָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא פָּעַל אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְכֵן כְּמַיִם הַפָּנִים לִפְנִים.

Therefore at the later set of blasts—the rabbinically instituted blasts—it becomes revealed to Satan that the awakening from Above has in fact produced an awakening from below, “as water reflects a face back to a face.”
אָמַר הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי וְכוּלֵי וְכֵן הוּא הָאֱמֶת דְּכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּעֵת תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר נִתְעוֹרֵר לְמַעְלָה מִקְצָת מִשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל דִּלְעָתִיד וּמִמֵּילָא הוּא מִתְעַרְבֵּב לְגַמְרֵי.

He then says, “Now it is surely so,” and becomes thoroughly confounded. And this is the truth: every Rosh Hashanah, when the shofar is sounded, a measure of the future Great Shofar is awakened above, and through that awakening Satan is thrown into complete confusion.

וְעַל כֵּן תּוֹקְעִין אָז כְּשֶׁעוֹמְדִין בִּתְפִלָּה שֶׁהוּא רוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּכָל כֹּחָם הוּא בַּפֶּה דִּתְפִלָּה דְּמַכִּירִים שֶׁהֵם חֲסֵרִים רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזְרָם עַל הַכֹּל וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בַּעֲמִידָה כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמְבַקֵּשׁ מֵרַבּוֹ.

This is why those blasts are sounded while standing in prayer. Prayer represents Knesset Yisrael, whose power is in the mouth: they recognize that they themselves are lacking and that only the blessed Hashem supplies every need. Therefore prayer is recited while standing, like a petitioner before his master.
וְזֶה כָּל הַבְּדְּלְ בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּמוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה דְּלֵית לַה מִגַּרְמָהּ כְּלוּם עַל כֵּן נִמְשָׁכִים בְּקַל אַחַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
This is the essential distinction of Israel, who count according to the moon. The moon has nothing of its own, and for that reason Israel can be drawn after the blessed Hashem with ease.
וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מוֹנִין לַחַמָּה דְּרוֹצִים לִהְיוֹת אָכִיל דִּילֵיהּ וְלֹא לְהִצְטָרֵף לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל.
The nations, by contrast, count according to the sun, for they desire to “eat from their own” and not to join themselves to the blessed Hashem at all.

וְעַל כֵּן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דְּמַלְכִּי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא מִתִּשְׁרֵי כִּי עִנְיַן מַלְכוּתָם הוּא כְּדֵי לְהַאֲבִידָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה975 Chullin 89a — R. Ile’a said: The world endures only for the sake of one who restrains himself at a time of strife, as it is said, “He suspends the earth upon nothingness.” Rashi: "Restrains himself [bolem]" — closes his mouth; and like it in Bekhorot (40b), "its mouth is stopped [balum] and its feet are bound." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Chullin 89a): R. Ile'a means that the earth stands firm because its place is the center, and the center is fitted to be the enduring foundation that bears everything, since it inclines to no extreme. One who restrains himself at a time of strife and does not make himself a party to contention likewise does not depart from the middle, for the parties to a quarrel are two opposite extremes; his measure is therefore the measure of the earth, which stands in the center and does not lean from the balance, and through his measure the whole world endures. (חוּלִין פט.) נָתַתִּי גְּדוֹלָה לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר וְכוּלֵי וּשְׁאָרֵי דְּנִתְגָּאוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה.

Therefore the new year for the kings of the nations is reckoned from Tishrei. The purpose of the greatness of their kings is ultimately to bring about their downfall, as the Sages said: “I gave greatness to Nebuchadnezzar,” and to others, and through that greatness they became arrogant.
כִּי הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא הַמִוְשֶׁל בְּכָל עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגָּאֶה לַחְשׁוֹב הַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ.
For a king rules over all, and through this power he is prone to become proud and imagine that everything belongs to him.

וְהֵם הַמְּלָכִים שֶׁמַלְכּוֹ בְּאֶרֶץ אֱדוֹם לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מֶלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר דְּיָדוּעַ סוֹדָם מֵהָאֱלֹקִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּמַלְכִין קַדְמָאִין שֶׁהוּא הַכֹּל הַבִּטּוּלִים שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁהָיָה בְּמִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים וְכָל מְלוּכַת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ מִזֶּה.

These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over Israel. Their secret, as taught by the Ari concerning the primordial kings, is known: the various nullifications rooted in the primordial plane of thought are the source from which the kingship of the nations extends.

כִּי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֶעָתִיד דִּנְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר וְעֲתִידִין לְיִקָּרֵא בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא עה:)976 Bava Batra 75b — Rabba said in the name of R. Yochanan: In time to come the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "Every one that is called by My name, whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him." And R. Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R. Yochanan: Three are called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and these are they: the righteous, the Messiah, and Jerusalem. Rashbam: "They are called by His name" — that their own name shall be "the Lord." Maharsha (s.v. "in time to come the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He"): A man is not of himself fit for the attribute of glory, which belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He — "My glory I will not give to another," and all that He created He created only for His glory. Glory comes to a man only by way of his Torah, which is itself God's glory, as "there is no glory but Torah." Hence "every one that is called by My name" means the righteous, all of whose deeds are for His glory; "whom I have created for My glory" speaks of this world, and "yea, I have made him" adds that in the World to Come too he will bear His name, on account of the deeds he did here for God's glory. Maharsha (s.v. "three are called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He"): It says "called upon His name" and not "called by His name," which shows that the divine Name is joined to theirs as a qualifier: "righteous to the Lord," "the Lord our righteousness," "the city of the Lord." Each bears the Name because all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven — so the righteous, so the Messiah, and so Jerusalem in time to come, to which none will be admitted but those whose every deed is for the sake of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): This is the ultimate cleaving, until one is called wholly by the name of the Lord, as they said, "In the future the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He." This will be when the ultimate perfection of the future is reached through the Messiah son of David, of the seed of Judah, by means of repentance, through which Israel is redeemed; for "in the place where penitents stand, the perfectly righteous cannot stand," a higher place. דְּיִהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל שֶׁלָּהֶם.

The primordial thought was directed toward the state Israel will attain in the future, when “the female will encircle the male” and Israel will be called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He; then, in truth, everything will be theirs.
אַךְ זֶהוּ כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה תַּכְלִית הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּרָאוּ כָּל בָּשָׂר כִּי פִּי הַשֵּׁם וְגוֹמֵר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כְּאוֹר הַחַמָּה.
But this can exist only at the ultimate revelation, when “all flesh together will see that the mouth of Hashem has spoken,” and when the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר זֶה וְרָאָה שֶׁאֵין הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים וְשִׁתֵּף בְּעֲשִׂיָּה מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים בְּנִיסָן שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ לְחָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה.

In this world such a state cannot yet exist. He saw that the world could not endure and therefore joined the attribute of mercy to the realm of action in Nisan, which is the first of the lunar months.

וּמִמֶּנּוּ מוֹנִין לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לַלְּבָנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חוּלִין שָׁם)977 Chullin 89a — "Not because you are more numerous than all the peoples did the Lord desire you" — the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: I desire you, for even at the hour when I bestow greatness upon you, you make yourselves small before Me. I gave greatness to Abraham, and he said before Me, "And I am but dust and ashes"; to Moses and Aaron, and they said, "And what are we"; to David, and he said, "But I am a worm and not a man." Rashi: "Not because you are more numerous" — because you do not make yourselves many but make yourselves few, therefore He desired you: you who are "the fewest" make yourselves small in humility. Maharsha: In the fullness of greatness a man calls to mind the lowliness of his creation. Abraham named the lowliness of the first forming, that Adam was made from the earth — "dust" at the beginning of the forming and "ashes" at its end, as in "and to dust you shall return"; Moses and Aaron added the lowliness of the forming of every man since, for "what are we" means that our forming was from a putrid drop, which is nothing at all. David said "I am a worm" of the lowliness of his own particular forming, for by right he should have been stillborn, and only the seventy years withheld from Adam for his sin were given to him. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Chullin 89a): The verse cannot be taken at face value, that He did not desire them because they are many, for it is plain to the eye that they are few, and Scripture does not state what the senses already show. Rather it means that He desired them because they do not magnify themselves when greatness reaches them: all that belongs to the nations is corporeal, and therefore in their greatness they magnify themselves, whereas Israel, who are not beings of matter, acquire by that greatness a yet higher, divine rank, and so they make themselves small. For one who exalts himself shows thereby that he is a being of matter, and one who makes himself small shows a rank that is not corporeal. נָתַתִּי גְּדוֹלָה לְדָּוִד וְהִשְׁפִּיל עַצְמוֹ וְכֵן כּוּלָּם.
From Nisan we therefore count the kings of Israel, who are compared to the moon. As the Sages said: “I gave greatness to David, and he humbled himself,” and so it is with all of them.
כִּי זֶה כָּל מַלְכוּתָם לְהַכִּיר דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדְּמַלְכוּתוֹ בְּכָל מָשָׁלָה.
For the entire purpose of their kingship is to recognize that everything comes from the blessed Hashem and that His sovereignty rules over all.

וְדָוִד הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזוֹהַר (חֵלֶק ג מט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)978 Zohar 3:49b — “And if the priest examines it.” R. Yose taught: It is written, “You who hear prayer, to You all flesh comes.” “You who hear prayer” — this is the Holy One, blessed be He. R. Chizkiyah said: “You who hear prayer” — it should have said “who hear prayers”; what is “who hear prayer”? Rather, “prayer” is the Assembly of Israel, who is herself prayer, as it is written, “But I am prayer” — and David said it on behalf of the Assembly of Israel; and what he said, “But I am prayer,” is all one. עַל פָּסוּק וַאֲנִי תְּפִלָּה.
David therefore represents the level of prayer, as the Zohar teaches on the verse, “But I am prayer.”
כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל אוּמָּה הוּא הַמֶּלֶךְ וְכָל עִנְיַן הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מִמַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ דְּמְבָרְכִין שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ.
The root of every nation is its king, and all earthly kingship extends from His sovereignty, as reflected in the blessing recited upon seeing a king: “Who has apportioned of His glory...”

וְלְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הוּא לִבְרִיּוֹתָיו כֵּיוָן דְּהֵם אֵין מַכִּירִים זֶה רַק דְּבַעַל כָּרְחָם לֵב מְלָכִים בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם לִהְיוֹת כְּגַרְזֶן בְּיַד הַחוֹצֵב וְנִקְרָא בְּרִיּוֹתָיו לְבַד דְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרָיו.

Concerning the kings of the nations the blessing says “to His creatures,” because they do not recognize this truth; rather, against their will, “the hearts of kings are in the hand of Hashem,” and they function like an axe in the hand of the one who hews with it. They are therefore called merely His creatures, who are compelled to be drawn after Him.

מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא לִירֵאָיו כִּי אֵצֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא הַתַּקִּיף הַגָּדוֹל יֵשׁ עוֹד אַדְּרַבָּה יִרְאָה יְתֵירָה מִפְּנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּכֵּיוָן שֶׁכְּוָרָע בִּתְפִלָּה שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף (בְּרָכוֹת לד:)979 Berakhot 34b — R. Yitzchak bar Nachmani said: It was explained to me by R. Yehoshua ben Levi himself — an ordinary person bows as we have said; a High Priest, at the beginning of each and every blessing; the king, once he has knelt, does not rise again [until he has finished the entire prayer], as it is said, "And it was, when Solomon finished praying, that he rose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling upon his knees." Rashi: "He does not rise" — until he has finished [the entire prayer]. "He rose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling" — the beginning of the verse is "And it was when Solomon finished praying," and only then, "he rose from kneeling." Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAvodah 10): One bows only where one draws near to God, just as a man does not bow to a king while he is not before him, but bows when he draws near; and an ordinary person has such nearness only in the blessings of the Patriarchs and of thanksgiving. The High Priest is close to God by way of beginning, for he is first and head among men — he takes his portion first and blesses first — and therefore he bows at the head of every blessing. The king, however, is reckoned among the people as the whole of it and is close to God in every respect, for "the kingdom of earth is like the kingdom of Heaven"; and because he is king he must nullify his importance before God, before Whom his kingship counts for nothing, and so he remains bowed throughout. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The full force of desire is found in kings, who are able to fulfill all their desires; therefore, corresponding to this, the kings of Israel, from the side of holiness, also possess the full force of fear, as in "once he has knelt he does not rise again." For Israel, who fear the Blessed One, on the contrary, to fear Him is all their desire and longing, and this is the fulfillment of their desire. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): In the kings of Israel, over whom one blesses "[Blessed is He] who has apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him," fear reaches its utmost force, as they said, "a king, once he has knelt, does not rise again"; this is because of the force of the fear upon him, "and he was in dread of My name," for the attribute of the Kingdom of Heaven is the attribute of fear. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, II Kings): In truth every king has fear in an intensified degree, as the Gemara says, "a king who kneels does not rise again"; in Menasheh the fear was greater still, beyond what a person can bear, and all his sin was that he sought ways to make the fear depart from him so that he would have free choice, since the overpowering fear had taken his choice away. דְּמַכִּיר חֶסְרוֹנוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהָרִים רֹאשׁ כְּלָל נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

Concerning the kings of Israel, however, the blessing says “to those who fear Him.” Precisely because the king is the most powerful person, he possesses an even greater fear before the blessed Hashem. Thus once a king bows during prayer he does not straighten again, for he recognizes his deficiency so deeply that he cannot lift his head at all before the blessed Hashem.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Nisan, Miracles, and the Power Entrusted to Israel
Israel can draw mercy beyond nature, while the same shofar-force becomes judgment for those outside that covenant.

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַחוֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם עַל נִיסָן שֶּׁמּוֹרֶה נִסִּים כִּי זֶה כָּל כֹּחוֹ דְּבוֹ בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִצִּידּוֹ יֵשׁ חֶסְרוֹנוֹת רַק דְּשִׁתֵּף מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים שֶׁהוּא עֲשִׂיַּת נִסִּים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִהַטֶּבַע שֶׁהוּא בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אֱלֹהִים שֶׁהוּא הַנְהָגָה בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין.

This is the meaning of “This month shall be for you” with reference to Nisan, whose very name points to miracles. Its power lies in the fact that the world in the realm of action contains deficiencies, and therefore the attribute of mercy was joined to justice; this produces miracles that transcend nature, whose ordered governance is associated with the Divine Name Elohim and with strict justice.
וְזֶה נִמְסַר רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָא עָבִיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא נִיסָא לְשֶׁיִקָּרֵא שֶׁהֵם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
This power was entrusted only to Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not perform a miracle on behalf of falsehood, which characterizes the nations of the world.
וְבִּפְסוּק זֶה הוּא מִצְוַת קִדּוּשׁ הַחוֹדֶשׁ דְּהוּא מַה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁהַזְּמַן נִמְסַר לָהֶם לְקָדְשׁוֹ דְּזֶהוּ כָּל תַּכְלִית בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם.

The same verse contains the commandment of sanctifying the new month: Israel sanctifies the appointed times, and time itself was entrusted to Israel to sanctify. This is the ultimate purpose of the world’s creation.
וְעַל כֵּן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה קָבְעוּ דִּינֵי קִדּוּשׁ הַחוֹדֶשׁ בְּמַסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אַף שֶׁהַקְּרָא נֶאֱמַר בְּנִיסָן.
Therefore the Sages placed the laws of sanctifying the new month in tractate Rosh Hashanah, even though the Scriptural command was stated concerning Nisan.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִמְסַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה980 Rosh Hashanah 2a — There are four New Years: the first of Nisan is the New Year for kings and for the festivals; the first of Elul is the New Year for the tithe of cattle; the first of Tishrei is the New Year for years, for Sabbatical years and Jubilees, for planting and for vegetables; the first of Shevat is the New Year for the tree, according to Beit Shammai — and Beit Hillel say the fifteenth of it. Rashi: "For kings": it was customary to date documents by the years of the king, from the year in which he came to the throne, for the sake of peace with the government; and the Sages fixed the first of Nisan as the beginning of his year, so that even if he came to the throne in Shevat or Adar, his year is completed when Nisan arrives and his second year is counted from then. "For the tithe of cattle": one may not tithe from animals born in this year for those born in the next; "for Sabbatical years and Jubilees": once Tishrei has begun, plowing and sowing are forbidden by Torah law; "for planting": for counting the years of orlah; "for vegetables": one may not tithe from vegetables picked before Rosh Hashanah for those picked after it. "For the tree": one may not tithe from fruit that budded before Shevat for fruit that budded after it, since for a tree [the year] follows the budding. Tosafos (s.v. "for kings"): Rashi explained [the dating of documents by kings] as being for the sake of peace with the government, but this is not so: here the Mishnah speaks of the kings of Israel, and its purpose is for documents. Peace with the government is required only in a bill of divorce, because it is a weighty matter, since by it the woman is permitted to all men. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on Tosafot s.v. "for kings"): Tosafot were troubled that in the Diaspora documents are dated only by the kings of Greece, with no concern for the peace of the government that rules there; on this they answered that peace with the government is required only in a bill of divorce. (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וָאֶתְחַנַּן) אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם נֵרֵד לְבֵית דִּין שֶׁלְּמַטָּה וְאָנוּ מְבָרְכִים מִקְדָּשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן דְּהַכַּוָּנָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפְּסָחִים (קיז:)981 Pesachim 117b — Rava said: I found the Elders of Pumbedita sitting and saying — on the Sabbath, both in the prayer and in the sanctification over wine, one concludes "who sanctifies the Sabbath"; on a Festival, both in the prayer and in the sanctification, "who sanctifies Israel and the seasons." ... Your reasoning: the Sabbath, which is fixed and standing of itself, [is concluded] both in the prayer and in the sanctification with "who sanctifies the Sabbath"; a Festival, which it is Israel who establish — for they intercalate the months and fix the years — [is concluded] "who sanctifies Israel and the seasons." Rashbam: ["The Elders of Pumbedita":] R. Yehuda and R. Eina, [as named] at the end of the first chapter of Sanhedrin (17b). ["On the Sabbath":] an ordinary Sabbath that is not a Festival; ["on a Festival":] one that is not on the Sabbath, for on a Sabbath that is a Festival one concludes with both, "who sanctifies the Sabbath and Israel and the seasons," as explained in Tractate Beitzah (17a). ["The Sabbath, which is fixed and standing":] from the six days of Creation, and it does not depend on the fixing of the month. יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי וְכוּלֵי כִּי אַחַר שֶׁבְּנִיסָן נִמְסַר הַכֹּל לָהֶם מִמֵּילָא גַּם תִּשְׁרֵי מָסַר לָהֶם וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזוֹהַר (חֵלֶק ג צט ב, וְתִּיקּוּנֵי זוֹהַר תִּיקּוּן כא)982 Zohar 3:99b — And when this shofar is aroused, and when men return from their sins, they must draw out the sound of a shofar below; and that sound ascends on high, and then another, supernal shofar is aroused, and mercy is awakened, and judgment is removed. And we must perform the act with a shofar, to arouse that other shofar, and to bring forth through this shofar below those sounds, to show that all those sounds above, which are all included in that supernal shofar, should be aroused to go forth. And by these sounds below Israel gives strength above. עַל שׁוֹפָר דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא יָהֵיב עֵיטִין בְּכּוּלָּא שֶׁהֵם מַעֲמִידִין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכִּסֵּא דִּין לְכִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים.

For in truth Rosh Hashanah itself was also entrusted to Israel. As the Midrash says, “I and you will descend to the earthly court,” and we recite the blessing “Who sanctifies Israel and the Day of Remembrance,” parallel to the principle that Israel sanctifies the festivals. Once everything was entrusted to Israel in Nisan, Tishrei too was necessarily entrusted to them. Thus the Zohar and Tikkunei Zohar teach concerning the shofar that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel counsel in all things, so that they cause Him, as it were, to move from the throne of judgment to the throne of mercy.
עַל יְדֵי תְּקִיעוֹת דִּמְיוּשָׁב מְבַלְבְּלִין הַיְשִׁיבָה בְּדִין וְעוֹמֵד וְאָז תּוֹקְעִין כְּשֶׁעוֹמְדִין וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים.
Through the blasts sounded while sitting they disturb the sitting of judgment, so that He rises; then they sound the blasts while standing, and through this He sits upon the throne of mercy.
אֶלָּא דְּרַחֲמִים אֵלּוּ הֵם רַחֲמִים רַבִּים יוֹתֵר מִרַחֲמִים דְּנִיסָן שֶׁהֵם שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי דִּין מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן אֵלּוּ הַבָּאִים אַחַר הַדִּין.

Yet this mercy is an even greater mercy than the mercy of Nisan. The mercy of Nisan comes without first passing through judgment, whereas the mercy of Rosh Hashanah emerges after and through the judgment itself.

וְעַל כֵּן אֵין אוֹמְרִים הַלֵּל וְלְגַבֵּי רִאשׁוֹן מִקְרָא הַהַלֵּל שֶׁהוּא לִפְנֵי הַתְּקִיעוֹת אָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֵב:)983 Rosh Hashanah 32b — R. Abbahu said: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, why do Israel not sing song before You on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur? He said to them: Is it possible — the King sits upon the throne of judgment, and the books of the living and the books of the dead are open before Him, and Israel are to sing song? Maharsha: Song [that is, Hallel] would properly have been said on Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur, since they are called "appointed seasons" and are hallowed by the prohibition of work, were it not for this reason: "Is it possible — the King sits upon the throne of judgment…" (as explained in Arakhin 10b). מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִּין וְאַחַר כָּךְ דְּיוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא בְּיוֹם הַדִּין וְהַדִּין גּוֹרֵם לֵישֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשּׁוֹפָר לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עוֹד הַלֵּל.

This is why Hallel is not recited. Concerning the first Scriptural passage of Hallel, which precedes the shofar blasts, the Sages said: “The King sits upon the throne of judgment.” Although afterward He sits upon the throne of mercy, it remains the Day of Judgment, and the judgment itself is what brings Him to the throne of mercy through the awakening of the shofar. Such a process is not the setting for Hallel.
