שֶׁהַהִלּוּל הוּא עַל נֵס שֶׁחוּץ מִהַטֶּבַע מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ וּבָא עַל פִּי טֶבַע הַגָּמוּר.
Hallel is sung over a miracle that stands outside the natural order; here, however, mercy is drawn through the full working of the ordered system itself.

וְעַל כֵּן פָּתְחוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אַרְבָּעָה רָאשֵׁי שְׁנֵים, וְכֵן (שָׁם טז.)984 Rosh Hashanah 16a — At four seasons the world is judged: on Passover, concerning grain; on Shavuot, concerning the fruit of the tree; on Rosh HaShana all who come into the world pass before Him like sheep, as it is stated: "He who fashions their hearts together, who understands all their deeds"; and on the Festival [of Sukkot] they are judged concerning water. Rashi: "At four seasons" — of the year, the world is judged. "Like benei maron" and the verse "He who fashions their hearts together" are explained in the Gemara [18a]. Tosafos (s.v. "on Pesach concerning the grain"): From the account in chapter Mi She-meito (Berakhot 18b) of the pious man whose wife provoked him on the eve of Rosh Hashanah, it appears that it was on Rosh Hashanah that he heard two spirits telling each other what they had heard from behind the curtain: that whoever sows at the first rainfall, hail will strike it. Perhaps in heaven on Rosh Hashanah they were recalling the judgment decreed on Pesach; or else [that account] follows R. Yehuda, who says that all are judged on Rosh Hashanah and the sentence concerning grain is [sealed] on Pesach. Maharsha (32b, s.v. "why do Israel not sing before You"): It is explained in chapter Ein Ne'erachin [Arakhin 10b] that it would have been fitting to say song on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, since they are called "appointed times" and are sanctified by the prohibition of labor, were it not for this reason: "Is it possible that the King sits upon the throne of judgment…" Maharsha (s.v. "on Pesach"): The Ran derives the judgment of Rosh Hashanah from "at the covering [of the moon] for our festival day… for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment of the God of Jacob" (Psalms 81:4–5); but our sugya implies that [the Mishnah] relies also on "Remembrances, so that your remembrance may rise before Me for good" — something needed on the day of judgment, which is why it is called "a remembrance of terua," for the remembrance of all who come into the world comes before Him. That all are judged on Rosh Hashanah means every individual in every matter, as we say on Rosh Hashanah, "who by hunger and who by thirst"; whereas at each of the other three seasons the world as a whole is judged on one of the three things named. Maharsha (s.v. "pass"): For the other three seasons the Mishnah uses the term "judged," but here it changes to "pass [before Him]." According to the conclusion below, that the Mishnah follows [the school of] R. Yishmael, whereby man's sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur and the Mishnah speaks of the beginning of judgment, this is well: since it is not sealed on Rosh Hashanah, it uses only the term "pass." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 16a): Rosh Hashanah is the head of the year, its root and essence, and man too is the beginning and essence of creation, comprising all of it, and is called "the head of the dust of the world" [Proverbs 8:26]; therefore it is fitting that man be judged on Rosh Hashanah, this day, the essence of the whole year, being his in particular. And the four seasons correspond to the four elements by which the world is conducted: on Pesach the grain, the growth of the earth; on Shavuot the fruit of the tree, which grows by the air; and on Rosh Hashanah all who come into the world, corresponding to fire, for the soul of man is the natural heat of the heart. אַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים הָעוֹלָם נִדּוֹן בְּנִיסָן וְאַחֲרָיו רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כִּי לְעוֹלָם נִיסָן קוֹדֶם רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כְּפִי סֵדֶר הֶחֳדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא הַגּוֹרֵם לִהְיוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה גַּם כֵּן מִתְקַדֵּשׁ עַל פִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל.

This is why the Sages opened the tractate with “four new years,” and likewise taught that at four periods the world is judged, placing Nisan before Rosh Hashanah. According to the order of the months, Nisan always precedes Rosh Hashanah, and it is Nisan that enables Rosh Hashanah itself to be sanctified through Israel.

וְאָמַר נִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַן דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי אַף דְּבְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן אֵינוֹ רֶגֶל רַק אָז תְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּמְסָר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְקָדְשׁוֹ וְבִּקְדוּשַּׁת רֹאשׁ חָדָשׁ נִיסָן מִתְקַדֵּשׁ הָרֶגֶל שֶׁבּוֹ וְנוֹדַע זְמַנּוֹ וְזֶהוּ לְחָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה.

The first of Nisan is therefore the new year for festivals, expressing the sanctity of time that Israel sanctifies. Although the first of Nisan is itself not a festival, it marks the beginning of Creation in the realm of action that was entrusted to Israel to sanctify; through the sanctity of Rosh Chodesh Nisan, the festival within that month becomes sanctified and its time becomes known. This is the order of the lunar months.

אֲבָל הַשְׁנֵים הוּא לַחַמָּה רַק דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין מוֹנִין שְׁנוֹת חַמָּה רַק מַשְׁוִים לִהְיוֹת הַשָּׁנָה גַּם כֵּן לַלְּבָנָה וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵם מַכִּירִים דְּכָל הַשְׁפָּעוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה [הַמַּסְתִּירִים הַהִתְגַּלּוּת אֵצֶל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת] הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

The reckoning of years, however, follows the solar cycle. Israel nevertheless do not count purely solar years; they align the solar year with the moon, thereby acknowledging that all the forces and influences of this world—even those that conceal Divine revelation among the nations—come entirely from the blessed Hashem.
וְלְבְּנה מְקַבֶּלֶת שִׁפְעָה מִחַמָּה וְלֹא כְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַמוֹנִין לַחַמָּה לְבַד.
The moon receives its light from the sun, unlike the nations, who reckon by the sun alone.

וְאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא י"ב א' דְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹנִין לְמַבּוּל מִתִּשְׁרֵי וְלְתְּקִיפוּת מִנִיסָן וְחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מוֹנִין גַּם לְמַבּוּל מִנִיסָן וּמַה חָכְמָה שַׁיָּיךְ בְּעִנְיָן זֶה.

The Gemara states that the sages of Israel count the Flood from Tishrei and the solar seasons from Nisan, while the sages of the nations count even the Flood from Nisan. What “wisdom” is involved in this calendrical distinction?
וְגַם מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב לְמַבּוּל וְלֹא לִשְׁנֵים.
And why does the Gemara specify the Flood rather than simply saying that they count years differently?

אֲבָל הַכַּוָּנָה דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ חָכְמַת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּמְבָרְכִין גַּם כֵּן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לִבְרִיּוֹתָיו שֶׁהוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מֵחָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִילָּה טז.)985 Megillah 16a — "And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to all his friends." It calls them "his friends" and it calls them "his wise men." R. Yochanan said: Whoever says a word of wisdom, even among the nations of the world, is called a wise man. Maharsha: The "word of wisdom" for which they earned the name of wise men is a word of the wisdom of the Torah, namely what the verse goes on to say: "If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews" — if he descends from the other tribes you can prevail over him, but if from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim or Manasseh you cannot. For that Mordecai was a Jew they already knew, since it had been published throughout the provinces; until now they had supposed he came from one of the other tribes and that Haman could prevail over him, and only when they saw the beginning of Haman's fall did they take fright and say that he might be of those tribes for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, "stirs up His might." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): As stated in Megillah, one who says a word of wisdom among the nations is called a wise man — learned from Haman's "wise men," who grasped the truth that he would fall before the seed of the Jews. For this is the whole wisdom of the nations: to grasp the superiority of Israel, that they cannot prevail against them; but to grasp the wisdom of truth, the wisdom of the Torah — the apprehension of His truth — is impossible for them, for "He has not done so for any nation." כָּל הָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר חָכְמָה אֲפִילּוּ בָּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה פָּרָשָׁה ב ט)986 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." If a man says to you: There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written, "And I will destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau." [If he says:] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, as it is written, "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Although the sages of the nations may originate wisdom in matters of the service of the Blessed One, it is not reckoned as Oral Torah — only what the Sages of Israel originate. And this is "He shone forth from Seir to them": human wisdom, which is chiefly in Seir, as the Sages said, "There is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'"; and this shone forth to Israel, to be theirs alone, for nothing is called wisdom but the wisdom of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 17): "You have taken gifts among men [ba-adam]" — these are the spoils taken from Esau, the power of "we will do"; for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom,'" that is, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, to rectify the excess of anger, while might is used only to conquer the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it. יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בֶּאֱדוֹם תַּאֲמִין שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר.

The explanation is that the root of the wisdom of the nations is reflected in the blessing, “Who has given of His wisdom to His creatures”: their wisdom too ultimately derives from His wisdom. Thus the Sages said, “If someone tells you there is wisdom among Edom, believe it,” as Scripture says, “I will destroy the wise men from Edom.”

וְחָכְמָה הוּא הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת וּבִלְעָם רֹאשׁ לְחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הִכִּיר הָאֱמֶת בְּמַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בִּנְבוּאוֹתָיו וְעִם כָּל זֶה אָמַר הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ לְעַמִּי וְלֹא נִמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶם לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר כִּי עַצְמוּתוֹ אֵין כֵּן וְעַל כֵּן א' מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לִבְרִיּוֹתָיו עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל עַל מִכְּבוֹדוֹ.

Wisdom means recognition of truth. Balaam, the foremost of the sages of the nations, recognized the truth of Israel’s greatness, as is explicit in his prophecies; nevertheless he said, “Behold, I am going to my people,” and did not join Israel as a convert, because his essential root was not of that nature. Therefore the blessing concerning gentile wisdom says “Who has given of His wisdom to His creatures,” just as was explained above regarding “of His glory.”

מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר לִירֵאָיו כִּי רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם דְּעַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁמַּכִּיר מְצִיאוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בָּא לְיִרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ב' מִיסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה וּבַהַגָּהָה דְּרֵישׁ שׁוּלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים.

Concerning the sages of Israel, by contrast, the blessing says “to those who fear Him,” for the beginning of Israel’s wisdom is fear of Hashem. Through wisdom a person recognizes the reality of the blessed Hashem and thereby comes to awe, as Maimonides explains at the beginning of the second chapter of Foundations of the Torah and as noted at the beginning of Orach Chaim.

וּבֶאֱמֶת הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם וְנוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ תְּקִיפוּת וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (גִּיטִּין סב.)987 Gittin 62a — Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda were sitting when Geneiva passed by them. Meanwhile he came over to them and said: Peace upon you, kings, peace upon you, kings. They said to him: From where do you know that the Sages are called kings? He said to them: As it is written, "Through me kings reign." Rashi: "A man of Torah" — a son of Torah. "A contentious man" — one who disputes with the Sages, for he used to vex Mar Ukva, who was head of the court, as stated in the first chapter. Maharsha: The very same incident appears at the end of the chapter "Kol HaGet," where it is not mentioned that he greeted them, because there the Gemara needed only the matter it was dealing with; here, however, the main point for which it is brought is that we double the greeting for Torah scholars, who are called kings. The matter is plain: a king of Israel, and the Torah scholar likewise, makes peace above and below, as they said that whoever occupies himself with Torah for its own sake makes peace in the household above and the household below, as it is stated, "Let him take hold of My strength, let him make peace with Me." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 62a): A king's greeting is doubled, one for himself and one on account of his kingship, since in the king's peace lies the peace of everything; but that reason does not fit a Torah scholar. Rather, one may say it is because the Sages said that Torah scholars increase peace in the world, just as the king increases peace in the world — for were it not for fear of the government, a man would swallow his fellow alive. And so, since Torah scholars increase peace in the world, we double the greeting to them: one for his own peace and one for the peace of the world. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 27): A Torah scholar who can produce novel insights through pilpul — the level of Moses — thereby attains the level of kingship, as stated, "Who are kings? The Rabbis," and of prophecy. Kingship, too, attains true sovereignty from the well and flowing spring that is the source of wisdom, as it says, "Through me kings reign": kingship derives from the Torah, and when it is a flowing spring it never ceases and the reign endures, like that of King David. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): The blessing of Israel, who are called "man," is "subdue it and rule" — to conquer all the earthliness and physicality of this world. The Torah is the template of all creation, and "Who are kings? The Rabbis" — for through their attainment in Torah they rule over all of creation. מַאן מַלְכֵי רַבָּנָן.
In truth, “wisdom strengthens the wise” and gives a person firmness and power; therefore the Sages said, “Who are the kings? The rabbis.”

וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי תְּקִיפוּת נַעֲשָׂה בְּרִיָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְחוֹשֵׁב דְּהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי תְּקִיפוּת מוֹסִיפִין יִרְאָה וּתְקִיפוּת דְּחָכְמָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

Among the nations, such strength causes a person to become an independent entity in his own eyes and to imagine that everything is his. Among Israel, however, strength of wisdom produces additional awe: the firmness given by wisdom consists precisely in recognizing that everything comes from the blessed Hashem.

וּבִלְעָם נִתְפָּאֵר וְיוֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן הוּא הַיְדִיעָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ [הַבְּחִירָה] וְעַל כֵּן רָצָה לְהַכְחִישׁ בְּבְּחִירָה לְגַמְרֵי וְאָמַר הִנְנִי הוֹלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר כִּי הוּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִבְחוֹר בַּטּוֹב כְּלָל.

Balaam boasted that he “knows the knowledge of the Most High.” This is knowledge of Divine foreknowledge, which stands opposite human free choice; therefore he sought to deny free choice entirely and said, “Behold, I am going to my people,” as though he had no possibility of choosing the good.

וְכֵן הָאֱמֶת אֵצֶל שׁוֹרֶשׁ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כִּי הַגֵּרִים שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא מַה שֶׁנִּשְׁמָתָם עָמְדָה בָּהָר סִינַי כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קמו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)988 Shabbat 146a — When the serpent came upon Eve he cast filth into her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai — their filth ceased; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai — their filth did not cease. Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi: What of converts? He said to him: Even though they themselves were not there, their guardian spirits were there, as it is written: "with him who stands here with us this day before the Lord our God, and with him who is not here with us this day." Rashi: "When the serpent came upon Eve": when he counseled her to eat from the tree, he came upon her, as it is written, "The serpent beguiled me (השיאני)" — a term of marriage (נשואין). "What of converts": who were not at Mount Sinai — from where did their contamination cease? "Their mazal was there": at Sinai; and all who stood at Mount Sinai were sanctified, purified and healed of every blemish, even the blind and the lame among Israel, as taught in the Sifrei. Maharsha: All the generations yet to come were included in "him who is not here with us this day" (as stated in Shevuot 39a); but of Israel one can say that although their bodies were not there, their souls, bound up in the bond of life, were present, whereas of converts this cannot be said — only that their mazal was there. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 146a): As explained on Sotah 9a, the serpent came upon Eve because he wished to kill Adam and marry Eve; he truly joined himself to her, and through that improper union he cast filth and abomination into her. Because Eve had a union with the serpent, the contamination passed from it to her, so that all the nations bear contamination on account of that union; but Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, were freed of it, for against Eve's union with the serpent stands Israel's union with the Holy One, blessed be He, and this ended the contamination that came of joining with the serpent. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 17): Although the law follows R. Yehudah ben Beseira that words of Torah do not contract impurity, that is only after the giving of the Torah, when "their filth ceased": the root of the impurity of lust, which came through the serpent's coming upon Eve and is therefore found more in women, is not severed by the Torah as a "spice" but ceased through the Torah entirely. Therefore converts too need immersion before accepting the Torah: although their guardian angel stood at Mount Sinai and their filth too ceased thereby, it does not leave the convert at his birth, and while a gentile he is like all the filth-laden nations; only when he converts does it cease, through his acceptance of the Torah, as it did for all Israel at the giving of the Torah. וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחִיזָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁם עִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל כֵּן מְסַלֵּק מִעָלָיו יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם לְגַמְרֵי.

In relation to the root of the nations this is indeed so. The converts among them are those whose souls already stood at Mount Sinai, as the Sages taught, and who therefore possess a root shared with the children of Israel. Balaam, by contrast, removed from himself the fear of Hashem completely.
וְזֶהוּ מוֹנִין לְמַבּוּל מִנִיסָן כִּי הַמַבּוּל הוּא הַשְׁחָתַת הָעוֹלָם בַּעֲבוּר הַחֲטָאִים.
This is why the sages of the nations count the Flood from Nisan: the Flood was the destruction of the world because of sin.

וּמִצַּד חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא נִמְנֶה מִתִּשְׁרֵי דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין כִּי אָז לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁהֵם יְכוֹלִין לַעֲלוֹת לַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּמִדַּת הַדִּין לְהַמְתִּיקָהּ לְרַחֲמִים וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א סז ב)989 Zohar 1:67b — Once the Holy One, blessed be He, told him that He would save him in the ark — as it is written, "And I, behold, I am bringing the flood of waters," and "I will blot out all existence that I have made from the face of the earth," and "But I will establish My covenant with you... and you shall come into the ark" — since He told him that he and his sons would be saved, he did not ask mercy for the world, and they perished. Therefore the waters of the flood are called by his name, as it is said: "For this is to Me like the waters of Noah, when I swore that the waters of Noah should no more pass over the earth." דְּנִקְרְאוּ מִי נח שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל כִּי אֵלּוּ הִתְפַּלֵּל נַעֲנָה דְּהַתְּפִלָּה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר וְהָיָה מִתְעוֹרֵר שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּיְכוֹלִים לַהֲפֹךְ הָרָע לְטוֹב וּמְבָרְרִים דְּאֵין רַע.

From the perspective of Israel’s wisdom, however, it is counted from Tishrei, meaning that it proceeded from the attribute of strict justice. Israel had not yet appeared in history—Israel who arose in primordial thought and can ascend to that level of thought itself, sweetening judgment into mercy. The Zohar therefore calls the Flood “the waters of Noah” because Noah did not pray; had he prayed, he would have been answered. Prayer is the root of Knesset Yisrael, and it would have awakened Israel’s root, which can transform evil into good and clarify that evil has no independent reality.

וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן מִנַּיִן שְׁנוֹת הַבְּרִיאָה מִתִּשְׁרֵי שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּהֵם מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים כְּפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְעַל כֵּן הַמּוֹלָדוֹת שֶׁהוּא קְבִיעוּת חָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה מוֹנִין לְבָּהָר"דְּ (רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן הֲלָכוֹת קָדוֹשׁ הַחוֹדֶשׁ וְ, ח)990 Mishneh Torah, Sanctification of the New Month 6:8 — And the first molad, from which you begin, is the molad that occurred in the first year of creation. It was on the night of the second day, five hours into the night and 204 parts; their mnemonic is BaHaRaD, and from it the reckoning begins. שֶׁהוּא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּתִשְׁרֵי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם כַּנּוֹדָע בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹן הָעִבּוּר.

This is also why the years of Creation are counted from Tishrei, corresponding to the level of primordial thought according to which Israel sanctifies the times. Thus the lunar conjunctions, which determine the lunar months, are calculated from the traditional epoch of BeHaRaD, following the view that the world was created in Tishrei, as is known from the calculations of intercalation.
וּתְקִיפוּת דְּחַמָּה מוֹנִין מִנִיסָן שֶׁאָז הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת הַבְּרִיאָה דְּלְבְּנה מְקַבֶּלֶת מִחַמָּה וְאָז הוּא כֹּחַ הַחַמָּה.
The solar seasons, however, are counted from Nisan, because that is when Creation became manifest in the realm of action: the moon receives from the sun, and the power of the sun becomes operative.

וְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִיתַּן לָהֶם אוֹתוֹ חוֹדֶשׁ לְקִדּוּשׁ הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁגַּם הִיא בִּתְחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה אוֹר גָּדוֹל וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד דְּמִצַּד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שְׁנֵיהֶם מְאוֹרוֹת גְּדוֹלִים רַק מִצַּד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה נִתְקַטְּנָה כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַאן דְּאָכֵיל דְּלָאו דִּילֵיהּ בָּהֵית וְכוּלֵי (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּעָרְלָה פֶּרֶק א)991 Jerusalem Talmud Orlah 1:3 — How does one know [from which vine the sunken shoot draws its life]? R. Bivai in the name of R. Ḥanina: If the leaves are turned toward the young vine, it is clear that it lives by the strength of the old one; and if the leaves are turned toward the old vine, it is clear that it lives by the strength of the young one. R. Yudan bar Ḥanin said: The sign is that one who eats from what belongs to another is ashamed to look at him. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "How does one know"): The leaves meant are those of the young vine: if they are turned toward the young vine itself, that is, away from the old one, it is certain that it lives by the strength of the old, and that is just why it turns its face away from it; and if they are turned toward the old vine, it is known that it lives by its own strength. This is what R. Yudan bar Ḥanin's sign means — one who eats from what belongs to his fellow is ashamed to look him in the face, and so turns his face the other way. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 12): In truth "all our deeds You have wrought for us," and everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, which is in the heart alone; only, the Blessed One wanted us to exert ourselves so that [our deeds] be called by our name and we come [to the good] by our own wages — for "one who eats what is not his…" — just as the Sages instituted for a wife that her handiwork is in exchange for her sustenance. Beis Yaakov (Vayigash 12): This is what the Sages intended in saying it is "more comfortable for a person" [not to have been created], rather than "better": for in truth it is better for him to have been created, since while the soul is in the world of souls the life in its hand is very constricted — "bread of shame," as stated in the Yerushalmi, "one who eats what is not his is ashamed to look at him." A person cannot reach the place of his root that befits him unless he passes through this world and is tested. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 16): On Pesach the salvation came without any service on man's part, as it is written, "and you were naked and bare" — naked of commandments. Yet in truth Israel is not at ease with this, as stated in the Yerushalmi, "one who eats what is not his is ashamed to look at him"; therefore the Blessed One afterwards set it that a person should clarify himself, so that the service be called the toil of his own hands — and this is "bring the Omer before Me on Pesach." וְהַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַבּוּשָׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנְדָרִים כ' א' וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּיְשָׁנִים שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא בָּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.

Israel were given that month in order to sanctify the moon. In primordial thought the moon too was a great light, as it will again be in the future, when from the perspective of that thought the two luminaries are both great. Only in the realm of action was the moon diminished, because in this world “one who eats what is not his own is ashamed.” Awe is itself identified with this holy shame, and this is the quality of Israel—who are characterized by bashfulness—which is absent from the nations.

וְעַל יְדֵי הַהִתְקַטְּנוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים דְּבַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עִיקַּר הַקִּדּוּשׁ נִקְבַּע עַל תִּשְׁרֵי בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר כֹּחָם דְּמַגִּיעִים בִּקְדֻשָּׁתָם עַד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לִהְיוֹת מוֹנִין שְׁנַת לְבְּנה מִתִּשְׁרֵי דְּהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם מְאוֹרוֹת גְּדוֹלִים.

Through this very diminishment, Israel sanctify the appointed times. In the Oral Torah the central sanctification is therefore fixed in Tishrei, on Rosh Hashanah, for Israel’s unique power is that their sanctity can reach all the way to the root of Divine thought. They therefore count the lunar year from Tishrei, corresponding to the thought in which both luminaries are great.
וְזֶה כָּל חָכְמַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לִידַּבֵּק בְּחָכְמָתוֹ וְמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה גַּם חָכְמָתָם תּוֹרָה.
This is the entire wisdom of the sages of Israel in the Oral Torah: to cleave to His wisdom and His thought, through which their own wisdom itself becomes Torah.

וְזֶה אֵינוֹ בְּחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּכָל חָכְמָתָם שֶׁמַּכִּירִים שֶׁזֶּה רַע וְזֶה טוֹב אֲבָל חוֹשְׁבִים דְּלָרַע אֵין תִקְנֶה דְּכֵן הוּא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה לְבַד כְּמַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב' דְּמַכּוֹת וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְחֶזְקֵאל רֶמֶז שֶׁנָּח)992 Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 358 — "The soul that sins, it shall die." They asked Wisdom: The sinner — what is his punishment? She said to them: "Evil pursues sinners." They asked Prophecy: The sinner — what is his punishment? It said to them: "The soul that sins, it shall die." They asked the Torah: The sinner — what is his punishment? It said: Let him bring a guilt offering and it will atone for him. They asked the Holy One, blessed be He: The sinner — what is his punishment? He said to them: Let him repent and it will atone for him. That is what is written: "Good and upright is the Lord; therefore He instructs sinners in the way." שֶׁאֵלּוּ לַחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵי א' חֲטָאִים תִּרְדֹּף רָעָה וְכוּלֵי.

This is not so with the sages of the nations. Their wisdom can recognize that one thing is evil and another good, but they believe that evil, once present, has no rectification; such is the conclusion of unaided wisdom. Thus the Midrash teaches that when Wisdom was asked what should happen to the sinner, it answered, “Evil pursues sinners.”
וְעַל כֵּן מוֹנִין לְמַבּוּל מִנִיסָן שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָתָם דְּגַם מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא מַבּוּל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כִּי הַחֵטְא מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּהֶכְרֵחַ אַחֲרָיו הַעוֹנֶשׁ.

Therefore they count the Flood from Nisan. According to their understanding, even under strict justice there could have been no alternative to the Flood, for sin necessarily draws punishment after it.
וְסוֹבְרִים דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת כְּלָל מִמַּה שֶׁהוּא דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה בִּלְעָם אַף דְּיָדַע שֶׁזֶּה תַּכְלִית הָרָע.
They believe that a being cannot truly change from what it is. Thus Balaam did not change even though he knew that his path represented the ultimate evil.
וְהוּא הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן שָׁרְשׁוֹ שָׁם אֲבָל הוּא חָשַׁב דְּהַכֹּל הֵם כֵּן.
For concerning his own root this was indeed true; his error was to assume that all beings are the same.

וְזֶה חָכְמַת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְהַפְרִיד הַיְדִיעָה מִבְּחִירָה שֶׁהוּא חַמָּה מִלְבְּנה שֶׁהוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵיהּ דְּנַעֲשָׂה רַק עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵּן לְכָל גּוֹי וּמִשְׁפָּטִים בְּלְ יְדָעוּם.

This is the wisdom of the nations: to separate Divine foreknowledge from human choice, like separating the sun from the moon. Their true union—the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah—is achieved only through Israel; “He has not done so for any nation, and His ordinances they do not know.”
כִּי עִיקַּר הַמִּשְׁפָּט דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא לְהַמְצִיא עֵצוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל דָּבָר כִּי הוּא חָפֵץ לְצֶדֶק בְּרִיּוֹתָיו.
For the essence of the blessed Hashem’s judgment is to devise counsels through which every matter can be rectified, because He desires to vindicate and make righteous His creatures.

וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין י"ז סוֹף עַמּוּד א)993 Sanhedrin 17a — Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: None are seated on the Sanhedrin but one who knows how to render a creeping thing ritually pure from the Torah. Rav said: I can argue the case and render it pure. Tosafos (s.v. "who knows how to render a creeping thing pure"): Rabbeinu Tam asks what we gain from empty cleverness that renders pure a creeping thing the Torah declared impure; he explains that it means exempting it from the impurity of carcasses, so that it does not convey impurity by being carried. For since the snake, a creeping thing, is counted a "beast", all creeping things might be included under "the carcass of a beast", and one renders them pure by a kal vachomer from the snake, which kills and so multiplies impurity yet is pure. Tosafot object to this, and suggest instead an argument from the carcass of a pure bird, which conveys impurity in the gullet but has none externally: all the more so should a creeping thing, which has no impurity in the gullet, have none externally. Maharsha: The point is that only one who is able to find grounds of acquittal for one who is liable is seated on the Sanhedrin; that is the allusion — one who knows how, in a matter that is certainly impure, such as a creeping thing, to find grounds to render it pure. Maharal (Derush al HaTorah): Rendering the creeping thing pure is not empty cleverness but something essential in the Torah, for one must know things in their essence, in all their aspects, and the creeping thing does have, in its very essence, aspects that point to purity, even though the Torah declared it impure. Just as one who says wood is of the element of air, since it floats, and one who says it is of earth, since it visibly contains earth when burned, both speak truly, though only the first speaks of its essence, so this is true reasoning, by which one grasps the creeping thing as it is in every aspect. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 15): On "None are seated on the Sanhedrin but one who knows how to render a creeping thing pure," Tosafos asked what need there is for such futile sharpness. The explanation is that it is so that he can plead merit for one who confesses and does not turn back, who is like a man immersing with a creeping thing in his hand: it is in his power to plead merit even for him, that he too has a remedy, for in the end [it] will enter his heart and he will be purified. אֵין מִוְשֶׁיָבִין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
Therefore the Sages said that a person may not be appointed to the Sanhedrin unless he knows how to declare the sheretz pure from the Torah.
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּמִשְׁפְּטֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהַמִּשְׁפָּט מָסוּר לָהֶם.
Such a capacity exists only within the laws and judgments of Israel, for judgment itself was entrusted to them.
כִּי הַמִּשְׁפָּט עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וּמַה שֶׁהֵם מַמְצִיאִים הוּא הַכֹּל תּוֹרָה וְאִם כֵּן כָּךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
The judgment must accord with Torah, and whatever the sages truly derive within Torah becomes Torah; consequently that becomes the judgment itself.
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן דִּינִין דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לָצֵאת מִהַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי הַנִּימוּס הָרָאוּי לְהַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם.
The laws of the nations, by contrast, cannot transcend the fixed legal order and social convention required for the governance of the world.

וְשׁוֹפָר הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלִי הַדַּיָּינִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז:)994 Sanhedrin 7b — "Which you shall set before them" — it should have said, "which you shall teach them." R. Yirmeya, and some say R. Ḥiyya bar Abba, said: These are the tools of the judges. Rav Huna, when he would go out to sit in judgment, would say: Bring out for me the implements of my trade — a rod and a strap, a shofar and a sandal. Rashi: "These are the tools of the judges" — for "setting" applies to them, as they are movable objects. The rod is for disciplinary lashes until [the recalcitrant party] relents; the strap for lashes; the shofar for excommunication and the ban; the sandal for chalitzah. Maharsha (s.v. "Bring out for me the implements"): "Bring out for me the implements of judgment" — so reads the Yalkut. In Eruvin (54b) the same verse, "which you shall set before them," teaches that a teacher must show his student the reasons, and Rashi there derives this too from its not saying "which you shall teach them"; one must therefore say that the two expositions carry equal weight. But for Rashi's explanation, it would seem that there it is expounded from "before them" — that one must show him the reasons — as the Mechilta says: "Arrange them before them like a set table." וְמַזְכִּירִין שׁוֹפָר דְּפּוּרְעָנֻיּוֹת דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא לְ"ב ב'.

The shofar is likewise among the instruments of judges, as the Sages state in Sanhedrin. The liturgy therefore also mentions the shofar of punishment directed toward the nations, as the Gemara teaches.
כִּי מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי דְּכָל קַרְנֵי רְשָׁעִים אֲגַדֵּעַ תְּרוֹמַמְנָה קַרְנוֹת צַדִּיק.
For when “all the horns of the wicked I will cut off,” automatically “the horns of the righteous will be exalted.”
וְשֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה וְמַרְפֵּא בִּכְנָפֶיהָ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
For Israel, the same sun becomes “a sun of righteousness with healing in its wings.”

וְלְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יְלַהֵט אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם דְּמוֹצִיא חַמָּה מִנַּרְתֵּקָהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נְדָרִים ח: וּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ע"ח995 Nedarim 8b — R. Shimon ben Lakish said: There is no Gehinnom in the world to come; rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the sun out of its sheath — the righteous are healed by it and the wicked are judged by it, as it is said: "But to you who fear My name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings." And not only that, but they take delight in it, as it is said: "And you shall go forth and grow fat like calves of the stall." And the wicked are judged by it, as it is said: "For behold, the day is coming, burning like an oven." Rashi: “The righteous are healed by it” — by that sun of the time to come; but in the sun of this world there is no healing. And “the day that comes shall set them ablaze” means the sun of that day. Tosafos (s.v. “and it differs from R. Shimon ben Lakish”): The exposition that applies “healing in its wings” to this world differs from R. Shimon ben Lakish, who applies the verse to a healing in the World to Come. Yet R. Shimon ben Lakish too concedes what people say, “when the sun rises the sick man rises”; he simply does not derive it from this verse. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Nedarim 8b): There is no Gehenna in the time to come because Gehenna is a deficiency of being, and in the time to come there is no deficiency of being, since everything will then be in its completeness. Rather the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the sun out of its sheath: the sheath is the obstructions and screens that in this world hinder the sun from performing its work, and in the time to come He will remove them. When the sun has no obstruction it burns the wicked, for the wicked cannot stand before a thing that is not material; but the righteous, who are separated [from matter], take delight in it, for the enjoyment of light belongs to the intellect, which is separate from the physical. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas HaChodesh 7): The nations count by the sun, which is fire, whereas Israel count by the moon, which is all light, for the moon only receives light from the sun and is not of fire. This is the meaning of "the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the sun out of its sheath; the righteous are healed by it": they attain only the light of the sun, like the moon that receives its light; "and the wicked are judged by it," for its fire burns them, as it is said, "the coming day shall set them ablaze." Sod Yesharim (Hoshana Rabbah 9): The very bestowal that is life to Israel, who receive it willingly, turns against the idolaters, who take it by compulsion and insolence, until they are utterly nullified by it. As the Gemara says, the Holy One, blessed be He, "brings the sun out of its sheath" and it heals Israel, while from it comes complete nullification to the idolaters.).
But for the nations “that coming day will burn them,” for the Holy One will take the sun out of its sheath, as the Sages taught.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הִתְגַּלּוּת הָאוֹר בָּעוֹלָם נִכְלֶה הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְנֶאֱבָד מֵעַצְמוֹ.
When the Divine light is revealed with full force in the world, the darkness is consumed and disappears of itself.

וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשּׁוֹפָר לְעוֹרֵר לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא מְעוֹרֵר יִרְאָה בַּלֵּב הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה וְרֹאשׁ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.

So too the awakening of the shofar rouses the hearts of Israel toward the blessed Hashem. For Israel it awakens awe in the heart, arising from the beginning of wisdom and from the first revelation of the year on Rosh Hashanah.
וְאֵצֶל הָאוּמּוֹת נַעֲשָׂה מִזֶּה סְעָרוֹת תֵּימָן הַסַּעַר אֲשֶׁר עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים יִחוּל.
For the nations, however, that same force becomes the “storms of the south,” the storm that whirls upon the heads of the wicked.

כְּמוֹ דְּמְשַׁמְּתִין עַל יְדֵי שִׁיפּוּרָא שֶׁהוּא שָׁם מִיתָה לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְחַיִּים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הַדְּבֵקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּאֱמוֹר.

This resembles excommunication being pronounced by the blast of a shofar: the same sound constitutes death for the nations and life for Israel, who cleave to Hashem, the living God and eternal King, as explained.

sections.en: Purim, Amalek, and the Concealed Root of Israel

items.h: Purim reveals the deepest root of Israel's holiness, beyond Amalek's reach, through the rise of Oral Torah, Esther, and the enduring bond that survives concealment.

Seif 1 — Sacred Time and Esther's Establishment
A salvation becomes eternally active when its merit is fixed in Israel; Esther sought to establish Purim in this way.

p: יָדוּעַ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים,
It is known concerning the sanctity of sacred times,
דְּבְכָל שָׁנָה בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם
that each year on that same day,
מִתְעוֹרֵר הָעִנְיָן הַנַּעֲשֶׂה אָז בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם.
the matter that occurred then on that day is awakened anew.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהָעִנְיָן נִקְבָּע וְקַיָּם לְדוֹרוֹת,
This applies when the event has been established and made enduring for the generations;
כִּי כָּל דְּבַר טוֹבָה הַנַּעֲשֶׂה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
for every good thing that occurs to Israel—
מֵהַצָּלָה וִישׁוּעָה,
every deliverance and salvation—
הַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
comes through judgment,
מִצַּד אֵיזֶה זְכוּת שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן.
by virtue of some merit that was awakened at that time.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אוֹתוֹ זְכוּת נִקְבָּע קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
When the holiness of that merit becomes permanently rooted in Israel throughout the generations,
אָז גַּם קְדֻשַּׁת אוֹתוֹ הַזְּמַן קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם לְדוֹרוֹת,
the sanctity of that time likewise becomes fixed and enduring for the generations,
לִהְיוֹת מִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ אוֹתוֹ זְכוּת
so that the power of that merit
וְאוֹתָהּ יְשׁוּעָה פְּרָטִית בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה.
and of that particular salvation is reawakened each and every year.

וְזֶהוּ (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה זַ996 Megillah 7a — Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said: Esther sent word to the Sages — Establish me for the generations! They sent back to her: You will stir up the envy of the nations against us. She sent to them: I am already written in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Rashi: "She sent to them" — in the second year, to establish it upon them as an obligation; "establish me" — as a festival and for the reading, that I may have a name thereby. "You are stirring up envy against us" — for the nations will say that we rejoice to recall their downfall; and to this she answered that she is already written [in their chronicles], and there they will see what befell them at the hands of Israel. Maharsha: This whole exchange is already intimated in the verses: first "And Mordecai wrote… to enjoin upon them that they should keep [these days]" (Esther 9:20–21), and they would not accept it, because of "you are stirring up envy"; then "And Esther wrote… to confirm this second letter of Purim" and "he sent letters" (Esther 9:29–30), which close by saying that envy need not be feared, for they are "words of peace and truth." And her reply is the verse "are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia" (Esther 10:2). עַמּוּד א׳)
This is the meaning (Megillah 7a)
שֶׁשָּׁלְחָה אֶסְתֵּר לַחֲכָמִים: ״קִבְעוּנִי לְדוֹרוֹת״,
of Esther sending to the Sages, “Establish me for the generations,”
שֶׁבְּיַד הַחֲכָמִים דָּבָר זֶה,

וְשׁוּרְיָינָא דְּעֵינָא בְּלִבָּא תָּלֵי (מַסֶּכֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ״ח997 Avodah Zarah 28b — There was a certain maidservant in the house of Mar Shmuel whose eye became inflamed on Shabbat. She cried out, and there was none who attended to her, and her eye burst. The next day Mar Shmuel went out and expounded: An eye that has rebelled — it is permitted to apply eye salve to it on Shabbat. What is the reason? Because the tendons of the eye are bound up with the understanding of the heart. Rashi: "An eye that has rebelled" — it seeks to come out [of its socket], like a man who rebels and goes out; and its being "bound up with the heart" means that the light of the eye is intertwined with and held fast in the membranes of the heart [so that the danger is to life itself]. Tosafos (s.v. "the tendons of the eye are bound up with the heart"): Rashi explains that the light of the eye depends on the membranes of the heart, but it seems rather that the reading is "upon the understanding of the heart" — that is, the eye's seeing depends upon the heart's understanding. Accordingly the word for "tendons" is spelled with a shin, from "I behold him," or with a samekh, from the expression "he surveys his property"; and "understanding" is with a bet, from the word for comprehension, as is said of the Chariot, "he would see with the understanding of the heart." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 190): Joseph [whose level is the eye] reported that his brothers "cast their eyes" [on the daughters of the land], for he held that "the tendons of the eye are bound up with the heart," as they also said, "a bride whose eyes are beautiful [needs no examination of her whole body]." But in truth the essence is the heart, "for from it are the issues of life," since in it lies the essence of vitality and of cleaving to the living God. עַמּוּד ב׳).
and “the sinews of the eye depend upon the heart” (Avodah Zarah 28b).

Likewise, among inner faculties the power of sight acts upon the heart,

עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נָשׂא, פָּרָשָׁה י998 Bamidbar Rabbah 10:2 — What did the Holy One, blessed be He, see, that He asked of Israel the heart and the eyes, that they should follow after Him? Because transgression depends on them, as it is written: "and you shall not stray after your heart and after your eyes" — the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin. "For a harlot is a deep pit" — as Moses said, "after which you go astray," to say that unchastity depends on them: the eyes see the harlot, and the heart muses after her. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 16): The Sages' words "the eye sees, the heart desires, and the organs of action complete [the deed]" describe three levels. Wisdom is the stage still at "the eye sees" alone, momentary and not yet spread through to the end, unlike prophecy, which has passed through all the levels and is fully possessed; yet wisdom is superior, in the manner of "better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the soul" (Ecclesiastes 6:9). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 1): A thought that reaches the root of wisdom in the brain is joined to the understanding in the heart, so that it is at once felt in the heart and gives birth to the powers of action, as in "the eye sees, the heart desires, and the organs of action complete [the deed]"; for we find seeing associated with wisdom, as it is written, "my heart has seen much wisdom" (Ecclesiastes 1:16). Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Tetzaveh): The kapores corresponds to the heart and the menorah to the eyes, and these alone were of pure gold [without a core of acacia wood], because in them a person must be clean of any self-interest in this world, since "the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin: the eye sees and the heart desires." The eye should be stripped of all worldly desire and serve only as an instrument for the soul, like clear glass through which the soul looks at each thing and judges whether to accept it; but when the eye itself craves the delights of this world, it is no longer the soul's instrument but acts on its own and covets, and the soul cannot sort the good from the bad.׳):

Therefore, “a bride whose eyes are beautiful,

אֵין כָּל גּוּפָהּ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה (מַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית כ״ד999 Taanit 24a — Oshaya the Younger of the company taught before them: "And if it be committed in error by the eyes of the congregation." A parable of a bride who is in her father's house: so long as her eyes are beautiful, her whole body requires no examination; if her eyes are bleary, her whole body requires examination. Rashi: "The Younger of the company": the youngest in the academy, so called because there was another Oshaya there; "the eyes of the congregation": the elders, who give light to the eyes of the people. "So long as her eyes are beautiful": then certainly her whole body is beautiful. "If her eyes are bleary": since those of the Nasi's house, who were the eyes of the congregation, were wicked, the deeds of the common people need not be examined, and therefore Heaven paid them no heed. Maharsha: He cites this verse from the portion of Shelach rather than the earlier one in Vayikra, "and the matter be hidden from the eyes of the assembly" (Leviticus 4:13), because there the plain sense can stand, "the eyes of the assembly" referring to the matter's being hidden; but here, "if it be done by the eyes of the congregation," no hiding is mentioned, only doing, and doing does not apply to eyes. Therefore they expounded that the eyes of the congregation are the elders and leaders of the generation, through whom [the error] was done; and since he likens the leaders to eyes, the parable followed: "so long as her eyes are beautiful..." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 2): The two months Tammuz and Av are called "the eyes of the Matrona," for sight is the most distant kind of apprehension, and these months are the days of smallness and distance, the eyes that see from afar. And "a bride whose eyes are beautiful, her whole body requires no examination; if her eyes are bleary, her whole body requires examination" (Taanit 24a); therefore in these two months, so that the whole body should not, Heaven forfend, have to be examined, her eyes were made beautiful, and then the whole body requires no examination. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Ahasuerus's feast was a trial for Israel in self-sacrifice, and the Great Sanhedrin, called "the eyes of the congregation," were present at it; since the desire for this world, which makes one shrink from self-sacrifice, begins with the eye that sees, they said in Taanit (24a), "A bride whose eyes are beautiful, her whole body requires no examination." Hence, had this trial been resolved for the good through the Sanhedrin, the eyes of the congregation, that would have sufficed, for then the whole body needs no further examination; but when their eyes were not found beautiful, though this does not testify to a defect in the rest of the body, the whole body nevertheless requires further examination and clarification. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 6): King David, peace be upon him, was praised as "of beautiful eyes," and "a bride whose eyes are beautiful, her whole body requires no examination"; so in truth he too was of utmost beauty, fenced off from all the filth of this world's desires, which darken and blacken. Only the revelation was in the eyes, for the eye and the heart are the two agents of sin, and the heart is hidden from all — "the Lord sees into the heart," while man sees what is before the eyes, which is revealed. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Unsightliness of the eyes is the principal thing in a woman, as the Sages said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, "every bride whose eyes are beautiful...," for desire begins with the eye that sees and the heart that desires. The essence of beauty is the subduing of desire: one who is mighty and conquers his inclination in desire, "his whole body requires no examination," for this is the level of the fear of God; but of one whose eyes [are bleary], "her whole body requires examination" — and even so, examination at least avails, so that one need no longer heed the unsightliness of the eyes. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): Beauty exists only for the sight of the eyes, and the blind do not sense beauty of appearance; therefore the essence of beauty, too, lies only in the eyes, as they said in Taanit (24a), "A bride whose eyes are beautiful, her whole body requires no examination" — for the beauty of the eyes testifies to the beauty of the body as well, and likewise, "if her eyes are bleary...," the ugliness of the eyes testifies to the ugliness of the body. Just as beauty is sensed only by the eye, so the very substance of beauty was placed in it, since this organ is the vessel for it. עַמּוּד א׳).

אַדְּרַבָּה, אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה ט״ז1000 Megillah 16b — "For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the multitude of his brethren." "By the multitude of his brethren" — and not by all his brethren: this teaches that a part of the Sanhedrin parted from him. Rashi: They parted from him because he neglected words of Torah and entered public office. Maharsha: "His brethren" are his colleagues, who were of the number of the Men of the Great Assembly. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 10:3): Some of the Sanhedrin applied to him "Do not lust after the table of kings," as though royalty stood above the crown of Torah, whereas the crown of Torah is above the crown of kings; and though all that Mordecai did was only to save the lives of Israel, Torah study is greater than saving lives, for saving a life keeps the soul from death, while Torah study gives eternal existence even in the World to Come. Therefore, even if his intention was to save lives, he ought not to have done this, for the Torah is above all — and so some of the Sanhedrin parted from him. Yet the majority did not part from him, for saving lives too brings the life of the World to Come, as "better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come." עַמּוּד ב׳)

Amalek and Yitro were both in Pharaoh's counsel. When Yitro saw that the Holy One, blessed be He, had destroyed Amalek from this world and from the World to Come, he was stricken with remorse and repented, and he said: I have nowhere to go but to the God of Israel. Hence, "strike the scoffer" — this is Amalek; "and the simple will become prudent" — this is Yitro. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): When a word of Torah departs from a person, a word of scoffing enters in its place, and these are the words of Amalek, as the Sages said (Shemos Rabbah 27) on the verse "Strike the scoffer": "this is Amalek"; for this is the root of the nations, that every way of truth is to him a matter for scoffing. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 2): Amalek is the husk of the dog, the husk of pride and honor, of which Scripture says, "The proud, arrogant man, scoffer is his name," as it is expounded, "Strike the scoffer — this is Amalek," for he is the scoffer. All the nations heard and trembled, having seen open and manifest miracles they could not deny, but he pushed everything aside through scoffing and denied; and this comes from pride, for it is inconceivable to him that anything should be hidden from his intellect and beyond his grasp, and so he became a scoffer. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 259): Just as the root of all good is faith, so the root of all evil is scoffing, the opposite of faith, which mocks everything; this is why "Amalek is the first of nations," as the Midrash says (Shemos Rabbah 27) on "Strike the scoffer — this is Amalek; and the simple will become prudent — this is Yitro." כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת (פ״ט1003 Shabbat 89b — "The wilderness of Sinai" — for hatred toward the nations of the world came down upon it. And what is its name? Horeb is its name. And this differs from R. Abbahu, who said: Mount Sinai is its name, and why is it called Mount Horeb? Because desolation toward the nations of the world came down upon it. Rashi (on 89a, s.v. "hatred toward the nations"): "Hatred toward the nations" — because they did not accept the Torah on it. Maharsha: According to the first view Horeb is the mountain's principal name, since it is the first name by which the Torah calls it — "and he came to the mountain of God, to Horeb"; R. Abbahu holds that Sinai is its principal name because Scripture for the most part calls it Sinai. Maharal (Gevuros Hashem, ch. 23): R. Abbahu means that Mount Sinai has only two names: its essential name, and a name for what follows necessarily from its essence. What follows here is the destruction of the nations rather than the good that came to Israel, for that good did not come on the mountain but comes only when Israel fulfil the Torah, whereas the nations, having refused to accept the Torah, received their sentence at once, when the giving of the Torah to Israel came into being. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 26): "What is its name? Horeb is its name," for everything follows from this: every wilderness is a place laid waste, and all five names derive from it. R. Abbahu holds that its essential name is Sinai and that it is called Horeb for the destruction that descended from it upon the nations: before the giving of the Torah the nations were the principal existence in the world, and when the Torah was given all of them became desolate, as though the whole world had been destroyed. עַמּוּד ב׳):
as they said in Tractate Shabbat (89b):
״הַר חוֹרֵב — שֶׁיָּרְדָה חֻרְבָּה״ וְכוּלֵי.
“Mount Horeb—because destruction descended upon them there.”
חוּץ מֵעֲמָלֵק,
Except for Amalek,
שֶׁבָּא וְקָפַץ לְתוֹךְ אַמְבַּטִּי הָרוֹתַחַת.
who came and jumped into the scalding bath.
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָרְתִיחָה הָיְתָה גַּם נֶגְדּוֹ,
For even though that heat was directed against him too—
כִּי כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת הֵם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹתָיו —
since all the nations are extensions of his forces—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, נֶגֶד שָׁרְשׁוֹ בִּפְרָט
nevertheless, specifically against his ultimate root
לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה דְּבַר תּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
no teaching of Torah was revealed in this world.
כִּי מִכָּל הָאוּמּוֹת יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה קְלִיטָה לְטוֹב,
For from every other nation there is some spark that can be absorbed for good,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל כֹּחַ רַע גַּם כֵּן
meaning that within every evil power there is also
אֵיזֶה פְּרָט שֶׁפְּעָמִים הוּא טוֹב.
some particular detail that at times can be turned to good.
וְכָל הָאוּמּוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת פְּרָטִים,
All the nations are particularized powers;
רַק הֵם מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בּוֹ בְּצַד הָרָע,
they merely use them on the side of evil,
שֶׁהוּא הַצַּד שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת דְּמִכֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק.
which is the side of cynical mockery derived from Amalek.
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בְּצַד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ
Israel, however, uses the good side within it
עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה.
in accordance with the Torah.
אֲבָל עֲמָלֵק הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבְּכָל כֹּחַ וְכֹחַ,
Amalek, by contrast, is the root of evil within every power,
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַלֵּיצָנוּת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
and the root of mockery in the world.
וּבוֹ נֶאֱמַר ״תִּמְחֶה״,
Of him it is said, “You shall blot out,”
שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ קְלִיטָה לְטוֹב כְּלַל,
because no good can be absorbed from him at all,
וְאֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּרִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
and converts are not accepted from him.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא מָצוּי בָּעוֹלָם,
As long as he exists in the world,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמֹד עַל עִנְיָנוֹ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה.
it is impossible to grasp his phenomenon through wisdom alone.
רָצָה לוֹמַר: כִּי כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם לֹא עָשָׂה אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
That is to say: nothing in the world created itself,
וְאֵין שָׁם מְצִיאוּת נִפְרָד כְּלַל,
and there is no separate, independent existence whatsoever,
דְּ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״.
for “there is nothing besides Him.”
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בְּכָל כֹּחוֹת הָאוּמּוֹת,
Therefore, even within each force of the nations,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ בְּכֹחַ זֶה לְטוֹב,
there must inevitably be some root of good in that force
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קִיּוּם אוֹתָהּ אֻמָּה.
through which that nation maintains its existence.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה
And through the Torah,
קוֹלְטִים יִשְׂרָאֵל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ.
Israel absorbs the good contained within that power.
וְעַל כֵּן הֶחֱזִיר הַתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה
This is why the Torah was first offered
עַל כָּל אֻמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן,
to every nation and tongue,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד כָּל כֹּחוֹתֵיהֶם.
corresponding to all their specific powers.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
Afterward He came to Israel
וְהוֹפִיעַ אֲלֵיהֶם מִשֵּׂעִיר וְהַר פָּארָן,
and shone forth to them from Seir and Mount Paran,
שֶׁכָּל הָאוּמּוֹת נָתְנוּ לָהֶם מַתָּנָה,
meaning that all the nations gave them gifts,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר, חֵלֶק ג׳, קצ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳ — קצ״ג עַמּוּד א1004 Zohar 3:192b — He said to him: Since it is so, give Me counsel — how shall I bring it about that the children of Jacob accept it? He said to Him: Master of the world, they must be bribed. Take light from the radiance of the hosts of heaven and place it upon them, and by this they will accept it; and let mine be given first. He stripped from himself the radiance that covered him and gave it to Him, to give to Israel. That is what is written: "and He shone forth to them from Seir" — from Seir literally, this is Samael. And so Rahab: "let my birthright be his, and this light that I have inherited, take and give to them" — and so He did, as it is written: "He appeared from Mount Paran."׳).
as our Sages expounded (Zohar III, 192b–193a).
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם מִכֹּחַ שֶׁלָּהֶם
That is, even the power belonging to them,
מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה,
from the side of their holy root,
נִתַּן כֻּלּוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
was yielded entirely to Israel.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָם כֹּחַ פְּרָטִי כְּלַל,
For Israel is not a particularized, limited force at all,
כִּי הֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּלַל הָעוֹלָם,
because they are the root of the totality of the world,
שֶׁנֶּגְדָּם הוּא עֲמָלֵק ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ —
and opposite them stands Amalek, “the first of the nations”—
שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע,
the root of evil,
וְהֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב.
whereas Israel is the root of good.
וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה קָלְטוּ
At the giving of the Torah they absorbed
גַּם כָּל כֹּחוֹת פְּרָטִים שֶׁבְּטוֹב שֶׁל כֹּחַ כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת,
every particular good spark within the power of all nations,
וְהֵם נִפְרְדוּ לָרַע לְחֵלֶק עֲמָלֵק.
while the nations were separated toward evil, to the lot of Amalek.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּהַר סִינַי
Therefore at Mount Sinai
יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה וְחֻרְבָּה לָהֶם,
hatred and destruction descended upon them,
דְּרַק מֵאָז נִתְרַחֲקוּ.
for only from that point onward were they completely distanced.
דְּמִקּוֹדֶם הָיָה שֹׁרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב גַּם כֵּן בְּקִרְבָּם,
Before that, the root of good was still present within them,
וְהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן נְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
and there were also prophets among the nations of the world,
כִּי יֵשׁ מֵהֶם טוֹבִים.
because some good remained among them.
וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה קָלְטוּ הַכֹּל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
At the giving of the Torah, Israel gathered all of that good;
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא טוֹב בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם —
and anyone among the nations who is truly good—
צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּר,
must convert,
לִהְיוֹת כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל.
becoming like a newborn child under the name Israel.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִטַּע בְּאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
As long as he has not been grafted into the Jewish nation,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת טוֹב כְּלַל,
it is impossible for him to be intrinsically good,
כִּי אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
for after the giving of the Torah
הוּא שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עֲמָלֵק לְבַדּוֹ הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
Amalek alone became the first principle of the nations,
וְאֵין לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת רֵאשִׁית טוֹב כְּלַל.
and the nations no longer possess an independent root of good.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Amalek against the Hidden Root of Torah
Amalek opposes the deepest Torah-root beyond ordinary wisdom, the level not fully revealed even through Moshe.

p: וּבִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף
At the splitting of the Red Sea
הָיָה הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
was the initial awakening toward the giving of the Torah,
שֶׁעִקַּר הַתּוֹרָה
for the essence of the Torah
הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיג הָעוֹלָם,
is the revelation of how the blessed Hashem conducts the world,
וְהַכֹּל הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ.
and that all is from Him, and there is nothing besides Him.
וּבִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
At the splitting of the Sea this was revealed through sight,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְכִילְתָּא וְהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח)1005 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Shirah 3:10 — "This is my God." R. Eliezer says: How do you know that a maidservant saw at the sea what Isaiah and Ezekiel did not see? For it is said, "and by the hand of the prophets I was likened," and "the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God." They told a parable: to what may the matter be compared? To a king of flesh and blood who entered a province surrounded by his guard, with warriors at his right and left and his troops before and behind him, and all were asking, "Which one is the king?" — for he is flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself at the sea, none of them needed to ask, "Which is He?" As soon as they saw Him they recognized Him, and they all opened their mouths and said: "This is my God and I will glorify Him, the God of my father and I will exalt Him." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): At the splitting of the Red Sea came the revelation of sight — "a maidservant saw at the Sea," etc. — which they afterwards attained as a possession at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:35): Therefore the Sages said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea," etc.: with the complete destruction of Egypt, the hidden root of evil, the hidden root of good was clarified — that the root of things is from the Blessed One alone — and this is the ultimate unity, when it becomes clear to the eye. Then she saw the entire Account of the Chariot of Ezekiel, that is, how the Blessed One rides upon all of creation, which is only a throne and chariot for Him and nothing apart from Him or a thing in its own right. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on completing the Talmud 2): The Talmud opens in Berakhos with Shema, prayer and blessings — speech addressed to the Blessed One and clear recognition of His truth — in the manner of "a maidservant saw at the Sea": when a Jew first begins to draw near to words of Torah, the Blessed One opens a great light for him. Afterwards the light is dimmed, as at Sinai, where after the first utterance the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down dew; for there are depths and light above light, and the Blessed One wishes to raise a person ever higher. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): Holy sight stems from awe, the level of Isaac; its clarification began with Isaac's birth and continued four hundred years until the Exodus, when "a maidservant saw at the Sea," as the Sages said — for then the seeing was completed in full. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bo 3): The distinction made in the plague of pestilence was of the aspect of supernal wonder, as at the splitting of the Red Sea, which depended on Atika [the Ancient One]; and when the Sages said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see," this is the revelation of Atika, of whom it is written, "doing wonders." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 189): Apprehending God through His governance — how the Blessed One "rides" upon His creatures — is called the Account of the Chariot, the level of "knowledge" of Moses our teacher. The generation of the wilderness, called the "generation of knowledge," of whom it is said, "a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see" — that is, the Account of the Chariot — were all prepared for this knowledge, the level of Moses, the leader who encompassed them all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Bava Metzia): At the Exodus Israel attained by sight, as it says, "a maidservant saw at the Sea," and they thought that by this seeing they had acquired the light as a full possession. But afterwards they went three days without finding water — without longing, for "water" is Torah — and recognized that they did not yet have a full possession, until they attained it completely at the giving of the Torah. What a person attains by sight he can later acquire fully through effort, and only what he acquires by his own effort remains his in the World to Come.:
as it is written (Mekhilta and the holy Zohar, Beshalach):
״רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל״.
“A maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי,
And as I heard,
דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא בְּקִנְיָן
that the giving of the Torah was by permanent acquisition
מַה שֶׁהָיָה בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף בִּרְאִיָּה,
of that which at the Sea was experienced through sight alone,
דְּהָרְאִיָּה אֵינוֹ קִנְיָן בַּלֵּב.
for sight by itself is not yet an internal acquisition in the heart.
רַק לְפִי הַסָּלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בַּגְּמָרָא רֵישׁ בָּבָא מְצִיעָא:
Only according to the initial Talmudic premise in Bava Metzia:
״בִּרְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא קָנֵי״,
“Does mere sight acquire?”
הַיְינוּ דְּסָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת בְּנֵי אָדָם הוּא כֵּן.
meaning that this is how ordinary human thought initially imagines it.
וּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב בָּרוֹקֵחַ:
And the Sea conforms to what is written in the Rokeach:
״אֵין חֹזֶק כַּחֲסִידוּת בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ״.
“No strength of piety equals its first awakening.”
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשְׁקָע אוֹתוֹ חֵשֶׁק,
Afterward, that intense yearning subsides,
כִּי הוּא רְאִיָּה לְבַד,
because it was merely a temporary vision;
וְצָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר וּלְעוֹרְרוֹ
and one must return and reawaken it
עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא לִהְיוֹת קִנְיָן בַּלֵּב.
until it becomes an enduring possession in the heart.
וּלְעוֹלָם הָרְאִיָּה
In all cases, the initial vision
הוּא כְּפִי מַה שֶׁהוּא מוּכָן לְהַשִּׂיג בְּקִנְיָן,
corresponds to what a person is prepared to acquire;
מַרְאִין לוֹ תְּחִלָּה: ״לָזֶה אַתָּה מוּכָן״.
first he is shown: “For this level you are designated.”
וּמִיָּד בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף:
Immediately upon the splitting of the Sea:
״שָׁמְעוּ עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן״.
“The nations heard and trembled.”
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ לִרְפִידִים —
Afterward they arrived at Rephidim—
רִפּוּי יָדַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
a weakening of hands from the words of Torah,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן בְּקִנְיָן.
because it was not yet held as a solid acquisition.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת
And although in absolute truth
שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בַּתּוֹרָה
the root of Israel was already cleaved to the Torah
עוֹד מִימֵי אָבוֹת,
from the Patriarchal era,
שֶׁקִּיְּמוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ,
who fulfilled the entire Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת,
nevertheless it was not yet outwardly manifested;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא רִפּוּי יָדַיִם — כֹּחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
therefore it is called a weakening of hands—the faculties of deed.
וְאָז בָּא עֲמָלֵק,
And then Amalek came,
כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בַּתּוֹרָה,
for as long as Israel remains attached to the Torah,
שֶׁהֵם עַנְפֵי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם הַמִּתְגַּלִּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which are the revealed branches of the hidden root in this world,
אֵין מָקוֹם לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע לִקְרַב לָהֶם.
there is no opening for the root of evil to approach them.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר רָפוּ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
However, when they grew lax in Torah,
אַף דְּרִפְיוֹן זֶה הוּא יְרִידָה שֶׁלְּצוֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה
even though this laxity was a descent for the sake of ascent
וְקִנְיָן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר כָּךְ,
and for the subsequent true acquisition of Torah—
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה לְשׁוּם אֻמָּה
so that no other nation
הַרְגָּשָׁה בְּרִפְיוֹן זֶה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
sensed this internal weakness within Israel
שֶׁיָּסִיר פַּחְדָּם מֵעֲלֵיהֶם.
in a way that would lift their dread of them—
וּבֶאֱמֶת רִפְיוֹן זֶה אֵינוֹ רִפְיוֹן כְּלַל,
and in truth this laxity is not genuine weakness at all,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה,
since its ultimate objective is ascent;
וְכָל דָּבָר נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ וְתַכְלִיתוֹ.
and everything is defined by its eventual outcome and purpose.
אַךְ זֶהוּ מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת,
Yet that is only from the perspective of truth;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַלֵּיצָנוּת
from the perspective of mockery,
אֵין מַבִּיטִים עַל הַתַּכְלִית שֶׁבְּכָל דָּבָר כְּלַל.
one does not look at the ultimate purpose of anything at all.
וְאָמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ״ — שֶׁהִקְרִירְךָ,
Thus Scripture states: “who happened upon you (karcha)”—that he cooled you (hikrircha),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵבִיא קְרִירוּת וְרִפְיוֹן בַּלֵּב,
meaning he injected chill and cynicism into the heart;
דְּזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק:
for this is the essential root of Amalek:
לְקָרֵר הַלֵּב
to freeze the heart
מִלְּבַקֵּשׁ וּלְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
from seeking and striving in Torah
וְהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and attaining the blessed Hashem.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
This stands opposite the fiftieth root hidden in this world,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמָה
meaning there is a taproot of wisdom
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב כָּל כָּךְ,
established so firmly in the heart,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת לְרִפְיוֹן כְּלַל.
that no reality of laxity could ever exist.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר
And the full revelation of this is impossible
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת עֲמָלֵק,
as long as Amalek has existence,
שֶׁהוּא מְצִיאוּת הָרִפְיוֹן וְהַקֵּירוּר.
for he is the very embodiment of spiritual laxity and chill.
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת כֵּן,
And from the vantage of this world it must be so,

עַל דֶּרֶךְ (מַסֶּכֶת גִּטִּין מ״ג1006 Gittin 43a — Rabba bar Rav Huna then set an interpreter before him and expounded: "And let this stumbling block be under your hand" — a man does not stand upon words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them. Although they said that one who betroths half a woman, she is not betrothed, still a woman who is half maidservant and half free who was betrothed, her betrothal is a valid betrothal. Rashi (s.v. "and let this stumbling block be under your hand"): He set up an interpreter before him in order to expound a second time, and he opened from the verse, which was said of the men of Jerusalem when Torah had ceased among them, so that they would say to one another, "You have a cloak, be our chief" — that is, matters covered over like your cloak, in which you are expert, tell them to us and be our chief. "And let this stumbling block be under your hand" means words of Torah, upon whose truth a man does not stand until he has stumbled in them by ruling in error and is put to shame, and then he sets his heart to it and understands. So I too stumbled in my ruling, and therefore I retract. Maharsha: When he first taught this ruling it is not said that he set an interpreter before him. Perhaps an interpreter was set up only for the exposition of a verse that was published to the many, as here with "and let this stumbling block be under your hand," whereas earlier he had published to the many only the ruling itself. עַמּוּד א׳):
in accordance with (Gittin 43a):
״אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשָׁל״,
“A person does not master words of Torah unless he first stumbles,”
וְ״שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם״ —
and “A righteous person falls seven times and rises”—
שֶׁהַנְּפִילָה צוֹרֶךְ קִימָה.
for the fall is indispensable for the rise.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה1007 Berakhot 5a — It is taught: R. Shimon ben Yochai says: Three good gifts did the Holy One, blessed be He, give to Israel, and all of them He gave only by means of suffering. These are they: the Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. Maharsha: Each of the three is called good in Scripture: of the Torah it is written "a good teaching I have given you," of the Land, "the good land which He gave you," and of the World to Come, "behold, I have set before you this day life and good." Torah is given through suffering because the pleasures of this world are the neglect of Torah, as they said, "such is the way of Torah: bread with salt shall you eat"; the Land was given through suffering to teach that it was not given for eating its fruits and delighting in its abundance, which would bring a man to rebel, as it is written, "lest you eat and be satisfied… and your heart grow haughty and you forget"; and the World to Come is given by way of the sufferings of this world, which scour the righteous man's sins so that he may receive his reward in full. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaYissurin 2): Suffering is the refining of the soul; therefore, when Israel were to acquire a level separate from the body, they first required the scouring and cleansing of the soul until they were fit to receive that holy level. The three gifts correspond to three ascending degrees of holiness: the Land of Israel is holy, yet in itself it is corporeal and merely possesses holiness; the Torah is higher, being intellectual and not corporeal, though it still has a bond with corporeal man; and the World to Come is wholly separate. Each, therefore, could be attained only through suffering, which diminishes the body and so brings a man to what is separate from it. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:56): Sufferings and judgments are needed to arouse [Israel] to repentance so that there may be an opening for birth, for against kindness there is room for accusation. Every birth is possible only through suffering, as the Sages said, "Three good gifts, and all of them through suffering"; for there is always an accusation, since it is not yet made clear that the salvation is deserved by right. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): The Egyptian exile was a preparation for the giving of the Torah, as stated in Shemos Rabbah and in the first chapter of Berakhos: "Three good gifts... through suffering." A "gift" is what comes not by obligation and recompense, that is, not through any arousal from below at all; therefore the Torah is everywhere called a gift, [given] without any effort, for by virtue of "yet I loved Jacob" they are good by their very birth, without any choice, and so the Torah was given to them — and the preparation for this was the Egyptian exile. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bo 11): [The first] "Let there be light" corresponds to Parashas Shemos, which tells of the exile, the preparation for the giving of the Torah, as the Midrash says on "but he who loves him chastens him early," and as the Gemara says, "Three good gifts... through suffering, and these are: Torah, etc." The sufferings of the Egyptian exile were a preparation through which they merited the giving of the Torah. Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 55): As it is taught, "Three good gifts the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to Israel, and all of them through suffering," and one of them is the Sanctuary, the place fixed for prayer and for the fear of God. This is like the saying "A person does not stand firm in words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them": for all things that require fixity — to be established permanently, an acquisition for all eternity — require endurance. Sod Yesharim (Sukkos 54): In this world it is impossible to bring forth the precious from the vile without endurance, for only through great endurance can one acquire words of Torah, which are called "precious," as it is taught: "Three good gifts were given to Israel, and all of them were given only through suffering." Of this the verse says, "And it shall come to pass on that day that there shall be no light of precious things and frost," for in this world precious things can be received only through suffering, unlike in the time to come.׳ עַמּוּד א׳):
And as they taught in Berakhot (5a):
״שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת״ וְכוּלֵי
“Three precious gifts...”
וְכֻלָּם עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין,
and all were granted through affliction,
וְיִסּוּרִין הוּא הֵפֶךְ הַטּוֹב.
even though affliction is the antithesis of good.
רַק שֶׁכֵּן הוּא מִדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
Rather, such is the structure of this world:
לִהְיוֹת דַּוְקָא ״בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״,
