to proceed specifically “first through darkness and only then to light,”
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת רַע בָּעוֹלָם.
and through this dynamic, evil finds temporary room to exist.
וְאוּלָם צוֹרֶךְ שֹׁרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת זֶה,
However, the inner reason for the root of this dynamic,
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן דַּוְקָא,
and why it must be so specifically,
זֶהוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י׳ עַמּוּד א׳):
is like what they said in Berakhot (10a):
״בַּהֲדֵי כִּבְשֵׁי דְרַחֲמָנָא לָמָּה לָךְ?״
“Why pry into the hidden secrets of the Merciful One?”
שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה שֶׁתּוֹלִיד רָשָׁע וָרָע.
when He wills that one bear a wicked child and bring evil into being.
וְלֹא נִתְגַּלָּה טַעְמוֹ לְשׁוּם נָבִיא,
Its reason was never disclosed to any prophet,
וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
not even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
הוּא בִּכְלַל ״וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ״.
which is included in “but My face shall not be seen.”
כִּי מִצַּד הָאֲחוֹרַיִם
For from the aspect of the ‘back’
יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לְהֶעְלֵם וְהַסְתָּרוֹת,
there is room for concealment and obscurity,
וְהוּא הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and this is the comprehension allotted to this world.
״וּפָנַי״ הוּא הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
“My face” is the direct perception reserved for the World to Come,
שֶׁאֵין שָׁם מָקוֹם לְשׁוּם הַסְתָּרָה כְּלַל.
where no concealment can possibly remain.
וְזֶהוּ הַשָּׂגַת שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנִּזְכָּר,
And this is the comprehension of the aforementioned Fiftieth Gate,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מָקוֹם עוֹד לְרִפְיוֹן.
wherein no susceptibility to laxity can ever exist again.
וּבְהַשָּׂגַת שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמָה זוֹ
And through grasping the root of this wisdom,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דַּעֲמָלֵק
which corresponds to and stands against the root of Amalek,
יוּכְלוּ לְהָבִין עִנְיַן מְצִיאוּת זֶה דְּרַע הַקּוֹדֵם לַטּוֹב
they will be able to understand the concept of this reality where evil precedes good,
כְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא כִּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר בִּפְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
just like this world, which is like an antechamber before the World to Come.
[וְשָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי "וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי"
And I heard that "And you shall see My back" (Exodus 33:23)
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַחַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג מַה הָיָה כַּוָּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה
means that after an event has occurred, one can grasp what the intention of Hashem, blessed be He, was in that occurrence,
בְּכָל פְּעֻלָּה וְעִנְיָן הַהֹוֶה בָּעוֹלָם;
in every action and circumstance taking place in the world;
אֲבָל "וּפָנַי" הַיְינוּ קֹדֶם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
however, "but My face" refers to before the occurrence,
זֶה לֹא נִגְלָה גַּם לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this was not revealed even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him—
מַה הָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה,
namely, what the divine will of Hashem, blessed be He, was regarding that event beforehand,
וְגַם זֶה מְכֻוָּן עַל פִּי דְּרָכֵינוּ.
and this also aligns directly with our path.
וְכָל עִנְיַן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַה הַמְּכֻוָּן בּוֹ לֹא יִתְגַּלֶּה אֶלָּא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And the entire matter of this world—what the ultimate intent is within it—will not be revealed until the World to Come;
וְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא הַשָּׂגַת אָחוֹר,
and this world is called the apprehension of the "back,"
שֶׁמַּשְׁמָעוֹ מַה שֶּׁאַחַר כָּךְ,
which signifies that which follows afterward,
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַשִּׂיגִין מְצִיאוּת עוֹלָם הַבָּא
for in this world one can grasp the existence of the World to Come,
אֲבָל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג עִנְיַן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַה הוּא,
yet it is impossible to fully grasp the essential nature and purpose of this world itself,
רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא אָז יַשִּׂיגוּ הַפָּנִים וְהַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן.]
and only in the World to Come will they then comprehend the "face" and the precursor as well.
כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת לָרַע,
For as long as there is an active reality of evil,
אִם יָאִיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵינֵיהֶם לָדַעַת צֹרֶךְ שֹׁרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת זֶה,
if Hashem, blessed be He, were to enlighten human eyes to understand the divine necessity of evil's root existence,
יוּכְלוּ לִדְבֹּק בָּרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
people might cleave to evil, Heaven forbid,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל [וּסְדוֹם]
just as occurred in the Generation of the Flood and Sodom,

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:)1008 Sanhedrin 108b — "And it came to pass after the seven days that the waters of the flood were upon the earth" (Genesis 7:10) — what was the nature of those seven days? ... Another explanation: during those seven days He gave them a taste of the World to Come, so that they would know what goodness they had forfeited. Maharsha: "He gave them a taste of the World to Come": other transgressors, such as the people of Sodom, have no portion in the World to Come, yet they stand in judgment so that they may see the excellence of the World to Come and grieve over it, as it is written, "They shall see and be ashamed"; but these, who do not stand in judgment at all (as said above, "neither judgment nor spirit"), would never see its excellence and grieve over it — therefore He gave them a taste of the World to Come in this world, during the seven days, so that in the year they floated upon the waters they would grieve over what they had lost thereby. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 108b): Because they were lost from the World to Come, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them the World to Come in this world; and since the World to Come is the final end, these seven days, which came at the very end, were a taste of the World to Come — seven, because it was given them within this world, which was created in seven days. This befell the generation of the flood in particular because they were blotted out from the earth entirely, as it is written, "I will blot out man," unlike other punishments the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon sinners; once they had received the World to Come in this world, nothing at all remained to them, and so they were fit to be blotted out completely.
about whom our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 108b):
שֶׁהִטְעִימָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them a taste resembling the World to Come.

וְכַיָּדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג רטז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)1009 Zohar 3:216b — And further the Rabbis established: the generation that goes is the generation that comes — a lame man went, a lame man came; a blind man went, a blind man came. And further the Rabbis established that Moses was destined to receive the Torah in the generation of the Flood, but [it was not given] because they were wicked. This is what is written, “for that he also is flesh” — “beshagam” is Moses [by numerical value]. And why is he called “beshagam”? Because Ecclesiastes dropped the letter bet from “beshagam” in order to conceal the matter, saying, “I said that this too is vanity.” Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): The generations of the Flood and of the Dispersion are the general categories of the "secrets of illicit relations," for they correspond to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah: in the generation of the Flood it was fitting for the Torah to be given, as the Zohar says and as the Sages said on the verse, "beshagam" — this is Moses. And correspondingly their sin was the emission of seed, in the Yesod, as is known from the Zohar that writing belongs to the Yesod. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Noach 1): The ten generations from Adam to Noah were meant to repair all the damage of Adam's sin and to be refined in all the attributes, and then, in the generation of the Flood, it was fitting for the Torah to be given; the soul of Moses was present then, as hinted in "beshagam," which equals Moses in numerical value. They would have merited the Written and the Oral Torah, hinted in "all the fountains of the great deep burst forth" [the springs of wisdom below] "and the windows of heaven were opened" [the gates of wisdom above], and would have repaired all the damage of the serpent, as will be in the future; but because they provoked Him, these turned into raging waters and they were all swept away in the waters of the Flood.
And as is known from what is written in the Zohar (Part III, 216b):
דְּאָז הָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
that it was originally fitting for the Giving of the Torah to happen then,
וּ"בְשַׁגַּם" זֶה מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן אָז כַּנּוֹדָע,
and "for that he also" Hebrew: b'shagam, numerically equivalent to 345 refers to Moses, who was already present in potential then, as is known;
רַק שֶׁהָיוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַלְכִין קַדְמָאִין דְּמִיתוּ
except that they fell according to the mystical pattern of the "Primordial Kings who died" the realm of Tohu,
שֶׁרָצוּ לְהַשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי כֹּחָן.
because they sought to grasp more than their capacity could sustain.

וּבְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ מוֹלִיכִין (מַכּוֹת י:)1010 Makkot 10b — Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav Huna said, and some say that Rav Huna said that R. Elazar said: From the Torah, from the Prophets, and from the Writings we learn that along the path a man wishes to go, they lead him. From the Torah, as it is written, "You shall not go with them," and it is written, "Arise, go with them." From the Prophets, as it is written, "I am the Lord your God, who teaches you for your profit, who leads you by the way that you should go." From the Writings, as it is written, "If it concerns the scoffers, He will make them scoff, but to the humble He gives grace." Rashi: "By the way that you should go" — by the way you choose to go. "If it concerns the scoffers" — if a man comes to attach himself to them; "He will make them scoff" — they do not hold him back. Maharsha: It does not say that the Holy One, blessed be He, leads him, but "they lead him" — for, as we have written in many places, every thought, word and deed of a man creates an angel answering to it, whether for good or for ill. Hence "along the path a man wishes to go": the choice is given him by Him, blessed be He, since all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven; but according to his own will and mind he is led by those angels that are created out of that will and thought of his. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Makkos 10b): This is an exalted matter, for everything goes according to the man who receives, as has been explained in many places. Therefore he said, "along the path a man wishes to go, they lead him": since a man desires a thing, his will is done for him, whether for good or for evil, and nothing is done to him against his will — as here, where he wishes to go even though it is to his own harm, and they do not restrain him. And although the matter appears simple, it is a deep one. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 64): At times a person sees clearly that the Blessed One assists him and agrees with his deeds, and yet this is no proof that his deeds are truly upright; of this it is said, "who leads you in the way you would go," and the Sages expounded (Makkos 10b), "Along the path a man wishes to go, they lead him." So with Elijah: though the withholding of the rains was hard before the Blessed One, He nevertheless told him, "Go and hide," and helped him hide from Ahab by a miracle.,
And "along the path a person wishes to go, he is led" (Makkot 10b);
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה לָהֶם הֶאָרוֹת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
so Hashem, blessed be He, showed them illuminations of the World to Come
לְהַשִּׂיג שֹׁרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
to grasp the root purpose of this world's existence.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁהֵבִינוּ אֵיךְ שֹׁרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת הָרַע גַּם כֵּן מֵאֲמִתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
And because they understood how the root reality of evil also stems from His divine truth,
דְּ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ",
since "there is none else besides Him,"
הָלְכוּ בִּשְׁרִירוּת לִבָּם וְאַחַר תַּאֲוָתָם,
they followed the stubbornness of their hearts and pursued their lusts,
בְּחָשְׁבָם דְּעִם כָּל זֶה אֵין נִתּוּקִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
thinking that despite all this, they were not severed from Hashem, blessed be He,
דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because everything ultimately derives from Hashem, blessed be He.

וְכֵן בִּלְעָם נִקְרָא מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת דְּבָרִים)1011 Devarim Rabbah 1:2 — Another matter: "These are the words" — this is what Scripture says: "One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one with a smooth tongue" (Proverbs 28:23). R. Pinchas said in the name of R. Chama bar Chanina: "One who rebukes" — this is Moses; "a man" — this is Israel, as it is stated, "And you, My flock, the flock of My pasture, are man" (Ezekiel 34:31). "Will find favor" — this is Moses, as it is written, "You have also found favor in My eyes" (Exodus 33:12). "Than one with a smooth tongue" — this is Balaam, who was smooth in his prophecies, so that their hearts grew haughty and they fell at Shittim.
Similarly, Balaam is called a "smoother of the tongue" / flatterer (Midrash Rabbah, Devarim 1:2),
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהוּא חַד עִם עֲמָלֵק,
as it is known that he is rooted in the same singular source as Amalek;
רַק שֶׁהוּא מִנְּבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
except that he was among the prophets of the nations of the world
וְיָדַע שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרַע,
and understood the root of evil,
וְהִשִּׂיג דְּהָעִקָּר הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם הַמְּהַפְּכִים כָּל רַע לְטוֹב.
and grasped that the essential core is Israel, who transform all evil into good.
רַק הֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם זֶה
Yet he used smooth, seductive speech toward Israel to expose this insight to them:
דְּגַם הָרַע דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַכֹּל מֵאֲמִתַּת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that even the evil among Israel is entirely rooted in His true will;
וְעַל כֵּן "לֹא הִבִּיט אָוֶן בְּיַעֲקֹב" וְגוֹמֵר,
and therefore he proclaimed, "He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob..." (Numbers 23:21),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חָטְאוּ בַּשִּׁטִּים.
and through this enticement, they fell into sin at Shittim.
וְהֵם לֹא טָעֲמוּ רַק מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְשֶׁמֶץ דָּבָר מֵהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ,
Yet they merely tasted a semblance of the World to Come and an infinitesimal whisper of this apprehension,
כִּי עִקָּרוֹ "עַיִן לֹא רָאֲתָה",
for its essence remains "eye has not seen" (Isaiah 64:3),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה זוֹ הַהַשָּׂגָה כְּלָל.
and it is entirely impossible to fully comprehend this revelation in this world.
וְעַל כֵּן הַמִּלְחָמָה נֶגֶד עֲמָלֵק לֹא הָיָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Therefore, the war against Amalek was not waged directly through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַחֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה,
even though he is the fountainhead of all the wise of Israel and the root of the Torah,
שֶׁמִּצִּדָּהּ נִצּוּחַ כָּל אֻמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן חוּץ מֵעֲמָלֵק,
through whose power all foreign nations and tongues are conquered—except for Amalek,
שֶׁהַשַּׁעַר שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
because the divine gate within the Torah corresponding to Amalek is hidden in this world.
וְהֻצְרַךְ לִשְׁלֹחַ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מְשָׁרְתוֹ שֶׁנִּקְרָא "נֹצֵר תְּאֵנָה",
Instead, he had to dispatch Joshua his attendant, who is allegorized as "he who guards the fig tree" (Proverbs 27:18),

שֶׁהָיָה מְסַדֵּר הַסַּפְסָלִים (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פִּינְחָס)1012 Bamidbar Rabbah 21:14 — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "The keeper of a fig tree shall eat its fruit" (Proverbs 27:18) — your sons sat idle and did not occupy themselves with Torah, while Joshua served you much and paid you much honor. He would come early and stay late in your house of assembly; he would arrange the benches and spread out the mats. Since he served you with all his strength, he is worthy to serve Israel, for he shall not lose his reward. "Take you Joshua son of Nun" (Numbers 27:18) — to fulfill what is said, "The keeper of a fig tree shall eat its fruit." וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
who would arrange the benches in the study hall (Midrash Rabbah, Pinchas 21:14) and serve the Torah through practical devotion.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)1013 Berakhot 7b — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: The service of Torah is greater than its study, as it is stated: "Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water upon the hands of Elijah" (II Kings 3:11). It does not say "who learned," but "who poured" — this teaches that its service is greater than its study. Maharsha: There are many laws a man learns from his teacher that are not rulings for practice, as is said in several places; hence the service is the greater, for in serving his teacher he sees the law carried out in practice. Maharal (Derech Chaim 6:6): One who attends upon a Torah scholar is joined to his master through that service, and through it he receives from him. There is no doubt that when the wick is brought near the lamp, the lamp kindles it; so too, when the disciple draws near his master by serving him, the master pours out the Torah upon him. Learning from a master is not such a joining; it is the serving that is a drawing near to the scholar himself, and it is thereby that he receives from him.
And our Sages of blessed memory declared (Berakhot 7b):
"גְּדוֹלָה שִׁמּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מִלִּמּוּדָהּ".
"Service of Torah is greater than its theoretical study."
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּהַלִּמּוּד הֲרֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ גְּבוּל עַד כַּמָּה הוּא מַשִּׂיג,
And I heard that intellectual study has a defined limit to what it can grasp,
אֲבָל הַשִּׁמּוּשׁ הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ,
whereas personal service stems from the deep yearning and boundless love harbored by the attendant,
שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ הוּא מְשַׁמֵּשׁ וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהָקִים דֶּגֶל הַתּוֹרָה – זֶה אֵין לוֹ גְּבוּל.
by virtue of which he attends and strives to uphold the banner of Torah—and this knows no boundary.
כִּי הוּא אֵינוֹ מַשִּׂיג עַצְמוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה לַחֲכָמִים,
For while he may not intellectually perceive the inner essence of Torah revealed to the wise scholars,
רַק חוֹמֵד וְכוֹסֵף לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
he passionately yearns and longs for the words of Torah,
הַיְינוּ לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ.
which touches the primordial transcendent root of the entire Torah.
וּלְכָךְ מִצַּד הַשִּׁמּוּשׁ יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלָלוֹ כֹּחַ שֶׁל שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם,
Therefore, through this selfless service, one taps into the power of the hidden Fiftieth Gate,
וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא נִצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק.
and from that sublime vantage point comes the vanquishing of Amalek.

וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק יג)1014 Pesikta Rabbati 13:1 — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: Do your part — "You shall blot out the memory of Amalek" (Deuteronomy 25:19) — and I will do Mine: "I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek" (Exodus 17:14). He did not do so. Rather, once Saul became king, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: The seed of Amalek falls only by the hand of the son of Rachel. So too you find at Rephidim, that he fell by the hand of Joshua, as it is stated, "Joshua weakened Amalek" (Exodus 17:13). The Holy One, blessed be He, said: This tribe is forever appointed to exact payment from Amalek. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Therefore Amalek falls only by the hand of the seed of Rachel, for they are the clarification and distinction between the woman of valor and the woman of harlotry: the whole matter of Amalek is to make the woman of harlotry resemble the woman of valor, but from the side of Rachel's seed there is no connection between them at all, for she is the root of the woman of valor. They correspond to the attribute of "the righteous one, foundation of the world," and there, in the holy covenant, lies the distinction between Israel and the nations — these circumcised and those uncircumcised in their very root — so that the nations cannot attach themselves to them or resemble them at all. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 13): [Bar Kokhba] reasoned that those who prevail [over Amalek] must be their very opposites, which is why they said (Bava Basra 123b; Bereishis Rabbah 73), "Amalek falls only by the hand of the seed of Rachel": of Amalek it is written, "and he did not fear God," while Joseph said, "I fear God" — he is his opposite, and therefore can overcome him. Sod Yesharim (Parashas Zachor 14): All the deeds and labors required of a person serve to break through the concealment of Amalek, which covers the Face, for "Amalek falls only by the hand of the seed of Rachel," as stated in the Gemara — that is, his whole downfall is possible only through strenuous labors; but when the memory of Amalek is blotted out of the world, the Face will be revealed and the forehead will appear.
This is also why the Rabbis taught (Pesikta Rabbati 13:1):
"אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל".
"Amalek falls only by the hand of the descendants of Rachel."
הַיְינוּ דְּלֵאָה הִיא הַמּוֹלִידָה שְׁבָטִים בְּפֹעַל,
The explanation is that Leah gave birth to the tribes in active manifestation,
וְרָחֵל כָּל יָמֶיהָ חָמְדָה וְכָסְפָה לְהוֹלָדַת שְׁבָטִים,
whereas Rachel spent her life desiring and yearning for the birth of tribes,
וּבְפֹעַל לֹא הוֹלִידָה אֶלָּא שְׁנַיִם;
yet in actuality gave birth to only two;
אֲבָל הַחִימּוּד וְהַכִּיסּוּף הוּא גָּדוֹל מֵהַהִתְגַּלּוּת לַפֹּעַל,
nevertheless, the intensity of yearning and holy longing surpasses outer tangible manifestation,
וְעַל כֵּן הִיא נִקְרֵאת "עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת".
which is why she is called the bedrock and foundation of the house (akeret habayit).

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא)1015 Bereshit Rabbah 71:5 — Leah seized the distaff of thanksgiving, and there arose from her masters of thanksgiving: Judah — "Judah acknowledged and said, She is more righteous than I"; David said, "Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good"; Daniel said, "To You, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise." Rachel seized the distaff of silence, and all her children arose masters of secrets: Benjamin — "jasper" (yashpeh), read as yesh peh, "there is a mouth": he knew of the sale of Joseph and did not tell. Saul — "but of the matter of the kingdom he did not tell him." Esther — "Esther had not told her kindred nor her people."
Concerning this, our Rabbis of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah 71:5):
דְּאָחֲזָה פֶּלֶךְ הַשְּׁתִיקָה,
that she grasped the craft of silence;
רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּהַהִתְגַּלּוּת לַפֹּעַל הוּא גָּלוּי לַכֹּל,
meaning that outward manifestation is revealed to all,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַכִּיסּוּפִין שֶׁעִקָּרָם בַּלֵּב אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי,
whereas deep yearnings centered within the secret heart are unrevealed,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא שְׁתִיקָה,
and this profound inwardness is termed "silence,"
וְכֵן כָּל זַרְעָהּ אַחֲרֶיהָ.
and so it is with all her descendants after her.
וְעַל כֵּן נְפִילַת עֲמָלֵק בְּיָדָם,
Therefore, Amalek's downfall occurs specifically through their hands,
שֶׁהֵם מִצַּד הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַחֵשֶׁק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
for through their inward passion and unquenchable desire for words of Torah,
יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחִיזָה גַּם בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
they hold a firm grasp within the concealed, transcendent root of the Torah
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלָּה לַפֹּעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
that has not yet been outwardly disclosed in this world.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Haman, Sleep, and the Fiftieth Gate
Haman attacks Israel at the root of concealed good, yet the deepest gate of Jewish attachment can never be severed.

p: וּבִימֵי הָמָן
In the days of Haman,
שֶׁאָז הָיָה תַּכְלִית תִּגְבֹּרֶת כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק בָּעוֹלָם,
when the power of Amalek reached its ultimate strength in the world,
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
for this reason the Sages, of blessed memory, taught

בְּמַסֶּכֶת חוּלִין (קל״ט1016 Chullin 139b — They asked Rav Mattana: Where is Haman [alluded to] in the Torah? "Have you eaten of [hamin] the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?" (Genesis 3:11). Rashi: "From where" — for the affair of Haman. "Of [hamin] the tree" — that he would be hanged upon the tree. Maharsha: Each of these four — Moses, Haman, Esther and Mordecai — is known by a further name as well, and one might have argued that the familiar name is not the one rooted in the Torah, since Moses was so named by Pharaoh's daughter in the Egyptian tongue, while Haman, Mordecai and Esther appear to be Persian names; the Gemara therefore asks in each case from where in the Torah that particular name comes. For Haman it answers "Of the tree," from the episode of the serpent, because he was a viper's brood out of Esau and Amalek, whose power is the power of the primeval serpent; and the Midrash says that Haman and the serpent both opened with "af," and that both set their eyes upon what was not fitting for them. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Chullin 139b): This too is an exceedingly profound matter. For Haman was of the seed of Amalek, whose power is that of Samael the wicked, who rode upon the serpent and enticed the woman to eat of the tree of knowledge and brought death into the world; and just so did Haman seek to bring annihilation and death upon Israel, who in particular are called "man." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Therefore they said in Chullin, "Where is Haman indicated in the Torah? 'Have you eaten of [hamin] the tree'" — this was the first accusation of the attribute of judgment, over the first sin in the world, for the questioning and the accusation began with the word hamin. And this is the root of Haman "from the Torah": there is nothing without a root in holiness, for otherwise it would have no existence in the world, and since all the worlds were created through the Torah, the blueprint of all the works of creation, everything must have its root in the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): The root of Haman, which the Sages said in Chullin is alluded to in the verse "Have you eaten of [hamin] the tree": the word hamin expresses a question, and this opened the way to the error that the Blessed One needs to ask — and the Blessed One willed it so, that whoever wishes to err may come and err. From this extends the root of Haman, the root of the error of thinking that the Blessed One has withdrawn His knowledge from the lower worlds, the root and beginning of sinking into imaginings and separation from the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman did not believe there could be any holiness in bodily enjoyments such as eating and drinking, and this grew from the root of the serpent who enticed Adam in this. There is a hint of it in the Gemara, "Where is Haman indicated in the Torah? 'Have you eaten of [hamin] the tree,'" for there it is written, "of which I commanded you not to eat, have you eaten" — and this is the root of the kelipah of Haman: to be immersed in the lust of eating for bodily pleasure, as the serpent enticed. עַמּוּד ב׳):
in Tractate Chullin (139b):
״הָמָן מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן?״
“Where is Haman indicated in the Torah?”
״הֲמִן הָעֵץ״ וְגוֹמֵר,
From: “Have you eaten from the tree...?”
דַּאֲחִיזָתוֹ בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
for his hold reaches into the root of the primordial sin of Adam,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע בָּעוֹלָם.
from which all branches of the root of evil proliferated throughout the world.
כִּי טַעֲנָתוֹ ״יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד״,
For his accusation, “There is a certain people (yeshno),”

שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״ג1017 Megillah 13b — "There is one people scattered abroad and dispersed" (Esther 3:8). Rava said: There was none who knew how to slander like Haman. He said to him: Come, let us destroy them. He said to him: I fear their God, lest He do to me as He did to those before me. He said to him: "There is" [yeshno] — they have slumbered [yashnu] away from the commandments. He said to him: But there are sages among them. He said to him: They are "one people" [all alike]. Rashi (s.v. “There are Sages among them”): From Haman’s reply we learn that this is how Ahasuerus had answered him. Maharsha: The verse is superfluous, and its expressions are doubled — it need only have written “there is” [yesh] and not “yeshno” — and therefore they expounded that Haman told him they had slumbered away from the commandments: either from the word “change,” that they alter their commandments, or from the word “sleep,” that they sleep away from them. And from the superfluous word “one” they expounded Ahasuerus’s objection, “There are Sages among them” who will shield them by their good deeds — to which Haman answered, “They are one people”: just as the rest of the people do not keep the commandments, so too the Sages among them do not keep them. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:8): As for their expounding "there is" [yeshno] as "they have slumbered from the commandments," it seems that the exposition does not rest chiefly on the word yeshno being a form of "sleep"; rather, the expression "there is a people" itself implies it — that they are nothing but a people, whereas the commandments do not derive from their being a "people" but from the name "Israel," for all the other nations, which are peoples, have no commandments. So he said that these too are merely "a people," like every other people that is called only "a people," since they do not perform the divine commandments. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): Haman — of whom the Sages said that none knew how to slander like him — aimed his accusation against Israel above: he said, "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and of the Rabbis, "They too are one people," that is, he accused Israel's own sanctity, which comes through Torah and mitzvos, saying that all of them, even the Torah scholars, had slumbered from Torah and mitzvos. And against the sanctity that comes from the Blessed One he said that He of whom it is said "the Lord is One" has fallen asleep away from His people. Sod Yesharim (Purim 25): "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and in the Midrash, "[Haman] said: their God is asleep" — as the Arizal wrote, this is like the deep sleep at the beginning of Creation: when a person nullifies himself entirely and surrenders all his selfhood to the Blessed One, He returns to him a sprouting of salvation all the more, and every salvation must be preceded by such nullification. The destruction and exile were such a self-nullification, in which Israel surrendered to the Blessed One all the might they had drawn from the mitzvos dependent on the Land, until they appeared to be sleeping from the mitzvos, and from this the Second Temple sprouted. At that very time, when they appeared to be asleep, Haman said "their God is asleep, they have slumbered from the mitzvos," seeking to accuse Israel, and the Blessed One showed him, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps." עַמּוּד ב׳):
which the Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 13b) as:
״יְשֵׁנִים מִן הַמִּצְוֹת״,
“they are asleep (yeshenim) from the commandments,”
וְכֵן אָמַר: ״אֱלֹהֵיהֶם יָשֵׁן הוּא״
and likewise he claimed: “their God is asleep”

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק זֶה)1018 Esther Rabbah 7:12 — "Haman said to King Ahasuerus: There is [yeshno] one people" (Esther 3:8) — the One of whom it is said "the Lord is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4) is asleep [yashen] to His people. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: There is no sleep before Me, as it is written, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps" (Psalms 121:4); and you say that there is sleep before Me? By your life, out of sleep I will rouse Myself against that man and destroy him from the world, as it is written, "Then the Lord awoke as one asleep… He drove His foes back" (Psalms 78:65–66). Sod Yesharim (Purim 25): On the Gemara's "they are asleep from the commandments" and the Midrash's "[Haman] said, their God is asleep," the holy Arizal wrote that this was also the matter at the beginning of creation, "And the Lord God cast a deep sleep." When a person nullifies himself completely and hands all the power of his own being over to the Blessed One, the Blessed One returns to him a sprouting of salvation all the more, and before every sprouting of salvation there must first be such a nullification. So the destruction and exile were a nullification in which Israel handed back to the Blessed One all the might they had from performing the commandments, until they seemed asleep from the commandments, and this is the deep sleep.,
(as they taught in Midrash Rabbah on this verse),
לֹא הָיָה שֶׁקֶר
was not an outright falsehood
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בְּסוֹף הַמַּאֲמָר).
(as will be explained further at the conclusion of this discourse).

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית כ״ג1019 Taanit 23a — R. Yochanan said: All the days of that righteous man he was troubled by this verse: "A song of ascents. When the Lord brought back the return of Zion, we were like dreamers." He said: Is there anyone who sleeps seventy years in a dream? ... He sat down and was eating bread when sleep came upon him. A rock formation enclosed him, he was hidden from sight, and he slept seventy years. Rashi: "That righteous man": Choni the Circle-Drawer was troubled by this verse. "We were like dreamers": the Babylonian exile, which lasted seventy years, seemed like a dream; and "seventy years in a dream" is said in wonder: is there anyone who sleeps seventy years in his dream, a person who sleeps seventy years in a single sleep? "A rock formation enclosed him": a crag of rock rose up around him; "and he was hidden from sight": and people did not find him there. Maharsha: He asked "Is there anyone who sleeps seventy years?" because there is no dream without sleep; and although "dreamers" is plural, it implies [dreaming] without a break, so it must be a single sleep. The verse likens the years of the exile to no more than a dream, just as a man's seventy years are likened to dreaming ("He shall fly away like a dream," Job 20:8), and this is what pained him: that a man's world should be reckoned only as a dream that has no substance. Through his own sleep of seventy years they showed him that the plain sense of "we were like dreamers" is indeed possible. עַמּוּד א׳)
Just as the Sages remarked (Taanit 23a)
בְּחוֹנִי הַמְּעַגֵּל:
regarding Choni the Circle-Maker:
״מִי אִיכָּא דְּנָאֵים שִׁבְעִין שְׁנִין?״
“Is there anyone who sleeps for seventy years?”
דְּכָל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל
for the entire seventy years of the Babylonian exile
הָיָה כְּמוֹ שֵׁנָה,
resembled a state of sleep,
כִּי לֹא חָטְאוּ כְּלַל.
because they did not actively sin at all.

וְשֵׁינָה לָרְשָׁעִים — הֲנָאָה לָהֶם (מַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין ע״א1020 Sanhedrin 71b — Wine and sleep for the wicked are a benefit to them and a benefit to the world; and for the righteous they are an evil to them and an evil to the world. Rashi: As long as they are drinking and sleeping they do not sin and do no harm to people. For the righteous it is an evil to them, for [then] they are not occupied with Torah; and an evil to the world, for the Torah with which they occupy themselves protects the generation, and when they are idle from it, punishment comes to the world. Maharsha: From the pleasure of the wine on which he becomes drunk he comes to the pleasure of sleep in the morning until the fourth hour, as is said of the gentile kings. So it is with the rebellious son: wine and sleep are a benefit to him and a benefit to the world, for as long as he has the means to buy wine and is asleep he does not rob people, until he has used up his property. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): "Wine and sleep for the wicked are a benefit to them, etc., but for the righteous an evil, etc." — for wine "was created only to comfort mourners and to give reward to the wicked," who through it are sunk in lust as they please, which is their whole desire and their benefit; and it is also a benefit to the world that they are sunk in lust and do no harm to others. For the righteous, however, it is the beginning of a fall: even when wine causes no outright evil, it brings on sleep and a slackening of the hands from the service of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 238): Sleep too is good for re-awakening after the mind has fallen into a confusion of alien thoughts: in sleep the mind departs and afterwards a new soul returns, so that one can strengthen himself anew and forget all that was the day before. This is the reason for "sleep for the wicked, etc." and the reverse for the righteous: the mind and holy thoughts they held all day depart, and the next day they need a fresh strengthening and a new beginning, and all beginnings are hard, whereas within the day the thought remains bound and continues. With the wicked it is the reverse: their scheming thought continues all day, so that it can hardly cleave to words of Torah except with great difficulty, so strongly is it bound to the alien things he thinks of. עַמּוּד ב׳),
And “Sleep for the wicked is beneficial to them” (Sanhedrin 71b),
דְּבְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
for among the nations of the world
טוֹב כְּשֶׁיְּשֵׁנִים וּבְטֵלִים מִפְּעֻלָּה,
it is advantageous when they sleep and remain passive,
שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רַע,
for during that time they do not commit evil,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
as the Sages of blessed memory noted

(תַּלְמוּד יְרוּשַׁלְמִי, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, פֶּרֶק א׳, הֲלָכָה ג׳, לְגִרְסַת קָרְבַּן הָעֵדָה, וּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה נ1021 Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:3; Bereshit Rabbah 50:3 — R. Levi said: The Holy One, blessed be He, judges the nations of the world only at night, at the hour when they are asleep [and idle from transgressions], and He judges Israel only by day, at the hour when they are occupied with the commandments. That is what is written: "And He will judge the world in righteousness; He will render judgment to the peoples with equity" (Psalms 9:9). Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 25): [Citing the Midrash that Israel are not judged together with the nations, but Israel by day and the nations by night:] This too shows how they are set apart: Israel is judged by day because they are true existence, and existence is likened to day, in which everything is found. The nations, who lack true existence, are judged at night, in keeping with their level, for at night nothing is found.׳):
(Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh Hashanah 1:3 according to the Korban HaEdah, and Bereishit Rabbah 50):
לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דָּן כְּשֶׁיְּשֵׁנִים וְכוּלֵי.
the nations of the world He judges while they sleep...
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בַּצַּדִּיקִים,
This is not so with the righteous;
הַשֵּׁינָה רַע,
sleep is considered a detriment for them,
דִּצְרִיכִים לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעֻלַּת טוֹב,
because they are required to engage in active striving and deeds of goodness,
וְלֹא לִהְיוֹת יוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל,
and not to sit inactive,
דִּכְיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי.
which is comparable to sleep.
וְכָל חֵטְא דְּעֹנֶשׁ הָמָן
And the entire sin that gave pretext to Haman's punitive decree—
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַצֶּלֶם
whether for bowing to the image of Nebuchadnezzar
אוֹ נֶהֱנוּ מִסְּעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע —
or deriving pleasure from the feast of that wicked man—
הַכֹּל לֹא הָיָה אִסּוּר,
none of it constituted a formal Torah prohibition,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מַה שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (מַסֶּכֶת כְּתוּבּוֹת ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳
as is known from what Tosafot wrote (Ketubot 33b

וְשָׁם)1022 Tosafot on Ketubot 33b — "Had they flogged Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, they would have worshipped the image" — this is difficult: from where do we know it? … Rabbeinu Tam explained that that image was not actual idolatry, but was made in honor of the king; even so there was a sanctification of the Name in it, and therefore they gave themselves over to death. That is what is written, "We do not serve your god, and we do not bow to the golden image that you have set up" (Daniel 3:18) — implying that the image did not have the standing of a deity.
and elsewhere)
גַּבֵּי ״אִלְמָלֵא נַגְדּוּהוּ״ וְכוּלֵי,
regarding “Had they tortured Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah...”,
דְּהָיָה אַנְדַּרְטָא,
explaining that it was merely an imperial statue and not true idolatry,
וְלֹא הֻצְרְכוּ לִמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ.
and strictly speaking they were not required to surrender their lives.
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בַּסְּעוּדָה,
All the more so regarding the feast,
שֶׁהֻכְרְחוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ.
where they were coerced to fulfill the royal decree.
אַךְ אַף דְּהוּא בְּהֶתֵּר,
Yet although their action was technically permitted,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא כְּמוֹ שֵׁנָה
nevertheless it was like a state of sleep
וְהֶעְדֵּר פְּעֻלָּה לְקַדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
and a failure of initiative to sanctify the Name of Heaven
עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
at the very least;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה לִיחֶזְקֵאל:
just as Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah declared to Ezekiel:

דְּבָעֵינַן שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ: ״כָּל עַמְמִין סָגְדִין חוּץ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל1023 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:8 — Nevuchadnezzar set up an image and singled out three from every nation, and three from Israel — and these were Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah. The three from Israel stood firm and gave their lives and did not serve idols. They went to Yechezkel and said to him: Shall we bow to it or not? He said to them: I have received from Yeshayahu my teacher — “Hide yourself for a brief moment until the wrath passes.” They said to him: What do people say — that this image, every nation bows to it? He said to them: And what do you say? They said to him: We wish to give it a blemish, so that they should not be able to say that this image, every nation bowed to it except Israel. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 14): Even with Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah we find that Yechezkel told them, "I have received from Yeshayahu my teacher: 'Hide yourself for a brief moment,'" and they wished to sanctify the Name of Heaven, not to go out to war. As for the Hasmoneans who went out to war, there is certainly no place for such a war by a handful of men; it was only because this level appeared in them then, that they knew everything comes by miracle.״
“We desire that onlookers say: All peoples bow down except Israel”
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ז׳, ח׳).
(as recorded in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:8).
וְאָז נִתְגַּדֵּל הָמָן,
And at that moment Haman grew in prominence,
שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
for he personifies “the first of nations”,
שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת הָרָע
inasmuch as the root existence of evil
הוּא בִּטּוּל הַטּוֹב
manifests through the suppression and dormancy of the good,
לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ שֵׁנָה.
causing it to sink into a state resembling sleep.
וְהוּא חָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת
And he devised schemes
לְהַאֲבִיד לְגַמְרֵי, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
to eradicate Israel completely, Heaven forbid,
וְהִתְחַכֵּם לִקְנוֹתָם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ.
and cunningly planned to acquire them with his wealth.

וְאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (פְּתִיחָה דְּאֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה)1024 Esther Rabbah, Petichta 10 — R. Berechiah opened: "Who has wrought and done it, calling the generations from the beginning?" (Isaiah 41:4). From the beginning of the creation of the world the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed for each one what befits him: Adam, first of the created; Cain, first of the killers; Abel, first of the slain; Noah, first of the survivors; Abraham, first of the circumcised; Isaac, first of the bound; Jacob, first of the wholehearted; Judah, first of the tribes; Joseph, first of the pious; Aaron, first of the priests; Moses, first of the prophets; Joshua, first of the conquerors; Othniel, first of those who apportioned; Samuel, of those who anoint; Saul, of the anointed; David, first of the singers; Solomon, first of the builders; Nebuchadnezzar, first of the destroyers; Ahasuerus, first of the sellers; Haman, first of the buyers. And when all saw that it was so, they began to cry "Woe [vai]!" — "And it was [vayhi] in the days of Ahasuerus.":
The Sages taught in the Midrash (Esther Rabbah, Petichta):
״אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ — רֹאשׁ לַמּוֹכְרִים,
“Ahasuerus was foremost among sellers,
וְהָמָן — רֹאשׁ לַקּוֹנִים״.
and Haman was foremost among buyers.”
וְלֹא רָצָה לִפְעֹל
Haman did not seek merely
שֶׁאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּעַצְמוֹ יִגְזֹר עֲלֵיהֶם כֵּן.
to have Ahasuerus himself directly decree their execution.
הָעִנְיָן, כִּי יָדוּעַ
The rationale is that it is known
דְּמַה שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ כּוֹבֵשׁ בַּמִּלְחָמָה — הִיא שֶׁלּוֹ,
that whatever a monarch conquers through war becomes his absolute possession;
וּבְמַסֶּכֶת גִּטִּין (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
and in Tractate Gittin (38a) we learn
דַּאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי — יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹנֶה.
that a gentile can legally acquire a Jew as a slave.
וְנוֹדַע כִּי הָעֶבֶד —
And it is established that regarding a slave,
כֹּחַ הָאָדוֹן עָלָיו,
the sovereignty of the master completely governs him,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כֹּחַ אַחֵר.
such that he possesses no independent legal self-determination.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם,
And this was the nature of the Egyptian exile,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא: ״גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי״,
termed “a nation extracted from the midst of another nation”,
כְּאִלּוּ מֻבְלָעִים בְּתוֹכָם,
as though fully swallowed within them,

וּכְעֻבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב, מִזְמוֹר ק״ז)1025 Midrash Tehillim 107:4 — "From the lands He gathered them." Just as a bird lies in the hand of the fowler — if he wishes he kills it, and if he wishes he keeps it alive — so were Israel sunk in the hand of the Egyptians. R. Abbahu son of R. Acha said in the name of our master: Israel lay within Egypt like a fetus lying within the womb of an animal; and just as the shepherd puts his hand into her womb and draws it out, so did the Holy One, blessed be He, do, as it is said, "to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation" (Deuteronomy 4:34). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Egypt, to whom Israel were slaves in complete servitude (and what a slave acquires, his master acquires), had all the holiness of Israel swallowed up within it, as the Sages said on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation" that they were like a fetus in its mother's womb; and a fetus is reckoned as its mother's thigh, so great was the power of Egypt's connection to the holiness of Israel. Therefore the Torah did not write the prohibition of the Egyptian and the Edomite, only the permission of the third generation, and in the words "you shall not abhor." Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 14): The Exodus is called a birth in Ezekiel, "and as for your birth, on the day you were born," and so it is said of "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb. And the Sages said that the song of Egypt is in the feminine, unlike that of the future, when there will be the birth of a male, for then they will be redeemed through repentance; whereas the Exodus was the birth of a female, which has nothing of its own. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Because some root of Israel was hidden in Haman, his downfall came in Nisan, on Pesach, the time prepared for Israel's going out from the straits of the husks, when the root of Jewishness goes out from every place in which it is sunk. For on Pesach, as it were, He took out "a nation from the midst of a nation," which the Sages expounded "like a fetus in its mother's womb" — that even purity that has been swallowed up is expelled and comes out; and then Mordechai was given the house of Haman and absorbed all the good, and the evil perished of itself. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 3): Remembering the Exodus is a segulah for being remembered with children, for by recalling that miracle one arouses the power of remembrance and brings about the remembrance of the barren as well; for the Exodus too was in the mystery of birth, as the Sages said on "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus slipping out of its mother's womb, and as is known from the Arizal that the Egyptian exile was in the mystery of gestation. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): The seed of Jacob, the root of truth in the world, was swallowed up within [Egypt], as it is said on "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb: that filth so surrounded them that they had no revealed existence of their own. And "he swallowed wealth and shall vomit it up" at the Exodus, when they were chosen as a unique people through the removal of the darkness of Egypt's filth that surrounded them. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, from the Tanchuma 15): On the side of nature it is said "for My name is within him [bekirbo]," "within" meaning hidden and not perceptible to the eye, as the Sages said on "a nation from the midst [mikerev] of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb: it is hidden, yet the fetus is nonetheless recognized, for through understanding one knows there is a fetus in her womb, though it is not actually visible to the eye. This is from the side of wisdom, whereas prophecy is the complete seeing of the name of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): As long as Israel were still in the Egyptian exile (and the Sages said on "a nation from the midst of a nation" that they were truly within them, wholly surrounded by them, like a fetus, which is its mother's thigh and has no life of its own), [Moses] had to be in Midian. Only after they left Egypt and were chosen as a distinct people was this clarified; but while they were in Egypt like a fetus in its mother's womb, the name "seed of Abraham" still applied to all who were of his seed. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Va'eschanan): "Or has God ventured to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation": Israel are so beloved before the Blessed One that even when they do deeds like those of the idolaters, the deeds of Israel are nonetheless good — just as Moses our teacher would not accept the mirrors of the women until the Blessed One answered him that in Israel there is great holiness in this. This is what is called "a nation from the midst of a nation," that the deeds of Israel are good, as the Midrash says: Israel were placed within Egypt like a fetus placed within the womb of an animal, and just as the shepherd puts his hand into her womb and draws it out, so did the Holy One, blessed be He. Sod Yesharim (Parashas Zachor 11): In Egypt Israel were in the aspect of a fetus, as the Midrash says, "like a fetus placed within the womb of an animal ... so did the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, 'to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation'": that is, the Blessed One so surrounded them in Egypt that they were raised above the bounds of this world and returned there to the level of a fetus, as it is written, "when His lamp shone over my head." And "just as the shepherd puts his hand within her womb" means that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them the one commandment of circumcision, which is two: the cutting, signifying the abiding recognition that they stem from the root of the Blessed One's will, and the uncovering, alluding to all the fences by which Israel restrain themselves.,
like a fetus enclosed in its mother's womb (Shocher Tov, Psalm 107),
כִּי הָיוּ שָׁם עֲבָדִים.
for they were literal slaves there.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוֹצִיאָם מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵרוּת,
Yet the blessed Hashem liberated them from servitude into freedom,
כִּי ״עֲבָדַי הֵם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי״ וְגוֹמֵר,
stating: “For they are My servants whom I brought forth...”
שֶׁזֶּהוּ כֹּחַ הַהוֹצָאָה:
for the essential power of the Exodus lies in this:
בִּהְיוֹתָם עֲבָדָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
in their becoming servants exclusively to the Blessed One,

וְלֹא עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים (מַסֶּכֶת קִדּוּשִׁין כ״ב1026 Kiddushin 22b — R. Shimon bar Rabbi would expound this verse as a kind of ornament: Why are the door and the doorpost different from all the other furnishings of the house? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The door and the doorpost were witnesses in Egypt when I passed over the lintel and over the two doorposts, and I said, "For to Me the children of Israel are servants" — and not servants of servants; and I brought them out from slavery to freedom. Yet this man went and acquired a master for himself; let him be pierced before them. Rashi (s.v. "as a kind of ornament"): A "chomer" is a string of pearls or a sachet of spices hung at the neck for adornment. Tosafos (s.v. "as a kind of ornament"): Rashi explained it as a string of pearls or of spices that women hang at the neck for adornment; but Rabbeinu Tam explained "chomer" to mean a deed, and so the Arukh explains it from the Arabic, in which one asks his fellow what his deeds are by saying "mah chamrakh". Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kiddushin 22b): When the Holy One, blessed be He, passed over the houses of Israel and did not enter their doorway to destroy, it was made visible at their doorway that they receive no master other than Him; and this is why the blood was set upon the doorposts of the house — to say that the man who is within the house belongs to God. It was not set upon the ear, for the body is not the essence of a man, whereas the house serves the rational man and so shows that man is a vessel serving God to receive His service; hence the door and the doorpost were the witnesses that Israel are servants of the Holy One, blessed be He. The piercing shows this man's lowliness in accepting the mastery of a human being, and therefore his ear, which is his vessel of reception, is cut into until he is reckoned a mere unformed lump. עַמּוּד ב׳),
“and not slaves to other slaves” (Kiddushin 22b),
וְאֵין כֹּחַ לְשׁוּם שָׁלְטָנוּת אַחֵר עֲלֵיהֶם.
leaving no other earthly ruler with ultimate jurisdiction over their souls.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
Therefore at the Giving of the Torah,

הָיָה חֵרוּת מִן הַמַּלְכֻיּוֹת (מַסֶּכֶת עֵירוּבִין נ״ד1027 Eruvin 54a — R. Eliezer said: What is meant by "engraved [charut] upon the tablets" (Exodus 32:16)? Had the first tablets not been broken, the Torah would never have been forgotten from Israel. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: No nation or tongue would ever have ruled over them, as it is stated "charut" — read not "charut," engraved, but "cheirut," freedom. Rashi: "It would never have been forgotten": charut means engraved and never effaced; by means of the tablets the Torah was engraved upon Israel so as never to be forgotten from them. "Upon the tablets": on account of the tablets the children of Israel were free men. Maharsha: Scripture should have said "engraved [chakuk] upon the tablets," which is the word used elsewhere for engraving; rather, charut is said of the heart, and "upon the tablets [luchot]" is like "upon his cheeks [lechayav]" in the exposition above — of one who does not weary of reviewing his learning — for then his learning becomes engraved and kept in his heart and endures with him. And he who says "read not charut but cheirut" likewise expounds it from the fact that "engraved" is not written. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 47): Scripture says charut rather than "engraved," and the writing of the tablets went through from either side, which marks a wholly complete and unmistakable form — fitting for the Torah, whose intelligible form is wholly clear, unlike man's intellect, which stands in matter. Whatever is free of matter is free, for servitude belongs to matter alone; hence "read not charut, engraved, but cheirut, freedom." And because the power of the kingdoms is material, while one who occupies himself with Torah cleaves to an intellect separate from matter, the kingdoms cannot rule over him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 12): Freedom corresponds to the gift of the Land of Israel, for having a land of their own stems from their freedom, that they are free men with a government of their own, and joy corresponds to the gift of the World to Come; all three come through suffering, that is, through human toil and effort. All three are included in the Torah: for "the precepts of the Lord... rejoice the heart," and [the Sages] also said, "read not charut but cheirut"; therefore it is called "a threefold Torah." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 21): After they had refined all seven attributes [in the weeks of the counting], and then [attained] the understanding of the heart, Israel merited the "gate of freedom" at the receiving of the Torah, as in "read not charut but cheirut," and "none is free but one who occupies himself with Torah." Through the holiness of the Sabbath that comes by their own preparation they merited that no nation or tongue should rule over them, for in this they are distinguished from every nation and tongue. At the giving of the Torah the Sabbath was given to them as a complete gift and engraved on the tablets, to be engraved and fixed in the hearts of Israel; this is the engraving of "charut" that we read as "cheirut," to merit the gate of freedom of the upper Sabbath. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 8): Of the first tablets it is said, "engraved [charut] upon the tablets," and [the Sages] said, "read not charut but cheirut." The holy Shelah writes that wherever "read not" appears, it means that you can read it the second way only if you read it the first: here, if [the Torah] is engraved on the tablet of their heart, on the heart of stone, then you can read "cheirut" — freedom from the angel of death and from the evil inclination, the "heart of the fool at his left." As [the Midrash] says, when Israel heard "I am the Lord your God" the study of Torah was implanted in their hearts, and when they heard "You shall have no [other gods]" the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 2): Therefore the Sages said of the giving of the Torah, "read not charut but cheirut" — freedom from the evil inclination. This is as it is said, "I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Me": the eagle soars in the air, midway between heaven and earth, but you are borne above the eagles' wings, for you are brought to Me, to the Most High. Therefore when they said "we will do and we will hear," meriting also "we will hear," they were free from the evil inclination, from the angel of death and from every nation and tongue — through complete unification, for where there is complete unity there is no room at all for separation. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Balak): "God who brings them out of Egypt is for them like the soaring strength of the wild ox": immediately upon leaving Egypt they had the nature of the wild ox, of which it is written, "Will the wild ox be willing to serve you?" — for it accepts no man's yoke. This is the great praise of Israel: though they had been enslaved in Egypt at crushing labour, immediately upon leaving they received the Torah, which is freedom from every yoke and servitude, as it is said, "engraved upon the tablets" — read not charut, engraved, but cheirut, freedom. עַמּוּד א׳).
there was fundamental liberation from the earthly kingdoms (Eruvin 54a).
וּכְשֶׁגָּלוּ וְחָזְרוּ וְנִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ,
Consequently, when they were later exiled and subjected once again,
לֹא הָיָה עוֹד עַבְדוּת גָּמוּר
it could never again become absolute enslavement
כְּמוֹ גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם,
like the Egyptian bondage,
שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
which transpired prior to the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד מַרְאִית הָעַיִן,
where at least superficially from the vantage of perception,
עַל כָּל פָּנִים, נִדְמֶה לְעַבְדוּת גָּמוּר.
it seemed to resemble total servitude.
אֲבָל אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
However, after the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁנִּקְנוּ לַעֲבָדִים לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
once they were permanently acquired as servants unto the Blessed One,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת עוֹד עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים כְּלַל.
it is fundamentally impossible for them ever to be true slaves to mortals.
וְקִנְיַן גּוֹי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל —
Thus, a gentile's legal purchase of a Jew—
הוּא רַק שִׁעְבּוּד גּוּף,
effects only physical servitude of the body,
וְלֹא שִׁעְבּוּד כֹּחוֹתָיו כְּלַל.
and cannot subjugate his inner spiritual faculties whatsoever.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת1028 Sanhedrin 105a — Shmuel said [of the “triumphant retort” that the Assembly of Israel gave the prophet]: Ten men came and sat before the prophet. He said to them: Repent. They said to him: A servant whose master has sold him, and a woman whom her husband has divorced — has either any claim upon the other? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the prophet: Go and say to them, “Where is your mother’s bill of divorce with which I sent her away? Or which of My creditors is it to whom I sold you? Behold, for your iniquities were you sold, and for your transgressions was your mother sent away.” And this accords with what Reish Lakish said: What is meant by the verses “David My servant” and “Nevuchadnezzar My servant”? It was revealed and known before Him who spoke and the world came into being, that Israel would one day speak thus; therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, anticipated them and called them His servant — for a servant who acquires property, to whom does the servant belong and to whom the property? Rashi: Shmuel explains what the "victorious answer" was: since the Holy One, blessed be He, has sold us to Nebuchadnezzar and driven us away from Him, has He any further claim on us? He called that wicked man "My servant" as He called David — not because they are alike, but because it was revealed before Him that Israel would one day say "He has already sold us to Nebuchadnezzar," so He anticipated them in order to give them a reply. "The servant — to whom? The property — to whom?": that is, Nebuchadnezzar is My servant and all that he acquired is Mine, so you have not yet left My domain. Maharsha: Ten men came because the Divine Presence rests upon every ten, and they came to cast off its yoke: since Israel are called both God's sons and His servants, they argued that as servants they had been sold to Nebuchadnezzar, and as sons their mother had already been divorced, so that sons born to her after the divorce are not His. The answer is that she is like a wife who rebelled and left her husband without a bill of divorce — "for your transgressions" — so he is still her husband and the sons are his; and as for servants, the Holy One, blessed be He, would sell a servant only to a nation to whom He owed a reward, but to Nebuchadnezzar He owed nothing ("which of My creditors"). Rather, "for your iniquities were you sold," as a master hands a rebellious servant over to another — even to his second servant — to chastise him with bondage, as it says, "Nebuchadnezzar My servant." סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ה עַמּוּד א׳):
And the Sages of blessed memory noted (Sanhedrin 105a):
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר ״עֲבָדַי״,
this is why Nebuchadnezzar proclaimed “my servants”,
וְ״עֶבֶד שֶׁקָּנָה נְכָסִים״ וְכוּלֵי.
invoking the halachic rule: “a servant who acquires property...”
וְהַיְינוּ עִנְיַן:
And this is the inner meaning of:

״בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל — גָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם״ (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה כ״ט1029 Megillah 29a — It was taught: R. Shimon ben Yochai says: Come and see how beloved Israel is before the Holy One, blessed be He — for in every place to which they were exiled, the Divine Presence is with them. They were exiled to Egypt, the Divine Presence was with them, as it is said, "Did I indeed reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt." They were exiled to Babylonia, the Divine Presence was with them, as it is said, "For your sake I was sent to Babylonia." And when they are destined to be redeemed, the Divine Presence is with them, as it is said, "Then the Lord your God will return your captivity" — it does not say "will bring back" but "will return," teaching that the Holy One, blessed be He, returns with them from among the exiles. Maharsha: The verse was not needed merely to show that the Divine Presence spoke with them in Egypt, for the Torah records explicit speech of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Moses and Aaron there; rather, since “the whole earth is full of His glory,” the point is that a revelation of the Divine Presence belongs to designated places, such as the Tabernacle and the Temple — and the doubled “Did I indeed reveal Myself” teaches that there was such a revelation in the Egyptian exile. One may also explain that the doubled expression hints at exile [galut], as though the Divine Presence too suffers in the exile. And the closing clause teaches that at the redemption the revelation of the Presence returns to Jerusalem and does not remain in the place of Israel’s exile. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 10): There is more reason for Him to be with Israel in exile than when they come out of it, for it is His way that His Presence dwells “with the contrite and lowly of spirit,” and in exile Israel are crushed. Hence, when they leave the exile one might suppose He is no longer with them, and the baraita teaches that He is with them then also — not because they still stand in need of His protection, but because Israel are never parted from the Divine Presence, since He has joined His name to theirs, and to such attachment there is no separation. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 11): Through the Torah there is rescue and freedom from the leaven in the dough and from the subjugation of exile; only the [final] heh [of the Divine Name] is in exile, as it is written (Megillah 29a), "the Divine Presence went into exile with them." For the Torah, which is from Heaven, is not subject to exile; exile applies only to the "candle" of the mitzvah, the effort and deed of human beings, which the exile hinders — and this is what is called Shechinah, that the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells actually within Israel. עַמּוּד א׳),
“Wherever Israel was exiled, the Shechinah was exiled alongside them” (Megillah 29a),
וּ״מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה״.
and “His kingship rules over everything”.
וְעַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְשָׁם,
And through Israel's dispersion thither,
נִתְפַּרְסֵם גַּם שָׁם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ,
His Divinity became revealed in those foreign lands as well,
וְשֶׁגַּם הֵם מִכֹּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
demonstrating that those nations also subsist solely by His vitality;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִים הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם.
and Israel extracts whatever spark of good resides in them.
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת קִנְיָן
Therefore foreign nations possess no true property acquisition
בֶּאֱמֶת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלַל,
in the reality of a Jew at all,
רַק מִצַּד הַגּוּף,
except strictly on the physical plane of the body,
שֶׁהוּא הַחֹמֶר הַמְכַסֶּה
which is the coarse matter that veils
וּמַאֲפִיל הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת.
and darkens the perception of the truth.
וְעִקַּר קִנְיַן עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And the primary halachic source for a gentile's acquisition of a Jew
יָלְפִינַן בְּמַסֶּכֶת גִּטִּין שָׁם
we derive in Tractate Gittin there
מִקְּרָא דְּ״וַיִּשְׁבְּ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁבִי״,
from the verse: “and took some of them captive”,
הַנֶּאֱמָר בִּכְנַעֲנִי מֶלֶךְ עֲרָד,
stated concerning the Canaanite king of Arad,
דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
concerning whom the Sages of blessed memory noted
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת חֻקַּת),
in Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma (Parshat Chukat),
וְהוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (רֵישׁ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה),
and cited in Tosafot (at the beginning of Rosh Hashanah),
שֶׁהוּא עֲמָלֵק.
that he was actually Amalek in disguise.
כִּי עִנְיָן זֶה
For this phenomenon,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת עַבְדוּת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
that there should exist any form of servitude for Israel,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד עֲמָלֵק.
arises purely from the side of Amalek.
דְּאַף שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִים
For even when Jews sin
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם מַמָּשׁ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
to the point that they resemble other nations in physical action,
וְהִגְדִּילוּ עֲווֹנוֹת, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
and their iniquities have multiplied, Heaven forbid,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְעוֹלָם ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״,
nevertheless: “a Jew, even though he has sinned, remains a Jew”,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהֵעָקֵר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵהֶם כְּלַל.
and it is impossible for the name and status of Israel ever to be eradicated from them.
וְהִמְשִׁילוּ עַל זֶה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And our Sages of blessed memory offered a parable for this

בְּמַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין (מ״ד1030 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is still Israel. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle, and myrtle they call it. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious. עַמּוּד א׳):
in Tractate Sanhedrin (44a):
״לַאֲסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי הוֹצֵי —
“To a myrtle that stands among briars—
אָסָא שְׁמֵיהּ וְאָסָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ״.
a myrtle remains its name, and a myrtle people call it.”
הַיְינוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל
Meaning that the foundational root of Israel
לְעוֹלָם דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
is eternally bound to the Blessed Name
מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם הַנֶּעְלָם,
through their supernal hidden root,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is not openly manifest in this world.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And this accords with the teaching of the Sages

(זֹהַר חָדָשׁ, רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ)1031 Zohar Chadash, Yitro 3 — He said to him: Come and see, my son. The Holy One, blessed be He, made His covenant with Abraham only to bring Israel out of the exile of Egypt, and not from beneath the subjugation of any other alien power. For certainly, when Israel were in Egypt they were defiled and befouled themselves with every kind of impurity, until they lay beneath forty-nine forces of impurity; and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought them out from beneath the dominion of all those forces. And further, He brought them into the forty-nine gates of understanding that correspond to them.:
(Zohar Chadash, beginning of Parshat Yitro):
דִּבְמִצְרַיִם אִלְמָלֵא מִהֵר לְגָאֳלָם,
that in Egypt, had He not hurried to redeem them,
הָיוּ נִכְנָסִים בְּשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים דְּטֻמְאָה,
they would have entered the Fiftieth Gate of Impurity,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגָאֳלָם עוֹד.
whereupon redemption would have become impossible.
הַיְינוּ: שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים
That is to say: the Fiftieth Gate
הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְגַּלֶּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
is the root that cannot be openly revealed in this mundane world
(כִּי הוּא נֶגֶד הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
(for it corresponds to the World to Come,
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּאַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה
as is known that forty-nine
הוּא שִׁבְעָה פְּעָמִים שִׁבְעָה,
is seven times seven,
שֶׁהֵם שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן,
which represent the seven attributes of Creation,
וְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הוּא הַבִּינָה,
while the Fiftieth Gate is Binah (Understanding),
תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ וְיוֹבֵל הַגָּדוֹל,
the gate of complete liberation and the Great Jubilee,
שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא),
which embodies the World to Come),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּקַלְקְלוּ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
and the peril was that they might damage, Heaven forbid,
שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם מֵהָאָבוֹת.
the primal root of Jewish sanctity bequeathed to them from the Patriarchs.
כִּי קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
For prior to the Giving of the Torah,
הָיָה עֲדַיִן מָקוֹם מְצִיאוּת
there still existed a vulnerability
לְקַלְקֵל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ גַּם כֵּן,
for even that root to be damaged;
וְעַל כֵּן הֻצְרַךְ לְמַהֵר הַגְּאֻלָּה.
and on that account the Exodus had to be rushed.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהַגְּאֻלָּה דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And because the redemption led by Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
הָיָה רַק מֵאַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה שַׁעֲרֵי טֻמְאָה,
was specifically from the forty-nine gates of impurity,
וְהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת אַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה שַׁעֲרֵי קְדֻשָּׁה,
effected through the disclosure of forty-nine gates of holiness,
עַל כֵּן לֹא נִגְלָה אֵלָיו שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים.
the Fiftieth Gate was not disclosed to him.
וּבִשְׁאָר גָּלֻיּוֹת
Whereas in all subsequent exiles,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר עוֹד לְהִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ עַד לְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים כְּלַל,
it is no longer possible for a Jew to sink into that Fiftieth Gate at all,
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל —
for the essential root of Israel—
אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלַל שֶׁיֵּעָקֵר עוֹד מֵהֶם,
can never again be severed or uprooted from them,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִהְיֶה, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
and even if an individual were, Heaven forbid,
בְּכָל אַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה שַׁעֲרֵי טֻמְאָה,
submerged in all forty-nine gates of impurity,
בְּשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּטוֹב,
at the Fiftieth Gate—the concealed taproot of good—
דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
he remains irrevocably attached to the Blessed One.

items.h:
Seif 4 — The Root of Evil and the Boundary of Captivity
Amalek can seize only Israel's external boundary; he cannot gain true ownership over their intrinsic holy root.

p: וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּרַע,
Amalek, who represents the hidden root of cosmic evil,
כָּל יִשְׁעוֹ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ דְּטוֹב,
directs his entire ambition to overpowering the holy root of good,
וּמַכְחִישׁ זֶה
and actively denies this,
שֶׁאֵין מְצִיאוּת שֹׁרֶשׁ טוֹב, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
claiming that no inherent root of good exists at all, Heaven forbid.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִמְחָה לְגַמְרֵי מִן הָעוֹלָם,
And so long as he has not been blotted out entirely from the world,
וְיֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת שֹׁרֶשׁ רַע,
and some manifest presence of the root of evil still endures,
יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת זֶה
there remains room
מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
from the outward perspective of this world
לַחְשֹׁב שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהִנָּתֵק מִן הַיַּהֲדוּת לְגַמְרֵי,
to imagine that one could sever himself entirely from Jewishness—
כְּעִנְיַן הַמּוּמָרִים הַגְּמוּרִים לְהַכְעִיס,
like the case of total, defiant apostates
שֶׁחוֹשְׁבִים כְּאִלּוּ נֶחֱלַף
who imagine as though they have been altered
וְנַעֲשָׂה עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.
and transformed into actual idolaters.
וְזֶהוּ מְצִיאוּת קִנְיַן גּוֹי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And this underlies the phenomenon of a gentile legally acquiring a Jew
מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
from the framework of this physical world,
שֶׁהָעַבְדוּת הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב
for such enslavement exists only insofar as it appears
כְּאִלּוּ אֵינוֹ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, עַבְדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
as though he were no longer, Heaven forbid, a servant of the Blessed One;
וְזֶהוּ עִקָּרוֹ מִצַּד עֲמָלֵק.
and this premise originates essentially from Amalek.
וּכְשֶׁרָאָה מַפַּלְתּוֹ תְּחִלָּה,
And when Amalek witnessed his initial downfall at Rephidim,
הִתְחַכֵּם אַחַר כָּךְ לְשַׁנּוֹת כְּסוּת וְלָשׁוֹן
he subsequently devised a scheme to disguise his clothing and language
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מְפַיֵּט,
as Tosafot noted, quoting the liturgical poet on Rosh Hashanah,

וְכֵן הוּא בְּיַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי, פָּרָשַׁת חֻקַּת)1032 Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 3a — "And the Canaanite, king of Arad, heard" (Numbers 21:1) — in the Midrash we say that this was Amalek, as the liturgical poet composed in the hymn for Parashat Zakhor: "Dress and tongue he changed, to be as the king of Arad." Even so it is properly inferred that Sihon was still alive, since Amalek himself changed to come in his likeness.
and likewise in Yalkut Shimoni, Parshat Chukat,

וּלְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לִכְנַעֲנִי1033 Numbers 21:1 — “And the Canaanite king of Arad, who dwelt in the south, heard that Israel had come by the way of Atharim, and he made war against Israel and took some of them captive.” Rashi: He heard that Aaron had died and that the clouds of glory had departed, and so he thought he was now free to make war against Israel.
