"The dweller in the south" is Amalek, but he changed his speech to the tongue of Canaan so that Israel would pray that Canaanites be given into their hand and their prayer would not avail; seeing that their dress was Amalekite while their language was Canaanite, Israel prayed in general terms, "If You will indeed give this people into my hand." Ramban: The correct view is that this king of Arad dwelt in the south on the western side of the Jordan, in the land of Canaan near the border of Judah, and heard from afar of the coming of the children of Israel, and came by the way of Atharim to the plains of Moab to fight them there — this is the sense of "and he heard." According to Onkelos, "the way of Atharim" is the route the spies had taken, for when the spies went up through the south the inhabitants of the land noticed them, and this Canaanite followed that same road until he reached Israel's camp..
and masquerade as a Canaanite.
וְהָיָה כְּשֶׁשָּׁמַע מִיתַת אַהֲרֹן,
And this occurred when he heard of the passing of Aaron,
עַמּוּד הָעֲבוֹדָה,
the Pillar of Divine Service,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב בַּפּוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ,
who embodies the actual, tangible root of good
בַּעֲבוֹדָה מַמָּשִׁית לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
in concrete service rendered to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְנִסְתַּלְּקוּ עַנְנֵי כָּבוֹד.
and the Clouds of Glory departed.
יָדוּעַ דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם בַּכָּתוּב,
It is known that wherever mentioned in Scripture,
הִתְגַּלּוּת עַמּוּד עָנָן
the manifestation of the pillar of cloud
הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָה וּכְבוֹד הַשֵּׁם,
is the revelation of the Shechinah and the Divine Glory;
וּבִזְכוּת אַהֲרֹן, שֶׁהוּא עֲבוֹדַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת,
and through the merit of Aaron, who performed the sacrificial rites,
הָיוּ עַנְנֵי כָּבוֹד,
Israel was sheltered by the Clouds of Glory,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שְׁכִינָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
which was the open presence of the Shechinah within Israel,
וּכְשֶׁמֵּת — נִסְתַּלְּקוּ.
and when he died, they withdrew.
וְחָשַׁב דְּהָיָה הִסְתַּלְּקוּת גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה לְגַמְרֵי,
Amalek presumed that the revelation of the Shechinah had departed completely,
עַד שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים.
such that Israel could now be reduced to slaves of slaves.
אֲבָל יָדַע מֵאָז שֶׁבָּא בִּרְפִידִים,
Yet he already knew from his earlier encounter at Rephidim,
דְּהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
which was before the Giving of the Torah,
וְגַם כֵּן הָיוּ בְּרִפְיוֹן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
when they were likewise in a state of laxity in Torah,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה רָאָה שֶׁלֹּא יָכֹל לָהֶם —
and even so he saw that he could not conquer them—
יָדַע דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁלֹט עֲלֵיהֶם,
he knew it was impossible through his own overt power to dominate them;
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְפַּשֵּׁט שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
namely, to inject the root of evil, Heaven forbid, into Israel
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית גַּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
to the point that he would become their primary head as well.
עַל כֵּן הִתְחַכֵּם לְשַׁנּוֹת עַצְמוֹ.
Therefore he devised a scheme to mask himself.
וְשִׁנּוּי זֶה שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה,
And this transformation recorded in the Torah,
וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה מִצַּד הַלְּבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי בִּלְבַד,
was certainly not confined to physical attire alone,
רַק גַּם מִצַּד לְבוּשֵׁי הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
but extended to the spiritual garments of the soul.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ לָהּ שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁהִיא תְּקוּעָה בּוֹ,
For every soul has an indelible root wherein it is embedded,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹתוֹ כְּלַל,
which cannot be altered under any circumstances;
וְיֵשׁ לָהּ לְבוּשִׁים
and it possesses garments
שֶׁזֶּה אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת.
that can indeed be changed.
וְיֵשׁ לְבוּשׁ עַצְמִי שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא נִכָּר,
There is a characteristic garment through which one is commonly identified,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת וּלְהַלְבִּישׁ לְבוּשׁ אַחֵר.
yet one can nevertheless swap it and assume another disguise.
וּמִצַּד לְבוּשֵׁי הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
Thus, through the garments of the soul—
דְּהַיְינוּ מַה שֶׁהוּא נִכָּר לַאֲחֵרִים,
namely, the exterior facade visible to outsiders,
שֶׁהָאֲחֵרִים אֵין מַכִּירִים שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם, רַק הַנִּגְלֶה —
since outsiders cannot perceive the concealed root, but only what is revealed—
שִׁנָּה עַצְמוֹ לְאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת.
he transformed himself into the guise of another nation.
וּבְמַסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳) אָמְרוּ דְּהוּא סִיחוֹן,
And in Tractate Rosh Hashanah (3a) the Sages taught that this king was Sihon,
וְכָאן נִשְׁתַּנָּה שְׁמוֹ לַ״עֲרוֹד״,
while here in Scripture his name changed to Arad,
שֶׁהוּא חֲמוֹר הַבָּר.
denoting a wild desert donkey (arod).
וְגַם סִיחוֹן,
And Sihon as well,
שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְ״סַיִחַ״,
whose name resembles sayach (a young foal),
הוּא חֲמוֹר.
belongs to the donkey species.
וְהַפְּלֻגְתָּא שָׁם:
And the debate among the Sages there,
אֵיזֶה עִקַּר שְׁמוֹ,
as to which was his principal name,
הַיְינוּ עִקָּרוֹ שֶׁל סִיחוֹן מַה הוּא.
clarifies what the fundamental essence of Sihon truly was.
דְּכָל הַשֵּׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
For all names in the Torah
מוֹרוֹת עַל עֶצֶם כֹּחָם,
signify the essential spiritual power of their subjects,
שֶׁהָיוּ כֹּחַ חֲמוֹר.
and here both names reflected the donkey-nature.
כִּי כְּנַעַן
For Canaan
הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הָעַבְדוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם,
is the cosmic root of all human servitude in the world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״אָרוּר כְּנָעַן, עֶבֶד עֲבָדִים יִהְיֶה״,
as it is written: “Cursed be Canaan, a servant of servants shall he be”,
שֶׁבּוֹ נִזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה עִנְיַן הָעַבְדוּת,
marking the first explicit mention of servitude in the Torah,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת מְצִיאַת הָעַבְדוּת.
from which the foundational reality of slavery sprang.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And likewise the Sages of blessed memory noted

בְּמַסֶּכֶת פְּסָחִים1034 Pesachim 113b — Five things did Canaan charge his sons: love one another, love robbery, love licentiousness, hate your masters, and do not speak the truth. Maharsha: Because it was decreed upon his sons that they be slaves, as it is written, "and Canaan shall be a servant to them" — and following what was said above, that slaves love one another — he charged his sons to love one another. "Love robbery" accords with what was said, "one who increases slaves increases robbery," and "love licentiousness" with "one who increases maidservants increases licentiousness." "Hate your masters" — for by that decree each of his sons has a master over him; and "do not speak the truth," as it is written, "Canaan, in whose hand are deceitful balances." (קי״ג עַמּוּד ב׳):
in Tractate Pesachim (113b):
״צִוָּה כְּנַעַן אֶת בָּנָיו״ וְכוּלֵי,
“Canaan commanded his sons...”
עַל עִנְיְנֵי הָעֲבָדִים.
regarding typical traits of enslaved people.
אַף שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מִזֶּרַע כְּנַעַן,
Even when an enslaved individual does not physically descend from Canaan,
נִקְרָא ״עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי״,
he is legally designated a “Canaanite slave”,
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הָעַבְדוּת בָּא מִכֹּחַ כְּנַעַן.
for the spiritual root of all subjugation originates in Canaan.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא בָּזֶה ״הַכְּנַעֲנִי״
Therefore this attacker is called “the Canaanite”
עַל שֵׁם מַלְכוּתוֹ,
after the character of his sovereignty,
שֶׁרָצָה שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעַבְדוּת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
for he desired that the primal root of slavery
יִמְשֹׁל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
should rule over Israel, Heaven forbid,
לִהְיוֹת עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים גָּמוּר.
reducing them to absolute servants of servants.
וְעֶבֶד נִמְשַׁל לַחֲמוֹר,
And an enslaved person is compared to a donkey,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת יְבָמוֹת ס״ב1035 Yevamot 62a — Rav said: All agree with regard to a slave that he has no lineage, for it is written: "Remain here with the donkey" (Genesis 22:5) — a people that is like a donkey. Rashi: "Remain here": [among those addressed was] Eliezer, who was Abraham's slave. Tosafos (s.v. "all agree regarding a slave that he has no lineage"): Hence if he is freed, he has not fulfilled [the commandment of] procreation [through the children he had as a slave]. And if you ask: of one who is half slave and half free it is said that he cannot marry a maidservant, implying that could he marry one it would suffice for him — yet he would not fulfill procreation thereby? One may answer that were he able to marry a maidservant his master would not be compelled to free him, since he could at least fulfill [the purpose of] "He formed it to be inhabited," even though he would not fulfill procreation thereby. Maharal (Derech Chaim 6:2): Servitude belongs to matter, for from the aspect of form there is no servitude; and this is what the Sages hinted regarding the Canaanite slave, "Remain here with the donkey [chamor]" — a people that is like a donkey. For by virtue of the servitude in him he resembles matter [chomer]: one who is subjugated is acted upon by another, and that is the nature of matter, which is acted upon; but form is never acted upon at all, so servitude cannot be ascribed to it, only freedom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 11): [On Rashi's comment that Moses' donkey was the very one Abraham saddled for the binding of Isaac,] there is a difficulty: Abraham's donkey is expounded (Yevamos 62a), "Remain here with the donkey" — "a people that is like a donkey," which is to its discredit. But the donkey [chamor] alludes to the body, which is matter [chomer]: Abraham "saddled his donkey" — he subdued the body so that there be holiness in it, and while he rode it, it was turned to good and alludes to holiness. Afterward, however, when he left it with Ishmael and Eliezer — Ishmael being the husk of the donkey — with them it was the donkey of the husk, the husk of desire, and of this he said to them, "a people that is like a donkey." עַמּוּד א׳)
as the Sages of blessed memory derived (Yevamot 62a)
עַל פָּסוּק: ״עִם הַחֲמוֹר״ —
from the verse: “with the donkey”—
״עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר״,
meaning “a people resembling the donkey”,
דְּעִקָּרוֹ בַּעֲבָדִים
referring primarily to enslaved servants
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יִחוּס כְּלַל,
who possess no legally recognized lineage,
רַק כַּחֲמוֹרִים,
existing merely like donkeys,
שֶׁהֵם עִקַּר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
which are the primary beasts of burden
הַמִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים לִבְנֵי אָדָם לַעֲבוֹדָתָם,
subjected to man for grueling labor,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה1036 Avodah Zarah 5b — "That send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey" (Isaiah 32:20) — the school of Elijah taught: A person should always set himself to words of Torah like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to the burden. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 5b): That a person should set himself to words of Torah like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to the burden means that he should engage in Torah with his whole body and soul: he must strain his intellect to learn, for the Torah is hard to understand, and in this he is like the ox, which is occupied in hard labor, pulling in the yoke. And since he also carries a heavy load that weakens his whole body, for at times he goes without food and drink and other things on account of the Torah, in this he is like the donkey, which carries a great burden and bears it upon its body.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כַּחֲמוֹר לְמַשָּׂאוֹי״.
as they remarked (Avodah Zarah 5b): “like a donkey designated for a load.”
וְכֵן הָעֲבָדִים
Similarly, enslaved servants,
שֶׁהֵם נִקְנִים בְּקִנְיָן גָּמוּר לְאָדוֹן,
who are thoroughly acquired by a master
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
and retain no independent status of their own,
הֵם ״עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר״.
are considered “the people resembling a donkey”.
וְסִיחוֹן הָיָה חֲמוֹר הַבָּר
And Sihon was like a wild desert donkey
שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל מָרוּת,
refusing all domestic control,
וְרָצָה לִלְחֹם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and boldly came out to wage war with Israel.
וּלְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר ״עֲרוֹד שְׁמוֹ״,
And according to the authority holding that his actual name was Arad,
דְּהַיְינוּ עִקָּרוֹ חֲמוֹר הַבָּר,
meaning his core nature was indeed that of an untamed wild donkey,
רַק שֶׁבְּמִלְחָמָה שֶׁלּוֹ,
except that in his actual war against Israel,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִצַּח כְּלוּם,
since he could prevail in nothing,
וּכְשֶׁנִּרְאָה לִפְנֵי ״אָדָם״,
and confronting the lofty stature of Adam—
שֶׁהֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל הַקְּרוּיִם ״אָדָם״ —
namely Israel, who are called Adam—
מִיָּד נִכְבַּשׁ לִפְנֵיהֶם,
he was instantly vanquished before them,
עַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״סִיחוֹן״,
and was therefore designated “Sihon”,
שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְסַיִחַ שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר,
resembling a runaway foal in the wilderness.
וְאַף שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר,
And even in the desert,
אַף דְּסַיִחַ אֵינוֹ חֲמוֹר מִדְבָּרִי,
though a domesticated foal is not biologically a wild donkey,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, הֲרֵי בָּרַח לַמִּדְבָּר
nevertheless it has broken away into the wilderness
וְרָצָה לִמְרֹד בַּאֲדוֹנָיו,
attempting to rebel against its master,
אֲבָל מִיָּד שֶׁבָּא לִלְחֹם עִמָּהֶם — נִכְבַּשׁ.
yet the moment it confronts them, it is subdued.
וְרַק בַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּדְמָה לוֹ,
Only when Amalek disguised himself as Sihon
and took captives from Israel,
הָיָה כֶּעָרוֹד,
did he act like an untamed wild donkey (arod),
שֶׁהוּא חֲמוֹר הַבָּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִכְנָע
which refuses to yield
גַּם בְּבוֹא אֲדוֹנוֹ.
even upon the arrival of its master.
וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״סִיחוֹן שְׁמוֹ״,
And according to the opinion that his true name was Sihon,
הַיְינוּ עִקָּרוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת,
meaning that in his essential reality,
אֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַמְּרִידָה בְּאָדוֹן לְגַמְרֵי
he did not possess absolute defiant rebellion against a master
כַּחֲמוֹר הַבָּר כְּלַל,
like a true wild donkey at all,
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר עֲמָלֵק לָבַשׁ לְבוּשׁוֹ.
except when Amalek donned his external attire.
דַּעֲמָלֵק, מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
For Amalek, by virtue of being the head of the nations,
בְּכֹחוֹ לִלְבֹּשׁ לְבוּשׁ שֶׁל כָּל אֻמָּה,
possesses the capability to clothe himself in the guise of any nation,
שֶׁכֻּלָּם אֲחוּזִים בּוֹ.
since all are bound to his root.
וּמִצַּד שָׁרְשׁוֹ הָאָחוּז בַּעֲמָלֵק,
And through the element within them tied to Amalek,
כַּאֲשֶׁר נִכְלָל בִּמְקוֹרוֹ הָרָע,
whenever a nation merges into that evil source,
אָז נִדְמֶה כַּחֲמוֹר הַבָּר.
it takes on the characteristics of an untamable wild donkey.
וְחָשַׁב דִּבְהִיוֹת אַחַר שֶׁחָטְאוּ
And Amalek calculated that since Israel had stumbled,
יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת,
they were now subject to foreign imperial servitude,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְדַּמֶּה לְאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת
so that by disguising himself as a different nation
יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד בָּהֶם,
he could place his yoke upon them,
וְהֵבִין דְּשִׁעְבּוּד זֶה הוּא עַבְדוּת גָּמוּר.
presuming that this subjugation would constitute absolute slavery.
וְחָשַׁב: כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ אַחֵר
He reasoned: when he cloaks himself in another nation's garments
וְיִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד בָּהֶם,
and subjects them to labor,
מִמֵּילָא יִהְיוּ כַּעֲבָדִים גְּמוּרִים,
they will automatically become total slaves,
לִהְיוֹת תַּחַת כֹּחַ שֶׁלּוֹ.
falling completely under his domain.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
Yet the Sages of blessed memory noted
(יַלְקוּט, הוּבָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי)1037 Rashi on Numbers 21:1 — "And he took from them a captive" — it was no more than a single maidservant.
(Yalkut, cited by Rashi)
דְּהַשֶּׁבִי הָיָה שִׁפְחָה אַחַת.
that the captive taken was merely a single maidservant.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּמוּר,
This indicates that over a full Jew,
אֲפִילּוּ דֶּרֶךְ שִׁבְיָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד הַגּוּף,
even by means of captivity and physical confinement,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד כְּלַל,
it is impossible for the root of Amalek to establish true servitude,
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִדְמֶה כְּהַעֲלָמַת שֹׁרֶשׁ טוֹב.
in a way that could ever obscure the inner holy root.
רַק שִׁפְחָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
He could seize only a Canaanite maidservant owned by a Jew,
שֶׁגַּם הִיא כְּבָר מְחֻיֶּבֶת בְּמִצְוֹת,
who, though already obligated in mitzvot,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת עוֹד
and unable to alter her status
לִפְטֹר עַצְמָהּ מֵחוֹבַת הַמִּצְוֹת,
so as to release herself from fulfilling the commandments,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינָהּ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּמוּר,
remains nevertheless distinct from a full-fledged Jew,
כִּי כָּל כֹּחָהּ הוּא רַק מִצַּד שֶׁהִיא שִׁפְחָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
inasmuch as her spiritual status derives entirely from being bound to Israel,
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד מֶמְשֶׁלֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הָעַמִּים.
which is an expression of Israel’s sovereignty over the nations.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִסְתַּלְּקוּ עַנְנֵי כָּבוֹד וְגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
And when the Clouds of Glory and the open Shechinah departed,
וְנִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק,
and Amalek's force was aroused,
שָׁלַט עַל זֶה,
he gained dominion specifically over that external boundary:
לְהָסִיר מֶמְשֶׁלֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
to remove Israel's overt sovereignty,
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כֹּחַ עַל הַשִּׁפְחָה שֶׁלָּהֶם.
giving him power to seize their maidservant.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, גַּם זוֹ לֹא קָנָה לְעַבְדוּת גָּמוּר,
Yet even so, he did not acquire her into absolute ownership;
רַק הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ שִׁבְיָה.
it remained strictly a temporary state of captivity.

items.h:
Seif 5 — Haman's Purchase and the Power of Longing
Haman seeks absolute acquisition, but Israel's deepest yearning - rooted beyond limited national powers - prevents total destruction.

p: וְהָמָן שֶׁרָאָה
Haman, seeing
שֶׁגַּם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה לֹא הִצְלִיחַ
that even in this matter he did not succeed
דֶּרֶךְ כִּבּוּשׁ מִלְחָמָה,
by way of conquest in war,
נִתְחַכֵּם לִקְנוֹתָם דֶּרֶךְ קִנְיָן.
devised a new strategy to acquire them through purchase.
כִּי חָשַׁב
For he reasoned
דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הַמּוֹלֵךְ עֲלֵיהֶם,
that Ahasuerus ruled over them
וּמִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים הֵם לוֹ כַּעֲבָדִים גְּמוּרִים.
and that they were already subjected to him as complete slaves.
אֶלָּא שֶׁכָּל אֻמָּה
However, since each nation
בִּהְיוֹתָהּ כֹּחַ פְּרָטִי,
is a particularized, limited power,
שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ גַּם כֵּן שֹׁרֶשׁ טוֹב
and within that very power there is also a good root
מַה שֶּׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
that exists within Israel,
עַל כָּרְחָם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם
they inevitably could not
לְהַאֲבִידָם לְגַמְרֵי,
destroy them completely,
שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם בָּהֶם אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ לְטוֹב.
since they too contain that corresponding power for good.
אֲבָל בִּהְיוֹת הוּא
Haman, however, being
שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם,
the root of evil dominating them,
חָשַׁב דְּיוּכַל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
thought that he would be able, Heaven forbid,
לְהַאֲבִידָם לְגַמְרֵי.
to destroy them completely.
וְדֶרֶךְ כִּבּוּשׁ —
And conquest—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּמְשֹׁל בָּהֶם וְיִהְיוּ לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים,
meaning to rule over them so that they would become his slaves,
שֶׁחָשַׁב לְהַכְנִיס שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרָע גַּם בָּהֶם —
whereby he planned to implant the root of evil within them too—
זֶה רָאָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר,
he saw that this was impossible;
עַל כֵּן חָשַׁב
therefore he resolved
לְהַאֲבִידָם לְגַמְרֵי.
to annihilate them entirely.
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר דֶּרֶךְ כִּבּוּשׁ מִלְחָמָה,
Yet this could not be done through military conquest,
שֶׁהוּא הַנִּצּוּחַ שֶׁבַּמִּשְׁפָּט
because that is a victory established through judgment
מִצַּד הִתְגַּבְּרוּת אוֹתוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ,
by the overwhelming strength of one root over another,
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלַל.
and in this matter such a victory is entirely impossible.
רַק חָשַׁב
Instead, he calculated
שֶׁיּוּכַל לִקְנוֹתָם בְּכֶסֶף,
that he could buy them with silver,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ קִנְיַן כַּסְפּוֹ כְּכָל עֲבָדִים,
so that they would become his monetary property like ordinary slaves,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם כְּבָר עֲבָדִים לַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
since they were already servants to Ahasuerus;
וְאָז מִמֵּילָא חָשַׁב
and then he presumed
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מֻכְנָעִים תַּחַת כֹּחַ שֶׁלּוֹ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
that they would automatically fall subdued under his own power, Heaven forbid.
וַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ נִקְרָא:
And Ahasuerus is called:
״אֶחָיו שֶׁל רֹאשׁ״ —
“the brother of the head”—

״זֶה הֶחֱרִיב וְזֶה בִּקֵּשׁ לְהַחֲרִיב״ (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״א1038 Megillah 11a — "Ahasuerus" — Rav said: The brother of the head, and of the same character as the head. The brother of the head — the brother of the wicked Nebuchadnezzar, who is called "head," as it is stated: "You are the head of gold" (Daniel 2:38). Of the same character as the head — that one killed and this one sought to kill; that one destroyed and this one sought to destroy, as it is stated: "And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem" (Ezra 4:6). Rashi: "The brother of the head" — that is to say, he resembled him. "Of the same character" — born under the same constellation; the two of them were of one mind. "He sought to destroy" — the foundation that Zerubbabel had laid for the Temple in the days of Cyrus, before Ahasuerus, as is told in the book of Ezra; and "an accusation" means that he was appointed an adversary to them, that they should not build it. Maharsha: In the Torah too a reason is given for a number of names, and so the Sages saw fit in their expositions to give a reason for certain names, after the manner of R. Meir, who would draw inferences from a name. He was certainly not his brother in fact; rather "the brother of the head" means what is then said, "of the same character as the head" — for brothers for the most part resemble one another — and the resemblance lay in their sharing one constellation, that one killed and the other sought to kill, their star being Mars, as they said, one born under Mars will be a shedder of blood. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 1:1): "The brother of the head" means that Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus were equal and alike in the power of their dominion: the name "Ahasuerus" indicates the essence of his kingship, which was weighed in the balance against the kingdom of the wicked Nebuchadnezzar, and therefore it calls them "brothers." Of Nebuchadnezzar it is said "You are the head of gold," while the kingdom of Persia is likened to silver, and silver and gold are everywhere paired as brothers. And both stood opposed to the holiness of Israel; therefore "that one destroyed and this one sought to destroy." עַמּוּד א׳).
“this one destroyed, and this one sought to destroy” (Megillah 11a).
כִּי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר נִקְרָא ״רֹאשׁ״,
For Nebuchadnezzar is called “head,”
שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ לַמַּחֲרִיבִים,
being chief among the destroyers,
כִּי חֻרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
for the destruction of the Holy Temple
דּוֹמֶה לְחֻרְבַּן הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
is comparable to the destruction of the entire universe.
וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר,
And such a catastrophe is impossible,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּת דְּ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״.
except through the surging power of “the first of nations.”
וְכָל הָנֵי ״רֹאשׁ״
And all those designated as “head”

דְּנֶחְשַׁב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ1039 Esther Rabbah, Petichta 10 — R. Berechiah opened: “Who has wrought and done it, calling the generations from the beginning?” From the beginning of the world’s creation the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed for each and every one what befitted him. Adam was head of created beings; Kayin head of murderers; Hevel head of the murdered; Noach head of the saved; Avraham head of the circumcised; Yitzchak head of the bound; Yaakov head of the wholehearted; Yehudah head of the tribes; Yosef head of the pious; Aharon head of the priests; Moshe head of the prophets; Yehoshua head of the conquerors; Otniel head of those who apportioned; Shmuel head of those who anoint; Shaul head of the anointed; David head of the singers; Shlomo head of the builders; Nevuchadnezzar head of the destroyers; Achashverosh head of the sellers; Haman head of the buyers. And when they saw all this they began to cry “Woe!” — “And it came to pass in the days of Achashverosh.” (פְּתִיחָה דְּאֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה),
enumerated in the Midrash (Esther Rabbah, Petichta),
הוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הָרֵאשִׁית וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
stem from the intensification of the first principle and root,
אִם בַּטּוֹב אוֹ בְּהֵפֶךְ.
whether on the side of good or its opposite.
וַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ נַעֲשָׂה ״רֹאשׁ לַמּוֹכְרִים״,
Ahasuerus became the “chief of sellers,”
וְזֶהוּ ״שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַחֲרִיב״,
and this is why he is described as one who “sought to destroy”;
כִּי הוּא נִמְשַׁל
for he is compared

לְבַעַל הַתֵּל וּבַעַל הֶחָרִיץ1040 Megillah 14a — To what may Achashverosh and Haman be compared? To two men, one of whom had a mound in the middle of his field and the other a ditch in the middle of his. The owner of the ditch said: Who will give me this mound for money? And the owner of the mound said: Who will give me this ditch for money? In time they met. The owner of the ditch said to the owner of the mound: Sell me your mound. He said to him: Take it for nothing — and would that you had taken it long ago. Rashi: That is to say, one may learn from Ahasuerus that he too had it in mind to destroy them. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): Haman's offer of ten thousand talents, and the king's reply, "The silver is given to you, and the people also, to do with them as seems good to you," are exactly the parable: "Sell me your mound," and the answer, "Take it for nothing." Ahasuerus is the owner of the mound — the mound being Israel, whom he had no wish to keep — and Haman is the owner of the ditch and pit, who wanted the mound only to cast it into his pit; and in him was fulfilled "He who digs a pit shall fall into it." Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:9): Ahasuerus, like the rest of the four kingdoms, was opposed to Israel, and so to him Israel were like a mound in the middle of a man's field, something superfluous that does not belong to him, for Israel have no part in the kingdom of the nations; yet a mound does the owner of the field no harm, and a king — above all one who, like Ahasuerus, reigned over the whole world, his kingship coming to him from the Holy One, blessed be He — exists to sustain all things, so that reason does not allow destruction to come from him. The ditch, however, is a pit, a thing of lack and privation, and to Haman Israel were reckoned a pit. It was Haman who took them out of the domain of Ahasuerus, as Scripture says, "when a man rose up against us" — a man and not a king: for a king is there to sustain existence, whereas a man, on the contrary, seeks to destroy his fellow. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Emor 3): Haman's decree was something that had never entered anyone's mind: oppressors such as Sennacherib and Nebuchadnezzar exiled Israel, but who had ever heard of handing over an entire nation to slaughter for nothing? Even Achashverosh, in whose heart it had arisen, as the Gemara says in the parable of the owner of the mound and the owner of the ditch, could not bring it to his lips until Haman came. (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״ד עַמּוּד א׳),
to the owner of the mound and the owner of the ditch (Megillah 14a),
שֶׁהוּא נֶהֱנֶה מְאֹד מִדָּבָר זֶה,
who thoroughly relished this transaction,
אֲבָל לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּעַצְמוֹ — לֹא הָיָה יָכֹל.
yet to execute it on his own—he was unable.
כִּי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר
For Nebuchadnezzar
הֶחֱרִיב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
destroyed the Holy Temple,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה בַּפּוֹעַל,
which was the tangible, revealed presence of the Shechinah,
וְהִגְלָם מֵאַרְצָם,
and exiled them from their land,
שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בְּמַדְרֵגַת שֵׁנָה.
so that they entered a state resembling sleep.
וּלְהַחֲרִיב גַּם זֶה —
And to annihilate even this hidden vitality—
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּטּוּל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
could only be done by nullifying the core root itself,
שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר,
which is an absolute impossibility;
רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁחָשַׁב
it could only be attempted because he thought
לְהַגְבִּיר הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּרַע,
to empower the root of evil
וּלְהַגְדִּיל לְהָמָן,
by exalting Haman,
וְהוּא יִמְכְּרֵם לוֹ,
and selling Israel to him,
שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיּוּכַל לָהֶם בָּזֶה.
imagining that Haman might prevail over them in this manner.
וְזֶהוּ רַק ״שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַחֲרִיב״,
This is why the text specifies only that he “sought to destroy,”
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת דָּבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלַל,
because in absolute truth this is impossible,
וּמֵעוֹלָם לֹא הָיוּ עֲבָדִים לַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
and they were never true slaves to Ahasuerus,
רַק בְּדָבָר הַנּוֹגֵעַ לַגּוּף —
except in matters pertaining strictly to the body,
לְמִסִּים וְאַרְנוֹנוֹת,
such as taxes and civic levies,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ל״ג)1041 Vayikra Rabbah 33:6 — Immediately, "Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego answered and said to the king: Nebuchadnezzar." If "king," why "Nebuchadnezzar"? And if "Nebuchadnezzar," why "king"? Rather: in tributes, levies, fines and head-taxes you are king over us; but as for this thing you tell us — Nebuchadnezzar you are, and Nebuchadnezzar is your name; you and a dog are worth the same to us..
as Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah told Nebuchadnezzar (Vayikra Rabbah 33).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם
Nevertheless,
נִקְרָא הוּא ״רֹאשׁ לַמּוֹכְרִים״,
he is called “chief of sellers,”
שֶׁמְּכִירָתוֹ הוּא מִצַּד
because his act of selling arose from
הִתְגַּבְּרוּת כֹּחַ הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם דַּעֲמָלֵק בּוֹ.
the intensification of Amalek's “first of nations” force within him.
וְהָמָן, שֶׁהוּא עֲמָלֵק עַצְמוֹ,
And Haman, who is Amalek personified,
הוּא ״הָרֹאשׁ לַקּוֹנִים״,
is the “chief of buyers,”
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל כַּוָּנַת הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם:
for this is the overarching aim of the first of nations:
לִשְׁלֹט בְּרֵאשִׁית דִּקְדֻשָּׁה,
to dominate the holy first principle—
הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״רֵאשִׁית״,
namely Israel, who are termed “first”—
וְהִמְצִיא זֶה דֶּרֶךְ קִנְיָן.
and he sought to execute this by legal acquisition.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״ג1042 Megillah 13b — "If it please the king, let it be written that they be destroyed, and ten thousand talents of silver" (Esther 3:9). Reish Lakish said: It was revealed and known before Him who spoke and the world came into being that Haman was destined to weigh out shekels against Israel; therefore He caused their shekels to precede his shekels. And this is what we learned: On the first of Adar announcement is made concerning the shekels and concerning the diverse kinds. Rashi: “Announcement is made” — the court proclaims that the shekels are to be brought to the Temple. “And concerning the diverse kinds” — the seeds have grown somewhat and their sprouting is recognizable, and they are uprooted from the fields at the court’s proclamation. Maharsha: The ten thousand talents of silver come to a half-shekel for each of Israel, as Tosafot writes further on. The time for giving the shekels — before the New Moon of Nisan, so that the offerings may be brought from the new contribution — is explicit in the Torah; but that announcement is made about them on the first of Adar is not, for the Sages fixed that the proclamation be made thirty days beforehand. Accordingly, “He caused their shekels to precede his shekels” refers to the proclamation made about them. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:9): The shekels that Israel give are for the offerings, and the offerings are as though a man offered himself to the Holy One, blessed be He; the giving of the shekels is therefore as though one gave himself to Him, so that Israel then belong wholly to the Holy One, blessed be He — and how could they be handed over to Haman, when they have already been delivered to Him? Therefore He set their shekels before the shekels of Haman, who was paying shekels to the king to buy them, and this availed him nothing, for through the giving of the shekels they already belonged wholly to the Holy One, blessed be He. Since Israel were under Ahasuerus and Haman was buying them from him, a purchase meant, Heaven forfend, to destroy them utterly, the Holy One, blessed be He, set their shekels first, so that it would be known that Israel are His and Haman could not acquire them. עַמּוּד ב׳):
And the Sages of blessed memory taught (Megillah 13b):
דְּהַשְּׁקָלִים כִּפְּרוּ עַל זֶה,
that Israel's half-shekels atoned for and neutralized this plot;
דְּעִנְיַן הַשְּׁקָלִים —
for the essence of the shekels
שֶׁהֵם כֹּפֶר נֶפֶשׁ,
is that they serve as a ransom for the soul.
כִּי הַמָּמוֹן נִקְרָא ״יְקוּם״,
For wealth is termed yekum,

שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד הָאָדָם עַל רַגְלָיו (מַסֶּכֶת פְּסָחִים קי״ט1043 Pesachim 119a — "Riches kept by their owner to his hurt" — R. Shimon ben Lakish said: This is the wealth of Korah. "And all the substance that was at their feet" — R. Elazar said: This is a man's money, which stands him upon his feet. Rashi (Rashbam): "Which stands him upon his feet" — for it gladdens his heart. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael 35): That which sustains a man is his livelihood, and his money is a man's standing, as it is written, "and all the substance that was at their feet" — this is a man's money. עַמּוּד א׳),
which establishes a person upon his feet (Pesachim 119a),
וְהוּא מוֹסֵר זֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and the Jew surrenders this to the blessed Hashem,
לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו הַגּוּפָנִיִּם
proclaiming that all of his physical capacities
גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
likewise emanate from the blessed Hashem.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה
And through this,
אָנוּ עֲבָדָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
we are servants to the Blessed One,
וְלֹא עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים כְּלַל.
and by no means servants to other servants.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהִקְדִּים שִׁקְלֵיהֶם לִשְׁקָלָיו,
This is why He caused their shekels to precede Haman's shekels,
לִהְיוֹת קִנְיָנוֹ קוֹדֵם,
so that His acquisition came first,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָחוּל קִנְיָן אַחֵר.
making it impossible for any subsequent acquisition to take effect.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ז1044 Esther Rabbah 7:13 — [Elijah] said to him: A letter of annihilation has already been written against Israel. Moses said to him: If it is sealed with clay, our prayer is heard; but if it was sealed with blood, what has been, is. He said to him: With clay it is sealed. Moses our teacher said to him: Go and inform Mordechai.׳):
And this is the import of what the Sages stated (Esther Rabbah 7):
שֶׁנֶּחְתַּם בְּחוֹתָם שֶׁל טִיט,
that the decree was sealed with a seal of clay,
וְלֹא בְּחוֹתָם שֶׁל דָּם.
and not with a seal of blood.
כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
For blood represents the soul,
וְהַטִּיט הוּא הַגּוּף,
while clay represents the physical body,
שֶׁנּוֹצַר עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה.
formed from the dust of the earth.
וְכָל שְׁלִיטַת הָעַבְדוּת
And all dominion of slavery
דְּיֵשׁ קִנְיָן לַגּוּף —
in which a purchaser acquires the body—
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַגּוּף,
applies strictly to the physical frame,
וְלֹא מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
and not to the soul,
אֲפִילּוּ נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית,
not even to the animal soul,
דְּהַיְינוּ שִׁעְבּוּד הַכֹּחוֹת
meaning the subjugation of its faculties
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל עֲבָדִים.
in the manner that exists in ordinary servitude.
וּמִמֵּילָא לֹא יוֹעִיל קִנְיַן הָמָן,
Consequently, Haman's intended transaction was ineffective,
שֶׁהָיָה עִקַּר כַּוָּנָתוֹ
since his primary objective was
שִׁעְבּוּד הַכֹּחוֹת,
the spiritual subjugation of their inner powers,
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר.
and that is impossible.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
Nevertheless,
מִצַּד שִׁעְבּוּד הַגּוּף
from the perspective of bodily subjection
הָיָה גְּזֵרָה לְמַרְאִית עַיִן,
there was an apparent decree,
שֶׁהוּא הַחוֹתָם שֶׁל טִיט.
which is the seal of clay.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״ב1045 Megillah 12a — [R. Shimon ben Yochai said that the Jews of that generation were liable to destruction because they had prostrated themselves to the image.] They said to him: But is there favoritism in the matter [that they were nevertheless delivered]? He said to them: They did it only for appearance's sake, and so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only for appearance's sake. And this is what is written: "For He does not afflict from His heart" (Lamentations 3:33). Rashi: "But is there favoritism in the matter?" — that is, how then did they merit a miracle? "They did it only for appearance's sake" — out of fear. Maharsha: That is, they acted so only from fear of being killed, as is set out in the book of Daniel, and did not intend in their hearts to serve the idol; so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only outwardly, frightening them that they deserved destruction so that they should take alarm and repent on that account. And this is the sense of "For He does not afflict from His heart": when a man commits a transgression with his heart not in it, the Holy One, blessed be He, "grieves the children of men" only in order that he should repent and be delivered from the trouble. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 33): Though the Jews were only joining gentiles at a single feast, the Gemara calls this "serving idols in purity," and this was the accusation: that they took pleasure in the feast of that wicked man, which is a trace of idolatry, and likewise that they bowed to the image — though it was only a [royal] statue and they did it only for appearance's sake, it is nevertheless a trace of idolatry, and "round about Him it storms greatly" [He is exacting with those near Him]. Because they then purified themselves in this matter until they had slaughtered the inclination to idolatry entirely, the Blessed One wished to establish a feast for them, to show that even in their drunkenness they need fear nothing, their hearts being already whole with Him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The acceptance of the Torah in the days of Ahasuerus, though out of love, was in concealment, for in what was revealed there were claims against them, as the Sages said that "they did it only for appearance's sake" — that is, only in the outward, revealed deed, while the inwardness of their heart is for God. This was the redemption of that time, which made clear concerning Israel's sins that even when they sin, the inwardness of their heart is for Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 255): The Megillah opens with the feast because the decree sprouted from it, as the Sages said, "because they took pleasure"; and although the Gemara concludes that it was because they bowed to the image, they were not punished for that at the time, since in truth they did it only for appearance's sake, and "the Lord sees into the heart" — there was sin only from the human side, for "man sees what is before the eyes." As long as they conduct themselves with a generous eye, the Blessed One too has a generous eye toward them, bestowing on them by His measure of "seeing into the heart"; but on account of "they took pleasure" — the incitement of the power of the narrow eye — the Blessed One too said, "Mine is mine and yours is yours," judging by what is before the eyes. עַמּוּד א׳):
And this is what they taught (Megillah 12a):
דְּלֹא נַעֲשָׂה רַק לִפְנִים,
that the decree was enacted only outwardly,
דְּמֵעוֹלָם לֹא הָיָה גְּזֵרָה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלַל,
for in absolute truth no genuine decree ever existed,
כִּי זֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלַל,
because such destruction is fundamentally impossible;

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״אִם״ וְגוֹמֵר ״כֵּן״ וְגוֹמֵר1046 Jeremiah 33:19-22 — “And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: Thus says the Lord — if you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night should not come in their season, then also My covenant with David My servant may be broken … As the host of heaven cannot be counted nor the sand of the sea measured, so will I multiply the seed of David My servant.” Rashi: "If you can break My covenant with the day" — if you are able to annul the covenant I made with the day and with the night that they be in their season, which I made with Noah and his sons: "and day and night shall not cease." Radak: If you can annul the covenant I made with Noah and his sons, "while the earth remains… day and night shall not cease" — then My covenant with David might be annulled too. But just as that covenant is never broken and never ceases, so the covenant I made with David that his kingship endure will not be annulled, nor the covenant I made with Aaron and his sons. "In their season" means according to the order of the seasons. Metzudas Dovid: "If you can break" — if you are able to annul the covenant I established with the day and the night, that they not be at the times I fixed for them — then My covenant with David would also be broken, that he have a son reigning on his throne, and so too the covenant with the priests, the sons of Levi, who minister to Me. Just as it is not in your power to annul the covenant with day and night, so it is impossible for the covenant with David and with the priests to be annulled. "Which cannot be numbered" — as the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured for their sheer quantity, so will I multiply the seed of David and the priests of the sons of Levi. Malbim: He explains that the covenant of kingship and of priesthood is as necessary to the continuance of the whole of existence as the laws of nature are. Just as it is impossible for Him to annul His covenant with existence as a whole, so it is impossible for Him to annul the covenant of kingship and priesthood — neither to abolish them altogether, since He will not break His covenant with day and night, nor to let the appointed time of the redemption pass without their coming, just as day and night cannot fail to be in their season.,
as Scripture indicates in the covenantal oaths,
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and as the Sages of blessed memory taught

בְּמַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית (ג1047 Taanit 3b — From where do we know that the winds are never withheld? R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: For Scripture says, "For as the four winds of the heavens I have spread you abroad, says the Lord." What is He saying to them? If you say the Holy One, blessed be He, is saying to Israel that He scattered them to the four winds of the world — then it should have said "to the four" rather than "as the four." Rather, this is what He is saying: Just as the world cannot exist without winds, so the world cannot exist without Israel. Rashi: "Just as the world cannot exist without winds": for it would not endure because of the excess of vapor and heat. "Without Israel": for the world endures only for the sake of Israel; and this is what the verse says — "For as the four winds of the heavens I have spread you," [that is,] to the winds of the world, so that it may endure, as it is said: "If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth" (Jeremiah 33:25). Maharsha (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 10b): The derasha gives the reason they are scattered: because they are the existence of the world, like the winds. Rashi explains in the first chapter of Taanit that without winds the world would not endure the excess of vapor and heat; but by the analogy it seems that the winds sustain the dry land, for wind dries the earth, and without it the whole world would by nature be water upon water, as it is written of the Flood, "And God made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters subsided" (Genesis 8:1). So too Israel: without them the world would revert to chaos and void; and by His spreading and scattering them to the four winds of the world, His faith and His Torah became known throughout the world — and that is the world's existence. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 10b): Scripture says "as the four winds," not "in the four winds," which would imply only that Israel are [scattered] in the four directions: it likens Israel to the four winds, which are the whole world — just as [the world] cannot be without the four winds, so Israel are the essence of the world and it cannot be without them; and it is fitting that what is the whole world should have its place in all four directions, from which itself it follows that Israel cannot be destroyed, for they are the whole world, and the whole world cannot be destroyed. One may also explain "without winds" as wind proper, for man and every living creature cannot exist without it — wind is but the blowing of the cool air by which everything subsists; as the winds are the existence of the world, so are Israel, and therefore He scattered them to the four winds. Thus the very dispersion of their exile to the four ends of the world attests to their high standing.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
in Tractate Taanit (3b)
עַל פָּסוּק: ״כְּאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת״ —
on the verse: “as the four winds”—
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that the universe cannot exist without Israel;
שֶׁהוּא אַחַר הַגָּלוּת בְּאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת,
meaning that even after being dispersed to the four corners of the earth,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְאַבְּדָם כְּלַל.
it remains entirely impossible to destroy them.
וְקִבַּלְתִּי
And I have received a tradition
דְּהַסַּנְהֶדְרִין וְכָל אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
that the Sanhedrin and all the Men of the Great Assembly
שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
of that generation
יָדְעוּ הָאֱמֶת,
knew the underlying truth,
שֶׁהוּא רַק גְּזֵרָה לִפְנִים,
that this was only an outward decree,
וְלֹא עָשׂוּ חֶשְׁבּוֹן מִזֶּה כְּלַל;
and they paid no serious heed to it at all;
רַק מָרְדֳּכַי,
only Mordechai,
דְּנֶעְלַם מִמֶּנּוּ עִנְיָן זֶה,
from whom this inner secret was concealed,
הוּא שֶׁזָּעַק וְהִזְעִיק עַל הָעִנְיָן,
was the one who cried out and rallied the people over it;
כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי.
thus I heard.
וְהָעִנְיָן —
And the deeper meaning is
דְּרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that Hashem, blessed be He, desired
לְהַעֲלִים זֶה מִמָּרְדֳּכַי,
to conceal this from Mordechai,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל וְיַרְעִישׁ עַל זֶה,
in order that he should pray and arouse a great spiritual outcry over it;
וְהוֹדִיעוּהוּ זֶה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
and they subsequently revealed this to him through Divine inspiration,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ז1048 Esther Rabbah 7:13 — Elijah turned back and said to Moses: O faithful shepherd, how many times did you stand in the breach for Israel and annul the decree against them, that they not be destroyed. What will you answer to this trouble? Moses said to him: Is there any fit man in that generation? He said to him: There is, and his name is Mordechai. He said to him: Go and inform him, so that he may stand there in prayer and I here, and we shall plead for mercy for them before the Holy One, blessed be He. He went at once and informed Mordechai, as it is written: "And Mordechai knew all that had been done, and Mordechai rent his garments."׳)
as the Sages of blessed memory expounded (Esther Rabbah 7)
עַל פָּסוּק: ״וּמָרְדֳּכַי יָדַע״.
on the verse: “And Mordechai knew.”
הַיְינוּ כִּי כָּל כַּוָּנַת הָעִנְיָן
That is, the entire purpose
שֶׁנִּתְגַּדֵּל הָמָן,
of Haman's elevation
הָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי זֶה
was so that through this very process
מְחִיָּתוֹ וּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק,
his own eradication and the destruction of Amalek would occur,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֱלֹהִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק, זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
in accordance with what the divine Rabbi Isaac (the Ari), of blessed memory, wrote
עַל פָּסוּק: ״עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ״ —
on the verse: “a time when man rules over man to his harm”—
״אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל״ בְּ״אָדָם דִּקְדֻשָּׁה״,
namely, the “wicked man” ruling over the “holy man,”
״לְרַע לוֹ״ — לָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל.
which results “to his harm”—to the ruin of the wicked man himself.
כִּי אוֹתָהּ גְּזֵרָה דְּהָמָן עַצְמָהּ
For that very decree of Haman
גָּרְמָה לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ,
caused the reversal,
שֶׁהֻצְרְכוּ לְקַיֵּם ״כְּתָב הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר אֵין לְהָשִׁיב״,
since they had to uphold “the king's writing that cannot be revoked,”
לוֹמַר דְּהַכַּוָּנָה הָיָה בְּהֵפֶךְ,
declaring that the original intent had actually been the reverse,
וְהָמָן עִקֵּם הַדְּבָרִים.
and that Haman had distorted the matter.
וְכֵן הָעֵץ אֲשֶׁר הֵכִין לְמָרְדֳּכַי
Likewise, the gallows that he prepared for Mordechai
גָּרַם לוֹ לְהִתָּלוֹת עָלָיו,
caused him to be hanged upon it;
בְּאֹפֶן דְּהַשְּׁלִיטָה שֶׁלּוֹ
so that his brief dominion
הָיָה הַכֹּל לְרַע לוֹ,
functioned entirely to his own detriment,
וְכֵן עָשְׁרוֹ הָיָה שָׁמוּר לוֹ לְרָעָתוֹ.
and his wealth was similarly preserved for his misfortune.
וְלִהְיוֹת הוּא הַגּוֹרֵם לָזֶה,
And because Mordechai was the prime catalyst for this,
דְּאִיקְנֵי בֵּיהּ הָמָן,
inciting Haman's jealousy,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה י״ג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א1049 Megillah 13a — Rava said: The congregation of Israel said the reverse — "See what a Judean did to me and how a Benjaminite repaid me." What a Judean did to me — that David did not kill Shimei, from whom Mordecai was born, of whom Haman was jealous. And how a Benjaminite repaid me — that Saul did not kill Agag, from whom Haman was born, who caused Israel suffering. Rashi (12b, s.v. “the reverse”): “The reverse” — that is, as a cry of complaint and not as praise: a Judean man and a Benjaminite man brought this suffering upon me. Maharsha (12b): The phrase “how a Benjaminite repaid me” seems imprecise, for what repayment is there here? At first sight one would say that the Judean, David, did a good deed in not killing Shimei, from whom Mordecai was born, who brought the redemption by his prayer, and that the Benjaminite — Mordecai — repaid and repaired what Saul had spoiled in not killing Agag. The congregation of Israel says the reverse: the Judean repaired nothing by bringing it about that Mordecai was born, for had there been no Mordecai there would have been no calamity at all, since Haman was jealous of Mordecai alone; and the Benjaminite likewise made no repayment for what Saul spoiled, since had Saul killed Agag, Haman would never have been born. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 2:5): In Rava's view the redemption came about solely on account of Israel as a whole, who were worthy of it, and not on account of the tribes, for in the tribes there was a disposition toward the calamity. Judah is the tribe to which dominion belongs and which seeks it, and because Mordecai, "a Judean man," would not bow to Haman, Haman grew jealous of him and sought to rule over him; Benjamin, the smallest of the tribes, has less of dominion, so that Saul, "a Benjaminite man," did not master Agag to put him to death but granted him life. Thus, on the contrary, it was through the tribes that Haman's opposition arose, and the redemption came from the Holy One, blessed be He, who delivered them from his hand.׳):
as the Sages of blessed memory noted (Megillah 13a):
״מַה עָשָׂה לִי יְהוּדִי״ וְכוּלֵי.
“What has this Jew done to me...”
וְהַגַּם דְּהַתַּכְלִית הָיָה לְטוֹב,
And although the ultimate outcome was good,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְפִי שָׁעָה,
nevertheless, for the time being,
אוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ הַסּוֹף —
to those who did not know the final outcome—
הָיָה אֵבֶל גָּדוֹל לָהֶם.
it was an occasion of great grief.
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה מִמִּשְׁפָּטוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
Therefore it was part of His righteous judgment
שֶׁיִּסְבֹּל מָרְדֳּכַי גַּם כֵּן מִצַּעַר זֶה,
that Mordechai too should endure this intense anguish;
וְגַם תְּמוּרַת זֶה
and in compensation for this,
הוּא יִהְיֶה הַגּוֹרֵם לְנִצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק דְּאַחַר כָּךְ גַּם כֵּן,
he would also become the agent of Amalek's eventual vanquishing,
וְלוֹ נִתַּן כָּל בֵּית הָמָן.
and to him was given Haman's entire estate.
כִּי זֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הַזְּעָקָה שֶׁלּוֹ,
For this unfolded through his outcry,
וְכָל הַיְּהוּדִים נִקְרְאוּ אָז ״עַם מָרְדֳּכַי״,
and all Jews were then referred to as “the people of Mordechai,”
כֻּלָּם טְפֵלִים לוֹ,
all being secondary to him,
וְהוּא הָעִקָּר בַּתְּחִלָּה וְסוֹף.
while he remained primary from beginning to end.
וְגַם מַה דְּאִיקְנֵי בֵּיהּ הָמָן —
Furthermore, Haman's jealousy of him
זֶהוּ הַגּוֹרֵם הַיְשׁוּעָה;
became the very catalyst for the deliverance;
שֶׁמַּה דְּלֹא יִכְרַע וְלֹא יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה,
for Mordechai's refusal to bow and prostrate,
גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ אִסּוּר מִצַּד הַדִּין.
was not strictly forbidden by the letter of the law.

וּלְפִי מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ג׳, וְזֹהַר, חֵלֶק ג׳, ק״ט עַמּוּד א1050 Esther Rabbah 3:10 — R. Yudan and R. Levi in the name of R. Yochanan: Wherever it is said in this scroll "King Ahasuerus," Scripture is speaking of King Ahasuerus; but wherever it says "the king" without qualification, the word serves both the sacred and the profane [that is, it may refer to the King of Kings]. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): The Sages said that wherever "the king" appears without qualification it speaks of the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, by virtue of His clothing Himself in Ahasuerus to bestow [His bounty]. This is the reason for Mordechai's intention to save him from Bigsan and Teresh: even in the height of the darkness he understood the purpose of all that was happening, that Esther's being taken by Ahasuerus was no accident, and that everything was truly by the providence of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 6): The Sages said, "No one knew how to slander like Haman," and the Midrash says that every unqualified "king" speaks of the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He; if so, all his words, "it is not worthwhile for the king to tolerate them" and "I will weigh out into the king's treasuries," were directed on high. He first accused them of their sins, [claiming] that they had already entirely corrupted the whole stature of man. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 2): "No one knew how to slander like Haman" refers not to his slandering and disparaging Israel before Ahasuerus but to his accusing Israel before the Blessed One, saying, "and they do not keep the king's laws," for wherever the Megillah says "the king" without qualification, Scripture speaks of the King of the kings of kings. His accusation concerned Daniel's decree against their bread, wine and daughters: Haman judged that it was not from the law and command of the King, the Holy One, blessed be He, and claimed they did it only out of haughtiness. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): Through Esther's feast Mordechai attained the holiness of the World to Come, going out "in royal apparel," for even in his garment he cleaved wholly to the kingdom of Heaven: every unqualified "king" in Esther speaks of the King of the kings of kings, as they said in the Midrash, and likewise unqualified "royalty," as they said in the Megillah on "And Esther clothed herself in royalty," that the holy spirit clothed her, that is, the kingdom of Heaven.׳)
And according to the Midrash (Esther Rabbah 3) and Zohar (III, 109a),
דְּכָל מָקוֹם ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״ סְתָם —
that wherever the Megillah mentions “the king” without specification,
בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים מְדַבֵּר,
it alludes to the King of kings,
וַדַּאי בְּכָל הַמְּגִלָּה כֵּן.
this applies throughout the entire Megillah.
וְאִם כֵּן, גַּם מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב:
If so, what is written:
״וְכָל עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ כּוֹרְעִים״ וְגוֹמֵר,
“And all the king's servants who were in the king's gate bowed...”
הַכַּוָּנָה: עַל עַבְדֵי מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
refers to the servants of the Sovereign of the universe,
הַיּוֹשְׁבִים בַּשַּׁעַר — הֵם הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין,
who sit in the gate—namely the Sanhedrin;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּבַכָּתוּב בְּכָל מָקוֹם,
as it is known that throughout Scripture,
הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין נִקְרָאִים ״יוֹשְׁבִים בַּשַּׁעַר״,
the Sanhedrin are called “those who sit in the gate,”
רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ,
meaning at the King's gate,
שֶׁשָּׁם דָּנִין דִּינֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
where the King's laws are adjudicated.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהַסַּנְהֶדְרִין יוֹשְׁבִים —
And wherever the Sanhedrin sits,
נִקְרָאִים שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִים בַּשַּׁעַר;
they are designated as “sitting in the gate”;
וְגַם מָרְדֳּכַי מֵהַיּוֹשְׁבִים בַּשַּׁעַר,
and Mordechai was among those sitting in the gate,
שֶׁגַּם הוּא אָז מִכְּלַל הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין,
for he was then a member of the Sanhedrin,
דְּרַק אַחַר כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
and only later did some withdraw from him.
וּמִצַּד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִשְׁפַּט הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין —
From the perspective of Torah law and the Sanhedrin's jurisprudence,
אָסוּר לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בְּרָשָׁע שֶׁהַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ,
it is forbidden to provoke a wicked person while fortune smiles upon him,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ז1051 Berakhot 7b — R. Yitzchak said: If you see a wicked man upon whom the hour smiles, do not provoke him, as it is stated: "His ways prosper at all times" (Psalms 10:5). And not only that, but he prevails in judgment, as it is stated: "Your judgments are far above, out of his sight." And not only that, but he sees the downfall of his foes, as it is stated: "As for all his adversaries, he snorts at them." Rashi: "His ways prosper" — they succeed. "Your judgments are far above, out of his sight" — Your judgments are removed to a distance from him. "He snorts at them" — with his breath he drives them off like straw. Maharsha: His fortune is certainly only for the hour, as that passage says, "they shall soon wither like grass," "yet a little while and the wicked is no more" — it is the luck of the hour that brings it about; and "his ways prosper at all times" likewise means all that time in which he prospers by his fortune. It is from the words "at all times" that R. Yitzchak inferred that one must beware of him, both at law and in provoking him, for the whole time that his ways prosper through the fortune of the hour. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaShalom 3): These teachings come to make plain that strife is a thoroughly ugly trait, but that it is not ugly in every setting, for contention with the wicked and with those who abandon the Torah is good; and when the matter is one of Heaven, a man may provoke the wicked, so long as the hour is not smiling upon him. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Thirteen Principles of Conduct 12): One upon whom the hour smiles prevails in the judgment of Heaven, being judged as righteous for the time being. So too in human judgment, pleading for mercy is effective even before a court and a Sanhedrin, for through it he may prevail in judgment: not that they will pervert the judgment, but that their eyes will be opened to find merit, since in every matter there is a scale of merit and a scale of guilt. And now that there is no Sanhedrin, Heavenly judgment, the judgment of the four death penalties and other punishments have still not ceased, and through mercy he prevails in judgment and goes free.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳),
as the Sages taught in Berakhot (7b),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
and as recorded in the Midrash
טַעֲנַת הָמָן מִיַּעֲקֹב,
regarding Haman's argument from Jacob,
דְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לְעֵשָׂו.
who bowed down to Esau.
וּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ: דְּבִנְיָמִין לֹא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה,
Mordechai's reply was: Benjamin did not bow down;
אַף דְּעַדַיִן לֹא נוֹלַד,
for although he was not yet born,
הַכַּוָּנָה דְּסוֹף סוֹף
the meaning is that ultimately,
אֵין בּוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ
there was not in his spiritual root
אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַהַכְנָעָה לָרָשָׁע.
that capacity for submission to the wicked.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא בָּזֶה ״יְמִינִי״
Therefore Mordechai is designated a “Yemini”
עַל שֵׁם בִּנְיָמִין,
after Benjamin,
דְּבָא מִכֹּחוֹ בָּזֶה.
since he drew his unyielding strength from him.
וּבְעֵינֵי הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין — לֹא יָשְׁרוּ מַעֲשָׂיו.
In the eyes of the Sanhedrin, his actions were improper.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְפִי כַּוָּנַת מָרְדֳּכַי,
Nevertheless, according to Mordechai's pure intent,
הָיָה זֶה לְקִדּוּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
this stance was for the sanctification of the Divine Name,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה,
in the manner of Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
דְּיֵימְרוּ: ״יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא סָגְדִין״,
so people would proclaim: “Israel does not bow down!”
וּלְהַרְאוֹת הֵפֶךְ מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הָמָן:
and to demonstrate the exact opposite of Haman's belief:
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגַּם הֵם עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
that even though they were subjects of Ahasuerus,
אֵינָן עֲבָדִים גְּמוּרִים כְּכָל עֲבָדִים כְּלַל.
they were by no means absolute slaves like ordinary chattel.
וְגַם אַחַר כָּךְ
Later on as well,
הַחֲכָמִים בְּשִׁיטָתַיְהוּ אָזְלֵי,
the Sages remained steadfast in their cautious approach,

שֶׁהֱשִׁיבוּ לְאֶסְתֵּר1052 Megillah 7a — Esther sent to the Sages: Establish me for the generations. They sent back to her: You will arouse the envy of the nations against us. She sent to them: I am already written in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Rashi: "She sent to them" — in the second year, to establish it upon them as an obligation; "establish me" — as a festival and for the reading, that I may have a name thereby. "You are arousing envy against us" — for the nations will say that we rejoice to recall their downfall; and to this she answered that she is already written [in their chronicles], and there they will see what befell them at the hands of Israel. Maharsha: This whole exchange is already intimated in the verses: first "And Mordecai wrote… to enjoin upon them that they should keep [these days]" (Esther 9:20–21), and they would not accept it, because of "you are arousing envy"; then "And Esther wrote… to confirm this second letter of Purim" and "he sent letters" (Esther 9:29–30), which close by saying that envy need not be feared, for they are "words of peace and truth." And her reply is the verse "are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia" (Esther 10:2). (מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳):
replying to Esther (Megillah 7a):
״קִנְאָה אַתְּ מְעוֹרֶרֶת״ וְכוּלֵי,
“You are arousing jealousy against us among the nations...”
שֶׁחֲשָׁבוּהָ דְּאָזְלָה בְּשִׁיטַת מָרְדֳּכַי,
for they presumed she was following Mordechai's assertive approach
שֶׁלֹּא לָחוּשׁ מַה דְּאִיקְנֵי בֵּיהּ.
of disregarding the envy of enemies.
וּבֶאֱמֶת, אֵין זֶה רָאוּי
In truth, provocative actions are inappropriate
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בַּגָּלוּת,
as long as Israel remains in exile,
עַד שֶׁהֵשִׁיבָה לָהֶם: ״כְּבָר״ וְכוּלֵי,
until she answered them: “It is already written...”
שֶׁאֵין בָּזֶה חֲשַׁשׁ קִנְאָה.
showing there was no fear of inciting new jealousy.
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר
This explains why
דִּלְעִנְיַן זֶה נִכְתַּב בְּסוֹף הַמְּגִלָּה:
at the conclusion of the Megillah it states:
״וְכָל״ וְגוֹמֵר ״פָּרָשַׁת״ וְגוֹמֵר ״כְּתוּבִים״ וְגוֹמֵר,
“And all the acts of his power... are written in the book of the chronicles...”
לְהוֹדִיעַ זֶה,
to demonstrate this fact:
דִּכְבָר כָּתוּב גַּם שָׁם.
that it was already recorded in Persian state archives.
וּפְשׁוּטוֹ —
And in its plain historical sense,
גַּם מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״מַעֲשֵׂה תָּקְפּוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ״,
what is written, “the acts of his power and might,”
דְּקָאֵי עַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
refers to Ahasuerus;
וְכֵן מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וַיָּשֶׂם מַס״ וְגוֹמֵר,
and likewise: “The king imposed a tax...”
שֶׁאֵין זֶה מִצּוֹרֶךְ הַנֵּס,
which is not strictly needed for the narrative of the miracle,
נִכְתַּב גַּם כֵּן מִפְּנֵי הָאוּמּוֹת,
was also included on account of the nations,
כְּאִלּוּ הַמְּגִלָּה נִכְתְּבָה לִכְבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
as though the scroll were chronicled in honor of Ahasuerus,

Half the kingdom, but not the whole kingdom, and not a thing that forms a barrier to the kingdom. And what is that? The building of the Temple. Rashi (s.v. "and not a thing that forms a barrier to the kingdom"): The building of the Temple, which stands at the middle of the world, as we say in Tractate Yoma: the foundation stone, from which the world was founded. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): He certainly did not mean that he would hand over half the kingdom itself, for it is not the way of a king to give half his kingdom to another, still less to his wife; he meant that he would grant a request that turns upon half the kingdom. And since the Gemara's word is "forms a barrier," it appears that they read "half" [chatzi] in the sense of "interposition" [chatzitzah] — that the building of the Temple would bring harm to the kingdom, as they wrote to the king in the days of Ezra of "that rebellious city, hurtful unto kings." Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 5:3): The Gemara too explains that the gift could only be something that does not reach the essence of the kingdom — just as, on the plain sense, a king who gave away more than half would no longer be king; and the Temple is the essence of the kingdom, so that granting it would be the annulment of Ahasuerus's kingdom. For Ahasuerus made his whole feast only once he declared that Israel would no longer be redeemed, since their kingdom annuls his. Hence "up to half the kingdom," and not the thing that is the whole kingdom, namely the Temple: were the Temple built, Israel would [again] be in their sovereignty, and the sovereignty of Israel annuls the kingdom of Ahasuerus, which is one of the four kingdoms that God, blessed be He, set in His world. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 8): It was truly then the appointed time of visitation, but because of Haman's accusation the Temple could not actually be built at that time, as they said, "half the kingdom, but not a thing that forms a barrier to the kingdom — the building of the Temple." בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין אִישׁוּת לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
in halachic reality no valid institution of marriage applies to idolaters,
וְלֹא תָּפְסֵי קִדּוּשֵׁי דִּידֵיהּ,
and his betrothal is null and void,
וְאֵין כָּאן קִנְיַן אִישׁוּת;
so there was no true marital ownership whatsoever;
וְהִיא, אַדְּרַבָּה, שָׁלְטָה בּוֹ
and she, on the contrary, dominated him
לַהֲרֹג אוֹהֲבוֹ מִפָּנֶיהָ,
to have his confidant Haman executed for her sake,
וְלִהְיוֹת, אַדְּרַבָּה, יִשְׂרָאֵל אָז
and to bring Israel, instead,
בְּתַכְלִית הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַכָּבוֹד,
to the peak of prominence and honor,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כֵּן לִפְנֵי שׁוּם מֶלֶךְ.
unmatched under any previous ruler.
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶׁכָּתַב בְּסֵפֶר יוֹסִיפוֹן,
And it is known what is written in Sefer Yosippon,
מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב דְּהַגִּבּוֹר מֵהַכֹּל —
stating that the mightiest of all forces
הִיא הָאִשָּׁה,
is woman,
שֶׁגַּם הַמֶּלֶךְ כָּפוּף לְפָנֶיהָ.
before whom even the king is subdued.
וְלֹא עוֹד,
Furthermore,
שֶׁהוֹלִידָה מִמֶּנּוּ בֵּן שֶׁמָּלַךְ אַחֲרָיו,
she bore him a son who reigned after him,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִקְרָא בְּנוֹ לְבַד,
who is not designated as Ahasuerus's son alone,
רַק בְּנָהּ גַּם כֵּן;
but also as Esther's son;
כִּי בֶּן יִשְׂרְאֵלִית מִן הַגּוֹי —
for the offspring of an Israelite woman by a gentile—
הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר,
is halachically a legitimate Jew,
וּמִתְיַחֵס אַחֲרֶיהָ גַּם כֵּן.
and traces maternal lineage to her.
וּלְדַעַת קְצָת פּוֹסְקִים —
And according to certain authorities,
צָרִיךְ טְבִילָה,
the child requires ritual immersion,
דְּנִקְרָא בֶּן גּוֹי גַּם כֵּן,
since he is partially associated with the gentile father;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר1059 Poked Akarim §5 — I have already written elsewhere that the statement "of the descendants of Haman …" does not mean that one of his offspring converted, for converts are not accepted from him. Rather, a gentile of his offspring came upon a Jewish woman by force and she conceived by him, and [the child] is called "of his descendants," just as Scripture calls the blasphemer "the son of the Egyptian" (Leviticus 24:10). Only "your son" born of a gentile woman is not called your son and is related to her alone; but the son of an Israelite woman by a gentile, whether one holds that the child is fit or that he is a mamzer, is related to both.
and as I wrote elsewhere,
דְּמִתְיַחֵס אַחַר שְׁנֵיהֶם,
that such an offspring has ties to both parents,
כִּדְאַשְׁכְּחַן בִּקְרָא דְּנִקְרָא:
as found in Scripture, where such a person is titled:
״בֶּן אִשָּׁה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית״
“the son of an Israelite woman”
וּ״בֶן אִישׁ מִצְרִי״.
and “the son of an Egyptian man.”
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And as the Sages of blessed memory noted
בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה שָׁם:
in Vayikra Rabbah there:
״דָּרְיָוֶשׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן, בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אֶסְתֵּר,
“The later Darius, son of Esther,
הָיָה טָהוֹר מֵאִמּוֹ
was pure from his mother
וְטָמֵא מֵאָבִיו״.
and impure from his father.”
וְאֵינוֹ כִּשְׁאָר אֻמּוֹת,
And this differs from unions among other nations,

דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת יְבָמוֹת ע״ח1060 Yevamot 78b — When Ravina came [from the Land of Israel] he said that R. Yochanan said: Among the nations, follow the male; once they have converted, follow whichever of the two is the more flawed. Rashi: "Among the nations": among the seven nations, with regard to "you shall let no soul live" (Deuteronomy 20:16), follow the males, as is explained below. "Once they have converted, follow the more flawed of the two": with regard to lineage, as is explained [below]. עַמּוּד ב׳):
where the Sages stated (Yevamot 78b):
״הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הַזָּכָר״
“Follow the male line”
בִּשְׁתֵּי אֻמּוֹת הַמִּזְדַּוְּגִים;
when two gentile nations intermarry;
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן אֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל —
whereas when another nation intermingles with Israel—
מִשְׁפָּט אַחֵר לָהֶם:
a unique halachic principle applies:
דִּבְגוֹיָה — וַלְדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ,
with a gentile woman, the child takes her status;
וּבְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית — הַוָּלָד מִתְיַחֵס אַחַר שְׁנֵיהֶם.
while with a Jewish woman, the child relates to both.
וְעַל כֵּן, אַף דְּקַיְימָא לָן דְּכָשֵׁר,
Therefore, though we hold that the child is legitimate,

מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מ״ה1061 Yevamot 45a — A certain man came before Rav and said to him: A gentile or a slave who had relations with a Jewish woman — what is the child's status? He said to him: The child's lineage is unflawed. He said to him: Then give me your daughter. He said: I will not give her to you. Shimi bar Chiyya said to Rav: People say — a camel in Media dances upon a kav [a small measure]; here is the kav, here is the camel, and here is Media, and it does not dance. He said to him: Even were he like Joshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter. Rashi: "A certain man who came": the son of a gentile by a Jewish woman. "People say, a camel in Media dances on a kav": a large camel dances on its four legs inside a small kav in the kingdom of Media, and it is an exaggeration. "Here is the kav, here is the camel, and here is Media": let it come and dance before us; that is to say, you who permitted a novel thing, make your words true and give him your daughter. Maharsha (Chiddushei Halachos, on "even were he like Joshua son of Nun"): Perhaps he hinted to him that although he is not a mamzer, he is nevertheless flawed, as was said above in this sugya according to R. Yehoshua ben Levi, and his daughter is disqualified from the priesthood, since the daughter of a male chalal is disqualified from the priesthood, as we say in chapter Asarah Yuchasin; this is why he mentioned Joshua son of Nun, who had no son but had a daughter. Alternatively, he told him that even were he as eminent in his qualities as Joshua son of Nun, he still would not give him his daughter, for fear that she would be disqualified from the priesthood. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 77): Even a very great man with a flaw in his lineage should not be joined [in marriage], for if his greatness keeps it from harming him, it will harm his offspring, as Rav said, "Even were he like Joshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter." Rav was precise to say "like Joshua son of Nun" and not "like Moses," for Moses is the root of the Torah, and from the side of the crown of Torah, which lies ready for all, there is no concern for lineage. Had the man been "like Moses" (the great Torah scholar of the generation) Rav would have given her; "like Joshua son of Nun" means a righteous man who "rules in the fear of God." עַמּוּד א׳)
the Gemara in Yevamot (45a) nevertheless records
דְּאָמַר רַב:
that Rav declared:
״אֲפִילּוּ הֲוָה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן נוּן —
“Even if he were righteous like Joshua son of Nun—
לָא יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא״.
I would not give him my daughter in marriage.”
וּמַה שֶׁאָמַר ״יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן נוּן״,
And why he specifically cited “Joshua son of Nun,”

יוּבַן כְּפִי מַה שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר1062 Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses §16 (on the two Adars) — From his [Joseph's] seed came Joshua, the head of those who fought Amalek, and after him Saul of Benjamin, who left Agag alive, from whom Haman came forth. … As the Sages said (Sanhedrin 96b, in the Ein Yaakov's reading), of the descendants of Haman taught Torah in public, and who was this? Rav Shmuel bar Shilas. I have already explained elsewhere that to my mind it is clear that this came about through one of the seed of Amalek coming upon a Jewish woman, for converts are not accepted from Amalek (Mechilta, end of Beshalach) … and we hold (Yevamos 45b) that the child is fit; yet we find that the Torah called him "the son of an Egyptian man," and so too he is called "of the descendants of Haman." And perhaps Rav Shmuel bar Shilas himself was named after his mother (Shilas being a woman's name, the sister of R. Chiya, as written in the Responsa of the Geonim), in the manner of Rav Mari bar Rachel.,
is understood through what I have written elsewhere,
דְּנִרְאֶה לִי דֶּרֶךְ הַשְׁעָרָה קְרוֹבָה,
that it appears to me as a compelling deduction,
דְּהַהוּא גַּבְרָא
that the individual who asked Rav
הוּא הָיָה רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת,
was Rav Shmuel bar Shilat,
דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
concerning whom the Sages stated

(מַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳, לְגִרְסַת ״עֵין יַעֲקֹב1063 Sanhedrin 96b — The Sages taught: Naaman was a resident alien; Nebuzaradan was a righteous convert. Descendants of Sisera studied Torah in Jerusalem; descendants of Sennacherib taught Torah in public — and who were they? Shemaya and Avtalyon. Descendants of Haman studied Torah in Bnei Brak [the Ein Yaakov text reads: and who was he? Rav Shmuel bar Shilat]. Rashi: A resident alien: one who did not accept upon himself the other commandments, but accepted upon himself not to worship idols. Maharsha: Just as Nebuzaradan contemplated repentance in his heart and merited to enter under the wings of the Shechinah, so of these wicked men — Sisera, Sennacherib who blasphemed against Heaven, and Haman the wicked — who persisted in their wickedness and were killed for it, the descendants contemplated repentance and merited to enter under the wings of the Shechinah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 96b): The power that Sennacherib had was a supernal power, only it inclined toward the side of impurity; and as a physician removes the bad until the good remains, so the Holy One, blessed be He, removed the bad from Sennacherib's power until the good remained. So too with Nebuzaradan: although he destroyed the Temple, a supernal power was mixed into his power, and when that bad was removed he was healed of his wickedness and became a righteous convert, and likewise Naaman, who was a resident alien; and so with Haman — it cannot be that there was no supernal power within his power, and when the dross was removed, refined silver remained. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 7): What is recounted here of the wicked whose seed converted into Israel and taught Torah in public is a wondrous matter: when the wicked are extreme in wickedness and have very great power, as these had, their power cannot but be joined to a supernal power, the power of God, blessed be He, except that with them it was in impurity. But in the children, once they converted, that power was refined, purified and made white, and therefore their descendants were great men who taught Torah in public. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Saul's mercy [on Agag] was not, Heaven forbid, of an evil kind; he sensed some good in him, as the Sages said, "of the descendants of Haman some taught Torah in public — and who was it? Rav Shmuel bar Shilat." In my view it is clear that this came about through one of Amalek's seed coming upon a Jewish woman, since converts are not accepted from Amalek, as with a captive or through some other coercion, the child being legitimate; and just as the Torah calls [the blasphemer] "son of an Egyptian man," so he is called "of the descendants of Haman." Perhaps Rav Shmuel bar Shilat himself was named for his mother, Shilat being a woman's name, the sister of R. Chiya, as written in the responsa of the Geonim, like Rav Mari bar Rachel. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): "Of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah," for the root of Haman is the error of thinking that the Blessed One has withdrawn His knowledge from the lower world, yet for the commandments of the Torah one needs faith in free choice, which is in man's hand and is the opposite of [divine] knowledge. Since some measure of withdrawal of knowledge is of benefit to the words of Torah and the keeping of the commandments, Saul thought this was the root that must not be destroyed, and for this he had mercy; and from this aspect come [Haman's] descendants who studied Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 2): The desire for children is the longing particular to a Jew, as I heard on "of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah": this came about because Saul let Agag live that night, for Agag grieved lest his seed come to an end, and in reward Haman issued from him. And I heard that this grief is a trait of the seed of Israel (the nations are not pained at all by the end of their seed, caring only for their own enjoyment), and it came from the root in him of Haman's descendants, who went out and cleaved to Israel [and this was his reward, the issuing of Haman, in whom the power that would produce those descendants was revealed, which is why they are named for him, "the descendants of Haman"]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 1): These three statements were said in the name of Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, for it is said, "of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah in Bnei Brak," and in the Ein Yaakov, "and who was it? Rav Shmuel bar Shilat"; therefore he said these three statements, which concern the obliteration of Amalek, who accuses Israel over the holiness of the covenant. Just as it is said of Ovadiah the Edomite convert, "from the forest itself comes the handle for the axe," so his son, being of the seed of Haman and Amalek, said these teachings concerning the obliteration of Amalek in Adar, and therefore in it we increase joy. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): As I explained elsewhere, the feminine element in Amalek can be absorbed only in this way: of Amalek it is written "you shall blot out," and converts are not accepted from Amalek, yet "of the descendants of Haman some taught children in Jerusalem." It must therefore have come about through a gentile of his descendants coming upon a Jewish woman, for the child is legitimate and a Jew, yet is also called son of the gentile, as the Torah says, "and he was the son of an Egyptian man." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Vayechi): Benjamin brings into holiness every good thing and holy spark he sees among the nations. Thus Saul had mercy on Agag, who said, "Woe is me, lest my seed be wiped out"; and though this mercy was reckoned to him as a sin, the Blessed One nonetheless reckoned that a good thought would remain from this act, as the Gemara says, "of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah in Bnei Brak." This made clear Saul's intention, to bring out the good and holiness that was in Agag, for Saul was of Benjamin, which is why [Benjamin] is called "a wolf that tears." Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Ta'anis 2): With the Blessed One all is complete mercy, and He gives place to everything in the world, for from His side everything was created only for a good end, and the Holy One, blessed be He, created nothing in vain, to the extent that the Sages said, "of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah in Bnei Brak; of the descendants of Sisera some studied Torah in Jerusalem." So too the Blessed One gave a place to Ammon and Moab, though Israel suffered from them, for the sake of the two good doves destined to come from them.
