Sod Yesharim (Shabbos Chol HaMoed Sukkos 40): On this the verse concludes, "On that day I will give Gog a place there, a grave in Israel": since the Blessed One created them there is surely glory of Heaven in them, for the Holy One, blessed be He, created nothing in vain, and it will remain within Israel, like the glory of Heaven left over from all who oppressed Israel, such as Haman and Sennacherib in their time, of whom the Gemara says, "of the descendants of Haman some studied Torah in Bnei Brak," and likewise "of the descendants of Sisera some studied Torah," and of the descendants of Sennacherib. But they themselves, in their own grasp, were lost and utterly nullified.״)
(Sanhedrin 96b according to the Ein Yaakov text):
שֶׁהָיָה מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן,
that he was among the descendants of Haman,
וְנִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם אִמּוֹ,
and was named after his mother,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּתְשׁוּבַת הַגְּאוֹנִים.
as recorded in the Geonic responsa.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל,
This parallels the case of Rav Mari bar Rachel,
לְפִי שֶׁאָבִיו בָּא עָלֶיהָ בְּגַיּוּתוֹ.
so called because his father cohabited with her while a gentile.
וְכֵן הוּא,
And this reasoning is consistent,
כִּי אֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּרִים מֵעֲמָלֵק
for converts are not accepted from Amalek

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא, סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח)1064 Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Amalek 2:50 — R. Eliezer says: The Omnipresent swore by His throne — if one of any of the nations of the world comes to convert, Israel shall accept him, but one of the house of Amalek they shall not accept, as it is stated: "And David said to the youth who told him: From where are you? And he said: I am the son of an Amalekite convert" (II Samuel 1:13). At that moment David recalled what had been said to Moses — that if one of any of the nations of the world comes to convert, Israel shall accept him, but one of the house of Amalek they shall not accept — as it is stated: "And David said to him: Your blood is upon your own head, for your own mouth testified against you" (II Samuel 1:16). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Among the nations, those with more connection to holiness are the worse and hold a greater force of impurity, so that one must keep further from them; and Amalek has more connection to holiness than any nation — sprung from two of the patriarchs and matriarchs, his mother Timna having gone round the doors of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob seeking to convert, and his father Eliphaz raised in Isaac's lap. Therefore he was distanced more than all the nations, his name to be blotted out from under the heavens, and the Mekhilta says that no convert is accepted from Amalek. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): I have explained elsewhere that in my view it is clear that [the descendants of Haman who studied Torah] came through one of the seed of Amalek coming upon a Jewish woman, since converts are not accepted from Amalek; rather, it happened through a woman taken captive among them, or otherwise by force. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Apart from [a child born to a Jewish woman forced by one of Haman's seed], no convert is accepted from Amalek, as the Mekhilta says, for once the name Amalek has come upon them in actuality there is no trace of the moisture of holiness in them: his whole root is the evil latent and hidden, to be drawn into action, and were there room to turn him to good he would not be evil at all. A nation whose root of evil lies in outward action can be transformed, but Amalek himself cannot be transformed at all, for the essence does not change, only its outward extension. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 2): In Egypt the task was to extract the holy sparks, and many of the mixed multitude were fit to cleave to Israel; not so Amalek, for the Mekhilta says that the Blessed One swore that no convert would be accepted from Amalek, and likewise the command was to destroy "from ox to sheep." As for "of Haman's descendants studied Torah in Bnei Brak," though converts are not accepted from Amalek, it seems that Rav Shmuel bar Shilat descended from one of them who came upon a Jewish woman, and so issued from Haman unintentionally. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Of Amalek it is written "you shall blot out," and the Sages said in the Mekhilta that converts are not accepted from Amalek; yet "of Haman's descendants taught children in Jerusalem," so it must have come about through a gentile of his descendants coming upon a Jewish woman, for the offspring is fit and is a Jew, though he is also called the son of the gentile. Absorbing anything from Amalek is possible only in this way, by force and without intent. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 264): Every evil trait includes some good, since it is also set within Israel, and from its good side come the pious of the nations; but the only good in mockery is the mocking of idolatry, which belongs to this world alone. In the future, when the evil inclination is abolished and there is no place for idolatry, there is no place for mockery at all — no remnant of it in the World to Come and no turning into "a clear language," only "you shall blot out" — as the Sages said in the Mekhilta, that no convert is accepted from Amalek. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 10): Hence the Mekhilta says that converts are not accepted from Amalek, for he is the root of evil in which there is no good; even when he comes to convert and says he wishes to be good, it is only a "spreading out of the hooves" [the pig's display of a false sign of purity], which is the root of Esau.;
(as recorded in the Mekhilta at the end of Beshalach);
וּמַה דְּ״מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן״ וְכוּלֵי,
and regarding the teaching that “descendants of Haman taught Torah,”
סִבֵּב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סִבּוֹת
the blessed Hashem orchestrated events
דְּבָא בְּגַיּוּתוֹ עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
such that an Amalekite while a gentile fathered a child with a Jewish woman,
דְּהַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר;
so that the resulting offspring was halachically Jewish;
וְנִזְדַּמְּנָה לְפָנָיו שִׁילַת,
and there happened before him Shilat,
אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא,
the sister of Rabbi Chiya
דּוֹדָתוֹ דְּרַב,
and aunt of Rav,
מִזֶּרַע שִׁמְעִי אֲחֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
descended from Shimei, brother of King David, peace be upon him

(מַסֶּכֶת כְּתוּבּוֹת ס״ב1065 Ketubot 62b — Rabbi [Yehuda the Prince] arranged to take a daughter of the house of R. Chiya for his son. When he came to write the marriage contract, the girl died. Rabbi said: Heaven forbid, is there some disqualification here? They sat and examined the families, and found that Rabbi was descended from Shefatya son of Avital, while R. Chiya was descended from Shim'i, David's brother. Rashi: "Is there some disqualification" means that the two were not fitly matched to one another. Shefatya was a son of David — Avital was the name of David's wife — while R. Chiya was descended from Shim'i; and this is the disqualification: Rabbi was of the house of David, and a girl descended from Shim'i was not a fit match for his son, since she was not of royal stock. Maharsha: Rashi's explanation is a little difficult: did the kings of the house of David marry only the daughters of kings? Were it not for his explanation it would seem that Rabbi meant, Heaven forbid that we should ascribe the cause of her death to a disqualification in one of us — her death is to be ascribed to something else; and upon this they examined the families and found that there was no disqualification, for the two were of one family, both descended from Yishai. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kesubos 62b): Rashi's explanation is somewhat difficult: whence do we know that R. Yose ben Zimra [with whose house Rabbi next made the match] was descended from David, and so with all the others into whose families Rabbi's sons married — and must they be of the house of David? It seems rather to be the reverse: they examined and found no disqualification at all, this one descending from Shefatya and that one from Shim'i, and so they did not ascribe her death to any disqualification, but held that the girl died of herself. עַמּוּד ב׳).
(Ketubot 62b).
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לְרַב:
Therefore he said to Rav:
״הַב לִי בְּרַתָּךְ״,
“Give me your daughter,”
בִּהְיוֹתוֹ קְרוֹבוֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ,
being his relative on his mother's side,
וּמִזֶּרַע גְּדוֹלִים מִבֵּית אִמּוֹ.
and from an illustrious lineage through his mother's family.
(וְאַף דְּבַגְּמָרָא מַסִּיק:
(And although the Gemara concludes:
״לָא״ וְכוּלֵי ״יְהֵיב בֵּיהּ עֵינֵיהּ וּשְׁכֵיב״;
that Rav refused and cast his gaze upon him, and he died;
וְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים,
whereas Rav Shmuel bar Shilat is known to have had sons,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית (כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
as found in Tractate Taanit (29b)
ג׳ מֵימְרוֹת מֵרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת,
recording three statements by Rav Yehudah, his son,
וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת;
and similarly in numerous passages;
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר
it can be explained
שֶׁבְּיַלְדוּתוֹ הִשִּׂיאוּהוּ
that in his youth they married
לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת בַּת גֵּרִים,
Rav Shmuel bar Shilat to the daughter of converts,
וּמִמֶּנָּה הוֹלִיד כָּל בָּנָיו.
and through her he fathered all his children.
וּבְזִקְנוּתוֹ שָׁאַל לְרַב רַבּוֹ
Then in his old age he inquired of his teacher Rav
אִם מֻתָּר לִשָּׂא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
whether he was permitted to marry a born Jewish woman;
וּכְשֶׁהִתִּירוֹ,
and when Rav ruled that it was permitted,
אָמַר לוֹ: ״הַב לִי בְּרַתָּךְ״,
he asked him: “Give me your daughter,”
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן דּוֹדָתוֹ,
since he was his first cousin;
וְלֹא רָצָה וְהֶעֱנִישׁוֹ.
yet Rav declined and punished him.
וְכֵן מַה שֶׁמָּצִינוּ
Likewise what we find
בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת (קנ״ג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
in Tractate Shabbat (153a)
דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת:
where Rav instructed Rav Shmuel bar Shilat:
״אַחִים בְּהֶסְפֵּידָא״ וְכוּלֵי,
“Warm up the crowd in my funeral eulogy...”
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם כֵּן
can likewise be explained
שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה זוֹ
as having occurred prior to that incident
שֶׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ עַל יָדוֹ,
wherein he was punished by Rav,
וְהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁיַּסְפִּידוֹ.
when Rav still anticipated that he would eulogize him.
כֵּן שָׁמַעְנוּ מִפִּי רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
So we heard directly from the holy mouth of our master,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the righteous be for a blessing in the World to Come,
בְּעַל פֶּה).
orally).
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר:
And concerning this, Rav said:
״אֲפִילּוּ הֲוָה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן נוּן״,
“Even if he were like Joshua son of Nun,”
שֶׁהוּא הַנִּלְחָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עִם עֲמָלֵק עַצְמוֹ
who was the very first warrior to fight Amalek
וְהַמַּחֲלִישׁ כֹּחוֹ.
and diminish his power.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת
For in truth,
״מִנֵּיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא —
“from the forest itself—
אָזֵיל בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא״,
comes the handle for the axe,”

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ט1066 Sanhedrin 39b — "The vision of Obadiah: Thus said the Lord God concerning Edom" (Obadiah 1:1). Why did Obadiah in particular prophesy concerning Edom? R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said — let Obadiah come, who dwelt between two wicked ones and did not learn from their deeds, and prophesy concerning Esau the wicked, who dwelt between two righteous ones and did not learn from their deeds. Ephraim Miksha'ah, the disciple of R. Meir, said in the name of R. Meir: Obadiah was an Edomite convert. And this is what people say: from the forest itself comes the handle of the axe. Rashi: "Two wicked ones" — Ahab and Jezebel; "two righteous ones" — Isaac and Rebecca. "From the forest itself comes the handle for the ax": from the forest's own wood [a piece] goes into the ax to become its handle, and with it the forest is cut down; so too Obadiah against Edom, and David against Moab, for he descended from Ruth the Moabite. Maharsha (s.v. "Obadiah was an Edomite convert"): That is, the prophecy is all the more confirmed because Obadiah was one of their own, testifying against them — just as David dealt with Moab as he did with no other nation he conquered because he himself came from Moab, so that it would be all the more established that they deserved it. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 39b): A person is more readily able to act upon himself than upon another, for a thing is close to itself; therefore it was Obadiah [the Edomite] who prophesied concerning Edom, to bring the punishment upon Edom. That is the meaning of "from the forest itself comes the handle for the ax": punishment commonly comes upon a person from his own side, since he is close to acting upon himself, whereas through others it is not so readily brought about. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 5): R. Akiva, the foundation of the Oral Torah, was a son of converts and came from Esau, in the manner of what the Sages said in Sanhedrin about Obadiah, an Edomite convert who prophesied against Edom, because "from the forest itself [comes the handle for the axe]." That is, because Esau came from Isaac, on which account the Sages call Esau "an apostate Israelite"; and since there was in some respect a connection to Isaac, the beginning of the Israelite lineage, Esau too had some share in it. עַמּוּד ב׳)
as the Sages stated in Sanhedrin (39b)
עַל עֹבַדְיָה גֵּר אֲדוֹמִי,
regarding Obadiah, the Edomite convert,
דְּנִתְנַבֵּא עַל אֱדוֹם.
who prophesied the doom of Edom.
וְכֵן בְּוַדַּאי מִמֶּנּוּ יִצְמַח
And so too, from Amalek's seed would surely sprout
עִקַּר מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק
the ultimate instrument of Amalek's eradication
וַעֲקִירַת שָׁרְשׁוֹ לְגַמְרֵי.
and the complete uprooting of his existence.
וְכֵן עֵסֶק הַלִּמּוּד תּוֹרָה
And similarly, the endeavor of teaching Torah
לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
to young school children,
שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית קַטְנוּת הַשֵּׂכֶל,
which addresses the most rudimentary level of intellect,
דְּגַם הָרַב מַקְטִין שִׂכְלוֹ אָז
where the teacher contracts his own intellect
כְּפִי עֵרֶךְ הָרָאוּי לַהֲבָנַת הַתַּלְמִיד.
to match the capacity of the child's understanding.
וְהוּא עֵסֶק שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
This reflects the work of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
as taught at the beginning of Tractate Avodah Zarah (3b):
שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת מַאי עָבֵיד?
“During the final three hours of the day, what does He do?
מְלַמֵּד וְכוּלֵי.
He sits and instructs the schoolchildren...”

וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סוֹף מַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה)1067 Megillah 31a — R. Yochanan said: Wherever you find the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility. This is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and stated a third time in the Writings. It is written in the Torah: "For the Lord your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords" (Deuteronomy 10:17), and immediately after it is written, "He executes justice for the orphan and the widow" (Deuteronomy 10:18). Maharsha: “Wherever” is not exact, for in many verses His might is mentioned without His humility following; it means rather: in the Torah, in the Prophets and in the Writings alike. Nor is “might” exact, since the verses cited from the Prophets and the Writings use no term of might; it means wherever the exaltedness of the Holy One, blessed be He, is spoken of, and “might” was chosen because the verse from the Torah contains “the great, the mighty and the awesome God.” The point is that His way is not the way of flesh and blood, where the mighty man keeps the crushed and lowly of spirit — orphans and widows — at a distance; He, on the contrary, draws them near and watches over them all the more. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 1): R. Yochanan means that humility is itself the very greatness, the greatness above all greatness, than which there is none higher; were it not so, His humility would not be found in every place where His greatness is found. For one who possesses humility is bounded and defined by nothing, and this indicates absolute simplicity, and what is absolutely simple is without limit. Therefore “He executes justice for the orphan and the widow” follows upon His greatness: out of that simplicity He is not confined to doing justice for the great rather than the small, but does justice for all alike. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 47): At the Sea the Blessed One appeared as a mighty warrior only because Pharaoh had grown haughty, so He clothed Himself, as it were, in a garment of might against him. When Israel's hearts opened to sing, they grasped this and said, "I will sing to the Lord, for He is exalted" [over the proud] — all His majesty is directed only against the proud, while the truth is "I, the Lord, dwell with the contrite," as the Sages said, "wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility ... to revive the heart of the contrite." Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 4): Holiness denotes God's exaltedness and greatness as a person recognizes it, and the ultimate knowledge of created beings is to know that the Blessed One is set apart and exalted far beyond created intellect. That is why the Sages said, "wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility": in the very place where His greatness and exaltedness is grasped by a creature, there is His humility, to be grasped even by the lowliest creature, for in grasping His exaltedness he grasps the Blessed One. Hence "Holy, holy, holy" concludes "the whole earth is full of His glory" — His glory is grasped throughout the earth and fills all the lowly parts of creation. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 45): The name Shaddai teaches that the Blessed One measures out for each creature its fitting place and watches over the small as over the great: unlike flesh and blood, for whom some things are essential and others secondary and superfluous, for the Blessed One all matters are equal, and there is "enough" [dai] in His divinity for every creature, even the smallest. This flows from the secret of the Most High, that "wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility," and it is hinted in the verse, "He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High abides in the shadow of Shaddai.":
And this exemplifies what the Sages stated (Megillah 31a):
״בִּמְקוֹם גְּדֻלָּתוֹ —
“Wherever you find His boundless majesty,
שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ״ וְכוּלֵי.
there you find His profound humility.”
כִּי מִצַּד הַגַּדְלוּת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the infinite greatness of the blessed Hashem
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת מֻשָּׂג כְּלַל דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה,
cannot be grasped through ordinary intellectual attainment,
רַק לְמִי שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת.
except by one situated in utter simplicity and lowliness.
דְּעַל כֵּן בָּחַר בִּבְנֵי אָדָם
This is why He chose mortal human beings
יוֹתֵר מִמַּלְאָכִים,
over celestial angels,
דִּכְפִי הַשָּׂגָה שְׁפָלָה שֶׁלָּהֶם,
for through their low and humble state of perception,
יֵשׁ לָהֶם דְּבֵקוּת
they can cleave
עִם גַּדְלוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה הַיּוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹנָה.
to the highest dimension of Divine greatness.
וְכֵן הַשָּׂגַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
So too, the perception of school children,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית קַטְנוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה,
which is the simplest and most elementary attainment,
הֵם יְכוֹלִים לִלְמֹד מִפִּיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
enables them to learn directly from the mouth of the Holy One;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
in the sense of the verse:
״מִפִּי עוֹלְלִים וְיֹנְקִים יִסַּדְתָּ עֹז״,
“From the mouths of babes and sucklings You established strength,”
שֶׁעַל יָדָם הוּא יְסוֹד הַתּוֹרָה מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא;
for through them the bedrock of Torah is built from below upward;
הַיְסוֹד הוּא קָבוּעַ בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת לְמַטָּה.
the foundation is set at the lowest point below.
וְכֵן בְּלִמּוּד הַתּוֹרָה לְמַטָּה,
And so it is in human Torah study below:
הַיְסוֹד הוּא ״גִּירְסָא דְּיַנְקוּתָא״.
the foundation is the simple learning of childhood.
וּבֶאֱמֶת, הַחַיּוּת —
And in truth, spiritual vitality moves
״רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק״,
“running and returning, like the appearance of lightning,”
דְּמֵאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם שֶׁיּוֹצְאִים מִשָּׁם — הֵם שָׁבִים.
returning to the very source from which it emerged.
דְּ״מַאן דְּאִיהוּ זְעֵיר — אִיהוּ רַב״;
For “he who is small is truly great”;
וְאַחַר שֶׁמֵּאִיר אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם,
and once that lowest point is illuminated,
נַעֲשָׂה מָקוֹם הַיּוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹן.
it becomes the most exalted realm.
כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
From the side of Hashem, blessed be He,
הַיְסוֹד הוּא הַיּוֹתֵר רָם וְגָבוֹהַּ
the foundation is the loftiest and most sublime height,
מֵעַל הַשָּׂגַת כָּל גְּבוֹהִים,
far above the reach of all elevated minds,
וְהוּא שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל בְּרִיָּה,
and this is the Fiftieth Gate concealed from every creature.
וּבוֹ דָּבוּק
And to it clings
הַשָּׂגַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
the simple perception of young schoolchildren,
שֶׁהוּא הַהַשָּׂגָה הַיּוֹתֵר פְּשׁוּטָה,
which is the most straightforward, unadorned comprehension,
שֶׁכָּל הַנֶּעֱלָמוֹת כֻּלָּם
in which all hidden, esoteric wisdoms
כְּלוּלִים בְּפַשְׁטוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה,
are implicitly contained in its simplicity,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֱמֶת גָּמוּר.
which itself constitutes absolute truth.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת ס״ג1068 Shabbat 63a — Rav Kahana said to Mar son of Rav Huna: But this verse is written concerning words of Torah! He said to him: A verse never departs from its plain meaning. Rav Kahana said: When I was eighteen years old and had already learned the whole Talmud, I did not know until now that a verse never departs from its plain meaning. Rashi: "This is written concerning words of Torah": [the verse means:] be careful to review your learning, so that it is ready for you at the time of judgment to bring a proof, like a sword on the thigh of a mighty man to prevail in battle — and that is "your glory and your majesty". Maharsha: The whole psalm — "My heart overflows with a goodly matter… my tongue is the pen of a ready scribe" — is expounded of a Torah scholar occupied with words of Torah, and he answered that a verse never departs from its plain meaning: the thing signified is certainly words of Torah, but the parable, which is the plain sense of the verse, speaks of an actual warrior, whose sword on his thigh is his adornment. Rashi explains "written concerning words of Torah" as reviewing one's learning so that it is ready like a sword on the thigh; one may also explain it by the exposition of "the roundings of your thighs" (Song of Songs 7:2): just as the thigh is hidden, so words of Torah [are to be studied] in private. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 63a): The plain meaning comes first in understanding, before the midrashic exposition, and so the plain meaning must also be true; for were only the exposition true, it could not, Heaven forbid, be called a Torah of truth, since the plain meaning is prior to the exposition. Moreover, the Torah would then have been given only to the select few of the generation who know the exposition, not to all Israel, whereas the Torah was given to all Israel, great and small; therefore the plain meaning must be true, and a verse never departs from its plain meaning. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim 12): Although [the Ra'aya Mehemna] reads "Come, eat of my bread" as the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah, nevertheless a verse does not depart from its plain meaning, as we find with "Gird your sword": though it is written of words of Torah, "a verse does not depart from its plain meaning." So too here, the intent is that through eating one merits words of Torah, as we say of the second Sabbath meal, "the light rests upon it," that through the meal one merits the light. Sha'ar HaEmunah (Introduction to Beis Yaakov 28): One must believe all the expositions of the Sages, that they are true in their plain sense as well, as Ramban wrote: the Sages said, "A verse does not depart from its plain meaning," and did not say, "A verse is expounded according to its plain meaning"; we learn that although the Torah has seventy facets, none of them contradicts the plain meaning. עַמּוּד א׳):
In accordance with what they taught (Shabbat 63a):
״אֵין מִקְרָא יוֹצֵא מִידֵי פְּשׁוּטוֹ״,
“A scriptural verse never loses its plain meaning,”
וְכָל הַסּוֹדוֹת גְּנוּזוֹת בִּפְשׁוּטוֹ.
and all mysteries remain concealed within the plain meaning.
וְאַרְבָּעִים וְתִשְׁעָה שַׁעֲרֵי הַשָּׂגוֹת —
And forty-nine gates of understanding—
מִינֵי חָכְמָה זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ יֵשׁ;
represent levels of wisdom ascending one above the other;
וְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הוּא
whereas the Fiftieth Gate is the point
מַה שֶׁכֻּלָּם חוֹזְרִים לַמָּקוֹר
where they all return to their primal source
לְהִכָּלֵל בְּאֶחָד,
to be integrated into absolute Oneness,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ חוֹזֵר לִהְיוֹת הַתְחָלָה,
from which everything becomes a new beginning,
שֶׁהַכֹּל כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ,
where all returns to ultimate simplicity,
שֶׁכָּל הַחָכְמוֹת כֻּלָּם שָׁם
and all forms of wisdom are there
גְּלוּיִם בִּפְשׁוּטוֹ הַגָּמוּר;
manifest within the plain truth itself;
וְהוּא מַמָּשׁ הַשָּׂגַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן.
and this is identical to the pure perception of young schoolchildren.
וְהַהֶבְדֵּל אֵינוֹ מֵעַצְמוּת אוֹתָהּ הַהַשָּׂגָה,
The difference lies not in the core essence of that perception,
רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת:
but merely in the degree of its expansion:
דְּהַשָּׂגַת הַנֶּעֱלָמוֹת
for the attainment of the hidden mysteries
שֶׁבְּהַשָּׂגַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן —
within the perception of schoolchildren
כָּלוּל הַכֹּל בְּהֶעְלֵם,
is completely cloaked in concealment,
וְשָׁם — הַכֹּל בְּגִלּוּי.
while in the Fiftieth Gate—all is revealed.
אֲבָל עַצְמוּת הַהַשָּׂגָה
Nevertheless, the essential quality of the attainment
הוּא תַּכְלִית הַפְּשִׁיטוּת
is that supreme simplicity
בְּהַשָּׂגַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
found in the perception of children,
דְּעַל כֵּן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and for this reason the Holy One, blessed be He,
יוֹשֵׁב וּמְלַמְּדָם תּוֹרָה.
sits and teaches them Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן, מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן,
Therefore, from the descendants of Haman,
שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
who represents the first of nations,
כַּאֲשֶׁר נִקְלַט מִמֶּנּוּ לִקְדֻשָּׁה
when a spark was absorbed from him into holiness
וְנַעֲשָׂה הָרֵאשִׁית דִּקְדֻשָּׁה,
and transformed into the holy first principle—
שֶׁהוּא הַדְּבֵקוּת בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם —
namely attachment to the concealed supernal root—
בָּא הַלִּמּוּד לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן.
there emerged the vocation of instructing schoolchildren in Torah.
וְהַקְּלִיטָה הָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי אִשָּׁה,
And this holy absorption occurred through a woman,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּפַּלְתּוֹ הָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי אִשָּׁה.
just as Haman's downfall was brought about through a woman.
כִּי נָשִׁים אֵין לָהֶם
For women do not have
שׁוּם שַׁיָּכוּת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
the same formal obligation in the analytical study of Torah,
דְּ״הַמְלַמֵּד בִּתּוֹ תּוֹרָה —
for “whoever teaches his daughter Torah—

כִּמְלַמְּדָהּ תִּפְלוּת״ וְכוּלֵי (מַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה כ1069 Sotah 20a — From here Ben Azzai says: A man is obligated to teach his daughter Torah, so that if she drinks she will know that merit suspends [the punishment] for her. R. Eliezer says: Whoever teaches his daughter Torah is as though he teaches her licentiousness. Rashi: "She will know that merit suspends for her" — she will see and learn in the section of the sota that merit suspends [punishment], as we derive from "and she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" (Numbers 5:28): she is cleared through merits for as long as it takes to bear seed, nine months — and some say longer, as the Gemara explains. Rashi (Sotah 21b): "Promiscuity — could you think so?" — would he call the Torah promiscuity? "As if" — for from [the Torah] she comes to understand cunning, and does her deeds in secret. Tosafos (s.v. "Ben Azzai says: A man is obligated"): According to the Yerushalmi, Ben Azzai does not hold like R. Elazar ben Azariah, who expounded "Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones" (Deuteronomy 31:12) — the men came to learn, the women to hear; and it seems this means that the women's commandment to hear is so that they know how to fulfill the commandments, not so that they know that merit suspends. [The Yerushalmi further relates that] a matron asked R. Eliezer why, when the sin of the Calf was one, they died by three deaths, and he answered her, "A woman has no wisdom except at the spindle"; when his son Hyrcanus said to him, "Because you would not answer her one word of Torah, you have lost me three hundred kor of tithe every year," he replied, "Let the words of Torah be burned, and let the words of Torah not be handed over to women." Maharsha (Sotah 21b): [On R. Eliezer's reason, that when wisdom enters a person cunning enters with it:] for a man this is a benefit, enabling him to understand the cunning of the wicked and to use cunning against them — and so the verse concludes, "and I find out knowledge of devices" (Proverbs 8:12), that is, through the knowledge of Torah I find out the devices of others, in the manner of "and with the crooked You show Yourself subtle" (II Samuel 22:27). But women are light-minded, [and the concern is] lest they use cunning and come to transgression and ruin. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sotah 21b): [R. Eliezer's reason, that] once wisdom enters a person cunning enters him, is because acquiring intellect causes a person to acquire the faculty of the material intellect, which is cunning. That is why [the verse] says "I, wisdom, dwell with cunning" (Proverbs 8:12): the speculative intellect dwells with a person by means of the bodily intellect, which is cunning. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): When one whose heart is not wholly clean attains the wisdom that flows from the heart, words of disparagement flow from his heart, like the flaw of his heart. On this the Sages said, "Whoever teaches his daughter Torah, it is as though he teaches her licentiousness": since a woman has extra understanding, wisdom in her would flow from the heart, and words of licentiousness might, Heaven forbid, flow forth.׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
is as if he taught her triviality” (Sotah 20a),
שֶׁהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ״ וְכוּלֵי,
which aligns with the warning to “those who turn to the left,”
כִּי הִיא מִסִּטְרָא דִּשְׂמָאלָא.
for woman corresponds to the side of the left (Gevurah).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Nevertheless, King Solomon, peace be upon him,
הִמְשִׁיל הַתּוֹרָה לְאִשָּׁה;
compared the Torah to a woman;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת יְבָמוֹת (ס״ג1070 Yevamot 63b — And Rava said: Come and see how good a good wife is and how bad a bad wife is. How good is a good wife? As it is written: "Whoever has found a wife has found good" (Proverbs 18:22). If the verse speaks of her, how good is a good wife, that Scripture praises her; and if the verse speaks of the Torah, how good is a good wife, that the Torah is likened to her. Maharsha: At first sight "that Scripture praises her" would refer to "has found good," but then a good wife as such is not stated in the verse; rather, he relies on the end of the verse, "and obtains favor from the Lord," so that "whoever has found a wife has found good" means a good wife. The exposition concerning the Torah likewise relies on the end of the verse, and it is made because in its plain sense the verse should have said "whoever has found a good wife obtains favor"; of the Torah it reads: "whoever has found a wife" — which wife? The one I spoke of in "has found good," that is, the Torah, which is called "good." The Torah is likened to a good wife, who is beloved to her husband, as it is said, "with her love be ravished always" (Proverbs 5:19). Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 63b): It is already known that the Torah is called a man's wife: just as a wife completes a man until he is whole, so the Torah completes him until he is whole; and just as a wife joins herself to a man and is one with him, so the Torah joins itself to a man and is one with him. The difference between them is that man and wife are one body, whereas the Torah joins itself to the soul, which is not a body. Thus the good wife, and the Torah, which is called a good wife, are each a union of good. עַמּוּד ב׳):
and as the Sages remarked in Yevamot (63b):
״אִי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִשְׁתָּעֵי קְרָא,
“If the verse speaks of the Torah,
כַּמָּה טוֹבָה אִשָּׁה טוֹבָה״ וְכוּלֵי;
how good is a good woman...”;
כִּי ״הָנֵי נְשֵׁי בְּמַאי קָא זַכְיָן?
for “by what merit do women earn the World to Come?
בְּאַתְנוּיֵי לְגַבְרַיְהוּ
By sending their husbands to learn,

וְאַקְרוּיֵי בְּנַיְהוּ״ וְכוּלֵי (מַסֶּכֶת1071 Berakhot 7b — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon bar Yochai: Greater is the service of Torah than its study, as it is said, “Here is Elisha son of Shafat, who poured water on the hands of Eliyahu” — it does not say “who learned,” but “who poured.” This teaches that the service of Torah is greater than its study. Maharsha: It is plain: there are many laws a man learns from his teacher that are not for practice, as is said in several places. He therefore says that the service of Torah is the greater, for in attending upon his teacher he sees the law put into practice. Maharal (Derech Chaim 6:6): One who attends upon a Torah scholar is joined to his master through the service of Torah, and by that joining he receives from him; for there is no doubt that when the wick is brought near the lamp, the lamp kindles the wick. It is not so when the disciple merely learns from his master, for study does not draw him close to the master himself as attendance upon him does. בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳).
and bringing their sons to school...” (Berakhot 17a).
רָצָה לוֹמַר
This means
דְּעִקַּר הַזְּכוּת הוּא
that the primary spiritual merit
עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה דַּוְקָא;
comes specifically through Torah study;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ
and regarding this the Sages taught
דְּהֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן חֵלֶק בְּלִמּוּד תּוֹרָה,
that women also possess a direct share in Torah learning,

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם ז1072 Berakhot 7b — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yochai: Greater is the service of Torah than its study, as it is stated: “Here is Elisha son of Shafat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.” It does not say “who learned,” but “who poured” — which teaches that its service is greater than its study. Maharsha: There are many laws a man learns from his teacher that are not rulings for practice, as is said in several places; hence the service is the greater, for in serving his teacher he sees the law carried out in practice. Maharal (Derech Chaim 6:6): One who attends upon a Torah scholar is joined to his master through that service, and through it he receives from him. There is no doubt that when the wick is brought near the lamp, the lamp kindles it; so too, when the disciple draws near his master by serving him, the master pours out the Torah upon him. Learning from a master is not such a joining; it is the serving that is a drawing near to the scholar himself, and it is thereby that he receives from him.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
in accordance with what they noted (Berakhot 7b):
״גְּדוֹלָה שִׁמּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה״ וְכוּלֵי,
“Greater is the service of Torah than its study,”
שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן עוֹסְקִים בְּשִׁמּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
for they too are deeply engaged in serving the Torah
לְגַבְרַיְהוּ וּלְבְנַיְהוּ.
through facilitating their husbands and children.
וְהַשִּׁמּוּשׁ — שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַחֵשֶׁק,
And this service—stemming from pure yearning and devotion—
עִקָּרוֹ בְּאִשָּׁה.
finds its purest expression in woman.
כִּי הָאִישׁ
For a man
יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִלּוּי הַחֵשֶׁק גַּם כֵּן
can satisfy his intellectual desire
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלּוֹמֵד בְּעַצְמוֹ,
through studying independently,
וְאֵין נִקְרָא מְשַׁמֵּשׁ
and he is termed an attendant
אֶלָּא כָּל זְמַן חַיֵּי הָרַב,
only during his master's lifetime;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נַעֲשָׂה הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ רַב,
subsequently becoming a master himself,
שֶׁהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ נִתְמַלֵּא;
whereby his yearning is realized.
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאִשָּׁה,
This is not so with woman,
דְּאֵין לָהּ מִלּוּי,
who lacks that direct intellectual outlet,
רַק חֵשֶׁק לְבַד —
retaining pure, unquenched desire alone—
זֶהוּ תֹּקֶף דְּכֹחַ הַחֵשֶׁק וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
which represents the ultimate strength of pure longing and its supernal root.
וְלָכֵן בִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ לַעֲמָלֵק
Therefore concerning Joshua's battle against Amalek,
נֶאֱמַר רַק: ״וַיַּחֲלֹשׁ״,
it is written only: “And Joshua weakened Amalek,”
כִּי הַנִּצּוּחַ הָיָה מִצַּד כֹּחַ שִׁמּוּשׁוֹ,
because the victory derived from the power of his service to Moses,
כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
as discussed earlier,
וְכֹחַ זֶה בָּאִישׁ — חָלוּשׁ.
and this receptive, servant capacity in a man appears in an attenuated form.

items.h:
Seif 6 — The Double-Edged Sword of the Mouth
Israel defeats Esau through the spoken sword of Torah, joining Written Torah and Oral expression in the holy mouth.

p: וְאָמַר: ״לְפִי חָרֶב״.
It says: “according to the edge of the sword”.
הָעִנְיָן, כִּי הַתּוֹרָה
The explanation is that the Torah
הִיא חֶרֶב לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
is a sword against idolaters,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וְחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדָם״,
and as it is written: “a double-edged sword in their hand”,
עַל יְדֵי ״רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם״.
wielded through “the high praises of God in their throat”.
וּבִרְכַּת עֵשָׂו ״עַל חַרְבְּךָ״
And Esau's blessing “by your sword”
אֵין שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם
has no dominion over Israel
בַּזְּמַן שֶׁ״הַקּוֹל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״,
so long as “the voice is the voice of Jacob”,
וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם חֶרֶב דְּפֶה.
and they wield the spiritual sword of the mouth.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״פִּיפִיּוֹת״
Therefore this sword is called pipiyot,
לְשׁוֹן ״פֶּה״,
from the word peh (mouth),
וְהֵם שְׁנֵי פִּיּוֹת:
for they represent two distinct mouths:
פֶּה דְּתוֹרָה וְדִתְפִלָּה.
the mouth of Torah and the mouth of prayer.
וְעַל כֵּן ״רוֹמְמוֹת״ —
Therefore the word romemot (high praises) appears
לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
in the plural form,
דִּתְפִלָּה גַּם כֵּן מִדְּבָרִים
for prayer likewise belongs to those matters

שֶׁעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם (שָׁם ו1073 Berakhot 6b — One of the Sages said to Rav Beivai bar Abaye, and some say Rav Beivai said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: What is "when vileness is exalted among the sons of men"? He said to him: These are matters that stand at the summit of the world, and men treat them lightly. Rashi: "When vileness is exalted" — this is the end of the verse cited above ["The wicked walk round about"]. "Matters that stand at the summit of the world" — such as prayer, which ascends on high. Maharsha: It is evident that this refers back to the opening of the verse: one who prays around the synagogue, that is, outside it, is called wicked, because he treats prayer lightly — and prayer is among "the matters that stand at the summit of the world." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Tehillim 34): Although in human eyes the deed seems to be the main thing, the chief guarding is truly of the mouth and tongue, for everything is clarified through the tongue — as the Baal Shem Tov explained the Gemara's "things that stand at the height of the world": it is words [spoken words] that stand at the height of the world. As the holy Zohar says, "once he has brought a word out of his mouth, that word becomes a voice, splits the airs and firmaments, and rises on high."׳ עַמּוּד ב׳).
that stand at the highest pinnacle of the cosmos (Berakhot 6b).
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר:
This means:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה
just as with the Torah,
כָּל מִצְוֹתֶיהָ בְּעִנְיָנִים גַּשְׁמִיִּים,
all its practical commandments deal with physical matters,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יָדוּעַ
and yet it is known
דְּהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
that it is the heavenly will of the blessed Hashem,
וְיֵשׁ לְכָל שֹׁרֶשׁ בְּעֶלְיוֹנֵי עֶלְיוֹנִים;
and each mitzvah possesses a root in the highest celestial spheres;
אַף הַתְּפִלָּה,
so too with prayer,
שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ דְּבָרִים גַּשְׁמִיִּים,
though a person petitions for mundane, material needs,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם רוֹב צָרְכֵי הָאָדָם,
which constitute the majority of human concerns
שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם עִקַּר הַתְּפִלָּה בְּעֵת הַצּוֹרֶךְ,
for which one primarily supplicates in times of need,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, שָׁרְשָׁם עוֹמֵד בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
nevertheless their inner spiritual root stands at the summit of the universe,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה
and through this spiritual connection
הוּא נִצּוּחַ כָּל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.
comes the vanquishing of all idolatrous nations.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And this is what the Sages of blessed memory taught

(פְּתִיחָה דְּאֵיכָה, פְּתִיחָה ב1074 Eikhah Rabbah, Petichta 2 — R. Abba bar Kahana said: The nations of the world had no philosophers like Balaam son of Beor and Avnimos the weaver. They said to them: Can we prevail against this nation? They said to them: Go and make the rounds of their synagogues; if the children are chirping aloud, you cannot prevail against them, and if not, you can. For so their father assured them, saying, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau" (Genesis 27:22): so long as Jacob's voice is in the synagogues and the study houses, the hands are not the hands of Esau; but whenever his voice is not chirping in the synagogues and the study houses, the hands are the hands of Esau.׳):
(Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 2):
״קּוֹל יַעֲקֹב״ —
“The voice of Jacob”—
בְּבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת;
in the synagogues and in the houses of study;
רָצָה לוֹמַר:
meaning:
תְּפִלָּה וְתוֹרָה.
prayer and Torah.
וְרֹאשׁ בִּרְכוֹת הַתְּפִלָּה
And the first of the petitions
בִּשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת,
among the twelve intermediate blessings of the Amidah,
שֶׁהֵם בַּקָּשַׁת צְרָכִים,
which comprise requests for human needs,
הוּא חֲנִינַת הַדַּעַת,
is the prayer for the granting of spiritual wisdom and insight (Daat),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ רֹאשׁ וְעִקַּר כָּל צָרְכֵי הָאָדָם
for this is the foremost and primary requirement of man
בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
in this physical world;
וּלְכָךְ נִבְרָא:
and for this purpose was he created:
לְהַשְׂכִּיל וְלָדַעַת אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
to contemplate and know the blessed Creator.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
And this knowledge is attained through the Torah,
אֶלָּא דְּהָא בְּלֹא הָא לָא סַגִּי,
yet one without the other cannot suffice,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת נִדָּה (ע1075 Niddah 70b — What shall a man do and become wise? He said to them: Let him increase his sitting [in the study house] and lessen his trade. They said: Many have done so and it did not avail them. Rather, let them ask mercy of Him to whom wisdom belongs, as it is said, "For the Lord gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." What then does he teach us [by saying he should increase his sitting]? That the one without the other does not suffice. Rashi: "What then does he teach us?" — why did he need to tell them that a man should increase his sitting [in the study house], seeing that the matter depends upon [God's] mercy?׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
as the Sages taught in Tractate Niddah (70b):
דְּאַף שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה בִּישִׁיבָה,
even if one sits long and toils in the academy,
צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים
he must also plead for mercy
מִמִּי שֶׁהַחָכְמָה שֶׁלּוֹ.
from the One to Whom all wisdom belongs.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּזֶהוּ עִקַּר הַחָכְמָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
For this is the foundational wisdom of Israel:
כְּשֶׁמַּכִּירִים שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
when they recognize that everything derives from the blessed Hashem,
וְגַם הַחָכְמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that wisdom itself is a gift from the Blessed One,
דְּ״יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין״.
“Who gives wisdom unto the wise”.
וְ״חַכִּים״ — לְשׁוֹן הַכָּרָה,
And chakim denotes recognition,
בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּלְמוּד: ״חַכִּים לֵיהּ לִפְלוֹנִי״;
as in the Talmudic phrase: “he recognizes so-and-so”;
וּמִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and one who truly acknowledges the Blessed Creator,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַחָכְמָה,
which is the ultimate pinnacle of all wisdom,
אֵלָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן חָכְמָה,
to him Hashem grants divine wisdom,
רָצָה לוֹמַר: הַיְדִיעָה אֵיךְ לְהַכִּירוֹ.
meaning the deeper insight into how to perceive Him.
וּתְחִלַּת הַהַכָּרָה הוּא הַתְּפִלָּה,
And the very threshold of this recognition is prayer,
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא: ״תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא״ וְכוּלֵי,
wherefore it is designated “the portal through which to enter” (Zohar),
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה
because through prayer
הוּא הַכְּנִיסָה לְכָל מִינֵי הַשָּׂגוֹת
one accesses all levels of spiritual comprehension
וְרָזָא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא,
and the inner mystery of faith,
וְהוּא הָרוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and it corresponds to the archetype of Knesset Yisrael.
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל:
For this awareness represents the quintessential root of Israel:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַכִּיר
that a person recognizes
שֶׁהַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ
that his inner lack and void
אֵין מִי שֶׁיְּמַלְּאֶנּוּ אֶלָּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
can be filled by none other than the blessed Hashem.
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this is the high spiritual rung of King David, peace be upon him,
כַּנּוֹדָע בְּסוֹד ״וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה״,
as known in the mystical secret of “And I am prayer”,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״אַדְמוֹנִי״,
who is described as ruddy (admoni),
וְנֶגֶד אֱדוֹם,
paralleling the reddish power of Edom,
שֶׁיָּדָיו גַּם כֵּן חַדּוֹת וַחֲרוּצוֹת
whose hands are likewise sharp and zealous
לִרְדּוֹת עוֹלָמוֹ,
to conquer and dominate his world,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה
except that David acts

אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג)1076 Bereshit Rabbah 63:8 — "Ruddy" — R. Abba bar Kahana said: as though a shedder of blood. And when Samuel saw that David was ruddy, as it is written, "And he sent and brought him, and he was ruddy," he was afraid and said: Is this one too a shedder of blood, like Esau? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "with beautiful eyes" — Esau kills of his own accord, but this one kills by the decision of the Sanhedrin. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 5): King David too was "ruddy," his hands sharp and keen to subdue those who ought to be subdued, yet "with fair eyes," doing nothing except by the decision of the Sanhedrin; he comprised both opposites, and through this he had the power to transform [evil into good]. This is the perfection of kingship, the rose that has red and white, each in its proper place, for kingship is the moon, which has nothing of its own; so David did nothing of his own mind, only what the Blessed One illumined his eyes with by the light of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 175): The trait of kingship, however, is precisely the opposite [of the care never to cause anyone pain, even for a mitzvah]: the Sages said of King David that his hands were "sharp and keen to rule the world with them," and that he was "ruddy" like Esau, only "with fair eyes," by the decision of the Sanhedrin, and therefore he merited kingship. Saul was removed because he became merciful to the cruel, for the trait of kingship is the harsh attribute of judgment.,
solely with the authorization of the Sanhedrin (Bereishit Rabbah 63),
רָצָה לוֹמַר: הַכֹּל עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה.
meaning: everything is conducted strictly according to Torah.
וְהוּא זָכָה דְּ״הַשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ״ —
And he merited that “Hashem was with him”—

שֶׁהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם (מַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ג1077 Sanhedrin 93b — Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: Doeg spoke this entire verse — "who knows how to play, and a mighty man of valor, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely man, and the Lord is with him" — only as slander. "Who knows how to play," that he knows how to ask; "a mighty man," that he knows how to answer; "a man of war," that he knows how to give and take in the war of Torah; "a comely man," that he presents the reasoning of the halakhah; "prudent in speech," that he infers one matter from another; "and the Lord is with him," that the halakhah accords with him in every place. Rashi: Doeg — whom the Gemara below identifies as "one of the young men" — recounted David's praise only so that Saul would envy him and kill him. "To give and take in the war of Torah" means to debate in the Talmud, and "presents the reasoning of the halakhah" means that he brings proof for his words. Maharsha: Doeg departed from what had been asked: Saul's servants had said, "Let them seek a man who knows how to play on the lyre," but he said "knows how to play" without "on the lyre," and added qualities — "a mighty man of valour" and the rest — that no one had asked of him. From this they expounded that "knows how to play" refers not to the lyre but to knowing how to ask, and that he went on to say what had not been asked — "a mighty man," mighty in Torah, to answer, and so "a man of war"; and his intent was slander, as it says in perek Get Pashut: whoever recounts his fellow's praise excessively comes to speak of his faults. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 32): "Knows how to play" is "knows how to ask," for the one who knows how to play and the one who asks share a single quality: the Torah gladdens a man's heart, and one who asks gladdens the heart of the listener and opens it until he rejoices, as one who knows how to play does; the answer that defeats the questioner is "a mighty man of valour," and one who gives and takes in Torah, raising difficulties and resolving them, is "a man of war." "And the Lord is with him" — the halakhah accords with him everywhere — because He, blessed be He, is truth, and when a man's words are true according to the halakhah, the Holy One, blessed be He, is with him. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 3): The Sages said, "and the Lord is with him — that the halakhah accords with him": to arrive at the true halakhah one must be holy within, with the Lord truly with him, free of any bodily self-interest; then he can arrive at the truth of the halakhah. The test of "the Lord is with him" is purity in these three chief traits, for all bad traits stem from matter and from self-interest. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 1): [Knowing the fitting practice for each soul and each generation] comes through complete cleaving to the Blessed One, as in Sanhedrin: "and the Lord is with him — that the halakhah accords with him in every place." That is, bringing the teaching out in accordance with the halakhah comes about because the Lord is always with him, as it says, "I have set the Lord before me always," his heart's whole aim being only to be an agent of the Merciful One in His service, not drawn after any worldly matter. עַמּוּד ב׳),
meaning the halachah is established in accordance with him everywhere (Sanhedrin 93b),
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה
because through heartfelt prayer
זוֹכֶה לְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.
one merits the wisdom of Torah in its ultimate wholeness.
וְהוֹלִיד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And David fathered King Solomon, peace be upon him,
גְּדוֹל הַחֲכָמִים
the wisest of all men
שֶׁבְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
in the entire world across all generations,
וְחָכְמָתוֹ הוּא חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה, כַּנּוֹדָע.
and his wisdom was the lower wisdom (Chokhmah Tata'ah), as is known.
הַיְינוּ כַּיָּדוּעַ,
This is according to the mystical principle
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that the Written Torah and the Oral Torah
הֵם חָכְמָה עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה;
correspond respectively to the Supernal Wisdom and the Lower Wisdom;
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
for the Written Torah is received
מֵאֵת הַשֵּׁם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם.
directly from Hashem, descending from heaven.
וְזֶהוּ מַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
And this was the allotted portion given to Moses,
שֶׁבָּא וְהוֹרִידָהּ לָאָרֶץ,
who ascended and brought it down to earth,
וְהוּא נִקְרָא ״אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים״,
and he is titled “the man of God”,
״בַּעְלָהּ דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא״, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
the “husband of the Matronita,” as is known,
דְּהֵם סוֹד זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה.
which correspond to the esoteric balance of male and female.
וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם —
Whereas King Solomon, peace be upon him—
מִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
embodied the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty),
סִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא וּפֶה,
the feminine aspect and the spiritual organ of the mouth,
וְ״תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה״ קָרֵינַן לָהּ,
and we designate this “the Oral Torah”,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַאֲמַר ״פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ״,
as stated in the discourse of Patach Eliyahu,
כִּי הִיא הַחָכְמָה הַמִּתְחַדֶּשֶׁת
because it is the fresh, innovative insight
בִּלְבָבוֹת דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
arising continuously within the hearts of Knesset Yisrael.
וְעַל כֵּן הִמְשִׁיל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Therefore King Solomon, peace be upon him,
חָכְמָתוֹ לְאִשָּׁה.
compared his wisdom to a woman.
וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And within Israel,
גַּם זֶה נִקְרָא ״תּוֹרָה״,
even this humanly articulated insight is called Torah,
מֵאַחַר דְּמַכִּירִים שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
since they recognize that everything emanates from the blessed Hashem,
וְגַם חָכְמָתָם
and that their own innovative wisdom
הוּא חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
is the very wisdom of the blessed Hashem.
אֲבָל אֵצֶל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
However, among the gentile nations
יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן חָכְמָה,
there also exists intellectual wisdom,
וּמְבָרְכִין עַל חַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם:
and one recites over the sages of the nations:
״שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ״,
“Who gave of His wisdom to flesh and blood”;
וּפֵרוּשׁוֹ קַמָּאֵי,
which the early commentators explain:
שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא בִּנְתִינָה,
that to them it was given as a detached gift;
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן אֵצֶל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל:
whereas over the sages of Israel the blessing is:
״שֶׁחָלַק״ וְגוֹמֵר,
“Who apportioned of His wisdom to those who revere Him”,
כִּי ״חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ״,
because “the portion of Hashem is His people”,

וּכְמוֹ הַחֵלֶק הַדָּבוּק בַּכֹּל (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה, פָּרָשָׁה ב׳, ט1078 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." If a man says to you: There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written, "And I will destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau." [If he says:] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, as it is written, "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Although the sages of the nations may originate wisdom in matters of the service of the Blessed One, it is not reckoned as Oral Torah — only what the Sages of Israel originate. And this is "He shone forth from Seir to them": human wisdom, which is chiefly in Seir, as the Sages said, "There is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'"; and this shone forth to Israel, to be theirs alone, for nothing is called wisdom but the wisdom of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 17): "You have taken gifts among men [ba-adam]" — these are the spoils taken from Esau, the power of "we will do"; for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom,'" that is, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, to rectify the excess of anger, while might is used only to conquer the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it.׳).
resembling an intrinsic part permanently cleaved to the Whole (Eichah Rabbah 2:9).
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
And our Sages of blessed memory declared:
״יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת — תַּאֲמִין,
“If someone says to you there is wisdom among the nations, believe it,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם׳;
as it is written: ‘I will destroy the wise men from Edom’;
תּוֹרָה — אַל תַּאֲמִין״;
but if he says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it”;
כִּי חָכְמָתָם אֵינָהּ קְרוּיָה תּוֹרָה כְּלַל,
for their wisdom cannot be called Torah at all,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהִיא נִפְרֶדֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
since it is severed and divorced from the blessed Hashem.
וְלָמְדוּ חָכְמָתָם מֵאֱדוֹם,
And the Sages derived the existence of gentile wisdom specifically from Edom,
כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ עִקַּר חָכְמַת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
because from Edom stems the core intellect of the gentile world.
כִּי כָּל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת חָכְמָה בָּעוֹלָם,
For any proliferation of intellect in the universe
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם.
emanates solely from the radiant spread of the Torah's wisdom through creation.
וְ״אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא״
And “Torah emerges from the side of Gevurah (Might)”

(זֹהַר, חֵלֶק ג׳, פ׳ עַמּוּד ב1079 Zohar 3:80b — Purity is found in the Torah, as it is written, "The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever" (Psalms 19:10). He said to him: "The fear of the Lord" is written, and not "Torah"! He said to him: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Might. He said to him: And does it come from there? It comes from here, as it is written, "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord" (Psalms 111:10), and it is written, "The fear of the Lord is pure." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 21): There was still lacking one more Sabbath, that of the attribute of Gevurah, which is the essential one for the Giving of the Torah, since "the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah." As long as they had not received the Torah and brought it down to earth, the revelation of the supernal holiness of that attribute's Sabbath, namely its inclusion within the attribute of Chesed, so that "from His right hand [went] a fiery law for them," was not yet within their reach; that came about on the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah.׳),
(Zohar III, 80b),
מִיִּצְחָק אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
emanating through Isaac our patriarch, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב,
who fathered Jacob,
שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ ״אֱמֶת״,
whose foundational attribute is Truth,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה
which is the inner root of the Torah
דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ ״אֱמֶת״,
of which it is written “truth”,
וְנִקְרֵאת ״תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת״,
and is called “the Torah of truth”,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקַּר הַתּוֹרָה:
which is the essential purpose of the Torah:
שֶׁהִיא חָכְמָה אֲמִתִּית הַקַּיֶּמֶת לָעַד.
that it is absolute, enduring truth established forever.
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמַת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
Not so the external wisdom of the nations,
דְּאֵין לָהּ מְצִיאוּת אֶלָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which has existence solely within this physical world;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִים מֵהֶם הַטּוֹב
and Israel extracts from them whatever sparks of good
הַשַּׁיָּךְ לְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה.
are properly affiliated with the wisdom of the Torah.
וְיָבוֹא יוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי״ וְגוֹמֵר,
And the day will arrive when it is fulfilled: “I will destroy the wise men from Edom”,
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין לָהּ שַׁיָּכוּת לְתוֹרַת אֱמֶת
and therefore that wisdom has no permanence in the Torah of truth
שֶׁקַּיֶּמֶת לְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים.
which endures for all eternity.
וְרַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And only in this mundane world,
דִּ״בְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא״,
where “first comes darkness”,
בָּאָה חָכְמָה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִסִּטְרָא דְּחֹשֶׁךְ,
did this wisdom likewise emerge from the realm of darkness,
וְנוֹלַד עֵשָׂו —
and Esau was born—
הַקְּלִפָּה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַפְּרִי,
the coarse shell that precedes the inner fruit,
וְ״צַיִד בְּפִיו״.
with “game in his mouth”.
וְיָדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָאֱלֹהִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק, זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
And known are the teachings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory,
דְּרוֹמֵז לְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
that this secretly alludes to the mysteries of the Oral Torah,
וְהֵם נִשְׁמוֹת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
being the elevated souls of Rabbi Akiva,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ,
who is the fountainhead of all the Oral Torah in our hands,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין פ״ו1080 Sanhedrin 86a — R. Yochanan said: An anonymous mishnah is R. Meir; an anonymous Tosefta is R. Nechemyah; an anonymous Sifra is R. Yehudah; an anonymous Sifrei is R. Shimon — and all of them follow R. Akiva. Rashi: An anonymous Sifra is Toras Kohanim; an anonymous Sifrei is [the midrash on] the Book of Numbers and Deuteronomy. "Following R. Akiva" — they stated them from what they had learned from R. Akiva. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Things not revealed to Moses were revealed to R. Akiva and his colleagues, for he is the root of the Oral Torah, as it says, "all of them follow R. Akiva"; for he is the "game in the mouth" of Esau the wicked, through Esau's root in Isaac, where the spark of R. Akiva lay. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:79): R. Akiva, who is the foundation of the Oral Torah, as it says, "and all of them follow R. Akiva," was a son of converts, because the Oral Torah comes from the hind side of the Written Torah, which is the level of converts. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 7): R. Akiva is the foundation of the Oral Torah, as it says, "an anonymous Sifrei ... an anonymous Sifra ... and all of them follow R. Akiva"; the phrase "until R. Akiva came and taught" is said of him and of no other, for he was the principal and foundation of the study of the Oral Torah. Its sum is the Sifrei, Sifra, Mishnayos and Baraisos, in which all the words of the Talmud are hinted, as all the words of the decisors, early and late, are hinted in the Talmud: there in concealment, then spreading out, revelation after revelation. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 5): The foundation of the Oral Torah is R. Akiva, as it says in Sanhedrin, "and all of them follow R. Akiva," and in Yevamot, "the world was desolate until R. Akiva came and taught it"; he is the counterpart of Moses and greater than him, for Moses is the foundation of the Written Torah and R. Akiva the foundation of the Oral Torah. He was a son of converts and came from Esau, as the Arizal explained "for game was in his mouth": that [R. Akiva] was in [Esau's] mouth, which is the secret of the Oral Torah. עַמּוּד א׳):
as taught in Sanhedrin (86a):
״וְכֻלְּהוּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא״.
“and all of them follow the methodology of Rabbi Akiva”.
וְאַף דְּהָיָה מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל סִיסְרָא,
And although he descended from Sisera,
הָיָה מִבְּנֵי בְּנוֹתָיו שֶׁל עֵשָׂו.
he was derived maternally from the daughters of Esau.

וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּנָפֵיק מִנֵּירוֹן (מַסֶּכֶת גִּטִּין נ״ו1081 Gittin 56a — They sent Nero Caesar against them. When he came, he shot an arrow eastward and it came and fell in Jerusalem; westward, and it came and fell in Jerusalem; to the four directions of the heavens, and it came and fell in Jerusalem. He said to a child: Recite for me your verse. He said to him: "And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom by the hand of My people Israel." He said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to destroy His House, and wishes to wipe His hands on that man. He fled and went and converted, and R. Meir descended from him. Rashi: "He shot an arrow eastward" — to practise divination, when he was near Jerusalem. "By the hand of My people Israel" — through My people Israel. "To wipe His hands" — to clean His hands [upon that man]. Maharsha: He did this by way of divination when he was near the city, as Rashi explains; but it appears that he stood at one of the four sides of the city and shot his arrows to the four directions, in which case one of the four necessarily faced Jerusalem and there would be no wonder in its falling there — so perhaps he was not near enough to reach the city by shooting, and the wind carried the arrow to the city by a miracle. "And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom" — "My vengeance," because they destroyed the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the Second Temple, and the vengeance is to be by the hand of My people Israel, unlike the First Temple, where the vengeance came not through Israel but through the kingdom of Persia. And this is what he said: the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to destroy His House — for were it not His will it would not be in our power to destroy it — and wishes to wipe His hands on that man. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 5): Nero was not at the utmost degree of wickedness, and the Caesar's order that he destroy Jerusalem laid upon him a thing for which he was not fitted; and whoever is compelled to something for which he is not fitted and prepared braces himself against it. Therefore Nero stood firm against it and converted altogether — whereas Titus the wicked was indeed fitted for that wickedness. עַמּוּד א׳),
And Rabbi Meir descended from Nero (Gittin 56a),
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת,
who stands as the root of the Mishnayot,
דִּ״סְתָם מַתְנִיתִין — רַבִּי מֵאִיר״,
for an anonymous Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir,
שֶׁהֵם עִקַּר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
which form the very core of the Oral Torah;
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, מִסְּתָמָא יֵשׁ בּוֹ
and similarly, there evidently resided in that nation
עֲדַיִן אֵיזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ
some holy spark
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִקָּלֵט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
destined to be absorbed and gathered into Israel.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ אֶצְלָם
And from this concealed root flows
הַחָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִיּוּת,
their external secular wisdom,
עַד שֶׁיִּגָּמֵר כָּל קְלִיטַת הַטּוֹב,
until the extraction of all holy sparks is completed,
וְאָז תֹּאבַד כָּל חָכְמָתָם גַּם כֵּן.
whereupon all their wisdom will likewise perish.
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא בְּסִטְרָא דְּרַע
And Amalek, on the side of evil,
תַּמְצִית וּכְלוּלוּת הָרָע שֶׁבְּעֵשָׂו.
is the distilled essence and totality of corruption within Esau.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּכְלַל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And just as among the seed of Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
דְּהַגַּם דְּכֻלָּם קֹדֶשׁ,
although they are all fundamentally holy,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ נִבְחָר גַּם בָּהֶם,
there is yet a chosen sanctified tier among them,
וְנִבְדַּל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ ״קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים״,
and Aaron was set apart to be consecrated as “holy of holies”,
וְכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו —
and his descendants after him—
מִשְׁפַּחַת כְּהֻנָּה לְבַד
the priestly family alone
נִבְדָּלִים לִקְדֻשָּׁה מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
are sanctified above the congregation of Israel,
וְרִבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְוֹת יְתֵרוֹת;
and Scripture assigned them additional commandments;
כֵּן ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״,
so too, in direct negative mirror-image,
עֲמָלֵק בְּזֶרַע עֵשָׂו
Amalek among the descendants of Esau
רִבָּה בְּעַצְמוֹ טֻמְאוֹת יְתֵרוֹת,
heaped upon himself excess defilement,
וְנִבְדַּל מִכְּלַל זֶרַע עֵשָׂו
and separated himself from all of Esau's seed
לִהְיוֹת אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה.
to become the supreme progenitor of all spiritual impurity.
וְעַל כֵּן בָּא שֵׁנִית
Therefore Amalek launched his second assault
בְּשָׁמְעוֹ מִמִּיתַת אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
upon hearing of the death of Aaron the Priest, peace be upon him.
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is not mentioned
בְּמִלְחַמְתּוֹ,
in the active warfare against him,
כִּי שָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּרֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִפָּה, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
because Amalek's taproot is in the primal head of the unholy shell, as noted,
שֶׁנֶּעְלַם אוֹתוֹ שַׁעַר רֵאשִׁית דִּקְדֻשָּׁה.
standing opposite that Fiftieth Gate of holiness that was concealed.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בַּמִּלְחָמָה רִאשׁוֹנָה:
Therefore in the first battle at Rephidim it states:
״כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ״,
“Whenever Moses held up his hand”,
וְהַיְינוּ בִּתְפִלָּה,
meaning through prayer,
שֶׁאָחַז אָז בְּדַרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה —
for Moses then grasped the spiritual level of prayer—
מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which is the attribute of King David, peace be upon him,
הַנִּקְרָא ״מֶלֶךְ הָאָרֶץ״,
who is called “king of the earth”,
סִטְרָא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
the dimension of Knesset Yisrael,
שֶׁהוּא הָאִשָּׁה יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם,
symbolized by the woman who fears Hashem,
בְּתֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק,
in the utmost intensity of pure yearning,
דְּבָזֶה יֵשׁ דְּבֵקוּת עִם שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים גַּם כֵּן.
through which there is a cleaving even to the Fiftieth Gate.
אֲבָל בְּפַעַם שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁבָּא,
However, in the second attack (at Hormah),
אַחַר שֶׁנִּגְזַר עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
after it had been decreed upon Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
שֶׁלֹּא לִכָּנֵס לָאָרֶץ,
that he would not enter the Holy Land,
נֶאֱמַר: ״וַיִּדַּר יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶדֶר״ וְגוֹמֵר,
Scripture states: “And Israel vowed a vow...”,
״וַיִּשְׁמַע הַשֵּׁם בְּקוֹל יִשְׂרָאֵל״ וְגוֹמֵר.
“and Hashem listened to the voice of Israel...”
וְהוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this invokes the specific attribute of Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהִתְחִיל לִהְיוֹת נוֹדֵר בְּעֵת צָרָה.
who first introduced the practice of making a vow in a time of distress.
וְעִנְיַן הַנֶּדֶר,
And the spiritual mechanism of a vow,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: ״כִּי יַפְלִא״,
described by the Torah as ki yafli (“when one sets apart a wondrous vow”),
שֶׁהוּא מִדְּבָרִים הַמֻּפְלָאִים
is that it derives from realms wondrous (mufla)
וְנֶעְלָמִים מִכָּל בְּרִיָּה,
and concealed beyond the reach of any creature,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת
which cannot be deduced
עַל פִּי חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה כְּלַל
from the standard revealed wisdom of the Torah
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אָסוּר לוֹ אוֹ צָרִיךְ לוֹ,
that this matter is forbidden or incumbent upon him,
כִּי הוּא מִצַּד הַשַּׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנֶּעְלָם.
because it draws from the hidden Fiftieth Gate.
וְרַק ״יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה״,
And only “Israel arose in the primordial Divine thought”,
הִיא הַחָכְמָה הַנִּקְרֵאת ״פֶּלֶא״,
which is the transcendent wisdom termed Peleh (Wonder),
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּתוֹרָה,
the concealed root of the Torah,
שֶׁהִיא ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה״,
for the Torah is “an offshoot of Supernal Wisdom”,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ז)1082 Bereshit Rabbah 17:5 — R. Chanina bar Yitzchak said: There are three unripe fruits [novelot]: sleep is an unripe fruit of death; a dream, of prophecy; the Sabbath, of the World to Come. R. Avin adds two more: the orb of the sun is an unripe fruit of the light above; the Torah, of the wisdom above. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Written Torah is only the "unripe fruit" of the supernal Wisdom; the chief desire for words of Torah lies in the Oral Torah, in the renewal of Torah insights in the hearts of Israel, which is the drawing-down of the supernal Wisdom itself, above the revelation of the Written Torah through Moses. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): The Written Torah is the prophetic attainment of a great prophet such as Moses, but "a sage is greater than a prophet," for by the holy spirit he attains, from the supernal holiness, the supernal Wisdom that is above the Written Torah, which is the "unripe fruit" of the supernal Wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): The Written Torah is the "unripe fruit" of the supernal Wisdom, but the Oral Torah draws wisdom from the very body of the supernal Wisdom; therefore "a sage is greater than a prophet," for the prophecy of the sages is their attainment of wisdom through the holy spirit. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): The Oral Torah is attained through the holy spirit and is a drawing-down from the supernal holiness, which is the supernal Wisdom, whereas the Written Torah is the "unripe fruit" of the supernal Wisdom..
as recorded in Bereishit Rabbah (17).
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבוּקִים בְּאוֹתוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ,
And all Israel are cleaved to that transcendent root,
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה
and from this level
יָבוֹא בְּמַחְשֶׁבֶת אָדָם לִדּוֹר אֵיזֶה נֶדֶר,
the impulse enters a person's thought to make a specific vow,
וְהוּא מִצַּד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנֶּעְלָם
reflecting the hidden will of Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלָּה בַּתּוֹרָה.
that was not explicitly revealed within the Torah.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה
And through this divine connection
הוּא הַנִּצּוּחַ לַעֲמָלֵק,
comes the victory over Amalek,
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לְכָל מִינֵי צָרוֹת וְיִסּוּרִין,
who is the cosmic source of all distress and affliction
רָצָה לוֹמַר: הַבָּאִים עַל אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי,
that strike a Jewish individual,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
who is required to examine his deeds;
וְאִם פִּשְׁפֵּשׁ וְלֹא מָצָא חִסָּרוֹן כְּלַל מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה —
and if he examined and found no specific violation of Torah—

יִתְלֶה בְּבִטּוּל תּוֹרָה (מַסֶּכֶת בְּרָכוֹת ה1083 Berakhot 5a — Rava, and some say Rav Chisda, said: If a man sees that sufferings come upon him, let him examine his deeds, as it is said, "Let us search and examine our ways, and return to the Lord." If he examined and found nothing, let him attribute it to neglect of Torah, as it is said, "Happy is the man whom You chasten, O Lord, and whom You teach out of Your Torah." Rashi: "He examined and found nothing" — he found no transgression in his hand on account of which these sufferings would be fitting to come. "Happy is the man whom You chasten, O Lord, and whom You teach out of Your Torah" — for it is through suffering that a man must come to the study of Torah. Maharsha: "He examined and found nothing" cannot mean that he found no sin at all, for "there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins"; it means that he found no grave transgression of his on account of which these particular sufferings should come, as Rashi explains. From the verse "Happy is the man whom You chasten" we learn both things — that sufferings come through neglect of Torah, and that through Torah they keep away from a man: let him examine them and recognize that they came through neglect of Torah, and then "You teach him out of Your Torah," for he will return to occupy himself with it so that they depart from him. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaYissurin 1): A man is to attribute his sufferings first to sin and only afterwards to neglect of Torah, because sin is the primary and nearest cause of suffering: sin is a deficiency in a man — such is the meaning of the word "chet" — and when a man has sinned and is deficient, it is fitting that sufferings, which diminish a man, should come upon him. Neglect of Torah is not so, for one who neglects Torah is not deficient in himself; he is called deficient only in that he could have perfected himself further through the Torah and instead remains in the deficiency in which he was created. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 11): The Toras Kohanim concludes that David justified the judgment upon himself, as it says, "My wounds stink and fester because of my folly"; this is in the manner of the Gemara, "If a man sees sufferings coming upon him, let him examine his deeds... if he found nothing, let him attribute it to neglect of Torah." That is the meaning of "because of my folly," namely neglect of Torah: though he found no sin in his hand, he justified the judgment upon himself. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 14): It is impossible to be saved at every moment from neglecting a positive commandment such as Torah study, for whenever one turns his heart to idleness for a moment he neglects a positive commandment. That is why they said, "If he examined and found nothing, let him attribute it to neglect of Torah": this is found in every person, even a perfectly righteous man who examined and found no sin at all and presumably toils in Torah all day — he can still attribute it to a few moments' neglect of Torah — except for the rare remnant, such as R. Shimon ben Yochai and his companions, the true Torah scholars, all of whose speech and heart's musing, even in worldly matters, are words of Torah.׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
he should attribute it to bitul Torah (Berakhot 5a),
רָצָה לוֹמַר: רִפּוּי יָדַיִם,
meaning laxity of hands,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה
for through this weakness
מִתְעוֹרֵר שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּרַע דַּעֲמָלֵק.
the hidden root of Amalek's evil is aroused.
וַעֲצַת יִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא,
And the counsel of Yisrael Saba (Jacob our Patriarch),
שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
whose form is engraved on the Throne of Glory,
כִּי הוּא ״הַקַּו הָאֶמְצָעִי הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה״,
being the central pillar traversing from one extreme to the other,
וְדָבוּק בְּפֶלֶא הָעֶלְיוֹן —
and bound directly to the Supernal Wonder—
הוּא לִדּוֹר נֶדֶר.
is to invoke this power by making a vow.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בְּמִקְרָא זֶה
Therefore this verse employs
הַשֵּׁם ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וְלֹא ״בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
the singular name “Israel”, and not “the Children of Israel”,
דְּדֶרֶךְ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם
for it is the method of our Sages everywhere
לְפָרְשׁוֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא.
to interpret this as referring to Yisrael Saba himself.
וְזֶהוּ: ״וַיִּשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל״,
And this is why it says: “and He listened to the voice”,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי ״הַקּוֹל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״,
for through the power of “the voice is the voice of Jacob”,
אֵין הַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו שׁוֹלְטוֹת.
the hands of Esau cannot dominate.
וְקוֹל הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דִּדְכוּרָא,
And voice belongs to the masculine aspect,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּקוֹל וְדִבּוּר הֵם זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה,
as voice and articulated speech represent male and female,
דְּדִבּוּר רוֹמֵז לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
wherein speech alludes to the Oral Torah.
וְסֵפֶר דְּבָרִים,
And the Book of Deuteronomy,
שֶׁאֲמָרָן מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ
which Moses spoke from his own mouth

(זֹהַר, חֵלֶק ג׳, רס״א עַמּוּד א1084 Zohar 3:261a — That which is called Mishneh Torah — Moses said it of his own accord; and we have already established the matter. Why is this so? Supernal Wisdom is called the whole of the Torah, and from it everything issues by way of that innermost voice. Afterward all is settled and joined in the place called the Tree of Life, and upon it depend the general and the particular, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah; and it is called Torah and Mishneh Torah. At first there was unceasing Might, and now all is one.׳),
(Zohar III, 261a),
הוּא הַשָּׂגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
represented the Oral Torah's attainment
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
in Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא רַק ״מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה״ שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
serving as a repetition and review of the Written Torah.
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
For the root of Moses our teacher
הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
is anchored in the Written Torah,
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם דִּבּוּרָיו נִקְרָאִים תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
and therefore even his own spoken words are categorized as Written Torah.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ,
Nevertheless, because they issued from his own mouth,
נִקְרָא הַסֵּפֶר ״דְּבָרִים״,
the book is titled Devarim (Words),
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִכְלָל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
yet it remains completely incorporated within the Written Torah.
וַחֲמִשָּׁה קוֹלוֹת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And the five voices heard at Mount Sinai
הֵם נֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חֻמְשֵׁי תּוֹרָה.
correspond to the Five Books of the Torah.
