וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, ״מֹשֶׁה יְדַבֵּר״ —
And at Sinai, “Moses spoke”—
הוּא הַשָּׂגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
signified the revelation of the Oral Torah,
וְכָל מַה שֶׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ,
including every insight a veteran disciple would ever innovate,
דְּנִגְלָה הַכֹּל לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
all of which was unveiled to Moses our teacher

(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה, רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כ״ב)1085 Vayikra Rabbah 22:1 — “All,” “the all”; “words,” “the words”; “commandment,” “the commandment” — Scripture, Mishnah, laws, Talmud, Toseftot and Aggadot, and even what a veteran student is destined to say before his teacher: all of them were said to Moshe at Sinai. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Through "I have put My words in your mouth," all the wisdom of the sages of the Oral Torah is the words of the living God, as [the Sages said,] all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was said to Moses at Sinai. Therefore "a sage is greater than a prophet": though [his attainment] is in concealment, he attains more and merits "to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:80): In the wisdom of R. Akiva, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, there is certainty only when the Blessed One enlightens [the sage's] eyes [to see] that this law is a halakhah to Moses from Sinai, as the Sages said that all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was said to Moses at Sinai. This means that it is true wisdom: he recognizes and knows that it is certainly a halakhah to Moses from Sinai, so that his innovation is the innovation of a veteran student. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 7): The Oral Torah is what the Scribes innovated, flowing from the hearts of Israel, and what a veteran student will in the future innovate, and the Sages said that all of it was revealed to Moses. Just as all souls were revealed to Adam because, as their father, he contained them all, so Moses, whose soul contained all the wisdom of the Written Torah, thereby contained all the wisdom of the Oral Torah as well, since it all flows from it and is hinted in it. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): It is not that Moses did not attain what the sage attains: by the holy spirit he certainly attained it, and all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was revealed to him, which is the attainment of the Oral Torah by way of wisdom and understanding of the heart. But in prophecy, what the Blessed One showed him in the manner of the prophets was revealed to him only according to his level. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): "And I will proclaim the name of the Lord" refers to the thirteen attributes of mercy, which are the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, the foundation of the Oral Torah; and then He revealed to [Moses] all that a veteran student would in the future innovate. Therefore He said, "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," even to one who is not worthy, for [Moses] saw that young students would in the future innovate great things hidden from the great ones of the generations before them. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 5): Hillel's chief foundation was the Oral Torah, hence [the Sages] said he was fit for the Shechinah to rest upon him, for the revelation of the Oral Torah comes through the resting of the Shechinah, and through this all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was revealed to Moses..
(Vayikra Rabbah 22).
״וְהָאֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל״ —
“And God answered him with a voice”—
הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
represented the Written Torah.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת בְּרָכוֹת מ״ה1086 Berakhot 45a — R. Shimon ben Pazzi said: Whence do we know that the translator may not raise his voice above that of the reader? For it is said, "Moses would speak and God would answer him with a voice." "With a voice" need not have been said; and why is it said? With the voice of Moses. Tosafos (s.v. "with the voice of Moses"): If you ask: how is a proof brought from here? What is needed is a case where Moses was translating and did not raise his voice above that of the Holy One, blessed be He, who was reading — yet the verse shows that the Holy One was reading and Moses translating. The Rif explained: presumably Moses answered with all his strength, so as to make his voice heard to the whole people, while the Holy One had no need to raise His voice, since He was speaking to Moses alone; even so He raised it, so that the voice of Moses the translator should not be louder than the voice of the Holy One who was reading. Maharsha: All of Tosafot's discussion rests on their understanding that the Holy One, blessed be He, was the reader and Moses the translator. Were it not for their words, it would seem better to explain that Moses was the reader and the Holy One the translator: Moses read only in the holy tongue, which not everyone understands, whereas every utterance that issued from the mouth of the Holy One was divided into seventy languages (Shabbat 88a) — that is, He translated for each one according to the language he understood. עַמּוּד א׳):
And the Sages of blessed memory noted (Berakhot 45a):
״בְּקוֹלוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה״,
“with the voice of Moses”,
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
because the Written Torah
נִקְרָאת ״תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה״,
is specifically called “the Torah of Moses”,
וְהוּא עִקַּר מַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ,
and it constitutes his primary allotted portion,
לֹא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
rather than the Oral Torah;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר: ״לֹא אִישׁ דְּבָרִים אָנֹכִי״.
which is why he proclaimed: “I am not a man of words (devarim)”.

items.h:
Seif 7 — Moshe, Amalek, Da'at, and Keter
Amalek mirrors Moshe's spiritual level in corruption, explaining why Joshua could only weaken him before Torah's full maturation.

p: וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁקָּם בְּדוֹרוֹ
Amalek, who arose specifically in the generation
שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
כִּי הָיָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בִּקְלִפָּה,
did so because he was his exact counterpart within the realm of the kelipah;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהוּא אֶחָד עִם בִּלְעָם,
as is known that he is united in root with Balaam,
שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר: ״וְיֹדֵעַ דַּעַת
who boasted: “and knows the knowledge
עֶלְיוֹן״ וְגוֹמֵר,
of the Most High...” (Numbers 24:16),
שֶׁהוּא הַדַּעַת דְּרַע.
which represents the evil, corrupted facet of Daat.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַדַּעַת
And it is known that Daat
הוּא הַמַּשְׁלִים עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת בִּפְנִימִיּוּת,
is that which completes the ten sefirot internally,
וְהַכֶּתֶר בְּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת.
while Keter completes them in their transcendent exteriority.

And regarding this, the Sages noted

לְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּמַסֶּכֶת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (כ״א1088 Rosh Hashanah 21b — Rav and Shmuel [differed on the verse “The words of the Lord are pure words… refined sevenfold”]. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all of them were given to Moses save one. “Kohelet sought to find out words of delight” (Ecclesiastes 12:10) — Kohelet sought to be like Moses; a Divine voice went forth and said to him, “and that which was written uprightly, even words of truth”: “And there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses” (Deuteronomy 34:10). And the other said: Among the prophets none arose, but among the kings one did arise. Rashi: Rav and Shmuel are expounding the end of this verse: "refined sevenfold" means seven sevens, which are fifty less one — the gates that were transmitted to Moses; and we learn that fifty were created, since he was made "but little less than God" (a verse from the psalm "What is man that You are mindful of him"). Maharsha: The "words of delight" that Kohelet sought are the gates of intellect and understanding in which the Holy One, blessed be He, delights that man should gain understanding, as it is said: "that he understands and knows Me… for in these I delight" (Jeremiah 9:23). The Divine Voice's "written uprightly" follows the teaching that the "Book of the Upright" is Deuteronomy, of which it is said "and you shall do the upright and the good" (Avodah Zarah 25a): what is written in Deuteronomy — "And there has not arisen a prophet… like Moses" — is words of truth. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 21b): The fiftieth gate corresponds to the Jubilee, which is holy of holies: it is the apprehension of the Holy One, blessed be He, in His own true essence, known to none but Himself, whereas the forty-nine — seven times seven, for the world created in seven days is sevenfold and each of its sevens contains all seven — belong to man, who is in the world. Moses, the seventh righteous man (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehath, Amram, Moses), was fit for the forty-nine, but the fiftieth, which binds and unites all the gates, is beyond one who is in this world, founded as it is on seven. It is called "little" because it is a single gate — little in quantity and great in quality. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 21b, s.v. "but among the kings one did arise"): The Sages expounded the verse because it should have said "Kohelet sought to find delight, to write upright words": "delight" means that he desired to be like the wisest of men, Moses, and "written uprightly" is the answer — though he desired it, so uprightness requires, for no prophet like Moses has arisen again. Nor may one object that if none arose among the prophets, all the more so none could arise among the kings: kingship has a great level of its own, above all the king of Israel — like Solomon, who "sat on the throne of the Lord" (I Chronicles 29:23) and ruled over the upper and the lower beings — to whom an inner level belongs by virtue of kingship. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 5): Of King Solomon they said "among the prophets none arose [like Moses], but among the kings one did arise": that is, by way of the attribute of Kingship, the revelation of the glory of His Presence among the lower beings, which is the apprehension of the holy spirit, the prophecy of the Sages, who surpass prophets. For prophets see only what they are shown, whereas those who possess the holy spirit attain the matter through contemplation and the searching of their intellect, and this is through the attribute of Kingship, the lower Wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Noach 8): Solomon said, "God is with me and His wisdom is mine, and I am able to do my will," which is his saying "I will multiply and not turn aside"; this came about because the supernal Wisdom was given over to him, and of him there is an opinion in the Gemara that of "there has not arisen a prophet like Moses": among the prophets none arose, but among the kings one did. Because he said "God is with me and His wisdom is mine," he said "I will multiply and not turn aside"; unlike Moses, who did not recognize the eminence of his own level at all, but held himself only in the aspect of faith like all Israel. עַמּוּד ב׳):

וְהַשָּׂגַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא —
Whereas the perception of the World to Come—
״עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה״;
is that which “no eye has seen”;
רָצָה לוֹמַר: עֵינֵי הַנְּבִיאִים
meaning: even the visionary eyes of prophets
הָרוֹאִים בָּעַיִן.
who perceive through direct visual manifestation.
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן הַשָּׂגַת הַחֲכָמִים,
Not so the profound comprehension of Torah sages,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם,
which operates through the subtle medium of hiddenness,
יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג
they are able to touch and grasp
גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם.
even the most transcendent, concealed root.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר:
And although concerning this realm it was cautioned:
״בְּמֻפְלָא מִמְּךָ אַל תִּדְרֹשׁ״ וְכוּלֵי,
“Into that which is wondrous beyond you, do not inquire...” (Chagigah 13a),
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם מֵעֵין כָּל בְּרִיָּה
for the root concealed from the eye of every creature
נִקְרָא ״מֻפְלָא״,
is called mufla (wondrous),
שֶׁהוּא פֶּלֶא הָעֶלְיוֹן,
being the Supernal Wonder,
שֶׁאֵין רְשׁוּת לַחְקֹר שָׁם כְּלַל;
where one has no license to philosophically investigate at all;
הַיְינוּ לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
this prohibition applies to comprehending it exhaustively
דֶּרֶךְ הַחָכְמָה.
through human intellectual mastery.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
Yet nevertheless,
יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ,
the sages possess a deep, intuitive anchor within it,
מִצַּד שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמָתָם;
because from that very height stems the root of their Torah wisdom;
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהִיא חָכְמַת לִבָּם
and since it is the authentic wisdom of their hearts
שֶׁשָּׁבָה לִהְיוֹת תּוֹרָה,
that has been transformed into living Torah,
הֲלֹא הִיא אֲחוּזָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁהּ.
it remains irrevocably bound to its celestial origin.
וְעַל כֵּן נִצּוּחַ עֲמָלֵק —
Therefore, the vanquishing of Amalek—
רַק עַל יְדֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
could be accomplished only through Joshua,
וְגַם בִּהְיוֹתוֹ מִזַּרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל;
and specifically through his descent from Rachel;
דְּרָחֵל הִיא הָרוֹמֶזֶת לְעָלְמָא תַּתָּאָה,
for Rachel embodies the Lower World (Alma Tata'ah),
מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת,
the attribute of Malchut,
סוֹד חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה.
the mystical secret of the Lower Wisdom.
וְזֶהוּ: ״לְפִי חָרֶב״;
And this is the meaning of: “according to the edge (literally, mouth) of the sword”;
כִּי כְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה —
for the totality of the Torah—
הִיא הַחֶרֶב,
is the sword itself,
וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
while the Oral Torah
נִקְרָא ״פִּי הַחֶרֶב״;
is called “the mouth/edge of the sword”;
וְשָׁם עִקַּר שִׁנּוּן הַחֶרֶב,
and therein lies the lethal sharpening of the blade,
הַמַּכֶּה וּמֵמִית לְכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
which strikes down and slays all the idolatrous forces,
דְּעִקַּר נִצּוּחָם
since their ultimate defeat
הוּא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
is effected through the Oral Torah;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
as the Sages of blessed memory expounded

(מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא, פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא, ל״ד)1089 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34 — R. Yehudah bar Shalom said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "Write these words," Moses asked that the Mishnah too be put in writing. But the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the nations of the world were destined to translate the Torah and read it in Greek, and to say, "We are Israel." Until now the scales are balanced. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the nations: You say that you are My children — I do not know; only those who hold My mysteries are My children. And which are they? This is the Mishnah, which was given orally, and from which everything is to be expounded. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): After prophecy departed, the sages of the Oral Torah began, and the Sages said, "He has set me in dark places — this is the Talmud of Babylonia"; but this is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says in Tanchuma, "Those who hold My mysteries are Israel." For it is written, "He made darkness His hiding place" — there are His hidden things; and though it is darkness and the hiding of the Face, the darkness is cast by the shadow of His hand, shielding us by way of concealment, as one must make shade to protect against the blazing sun. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:86): The Blessed One teaches human beings to exert effort, which is why the Torah began for Israel as the Written Torah; He wishes a person to arrive at His mysteries — as in the Midrash, "He who holds My mysteries…" — and to understand what He indicates to him with the compass. This is the essential effort: to come to the Oral Torah, which is the recognition that everything is from the Blessed One, the "finding" that comes after toil. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): The novel insights of Torah belong to the Oral Torah, whereas in the Written Torah, which is written and set down [before all], there are no novel insights; therefore the nations claim on the strength of the Written Torah, "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers, "He who holds My mysteries…," for the Oral Torah exists only in the hearts of the children of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Edom claims that they are the good and the pure by birth; therefore Haman's decree was a preparation for the Oral Torah, as the Midrash says: because the nations are destined to say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "He who holds My mysteries…" — for it is the Oral Torah that clarifies this. The Oral Torah is what springs from the heart of Israel, the hearts of the children of Israel being its originators, so that it is theirs alone, and this is the testimony that they, and no others, are the masters of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Just as there is wisdom among the nations but no Torah among the nations, so it says in Tanchuma, "He who holds My mysteries…": the Oral Torah was given over only to Israel. The nations, even if they study Torah and innovate in it by their wisdom, speak vanity and not Torah at all, for they innovate from their own wisdom, whereas the Torah is the wisdom of the Blessed One; but the sages of Israel bless over the Torah first and know that the Blessed One is the Giver of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 3): The essence of the Torah is the Oral Torah, which reveals the hidden things of the Written Torah, as it says in Shemos Rabbah that the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek… "He who holds My mysteries…." This is an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob alone: the Torah is handed over to them according to what they clarify through their dialectic and their wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): They said in Tanchuma that the Oral Torah was given because the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek and say "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say, "He who holds My mysteries…." That is, the nations too have a connection to the Written Torah, which is why it was revealed in writing to all who come into the world; but the Oral Torah is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, which cannot be revealed in writing at all, only "the secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him" — the Congregation of Israel, who look to the Blessed One from the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): All the innovation of the Oral Torah comes through the unions and complete cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is His mysteries, as they said in Tanchuma at the end of Ki Sisa: because the nations of the world are destined to translate the Torah and say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "He who holds My mysteries…." This is the telling of secrets, which is for Jacob alone — and "telling" does not mean in writing — so "He tells [His words to Jacob]" means the Oral Torah, the handing over of the words of Torah of which it is said "He has not done so for any nation"; whereas the Written Torah alone was written on the stones in seventy languages.:
(Midrash Tanchuma, Parshat Ki Tisa 34):
דַּעֲתִידִין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר:
in the future the nations of the world will claim:
״אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
“We are Israel!”
״מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי״ וְכוּלֵי.
and Hashem replies: “Only he who possesses My secret oral tradition...”
וַעֲמָלֵק בְּיִחוּד,
And Amalek in particular,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַצְּחוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
cannot be subdued except through this unique power.
וְאָז
And in that initial desert battle,
לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן ״פִּי הַחֶרֶב״ הַגָּמוּר,
the absolute “mouth of the sword” had not yet fully matured,
כִּי הָיָה בְּדוֹר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
because it took place in the generation of Moses our teacher,
וְקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב גַּם כֵּן;
and even prior to the Giving of the Written Torah;
רַק ״הֶחֱלִישׁוֹ״;
it thus only “weakened” him;
״לְפִי״ — הַלָּשׁוֹן מוֹרֶה עַל הַסְּמִיכוּת:
“le-fi” (towards the mouth)—the terminology signifies proximity:
סָמוּךְ לְפִי הַחֶרֶב,
drawn near to the cutting edge of the sword,
כִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיָה סָמוּךְ לָזֶה.
for Joshua stood immediately adjacent to this power.

items.h:
Seif 8 — Haman and the Birth of Oral Torah
Haman emerges as the shell preceding the Men of the Great Assembly, while Esther reveals Israel's hidden bond within exile.

p: וְהָמָן קָם
And Haman arose
בַּזְּמַן תְּחִלַּת צְמִיחַת
at the time of the first burgeoning
יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
of the foundation of the Oral Torah,
עַל יְדֵי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה.
established through the Men of the Great Assembly.
וְהוּא הַקְּלִפָּה
And he was the unholy shell
שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַפְּרִי אָז,
that preceded the fruit at that era;
שֶׁלָּמְדוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
for our Sages of blessed memory derived

בְּמַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה (ט״ז1090 Megillah 16a — "And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to all who loved him" — it calls them "those who loved him" and it calls them "his wise men." R. Yochanan said: Whoever speaks a word of wisdom, even among the nations of the world, is called a wise man. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): The "word of wisdom" for which they are called wise men is a word of Torah wisdom, namely the advice that follows: "If he descends from the other tribes you can prevail over him, but if from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim or Manasseh, you cannot prevail over him." They already knew that Mordecai was a Jew, for the decree against the Jews had been published in every province; but until now they had supposed he came from one of the other tribes and that Haman could prevail over him, and only now, seeing the beginning of Haman's fall, did they take fright and say "If Mordecai be of the seed of the Jews" — that is, of those tribes over whom you cannot prevail. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 7): As stated in Megillah, one who says a word of wisdom among the nations is called a wise man — learned from Haman's "wise men," who grasped the truth that he would fall before the seed of the Jews. For this is the whole wisdom of the nations: to grasp the superiority of Israel, that they cannot prevail against them; but to grasp the wisdom of truth, the wisdom of the Torah — the apprehension of His truth — is impossible for them, for "He has not done so for any nation." עַמּוּד א׳):
in Tractate Megillah (16a):
דְּהָאוֹמֵר דְּבַר חָכְמָה בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם —
that one who articulates a word of wisdom among the nations—
נִקְרָא ״חָכָם״;
is termed a “sage”;
מֵחֲכָמָיו דְּהָמָן,
as derived from the “wise men” of Haman,
שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים ״חֲכָמָיו״,
who are explicitly designated “his wise men”,
כִּי לָקְחוּ חָכְמָתָם מִמֶּנּוּ.
because they drew their wisdom from him.
כְּנִכְתָּב לְעֵיל,
As written above,
דְּכָל שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמָה
that the entire root of secular wisdom
שֶׁל כָּל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
found among all the nations of the world
הוּא מִזֶּרַע עֵשָׂו.
stems from the seed of Esau.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ שָׁרְשָׁם
And the deepest taproot of their wisdom
בַּעֲמָלֵק,
lies embedded in Amalek,
וּבְהָמָן בְּיִחוּד,
and particularly in Haman,
שֶׁהָיָה אָז
who emerged precisely then
בִּצְמִיחַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
during the sprouting of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְהַפְּכוּת חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית
which represents the transformation of human intellect
לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
into words of holy Torah,
לִהְיוֹת גַּם חָכְמָתָם
so that their human wisdom as well
קְרוּיָה ״חָכְמָה״ בֶּאֱמֶת.
is rightfully recognized as true wisdom.
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הַוָּלָדַת כָּל דָּבָר,
And it is known that the birth of any reality
הוּא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ
must inevitably be preceded
לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלָּה נִפְסָד וּכְאַיִן,
by a state of decay and reduction to nothingness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַזֶּרַע נִפְסָד בָּאָרֶץ
just as a seed must decompose in the soil
טֶרֶם יַצְמִיחַ.
before it can sprout forth.
וְכֵן בַּגָּלוּת,
So too during the Babylonian exile,
נִשְׁכְּחָה לְגַמְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה מֵהֶם
the Torah was almost completely forgotten from among them
בִּכְלַל הָאֻמָּה,
throughout the general nation,
עַד שֶׁמָּצְאוּ כָּתוּב
until they literally had to discover written in the scroll
לַעֲשׂוֹת סֻכּוֹת,
the command to build sukkot,
כִּי לֹא יָדְעוּ מִזֶּה.
because they were no longer aware of it.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּבָבָם
And even though their heart
נָכוֹן עִם הַשֵּׁם בְּיוֹתֵר,
was exceedingly faithful and steadfast toward Hashem,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
nevertheless,
עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה
their active engagement in Torah study
הָיָה שָׁם בִּבְחִינַת שֵׁנָה וְהֶעְלֵם;
lingered there in a state of sleep and concealment;
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״עֵילָם״ —
which is why that province was termed Elam—
לְשׁוֹן ״הֶעְלֵם״.
cognate with he'elem (concealment).

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת פְּסָחִים פ״ז1091 Pesachim 87a — "We have a little sister, and she has no breasts." R. Yochanan said: This is Elam, which was privileged to learn but was not privileged to teach. Rashi: ["Breasts":] to nurse others; ["she has none":] for no benefit comes from her. ["This is Elam":] in which Daniel was, as it is stated, "And I was in Shushan the capital, which is in the province of Elam" (Daniel 8:2); he was privileged to learn but did not spread Torah in Israel — whereas Babylonia raised Ezra the Scribe, of whom it is written, "For Ezra had set his heart to expound the Torah of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statute and judgment" (Ezra 7:10). Maharsha: ["This is Elam, which was privileged to learn":] such as Daniel and Mordechai, as Rashi explains in the second chapter of Kiddushin. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 7): [He cites this statement as it is brought in Kiddushin 49b: of ten measures of haughtiness Elam took nine, and the poverty that is the sign of haughtiness is poverty of Torah, "as it is written, 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts' — this is Elam, which was privileged to learn but was not privileged to teach."] It is clear from this that the haughty man is a physical being; therefore the sign of haughtiness is poverty of Torah. עַמּוּד א׳):
And the Sages of blessed memory remarked (Pesachim 87a):
דְּלָא זָכְתָה לְלַמֵּד;
that Elam “did not merit to teach”;
הַיְינוּ לְהַרְבִּיץ תּוֹרָה,
meaning to disseminate Torah publicly,
שֶׁהוּא הַלִּמּוּד לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
which is the primary instruction of young schoolchildren,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
from which springs the foundation of the Oral Torah;
דְּעַל כֵּן הִזְהִירוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה:
which is why the Men of the Great Assembly exhorted:
״הַעֲמִידוּ תַלְמִידִים הַרְבֵּה״,
“Raise up many disciples,”
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה
and through this,
״תַּעֲשׂוּ סְיָג לַתּוֹרָה״ —
“make a fence for the Torah”—
הֵם הַסְּיָגוֹת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
which are the protective enactments of the Oral Torah.
וּבְהָמָן גַּם כֵּן
And within Haman as well
הָיָה גָּנוּז כֹּחַ זֶה,
this power lay concealed,
דְּמִבְּנֵי בָנָיו
for his future descendants
לָמְדוּ לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן;
would teach Torah to schoolchildren;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא
except that in Haman himself,
הָיָה צַד הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ
it existed in its corrupt manifestation,
שֶׁקָּדַם לַפְּרִי,
as the shell preceding the fruit,
וְרָצָה לִגְבֹּר עַל הַטּוֹב
and he sought to overpower the good
וּלְעָקְרוֹ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לְגַמְרֵי.
and to uproot it completely, Heaven forbid.
וְזֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר;

נִתְגַּלָּה עַל יְדֵי זֶרֶשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ וַחֲכָמָיו,
was brought to light by Zeresh his wife and his wise counselors,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לְפָנָיו,
when they warned him that he would fall before Mordechai,
וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ;
and not articulated by Haman himself;
אַף דְּגַם הוּא הֵבִין זֶה,
for though Haman intuitively sensed this truth,
רָצָה לְהַעֲלִים הַדָּבָר,
he sought to suppress and conceal it,
וְהֵם הוֹצִיאוּהוּ לִידֵי גִּלּוּי,
whereas they forced it into open speech,
וְאָז נִתְקַיֵּם תֵּיכֶף וְנֶאֱבַד.
and once exposed, it was immediately fulfilled and he was destroyed.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיָן שֶׁנִּתַּן בֵּית הָמָן לְאֶסְתֵּר,
And this explains why the house of Haman was given first to Esther,
וְהִיא נְתָנַתּוּ לְמָרְדֳּכַי,
and she then transferred it to Mordechai;
כִּי אֶצְלוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה בְּיוֹתֵר;
for within him this mastery over concealment was greatest;
מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן נָשִׁים,
whereas regarding women,

אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת ל״ג1094 Shabbat 33b — He and his son went and hid in the study hall. Every day his wife would bring them bread and a jug of water, and they would eat. When the decree grew harsh, he said to his son: Women are of light mind; they may torment her and she will disclose us. They went and hid in a cave. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 33b): That is, he was hiding himself, and his wife would bring him his food; afterwards he hid himself more and more, and the Blessed One sustained him, since he could not go out like other men. עַמּוּד ב׳):
our Sages of blessed memory noted (Shabbat 33b):
דְּדַעְתָּן קַלָּה וְאֵינָן בַּעֲלֵי סוֹד,
that their temperament is impressionable and they cannot guard secrets long,
וְעַל כֵּן הִיא בַּסּוֹף גִּלְּתָה הַהֶעְלֵם,
and therefore she ultimately brought the secret into open revelation,
וְאֵצֶל מָרְדֳּכַי, אַדְּרַבָּה,
while with Mordechai, on the contrary,
נִתְחַזֵּק כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם יוֹתֵר.
the power of holy concealment grew even stronger.
וְכָל כֹּחַ קְלִיטַת הַטּוֹב דְּהָמָן
And all absorption of the good sparks from Haman
אַחַר כָּךְ,
in subsequent generations,
כְּפִי מַה שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְמַעְלָה,
in accordance with what I wrote above,
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הֶעְלֵם,
was likewise effected through concealment,
כְּבִיאַת גּוֹי בְּיִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
akin to the union of a gentile with an Israelite woman,
דְּאֵין לוֹ אִישׁוּת בָּהּ,
where no formal Jewish marital status binds them,
וְהַבֵּן כִּשְׁתוּקִי,
and the offspring resembles a shetuki (one whose paternity is silenced),
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אָב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלַל.
having no halachic father within Israel at all.
וְהָמָן דְּנִתְגַּדֵּל אֵצֶל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
And Haman, who was exalted under Ahasuerus,
שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת עִמּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר;
shared an intrinsic affinity with him, as noted;
דְּגַם הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּפָרַס,
for even regarding the good trait found in Persia,

אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת1095 Berakhot 8a-b — A man should always complete his portions together with the congregation — twice the Scripture and once the Targum. Rashi: "Even 'Atarot and Divon'" — a verse which has no Targum. Tosafos (s.v. "he should complete his portions with the congregation"): "With the congregation" means at any time in the week, since the portion begins to be read from the Minchah of Shabbat until the Shabbat following. As for when it must be finished, the Midrash relates that R. Yehudah the Prince charged his sons at his death not to eat bread on Shabbat until they had finished the whole portion; if a man finishes it after his meal he has still done properly, but the choicest way is before it. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAvodah 13): The Torah was given at Sinai, repeated in the Tent of Meeting, and given a third time in the plains of Moab, where Moses "undertook to explain this Torah" [in seventy languages, per Rashi]; hence twice Scripture and once Targum, the Targum being the explanation — for each needs it only in his own language, and the language of the masses of Israel was Aramaic. The inner reason is that the three readings correspond to the three worlds: the two readings of Scripture to this world and the intermediate world, and the Targum to the upper world, for Aramaic is not the particular language of one nation but a language inclusive of all, and so points to the world that includes all. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 13): The Torah has three levels — the revealed, open to all; the hidden, grasped only by the wise; and what points to the World to Come, beyond any man's grasp — and the three readings correspond to them. He prefers to take them from the bottom up: the Targum corresponds to the highest level, the World to Come, for Aramaic is not reckoned a language, so that in it thought is primary, and thought is the highest level. (ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
the Sages of blessed memory observed in Berakhot (8b):
שֶׁהֵם צְנוּעִים וְכוּלֵי;
that they are modest...;
וְעַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּיִחוּד אָמְרוּ
and concerning Ahasuerus specifically they taught

בַּמְּגִלָּה (י״ג1096 Megillah 13a — "In the evening she would come, and in the morning she would return." R. Yochanan said: From the disgrace of that wicked man we learn his praise — that he did not engage in marital relations by day. Rashi: “From the disgrace of that wicked man” — his disgrace is this, that he would take these women and then send them away. Maharsha: Scripture surely did not come to relate the praise of a wicked man but his disgrace, as Rashi explained; it is only that out of his disgrace we incidentally learn his praise. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 2:12–14): Scripture writes this to show that the affair was conducted in the most modest manner possible and not in the way of harlotry, for the honor of Esther, since it would be a disgrace to her to be taken by a gentile in the way of harlotry — and it would be astonishing, too, for the redemption to come about through harlotry, which is a disgrace and a reproach. It may also be said that Scripture speaks of the wicked man's modesty not in order to praise a wicked man, but to tell on what account Esther fell to the lot of Ahasuerus: because there was modesty in him, and modesty is the very essence of Esther, whose name denotes that she kept herself hidden from all. עַמּוּד א׳):
in Megillah (13a):
״מִתּוֹךְ גְּנוּתוֹ״ וְכוּלֵי,
“From his very disgrace...”
וְהַיְינוּ הַצְּנִיעוּת
referring to this trait of modesty
בְּדָבָר אֶחָד שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּפָרַס.
in the one matter practiced in Persia.
וְנִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֶצְלוֹ
And it was made explicit regarding him
שֶׁהוּא הָרֹאשׁ וְהַגָּרוּעַ שֶׁבָּהֶם,
that he was the worst and most depraved of them,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, הָיָה בוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה
nevertheless, this capacity for modesty existed within him
לְטוֹב גַּם כֵּן;
for the good as well;
וְהַקְּלִיטָה מֵהֶם —
and the extraction of sparks from them—
גַּם כֵּן עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה.
proceeded likewise through this hidden path.
וְאֶסְתֵּר, בִּלְקִיחָתָהּ לַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
And Esther, upon being taken to Ahasuerus
וּבְמַלְכוּתָהּ,
and assuming her royal throne,
נִקְרֵאת ״אֶסְתֵּר״ —
was named “Esther”—
לְשׁוֹן הַסְתָּרָה וְהַעֲלָמָה,
from the root of secrecy and concealment,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמְּגִלָּה שָׁם.
as our Sages derived in the Talmud there.
וּתְחִלַּת שְׁמָהּ ״הֲדַסָּה״,
While her original Hebrew name was “Hadassah” (myrtle),
מוֹרֶה עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
pointing directly to the root of Knesset Yisrael;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם:
and as they explained there:
דְּצַדִּיקִים נִקְרָאִים ״הֲדַסִּים״,
that the righteous are designated “myrtles”;
וְהַיְינוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַצִּדְקוּת
which signifies the deep core of righteousness
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
inherent within every single Jew,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים״;
as it is written: “And your people are all righteous”;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַסֶּכֶת סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד1097 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among thorns, its name is still myrtle and people call it myrtle. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious. עַמּוּד א׳)
and as they stated in Sanhedrin (44a)
הַמָּשָׁל עַל הַחוֹטֵא:
the parable concerning the Jewish sinner:
״לַאֲסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי הוֹצֵי״,
“to a myrtle standing among thorns”,
שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל לַהֲדַס
being compared to a myrtle
עַל שֵׁם צִדְקוּתוֹ.
by virtue of his indelible inner righteousness.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ל׳):
And this accords with what is written in Vayikra Rabbah (30):
דַּהֲדַס — רֵיחַ וְלֹא טַעַם,
that the myrtle possesses fragrance but no taste,
מוֹרֶה עַל בַּעֲלֵי מִצְוֹת
symbolizing those who possess good deeds
וְלֹא תוֹרָה;
but lack deep Torah wisdom;
וְזֶהוּ גַּם בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and this remains true even of the transgressors of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
as the Sages stated:
״אֲפִילּוּ רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבָּךְ —
“Even the empty among you—
מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן״.
are as full of mitzvot as a pomegranate.”
וְדֶרֶךְ גִּדּוּל הַהֲדַס
And the natural growth of the myrtle
לִפְעָמִים בֵּינֵי הוֹצֵי,
is frequently amidst briars,
וְהֵם הַחֲטָאִים הַסּוֹבְבִים,
which represent the sins that encompass the person,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, ״אָסָא שְׁמֵיהּ״.
and yet “a myrtle remains its name.”
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן אֶסְתֵּר:
And this is the entire underlying theme of Esther:
לְבָרֵר דְּאַף שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל
to demonstrate that even when Israel finds itself
בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶסְתֵּר וְהַהֶעְלֵם,
in the deepest abyss of hiddenness and exile,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם,
nevertheless,
דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
they remain inextricably bound to the Blessed One
בְּשָׁרְשָׁם הַנֶּעְלָם.
through their transcendent, concealed root.

items.h:
Seif 9 — Esther's Name for All Generations
Esther fixes Purim eternally so Israel will know that no exile or impurity can sever their essential holiness.

p: וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
And this is the entire purpose of the effort
בִּקְבִיעוּת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים לְדוֹרוֹת,
in establishing the days of Purim for all generations,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וַתִּכְתֹּב אֶסְתֵּר״ וְגוֹמֵר,
as it is written: “Then Esther wrote...” (Esther 9:29),
״וּמַאֲמַר אֶסְתֵּר קִיַּם״ וְגוֹמֵר;
“And the decree of Esther confirmed...” (Esther 9:32);
דְּרַק עַל יָדָהּ הוּא
for specifically through her
שֶׁנִּתְקַיֵּם לְדוֹרוֹת.
was it established for future generations.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת מְגִלָּה (ז׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳) גַּם כֵּן,
And as the Sages noted in Tractate Megillah (7a) as well,
דְּשָׁלְחָה לַחֲכָמִים: ״קִבְעוּנִי״;
that she sent to the Sages: “Establish me”;
וְרַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי פֵּרֵשׁ שָׁם:
and Rashi explained there:
״לִהְיוֹת לִי לְשֵׁם״,
“that I may have a lasting name”,
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא כִּוְּנָה
and certainly she did not intend
לְהַגְדִּיל כְּבוֹדָהּ בָּזֶה.
to aggrandize her own personal prestige thereby.
רַק הַכַּוָּנָה לַשְּׁכִינָה
Rather, her intention was focused on the Shechinah
וְלִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם וּלְשֵׁם,
and the glory of Heaven and the Divine Name,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם (י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳):
in accordance with what they expounded there (Megillah 10b):
״תַּחַת הַסִּרְפָּד יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס״ —
“Instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle”—
זוֹ אֶסְתֵּר הַצַּדֶּקֶת;
this refers to the righteous Esther;
״וְהָיָה לַה' לְשֵׁם״ —
“and it shall be to Hashem for a name”—
זוֹ מִקְרָא מְגִלָּה;
this refers to the reading of the Megillah;
״לְאוֹת עוֹלָם לֹא יִכָּרֵת״ —
“for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off”—
אֵלּוּ יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים.
these are the days of Purim.
הַכַּוָּנָה
The meaning is
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִכְרָת זֶה;
that this holy bond can never be severed;

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ מִשְׁלֵי, פֶּרֶק ט1098 Midrash Mishlei 9:1 — "She has also set her table" (Proverbs 9:2) — she set a table for herself in this world and in the World to Come. And what is it? It is the good name she acquired for herself in this world and in the World to Come. For all the festivals are destined to be nullified, but the days of Purim will never be nullified, as it is stated, "And these days of Purim shall not pass from among the Jews" (Esther 9:28). R. Elazar said: Yom Kippur too will never be nullified, as it is stated, "And this shall be for you an everlasting statute, to atone for the children of Israel from all their sins once a year" (Leviticus 16:34). Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): On this they said, "Even if all the festivals are nullified, the days of Purim will not be nullified": each festival marks a going-out from some particular immersion in evil, and its holiness is what its particular miracle fixed in the hearts of Israel, so that when evil is wholly eradicated and a greater holiness is revealed it is eclipsed, like "a lamp at midday." But Purim is a going-out not from a particular immersion but from the general root of evil, Amalek, who denies [Israel's] root; Purim clarifies that the root of Israel is such that even when they are in every evil it is not true [of them], and this will never be nullified, for every redemption is a going-out from evil to good, whereas Purim shows that even while [a Jew] is in evil he is not evil at all.׳):
and in the manner of what they taught (Midrash Mishlei 9):
״אֲפִילּוּ כָּל הַמּוֹעֲדִים בְּטֵלִים,
“Even if all other festivals were annulled,
יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים לֹא״ וְכוּלֵי.
the days of Purim will never be annulled...”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאִם, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
Meaning that even if, Heaven forbid,

that the regular festivals were suspended,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
in the sense of the verse:
״חָדְשֵׁיכֶם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם שָׂנְאָה נַפְשִׁי״ וְגוֹמֵר;
“Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates...” (Isaiah 1:14);
כִּי כָּל מוֹעֲדִים —
for all festivals—

are outward signs of the covenant of the blessed Hashem with Israel,
דְּלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי.

And although in absolute reality this is so,

for “Where is your mother's bill of divorce?” (Isaiah 50:1),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת כְּלַל
and it is utterly impossible

there seems to be a severing of the connection, Heaven forbid.
אֲבָל פּוּרִים

and their Father in Heaven,

in the innermost depths of their hearts—

a Jew is still fundamentally bound to the blessed Hashem.
וְזֶה כָּל קְדֻשַּׁת הַפּוּרִים,

therefore it is “an everlasting sign”

where Israel was righteous

אֲבָל אָז,
In the miracle of Purim, however,

showing that even in a state of sleep or drunkenness—
הַשֵּׁם עִמָּהֶם,
Hashem remains with them;

and “asleep from the commandments”;

צָמַח זֶה.
the myrtle sprouted forth.

זֶה — נַעֲצוּץ וְסִרְפָּד,
this one remains a thorn and brier,
וְזֶה — בְּרוֹשׁ וַהֲדַס.
while this one is a cypress and myrtle.

עַל פָּסוּק: ״וְלִבִּי עֵר״.
