מְטַנְּפָם כְּלַל.
can ever contaminate their essential soul.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק:
And as the Sages expounded on the verse:
“because the sun has tanned me” (Song of Songs 1:6):
דִּבִּרְחִיצָה מֻעֶטֶת מִתְלַבְּנִים,
with a slight washing they are instantly restored to whiteness;
וְהַכֹּל רַק כְּהוֹצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לַאֲסָא.
and all external sins are merely like briars surrounding the fragrant myrtle.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן לְקִיחַת אֶסְתֵּר
And this is the inner purpose of Esther being taken
לְבֵית אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ:
into the house of Ahasuerus:
לְבָרֵר דָּבָר זֶה
to reveal this foundational reality
שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים,
of the sanctity of the days of Purim,
שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אָז אוֹר זֶה דִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
wherein this transcendent light of Israel's intrinsic holiness was unveiled:
שֶׁכָּל טִנֹּפֶת לֹא תְּטַנְּפֵם,
that no external filth can ever defile them,
וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר הַמּוֹנְעָם מִקְּדֻשָּׁתָם כְּלַל;
and nothing can ever obstruct their holiness;
דְּ״גַם כִּי אֵלֵךְ״ וְגוֹמֵר ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״,
for “Even though I walk in the valley of the shadow of death... You are with me” (Psalm 23:4),
דַּאֲפִילּוּ יִהְיוּ בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ —
meaning that wherever they may find themselves—
דְּבוּקִים בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
they remain eternally cleaved to Hashem, blessed be He.

sections.en: Adar, Joy, and Hidden Da'at

items.h: Adar reveals joy that persists within concealment; the birth and death of Moshe express hidden Da'at, while Purim shows that departed light remains inwardly present.

Seif 1 — Why Adar Increases Joy
Adar adds joy because Torah reveals an inner uprightness that can rejoice in Hashem even before outward perfection is complete.

p: עִנְיַן "מִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה" (תַּעֲנִית כט.)1099 Taanit 29a — R. Yehuda son of R. Shmuel bar Sheilat said in the name of Rav: Just as when Av enters we diminish gladness, so when Adar enters we increase gladness. Rashi: "When Adar enters": they were days of miracles for Israel, Purim and Passover. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Jacob's taking of the blessings from Esau, to merit the good of this world, came through the power of Adar, the month in which Israel prevails over the nations: though the deed took place on Passover, what he took from Esau's portion, its physicality in this world, came through the power of Adar, which precedes Nissan. Therefore "when Adar enters we increase gladness," the reverse of Av, in which gladness is diminished. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 1): The comparison is learned from Av: just as in Av, in which a day of mourning occurred, gladness is diminished from the New Moon, so in Adar, in which a day of gladness occurred, the gladness begins from the New Moon and fills the whole month. It is Adar and not Nissan, though the redemption of Nissan is greater, because the Exodus came entirely from the Blessed One's side, whereas Adar, formed by the letter kuf that alludes to holiness from Israel's side, saw Amalek wiped out by Israel, the miracle wrought through Mordechai and Esther, and the Oral Torah accepted anew with gladness and love. Gladness comes from Israel's accepting the yoke of His kingship from their own side, and therefore "when Adar enters we increase gladness.",
The matter of "When Adar enters, we increase in joy" (Ta'anit 29a),
וַהֲרֵי בְּנִיסָן עִיקַּר גְּאוּלַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
yet behold, in Nisan is the primary redemption of Israel,
וּבְסִיוָון קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה,
and in Sivan is the reception of the Torah,
וּבְסֻכּוֹת "זְמַן שִׂמְחָתֵנוּ",
and on Sukkot is the "time of our rejoicing",
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר עַל יְדֵי זֶה עַל כְּלַל הַחֹדֶשׁ "מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה".
and yet it was not said on account of this regarding the entire month as a whole that "we increase in joy".
וְגַם מַה הַלָּשׁוֹן "מַרְבִּין"?
Furthermore, what is this wording of "we increase"?
מַשְׁמָע דְּיֵשׁ שִׂמְחָה תָּמִיד, אֶלָּא דְּאָז מַרְבִּין בָּהּ;
It implies that there is joy continuously, only that then we increase in it;
וְאֵיזֶה שִׂמְחָה תְּמִידִית יֵשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּגָּלוּת,
and what perpetual joy is there for Israel while they are in exile,
וְנֶאֱמַר (הוֹשֵׁעַ ט, א): "אַל תִּשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל גִּיל וְגוֹמֵר"?
when it is stated (Hosea 9:1): "Rejoice not, O Israel, unto exultation, etc."?
אֲבָל וַדַּאי הַכַּוָּנָה עַל שִׂמְחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּה' מְעֻוזָּם,
However, certainly the intention refers to the joy of Israel in Hashem, their Stronghold,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים לב, יא): "שִׂמְחוּ בַה' וְגִילוּ צַדִּיקִים, וְהַרְנִינוּ כָּל יִשְׁרֵי לֵב",
as it is written (Psalms 32:11): "Be glad in Hashem and rejoice, O righteous, and shout for joy, all you who are upright in heart",
וְהוּא שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְווֹת וְתוֹרָה,
and that is the joy of mitzvot and Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט): "פִּקּוּדֵי ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב",
as it is written (Psalms 19:9): "The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart",
דְּהַיַּשְׁרָנוּת מוֹלִיד שִׂמְחָה בַּלֵּב,
for uprightness engenders joy in the heart,
כִּי (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ג): "תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם",
for (Proverbs 11:3): "The integrity of the upright shall guide them",
וְ(מִשְׁלֵי י, ט): "הוֹלֵךְ בַּתֹּם יֵלֶךְ בֶּטַח" וְאֵין חָסֵר כְּלוּם,
and (Proverbs 10:9): "He who walks in integrity walks securely," and nothing is lacking,
וְעַל כֵּן "לְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה".
and therefore, "for the upright in heart there is joy."

וּבְתַעֲנִית (טו.)1100 Taanit 15a — R. Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say — not all is for light and not all is for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright are for gladness. The righteous are for light, as it is written, "Light is sown for the righteous"; and gladness for the upright, as it is written, "And gladness for the upright in heart." Rashi: The correct reading is: "Not all is for light and not all is for gladness, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart'": the upright are for gladness, for the upright are superior to the righteous. Tosafos (s.v. "light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart"): One cannot say here, as above [of the kings and the princes], that the upright have both gladness and light: if "the upright in heart" referred back to light, "the righteous" would likewise refer forward to gladness, since the two stand side by side; and there is surely a difference between them, for otherwise Scripture would have joined them and written, "for the righteous and the upright in heart, light and gladness." Above, the kings and the princes were not side by side, but "shall see and arise" stood between them, and so applied to the princes written after it as well as to the kings before it; here, however, the verse can only mean light for the righteous and gladness for the upright in heart. Maharsha: Rashi explains that the upright are superior to the righteous, whereas the Rashba writes that the upright are a level below the righteous, as appears from the order in Nishmat: "upright, righteous, pious, holy"; yet the Rashba's claim that the righteous merit light, the essence of delight, and all the more so gladness, does not fit the wording "not all is for gladness." Rather, "light" denotes spiritual delight in the World to Come and "gladness" bodily delight: the righteous merit light in the World to Come, and it is called "sown" because, as what is sown sprouts and grows, so the light of the righteous one's apprehension sprouts and grows continually, as it is said, "the righteous sit and enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah." The upright do not merit this, but only gladness, a bodily delight that gladdens the heart of the upright. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The holiness of bodily matters — being able to do them in holiness without having to hold back from anything one's heart desires, since all is holy to God — brings gladness, as Ta'anis says, "the righteous are for light and the upright for gladness": the righteous man fences himself in and subdues his desires, and so dwells without much gladness, meriting only "light," which is Torah, an inner feeling; but the upright of heart, whose heart is straight and desires only what the Blessed One wishes him to desire, need not fence himself in, and he has gladness. And this is the essence of the gladness of Adar, through the revelation of the uprightness of Israel's heart. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 8): "The righteous are for light": the righteous man is one whose heart is not yet entirely straightened — the foolish heart is not yet purified and he still wrestles with it — and he needs light, that the Blessed One illuminate him with wisdom and understanding to subdue his inclination. Afterwards, when his heart is straightened and even the foolish heart is cleansed of foolish thoughts, "the light of the righteous rejoices," and this is "gladness for the upright in heart," for he has become entirely whole and cleaves to the Holy One, blessed be He, and from this comes gladness. אָמְרוּ:
And in Ta'anit (15a) they taught:
"לֹא הַכֹּל לְאוֹרָה וְלֹא הַכֹּל לְשִׂמְחָה,
"Not all are for light and not all are for joy;
צַדִּיקִים לְאוֹרָה וִישָׁרִים לְשִׂמְחָה וְכוּלֵי".
the righteous are for light, and the upright are for joy, etc."
פֵּירוּשׁ, צַדִּיק הוּא הַמּוּגְדָּר בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
The explanation is: a righteous person is one who is guarded in his actions,
אַף שֶׁהַלֵּב אֵינוֹ שָׁלֵם וְיָשָׁר עֲדַיִן,
even though his heart is not yet whole and upright,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַגְבִּיר שִׂכְלוֹ עַל יִצְרוֹ לְבִלְתִּי יִגָּרֵר אַחֲרָיו,
he nonetheless asserts his intellect over his inclination so as not to be dragged after it,
וְזָהִיר בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בַּפּוֹעַל כָּל רְמַ"ח (מָאתַיִם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה) מִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה וּשְׁסָ"ה (שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ) מִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
and is vigilant in actual practice regarding all 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments.
וְהַמַּעֲשִׂים מְבִיאִים קְדוּשָּׁה לַלֵּב,
And deeds bring holiness to the heart,
דְּעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו",
which is why we bless "Who has sanctified us with His commandments",
פֵּירוּשׁ, קְדוּשָּׁה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא הַבְדָּלָה,
the meaning being: holiness in every place denotes separation,
לְהַבְדִּיל וּלְהַפְרִישׁ הַלֵּב מֵחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
to separate and detach the heart from the physical pleasures of this world;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לָאוֹר הַזָּרוּעַ,
and through this he merits the sown light,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת חִידּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְּאִירִים לַלֵּב.
which is the attainment of novel Torah insights from the Oral Torah that illuminate the heart.
כִּי "אוֹרָה" – זוֹ תּוֹרָה,
For "light"—this is Torah,
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הִיא "הָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח",
and the Written Torah is "the truth that springs up from the earth",
שֶׁהִיא כִּזְרִיעָה בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which acts like a planting within the hearts of the children of Israel,
לְהַצְמִיחַ מִתּוֹךְ לְבָבָם הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד תּוֹסֶפֶת מְרוּבָּה עַל הָעִיקָּר.
to sprout forth from within their hearts a vast addition far exceeding the original seed.

וּכְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּגִיטִּין (ס:)1101 Gittin 60b — R. Elazar said: The Torah — the greater part of it in writing and the lesser part by mouth, as it is said, “I wrote for him the greater part of My Torah, but they were reckoned as a stranger's.” And R. Yochanan said: The greater part by mouth and the lesser part in writing, as it is said, “For by the mouth of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.” Rashi: "The greater part in writing" — the greater part of the Torah depends upon exposition, being written so as to be expounded by "general and particular," by verbal analogy, and by the other principles through which the Torah is expounded. "And the lesser part orally" — that for which there is no hint by which to learn it in the Torah, but which was said to Moses by mouth. "For on the basis of [by the mouth of]" — the covenant was cut over what is oral, which shows that it is the greater part. Tosafos (s.v. "he is expressing bewilderment"): In the Midrash it is said that "they were reckoned as a stranger's" means that the nations wrote out the Torah, and had the whole of it been written for Israel the nations would have written it all. Therefore the Merciful One says: Shall I write for him the greater part of My Torah? — for even what I did write for them "is reckoned as a stranger's," since strangers have copied it. Rashi explained it in another way. Maharsha: On Rashi's explanation I do not know what R. Yochanan is disputing when he says the greater part is oral, for those matters are certainly few in comparison with the whole Torah together with what is expounded by the principles. Perhaps what each sage of his generation innovated is also called "oral," as is said in the Midrashim; and were it not for Rashi's explanation it would seem that everything that issues from exposition by the principles is called "oral," as they said of a verbal analogy that no man may derive one of himself unless he received it from his teacher back to Moses. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 60b): One Master holds that the Written Torah has the higher rank, since the Oral Torah is with a man alone and in his mouth, and it issues from the Written Torah: the trunk of the tree is more than the branches, and the Oral Torah, which comes out of the Written Torah as the branch from the tree, is not the equal of the whole of what is written. And the other Master holds the reverse — that the Oral Torah is more than the Written, since it spreads out and issues from the Written Torah, and that which spreads out from a thing is more than it. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Novellae on the Mitzvos 1): As for the practical difference in this dispute [whether the greater part of the Torah is written or oral], the Be'er Sheva wrote that it concerns something the Sadducees concede: according to R. Elazar the thirteen hermeneutical principles are as the written [Torah], and the Sadducees concede them, while according to R. Yochanan the Sadducees do not. The Pri Megadim already noted that there are many other differences, one being whether they may be written down: since "words that are written you may not recite orally, and words that are oral you may not recite in writing," according to R. Elazar they would write down the thirteen principles, and according to R. Yochanan they would not.: "רוֹב תּוֹרָה בְּעַל פֶּה",
And in accordance with the authority who says in Gittin (60b): "Most of the Torah is oral",
וְגַם מַאן דְּאָמַר "רוּבָּהּ בִּכְתָב" לֹא פָּלֵיג אַמְּצִיאוּת,
and even the authority who says "most of it is in writing" does not disagree with reality,
רַק סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כֵּיוָון דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְהַכֹּל נִדְרָשׁ מִתּוֹךְ הַכְּתוּבִים,
rather he maintains that since there is nothing that is not hinted at in the Torah and all is derived from the verses,
וְכֵיוָון דְּאִתְיְהִיב לְמִידְרַשׁ כְּמַאן דִּכְתִיב מְפוֹרָשׁ דָּמֵי,
and since it was given over to be expounded, it is considered as if explicitly written,
קָרֵי לֵיהּ "רוֹב בִּכְתָב",
and therefore he calls it "most in writing",
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה כָּתְבוּ הַמְּפָרְשִׁים.
and commentators wrote along similar lines.
אֲבָל וַדַּאי עַצְמוּת הַכְּתָב דָּבָר מוּעָט מְאֹד,
However, certainly the essential text itself is very concise,
וְעִיקַּר מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (אִיּוֹב יא, ט): "אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ"
and the primary meaning of what is written (Job 11:9): "Its measure is longer than the earth"
הוּא מִצַּד בֵּיאוּרָהּ שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַנִּצְמָח מִלִּבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי אוֹר שֶׁבִּכְתָב הַזָּרוּעַ בָּהֶם.
is from the aspect of its oral exposition that sprouts from the hearts of the children of Israel through the light of the Written Torah sown within them.
וַאֲמִיתַּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהָאִיר הַלֵּב מֵאֲפֵלָתָהּ,
And the authentic Oral Torah—that which a seasoned disciple is destined to innovate so as to illuminate the heart from its darkness—
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לַצַּדִּיקִים,
belongs only to the righteous,
דְּ"לָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים: מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי" (תְּהִלִּים נ, טז),
for "to the wicked God said: What right have you to recount My statutes" (Psalms 50:16),
וְאִם אֵינוֹ דוֹמֶה לְמַלְאָךְ אַל יְבַקְשׁוּ תּוֹרָה מִפִּיהוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו:).
and if he does not resemble an angel, let them not seek Torah from his mouth (Chagigah 15b).
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דִּגְמַר תּוֹרָה מִפּוּמֵיהּ דְּאַחֵר,
And Rabbi Meir who learned Torah from the mouth of Acher,

"תּוֹכוֹ אָכַל וְכוּלֵי1102 Chagigah 15b — And how did R. Meir learn Torah from the mouth of Acher? Did not Rabbah bar bar Chanah say in the name of R. Yochanan: What is meant by “For the priest’s lips shall guard knowledge, and Torah shall they seek from his mouth”? If the teacher resembles an angel of the Lord of Hosts, let them seek Torah from his mouth; and if not, let them not seek Torah from his mouth. Reish Lakish said: R. Meir found a verse and expounded it — “Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and set your heart to My knowledge.” It does not say “to their knowledge” but “to My knowledge.” And the Gemara concludes: R. Meir found a pomegranate — he ate its inside and cast away its peel. Rashi: "It does not say 'to their knowledge'" — evidently the verse is speaking of wicked men, and even so it says, "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise." Maharsha: "For the priest's lips shall guard knowledge": the priest of the tribe of Levi is the one who instructs Israel in the Torah, and though he guards knowledge upon his lips to teach you Torah, if you would seek Torah from his mouth, look first whether he resembles an angel in his deeds. As for R. Meir's derashah: every limb of a man is created to do his Maker's will, the ear above all, that it should be obedient to hear the words of the wise; but the heart and the limbs of action are not to be obedient to the mind of the Sages in every instance, lest they be wicked men — hence "set your heart," and all the other limbs with it, "to My knowledge," that is, to Heaven. Acher was defective both in character and in doctrine, and R. Meir kept himself from both: as to doctrine, he ate the outer fruit, the Torah Acher taught openly, and threw away the pit, the corruption within his heart, such as "there are two authorities"; as to deeds, he threw away the peel, and ate the inside, the commandments of the Torah, which are likened to the seeds within the pomegranate. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 8): To learn Torah from a scholar who is not fit is to have union and attachment with a wicked man, and of this they said, "Do not join yourself to a wicked man"; and the difference between an adult and a minor is that the minor is truly reckoned his teacher's disciple and is bound to him, whereas the adult has no such union with the teacher. R. Meir relied on this, that the Torah is separate from the man who holds it, and the sin is not on the side of the Torah but on the side of the man who receives it — just as the edible part of a pomegranate is separate from its peel, and though the peel is foul the inside is not spoiled by it. And R. Meir in particular learned Torah that was wholly of the intellect, a divine intellect entirely separate from the man, which has no attachment to the wicked at all." (שָׁם),
"ate its core, etc." (there),
הַיְינוּ דִּפְנִימִיּוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל "עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
this means that in the interiority of Israel, "your people are all righteous",

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ1103 Berakhot 17a — R. Alexandri, after his prayer, used to say: Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that it is our will to do Your will — and what prevents it? The leaven in the dough and subjection to the kingdoms. May it be Your will that You deliver us from their hand, and that we return to fulfil the statutes of Your will with a whole heart. Rashi: "And what prevents it" — from our doing Your will. "The leaven in the dough" — the evil inclination in our heart, which leavens us. Maharsha: He explains it after what Maimonides wrote in the Eight Chapters, that a man must keep to the middle path in his traits and his deeds. The evil inclination drives him to one extreme within what is permitted him — to be arrogant and to indulge in permitted desire — and is therefore likened to the leaven in the dough, which raises the dough and makes it more than its true measure; while subjection to the gentile kingdoms forces him to the opposite extreme, for they do not allow Israel to hold themselves up but abase them utterly and withhold from them every good, even what they need for the service of God. Thus "our will is to do Your will" — to walk the middle path — "and what prevents it?" These two, each pulling toward its own extreme; may it be Your will to subdue them before us and behind us, that is, both extremes, "and we shall return" to walk in the middle. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 21): In Israel a thought that is not for its own sake comes only from the [evil] inclination, which accustoms one to seek his own pleasure in everything, but the depths of the hearts of the children of Israel are solely for the sake of Heaven, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." Hence, when there is an actual deed, that suffices to join it to the will in the depths of the heart, and no account is taken of the thought of the "yeast in the dough" that confuses it. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 1): The sign of the covenant testifies that the holy flesh of Israel does not desire evil, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will … and who prevents us …": this depth of will stems from our father Abraham, while the Torah is the spice against the [evil] inclination and the Land of Israel is the opposite of subjugation to the kingdoms. "Our will," the depth of the will, is freedom from the evil inclination and from subjugation; hence no exile came from Abraham's side, and the sufferings come only from the side of the inclination and the subjugation. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): Though Israel sank in exile into the forty-nine gates of impurity, this was a clarification before Him who examines hearts of the difference between the nations' immersion, which stems from the essence of their hearts, and Israel's, which comes only from their being mixed among the nations, whereas in the essence of their hearts "it is revealed and known that our will is to do [Your will]." The essence of Israel's hearts is not immersed in impurity at all, and from this side comes the redemption from the nations. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): Even the wicked of Israel are all righteous, just as all Israel are called circumcised, even one actually uncircumcised; so one who is wicked in deed is so only from the side of the [evil] inclination and not from his heart, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …," and as the Rambam explains the reason for coercing [a husband] until he says "I want." Though he is called wicked for his actual sin, even the sinners of Israel are full of regret, and there is no wicked Jew who does not regret for some moment once the pleasure has passed and the inclination no longer incites him, because of the depth of good in the depths of his heart. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 24): On Atzeres, the time of accepting the yoke of Torah and mitzvos, there is a mitzvah to give pleasure to the body as well, for the yoke is felt mainly by the body, whereas as for the soul, "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will." By this we show that although for the body it is a yoke, it nevertheless rejoices in accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, of Torah and of mitzvos. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The holiness of the name Israel at the root of every Jew cannot be uprooted, and even if he multiplies sins it is all from the side of the "yeast in the dough" and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" that surround the root of Judaism, as it says, "It is revealed and known that our will …" Therefore he is compared to a myrtle standing among reeds: the sins are only in the reeds surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 263): The reason the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to the deed is that in truth "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God" and "the Lord's portion is His people," as it says, "It is revealed and known … and who prevents us …"; but in idolatry, where one denies [God], God forbid, even an evil thought is joined [to the deed]. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): In the depths of the heart "it is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will — and who prevents us …": even the hindrances in a heart that inclines to evil lie only in the revealed part of the heart, from the "yeast in the dough" that sits at the openings of the heart and the "subjugation to the kingdoms" — the thorns that surround the rose and clothe it, one from without and the other from within. But it is all only a garment and not the essence, which is the depth of his heart, where his essential vitality cleaves to the Blessed One. (בְּרָכוֹת יז.): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי".
and as they said (Berakhot 17a): "It is revealed and known that our will, etc., and what deters us, etc."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (הִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין ב, כ) בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אָנִי",
And as the Rambam wrote (Laws of Divorce 2:20) regarding the rationale for "they compel him until he says: I want to",
דְּעֶצֶם רְצוֹנוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן,
that his essential will is truly so,
וְכוֹפִין רַק לִמְנוֹעַ הֲסָתַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁהוּא חוּץ מֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹנוֹ וְהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לָאָסָא.
and they compel him only to eliminate the incitement of the evil inclination which remains outside the truth of his will, like thorns encircling a myrtle.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאַחֵר
Therefore, also in the Oral Torah comprehension of Acher,
הָיָה תּוֹךְ הָרָאוּי לִהְיוֹת נֶאֱכָל מִצַּד הַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁבּוֹ שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק,
there was an inner fruit worthy of being eaten by virtue of his inward essence wherein he was righteous,
דְּכָל רִשְׁעוּתוֹ רַק מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
for all his wickedness was merely from the lip outward due to the evil inclination,
וְזֶהוּ קְלִיפָּתוֹ שֶׁזָּרַק.
and this was the peel that he discarded.
וּלְעַצְמוֹ לֹא הֵאִירָה תּוֹרָתוֹ מִפְּנֵי רִיבּוּי הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבַבְתָּהּ.
Yet for himself, his Torah did not illuminate him because of the vastness of the peel surrounding it.
אֲבָל רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַבְדִּיל וּלְהַפְרִיד הַתּוֹךְ מִן הַקְּלִיפָּה,
However, Rabbi Meir was able to distinguish and separate the core from the peel,
כִּי הוּא הָיָה מָלֵא אוֹר כִּשְׁמוֹ,
because he was filled with light like his name,

שֶׁעַל כֵּן בְּתוֹרָתוֹ כָּתוּב "כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר" בְּאָלֶ״ף (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כ)1104 Bereshit Rabbah 20:12 — “And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin [or, with an ayin], and clothed them.” In R. Meir’s Torah they found written “garments of light [or, with an alef].” These are the garments of Adam the first man, which resembled rue, broad below and narrow above. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 12): This is the secret of "garments of light" with an alef, written in R. Meir's Torah: as it will be in the future, light in place of the body's skin, so that neither breaking nor death applies at all. When the dew of the resurrection descends — the complete unification of the Blessed One's light — the skin and flesh formed over [the dead] will come from the truth of the Blessed One's "garments of light," and it will be revealed that death was all only in appearance.,
which is why in his Torah scroll it was written "garments of light (or)" with an Alef (Bereishit Rabbah, end of Parashah 20),
שֶׁגַּם הַלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁל עוֹר מָלֵא אוֹר;
signifying that even the garment of skin was full of light;
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ אוֹר הָאֲבוּקָה שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁךְ אֵלָיו כָּל אוֹר קָטָן שֶׁמִּתְקָרֵב לוֹ,
and he was like the light of a torch that draws to itself every small light that approaches it,
כָּךְ הָיָה יָכוֹל לִמְשׁוֹךְ אוֹר הַפְּנִימִי שֶׁהָיָה בְּאַחֵר אֵלָיו.
so was he able to draw the inward light that was within Acher unto himself.
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ לְהַרְהֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה קוֹדֶם הַלִּימּוּד,
Therefore, one should reflect in repentance before study,
דְּאָז נִקְרָא צַדִּיק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִידּוּשִׁין (מט:),
for then he is termed righteous, as they stated in Kiddushin (49b),
וְזוֹכֶה לָאוֹר הַזָּרוּעַ,
and he merits the sown light,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִזְרָע מַה שֶּׁיִּלְמוֹד בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבוֹ,
that whatever he studies will be sown deep within his heart,
לְהַצְמִיחַ אוֹרָה מְרוּבָּה בְּקִרְבּוֹ לִהְיוֹת עַל כָּל דְּרָכָיו נוֹגַהּ אוֹר שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל מֵעַתָּה.
to sprout abundant light within him so that radiant illumination rests upon all his paths, preventing him from stumbling from now on.
וּלְעוֹלָם אֵין הַלֵּב מֵאִיר לְגַמְרֵי אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ הַשָּׂגַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֲמִיתִּיִּים הַמִּתְחַדְּשִׁים בְּלִבּוֹ,
And the heart never radiates completely except through the comprehension of true Torah concepts that are renewed in his heart,
וְ(קֹהֶלֶת ח, א): "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו".
and (Ecclesiastes 8:1): "A man's wisdom illuminates his face."
וְכֵן הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית גָּנוּז לַצַּדִּיקִים,
And likewise, the light created during the six days of Creation is hidden away for the righteous,
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר: אוֹר הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לָאָדָם קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא יוּכַל לִזְכּוֹת לָהּ גַּם כֵּן אַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיָשׁוּב.
meaning: the light of comprehension that was fitting for man before the sin can also be merited after he sins and repents.
וְאַף דְּעִיקַּר שֵׁם צַדִּיק הַיְינוּ צַדִּיק מֵעִיקָּרוֹ,
And even though the primary title of 'tzaddik' denotes one righteous from his inception,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה נִקְרָא צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל כַּנִּזְכָּר,
nevertheless a penitent is also termed a great righteous person as mentioned,
לְפִי שֶׁהַתְּשׁוּבָה עוֹקֶרֶת הַחֵטְא לְמַפְרֵעַ דּוּגְמַת הַתָּרַת נֶדֶר עַל יְדֵי הֶחָכָם,
because repentance uproots the sin retroactively in the manner of the annulment of a vow by a sage,
וְהוּא כְּאִילּוּ לֹא חָטָא מֵעוֹלָם.
and he is considered as if he had never sinned.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יִרְמְיָה נ, כ): "בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְגוֹמֵר יְבֻקַּשׁ אֶת עֲוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
And in the manner of what is stated (Jeremiah 50:20): "In those days, etc., the iniquity of Israel shall be sought, and there shall be none, etc.",
וְכָל הַשָּׂגָה מְכוּנָּה "אוֹר",
and every conceptual attainment is called "light",
שֶׁהוּא מֵאִיר לָאָדָם בְּכָל עִנְיָנִים כַּמְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְקוֹם אוֹרָה שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְּטוֹב דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל,
for it illuminates for man in all matters like one walking in a place of brilliance who clearly perceives his way so he will not stumble,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלוֹת.
unlike walking through darkened alleys.
וְזֶהוּ הָרָאוּי לַצַּדִּיקִים,
And this is what is fitting for the righteous,
אֲשֶׁר זֶה מַדְרֵגָתָם בְּהַגְדָּרַת מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לִשְׁמוֹר רַגְלָם מִלָּכֶד.
whose spiritual rung consists of fencing in their deeds to guard their feet from ensnarement.
אֲבָל הַשִּׂמְחָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַה שֶּׁהוּא דָּבוּק בּוֹ,
However, joy exists solely in Hashem, blessed be He, in that one is cleaving unto Him,
וַאֲפִילּוּ עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ דָּבוּק, וַאֲפִילּוּ מְרוּחָק לְגַמְרֵי,
and even if he does not yet cling, and even if he is totally distant,
רַק שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם מְבַקְשׁוֹ וְחָפֵץ לִידַּבֵּק בּוֹ,
yet he nevertheless seeks Him and desires to cling unto Him,
נֶאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א טז, י; תְּהִלִּים קה, ג): "יִשְׂמַח לֵב מְבַקְשֵׁי ה'".
it is stated (I Chronicles 16:10; Psalms 105:3): "Let the heart of those who seek Hashem rejoice."
וְעַל יְדֵי אוֹר תּוֹרָה וְנֵר מִצְוָה יוּכַל לִזְכּוֹת לְשִׂמְחָה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן,
And through the light of Torah and the lamp of a mitzvah one can merit this joy as well,
כִּי מַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אָחִיד בְּגוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא,
for whoever holds onto the Torah holds onto the King's essence,
וְהַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לַמּוּטָב אֲפִילּוּ "אוֹתִי עָזָבוּ" חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ אֵיכָה (פְּתִיחָה ב).
and the illumination within it restores him to good even if "they have forsaken Me," Heaven forbid, as written in Midrash Eichah (Introduction 2).
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר לְבָבוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ ה' אֱלֹהָיו,
For through this he arouses his heart to seek Hashem his God,
וְאָז זוֹכֶה לְיִשְׁרַת לֵב.
and then he merits uprightness of heart.
דְּכָל הַיַּשְׁרוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַתְּמִימוּת עִם ה' אֱלֹהָיו,
For all uprightness in the heart is nothing other than simple faith with Hashem his God,
דְּיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא וּמַנְהִיג וְשֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר חוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ,
knowing that there is a Creator and Guide and that there is nothing outside of Him,
וְזֶה מְפַשֵּׁט כָּל עַקְמוּמִיּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
and this straightens all tortuous crookedness within the heart.
וְאַף אִם עֲדַיִן הַיֵּצֶר כָּרוּךְ בַּעֲקֵבוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ מוּגְדָּר בְּמַעֲשָׂיו כְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר,
And even if the inclination is still wrapped around his heels and he is not fenced in his deeds like a full tzaddik,

עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת סג.)1105 Berakhot 63a — Bar Kappara expounded: Which is the brief passage upon which all the essentials of the Torah depend? "In all your ways know Him, and He will make your paths straight." Rava said: Even for a matter of transgression. Rashi (s.v. "in all your ways"): "In all your ways" — even to commit a transgression. "Know Him" — give thought to whether it is required for a mitzvah, as with Elijah on Mount Carmel, and [if so] transgress it. Maharsha: He did not say "remember Him" but "know Him" — a true knowledge of His existence, and that He is able and watches over all your ways, to give good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked. And it concludes, "and He will make your paths straight," after the manner of what they said: in the way a man wishes to go, he is led, and one who comes to purify himself is assisted. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 34): As it is written, "In all your ways know Him," and the Sages said, "even for a matter of transgression" — then "He will straighten [your paths]." That is, one should give himself over to the Blessed One even to the point of losing his entire share in the World to Come when such is the will of the Blessed One — as I heard concerning the trial of the Binding — and then "He will straighten": the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself straightens you and separates the evil from you without toil. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 19): On "In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths," Rava said, "even for a matter of transgression," and the reading of Ein Yaakov is: "Rav Pappa said, this is what people say: the thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One." That is, even though he commits an explicit transgression of "You shall not steal," since he does not forget the Blessed One and believes in Him at the moment of the act, calling upon the Merciful One, of this it is said "and He will straighten your paths": the Blessed One will straighten his paths, so that "the banished one is not banished from Him," and he will have a rectification. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Beshalach): "Encamp opposite it by the sea": it is written, "In all your ways know Him" — even for a matter of transgression; and this is the meaning of "encamp opposite it": even though you perform deeds like those of the Egyptians, nevertheless the deeds of Israel are good, for the Israelite nation, the portion of the Blessed One, cleaves to simple life without any garment and draws from that source of life alone. All these powers, when among Israel, are full of holiness even though they resemble those of Egypt, for the Blessed One testifies about them that in the heart of Israel there is nothing but love of the Blessed One. Tiferes Yosef (Talmud Anthology, Berakhos 7): [By placing "I am" before "You shall have no other gods," the Blessed One showed that] even one who has, Heaven forbid, stumbled in a deed that is not good is not barred from repentance and can perform mitzvos though he is not yet cleansed of "turning from evil." This is what the dictum "In all your ways know Him," on which all the essentials of the Torah depend, teaches; and as Rava concludes, "even for a matter of transgression" — that is, a person should not despair after stumbling in sin, for repentance is never withheld from him.: "בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" – אֲפִילּוּ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה, "וְהוּא יְיַשֵּׁר אֹרְחֹתֶיךָ".
concerning this they taught (Berakhot 63a): "'In all your ways acknowledge Him'—even for a matter of transgression, 'and He will direct your paths'."
וּבְעֵין יַעֲקֹב שָׁם הַגִּירְסָא:
And in Ein Yaakov the reading there is:
הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרֵי אִינָשֵׁי: "גַּנָּבָא אַפּוּם מַחְתַּרְתָּא רַחֲמָנָא קָרֵי",
this is what people say: "The thief at the opening of the breach calls upon the Merciful One",
רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּרוֹב גַּנָּבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בִּכְלָל נִקְרָאִים יְשָׁרִים,
meaning to say that most Jewish thieves are generally termed upright,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פח:)1106 Shabbat 88a-b — A certain heretic saw Rava sitting engrossed in his study, his fingers beneath his leg and pressed until they spurted blood. He said to him: Impulsive people, who put your mouths before your ears — you still stand in your rashness! You should first have listened; if you were able, you should have accepted, and if not, you should not have accepted. He said to him: Of us, who walk in wholeheartedness, it is written, “The integrity of the upright shall guide them”; of those people, who walk in guile, it is written, “But the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.” Rashi: ["His fingers":] the fingers of his hands. ["And he was pressing them":] he was crushing them under his legs and did not notice, from his absorption. ["A rash people":] hasty. ["Who put your mouths before your ears":] before you had heard how hard it is and whether you could stand up to it, you took it upon yourselves to fulfill it. ["We, who walk in wholeheartedness":] we walked with Him in simplicity of heart, as those who act out of love, and relied on Him not to burden us with something we could not withstand. Maharsha: ["The integrity of the upright shall guide them":] Besides Rashi's explanation, one may explain it in the manner of "In the way a person wishes to go, he is led" and "One who comes to purify himself is helped": the upright, who wish to walk the straight path even though it is hard for them to do, are guided with help from Heaven; and conversely, "the crookedness of the treacherous," who walk a crooked and not a straight path, "shall destroy them," for "one who comes to defile himself, [the way] is opened for him." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 29): The heretic held that this was out of order — by right a person should first hear a thing and afterwards know to do it — and so he said that Israel's putting "we will do" before "we will hear" came from their rashness, that they are disorderly in their actions. Rava answered him that the matter is the reverse of what he thought: it is the ways of those who walk in guile that depart from order, but Israel walk in their integrity, and the action of whoever is wholehearted never departs from the proper order — and by the proper order the doing should come first, for that is what man was created for. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 8): The garment for attaining the truth of the Torah is wholeheartedness, to be wholehearted with the Lord, for "the integrity of the upright shall guide them," as they said in Perek R. Akiva: "We who walk in wholeheartedness..." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei): To be easily enticed toward the good is a fine trait for which Israel were praised: they are drawn after the Blessed One with great haste, without deliberation or delay, as the heretic said to Rava, "Rash people, who put your mouths before your ears." Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 20): Rava's reply to the Sadducee who called Israel "rash people, who put your mouths before your ears" and said they should first have listened to see whether they were able, namely "We who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, 'The integrity of the upright shall guide them,'" means that we are wholehearted in the will of the Blessed One, [confident] that He will surely help us to complete it for the good; and this is what is called "whose strength is in You." Sod Yesharim (Seventh Day of Pesach 14): At times a person must set aside his human form [of reasoning] to fulfill the will of the Blessed One, like a horse ridden by its master, as in the heretic's charge against Rava and Rava's reply: Israel, who at their root cleave to knowledge, are taught by that knowledge that at times they should set aside their power of choice to fulfill the will of the Blessed One. But the nations, who branch from the supernal princes that stand in awe without knowledge, have no bond with their prince and act without knowledge or choice, like a horse of the Other Side; and even when they sometimes yield before the Blessed One, it is only so as to spread out afterwards with great force, as Balaam did.: "אֲנַן כְּתִיב בַּן: 'תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם'".
as they said in the chapter of Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 88b): "Regarding us it is written: 'The integrity of the upright shall guide them'."
כִּי כֻּלָּם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים,
For they are all believers, children of believers,
וְהָאֱמוּנָה הַתְּקוּעָה בְּקֶרֶב כָּל אִישׁ יִשְׂרְאֵלִי דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִיא הַגּוֹרֶמֶת לוֹ יִשְׁרַת לֵב.
and the faith implanted deep within every Jewish person that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He, is what generates uprightness of heart within him.
וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גּוֹבְרוֹ וּמַחֲטִיאוֹ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, הוּא לֹא זָז מֵאֱמוּנָתוֹ,
And even when the evil inclination overpowers him and causes him to sin in action, he does not budge from his faith,
וְגַם שָׁם "רַחֲמָנָא קָרֵי",
and even there "he calls upon the Merciful One",
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מְעַוֵּור עֵינָיו וְלֹא יָדַע שֶׁזֶּה דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה.
only that the inclination blinds his eyes so he does not recognize that this is a matter of sin.
וְאַף דְּסוֹף סוֹף הוּא תּוֹעֶה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַיָּשָׁר,
And although he ultimately strays from the straight path,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְיַישֵּׁר אוֹרְחוֹתָיו,
nevertheless through this Hashem, blessed be He, straightens his ways,
וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא "יִשְׁרֵי לֵב" הַזּוֹכֶה לְשִׂמְחָה.
and he is the one termed "upright in heart" who merits joy.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָ"אוֹרָה זוֹ תּוֹרָה" שֶׁתְּהֵא מְאִירָה עֵינָיו וּלְבָבוֹ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְהַר בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
Even though he does not merit the "light that is Torah" to illuminate his eyes and his heart so long as he is not cleansed in his actions,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זוֹכֶה לְשִׂמְחָה בַּה' עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
he nonetheless merits joy in Hashem through the Torah,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא זָכָה לָהּ הַצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יִשְׁרוּת לֵב,
which the fully righteous person who lacks this inner uprightness of heart has not yet merited,
שֶׁלִּבּוֹ דּוֹאֵג בְּקִרְבּוֹ תָּמִיד.
whose heart remains anxious within him continuously.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Tzaddik and Upright in Heart
Righteous action and inner uprightness are distinct yet connected stages, while Amalek attacks the passage from one to the other.

p: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת,
And even though they are two distinct rungs,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם בֶּאֱמֶת נִמְשָׁכִים זֶה מִזֶּה וּכְלוּלִים יַחַד.
nevertheless they are truly drawn one from the other and included together.
וְאִיחֵר "יִשְׁרֵי לֵב",
And Scripture placed "the upright in heart" later,
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה כָּל אֶחָד צַדִּיק,
because initially each one is a tzaddik,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא לְיִשְׁרַת לֵב.
and afterward he attains uprightness of heart.
וּמַה דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יְשָׁרִים הוּא לְפִי שֶׁכֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים גַּם כֵּן.
And that all Israel are upright is because they are all righteous as well.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם מַדְרֵגוֹת מַדְרֵגוֹת הֵם,
Only that nevertheless there are varied gradations,
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁזֶּה גּוֹבֵר בּוֹ וְהוּא הָעִיקָּר אֶצְלוֹ לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק בְּמַעֲשָׂיו;
and there is one in whom this quality predominates and with him the primary focus is being righteous in his deeds;
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁהַיִּשְׁרוּת לֵב גּוֹבֵר בּוֹ,
and there is one in whom uprightness of heart predominates,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם סוֹף סוֹף גַּם הַצַּדִּיק זוֹכֶה לְיִשְׁרַת לֵב.
and nevertheless ultimately the tzaddik also merits uprightness of heart.
וְעַל כֵּן אַחַר שֶׁזָּכַר מַדְרֵגַת יִשְׁרֵי לֵב, חָזַר לְהַזְכִּיר הַצַּדִּיק;
Therefore, after mentioning the rung of the upright in heart, Scripture returned to mention the tzaddik;
וְאָמַר: "שִׂמְחוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּה' וְגוֹמֵר",
and stated: "Rejoice, O righteous, in Hashem, etc.",
דְּגַם הֵם מַגִּיעִים לְמַדְרֵגַת הַשִּׂמְחָה,
showing that they too reach the rung of joy,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִצַּד עַצְמָם,
only that it is not from their own independent initiative,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁמַּחֲזִירָם לַמּוּטָב וְלִשְׂמוֹחַ בַּה'.
rather through the illumination of the Torah that restores them to goodness and to rejoice in Hashem.
כִּי זֶהוּ תַּכְלִית וְעִיקַּר הַכֹּל,
For this is the ultimate purpose and essence of all,
וְכָל הַמְכֻוָּון בְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ וְתַרְיַ"ג (שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלוֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה) מִצְווֹתֶיהָ –
and the entire intent in the whole Torah and its 613 commandments—
לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק עַל יָדָם בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
is to cling through them unto the Living God,
וּלְהַשִּׂיג אֲמִיתַּת דִּבּוּר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה:
and to apprehend the truth of the first utterance that we heard from the Mouth of Omnipotence:
"אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר";
"I am Hashem your God, etc.";
וְנֶאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ד, ד): "וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּה' וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is stated (Deuteronomy 4:4): "And you who cling unto Hashem, etc.",
דְּכֻלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת בִּדְבֵיקוּת זֶה,
demonstrating that all possess an intrinsic attachment to this cleaving,
דְּ"חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ".
for "Hashem's portion is His people."
וְזֶהוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה תְּמִידִית שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי מַה שֶּׁנּוֹצַר יְהוּדִי,
And this is the perpetual joy that a Jewish person possesses in that he was created a Jew,
וְנִיטַּע תּוֹךְ מַטַּע ה' לְהִתְפָּאֵר זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב,
and planted within the planting of Hashem for glory as the seed of Jacob,
דְּזוֹ שִׂמְחָה שֶׁאֵין עֶצֶב עִמָּהּ,
for this is a joy that bears no sorrow with it,
וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר הַחוֹצֵץ וּמְעַכֵּב בְּעַד שִׂמְחָה זוֹ מַה שֶּׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת לוֹ חֵלֶק בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים.
and nothing intervenes or impedes this joy in having merited an eternal portion in the Living God.
וַאֲפִילּוּ נִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקַּע וְהִגְדִּיל עֲווֹנוֹת לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר,
And even if one has sunk into wherever he has sunk and multiplied sins without measure,
עֲדַיִן לֹא נִיתַּק וְנִכְרַת דְּבֵיקוּת שָׁרְשׁוֹ בִּמְקוֹרָהּ,
the cleaving of his root unto its primordial Source has still not been severed or uprooted,
שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיְתָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
which is an impossibility within the offspring of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, whose bed was whole,
וְ"לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח".
and "none banished shall be expelled from Him."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּשֵׁם כְּלַל הַכְּנֵסִיָּה בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה וְהַשִּׁפְלוּת:
And this parallels what King David, peace be upon him, proclaimed in the name of the entire Congregation when in the ultimate descent and lowliness:
"גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד).
"Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4).
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הוֹלֵךְ בַּדְּיוֹטָא הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁבַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלוֹת
For even if one walks in the lowest tier among the dark alleyways
דְּהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וַהֲבָלָיו, שֶׁהֵם דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל תֹּהוּ וְעַד אַרְגִּיעָה וּמְכוּנִים בְּ"גֵיא צַלְמָוֶת",
of sinking into the desires and vanities of this world, which are transient illusions of void termed "the valley of the shadow of death",
לֹא אִירַע רַע כְּלָל מֵאַחַר דְּ"אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
no harm will befall him at all since "You are with me",
אֲפִילּוּ אַפּוּם מַחְתַּרְתָּא,
even at the mouth of the breach;
אִם כֵּן "הוּא יְיַשֵּׁר אוֹרְחוֹתָיו".
consequently, "He will straighten his paths."
וְזֶהוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לָאָדָם בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ,
And this is the joy that a person must have in his divine service,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים ק, ב): "עִבְדוּ אֶת ה' בְּשִׂמְחָה",
as it is written (Psalms 100:2): "Serve Hashem with joy",
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן בְּיִרְאָה: "וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה",
even though it must also be in awe: "and rejoice with trembling",
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא יָזוּז שִׂמְחָה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִנֶּגֶד עֵינָיו מַה שֶּׁהוּא זוֹכֶה לַעֲבוֹד לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
nonetheless this joy must likewise never depart from before his eyes over having merited to serve Hashem, blessed be He;
וְהֲיֵשׁ שִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ?
and is there any joy greater than this?

וְהַצַּדִּיקִים עוֹשִׂין מֵאַהֲבָה וּשְׂמֵחִין בְּיִסּוּרִין גַּם כֵּן (שַׁבָּת פח:)1107 Shabbat 88b — Our Rabbis taught: Those who are insulted and do not insult in return, who hear themselves reviled and do not answer, who act out of love and rejoice in suffering — of them Scripture says, "And they that love Him are as the sun going forth in its might." Rashi: Those who are insulted and do not insult: others come at them with insolence, but they do not come at others. They act out of love of the Omnipresent and rejoice in suffering — that is, in the insult that comes upon them. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, Gittin 36b): Whoever has all these traits is counted among "those who love Him": one who is insulted and does not insult, who hears his disgrace and does not answer, is surely beloved of people, and whoever is beloved of people is beloved of Heaven; "they rejoice in suffering" means that they accept suffering with love. They are likened to the sun, of which it is said that it "rejoices as a strong man" — doing the will of the Omnipresent with joy and love — and that "there is nothing hidden from its heat," for its dominion extends over the whole world; so too one who has all these traits is given kingship and dominion by the Torah. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 88b): This is said here because the nations taunt Israel over the greatness of their sin — "you played the harlot under the wedding canopy" — and Israel are insulted by them and keep silent. One who is insulted and does not insult in return is acted upon without acting on others, and so is free of the brazenness that anyone who retorts must have, even when provoked; he thus keeps the evenness and simplicity that belong to what is separate from matter, and acting out of love and rejoicing in sufferings, which diminish the body and purify the soul from the material, likewise show that such people are separate. Therefore they are likened to the sun going forth in its might, for light is separate from the physical: they shine because their souls are wholly separate, the opposite of the wicked, who "shall be silent in darkness.",
And the righteous act out of love and rejoice in afflictions as well (Shabbat 88b),
מֵאַחַר שֶׁמַּכִּירִין שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלֹא בְּמִקְרֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
since they recognize that everything is from Hashem, blessed be He, and not by chance, Heaven forbid,
רַק כְּאָב הַמַּכֶּה אֶת בְּנוֹ לְהַיְישִׁירוֹ,
rather like a father who strikes his son to set him straight,
אוֹ הָרוֹפֵא שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה דְּבָרִים מְיַיסְּרִים לַחוֹלֶה כְּדֵי לְהַחֲיוֹתוֹ,
or a physician who administers painful treatments to the sick in order to revive him,
דְּוַודַּאי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיצַר הוּא עַכְשָׁיו – שָׂמֵחַ לְאַחַר זְמַן.
for certainly, even though he experiences distress now, he rejoices afterward.
וְהַמֵּבִין וּמַכִּיר גַּם בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה – הוּא שָׂמֵחַ.
And one who understands and recognizes this even during the ordeal itself rejoices.
וּבְשִׂמְחָה זוֹ שֶׁנּוֹהֶגֶת אֵצֶל אִישׁ הַיְּהוּדִי תָּמִיד,
And in this joy which is standard for the Jewish person continually,
וְאֵין זָז מִמֶּנּוּ בֵּין בְּטִיבוּ בֵּין בְּעָאקוּ (פֵּירוּשׁ: בְּצַעֲרוֹ) וּבְכָל חִילּוּפֵי הַזְּמַנִּים –
and never departs from him, whether in goodness or in distress, and through all changes of times—
בָּהּ מַרְבִּין מִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר,
in this joy we increase when Adar enters,
שֶׁהוּא הַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה.
which is the month that was overturned from grief to joy.
דְּהָמָן חָשַׁב לַעֲקוֹר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִזָּכֵר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹד,
For Haman intended to uproot the core of Judaism entirely so that the name of Israel would be remembered no more,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה כֵן לְפָנָיו בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם וּבָבֶל וּפָרַס דְּרַק שִׁעְבְּדוּם.
which was not the case before him in the exile of Egypt, Babylonia, and Persia, where they merely subjugated them.
דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּצְטַוֵּוינוּ לִמְחוֹתוֹ וּלְאַבֵּד כָּל זֵכֶר לוֹ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה.
For this is the archetype of Amalek, whom we were commanded to blot out and destroy every memory of, measure for measure.
כִּי הוּא גַּם כֵּן שֶׁנִּזְדַּוֵּוג לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְפִידִים,
Because he likewise confronted Israel at Rephidim,
שֶׁיָּצָא עֲלֵיהֶם לִלְחוֹם עִמָּהֶם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ כֵן אָז עֲדַיִן שׁוּם אוּמָּה.
marching out to wage war against them, which no nation had yet done at that time.
דְּמִצְרַיִם הָיוּ בֵּינֵיהֶם וְשִׁעְבְּדוּם,
For the Egyptians had them living in their midst and enslaved them,
וּמִלְחֶמֶת סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג וְהַשְּׁאָר הוּא מַה שֶּׁקָּרְבוּ עֲלֵיהֶם וְנִלְחֲמוּ כְּנֶגְדָּם;
and the war of Sihon, Og, and the rest occurred when Israel approached them and they fought back;
אֲבָל הוּא יָצָא כְּנֶגְדָּם וְחָשַׁב כִּי עַתָּה שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם וְהֵם כֻּלָּם יַחַד בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד – יוּכַל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לַעֲקוֹר אֶת הַכֹּל.
however, Amalek actively marched out against them, calculating that now that they had departed Egypt and were gathered together in one place, he could uproot everything, Heaven forbid.
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה רְצוֹן עֵשָׂו זְקֵינוֹ גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם.
And this was also the objective of his grandfather Esau against Jacob, yet they did not succeed.
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ"צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר",
For although "the wicked watches for the righteous, etc.",
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ.
the Holy One, blessed be He, will not abandon him into his hand.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִדְּנִצְטַוֵּוינוּ לִמְחוֹתוֹ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּפָעַל אֵיזֶה דָּבָר,
Yet nevertheless, from the fact that we were commanded to blot him out, deduce that he accomplished something,
דְּאִם לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ כְּלוּם כְּמוֹ לְעֵשָׂו, מַה שַּׁיָּיךְ "זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְגוֹמֵר"?
for had he achieved nothing just like Esau, how would "Remember what he did, etc." be applicable?
וְאַף דִּבְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרֵף לְמַעֲשֶׂה
And although regarding the nations of the world the Holy One, blessed be He, joins an evil intent to the deed

(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א דְּפֵאָה)1108 Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 — A good thought the Omnipresent joins to the deed; an evil thought the Omnipresent does not join to the deed. A good thought He joins to the deed, as it is written, "Then those who fear the Lord spoke with one another"; an evil thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join to the deed, as it is said, "Had I regarded iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not hear." This is said of Israel, but with the nations it is the reverse: a good thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join to the deed, and an evil thought He does join to the deed — as it is written, "from the slaughter, from the violence done to your brother Jacob." Did he actually kill him? Rather, this teaches that he thought to kill him, and Scripture accounted it to him as though he had killed him. Pnei Moshe: "Then those who fear the Lord spoke with one another" — the verse ends "and thought upon His name," from which it is expounded that even one who sat down to perform a commandment and was prevented by force and did not perform it, Scripture accounts it to him as though he had performed it. "From the slaughter, from the violence done to your brother Jacob" — "from the slaughter" belongs to the close of the preceding verse, and since it is superfluous there it is expounded together with what follows: because you killed your brother by your own violence. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kiddushin 40a): A good thought is one that is fit to be brought to actual performance, and one who comes to purify himself is helped; therefore a good thought is reckoned as though he had already done the deed. An evil thought He does not join to the deed, because one who comes to defile himself is not helped, and further, because a thing that ought to be done is already counted as done, whereas an evil thing ought not to be done at all, and so it is not reckoned a deed until it is actually done.,
(as written in Yerushalmi Peah 1:1),
הַיְינוּ לְעָנְשָׁם;
that is only to punish them;
אֲבָל לְצַוּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹר – עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּעָשָׂה אֵיזֶה דָּבָר נֶגְדָּם.
but to command Israel to remember—perforce he enacted a real effect against them.
וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ",
And that is what is written: "How he met you (karkha / cooled you off)",

וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא ט)1109 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 9 — "How he happened upon you [karkha]" (Deuteronomy 25:18) — and the Sages say: he cooled you [heikercha] before others. R. Chunya said: A parable — to a scalding bath into which no creature could go down. A certain scoundrel came and leaped into it; though he was scalded, he cooled it for others. So here: when Israel came out of Egypt and the Holy One, blessed be He, split the sea before them and the Egyptians were drowned in it, dread of them fell upon all the nations, as it is stated, "Then were the chiefs of Edom dismayed" (Exodus 15:15). When Amalek came and engaged them, though he got his due at their hands, he cooled them before the nations of the world.:
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 9):
אַף עַל פִּי דְּנִכְוָה בָּהּ, קֵירְרָהּ בִּפְנֵי אֲחֵרִים.
even though he was scalded by it, he cooled the bath before others.
הַיְינוּ דְּלוּלֵא מִלְחַמְתּוֹ אָז, לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן מִתְעוֹרְרִים לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
Meaning that were it not for his battle then, no nation or language would have been emboldened to provoke Israel,
כִּי רְעָדָה אֲחָזָתַם וְנָפַל פַּחְדָּם עֲלֵיהֶם.
for trembling had seized them and fear of Israel fell upon them.
רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ לִלְחוֹם,
Only through his initiation of war,
וְהוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת,
and being "first of the nations" and the spiritual taproot of all nations,
נוֹלַד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת זֶה בְּכָל הָאוּמּוֹת.
was this audacity awakened across all the nations.
וְאַף דְּהוּא נִכְוָה,
And even though he was scalded,
כִּי בָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ בְּתַכְלִית הַמַּעֲלָה מוּכָנִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה,
because he attacked when they were at the pinnacle of ascent ready to receive the Torah,
וְאַף דִּלְשָׁעָה רָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם בִּרְפִידִים לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא כְּרֶגַע,
and even though their hands slackened temporarily at Rephidim it was only for a moment,
וְתֵיכֶף שֶׁבָּא עֲלֵיהֶם שִׁעְבְּדוּ לִבָּם לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וְעַל כֵּן הוּא נִכְוָה;
and immediately when he came upon them they subjugated their hearts to their Father in Heaven, and therefore he was scalded;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם פָּעַל הִתְקָרְרוּת אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים שֶׁלֹּא יִירְאוּ עוֹד לִלְחוֹם.
nevertheless he brought about a cooling effect among others so they would no longer fear to fight.
וְהֵם בָּאוּ בִּזְמַן מְאוּחָר בִּימֵי הַשּׁוֹפְטִים,
And they arrived at a later period in the era of the Judges,
וְאָז לֹא נִכְווּ עוֹד,
and then they were no longer scalded,
וְעַל כֵּן נִצְטַוֵּוינוּ לִזְכּוֹר זֶה לִמְחוֹתוֹ.
and therefore we were commanded to remember this in order to blot him out.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Remembering Below, Blotting Out Above
Human remembrance awakens the eradication of Amalek, while hidden Da'at remains attached to its source beyond conscious awareness.

p: וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא ד)1110 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 4 — Israel said: Master of the Universe, we cannot prevail against him. The Holy One, blessed be He, says to them: You mention his name below, and I will blot out his name above, as it is stated, "Let them be before the Lord always" (Psalms 109:15) — all that he did, he did against Me — "and may He cut off their memory from the earth.":
And our Sages of blessed memory taught (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 4):
"אַתֶּם זוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה וַאֲנִי מוֹחֶה מִלְּמַעְלָה",
"You remember him from below, and I blot him out from Above,"
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַזְּכִירָה הוּא נִמְחֶה.
for through the remembrance he is blotted out.
כִּי כָּל כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁפָּעַל בָּאוּמּוֹת הוּא בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת;
Because the entire force of Amalek that had an impact on the nations was through initiation;
בִּהְיוֹת הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית, עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ נִתְעוֹרְרוּ כָּל עַמִּים כּוּלָּם.
being the "first", through his initial awakening all peoples were stirred up.
כְּמוֹ בָּאָדָם: עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ, אֵבָרֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִתְעוֹרְרִים לִפְעוֹל כְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ.
Just as in man: through the arousal of thought in his brain, the limbs of action are awakened to act according to his thought.
וְרֵאשִׁית דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, "כִּי אַתָּה אָבִינוּ";
And the Primordial Source of Israel is Hashem, blessed be He, "for You are our Father";

אֶלָּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נב)1111 Shemot Rabbah 52:5 — R. Shimon ben Yochai asked R. Elazar son of R. Yosei: Did you by chance hear from your father the meaning of "with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him"? He said to him: Yes. This is like a king who had an only daughter whom he loved exceedingly, and he would call her "my daughter"; he did not cease loving her until he called her "my sister," and he did not cease until he called her "my mother." So the Holy One, blessed be He: at first He called Israel "daughter" — "Hear, O daughter, and see"; He did not cease loving them until He called them "My sister" — "Open to Me, My sister, My beloved"; He did not cease loving them until He called them "My mother" — "Attend to Me, My people, and My nation [u-le'umi] give ear to Me," which is written u-le'immi, "and My mother." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:85): [The words of the Sages] are beloved even though [the Oral Torah] is in darkness, as Shir HaShirim Rabbah says, "He did not cease loving her until He called her My daughter ... until He called her My sister ... until He called her My mother": for at first their speech is only in the manner of a bat kol [lit. "daughter of a voice"], the Oral Torah being a bat kol of the Written Torah, and as Avodah Zarah says, "At first it is called the Torah of the Lord, and in the end, his Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): This is in the manner of "the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and the righteous one annuls," which was promised to King David in particular; and it is said of "the crown wherewith his mother crowned him," "He did not cease loving her until He called her My mother," for this is the level of "the righteous one annuls," and "the crown wherewith [she] crowned" is the attribute of Kingship. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayakhel 5): To this the verse alludes, "with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him," as the Midrash says, "He did not cease loving her ... until He called her My mother": the crown that the Holy One, blessed be He, will Himself, as it were, be on the head of every righteous person is described as though they make the crown for the Holy One, blessed be He. For in attaining the level of keter — the crown on the head of every righteous person — they attain in essence the crown of the Holy One, blessed be He, "wherewith his mother crowned him," since no thought can grasp Him at all and all emanation up to keter is relative to those who receive it. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, note on the angels' names 11): This is the meaning of "Yishmael, My son, bless Me": blessing is the increase and multiplication brought about by union, and the arousal from above is born through the arousal from below — which is the reason for "He did not cease loving her until He called her My mother." This is "bless Me," and he answered, "May it be Your will...," that is, that the will to bestow be born in You, and then there was complete union. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): When a person has completed all ten of his sefiros in holiness up to the level of keter, the level of nothingness and humility, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him "My twin," for the two are equal, and "He did not cease loving her until He called her My mother," as the Sages said — that is, he is, as it were, even greater than Him, as though he gave birth to the beginning of thought, which is the Blessed One's. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 7): Although the attribute of Kingship is the last, when it expands into a full stature they said of it, "He did not cease loving her until He called her My daughter, and My sister, and My mother": the Community of Israel as a whole, whose souls are a divine portion from above, are the last of the emanated levels, the one that can be clothed in the bodily garb of this world so that the Blessed One's Presence dwells below, which is the purpose and end of all emanation. Therefore, though they are the end of all creation, they are also its head and essence, for "the end of the deed is first in thought," and Israel arose first in [God's] thought. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 187): The books [of Torah] are at first a person's teachers, and when he draws new insights through them they become his companions; thus "He did not cease loving her until He called her My daughter ... My sister ... My mother," "My mother" being the stage of the student, when in the end it becomes "his Torah," as though he gave birth to the very Torah given to Moses at Sinai — for [the Sages] gave birth to the root of Torah and wisdom in the world. "My daughter" is the initial arousal from below in intense longing; "My sister," when the arousal from above comes to assist and new insights are born to him; and "My mother," when he recognizes that the insights are from the Blessed One, for after this acknowledgement the Blessed One says that all is his, even the arousal from above, in the sense of "Give strength to God." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 8): When one cleaves entirely to his source, he comes to feel that even all his own striving in holiness is supernal holiness, and this is the secret of "He did not cease loving her until He called her My mother." "My daughter" is when man's holiness is drawn from the holiness above, as with the festivals, which are sanctified by the holiness they receive from the Sabbath; "My sister" is the holiness of the Sabbath, when all Israel are sanctified with the Sabbath's own holiness; and "My mother" is Yom Kippur, the Sabbath of Sabbaths, from which holiness flows to the Sabbath, for the holiness that Israel sanctify rises to its source, the supreme source of all holiness. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Ruth): When a person takes refuge in the Blessed One and ascribes all his deeds to Him, the Blessed One repays him measure for measure and ascribes even the thought behind his deeds to him. This is the Midrash on "the crown wherewith his mother crowned him": after King David said, "and from Your hand we have given You," ascribing the entire deed to the Blessed One, "He did not cease loving her until He called her My mother" — "mother" being the thought, for even the thought is called by your name. Tiferes Yosef (Emor 2): "His sister" denotes the love and bond the Blessed One has with Israel from birth, without any drawing near on their part, solely from His first kindness in choosing Israel; this is the intent of the Midrash, "He did not cease loving her until He called her My sister." "Sister" thus denotes the first kindness, as it says, "Remember Your mercies, O Lord, and Your kindnesses, for they are from of old.":
except that our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shemot Rabbah 52):
לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "אִמִּי",
He did not cease cherishing Israel until He called them "My mother",
וְהַיְינוּ כְּטַעַם: "תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים" (תְּהִלִּים סח, לה),
which aligns with: "Ascribe strength unto God" (Psalms 68:35),
דְּכָךְ הָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
for such was the will of Hashem, blessed be He:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאָדָם בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא מוֹלִיד אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא,
that man through an awakening from below should engender an awakening from Above,
וּכְאִלּוּ הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית וְהָאֵם הַמּוֹלִידָה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא אַחַר כָּךְ,
as if he were the primary cause and the mother generating the supernal awakening afterward,
שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לְמַעְלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר.
which stirs Above corresponding to how he stirs below.
וְהַזְּכִירָה הוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
And remembering is the arousal of thought,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְמָר הַפְּעוּלָה מִלְּמַעְלָה,
and through this the action is brought to fruition from Above;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשִׂים יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרֵאשִׁית דִּלְמַעְלָה,
for through this Israel become the primary force of the supernal Realm,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אִתְעָרוּתָא זוֹ לִמְחוֹת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק,
when there is within them this arousal to blot out the remembrance of Amalek,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם רֵאשִׁית וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְרַע כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם,
meaning that there should remain no inception or provocation to evil whatsoever in the world,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר דִּלְעָתִיד.
which is the ultimate nullification of the evil inclination in the future.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁעֲמָלֵק קַיָּים, דְּיֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לַיֵּצֶר,
And as long as Amalek exists, such that an existence for the evil inclination persists,
"אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ" (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:),
"were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it" (Kiddushin 30b),
וְאִם כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית.
and if so, Hashem, blessed be He, is the primary Originator.
וּכְמוֹ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
And just as during the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah,
דְּ"קוֹל דּוֹדִי בָּא" בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא,
where "the voice of my Beloved came" through an awakening from Above,
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא הָיָה מְצִיאוּת הָרֵאשִׁית,
and within this physical world the primary initiation was not theirs,
וְיֵשׁ עֲדַיִן מְצִיאוּת לְרֵאשִׁית דְּרַע.
and there consequently remained reality for the primary root of evil.
וּמְחִיַּת הָרֵאשִׁית דְּרַע הוּא גְּאוּלָּה הָעֲתִידָה,
And the blotting out of the primary root of evil is the future redemption,

אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז:)1112 Sanhedrin 97b — Rav said: All the appointed ends have passed, and the matter depends only on repentance and good deeds. And Shmuel said: It is enough for the mourner that he stand in his mourning. This parallels a dispute of the Tannaim: R. Eliezer says: If Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. R. Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, are they not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, will set over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel will repent, and He will restore them to the good. Maharsha: R. Eliezer's "if Israel repent" means a willed repentance, of their own accord, whereas R. Yehoshua holds that when the time of redemption comes, the Holy One, blessed be He, sets over them a king whose decrees are harsh and restores them to the good so that they repent — a compelled repentance. He rejects Rashi's reading that in R. Yehoshua's view they are redeemed without any repentance at all, for if so, why would R. Yehoshua speak of a king like Haman who restores them to the good? Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 97b): R. Eliezer does not mean that without repentance there will be no redemption and the matter will remain in doubt, for there is no doubt about the redemption of Israel; rather, exile is an accidental thing — in itself, for by the order of the world the Israelite nation ought to be in its land and not under the dominion of others, and if exile depends on sin, sin too is not essential but accidental, and what is accidental has no permanence — and God, blessed be He, will remove from them the sickness of the soul as He removes sickness of the body, as it is written, "And the Lord will circumcise your heart," so that it is impossible that they will not repent. R. Yehoshua did not hold that it depends specifically on Israel's repentance, as though the redemption lay in Israel's hands: Israel must indeed repent and then they will be redeemed, but if God, blessed be He, wishes to redeem Israel and they do not repent, He sets over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's and restores them to the good. In the end, according to all, it is impossible that the exile be permanent. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 37): Answering Abraham's "Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it," He said "Know surely" and told him of the [subjugation to the] kingdoms, for the Land is merited through sufferings, which sweeten the flesh, the bodily part of man that corresponds to deeds. Only through this is there hope for the complete end, as they said, "He sets up a king as harsh as Haman," and then there will be an inheritance and possession without interruption. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Of the future redemption it is said, "As in the days of your going out of Egypt I will show him wonders": when it comes "in its time" and they are not worthy, then even though the Holy One, blessed be He, will set up a king as harsh as Haman so that they repent, that repentance comes from an arousal from Above, and on this the nations have a claim, that had He aroused them from Above they too would have been aroused. Such a redemption "in its time," like the Exodus, comes from an arousal from Above: a sudden redemption without prior merit or effort, whose light is not yet grasped in this world before it appears. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): The King of the world, as it were, removed the ring of His rule and handed it to Haman, holiness clothing itself in Haman's sackcloth, since Israel were asleep to the commandments and could be roused only in this way, while the true intent was the reverse: to exalt Israel and destroy Haman, the seed of Amalek and all Israel's enemies. So too in the future, if, Heaven forbid, they should need a king as harsh as Haman, the Blessed One will clothe Himself within him, for "the king's heart is in the hand of the Lord," and through that clothing in the garment of Esau [Israel's enemies] will be wiped out from the world.: דְּאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
and our Sages of blessed memory taught (Sanhedrin 97b): it depends exclusively on repentance,
הַיְינוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא דַּוְוקָא;
meaning specifically through an awakening from below;
וְעַל יְדֵי גּוֹדֶל הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתָם לִמְחוֹת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר, דְּהוּא עִנְיַן הַזְּכִירָה דַּעֲמָלֵק,
and through the intensity of their yearning to eradicate the root of the inclination, which is the remembrance of Amalek,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִפְעֲלוּ לְמַעְלָה אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן,
they will thereby effect this Above with Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשׂוּ הֵם הָרֵאשִׁית דְּטוֹב בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
because through this they become the primary source of good in this world.
וּמִמֵּילָא שׁוּב אֵין מְצִיאוּת לְרֵאשִׁית דְּרַע כְּלָל,
And automatically there remains no existence for the root of evil at all,
וְכָל הַגּוֹיִם נַעֲשִׂים גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים.
and all the nations become attached proselytes.
וּכְמוֹ בִּימֵי הָמָן: "רַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים כִּי נָפַל פַּחַד וְגוֹמֵר" (אֶסְתֵּר ח, יז),
And just as in the days of Haman: "Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear, etc." (Esther 8:17),
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָבַד הָרֵאשִׁית שֶׁלָּהֶם.
because their prime root had been lost.
וְהָמָן הוּא נִתְגַּבֵּר יוֹתֵר מֵעֲמָלֵק,
And Haman grew even more formidable than Amalek,
שֶׁכְּבָר הוֹצִיא גְּזֵירָה כְּתוּבָה וַחֲתוּמָה;
for he had already extracted a decree written and sealed;

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז)1113 Esther Rabbah 7:13 — [Elijah] said to him: A letter of annihilation has already been written against Israel. Moses said to him: If it is sealed with clay, our prayer is heard; but if it was sealed with blood, what has been, is. He said to him: With clay it is sealed. Moses our teacher said to him: Go and inform Mordechai.:
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Esther Rabbah 7):
דְּנֶחְתַּם בְּטַבַּעַת מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן,
that it was sealed with the ring of the King of the universe as well,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה בְּחוֹתָם שֶׁל טִיט.
only that it was with a seal of clay.

Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, are they not redeemed at all? And this is like what our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin ibid.) regarding the future:
דְּאִם אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַעֲמִיד מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן;
that if they do not repent, the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints a king as harsh as Haman;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה יד.)1115 Megillah 14a — "And the king removed his ring from his hand." R. Abba bar Kahana said: The removal of the ring was greater than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses who prophesied to Israel, for all of them did not return Israel to the good way, whereas the removal of the ring returned them to the good way. Rashi (s.v. “returned them to the good way”): For they decreed fasts upon them for repentance, as it is written, “fasting, and weeping, and wailing; sackcloth and ashes were spread for many” (Esther 4:3). Maharsha: The king’s decree is made to depend upon the removal of the ring, for by it they were handed over to Haman, as the verse says, “the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you.” And in the Midrash: Ahasuerus hated Israel more [than Haman did] — the way of the world is that the buyer gives a pledge to the seller, yet here it is written, “And the king removed his ring.” That is the point here: the removal of the ring, in which they saw how great Ahasuerus’s hatred was, is what returned them to the good way, for they repented with their whole heart. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:10): The prophets prophesied of chastisement from the Holy One, blessed be He, so that it might not come upon them, and since He has compassion on His creatures, they were not so greatly afraid.
