But the removal of the ring showed that the king was removing this matter from himself and placing it in the hand of a man: as long as it is in a king's hand — and it is the Holy One, blessed be He, who establishes kings, so that they are like His messengers — they too do not wish to destroy everything; but when it is handed over to a commoner, him they fear. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 6): The essential salvation of Israel comes when they are saved in the very thing whose lack brought on the trouble, so that the healing grows from the blows themselves — as the Megillah says, "Greater was the removal of the ring...," for it returned them to the good, and in Perek Chelek this is taken as the model: "He sets over them a king as harsh as Haman." For in Haman's days they returned in complete repentance and accepted the whole Torah upon themselves and their descendants out of love; that was the essential salvation brought about through the decree, and with it the decree was annulled of itself. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): In the days of Haman Israel were returned to the good by something the forty-eight prophets had not achieved, as the Sages said, "Greater was the removal of the ring...": since "the king" in the Megillah means the King of the world, it was He who, as it were, removed the ring of His dominion for a short while and handed it to Haman, as though Haman were the ruler doing as he pleased. This was holiness clothing itself in Haman's sackcloth, because Israel were asleep from the mitzvos and could be roused only in this way, while the true intent was the opposite: to exalt Israel and to destroy Haman, the seed of Amalek and all Israel's enemies.: "גְּדוֹלָה הֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת מִמַּ"ח (אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה) נְבִיאִים,
and as they said (Megillah 14a): "Greater was the removal of the signet ring than the forty-eight prophets,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁבוּ".
for through it they repented."
וְהַנְּבִיאִים שֶׁבָּאוּ בְּדִבְרֵי ה' – זֶהוּ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא,
And the prophets who came with the words of Hashem—this was an awakening from Above,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּא לְעוֹרְרָם בִּהְיוֹת הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית שֶׁלָּהֶם,
wherein Hashem, blessed be He, came to awaken them being Himself their primary Source,
וְלֹא הוֹעִיל;
yet it did not succeed;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא הַבְּחִירָה עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הַמַּעֲלִים דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית,
because Hashem created free choice through the power of the evil inclination that conceals the fact that Hashem is the Source,
וַעֲדַיִן לֹא הוּטְהֲרוּ מִיֵּצֶר רָע הֶחָפֵץ לְהַפְרִידָם מִדִּיבּוּקָם בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
and they were not yet purified of the evil inclination which seeks to sever them from their attachment to the Living God,
וְאֵין מַנִּיחַ שֶׁיֵּצֵא לַפּוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁלָּהֶם,
and does not allow that which is in the deep primordial thought of their root to be actualized in deed,
עַד הֲסָרַת הַטַּבַּעַת.
until the removal of the signet ring.

דִּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קט עַמּוּד א)1116 Zohar 3:109a — R. Shimon said: We find "courts" in that of which it is said, "And she stood in the inner court of the king's house, opposite the king's house" (Esther 5:1). And everywhere "the king" without qualification is the Holy One, blessed be He. "And she stood" — "standing" means nothing other than prayer. "Opposite the king's house" — opposite the Temple, for all Israel must direct their prayer there, and must be opposite the Temple. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 5): For one who understands, the whole Megillah is the story of the "slumber" of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, from beginning to end. It begins from the feast of Shushan, for from there begins "the king" without qualification rather than "King Ahasuerus," meaning the King of kings of kings who clothed Himself [in him], and the hundred and eighty days before it were the preparation for receiving that clothing of the King of kings of kings. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 13): Haman said, "To whom would the king desire [to do honor]?" — and it is known from the Sages that "the king" without qualification speaks of the King of kings of kings: he thought that he was esteemed by the Blessed One as well, since not for nothing had He made him great and delivered Israel into his hand to destroy them, because they had grown lax in (lit. “slept from”) the commandments, and he imagined that He had chosen him in their stead. It became a mockery afterward, when he heard the king's words that it was Mordechai the Jew in whom he delighted, and that he himself would be a servant before him.:
For our Sages of blessed memory already said (Zohar Part III, 109a):
דְּ"הַמֶּלֶךְ" סְתָם בְּמַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם מְדַבֵּר,
that "the king" unspecified speaks of the King of the universe,
שֶׁהוּא כִּבְיָכוֹל הֵסִיר טַבַּעְתּוֹ וּנְתָנָהּ לְהָמָן.
that He, as it were, removed His signet ring and gave it to Haman.
הַיְינוּ דְּוַודַּאי חָלִילָה שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַל הַדַּעַת הָעֶלְיוֹן יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ לְהַשְׁמִיד שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר לוֹ לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ;
Meaning that Heaven forbid that it should enter the Supernal Mind, blessed be His Name, to destroy the root of Israel whom He chose as His treasured people;

וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יב.)1117 Megillah 12a — [R. Shimon ben Yochai said that the Jews of that generation were liable to destruction because they had prostrated themselves to the image.] They said to him: But is there favoritism in the matter [that they were nevertheless delivered]? He said to them: They did it only for appearance's sake, and so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only for appearance's sake. And this is what is written: "For He does not afflict from His heart" (Lamentations 3:33). Rashi: "But is there favoritism in the matter?" — that is, how then did they merit a miracle? "They did it only for appearance's sake" — out of fear. Maharsha: That is, they acted so only from fear of being killed, as is set out in the book of Daniel, and did not intend in their hearts to serve the idol; so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only outwardly, frightening them that they deserved destruction so that they should take alarm and repent on that account. And this is the sense of "For He does not afflict from His heart": when a man commits a transgression with his heart not in it, the Holy One, blessed be He, "grieves the children of men" only in order that he should repent and be delivered from the trouble. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 33): Though the Jews were only joining gentiles at a single feast, the Gemara calls this "serving idols in purity," and this was the accusation: that they took pleasure in the feast of that wicked man, which is a trace of idolatry, and likewise that they bowed to the image — though it was only a [royal] statue and they did it only for appearance's sake, it is nevertheless a trace of idolatry, and "round about Him it storms greatly" [He is exacting with those near Him]. Because they then purified themselves in this matter until they had slaughtered the inclination to idolatry entirely, the Blessed One wished to establish a feast for them, to show that even in their drunkenness they need fear nothing, their hearts being already whole with Him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The acceptance of the Torah in the days of Ahasuerus, though out of love, was in concealment, for in what was revealed there were claims against them, as the Sages said that "they did it only for appearance's sake" — that is, only in the outward, revealed deed, while the inwardness of their heart is for God. This was the redemption of that time, which made clear concerning Israel's sins that even when they sin, the inwardness of their heart is for Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 255): The Megillah opens with the feast because the decree sprouted from it, as the Sages said, "because they took pleasure"; and although the Gemara concludes that it was because they bowed to the image, they were not punished for that at the time, since in truth they did it only for appearance's sake, and "the Lord sees into the heart" — there was sin only from the human side, for "man sees what is before the eyes." As long as they conduct themselves with a generous eye, the Blessed One too has a generous eye toward them, bestowing on them by His measure of "seeing into the heart"; but on account of "they took pleasure" — the incitement of the power of the narrow eye — the Blessed One too said, "Mine is mine and yours is yours," judging by what is before the eyes. עַל זֶה: דְּהָיָה רַק לִפְנִים,
and therefore our Sages said concerning this: that it was only outward appearance,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַחוֹתָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה לֹא הָיָה מִלִּבּוֹ וְעַל יְדֵי פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה,
meaning that the supernal decree was not from His innermost heart and supernal retinue,
רַק שֶׁמָּסַר טַבַּעְתּוֹ לְהָמָן שֶׁהוּא יַחְתּוֹם מַה שֶּׁיִּרְצֶה.
only that He handed His ring to Haman so that he could stamp whatever he wished.

כַּיָּדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הָמָן: "אֱלֹהֵיהֶם יָשֵׁן" (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם)1118 Esther Rabbah 7:12 — "And Haman said to King Ahasuerus: There is [yeshno] one people" (Esther 3:8) — He of whom it is said, "The Lord is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4), sleeps [yashen] away from His people. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Before Me there is no sleep, as it is written, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps" (Psalms 121:4); yet you have said that there is sleep before Me. By your life, out of sleep I will rouse Myself against that man and destroy him from the world, as it is written, "And the Lord awoke like one asleep, and He smote His foes backward" (Psalms 78:65). Sod Yesharim (Purim 25): On the Gemara's "they are asleep from the commandments" and the Midrash's "[Haman] said, their God is asleep," the holy Arizal wrote that this was also the matter at the beginning of creation, "And the Lord God cast a deep sleep." When a person nullifies himself completely and hands all the power of his own being over to the Blessed One, the Blessed One returns to him a sprouting of salvation all the more, and before every sprouting of salvation there must first be such a nullification. So the destruction and exile were a nullification in which Israel handed back to the Blessed One all the might they had from performing the commandments, until they seemed asleep from the commandments, and this is the deep sleep.,
As is known what Haman claimed: "Their God is sleeping" (Midrash Rabbah ibid.),
שֶׁהָיָה אָז בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל דּוּגְמַת שֵׁינָה,
for then in the Babylonian exile it was like sleep,
כְּאִלּוּ נִסְתַּלֵּק עֵינָא פְּקִיחָא דְּהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
as though the open, watchful eye of His providence had departed from the lower realms, Heaven forbid,
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "עוּרָה לָמָּה תִישַׁן וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים מד, כד),
regarding which it is written: "Awake, why do You sleep, etc." (Psalms 44:24),
וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּאִלּוּ הֵסִיר טַבַּעְתּוֹ וְנָתַן הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה לְהָמָן לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ כִּי הוּא סִילֵּק הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ.
and behold, this was as if He removed His signet ring and handed dominion to Haman to act as he wished, since He withdrew His manifest providence.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "חוֹתָם שֶׁל טִיט",
And this is termed a "seal of clay",
הַיְינוּ חוֹתָם שֶׁמִּצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה.
meaning a seal originating from this physical world, dust of the earth.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חוֹתָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּשֶׁנִּגְזַר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הוּא "חוֹתָם שֶׁל דָּם",
Whereas a true supernal seal when decreed, Heaven forbid, is a "seal of blood",
דְּהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּבוֹ מִשְׁכַּן נֶפֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִית שֶׁמֵּעֶלְיוֹנִים;
which represents the life-soul wherein dwells the spiritual soul of supernal origin;
אֲבָל טִיט הוּא חוֹתָם גּוּפָנִי לוֹמַר דְּנֶחְתַּם רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
but clay is a bodily seal, meaning it was enacted solely within this transient world.
וּמִצַּד דִּכְבְיָכוֹל הָיָה אָז בְּמַדְרֵגַת שֵׁינָה וּכְאִלּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עָזַב אֶת הָאָרֶץ, הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב זֶה גַּם כֵּן לְחוֹתָם.
And because He was, as it were, in a state of sleep, as if He had forsaken the earth, Heaven forbid, this too was deemed an effective seal.
וְזֶה הַחוֹתָם אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁבָּר בְּקַל,
And this seal can easily be shattered,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יָעִירוּ וִיעוֹרְרוּ אֶת הָאַהֲבָה בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא לְעוֹרֵר אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא,
when they awaken and stir love through an awakening from below to evoke an awakening from Above,
וּמִתְגַּלֶּה כִּי אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה,
and it becomes revealed that there is none else beside Him and His kingdom rules over all,
וְאֵין עוֹד מָקוֹם לְחוֹתָם טִיט כְּלָל.
and there is no longer any place for a seal of clay at all.
וְנִמְצָא דַּהֲסָרַת הַטַּבַּעַת הוּא מַמָּשׁ הַהֵיפֶךְ מִמַּ"ח (אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה) נְבִיאִים,
Consequently, the removal of the ring was the exact opposite of the 48 prophets:
שֶׁהָיָה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא לְעוֹרֵר אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְלֹא הוֹעִיל,
which had been an awakening from Above to stir an awakening from below and did not help,
וַהֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת הוּא סִילּוּק הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא לְגַמְרֵי.
whereas the removal of the signet ring was the complete withdrawal of the awakening from Above.
וְאָז בִּזְמַן הֲסָרַת הַטַּבַּעַת הָיָה תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַשֵּׁינָה,
And at the moment of the ring's removal was the absolute climax of slumber,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר הָמָן לוֹמַר "יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד וְגוֹמֵר",
through which Haman was emboldened to claim "There is (yeshno) a certain people, etc.",

כְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יג:)1119 Megillah 13b — "There is one people scattered abroad and dispersed" (Esther 3:8). Rava said: There was none who knew how to slander like Haman. He said to him: Come, let us destroy them. He said to him: I fear their God, lest He do to me as He did to those before me. He said to him: "There is" [yeshno] — they have slumbered [yashnu] away from the commandments. He said to him: But there are sages among them. He said to him: They are "one people" [all alike]. Rashi (s.v. “There are Sages among them”): From Haman’s reply we learn that this is how Ahasuerus had answered him. Maharsha: The verse is superfluous, and its expressions are doubled — it need only have written “there is” [yesh] and not “yeshno” — and therefore they expounded that Haman told him they had slumbered away from the commandments: either from the word “change,” that they alter their commandments, or from the word “sleep,” that they sleep away from them. And from the superfluous word “one” they expounded Ahasuerus’s objection, “There are Sages among them” who will shield them by their good deeds — to which Haman answered, “They are one people”: just as the rest of the people do not keep the commandments, so too the Sages among them do not keep them. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:8): As for their expounding "there is" [yeshno] as "they have slumbered from the commandments," it seems that the exposition does not rest chiefly on the word yeshno being a form of "sleep"; rather, the expression "there is a people" itself implies it — that they are nothing but a people, whereas the commandments do not derive from their being a "people" but from the name "Israel," for all the other nations, which are peoples, have no commandments. So he said that these too are merely "a people," like every other people that is called only "a people," since they do not perform the divine commandments. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): Haman — of whom the Sages said that none knew how to slander like him — aimed his accusation against Israel above: he said, "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and of the Rabbis, "They too are one people," that is, he accused Israel's own sanctity, which comes through Torah and mitzvos, saying that all of them, even the Torah scholars, had slumbered from Torah and mitzvos. And against the sanctity that comes from the Blessed One he said that He of whom it is said "the Lord is One" has fallen asleep away from His people. Sod Yesharim (Purim 25): "They have slumbered from the mitzvos," and in the Midrash, "[Haman] said: their God is asleep" — as the Arizal wrote, this is like the deep sleep at the beginning of Creation: when a person nullifies himself entirely and surrenders all his selfhood to the Blessed One, He returns to him a sprouting of salvation all the more, and every salvation must be preceded by such nullification. The destruction and exile were such a self-nullification, in which Israel surrendered to the Blessed One all the might they had drawn from the mitzvos dependent on the Land, until they appeared to be sleeping from the mitzvos, and from this the Second Temple sprouted. At that very time, when they appeared to be asleep, Haman said "their God is asleep, they have slumbered from the mitzvos," seeking to accuse Israel, and the Blessed One showed him, "Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.": "יָשְׁנוּ מִן הַמִּצְווֹת".
in line with the words of our Sages (Megillah 13b): "they have slept (yashnu) from the mitzvot."
דְּאַף דְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְווֹת כְּרִמּוֹן,
For although the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם, חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל הַמְּעוֹרְרָם;
this is only from the side of their soul's root, a portion of God from Above that stirs them;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר זֶה הָיָה בְּשֵׁינָה, הָיוּ הֵם יְשֵׁנִים מֵהַמִּצְווֹת.
and when this was in a state of slumber, they slept from the mitzvot.
וְהָיָה בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא לִגְרוֹם אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא,
And it became imperative for an awakening from below to generate an awakening from Above,
וְזֶה הוֹעִיל יוֹתֵר,
and this proved far more effective,
דְּעַל יְדֵי הָרִיחוּק מִתְעוֹרֵר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאַהֲבָה יוֹתֵר;
for through distance the root of love is stirred all the more intensely;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּכַאֲשֶׁר הַבֵּן עִם אָבִיו יַחַד בִּתְמִידוּת הָאַהֲבָה כְּבָר בְּהֶרְגֵּל וְלִפְעָמִים יוּכַל לְוַותֵּר קְצָת נֶגְדּוֹ,
as is known, when a son is continuously together with his father love becomes habitual and sometimes he may compromise his respect,
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּרִיחוּק וּמִתְעוֹרֵר בְּלִבּוֹ זִכְרוֹן אַהֲבַת אָבִיו – הוּא בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם יוֹתֵר,
yet when he is distant and the memory of his father's love is aroused in his heart, it bursts forth with far greater strength,
שֶׁמִּצַּד הָרִיחוּק הֶעָצוּם צָעַק לִבָּם אֶל ה' לְהִתְקָרֵב יוֹתֵר.
such that from the tremendous distance their heart cried out to Hashem to draw closer.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן "מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן" הַמְּעוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
And this is the matter of a harsh king like Haman who stirs them to repentance,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּרַע הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ לְגַמְרֵי הָרֵאשִׁית דְּטוֹב בְּגֶדֶר שֵׁינָה גְּמוּרָה.
representing the ultimate depth of the root of evil that makes one entirely forget the Source of good in complete sleep.
וְאָז: "וַיִּקַץ כְּיָשֵׁן ה' כְּגִבּוֹר מִתְרוֹנֵן מִיָּיִן" (תְּהִלִּים עח, סה),
And then: "Hashem awoke as one from sleep, like a mighty man recovering from wine" (Psalms 78:65),
כִּי כָּל שִׁיקּוּעִים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא שִׁכְרוּת מִיַּיִן,
for all immersion in this world is termed drunkenness from wine,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְמַאן דְּאָמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יט)1120 Bereshit Rabbah 19:5 — "She took of its fruit and ate" — R. Aivu said: She squeezed grapes and gave him. R. Simlai said: She came upon him with settled reasoning. She said to him: What do you suppose — that I will die and another Eve will be created for you? "There is nothing new under the sun." Or perhaps that I will die and you will sit alone? "He did not create it a waste; He formed it to be inhabited.": "עֲנָבִים סָחֲטָה",
as occurred with Adam the First according to the one who states (Bereishit Rabbah 19): "she squeezed grapes",

וּבְנֹחַ1121 Genesis 9:20-21 — “And Noach, a man of the earth, began and planted a vineyard. And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself within his tent.” Rashi: "And Noah began" — he made himself profane, for he should have occupied himself first with some other planting. "A man of the ground" means the master of the ground, like "the husband of Naomi"; and when he entered the ark he had brought in with him vine-shoots and cuttings of fig trees. "His tent" is written אהלה, an allusion to the ten tribes, who were called after Samaria — which was called Oholah — and who were exiled on account of wine, as it is said, "who drink wine in bowls." Ramban: Against Rashi he explains "a man of the ground" as one who dedicated himself to working the ground, to sowing and to planting, because he found the earth laid waste — just as "the men of the city" means those who dwell in it. "And he began" means that he began the planting of vineyards: earlier men had planted single vines, but Noah, out of his craving for wine, did not plant the vine singly like other trees, but set out many rows together and made a vineyard.,
and with Noah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כּוֹס בְּיַד ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים עה, ט) שֶׁמַּשְׁקֶה כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת וּמְשַׁכְּרָם.
and as written: "There is a cup in Hashem's hand, etc." (Psalms 75:9) which gives drink to all the nations and intoxicates them.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם נִשְׁאָרִים כָּךְ בְּשִׁכְרוּתָם,
Except that the nations remain trapped in their drunkenness,

אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מִתְעוֹרְרִים מִשִּׁכְרוּתָם וּמִתְפַּתִּים בְּיֵינָם כִּי יֵשׁ בָּהֶם מִדַּעַת קוֹנָם (עֵירוּבִין סה.)1122 Eruvin 65a — R. Chanina said: Whoever is won over by his wine has in him something of the mind of his Maker, as it is stated: "And the Lord smelled the sweet savor, and the Lord said in His heart: I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake" (Genesis 8:21). Rashi: "One who is won over by wine" — that when men appease him over some matter he is reconciled while his heart is merry with wine. "The sweet savor" — we said above that smelling is like drinking, and it is written, "and the Lord said in His heart: I will not again curse," that is, He was reconciled. Maharsha: Rashi's explanation is forced. Rather, when a man sins against his fellow it is the way of the world to appease him with a feast and with his own wine; and the Gemara means that if a man does not insist upon being appeased with the wine of the one who wronged him, but is won over by wine of his own, he has in him something of the mind of his Maker — for the Holy One, blessed be He, consented to be appeased by an offering that was already His own, as it is written, "If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world is Mine and its fullness." This is why it says "by his wine" rather than "by wine.".
whereas Israel awake from their drunkenness and become appeased in their wine because they carry within them the awareness of their Maker (Eruvin 65a).
וְ"דַעַת" נִקְרָא הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁבִּפְנִימִיּוּת וְהֶעְלֵם, כְּטַעַם "מֹשֶׁה מִלְּגָאו",
And "Da'at" (knowledge) designates apprehension that is inward and hidden, mirroring "Moses from within",
דְּעַל כֵּן דַּעַת זֶה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִּׁ"י פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא (שְׁמוֹת לא, ג),
which is why Da'at is the Holy Spirit, as Rashi wrote in Parashat Ki Tisa (Exodus 31:3),
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגָה נֶעְלֶמֶת שֶׁמִּצַּד דִּיבּוּק הַנְּשָׁמָה בִּמְקוֹרָהּ וְרֵאשִׁיתָהּ;
which is a concealed grasp born of the soul's clinging unto its Origin and Source;
וְאַף בְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה וְהַשִּׁכְרוּת הֵם דְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת בְּרֵאשִׁיתָם,
and even during sleep and drunkenness they remain truly cleaved to their Source,
רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
only that it remains hidden within this world.

items.h:
Seif 4 — Moshe's Birth, Death, and Hidden Da'at
Adar contains both revelation and concealment of Moshe's Da'at, teaching that departed light persists inwardly with greater reach.

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר,
And this is the essence of the month of Adar,
שֶׁבּוֹ נוֹלַד וָמֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
wherein Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was born and passed away,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדַּעַת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל;
who is the spiritual root of Da'at (Divine Awareness) of Israel;
וְלֵידָתוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת בָּעוֹלָם,
and his birth represents the revelation of Da'at in the world,
וּמִיתָתוֹ הוּא הִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר בְּהֶעְלֵם.
while his death represents his departure whereby it remained in concealment.
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אוֹרוֹת שֶׁנִּתְגַּלּוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
As is known, all spiritual lights that were once revealed in this physical world,
אַף דְּנִסְתַּלְּקוּ – הַיְינוּ מִן הַגִּילּוּי,
even though they departed—this applies only to outer revelation,
אֲבָל לֹא נִסְתַּלְּקוּ לְגַמְרֵי, רַק נִשְׁאֲרוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם.
yet they did not depart completely, but rather remained in concealment.
וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֵם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִינֵי הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַלְּבָנָה,
And the twelve months correspond to the twelve modes of renewal belonging to the moon,
הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע;
which alludes to the Congregation of Israel, as is known;
וְנִיסָן הוּא רֵאשִׁית הִתְחַדְּשׁוּתָם,
and Nisan is the inception of their renewal,
שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה רֵאשִׁית הִתְגַּלּוּת אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
wherein was the primary revelation of the Jewish nation,
שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵירוּת לִהְיוֹת לְעַם מְיוּחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
when they went forth from bondage to freedom to become a distinct nation unto themselves.
וַאֲדָר הוּא הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּמִינֵי הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת,
And Adar is the final among these modes of renewal;
אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר עָבְרוּ כָּל מִינֵי שִׁינּוּיִים דִּתְקוּפַת הַשָּׁנָה,
after all varieties of seasonal shifts throughout the year have already passed,
הוּא מְעוּתָּד לַחֲזוֹר לַהַתְחָלָה וּנְקוּדָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
it is destined to cycle back to the beginning and to the primal point,
וְלֹא פָּעֲלוּ בוֹ כָּל הַשִּׁינּוּיִים כְּלוּם.
and none of the changes have impacted its essential core in the least.
וַאֲדָר הוּא הַמַּחֲזִיר לְנִיסָן,
And Adar is that which returns the cycle unto Nisan,
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ זֶה דְּהַחֲזָרָה
for within it resides this restorative power of returning,
אַחַר שֶׁעָבַר כָּל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר וְנִתְרַחֵק מֵהַהַתְחָלָה תַּכְלִית הָרִיחוּק הָאֶפְשָׁרִי;
after all that has transpired has passed, reaching the furthest conceivable distance from the beginning;
וּבַקָּצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן הוּא מַחֲזִירוֹ שֵׁנִית לַהַהַתְחָלָה,
yet at the outermost boundary it restores it anew to the beginning,
וּרְחוֹקִים נַעֲשׂוּ קְרוֹבִים בְּתַכְלִית הַקֵּירוּב
and the distant become near in absolute closeness
עַד שֶׁחוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה עַצְמָהּ.
until it returns to the source itself.
וְזֶהוּ בְּכֹחַ הַדַּעַת
And this is effected through the power of Da'at,
הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
which unites Chokhmah (Wisdom) and Binah (Understanding),
"רֵיעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, ד עַמּוּד א),
"two companions that never separate" (Zohar Part III, 4a),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּתוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן הֵם מִתְפָּרְשִׁין וּמִתְרַחֲקִין לִפְעָמִים;
even though within their outward offspring and derivatives they sometimes appear separated and distant;
זֶהוּ מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
this is merely from the perspective of external manifestation in this world,
דְּאֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁעֲמָלֵק קַיָּים,
for the Divine Name is not complete so long as Amalek exists,
לִהְיוֹת נִיכָּר הִתְכַּלְלוּת הַתּוֹלָדוֹת בָּאָבוֹת אֵיךְ כּוּלּוֹ חַד.
so as to overtly recognize the absorption of the derivatives within the Patriarchal roots, demonstrating how everything is one.
וְנִרְאִין אוֹתִיּוֹת יוֹ״ד-הֵ״א שֶׁהֵם אַבָּא וְאִימָּא לְשֵׁם נִפְרָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
And the letters Yud-Hei, representing Abba and Imma (Wisdom and Understanding), appear as a distinct, isolated name unto itself,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חִיבּוּר עִם זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (וָא״ו-הֵ״א);
possessing no apparent connection to masculine and feminine tiers (Vav-Hei);
וְ"זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם" כְּתִיב (שְׁמוֹת ג, טו; פְּסָחִים נ.),
and "This is My Name forever (le'olam)" is written deficiently as le'alem (to conceal),
דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶעְלָם אֵיךְ כּוּלּוֹ חַד בֶּאֱמֶת,
for in this world it is concealed how everything is in absolute truth one,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד: "ה' אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד" (זְכַרְיָה יד, ט),
as will be manifested in the ultimate future: "Hashem will be one and His Name one" (Zechariah 14:9),
דְּיִהְיֶה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּבוּקִים לְגַמְרֵי בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית הָרָמוּז בְּקוּצוֹ שֶׁל יוֹ״ד
wherein the Congregation of Israel and the final Hei will be completely cleaved to the depth of the Primordial Root hinted at in the thorn of the Yud

(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, סה עַמּוּד ב)1123 Zohar 3:65b — And the secret of the matter is this: "Ehyeh" — this is the whole comprised together. For when the paths are concealed and undifferentiated and are gathered in one place, then it is called "Ehyeh" — all comprised, hidden and unrevealed. After the beginning issued from it, and that river conceived so as to draw all forth, then it is called "Asher Ehyeh" — that is to say, I shall be ready to draw forth and to bring all to birth. וְכוּלּוֹ חַד.
(Zohar Part III, 65b) and all will be unified as one.
וּבַאֲדָר הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַגָּעָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן;
And in Adar resides the capacity to reach this via the king as harsh as Haman;
וּלְפִיכָךְ טָעָה הָמָן וְחָשַׁב שֶׁיַּצְלִיחַ אָז,
and on this account Haman erred, presuming he would triumph then,
כִּי רָאָה שֶׁגְּזֵירָתוֹ מַצְלַחַת בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה.
for he observed that his decree appeared to succeed during this month.
וְהַהַצְלָחָה הָאֲמִיתִּית מִגְּזֵירָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר פּוֹעֶלֶת בְּקֶרֶב לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּשׁוּבָה
Yet the genuine success of a decree occurs when it evokes heartfelt repentance within the hearts of Israel
וּמְבִיאָה יְשׁוּעָה וּבִיטּוּל הַגְּזֵירָה,
bringing forth deliverance and the ultimate annulment of the decree;

דְּזֶה טַעַם (כְּתוּבּוֹת ג:)1124 Ketubot 3b — Then let them abolish the ordinance altogether! A decree of persecution is bound to be annulled, and we do not abolish a rabbinic ordinance on account of a decree of persecution. Rashi (s.v. "then let them abolish it"): "Then let them abolish it" — since there are times when there is danger. Tosafos (s.v. "we do not abolish a rabbinic ordinance on account of a decree of persecution"): When the Talmud asked earlier "let them abolish it," it did not answer in this way, because there the question was that they abolish it and fix another day: since the persecutors intend only to make them transgress their religion, once another day were fixed they would not trouble themselves, and the rabbinic ordinance would not be uprooted, one fixed day still remaining. Here, however, the question is that they abolish it and fix no day at all — for if any day were fixed he would come and violate her on it — and to this the answer is that we do not abolish a rabbinic ordinance before a decree of persecution so as to leave no fixed day whatever.: "גְּזֵירָה עֲבִידָא דְּבָטְלָה",
for this is the rationale of (Ketubot 3b): "A decree is made to be nullified",
שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁוֹ: דַּעֲשׂוּיָה לְכָךְ כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּבַטְּלוּהָ.
of which I heard the exposition: it is fashioned specifically so that they will bring about its annulment.
וְהוּא חָשַׁב דְּמִיתַת מֹשֶׁה הוּא הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַדַּעַת לְגַמְרֵי,
And Haman presumed that Moses' death signified the total departure of Da'at,
וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ בְּשֵׁינָה גְּמוּרָה וּכְשִׁכְרוּת הָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹרְרָם.
such that Israel remained in absolute slumber and like the stupor of the nations whom it is impossible to rouse.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֲרֵי בּוֹ נוֹלַד גַּם כֵּן,
Yet in truth, behold, in this month he was born as well;
וְאִם כֵּן אַדְּרַבָּה, חֹדֶשׁ זֶה מוּכָן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת;
and if so, on the contrary, this month is primed for the revelation of Da'at;
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם מִיתָתוֹ לֹא הָיָה הִסְתַּלְּקוּת,
and therefore his death was likewise not an ultimate departure,
דְּאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁהַחֹדֶשׁ הַמּוּכָן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת יִהְיֶה מוּכָן לְהֶפְכּוֹ גַּם כֵּן?
for how could a month designated for revelation simultaneously be designated for its opposite?
וְעַל כֵּן דְּגַם הִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ אֵינוֹ הִסְתַּלְּקוּת גָּמוּר, רַק מִצַּד מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי בָּשָׂר;
Therefore, even his passing is not a total departure, appearing so only to eyes of flesh;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אַדְּרַבָּה, גַּם זֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת,
yet in truth, on the contrary, this too is a revelation,
וְעוֹד יוֹתֵר, שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת נִגְלֶה בְּפוֹעַל גָּמוּר עוֹד,
and even more so: it no longer requires overt manifestation in external actuality,
דְּדַי גַּם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּהֶעְלֵם
for it is sufficient even that it remain in concealment,
כִּי כְּבָר נֶחְקַק דָּבָר זֶה בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
since this truth has already been engraved within the depths of the hearts of the children of Israel;
כְּטַעַם "שְׁבִיק חַיִּין לְכָל חַי",
mirroring the expression "he left life unto all the living",
שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ חַיּוּתוֹ לָהֶם, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם.
in that he bequeaths his vitality unto them, except that within them it abides in concealment.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יוֹתֵר,
Nevertheless, it expands even more broadly,
וְשֶׁאַף בְּהֶעְלֵם יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת הַגָּמוּר.
and even within concealment there remains absolute Da'at.
וְזֶה טַעַם "חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע" (מְגִילָּה ז:) וְהֶעְדֵּר הַדַּעַת,
And this explains the obligation "to become intoxicated until he knows not" (Megillah 7b) and the suspension of conscious awareness;
וְנִקְרָא "בִּיסּוּם" וְלֹא "שִׁכְרוּת",
and it is specifically termed bisum (sweetening) rather than shikhrot (drunkenness),
דְּעַל יְדֵי שִׁכְרוּת: "כָּל שֻׁלְחָנוֹת מָלְאוּ קִיא צֹאָה" (יְשַׁעְיָה כח, ח), כְּהִתְעוֹת שִׁכּוֹר בְּקִיאוֹ;
for through base drunkenness: "all tables are filled with vomit and filth" (Isaiah 28:8), like the staggering of a drunkard in his vomit;
אֲבָל בִּיסּוּם אַדְּרַבָּה, מַשְׁמָעוֹ רֵיחוֹ טוֹב וּבֹשֶׂם,
whereas bisum, on the contrary, connotes pleasant fragrance and spice,

וְ"חַמְרָא וְרֵיחָנֵי פַּקְחִין" (יוֹמָא עו:)1125 Yoma 76b — Rava raised a contradiction: it is written "yeshammach" but we read "yesammach" — if he is worthy, [wine] gladdens him; if he is not worthy, it desolates him. And this is what Rava said: Wine and fragrances made me wise. Rashi: "It is written yeshammach": with a shin, a term of desolation, while we read "[wine] yesammach," a term of gladness. "Made me wise": they opened my eyes — made me clever. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 70a): Wine is a hidden thing, and whatever is hidden has two aspects: insofar as it is hidden it shares the rank of the intellect, which is hidden, and insofar as it is not revealed it is absent and lacks existence. So if he is worthy, that is, he possesses intellect, wine gladdens him and gives him existence, for gladness is complete existence, when one's soul is whole; and if he is not worthy, having no intellect, it desolates him, giving him absence through its second aspect. And this is what Rava said, "Wine and fragrances made me wise": wine is fit to open a man's mind because it issues from a hidden place, which is the rank of the intellect. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaPerishus 1): Havdalah belongs over wine specifically, for every distinction separates two things that appear alike, and that is the work of knowledge and intellect — which is why havdalah was set in the blessing "Who graciously grants knowledge." And the Sages said, "Wine and fragrances make one wise"; therefore havdalah is principally made over wine, which is suited to distinguishing. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 2): Of a little [wine], as much as one needs, it says, "Wine and fragrances made me wise," for it adds wisdom; but much removes wisdom and uproots it entirely, and perfection in wisdom is not to become drunk — as "Who is wise? One who knows his place" and level, and does not climb to be wiser than his place. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 9): Wine confounds the mind — ten tribes were exiled on its account — yet the four cups of Passover night [show] that with Israel it is the reverse: "Wine and fragrances made me wise," one drinks it and it is good for him. Through it they attain the lower wisdom, for they drink not at all out of desire but only to gladden the soul for the service of the Blessed One, and thereby speech is purified in the telling of the Exodus. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Ki Sisa): [The calf-worshippers' "bowing down" is the reverse of the section on spices,] for spices open a person's heart, and as he smells them his intellect rises upward with the scent, as the Gemara says, "Wine and fragrances made me wise"; bowing where it is not the Blessed One's will is the reverse, for one's stature and intellect are bent and go down.,
and "wine and fragrances sharpen the mind" (Yoma 76b),
לֹא כְּשִׁכּוֹר שֶׁהוּא כְּשׁוֹטֶה לְכָל דָּבָר.
unlike a base drunkard who is deemed a fool in all matters.
וְאַף דְּ"לָא יָדַע בֵּין וְכוּלֵי",
And even though he "knows not between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordechai,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַדַּעַת הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם;
nevertheless Da'at remains present within concealment;
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הָרִיחוּק שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִנִּיסָן עַד אֲדָר נִדְמֶה לְרִיחוּק גָּמוּר,
and corresponding to the extremity of the distance from Nisan to Adar it appears as complete alienation,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה חוֹזֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית
yet in truth, on the contrary, through this it returns to the profound Primordial Root,
בְּסוֹד "נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן" (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א, ז).
in the mystical secret of "their end is wedged in their beginning" (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7).
וְעַל כֵּן אָז הוּא רִיבּוּי הַשִּׂמְחָה,
Therefore at that time occurs the amplification of joy,
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהַשִּׂמְחָה הַבָּאָה מִבֵּן שֶׁהָיָה בְּרִיחוּק הַרְבֵּה מֵאָבִיו וְנִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו –
as is known: the joy felt over a son who was at a great distance from his father and was reunited with him—
שֶׁשִּׂמְחָתוֹ עֲצוּמָה הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מֵהַבֵּן שֶׁהוּא עִמּוֹ תָּמִיד.
his joy is vastly greater than that over the son who remains with him continually.
וְזֶהוּ הָרִיבּוּי שִׂמְחָה דַּאֲדָר שֶׁהוּא מִיָּד שֶׁנִּכְנַס,
And this is the increase of joy of Adar which commences immediately as it enters,
כִּי כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים הוּא שֶׁבְּאֵיזֶה זְמַן נִקְבַּע אוֹתוֹ אוֹר וּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁהֵאִיר בּוֹ מֵאָז,
for the sacred character of holy seasons means that in that appointed time is fixed the specific illumination and holiness that shone then,
דְּנִשְׁאַר הָרְשִׁימָה שֶׁבּוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם.
such that its latent imprint remains established and enduring throughout all history.
כְּמוֹ בַּנֶּפֶשׁ: בְּהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַצַּדִּיק, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹרוֹ נִשְׁאַר עוֹד בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יוֹתֵר;
Just as within the soul: upon the departure of a tzaddik, his illumination nonetheless persists in even broader expansion;
כֵּן בַּשָּׁנָה וּבַזְּמַן, כָּל יוֹם שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בּוֹ פַּעַם אַחַת,
so too within the yearly cycle of time: any day wherein a miracle was once established,
אַף שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֵּק, אוֹרוֹ נִשְׁאַר בְּהֶעְלֵם עוֹד בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יוֹתֵר בְּכָל נַפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם.
even though the manifest event passed, its light remains in concealment with even greater expansion across all Jewish souls.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר דְּפוּרִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה שֶׁגַּם בְּהֶעְלֵם יֵשׁ אוֹר.
And the disclosure of the light of Purim is this very revelation: that even within concealment light endures.

items.h:
Seif 5 — Purim Reveals the Hidden Light of Every Yom Tov
Purim makes visible the concealed light that remains within every festival after its original miracle has passed.

p: וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (מְגִילָּה טז:)1126 Megillah 16b — On "The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor," Rav Yehuda expounded: "Gladness" — this is the festival, and so it says: "And you shall rejoice on your festival." Rashi: "This is the festival" — they took the festivals upon themselves once more. Maharsha: Haman had decreed in particular against those commandments that serve as a sign and a testimony for Israel, and when his decree was annulled they returned to their former state. "Gladness" is the festival, which is a day of rest, and accordingly it is said of them that they turned from mourning to a festival. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Introduction): "Gladness" is the festival, as it is written, "Therefore the Jews of the villages, who dwell in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month of Adar gladness and feasting and a festival day": although they did not take it upon themselves to make it a festival day, the gladness of a festival day is nonetheless there. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 4): "The Jews had light" — this is the illumination of the yesod of Abba, which is called Torah; and "gladness — this is the festival," the sanctity of the times, which Israel sanctify: by virtue of Purim, the clothing of His wisdom in the Written Torah within the Congregation of Israel, the festival that Israel sanctify becomes holy like the Sabbath, which is fixed and established and sanctified by the Blessed One, for all is one; and from the sanctity of Purim comes an addition of joy to every festival. "And joy — this is circumcision": the sanctity of the yesod, in guarding the covenant. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 7): Israel is sanctified with three sanctities, rooted in "You shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy": their own, through the awakening from below; the sanctity rooted in the Patriarchs; and the sanctity from above, from the Blessed One; and after the miracle all three were revealed. "Light — this is Torah" and "gladness — this is the festival" revealed Israel's own sanctity, for they engaged in Torah and mitzvos and "accepted it anew in the days of Ahasuerus," and the festival is the sanctity of time, which Israel sanctify — for although they did not accept Purim as a festival with a prohibition of labor, its joy and mitzvos fall at a time fixed by the month, which Israel sanctify. "Joy — this is circumcision" revealed the sanctity that comes from the Patriarchs, and "honor — these are the tefillin" revealed Israel's sanctity from the side of the Blessed One, for they are bound at the root. Sod Yesharim (Purim 1): On this day the Blessed One revealed openly to Israel the light of all the things that Amalek denies. "Gladness — this is the festival": the festivals are called "the face of the Lord," for just as a face attests to all the limbs of the body, so at the time of a festival one can recognize all that the Blessed One seeks of a person, since in those days there is a straight path for every individual soul that seeks the Lord to reach what is sought of it; and Amalek denies this, saying that in this world there can be no straight path to recognizing the light of His will.: "'וְשִׂמְחָה' – זֶה יוֹם טוֹב",
And this is the inner meaning of what they expounded (Megillah 16b): "'And gladness'—this refers to Yom Tov",
דְּעַל יְדֵי פּוּרִים זָכוּ לִקְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַיָּמִים טוֹבִים בִּשְׁלֵימוּת יוֹתֵר וְלִשְׂמוֹחַ בָּהֶם יוֹתֵר.
for through Purim they merited the holiness of all the festivals in greater perfection and to rejoice in them more profoundly.
כִּי עִנְיַן כָּל הַיּוֹם טוֹב הוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם בְּהֶעְלֵם הָאוֹר שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ כְּבָר בְּגִילּוּי,
For the nature of every Yom Tov is that on that day there resides in concealment the light that was once revealed,
וּפוּרִים הוּא גִּילּוּי דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ אוֹר בְּהֶעְלֵם אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְגוּלֶּה;
and Purim is the overt revelation of this reality: that light exists within concealment even when it is not manifest;
וְעַל כֵּן הִתְחִיל הַרְגָּשַׁת שִׂמְחַת פּוּרִים מִתְּחִלַּת הַחֹדֶשׁ.
and therefore the sensation of Purim's joy commences from the start of the month.
כִּי חֹדֶשׁ זֶה הוּא תַּכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם,
For this month represents the climax of concealment,
וּבוֹ וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִצְמָח תַּכְלִית הַגִּילּוּי,
and within it and out of it sprouts the ultimate revelation,
דִּבְכָל שָׁנָה נִיסָן שֶׁאַחַר אֲדָר הוּא הַגִּילּוּי הַנִּצְמָח מִן הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה עוֹד יוֹתֵר;
for every year the month of Nisan following Adar is the revelation sprouting from concealment, shining forth even more;
וְגִילּוּי דַּאֲדָר הוּא שֶׁגַּם הַהֶעְלֵם אֵינוֹ הֶעְלֵם.
and the revelation of Adar demonstrates that even concealment is not true concealment.
וְעִיקַּר הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה הוּא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר וּבַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר, דְּאָז קַיְימָא סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא;
And the core of this revelation unfolds on the fourteenth and fifteenth, when the moon stands in full perfection;
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי אוֹר זֶה דְּנִתְגַּלָּה דְּאֵין הֶעְלֵם,
yet by virtue of this light which reveals that there is no concealment,
אִם כֵּן גַּם מִיָּד שֶׁנִּכְנַס הַחֹדֶשׁ בִּהְיוֹתוֹ בְּאִתְכַּסְיָא – גַּם כֵּן מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה,
it follows that immediately when the month enters while the moon is veiled in obscurity, we likewise increase in joy,
וְהוֹלְכִין עַד יוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁהוּא תּוֹקֶף הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַגָּמוּר לַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁבַּהֶעְלֵם.
and proceed onward until the fourteenth day, which is the height of joy and the complete revelation within the deepest concealment.
וְלַמּוּקָּפִים הוּא בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר, דְּאָז הוּא עִיקַּר אַשְׁלָמוּתָא דְּסִיהֲרָא,
And for walled cities it occurs on the fifteenth, for then is the essential fullness of the moon,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּקְבַּע פֶּסַח וְסֻכּוֹת בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר,
just as Passover and Sukkot were established on the fifteenth,
דְּכָל קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת תַּלְיָא בְּסִיהֲרָא,
since the entire sanctity of the festivals depends upon the moon,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים בְּקִידּוּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ וְעַל כֵּן עִיקָּרָם בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא.
and Israel sanctifies the seasons through sanctifying the new moon, hence their main observance is at its fullness.
וּפוּרִים גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים,
And Purim is likewise numbered among the sanctities of the sacred seasons,
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם,
except that it represents the sanctity of Israel stemming from concealment,
דְּהוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּ"גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יב),
which is the revelation that "even all our deeds You have wrought for us" (Isaiah 26:12),
וְשֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל נִיתָּקִים לְעוֹלָם וַאֲפִילּוּ רֶגַע אֶחָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that Israel are never severed, even for a single moment, from Hashem, blessed be He,
וְגַם קְדוּשָׁתָם קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
and their holiness is likewise fixed and eternal.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּפוּרִים לְשׁוֹן "וְנוֹחַ וְגוֹמֵר" (אֶסְתֵּר ט, כב),
Therefore Scripture used regarding Purim the language of "and rest, etc." (Esther 9:22),
שֶׁקְּרָאוּהוּ מְנוּחָה וְנַיָּיחָא כְּמוֹ שַׁבָּת;
terming it rest and serenity akin to Shabbat;
כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּפְעוּלָה אֵין לוֹ נַיָּיחָא,
for as long as man requires exertion and outward action he has no true serenity,
וְעַל כֵּן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מָלֵא טִרְדָּא,
and therefore this world is full of distraction and toil,
וּכְשֶׁמֵּת "נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ",
and when a person passes away, "his soul rested",
וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת וּמְנוּחָה,
and the World to Come is a day that is entirely Shabbat and rest,

דְּ"צַדִּיקִים יוֹשְׁבִים וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת יז1127 Berakhot 17a — A favourite saying of Rav was: The World to Come is not like this world. In the World to Come there is no eating, no drinking, no procreation, no commerce, no envy, no hatred and no rivalry; rather the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads and delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence. Rashi: "And they ate and drank" — they were sated by the radiance of the Divine Presence as though they had eaten and drunk. Maharsha: He derives the point from the redundancy and the change of wording in the verse: Scripture had already said "and they saw the God of Israel," and then says again "and they beheld God" — and "beholding" generally denotes an intellectual vision, a prophecy. They beheld and took delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence as though they had eaten and drunk; for at the giving of the Torah they were in the likeness of the World to Come, their crowns upon their heads, as it is said [in Shabbat 88a] that every Israelite received two crowns, and they were removed from bodily things, as it is said of Moses that he did not eat for forty days. Maharal (Derech Chaim on Avot 3:16): The meaning is that in the World to Come a man needs no completing, unlike this world, in which a man must receive his completion; there he will be complete on a higher level. He will therefore need no eating and drinking to complete himself, nor procreation — for offspring are a man's completion — nor commerce, by which a man supplies what he lacks; and there will be no envy or hatred, since these are themselves a defect. And "the righteous sit": the World to Come is not a thing of motion as this world is, and sitting signifies that a man is already complete in actuality and no longer moving toward his completion. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 4): Seeking to be a son of the World to Come purely for one's own sake is no different from seeking a reward in this world; but the essence of the World to Come, that "they delight in the radiance of the Shechinah," is not self-benefit. One can merit this even in this world — the "one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world" that is better than all the World to Come — when the reward of a mitzvah brings one to repentance, love and cleaving; for such a reward one may hope, and serving for it is wholly for its own sake, out of love. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 7): Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come, and the World to Come is the absence of the action of "today to do them" — only "the righteous [sit] … and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah" — and Shabbat holds a semblance of this, which is why, though there is no reward for mitzvos in this world, Shabbat is called "a good gift." In this world one employs the powers of action, whereas the World to Come is the heart alone. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 11): From within this world, which is likened to night, they will merit the light of the World to Come, which is wholly day with no darkness or evil — the light of the world of Atzilus, the light of the seven days of creation hidden away for the righteous — when they sit "with their crowns on their heads," that is, their attachment to their root in the Blessed One, "and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah," that is, the upper Shechinah. This is the first heh of the Name, alluding to the understanding in the heart, the secret of the World to Come, where the attachment of the hearts of Israel to their source is revealed. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 1): With the creation of man "tohu and bohu" were set aside, for a person can raise his actions without limit and reach a lofty place, as stated: "In the World to Come there is no eating and no drinking … rather the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah." Through the act of the mitzvah of shofar one arouses the "great shofar," which shows that Israel raise all their actions up to the "upper sun," to the place where the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Shechinah, and through the shofar one can reach with one's actions and service to the light of the Infinite..),
wherein "the righteous sit crowned, etc." (Berakhot 17a),

דְּ"הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם וּמָחָר לְקַבֵּל שְׂכָרָם" (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.)1128 Avodah Zarah 3a — R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by "which I command you this day"? This day to do them, and not tomorrow to do them; this day to do them, and not this day to receive the reward. Rashi: "This day to do them" — in this world; "and not tomorrow" — because one cannot perform them in the World to Come. Tosafos (s.v. "this day to do them, and not tomorrow to do them"): Tosafot asks why the Sages objected to the men of Jericho, who ran the words of the Shema together and did not pause at "this day, upon your heart," so that it sounded like "this day upon your heart and not tomorrow upon your heart" (Pesachim 57a) — what harm is there in that, seeing that it is true, as is implied here? He answers that there one might err and take "this day" and "tomorrow" quite literally, whereas here "this day to do them" stands in a verse that speaks of the payment of reward — "and repays them that hate Him" [Deuteronomy 7:10] — and the reward of the righteous is paid in the World to Come. Maharsha: The objection could have been raised from the Holy One's own words just above, "Fools of the world! One who took trouble on the eve of the Sabbath..." — except that even so He deals with them beyond the letter of the law and tells them to make a sukkah. It may therefore be that the objection is drawn not from "this day to do them and not tomorrow to do them" but from "this day to do them, but not this day to receive the reward": since the nations have already received the reward of their commandments in this world — "and repays them that hate Him to their face" — they receive nothing further in the World to Come, for otherwise justice would be impaired, Israel receiving only the reward of the World to Come. And by the commandment of sukkah He hinted to them that they should have kept the commandments in this world, which is like a sukkah, a temporary dwelling. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 3a): The Gemara’s objection from this teaching [to the nations’ being offered the sukkah in the time to come] is the very same difficulty as above — "one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, from where will he eat on Shabbat?" — only that here it is written in the Torah, and since it is written in the Torah, it cannot possibly be otherwise at all. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 1): Tefillin, the recognition of God's name upon a person in actual deed, belong only to the weekdays and not to Shabbat and festivals, when the recognition in the heart must be clear without any deed, like the world to come, a day [of clear intellectual illumination] that is entirely Shabbat, a cessation from deeds, as it says, "today to do them and not tomorrow." Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 25): Shabbat is [the day on which God Himself is one's light, needing no fire of fear]; nevertheless one must toil to cook the food on the eve of Shabbat, for "one who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, what will he eat on Shabbat?" and "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward": this light does not come to a person by itself. So too the Shabbat lamp must be lit from the eve of Shabbat, for on Shabbat there is no longer time to arouse fear, the day being entirely love and cleaving to God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): This world is the world of toil, and "one who toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat" refers to the world to come, the day that is entirely Shabbat, where there is no doing even of Torah and mitzvot, as they said, "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward"; and Shabbat is a semblance of the world to come, the time of the Blessed One's rest. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Savo 16): The verse ["all these blessings will come upon you"] certainly does not speak of the reward and punishment for the mitzvot, which are not in this world, for it is only "today to do them and tomorrow to receive their reward"; it speaks of the blessings of this world, that God will give every assistance so that one can serve Him all the more. And if, Heaven forbid, they do not listen, the reverse too will serve as an assistance, through which they will take it to heart to return and mend their ways. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, from the Yerushalmi 14): The world to come is likened to day because there will be no departure there from the [fixed] order, such departure coming about through changes in deeds, as they said, "today to do them and not tomorrow to do them." But in this world, the day of action, where choice is in man's hand, the order changes through deeds: toward evil, as troubles and exile, through evil deeds, and toward good through cleaving to the Blessed One.,
for "today is for performing them, and tomorrow is for receiving their reward" (Avodah Zarah 3a),
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא;
and Shabbat is a semblance of the World to Come;
וּפוּרִים גַּם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
and on Purim likewise there is no need for any dependent human exertion,
דְּגַם כְּשֶׁמְּבוּסָּם וְעַד דְּלָא יָדַע – דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for even when a person is sweetened and "until he knows not," he remains cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי יֵשׁ לָהֶם נַיָּיחָא מֵאוֹיְבֵיהֶם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע עַל יְדֵי מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק.
because they possess tranquility from their adversaries—the evil inclination—through the obliteration of Amalek.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ דוֹמֶה,
Nevertheless it is not identical to Shabbat,
דְּמִצְוָתוֹ הַשְּׁבִיתָה,
for the commandment of Shabbat is cessation from labor,
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר קְדוּשָׁתוֹ הַקְּבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, עַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ נִתְלֶה בְּסִיהֲרָא כְּלָל.
and this constitutes its inherently fixed and enduring holiness, which is why it does not depend on the moon at all.
אֲבָל פּוּרִים אַדְּרַבָּה, עִיקָּרוֹ נִתְלֶה בְּסִיהֲרָא,
However regarding Purim, on the contrary, its essence is linked to the moon,
רַק שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה מִסִּיהֲרָא שִׁמְשָׁא,
except that it transforms the moon into the sun,
שֶׁגַּם הִיא אוֹר קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים וְאֵין בָּהּ הֶעְלֵם.
such that it too becomes an established, enduring light bearing no concealment.

וְיָדוּעַ דְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת מִתְכַּסְיָא סִיהֲרָא לְגַמְרֵי (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ:)1129 Rosh Hashanah 20b — R. Zeira said in the name of Rav Nachman: For twenty-four hours the moon is hidden. For us, six hours of the old moon and eighteen of the new; for them, six of the new and eighteen of the old. Rashi: For six hours before its renewal and six hours after, the moon is hidden from everyone because of its smallness, and for twelve hours before and after that it is seen from one side only: before its renewal it always stands in the south-eastern corner, visible to those in the east, and after it in the south-western corner, visible to those in the west (so he found in the Yesod of R. Saadia). Hence Babylonia, lying in the east, sees the old moon until six hours before the renewal but does not see the new one until eighteen hours after it, while the Land of Israel, in the west, sees the new moon six hours after the renewal but loses sight of the old one eighteen hours before it. Maharal (Be'er HaGolah, Sixth Well): The Sages' six hours is the earliest that the moon can be seen anywhere in the world at all — by one with the wisdom to discern it, in air as clear as can be, from a high city at the far end of the west — a measure received in the secret of intercalation from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, through Moses, whereas the astronomers reckon only from when it is plainly visible to all. Nor does "for us… for them" mean Babylonia and the Land of Israel, which are less than two hours apart, but the people of the east and those at the very end of the west. And since a sighting after six hours is possible in some way, witnesses who report it are not refuted. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 3): This is why the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "Bring atonement for Me for having diminished the moon": as it were, the Blessed One says that everything came from Him, for He created the evil inclination so that there would be the diminishing of the moon — the moon being the aspect of the Congregation of Israel — such that "for twenty-four hours the moon is hidden." That is, "first darkness," and afterward a small light begins to glimmer, growing brighter each time.,
And it is known that for twenty-four hours the moon is completely hidden (Rosh Hashanah 20b),
וְיוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר הוּא אֶמְצַע הַחֹדֶשׁ מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה יוֹם, שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת, וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת תִּשְׁעִים וּשְׁלוֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים (כ״ט י״ב תשצ״ג);
and the fifteenth day is the midpoint of the month calculated from 29 days, 12 hours, and 793 parts;
וְאִם נְנַכֶּה שְׁעוֹת הַהֶעְלֵם דְּמִכַּסְיָא – כַּאֲשֶׁר אֵין שָׁם הֶעְלֵם, יוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר הוּא הָאֶמְצַע.
and if we deduct the hours of concealment when the moon is hidden—such that when there is no concealment recognized—the fourteenth day is the true midpoint.

וְעַל כֵּן הַיְּהוּדִים הַפְּרָזִים, שֶׁהֵם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָא מִיגַנְיָין מֵעֲמָלֵק (מְגִילָּה ה:)1130 Megillah 5b — With regard to the sale of houses in walled cities he had no doubt. Where he was in doubt was with regard to the reading of the Megillah: what are the unwalled towns and what are the walled cities of which Scripture speaks concerning the reading of the Megillah? Is it because these are exposed and those are not exposed — and this city too is exposed; or perhaps because these are sheltered and those are not sheltered — and this city too is sheltered? On that account he was in doubt. Rashi: “Where he was in doubt was with regard to the reading of the Megillah” — for there no wall is specified; Scripture writes only of unwalled towns and of those that are not unwalled, and he was in doubt whether “unwalled” denotes a place that lies exposed or denotes a city that is easily taken.,
Therefore the Jews of the open towns, who are the majority of Israel and not walled off from Amalek (Megillah 5b),
מַקְדִּימִין לְעִנְיַן הַנַּיָּיחָא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁכְּבָר יֵשׁ לָהֶם מְנוּחָה,
anticipate the celebration of rest on the fourteenth, having already attained tranquility,
כִּי "יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ" (קֹהֶלֶת ב, יג),
for "light has preeminence over darkness" (Ecclesiastes 2:13),
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחֹשֶׁךְ כֵּן תּוֹקֶף הָאוֹר.
and in proportion to the intensity of darkness, such is the strength of light.
וְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר שֶׁבַּהֶעְלֵם, כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל רִיחוּקָם, מִתְגַּדֵּל הַשִּׂמְחָה וּמִתְרַבֶּה בְּיוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁאֵין הֶעְלֵם,
And with the disclosure of the concealed light, commensurate with their felt distance, joy magnifies and increases immensely until concealment ceases to exist,
וְעַל כֵּן אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר הוּא הָאֶמְצַע וְאַשְׁלָמוּתָא דְּסִיהֲרָא.
and therefore the fourteenth is the midpoint and full illumination of the moon.
אֲבָל הַמּוּקָּפִים, דִּמְגַנְיָין וּמוּגְדָּרִים מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע דַּעֲמָלֵק,
However the dwellers of walled cities, who are protected and fenced off from the root of Amalek's evil,
וְאֵינָם כְּ"עִיר פְּרוּצָה אֵין חוֹמָה אֲשֶׁר אֵין מַעְצוֹר לְרוּחוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, כח),
and are not like "a breached city without a wall, where a man has no control over his spirit" (Proverbs 25:28),
הֵם צְרִיכִים מִלְחָמָה יְתֵירָה נֶגְדּוֹ,
they require an even greater spiritual battle against him,
כִּי "כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ" (סֻכָּה נב:),
for "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he" (Sukkah 52b),
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְנַצְּחוֹ,
because he possesses the strength to vanquish it,

דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְנַסֶּה אֶלָּא קַנְקַנִּים שְׁלֵימִים (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לב)1131 Bereshit Rabbah 32:3 — It is written: "The Lord tests the righteous, but the wicked and the lover of violence His soul hates." R. Yonatan said: This potter does not test flawed jars, for he cannot strike them even once without breaking them; and which does he test? Sound jars, for even if he strikes them many times they do not break. So too the Holy One, blessed be He, does not test the wicked but the righteous, as it is said: "The Lord tests the righteous," and it is written: "God tested Abraham." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 28): Since the Blessed One tested [David] with desire, and "the Holy One, blessed be He, tests only sound jars," as stated in Bereishis Rabbah 32, it follows that he was whole in this matter to the utmost perfection, and his refinement came through this very test. For although he did not succeed in outward appearance, and his enemies on that account considered him an adulterer and a man of lust, in truth he was proven by it, for the Sages said that he did not sin..
for the Holy One, blessed be He, tests only intact vessels (Bereishit Rabbah 32).
וּלְפִי שֶׁהֵם אֵין לָהֶם לֵב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַּת נֶפֶשׁ כָּל כָּךְ,
And because they do not possess a heart that experiences such bitter anguish of the soul,
עַל כֵּן אֵין מְמַהֲרִים כָּל כָּךְ בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַשִּׂמְחָה עַד אַחַר נִיצּוּחָם כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתָם.
therefore they do not hasten so quickly to sense joy until after their triumph commensurate with their spiritual level.
וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם הֶעְלֵם גָּמוּר מִקּוֹדֶם,
And because they lacked total concealment beforehand,
גַּם כֵּן לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר אֶצְלָם אוֹר זֶה שֶׁאֵין הֶעְלֵם וְנִשְׁאַר חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר אֶמְצָעִי;
this light demonstrating that there is no concealment was likewise not clarified to them, leaving the fifteenth as their midpoint;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לָהֶם מַעֲלָה יְתֵירָה בַּמֶּה שֶׁהֵם מָחוּ עֲמָלֵק בְּיוֹתֵר.
nevertheless they possess a superior virtue in that they blotted out Amalek even more profoundly.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם מִסְפַּר חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר (ט״ו) הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם יוֹ״ד-קֵ״א,
And everywhere the number fifteen corresponds to the holy Name Yud-Hei,
שֶׁהֵם הָרֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין;
which are the two companions that never part;
וְהֵ״א – דָּלֶ״ת הֲוַות, רַק בָּתַר דְּקַבִּילַת עוּבְרָהּ,
and the Hei was originally a Dalet, only after receiving the embryonic seed,

הוּא הַנְּקוּדָּה שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ, נַעֲשָׂה הֵ״א (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קעח עַמּוּד ב)1132 Zohar 2:178b — From the yod issue male and female, vav and dalet; in this place the vav is male and the dalet female. The heh is female. The heh was at first a dalet, and once she conceived by the vav within her she brought forth a vav, and a yod is seen in her form, comprising yod, heh and vav. Having brought forth the yod, which is male and female, she then settled and covers the Mother. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): [Israel] are called by their essential name after Judah, whose name comprises the entire name of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the addition of the letter dalet, which alludes to poverty (dalus); and "the heh was a dalet, and only after she conceived did she become a heh." Scripture's "poor" and "afflicted" refer to Israel, for their whole virtue is that they recognize their lack and have no strength and nothing at all except what the Blessed One gives, bestows and helps; and then the Blessed One bestows upon them, and the dalet becomes a heh, which is the completeness of the Congregation of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 257): The Zohar calls kuf and resh "letters of falsehood"; this is explained by Zohar II 178b, that the heh was a dalet and became a heh only after she conceived, and by Pri Etz Chaim, that the kuf likewise was a resh. Dalet (from dalus, "poverty") and resh are alike in denoting poverty and lack — a thing that "has nothing of its own" and seeks completion — except that the one is formed of straight lines and the other of crookedness: the one longs only for the flow of the Blessed One's straight line, and the fetus she conceives is likewise of the straight line, while the other is in crookedness..
which is the inner point placed within it, did it become a Hei (Zohar Part II, 178b).
וְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר (י״ד) הוּא חִיבּוּרָם קוֹדֶם קַבָּלַת הָעוּבָּר,
And fourteen represents their union prior to receiving the embryo;
הַיְינוּ הוֹלָדָתָן זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה שֶׁהוּא יְצִיאַת הַדָּבָר לַפּוֹעַל בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר.
namely their bringing forth male and female, which is the actualization of the matter into full fruition on the fifteenth.
וְעַל כֵּן כּוּלָּם צְרִיכִים לִהְיוֹת עוֹשִׂים שְׁנֵי הַיָּמִים,
Therefore all must observe both days,
רַק אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר עִיקָּר, וּבוֹ עוֹשִׂין מִצְווֹת הַיּוֹם
only that for these the fourteenth is primary, and on it they fulfill the mitzvot of the day,
שֶׁהֵם אַרְבַּע נֶגֶד אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם:
which are four, corresponding to the four letters of the Tetragrammaton:
מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים נֶגֶד שְׁנֵי הַהֵהִי״ן
mishloach manot and matanot la'evyonim correspond to the two letters Hei,
שֶׁרוֹמְזִים לַמְּקַבְּלִים הַמְּקַבְּלִים שֶׁפַע מֵהַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ:
which allude to the recipients who receive divine influx from the benefactor:
הֵ״א רִאשׁוֹן הוּא רֵעֵהוּ מִתְּרֵין רֵעִין,
the first Hei is "his friend" (re'ehu) from the two close companions,
וְהֵ״א שֵׁנִי הִיא דַּלָּה וְאֶבְיוֹנָה;
and the second Hei is impoverished and destitute;

וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "דַּל" וְ"אֶבְיוֹן" בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר כַּיָּדוּעַ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא)1133 Bereshit Rabbah 71:1 — "For the Lord listens to the needy and does not despise His prisoners." R. Binyamin ben Levi said: the beginning of this verse does not match its end, nor its end its beginning. Rather: "For the Lord listens to the needy" — these are Israel, for R. Yochanan said, wherever "poor," "afflicted," or "needy" is said, Scripture speaks of Israel. "And does not despise His prisoners" — these are the barren women, who are shut up within their houses and humiliated; and once the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers them with children, they stand upright. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 14): Israel count by the moon, which "has nothing of its own"; so too, "wherever 'crushed,' 'poor,' and the like is said, Scripture speaks of Israel" (Bereishis Rabbah 71), for they recognize their poverty, that they have nothing at all of their own. Even when one increases in service and effort, all that he adds in service and in recognition of His Godliness he adds in recognition of his own lowliness and smallness..
and in every biblical context "the poor" and "the needy" refer to the Congregation of Israel, as is known (Bereishit Rabbah 71).
וְהַמְּגִילָּה הוּא הָרָשׁוּם בִּכְתָב אֱמֶת,
And the Megillah is that which is inscribed in the writing of truth,
הִיא מִדַּת אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב דְּהִיא סוֹד סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה,
which is the attribute of "truth to Jacob" (Tiferet), being the mystical secret of the Torah scroll,

וְכֵן מְגִילָּה נִקְרֵאת "סֵפֶר" כַּאֲמִיתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה (מְגִילָּה טז:)1134 Megillah 16b — "And when she came before the king, he said with the scroll" (Esther 9:25). It should have said "she said"! R. Yochanan said: She said to him — let what is written in the scroll be said by mouth. "Words of peace and truth" (Esther 9:30). R. Tanchum said, and some say R. Assi said: This teaches that it requires ruled lines, as does the Torah itself. Rashi: "With the scroll" means that the scroll must be written before them at the time of the reading. The correct reading is "Let what is written in the books be said by mouth" and not "she said to him"; the order of the verses is: "And the Jews took upon themselves… for Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite… and when she came before the king…" — that Haman sought to destroy them, and that Esther came before the king to plead with him: all of this is to be said year by year. "Like the truth of the Torah" means like a Torah scroll itself, for the requirement of ruled lines is a law given to Moses at Sinai. Tosafos (s.v. "it should have said 'she said'"): The verse means that when she came before the king she said to him — over and above the letter that was with him, to be carried out and sent to all the provinces — she said to him further that his evil design should return upon his own head. Since the verse says "when she came… he said," it implies that we are bound to say by mouth what she said. Maharsha: Rashi's arrangement of the verses — that all of this, that Haman sought to destroy them and that Esther came before the king, is to be said year by year together with the scroll — appears to accord with the opinion stated below in the second chapter that one reads the Megillah from "After these things." Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 9:30): Ruled lines signify the complete straightness of the book written with them, and this befits the Torah alone, for the Torah is complete straightness and never departs from it — whereas the Prophets, which tell of the kindness God, blessed be He, does beyond the line of strict law, need no ruling. But in the Megillah, Haman sought to destroy Israel entirely, and God would certainly not allow them to be destroyed, since they have the Torah on which the world stands; Haman's downfall was therefore sheer straightness, a peace in which there is truth. Hence it needs ruled lines "like the truth of the Torah," for there is no truth greater than the Torah, all of whose words are truth and straightness. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 32): No Divine Name is written anywhere in the Megillah, for the Name of Heaven was not revealed to the eye; nevertheless it "requires ruled lines like the truth of the Torah," for the Torah too was given scroll by scroll, the meaning of megillah being the revelation of words of wisdom. The Torah issues from the yesod of Abba, the influx of wisdom, while the Megillah is the yesod of Abba entering the Nukva and emerging from it — the Blessed One's wisdom entering the hearts of Israel and revealed from within the hearts of the Sages of Israel.;
and likewise the Megillah is termed a "sefer" like the authentic truth of the Torah (Megillah 16b);
וְעַל כֵּן מַתְחֶלֶת בְּוָא״ו ("וַיְהִי") וּמְסַיֶּימֶת בְּוָא״ו ("זַרְעוֹ"),
which is why it opens with the letter Vav ("Vayehi") and concludes with a Vav ("Zar'o"),
וְהוּא הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה,
and this is the middle bar that secures from one end to the other end,
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא עִיקַּר הִתְגַּלּוּת הָאוֹר שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
wherein resides the essential revelation of the light shining out of darkness.
וְעַל כֵּן מַתְחִיל בְּמִלַּת "וַיְהִי" הַמּוֹרֶה צַעַר,
Therefore it begins with the word "Vayehi" which indicates distress,

כַּצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָן יִסּוּרִין (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סו)1135 Bereshit Rabbah 66:4 — R. Yitzchak bar R. Chiya said: The wicked, because they begin in tranquility and end in suffering, open with blessing and close with curse — "Blessed be those who bless you and cursed be those who curse you." The righteous, because they begin in suffering and end in tranquility, open with curse and close with blessing — "Cursed be those who curse you and blessed be those who bless you." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 170): This is the meaning of "The righteous — their beginning is suffering and their end is tranquility": in every matter, every good trait and good undertaking, the first entry into it comes with pain, as "all beginnings are hard." For this world is mostly evil, so whatever a person is aroused to, he first sees the evil force within it and is pained, and through the pain he sweetens it, and at once its end is tranquility. Beis Yaakov (Miketz 18): Joseph understood that Pharaoh had first seen good and then bad, for Pharaoh was of the wicked, whose order is "their beginning is tranquility and their end is suffering": the wicked spread themselves out in this world like the primordial worlds that were destroyed, upon which the Blessed One bestowed such abundant kindness that they imagined they had power of their own and did not accept His kingship, and so they perished entirely. But with Israel the good shines forth little by little, for His conduct with them is like the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," and thereby they have the power to gather the wayward and wild forces in man into holiness.;
mirroring the righteous whose beginnings are filled with suffering (Bereishit Rabbah 66);
וְסוֹפָן שַׁלְוָה – הוּא מִלַּת "זַרְעוֹ",
and whose end is tranquility—embodied in the concluding word "Zar'o" (his offspring),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשַּׁלְוָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים קכח, ו): "וּרְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ, שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל",
which is the absolute pinnacle of peace, as it is written (Psalms 128:6): "And see children unto your children, peace upon Israel",
וְ"שָׁלוֹם" רוֹמֵז לְמִדַּת הַיְסוֹד שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה הַשְׁפָּעַת הַזֶּרַע,
and "peace" alludes to the sefirah of Yesod whence flows the seed,
וְהוּא סוֹף הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת אֵלָיו אוֹת הַוָּא״ו.
and it is the conclusion of the six cosmic extremes (Zeir Anpin) to which the letter Vav alludes.
וְהָמָן נִתְפָּאֵר בְּרוֹב בָּנָיו וְחָשַׁב לְהַאֲבִיד בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And Haman boasted in the multitude of his sons and plotted to destroy the children of Israel,
וְהָיָה לְהֵיפֶךְ,
yet the reverse transpired,
כִּי "עֲקָרָה יָלְדָה שִׁבְעָה" (שְׁמוּאֵל א ב, ה) הִיא חִיבּוּר אוֹתִיּוֹת וָא״ו-קוֹ״ף,
for "the barren woman has borne seven" (I Samuel 2:5), which is the union of the letters Vav and Kuf,
"וְרַבַּת בָּנִים אֻמְלָלָה".
while "she that has many children languishes."
וְעַל כֵּן יוּכְלוּ לִפְעוֹל פִּיקּוּד עֲקָרִים וַעֲקָרוֹת בְּפוּרִים
And therefore people can effect the remembrance of barren men and women on Purim,
אוֹתָם שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם כְּבָר יָמִים שֶׁל צַעַר הַרְבֵּה;
specifically those who have already endured prolonged days of sorrow;
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁ"נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן" לְהַחֲזִיר הַכֹּל לִמְקוֹרָן – זוֹכִין לְבָנִים.
for through "their end being wedged in their beginning" to restore everything to its Divine Origin, they merit children.
כִּי כָּל עֲקָרִים וַעֲקָרוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשָׁךְ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק
For all barrenness in Israel is drawn from the root of Amalek,

שֶׁהָיָה מְחַתֵּךְ מִילוֹתֵיהֶם וְאוֹמֵר "טוֹל מַה שֶּׁבָּחַרְתָּ" (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא)1136 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 10 — "And he cut off [vayzanev] all those lagging behind you" (Deuteronomy 25:18) — he struck them a blow to the tail. This accords with what R. Chanina bar Shikla said: What did the house of Amalek do? They would cut off the circumcised flesh of Israel and fling it heavenward, saying, "In this You chose — take for Yourself what You chose.",
who excised their circumcisions and cast them upward, taunting: "Take what You have chosen" (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei),
דִּמְקַטְרֵג עַל מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹחֵר בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל;
prosecuting against Hashem's choosing the seed of Israel;
וְהַבְּחִירָה הוּא מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם וְתוֹלָדָה, דְּ"מָסְפַּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כג, י),
and this chosenness is based upon their holy root and lineage, as in "who can count the dust/issue of Israel" (Numbers 23:10),
וּבִהְיוֹתוֹ בֶּן שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים דְּאֵין יוֹדֵעַ עֲדַיִן כְּלוּם נִימּוֹל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִבְחָר לְחֶלְקוֹ.
and at eight days of age, while knowing nothing yet, an infant is circumcised unto Hashem and chosen as His portion.
וַעֲמָלֵק, שֶׁהוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּרַע טֶרֶם שֶׁיָּצָא לַפּוֹעַל וְהִתְגַּלּוּת,
And Amalek, who is the "first of the nations" and the concealed root of evil before it emerges into manifest actuality,
הוּא נֶגֶד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּטוֹב.
stands directly opposite the concealed root of good.
וְכָל רִיבּוּי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם חֶלְקוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And all multiplying of Israel, who are His blessed portion and heritage,
אֵינוֹ כְּרִיבּוּי דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁהוּא הִתְרַבּוּת גּוּפוֹת כְּרִיבּוּי דְּסוּסִים וַחֲמוֹרִים,
