וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה (שַׁבָּת פו:)1170 Shabbat 86b — Rava said: All agree that they came to the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon, for it is written here "On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai," and it is written there "This month shall be for you the first of months" — just as there it is the New Moon, so here it is the New Moon. And all agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat: it is written here "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it," and it is written there "And Moses said to the people: Remember this day" — just as there it means on that very day, so here on that very day. Rashi: ["It is written here":] "this" [in the one verse] and "this" [in the other] serve for the verbal analogy. ["Just as there":] "Remember this day" — the remembrance of the Exodus was told them on that very day, as "this" indicates; so too here, "Remember the Sabbath day" was told them on the very day of the Sabbath. Tosafos (s.v. "and it is written there, 'This month shall be for you'"): In Pesachim (6b) the Gemara asks of this very verse how we know it was spoken at the New Moon; but it certainly was, for the Midrash (Mechilta) says that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed [the new moon] to Moses with His finger — the question there is only whether Moses relayed it to Israel on that same day, which R. Shimon ben Gamliel's rule, that the laws of Passover are expounded two weeks beforehand, requires. And though here too one could derive "wilderness" from "wilderness," as is done there, it is preferable to derive "this" from "this." Maharsha: Scripture should have written "on that day they came"; [since it says "this day,"] the word "this" is expounded as coming for the verbal analogy, as "this" is likewise expounded in "this our son." In "This month," by contrast, "this" is certainly needed for itself, for the Midrash says that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "See [it] thus and sanctify it," showing it to him with His finger. Maharal (Derech Chaim 2:8): Had the Torah been given on a weekday, a person would say that just as there is rest from labor, so there is rest from Torah; it was therefore given on the Sabbath, a rest from labor that is no rest from Torah, and all the more so there is no rest from Torah on the weekdays. Further, man by his very creation is not meant to be at rest and complete — "man is born to toil" (Job 5:7) — and had the Torah not been given on the Sabbath, he would be at rest and complete on it; so it was given on the Sabbath, and through the Torah man is not at rest. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 27): They came to the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon because the time of the third month is fit for the Torah and has a preparation for it, as does the place, the wilderness of Sinai. And on every view the Torah was received on the Sabbath, for that is the day on which blessing comes from the upper realms to the lower — "And God blessed the seventh day" — and so it is prepared for the Torah, which is wholly blessing, to come from above to below as well. Further, the Sabbath is holy and separate from the physical, in that no labor is done on it, so it is fitting that the Torah, which is pure intellect abstracted from the physical, be given on it — all the more since the Sabbath is the completion of the world, and the giving of the Torah to the world is itself the completion of the world.,
and all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given (Shabbat 86b),
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת: הַשְׁפָּעַת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
which is the ultimate essence of the Sabbath's holiness: the outpouring of Torah light unto Israel.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Passover, Shavuot, and the Opening from Below
Passover begins the movement from darkness, and human effort opens the small aperture through which Torah-light is received.

p: וּכְלַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים גַּם כֵּן חֲלוּקִים לִשְׁנַיִם אֵלּוּ:
And the general category of the holiness of the seasons is likewise divided into these two:
בְּפֶסַח יָצְאוּ מֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל,
on Passover they went forth from darkness to great light,
וְעַל יָדוֹ זָכוּ לְ"אוֹרָה זוֹ תּוֹרָה" בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת.
and through it they merited "light, which is Torah" on Shavuot.
וּבְעִנְיַן הַסְּפִירָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה מִיּוֹם הַפֶּסַח
And regarding the count toward the Giving of the Torah from the day of Passover,
נִקְרָא פֶּסַח בְּשֵׁם שַׁבָּת: "מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת" (וַיִּקְרָא כג, טו),
Passover is designated by the title Shabbat: "from the morrow of the Sabbath" (Leviticus 23:15),
כִּי זֶהוּ מִצַּד קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁבּוֹ נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה (שַׁבָּת פו:),
for this stems from the sanctity of Shabbat on which the Torah was given (Shabbat 86b),
וְעַל יָדוֹ הוּא הַזְּכִיָּה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
and through it comes the merit for the Giving of the Torah.
כִּי בְּיוֹם טוֹב נִכְלָל שְׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת דְּחֹדֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת,
For within Yom Tov are encompassed the two sanctities of the new moon and Shabbat,
כִּי "יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ",
since "Israel sanctifies it",
וְגַם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוֹסִיף בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
and Hashem, blessed be He, also infused within them an established and permanent holiness of His own
עַל יְדֵי הַנֵּס שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהֶם בָּהֶם.
by virtue of the miracle He performed for them on these days.
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַיָּמִים טוֹבִים קְרוּיִים שַׁבָּת גַּם כֵּן,
Therefore all festivals are likewise termed Shabbat,
וְהַפֶּסַח בְּיִחוּד שֶׁבּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ גּוֹבֶרֶת.
and Passover in particular, wherein this higher divine sanctity predominates.
וְכֵן הָיָה עִנְיַן יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי" (דְּבָרִים ד, לד),
And so was the reality of the Exodus from Egypt, "a nation from the midst of a nation" (Deuteronomy 4:34),
כְּאִלּוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָשָׂה כֵּן מֵעַצְמוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ בְּלִי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם כְּלָל.
as though Hashem, blessed be He, enacted this solely from Himself and His will, devoid of any dependent exertion of theirs.
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה בְּחֹמֶר וּבִלְבֵנִים וְגוֹמֵר,
And their sole exertion through which they merited this was through labor with mortar and bricks, etc.,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א)1171 Zohar 1:27a — "And they embittered their lives with hard labor" — this is a difficult question; "with mortar (chomer)" — this is an inference a fortiori (kal va-chomer); "and with bricks (levenim)" — this is the clarifying (libbun) of a law; "and with all manner of labor in the field" — this is a baraita; "all their labor which they made them serve with rigor (be-farekh)" — this is the Mishnah.:
as written in the Zohar (Part I, 27a):
"בְּחֹמֶר" – דָּא קַל וָחֹמֶר, "וּבִלְבֵנִים" – לִיבּוּן הִלְכְתָא וְכוּלֵי,
"with mortar"—this is the kal va-chomer reasoning; "and with bricks"—the clarification of halakhah, etc.,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה.
whereby through this they merited the reception of the Torah.
וַהֲרֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה הָיָה בְּעַל כָּרְחָם וְלֹא מֵרְצוֹנָם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם.
Yet behold, that servitude was under compulsion, not from their independent volition or conscious spiritual striving.
וְכֵן הוּא: כָּל שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲשִׂים בֶּאֱמֶת
And such is the case: the entirety of perfected human action in truth
הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר שֶׁהוּא מִפְּעוּלַּת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם,
is merely what Hashem graciously ascribes to the deed and effort of man,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יב),
whereas in truth "even all our deeds You have wrought for us" (Isaiah 26:12),
וְהוּא "הַנֹּתֵן לְךָ כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חָיִל" (דְּבָרִים ח, יח).
and He is the One "Who gives you power to get wealth and strength" (Deuteronomy 8:18).
וְאָז יָצְאוּ לְחֵירוּת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַדִּבּוּר שֶׁהָיוּ בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם,
And then they went forth into freedom in the rectification of action and speech which had been suppressed in Egyptian exile,
שֶׁהָעֶבֶד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו וְדִבּוּרָיו הַנִּגְלִים מְשׁוּעְבָּד לַאֲדוֹנוֹ.
wherein a slave in all his manifest physical actions and outward words is subservient to his master.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִקְדוּשַּׁת פֶּסַח וְשָׁבוּעוֹת שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד מַעֲשֶׂה וְדִבּוּר:
And through this liberation they merited the sanctities of Passover and Shavuot, which correspond to action and speech:
פֶּסַח עִיקָּרוֹ בְּמִצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת,
Passover fundamentally consists of concrete practical commandments,
וְשָׁבוּעוֹת בְּדִבְּרוֹת דְּתוֹרָה.
and Shavuot in the spoken utterances of the Torah.
וְסֻכּוֹת הוּא זְמַן הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
And Sukkot is the season of inner joy in the heart,
שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יְדֵי יִשְׁרַת לֵב דִּתְמִימוּתָם בְּהַקְדָּמַת "נַעֲשֶׂה" לְ"נִשְׁמָע",
which they merited through the uprightness of heart of their holy simplicity in advancing "we will do" before "we will hear",
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא דְּעִיקָּרָהּ בַּלֵּב,
and the repentance following the sin, the primary locus of which is in the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, י): "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב".
as it is written (Isaiah 6:10): "and understand with his heart, and return".
וְגַם כֵּן חָלוּק לִשְׁנַיִם נֶגֶד מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא:
And this realm is likewise subdivided into two, corresponding to brain and heart:
סֻכּוֹת נֶגֶד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁשָּׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר,
Sukkot corresponds to the desire within the heart, which is the dwelling place of the inclination,
וְיֵשׁ אֲחִיזָה וְשַׁיָּיכוּת קְצָת לִקְלוֹט גַּם מֵהָרַע וְשִׁבְעִין עַמְמִין לְהָפְכוֹ לְטוֹב;
wherein there exists some grasp and connection to absorb even from the evil and the seventy nations so as to transform it into good;
וּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת נֶגֶד מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
while Shemini Atzeret corresponds to the pure thought within the brain,
דְּשָׁם הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְגַּלּוּת יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
for there is the inception of manifestation ex nihilo,
וִיצִיאַת רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מִקַּדְמוּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם,
and the emergence of the prime thought drawn from the Primordial Thought that transcends human grasp,
דְּשָׁם אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לָרַע כְּלָל,
wherein evil holds no connection whatsoever,
כְּטַעַם: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא" הָרוֹמֶזֶת לַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
mirroring: "The soul You placed within me is pure," which alludes to the soul residing in the brain.

וְזֶהוּ (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פִּינְחָס טז)1172 Midrash Tanchuma, Pinchas 16 — So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: All the offerings you brought during the seven days of the Festival, you were offering for the nations of the world; but on the eighth day let us make do, I and you, with whatever you can find — "one bull, one ram.": "אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם לְבַד",
And this is (Midrash Tanchuma, Pinchas 16): "Just Me and you alone",
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין שָׁם פֵּירוּד כְּבֵין פֶּסַח לְשָׁבוּעוֹת,
and therefore there is no lengthy interval there as between Passover and Shavuot,
כִּי הֵם "רֵיעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין" וְנִמְשָׁכִים תְּכוּפִים זֶה אַחַר זֶה.
for brain and heart are "companions that never separate," continuing immediately one after the other.
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
And Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,
אַף שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי",
although they too are sanctified by Israel ("Israel sanctifies the seasons"),
וּמִכְּלַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים הַנִּתְלָה בִּימֵי הַחֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא בְּיוֹם קָבוּעַ כְּשַׁבָּת,
and belong to the category of seasonal holiness dependent upon the days of the month rather than a fixed cycle like Shabbat,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינָן בִּכְלַל הַמּוֹעֲדִים,
they are nonetheless not counted within the standard category of the pilgrimage festivals,
כִּי מְשׁוּנִּים מֵהֶם:
because they differ fundamentally from them:
שֶׁהַמּוֹעֲדִים נִקְבְּעוּ עַל נִסִּים שֶׁכְּבָר זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם לְאוֹתָם נִסִּים,
for the festivals were instituted over historical miracles that Israel already merited through their striving,
וְנִקְבַּע אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם.
and that sanctity became permanently etched within their hearts for all generations.
אֲבָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הֲרַת עוֹלָם וְהַבְּרִיאָה יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן,
However, Rosh Hashanah, which is the time of the world's conception and Creation ex nihilo,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עֲדַיִן אָדָם לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל עַל זֶה,
wherein man did not yet exist to strive for this,
הֲרֵי לֹא הָיָה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם כְּלָל.
behold, it was completely independent of human exertion.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסָרוֹ לִבְנֵי אָדָם לִהְיוֹת נַעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵיהֶם וְשֶׁהֵם יְקַדְּשׁוּ לוֹ,
Only that Hashem, blessed be He, entrusted it unto human beings to be enacted through them, and that they sanctify it,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וָאֶתְחַנַּן1173 Devarim Rabbah 2:14 — R. Yochanan said: When the ministering angels gather before the Holy One, blessed be He, to say, When is the New Year and when is the Day of Atonement? — the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them: Why do you ask Me? You and I, let us go down to the court below. Whence do we know it? As it is written, "who has God near to it" — it is not written here "who has a nation near to it," but "who has God near to it," He and all His retinue. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): The nations are under time, which rules over them, but Israel are above time and rule over it, for the Blessed One handed time over to them, as the Sages said, "You and I, let us go to the court below": "This month shall be for you" is entrusted to Israel, and as the court below fixes the time — when they sanctify the new month or intercalate the year — so it is, for Israel sanctify the times. According to their deeds the time becomes prepared, not of itself. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): All the judgments in all the upper worlds follow the Torah, and the Torah has already been handed over to those below, as the Sages said regarding the fixing of Rosh Hashanah, "You and I, let us go to the court below": if the court intercalated the month, the judgments above are annulled from that day. So too in every doubtful matter of the Torah — as the Sages decide in this world, so is the decision in all the upper worlds. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): On a festival one is sanctified from above, for though "Israel sanctify" it, it also has something of the fixed holiness of the Sabbath; yet that holiness comes through Israel's sanctifying, by virtue of their holiness in this world — for the times depend on the court below, which is in this world, as the Sages said, "You and I, let us go to the court below." The Sabbath, a semblance of the World to Come, is the sanctification for the World to Come. ב, יד):
and as they stated (Devarim Rabbah, Va'etchanan 2:14):
"אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם נֵלֵךְ לְבֵית דִּין שֶׁלְּמַטָּה לִשְׁאוֹל מָתַי קִידְּשׁוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה".
"I and you will go to the earthly court below to ask when they sanctified Rosh Hashanah."
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי עִיקַּר הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וְיַעֲבוֹד ה',
And this is because the essential purpose of Creation was so that man might exert himself and serve Hashem;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: דְּנִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהֵם עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה א, ד),
and as they taught: the universe was created for Israel, and they arose in Divine Thought first (Bereishit Rabbah 1:4),
וּבִשְׁבִיל הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּדְּלוּ אַחַר כָּךְ וְיִזְכּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם – בְּרָאָם תְּחִלָּה.
and on account of the spiritual striving which He foresaw they would exert subsequently and merit through their deeds, He created them first.
נִמְצָא גַּם תְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם,
Thus even the inception of Creation was for the sake of their exertion,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּאַחַר כָּךְ;
except that it was on account of subsequent future striving;
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, אָז הָיָה תְּחִלָּה יְצִירַת בְּרִיָּה לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ, וְהוּא הַתְחָלַת הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת –
and on the contrary, then was the initial creation of mortal beings to strive in His service, marking the commencement of effort—
הֵיפֶךְ הַמּוֹעֲדִים הַבָּאִים אַחַר וּבְסוֹף הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
the opposite of the festivals which arrive after and at the culmination of striving,
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לִקְבּוֹעַ לוֹ יוֹם שְׁבִיתָה הַבָּא אַחַר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת.
wherein one merits through his effort to establish a day of rest following that striving.
אֲבָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה הַתְחָלַת הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַשְּׁבִיתָה,
However, Rosh Hashanah is, on the contrary, the inception of striving which is the antithesis of resting,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְבַּע גַּם כֵּן יוֹם שְׁבִיתָה,
yet nonetheless it was established as a day of rest as well,
כִּי "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
for "the end of action is conceived in initial thought",
וּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל מַה שֶּׁיִּזְכּוּ בַּסּוֹף עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם לְקַדֵּשׁ לַזְּמַנִּים,
and the start of Creation is on account of what they will ultimately merit through their effort to sanctify the seasons,
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָלָה זֶה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ – מִתְּחִלָּה בְּרָאָם.
and because this arose in Thought before Him, He created them from the beginning.
וְנִמְצָא תְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַעֲלָאַת מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַזּוֹכִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם לִשְׁבִיתָה;
Thus the beginning of Creation was for the sake of the rising Thought that Israel would merit rest through their striving;
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְבַּע אוֹתוֹ יוֹם גַּם כֵּן לְיוֹם קָדוֹשׁ דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ".
through this, that day was established as a holy day that "Israel sanctifies".
אֲבָל אֵינוֹ מַה שֶּׁהֵם קִדְּשׁוּהוּ בַּפּוֹעַל בִּבְחִירָתָם בַּטּוֹב,
Yet it is not a day that they sanctified in active deed through their personal choice of good,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קִידְּשׁוֹ עַל שְׁמָם מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁיִּבְחֲרוּ בַּטּוֹב.
rather Hashem, blessed be He, sanctified it in their name from the perspective of Foreknowledge, knowing they would choose good.
וַהֲרֵי מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לִיקָּרֵא עַל שְׁמָם;
And behold, from the aspect of absolute Foreknowledge there is no room for human free choice, nor does it strictly warrant being credited to their name;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קְרָאוֹ עַל שְׁמָם,
nonetheless Hashem, blessed be He, titled it in their name,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ לְמַעְלָה בְּעִנְיַן קְדוּשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בֶּעָבָר גַּם כֵּן.
just as we noted above concerning the sanctity of past action as well.

אֲשֶׁר עַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּחֲגִיגָה (טו.)1174 Chagigah 15a — Acher asked R. Meir: What is meant by that which is written, "God has made the one corresponding to the other"? He said to him: Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created its counterpart. He created mountains, He created hills; He created seas, He created rivers. He said to him: R. Akiva your teacher did not say so, but rather: He created the righteous, He created the wicked; He created the Garden of Eden, He created Gehinnom. Each and every person has two portions, one in the Garden of Eden and one in Gehinnom. Maharsha: "Corresponding" here means what is equal to a thing: mountains and hills, which match each other in height, and likewise seas and rivers. But the righteous and the wicked are not equals; they are a thing and its opposite, and the correspondence is only partial — He created the righteous and He created the Garden of Eden, He created the wicked and He created Gehinnom, creating for each what belongs to it. And since the choice to be righteous or wicked is given to man, for all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, and the Holy One, blessed be He, withholds from no creature its reward or its punishment, He created the Garden of Eden for all, should they all merit it, and Gehinnom for all, should they not. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): All of man's service in this world is to sort the good from the evil and set each apart, as they said, "each and every one has two portions... if worthy, being righteous, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion": although He created righteous and wicked, in each there is also a portion of the opposite, and "God has made the one corresponding to the other," so that opposite every righteous person stands a wicked one in the portion of evil. The righteous must refine himself and separate the evil from himself so that it remains wholly in the wicked one's portion, and absorb the portion of good in that wicked one which belongs to him; thus he is completed wholly in holiness, and the evil, left wholly evil, goes to perdition. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 250): Esau had the greater force of desire, and Jacob acquired his birthright with a "pottage," his own boiling for the delights of this world: he gave Esau that boiling and absorbed the good boiling, the boiling of Torah. This is in the manner of "if worthy, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion... if guilty, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion": Jacob exchanged with Esau, giving him his share of boiling in its animal form and receiving the good from him [such as the souls of R. Akiva and R. Meir, absorbed into the seed of Jacob through this acquisition], for each person necessarily has two portions, the good inclination and the [evil] inclination. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): "God has made the one corresponding to the other" was the whole matter of creation, and man's task in this world is to recognize and separate good from evil: there is no righteous person without a wicked "fellow" opposite him, joined to him through this correspondence that God made. About this they said, "each one has [two portions]... if worthy, being righteous, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in the Garden of Eden; if guilty, being wicked, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in Gehinnom"; and not for nothing did they call him "his fellow," for there is necessarily a bond between them through which one can take his fellow's portion, the one for good and the other for the opposite. וּבְבָבָא בַּתְרָא (טז.)1175 Bava Batra 16a — "You know that I am not wicked, and there is none that can deliver out of Your hand." Rava said: Job sought to exempt the whole world from judgment. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, You created the ox with cloven hooves and You created the donkey with closed hooves; You created the Garden of Eden, You created Gehinnom; You created the righteous, You created the wicked. Who can stop You? Rashi: He sought to exempt the whole world from the judgment of the Holy One, blessed be He, by saying that sinners act under compulsion at God's own hand, since He created the evil inclination; "You know that I will not be wicked" means: had You so wished, I would not have been wicked. You made the ox's hooves cloven and the donkey's closed — this one You declared pure and that one impure, and it all comes from Your hand, for it was You who set the marks of impurity in it. You created the righteous by means of the good inclination and the wicked by means of the evil inclination; therefore there is none that can deliver out of Your hand, for who can restrain You — those who sin are under compulsion. Maharsha: Job denied free choice and held that a man is compelled in his deeds by his nature from birth; hence the analogy drawn from two opposite creatures — the ox, the choicest of the permitted kinds, and the donkey, the lowest of the forbidden, so named for its grossness [ḥomer]. Neither is praised or blamed for what it is, since each is compelled by the nature it was created with, as the philosopher said, "the compelled is neither praised nor blamed," and as that old man answered R. Shimon ben Elazar, "Go to the craftsman who made me." So too, Job argued, the righteous and the wicked are such from their very creation and neither deserves reward or punishment — and this is what is meant by his exempting the whole world from judgment. וּבְסוֹטָה (כב.)1176 Sotah 22a — Is that so? But R. Yochanan said: We learned fear of sin from a virgin and the receiving of reward from a widow. Fear of sin from a virgin — for R. Yochanan heard a certain virgin fall upon her face and say: Master of the Universe, You created the Garden of Eden and You created Gehinnom, You created the righteous and You created the wicked. May it be Your will that men not stumble on my account. Rashi: "Receiving reward from a widow": she troubled herself more than necessary in order to receive reward, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain — we learned that a person should exert himself in a mitzva so as to receive greater reward. "You created the righteous" — to inherit the Garden of Eden; "You created the wicked" — to inherit Gehinnom; "that men not stumble on my account" — losing their share in the Garden of Eden through me and inheriting Gehinnom. Maharsha: He does not object from the virgin — and indeed the answer says nothing about her — for a "praying virgin" implies one who prays excessively day and night, as the Aruch explains, whereas this virgin of the fear of sin prayed at the proper time; but a "gadabout widow," whose habit is to visit her neighbors constantly, fits this widow of the receiving of reward, who came every day to pray in the study hall, so the objection is well taken from her. The virgin did not pray for herself, that she not stumble with men and be punished, perhaps because she knew she could stand firm; she prayed only that they not stumble over her by forcing her and be punished on her account — as it is said, one on whose account his fellow is punished is not admitted into the precinct of the Holy One, blessed be He. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sotah 22a): A virgin is predisposed to fear of sin, for she does not have [sinful] thoughts as a man does, whereas a man is not so readily disposed to fear of sin; and the widow loves to do the mitzva, for just as a woman is created by nature ready to serve her husband and heed his voice, so she loves to heed the Holy One, blessed be He, and serve her Creator. He says specifically "a virgin" and "a widow" because while a woman has a husband her way is to be drawn after him in everything; hence it is the virgin who is ready for the fear of God and the widow who is ready to serve her Creator. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Darkness too is part of the world's creation, and the Blessed One even arranged a deed of the wicked for a perfectly righteous man like King David, "to raise up the yoke of repentance"; on this the Sages said, "You created the righteous, You created the wicked." Though they said that "righteous or wicked" is not decreed (Niddah 16b), in truth one can recognize even in children that some are formed from the outset with a good nature and some with the opposite — this falls under "wise or foolish" — and it has nothing to do with the choice between righteous and wicked, for even one created righteous has an inclination that overpowers him every day, and one created wicked has the choice to subdue his innate inclination and return to the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): Abraham, who sought to justify all creatures, hated to condemn even the wicked, such as the people of Sodom, for all are the Blessed One's creatures, and His praise rises even from the wicked in Gehinnom. As the Sages said, "You created the righteous and You created the wicked" — the wicked too are part of creation, and there is a need for them, so that there be the advantage of light over darkness; that is why the creation of the world began with darkness. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Although everything is by choice, the Sages also said, "You created the righteous, You created the wicked," as in the blessing of R. Nechunya ben HaKanah, "that You have set my portion among those who sit in the study hall" — for in truth everything is from the Blessed One. So one who has learned much Torah should not claim credit for himself, as though his own effort brought it about. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 100): "Righteous" and "pious" are two degrees innate in a person from birth, and of this it says, "You created the righteous, You created the wicked"; for though "righteous or wicked" is not decreed (Niddah 16b), these are two forces in the upper worlds, only that in place of "wicked" the name is "pious" [for the pious man, like the wicked, departs from the line of strict law, but toward kindness]. The two forces are mixed in everyone, but not equally: in one this prevails, [in another that].:
Which is why they stated in Chagigah (15a), Bava Batra (16a), and Sotah (22a):
"בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים, בָּרָאתָ רְשָׁעִים",
"You created the righteous, You created the wicked",

אַף דְּאִילּוּ צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע לָא קָאָמַר1177 Niddah 16b — The angel appointed over conception is named Night. He takes the drop and sets it before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says: Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop — mighty or weak, wise or foolish, rich or poor? But “wicked or righteous” he does not say — in accordance with R. Chanina, who said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven. Rashi: “Everything is in the hands of Heaven” — all a man's qualities and all that befalls him come upon him by the decree of the King, except this one. “But to fear” — this alone He asks of you, because everything else is in His hand and this is in yours. Tosafos (s.v. “the angel appointed over conception”): But over birth no angel is appointed, as is said at the beginning of Ta'anit: three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He — of a woman in childbirth, of rain, and of the resurrection of the dead. Even those three keys are at times handed over to an agent for a time, for Elijah held the key of rain and revived the dead, and so did Elisha and many righteous men; and even Beri, who is the prince of rain, acts only by the permission of the Holy One, blessed be He. Tosafos (s.v. “everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven”): In “Elu Na'arot” it is said that everything is in the hands of Heaven except cold and heat. Here the statement concerns a man's nature and his traits, while there it concerns the things that befall him, such as illnesses and calamities, all of which are decreed upon him and against which he cannot guard himself — except cold and heat, against which he can guard himself. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “this drop, what shall become of it — mighty or weak, wise [or foolish]”): This is the meaning of the verse “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom”: what is compelled is neither praised nor blamed, and therefore these three — wisdom, might and wealth — which are compelled by the decree from the hour of a man's formation, are no ground for glorying. “But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me” — for that is the thing which depends upon his choice. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 16b): He is called Night because the gestation takes place in the woman's belly, “like the bones in the womb of her that is with child,” and the child is there in darkness. Therefore the angel appointed over gestation is called Night, since in the belly it is always night and never day. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part I 4): "If you have learned much Torah, do not claim credit for yourself" [as if] you were better than others, "for that is why you were created," as stated in Niddah: "wise or foolish." And so the early authorities explained "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom … but let him who glories glory in this," in keeping with what is said there: "righteous or wicked he does not say." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 11): The Torah is called "a good lekach [lit. "taking"] I have given you," both a taking and a gift: in truth it is a good gift that the Blessed One gave in this world, a semblance of the World to Come, of which it is said "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," without any effort, for "wise or foolish" is from birth, and only "righteous or wicked he does not say," and "all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven." That fear of Heaven, which is a man's own effort, is "the beginning of wisdom," and so [the Torah] appears as something taken, because of his effort in fear of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): The Sages said "You created righteous, You created wicked," yet they said "righteous or wicked he does not say"; but in truth "a gourd is known by its shoot," and one can recognize even in children that some are formed from the outset with a good nature, to walk in innocence and uprightness, and some the opposite, and this falls under "wise or foolish," for the intent is not human wisdom but the wisdom of truth, to conduct oneself as is fitting. This has nothing to do with the choice between righteous and wicked: even one created righteous has an inclination that overpowers him every day, and the choice is his, and one created wicked likewise has the choice to subdue the inclination of heart he was born with and return to the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 100): "Righteous" [tzaddik] and "pious" [chasid] are two levels in a person from birth, and of this it was said "You created righteous, You created wicked"; and although "righteous or wicked he does not say," as stated in Niddah, these are rather two forces in the upper worlds, except that in place of "wicked" the name there is "pious." The two forces are mixed in every person, only they are not equal, and in one person this one prevails. (נִדָּה טז:) דְּעַל זֶה הוּא הַבְּחִירָה;
even though regarding 'righteous or wicked' the angel does not declare (Niddah 16b), this being subject to free choice;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא מִתְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה כֵּן לְעִנְיַן גְּמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דְּצַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע,
nevertheless, in primordial truth it is established from Creation regarding the ultimate outcome of the righteous and the wicked,
שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ צַדִּיקִים שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֲלֵיהֶם פְּעָמִים כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָרְשָׁעִים וְאֵין יָכוֹל לִמְלוֹט כִּמְעַט מֵהַמִּכְשׁוֹל,
for there are righteous individuals who sometimes encounter circumstances resembling the actions of the wicked, scarcely able to escape the pitfall,

וּכְטַעַם (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ): "אָדָם אֵין צַדִּיק [בָּאָרֶץ] אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה [טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא1178 Ecclesiastes 7:20 — “For there is no righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin.” Rashi: "For there is no righteous man on earth" — therefore he must examine his deeds. Metzudas Dovid: There is no man in all the earth righteous in all his ways, who always does good and never sins; and wisdom is a stronghold for the wise, for it counsels him to examine his deeds and to hasten to repent.]",
mirroring (Ecclesiastes 7:20): "there is no righteous man on earth who does good and sins not",
וְאַף דְּהוּא צַדִּיק וְנִשְׁמָר בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ.
even though he is genuinely righteous and vigilant with all his strength.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן (קֹהֶלֶת י, ז): "עֲבָדִים רֹכְבִים עַל סוּסִים, וְשָׂרִים הֹלְכִים כַּעֲבָדִים",
And this is the matter of (Ecclesiastes 10:7): "servants riding upon horses, and princes walking as servants",

שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן ס)1179 Tikkunei Zohar 93b — So too you find a man whose body is fair and all whose marks are fair, while his soul within is a wicked soul; and you find a man whose body is ill in all its marks, while his soul within is fair — this is "a righteous man to whom evil befalls." Good within and his garment ill — this is "poor and riding upon an ass"; evil within and his garment fair without — of this it is said, "I have seen slaves upon horses." And everything is recognized by a man's deeds; not for nothing did the ancients establish that not study but deed is the essential thing, for fools look at the body, which is only a garment. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): In "a red strap on a white horse," the horse is the body upon which the soul rides, as is said in the Tikkunei Zohar on the verse "slaves riding upon horses"; when it is white it is clean and full of kindness, yet even the best of horses needs a strap to be struck with, and that is the red, the attribute of judgment. Sod Yesharim (Rosh Hashanah 18): "I saw slaves upon horses, and princes walking like slaves upon the earth": my father, my master and teacher, the holy gaon, of blessed memory, explained that "slaves upon horses" denotes garments that are fair and very clean while at the root there is a deficiency, as the Tikkunei Zohar explains, "evil within and his garment fair without — of this it is said, 'I have seen slaves upon horses'"; and "princes walking upon the earth like slaves" denotes coarse and turbid garments, though at their root there is no deficiency at all. עַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן לְעֵרֶךְ הַגּוּפוֹת1180 Tikkunei Zohar 60 — Evil within, while its garment is fair without — of this it is said, “I have seen servants upon horses.”.
which the Tikkunim (Tikkun 60) expounds as referring to holy souls mismatched with physical bodies.
וְשָׁם בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (טז.): דְּאִיּוֹב בִּקֵּשׁ עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִפְטוֹר כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ מִן הַדִּין,
And there in Bava Batra (16a): Job sought through this to exempt the entire universe from judgment,

וְהֵם הֱשִׁיבוּהוּ: דְּ"בָּרָא תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין1181 Bava Batra 16a — Rava said: Iyov sought to exempt the whole world from judgment. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, You created the ox with cloven hooves and You created the donkey with closed hooves; You created the Garden of Eden and You created Gehinnom; You created the righteous and You created the wicked — who can stay Your hand? And what did his companions answer him? If so, “You even annul fear and diminish devotion before God” — the Holy One, blessed be He, created the evil inclination, and He created the Torah as its remedy. Rashi: He sought to exempt the whole world from the judgment of the Holy One, blessed be He, by saying that sinners act under compulsion at God's hand, since He created the evil inclination: You created the righteous by means of the good inclination and the wicked by means of the evil inclination, and who can restrain You? To this the friends answer that the Torah is the remedy which dispels sinful thoughts — as they said elsewhere, "If this loathsome one meets you, drag him to the study house" — so that sinners are not under compulsion at all, since they are able to save themselves. Maharsha: Job denied free choice and claimed that a man is compelled in his deeds by the nature he was created with — as the ox and the donkey are, neither praised nor blamed for the hooves they were given — so that the righteous deserve no reward and the wicked no punishment. His friends answered him in order to uphold free choice: the Holy One, blessed be He, did create the evil inclination in man, but He placed the remedy in man's own hand, the Torah, by which he may choose the good. "You even annul fear" means that it is you yourself who annul it, for the fear of Heaven lies in your hand; "and diminish devotion before God" — it is the one thing withheld from Him, since all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 15): Through the Torah one can rectify everything, as they said, "He created the evil inclination, He created Torah as its spice": [the evil inclination] stems from its root in creation through the serpent's counsel, which came from the Blessed One, who created the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil and gave man the choice to eat of it, whereby the feeling of bodily lust entered the heart. At the giving of the Torah they were freed from the evil inclination, since through the Torah, the spice, they can rectify this, as Rambam wrote that lusts are found only in a heart empty of words of Torah.";
and the Sages countered him: "He created the Torah as a spice/remedy";
וּלְשׁוֹן "תַּבְלִין" מַשְׁמָע שֶׁאֵין מֵסִיר הַדָּבָר לְגַמְרֵי רַק שֶׁמְּתַבְּלוֹ.
and the term "spice" implies that it does not eliminate the base substance completely, but merely seasons and refines it.
וְזֶהוּ שָׁבוּעוֹת שֶׁאַחַר הַפֶּסַח וִימֵי הַסְּפִירָה,
And this is Shavuot following Passover and the days of the Omer count,
לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק מֵעִיקָּרוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין.
to become righteous from one's root through the Torah as a spice.
וּבַתְּחִלָּה נִקְרָא "תּוֹרַת ה'", כִּי הַכֹּל מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
And initially it is termed "the Torah of Hashem," for all is bestowed from Heaven,

וְאַחַר כָּךְ "תּוֹרָתוֹ" (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.)1182 Avodah Zarah 19a — And Rava said: At first it is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and in the end it is called by his own name, as it is said: "His delight is in the Torah of the Lord," and then, "and in his Torah he meditates day and night." Rashi: "It is called by his own name" — by the name of the student who toiled in it, as it is written "and in his Torah," which implies the Torah of the man himself. Maharsha: That a Torah scholar's Torah is his own is set out in the first chapter of Kiddushin from this very verse, "and in his Torah he meditates": at the beginning of study it is called "the Torah of the Lord," and once he has learned it and made it fluent it is called "his Torah." This is of a piece with the teaching that at first Moses would learn the Torah and forget it, until it was given to him as a gift — that is, he kept learning it from his teacher until it became an acquisition in his soul. So too with what Rava adds, that a person should first study and only then analyze: until his learning is fluent in his mouth it is not yet his own Torah, and only when he afterwards meditates and delves into it himself does it become his Torah, given to him as a gift. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 19a): This comes to say that the Torah has a relation to the man, until it is called his Torah. Before he has received it, it is called "the Torah of the Lord," for it is the wisdom and order of the Blessed One by which He created all; but once he has received it, it is called the Torah of the man, for it is his Torah and his completion — the way in which he is to walk and the deed he is to do — and it belongs to him entirely, since the Torah is his completion., דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קוֹרֵא הַכֹּל עַל שְׁמוֹ.
and subsequently "his Torah" (Avodah Zarah 19a), for Hashem credits everything to man's name.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (יז:)1183 Rosh Hashanah 17b — R. Yochanan said: Were the verse not written, it would be impossible to say it. It teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself like a prayer leader and showed Moses the order of prayer. He said to him: Whenever Israel sin, let them do before Me according to this order, and I will forgive them. "The Lord, the Lord" — I am He before a man sins, and I am He after a man sins and repents, "God, merciful and gracious." Rashi (s.v. "the Lord, the Lord"): The attribute of mercy: I have mercy before he sins, and I have mercy after he sins, if he repents. Tosafos (s.v. "thirteen attributes"): Rabbeinu Tam says that the first two Names are two [of the thirteen] attributes, as we say here: "I am the Lord before he sins," to have mercy on him, "and I have mercy after he sins, if he repents" — for "the Lord" is the attribute of mercy, unlike "God" [Elohim], which is the attribute of judgment. But Rabbeinu Nissim in Megillat Setarim does not count the first Name, since there is a pause between the Names, the verse meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, whose Name is "the Lord," proclaimed: "The Lord… merciful and gracious." Maharsha (s.v. "the Lord, the Lord: I am He before he sins"): For even before he sins [a man] needs mercy, since the world was created only through the Holy One, blessed be He, joining mercy [to judgment], as it is said, "on the day that the Lord God made" [Genesis 2:4]; and "I am He" — that repentance avails a man even after he sins, to have mercy on him. Maharsha (s.v. "were the verse not written, it would be impossible to say it"): The verse was stated only to make the ear understand, for so it appeared to Moses in prophecy — as though the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself like a prayer leader; this is "and the Lord passed before him," like a prayer leader who passes his tallit over his face and recites in this order, which the Holy One, blessed be He, did to teach that they should do so whenever [Israel sin]. And in an old book of the wisdom of the kabbalists I found: the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself in the same white tallit in which He wrapped Himself at the creation of the world, of which it is said, "who covers Himself with light as with a garment" [Psalms 104:2]. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 17b, s.v. "I am He before a man sins"): These thirteen attributes are the ways of the Lord in existence, the attributes of His goodness by which He does good to man, and even one who has not sinned needs His goodness, for a creature has no claim upon its Creator — all is kindness and mercy, not debt. Moreover, He is called by His unique Name, the Name of Being, which signifies simple being without regard to deeds; the wicked man who has repented is now righteous and equal to one who never sinned, and since their being is equal, both being without sin, the Blessed One joins Himself to both by that Name: "I am the Lord before he sins and after he sins." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Rosh Hashanah 17b, s.v. "it teaches that He wrapped Himself"): Had the aim been only to teach what to pray, it should have said to him "thus and thus shall you recite," like all the rest of the Torah, with no need for "and the Lord passed before him and proclaimed"; rather, it teaches that He also showed him how the order of prayer is done. For Moses had asked, "Show me, I pray, Your glory" (Exodus 33:18), seeking to comprehend the good attributes of the Blessed One; and since he asked for a seeing, it could be granted only through an act — He showed him that when they do before Him according to this order, the attribute of His goodness opens to them. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): Yom Kippur includes all three holinesses in the atonement that follows sin, for with complete atonement it is as though he had not sinned, as the Sages said on the verse "The Lord, the Lord": one before he sins and one after he sins and repents. For the Tetragrammaton, which brings everything into being, includes all the holinesses in a person — his beginning to sanctify himself a little is its final letter, and the three degrees in which he is sanctified are its first three letters — and just as he has all the holinesses before he sins, so too afterward, when he repents and is atoned.:
And our Sages of blessed memory taught in Rosh Hashanah (17b):
"אֲנִי ה' קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא, וַאֲנִי ה' אַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיָשׁוּב",
"I am Hashem before man sins, and I am Hashem after he sins and repents",
כִּי לְעוֹלָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזְרוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי סִיַּיעְתּוֹת וְקוֹרֵא הַכֹּל עַל שְׁמוֹ.
for Hashem eternally aids him with every manner of divine assistance and calls it by man's name.
וְזֶהוּ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁאַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
And this is Yom Kippur following Rosh Hashanah,
שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ אָז לוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת אַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיָשׁוּב וְנִתְכַּפֵּר הַכֹּל,
wherein the second Tablets were given after sin and repentance when all was atoned,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְשִׂמְחָה דְּסֻכּוֹת דְּהַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
and through this one merits the joy of Sukkot, which is the perfection of the hidden recesses of the heart.
וְנִקְרָא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים "שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן",
And Yom Kippur is titled "a Sabbath of solemn rest" (Shabbat Shabbaton),
דְּגַם זֶה קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא,
for this too is an inherently fixed and eternal holiness;
כִּי כַּפָּרָה זוֹ אַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו שֶׁנּוֹתֵן יָד לַפּוֹשְׁעִים,
for this atonement after sin stems purely from Hashem in His abundant mercy and grace extending a hand to transgressors,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיט.)1184 Pesachim 119a — R. Kahana said in the name of R. Yishmael son of R. Yosei, who said in the name of R. Shimon ben Lakish in the name of R. Yehuda Nesia: What is meant by "and the hands of a man were beneath their wings"? "His hand" is written [in the singular] — this is the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, spread out beneath the wings of the living creatures, to receive penitents out of the grasp of the attribute of justice. Rashi: ["From the attribute of justice":] which accuses and says, "Do not accept them" — and He accepts them in secret. Maharsha: It is His right hand, which is mercy — as in [the phrase] "His right hand is extended to receive those who return." Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTeshuvah 8): [He cites this passage in explaining the name of Elazar ben Durdaya:] "Elazar" ["God helps"] denotes the power in man for repentance, for the Blessed Name helps man, as they said, "One who comes to purify himself is assisted." The right hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, is extended to receive penitents and to raise them up from the pit so that they are not lost; therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is his help. עַל פָּסוּק (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, ח): "וִידֵי אָדָם [מִתַּחַת כַּנְפֵיהֶם]":
and as they expounded (Pesachim 119a) on the verse (Ezekiel 1:8): "And the hands of a man under their wings":
פְּשׁוּטוֹת לְקַבֵּל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּתְשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהוּא בָּא בְּמַחְתֶּרֶת לְקַבְּלָם.
they are outstretched to receive the transgressors of Israel in repentance, tunneling beneath the Throne to accept them.
וְעַל כֵּן לוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת נִיתְּנוּ בַּחֲשַׁאי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּפִי מִדַּת הַדִּין.
Therefore the second Tablets were given in secrecy, not according to the strict attribute of Justice.
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּוַודַּאי מִדַּת בְּנֵי אָדָם גַּם כֵּן אִם יִתְחָרֵט הַחוֹטֵא נֶגְדּוֹ וִיבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ מְחִילָה שֶׁיִּמְחוֹל וְלֹא יְהֵא אַכְזָר,
And although it is human nature as well that if an offender expresses remorse and seeks forgiveness one should pardon and not be cruel,
וּמִדַּת הַדִּין אֵינָהּ מִדַּת אַכְזָרִיּוּת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט הָרָאוּי;
and the attribute of Justice is not cruelty, Heaven forbid, but fair, equitable judgment;
אֲבָל זֶהוּ אִלּוּ הָיָה הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ מִתְנַחֵם וּמִתְחָרֵט,
yet that applies only when the offender himself initiates remorse and repentance;
אֲבָל שֶׁיָּבוֹא הַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַחוֹטֵא נֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁיָּבוֹא לְבַקֵּשׁ מְחִילָתוֹ –
whereas for the Supreme Sovereign to come seeking out the rebel, urging him to request pardon—
זֶה וַדַּאי אֵינוֹ כְּמִדַּת בְּנֵי אָדָם וְלֹא בְּמִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
this is certainly unlike human conduct and transcends standard judicial procedure.
וְכָל תְּשׁוּבַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר לִבּוֹ לָשׁוּב בְּהִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה הַנּוֹפְלִים בַּלֵּב,
And every repentance of a penitent is prompted by Hashem stirring his heart with thoughts of return falling within,
וְלוּלֵא זֶה לֹא הָיָה בְּיַד הָאָדָם לְעוֹרֵר עַצְמוֹ אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִלְכַּד בְּרֶשֶׁת הַיֵּצֶר.
for without this, it would not be within man's power to arouse himself once ensnared in the inclination's trap.
שֶׁאִם מִתְּחִלָּה קוֹדֶם שֶׁגָּבַר עָלָיו לֹא יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד נֶגְדּוֹ,
For if at the beginning before it overpowered him he could not withstand it,

כָּל שֶׁכֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ אַחַר שֶׁ"נַעֲשָׂה אִישׁ" (סֻכָּה נב:)1185 Sukkah 52b — Rava said: At first [Scripture] calls it a wayfarer, then it calls it a guest, and finally it calls it a man, as it is said, "And there came a wayfarer to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd to prepare for the guest," and it is written, "And he took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him." Rashi: "Wayfarer": one who passes him on the road and does not lodge with him; "guest": a lodger; "man": the master of the house. "And there came a wayfarer": this is said of David and Bathsheba, the prophet speaking to David of the evil inclination that had come upon him. Maharsha (s.v. "it calls it a wayfarer"): The incident itself follows this pattern: at first, "David arose ... and walked about on the roof" — it is called "wayfarer," as explained in Perek Chelek on this verse, where Satan appeared to him in the likeness of a bird; then, "he took her, and she came to him, and he lay with her ... and she returned to her house" — it is called "guest"; and afterwards, when Uriah was killed at David's command and he took her as his wife, it is called "man." Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv Koach HaYetzer 2): At man's creation deficiency clung to him, but not wholly, for were it wholly attached to him man could not exist at all; so it is called a "wayfarer," who passes by a man and is joined to him only somewhat, without lodging with him. If a man is drawn after it, the deficiency clings to him further and it is called a "guest," who lodges with him; and if he is drawn after it still more, it is called "man," that is, the master of the house, for then the man is not merely joined to evil but is himself deficient and evil.;
all the more so afterward, once it has "become a master" over him (Sukkah 52b);
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ, וּמְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם לָשׁוּב.
rather the Holy One in His abundant grace does not abandon him to its hand, stirring him daily to return.
וְנִמְצָא הָעִיקָּר מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
Thus the essential initiation is from Heaven,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קוֹרְאוֹ עַל שֵׁם הָאָדָם וְדִ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי" לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
except that Hashem credits it to man's name, affirming that "Israel sanctifies" Yom Kippur;
וְהוּא צוֹוֵוחַ: "שׁוּבוּ בָּנִים שׁוֹבָבִים" (יִרְמְיָה ג, יד),
and He cries out: "Return, O backsliding children" (Jeremiah 3:14),

וּ"פִתְחוּ לִי כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט וַאֲנִי וְכוּלֵי" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב)1186 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:2 — "Open for me" — R. Yasa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, open for Me one opening of repentance the size of the eye of a needle, and I will open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 20): This is like "Open for Me [an opening] like the eye of a needle and I will open for you [one] like the entrance of the Hall": they open by knowing that everything is from the Blessed One, and then the Blessed One opens the chambers of their hearts to know and understand in depth how everything is from Him. And Israel plead, "Return us to You and we will return," asking that even the opening of this wisdom come from the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 11): The mitzvah of the Chanukah light, where "the kindling makes the mitzvah," alludes to the ardor aroused in the soul by fear of the Lord. As the Sages said on "Open for me": "Open for Me one opening of repentance the size of the eye of a needle, and I will open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter" — so too the main thing is that one kindle within himself fear and awe to overcome the evil inclination, and afterward "the Lord will not abandon him into his hand." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 152): The arousal from below must come first, as the Sages said, "Open for Me [an opening] the size of the eye of a needle": the least measure of fear suffices, and then wisdom flows into his heart in proportion; through the wisdom he comes to more fear, then more wisdom comes, and so on, until there are openings [through which wagons can enter]. The early authorities added, "provided the hole goes through from side to side" — that is, the arousal to abandon sin and all worldly matters must be complete, from the depths of his heart, even if only for a single moment.,
and "Open for Me an aperture like the eye of a needle, and I will open for you portals wide as an entrance hall" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת גַּם הַפְּתִיחָה כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ,
even though in truth even that needle-thin opening originates from Him,
וְעַל יְדֵי הַבַּת קוֹל דְּ"שׁוּבוּ וְגוֹמֵר" נִתְעוֹרֵר הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב כַּיָּדוּעַ זֶה בַּסְּפָרִים.
and through the Heavenly Voice calling "Return, etc." thoughts of repentance are stirred in the heart, as known from holy books.

items.h:
Seif 4 — Yom Kippur as Fixed Holiness
Yom Kippur atones from an eternal root unique to Israel, sending sin back to the alien spiritual realm from which it came.

p: וּלְרַבִּי, דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר בְּלֹא תְּשׁוּבָה (יוֹמָא פה:),
And according to Rebbe, that Yom Kippur atones even without repentance (Yoma 85b),
זֶה וַדַּאי קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא;
this is certainly an inherently fixed and eternal holiness;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
nevertheless, it atones exclusively for Israel.
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק א':
And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah, beginning of chapter 1:
(תְּהִלִּים קלט, טז) "'יָמִים יֻצָּרוּ וְלוֹ אֶחָד בָּהֶם' – זֶה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל",
(Psalms 139:16): "'The days were fashioned, and one among them is His'—this is Yom Kippur for Israel",
וְשָׁם גַּם כֵּן עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
and there likewise regarding the Sabbath day for Israel,
דְּגַם כֵּן לֹא נִיתְּנוּ אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְגוֹי שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין נח:).
that it was also given exclusively to Israel, and a gentile who observes Shabbat incurs guilt, etc. (Sanhedrin 58b).
אֲבָל זֶהוּ לְעִנְיַן הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּנֵי אָדָם לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹבְתִים לְהִדַּמּוֹת לְיוֹצְרָם,
However, this pertains to human effort in resting to emulate their Creator,
"זֶה לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי", דְּלָהֶם לֹא נִיתַּן שְׁבִיתָה כְּלָל.
this He did not do for any nation, for unto them no active rest was granted at all.
אֲבָל מִצַּד שְׁבִיתַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ, שֶׁהִיא הַקְּדוּשָּׁה קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא דְּשַׁבָּת –
However, from the perspective of Hashem's own cosmic rest therein, which is the fixed sanctity of Shabbat—
זֶה גַּם בַּגּוֹיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (סה:):
this encompasses even gentiles, as they stated in Sanhedrin (65b):
דַּאֲבִיו שֶׁל טוּרְנוּסְרוּפּוּס לֹא עָלָה עָשָׁן מִקִּבְרוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת,
that from the grave of Turnus Rufus's father no smoke arose on Shabbat,
דְּגַם לַגּוֹיִם אֵין דָּנִין בְּשַׁבָּת;
for even gentiles are not judged in Gehinnom on Shabbat;
וְכֵן בַּעֲלַת אוֹב אַף בַּגּוֹיִם א״ע בְּשַׁבָּת.
and likewise, a spirit summoned through necromancy does not ascend on Shabbat, even if the deceased was a gentile.
כִּי שְׁבִיתַת הַשַּׁבָּת וּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ הוּא מִתְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם,
For the Sabbath's rest and holiness originate from the very Creation of the universe,
וְעֶצֶם קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ הִיא שָׁוָה לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם,
and the essential sanctity of the day itself applies equally to all inhabitants of the world,
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נְתָנוֹ מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
only that Hashem bestowed its active observance as a precious gift unto Israel.
אֲבָל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִיקַּר כַּפָּרָתוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
However, Yom Kippur's essential atonement applies exclusively to Israel alone;
וְ"הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּעֳלוֹ, כִּי כָל דְּרָכָיו מִשְׁפָּט" (דְּבָרִים לב, ד),
and "The Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice" (Deuteronomy 32:4),
וּבְוַדַּאי כֵּן הוּא מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט לְכַפֵּר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲווֹנוֹתֵיהֶם וַאֲפִילּוּ לְשֶׁאֵין שָׁבִים;
and this is assuredly true judicial equity to atone for Israel's sins even for those who have not formally repented;
כִּי גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ הָאֲמִיתִּי לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ,
for it is revealed and known before Him that our authentic will is to do His will,
וְרַק הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבַּעִיסָּה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת גּוֹרְמִים,
and only the yeast in the dough and foreign subjugation cause us to stumble,
וְכָל הַחֲטָאִים רַק מִסִּבָּתָם,
and all sins result only from these,
וְדוֹמִים רַק לַהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לָאָסָא וְעֶצֶם הָאָסָא זַךְ וְנָקִי.
resembling merely thorns encircling a myrtle, while the myrtle itself remains pure and pristine.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים: (וַיִּקְרָא טז, כב) "וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר [אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם] אֶל אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה" –
Therefore on Yom Kippur: (Leviticus 16:22) "And the goat shall bear all their iniquities unto a solitary land"—
הוּא "אֶרֶץ לֹא עָבַר בָּהּ אִישׁ" (יִרְמְיָה ב, ו),
which is "a land where no man passed" (Jeremiah 2:6),
כִּי מִשָּׁם הֵם בָּאִים וּלְשָׁם הֵם שָׁבִים לָלֶכֶת.
for from there sins originate and thither they return.
וְהַשָּׂעִיר הָרוֹמֵז לְעֵשָׂו "אִישׁ שָׂעִיר", רָצָה לוֹמַר שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת,
And the he-goat alluding to Esau "a hairy man" (ish sa'ir), denoting foreign subjugation,
נוֹשְׂאָם עִמּוֹ אֶל אַרְצוֹ,
bears them with him to his own barren land,
אֲשֶׁר שָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַשְּׂאוֹר הַמַּחְמִיץ לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
wherein lies the habitat of the leaven that sours all mankind.
כִּי שְׁנֵיהֶם חַד וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא:
For internal inclination and external exile are one, linked inextricably together:
כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ מוֹשִׁיעִים בְּהַר צִיּוֹן לִשְׁפּוֹט אֶת הַר עֵשָׂו,
when saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau,
אָז: "וְהָיְתָה לַה' הַמְּלוּכָה" (עֹבַדְיָה א, כא) עַל כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו,
then "the kingdom shall be Hashem's" (Obadiah 1:21) over all His works,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם שְׁלִיטָה אַחֶרֶת בְּשׁוּם כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹת הַלֵּב,
so that there will be no other dominion over any capacity of the heart,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַמְּלוּכָה הָאֲמִיתִּית.
which represents the essence of authentic sovereignty.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁעֲמָלֵק קַיָּים אֵין הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא יא);
And as long as Amalek exists the Throne is not whole (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 11);

רָצָה לוֹמַר, כַּיָּדוּעַ: דְּנִשְׁמָתִין דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אִתְגְּזַרוּ מִכּוּרְסְיָא (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן ו)1187 Tikkunei Zohar 23a — So too Metatron pleads merit for his birds, which are the spirits that fly into human beings: from the Throne come the souls, from this Living Creature the spirits, and from the Ofan the lower souls — and these are in Creation, Formation, and Action.,
meaning, as is known: the souls of Israel were hewn from the Supernal Throne (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 6),
וְאֵין טָהֳרָתָן שְׁלֵימָה לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסְאוֹ,
and their purity is not fully manifest for Hashem to sit upon His Throne,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז)1188 Bereshit Rabbah 47:6 — Reish Lakish said: The patriarchs are themselves the chariot, as it is said: "God ascended from upon Abraham"; "God ascended from upon him"; "and behold, the Lord stood upon him.": "הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה",
as they stated (Bereishit Rabbah 47): "The Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot",
וְכֵן כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶרְכָּבוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם.
and so too the collective of Israel forms the Chariot upon which He rests.
וְהָאָלֶ״ף הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת בְּסוֹף מִלַּת "כִּסֵּא" רוֹמֶזֶת לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם דִּגְנִיז בְּגַוֵּויהּ;
And the silent alef at the end of the word kisei
alludes to the Holy One, Master of the world, hidden within it;
וְהִיא חֲסֵרָה גַּם בַּכְּתָב כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק בָּעוֹלָם.
and it is also omitted in writing as long as the seed of Amalek endures in the world.
כִּי אוֹתִיּוֹת כַּ״ף-סַמֶּ״ךְ:
For in the letters Kaf and Samekh:
הַכַּ״ף רוֹמֶזֶת לְכֶתֶר, וְכֵן הוּא דְּמוּת הַכְּתָב,
the Kaf alludes to Keter (the Crown), corresponding to the shape of the script,

וְכֵן מוֹשְׁחִין מְלָכִים כְּמִין כַּ״ף (הוֹרָיוֹת יב1189 Horayot 12a — Our Rabbis taught: How are kings anointed? In the shape of a crown. And priests? In the shape of a chi. What is meant by “in the shape of a chi”? Rav Menashya bar Gadda said: In the shape of a Greek kaf. Rashi: "In the shape of a crown" — he goes round about [the head] with his finger in a circle, like a diadem. "In the shape of a Greek kaf" — he begins to anoint with his finger between the eyelids and draws his finger over the head, going on until he reaches the nape, in the shape of a Greek kaf..),
and thus kings are anointed in the shape of a Kaf (Horayot 12a),
וְהוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת שֶׁל הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא,
which is the crown of royalty of Him Who sits upon the Throne,
שֶׁהוּא הָרָצוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵרְצוֹן הָאָדָם,
representing the Supernal Will transcending human volition,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִשְׁפָּע וְנִמְשָׁךְ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לְמוֹחַ הָאָדָם.
whence thought flows down into the brain of man.
וְהַסַּמֶּ״ךְ רוֹמֵז לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,
And the Samekh alludes to the evil inclination,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה1190 Bereshit Rabbah 17:6 — R. Chanina son of Rav Idi said: From the beginning of the book until here no samech is written; once the woman was created, the Satan was created with her. (פָּרָשָׁה יז) עַל פָּסוּק (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, כא): "וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר":
as they expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (17) on the verse (Genesis 2:21): "and closed up (vayisgor) the flesh":
דְּבָא בִּיצִירַת הָאִשָּׁה, רוֹמֵז לְיֵצֶר הַתַּאֲוָה,
that with the creation of woman, it alludes to the inclination of desire,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ צוֹרֶךְ לְרִיבּוּי נְפָשׁוֹת,
which is the drive Hashem created because it is vital for the propagation of souls,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט:): דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא בִּטְּלוּהוּ לְגַמְרֵי.
as they noted in Yoma (69b): that therefore the Sages did not annul it completely.

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קלז1191 Zohar 1:137a — "The sister of Laban" — the sister of the evil inclination, the Aramean deceiver. As we have learned: at first, when it was befouled with sins in this world, it was called Lot; in the time to come, when it will not be befouled as before, like one who bathes and immerses away his defilement, they call it Laban ["white"]. In any case the evil inclination is not abolished from the world. And of that time it is written, "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh." What is "a heart of flesh"? R. Yehuda said: A heart to bring forth flesh, and for nothing else. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): I heard that Shittim denotes folly [shtut], which will be healed in the future — "a spring shall come forth from the house of the Lord and water the valley of Shittim" — that is, after the slaughter of the evil inclination, which is called Laban because it is whitened, as written in Midrash HaNe'elam, and as the Sages said on the verse "a heart of flesh," that it will be only a heart to bring forth flesh. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): The evil inclination was created to serve man in permitted needs that aid the service of the Blessed One — that is, once a person subdues it so that he rules over it and his heart is in his control; then the evil inclination is called Laban, for it has been whitened, as they said in Midrash HaNe'elam of the time to come, that it will not be entirely abolished but only whitened. This is like what they said on "I will give you a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh — and this is its servitude to the form of man in all the bad traits within the inclination's power, which also have some needed use. עַמּוּד א):
And so they said in the Zohar (Part I, 137a):
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא "לָבָן", דְּגַם לֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה, רַק דְּאִתְלַבַּן;
that therefore it was termed "Lavan" (white), for it will exist in the future too, only thoroughly cleansed;

וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם)1192 Zohar, Toldot 6:56 — R. Acha said: So it is. The Holy One, blessed be He, will arouse [the inclination] only for that which is needed for union, and not at every hour, to be with a man constantly as it is now, when it is always present and men sin through it — but for that union alone, and the arousal will be the arousal of the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written: “And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” What is “a heart of flesh”? R. Yehuda said: A heart to bring forth flesh, and for nothing else. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The inclination to bloodshed and anger will be nullified entirely, but the inclination of desire is needed for the service of the Lord as well; so the Zohar says it is called "white" because it is whitened and not nullified, as the Sages said, "I will give you a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh, and not for one's own pleasure. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Jacob our father "did not die," for his bed was complete, without any refuse or intent of bodily pleasure — as he said, "Give me my wife," which even the most frivolous would not say, for he intended only to raise offspring. And this is as it will be in the time to come, as is said on "I will give you a heart of flesh": a heart to bring forth flesh. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Jacob our father said, "Give me my wife," which even the most frivolous does not say, because of the shame that came after Adam's sin; but he felt no bodily pleasure and intended only to raise offspring, as it will be in the time to come, of which the Sages said on the verse, "a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh. For him this was like putting on tefillin or any mitzvah of the Torah, and shame had no place in it. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): The desire of Israel is the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the heart of Israel; even when they engage in matters of desire their intent is only for the sake of Heaven, all in holiness, and they have no heart of stone but only "a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh, as the Sages said on this verse. All the good of their heart is that through it they will beget sons, precious souls. עַל פָּסוּק (יְחֶזְקֵאל לו, כו): "וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר" – לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר1193 Zohar, Midrash HaNe'elam 137b — That is to say, for the bearing of children alone. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [In the time to come] the inclination to bloodshed and anger will be abolished entirely, but the inclination of desire is needed for the service of God as well; hence the Zohar says it is called "Lavan" [white], for it is whitened and not abolished, as the Sages said: "I will give [you] a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh, and not for one's own pleasure. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 4): Jacob our father did not die, for his bed was whole, without any dross or intent of bodily pleasure: when he said "Give me my wife" — which even the lowest of the low [would not say] — he intended only to raise offspring. This is like the time to come, as is said [in the Midrash HaNe'elam] on "I will give you a heart of flesh": a heart to bring forth flesh. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Jacob our father said "Give me [my wife]," which even the lowest of the low does not say, because of the shame that came after Adam's sin; but he felt no bodily pleasure at all and intended only to raise offspring. It was like the time to come, of which the Sages said on the verse "a heart of flesh": a heart to bring forth flesh — for him it was like putting on tefillin or any commandment of the Torah, and shame had no place in it. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Although a "good heart" denotes the longing and desire that fill the heart, the desire of Israel is the Holy One, blessed be He, and even when they engage in matters of desire their intent is only for the sake of Heaven, all in holiness: there is no heart of stone in them, only "a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh, as was said in the Pesikta on this verse. Thus the "good heart" of the righteous means that through it they will beget male children, precious souls, whereas the "good heart" of the nations is the mere filling of desire itself..
meaning as they stated on the verse (Ezekiel 36:26): "and I will give you a heart of flesh"—a heart dedicated to bringing forth progeny.
וַחֲלַל הַלֵּב הוּא עָשׂוּי דְּמוּת סַמֶּ״ךְ, וְשָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר;
And the cavity of the heart is formed in the circular shape of a Samekh, and there is the dwelling of the inclination;
וְאַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם גָּנוּז בְּגַוֵּויהּ, דְּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא "טוֹב מְאֹד".
and the Champion of the world is hidden within it, for in ultimate root it is "very good."
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׂעִיר הָרוֹמֵז לְיִצְרָא דְּכַעַס, שֶׁהוּא יִשָּׁחֵט וְלֹא יִשָּׁאֵר מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְעָנָף לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא;
Only that through the goat alluding to wrath, which will be slaughtered leaving neither root nor branch in the future;
כִּי זֶה נַחֲלַת עֵשָׂו לְבַד בִּרְצִיחָה.
for murderous bloodshed belongs exclusively to Esau.
וְהָאִשָּׁה הֵבִיאָה מִיתָה לָעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁנָּטָה לְצַד הָרַע
And woman brought death into the world through desire leaning toward evil
וְנִתְאַחֵד עִם יִצְרָא דִּרְצִיחָה,
and uniting with the murderous drive,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא מַה שֶּׁהָרַג קַיִן לְהֶבֶל וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרַם הַמִּיתָה.
whence arose Cain slaying Abel, thereby causing actual death.
וְזֶהוּ הַגּוֹרֵם לְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת,
And this is the root cause of subjugation to foreign kingdoms,
וְכֵן הֵם הַגּוֹרְמִים לִשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבַּעִיסָּה – הַכֹּל חַד, כָּל אֶחָד נִמְשָׁךְ מֵחֲבֵירוֹ.
and likewise they cause the yeast in the dough—all are one, each flowing from the other.
וְעַל כֵּן נָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר כָּל עֲווֹנוֹתָם לַעֲזָאזֵל,
Therefore the goat bore all their sins to Azazel,

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא סז:)1194 Yoma 67b — The school of R. Yishmael taught: "Azazel" — because it atones for the deed of Uzza and Azael. Rashi: "Uzza and Azael": angels of destruction who came down to earth in the days of Naamah, the sister of Tuval-Cain, and of them it is said, "the sons of God saw the daughters of men" (Genesis 6:2); that is to say, it atones for sexual transgressions. Maharsha: Rashi explains that they were angels of destruction who came down [to earth], of whom it is said, "the sons of God saw the daughters of men"; and Rashi explains similarly in Tractate Niddah, on "Sichon and Og were brothers, the sons of Shamchazai." Scripture singles out these two [in the name "Azazel"] because they were perhaps the chief ones.: לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עֻזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּתַאֲווֹת וַעֲרָיוֹת.
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Yoma 67b): to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael, which relate to lust and immorality.
וְהוּא "אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה",
And this is "a cut-off land" (eretz gezeirah),
דְּ"אֶרֶץ" הוּא רוֹמֵז לְנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹם הַמְקַבֵּל לַיּוֹשְׁבִים,
for "earth/land" alludes to the feminine recipient as is known, which receives its inhabitants,
וְ"אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה" אֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל כְּלוּם, רוֹמֵז לְאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים;
while a barren, cut-off land receives nothing, alluding to the unfaithful woman;
אַף שֶׁמִּצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן נִרְאֶה שֶׁאַדְּרַבָּה הִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת הַכֹּל, בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת כְּלוּם.
for though superficially she appears to receive all, in truth she receives nothing enduring.
וְכֵן הֵם כָּל אַרְצוֹת הָעַמִּים צוֹר וַחֲבֵרוֹתֶיהָ,
And such are all the lands of the nations, Tyre and her companions,
דְּתַמָּן שׂוֹבְעָא תַּמָּן זוּלָא, וְחוֹשְׁבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהֵם תַּכְלִית הַיִּשּׁוּב וְעִיקָּרוֹ;
wherein there is food and cheap indulgence, imagining in this world that they are civilization's summit;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם עִיקַּר אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה וּמִדְבַּר שְׁמָמָה מִכֹּל,
whereas in truth they are the ultimate barren cut-off land and desolation,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין שָׁם יִשּׁוּב הָאֲמִיתִּי הַקַּיָּים לָעַד.
since authentic, eternal civilization does not abide there.
וְזֶהוּ "מִדְבַּר הָעַמִּים" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ, לה),
And this is the "wilderness of the peoples" (Ezekiel 20:35),
כִּי הֵם לְבָבָם כְּמִדְבָּר, שֶׁאֵינָן בִּכְלַל יִשּׁוּב וּבְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה;
for their heart is like a wilderness, excluded from holy civilization and derekh eretz that precedes the Torah;
דְּאוֹתָם שֶׁבְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, הֵם מַכִּירִים מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וַעֲתִידִים לִהְיוֹת עֲבָדִים לָהֶם;
for those who possess authentic derekh eretz recognize the virtue of Israel and their Father in Heaven, and are destined to be their servants;
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ: לְהַכִּיר עֶרְכּוֹ וּמַעֲלַת מִי שֶׁגָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ.
and this is the essence of derekh eretz: recognizing one's own standing and the superiority of one greater than oneself.
אֲבָל שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַשָּׂעִיר "אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים לְזָקֵן" (דְּבָרִים כח, נ),
However, tyrannical subjugation stems from the he-goat "who will not regard the person of the elder" (Deuteronomy 28:50),
וְאֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּמִשְׁכָּנוֹ בְּאֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה;
lacking all derekh eretz, its habitation being in the cut-off land;
וּלְשָׁם נוֹשֵׂא כָּל עֲווֹנוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and thither it carries all the iniquities of the children of Israel,
כִּי אֵינוֹ מִשֶּׁלָּהֶם בְּעֶצֶם כְּלָל, רַק מִשָּׁם הֵם בָּאִים.
for these sins are not intrinsically theirs at all, originating entirely from that corrupt sphere.

items.h:
Seif 5 — Why Repentance Belongs Uniquely to Israel
Israel's inherited holiness allows sin to remain external to essence, unlike the nations whose spiritual identity is not rooted there.

p: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ שָׁבִים –
In contrast, regarding the idolatrous nations, even if they repent—

לֹא נִתְּנוּ תְּשׁוּבָה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא הַאֲזִינוּ ד)1195 Midrash Tanchuma, Ha'Azinu 4 — It is written, "The Lord shall lift up His countenance toward you" (Numbers 6:26), and another verse says, "Who lifts up no countenance" (Deuteronomy 10:17). If one repents, He lifts up His countenance toward him. Might this apply to all? Scripture therefore says "toward you" — and not to another nation.,
repentance was granted solely to Israel (Midrash Tanchuma, Ha'azinu 4),
אֲבָל לָהֶם אֵין כַּפָּרָה כְּלָל, כִּי אֶצְלָם הַחֵטְא בְּעֶצֶם.
yet for them there is no atonement at all, because with them sin is rooted in their very essence.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם לְרַבִּי נִקְרָא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי",
Therefore, even according to Rebbe, Yom Kippur is termed sanctified by Israel,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי עַצְמָם עַד שֶׁהֵם קְדוֹשִׁים בְּעֶצֶם –
for through sanctifying themselves until they are intrinsically holy—
דְּדָבָר זֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָבוֹת לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת –
which comes through the spiritual exertion of the Patriarchs for their descendants and all generations—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִקְדוּשַׁת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
through this they merited the sanctity of Yom Kippur.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּכַפֵּר גַּם לְשֶׁאֵין שָׁבִים, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת,
And even though it atones even for those who have not repented, which is why it is called Shabbat,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קוֹרְאוֹ עַל שְׁמָם דְּהֵם מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ,
nevertheless Hashem, blessed be He, credits it to their name as that which they sanctify,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה בְּעֶצֶם לִהְיוֹת קָדוֹשׁ מִלֵּידָה וּבֶטֶן וְהֵרָיוֹן וַדַּאי הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
even though essential sanctity from birth, womb, and conception is certainly solely through Hashem,
וּכְטַעַם "אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתָּ בְּאַבְרָהָם" (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ז).
mirroring the verse "Whom You chose in Abraham" (Nehemiah 9:7).
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מֵעַצְמוֹ,
Even though he was the first to exert effort on his own,
