דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא בְּרֵישׁ חֲגִיגָה (ג.): "תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים";
which is why he is titled at the beginning of Chagigah (3a): "the first of converts";
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר שֶׁזָּכָה לְשֵׁם הָאֶזְרָחִי לִהְיוֹת נִבְנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
nevertheless, after meriting the title of native-born (Ezrachi) to have the Jewish nation built from him,
נַעֲשָׂה גַּם הוּא אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא גֵּר, רַק כְּאִילּוּ הָיָה מִלֵּידָה כֵּן.
he too became an Ezrach in Israel and not a convert, as though he had been so from birth.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁעוֹרְרוֹ לְכָךְ,
For in truth his entire awakening and striving came through Hashem Who stirred him toward this,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב)1196 Bereshit Rabbah 2:3 — The Holy One, blessed be He, said: How long shall the world conduct itself in darkness? Let the light come. "God said: Let there be light" — this is Abraham. That is what is written: "Who roused righteousness from the east, called him to his foot?" Do not read it "roused" but "illumined." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Noach 7): "Let there be light — this is Abraham," as it says, "Who roused righteousness from the east" — do not read "roused" but "illumined": the arousal came about because the Blessed One made the light shine upon Abraham, and through this came the awakening from his own side, which stirred his heart [to ask] "Who created these?" The "do not read" does not emend the text: "roused" stands as written, but since there must be an awakening from below, the Blessed One rouses by sending light into the heart, through which the awakening comes from the person's side — and this is called "lending" [the light]. עַל פָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה מא, ב): "מִי הֵעִיר מִמִּזְרָח".
as our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 2) on the verse (Isaiah 41:2): "Who stirred up from the east."
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן נִתְלָה בְּסוֹד הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה,
And this also hinges upon the mystery of Foreknowledge and Free Will,
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מָסַר הַבְּחִירָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם,
that although Hashem granted free will unto mankind,
הֲרֵי מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה הַכֹּל שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
behold, from the perspective of Divine Foreknowledge everything belongs to Hashem, blessed be He.

items.h:
Seif 6 — Foreknowledge, Free Will, and the High Holy Days
Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur reveal Israel's goodness as fixed in divine foreknowledge beyond manifest human effort.

p: וְהַיְדִיעָה דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא קוֹדֶם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
And the Foreknowledge of Rosh Hashanah is prior to spiritual exertion,
מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת טוֹב וְצַדִּיק מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.
concerning that which is destined to be good and righteous from its root.
וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא אַחַר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
While Yom Kippur is after spiritual exertion,
וְגַם אַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח),
and even after man sins, nonetheless "they shall be as white as snow" (Isaiah 1:18),
לְפִי שֶׁהֵם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית (שַׁבָּת פט:);
because they are like these years pre-ordered from the six days of Creation (Shabbat 89b);
הַיְינוּ קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים מֵעוֹלָם מִצַּד אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning fixed and enduring from eternity through the truth of Hashem's will,
וְנִמְצָא מֵעוֹלָם לֹא חָטְאוּ וְלֹא סָרוּ כְּלוּם מֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹנוֹ.
and it emerges that they never sinned nor turned aside at all from the truth of His will.
וְעַל כֵּן אֵינָם בִּכְלַל הַמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁהֵם מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי" מִצַּד הַבְּחִירָה וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַנַּעֲשָׂה.
Therefore they are not included within the festivals which are sanctified by Israel through free will and exertion enacted.
אֲבָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא מַה דְּ"יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי" מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה,
However, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are what Israel sanctifies through Divine Foreknowledge,
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בָּהֶם שִׂמְחָה נִגְלֵית, כֵּיוָון דְּאֵינוֹ מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם הַנִּגְלוֹת.
and therefore overt festive joy does not apply to them, since they do not stem from their manifest exertion.

items.h:
Seif 7 — Rosh Hashanah: Fear as True Security
Israel seeks awe of Hashem, and hidden trust beneath judgment becomes the covered light of the renewed moon.

p: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הוּא פַּחַד,
And on Rosh Hashanah the manifest revelation is fear and awe,
וְאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים: "וּבְכֵן תֵּן פַּחְדְּךָ עַל כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיךָ",
and we plead: "And so, place Your fear upon all Your works",
כִּי זֶהוּ הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים:
for this is the difference between Israel and the nations:
שֶׁהֵם רוֹצִים בְּשַׁלְוָה וּבוֹרְחִים מִפַּחַד וַאֲפִילּוּ מִפַּחַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
that they desire worldly ease and flee from fear, even from the fear of Hashem;
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רוֹצִים בְּפַחַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
yet the children of Israel desire the awe of Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי זֶהוּ אֲמִיתַּת הַשַּׁלְוָה וְהַשִּׂמְחָה וַהֲסָרַת כָּל מִינֵי פַּחַד.
for this is the truth of tranquility and joy, and the removal of all other anxieties.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה1197 Avodah Zarah 65a — Rava found Bar Sheshach sitting in a bath, amid great luxury. He said to him: Have you, in the world to come, anything like this? He said to him: Ours is better than this. He said: Could there be anything greater than this? He said to him: You have the fear of the kingdom upon you; we shall have no fear of the kingdom upon us. He said to him: As for me, what fear of the kingdom is there upon me? While they were sitting, a royal officer came and said to Bar Sheshach: Rise, the king summons you. As he went out he said to Rava: May the eye that wishes to look upon evil for you burst. Rava said to him: Amen — and the eye of Bar Sheshach burst. Rashi: "Sitting in a bath" — in a bath of roses. "May the eye that wishes to look upon evil for you burst" — may the eye that craves to see your misfortune be torn out; for the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfils all your desires, so that even your casual speech proves true. (סה.):
And as they stated in Avodah Zarah (65a):
"אַתּוּן אִית לְכוּ אֵימְתָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא",
"You have the fear of the earthly government",
דִּבְתַכְלִית הַשִּׂמְחָה וְשַׁלְוַות תַּעֲנוּגֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם
for at the height of joy and the worldly pleasures which the gentiles had,
בָּא פַּחַד מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם וְעִרְבֵּב אֶת הַכֹּל;
the fear of a mortal king intervened and disrupted everything;
אֲבָל אֲנַן לֵית לַן אֵימְתָא דְּמַלְכּוּתָא,
whereas we bear no fear of mortal empire,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אָתָּה,
since we have no King but You,
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵימָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּטֶלֶת עָלֵינוּ – זֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שַׁלְוָתֵנוּ,
and that His dread rests upon us—this is the pinnacle of our inner peace,
וְאָנוּ מְצַפִּים וּמְבַקְשִׁים עַל זֶה: "וְיַחֵד לְבָבֵנוּ לְאַהֲבָה וּלְיִרְאָה אֶת שְׁמֶךָ".
and we yearn and plead for this: "and unite our hearts to love and fear Your Name."
וְזֶה סוֹד רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁהַשִּׂמְחָה מוּסְתֶּרֶת בְּפַחַד;
And this is the secret of Rosh Hashanah, that joy is hidden within awe;
כִּי הַיְדִיעָה שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת עוֹמֵד בְּפַחַד עַל כָּל פְּסִיעָה שֶׁלֹּא יִטֶּה מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for Foreknowledge prior to exertion stands, on the manifest level, in trembling over every step lest one deviate from Hashem's will.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ס.)1198 Berakhot 60a — A certain student was walking behind R. Yishmael son of R. Yosei in the marketplace of Zion. He saw that he was afraid. He said to him: You are a sinner, for it is written "The sinners in Zion are afraid." He said to him: But is it not written "Happy is the man who fears always"? He said to him: That verse is written concerning matters of Torah. Rashi: "That verse is written concerning matters of Torah" — "Happy is the man who fears always" means one who fears lest his learning be forgotten from him, for on that account he goes back and reviews it constantly. Maharsha: As Rashi explains; and the same is true wherever there is real ground to fear a calamity. The rebuke is directed only at fear that has no cause, as Tosafot write in Gittin 55a. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaBitachon 1): One who is afraid is the opposite of one who trusts in Him, blessed be He, of whom Solomon said, "the fear of man brings a snare, but he who trusts in the Lord shall be set on high." Moreover, fear itself brings sufferings upon a man: a vessel that is whole and strong need not fear breaking, but a flawed one breaks easily, so that a man's fear is itself evidence that he is not whole but is like a cracked vessel — and this is why he was told "you are a sinner," for it is sin that leaves a man liable to breaking. With Torah it is otherwise, for with respect to the Torah a man is always reckoned breakable, as they said that words of Torah are as hard to acquire as gold and as easy to break as vessels of glass; and therefore "happy is the man who fears always" is written of matters of Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 11): Jacob, whose attribute was Torah, was seized with fear on going down to Egypt lest his sons, in exile, be unable to engage in Torah and the evil inclination rule over them. This follows what they said: "The sinners in Zion are afraid" — but is it not written "Happy is the man who fears always"? — that is written concerning words of Torah; that is, happy is he who always fears lest he have any interruption from the study of Torah.:
And as they said (Berakhot 60a):
(מִשְׁלֵי כח, יד) "'אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד' – הַהוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב".
(Proverbs 28:14): "'Happy is the man that fears always'—that is written regarding words of Torah."
וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהוּא זְמַן בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם, הוּא זְמַן יְרִידַת הַסְּפִינָה לַיָּם,
And Rosh Hashanah, the time of the world's Creation, is like the moment a ship sets sail upon the sea,
שֶׁהִיא בְּפַחַד שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אֵיזֶה רוּחוֹת יַעַבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ.
surrounded by fear since one knows not what turbulent winds will sweep over it.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאָנוּ נָכוֹן לִבֵּנוּ בָּטוּחַ בַּה' שֶׁיּוֹצִיא כָּאוֹר מִשְׁפָּטֵנוּ;
Only that our heart is steadfast, trusting in Hashem that He will bring forth our judgment as the light;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא "חַג שֶׁהַחֹדֶשׁ מִתְכַּסֶּה בּוֹ",
and therefore it is "the festival on which the moon is covered",
הַיְינוּ חִידּוּשׁ אוֹר דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶעְלָם וּמְכֻסֶּה עֲדַיִן,
meaning that the renewed light of the Congregation of Israel is still veiled and covered,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאָנוּ בְּטוּחִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אוֹר לִנְתִיבָתֵנוּ.
save that we trust in Hashem, blessed be He, that there will be light for our path.

items.h:
Seif 8 — Hashem Is My Light
Rosh Hashanah's concealed moon teaches that Hashem Himself illuminates the path of service through darkness and uncertainty.

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא1199 Vayikra Rabbah 21:4 — “The Lord is my light and my salvation” — “my light” on Rosh Hashanah, and “my salvation” on Yom Kippur. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 27): "My light" is on Rosh Hashanah because then illumination comes to the heart from the revelation of the Kingdom of Heaven, and it is "my light" specifically: a man who lights a lamp lets all use its light, but the Holy One, blessed be He, lets His children see while His enemies do not — so on Rosh Hashanah fear falls upon the nations, while Israel receive an illumination of the heart that brings them near to the Blessed One. Through that point of truth revealed in them on Rosh Hashanah, the Blessed One guides the souls of Israel through the Ten Days of Repentance until the salvation is fully revealed on Yom Kippur., ד) עַל פָּסוּק (תְּהִלִּים כז, א): "אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי":
And this is what they expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4) on the verse (Psalms 27:1): "Hashem is my light and my salvation":
"אוֹרִי" – בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
"my light"—on Rosh Hashanah,
שֶׁאָז הַחֹדֶשׁ מִתְכַּסֶּה וְאֵין אוֹר גָּלוּי עֲדַיִן כְּלָל;
for then the moon is concealed and no manifest light is visible yet at all;
רַק מִצַּד הַיְדִיעָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הוּא אוֹמֵר דְּגַם בְּכִיסּוּי כָּזֶה יֵשׁ אוֹר,
only through Hashem's Foreknowledge, He reveals that even within such covering light persists,
וְהוּא "אוֹרִי" לְהָאִיר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
and He is "my light" to illuminate our spiritual striving,
דִּלְזֶה צָרִיךְ אוֹר מֵאִיר לְרַגְלוֹ וּנְתִיבוֹ לָדַעַת בְּאֵיזֶה דֶּרֶךְ מְהַלֵּךְ.
for which a person needs a light shining for his feet and path to know which way to walk.
וְהָאוֹר בָּא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹתִיּוֹת רְאִיָּה,
And the light comes through the power of reverence (yir'ah), which shares the letters of vision (re'iyah),
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת מַחֲוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק
And through this one merits that Isaac—
[דַּרְגָּא דְּפַחַד יִצְחָק כַּיָּדוּעַ]
the spiritual rung of the Awe of Isaac, as is known

הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ (שַׁבָּת פט:)1200 Shabbat 89b — They begin and say: "For You are our father." Isaac says to them: Before you praise me, praise the Holy One, blessed be He. And Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, with their own eyes. Immediately they lift their eyes on high and say: "You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old is Your name." Rashi: "For you are our father" — they said this facing Yitzchak, and he told them: Point toward the Holy One, blessed be He, for He is your father. Maharsha: Yitzchak divides the sins: those between Israel and the Omnipresent the Holy One, blessed be He, is to bear, and those between them and other people, which require appeasement, he will bear; "and if You say all are upon me" — that all are between them and other people — "I offered my life before You," and so can bear them all. Therefore they say to Yitzchak, "For you are our father," since he bears all their sins by the merit of having offered himself; but Yitzchak points them to the Holy One, blessed be He, for all their sins may be between them and Him, and at once they say, "You, O Lord, are our Father," that He atone for His Name's sake. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 13): "If You say all are upon me, I offered my life before You": since Yitzchak gave himself over to the Blessed One, he belongs to Him entirely, and therefore he bears their iniquity entirely. Israel lift their eyes to Yitzchak as though he were their redeemer, but this is not so — through his attribute they are joined to the Blessed One, but the atonement itself is His; and Yitzchak, who is never separated from Him, shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, "in their eyes," that is, through the attribute of judgment, which is his. Then they lift their eyes on high and say "our Redeemer," for He Himself redeems them, and not through another. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): "And if You say it is all upon me," that is, that the existence of the dross comes only from my side, because there is dross in me, "I offered up my soul," and I am a perfect burnt-offering before You, with no dross in me from myself; it comes only from the spreading-forth that the Blessed One willed in creating the world. When it is revealed that everything comes from the root, from the Blessed One, the screen that the sins made between Israel and their Father in Heaven is removed, and through this "the Holy One, blessed be He, is shown to them before their eyes," even though "man shall not see Me and live": for the Sages said that at the time of death they see, since then the screen of this world is removed, and so too with this revelation of "half upon You" the screen of this world will be removed. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:83): The Torah was given specifically to the earth, the place of concealment, where face-to-face recognition is not known, and so one must judge only by the intellect of one in concealment; and face-to-face recognition comes from the side of strength [gevurah], in the sense of "Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes." Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): The recognition of "I am the Lord your God" is the recognition of "You are with me," and this is from the side of Isaac, as they said, "Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes": complete seeing, face to face, comes through Isaac, for this apprehension, clear to the eye and in distinct levels, is from the attribute of contraction, which contracts apprehension into measures and levels. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 190): The root of Joseph is fear of sin, which is guarding the eye, and [fear, yirah,] has the letters of "seeing" [reiyah], in the sense of "Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes," for this comes from the power of Isaac and from his attribute. Beis Yaakov (Lech Lecha 17): [The blessing "Who revives the dead" is in the mystery of Isaac,] as the Gemara says: Isaac said to them, "Before you praise me, praise the Holy One, blessed be He," and Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes. This alludes to the resurrection of the dead: it is not in the power of any creature in the world to show a person his foundation and the root from which he was hewn, to heal the root of his deficiency and comfort him in his grief; this was entrusted to no intermediary but given into the hand of the Blessed One alone. Sod Yesharim (Sukkos 73): Isaac's attribute is always to hear from the depth of the supernal root, and the sight of the surface hue was a small thing to him; so the Gemara says that the Holy One says to Abraham and to Jacob, "Your children have sinned," but Isaac answered, "[They are] Your children, and not mine," for he always looked to the depth of the supernal root, where Israel are always called children of the Omnipresent, and therefore every kind of salvation for Israel is aroused from his side. Even the salvation that cannot be recognized in this world except by hearing, Isaac will show in the future to sight as well, so that it will be explicitly recognized upon all the hues of Israel's garments how His light dwells within them, as the Gemara says, "And Isaac shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes.";
points out the Holy One, blessed be He, directly to their eyes (Shabbat 89b);
וְיִזְכֶּה לְהָאָרַת פָּנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּאִיר לוֹ לִרְאוֹת בְּאֵיזֶה דֶּרֶךְ מְהַלֵּךְ,
and he merits the shining of His countenance to see which path he treads,
וְיָאִיר לוֹ בְּחֶשְׁכַּת לַיְלָה וְהַחֹדֶשׁ הַמִּתְכַּסֶּה.
illuminating for him through the darkness of night and the covered moon.

items.h:
Seif 9 — Hashem Is My Salvation
Yom Kippur rescues Israel after failure, removing accusation and revealing a heart purified from the evil inclination.

p: "וְיִשְׁעִי" – בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה שָׁם),
"And my salvation"—on Yom Kippur (Vayikra Rabbah ibid.),
זֶהוּ הַיְשׁוּעָה אַחַר שֶׁחָטָא וּכְבָר נִכְשַׁל בַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלוֹת,
this being the salvation after one sinned and stumbled in dark alleyways,
וְנָפַל בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לַמָּקוֹם שֶׁנָּפַל;
falling into the valley of the shadow of death, Heaven forbid, wherever he fell;
הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹשִׁיעוֹ בְּעֵת צָרָה וּמַצִּילוֹ וּפוֹדֵהוּ מִכָּל מִינֵי רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
Hashem saves him in the hour of distress, delivering and redeeming him from all evil, Heaven forbid,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַיְשׁוּעָה עַד שֶׁמֵּעַתָּה "מִמִּי אִירָא".
which is the absolute summit of salvation, such that from now on "whom shall I fear?"
כִּי כְּבָר נִשְׁלַם שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָרֵא אֶלָּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the perfection of awe of Rosh Hashanah is completed wherein he fears none but Hashem,
וְאֵין לִי לִירָא עוֹד מִשּׁוּם בְּרִיָּה וּמִשּׁוּם דָּבָר בָּעוֹלָם:
and one has no need to fear any creature or entity in the world:
לֹא מִשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבַּעִיסָּה וְלֹא מִשִּׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת,
neither from the leaven in the dough nor from the subjugation of empires,
כִּי כְּבָר הוּא צַדִּיק וְנוֹשָׁע.
for he is already righteous and delivered.
וּלְכָךְ אָז הַשִּׂמְחָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת יוֹתֵר,
And therefore joy is then far more manifest,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ1201 Taanit 26b — R. Shimon ben Gamliel said: Israel had no festivals as joyous as the fifteenth of Av and the Day of Atonement, for on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out and dance in the vineyards. And what would they say? Young man, lift up your eyes and see what you choose for yourself. Do not set your eyes on beauty; set your eyes on family. “Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain; a woman who fears the Lord — she shall be praised.” And it says: “Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her in the gates.” Rashi: "And dance": as in "to dance in the dances" (Judges 21:21). Maharsha (on 31a): The Mishnah's "Young man, lift up your eyes and see... do not set your eyes on beauty" accords with what is said in [Kiddushin, ch.] HaIsh Mekadesh, that a man may not betroth a woman until he has seen her: not for the sake of beauty, since it says "do not set your eyes on beauty," but so that he sees that she has no blemish or unsightly feature. Actions fall into three kinds, the good, the pleasant, and the useful: in the baraita the beautiful maidens urge the pleasant, those of distinguished family the good, and the unattractive ones the useful, but the Mishnah records only the party that urged choosing the good. (תַּעֲנִית כו:): "לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי [כְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים],
as they stated (Ta'anit 26b): "There were no days as joyful for Israel, etc., as Yom Kippur,
שֶׁבָּהֶן בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאוֹת וְחוֹלוֹת וְכוּלֵי";
wherein the daughters of Israel would go out and dance in the vineyards, etc.";
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַמִּצְוָה הַנִּגְלֵית בּוֹ הוּא אַדְּרַבָּה לְעַנּוֹת נֶפֶשׁ,
even though the manifest commandment of the day is, on the contrary, to afflict the soul,
הַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל:
this is because this represents the true summit of joy for Israel:
לֹא עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וְעִינּוּגֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
not achieved through eating, drinking, and mundane physical pleasures.
וְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיִתְכַּפֵּר, אָז זוֹכֶה לִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִים שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר (בְּרָכוֹת לד:);
And after one sins and is atoned for, he merits the place where penitents stand, which is greater (Berakhot 34b);
כִּי הַצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא עֲדַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַשִּׂיג שִׂמְחָה עַל יְדֵי עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּשֶׁלּוֹקְחָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם;
for the complete tzaddik who never sinned in this world attains joy through worldly elements when directing them for the sake of Heaven;
וְזֶהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת וְכֵן קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת דִּקְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא.
and this is the sanctity of the festivals, as well as the inherently fixed holiness of Shabbat.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת "עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" גַּם כֵּן,
For in truth "Your people are all righteous" as well,
דְּיֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כָּל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת,
in that within every individual of Israel reside all the spiritual gradations;

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים בְּנִדָּה (יד.)1202 Niddah 14a — It was likewise taught: Camel riders are all wicked; sailors are all righteous; donkey drivers — some of them wicked and some of them righteous. [Tosafot: But in Kiddushin 82a it is said that camel drivers are for the most part fit and donkey drivers for the most part robbers. One may answer that here it speaks of those who ride, and on account of [lustful] thought, whereas there it does not speak of riders but of those who load their goods upon the camels and go far on foot in a place of danger.] Rashi: Camel riders — their members are warmed against the flesh of the camel and they emit seed. Sailors are all righteous — because they dwell in danger, and their hearts are turned to their Father in Heaven. Tosafos (s.v. “camel riders are all wicked; donkey drivers, some wicked and some righteous”): In the chapter “Asara Yochasin” it is said that camel drivers are for the most part fit and donkey drivers for the most part robbers. One may answer that here it speaks of those who ride, and on account of [lustful] thought, whereas there it does not speak of riders but of those who load their merchandise upon the camels and walk far on foot in a place of danger; and donkey drivers [are called robbers] because they deal deceitfully in buying and selling. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “sailors are all righteous”): The mishna at the end of “Asara Yochasin” says that sailors are for the most part pious, but that is said with regard to robbery, for they also practice the ways of piety with those who are with them in the ship. Here, however, the matter is thoughts of transgression, and in that respect they are not pious, since no man escapes a sinful thought on any day; but they are righteous, for they do not arouse themselves deliberately, out of their dread of the water. עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "הַגַּמָּלִין כּוּלָּם רְשָׁעִים וְרוּבָּן כְּשֵׁרִים":
following what the early commentators wrote in Niddah (14a) on the dictum: "camel drivers are all wicked yet most are kosher":
דְּהָא וְהָא אִיתְנְהוּ, וּלְגַבֵּי דְּהָא נִקְרָא צַדִּיקִים וּבְהָא רְשָׁעִים.
that both dimensions exist simultaneously: in one aspect they are righteous, and in another wicked.
וְכֵן כָּל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְווֹת כְּרִמּוֹן (עֵירוּבִין יט.),
And likewise all transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate (Eruvin 19a),
וּמִצַּד אוֹתָן מִצְווֹת נִקְרְאוּ צַדִּיקִים, וּמִצַּד הַחֲטָאִים הֵם בַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה;
and on account of those mitzvot they are called righteous, while on account of the sins they are penitents;
וְאֵין יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג עוֹד כָּל כָּךְ שִׂמְחָה עַל יְדֵי עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְגַּשְּׁמוּ אֶצְלָם,
yet they can no longer attain joy so easily through worldly matters which have already become coarsened for them,
וְגַם כִּי "אֵין קָטֵיגוֹר נַעֲשֶׂה סָנֵיגוֹר" (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כו.).
and also because "an accuser cannot become an advocate" (Rosh Hashanah 26a).
אֲבָל הִנֵּה הֵם מִצַּד הַזֶּה אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַכַּפָּרָה
However, through this dimension, following repentance and atonement,
מַשִּׂיגִים לְאוֹר יוֹתֵר גָּבוֹהַּ וְהַשָּׂגַת שִׂמְחָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁמֵּעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
they attain a far loftier light and total joy reflecting the World to Come,
וְלֹא מִצַּד הֲנָאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וַחֲמוּדוֹתָיו, וְלִהְיוֹת דּוֹמִין לְמַלְאָכִים.
unconnected to physical indulgence, becoming like the ministering angels.
וּבִזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים הָיוּ הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת פּוֹעֲלִים כֵּן בְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And when the Temple stood, the sacrifices effected this within the hearts of Israel,
שֶׁהָיוּ בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן דּוֹמִים לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת;
so that they genuinely resembled the ministering angels;

כִּי הַשָּׂטָן הוּא יֵצֶר רָע (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.)1203 Bava Batra 16a — Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death. He is the Satan — as it is written, "And the Satan went out from before the Lord." He is the evil inclination — it is written there, "only evil all the day," and it is written here, "only do not put forth your hand against him." He is the Angel of Death — as it is written, "only spare his life," which shows that his life stands in his hand. Rashi: "Evidently his life rests in his hand" — it lies with Satan to take the soul, and God warned him not to take it. Maharsha: Our texts misquote the verse: it reads "only [akh] spare his life," not "only [rak]." The verbal analogy holds nonetheless, since "only [akh]" and "only [rak]" are alike terms of limitation. The hint in it is this: "only evil all the day" — let a man limit his evil inclination and master it, and then "only spare his life" — the Holy One, blessed be He, will limit the power of the angel of death, that he not rule over his soul. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14): [At Sinai,] when neither death nor the Satan ruled over [Israel], the whole original flaw from the serpent was repaired; and since death was annulled, the evil inclination was annulled entirely, as it says, "He is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death." Beis Yaakov (Bereishis 63): As the Gemara says, "It was taught: he descends and leads astray, ascends and provokes, takes permission and takes the soul … he is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the angel of death": that is, the sin itself is the punishment, and they are not separate at all. At first a person is stirred to sin and drawn after it, and when he sinks into the sin until he commits it without any pleasure, that itself is the punishment — being separated from life and sunk wholly beneath the evil.,
for Satan is the evil inclination (Bava Batra 16a),

וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּלֵית לֵיהּ רְשׁוּתָא לְאַסְטֹונֵי (יוֹמָא כ.)1204 Yoma 20a — And what did Satan say? He said to him: On the Day of Atonement Satan has no license to accuse. From where is this known? Rami bar Chama said: The numerical value of "ha-Satan" is three hundred and sixty-four. For three hundred and sixty-four days he has license to accuse; on the Day of Atonement he has no license to accuse. Maharsha (s.v. "And what did Satan say"): Although it is well known in the Midrashim that on the Day of Atonement Satan has no license to accuse, because [Israel] are then cleansed of sin, [the question is:] now, when several sins are committed on the Day of Atonement through [the custom of] keeping awake, what does Satan say? And he answered that even so he has no license on the Day of Atonement, for the numerical value of "ha-Satan" is three hundred and sixty-four.,
and on Yom Kippur when he has no license to accuse (Yoma 20a),
הָיָה נִשְׁלָף גַּם כֵּן יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
the evil inclination was likewise extracted from the hearts of the children of Israel.

items.h:
Seif 10 — The Daughters of Israel and the Heart of Flesh
Yom Kippur's purity makes even delicate encounters free of impropriety, exposing sin as an alien intrusion.

p: וְעַל כֵּן אָז הָיוּ בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל חוֹלוֹת וְאוֹמְרוֹת: "בָּחוּר שָׂא עֵינֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי",
Therefore the daughters of Israel would dance and declare: "Young man, lift up your eyes, etc.",
שֶׁזֶּה נִרְאֶה כִּפְרִיצוּת גְּדוֹלָה,
which might appear on the surface as great levity;
וְאֵיךְ לֹא מִיחוּ בָּהֶם חֲכָמִים, וְאַדְּרַבָּה סִפְּרוּ לִשְׁבַח וּלְמִנְהָג הָגוּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל?
and how could the Sages not protest, but rather relate it with praise as an honorable custom in Israel?
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אָז בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָיוּ הַכֹּל מַרְגִּישִׁים בְּעֶצֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר,
However in truth, on Yom Kippur all felt the essence of a heart of flesh,
בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה נִיכָּר לַכֹּל שֶׁאֵין בְּדָבָר זֶה שׁוּם פְּרִיצוּת כְּלָל.
such that it was obvious to all that there was no trace of impropriety whatsoever.

וְעַל כֵּן לְעִנְיַן הַנְּעִירָה בְּלֵיל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא יט:)1205 Yoma 19b — The notables of Jerusalem would not sleep the whole night, so that the High Priest should hear the sound of the din and sleep not overtake him. It was taught: Abba Shaul said: In the outlying provinces too they would do so, in memory of the Temple — except that there they would come to sin. Rashi: "Of the notables of Jerusalem": some of the eminent men of Jerusalem would do so, not sleeping. "Except that they would sin": men and women would make merry together and come to transgression.:
And therefore regarding the staying awake on the night of Yom Kippur they stated (Yoma 19b):
דְּגַם בַּגּוֹלָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כֵּן אֶלָּא שֶׁחוֹטְאִין,
that in the Diaspora they also practiced this, but people sinned,
אֲבָל בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ חוֹטְאִין כְּלָל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
whereas in the era of the Temple they did not sin at all on Yom Kippur.
רַק מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
Only that since the destruction of the Temple,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם עִיצוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם מְכַפֵּר וּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ לֹא סָרָה,
even though the sanctity of the day itself atones and its holiness has never departed,
וּבַשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל הוּא מַמָּשׁ כְּמִקּוֹדֶם,
and in the Heavens above reality remains exactly as before,
וְעַל כֵּן לֵית לֵיהּ רְשׁוּתָא לְאַשְׂטֹונֵי שֶׁהַהַשְׂטָנָה לְמַעְלָה אֵין בְּכֹחוֹ –
wherefore the Accuser has no permission to prosecute Above—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהֲסָתָה לְמַטָּה לֹא נִיטְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ.
nevertheless, inciting below was not entirely stripped from him.
לְפִי שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לְמַטָּה בָּטְלוּ הַמַּעֲשִׂים דַּעֲבוֹדַת הַיּוֹם בַּפּוֹעַל וּנְשִׂיאַת הַשָּׂעִיר הָעֲווֹנוֹת,
Because on the manifest level below, the physical sacrificial rites and the goat bearing away iniquities ceased,
וְעַל כֵּן חָטְאוּ.
and therefore they stumbled into sin.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר עַל זֶה (בְּרֵאשִׁית ד, ז): "לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ",
And Hashem stated regarding this (Genesis 4:7): "sin couches at the door",
שֶׁהוּא מֵהֲסָתַת הַיֵּצֶר וְשֶׁאֵין לְהַעֲנִישׁ כְּלָל עַל זֶה;
which derives from the external instigation of the inclination, for which they should not be punished;
דְּזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן כַּפָּרַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
for this is the underlying meaning of Yom Kippur's atonement,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר שֶׁכָּל הָעֲווֹנוֹת הֵמָּה עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׂעִיר וּבְאֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה.
wherein Hashem proclaims that all sins belong on the head of the goat and in the solitary land.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה הוּא רוֹבֵץ עַל מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב,
Only that throughout the year it couches at the thresholds of the heart,
וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְשַׁלְּחוֹ לְדַרְכּוֹ שֵׂעִירָה.
and on Yom Kippur Hashem sends it away on its path toward Seir.

items.h:
Seif 11 — The Avodah of Our Lips
Reciting the Temple service enacts its spiritual reality through speech and anticipates the complete removal of the evil inclination.

p: וְעַל כֵּן אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים סֵדֶר עֲבוֹדָה לְשַׁלֵּם "פָּרִים שְׂפָתֵינוּ" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ג),
Therefore we recite the Order of the Avodah to render "the calves of our lips" (Hosea 14:3),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל נַעֲשֶׂה גַּם הַיּוֹם בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל,
for in truth everything is enacted today as well in the Heavens above,
וְהַכַּפָּרָה שְׁלֵימָה גַּם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and atonement is complete even in outward manifestation in this world,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּפוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, רַק בְּדִבּוּר,
except that it is not in physical deed, but through speech,
שֶׁגַּם הוּא גִּילּוּי, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ גִּילּוּי מוּרְגָּשׁ כָּל כָּךְ בַּפּוֹעַל.
which is also a revelation, though not as tangibly felt in physical action.
עַד יֵעָרֶה עָלֵינוּ רוּחַ מִמָּרוֹם (יְשַׁעְיָה לב, טו),
Until the spirit is poured upon us from on high (Isaiah 32:15),
לִהְיוֹת מוּרְגָּשׁ בְּפוֹעַל גָּמוּר בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בְּכָל לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
to be felt in complete actuality on Yom Kippur within all Jewish hearts:
סִילּוּק וּבִיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִן הַלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי שִׁילּוּם פָּרִים שְׂפָתֵינוּ,
the total removal and nullification of the evil inclination through the calves of our lips,
וְאָז נִזְכֶּה לִגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן.
and then we shall merit the complete redemption speedily in our days, Amen.

items.h:
Seif 12 — The Future Slaughter of the Evil Inclination
Each Yom Kippur draws nearer the final, permanent eradication of the evil inclination and complete redemption.

p: וּשְׁחִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
And the slaughtering of the evil inclination (Sukkah 52a),
אֲשֶׁר כְּפִי דַּעְתִּי, אִם נִיתַּן רְשׁוּת לוֹמַר בָּזֶה עַד הַשְׁעָרַת הַדַּעַת תּוֹרָה וְדַעַת נוֹטָה,
which in my opinion, if permission is granted to suggest based on Torah intuition,
יִהְיֶה זֶה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים;
will take place on Yom Kippur;
וּכְבָר בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל הוּא קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ רְשׁוּתָא לְאַסְטֹונֵי.
and already in the Heavens above it is an established holiness wherein he has no permission to accuse.
וְכֵן בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת, עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתֵנוּ וַעֲבוֹדַת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה שְׁלוּחֵנוּ וּשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין,
And so during the Temple era, through our service and that of the High Priest who was our emissary and the court's emissary,
הָיָה גַּם סִילּוּק הַיֵּצֶר בַּלֵּב,
there was also the removal of the inclination within the heart,
אֲבָל הַכֹּל רַק לְשָׁעָה וּבְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם לְבַד, וְלֹא בְּכָל הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר יוּצָרוּ.
yet that was only temporary for that day alone, and not across all days created.
וְעַל כֵּן אַף בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן סִילּוּק יֵצֶר לְגַמְרֵי כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד מַמָּשׁ,
Therefore even on that day there was not yet total eradication as will manifest in the Messianic era,
דְּאִם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לָשׁוּב עוֹד אַחַר כָּךְ,
for if so, it could never have returned afterward,
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהָיוּ בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה חֵירוּת מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְהַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם.
operating rather as at the Giving of the Torah—freedom from the inclination according to each person's measure.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לָזֶה בִּימֵי הַגָּלוּת בְּלֹא עֲבוֹדַת קָרְבָּנוֹת בַּפּוֹעַל,
However, when they merit this in exile without physical sacrifices,
אָז יִזְכּוּ לְסִילּוּק גָּמוּר וְנִצְחִי.
they will then merit complete and eternal eradication.
וּבְכָל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתֵנוּ לָשׁוּב אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And on every Yom Kippur, through our effort to return to Hashem, blessed be He,
אָנוּ מְקָרְבִים דָּבָר זֶה כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט,
we draw this near like the eye of a needle,
וְהוֹלֵךְ וּמִתְרַחֵב עַד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִפְתָּחֶנּוּ לָנוּ כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם,
expanding progressively until Hashem opens it wide like the entrance hall of the Temple,
בִּזְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְגַמְרֵי, בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ, אָמֵן.
with the total slaughtering of the evil inclination, speedily in our days, Amen.

sections.en: Shabbat, Blessing, Holiness, and Israel

items.h: Shabbat joins expansive blessing with protective holiness, revealing Israel's unique capacity to cease from worldly labor and recognize that all action comes from Hashem.

Seif 1 — Shabbat's Blessing and the Light of the Face
Shabbat's blessing strengthens the heart with serene confidence, a state unavailable through ordinary worldly labor alone.

p: עִנְיַן בְּרָכָה וּקְדֻשָּׁה דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
The matter of blessing and holiness belonging to the Sabbath day,
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״א אוֹת א׳: שְׁנֵיהֶם בִּמְאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
and in Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11, ot 1: both of them are in the light of a person's countenance,
כִּי "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו".
for "a person's wisdom illuminates his face."
שֶׁהֶאָרַת הַפָּנִים הוּא מִצַּד חִיזּוּק הַלֵּב וּתְקִיפָתוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִדְאַג וְיִצְטָעֵר מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר.
For the illumination of the countenance comes from the strengthening of the heart and its fortitude, so that one does not worry or feel distress over anything.
"לֵב שָׂמֵחַ יֵיטִיב גֵּהָה",
“A joyful heart brings healing,”
וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" — נוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ עֹז וְחִיזּוּק, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵאִיר פָּנָיו.
and “wisdom strengthens the wise” — it gives him strength and fortitude, and through this his countenance radiates.
וְכָל מִינֵי דְּאָגוֹת הֵם רַק מִצַּד שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דִּיצִירַת כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And all kinds of anxieties are solely from the side of the six workdays of the creation of all affairs of this world,
שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַמָּלֵא צַעַר וּדְאָגָה.
which is a world full of grief and worry.
אֲבָל מִשֶּׁבָּא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה, שֶׁהוּא כְּאִלּוּ כָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ עֲשׂוּיָה,
However, when the Sabbath arrives, rest arrives, wherein it is as though all his work is completed,
וְלֹא יוֹסִיף עֶצֶב עִמָּהּ — פָּנָיו מְאִירִים.
and it will add no sadness with it — his face radiates.
כִּי מְנוּחָה דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּכִּיר בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁשָּׁוְא כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם,
For the rest of the Sabbath day means that one genuinely recognizes that all human striving is futile,
וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר חוּץ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and there is nothing outside of the Blessed Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): מַהוּ שַׁבָּת? שְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
as they said (Zohar, Part II, 88b): What is Shabbat? The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הוּא וּשְׁמוֹ לְבַד,
just as before the world was created it was He and His Name alone,
כֵּן גַּם עַתָּה אֵין כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה חוֹצֶצֶת בְּפָנָיו.
so too now, the whole of creation does not create any barrier before Him.
וּמַכִּיר שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁפָּעַל בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הֵם בֶּאֱמֶת פְּעֻלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And one recognizes that all the actions he performed during the six workdays are in truth the action of the Blessed Name,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ",
as it is written: “Indeed, all our works You have wrought for us,”
דִּלְכָךְ אֵינוֹ פּוֹעֵל רַק בְּעֵת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹעֵל,
wherefore he acts only when the Blessed Name acts,
וּכְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹבֵת — גַּם הוּא שׁוֹבֵת.
and when the Blessed Name rests — he also rests.
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה זוֹ מִסְתַּלְּקִים כָּל מִינֵי הַדְּאָגוֹת וְעַצְבוּת מֵהַלֵּב,
And automatically, through this realization, all manners of anxiety and sorrow are removed from the heart,
וְזֶהוּ הַבְּרָכָה בִּמְאוֹר פָּנִים,
and this is the blessing through the radiant countenance,
דְּעִנְיַן בְּרָכָה הוּא הוֹסָפָה.
for the concept of blessing is increase.
כִּי שַׁבָּת הוּא מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה שֶׁנָּתַן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
For Shabbat is a precious gift that He gave to Israel,
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב וְכוּלֵי,
and a non-Jew who observes the Sabbath is liable, and so forth,
דְּלָא כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִקְפּוֹץ קוֹפֵץ וְלוֹמַר שֶׁמַּכִּיר זֶה דְּכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם,
for not everyone who wishes to leap forward can do so and say that he recognizes that all human effort is nothing;
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, אֵצֶל הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְאֵינוֹ מִן הַיִּשּׁוּב
on the contrary, by ordinary worldly standards it is deemed improper and contrary to settled society
כְּשֶׁאֵין רוֹצֶה לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
when one is unwilling to engage in the affairs and labors of this world.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Shabbat, Shemittah, and the Land of Israel
Sacred cessation teaches Israel that worldly work is secondary and that the land ultimately belongs to Hashem.

p: אֵצֶל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן,
Among idolaters, it is indeed so,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל״ט:
and as they said in Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 39:
רָאָה אוֹתָם עֲסוּקִין בְּנִיכּוּשׁ בִּשְׁעַת הַנִּיכּוּשׁ וְכוּלֵי,
he saw them occupied with weeding at the time of weeding, and so forth,

אָמַר: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת1206 Bereshit Rabbah 39:8 — R. Levi said: When Avraham was travelling through Aram Naharayim and Aram Nachor, he saw them eating and drinking and behaving wantonly. He said: Would that I have no portion in this land. But when he reached the ladder of Tyre and saw them occupied with weeding in the weeding season and with hoeing in the hoeing season, he said: Would that my portion be in this land. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “To your seed I shall give this land.” Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 24): Rest is not fitting for the nations, for at once they turn to trivialities and frivolity; and so, when Abraham came to the ladder of Tyre and saw them weeding in the weeding season, he said "May my portion be in this land," since they were occupied with the settlement of the world. For "the tranquility of the wicked is bad for them and bad for the world" — rest does not suit them; but Israel, to the contrary, were commanded to rest on the Sabbath day. Beis Yaakov (Toldos 7): Like those whom Abraham saw weeding and hoeing in season, of whom he said "Would that my portion be in this land," the twelve princes of Ishmael desired the endurance of the world and could restrain themselves from a momentary pleasure that would harm a more lasting benefit in this world; therefore, though they aim only at this transient world, converts are better accepted from them, for once the Blessed One opens such a convert's eyes to eternal life he will surely abandon all the desires of this world. But those who eat, drink and behave wantonly, giving up no desire of this world, would not abandon the desire of their evil heart even if they knew of true eternal life. Sod Yesharim (Rosh Hashanah 47): They found favor in Abraham's eyes when he saw them occupied with the settlement of the world, weeding and hoeing in season, and he said "Would that my portion be in this land": being occupied with settling the world, they had proper conduct [derech eretz], and derech eretz precedes Torah, so he reasoned that since they had the derech eretz to engage in temporal life, once the Blessed One enlightened their eyes they would engage in eternal life. But when Israel entered the land, the Blessed One showed them that all that derech eretz was mere semblance, and that in truth those nations were wholly devoid of it, full of insolence and perversity..
he said: "May my portion be in this land."
כִּידוּעַ סוֹד אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
As is known, the mystical secret of the Land of Israel corresponds to the Sabbath day,
וּכְשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם —
and when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent:

"עָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם" (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ה1207 Berakhot 35b — R. Shimon ben Yochai says: Is it possible that a man should plow in the plowing season, sow in the sowing season, reap in the reaping season, thresh in the threshing season, and winnow when there is wind — what is to become of the Torah? Rather, when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by others, as it is said, "And strangers shall stand and pasture your flocks"; and when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by themselves, as it is said, "And you shall gather in your grain." Rashi: "Is it possible" is said in astonishment: is it possible as you say [R. Yishmael]? Tosafos (s.v. "here, when Israel performs the will of the Omnipresent"): If you ask: below [R. Shimon ben Yochai] establishes "and you shall gather in your grain" as speaking of a time when Israel does not do God's will! The answer is that the verse certainly speaks of those who do His will, but who do not do it so fully — they are not wholly righteous. Alternatively, this resolution disputes the one below: it comes to distinguish those who do His will from those who do not, whereas here the two are treated alike. Maharsha: One must ask how "and you shall gather in your grain" can be assigned to a time when Israel does not do God's will, when that passage opens "And it shall be, if you hearken... to love the Lord." The answer is as Tosafot say — it speaks of those who do His will but not fully, who are not wholly righteous: for in that passage it is written "with all your heart and with all your soul" but not "with all your might," as in the passage of Shema, and a man whose money is dearer to him than his body is therefore punished in money, in that his work is not done by others. And "moreover, others' work will be done by them" refers to a further class, who do not do His will at all. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Behar 5): The Gemara sets the verse "and you shall gather in your grain" where they do not do the will of the Omnipresent, which is astonishing, since the passage speaks of "If you will surely hearken to My commandments." We said that it speaks of those who do the Lord's commandments after hearing them, like R. Yishmael, plowing in the plowing season, and of them it says that they "gather" by themselves; whereas "doing the will of the Omnipresent" is like R. Shimon bar Yochai, who does the will of the Omnipresent even where he was not commanded, since creation was made only to serve its Maker. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 224): The Sages first explained "and you shall gather in your grain" as said of those who do the will of the Omnipresent, and afterwards as said of those who do not, as Tosafos asks; harder still, the paragraph itself says explicitly "If you will surely hearken," which is doing the will of the Omnipresent. But in truth "a sharp knife cuts the verses": the grain belongs to those who do the will of the Omnipresent, and the gathering to those who do not. The paragraph is said in the plural, for it is impossible for the many and the whole world to be like R. Shimon bar Yochai, and so it does not say "with all your might." עַמּוּד ב׳),
“Strangers shall stand and pasture your flocks” (Berakhot 35b),
וְאָמְרוּ: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִם אָדָם חוֹרֵשׁ בִּשְׁעַת חֲרִישָׁה וְכוּלֵי, תּוֹרָה מַה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ.
and they said: on the contrary, if a person plows at the time of plowing, and so forth, what will become of the Torah?
וְגַם לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַף כְּשֶׁאֵינָם בְּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And also for the collective of Israel, even when they are not on this lofty spiritual level,
צִוְּתָה תוֹרָה לִשְׁבּוֹת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת בַּיָּמִים
the Torah commanded them to cease work on the Sabbath day among the days
וְשָׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִית בַּשָּׁנִים: "שָׁבְתָה הָאָרֶץ שַׁבָּת לַהַשֵּׁם",
and in the seventh year among the years: “the land shall observe a Sabbath unto the Lord,”
לְהַכִּיר כִּי לַהַשֵּׁם הָאָרֶץ.
in order to recognize that the earth belongs to the Lord.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Israel's Torah and the Nations' Worldly Labor
Israel perfects the world through Torah, while the nations reach their proper role through the material order.

p: וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ,
And this is the holiness of the Land,
שֶׁהָאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיוּ בָּהּ קֹדֶם הָיוּ כְּעֵין דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה,
in that the nations of the world who were in it previously were akin to the worldly engagement that preceded the Torah,
שֶׁהָיוּ בִּכְלַל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם.
for they were within the category of worldly labor and the cultivation of the world.

וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נ״ט1208 Sanhedrin 59a — And R. Yochanan said: A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death, as it is stated: "Moses commanded us a Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob" (Deuteronomy 33:4) — an inheritance for us, and not for them. Rashi: "An inheritance" for us and not for them — so [his studying it] involves robbery, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain. Maharsha (on 58b, s.v. "a gentile who rests on the Sabbath"): Why should a gentile be liable to death precisely for these two things — resting on the Sabbath and engaging in Torah — which we are obligated to do? Because the Torah is called "betrothed" (as expounded in Pesachim, reading "inheritance" as "betrothed"): since most people do not engage in it, to them it is like a betrothed woman still in her father's house, while to one who engages in it, it is like a married wife and is called "his Torah." Gentiles have no category of a betrothed woman, so for a gentile, engaging in the Torah is as though he had relations with an Israelite's betrothed, for which he is judged under Israelite law. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 59a): Just as the Sabbath rest, which belongs to one who has reached actual completion, does not belong to the gentiles, so the supernal intellect [of the Torah] is not fitting for them, and they have no relation at all to that level. Therefore he is liable to death, for he has entered a level not fitting for him: when a gentile enters the level of the Torah, a level that is lacking and absent in him, he takes on privation, and so he is liable to death, which is privation. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): It seems to me that what they said in Sanhedrin, too, "A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death," refers to engaging in it in order to understand what is written in it, which is the Oral Torah; for all the words of the Written Torah are closed, and one who engages in it must interpret them, so that one cannot engage in the Written Torah at all without the Oral Torah. This is the "inheritance" and the "betrothed" of the congregation of Jacob alone, to whom the Torah is entirely handed over, whereas the Written Torah by itself was written on the stones in seventy languages. עַמּוּד א׳),
And an idolater who engages in the study of Torah is liable to death (Sanhedrin 59a),
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ יִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם וְהָעֵסֶק בְּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
for the Torah is the antithesis of mere worldly civilization and labor in worldly affairs,
וְלֹא נִיתְּנָה לַגּוֹיִם,
and it was not given to the nations,
וְאֶצְלָם נִקְרָא זֶה הַיְּצִיאָה מִמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הָרְאוּיָה לָהֶם.
and for them, this is considered a departure from the measure of worldly order that is fitting for them.
וּכְשֶׁבָּאָה לְחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם,
And when it came into the portion of the seed of Abraham,
זָכוּ בָּהּ לַתּוֹרָה,
they merited through it the Torah,
שֶׁהוּא הַהַכָּרָה דְּלַהַשֵּׁם הָאָרֶץ,
which is the realization that the earth belongs to the Lord,
וְכָל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and all affairs of this world are likewise from the Blessed Name.

וְעַל כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה נִקְרֵאת עֹז (זְבָחִים קט״ז1209 Zevachim 116a — When the Torah was given to Israel, His voice went forth from one end of the world to the other, and trembling seized all the kings of the nations in their palaces. They all gathered about Balaam the wicked and said to him: What is this sound of tumult that we have heard? He said to them: He has a precious treasure in His treasury, which was stored with Him for 974 generations before the world was created, and He has sought to give it to His children, as it is stated, "The Lord will give strength to His people." At once they all opened and said, "The Lord will bless His people with peace." Rashi: "And in his palace all say: Glory" [Psalms 29:9]: the beginning of the verse is "The voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve," and it speaks of the giving of the Torah — in the palace of each and every king, all say "Glory" to the Holy One, blessed be He. "He said to them: The Lord sits as King forever": He has already sworn that He will be King over His creatures forever and will not destroy them. "Nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created": together with the twenty-six from Adam to Moses our teacher, these make "the word He commanded to a thousand generations" (Psalms 105:8); "strength" is the Torah, which is the stronghold of Israel. Maharsha (s.v. "And Jethro heard … what tiding did he hear"): Since Scripture does not say which deed it was that Jethro heard of, R. Elazar of Modi'in explains it by the event that was itself a thing heard — the giving of the Torah, which was heard throughout the world, for its sound went from one end of the world to the other. Maharsha (s.v. "The Lord will give strength to His people"): Rashi explains "strength" as the Torah; one may add that Balaam answered them that there was no change of will before Him in giving it now to Israel and not earlier to one of the nations, but the people of Israel is fit to receive it because they are the boldest of the nations, and so the Torah, which is called "strength," was given to them to sap their strength, whereas the other nations could not keep it, as is said in chapter Ein Tzadin [Beitzah 25b]. Accordingly the nations responded, "The Lord will bless His people with peace": had the Torah not been given to Israel, no nation or tongue could stand before them, so that the Torah is a gift of peace to the nations along with Israel. Maharsha (s.v. "but a flood of fire He does bring"): This implies that the oath of the waters of Noah covers fire as well, whereas in the first chapter of Sotah [11a] the Egyptians reasoned that He had sworn only against a flood of water. Balaam means that He will not bring even a flood of fire upon the whole world, having sworn by the waters of Noah not to bring destruction upon the whole world; but upon a single nation He certainly brings it, as it is written, "For by fire will the Lord contend" — and so too a flood of water upon a single nation, in which the Egyptians erred. Maharsha (s.v. "which was hidden with Him nine hundred and seventy-four generations"): He told them all this because it was fitting that the Holy One, blessed be He, come with sounds so great that the whole world would hear, to make known to all the world that a precious treasure was hidden with Him, and that He had removed from before Him nine hundred and seventy-four generations because they were not fit to fulfil its commandments — whose fulfilment is the world's existence, and without which the world would be fit to return to chaos and void, as it is said, the Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the works of creation, if Israel accept [the Torah]. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Zevachim 116a): The one who says he heard of the giving of the Torah and came holds that it is not plausible he came on hearing of the war with Amalek: though the evil enemy had been removed, how would other nations thereby join Israel, since Israel are one nation and the proselyte is of another? But once Israel had received a supernal level, the level of the Torah, proselytes too are able to receive the Torah, and so Jethro came to convert, since proselytes can be included with Israel in receiving the Torah. Moreover, whereas the splitting of the Sea came from the side of the right and the war with Amalek from the side of the left, the giving of the Torah is from the Blessed Name Himself, belonging neither to the left nor to the right but to the middle, and there is no level above it. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 30): A great change draws a great change after it: the giving of the Torah from Heaven was a new thing — the Torah, which is the separate intellect, coming into actuality in the physical world — and so a great upheaval followed it; hence he said 'a precious treasure hidden in His storehouse,' and 'nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created,' to say that the Torah is separate from the physical world, and He, blessed be He, desired to give it to the world. And because all the words of the Torah are binding and necessary, and whatever is necessary is strong, its coming into the lower world drew after it things that come with strength, like thunders and lightnings, for like draws like. So the Midrash shows in saying "The Lord will give strength to His people": the sounds came because He was giving His people the Torah, which is called "strength" because all its words are binding. עַמּוּד א׳),
Therefore the Torah is called strength (Zevachim 116a),
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר עִנְיַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם,
and when the matter of the Giving of the Torah was awakened in the world,
נִתְעוֹרֵר הַחֵשֶׁק דְּיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם וּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
the desire for the cultivation of the world and the trait of worldly labor was awakened among the nations of the world.
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵמוּת דְּתוֹרָה,
For when Israel is at the pinnacle of perfection in Torah,
אָז גַּם כָּל הָעוֹלָם בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵמוּת;
then the entire world is likewise at the pinnacle of perfection;
וּשְׁלֵמוּת דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר עוֹסְקִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם לְצוֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and the perfection of the nations of the world is attained when they engage in worldly affairs and civilization for the sake of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד.
just as it will be in the future to come.

items.h:
Seif 4 — Na'aseh VeNishma and the Boundless Inheritance
Israel accepted Torah with wholehearted surrender and thereby received an inheritance not limited by human effort.

p: וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהֶחֱזִיר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הַתּוֹרָה עַל כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת,
And therefore, when the Holy One, blessed be He, offered the Torah to all the nations,
לֹא רָצוּ לְקַבְּלָהּ,
they did not want to accept it,
כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁהִיא הַמַּפְרִיעָה אוֹתָם מִמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
because they saw that it interferes with their orientation toward worldly civilization,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל שְׁלֵמוּתָם.
which constitutes their entire perfection.
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּסָגוּ בִּתְמִימוּתָא,
However, Israel, who walked in wholehearted simplicity,
הִקְדִּימוּ פֶּה לְאֹזֶן,
put mouth before ear,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ח1210 Shabbat 88a-b — A certain heretic saw Rava sitting absorbed in his studies, his fingers beneath his foot and he pressing them until they spurted blood. He said to him: Impulsive people, who put your mouths before your ears! You still persist in your rashness. First you should have listened; if you were able [to bear it], you should have accepted, and if not, you should not have accepted. He said to him: We, who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, “The integrity of the upright shall guide them.” Rashi: ["His fingers":] the fingers of his hands. ["And he was pressing them":] he was crushing them under his legs and did not notice, from his absorption. ["A rash people":] hasty. ["Who put your mouths before your ears":] before you had heard how hard it is and whether you could stand up to it, you took it upon yourselves to fulfill it. ["We, who walk in wholeheartedness":] we walked with Him in simplicity of heart, as those who act out of love, and relied on Him not to burden us with something we could not withstand. Maharsha: ["The integrity of the upright shall guide them":] Besides Rashi's explanation, one may explain it in the manner of "In the way a person wishes to go, he is led" and "One who comes to purify himself is helped": the upright, who wish to walk the straight path even though it is hard for them to do, are guided with help from Heaven; and conversely, "the crookedness of the treacherous," who walk a crooked and not a straight path, "shall destroy them," for "one who comes to defile himself, [the way] is opened for him." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 29): The heretic held that this was out of order — by right a person should first hear a thing and afterwards know to do it — and so he said that Israel's putting "we will do" before "we will hear" came from their rashness, that they are disorderly in their actions. Rava answered him that the matter is the reverse of what he thought: it is the ways of those who walk in guile that depart from order, but Israel walk in their integrity, and the action of whoever is wholehearted never departs from the proper order — and by the proper order the doing should come first, for that is what man was created for. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 8): The garment for attaining the truth of the Torah is wholeheartedness, to be wholehearted with the Lord, for "the integrity of the upright shall guide them," as they said in Perek R. Akiva: "We who walk in wholeheartedness..." Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei): To be easily enticed toward the good is a fine trait for which Israel were praised: they are drawn after the Blessed One with great haste, without deliberation or delay, as the heretic said to Rava, "Rash people, who put your mouths before your ears." Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 20): Rava's reply to the Sadducee who called Israel "rash people, who put your mouths before your ears" and said they should first have listened to see whether they were able, namely "We who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, 'The integrity of the upright shall guide them,'" means that we are wholehearted in the will of the Blessed One, [confident] that He will surely help us to complete it for the good; and this is what is called "whose strength is in You." Sod Yesharim (Seventh Day of Pesach 14): At times a person must set aside his human form [of reasoning] to fulfill the will of the Blessed One, like a horse ridden by its master, as in the heretic's charge against Rava and Rava's reply: Israel, who at their root cleave to knowledge, are taught by that knowledge that at times they should set aside their power of choice to fulfill the will of the Blessed One. But the nations, who branch from the supernal princes that stand in awe without knowledge, have no bond with their prince and act without knowledge or choice, like a horse of the Other Side; and even when they sometimes yield before the Blessed One, it is only so as to spread out afterwards with great force, as Balaam did. עַמּוּד א׳),
as they taught in Shabbat (88a),
דְּזֶהוּ מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם,
for this is the attribute of Jacob, a wholehearted man,
לִמְסוֹר עַצְמוֹ לְגַמְרֵי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
to yield oneself entirely to the Blessed Name
וְלֹא לַחְקוֹר כְּלָל אַחֲרָיו וְלִשְׁמוֹעַ מַה יֹּאמַר אִם יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל.
without questioning Him or first waiting to hear what He will say in order to decide whether one can accept it.
דְּזֶהוּ מִי שֶׁמְּחַשֵּׁב עַצְמוֹ לְדָבָר נִפְרָד וִיכֹלֶת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ;
For that is the calculation of one who considers himself an independent entity with self-contained ability;
אֲבָל מִדַּת "אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב"
but the attribute of “truth to Jacob”
הוּא לְהַכִּיר הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ שֶׁאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ,
is to perceive the absolute truth that there is nothing else besides Him,
וְאֵין לָאָדָם שׁוּם יְכֹלֶת אֶלָּא לְמַה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן לוֹ יְכֹלֶת.
and a person has no ability whatsoever other than that which the Blessed Name grants him ability to do.
וְאִם כֵּן מַה שַּׁיָּיךְ אִם יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל,
And if so, how is it relevant to ask whether he is able to accept it,
כֵּיוָן דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְצַוֶּה — יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל גַּם כֵּן.
since if the Blessed Name commands, he will certainly be given the ability to accept it as well.
כִּי הָאָדָם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא הַהֲכָנָה, מַה שֶׁהוּא מוּכָן לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For man possesses only the readiness, namely that he is prepared to do the will of the Blessed Name,
וַהַשֵּׁם הַטּוֹב בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה.
and the Lord will do that which seems good in His eyes.
וְזֶהוּ "תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם",
And this is “the integrity of the upright shall guide them,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אוֹרְךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ הֵמָּה יַנְחוּנִי יְבִיאוּנִי אֶל" וְגוֹמֵר;
and as it is written: “Send Your light and Your truth, let them guide me, let them lead me to...” and so forth;
"אוֹרָה" — זוֹ שַׁבָּת,
“light” — this refers to Shabbat,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״א)1211 Bereshit Rabbah 11:2 — When the sun set on Sabbath eve the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to hide away the light, but He showed honor to the Sabbath. This is what is written, "And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it" — He blessed it with light. Once the sun set on Sabbath night the light began and continued to serve, and all began to give praise; this is what is written, "Under the whole heaven He lets it loose, and His light to the corners of the earth.": בֵּרְכוֹ בְּאוֹרָה;
as they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11): He blessed it with light;
וֶ"אֱמֶת" — זוֹ תּוֹרָה,
and “truth” — this refers to Torah,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה1212 Berakhot 5b — R. Yochanan said to him: Granted, Torah and acts of kindness [atone], as it is written, “Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned.” “Kindness” — this is acts of kindness, as it is stated, “He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness and honor.” “Truth” — this is Torah, as it is stated, “Buy truth and do not sell it.” But one who buries his children — from where [do we know this]? Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaYissurin 2): Sins and iniquities all depend upon a man's material body, which is his deficiency, and it is from the side of that deficiency that the evil inclination rules him. Torah removes the corporeal — the more a man is drawn after Torah and wisdom, the more the baseness of the body is removed, and with it the sins that are that baseness — and acts of kindness likewise bring a man merit, for the piety in a man is from the side of his merit and his good; this is why they said that an unlearned man cannot be pious, since the grossness of matter in him makes merit impossible. Hence "through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned": both of them remove the baseness of matter and the sins that follow upon it.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳).
as they said in Berakhot (5b).
וְהַכָּרַת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הַכָּרַת הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ,
And the apprehension of Torah is the cognition of wisdom within the mind,
וְהַכָּרַת הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
while the apprehension of Shabbat is the realization deriving from the understanding in the heart.
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי",
And regarding both, “He did not do so for any nation,”
כִּי הֵם נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב,
for they are the inheritance of Jacob,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה י״א,
as they said in Bereishit Rabbah, end of parashah 11,
דְּיַעֲקֹב הוּא שֶׁשָּׁבַת, עַל כֵּן זָכָה לְנַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים;
that Jacob is the one who kept the Sabbath, and therefore he merited an inheritance without boundaries;
וְהוּא נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁזּוֹכִים לָהּ שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת,
and this is the heritage of Jacob that Sabbath observers merit,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר,
as it is written: “and I will nourish you...” and so forth,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת1213 Shabbat 118a — R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Yose: Whoever delights in the Sabbath is granted a boundless inheritance, as it is said, “Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I shall cause you to ride upon the high places of the earth, and I shall feed you the heritage of Yaakov your father.” Not like Avraham, of whom it is written, “Arise, walk about the land”; nor like Yitzchak, of whom it is written, “For to you and to your seed I shall give all these lands”; but like Yaakov, of whom it is written, “And you shall spread out to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south.” Rashi: "Without bounds": that is, it has no end. "Then you shall delight": this is written after "and you call the Sabbath a delight." "The heritage of Yaakov" — and not the heritage of Avraham and Yitzchak: "its length and its breadth" means this land and no more, and "these lands" means these and nothing further. Maharsha: The Beit Yosef (Tur, Orach Chayim 242) explains it as measure for measure: as he spends without limit for the Shabbat, so he is given an inheritance without limit. Alternatively, the delight of Shabbat touches the spiritual — the additional soul, through which one merits the day that is wholly Shabbat, which has no bound in space — so its reward too has no bound, and "you shall spread out" (ופרצת) is read here as the breaching of a fence, so that his inheritance has no fence or border. The blessing was given to Yaakov and not to Avraham and Yitzchak because in their merit bounded lands were given to other nations as well (to Lot and to the children of Esav), whereas in the merit of Yaakov, through whom the merit passed down from fathers to sons, this further blessing of an inheritance without bounds was added. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 118a): Delight by its nature has no constraint — one who is hemmed in by distress is not in delight at all — and since the Shabbat, being a day of rest, is the one day fit for delight, one who delights in it is given a portion likewise without constraint: an inheritance with a border is hemmed in by what lies beyond it, while one without a border extends in every direction. Further, holiness is the attribute of Yaakov (hence the blessing corresponding to him is "You are holy"), and the Shabbat is the holiness in the world; the holy, being separate from the physical, has no limit, since only the physical, which has extension, has an end — therefore Yaakov's inheritance, and that of one who delights in the Shabbat, is without bounds. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 3): Scripture says of Shabbat "in all your dwellings" in keeping with the teaching "Whoever delights in the Shabbat is given an inheritance without bounds … like Jacob, of whom it is written, 'And you shall spread out to the west and to the east.'" That is, wherever he goes the holiness of the Land of Israel goes with him; therefore on Shabbat a Jew merits that every place where he stands is holy ground, and in all one's dwellings one can attain the holiness of the Land of Israel, the inheritance from the Patriarchs. Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 5): Abraham was given a possession still within boundaries — "all the land which you see," that is, wherever you see the glory of Heaven — because Ishmael issued from him, and had it been given without limit he too would have taken of it without choice; likewise Esau issued from Isaac, so to him it was given with constrictions, "all these lands." But in Jacob there was no dross at all, so it was given to him without any boundaries: "And you shall spread out to the west and to the east." On Shabbat the verse mentions Jacob alone, "the heritage of Jacob your father," because Shabbat alludes to the future, when "the Lord shall be One and His name One," and then it is the inheritance without bounds, the portion of Jacob. (קי״ח עַמּוּד ב׳).
and as they taught in Shabbat (118b).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי נַחֲלַת הָאֻמּוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם,
And the meaning is that the inheritance of the nations is through their own striving,
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ לָהּ גְּבוּל כְּפִי הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת;
and therefore it has a defined limit corresponding to the measure of that striving;
אֲבָל נַחֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ כְּלָל,
however, the inheritance of Israel does not stem from human striving at all,
רַק מַה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן,
but only that which the Blessed Name bestows,
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בְּלִי גְּבוּל כְּמִדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and consequently it is boundless, like the measure of the Blessed Name,
שֶׁאֵין גְּבוּל לִנְתִינָתוֹ.
for there is no limit to His giving.

items.h:
Seif 5 — The Gift of Shabbat and Jacob's Recognition
Shabbat amplifies Jacob's inherited recognition that all action and rest ultimately come from Hashem alone.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁזָּכָה לוֹ וּלְבָנָיו אַחֲרָיו,
And this is the Sabbath that he merited for himself and for his children after him,
עַד דִּבְמָרָה אִתְפַּקַּד עַל זֶה לִהְיוֹת עוֹד מְצֻוִּים וְעוֹשִׂים.
until at Marah they were commanded concerning this, to become additionally those who are commanded and fulfill.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה מַתָּנָה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶם,
Even though this is a great gift that He gave them,
שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהַכִּיר זֶה שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם,
so that they could recognize this truth, that everything is in the hands of Heaven,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹעֵל — הוּא פּוֹעֵל,
and when the Blessed Name acts — he acts,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹבֵת — הוּא שׁוֹבֵת.
and when the Blessed Name rests — he rests.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לֹא נְתָנָהּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּתָּנָה בְּחִנָּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
Nevertheless, the Blessed Name did not give the gift for nothing to Israel,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי,
which He did not do for any other nation;

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי (מְגִלָּה כ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳ וְשָׁם נִסְמָן1214 Megillah 26b — As for giving a synagogue away as a gift, R. Acha and Ravina disagree: one forbids it and one permits it. The one who forbids reasons: by what should its sanctity lapse? And the one who permits reasons: had he not derived some benefit from him he would not have given it to him, so the gift turns out to be like a sale. Rashi: A gift — that is, where the townspeople gave the synagogue away to someone for ordinary, non-sacred use. Sod Yesharim (Eighth Day of Pesach 26): This free gift is as the Gemara says of a gift, "had he not derived benefit from him he would not have given it to him, so the gift becomes like a sale." A sale is what the Blessed One gives a person in exchange for his service, and a gift is what He gives beyond his service: when, after all his service, a person recognizes that he has accomplished nothing before the Blessed One for which reward would be due, the Blessed One gives him as a free gift even what service cannot attain. Thus the gift becomes like a sale — not that the Holy One, blessed be He, is lax, but He grants this free gift by strict justice, measure for measure: as this person gave himself over to the Blessed One entirely, not for any particular thing, so the Blessed One bestows all good things on him entirely, not for any particular service.):
and in the manner that they said in several places (Megillah 26b and cross-referenced there):
דְּמַתָּנָה כְּמֶכֶר,
that a gift is like a sale,
דְּאִי לָאו דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵיהּ — לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ.
for were it not that he derived some benefit from him, he would not have given it to him.
וְגַם אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן,
And likewise with the Blessed Name it is so,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה: "לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם",
and as it is written in the Torah: "I have given you good merchandise,"
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מַתָּנָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא "לֶקַח",
for even though it is a gift, it is nevertheless called "merchandise taken,"
כְּאִלּוּ הֵם לְקָחוּהָ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם.
as though they acquired it through their own striving.
וְאַף יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, אַף דִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ קְבוּעָה וְקַיָּימָא,
And even the Sabbath day, although its holiness is fixed and established from on High,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם צִוָּה בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְוָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
He nevertheless commanded it by way of a commandment to Israel,
וְשֶׁהֵם מְצֻוִּים לְקַדְּשׁוֹ בְּקִדּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם כְּאִלּוּ הֵם מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ.
and that they are commanded to sanctify it through the Kiddush of the day, as though they themselves sanctify it.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם זָכוּ לִקְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָבוֹת: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב,
For in truth, they merited this holiness through the striving of the Patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה,
from level to level,
עַד מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב, הַבָּחוּר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת,
up to the level of Jacob, the chosen of the Patriarchs,
שֶׁזָּכָה לַהַכָּרָה הַשְּׁלֵמָה דַּה' אֶחָד.
who merited the complete realization that the Lord is One.
וְהַכָּרָה זוֹ נִשְׁרְשָׁה בְּכָל בָּנָיו אַחֲרָיו בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
And this realization was rooted in all his children after him in their very spiritual essence;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא רַק בְּרָכָה בִּמְאוֹר פָּנִים,
and therefore it is called specifically a blessing in the light of the countenance,
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמְּאוֹר פָּנִים יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
for the root of the radiant countenance exists even during the six workdays,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת הוּא מִתְבָּרֵךְ.
only that on the Sabbath it becomes blessed and amplified.

items.h:
Seif 6 — Blessing as Expansion of Divine Light
Shabbat expands Israel's awareness that every blessing flows from Hashem, the sole source of all bounty.

p: וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הֶאָרַת פָּנִים,
And the nations of the world, who possess no illumination of the countenance,
כִּי שָׁרְשָׁם מִצַּד הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
because their root is from the side of darkness,
שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׁקּוּעַ בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹמֶה לְחֹשֶׁךְ וְלַיְלָה,
which is immersion in the affairs of this world that resembles darkness and night,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פְּסָחִים (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
as they said at the beginning of Pesachim (2a),
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר פָּנִים גַּם בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
it is impossible for them to attain the light of the countenance even on the Sabbath day,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת לָזֶה כְּלָל;
for they have no connection to this whatsoever;
