by the intellect of the person apprehending them when the concepts become fully integrated into his mind.

items.h:
Seif 13 — Hearing a Sage versus Reading a Book
Words spoken from the heart carry a living impression that books cannot reproduce, while writing preserves what exile would erase.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין דּוֹמֶה שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּי חָכָם לִרְאִיָּה בִּסְפָרִים,
This explains the well-known distinction that hearing a teaching directly from the mouth of a sage is not comparable to seeing it in books;
כִּי דְּבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִלֵּב חָכָם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם חַיּוּת גָּמוּר הַמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתָן דִּבּוּרִים
for words that issue from the heart of a sage contain complete vitality that clothes itself in those spoken words
דֶּרֶךְ הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גָּמוּר מֵחַיּוּת הַמְדַבֵּר עַצְמוֹ.
by way of a complete investiture of the speaker’s own vitality.
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ לִפְעוֹל בְּלֵב הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ, כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּ"דְבָרִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִן הַלֵּב נִכְנָסִים לַלֵּב".
Therefore, they possess the power to make an impression on the heart of the listener, as is known: “words that issue from the heart enter the heart.”
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּכְתִיבָה, הַהִתְלַבְּשׁוּת אֵינוֹ מִצַּד חַיּוּת פְּרָטִי שֶׁל חָכָם הַמְחַדֵּשׁ הַדָּבָר הַהוּא,
In writing, by contrast, the investiture does not derive from the personal vitality of the sage who innovated that teaching,
דְּאוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת אֵין יָכוֹל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּכְתָב,
for that individual vitality cannot clothe itself in written letters,
רַק מִצַּד הִתְכַּלְלוּת חַיּוּתוֹ בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים, יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק מִמֶּנּוּ,
but only from the inclusion of his vitality within the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, of which he is a part,
וְגַם חָכְמַת בְּנֵי אָדָם הַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and all human wisdom likewise stems entirely from the blessed Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ הִתְכַּלְלוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
This reflects the inclusion of the Oral Torah within the Written Torah,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל רָמוּז בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
for in truth everything is hinted at in the Written Torah,

וְגַם "כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ נֶאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי" (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כ״ב1234 Vayikra Rabbah 22:1 — “All,” “the all”; “words,” “the words”; “commandment,” “the commandment” — Scripture, Mishnah, laws, Talmud, Toseftot and Aggadot, and even what a veteran student is destined to say before his teacher: all of them were said to Moshe at Sinai. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): Through "I have put My words in your mouth," all the wisdom of the sages of the Oral Torah is the words of the living God, as [the Sages said,] all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was said to Moses at Sinai. Therefore "a sage is greater than a prophet": though [his attainment] is in concealment, he attains more and merits "to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth." Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:80): In the wisdom of R. Akiva, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, there is certainty only when the Blessed One enlightens [the sage's] eyes [to see] that this law is a halakhah to Moses from Sinai, as the Sages said that all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was said to Moses at Sinai. This means that it is true wisdom: he recognizes and knows that it is certainly a halakhah to Moses from Sinai, so that his innovation is the innovation of a veteran student. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 7): The Oral Torah is what the Scribes innovated, flowing from the hearts of Israel, and what a veteran student will in the future innovate, and the Sages said that all of it was revealed to Moses. Just as all souls were revealed to Adam because, as their father, he contained them all, so Moses, whose soul contained all the wisdom of the Written Torah, thereby contained all the wisdom of the Oral Torah as well, since it all flows from it and is hinted in it. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): It is not that Moses did not attain what the sage attains: by the holy spirit he certainly attained it, and all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was revealed to him, which is the attainment of the Oral Torah by way of wisdom and understanding of the heart. But in prophecy, what the Blessed One showed him in the manner of the prophets was revealed to him only according to his level. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): "And I will proclaim the name of the Lord" refers to the thirteen attributes of mercy, which are the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded, the foundation of the Oral Torah; and then He revealed to [Moses] all that a veteran student would in the future innovate. Therefore He said, "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," even to one who is not worthy, for [Moses] saw that young students would in the future innovate great things hidden from the great ones of the generations before them. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 5): Hillel's chief foundation was the Oral Torah, hence [the Sages] said he was fit for the Shechinah to rest upon him, for the revelation of the Oral Torah comes through the resting of the Shechinah, and through this all that a veteran student will in the future innovate was revealed to Moses.),
and even “everything a devoted student will innovate in the future was already stated to Moses at Sinai” (Vayikra Rabbah 22:1),
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דְּבַר ה' מִצַּד שָׁרְשׁוֹ וּמְקוֹרוֹ, כִּי מִשָּׁם לוּקָּח,
and everything is the word of Hashem in terms of its root and source, for from there it was taken,
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דְּבַר תּוֹרָה גָּמוּר וְהַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה'.
and all of it is complete Torah and the very word that Hashem spoke.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁל הַחַיּוּת הַכְּלָלִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And from this perspective of the collective vitality present in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד דְּבַר ה' שֶׁאָמַר: "עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ" וְגוֹמֵר, "לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַדָּבָר" וְגוֹמֵר, "שְׁאַל אָבִיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר,
which derives from the word of Hashem who said: “According to the Torah they teach you...,” “You shall not deviate from the matter...,” and “Ask your father...”
דְּעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ" עַל מִצְוֹת דְּרַבָּנָן,
which is why we recite the blessing “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us” over rabbinic commandments,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (כ״ג1235 Shabbat 23a — What blessing does he recite? He recites, "who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to kindle the Hanukkah light." And where did He command us? Rav Avya said: from "You shall not deviate [from the word they tell you]." Rav Nechemya said: from "Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you." Rashi: "And where did He command us?": for this is not from the Torah but from their [the Sages'] words. Maharal (Be'er HaGolah, Be'er 1): That the Blessed Name appointed the Sages to enact what is fitting is stated explicitly in Scripture: "You shall not deviate from the word that they tell you." Just as no one would say that what nature brings about is not from the Blessed Name, since it is He who ordered nature, so everything the Sages enacted is from the Blessed Name, who appointed the Sages to bring about with their intellect what is fitting to enact; for this reason we bless even over the commandments the Sages enacted, "who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us," to say that all of it was ordered by the Blessed Name. עַמּוּד א׳), דְּגַם זֶה מִצְוַת ה' דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל —
as the Sages explained in Shabbat 23a, that this too constitutes the commandment of Hashem in a general sense—
חַיּוּת זֶה יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת נִתְפָּס בִּכְתָב כְּכָל דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
this vitality can indeed be captured in writing like all written matters,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בִּכְתָב פְּרָטִי בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר פְּרָטִי שֶׁחִדְּשׁוּ סוֹפְרִים.
only that it expands into a specific written text concerning that particular insight innovated by the Scribes.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִכְנָס לְשֵׂכֶל הַמַּשִּׂיג,
And when it enters the intellect of the one studying it,
מִצַּד הִתְדַּבְּקוּתָם בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים דִּדְבַר ה' הַכְּלָלִי הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ,
by virtue of their attachment to the Source of Life through the general word of Hashem hidden within it,
יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל פְּרָטֵי הַחַיּוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
he can attain all the details of the vitality present in that matter,

כְּאִלּוּ שָׁמַע פֶּה אֶל פֶּה מִבַּעַל שְׁמוּעָה הָעוֹמֵד לְנֶגְדּוֹ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב׳ דִּשְׁקָלִים י״א1236 Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 2:5 — Giddul said: Whoever reports a teaching in the name of the one who said it should see the author of the teaching as though he were standing before him, as it is said, "Surely man walks about as a mere image." Pnei Moshe (at the parallel, Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:2, to which he refers here): "Surely man walks about as a mere image" — when one repeats a teaching in the name of the one who said it, he should see him with his own eyes as though that man were standing opposite him; for the man in whose name the teaching is repeated is thereby as one who walks about in image continually. עַמּוּד א׳).
as though he heard it mouth-to-mouth from the master of the teaching standing before him (Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 2:5 11a).
אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָזֶה הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֵׂכֶל הַמַּשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן יוֹתֵר מִבִּשְׁמִיעָה פֶּה אֶל פֶּה.
However, this requires intellectual exertion on the part of the student far greater than what is needed when hearing mouth-to-mouth.

וְאִלְמָלֵא נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ לוּחוֹת, לֹא הָיוּ שׁוֹכְחִים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כַּיָּדוּעַ (עֵירוּבִין נ״ד1237 Eruvin 54a — R. Eliezer said: What is meant by "engraved upon the tablets" (Exodus 32:16)? Had the first tablets not been broken, the Torah would never have been forgotten from Israel. Rashi: Charut means engraved and never effaced; by means of the tablets the Torah was engraved upon Israel so as never to be forgotten from them. Maharsha: Scripture should have said "engraved [chakuk] upon the tablets," which is the word used elsewhere for engraving; rather, charut is said of the heart, and "upon the tablets [luchot]" is like "upon his cheeks [lechayav]" in the exposition above — of one who does not weary of reviewing his learning. Then his learning becomes engraved and kept in his heart, and so endures with him. Maharal (Derush al HaTorah): Had the tablets not been broken, the Torah of the Blessed Name would have been wholly joined to Israel: the first tablets were "the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved," unlike the last tablets, which in themselves were only the work of Moshe though the writing was God's, so that the writing was not joined to them. Man who receives the Torah is like the tablets that receive the writing; had the body of the tablets given to Israel also been the work of God, the receiving man too would have been a body wholly prepared for the Torah, and it would not have departed from Israel. But now that there is no complete joining of the writing to the tablets, neither is man prepared to receive the Torah so that it joins him completely, and this keeps diminishing — which is what has caused the Torah to be forgotten and removed from Israel. עַמּוּד א׳),
And had the Tablets not been broken, words of Torah would never have been forgotten, as is known (Eruvin 54a),
לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִכְתֹּב תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and there would have been no need to commit the Oral Torah to writing.
אֲבָל זֶה גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל יְסוֹדָהּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בִּטּוּלָהּ,
Yet this too is part of the principle that its suspension serves its foundation,
דְּעַל יְדֵי שְׁבִירַת לוּחוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶחֱזִירוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
for through the breaking of the Tablets, they brought the Oral Torah back to being like the Written Torah,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
so that it could clothe itself in this world.

items.h:
Seif 14 — The Oral Torah as Israel's Inner Secret
The Written Torah's outer form can be copied, but its inner meaning belongs uniquely to Israel through Oral Torah.

p: וְזֶה דָּבָר גָּדוֹל וִיסוֹד הַתּוֹרָה,
This is a great matter and a foundational principle of the Torah:
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
for in truth, the essential core of the Torah is the Oral Torah,
כִּי מַה שֶּׁבִּכְתָב אֵין לָאָדָם תְּפִיסָה בּוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
since a person has no grasp of what is written except through the Oral Torah.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא ל״ד1238 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34 — R. Yehudah bar Shalom said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "Write these words," Moses asked that the Mishnah too be put in writing. But the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the nations of the world were destined to translate the Torah and read it in Greek, and to say, "We are Israel." Until now the scales are balanced. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the nations: You say that you are My children — I do not know; only those who hold My mysteries are My children. And which are they? This is the Mishnah, which was given orally, and from which everything is to be expounded. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): After prophecy departed, the sages of the Oral Torah began, and the Sages said, "He has set me in dark places — this is the Talmud of Babylonia"; but this is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says in Tanchuma, "Those who hold My mysteries are Israel." For it is written, "He made darkness His hiding place" — there are His hidden things; and though it is darkness and the hiding of the Face, the darkness is cast by the shadow of His hand, shielding us by way of concealment, as one must make shade to protect against the blazing sun. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:86): The Blessed One teaches human beings to exert effort, which is why the Torah began for Israel as the Written Torah; He wishes a person to arrive at His mysteries — as in the Midrash, "He who holds My mysteries…" — and to understand what He indicates to him with the compass. This is the essential effort: to come to the Oral Torah, which is the recognition that everything is from the Blessed One, the "finding" that comes after toil. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 12): The novel insights of Torah belong to the Oral Torah, whereas in the Written Torah, which is written and set down [before all], there are no novel insights; therefore the nations claim on the strength of the Written Torah, "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers, "He who holds My mysteries…," for the Oral Torah exists only in the hearts of the children of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 4): Edom claims that they are the good and the pure by birth; therefore Haman's decree was a preparation for the Oral Torah, as the Midrash says: because the nations are destined to say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "He who holds My mysteries…" — for it is the Oral Torah that clarifies this. The Oral Torah is what springs from the heart of Israel, the hearts of the children of Israel being its originators, so that it is theirs alone, and this is the testimony that they, and no others, are the masters of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Just as there is wisdom among the nations but no Torah among the nations, so it says in Tanchuma, "He who holds My mysteries…": the Oral Torah was given over only to Israel. The nations, even if they study Torah and innovate in it by their wisdom, speak vanity and not Torah at all, for they innovate from their own wisdom, whereas the Torah is the wisdom of the Blessed One; but the sages of Israel bless over the Torah first and know that the Blessed One is the Giver of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 3): The essence of the Torah is the Oral Torah, which reveals the hidden things of the Written Torah, as it says in Shemos Rabbah that the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek… "He who holds My mysteries…." This is an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob alone: the Torah is handed over to them according to what they clarify through their dialectic and their wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): They said in Tanchuma that the Oral Torah was given because the nations are destined to translate the Torah into Greek and say "We are Israel," and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say, "He who holds My mysteries…." That is, the nations too have a connection to the Written Torah, which is why it was revealed in writing to all who come into the world; but the Oral Torah is the mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He, which cannot be revealed in writing at all, only "the secret of the Lord is with those who fear Him" — the Congregation of Israel, who look to the Blessed One from the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): All the innovation of the Oral Torah comes through the unions and complete cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is His mysteries, as they said in Tanchuma at the end of Ki Sisa: because the nations of the world are destined to translate the Torah and say "We are Israel," the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "He who holds My mysteries…." This is the telling of secrets, which is for Jacob alone — and "telling" does not mean in writing — so "He tells [His words to Jacob]" means the Oral Torah, the handing over of the words of Torah of which it is said "He has not done so for any nation"; whereas the Written Torah alone was written on the stones in seventy languages.):
And as the Sages taught in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34):
שֶׁעֲתִידִין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל" וְכוּלֵי,
in the future the nations of the world will say, “We are Israel,” and so forth,
"מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ" וְכוּלֵי;
and the Holy One will respond: “He who possesses My secret mysteries...,” and so forth.
דְּמִצַּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהוּא הַלְּבוּשׁ גַּשְׁמִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
For regarding the Written Torah, which constitutes the physical garment in this world,
יוּכְלוּ גַּם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם תְּפִיסָה וַאֲחִיזָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
the nations of the world can also claim that they have a grasp and hold upon the words of Torah.
וּבֶאֱמֶת "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי",
In truth, however, “He has not done so for any nation,”
וַאֲפִילּוּ יְקַיְּמוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם
and even if they were to observe the entire Torah, it counts for nothing
אִם לֹא יִתְגַּיְּרוּ וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנּוּ,
unless they convert and are called by the name of Israel,
כִּי לֹא נִיתְּנָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנִּתְגַּלּוּ לָהֶם הַמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁבָּהּ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
for the Torah was given only to Israel, to whom its inner mysteries were revealed through the Oral Torah.

items.h:
Seif 15 — The Second Temple and the Rise of Oral Torah
With prophecy diminished, the Second Temple era became the great flowering of Torah's inner radiance through the sages.

p: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כ״ז1239 Heikhalot Rabbati 31:5 — R. Yishmael said: Thus said R. Akiva in the name of R. Eliezer the Great — our fathers did not consent to set stone upon stone in the Sanctuary until they had compelled the King of the world and all His ministers, and these yielded to them, and He revealed to them the secret of the Torah: how they were to perform it and how they were to make use of it. At once the Holy Spirit appeared from the great entrance in the House of the Lord — even though the Divine Presence did not descend and did not rest in the Holy of Holies, because of the decree — and they saw the Throne of Glory raised up and standing between the porch and the altar. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 93): Although the Divine Presence did not rest in the Second Temple, Sefer Heikhalot relates that they did not set stone upon stone in it until they compelled the Holy One, blessed be He, and He revealed to them the secrets of everything. This compelling corresponds to the overturning of the mountain over them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah — perhaps it was the abolishing of the evil inclination recounted in Yoma 69b; and since the counsel in a time of concealment is Torah, in the Second Temple the Sages of the Mishnah began, and all the virtues of the Torah were there in greater measure — which is truly greater, as "a sage is preferable to a prophet."):
And as it is written in Pirkei Heichalot (chapter 27):
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
that even though the Shechinah did not abide in the Second Temple,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה וְזִיוָהּ וַהֲדָרָהּ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
nevertheless the essence of the Torah, its radiance, and its splendor existed only in the Second Temple;
שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לִבְנוֹת עַד שֶׁהִבְטִיחָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם רָזֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
for they refused to build it until the blessed Hashem promised to reveal to them the secrets of the Torah;
יְעֻיַּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים.
let it be examined there in the text itself.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה,
This is because the beginning of the Oral Torah occurred during the Second Temple period through the Men of the Great Assembly;
שֶׁהֵם מְיַסְּדֵי הַבַּיִת, הֵם יִסְּדוּ גַּם כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
those who founded the House were the very ones who also founded the Oral Torah,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה1240 Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 5:1:3 — R. Yonah said: It is written, "Therefore I will give him a portion among the many, and he shall divide the spoil with the mighty" (Isaiah 53:12) — this is R. Akiva, who established the exposition of the laws and of the homiletic teachings. And some say: these are the Men of the Great Assembly. And what did they establish? General rules and particulars. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "this is R. Akiva, who established"): "Therefore I will give him a portion among the many" — that he should be renowned among the many, and that all of them should learn what he arranged; "and he shall divide the spoil with the mighty" — that he divided much spoil in words of Torah for the mighty, for those willing to toil in them. And according to those who say that it was the Men of the Great Assembly who established the exposition of the laws and of the homiletic teachings, what R. Akiva established were the general rules and particulars by which the Torah is expounded, as they are taught in the baraita of R. Ishmael.׳).
as the Sages stated in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim 5:1.
וּבִימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי, דְּקִיְּמוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ כְּבָר,
And in the days of Mordechai, when they reaffirmed what they had already accepted,
שֶׁחָזְרוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית,
returning to receive the Torah out of love rather than through the mountain suspended over them like a vat,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פ״ח1241 Shabbat 88a — "And they stood at the foot of the mountain" — Rav Avdimi bar Chama bar Chasa said: This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, held the mountain over them like a barrel and said to them: If you accept the Torah, well and good; and if not, there shall be your burial. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: From here comes a great protest against the Torah [that it was accepted under duress]. Rava said: Even so, they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus, as it is written, "The Jews confirmed and accepted" — they confirmed what they had already accepted. Rashi: ["At the foot of the mountain":] actually beneath the mountain. ["A barrel":] a vat into which beer is put. ["A great protest":] for if He summons them to judgment [asking] why they did not fulfill what they took upon themselves, they have an answer: that they accepted it under duress. ["In the days of Ahasuerus":] out of love for the miracle that was done for them. Tosafos (s.v. "He held the mountain over them like a barrel"): And although they had already put "we will do" before "we will hear," [He held it over them] lest they retract when they saw the great fire at which their souls departed. As for Avodah Zarah (2b), where [the nations ask,] "Did You hold the mountain over us like a barrel?" — implying that had He held it over them they would have had no answer — while here it is called a great protest against the Torah: [that passage concerns] their not having accepted it, but for not having fulfilled it there is an answer. Tosafos (s.v. "Rava said: they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus"): The Ri found it puzzling: in Megillah (7a) Shmuel proves from "The Jews confirmed and accepted" — they confirmed above what they had accepted below — that Esther was said with the holy spirit, and Rava says that every other proof has a refutation except Shmuel's; yet Shmuel's too is refuted, since Rava himself uses this verse for another exposition, and in Chagigah (10a) a verse's being needed for another exposition counts as a refutation. If one reads "Rabbah" there, it is well; or else, in Megillah he means that the others are refuted in their reasoning, whereas Shmuel's is open only to the objection that the verse is needed for another exposition. Tosafos (s.v. "a great protest against the Torah"): As for what is said in Nedarim (25a), that Moses made a covenant with Israel over the Torah and the commandments and adjured them, and in Sotah (37b), that they accepted the whole Torah at Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal — R. Tam says that this was at the Divine command, and so as though against their will; but in the days of Ahasuerus they accepted it of their own accord, out of love for the miracle. And the covenant Joshua made with them to serve the Lord was only [an undertaking] not to worship idols, as it is written, "Far be it from us to forsake the Lord" (Joshua 24:16). Maharsha: ["He held the mountain over them like a barrel":] Since it says not "beneath the mountain" but "in the nether part of the mountain," it implies within its lower part, like a barrel, which surrounds on the sides as well — and so "there shall be your burial," like a grave, which surrounds on the sides as well; [to Tosafot's question, why this was needed after "we will do and we will hear,"] one may further answer that their word in putting "we will do" before "we will hear" was not a complete acceptance until they afterwards took it upon themselves by covenant and oath. ["They confirmed what they had already accepted":] On its plain sense, referring to the Megillah, it should have said "accepted and confirmed," since acceptance certainly precedes confirmation; for this reason it is also expounded in Megillah (7a), "they confirmed above what they had accepted below," and in Shevuot (39a), of the Megillah reading as a later ordinance already included at Sinai — and these expositions are of equal weight, and all of them hold. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 32): He held the mountain over them not lest they retract — why should they, having already said "we will do and we will hear"? — but so that Israel should not say they accepted the Torah of themselves and might have refused: the whole world depends on the Torah, and without it would return to chaos, so it is not fitting that the completion of all existence hang on Israel's choice, something that might or might not be; therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, compelled them, and what is compelled admits no removal or annulment. "A great protest": in the end the acceptance was by compulsion, and that is not a complete acceptance, which must be by the recipient's will. In the days of Ahasuerus they accepted of their own will one commandment that the Blessed One had not decreed upon them, the reading of the Megillah — the last of all the commandments — and if they accepted that of themselves, all the more so the commandments that preceded it, so that it is as though the Torah had been accepted willingly from the beginning, the end proving the beginning. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3): On "until Your people pass over, O Lord": the first entry [into the Land] was only because they are "Your people," as a father pities his son even when he does not go in a good way, and their acceptance of the Torah too was under compulsion; but at the second entry, since "they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus" willingly and were righteous, they were "the people You acquired," acquired by exchange and not as a gift. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 4): Then too "they confirmed what they had already accepted" (Shabbat 88a), and there was surely an illumination in the heart of every Jew, an acceptance of the whole Torah like the illumination at Mount Sinai — yet without open miracles, thunder and lightning, but enclothed in the hearts of Israel themselves, who of their own accord fulfilled it all in their hearts. We suppose this a deficiency, but in truth it is an advantage, for accepting the words of Torah of their own accord is certainly greater, since otherwise there would be "a great protest against the Torah"; and accepting because of revealed miracles is not like accepting of their own accord without such revelation. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 9): As in the future, "with a mighty hand and with outpoured wrath will I reign over you," so too at the giving of the Torah the mountain was held over them like a barrel (Shabbat 88a), against their will, for this purpose: to establish that they are bound in servitude to the Blessed One against their will, and that it is impossible ever to leave His prior servitude. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 10): Amalek [in the generation of Mordechai and Esther] sought to abolish the Oral Torah from Israel, but it was overturned, and through this the Oral Torah was then established, as is said (Shabbat 88a), "they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus" — that is, the Oral Torah, for it was concerning it that the mountain was held over them like a barrel, whereas concerning the Written Torah they had said "we will do and we will hear." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 93): At first the Blessed One illuminates a person who is not yet accustomed to it, so that it is hard for him to hold it fast and he loses it; afterward he yearns for it and seeks it, and the Blessed One does not open to him again except with great difficulty. This is the matter of the giving of the Torah, which came through holding the mountain over them like a barrel, and afterward "they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus" willingly; yet no miracle was done for them in the days of Ezra as in the days of Joshua son of Nun. עַמּוּד א׳), אָז זָכוּ לְכָךְ.
as our Sages of blessed memory taught in Shabbat 88a, they then merited this.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַכְּפִיַּת הַר הָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
For the principal coercion at the mountain was directed at the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ, עַיֵּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים;
as the Sages taught in Midrash Tanchuma, Parashat Noach; see there in the text;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא קִבְּלוּהָ מֵרְצוֹנָם, לֹא נִמְסְרָה עֲדַיִן לָהֶם לְגַמְרֵי,
and as long as they had not accepted it willingly, it was not yet fully handed over to them,
וְהָיוּ מִתְנַהֲגִים עַל פִּי נְבִיאִים, הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה'.
and they were guided through the prophets, with everything in writing directly from the hand of Hashem.

items.h:
Seif 16 — Why a Sage Can Surpass a Prophet
Prophecy sees through spiritual vision, while a sage's intellectual Ruach HaKodesh can penetrate beyond visionary form.

p: וְאַף שֶׁהַנְּבוּאָה הוּא גִּלּוּי מְפֹרָשׁ מַרְאוֹת ה' יוֹתֵר מֵהַשָּׂגַת הַחֲכָמִים,
Although prophecy is an explicit revelation of visions of Hashem far beyond the intellectual perception of the sages,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳ דְּ"חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא",
nevertheless the Sages taught in Bava Batra 12a that “a sage is superior to a prophet”;
וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בְּרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן נַחְמָן דְּיָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג מַעֲמַקִּים יוֹתֵר.
and see Nachmanides there, who explains that the sage can attain greater depths.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה, שֶׁהִגִּיד דְּבָרִים בְּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים
And as is known from the holy Ari of blessed memory, who disclosed teachings concerning supernal worlds
שֶׁכְּפִי דַּעַת עַצְמוֹ הוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים
which by his own reckoning transcend the attainment of all the prophets,
וַאֲפִילּוּ הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כַּנּוֹדָע לַהוֹגִים בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
and even the attainment of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, as is well known to those who study his writings.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם הִשִּׂיגוּ דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
The distinction is that the prophets perceived through vision,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִרְאוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יוֹתֵר כְּפִי הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גּוּפָנִיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and one cannot see more in this world beyond what the physical garments of this world allow,
דְּעַל כֵּן דִּבְרֵיהֶם נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב בִּלְבוּשׁ גָּמוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is why their words could be committed to writing in a complete worldly garment.
אֲבָל הוּא הִשִּׂיג דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה בַּשֵּׂכֶל,
The sage, however, attains through the intellect,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן נַחְמָן שָׁם,
which is the attainment of the Holy Spirit, as Nachmanides wrote there;
וְשֶׁלֹּא דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג הַרְבֵּה.
and without the constraints of sensory vision, one can attain vastly more.

items.h:
Seif 17 — Rabbi Akiva and What Moshe Did Not See
Moshe received future Torah prophetically, yet later sages could inwardly comprehend innovations beyond prophetic sight.

p: וְזֶה מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְנָחוֹת (כ״ט1242 Menachot 29b — R. Yehudah said in the name of Rav: When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and tying crowns to the letters. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, who stays Your hand? He said to him: There is a man who is to arise at the end of many generations, Akiva ben Yosef by name, who will expound heaps upon heaps of laws from every tittle. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, show him to me. He said to him: Turn around. He went and sat at the end of the eighth row, and he did not understand what they were saying, and his strength ebbed. Rashi: "Crowns" — like the tagin of a Torah scroll. "Who stays Your hand?" — what is wanting in what You have written, that You must still add crowns to them? Maharsha: A knot is tied in order to call something to mind so that it not be forgotten, as is said of the fringes, "that you may remember"; so these knots upon the letters allude to inward, supernal matters in His crown, and serve to recall them. Moses supposed that human understanding could not reach their intent, and therefore asked, "Who stays Your hand?" — if these knots are of no use to a human mind too short to grasp them, what prevents You from remembering them without tying a knot at all? He was answered that He ties them precisely for the sake of human understanding: Akiva ben Yosef will expound from them not only inward matters but heaps upon heaps of laws that hang upon them. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Menachos 29b): "When Moses ascended on high" means that he was rising to the rank of the higher beings in order to receive the Torah, for the Torah cannot be received except by one who is raised out of the physical to that rank. Just as the body of the words of the Torah indicates the words of the Torah themselves, so the crowns set upon the letters indicate perceptions as fine as hairs, which issue from the Torah itself; and therefore they are marked by a tag, thin as a strand of hair. And "who stays Your hand?" means: these fine perceptions are remote from man, who is in this world of the senses and has no such subtlety of intellect, and since they are set apart from the words of the Torah, whom then do they serve? עַמּוּד ב׳)
This explains what the Sages said in Menachot 29b,
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לֹא הֵבִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not understand the words of Rabbi Akiva;

וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (חֻקַּת)1243 Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6 — "These things I have done and have not forsaken them" — it is not written here "I will do," but "I have done," for I have already done so for R. Akiva and his colleagues: matters that were not revealed to Moses were revealed to R. Akiva and his colleagues. "And his eye has seen every precious thing" — this is R. Akiva and his colleagues. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): A tzaddik at his passing leaves his power and life-force in this world, all the more so Moses, and his life-force is the beginning of the Oral Torah, the endless multiplication of words of Torah — to the point that they said R. Akiva's eye saw what Moses' eye did not see. Yet all of it came through what Moses drew down and the life-force he left in the world in the Written Torah called by his name, so that his passing is the open spreading of his power into all the hearts of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): Converts are like a surplus added onto Israel, yet "the advantage of the land is in everything" — even what seems an unneeded surplus has its advantage: "every precious thing" — R. Akiva's eye saw what Moses did not see, and he was descended from converts. Moses' mind was set at ease when they reached a certain law and [R. Akiva] said "this is a law to Moses from Sinai," for he saw that had he not received the Torah at Sinai and handed it to Israel, R. Akiva would have known nothing; all is contained in the Torah, concealed in the Written Torah and revealed in the Oral Torah, whose foundation is R. Akiva — and he was the son of converts because love of the Torah in its revealed form is strongest among converts. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): All new revelation of the Oral Torah comes through forgetting and concealment; so it spread more in the Second Temple than in the First, and after the Second Temple's destruction more still, in the generations of the Tannaim and Amoraim, until the Sages said that the eye of R. Akiva and his colleagues saw what Moses' eye did not see. R. Akiva founded the general rules and particulars of the Oral Torah and was the arms-bearer of Ben Koziva, for he was fit to bear the arms of the Messiah, the Oral Torah he attained being a likeness of the arms of the Messiah's Torah. דְּ"רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם",
and in Midrash Rabbah (Chukat) that “Rabbi Akiva’s eye saw what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not see.”
וְאַף דְּלֹא קָם כָּמוֹהוּ, הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַשָּׂגָתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
Though none arose like Moses, this refers specifically to attainment through visionary sight,
וְלוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ, וַאֲפִילּוּ מַה שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ.
for to Moses was revealed everything an advanced student would ever innovate, even what Rabbi Akiva would innovate.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת נְבוּאָה דֶּרֶךְ רְאִיָּה,
However, all of that was prophetic revelation through vision,
וְלֹא דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה שִׂכְלִיּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים אוֹתָם הַמְחַדְּשִׁים הַדְּבָרִים,
and not through the intellectual grasp experienced by those who innovate the concepts,
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה לֹא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
a mode of insight that was never permitted to be written;
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַלְבִּישׁ בִּכְתָב כְּלָל,
for such an essence cannot be clothed in writing at all,
רַק מַה שֶּׁ"לֵּב חָכָם יַשְׂכִּיל פִּיהוּ",
it can only be that “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth,”
וְעִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא סוֹד נֶעְלָם בְּלֵב הַמַּשִּׂיג.
and the essential core of the perception remains a hidden secret in the heart of the one who attains it.

items.h:
Seif 18 — Written Miracles and the Border of Purim
Recorded miracles descend into physical salvation; Purim stands where written revelation begins to give way to Oral Torah.

p: וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַנִּסִּים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב
Therefore, all miracles performed for Israel that were permitted to be written down
הֵם יְשׁוּעוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת, שֶׁנִּיצּוֹלוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵרוּת וּמִמָּוֶת לְחַיִּים,
are physical salvations, where they were delivered from slavery to freedom and from death to life;
כִּי כֻּלָּם יְשׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for all of them are the salvations of the blessed Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא הוֹשִׁיעָם בְּרַחֲמָיו וּבְרוֹב חֲסָדָיו בְּנֵס גָּלוּי לַכֹּל שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹזֵר וּמוֹשִׁיעַ.
Who delivered them in His mercy and abundant kindness through a miracle revealed to all that He is the Helper and Savior.
וִישׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹבֵר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת
And the salvations of the blessed Hashem traverse all the worlds
עַד שֶׁמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ גַּם בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי, וּבָא הַצָּלָה לַגּוּפוֹת גַּם כֵּן.
until they clothe themselves even in the physical World of Action, bringing rescue to physical bodies as well.
וְעַל כֵּן הָרֹשֶׁם הַנִּשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם נִיתַּן לִכְתֹּב גַּם כֵּן
Hence the enduring impression established for all generations could likewise be committed to writing
וּלְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַכְּתָב,
and clothed within the letters of the text;
וְכֵן נִקְבַּע מֵהֶם יָמִים טוֹבִים, שֶׁהוּא בְּעוֹנֶג הַגּוּף וְשִׂמְחָתוֹ וּשְׁבִיתָתוֹ מִמְּלָאכָה,
and likewise festivals were established from them, celebrated through bodily pleasure, joy, and cessation of labor,
כִּי נִפְעַל הַיְשׁוּעָה גַּם לַגּוּף.
because salvation was effected for the physical body as well.
וְזֶהוּ הַכֹּל מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי,
This all belongs to the aspect of this physical world,
צְרִיכִים הַנִּסִּים גַּם כֵּן לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשֵׁי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
in that the miracles too must clothe themselves in the garments of this world;
וְעַל כֵּן נִמְשְׁלוּ הַכֹּל לְלַיְלָה עַד אֶסְתֵּר,
therefore all of them were compared to night until Esther,
שֶׁהִיא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים הַנִּיתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
who marks the end of all miracles permitted to be written,
וְהִיא כְּמוֹ הַתְחָלָה לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and serves as an opening to the Oral Torah,
כִּי הוּא הַמִּצְוָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים שֶׁנִּתְחַדְּשָׁה לְמִצְוָה קְבוּעָה לְדוֹרוֹת עַל יְדֵי סוֹפְרִים וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה.
for it is the first rabbinic commandment established for all generations by the Scribes and the Men of the Great Assembly.

וְעַל כֵּן אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּלֹא נִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב1244 Megillah 7a — Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said: Esther sent to the Sages — Establish me for the generations! They sent back to her: You will arouse the envy of the nations against us. She sent to them: I am already written in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Rav, Rav Chanina, R. Yonatan and Rav Chaviva taught: Esther sent to the Sages — Write me for the generations. They sent to her: Have I not already written for you three times, and not four? Rashi: "Establish me" — as a festival and for the reading, that I may have a name thereby; "you are arousing envy against us" — for the nations will say that we rejoice to recall their downfall, and to this she answered that she is already written [in their chronicles], where they will see what befell them at the hands of Israel. "Three times" — in three places we are to mention the war with Amalek: in Exodus, in Deuteronomy, and in the book of Samuel; and this is what Solomon meant, that what you have made threefold you are not permitted to make fourfold. Maharsha (s.v. "Esther sent to the Sages: Establish me for the generations"): This whole exchange is already intimated in the verses: first "And Mordecai wrote… to enjoin upon them that they should keep [these days]" (Esther 9:20–21), and they would not accept it, because of "you are arousing envy"; then "And Esther wrote… to confirm this second letter of Purim" and "he sent letters" (Esther 9:29–30), which close by saying that envy need not be feared, for they are "words of peace and truth." And her reply is the verse "are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia" (Esther 10:2). Maharsha (s.v. "Write me for the generations"): Here her request was that the Megillah be included among the Writings, as Rashi explains on "and the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book" (Esther 9:32). They answered that Scripture itself had excluded it, for the verse preceding "Have I not written for you three times" reads "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise" (Proverbs 22:17) — that is, the Megillah belongs among the commandments that are only the words of the Sages, like the Chanukah lamp, and not among the commandments of Scripture that were spoken with the Holy Spirit. Only when they found a support in "Write this for a memorial in the book," which shows that the Megillah is itself one of the three, did they accede to her. Sod Yesharim (Purim 41): It was not clear to the Sages whether to fix the Megillah of Esther in the Written Torah or whether it is among the oral teachings that one may not write, as the Gemara implies: Esther sent to the Sages, "Establish me for the generations... Write me for the generations," and they sent back, "Have I not written for you three times and not four?" until they found a verse written in the Torah. So the Sages were in doubt whether to fix it in the Written Torah, for perhaps it is among the things of which it is said, "By the mouth of these words I have made a covenant with you": what is written, in writing, and what is oral, orally. (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳),
Therefore, one opinion holds that the Megillah was not permitted to be written (Megillah 7a),
וְשֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מִכְּלַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
arguing that it truly belongs to the domain of the Oral Torah;
וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּנִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִיא הַסּוֹף מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַכְּתָב,
and according to the one who holds it was permitted to be written, it is nevertheless the very end of the level of written scripture,
וּלְעוֹלָם סוֹף מַדְרֵגָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הוּא הַתְחָלָה וְכֶתֶר לַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁאַחֲרֶיהָ.
and the end of a higher level is always the beginning and crown of the level that follows.

items.h:
Seif 19 — Purim as Providence Clothed in Nature
Purim hides divine sovereignty within ordinary causality, revealing Hashem's rule through a salvation that appears natural.

p: וְהַיְינוּ דְּנֵס דְּפוּרִים לֹא הָיָה עוֹד נֵס נִגְלֶה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ,
This means that the miracle of Purim was no longer an overtly manifest miracle directly wrought by the blessed Hashem Himself,
וּלְמַרְאֵה עַיִן הָיָה קְצָת דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע, כִּי לְאַהֲבַת אֶסְתֵּר עָשָׂה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
and to outward appearances it occurred somewhat through natural causality, for Ahasuerus acted out of love for Esther.
וְזֶה טַעַם "וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת",
This is the deeper meaning of “and Esther clothed herself in royalty,”

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם י״ד1245 Megillah 14b — Esther, as it is written: "And it came to pass on the third day that Esther clothed herself in royalty." It should have said: in royal garments. Rather, she clothed herself with the divine spirit. Here it is written "and she clothed herself," and there it is written "And the spirit clothed Amasai." Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): "Royalty" is the last of the ten attributes, and from it the Divine Spirit is bestowed upon whoever is worthy of it. The verse brought as proof, "and the spirit clothed Amasai," certainly does not there speak of the Divine Spirit, for no prophecy of his is recorded anywhere; it means rather a spirit of willingness, as the commentators explain, like "and the spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah." It is cited here only because there too Scripture uses the language of "clothing" with regard to a spirit. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 5:1): Scripture does not say "royal garments," since even a commoner can put on royal garments; but of Esther, who was herself queen, it is fitting to say that when she put on royal garments she put on royalty entirely. The explanation [of the Gemara] is that when Esther put on royal garments in this way, she thereby put on the divine spirit as well, for the divine spirit clothed her, that is, it rested upon her — just as "and the spirit clothed Amasai" means that the spirit rested upon him. So "Esther clothed herself in royalty" means that when she clothed herself in royalty, the divine spirit then rested upon her. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Noach 3): The Oral Torah comes by the Holy Spirit, and so it is expounded that "Esther clothed herself in royalty" means she clothed herself with the Holy Spirit — that is, the Oral Torah, for Kingship is the aspect of the mouth, the Oral Torah. Of this it says "my word (imrasi) shall distill like the dew," which Recanati derives from "He has torn (bitza) His word," rendered in the Midrash "He tore His purple robe"; so "my word" is the garment of royalty, which is the Holy Spirit. עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתָּהּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
concerning which our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Megillah 14b): that the Holy Spirit clothed her;
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, נַעֲשֵׂית הִיא לְבוּשׁ לְאוֹתָהּ מִדָּה שֶׁהִלְבִּישָׁה הִיא אֶת הַמַּלְכוּת.
namely, the divine attribute of His blessed Sovereignty (Malkhut)—she became a garment for that very attribute, as she clothed Royalty itself.
וְכָל נִסִּים הַנִּגְלִים כִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וְהַדּוֹמֶה,
And all the openly revealed miracles, such as the Exodus from Egypt and the like,
אַף שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
even though they were carried out through Moses and Aaron and similar intermediaries,
הָיָה גָּלוּי לַכֹּל כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל,
it was evident to all that the blessed Hashem was the true Agent,
לְפִי שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בְּשֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא הַגִּלּוּי שֶׁהוּא הַמְהַוֶּה הַכֹּל.
because they were enacted through the Name Havayah, which is the revelation that He brings everything into existence.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר פַּרְעֹה: "מִי ה'" וְגוֹמֵר — רָצָה לוֹמַר שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
Therefore Pharaoh said: “Who is Hashem...” and so forth—meaning the Name Havayah,
דְּזֶה "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" וְאֵין לָהֶם הַשָּׂגָה בְּשֵׁם זֶה כְּלָל.
for concerning this, “He has not dealt so with any nation,” and they possess no perception of this Name whatsoever.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד שֵׁם הָאַדְנוּת, מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּבַכֹּל מָשָׁלָה,
This is not so from the aspect of the Name Adonut, the attribute of His blessed Kingship that rules over all,
וְגַם הַגּוֹיִם קָרוּ לֵיהּ "אֱלָהָא דֶּאֱלָהַיָּא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹף מְנָחוֹת (ק״י עַמּוּד א׳),
and even the gentiles refer to Him as the “God of gods,” as the Sages noted at the end of Menachot (110a),
אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּסַר הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם לְכוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְהַנְהָגַת הַטֶּבַע.
merely imagining that He relinquished the daily governance of the cosmos to celestial forces and the mechanisms of nature.
וְנֵס דְּפוּרִים הָיָה מְלֻבָּשׁ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע,
Thus the miracle of Purim was cloaked within the natural order;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, בֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה הַכָּרָה מְפֹרֶשֶׁת בָּזֶה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל עַמּוֹ.
nevertheless, in truth there emerged an explicit recognition of this throughout the entire world, that the blessed Hashem actively oversees His people.

items.h:
Seif 20 — Esther's Demand to Be Written
Esther insists that Purim's hidden providence be recognized as explicit divine salvation while its mitzvot celebrate bodily rescue.

p: וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרָה אֶסְתֵּר: "קִבְעוּנִי לְדוֹרוֹת",
And this is the reason that Esther said: “Establish me for all generations,”
וְהֵשִׁיבוּ: "קִנְאָה אַתְּ מְעוֹרֶרֶת", "כִּתְבוּנִי" וְכוּלֵי (שָׁם ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳);
and the Sages responded: “You are arousing jealousy against us,” and regarding “Write me down...” and so forth (Megillah 7a);
שֶׁהַכְּתִיבָה מוֹרָה עַל נֵס מְפֹרָשׁ וְנִיכָּר גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִישׁוּעַת ה',
for committing it to writing signifies a miracle explicit and discernible even within this world as the salvation of Hashem,
וְהֵם חָשְׁבוּ דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם סוֹבְרִים דְּהָיְתָה סִבָּה טִבְעִית.
whereas the Sages assumed that the nations of the world would view it merely as a natural occurrence.
וְהִיא הֱשִׁיבָתַם: "כְּבָר כְּתוּבָה" וְכוּלֵי —
And she replied to them: “It is already recorded...” and so forth—
רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּגַם הֵם כָּתְבוּ זֶה לְנֵס וִישׁוּעַת ה',
meaning that the nations themselves had likewise recorded it as a miracle and a divine deliverance.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה י״א עַמּוּד א׳: "אֵימָתַי רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ" וְכוּלֵי1246 Megillah 11a — R. Yochanan opened his exposition of this portion from here: “He has remembered His kindness and His faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.” When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordechai and Esther. Rashi: "When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordecai" — because the matter became known to all the nations, for letters went out through the whole world. Maharsha: Many of that generation were liable to destruction for having enjoyed Ahasuerus's feast, and were spared only on account of Mordecai and the righteous of his company; hence the verse says "He has remembered His mercy" — for those who were not worthy of redemption — "and His faithfulness" — for those who were worthy. And because the redemption came through a woman, Esther, it says "to the house of Israel," as in "Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob" — these are the women. "All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God" — because this deliverance reached the whole world, since, as the Gemara says further on, Ahasuerus reigned over the entire world. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Pesichah): This Megillah testifies to the renowned salvation that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed — not like the other miracles He did for them while Israel were in their own land and not under the hand of the nations, when the miracle was not revealed to the nations. But in the days of Ahasuerus, who ruled over the whole world, the salvation was wrought among the nations: when he decreed that Israel be destroyed and killed it was written throughout the land, and when the Holy One, blessed be He, saved them it became known to the whole world, and so "all the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God." Moreover, "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20), and when He saved them from Haman, of the seed of Amalek, it was as though He had saved them from all the nations; therefore all the ends of the earth saw it, for it was a great wonder in their eyes. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 4): "All the ends of the earth saw" does not refer to the nations of the world, for they did not see the salvation of our God, since it was clothed close to the way of nature, and the many who became Jews did so only out of fear of the Jews and of Mordechai. Rather, "all the ends of the earth" refers to Israel, who were then in the utmost lowliness and concealment, to the very ends of the earth, and precisely through this they saw the salvation of our God from within that very concealment. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 256): When Esther absorbed the trait of modesty, the salvation came in revelation, as in "When did all the ends of the earth see...? In the days of Mordechai and Esther." He had heard that "Megillah" denotes revelation, for then it was revealed that the way of nature too is the Blessed One's guidance, since the salvation came by way of nature and it was revealed to all that it was His doing — and this is the seeing of "all the ends of the earth." Salvation by way of nature is modesty and clothing rather than an open miracle, yet it is truly a greater revelation, even to the ends of the earth, for the recognition that nature too is from the Blessed One is the more manifest recognition. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Megillah): The miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, such as the Exodus and the splitting of the Sea, were beyond nature and are called "wonder"; the language of "seeing" does not fit them, for after the miracle the world remained as before, and only "hearing" applies. But in the miracle of Mordechai and Esther, which appeared to follow the course of nature, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed that all the ways of nature by which the world is conducted are likewise only for Israel's good, and to this the language of "seeing" applies, for it is evident to the eye at every moment. Tiferes Yosef (Purim 1): His honored grandfather and teacher explained: "the salvation of our God" denotes a salvation that endures forever, for with the Blessed One nothing is incidental; as He endures for all eternity, so His salvation endures for all eternity, akin to "Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation." Sod Yesharim (Purim 39): That is, they then saw plainly that all the concealment that had passed over them, and the salvation that followed, were all arranged in the Torah, and nothing new had been added to the Torah's order — as the Sages hinted, that the prophets neither took from nor added to what is written in the Torah except for the reading of the Megillah. Beforehand it had seemed that something new was being added, but once the Blessed One opened the salvation they recognized that it had all along been so arranged in the words of Torah, only it had been hidden from them through the concealment of Amalek. Sha'ar HaEmunah (Entrance to the Gate 14): The miracle of Purim was hidden, everything occurring by way of nature, and only after the miracle was revealed did they perceive how all the details combined into one miracle. This is "When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordechai and Esther": they reflected at the end and saw all the events together, and then they saw that the Blessed One guides all the nations even where they do not understand, though at the time His guidance appeared to follow the course of nature.;
And as the Sages said in Megillah 11a: “When did all the ends of the earth see...” and so forth;
דִּבְנֵס גָּלוּי הֲרֵי גָּלוּי לַכֹּל, אֲבָל זֶה שֶׁהָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לַמִּתְעַקְּשִׁים לִתְלוֹת בְּדֶרֶךְ טִבְעִי,
for in an open miracle the matter is immediately visible to everyone, whereas here it was possible for obstinate individuals to ascribe it to natural causes,
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כְּפִי הַסִּבּוֹת וְהַמְסֻבָּבִים הַנִּסְמָכִים הֵבִינוּ הַכֹּל דְּהוּא פֹּעַל ה' וִישׁוּעַת אֱלֹהֵינוּ,
yet because of the interconnected sequence of causes and effects, everyone comprehended that this was the work of Hashem and the salvation of our God;
זֶה נִקְרָא רְאִיַּת אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ —
this is termed the perception of the “ends of the earth”—
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהֵבִינוּ שֶׁגַּם בִּפְעֻלּוֹת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהֵם פְּעֻלּוֹת הַטִּבְעִיִּים יֵשׁ דֶּרֶךְ נִסִּי וִישׁוּעַת ה'.
meaning they recognized that even within earthly, mundane actions—which operate naturally—there exists a miraculous course and the direct salvation of Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ קְצֵה הַקּוֹמָה דִּישׁוּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִסָּיו הַנִּגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
This represents the outer perimeter of the structure of the blessed Hashem’s salvation and His revealed miracles in this world,
שֶׁמִּדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא מִדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה בְּכָל קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the attribute of Malkhut is the final attribute in every complete spiritual configuration, as is known,
וְהִיא לְהַרְאוֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וּבְהַנְהָגַת הָאָרֶץ הַזּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and its purpose is to demonstrate His sovereignty among the lower realms and within the terrestrial governance of this physical world.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם הִיא הָיְתָה יְשׁוּעָה גּוּפָנִית מִמִּיתָה לְחַיִּים,
Therefore, this deliverance too was a corporeal salvation from death to life,
וְלָכֵן קְבָעוּם יְמֵי מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה לַהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף גַּם כֵּן.
and for that reason they established them as days of feasting and gladness for the physical pleasure of the body as well.

items.h:
Seif 21 — Why Purim Is Not a Full Yom Tov
Purim's deepest victory is spiritual - renewed Torah and mitzvah - while political servitude remains, so labor was not suspended.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, יוֹם טוֹב לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ לִהְיוֹת שְׁבִיתָה גְּמוּרָה לַגּוּף
And nevertheless, they did not take upon themselves a full festival (yom tov) involving complete cessation of labor for the body,
מִשּׁוּם דְּ"אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן",
because “we are still the servants of Ahasuerus,”
וְלֹא הָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּה גְּמוּרָה לַגּוּף מִשִּׁעְבּוּד גַּם כֵּן;
and there was not a complete physical redemption from servitude;
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, הָעִיקָּר בַּיְשׁוּעָה דְּאָז הָיָה דְּ"לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה" וְגוֹמֵר,
since in any event, the essential core of the salvation then was that “the Jews had light...” and so forth,
דְּפֵירְשׁוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְיוֹם טוֹב וּמִילָה וּתְפִלִּין, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
which the Sages expounded at the end of the first chapter of Megillah (16b): this refers to Torah, festival, circumcision, and tefillin; see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְסַנְחֵרִיב וּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר כֻּלָּם לֹא בָּאוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד אֱמוּנָתָם דַּוְקָא,
This means that the exile of Egypt, Sennacherib, and Nebuchadnezzar did not come upon Israel specifically on account of their religious faith,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַעַזְבוּ אֱמוּנָתָם גַּם כֵּן הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בָּהֶם וּמַגְלִים אוֹתָם.
for even had they abandoned their faith, those conquerors would still have subjugated them and exiled them.
וְכֵן כָּל הַצָּרוֹת דְּעַד בַּיִת שֵׁנִי שֶׁהָיוּ מֵהָאֻמּוֹת לֹא מָצִינוּ גְּזֵרַת שְׁמָד,
And similarly, in all the afflictions suffered from the nations prior to the Second Temple, we find no decrees of religious apostasy (shemad),
דְּלָא אִכְפַּת לְהוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה,
for they did not care about religious dogma,
רַק בָּאוּ לְכָבְשָׁם וְלִלְחוֹם בָּם כְּמוֹ בְּאֻמָּה אַחֶרֶת,
they merely came to conquer them and wage war against them as against any other nation,
וְהוּא רַק צַעַר הַגּוּפָנִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם כָּל יִעוּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בִּשְׂכַר וָעֹנֶשׁ גּוּפָנִי.
and this was solely physical distress, just as all the promises of the Written Torah are phrased in terms of physical reward and punishment.

items.h:
Seif 22 — Why the Written Torah Speaks in Physical Reward
Written Torah is the physical garment of divine truth; its spiritual meanings are uncovered through the Oral Torah.

p: וְכָל הַקַּדְמוֹנִים נִתְקַשּׁוּ בָּזֶה עַל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִי,
And all the early commentators struggled with this question: why spiritual reward and punishment is not explicitly detailed in the Written Torah;
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה קֻשְׁיָא כְּלָל,
yet in truth this is no difficulty at all,
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, הַכְּתָב הוּא לְבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for in the Written Torah, the written script is the physical garment of the Torah in this world,
וְכָךְ הִיא הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל עוֹלָם מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ הַשַּׁיָּךְ לְאוֹתוֹ עוֹלָם,
and so it is that in every world the Torah clothes itself in the garment appropriate to that world:
וּבָעוֹלָם הָרוּחָנִי שָׁם אוֹתָן יִעוּדִים עַצְמָם הֵם בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת, וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵם בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת.
in the spiritual realm those very same promises exist spiritually, while in this world they appear materially.
וְדָבָר זֶה שֶׁל שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ פֵּירוּשׁ עַל שָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And this concept of spiritual reward and punishment is disclosed only by way of exposition upon the physical reward and punishment of the written text by the sages of Israel in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהֵם מַשִּׂיגִים מִסְטוֹרִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁהִיא בְּכָל עוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים.
for they apprehend the inner mysteries hidden within the Written Torah and how it exists across all supernal realms.
אֲבָל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב עַצְמָהּ, שֶׁהִיא לְבוּשָׁהּ הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
However, in the Written Torah itself, which is its manifest garment in this world,
אֵין לִכְתֹּב כְּלָל אֶלָּא הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
it is not appropriate to write anything other than what is manifest in this physical world.

items.h:
Seif 23 — Torah's Hidden Governance of the World
Hashem governs all realms through Torah, but both Torah's meaning and providence remain deeply concealed from ordinary perception.

p: וּמִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
From the standpoint of the Written Torah, meaning from the perspective of the blessed Hashem,
הָיָה רָאוּי כֵּן בֶּאֱמֶת לִהְיוֹת בָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה תֵּיכֶף הַשָּׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ כְּיִעוּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה;
it would indeed have been fitting that reward and punishment be realized immediately in this world according to the Torah's promises;
כִּי כָּל דְּבַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא פּוֹעֵל בְּשָׁוֶה בָּעוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים כְּמוֹ בְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי, כִּי אֶצְלוֹ הַכֹּל שָׁוֶה,
for every utterance of the blessed Hashem operates equally in the supernal realms as in the physical World of Action, since with Him all is unified,
וְהַנְהָגַת כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה.
and the governance of all realms proceeds solely according to the Torah.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת "נָעוּ מַעְגְּלֹתֶיהָ" שֶׁל תּוֹרָה,
However, in truth the paths of the Torah are deeply intricate and unfathomable;
וְאַף עַל פִּי דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנְחָא, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵידַע כְּלוּם מִמֶּנָּה אִם לֹא עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and even though it is written and laid before us, it is impossible to know anything of it except through the Oral Torah,
וַ"אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ", דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵין לָהּ קֵץ,
and “its measure is longer than the earth,” for the Oral Torah has no end,
וּבְכָל יוֹם אֶפְשָׁר לְתַלְמִיד וָתִיק לְחַדֵּשׁ חֲדָשׁוֹת,
and on each day it is possible for a devoted scholar to innovate fresh insights,
וּכְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ,
such as that student who knew how to declare the creeping creature ritually pure,
וְאֵין זֶה פִּלְפּוּל שֶׁל הֶבֶל כְּקֻשְׁיַת הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (עֵירוּבִין י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳);
and this is not empty sophistry, as the objection of Tosafot might suggest (Eruvin 13b);

דַּהֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה1247 Midrash Tehillim 146:4 — What is meant by “He releases the bound”? Some say: Every animal that became impure in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, will render pure in the time to come. (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר קמ״ו): "ה' מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים" — דֶּעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַתִּיר אִסּוּרִים.

for our Sages of blessed memory truly stated (Shocher Tov, Psalm 146): “Hashem frees the bound (matir asurim)”—meaning that in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will permit that which was forbidden.
וְחַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה תִּשְׁתַּנֶּה כִּי הִיא נִצְחִית;
And God forbid that the Torah itself should change, for it is eternal;

רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ג)1248 Vayikra Rabbah 13:3 — R. Avin bar Kahana said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said — a new Torah shall go forth from Me; a renewal of Torah shall go forth from Me. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Parah 6): "A new Torah shall go forth from Me — a renewal of Torah shall go forth from Me" means that then the garments made of the words of Torah will be new garments: the future banquet is ancient matters not yet revealed, and then there will be a renewed garment of Torah of which we have no grasp in this world. Hence "he who gathers [the heifer's ashes] shall wash his garments" [said of the Holy One, blessed be He, who gathers Israel's dispersed]: as it were, He will need to wash the garments, and there will be "a renewal of Torah shall go forth from Me." Sod Yesharim (First Night of Pesach 40): It is written "a new Torah shall go forth from Me," and the Sages explained, "a renewal of Torah shall go forth from Me": in truth the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world with the Torah, but the words of Torah were concealed in every kind of garb. And "Torah," as the Zohar explains, is that which teaches and reveals what was hidden at first and unknown — through the Torah the light is revealed that Israel arose [first] in [God's] thought, and this light is revealed out of all the garbings.: "חִדּוּשׁ תּוֹרָה מֵאִתִּי תֵצֵא",
it is only as the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 13:3): “A new dimension of Torah shall proceed from Me,”
שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אֵיזֶה חִדּוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה לְהַתִּיר דְּבָרִים שֶׁהָיָה אָסוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
meaning that a novel insight within the Torah will be revealed to permit things that were forbidden in this world,
וְאָז כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הַחִדּוּשׁ יַכִּירוּ הַכֹּל וְיֵדְעוּ שֶׁגַּם זֶה עַצְמוֹ מִכְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ חִדּוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה.
and when that revelation occurs, all will perceive and realize that this too was always part of the Torah and is not an arbitrary innovation contrary to it.
וַהֲרֵי כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים חִדְּשׁוּ סוֹפְרִים לַעֲקוֹר דְּבַר תּוֹרָה,
Indeed, the Scribes instituted several measures that suspend a Torah commandment,
כְּשׁוֹפָר וְלוּלָב שֶׁאֵין דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת,
such as the shofar and lulav not overriding Shabbat,
וּכְהֶתֵּר כְּתִיבַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכַדּוֹמֶה, וְזֶה חִדּוּשׁ מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.
and the permission to record the Oral Torah in writing and the like, which are enactments stemming from the Scribes.
וְיֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן חִדּוּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ,
And there is likewise profound innovation within the words of the Torah itself,
וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק הָיָה מַשִּׂיג אֵיזֶה הַשָּׂגָה אֵיךְ לְטַהֵר שֶׁרֶץ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד,
and that veteran disciple had attained an apprehension of how the creeping creature will be declared pure in the future,
וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה עֲמֻקּוֹת הַרְבֵּה שֶׁאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹם בֵּיאוּרָם.
and there are deep mysteries in this matter whose explanation does not belong here.
רַק עַל כָּל פָּנִים זֶה גָּלוּי לַכֹּל עַתָּה שֶׁנִּתְגַּלֵּית תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לַכֹּל,
At any rate, it is now evident to all, since the Oral Torah has been revealed to everyone,
כִּי בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֵין נוֹדָע כְּלוּם פֵּירוּשׁ שׁוּם מִצְוָה וְשׁוּם אַזְהָרָה, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָדַעַת מִמֶּנָּה כְּלוּם.
that from the Written Torah alone no interpretation of any commandment or prohibition is known, and it is impossible to understand anything from it independently.
וְעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹלָמוֹ שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה,
Therefore, one cannot fathom the blessed Hashem’s governance of His world, which operates in accordance with the Torah,
כֵּיוָן דְּהַתּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ גַּם כֵּן נֶעֶלְמָה.
since the Torah itself is likewise deeply concealed.

items.h:
Seif 24 — Oral Torah as Wisdom Found in Darkness
The sages uncover truth from concealment, while Mashiach's Torah will reveal dimensions beyond present attainment.

p: וְאַף שֶׁנִּגְלוּ מִסְטוֹרֶיהָ לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And even though its mysteries were revealed to the sages of Israel,
הַיְינוּ כְּפִי הַשָּׂגַת כָּל חָכָם כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג מִמֶּנָּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
this was according to the comprehension of each sage, in proportion to what was possible for him to attain of it in this world;
וַעֲדַיִן אֵין שִׁיעוּר לַנֶּעֱלָמוֹת.
and still there is no limit to what remains hidden.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה י״א, ח1249 Kohelet Rabbah 11:8 — "For if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all, and remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many" — "if many years," let him rejoice in the joy of the Torah; "and remember the days of darkness," these are the days of evil; "for they shall be many" — the Torah that a man learns in this world is vanity beside the Torah of the Messiah. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Parah 6): The saying "the Torah a person learns in this world is vanity beside the Torah of the Messiah" [and likewise "beside the Torah of the World to Come"] means that then the words of Torah will wear a different garment — new garments, a renewed garment of Torah of which we have no grasp in this world.׳):
And as our Sages of blessed memory said (Kohelet Rabbah 11:8):
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶבֶל הוּא לִפְנֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
that the Torah of this world is vanity compared to the Torah of Mashiach,
שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵמוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for then will be the complete revelation of the Oral Torah
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת לְנַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
according to the utmost that can possibly be revealed to the souls of Israel.
וְאָז יָבִינוּ הַכֹּל הַנְהָגוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And then everyone will comprehend the blessed Hashem’s conduct in this world,
אֵיךְ הָיָה "תָּמִים פָּעֳלוֹ" וְלֹא עַוְלָתָה בּוֹ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
how “His work was perfect” and there was no injustice in Him, Heaven forbid,
כְּטַעֲנַת כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים: "מַדּוּעַ דֶּרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים צָלֵחָה" וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
unlike the complaint raised by all the prophets: “Why does the way of the wicked prosper?” and the like.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה וְחַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת יִשְּׁבוּ הַרְבֵּה שְׁאֵלוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה
And our Sages of blessed memory and the sages of the Truth (Kabbalah) settled many such questions
עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַנִּגְלָה לָהֶם שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה בִּימֵי הַנְּבִיאִים.
based upon the Oral Torah that was revealed to them, which had not yet been revealed in the days of the prophets.
כִּי הַתְחָלַת גִּלּוּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה מֵעֵת חֲתִימַת הַנְּבוּאָה וְסִלּוּק גִּלּוּי הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי.
For the beginning of the revelation of the Oral Torah occurred from the sealing of prophecy and the departure of the manifest Shechinah from Israel, which was not present in the Second Temple.
כִּי כָּל דִּבְרֵי נְבוּאָה שֶׁהוּא דְּבַר ה' הֵם מִתְלַבְּשִׁים גַּם כֵּן בִּכְתָב,
For all words of prophecy, which are the word of Hashem, clothe themselves in written script as well,
כִּי הֵם מִתְגַּלִּים כְּפִי לְבוּשׁ הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן,
since they are manifested according to the garment of this world too,
וְ"רוּחַ ה' דִּבֶּר בּוֹ" בְּכָל מְדַבֵּר בִּנְבוּאָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
and “the spirit of Hashem spoke through him” applies to everyone who speaks through prophecy and the Holy Spirit,
וּמִמֵּילָא הוּא מוּגְדָּר וּמוּגְבָּל כְּפִי הַכְּלִי וְהַלְּבוּשׁ הַמַּגְבִּילוֹ,
and consequently it is bounded and restricted according to the vessel and the garment that limits it,
וְאֵין יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג רַק מַה שֶּׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַרְאוֹת לָהֶם בִּנְבוּאָה.
and they can apprehend only that which the blessed Hashem desired to show them through prophecy.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ חֲכָמִים גַּם כֵּן,
And even though they were sages as well,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִפְּאַת שֶׁפַע הַנְּבוּאָה וְגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁהָיָה אָז בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
nevertheless, owing to the abundance of prophecy and the revelation of the Shechinah that then existed in Israel,
לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב הַשָּׂגָה דֶּרֶךְ חָכְמָה מֵעַצְמוֹ לִכְלוּם,
attainment through self-generated wisdom was considered as nothing;
כִּי זֶה הַשָּׂגָה מְסֻפֶּקֶת וַאֲפֵלָה מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for that is a doubtful and murky perception from the perspective of this world,
שֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִים אִם הִיא הַשָּׂגָה אֲמִתִּית,
in which one does not know whether it is a true comprehension,

דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ״ד1250 Sanhedrin 24a — What is "Babel"? R. Yochanan said: mixed in Scripture, mixed in Mishnah, mixed in Talmud. "He has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead" — R. Yirmeya said: This is the Talmud of Babylonia. Rashi: "He has made me dwell in dark places" — for they are not gentle with one another [in debate], and their learning remains in doubt in their hands. Tosafos (s.v. "mixed in Scripture, in Mishnah"): Rabbeinu Tam explained that through our Talmud [in which all three are mixed] we discharge the Sages' instruction that a person should always divide his years into three — a third for Scripture, a third for Mishnah, a third for Talmud. Even so, we read the passage of the daily offering every day, and study the Mishnah "Which is the place [of the offerings]" and recite "R. Yishmael says: by thirteen principles." Maharsha: Since by grammar the name should have been בלל ["confounded"], the extra ב of בבל alludes to the two Torahs, Written and Oral: out of their arrogance they study them mixed and jumbled, learning Mishnah at five, the age for Scripture, and Talmud at ten, the age for Mishnah. The prophet Jeremiah said "He has made me dwell in dark places" of the Babylonian exile, and R. Yirmeya applied it to himself as a sign, for he came from Babylonia and had learned its confused and mixed study there. "Like those long dead" [כמתי עולם]: read not עולם but עילם — like those who came to Elam. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 24a): One might ask: was the city called Babel in the generation of the Dispersion on account of the Babylonian Talmud? But it was called Babel because there He confounded the language of all, which shows that Babel is a place fit for everything to be mixed together; therefore the Torah there is mixed of Scripture, Mishnah and Talmud. "He has made me dwell in dark places" was said of Israel's exile, when they were exiled from the Land and sat in darkness, that is, in Babylonia, which is called "a land of darkness" because it lies deep; so too the Talmud of Babylonia, being full of dialectic, has no clear halachah, for there is always more to debate and question until the matter is no longer clear. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 8): The Oral Torah spread chiefly in Babylonia, and so the Gemara says, "'He has made me dwell in dark places' — this is the Talmud of Babylonia": that is, there was the chief spread of the Oral Torah, bringing out light from within the darkness through the dialectic (pilpul) of Torah. עַמּוּד א׳): "בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים הוֹשִׁיבַנִי" — עַל תַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי.
wherefore they said in Sanhedrin 24a: “‘He has set me in dark places’—this refers to the Babylonian Talmud.”
וְזֶהוּ כָּל חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, לְהַשִּׂיג הָאֱמֶת מִצַּד הָאֹפֶל וְהַהֶעְלֵם.
And this is the entire wisdom of the Oral Torah: to apprehend the truth from within darkness and concealment.

items.h:
Seif 25 — From Prophetic Guidance to Intellectual Torah
When open prophecy receded, Torah wisdom became a repeatable form of guidance accessible through intellectual apprehension.

p: וְזֶהוּ בִּזְמַן הַהֶעְלֵם;
This applies in a time of concealment;
אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיָה הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא הָיוּ נִכְנָסִים לְהַשָּׂגוֹת שֶׁל מַחֲשַׁכִּים כְּלָל,
however, when the Shechinah rested openly in Israel, they did not enter into perceptions born of darkness at all,
כִּי הָיָה אָז כָּל הַהַנְהָגָה עַל פִּי נְבוּאָה,
for then the entire leadership and conduct was according to prophecy,
דְּהָיוּ נְבִיאִים כִּפְלַיִם כְּיוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם, מִלְּבַד בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר,
