since there were twice as many prophets as those who left Egypt, besides countless individuals possessed of the Holy Spirit,

אֶלָּא שֶׁנְּבוּאָה שֶׁלֹּא הֻצְרְכָה לְדוֹרוֹת לֹא נִכְתְּבָה (מְגִלָּה י״ד1251 Megillah 14a — There were in fact more, as it is taught in a baraita: Many prophets arose for Israel, double the number of those who came out of Egypt. But a prophecy that was needed for later generations was written down, and one that was not needed was not written down. Rashi: “A prophecy that was needed for later generations” — one from which to learn repentance or a ruling; all forty-eight of these were needed, and they are enumerated in Halachot Gedolot from Seder Olam, from Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses and Aaron down to Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi and Mordecai Bilshan. Since it was said above that Daniel was not a prophet, one must remove Daniel from the count and insert Shemaiah, who said to Rehoboam, “Do not go up and do not fight against your brethren the children of Israel” — and two of them I do not know. Maharsha: What was said above, that Elkanah was “one of two hundred seers,” refers only to his own generation; but taking all the generations together there were double the number of those who came out of Egypt. עַמּוּד א׳).
only that prophecy not required for future generations was not committed to writing (Megillah 14a).
אֲבָל כָּל הַהַנְהָגָה דִּלְפִי שָׁעָה הָיָה עַל פִּי נְבִיאִים,
However, all the immediate, temporary guidance was governed by prophets;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ אָבוֹת: "זְקֵנִים מְסָרוּהָ לִנְבִיאִים, וּנְבִיאִים מְסָרוּהָ לְאַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה",
and therefore the Sages taught at the beginning of Avot: “The Elders transmitted it to the Prophets, and the Prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly,”
וְלֹא חָשְׁבוּ סֵדֶר הַמְקַבְּלִים גַּם בָּהֶם דּוֹר אַחַר דּוֹר כְּמוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ,
and they did not list the detailed chain of recipients generation after generation among them as was done later,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהַקְדָּמַת חִבּוּרוֹ לְהַמְצִיא סֵדֶר קַבָּלָה גַּם בָּהֶם.
even though Maimonides reconstructed a generational order of transmission among them in the introduction to his code.
אַף דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּהַתַּנָּא לֹא סִדֵּר מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּכְּתוּבִים,
Even if one might argue that the Tanna did not enumerate figures already explicit in Scripture,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְהַזְכִּיר כְּלָל זְקֵנִים וּנְבִיאִים, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ.
nevertheless, if so, he should not have mentioned Elders and Prophets at all, let alone Moses and Joshua.
אֶלָּא דְּבֶאֱמֶת בִּנְבִיאִים לֹא שַׁיָּךְ קַבָּלָה מִפֶּה אֶל פֶּה בְּעִנְיַן הַנְּבוּאָה;
Rather, with prophets a mouth-to-mouth transmission does not truly apply regarding the prophecy itself;
אַף דְּהָיוּ תַּלְמִידֵי נְבִיאִים, הַיְינוּ קֹדֶם שֶׁהִגִּיעוּ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה,
for though there were disciples of the prophets, that was only before they attained prophetic rank,
אֲבָל מִשֶּׁזָּכָה לִנְבוּאָה בְּעַצְמוֹ, הֲרֵי הָיָה שׁוֹמֵעַ מִפִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ.
but once a prophet merited prophecy himself, he heard directly from the mouth of the blessed Hashem Himself.
רַק חָשֵׁיב דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל מְסִירַת הַנְהָגָה עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל:
The Mishnah merely traces the general transmission of Torah-based leadership in Israel:
בַּתְּחִלָּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הוּא שֶׁקִּבֵּל תּוֹרָה מִסִּינַי, וְהוּא הַנְהָגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מַמָּשׁ.
first Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who received the Torah from Sinai, representing the direct governance of the Written Torah;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ לִזְקֵנִים, וְהֵם שֶׁהֶאֱרִיכוּ יָמִים אַחַר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
and afterward to the Elders, who outlived Joshua,
וְהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן מִדּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, תַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהִשִּׂיגוּ עֲדַיִן הַנְהָגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
and were likewise from the generation of the wilderness, students of Moses our teacher who still grasped the Written Torah governance of Moses;
כִּי מִסְּתָמָא לֹא הִנְהִיגוּ וְלָמְדוּ אֶלָּא כְּפִי קַבָּלָתָם מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
for they presumably led and taught solely according to their direct tradition from Moses our teacher,
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָאִים "זְקֵנִים", שֶׁהָיְתָה יְדִיעָתָם רַק מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהֵם זְקֵנִים שֶׁהִכִּירוּ אֶת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
and therefore they are termed “Elders,” because their authority stemmed from being the elders who knew Moses our teacher personally.
וְהַקָּרוֹב דְּהָיוּ גַּם בְּעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ פְּחוּתִים מִבְּנֵי עֶשְׂרִים אוֹ יְתֵירִים עַל שִׁשִּׁים דְּלֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַגְּזֵרָה.
And it is likely that they were present at the Giving of the Torah, being under twenty or over sixty years old so as not to be included in the decree of the wilderness.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ לִנְבִיאִים בְּהַנְהָגַת הַנְּבוּאָה,
Afterward to the Prophets through prophetic leadership,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ לְאַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בְּהַנְהָגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
and afterward to the Men of the Great Assembly through the leadership of the Oral Torah;
וּמֵהֶם וָהֵילָךְ שַׁיָּךְ הַקַּבָּלָה פֶּה אֶל פֶּה,
and from them onward mouth-to-mouth transmission truly applies,

דִּ"דְבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב" (גִּיטִּין ס1252 Gittin 60b — R. Yehuda bar Naḥmani, the interpreter of R. Shimon ben Lakish, expounded: It is written, "Write down these words," and it is written, "For on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you." How can both stand? Words that are written you may not recite orally, and words that are oral you may not recite in writing. The school of R. Yishmael taught: "These" — these you may write, but you may not write down the laws. Rashi: "It is written: Write you these words" — evidently they were written; "and it is written: on the basis of [by the mouth of] these words" — evidently they were not written. "Words" that I told you in writing you may not transmit to Israel by mouth. "And words that are oral you may not express in writing" — from here you learn that the Talmud was not given to be written, and it was written only because the Torah was being forgotten. Maharsha: At first glance these verses prove only that there are matters in writing and matters that are oral, but not that one may not express the one in the manner of the other. The inference is drawn from the word "these" written in each of them, as is shown by the teaching of the school of R. Yishmael — and the school of R. Yishmael stated only one of the two halves. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Gittin 60b): The Oral Torah is not fit to be put in writing, because it consists of the particulars of the commandments and their explanations, and to this there is no end or limit, since the particulars have no end; nor would it be anything whole were he to write only part of it and not all, and writing requires that the whole be there in its completeness — all the more so the Torah, of which it is written, "The Torah of the Lord is perfect." And the reverse likewise: since the Written Torah is whole and complete, it must be in writing and not by mouth, for one who says words by mouth says one part after another, and even were he to say the whole Torah, at the moment he says the later part the earlier part is already not there, and the Torah of the Lord is not perfect as it ought to be. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 27): The curses of Mount Eval are spelled out in the Torah but not the blessings of Mount Gerizim, for what the Torah sets down in writing, open to all, are matters revealed and graspable by all, visible to the eye, while what is not revealed to the eye was said orally: "words that are oral, which you may not recite in writing," since such matters cannot be revealed to all, only to one who attains them. The curses were only in this world, whereas those blessings were of the World to Come, and therefore they were not given in writing. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 7): The Torah was written out clearly in the seventy languages, for from the side of writing, which is the revelation of wisdom, it was revealed to all who come into the world, and the ancient philosophers too attained knowledge of God through their wisdom; yet their hearts were not changed one iota, and the Holy One, blessed be He, dwelt only in the hearts of Israel, to whom the Oral Torah was given over, that is, the revelation through speech of the understanding in the heart. Therefore "words that are oral you may not recite in writing," for the essence of oral words is in speech, through which what is in the heart is revealed. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 4): The Mishnah begins and ends with mem, to say that its whole scope is to refine deeds to their proper completeness, which is the matter of the Oral Torah that "you may not recite in writing." For the conduct of the supernal wisdom is the reverse of what appears to the eye of flesh, to which deeds seem the revealed part and mind and heart the hidden, writing the revealed and the oral the concealed; in the wisdom of the Blessed One the hidden is revealed and the revealed hidden, for the deed is in truth an image and the hidden is beyond image. Therefore the study that pertains to mind and heart is in writing, and that which pertains to deeds is oral.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳),
for “words that are oral you may not write down” (Gittin 60b),
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג הָאֲמִתּוּת שֶׁבְּלֵב הֶחָכָם אֶלָּא בְּקַבָּלָה מִפֶּה אֶל פֶּה.
since it is impossible to grasp the truth in the heart of a sage except through direct reception from mouth to mouth.
וּלְעוֹלָם, כְּפִי הַנְהָגַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כֵּן הוּא הַנְהָגָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
And always, corresponding to the Torah's mode of leadership within Israel, such is the blessed Hashem’s governance across all worlds,
וְאַף הָאֻמּוֹת מִתְנַהֲגִים כֵּן בְּזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה.
and even the nations conduct themselves correspondingly in parallel.
וְכָל רִבּוּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶצְלָם וְחַרְטֻמִּים וּמְכַשְּׁפִים הָיָה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיָה גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה וּנְבוּאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל;
All the prevalence of idolatry, sorcery, and astrologers among them existed as long as there was open Shechinah and prophecy in Israel;
וּמִשֶּׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה וְהִתְחִיל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הִתְחִיל גַּם כֵּן אֶצְלָם חָכְמַת יְוָנִית שֶׁהִיא חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית.
and once it departed and the Oral Torah began, Greek wisdom—which is human philosophy—began among them as well.
כִּי הַתְחָלַת אַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הָיָה בִּתְחִלַּת מַלְכוּת יָוָן, שֶׁאָז הָיְתָה חֲתִימַת הַנְּבוּאָה,
For the beginning of the Men of the Great Assembly coincided with the start of the Greek empire, which was when prophecy was sealed,
וְעַל כֵּן יָוָן הֵם שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ בִּגְזֵרַת שְׁמָד,
and therefore Greece was the first kingdom to issue decrees of religious eradication,
וְכָל גְּזֵרוֹת וְצָרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָז וָהֵילָךְ וְגַם גָּלוּת אֱדוֹם, הַכֹּל הָיָה נֶגֶד הָאֱמוּנָה,
and all persecutions and afflictions visited upon Israel from then onward, including the exile of Edom, were aimed against faith,
שֶׁאִם הָיוּ רוֹצִים לְהִתְעָרֵב בַּגּוֹיִם וְלִהְיוֹת לְעַמָּא חַד, לֹא הָיוּ סוֹבְלִים שׁוּם גָּלוּת וְצַעַר כְּלָל.
for had Israel been willing to assimilate among the nations and become one people, they would have suffered no exile or distress whatsoever.
כִּי הַנְהָגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִיא הַהַנְהָגָה שֶׁעַל פִּי מִסְטוֹרָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
Because the governance of the Oral Torah is guidance according to the inner mysteries of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ גּוּפָנִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which was never revealed or embodied in a physical garment in this world,
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִכְתַּב, שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּהָאוֹתִיּוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת בִּכְתָב.
which is why it was not written, since it cannot clothe itself in physical written letters.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין יְכוֹלִים הָאֻמּוֹת לִסְבּוֹל,
And this the nations cannot bear,
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּכוּת וּתְפִיסָה בָּזֶה כְּבַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
for they have no connection or grasp in it as they do with the Written Torah,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ גַּם לָהֶם תְּפִיסָה מִצַּד הַלְּבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי, עַד שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לוֹמַר "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל".
where they possess an intellectual hold through its external garment, to the extent of claiming “We are Israel.”
וְלָכֵן לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם טַעֲנָה נֶגֶד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, רַק נֶגֶד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
Therefore they brought no complaint against the Written Torah, but only against the Oral Torah.
וְאָז הָיְתָה הַגְּזֵרָה עַל הַגּוּפוֹת, כִּי הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת הַתּוֹרָה הָיְתָה בִּלְבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי מַמָּשׁ.
In earlier times the decrees were upon physical bodies, for the Torah’s manifestation was in the physical realm;
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵין מִתְלַבֶּשֶׁת אֶלָּא בַּשֵּׂכֶל,
the Oral Torah, however, clothes itself only in the intellect,
עַל כֵּן אֵין הַגְּזֵרוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם עוֹד עַל הַגּוּף, אֶלָּא עַל הָאֱמוּנָה.
therefore their persecution shifted from the physical body to matters of faith.
וּגְזֵרַת הָמָן, אַף שֶׁהָיְתָה סְתָם "לְהַשְׁמִיד וְלַהֲרֹג",
And Haman’s decree, although explicitly phrased to “destroy and kill” physically,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר טַעֲנָתוֹ אֵצֶל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הָיָה: "יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד" וְגוֹמֵר,
nevertheless his main argument to Ahasuerus was: “There is a certain people...” and so forth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּמְגִלָּה וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד אֱמוּנָתָם,
and as the Sages expounded in Megillah and the Midrash, this was rooted in their faith,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְדָתֵיהֶם שֹׁנוֹת מִכָּל עָם".
as Scripture states: “and their laws are different from every other people.”
וְאַף שֶׁהַגְּזֵרָה בַּפֹּעַל הָיְתָה סְתָם,
And though the formal decree was destruction without religious qualification,
וְגַם הָמָן כִּוֵּן דַּוְקָא לִגְזֹר סְתָם כִּי הָיָה שׂוֹנֵא לְמָרְדֳּכַי וְעַמּוֹ בְּעֶצֶם,
and Haman specifically intended a blanket slaughter because he hated Mordechai and his people essentially,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ לַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הָיָה מִצַּד שִׁנּוּי הַדָּת וְהַתּוֹרָה.
nevertheless his instigation of Ahasuerus focused on the difference in their faith and laws.
כִּי כְּבָר הִתְחִיל הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
For the awakening of the Oral Torah had already begun within the souls of Israel,
שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַפּוֹעַל אַחַר הַנֵּס דְּ"קִיְּמוּ וְקִבְּלוּ".
which emerged into actuality following the miracle when “they confirmed and accepted.”
וְאָז "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה" — זוֹ תּוֹרָה,
And then “the Jews had light”—this refers to Torah,
הַיְינוּ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת גִּלּוּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning the renewed disclosure of the Oral Torah;
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֻכָּמָא הִיא לְגַבֵּי הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה וְנִקְרָא "בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים",
for even though it is dark compared to prophetic sight and is called “dark places,”
הַיְינוּ לְעִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר הַפְּרָטִי שֶׁנִּגְלָה לַנָּבִיא שֶׁהוּא בָּרוּר וְאֵין בּוֹ סָפֵק,
this limitation applies only to the specific, discrete point revealed clearly to a prophet without doubt,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג בְּחָכְמָה, יוּכַל חָכָם אַחֵר לַחֲלוֹק עָלָיו,
whereas when one attains through intellect another sage may disagree,
וְגַם הַשָּׂגַת הַנָּבִיא עַצְמוֹ הוּא בִּרְאִיָּה מַמָּשׁ.
and the prophet’s own perception is through literal vision.
אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן הַשָּׂגַת כְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה אֵצֶל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל — "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא",
However, regarding the comprehension of the Torah in its entirety for all of Israel, “a sage is superior to a prophet”;
דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין נִקְרָאִים "עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה", שֶׁהֵם הַמְּאִירִים עֵינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמוֹרִים לָהֶם הַדֶּרֶךְ בְּתוֹרַת ה',
for the Sanhedrin are called the “eyes of the congregation,” illuminating Israel’s eyes and directing them in the Torah of Hashem;
וְלִהְיוֹת מִתְגַּלֶּה הָאוֹר לַכֹּל שֶׁיּוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד לְהַשִּׂיג בַּתּוֹרָה וּלְהָבִין מִתּוֹכָהּ בְּכָל פְּרָט מַעֲשֶׂה — זֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and to reveal this illumination to everyone so that each individual can comprehend Torah and understand every practical detail—this is achievable solely through the Oral Torah.
דְּעַל יְדֵי נְבוּאָה הָיָה צָרִיךְ בְּכָל פְּרָט לֵילֵךְ אֶל הָרוֹאֶה,
For through prophecy one had to go to the seer for every practical inquiry,
וְהוּא הָיָה צָרִיךְ מַרְאֵה נְבוּאָה חֲדָשָׁה בְּאוֹתוֹ פְּרָט;
and the seer required a fresh prophetic vision for that individual matter;
אֲבָל הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה הִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת בְּכָל פְּרָט וּלְכָל נֶפֶשׁ בְּכָל עֵת וּזְמַן,
whereas intellectual apprehension encompasses every detail and is accessible to every soul at all times,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מִסְטוֹרֵי הַתּוֹרָה, לֹא כְּפִי לְבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי לְבַד.
since it grasps the inner mysteries of the Torah, and not merely its external, corporeal garment.

items.h:
Seif 26 — The Oral Torah as Israel's Unique Wisdom
Gentile wisdom can be genuine, but Torah innovation belongs to Israel because its root remains bound to Hashem's Torah.

p: וְזֶהוּ הָאוֹר שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אַחַר הַנֵּס דְּהָמָן,
And this is the light within the Torah that was revealed following the miracle over Haman;
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים,
and this is the primary distinction between Israel and the nations,
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁנּוֹבֵעַ מִלִּבְבוֹת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for the Oral Torah is that which flows from the hearts of the sages of Israel,
וּמַה שֶּׁהֵם מְחַדְּשִׁים הוּא תּוֹרָה שְׁלֵמָה.
and what they innovate constitutes complete Torah.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַה שֶּׁחַכְמֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת מְחַדְּשִׁים;
This is not so with what the sages of the gentiles innovate;

אַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָכְמָה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — אֵין תּוֹרָה בָּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה פָּרָשָׁה ב׳, ט1253 Eikhah Rabbah 2:13 — "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah" (Lamentations 2:9). If a man should say to you, There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it is written: "And I will destroy the wise men out of Edom, and discernment out of the mount of Esau" (Obadiah 1:8). [If he should say,] There is Torah among the nations — do not believe it, for it is written: "Her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Although the sages of the nations may originate wisdom in matters of the service of the Blessed One, it is not reckoned as Oral Torah — only what the Sages of Israel originate. And this is "He shone forth from Seir to them": human wisdom, which is chiefly in Seir, as the Sages said, "There is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'"; and this shone forth to Israel, to be theirs alone, for nothing is called wisdom but the wisdom of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Although there are wise men among the nations too — over whom one blesses "Who has given of His wisdom" — the essence of wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah. As the Sages already said, "There is wisdom among the nations — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom'; there is Torah — do not believe it," for the Torah is da'as, the apprehension of the Blessed One's wisdom, which is above human wisdom. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 17): "You have taken gifts among men [ba-adam]" — these are the spoils taken from Esau, the power of "we will do"; for "there is wisdom in Edom — believe it, as it says, 'I will destroy the wise out of Edom,'" that is, the wisdom of the Oral Torah, to rectify the excess of anger, while might is used only to conquer the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The Oral Torah — what the Sages of Israel draw forth from their hearts — is in the hands of Israel alone: if one says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it, for although there is wisdom among the nations, words of Torah are never made from their wisdom, only from the wisdom that springs from the heart of Israel. Not for nothing did the Sages phrase it, "If a person says to you there is Torah…" — why would anyone say so? But they foresaw by the holy spirit that the philosophizers of later generations would claim that the external wisdom of the Greeks is the secrets of the Torah, and informed us not to believe it.׳),
for though there is wisdom among the nations of the world, there is no Torah among the nations (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 2:9),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהַמְצִיא דְּבַר חָכְמָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּלָל.
and it is impossible for them to produce an insight of wisdom that would constitute words of Torah at all.
וְכֵן יוֹם טוֹב הוּא מַה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לַזְּמַנִּים,
Likewise, the festival is that which Israel sanctifies the appointed times,

וְגַם כֵּן נִיתַּן רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל "הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט״ו1254 Shemot Rabbah 15:2 — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: In the past it was in My hands, as it is said, “He made the moon for appointed times.” But from here onward it is handed over into your hands, into your authority — if you say yes, it is yes; if you say no, it is no. In any case, “this month shall be yours.”;
and this too was given only to Israel, "This month shall be unto you," as the Sages said in Shemot Rabbah, parashah 15;
וְאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם הוּא מִצַּד פְּעֻלָּתָם, וְזֶהוּ הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
and these two derive from their own initiative, representing the awakening from below.
וּמִילָה וּתְפִלִּין הוּא מַה שֶּׁמְּקַדְּשִׁים אוֹתוֹ הַרְבֵּה מִלְּמַעְלָה.
Circumcision and tefillin, by contrast, are that through which one is greatly sanctified from Above.
וּמִילָה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחִלּוּק בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים מִתּוֹלָדָה קֹדֶם לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
And circumcision is the root distinction between Israel and the nations from birth, prior to any personal human effort,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה דְּלֹא יָדַע כְּלוּם,
for he is circumcised at eight days when he possesses no conscious knowledge,

וְאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שְׁמָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (ל״א1255 Nedarim 31b — "Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me" — he is permitted with respect to uncircumcised Jews and forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world. "Benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to me" — he is forbidden with respect to uncircumcised Jews and permitted with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world; for the foreskin is named only for the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along. עַמּוּד ב׳),
and foreskin is designated solely by their name, as they taught in Nedarim 31b;
וּדְאַפִילּוּ עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ מוּלִים,
and even uncircumcised Jews are still categorized as circumcised,
וְהַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ עָרֵל בְּמֵזִיד, מִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁרְשׁוֹ יְהוּדִי וְנִקְרָא מָהוּל.
meaning that even if one remains uncircumcised intentionally, his root is nevertheless Jewish and he is reckoned as circumcised.
וּתְפִלִּין הוּא הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחַר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם,
And tefillin represents the binding of the blessed Hashem with Israel following their personal spiritual effort,
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ".
in that "all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you."
וְכָל זֶה זָכוּ אַחַר הַנֵּס דְּפוּרִים,
And to all this they merited after the miracle of Purim,
שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה הָאוֹר דְּתוֹרָה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
when the light of Torah was revealed in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְפַּרְסֵם כָּל שָׁרְשֵׁי מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
whereby all the fundamental roots of Israel's preeminence became widely known,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרְרוּ כָּל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נֶגְדָּם בְּפִרְסוּם בְּעִנְיְנֵי אֱמוּנָה.
which subsequently aroused all the nations of the world against them openly regarding matters of religious faith.
אֲבָל בִּימֵי הָמָן הָיָה רַק הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מֵעִנְיַן אֱמוּנָה,
In the days of Haman, however, it was only the initial stirring regarding faith;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּפִרְסוּם הָיָה סְתָם,
yet openly and formally the decree was generic destruction,
וְעַל כֵּן נִיתַּן לִכְתֹּב,
and therefore the Megillah was permitted to be committed to canonical writing,
כִּי הָיָה הַנֵּס עֲדַיִן מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּגוּפָנִית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בַּפֹּעַל,
for the miracle was still clothed within physical reality in this world according to how it unfolded in actuality,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּכֹּחַ הָיָה הָעִיקָּר בְּעִנְיַן הַתּוֹרָה.
though in potential its essential dimension lay in the spiritual matter of the Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן נִמְשַׁל לְשַׁחַר הַבָּא בְּסוֹף הַלַּיְלָה, שֶׁכְּבָר מַתְחִיל הָאוֹרָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
Therefore it was compared to the morning dawn that arrives at the end of the night, when the illumination of the Oral Torah already begins to break forth.
אֲבָל הַנֵּס דַּחֲנֻכָּה, שֶׁהָיָה הַצָּלָה מִשְּׁמָד לְבַד,
However, the miracle of Chanukah, which was an exclusive deliverance from forced religious apostasy,
לֹא נִקְבְּעוּ אֶלָּא לְהַלֵּל וּלְהוֹדוֹת וְלֹא שׁוּם עוֹנֶג גּוּפָנִי, כִּי לֹא הָיְתָה הַצָּלַת גּוּפוֹת.
was established solely for praise and thanksgiving without any requirement for bodily indulgence, because it did not involve physical rescue from death.
וְהַמִּצְוָה שֶׁבּוֹ בְּהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר,
And the mitzvah embodied within it is the kindling of the lamp,
כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיְשׁוּעָה, בְּ"אוֹרָה — זוֹ תּוֹרָה",
for this represents the true essence of the salvation, in that "light—this is Torah";
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב,
and therefore it was not permitted to be written down,
כִּי אֵין בּוֹ הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת בִּלְבוּשׁ גּוּפָנִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
because it contains no clothing in a physical garment in this world,
וְהוּא כְּכָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁ"אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאָמְרָם בִּכְתָב".
and is like all Oral Torah, of which it is ruled: "you are not permitted to set them down in writing."
שֶׁיְשׁוּעָה זוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁאֲרָה קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים לְדוֹרוֹת
For this salvation that remained permanently fixed for all generations,
כְּכָל קְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁנִּשְׁאָר בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן לְעוֹלָם,
like all sanctified seasons whose intrinsic holiness remains embedded in that recurring period forever,
קְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא יְשׁוּעַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁלֹּא יִטַּמָּא בְּחָכְמַת בְּנֵי נֵכָר,
this sanctity is purely the salvation of the soul and the intellect from being contaminated by the alien wisdom of foreigners,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד חָכְמַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
which stands in direct opposition to the wisdom of the sages of Israel in the Oral Torah.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁבַע חָכְמוֹת,
And it is known that there exist seven secular wisdoms,
וְהַמִּסְפָּר שְׁבִיעִי הִיא אֲמִתִּי, כִּי הַכֹּל הוּא זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה,
and this number seven is intrinsically true, for everything is created with a holy counterpart opposite an unholy one;
וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁל קְדֻשָּׁה חָלוּק לְשֶׁבַע,
and it is known that every realm of holiness is subdivided into seven,
שֶׁכְּנֶגְדָּם שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַשַּׁבָּת וְשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי שְׁמִטָּה כַּנּוֹדָע.
corresponding to which are the seven days of the week culminating in the Sabbath, and the seven years of the Shemitah cycle, as is known.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּחֲלוּקַת הַשֶּׁבַע מִינֵי חָכְמוֹת נָבוֹכוּ הַמִּתְחַכְּמִים וְאֵינוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁחִלְּקוּ הֵם סִדְרָם;
However, in the taxonomy of the seven wisdoms the secular philosophers became confused, and the reality is not as they arranged their order;
וְהֵם חָשְׁבוּ גַּם חָכְמַת הִגָּיוֹן,
for they counted Logic,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה אֵיךְ לַחְשׁוֹב דְּבַר חָכְמָה וְאֵיךְ לְהַמְצִיא הֶקֵּשֵׁי הַפִילוֹסוֹפִים וְכָל מִינֵי חָכְמוֹת,
which is the primordial root of thinking wisely and constructing philosophical syllogisms and all disciplines of knowledge,
מִכְּלַל שֶׁבַע חָכְמוֹת.
among the inventory of the seven wisdoms.
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה חוּץ מֵהֶם וּלְמַעְלָה מֵהֶם,
Yet in truth, this foundational faculty is outside of them and elevated far above them,
כִּי הִיא "אֵם הַבָּנִים" הַמּוֹלִידָה כָּל הַחָכְמוֹת, וְעִמָּהּ הֵם שְׁמוֹנָה,
for it is the "mother of the children" that engenders all the particular disciplines, and together with it they total eight;
וְנֶגְדָּם הֵם שְׁמוֹנַת יְמֵי חֲנֻכָּה,
and corresponding to them are the eight days of Chanukah,
שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל יָצְאוּ מִכָּל אוֹתָם חָכְמוֹת חִיצוֹנִיּוֹת לְחָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת.
wherein Israel emerged from all those external wisdoms into the wisdom of Truth.
וְהַנֵּס הָיָה רַק בְּשִׁבְעָה יָמִים,
And the supernatural miracle occurred strictly on seven of the days,
כִּי עַל יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן הָיָה לִדְלוֹק,
for there was sufficient oil naturally to burn on the first day;
רַק אוֹתוֹ יוֹם הָיָה דֻּגְמַת "אֵם הַבָּנִים" שֶׁבּוֹ,
yet that initial day stood as the archetype of the "mother of the children" within the set,
וְעַל יָדוֹ הָיָה הַנֵּס עַל כָּל שְׁאָר הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים,
and through it the miracle extended across all the remaining seven days,
וְעִיקַּר הַנֵּס הָיָה בּוֹ, שֶׁנּוֹסַף בּוֹ שֶׁפַע לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עוֹד לְשִׁבְעָה יָמִים זוּלָתוֹ.
and the crux of the miracle was embedded within it, in that divine bounty was added to it to flow through the other seven days alongside it.
וּבוֹ הוּא עִיקַּר הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְחָכְמַת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּעִנְיַן הַתְחָלַת הַמְצָאַת הַחָכְמָה,
And herein lies the primary distinction between Israel's wisdom and that of the nations concerning the genesis of human reasoning:
שֶׁאֵצֶל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם זֶה מִלִּבָּם מִתְחַכְּמִים אֵיךְ לְהַמְצִיא חָכְמוֹת, וְעַל כֵּן הַכֹּל הֶבֶל.
for among the nations even this origin is conceived by their own mortal minds formulating philosophies, wherefore all of it is ultimate vanity.
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּל חָכְמָתָם הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִתּוֹרָתוֹ,
The children of Israel, however, draw their entire wisdom from the blessed Hashem and from His Torah,
שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד לְכָל חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וּמִמֶּנָּה לוּקָּח הַכֹּל;
which serves as the bedrock for all wisdom of the Oral Torah, and from it everything is derived;
וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל כָּל הַחָכְמָה הוּא חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and the absolute root of all their wisdom is the wisdom of the blessed Hashem,
עַל כֵּן גַּם הַתּוֹלָדוֹת שֶׁמַּמְצִיאִים מֵעַצְמָם דָּבוּק בְּהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ.
wherefore even the derivative deductions they innovate of their own accord remain bound to the Root that is from the blessed Hashem, and everything is from Him.

items.h:
Seif 27 — The Eighth Day, Binah, and Increasing Chanukah Light
Circumcision and Chanukah point beyond the sevenfold world, where spiritual attainments accumulate and rise without being lost.

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן מִילָה בִּשְׁמוֹנָה,
And this is the inner meaning of circumcision on the eighth day,
הָרוֹמֵז לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּיוֹם שְׁמִינִי,
which hints that the innate root of Jewish identity from birth is likewise anchored to the eighth day,
שֶׁהוּא רוֹמֵז לְ"אֵם הַבָּנִים" הַמּוֹלִיד שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן,
which alludes to the "mother of the children" (Binah) that brings forth the seven days of the spiritual structure (middot),
דְּהֵם כָּל מִינֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, בֵּין בִּפְעֻלָּה בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בֵּין בִּשְׁבִיתָה בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
which embody every form of human endeavor, whether through active labor in the six workdays or through restful cessation on the Sabbath.
וְיוֹם שְׁמִינִי הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
The eighth day corresponds to the root of Binah (understanding) within the heart,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים בְּכָל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַמּוֹצִיאִים כָּל הָעִנְיָנִים לַפּוֹעַל בָּאֵיבָרִים.
from which flow the springs of life through all the faculties of the soul that execute every action through the physical limbs.
וּבָאִים בִּבְרִית חוֹתָמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּיוֹם זֶה
And we enter into the covenant of His blessed seal on this eighth day,
לוֹמַר כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת כָּל כֹּחוֹת אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הוּא רַק לַה' לְבַדּוֹ.
to proclaim that the primary source of all the faculties of a Jew is dedicated exclusively to Hashem alone.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַמַּעֲשִׂים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִיָּד בַּתּוֹלָדָה הַגּוּפָנִית.
And this pertains to the realm of practical actions, which is stamped immediately at bodily birth.
וִימֵי חֲנֻכָּה הֵם מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה,
The days of Chanukah, however, pertain to the realm of wisdom,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּשֶׁמֶן רוֹמֵז לְחָכְמָה בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת,
as is known that olive oil symbolizes wisdom in numerous scriptural and rabbinic passages,

דְּשֶׁמֶן מַחְכִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְנָחוֹת פ״ה1256 Menachot 85b — Tekoa is foremost for oil. "And Joab sent to Tekoa and fetched from there a wise woman" (II Samuel 14:2). What is special about Tekoa? R. Yochanan said: Since they are accustomed to olive oil, wisdom is common among them. Maharsha: The language of the verse implies that Yoav did not know of this woman in Tekoa; for had he known of her, it should have said, "And Yoav sent to the wise woman, to Tekoa." That is why the Gemara asks what is different about Tekoa. עַמּוּד ב׳),
for olive oil brings wisdom, as our Sages stated in Menachot 85b;
דְּעַל כֵּן שָׁלַח יוֹאָב אַחַר אִשָּׁה חֲכָמָה לִתְקוֹעַ, שֶׁהִיא אַלְפָּא לְשֶׁמֶן.
wherefore Joab sent to Tekoa for a wise woman, because Tekoa was preeminent in olive oil.
וּפַךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּמְצָא מִן הַמּוּכָן
And the cruse of oil that was found preserved and readily available
הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא אֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הַמּוּכָן בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
is the primordial root of wisdom that stands prepared for Israel within the Written Torah.
וּבָזֶה לֹא יָכְלוּ יְוָנִים לִגַּע לְטַמְּאוֹ;
And this the Greeks were totally unable to touch or defile;
כִּי בַּחָכְמָה הַנּוֹבֵעַ מִלִּבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יוּכְלוּ לְטַמֵּא, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
for the humanly developed wisdom issuing from the hearts of Israel in the Oral Torah they could potentially contaminate, God forbid,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה ט״ו1257 Chagigah 15b — As for Acher — what was his flaw? Greek song never ceased from his mouth. They said of Acher: when he would rise from the study hall, many books of the heretics would fall from his lap. Rashi: "As for Acher — what was his flaw" — that is, how did he come to this, and why did his Torah not shield him? He ought to have given up Greek song on account of the destruction of the Temple, for of song it is written, "They shall not drink wine with song" (Isaiah 24:9). And the books of the heretics fell from his lap before he abandoned himself to evil ways — which shows that there was already mud in his heart. Maharsha: Against Rashi's explanation: the Gemara should then have said simply that song never ceased from his mouth, not Greek song; rather it specifies Greek song because the heresy lay in the song itself, as they said that Greek wisdom is forbidden because it draws a man to heresy. This is why the Gemara fittingly goes on to the heretical books: he kept them by him, and in the study hall would hide them in his lap and guard them from being seen by the students, until at last, absorbed in his learning there, he forgot to guard them, and when he rose from his place they fell out of his lap onto the ground before the students. עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל אַחֵר:
as the Sages recounted in Chagigah 15b concerning Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah):
עַל יְדֵי דְּזֶמֶר יְוָנִי לֹא פָסַק מִפִּיו, יָצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה וְהִמְשִׁיךְ חָכְמָתוֹ לַחִיצוֹנִית.
because Greek song never ceased from his mouth, he fell into apostasy and channeled his wisdom into external philosophy.
אֲבָל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב — זֶה לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לְשַׁנּוֹת וְלִגַּע כְּלָל.
However, the foundational root of wisdom embedded within the Written Torah—this they could never alter or compromise in the least.
אַף דִּבְדוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים הִתְחַכְּמוּ לְפָרֵשׁ גַּם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כֻּלָּהּ עַל פִּי חָכְמַת יְוָנִית,
Even though in later generations rationalists subtly sought to interpret the entire Written Torah according to Greek philosophy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁצָּוַוח נֶגְדָּם בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת הָרַשְׁבָּ"א וְזוּלָתוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע,
as the Rashba and others vehemently protested in their responsa, as is well known,
אִלּוּ הָיָה זֶה, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז,
had this perversion occurred then, God forbid,
הָיָה כְּמוֹ בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁאִלְמָלֵי נִכְנְסוּ לְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁבְּטֻמְאָה, שָׁם לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לָצֵאת, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
it would have been like Egypt, where had they crossed into the fiftieth gate of impurity, they could never have emerged, Heaven forbid.
וְכֵן אָז, אִלּוּ הָיָה הִתְגַּבְּרוּת יְוָנִים נֶגְדָּם, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה,
And similarly at that time, had the Greek conquest over them unfolded, God forbid, in this subversive ideological manner,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁגָּבְרָה הָאֶפִּיקוֹרְסוּת בַּדּוֹר אַחֲרוֹן לְהַמְשִׁיךְ גַּם הַתּוֹרָה לְכַוָּנַת הַבְלֵיהֶם,
as heresy intensified in the modern era to twist the Torah to conform to their vanities,
הָיָה קָשֶׁה לָצֵאת.
it would have been exceedingly difficult to recover.
אֲבָל הַנֵּס הָיָה שֶׁהֵם כָּפְרוּ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְגַמְרֵי,
The miracle, however, was that the ancient Greeks rejected the Written Torah in its entirety,
וְנִשְׁאַר הַפַּךְ עַל יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן חָתוּם בְּחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
and so the cruse for the first day remained intact, sealed with the signet of the High Priest.
עִנְיַן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל רוֹמֵז עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
The concept of the High Priest symbolizes the divine root of Israel's wisdom,
כִּי עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים נֶאֱמַר: "יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים" וְגוֹמֵר,
for regarding the priests it is written: "They shall teach Your laws...", and "You shall come to the priests...",
שֶׁהֵם עִיקַּר חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמּוֹרִים.
for they are the primary rabbinic authorities and teachers of Israel.
וְהַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הוּא הַגָּדוֹל וְהָרֹאשׁ שֶׁבָּהֶם,
And the High Priest is the supreme head among them,
וְחוֹתָמוֹ הוּא הַמֵּעִיד שֶׁלֹּא נָגְעוּ בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה עֲדַיִן, שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר נְקִיָּה,
and his seal testifies that they had not yet laid a finger upon the root of wisdom, which remained undefiled;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִמְשִׁיכוּ אַחַר כָּךְ מִמֶּנָּה הַשֶּׁפַע לְשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי קוֹמַת הַמְשָׁכַת הַחָכְמָה,
and through this uncontaminated root they subsequently drew the divine flow into the seven-day framework of intellectual extension,
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה הַנֵּס עַל יְדֵי כֹּהֲנִים.
which is why the miracle occurred specifically through the agency of the Priests.

וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַפְּלוּגְתָּא (שַׁבָּת כ״א1258 Shabbat 21b — Our Rabbis taught: The obligation of Chanukah is a lamp for a man and his household. Those who beautify the commandment — a lamp for each and every one. And those who beautify it still further: Beit Shammai say, On the first day he lights eight, and from then on he decreases; and Beit Hillel say, On the first day he lights one, and from then on he increases. Ulla said: Two Amoraim in the West [the Land of Israel], R. Yosei bar Avin and R. Yosei bar Zevida, differed in this. One said: the reason of Beit Shammai is that [the lights] correspond to the days still to come, and the reason of Beit Hillel is that they correspond to the days that have gone. And one said: the reason of Beit Shammai is that they correspond to the bulls of the Festival [of Sukkot], and the reason of Beit Hillel is that one ascends in matters of holiness and does not descend. Rashi: "A lamp for a man and his household": one lamp each night — a man and all the members of his household suffice with one lamp. "Those who beautify" — [who are zealous] after the commandments — make one lamp each night for each and every member of the household. "The bulls of the Festival": which progressively decrease in the offerings of the portion of Pinchas; "one ascends in matters of holiness and does not descend": we derive this from a verse, in Menachot, chapter Shtei HaLechem (99a). Tosafos (s.v. "and those who beautify it still further"): It seems to the Ri that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel are building only on "a lamp for a man and his household," for in that there is the greater beautification, since it is recognizable when he adds or decreases that this corresponds to the days coming or the days gone; but if he makes a lamp for each one, then even if he adds from then on it is not recognizable, for people will think that this is how many people there are in the house. Maharsha (s.v. "the reason [of Beit Shammai] is that they correspond to the bulls of the Festival"): Beit Shammai certainly do not dispute that one ascends in holiness, which is derived from a verse; rather, just as with the bulls of the Festival there is a reason for decreasing — they correspond to the seventy nations, who will progressively diminish — so that "one ascends in holiness" need not concern us there, so too here there is a reason. For, as the Beit Yosef and the Re'em explain, the miracle took place on the first night as well: the oil was divided from the outset into eight parts, so that the eight portions of oil diminished from night to night. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 21b): According to the one who says Beit Shammai's reason is "corresponding to the bulls of the Festival," which diminish: they diminish because the last is always lesser by virtue of being last — the first is higher, and the last is lesser in itself. Beit Hillel say "one ascends in matters of holiness and does not descend": although the last is lesser in itself, nevertheless, from the side of man, a person is raised on the last [day] to greater holiness; therefore the one who received the miracle was raised higher, and added more, on the last day than on the first. Maharal (Ner Mitzvah): The bulls of the Festival diminished because the first day of the Festival is the higher — it is a festival day and "holy" — whereas the last day, though also a festival day, is a festival in its own right; therefore more bulls are offered on the first day than on the later ones. And "one ascends in matters of holiness" because holiness is a supreme level, which one does not reach at the outset but ascends to step by step until the last; therefore the one who receives the miracle is at first little, and is raised higher and adds more on the last day than on the first. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 8): Beit Hillel are of the side of mercy, the level of Abraham, and Beit Shammai of the side of judgment, the level of Isaac; and Chanukah holds both the victory, won by emptying the evil out of "the fool's heart at his left," and the miracle of the oil, which brought holiness into "the wise man's heart at his right." Beit Hillel hold that the main thing is to bring the light into the wise heart, so one increases, for "one ascends in holiness" — such is the order in which light shines, "brighter and brighter until the full day"; Beit Shammai hold that the main thing is to empty the evil from the fool's heart through fear, so one decreases, corresponding to the festival bulls, which diminish each time — emptying out the evil until only the remnant needed for Israel is left. עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל:
And this clarifies the dispute (Shabbat 21b) between the School of Shammai and the School of Hillel:
אִי פּוֹחֵת וְהוֹלֵךְ כְּנֶגֶד פָּרֵי הַחַג,
whether the lights decrease progressively corresponding to the bullocks of the Festival of Sukkot,
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהֵם נֶגֶד שִׁבְעִים אֻמּוֹת וְעַל כֵּן מִתְמַעֲטִים וְהוֹלְכִים, וְכָל כַּוָּנָתֵנוּ לְמַעֲטָם.
which are known to correspond to the seventy nations and therefore decrease progressively, our entire spiritual intent being to diminish their dominion.

וְכֵן בָּזֶה לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, שֶׁהֵם מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין וְהַצִּמְצוּם כַּנּוֹדָע (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳, רמ״ה עַמּוּד א1259 Zohar 3:245a — The Faithful Shepherd said: Hillel and Shammai — you, the one from the side of mercy and the other from the side of judgment, which are Chesed and Gevurah, the levels of Abraham and Isaac; and you are of their stock. Gather here, you and the eighty disciples that Hillel had; and likewise the disciples of Beit Shammai, to the banquet of the King.׳),
And in this same manner according to Beit Shammai, who align with the attribute of strict Judgment and Contraction (Zohar III, 245a),
דְּעַל כֵּן הֵם מַחְמִירִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם,
wherefore they rule strictly in all halachic matters,
כָּל הַכַּוָּנָה בְּהַדְלָקַת נֵר חֲנֻכָּה הוּא לְצַמְצֵם עַצְמֵנוּ וּלְהַבְדִּילֵנוּ מֵחָכְמַת הָעַמִּים וּלְמַעֲטָם,
the entire intent in kindling the Chanukah lights is to contract ourselves, to separate ourselves from the philosophy of the nations, and to diminish their power,
וְעַל כֵּן פּוֹחֵת וְהוֹלֵךְ.
and therefore the count decreases progressively.
וְזֶהוּ כְּנֶגֶד יָמִים הַנִּכְנָסִים,
And this corresponds to the incoming days,
כִּי לְמַעֵט חָכְמַת הָאֻמּוֹת לֹא אִכְפַּת לָן בְּמַה שֶּׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ וְנִסְתַּלְּקוּ,
for in seeking to diminish the wisdom of the nations, we are unconcerned with what has already departed and been eliminated,
דְּאֵין לָנוּ עֵסֶק עוֹד עִמָּהֶם, רַק עִם אוֹתָן שֶׁאָנוּ צְרִיכִים עֲדַיִן לִרְאוֹת לְסַלְּקָם מֵאִתָּנוּ.
as we have no further traffic with them, but only with those residual forces that we must still endeavor to banish from our midst.
אֲבָל לְבֵית הִלֵּל, דַּהֲלָכָה כְּוָתַיְיהוּ,
However, according to Beit Hillel, whose position the halachah follows,
עִיקַּר הַכַּוָּנָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ חָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּלְבָבֵנוּ,
the primary intention is to draw down the authentic wisdom of the Oral Torah into our hearts,
וְעַל יְדֵי אוֹר הָאֱמֶת מִמֵּילָא מִסְתַּלֵּק הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהַשֶּׁקֶר וְכָלֶה מֵאֵלָיו.
and through the radiant light of truth, darkness and falsehood are automatically banished and vanish of their own accord.
וְעַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ נֶגֶד יָמִים הַיּוֹצְאִים,
Therefore the lighting must correspond to the days that have already elapsed,
דְּכָל חָכְמָה שֶׁכְּבָר הִשִּׂיג צָרִיךְ לִרְאוֹת לְקָבְעָהּ וּלְהַשְׁרִישָׁהּ בְּלִבּוֹ,
for every insight of holy wisdom one has already acquired, he must strive to establish and root firmly within his heart,
וּ"מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ", מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא רוֹמֵז לְחָכְמַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
and we "ascend in holiness," since it alludes to the sacred wisdom.

וְנוֹדַע עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַנִּסְתָּר דְּ"קֹדֶשׁ" רוֹמֵז לְחָכְמָה עִלָּאָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳, קע״ו עַמּוּד ב׳ וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת1260 Zohar 3:176b — All those supernal crowns to which the Holy Name is joined are summoned from the place called Holiness; this is what is written, “holy convocations.” And when? At the time a festival is appointed in the world. Just as those supernal crowns are summoned from the supernal Holiness, so too the lower Holiness summons her hosts, to crown them and to raise them up. The supernal Holiness is known; the lower Holiness is the wisdom of Solomon, and she likewise summons all her hosts, and all those hosts are summoned to be crowned by this lower Holiness at the time when a festival rests upon the world.),
And it is known according to the esoteric tradition that "Holy" alludes to Supernal Wisdom (Chochmah Ila'ah; Zohar III, 176b and elsewhere),
וְחָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יוֹנֶקֶת מִמֶּנָּה,
and the Lower Wisdom of the Oral Torah draws its spiritual nourishment directly from it,
וְצָרִיךְ הַעֲלָאָה וְלֵילֵךְ מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה מַעְלָה מָעְלָה.
requiring continual elevation and advancing from level to level higher and higher.
וְעַל כֵּן מוֹסִיף וְהוֹלֵךְ כָּל פַּעַם בְּמַדְרֵגָה,
Therefore, one increases the lights each night, advancing incrementally in spiritual rank,
דְּגַם יָמִים הַיּוֹצְאִים לֹא יָצְאָה מַדְרֵגָתָם וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה מִמֶּנּוּ;
for even the preceding days have not seen their spiritual attainment vanish or depart from him;
אַדְּרַבָּה, הֵם עִמּוֹ כְּשֶׁהוֹלֵךְ לְמַדְרֵגָה עֶלְיוֹנָה יוֹתֵר.
on the contrary, they remain united with him as he ascends to an even higher level.

items.h:
Seif 28 — Thanksgiving, Praise, and the Giver of Torah
Chanukah culminates in recognizing the Giver behind Torah wisdom, the supernal source from which Israel's understanding receives life.

p: וּלְפִי שֶׁעִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ כְּחָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּחָכְמַת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּלָל,
And since the primary wisdom of the children of Israel is not like human wisdom concerning mundane matters of this world like the wisdom of the nations of the world at all,
רַק כָּל חָכְמָתָם הוּא בְּהַשָּׂגַת אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדֶרֶךְ עֲבוֹדָתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא יְדִיעַת הַתּוֹרָה עַל בּוּרְיָהּ.
rather all their wisdom consists in apprehending His blessed true essence and the path of His service, which is knowing the Torah thoroughly in its clarity.
עַל כֵּן עִיקַּר קְבִיעוּת הַיָּמִים הָאֵלּוּ לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל,
Therefore, the primary establishment of these days is to give thanks and to praise Your great Name,

שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר תַּכְלִית מְכֻוַּן הַבְּרִיאָה כֻּלָּהּ: "כָּל פָּעַל לְמַעֲנֵהוּ" — לְקִילּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר י״ט1261 Midrash Tehillim 19:1 — "For the leader. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God." This is what Scripture says: "The Lord has made everything for His own sake" (Proverbs 16:4) — for His praise, as it is said, "Sing to the Lord with thanksgiving" (Psalms 147:7). Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 2): The aim of the whole Torah is to come to a complete apprehension that there is a Creator, Ruler and Overseer, which was the purpose of the creation of the world: "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. All 613 commandments are counsels for reaching this, for the Torah is called truth, being counsels for reaching a clear apprehension in the heart, so manifest that it needs no faith. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 6): Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created for His glory, He created to reveal the glory of His kingship and His Presence among the lower beings, and "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise. The building of the Tabernacle and the Temple is man's work of building a place for His Presence after the sin, when the Presence is not revealed everywhere, in the pattern of the Blessed One's work in creation; had man not sinned, the whole world would have been a Tabernacle and a Sanctuary. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 2): The angels cry, "Where is the place of His glory?", but man grasps the Throne of Glory, for "the Lord made everything for His sake" — for His praise; the purpose of creation is the revelation of His glory, and its purpose is man. For the chief revelation of glory is when a person with free choice, whose body inclines toward impurity, nevertheless subdues his inclination and desires for the sake of Heaven's honor, which the angels, who have no evil inclination, cannot attain at all.).
for this is the essential purpose intended for the whole of creation: “Hashem made everything for His sake”—for His praise (Shocher Tov, Psalm 19).
וּמִזְמוֹר שֶׁל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת אַחַר גְּמַר שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן, וְנֶהֱנֶה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה וְשָׁבַת מִמְּלַאכְתּוֹ,
And the Psalm of the Sabbath day, following the conclusion of the six days of building when He took pleasure in all that He made and rested from His work,
יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְשַׁבֵּחַ וְאוֹמֵר: "טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַה'",
the seventh day offers praise and says: “It is good to give thanks to Hashem,”
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַנַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַנִּבְרָא בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית.
which is the ultimate purpose of all that was made and created throughout the Works of Creation.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת,
And this is the quintessential root of Jewishness,

דְּנִקְרָאִים כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֶסְתֵּר וּבְכָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה "יְהוּדִים" עַל שֵׁם יְהוּדָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צ״ח1262 Bereshit Rabbah 98:6 — "Judah, you — your brothers shall acknowledge you": your brothers acknowledge you, your mother acknowledges you, and I Myself acknowledge you. R. Shimon ben Yochai said: All your brothers shall be called by your name. A man does not say, "I am a Reubenite," or "I am a Simeonite," but rather, "I am a Jew."),
in that all of Israel are designated in the Book of Esther and throughout the Oral Torah as “Jews” (Yehudim) after the name of Judah (Bereishit Rabbah 98),
דְּנִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם "אוֹדֶה אֶת ה'", שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַמְּכֻוָּן דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
who was named for the expression “I will give thanks to Hashem,” which is the core intended purpose of all Israel.
וְכָל הִתְחַכְּמוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לְהַגִּיעַ מִזֶּה לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לִשְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And the entire intellectual exertion of the Oral Torah is meant to arrive from it at giving thanks and praise to His blessed Name.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּבַכְּתוּבִים נִתְפָּרֵשׁ הַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ"ה כִּכְתָבוֹ,
However, in the Written Torah and in Scripture the Name Havayah is set down according to its literal lettering,
וּבְנוּסַח "עַל הַנִּסִּים" שֶׁהוּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
whereas in the liturgy of Al HaNissim, which belongs to the Oral Torah,
דְּ"זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם" כְּתִיב, עַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים "לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל" וְלֹא בְּכִינּוּי הָאַדְנוּת.
since “This is My Name forever (le'allem—to conceal)” is written, we therefore recite “to Your great Name” and not through the designation of Adonut.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַהוֹדָאָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַמְּכֻוָּן בְּפֹעַל ה'
For the essence of thanksgiving, which is the ultimate end intended in the work of Hashem,
אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא, לְהַכִּיר אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִי לְבוּשִׁים וְצִמְצוּמִים וּמַסָכִים.
is directed solely toward the Name Havayah, blessed be He, to perceive His blessed true essence stripped of garments, contractions, and intervening veils.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה בָּזֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And even though there is no clear and direct apprehension of this in this world,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהוֹדָאָה הוּא רַק כְּלַפֵּי מִדַּת אֲמִתּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
nevertheless the thanksgiving is addressed solely toward the measure of His blessed absolute truth,

דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא יְהוּדָה כֻּלּוֹ עַל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה (סוֹטָה י1263 Sotah 10b — Joseph, who sanctified the name of Heaven in secret, merited that one letter of the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was added to his own, as it is written, "He appointed it in Yehosef for a testimony" (Psalms 81:6). Judah, who sanctified the name of Heaven in public, merited that his whole name is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Maharsha: The letter heh was added to Joseph — as the Targum renders, "He set it as a testimony upon Yehosef, that he did not approach his master's wife" — for with it his name holds the letters of the Tetragrammaton save the final heh, which is its essential part, since the final heh is silent in the Name. Judah sanctified the Name by his admission, "She is more righteous than I"; and although Leah named him at birth for "This time I will praise the Lord," which alone would have yielded only "Odeh" ["I will praise"], the Holy One, blessed be He, put it in her mouth to call him Yehudah, which contains the entire Tetragrammaton, with the dalet added to signify the admission through which he merited to be called wholly by His name. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sotah 10b): One who sanctifies the Name cleaves to His Name, so it is fitting that a letter of His Name be added to him; but what is done in public has already emerged into manifest actuality, so one who sanctifies the Name in public is fittingly called wholly by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. A single letter is only a part, which has no existence in manifest actuality; hence Joseph, whose sanctification was not in the open, was called by part of the Name. Each sanctified the Name according to his own attribute: Joseph's blessing lay in concealment — "and let them multiply like fish" (Genesis 48:16), for as fish are hidden so are his descendants, over whom the [evil] eye has no power — while Judah's blessing was in the open, for from him comes the kingship, which is manifest to the many.׳ עַמּוּד ב׳),
wherefore the entire name of Judah is formed around the Name Havayah (Sotah 10b),
וּבְהוֹסָפַת הַדָּלֶ"ת הָרוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
with the addition of the letter dalet, which alludes to Knesset Yisrael,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ע״א1264 Bereshit Rabbah 71:1 — “For the Lord hears the needy” — these are Israel; for R. Yochanan said: Wherever “poor,” “afflicted,” or “needy” is said, Scripture speaks of Israel. “And He does not despise His prisoners” — these are the barren women, who are imprisoned within their houses and forlorn; but once the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers them with children, they stand upright. Know this: Leah was the hated one of the household, and once the Holy One, blessed be He, remembered her she stood upright. That is what is written: “And the Lord saw that Leah was hated.” Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 14): Israel count by the moon, which "has nothing of its own"; so too, "wherever 'crushed,' 'poor,' and the like is said, Scripture speaks of Israel" (Bereishis Rabbah 71), for they recognize their poverty, that they have nothing at all of their own. Even when one increases in service and effort, all that he adds in service and in recognition of His Godliness he adds in recognition of his own lowliness and smallness.):
as our Sages of blessed memory explained (Bereishit Rabbah 71:1):
דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם "דַּלִּים" בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְדַבֵּר,
that wherever Scripture mentions the “impoverished” (dalim), it speaks of Israel,
שֶׁהֵם מוֹנִים לַלְּבָנָה דְּלֵית לַהּ מִגַּרְמַהּ כְּלוּם,
who count their calendar by the moon, which possesses nothing of its own,
רַק עֲתִידִים לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ כְּמוֹתָהּ כְּשֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
only that they are destined to be renewed like it when they receive from the blessed Hashem,
וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה מִדָּלֶ"ת הֵ"א, בָּתַר דְּקַבִּילַת עוּבְרָהּ, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
and then the dalet transforms into a heh, after she has received conception, as is known.
וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בְּהַגָּהוֹת רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה אִיסֶרְלֶישׂ,
And this is the underlying reason for what Rabbeinu Moshe Isserles wrote in his glosses,
דְּנוֹהֲגִין לוֹמַר זְמִירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת בַּסְּעוּדוֹת שֶׁמַּרְבִּין בַּחֲנֻכָּה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא סְעוּדַת מִצְוָה.
that it is customary to recite songs and praises during the enlarged feasts on Chanukah, and through this it becomes a feast of mitzvah.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַסְּעוּדָה בְּבָשָׂר וְיַיִן, דְּאֵין שִׂמְחָה אֶלָּא בָּהֶם, הַלֵּב שָׂמֵחַ,
For through feasting upon meat and wine, in which alone formal rejoicing consists, the heart rejoices,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַלֵּב הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי מִתְעוֹרֵר לוֹמַר שִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת,
and through this the Jewish heart is awakened to sing hymns and praises;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִלָּה י״ב1265 Megillah 12b — "On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine" (Esther 1:10) — was his heart then not merry with wine until now? Rava said: The seventh day was Shabbat. When Israel eat and drink they begin with words of Torah and with words of praise; but the nations of the world, when they eat and drink, begin only with words of licentiousness. Maharsha: Scripture need not have said "on the seventh day"; it comes to teach that it was on the Sabbath, which is called "the seventh," that his heart was merry with wine. Not so Israel, whose heart is not then merry with wine; rather, once they have eaten and drunk they begin with words of Torah, whereas the nations begin with words of licentiousness. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 4): We do find songs and praises even in this world, and Israel are praised for beginning with words of Torah and words of praise when they eat and drink on the Sabbath; yet from "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter and our tongue with song" the Sages derive that one may not fill one's mouth with laughter in this world, and by the same token song should be forbidden. [He answers that] the full revelation of joy belongs to the future, which is called "then"; but on the Sabbath, when the Ancient One is revealed, the mouth too is opened to say songs and praises, and this also falls under "then our mouth will be filled." עַמּוּד ב׳):
and as our Sages of blessed memory said (Megillah 12b):
דְּזֶהוּ הַחִלּוּק בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים, דִּכְשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּשְׂמֵחִים — אוֹמְרִים שִׁירוֹת;
this is the distinction between Israel and the nations, that when Jews eat, drink, and rejoice, they utter songs of praise;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הַסְּעוּדָה סְעוּדַת מִצְוָה, שֶׁהִיא מְבִיאָה לְהַלֵּל וּלְשַׁבֵּחַ, וְזֶה הָיָה עִיקַּר קְבִיעוּת הַיָּמִים.
and from this aspect the banquet constitutes a feast of mitzvah, since it leads to giving praise and thanksgiving, which was the primary enactment of the days.
וְדַעַת אַחֲרוֹנִים: רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה לוּרְיָא וְטוּרֵי זָהָב וְ"יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים" שֶׁבְּרַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה אִיסֶרְלֶישׂ,
And according to the opinion of the later authorities—Rabbeinu Shlomo Luria (Maharshal), the Taz, and the "some say" cited in the Rema—
דְּהַסְּעוּדוֹת עַצְמָן מִצְוָה, דִּקְבָעוּם לְשִׂמְחָה גַּם כֵּן;
the feasts themselves are inherently a mitzvah, for they established them for rejoicing as well;
וְכִדִבְרֵיהֶם הוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּפִּיּוּט לַחֲנֻכָּה,
and their words are corroborated within the liturgical poetry composed for Chanukah,
וּבִתְשׁוּבוֹת מוֹרֵנוּ הָרַב יִצְחָק בְּרוּנָא לִגְלֵג עָלָיו בָּזֶה.
though in the responsa of Mahari Bruna he mocked the author on this point.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בַּגְּמָרָא וּדְרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לֹא נִמְצָא זֵכֶר קְבִיעוּת שִׂמְחָה.

Rashi: "Megillat Ta'anit has been annulled" — the festive days that the Sages established for miracles that occurred on them, forbidding fasting on them (and on some, eulogy as well), which they wrote in one scroll, "These are the days on which one may not fast…"; now that the Temple is destroyed they are annulled, and eulogy and fasting are permitted. "And those too" — we treat the days of Megillat Ta'anit like these [four fasts]: just as these are annulled, so are those. "Which the Merciful One made contingent upon the building" — they were established as fasts through the destruction and as festivals through the building, as the Holy One, blessed be He, answered the exiles who asked when the Second Temple was built, "Shall I weep in the fifth month… as I have done these many years?" (Zechariah 7:3), that henceforth they would be for joy and gladness and for good festivals. Maharsha (s.v. "He calls them a fast and calls them joy," on the exposition adopted here): They are first called "fast," as they were in Babylon, and then "joy and gladness," implying that it would be so forever — yet we returned to fasting when the Second Temple was destroyed. Hence "when there is peace… when there is no peace," drawn from the end of the verse, "therefore love truth and peace" (Zechariah 8:19): they will be for joy and gladness only as long as you love truth and peace, and when truth and peace are not among you, you will return to fasting — as with the Second Temple, which was destroyed on account of baseless hatred (Yoma 9b). עַמּוּד ב׳);

וְעַל כֵּן נִיתְּנָה לִכְתֹּב גַּם כֵּן.
and therefore it was permitted to be written down as well.
וּמִמֵּילָא מֵאָז וָהֵילָךְ, גַּם קְדֻשַּׁת יְמֵי הַחֲנֻכָּה שֶׁהוּא הֶאָרַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה —
And automatically from then on, the holiness of the days of Chanukah, which is the illumination of the Oral Torah—
נִתְלַבְּשָׁה הַהֶאָרָה גַּם בַּגּוּף.
this illumination clothed itself in the physical body as well.
וְעַל כֵּן הִתְחִילוּ דּוֹרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים לִנְהוֹג שִׂמְחָה גּוּפָנִית וּסְעוּדוֹת גַּם כֵּן,
Therefore recent generations began to practice bodily rejoicing and festive meals as well;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן נְבִיאִים, בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים הֵם,
and though they are not prophets, they are the sons of prophets,
דִּכְבָר הִגִּיעָה הַהֶאָרָה לִהְיוֹת מוּרְגֶּשֶׁת בַּפֹּעַל בַּגּוּף גַּם כֵּן,
for the spiritual illumination has already arrived at being tangibly felt in the physical body too,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא הַמַּלְבּוּשׁ וּכְלִי הַקִּבּוּל לְהָאוֹר דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
since the body is the garment and receptive vessel for the light of the Oral Torah.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ הַמִּנְהָג לֶאֱכוֹל מַאֲכְלֵי חָלָב
And that which they recorded regarding the custom to eat dairy foods
הוּא דֻּגְמַת מִנְהַג מַאֲכְלֵי חָלָב בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת בְּקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
is parallel to the custom of dairy foods on Shavuot at the reception of the Written Torah;
כִּי הֶחָלָב יוֹנְקִים מִשְּׁדֵי הָאֵם,
for milk is nursed from the mother's breasts,
וְעִיקַּר קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא לְהַכִּיר נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יוֹנֵק הַכֹּל.
and the essence of receiving the Torah is recognizing the Giver of the Torah, blessed be His Name, from Whom all existence suckles and draws life.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה בַּחֲנֻכָּה בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And in this manner, on Chanukah regarding the Oral Torah,
הָעִיקָּר הוּא הַכָּרַת הַיְנִיקָה מֵ"אֵם הַבָּנִים", כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
the central theme is recognizing the spiritual nursing from the "mother of the children" (Binah), as mentioned above.

sections.en: Chanukah, Greek Intermixture, and the Clarification of Israel

items.h: The Chanukah light separates Israel from Greek spiritual mixture, clarifying Netzach, Hod, and Yesod and restoring the purity of Torah, covenant, and Jewish identity.

Seif 1 — The Greek Translation and the Corruption of Hod
The oil miracle answers Greece's attempt to turn Torah's radiant Hod into external human wisdom and worldly darkness.

p: עִנְיַן מִצְוַת נֵר חֲנֻכָּה לְזֵכֶר נֵס דַּחֲנֻכָּה,
The matter of the mitzvah of the Chanukah light in commemoration of the miracle of Chanukah:
וּבֶאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַנֵּס הָיָה הַצָּלָתָם מִשְּׁמַד הַיְּוָנִים,
and in truth, the essential miracle was their salvation from the religious persecutions of the Greeks,
וְהַנֵּס דְּשֶׁמֶן זֶה הָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ עִנְיָן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
while this miracle of the oil was an independent matter that came afterward,
דִּלְכָאוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְגוּף יְשׁוּעַת הַהַצָּלָה שֶׁהוּא הָעִיקָּר.
for seemingly it has no connection to the substance of the salvation of rescue, which is the primary element.
וּבְנוּסַח "עַל הַנִּסִּים" לֹא נִזְכַּר כְּלַל נֵס זֶה שֶׁהָיָה בַּשֶּׁמֶן,
Moreover, in the liturgy of Al HaNissim this miracle of the oil is not mentioned at all,
רַק דְּ"אַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ" וְכוּלֵי "וְהִדְלִיקוּ נֵרוֹת".
only that “afterwards Your children came...” and so forth, “and kindled lights.”
אֲבָל כָּל יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּקְבַּע מִמֶּנָּה זֵכֶר לְדוֹרוֹת,
However, regarding any salvation whereof an enduring commemoration was instituted for future generations:
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹשְׁעוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן מַה,
it is because the souls of Israel had already been redeemed in that specific realm wherein they had previously suffered some spiritual lack,
דְּמַחֲמָתוֹ הָיָה הַגְּזֵירוֹת וְהַצָּרוֹת מִקּוֹדֶם, דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט.
on account of which the decrees and afflictions had earlier come about, for everything occurs through exact divine justice.
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרְרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַקֵּן לְאוֹתוֹ הַחִסָּרוֹן בִּלְבָבָם, אָז נוֹשְׁעוּ מֵהַצָּרָה.
And once the children of Israel were aroused to rectify that deficiency within their hearts, they were then saved from the affliction.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר תִּיקְּנוּ לְגַמְרֵי אוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל כְּלָלוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Furthermore, when they thoroughly mended that matter to the very root of collective Knesset Yisrael,
בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁמֵּהַיּוֹם וָהֵילָךְ כָּל נְפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מְתוּקָּנִים בִּפְרָט זֶה,
in such a manner that from that day forward all the souls of the children of Israel are rectified in this specific detail,
אָז נִקְבְּעָה יְשׁוּעָה זוֹ זֵכֶר לְדוֹרוֹת.
then was this salvation established as an eternal remembrance for all generations.
וְקָבְעוּ אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה לִהְיוֹת לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן, לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עֲלֵיהֶם קְדֻשַּׁת תִּיקּוּן זֶה.
And the Sages established a designated mitzvah to serve as an awakening from below at that recurring time, to draw down upon them the sanctity of this rectification.
דְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁל קְדֻשָּׁה אֵין בָּא בְּעַצְמוֹ לַלֵּב
For any matter of holiness does not enter the heart entirely on its own,
אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וּפְתִיחָה כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט מִלְּמַטָּה,
except by means of an awakening from below and an opening like the eye of a needle from beneath;
וְקָבְעוּ מִצְוָה הָרְאוּיָה לִפְתִיחַת אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹר וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.
they therefore instituted a commandment uniquely suited to open that specific light and holiness within the heart.
וְיָדוּעַ מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה, דְּמַתִּתְיָהוּ תִּיקֵּן הַהוֹד שֶׁהָיָה מִקּוֹדֶם "הוֹדִי נֶהְפַּךְ עָלַי לְמַשְׁחִית"
It is known from the teachings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory, that Mattathias rectified the sefirah of Hod, which had previously fallen into “my splendor was turned into corruption upon me”
[וּמִקְרָא זֶה אָמוּר בְּדָנִיֵּאל י׳ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ דְּהִנֵּה שַׂר יָוָן בָּא, עַיֵּין שָׁם],
and this verse is spoken in Daniel 10 when it was revealed to him that behold, the celestial prince of Greece was coming; see there,
וְעַל כֵּן תִּיקְּנוּ "עַל הַנִּסִּים" בְּהוֹדָאָה.
and on this account they established the insertion of Al HaNissim within the blessing of Thanksgiving (Modim/Hod).
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים, כִּי הוֹד הוּא סְפִירָה שְׁמִינִית,
Therefore the festival lasts eight days, because Hod is the eighth sefirah from the top,
וּמַמְשִׁיכִים לַהּ עַל יְדֵי הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּרוֹת אוֹר מִשְּׁמוֹנֶה סְפִירוֹת הַקּוֹדֶמֶת עַד הַכֶּתֶר.
and through the kindling of the lamps they draw down to it an illumination spanning the preceding eight sefirot all the way up to Keter.
וּבֵיאוּר זֶה, כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּנֶצַח וָהוֹד הֵם תְּרֵין יַרְכִין אוֹ תְּרֵין בֵּיעִין דִּדְכוּרָא,
The elucidation of this is that, as is known, Netzach and Hod are the two thighs or the two testicles of the male form,
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר כֹּחוֹת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לַזּוּלַת.
which represents the spiritual faculties that channel influence outward to others.
וְשָׁם הָיָה נְגִיעַת שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
It was precisely there that the guardian angel of Esau struck our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
כִּי לֹא יָכוֹל לוֹ לְעַצְמוּתוֹ, שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ אֱמֶת וּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה וְאֵין בּוֹ פְּסֹלֶת כְּלָל,
for he could not overcome Jacob's essential being, which was completely truth, whose bed was whole, and who possessed no spiritual dross whatsoever;
אֲבָל נָגַע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ,
instead, he touched the hollow of his thigh,
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ע״ז: בַּצַּדִּיקִים וְצִדְקָנִיּוֹת, נְבִיאִים וּנְבִיאוֹת שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאֵיזֶה? זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁמָד.

which the Sages in Bereishit Rabbah, end of parashah 77, expounded as referring to the righteous men and women, the prophets and prophetesses destined to descend from him—and which is that? That is the generation of religious persecution.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בִּזְמַן הַשְּׁמָד שֶׁהִתְחִיל מֵהַיְּוָנִים כְּבָר פָּסְקָה נְבוּאָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
In truth, during the time of the persecution that began with the Greeks, prophecy had already ceased from Israel,

אֲבָל "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן נְבִיאִים — בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים הֵם" (פְּסָחִים ס״ו1267 Pesachim 66a — They said to him: Our teacher, if one forgot and did not bring a knife on the eve of Shabbat, what is the law? He said to them: I heard this ruling, but I have forgotten it. Leave it to Israel: if they are not prophets, they are the sons of prophets. The next day, one whose Paschal offering was a lamb stuck [the knife] in its wool, and one whose offering was a kid stuck it between its horns. He saw what they did and recalled the ruling, and said: This is the tradition I received from Shemaya and Avtalyon. Rashi: ["What is the law?"] Bringing the knife does not override Shabbat, since it could have been done the day before — so what is one to do? ["They are the sons of prophets"] — and you will see what they do. One whose offering was a kid, which has no wool but only hair, stuck it between its horns; this is not a load for which one transgresses the law of one's animal resting, since that is not the usual way of carrying, and in this manner they brought their knives — and "this is the tradition I received" means that the law is as these people did. Tosafos (s.v. "he sticks it in its wool"): And if you ask: [slaughter] requires a sacred vessel, as we derive (Zevachim 97b) from "and he took the knife" — one may answer that they consecrated [the knives]. Our sugya implies that the prohibition of a public domain applied in Jerusalem, which is difficult, since it is said (Eruvin 6b) that were Jerusalem's gates not locked at night one would be liable there for [carrying in] a public domain [— implying that, since they were locked, it was not one]; the Ri answered that here it was after breaches had been made in [its walls]. Maharsha: Certainly the fourteenth had fallen on Shabbat in earlier days, but it may have been long before, and how they had acted was forgotten — and Hillel too said, "I heard it once but have forgotten." To this he said: though they are not prophets, to know how they acted, they are nevertheless the sons of prophets, and perhaps there will be elders among Israel who remember how they acted before; and so it was made clear the next day. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaAnavah 7): [The Gemara (66b) learns from Hillel, who "began to rebuke them" and then said "I heard this ruling, but I have forgotten it," that whoever is haughty, if he is a sage, his wisdom departs from him.] Just as humility is a trait separate from the physical, so haughtiness is physical: one who singles himself out as a man of rank and not a simple person inclines toward the physical, above all when he regards himself as possessed of greatness.
