Therefore the separate, non-physical level — prophecy and wisdom — cannot be joined to one who is haughty, who in his own mind is great, for that is a physical trait. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tu BiShvat 2): "The custom of Israel is Torah," for "if they are not prophets, they are sons of prophets," so it is a custom of prophets [like the willow-beating, a custom of the prophets]; therefore through Israel's custom they can bring holiness into all kinds of fruit [on Tu BiShvat], so that they be only from the side of the Tree of Life and all eating be rectified in holiness. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 3): The generation of the wilderness all attained prophecy at the giving of the Torah — which is why the Sages said, "if they are not prophets, they are sons of prophets" — and from the grasp of "I am the Lord your God," which they all heard from the mouth of the Almighty, began the grasp of prophecy. עַמּוּד א׳) וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ הַנְּבוּאָה,
yet “even though they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets” (Pesachim 66a) and possess the latent power of prophecy,
כִּי מֵהַיְּרֵכַיִם, נֶצַח וָהוֹד, שָׁם יְנִיקַת הַנְּבִיאִים כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְעַל כֵּן קְרָאוּם כָּאן נְבִיאִים.
for from the thighs—Netzach and Hod—is the spiritual nurture of the prophets drawn, as is known, wherefore the Midrash calls them here “prophets.”
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הֶעֱמִיד קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה שֶׁל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כֻּלָּם זֶרַע אֱמֶת;
And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, erected the complete stature of Knesset Yisrael, all of them a seed of truth;
אֲבָל יָדוּעַ דְּמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, שֶׁהִיא רָזָא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, "רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת".
yet it is known that concerning the attribute of Malkhut, which is the mystery of Knesset Yisrael, “her feet descend unto death.”
וְהָעִנְיָן, דִּבְכָל קוֹמָה הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַמַּשְׁפִּיעִים לַזּוּלַת,
The underlying concept is that within every spiritual configuration the lower three sefirot are the faculties that channel influence outward to the other,
וְגַם בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ כֹּחַ זֶה לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לַזּוּלַת גַּם כֵּן;
and within Knesset Yisrael as well there exists this capacity to bestow influence upon that which lies beyond it;
וּמַה שֶּׁזּוּלַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיְינוּ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
and that which lies outside Knesset Yisrael is the nations of the world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִים שִׁבְעִים פָּרֵי הַחַג נֶגֶד שִׁבְעִים אֻמּוֹת.
just as we offer seventy bullocks on the Festival of Sukkot on behalf of the seventy nations.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, דְּמָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לִיתֵּן קְצָת מִצְוֹת וּלְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה גַּם לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צ״ח1268 Bereshit Rabbah 98:9 — R. Chanin said: Israel will not need the teaching of the King Messiah in the time to come, as it is said, "to him shall the nations seek" — not Israel. If so, why does the King Messiah come, and what does he come to do? To gather in the exiles of Israel, and to give them thirty commandments, as it is written, "And I said to them: If it seem good to you, give me my wages... and they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver." Rav said: These are the thirty mighty men. R. Yochanan said: These are thirty commandments. They said to R. Yochanan: Rav does not accept that the verse speaks only of the nations of the world.),
And as it will be in the future, when Mashiach will come to give certain commandments and teach Torah to the nations of the world as well (Bereishit Rabbah 98),
וְ"נָהֲרוּ אֵלָיו" וְגוֹמֵר "עַמִּים רַבִּים" וְגוֹמֵר, וְ"אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה".
when “many nations shall flow unto him...” and “Then will I turn to the peoples a pure language.”
וְזֶהוּ הָרַגְלִין הַיּוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת, מְקוֹם הַקְּלִיפּוֹת וְהָרָע שֶׁהוּא כֹּחוֹת הָאֻמּוֹת,
And this is the feet descending unto death, reaching down into the realm of the kelipot and evil that constitutes the forces of the nations,
לְהוֹצִיא גַּם הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם וּלְהַחֲזִירָם אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה.
in order to extract even the holy sparks embedded within them and restore them to the domain of holiness.
וְעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁבִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁרוֹצִים לְהַחֲזִיר גַּם כֹּחוֹת הָעַמִּים לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
And through this potency within Knesset Yisrael, desiring to return the forces of the nations to holiness,
עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁבָּרָע, דְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים",
there is aroused through the parallel power of evil—since “God has made one opposite the other”—
נִתְעוֹרֵר בָּאֻמּוֹת הַכֹּחַ וְהָרָצוֹן לִגְזוֹר שְׁמָד, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
the power and desire within the nations to decree religious destruction, God forbid, upon Israel,
לְהַחֲזִיר אַדְּרַבָּה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לָהֶם.
to draw Knesset Yisrael, Heaven forbid, conversely into their own unholy fold.
אֲבָל כָּל זְמַן שֶׁכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלֵמוּתָהּ,
However, so long as Knesset Yisrael remains in its integrity,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין כַּוָּנָתָם בְּהִתְחַבְּרוּתָם עִם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְהוֹצִיא הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם,
meaning that their intention in any interaction with the nations is solely for the sake of Heaven, to extract the holy sparks within them,
דְּהַיְּרֵכַיִם מְחֻבָּרִין עִם הַגּוּף,
such that the thighs remain firmly integrated with the torso,
אָז אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ"צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק" וְגוֹמֵר, "ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ".
then even though “The wicked watches the righteous... Hashem will not leave him in his hand.”

אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת נֶאֱמַר: "בְּהִתְחַבֶּרְךָ עִם אֲחַזְיָהוּ" וְגוֹמֵר1269 II Chronicles 20:35-37 — “And afterward Yehoshafat king of Yehudah joined himself with Achazyahu king of Israel, who acted wickedly. And he joined with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Etzyon Gaver. And Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Yehoshafat, saying: Because you have joined yourself with Achazyahu, the Lord has broken your works — and the ships were wrecked and could not go to Tarshish.” Rashi: "And they were not able" — the meaning is that the ships had not the strength to go, and they were wrecked. Radak: "He joined himself" — the aleph stands in place of a he, the form being the ordinary reflexive. "And they were not able to go to Tarshish" — that is, they did not muster strength. Metzudas Dovid: "He did wickedly" — although Ahaziah acted wickedly, Jehoshaphat did not hold back from joining with him, joining Ahaziah to himself to build ships together. "Because you have joined" — because of your joining with Ahaziah the Lord has breached your works: a breach and a break will come into what you do, and you will not succeed in it. Malbim: "He did wickedly" — Ahab had been incited by his wife Jezebel, but Ahaziah did wickedly of his own accord. "And he joined him" — they first built the ships in partnership and these were wrecked; this explains what is said elsewhere [I Kings 22:49], that Jehoshaphat built ships and they were wrecked, namely in partnership with Ahaziah, and "in Ezion-geber" was the harbor where they were wrecked.;
Yet in truth it was warned: “Because you have joined with Ahaziah...” and so forth;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּין לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ,
and even though one originally intended for the sake of Heaven,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָעוֹסֵק עִם מְנֻוָּל — מִתְנַוֵּל,
nevertheless, he who engages with the contaminated becomes himself contaminated,
וּכְמוֹ הַגּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִתְלַכְלֵךְ גּוּפוֹ בְּטִיט וְצוֹאָה.
like one who cleans out sewage pipes, who cannot avoid dirtying his body with mire and filth.
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה זְרִיזוּת וּגְבוּרָה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחַ שׁוּם טִנּוֹפֶת לִידָּבֵק בּוֹ,
And this requires exceptional vigilance and immense spiritual fortitude to allow no filth to adhere to him,
וְלֹא כָּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה.
and not every person merits this level.
וּבְהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ, אָז נִיתַּק כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ מֵהַגּוּף,
Thus when the angel wrestled with Jacob, the socket of the thigh became displaced from the body,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נִמְשָׁךְ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לַזּוּלַת עוֹד מֵהַגּוּף שֶׁהוּא הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ,
meaning that the outward influence to others was no longer drawn purely from the body of absolute truth,
רַק אֵיזֶה כַּוָּנָה זָרָה וְחִיצוֹנִית,
but became tainted with some alien and external motivation,
וְזֶה גָּרַם נְגִיעָתוֹ בּוֹ.
and this is what enabled the angel’s touch to take hold of him.
וּבָזֶה לְבַד יֵשׁ לוֹ נְגִיעָה בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And only in this vulnerability does the adversary have a point of contact against Knesset Yisrael:
כַּאֲשֶׁר הֵם רוֹצִים לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמָּהֶם,
namely, when they seek to attach themselves to the nations,
אַף שֶׁהוּא כְּדֵי לְהֵאָבֵק בָּם וּלְהַכְנִיסָם לִקְדוּשָׁה,
even when it is intended to wrestle with them and bring them into holiness,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם חִבּוּר זֶה גּוֹרֵם אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן וּנְתִיקָה מִכַּוָּנַת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
nevertheless this contact causes a subtle defect and a severance from Jacob’s pure intention of truth,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם בָּאִים כְּנֶגְדָּם לְנַתְּקָם לְגַמְרֵי בִּגְזֵרַת שְׁמָד,
and through this the nations rise up against them to sever them completely through decrees of apostasy,
שֶׁחוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְנַתֵּק וְלַעֲקוֹר הַיָּרֵךְ לְגַמְרֵי מֵהַגּוּף.
imagining they can permanently wrench and uproot the thigh away from the body.
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל,
Yet in truth this is utterly impossible,
כִּי הָיָה רַק נְתִיקָה לְפִי שָׁעָה בְּעֵת חֶשְׁכַּת לַיִל שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע לְהִזָּהֵר,
for it was only a temporary dislocation in the dark obscurity of the night when one could not exercise full vigilance;
וּכְשֶׁזָּרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְהֵאִירוּ עֵינָיו, נִתְרַפָּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ וְשָׁב הַיָּרֵךְ לְאֵיתָנוֹ בַּגּוּף.
and once the sun rose upon him and his eyes were illuminated, he was healed of his limping and the thigh returned to its full strength within the body.
וַאֲפִילּוּ הַמְּשֻׁמָּדִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִדַּח מֵהֶם נִדָּח לְעֵת קֵץ,
And even the apostates of Israel shall not have a single outcast cast away at the End of Days,
כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא הַיּוֹם — עוֹלָם הַבָּא הַדּוֹמֶה לְיוֹם —
when that Day arrives—the World to Come, which is compared to broad day—
"וְזָרְחָה לָכֶם יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה וּמַרְפֵּא בִּכְנָפֶיהָ";
as it says: “Unto you who fear My Name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings”;
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים "יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי", שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע.
and all of Israel are called “those who fear My Name,” which is the spiritual level of Knesset Yisrael, as is known.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם שׁוּם הִתְחַבְּרוּת לָעַמִּים;
And as long as Israel dwelt in the Land of Israel, they had no close mingling with the surrounding peoples;
רַק אַחַר הַגָּלוּת הִתְחִילוּ לְחַבֵּר עִמָּהֶם,
it was only after the exile that they began to associate closely with them,
וְעַד שֶׁחָטְאוּ בִּנְשִׂיאַת נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת,
reaching the point of sinning by taking foreign wives,
אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁבוּ עַל זֶה בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה עַל יְדֵי עֶזְרָא וּנְחֶמְיָה.
save that they returned concerning this in complete repentance under the guidance of Ezra and Nehemiah.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, כִּמְדוּמֶּה בְּעֵינַי,
Nevertheless, it appears in my view,
דְּהַבָּנִים שֶׁהִשִּׂיאוּ — הֵן הֵם אוֹ צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמְּדוּ בִּימֵי הַיְּוָנִים,
that the sons who were married off—either they themselves or their descendants were the ones who apostatized in the days of the Greeks,
וְעוֹרְרוּ הַשְּׁמָדוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ עַל יְדֵי מְשֻׁמָּדִים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כַּכָּתוּב בְּיוֹסִיפוֹן.
and instigated the persecutions, which were brought about through apostates from among the children of Israel, as recorded in Sefer Yosippon.
וְהָרִאשׁוֹנִים שֶׁנִּזְכְּרוּ בָּזֶה בַּכָּתוּב הֵם בְּנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל;
And the very first ones mentioned regarding this in Scripture are the sons of Joshua son of Jehozadak the High Priest;
וּכְשֶׁהֶעֱבִירוּ עֲוֹנוֹ בָּזֶה לִפְנֵי הַמַּלְאָךְ, אָמַר לוֹ בִּזְכַרְיָה ג׳:
and when they removed his guilt in this matter before the angel, Zechariah 3 records that he was told:

"שְׁמַע נָא" וְגוֹמֵר "וְרֵעֶיךָ הַיֹּשְׁבִים לְפָנֶיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר "מֵבִיא אֶת עַבְדִּי צֶמַח1270 Zechariah 3:8 — “Hear now, Yehoshua the High Priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men of portent — for behold, I bring My servant, the Branch.” Rashi: "You and your fellows" were Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; "men of a sign" means men fit to have miracles done for them, for a miracle was done for them as well. "For behold, I will bring My servant, the Shoot" — now Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, is a small man in the king's court, but I will make greatness and a name sprout for him, giving him favor in the eyes of the king so that his request to build the Temple and the city be granted. Radak: "You and your fellows" are the rest of the priests, and "they are men of a sign" means that they are worthy to have a sign done through them; the Sages expounded that the men of a sign were Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, for whom a sign was done. "For behold, I will bring My servant, the Shoot" has been explained of Zerubbabel, who had already come, and "I will bring" means that his standing will be raised further and his greatness will sprout like a plant of the earth that keeps growing. Others explain that this Shoot is the King Messiah. Metzudas Dovid: You are to hear and your fellows too are to hear — these are Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, who are likewise "men of a sign," since they too were saved from the fiery furnace as you were, so it was fitting that the address include them. And the word is this: "Behold, I will bring My servant, the Shoot" — this is the King Messiah, as it says, "And I will raise up for David a righteous shoot" [Jeremiah 23:5]. Malbim: He now explains to Joshua when he will have "those who walk among these that stand" — in the days of the Messiah — and this promise of the future is to be heard by him and by his fellows sitting before him, his disciples, who are "men of a sign" and fit for prophecy. "Behold, I will bring My servant, the Shoot" means that at the end of days I will bring the King Messiah; he is called "Shoot" to hint that the branch of the stock of Jesse is now cut off and lies hidden in the ground, like a seed buried in the depths of the earth which in its time will sprout and be revealed.".
“Hear now...” and so forth, “you and your companions who sit before you...” and so forth, “I am bringing My servant, the Tzemach (Sprout).”

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ג1271 Sanhedrin 93a — And the Sages say: They went up to the Land of Israel and married wives and fathered sons and daughters, as it is stated: "Hear now, Joshua the High Priest, you and your fellows who sit before you, for they are men of wonder." Who are the men for whom a wonder was performed? You must say: these are Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Rashi: "You must say: these are Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah" — hence they returned to the Land [of Israel], to Joshua the High Priest. Maharsha: According to the view that they went up to the Land of Israel, they no longer wished to hold the king's appointment, and that is why they are not mentioned again. "For they are men of wonder": they were cast [into the furnace] only in order to become a sign and a wonder, whereas you [Joshua], who were also cast in, were cast not for the sake of a wonder but as a punishment, because your sons married women unfit for the priesthood. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 93a): R. Yochanan, who says that they went up to the Land of Israel [the view the Sages of the baraita share], holds that, on the contrary, through the miracle that befell them they added holiness upon holiness, and so went up to the Land of Israel, the Holy Land, as befitted the miracle performed for them. In his view they cleaved to the attribute of holiness, and therefore they went up to the Land of Israel, for the Land of Israel is a holy land. עַמּוּד א׳):
And our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sanhedrin 93a):
דְּרֵיעָיו הֵם חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל, וַעֲזַרְיָה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לָהֶם מוֹפֵת,
that his companions were Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, for whom a public miracle was wrought,
דְּגַם הֵם כָּל עִסְקָם עִם הָעַמִּים לְבָרֵר אֲמִיתּוּת אֱמוּנָתֵנוּ לְעֵינֵי כָּל הַגּוֹיִם.
since their entire dealings with the nations were devoted to clarifying the absolute truth of our faith before the eyes of all peoples.
וְעַל כֵּן דָּנִיֵּאל הוּא שֶׁאָמַר: "הוֹדִי נֶהְפַּךְ" וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי הוּא הָיָה לוֹ שְׁלֵמוּת מִדַּת הַהוֹד.
Therefore it was Daniel who said, “My splendor was turned...”, because he possessed the perfection of the attribute of Hod.
וְהֵם הַיּוֹשְׁבִים לִפְנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק,
And they are the ones who sat before Joshua son of Jehozadak,
שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעָא דְּאַהֲרֹן וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ מִדַּת הַהוֹד כַּנּוֹדָע.
who descended from Aaron and held the office of High Priest, which is the root of the attribute of Hod, as is known.
וְהוּא, שֶׁהָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
And he, who was the first High Priest of the Second Temple,
מִסְּתָמָא נִתְחַזֵּק וְנִתְאַמֵּץ בְּמִדָּה זוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת,
presumably strengthened and exerted himself in this attribute in its utmost perfection,
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָאִים הֵם "רֵיעָיו הַיּוֹשְׁבִים לְפָנָיו",
wherefore they are called “his companions who sit before him,”
דְּזֶהוּ שְׁלֵמוּת הַהוֹד,
for this represents the perfection of Hod,
כְּעִנְיַן קַרְנֵי הוֹד דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁמֵּאִיר וְיוֹצֵא הוֹד מִמֶּנּוּ לְזוּלָתוֹ.
akin to the rays of majesty (Hod) of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, radiating and channeling splendor from him outward to others.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְפַּס הַצּוֹאָה בִּבְגָדָיו,
Yet through this reaching outward, the excrement adhered to his garments,
אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁבוּ בָּנָיו בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְזָכָה לִלְבּוֹשׁ מַחֲלָצוֹת.
save that his sons subsequently repented, and he merited to be clothed in robes of state (machalatzot).
וְנִרְאֶה לִי פֵּירוּשׁ "מַחֲלָצוֹת" —
And it appears to me that the meaning of machalatzot is:
הַיְינוּ מַלְבּוּשׁ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְחָלְצוֹ וּלְפָשְׁטוֹ תָּמִיד,
namely, a garment that can easily be removed and stripped off at any moment;
כִּי לֹא יַעֲזוֹב מַדְרֵגָתוֹ,
for he would not abandon his high spiritual level,
אֶלָּא שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְלַכְלֵךְ קְצָת יוּכַל לְפָשְׁטוֹ מִיָּד, וּבָזֶה יוּכַל לְהִתְחַזֵּק בְּמִדָּתוֹ.
only that should it become somewhat soiled, he could divest himself of it immediately, and thereby maintain strength in his attribute.
וְהִבְטִיחוּהוּ בְּבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא יִגְמוֹר הַתִּיקּוּן לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
And they promised him the coming of Mashiach, who will bring about the final rectification for the entirety of the world.
אוּלָם קוֹדֶם זֶה "הוֹדִי" דַּיְקָא — הַהוֹד דִּקְדוּשָּׁה —
However, prior to that time, it was specifically “my Hod”—the holy splendor itself—
הוּא עַצְמוֹ נֶהְפַּךְ לְמַשְׁחִית,
that was turned into a source of destruction;
דְּעַל יְדֵי הוֹפָעָתוֹ לִהְיוֹת מוּרְגָּשׁ גַּם לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
for because its radiance became perceptible to the nations of the world as well,
בָּאוּ לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמָּהֶם עַד שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְמַשְׁחִית.
the people came to assimilate with them, until through this very affinity it turned into corruption.
וְהַתְחָלַת שְׁמַד יְוָנִים הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַעְתָּקַת הַתּוֹרָה יְוָנִית,
The onset of the Greek persecution was brought about through the translation of the Torah into Greek (the Septuagint),
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַהוֹד דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד שֶׁגַּם מַלְכֵי עַמִּים הוֹדוּ לָהֶם.
which unfolded through the recognition of the majesty of Knesset Yisrael, to the point that even gentile kings acknowledged them.
כִּי בַּקָּשַׁת הַעְתָּקַת הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁהִכִּירוּ מַעֲלָתָהּ,
For Ptolemy's request to translate the Torah was because they recognized its sublime excellence,
וְכָבוֹד גָּדוֹל כִּבְּדָם תַּלְמַי עַל זֶה,
and Ptolemy accorded them immense honor on this account,
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה הַהַעְתָּקָה עַל יְדֵי כֹּהֲנִים.
wherefore the translation was undertaken specifically by priests.
אֲבָל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הִרְגִּישׁוּ שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה הֲפִיכַת הַהוֹד לְמַשְׁחִית,
Yet the sages of Israel sensed that this was the very turning of Hod into corruption,
וְגָזְרוּ תַּעֲנִית עַל זֶה,
and decreed a fast day over this event;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלַּת תַּעֲנִית: דְּהַחֹשֶׁךְ בָּא לָעוֹלָם אָז שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים,
and as recorded in Megillat Taanit: that darkness descended upon the world at that time for three days,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַהוֹד שֶׁהוּא זִיו וְאוֹר הַמֵּאִיר לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
which is the exact antithesis of Hod, which is the radiance and illumination that shines for all inhabitants of the world.

items.h:
Seif 2 — Moshe's Seventy-Language Torah and Holy Clarification
Moshe could expose Torah without mixture, while Chanukah clarifies and severs later bonds that threatened Israel's distinctness.

p: וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כָּתַב הַתּוֹרָה עַל הָאֲבָנִים "בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב" בְּשִׁבְעִים לָשׁוֹן1272 Tosafot, Sotah 35b — The Yerushalmi says: There were three sets of stones — the stones of the lodging place; the stones that Yehoshua set beneath the soles of the priests’ feet; and the tablets that Moshe gave them, as it is written, “Moshe began to explain this Torah,” and these too were of stone. R. Yitzchak said: It is plain to us that there were four sets of stones — for a fourth is said of him: “And these stones shall be for a memorial to the Children of Israel forever.” You cannot say the stones of the lodging place, for they were only for the hour and were then stored away; nor the stones that Yehoshua set beneath the soles of the priests’ feet, for they are sunk in the water; nor the tablets that Moshe gave them, for they had already entered the land with them. If so, upon what do we rely? Upon the stones that Yehoshua set up on the bank of the Jordan. (סוֹטָה ל״ה עַמּוּד ב׳, וְעַיֵּין יְרוּשַׁלְמִי הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת);
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, inscribed the Torah upon the stones, "well explained," in seventy languages (Sotah 35b; and see the Jerusalem Talmud cited in Tosafot);
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּנִצּוּחַ לָעַמִּים,
except that from the side of his attribute, which stands in total victory (Netzach) over the nations,
וּמַה שֶּׁקֵּירַב עֵרֶב רַב הָיָה רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁגִּיְּרָם — לֹא הֵזִיק זֶה.
and since his bringing close of the mixed multitude was only through properly converting them, this caused no spiritual harm.
כִּי הוּא לֹא הָלַךְ לִמְסוֹר לָהֶם,
For he did not go out to transmit it directly to them;
רַק כָּתַב עַל הָאֲבָנִים וְהִנִּיחַ הֶפְקֵר,
he merely inscribed it upon the stones and left it ownerless,
וְהֵם מֵעַצְמָם שִׁגְּרוּ נוֹטָרִין וְהֶעְתִּיקוּ.
and they of their own initiative dispatched scribes and copied it.
כִּי כֵּן הוּא הַמִּדָּה: "יָמִין דּוֹחָה וּשְׂמֹאל מְקָרֶבֶת",
For such is the divine attribute: "the right hand repels and the left hand draws close,"
וְהוּא מִדַּת אַהֲרֹן, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, "אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם";
and this was the attribute of Aaron, peace be upon him, a "lover of peace";

וְעַל כֵּן, אַף דְּמֵאֲחוֹרֵיהּ אֲתָא וְנַשְׁיֵהּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (צ״א1273 Chullin 91a — R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: The verse states "as he wrestled with him" — like a man who embraces his fellow, whose hand reaches the hollow of his fellow's right thigh [and so only the right sciatic nerve is forbidden]. And the Rabbis hold: he came upon him from behind and dislocated both of them. Rashi: One who embraces his fellow embraces him from the front, and his right hand reaches around from behind to the hollow of his fellow's right thigh. The Rabbis, who dispute R. Yehuda and forbid the nerve of both thighs, hold that the angel came upon him from behind and struck him on both of them, until the nerves slipped from their place and rose up. Maharsha: Rashi in his commentary on the Torah set aside Menachem's derivation of "as he wrestled [behe'avko]" from "dust [avak]" — that they raised dust — and explained it instead from the sense of binding, that he clasped and bound him. This requires study, for Rashi's explanation and Menachem's are themselves the two expositions over which the Tannaim divide here in our sugya, and the difficulty can be resolved only with a forced answer. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Chullin 91a): R. Yehoshua ben Levi holds that the angel reached only the hollow of Jacob's right thigh, because when two beings are locked together, each of them prevails through his principal strength, which is the right, and he overpowers the other at the other's principal strength as well; therefore the angel's hand reached Jacob on his right side. The Rabbis, who say he came from behind, hold that each of the two possessed what the other lacked — Jacob's form is engraved upon the throne of glory, while the angel has the rank of a being separate from matter, which Jacob, being a man, did not have — and since each has what the other has not, they are wholly opposed, and a thing wholly opposed to another comes to push it away entirely; therefore the angel came against him from behind, from both sides, and the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to both. These matters are exceedingly deep. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 25): Moshe and Aharon are known to be the two thighs, Netzach and Hod, and they drew everything near to the aspect of Jacob himself, to repair what is written, "and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was dislocated" — for the Rabbis say, "He came upon him from behind and dislocated both of them"; and Moshe and Aharon together repair both. עַמּוּד א׳),
and therefore, even though the angel came from behind him and struck them both, as they taught in Chullin 91a,
עִיקַּר הַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁלִיטָה הָיָה מִצַּד הַשְּׂמֹאל, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הַיָּמִין,
the primary beginning of the adversary's dominion came from the left side, which stands opposite the right,
דְּזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה שֶׁבּוֹ הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל חָפֵץ לְנַצֵּחַ וְלִפְשֹׁט אַדְּרַבָּה הוֹדוֹ.
for it is the unholy counterpart in which the base adversary desires to conquer and, on the contrary, extend his own splendor.
וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטָתוֹ בְּהַעֲלָמַת הַהוֹד דִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
And through his mastery in obscuring the Hod (splendor) of holiness,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה רוֹצֶה אַחַר כָּךְ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר גַּם עַל מִדַּת הַנִּצּוּחַ שֶׁלָּהֶם
he subsequently seeks through this to overpower their attribute of triumph (Netzach) as well,
כָּל זְמַן חֶשְׁכַּת הַלַּיְלָה,
throughout the duration of the darkness of the night,
עַד זְרִיחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לִרְפוּאוֹת,
until the rising of the sun to bring healing,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי חַשְׁמוֹנַאי,
which likewise came about through the Priests, the sons of the Hasmoneans,
שֶׁהֱשִׁיבוּ אוֹר הַהוֹד לִמְקוֹמוֹ עַל יְדֵי קִדּוּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם דְּאוֹתָן שֶׁמָּסְרוּ עַצְמָן עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם.
who restored the light of Hod to its rightful place through the sanctification of the Name of Heaven by those who gave their lives in martyrdom.
וְאֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן, רֹאשׁ הַמַּעְתִּיקִים הַתּוֹרָה יְוָנִית,
And Eleazar the Priest, the head of those who translated the Torah into Greek,
גַּם כֵּן תִּיקֵּן אֶת עַצְמוֹ בָּזֶה שֶׁזָּכָה לֵהָרֵג אַחַר כָּךְ עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם, כַּכָּתוּב בְּיוֹסִיפוֹן;
likewise rectified himself in this matter in that he subsequently merited to be martyred for the sanctification of the Name, as recorded in Sefer Yosippon;
שֶׁבָּזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה הַהוֹד דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for through this was revealed the Hod of the children of Israel,
שֶׁאֵין יְכֹלֶת בְּיַד הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל לְנַצְּחָם כְּלָל.
demonstrating that the base adversary has no power to conquer them whatsoever.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְנֵס דְּשֶׁמֶן,
And through this they merited the miracle of the oil,
שֶׁהֶרְאָה לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֵם רְאוּיִם לְהָאִיר לְפָנָיו בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
wherein the blessed Hashem showed them that they are worthy to shine before Him in the Holy Temple,

שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הָאוֹרָה יוֹצְאָה לָעוֹלָם (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ)1274 Bamidbar Rabbah 15:2 — The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: It is not because I need the lamps that I charged you concerning the lamps, but in order to give you merit. Know this: when a man builds a house he makes the windows narrow on the outside and wide within, so that the light may enter from outside and give light within. But Solomon, when he built the Temple, did not do so; he made the windows narrow within and wide without, so that the light should go out from the Temple and give light outside, as it is stated: "And he made for the house windows broad and narrow" (I Kings 6:4) — to make known to you that He is all light and has no need of their light. And why did He command you? To give you merit..
from where illumination issues forth to the entire world (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Behaalotecha).
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן מִצְוַת נֵרוֹת דְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
And this is the inner purpose of the mitzvah of the Menorah lamps in the Holy Temple,
שֶׁהוּא לְהָאִיר לְפָנָיו בַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלִים;
which is to shine before Him into the dark alleyways;
כִּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מְבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלִים מֵאוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הָאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
for this world consists of alleyways darkened from the light of the blessed Hashem by the nations of the world.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ל1275 Bereshit Rabbah 30:10 — R. Nechemiah said: To what may Abraham be compared? To the friend of a king who saw the king walking in dark alleys. The friend looked out and began to shed light upon him through the window. The king looked up and saw him, and said to him: Rather than giving me light through the window, come and give light before me. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Abraham: Rather than giving Me light from Mesopotamia and its neighboring lands, come and give light before Me in the Land of Israel.׳) עַל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And as the Sages said in Bereishit Rabbah (end of parashah 30) concerning our father Abraham, peace be upon him,
שֶׁבָּא וְהֵאִיר לְפָנָיו, כִּבְיָכוֹל, בַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלִים,
that he came and illuminated before Him, as it were, in the dark alleyways,
הַיְינוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁפִּרְסֵם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְכָל הָאֻמּוֹת.
meaning by virtue of his publicizing His blessed Divinity to all the nations.
וְזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן כָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת דְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
And this was likewise the intent of all the sacred services in the Holy Temple,
שֶׁהָיָה שָׁם גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה לְפַרְסֵם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ;
wherein the Shechinah was revealed in order to make His Divinity known;
וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּרוֹת הוּא לְהָאִיר לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם,
and the kindling of the lamps is to bring light to all inhabitants of the world,
גַּם לְאוֹתָם שֶׁבְּתַכְלִית הַחַשְׁכוּת.
even to those immersed in the deepest obscurity.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּנוּסַח "עַל הַנִּסִּים" פָּרַט מִכָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת מַה שֶּׁהִדְלִיקוּ נֵרוֹת,
Therefore, in the liturgy of Al HaNissim it singled out from all the Temple services that they kindled lamps,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת מִדַּת הַהוֹד שֶׁתִּיקְּנוּ אָז.
for this is the essential perfection of the attribute of Hod that they rectified then.
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר הַנֵּס שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בָּזֶה,
And the supernatural miracle that occurred to them therein was not explicitly mentioned,
דְּאֵין זֶה מֵעִנְיַן הַנֵּס וְהַיְשׁוּעָה דַּחֲנֻכָּה,
because that was not the primary substance of the historical miracle and salvation of Chanukah;
רַק הוּא מַה שֶּׁגִּלּוּ לָהֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁנִּתְרַצּוּ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ,
it was merely an indication revealed to them from Heaven that they were favorably accepted before Him,
וְשֶׁתִּיקְּנוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, עַד שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם סִיְּעוּם לְהָאִיר לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and that they had achieved full rectification, to the extent that Heaven assisted them in illuminating before Him.
וּמִזֶּה הֵבִינוּ לִקְבּוֹעַ יְמֵי חֲנֻכָּה לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם,
And from this they understood to establish the days of Chanukah for all generations,
לְהַדְלִיק נֵרוֹת גַּם שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בַּגְּבוּלִין.
to kindle lights even outside the Holy Temple throughout all dwelling places.
וְאַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן נֵר לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד אוֹ "נֵר אִישׁ וּבֵיתוֹ" עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
And following the Destruction of the Temple, there is likewise a light for each individual or at least "a lamp for a man and his household,"
לְהָאִיר בּוֹ לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
through which to radiate light to all the inhabitants of the world.
דְּעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר מִצְוָתָהּ לְהַעֲמִיד מִבַּחוּץ לְהָאִיר לָעוֹלָם;
Wherefore the primary fulfillment of the mitzvah is to place it on the outside to shine into the world;
וְרַק מִשֶּׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִם אוֹר זֶה נֶעְלַם,
and only once they became intermingled among the gentiles was this light concealed,
וְעַל כֵּן אָנוּ מַדְלִיקִין בַּבַּיִת כִּבִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה,
and therefore we kindle inside the home as in a time of danger,
דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן זְמַן הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָעַמִּים בִּגְזֵרַת שְׁמָד שֶׁבָּא מִצַּד הִתְחַבְּרוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם.
which is likewise the time when the nations are stirred to decrees of religious persecution arising from Israel's association with them.
וְכֵן אָנוּ עַתָּה תָּמִיד, בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ הָרַבִּים, בְּהִתְחַבְּרוּת בְּיוֹתֵר בֵּינֵיהֶם,
And so we are currently, due to our many iniquities, in extensive association among them,

עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ח1276 Avodah Zarah 8a — It was taught: R. Yishmael says: Jews outside the Land are idolaters in purity. How so? A gentile who made a feast for his son and invited all the Jews of his town — even though they eat their own food and drink their own drink and their own attendant waits upon them, Scripture accounts it to them as though they had eaten of the sacrifices of the dead, as it is stated: "And he call you, and you eat of his sacrifice." Rashi: "In purity" means without intent — they give the matter no thought at all. "And he call you" implies that since you are one whom he has invited, I account your eating as though it were of his sacrifice. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): As they said, "Jews outside the Land are idolaters in purity: a gentile who made a feast…" — it is called "in purity" because they eat and drink their own, so that, on the contrary, their distance from idolatry and the distinction between Israel and the nations is evident there; yet from the side of the gentile, who goes and gives thanks [to his god], there is in it a trace and taint of idolatry, though from the Jew's side it is in utter purity. So too at Achashverosh's feast, the Jews were given to eat and drink of their own. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 8): [Although at Achashverosh's feast they ate only kosher food,] our Rabbis nevertheless called such a case "idolaters in purity"; it resembles the idolatry of bowing to the image, which was likewise "in purity" according to the law, while the slumber of exile that had settled upon them caused the coldness and lack of fiery zeal to root out every trace of idolatry.׳ עַמּוּד א׳) דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּטָהֳרָה,
to the extent that the Sages said in Avodah Zarah 8a that Jews in the Diaspora serve idols in purity,
וְעַד שֶׁהִתִּירוּ מַאֲכָל וּמִשְׁתֵּה אֵידֵיהֶן וְכַיּוֹצֵא;
and even permitted food and drink of their festivals, and the like;
וְאֵין הָאוֹר בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּחוּץ,
and the light is not openly revealed on the outside,
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מֵאִיר מִבִּפְנִים,
nevertheless it shines from within;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב הוּא מֵאִיר אוֹר זֶה דְּהוֹד,
for in truth, in the depths of the heart this light of Hod shines,
וְכָל הִתְחַבְּרוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא בְּטָהֳרָה,
and all their association with them is in purity,
דִּכְבָר נִתְקַן זֶה עַל יְדֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ שֶׁהָיָה מִיָּד בַּשְּׁמָד הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְזַר עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
since this was already rectified by Mattathias, who arose immediately during the first religious persecution decreed upon Israel,
וְנִתְבָּרֵר זֶה דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק לְעוֹלָם בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and it was clarified that the depths of the hearts of Israel are forever cleaved to the blessed Hashem,
וְכָל חִבּוּרָם עִם הָאֻמּוֹת, בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ, הוּא רַק לִקְלוֹט נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת מֵהֶם.
and all their connection with the nations, in absolute truth, is solely to absorb holy sparks from them.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים פ״ז1277 Pesachim 87b — R. Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel among the nations only so that converts would join them, as it is stated: "And I will sow her to Me in the land" (Hosea 2:25). Does a man sow a se'ah of grain for any purpose other than to bring in many kor? R. Yochanan said it is derived from here: "And I will have compassion upon her that had not received compassion" (ibid.). Maharsha: ["He exiled... only":] for had it been as punishment for their sin, He could have punished them with other things; rather, it was so that converts should be added to them — that is, to make the faith known among the other nations as well. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:77): The Sages said, "Israel was exiled only so as to add converts," for the exile is because the Blessed One wished that even in dark places, in the concealment of His countenance, they should find His truth and recognize Him even "from behind," as it were; and from this aspect converts too are added, yet they are nevertheless hard for Israel "like a scab." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 10): The Land, being soft and not rocky, yields more fruit, as the Sages expounded "And I will sow her to Me in the land," that through sowing in the holiness of the Land comes the vast increase; and "they were exiled only so as to add converts" means that each gentile has a particular power that he cannot change at all, nor can the convert change it. What is added in exile is that Israel absorbs the power of the lands of the nations, the particular obstinacy and heart of stone of each place, and by clarifying that in that power they are not obstinate like the nations but can change it for the glory of Heaven as the Blessed One wills, converts are added: the power of the nations' heart of stone is also granted to join Israel and be called by the name of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Parah 3): The Midrash's "Israel from the nations" does not mean their descent from Terah, which is already covered by "Abraham from Terah," but refers to "The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel only so that converts would be added to them," which was explained to mean not actual converts but the holy sparks and vitality within the nations, as in "and You give life to them all," which are brought out through the exiles. All the nations have holy sparks from which their life derives, and for this reason exile among all seventy nations was needed. Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 10): Through the length of their wanderings Israel brings out further holiness that is found [among the nations], as it says, "The Holy One, blessed be He, did righteousness with Israel by scattering them among the nations," and "He exiled Israel among the nations only so that converts would be added to them." The matter is that every nation was created for His glory, that the glory of Heaven should come forth from it, only they are its opposite; by entering among the nations Israel clarifies how the glory of Heaven is built even from them, and in this lies great preciousness: to understand and bring forth the glory of Heaven even from its opposite. Tiferes Yosef (Rosh Hashanah 17): The main purpose of the exile is as the Talmud says on "the righteousness of His scattering in Israel": the Holy One, blessed be He, did righteousness with Israel so that converts would be added to them, like one who sows with a scattering hand, the whole aim of whose intention is that a crop should grow from it. So too, in the future the Blessed One will show that the aim of the exile was that souls be added to Israel, and that not a single individual was cast away. עַמּוּד ב׳): לֹא גָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְוַסְּפוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גֵּרִים,
And as they said (Pesachim 87b): Israel was exiled only so that converts should be added to them,
וְלָאו דַּוְקָא גֵּרִים בַּפֹּעַל,
which does not mean exclusively literal converts,
רַק הוֹסָפַת קְלִיטַת כֹּחוֹת הָעַמִּים לְהַחֲזִירָם אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה לְאַט לְאַט, עַד בּוֹא עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיָּשׁוּב הַכֹּל לִקְדוּשָׁה.
but rather the cumulative absorption of the spiritual forces of the nations to restore them to holiness gradually, until the End of Days when everything will return to sanctity.
וְאַף שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת אֵין זֶה גִּלּוּי עֲדַיִן,
And although externally this is not yet manifest,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב אוֹר זֶה גָּלוּי וּמֵאִיר הֵיטֵב, וּפוֹעֵל פְּעֻלָּתוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם.
nevertheless in the interior of the heart this light is revealed and shines brightly, effecting its purpose regardless.
וְכָל הַמּוּמָרִים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתְחַבְּרוּ לָהֶם לְגַמְרֵי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And regarding all those apostates of Israel who became completely bound to the nations in this world,
יָדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ"ן שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה רֹאשׁ בְּתוֹלַדְתּוֹ מֵעִרְבּוּב בְּנֵי נֵכָר.
the words of Nachmanides are well known, that this stems from some root producing poison and gall in his birth through an intermixture of foreign ancestry.

וְזֶה סוֹד שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת כ״א1278 Shabbat 21b — Its time is from sunset until traffic has ceased from the marketplace. And until when? Rabbah bar bar Chana said in the name of R. Yochanan: Until the last of the Tarmodites [the wood-sellers, who linger longest in the market] is gone. Rashi: "The foot of the Tarmodites": the name of a people who gather thin sticks of wood and linger in the market until the people of the market go home after dark and kindle fires in their houses; and when these need wood, they go out and buy it from them. Tosafos (s.v. "if he has not lit, he lights"): [He may light until traffic has ceased from the marketplace,] but from then on the time has passed. R. Yosef Porat says one should take care to light promptly at nightfall and not delay too long, yet if he did delay he should still light because of the doubt, since the Gemara gives another answer [that the measure refers to the quantity of oil]; and the Ri holds that nowadays there is no need to be concerned about when one lights, for we light indoors and the recognition is only for the members of the household. עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּהַדְלָקַת נֵר חֲנֻכָּה: "עַד דְּכָלְיָא רַגְלָא דְּתַרְמוֹדָאֵי",
And this is the mystical meaning I heard concerning what the Sages taught (Shabbat 21b) regarding the Chanukah light: "until the foot of the Tarmodites ceases,"

דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּכְלֶה עִרְבּוּב הַפְּסוּלִים מִבְּנֵי נֵכָר בְּמִשְׁפְּחוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַתַּרְמוֹדָאֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (י״ז1279 Yevamot 17a — What is Harpanya? R. Zeira said: A mountain [har] to which all turn [ponin]. It was taught in a baraita: Anyone who does not know his family or his tribe turns aside to there. The unfit of Harpanya are on account of the unfit of Meishan, and the unfit of Meishan on account of the unfit of Tarmod, and the unfit of Tarmod on account of the servants of Solomon. Rashi: "[A mountain] to which all turn": all the unfit who cannot find a wife turn and go there. "On account of the unfit of Meishan": which is near it, and they intermingle with them; and it is said in Kiddushin (71b), "Meishan is dead," and their unfitness is explained there. Tosafos (s.v. "the unfit of Meishan on account of the unfit of Tarmod"): As for the statement in Kiddushin (49b), "Ten kabin of brazenness descended to the world; Meishan took nine" — which is explained as being because they are mamzerim — it does not mention Tarmod, though its people are more unfit, perhaps because [the unfitness] spread in Meishan until they grew more numerous than in Tarmod; or perhaps in Tarmod the majority were gentiles, while in Meishan the majority were Israelites. עַמּוּד א׳).
meaning that the tainted intermixture of foreign elements within Jewish families caused by the Tarmodites should cease, as they taught in Yevamot 17a.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּנֵר חֲנֻכָּה מֵאִיר גַּם לָהֶם עַד שֶׁיִּכְלֶה גַּם זֶה הַפְּסֹלֶת הַמְּעֹרְבָב,
That is, the Chanukah light shines even upon them until this intermixed dross is eliminated,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד שׁוּם חִבּוּר גַּם לְמַרְאִית עַיִן.
so that there will no longer remain any union with them even in appearance.
דְּחִבּוּר זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ עַל יְדֵי עִרְבּוּבְיָא זֶה שֶׁבְּמִשְׁפְּחוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
For this attachment stems from this genetic mingling within the families of Israel,
כִּי מִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה חִבּוּר עָצוּם לִהְיוֹת לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד;
since from this arose a powerful bond of becoming one flesh;
וְנֵר חֲנֻכָּה מֵאִיר בְּתֹקֶף כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁיַּפְרִיד גַּם חִבּוּר זֶה,
and the Chanukah light shines with such potency that it severs even this bond,
וִיבָרֵר שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה רַק לִקְלוֹט אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לִקְלוֹט, וְלֹא זוּלַת זֶה.
and clarifies that even this was intended solely to absorb into holiness whatever was fit to be absorbed, and nothing beyond that.

items.h:
Seif 3 — The Decree of Intermarriage and the Hasmonean Revolt
The Hasmonean uprising begins against forced sexual mixture, revealing Chanukah as a defense of covenantal separation.

p: וּתְחִלַּת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים בַּיּוֹצֵר לַחֲנֻכָּה, הָיָה עַל זֶה: שֶׁלֹּא תִּבָּעֵל אֲחוֹתָם לַהֶגְמוֹן.
And the initial awakening of the Hasmoneans, according to what is recited in the liturgical Yotzer for Chanukah, was over this: that their sister should not be violated by the Greek governor.

וְגַם רַשִׁ"י בְּשַׁבָּת (כ״ג1280 Rashi on Shabbat 23a:2:1 — "They too were part of that miracle" — for the Greeks decreed that every betrothed virgin be violated first by the officer, and the miracle came about through a woman. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:124): The publicizing of the miracle through the Chanukah lights also concerns the preservation of lineage, as Rashi explains [on "they too were part of that miracle"] that the decree then was that a virgin who marries be violated by the officer; therefore the miracle came through the Kohanim, the most pedigreed in Israel, and through a lamp, for "one who is regular with lamps will have sons who are Torah scholars." עַמּוּד א׳) עַל "שֶׁאַף הֵן הָיוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַנֵּס" פֵּירֵשׁ: בַּגְּזֵרָה דְּתִבָּעֵל לַהֶגְמוֹן,
And Rashi too in Shabbat 23a, on the dictum "for they also were included in that miracle," explained: regarding the decree that a maiden must submit to the governor,
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עִיקַּר נֵס דַּחֲנֻכָּה — לְבַטֵּל עֵירוּב וְחִבּוּר זֶה.
for this was the essential miracle of Chanukah: to nullify this intermixture and union.
עַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁבָּא הוֹרְדוֹס לִידָּבֵק בְּזַרְעָם לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳);
Therefore, when Herod sought to graft himself onto their lineage he did not succeed, as they taught at the beginning of Bava Batra 3b;
כִּי זֶה כָּל שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל זַרְעָם אַחֲרֵיהֶם,
for this was the entire root holiness of the Hasmoneans extending throughout all their descendants after them,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁפָּעֲלוּ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה לְהִשָּׁאֵר קָבוּעַ לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחוּ לְהִתְעָרֵב עִמָּהֶם זֶרַע נֵכָר.
since they established the sanctity permanently for all generations that no alien seed be permitted to intermingle with them.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לְהַנִּיחַ עִרְבּוּבְיָא זֶה עֲדַיִן בָּעוֹלָם עַד עֵת קֵץ,
And because the blessed Hashem desired to allow this mixture to remain in the world until the End of Days,
עַל כֵּן נִתְעַלֵּם זֶרַע הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים,
the seed of the Hasmoneans was therefore hidden and eclipsed,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם)1281 Bava Batra 3b — Herod was a slave of the house of the Hasmoneans, and he set his eyes upon a certain girl of theirs. One day he heard a heavenly voice say: Any slave who rebels now will succeed. He rose and killed all his masters, sparing only that girl. When the girl saw that he wished to marry her, she went up to the roof and cried out: Whoever comes and says "I am descended from the house of the Hasmoneans" is a slave, for none of them remains except this girl — and this girl is casting herself from the roof to the ground. And she threw herself down. Tosafos (s.v. "whoever comes and says: I am descended from the house of the Hasmoneans, is a slave"): And so it is, for Shmuel says the same in Kiddushin 70b. From here there is a difficulty with Rashi's explanation in Sotah 41a, where the people said to Agrippa "you are our brother," and Rashi explains that they said so because his mother was an Israelite woman: if that were the reason, then since Herod's descendants married an Israelite woman, why was Agrippa still a slave — for Shmuel himself holds that the child of a gentile or a slave by an Israelite woman is fit? One must say rather that they did not marry an Israelite woman, and that they called him "our brother" only because a slave is our brother in the commandments. Maharsha: The Gemara is precise in saying that he wished "to marry her": he was a slave of the house of the Hasmoneans and had not yet been freed, and once he had killed them all he remained the slave of that girl alone. Had he married her he would thereby have been freed of himself, as is said of a master who marries his maidservant — and the same holds in reverse, of a woman who marries her slave. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 1): Ramban writes that the Hasmoneans were punished for taking the kingship, so that none of their seed remained — to the point that they said, "Whoever says, 'I come from the royal house of the Hasmoneans,' is a slave," for not even females remained of them. As for why so severe a punishment: at the time of the miracle the Hasmoneans were the root of the Oral Torah, the "lawgiver from between his feet" [descended from Judah through the female line], but Yannai, who denied the Oral Torah and took the kingship only as a ruling scepter, transgressed "the scepter shall not depart from Judah," and it was decreed that his seed come to an end.: דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר "מִבֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי אָתֵינָא" — עַבְדָּא הוּא.
as they said there: whoever declares "I come from the royal house of the Hasmoneans" is a slave.
וּבָרוּר בְּעֵינַי דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ "דְּלָא אִשְׁתַּיַּיר מִנַּיְיהוּ" וְכוּלֵי אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דְּלֹא נִשְׁאַר לְגַמְרֵי מֵהֶם,
And it is clear in my eyes that their statement that "none remained of them" does not mean that literally none of them survived,
וְחָלִילָה מִי שֶׁעָשָׂה הַתְּשׁוּעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה הַזֹּאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יִכְלֶה זַרְעוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם.
and God forbid that those who wrought this great salvation in Israel should have their lineage eliminated from the earth.
וְאַף דְּהָרַמְבַּ"ן פָּרָשַׁת וַיְחִי נָתַן טַעַם לָזֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנָּטְלוּ מְלוּכָה,
And although Nachmanides in Parashat Vayechi gave a reason for this, that they usurped the monarchy,
אֵין זֶה מַסְפִּיק לְהָסִיר הַשְּׁאֵלָה: לָמָּה יַגִּיעַ עֹנֶשׁ זֶה לְחַשְׁמוֹנַאי הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁלֹּא נָטַל מְלוּכָה, שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר כְּלוּם מִזַּרְעוֹ.
this does not suffice to resolve the question: why should such a punishment reach the righteous Hasmonean elder who never took the kingship, that nothing should remain of his seed?
אֲבָל בָּרוּר בְּעֵינַי דְּהַכַּוָּנָה שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מִזַּרְעוֹ בְּפִרְסוּם וּמִי שֶׁיִּתְיַחֵס אַחֲרָיו;
Rather, it is clear to me that the intention is that none of his descendants survived openly with public lineage traced back to him;
וּ"קַטְלִינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ מָרָתֵיהּ" הַיְינוּ כָּל אוֹתָם שֶׁמָּצָא, וְהֵם נֶעֶנְשׁוּ בַּעֲוֹנָם,
and Herod's "slaughtering all his masters" refers only to all those whom he managed to find, who were punished for their specific sin,
וְהַשְּׁאָר נֶחְבְּאוּ וְהֶעֱלִימוּ עַצְמָם וְלֹא פִּרְסְמוּ יִחוּסָם.
while the rest went into hiding, concealed their identities, and did not publicize their genealogy.
וּלְפִי שֶׁמָּשְׁכָה מַלְכוּת הוֹרְדוֹס וְזַרְעוֹ מֵאָה שָׁנָה,
And because the reign of Herod and his dynasty lasted a hundred years,
שֶׁכָּל אוֹתָם הַיָּמִים הָיָה יָרֵא לְפַרְסֵם עַצְמוֹ מִי שֶׁהָיָה מִבֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי,
during all of which anyone of the Hasmonean house feared to expose himself,
עַל כֵּן נִשְׁתַּקַּע וְנִשְׁתַּכַּח זֵכֶר יִחוּסָם מִן הָעוֹלָם;
the recorded knowledge of their lineage consequently faded away and was forgotten from the world;
וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר מִי שֶׁמִּתְיַחֵס אַחֲרֵיהֶם אֶלָּא אוֹתָם הָעֲבָדִים בְּנֵי הוֹרְדוֹס,
and there remained no one openly claiming descent from them except those slaves, the offspring of Herod,
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁנָּשָׂא מִבְּנוֹתָם כְּדֵי לְיַחֵס זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרֵיהֶם;
who claimed he had married one of their daughters in order to trace his seed to them;
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים גַּם זֶה הָיָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקַּע וְיִשְׁתַּכַּח יִחוּסוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם.
and at all events, this forgetting and sinking of their lineage into obscurity was ordained from Heaven.
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ יִחוּסוֹ הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הָרִחוּק מֵעֵירוּב בְּנֵי נֵכָר,
For the root of their pedigree stands at the absolute antithesis of any mixture with foreigners,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה אֱמֶת בְּכָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב גַּם כֵּן,
and although this is true fundamentally of all the seed of Jacob as well,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם, בִּפְרָט אַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן.
in this world it is nevertheless deeply concealed, especially after the Destruction of the Temple.
וּמֵהַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַחֻרְבָּן שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּחִלַּת מַלְכוּת הוֹרְדוֹס,
And from the initial stirrings of the Destruction, which began with the reign of Herod,
שֶׁהָיָה עֶבֶד וּמִבְּנֵי נֵכָר וּמָשַׁל עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ מַלְכוּת רוֹמִי,
who was an Edomite slave and ruled through the military power of the Roman Empire,
וְנִטְּלָה הַמַּלְכוּת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל;
and the sovereign crown was taken from Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן עַל יָדוֹ הָיָה הִתְעַלְּמוּת יַחַס הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים,
therefore through him came about the concealment of the genealogy of the Hasmoneans,
שֶׁהֵם הַמִּשְׁתַּדְּלִים לְכַלּוֹת "רַגְלָא דְּתַרְמוֹדָאֵי" וְעִרְבּוּב בְּנֵי נֵכָר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
who were the very ones dedicated to eliminating the "foot of the Tarmodites" and the mixture of foreign lineage from Israel.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּזֶה עִנְיַן סְמִיכוּת הַדְּרָשׁוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת כ״ב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳:
And it appears to me that this is the deeper link between the juxtaposed homilies in Shabbat 22a:

"נֵר חֲנֻכָּה שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים" וְכוּלֵי1282 Shabbat 22a — Rav Kahana said, Rav Natan bar Manyumi expounded in the name of R. Tanchum: A Chanukah lamp that one placed above twenty cubits is unfit, like a sukkah and like an alley. And Rav Kahana said, Rav Natan bar Manyumi expounded in the name of R. Tanchum: What is the meaning of that which is written, “And the pit was empty, there was no water in it”? From the implication of what is said, “and the pit was empty,” do I not know that there was no water in it? Rather, why does Scripture say “there was no water in it”? Water there was none in it, but snakes and scorpions there were in it. Rashi: “Unfit” — for the eye does not take in what is above twenty cubits, and so there is no publicizing of the miracle. “Like a sukkah and like an alley” — of which it is taught explicitly, in Eruvin and in tractate Sukkah, that they are unfit. Tosafos (s.v. “A Chanukah lamp that one placed above twenty cubits”): One might ask: it should have said “let him lower it,” as is said of an alley, where the Gemara explains that for an alley, which is rabbinic, it teaches the remedy. It says “unfit” because it wishes to compare it to a sukkah, which is from the Torah; or else it did not wish to go on at length — he must extinguish it, lower it and relight it — for to lower it and leave it as it is while it burns will not do, as is proven below. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 20): A Chanukah lamp placed above twenty cubits is unfit even though it was lit with every detail of the law, because the eye does not rule over it: the essence of the mitzvah is to see the lights, through which the "light sown for the righteous" is fixed in the heart, repairing the blemish of the covenant. The adjacent teaching, "but snakes and scorpions there were in it" [which showed Joseph in the pit that he still needed refining], was set beside it so that a person should not rely on himself that everything is already repaired, but know that the days of Chanukah are a preparation and training in this light toward the complete repair in the days of Shovavim. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Shabbos): Creation is comprised in three general categories — world, year and soul — and in each the Blessed One chose its choicest part to illuminate with a particular light; and this is what they said, "A Chanukah lamp placed above twenty cubits is unfit, like a sukkah and like an alley": the Chanukah lamp corresponds to soul, the sukkah to world, and the alley to year, for in time it is the Sabbath day that is the choicest.,
“A Chanukah lamp that was placed above twenty cubits...” and so forth,
"וְהַבּוֹר רֵק אֵין בּוֹ מַיִם" וְכוּלֵי;
and “The pit was empty, there was no water in it...” and so forth;
וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה דְּרָשִׁינְהוּ כָּךְ יַחַד בְּשַׁבַּת חֲנֻכָּה פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב,
for evidently the Sage expounded them together on Shabbat Chanukah during the week of Parashat Vayeshev,
וְדָרַשׁ הֲלָכָה מֵעִנְיַן הַיּוֹם וְאַגָּדָה מֵאוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה,
delivering a halachah of the festival day alongside an aggadah from that week's Torah portion,
וְשַׁיָּיכֵי לַהֲדָדֵי.
and they are profoundly connected to one another.
כִּי יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לַזּוּלַת,
For Joseph, who corresponds to the sefirah of Yesod and the root of channeling divine influence outward to others,
וְהוּא "הַמַּשְׁבִּיר בַּר לְכָל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ",
and who was "the provider of grain to all the peoples of the land,"
הוּא הָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הָרִחוּק מִבְּנֵי נֵכָר כַּאֲשֶׁר נִתְנַסָּה בְּפוֹטִיפַר;
stood at the absolute pinnacle of separation from foreigners when he was tested with Potiphar's wife;

וְכֵן לֹא רָצָה לִמְכּוֹר לָהֶם עַד שֶׁיִּמּוֹלוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא מִקֵּץ1283 Midrash Tanchuma, Miketz 7 — When the famine grew severe upon them in the land of Egypt, the Egyptians gathered and came to Joseph and said to him: Give us bread. He said to them: My God does not sustain the uncircumcised. Go and circumcise yourselves, and I will give you bread. They went to Pharaoh, crying out and weeping before him, as it is stated: "And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread" (Genesis 41:55). They said to him: We went to him, and he speaks empty words to us, saying, Circumcise yourselves. He said to them: Fools! ... Go to Joseph, and whatever he says to you, do.),
and likewise he refused to sell grain to the Egyptians until they circumcised themselves (Midrash Tanchuma, Miketz),
וְלֹא רָצָה לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לַעֲרֵלִים כְּלָל.
unwilling to channel sustenance to the uncircumcised at all.
כִּי הַנְּגִיעָה הָיָה רַק בַּיְּרֵכַיִם שֶׁהֵם הַמְּכִינִים הַהַשְׁפָּעָה,
For the adversary's touch struck only the thighs, which prepare the outward influence,
וְלֹא בַּיְסוֹד שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר יְצִיאַת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לַפֹּעַל,
and not the Yesod, which is the actual culmination of the influence brought into reality,
דְּזֶה וַדַּאי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם הָרָאוּי כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for this surely takes place only in its proper holy vessel according to the will of the blessed Hashem.
וּמַה שֶּׁהַשְּׁבָטִים מְכָרוּהוּ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן לְבָרֵר זֶה,
And the brothers' selling him was likewise to clarify this matter,
כִּי הֵם לֹא הֶאֱמִינוּ בְּצִדְקָתוֹ וְשֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
for they did not believe in his supreme righteousness and that he was the "foundation of the world" (Tzaddik Yesod Olam),
וְחָשְׁבוּ בִּמְכִירָה בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת יִתְבָּרֵר זֶה,
thinking that through his sale among the nations this truth would be tested:
שֶׁאִם הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כְּמִדָּתוֹ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּתְעָרֵב בַּגּוֹיִם לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹהֶם כְּלָל;
that if he was genuinely true to his spiritual stature, he could never assimilate among the gentiles to become like them at all;
וְאִם לָאו, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא בְּבֵית יַעֲקֹב וְלָמַד מֵאָבִיו הָיָה טוֹב,
whereas if not, then it was only while in Jacob's house learning from his father that he remained good,
וּכְשֶׁיָּבוֹא לְבֵין הַגּוֹיִם לֹא יִהְיֶה כֵּן.
and once exposed among the gentiles he would falter.
וְזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הַהַשְׁלָכָה לַבּוֹר:
And this was also the purpose of casting him into the pit:

"שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַיִם" — זוֹ תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה פ״ד)1284 Bereshit Rabbah 84:16 — "And they cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, there was no water in it" (Genesis 37:24) — water there was not in it, but snakes and scorpions there were in it. R. Acha said: "An empty pit" — Jacob's well had been emptied out. "There was no water in it" — there were no words of Torah in it, which are likened to water, as you say: "Ho, everyone who thirsts, come for water" (Isaiah 55:1). עַל פָּסוּק זֶה,
“wherein there was no water”—this refers to Torah, as the Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah 84 on this verse,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיַן יוֹסֵף,
and this applies directly to the trial of Joseph;
דְּכָל נִסָּיוֹן שֶׁהוּא לְבָרֵר עַצְמִיּוּתוֹ
for any trial designed to test an individual's intrinsic essence
הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲלִימוּ מִמֶּנּוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַמַּצִּילִים מֵהַחֵטְא,
occurs when the explicit protections of Torah that rescue from sin are obscured from him,
רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּלִבּוֹ וּבְעַצְמוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה כִּרְצוֹנוֹ,
leaving him solely to his own heart and inner will to act,
וְזֶהוּ הַנִּסָּיוֹן לְבָרֵר מַה שֶּׁבְּלִבּוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע.
and this constitutes the ultimate trial to demonstrate what is genuinely in his heart, as is known.
וְהִשְׁלִיכוּהוּ לַבּוֹר רֵיק מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
They cast him into a pit void of the outward presence of Torah,
אֲבָל נְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים הַמְּסִיתִים לְכָל מִינֵי רָע, שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנָּחָשׁ, יֵשׁ שָׁם,
yet serpents and scorpions inciting to every form of evil—which is the primordial serpent's root—were present there,
וּבָזֶה נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁהוּא מְרֻחָק מֵרַע בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
and through this it was proven that in his very root he is completely detached from evil.
וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת הַיְסוֹד דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this is the root holiness of Yesod within Knesset Yisrael,
שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכִים לְעֵצוֹת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
in that they do not depend solely on external admonitions of Torah;
כִּי הֵם מִתְקַשְּׁרִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְגַמְרֵי בִּיסוֹד קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם שֶׁלֹּא יִנָּתֵק,
for they are bound to the blessed Hashem entirely through a steadfast, unshakeable foundation that cannot be severed,
בֵּין עַל יְדֵי מְסִיתִים וּמְפַתִּים כְּנָחָשׁ וּשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה,
neither through enticers and seducers like the serpent and the leaven in the dough,
בֵּין עַל יְדֵי כְּפִיָּה וּגְזֵרוֹת וְיִסּוּרִין כְּעַקְרַבִּים וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת —
nor through coercion, harsh decrees, and afflictions like scorpions and foreign subjugation—
לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְעָרְבְבוֹ עִמָּהֶם גַּם בְּלִי שׁוּם סִיּוּעַ דְּתוֹרָה תַּבְלִין, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד הֲסָתַת פְּרָטִיּוּת דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע.
none of these can cause them to assimilate, even without the overt aid of the Torah's seasoning, which combats specific inclinations to sin.
אֲבָל נֶגֶד שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁלֹּא יִתְעָרֵב בַּגּוֹיִם,
However, regarding the essential root of Jewish identity never to assimilate with the nations,
בָּזֶה בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְדָּלִים מִשָּׁרְשָׁם מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן,
in this the children of Israel are intrinsically distinct from their root from the very womb,
וְנִימּוֹלִים לִשְׁמוֹנָה, טֶרֶם יֵדַע הַנַּעַר כְּלוּם,
being circumcised on the eighth day before the infant possesses any awareness,
בָּא בִּבְרִית חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים,
entering the covenant of the blessed Hashem's seal that separates Israel from the nations,

דְּאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת (נְדָרִים ל״א1285 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along. עַמּוּד ב׳),
for foreskin is associated solely with idolaters (Nedarim 31b),
וַאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מוּבְדָּלִים מֵהֶם,
and even the willful transgressors and ignorant of Israel remain distinct from them;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (גִּיטִּין נ״ז1286 Gittin 57a — He then raised up Jesus of Nazareth by necromancy. He said to him: Who is esteemed in that world? He said to him: Israel. Should I attach myself to them? He said to him: Seek their welfare, do not seek their harm; whoever touches them is as one who touches the apple of His eye. He said to him: What is the sentence of that man? He said to him: Boiling excrement — for the Master said: Whoever mocks the words of the Sages is sentenced to boiling excrement. Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations of the world. Rashi: "For the Master said" — in Eruvin, where it is derived from "and much study [lahag] is a weariness of the flesh": one who mocks [malig] much is sentenced to weariness of the flesh; and that verse is written concerning the words of the Scribes, "And furthermore, my son, be admonished" — be more careful with the words of the Scribes than with the words of the Torah. "The prophets of the nations," who are idolaters — this is Balaam, upon whom the Divine Presence was revealed and who nevertheless spoke wickedly. Maharsha: "Whoever touches them is as one who touches the apple of His eye" — it is plain that one who touches the pupil of the eye destroys its light; so one who touches them for harm destroys and extinguishes the light of the world. As for "whoever mocks the words of the Sages is sentenced to boiling excrement," which Rashi derives from "much study [lahag] is a weariness of the flesh" — there the derivation is rejected on the ground that the verse does not write "mockery"; it seems that whoever does expound it so holds that the letter ayin interchanges with heh, and since the man degraded the words of the Sages he is sentenced to a degrading punishment, in excrement. Maharal (Netzach Yisrael, ch. 5): Nothing but excrement befits one who mocks the words of the Sages, for he is the opposite of the Sages, in whom there is intellect separate from man; therefore, when he mocks them, he is judged by the opposite of it — boiling excrement, which is likewise separate from a man and goes out of him by reason of its baseness. The intellect is separate from a man because of its elevation, and excrement is separate from a man because of its baseness; and so one who mocks the words of the Sages is sentenced to boiling excrement. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:28): The sinners of Israel in their body, "the skull that has not worn tefillin," have no attachment in their root to the Blessed One — such was the one of whom they said, "Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations" — and they derive from the inclination to idolatry, whereas the root of the prophets of the nations is the inclination to lewdness itself. "The sentence of that man," boiling excrement, is the waste of food, from the this-worldly lust in eating that is the root of all the inclinations, the idolatrous one included; yet still "come and see the difference," for in Israel the essential root is not so, since they worshipped idols only to permit illicit relations, an inclination whose root is open to good. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 5): In truth Bilaam is not fit to be in this count [of the commoners who have no share in the World to Come], being a gentile after the giving of the Torah, and it is a great merit for him to be included among them — for indeed they said, "Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations of the world": that man belongs to the seventh level of those who have no share in the World to Come, the last level, which has already gone out of Israel, and even so he is better than Bilaam. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 10): Finding favor is without reason: even when Jacob, Heaven forbid, acts like Esau, "I loved Jacob" with a love without reason — as they said, "Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations of the world," which comes to teach us that even such a sinner of Israel is superior to Bilaam, who was a prophet of the nations. עַמּוּד א׳): תָּא חֲזִי מַה בֵּין פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לִנְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי.
as the Sages stated (Gittin 57a): "Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations," and so forth.
וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַפּוּרִים "עַד דְּלָא יָדַע בֵּין" וְכוּלֵי, דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ יְדִיעָה כְּלָל,
And this is the sanctity of Purim, "until one does not know between...", where conscious intellect is completely unnecessary;
וְאֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל,
and Amalek falls only into the hands of the descendants of Rachel,

וְעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָאִים כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ע״א1287 Bereshit Rabbah 71:2 — R. Shimon ben Yochai taught: Since everything depended on Rachel, Israel were called by her name — "Rachel weeping for her children." And not only by her name, but by the name of her son — "Perhaps the Lord, God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph." And not only by the name of her son, but by the name of her son's son, as it is said, "Is Ephraim a precious son to Me?");
and on this account all of Israel are called "the remnant of Joseph" (Bereishit Rabbah 71);
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפֹּעַל,
and this matter was openly revealed in actual practice,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מִדּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁמָד, הַרְבֵּה פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְרֵיקִים שֶׁמָּסְרוּ עַצְמָם עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם וְלֹא רָצוּ לְהִתְעָרֵב בַּגּוֹיִם.

as is known from the generation of religious persecution, when numerous Jewish sinners and empty youths sacrificed their lives for the sanctification of the Name rather than assimilate among the gentiles.
וְעַל כֵּן נֵס דְּפוּרִים נִיתַּן לִכְתֹּב,
Therefore the miracle of Purim was permitted to be set down in canonical writing,
וְהוּא סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים, נֶגֶד מִדַּת יְסוֹד וּמַלְכוּת — סִיּוּמָא דְּגוּפָא;
and it stands as the conclusion of all the miracles, corresponding to the attributes of Yesod and Malkhut—the completion of the spiritual body;
וְהוּא הַהֲכָנָה לְנֵס דַּחֲנֻכָּה,
and it serves as the preparation for the miracle of Chanukah,
שֶׁהוּא לְבַדּוֹ מֵהַנִּסִּים שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב שֶׁנִּקְבְּעוּ לְדוֹרוֹת,
which is unique among the miracles not permitted to be written down in being established for all generations,
כִּי הַנִּסִּים שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב אֵין לָהֶם הִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפֹּעַל עֲדַיִן,
for miracles not granted canonical scripture do not yet possess outward, corporeal manifestation,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּקָּבְעוּ לְדוֹרוֹת כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט.
and they cannot be instituted for posterity each on its own.
רַק נֵס חֲנֻכָּה הוּא כְּלָלוּת כָּל הַנִּסִּים דְּעֵת הַגָּלוּת שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנוּ לִכְתֹּב,
Rather, the miracle of Chanukah is the collective inclusion of all the unwritten miracles of the exile era,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ קְבִיעוּת לְדוֹרוֹת רַק בְּהֶאָרַת נֵר,
possessing a permanent observance for future generations exclusively through the kindling of the lamp,
שֶׁהוּא הֶאָרָה זוֹ דְּהִתְגַּלּוּת קְדֻשַּׁת הַיְסוֹד שֶׁבַּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת בַּפֹּעַל מַמָּשׁ,
which represents that illumination revealing the sanctity of Yesod externally in tangible deed,
לִהְיוֹת מֵאִיר גַּם בִּפְנִימִיּוּת, דְּהַיְינוּ בְּכָל מִינֵי עִרְבּוּבִים.
to shine into the innermost dimensions, namely throughout every form of worldly intermixture.
וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בַּפֹּעַל שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And once this intrinsic steadfastness was proven in deed even without the conscious study of Torah,
הוּא הוֹלֵךְ וּמִתְגַּלֶּה בְּכָל פְּרָטֵי הַכֹּחוֹת בְּכָל זְמַן הֶמְשֵׁךְ הַגָּלוּת;
it continues to unfold throughout all specific faculties during the entire course of the exile;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹתֶיהָ,
and this sustained revelation occurs solely through the words of Torah and its commandments,
כִּי "נֵר מִצְוָה וְתוֹרָה אוֹר" שֶׁהֵם הַמְּאִירִים לָאָדָם.
for "the mitzvah is a lamp and the Torah is light," which illuminate a person's path.
וְזֶהוּ יְשׁוּעָה דַּחֲנֻכָּה, שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וּלְקַיֵּם מִצְוֹתֶיהָ;
