And this was the salvation of Chanukah, enabling them to labor in Torah and fulfill its commandments;
וְנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים, שֶׁהֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and it was wrought through the Priests, who are the root of Torah within the children of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ" וְגוֹמֵר,
as it is written: “They shall teach Your laws...” and so forth,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְתוֹרָה יְבַקְשׁוּ מִפִּיהוּ",
and Scripture states: “The lips of the priest shall preserve knowledge, and they shall seek Torah from his mouth,”
שֶׁהַדַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר — דּוֹר דֵּעָה מְקַבְּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה — גְּנִיז בְּפוּמֵיהּ.

for Da'at (divine knowledge)—which was the spiritual level of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and the generation of the wilderness, the "generation of knowledge" who received the Torah—is concealed within his mouth.
שֶׁהַפֶּה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת מַה שֶּׁבַּלֵּב לַזּוּלַת,
For the mouth serves as the revealed conduit conveying that which is in the heart to another,
וְעַל יָדוֹ הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לַזּוּלַת וּלְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
and through it comes the revelation of words of Torah to others and to all who enter the world.

items.h:
Seif 4 — The Chanukah Lamp and the Purification of Mixture
The lamp removes foreign admixture from Israel's desires and clarifies Netzach, Hod, and the concealed holiness of Yesod.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַהֶאָרָה דְּנֵר חֲנֻכָּה שֶׁנִּקְבַּע לְדוֹרוֹת,
And this is the illumination of the Chanukah lamp that was established for all generations,
לְכַלּוֹת עַל יְדֵי אוֹר זֶה כָּל מִינֵי עִרְבּוּבְיָא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
to eliminate through this light every kind of foreign intermixture from Israel,
הַנִּמְשָׁךְ עַל יְדֵי עִרְבּוּב פְּנִימִיּוּת הַכֹּחוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְצוֹנוֹת מְעֹרָבוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם מְבֹרָרִים
which stems from the intermingling of the inner faculties of the children of Israel with mixed desires that are not purified
שֶׁהֵם רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְלֹא לְשׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה וּפְנִיָּה אַחֶרֶת,
so as to be directed solely for the sake of Heaven, free of any alien thought or self-serving motive,
כָּרָאוּי לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲשֶׁר הֵם דְּבוּקִים לְגַמְרֵי בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים.
as befits the essential root of Jewishness belonging to Knesset Yisrael, who are completely cleaved to the living God.
וּבֶאֱמֶת, כָּל כֹּחַ הַיְסוֹד נִמְשָׁךְ רַק מֵהַנֶּצַח וָהוֹד,
And in truth, the entire power of Yesod is drawn solely from Netzach and Hod;
וְאִם הַיְסוֹד מְבֹרָר — גַּם נֶצַח וָהוֹד מְבֹרָרִים.
and if Yesod is clarified and pure, Netzach and Hod are likewise clarified and pure.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵצֶל הַיְסוֹד הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בַּפֹּעַל,
Except that within Yesod this purity is revealed in actual deed,
וְאֵצֶל הַנֶּצַח וָהוֹד הוּא עֲדַיִן בַּכֹּחַ, וְהַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל נֶעְלָם עֲדַיִן.
whereas within Netzach and Hod it remains in potential, and its emergence into actualization is still hidden.
וּמִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לִטְעוֹת וְצָרִיךְ נֵר לְהָאִיר,
And from the perspective of this concealment there is room for error, requiring a lamp to illuminate;
וְעַל כֵּן "לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים פְּסוּלָה, דְּלָא שָׁלְטָא בֵּיהּ עֵינָא", וַעֲדַיִן הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם.
therefore, a lamp placed above twenty cubits is invalid because the eye does not discern it, and it remains in concealment.
וְעִיקַּר נֵר חֲנֻכָּה לְהוֹצִיא מִן הַהֶעְלֵם לַגִּילּוּי;
And the primary purpose of the Chanukah lamp is to bring forth from concealment into revelation;
וּבָזֶה "כָּלְיָא רַגְלָא", הֵם הָרַגְלִין דְּנֶצַח וָהוֹד דְּתַרְמוֹדָאֵי,
and through this "the foot ceases"—referring to the feet of Netzach and Hod of the Tarmodites,
שֶׁהוּא זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה נֶגֶד יְרוּשָׁלַיִם.
which is the unholy counterpart standing opposite Jerusalem.

וְעַל כֵּן הֵם נִפְנוּ עַל בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת ט״ז1288 Yevamot 16b — Why are converts not accepted from Tarmod? R. Yochanan and the elders differed: one said, because of the servants of Solomon, and one said, because of the daughters of Jerusalem. What is that? Rav Yosef and the Rabbis differed, both in the name of Rabbah bar bar Chana: one said twelve thousand men and six thousand archers, and one said twelve thousand men, of whom six thousand were archers. When the gentiles entered the Sanctuary, all of them turned to the silver and the gold, but these turned upon the daughters of Jerusalem, as it is said, "They ravished women in Zion, maidens in the cities of Judah." Rashi: "The servants of Solomon": who married Jewish women on account of their wealth and dwell there [in Tarmod] with the status of gentiles; and he holds that when a gentile or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman the child is a mamzer. "Because of the daughters of Jerusalem": as explained further on — the daughters of Jerusalem at its destruction, when the gentiles came and took them [as wives]. "Archers": those who draw the bow. Tosafos (s.v. "granted, according to the one who says because of the servants of Solomon"): Why need [the Gemara] attribute the reason to mamzerut? It could have said "because of the servants of Solomon" simply because slaves are forbidden to a Jewish woman! One may answer that their owners presumably despaired of them, and there is a view (Gittin 39b) that one who says "I have despaired of so-and-so my slave" need not give him a bill of manumission. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 16b): The same number is found for the escort of the dead (Ketubot 17a), and it is not by chance: a great force is fittingly so numbered, for twelve and six correspond to the twelve diagonal boundaries of the world and to its six sides — the twelve thousand men to the twelve diagonals, and the six thousand archers, who are the mighty men, to the six sides, which are the principal ones. The one who says that of the twelve thousand, six thousand were archers holds that the six sides are included within the twelve diagonal boundaries and are not separate from them; and so befits a great force, which spreads out on every side — corresponding to the diagonals and the sides. עַמּוּד ב׳),
Therefore they turned their lust upon the daughters of Jerusalem, as the Sages said (Yevamot 16b),
וּבָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה עִרְבּוּבְיָא בְּיִחוּסִין דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
and through this an intermixture was introduced into the genealogical lineages of Israel,

הַגּוֹרֶמֶת חֶשְׁכַּת עַיִן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (ס״ב1289 Pesachim 62b — Rami bar Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: From the day the Book of Genealogies was hidden away, the strength of the Sages was sapped and the light of their eyes was dimmed. Rashi: "Their strength was sapped": for the reasons of the Torah that were in it were hidden from them. "Was hidden away": was forgotten. Maharsha: No reason is given for the hiding away of the Book of Genealogies; possibly it was the reason stated in chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 71a), that when the Sages examined the families they came upon danger (Rashi: they would have disqualified powerful men, who would kill them), so that it was fitting to hide it away, and the Sages transmitted [the genealogies] to their students orally, once in seven years — hence "the strength of the Sages was sapped," in having to make it all known orally. "The light of their eyes" is the eye of intellect and of prophecy, and this is how the strength of wisdom was sapped, for without prophecy we do not know the strength of wisdom, which surpasses prophecy. He made it depend on lineage because prophecy rests only on those of pure lineage in Israel. עַמּוּד ב׳):
which causes darkness of the eyes, as they said in Pesachim 62b:
דְּמִשֶּׁנִּגְנַז סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין חָשְׁכוּ עֵינֵיהֶם,
that from the time the Book of Genealogies was hidden their eyes grew dark,
הַיְינוּ הָאוֹר רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַמֵּאִיר אֶת הָעֵינַיִם;
meaning the light of the Holy Spirit that illuminates the eyes;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב1290 Kiddushin 70b — R. Chama son of R. Chanina said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, causes His Presence to rest, He causes it to rest only upon families of unflawed lineage in Israel, as it is stated: "At that time, says the Lord, will I be the God of all the families of Israel" (Jeremiah 31:1). It does not say "of all Israel," but "of all the families." Rashi (s.v. "the families of Israel"): Families that are wholly of Israel. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): He could have adduced this from the Torah's own verse, "to be a God to you and to your seed after you" — "to your seed," that is, of unflawed lineage after you — to show that the Divine Presence rests only upon families of unflawed lineage in Israel. He cites the verse here instead because it is plainer in its simple sense, since the word "families" itself denotes lineage of seed. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Kiddushin 70b): The Divine Presence rests only upon those who are separated from forbidden relations, and wherever there is licentiousness it does not rest; therefore it rests only upon families of unflawed lineage, who were born in holiness and did not come from a forbidden union. There is a further reason, and it is the principal one: He causes His Presence to rest upon those who derive from Him in an unbroken chain, whereas those born of a disqualified union are not said to derive from His holiness — they were born in disqualification and are strangers, and therefore He does not cause His Presence to rest upon them. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:112): When [Tadmor, whose people became mamzerim,] is destroyed and the matter of disqualified lineage is wholly abolished from the world, there will be a festival, for a festival means the complete union between Israel and their Father in Heaven; and the Sages said, "the Shechinah rests only upon families of unflawed lineage." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Therefore prophecy departed then and the Shechinah did not rest in the Second Temple, for this [intermixing] causes the Shechinah's departure, as it says, "the Shechinah rests only upon families of unflawed lineage in Israel" — and the essence of lineage is that they not intermingle. This was the whole occupation of Ezra, who separated the foreign wives and thereby merited to compose the book of lineage, Chronicles, and made Babylonia like fine flour; and so Elijah will come to establish the lineage of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 7): The service depends on lineage, which is why the priests, the most select in lineage, perform it; and Aaron, chosen from among the chosen, is of unflawed lineage, and therefore it is said of him "Your Tummim and Your Urim" — the resting of the holy spirit — as the Sages said, "the Shechinah rests only upon families of unflawed lineage."׳): דְּאֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת.
and as they said (Kiddushin 70b): the Shechinah rests only upon families of unblemished lineage.
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם אֵין נְבִיאִים — בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים, לְכַוֵּן גַּם בְּהֶעְלֵם לָאֱמֶת, וְזֶהוּ רַק הַמְיוּחָסִים.
And all of Israel, if they are not prophets, are the sons of prophets, able to orient themselves to truth even in concealment, and this capacity belongs specifically to the lineage-pure.
וְגַם בְּפוּרִים "לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה",
And on Purim as well, "the Jews had light,"
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה אָז לְפִי שָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ חָזַר וְנֶעְלַם;
save that it was only temporary for that hour, and afterward retreated and became concealed again;
כִּי עִיקַּר הַפּוּרִים הוּא "עַד דְּלָא יָדַע", וּבְהֶעְדֵּר "אוֹרָה — זוֹ תּוֹרָה".
for the essence of Purim is "until one does not know," characterized by the absence of "light—this is Torah."
אֲבָל בַּחֲנֻכָּה, עִיקַּר זֵכֶר הַנֵּס הוּא עַל יְדֵי הָאוֹר הַנִּשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ לְדוֹרוֹת,
However, on Chanukah, the primary commemoration of the miracle is through the light that remains fixed for all generations,
לְהָאִיר בַּמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלוֹת,
to shine into the dark alleyways,
לָדַעַת כִּי "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ" עִרְבּוּבְיָא דְּ"אֵל נֵכָר".
to know that "Hashem alone shall guide him, and there is no" mixture of an "alien god" with Him.
וְזֶהוּ כְּסֻכָּה וּכְמָבוֹי:
And this is parallel to the laws of Sukkah and Mavoi (an alleyway):
דִּבְסֻכָּה נֶאֱמַר: "כָּל הָאֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל",
for regarding the Sukkah it is written: "All citizens in Israel shall dwell in booths,"
וְנֶאֱמַר: "זֹאת" וְגוֹמֵר "וְחַטַּאת כָּל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲלוּ לָחֹג אֶת חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת";
and it is written: "This shall be..." and so forth, "and the punishment of all nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Sukkot";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳), דְּהַנִּסָּיוֹן יִהְיֶה בְּמִצְוַת סֻכָּה,
and as the Sages taught at the beginning of Avodah Zarah (3a), the ultimate eschatological trial will be through the mitzvah of Sukkah,
דְּזֶה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹשְׁבִים בִּמְחִיצָה לְבַדָּם תַּחַת "צִלָּא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא".
for this belongs solely to Israel, who dwell in a partitioned domain alone under the "shade of faith."
וְכֵן מָבוֹי הוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה מְחִיצָה לְבַדּוֹ, וּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד — יְחִידוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
Likewise, the enclosing of an alleyway establishes a partition of its own, turning it into a private domain (reshut hayachid)—the realm of the Singular One of the universe,
וְלֹא רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מִסִּטְרָא דְּפֵירוּדָא,
and not a public domain (reshut harabbim), which stems from the side of fragmentation,
כְּעֵשָׂו שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ "נְפָשׁוֹת" רַבִּים,
like Esau, regarding whom Scripture writes "souls" in the plural,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֵּית יַעֲקֹב "נֶפֶשׁ" לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד, שֶׁהַכֹּל רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד.
unlike the House of Jacob who are described as "soul" in the singular, for everything forms a unified private domain.
וּבִשְׁנֵיהֶם פָּסוּל לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים, דְּלֵיכָּא הֶיכֵּירָא,
And in both of them an enclosure higher than twenty cubits is invalid because there is no visual recognition;
כִּי מְחִיצָה הַמְגַדֶּרֶת בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים צְרִיכָא הֶיכֵּירָא שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה עִרְבּוּבְיָא,
for the partition that creates a boundary between Israel and the nations requires clear recognition so that there be no intermingling;
וְכֵן לְנֵר חֲנֻכָּה.
and so it is with the Chanukah lamp.
וְזֶהוּ בֵּירוּר הַנֶּצַח וָהוֹד בְּאוֹר נִיכָּר,
And this is the clarification of Netzach and Hod through a clearly discernible light,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא הַיְסוֹד מְבֹרָר גַּם בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם,
and through this Yesod is automatically clarified even in absolute concealment,
שֶׁ"הַבּוֹר רֵק" וְכוּלֵי "אֲבָל" וְכוּלֵי,
where "the pit was empty..." and so forth, "however..." and so forth,
עִם כָּל זֶה הוּא בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עוֹמֵד.
and nevertheless he remains standing in his pristine sanctity.

sections.en: Purim, Adar, and Holiness within Concealment

items.h: Purim reveals that Israel's holiness persists precisely within hiddenness, overturning Haman's lot and exposing the covenant, peace, and divine light concealed within exile.

Seif 1 — Why Purim Is Named for the Persian Lot
The foreign name Pur reveals divine light emerging from Persian darkness for Israel while remaining concealed from the nations.

p: עִנְיַן קְרִיאַת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים עַל שֵׁם הַפּוּר וְהוּא הַגּוֹרָל,
The matter of naming the days of Purim after the "Pur," which is the lot,
אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹן פַּרְסִי נִקְרָא "פּוּר",
except that in the Persian language it is called "pur,"
וְהֻצְרַךְ הַכָּתוּב לִזְכּוֹר שְׁמוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן פַּרְסִי וּלְתַרְגְּמוֹ לִלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
and Scripture had to mention its name in the Persian tongue and translate it into the Holy Tongue,
לְפִי שֶׁהַיָּמִים קָרְאוּ כְּשֵׁם הַפַּרְסִי, שֶׁכְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הָיָה נִקְרָא כֵּן בְּפִי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָז.
because they named the days by the Persian name, as it apparently was called by the children of Israel at that time.

וְזֶה טַעַם "עַל כֵּן קָרְאוּ" וְגוֹמֵר1291 Esther 9:26 — “Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of the pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this matter and what had befallen them…” Rashi: "Therefore, because of all the words of this letter" — these days were established, and the letter was written so that the coming generations should know. "And what they had seen" refers to those who did these deeds; "and what had befallen them" — what Ahasuerus saw that he used the vessels of the Sanctuary and what befell them for it, and what Haman saw that he grew jealous of Mordecai and what befell him, that they hanged him and his sons. Malbim: The name "Purim" that they gave these days was after the "lot," to be a memorial of the force of the miracle: Haman's lot was overturned into our own, for the constellation then stood against Israel and was overturned by the providence of the Lord, who overrules the ordered powers. "Therefore" also refers forward — because of all the words of this letter, which told them the whole matter in detail and how the miracle stood at its full strength even on that day, they came to know "what they had seen concerning this.", וְלֹא פֵּירֵשׁ מִי,
And this is the reason Scripture says "Therefore they called..." and so forth, without specifying who,
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הֲמוֹן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קָרְאוּ כֵן, שֶׁכָּךְ הוּא מְפֻרְסָם שֵׁם יָמִים הַלָּלוּ אָז.
meaning that the common masses of Israel called them so, as that was the publicized name of these days then.
כִּי הַפּוּר הוּא שֶׁגָּרַם לְיָמִים אֵלּוּ,
For the pur was the catalyst that brought about these days;
כִּי לוּלֵי נָפַל לְהָמָן הַפּוּר עַל חֹדֶשׁ זֶה שֶׁבּוֹ יַצְלִיחַ, לֹא הָיָה מַתְחִיל לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלוּם.
for had the lot not fallen for Haman upon this month as the one in which he would succeed, he would not have begun to do anything.

וְהִנֵּה הַגּוֹרָל אֵינוֹ מִקְרֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמֵה' כָּל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ1292 Proverbs 16:33 — “The lot is cast into the lap, but its every judgment is from the Lord.” Rashi: "The lot is cast into the lap" — a man casts the lot privately, by himself. "But its every judgment is from the Lord" — to select for each and every one his portion. Metzudas Dovid: Those who cast lots place the slips in the lap or in some other hidden place and draw them out to assign the portions. Scripture says: do not question the lot and say that it came by chance, for while the slips were still cast into the lap, before they were drawn out, the judgment of the matter had already been decreed by the Lord, and each man received the portion God above apportioned to him. Malbim: There are matters that appear to be left to chance and are in fact governed by Providence, for where human choice and effort break off the eye of Providence appears — as when a matter is in doubt between two men and they cast a lot to learn to whom the disputed share belongs. Though the lot is cast in the lap, hidden from the human eye and given over to chance, the eye of the Lord's providence rests upon it, and the verdict the lot yields is no accident but "from the Lord" — as with the division of the land, where the lot fell by His providence.", כִּי הַכֹּל הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
And behold, the casting of lots is not chance, as it is written: "and its entire judgment is from Hashem," for everything is governed by the blessed Hashem;
וְכָל הָאֻמּוֹת גַּם כֵּן הֶאֱמִינוּ בְּגוֹרָלוֹת,
and all the nations likewise believed in lots,
אֶלָּא שֶׁ"כָּל הָעַמִּים יֵלְכוּ אִישׁ בְּשֵׁם אֱלֹהָיו" —
except that "all the peoples walk each in the name of its god" —
הֵם שָׂרֵי הָאֻמּוֹת הַמַּנְהִיגִים אוֹתָם, שֶׁכָּל פְּעֻלּוֹתֵיהֶם נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהֶם.
namely the celestial princes of the nations who lead them, from whom all their operations derive.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהֵם רַק לְשָׁעָה, כָּךְ כָּל פְּעֻלָּתָם,
And just as these princes have only a temporary existence, so is all their activity;
וְכֵן הוֹרָאַת גּוֹרְלוֹתֵיהֶם הוּא כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהָעִנְיָן לְשָׁעָה,
and likewise the indication of their lots reflects only the transient, temporal state of the matter,
וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָעִנְיָן בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ,
and not how the matter stands in its absolute, ultimate truth,
כְּגוֹרְלוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הֵם מוֹרִים הָאֱמֶת הַקַּיָּים לָעַד,
unlike the lots of the children of Israel, which stem from the blessed Hashem and indicate the truth that endures forever,
כְּחֲלוּקַּת הָאָרֶץ בְּגוֹרָל שֶׁהוּא חֶלְקוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
such as the division of the Land by lot, which established each tribe's portion and inheritance for all eternity.
אֲבָל גּוֹרַל הָמָן, אַף דְּגַם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה דָּבָר רֵיק,
However, Haman's lot, although it too was not an empty occurrence,
הוֹרָאָתוֹ הָיָה רַק כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן לְשָׁעָה,
its indication was solely according to what appeared outwardly for that temporary moment,
וּכְפִי מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ כֵּן הוּא,
and according to the imaginary thought where they presumed it to be so,
שֶׁהֵם מוּכָנִים, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לְיוֹם הֲרִיגָה לְאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ.
that Israel was destined, God forbid, for a day of slaughter in that month.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ "נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא",
Yet in absolute truth "the opposite occurred,"
כִּי הַאי עָלְמָא שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַדִּמְיוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּשׁוּב" וְגוֹמֵר "הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים",
for this world is the world of imagination, as it is written: "When Hashem returns..." and so forth, "we were like dreamers,"
נִקְרָא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא" שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת;
and is called the "world of falsehood," which is the antithesis of truth;
וְכָל שְׁלִיטַת הַשָּׂרִים וְעִנְיָנֵיהֶם הוּא רַק בְּהַאי עָלְמָא, הַמַּרְאֶה הַכֹּל דִּמְיוֹן הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת,
and the entire dominion of the celestial princes and their affairs is confined to this world, which displays everything as an illusion opposite the truth,
וְכֵן כָּל הוֹרָאוֹתֵיהֶם.
and so are all their prophetic indications.
כִּי כָּל הַשָּׂגָתָם הוּא כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן, וַהֲרֵי בַּדִּמְיוֹן פָּעַל הָמָן גְּזֵרָה רָעָה.
For all their perception is aligned with imagination, and indeed within the realm of imagination Haman effected an evil decree.
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הֵם זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה,
And it is known that they correspond one opposite the other:
הַקְּלִיפָּה וְהַחִיצוֹנִיּוּת מַלְבֶּשֶׁת אֶת הַפְּנִימִיּוּת וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה אֵיבָר נֶגֶד אֵיבָר,
the shell and the exterior clothe the inner essence and the holiness, limb corresponding to limb,
וּבְכָל עִנְיָן דִּמְיוֹן הָאֱמֶת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגּוֹיִם הוּא גַּם כֵּן דֻּגְמָתָן, רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ.
and in every matter the reflection of Israel's truth among the nations is likewise structured after it, only in inverted form.
וְעַל כֵּן כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת הָיָה גַּם כֵּן אוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן דְּהָרֹג וְאַבֵּד וּבֵין יְהוּדִים וְגוֹיִם,
Therefore, according to the truth there was likewise that very same dynamic of slaying and destroying between Jews and gentiles,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה נֶהְפָּךְ מֵהוֹרָאַת הַדִּמְיוֹן;
except that it was completely reversed from the indication of the imagination;
וְלָכֵן הַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יָבִינוּ הָאֱמֶת מִתּוֹךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן.
and therefore the wise will discern the inner truth through the outer illusion.
וְזֶה טַעַם "פּוּר הוּא הַגּוֹרָל",
And this is the meaning of "the Pur, that is the lot":
כִּי "פּוּר" הַפַּרְסִי וְשֶׁל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נְפִילָתוֹ הוּא כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן,
for the Persian "pur" of the nations falls according to illusion,
וּמְבָרֵר רַק אֵיךְ הַדָּבָר מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁל שָׁעָה,
clarifying only how the matter appears from the vantage point of temporal imagination;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַגּוֹרָל שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא הַמּוֹדִיעַ הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ.
nevertheless, it is identical to the "goral" in the Holy Tongue, which announces the absolute, ultimate truth.
וַהֲמוֹן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם אֵינָם נְבִיאִים — בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים הֵם,
And the common masses of Israel, if they are not prophets, are the sons of prophets;
קָרְאוּ לַיָּמִים עַל שֵׁם הַפּוּר וְהוֹרָאָתוֹ הַדִּמְיוֹן,
they named the festival after the "pur" and its imaginary manifestation,
כִּי זֶה כָּל קְדֻשַּׁת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים,
for this constitutes the entire sanctity of the days of Purim:
לְבָרֵר הָאֱמֶת הַגָּנוּז וְנֶעְלָם תּוֹךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן,
to clarify the truth concealed and hidden within the illusion,
עַד שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹן שָׁב לִהְיוֹת כְּלִי לְהָאֱמֶת שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ וְנִטְפָּל אֵלָיו.
until the illusion itself is transformed into a vessel for the truth within it and becomes subordinate to it.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּנֵס דְּפוּרִים,
And as it occurred in the miracle of Purim,
הַהֲרִיגָה בָּאוֹיְבִים הָיָה רַק עַל יְדֵי גְּזֵרַת הָמָן לִהְיוֹת הַיְּהוּדִים עֲתִידִים לַיּוֹם הַזֶּה,
the slaughter of the enemies was made possible solely by Haman's decree that the Jews should be prepared for that day,
הֻכְרְחוּ לַהֲפֹךְ הַדָּבָר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲתִידִים לַהֲרֹג בָּאוֹיְבִים.
whereby they were forced to reverse the matter so that they would be prepared to strike down their enemies.
וְנִמְצָא הַדִּמְיוֹן הוּא הוּא הַגּוֹרֵם הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת,
Thus the illusion itself was the very instrument that produced the salvation with even greater power,
וְעַל כֵּן הֻכְרַח לִהְיוֹת הַדִּמְיוֹן גַּם כֵּן לְצוֹרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ,
and therefore the illusion was necessarily designed for the sake of the subsequent truth,
וְנִמְצָא גַּם הַדִּמְיוֹן הוּא מִכְּלַל הַנֵּס וְהַיְשׁוּעָה שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ, כִּי הָיָה רַק לְצוֹרֶךְ יְשׁוּעָה.
meaning that the initial illusion was itself part of the miracle and salvation that followed, since it existed solely for the sake of salvation.
וְעַל כֵּן "חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי",
Therefore "one is obligated to become intoxicated,"
כִּי הַשִּׁכּוֹר הוּא מָלֵא דִּמְיוֹן וְאֵין לוֹ מַחְשֶׁבֶת אֱמֶת כְּלָל,
for the intoxicated person is filled with illusion and lacks rational thought entirely,
אֲבָל אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם הַדִּמְיוֹן הוּא אֱמֶת.
yet among the children of Israel even the illusion turns into truth.
וְעַל כֵּן קָרְאוּ לַיָּמִים "פּוּרִים",
Therefore they named the days "Purim,"
לְהוֹרוֹת כִּי הַפּוּר הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַגּוֹרָל וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל הַנֵּס.
to demonstrate that the pur is itself the divine lot and is likewise included in the miracle.

וְעַל כֵּן הַמְּגִלָּה מַתְחֶלֶת בְּאוֹת וָא"ו וּמְסַיֶּמֶת בְּוָא"ו, שֶׁהוּא אוֹת אֱמֶת כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא1293 Zohar 3:2a — "Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God" (Isaiah 7:11) — an actual letter, for they all drew upon the mystery of the letters. And so with Rahab, what is written? "And give me a true sign" (Joshua 2:12) — this is the letter vav, for this is the one called the letter of truth. And should you say that the other letters are not truth — they are; but this letter in particular is called the letter of truth.);
And therefore the Megillah opens with the letter vav and concludes with the letter vav, which is the letter of truth, as is known from the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Vayikra);
וְהוּא מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת,
and it represents the attribute of truth belonging to Jacob, whose entire progeny is a seed of truth;
דְּזֶהוּ מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת, כַּאֲשֶׁר כֻּלּוֹ כָּךְ, מַבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה וְאֵין בּוֹ דָּבָר מִלְּבַר,
for this is the essence of truth: when the whole reality is so, running from end to end without any alien element outside of it,
כִּי "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד".
for "the lip of truth shall be established forever."
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נֶהְפַּךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן אֱמֶת,
And when the illusion is transformed to become truth as well,
זֶהוּ שְׁלֵמוּת אוֹת אֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה.
this is the ultimate perfection of the letter of truth, which is the central bar traversing from one extreme to the other.
וּתְחִלָּתוֹ "וַיְהִי", שֶׁהוּא מוֹרֶה צָרָה,
And its opening word is "Vayehi," which denotes distress,

כְּמִדָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים: תְּחִלָּתָן יִסּוּרִין וְסוֹפָן שַׁלְוָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ו1294 Bereshit Rabbah 66:4 — R. Yitzchak bar R. Chiya said: The wicked, because they begin in tranquility and end in suffering, open with blessing and close with curse — "Blessed be those who bless you and cursed be those who curse you." The righteous, because they begin in suffering and end in tranquility, open with curse and close with blessing — "Cursed be those who curse you and blessed be those who bless you." Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 170): This is the meaning of "The righteous — their beginning is suffering and their end is tranquility": in every matter, every good trait and good undertaking, the first entry into it comes with pain, as "all beginnings are hard." For this world is mostly evil, so whatever a person is aroused to, he first sees the evil force within it and is pained, and through the pain he sweetens it, and at once its end is tranquility. Beis Yaakov (Miketz 18): Joseph understood that Pharaoh had first seen good and then bad, for Pharaoh was of the wicked, whose order is "their beginning is tranquility and their end is suffering": the wicked spread themselves out in this world like the primordial worlds that were destroyed, upon which the Blessed One bestowed such abundant kindness that they imagined they had power of their own and did not accept His kingship, and so they perished entirely. But with Israel the good shines forth little by little, for His conduct with them is like the creation of the world, "first darkness and then light," and thereby they have the power to gather the wayward and wild forces in man into holiness.);
in the manner of the righteous: their beginning is suffering and their end is tranquility (Bereishit Rabbah 66);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּסּוּרִין הַקּוֹדְמִין גַּם כֵּן הַשַּׁלְוָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, וְהֵם הַהֲכָנָה לַשַּׁלְוָה שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ.
and through the preceding afflictions the tranquility becomes even greater, as they serve as the preparation for the subsequent peace.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם זֶה מַתְחִיל בְּאוֹת אֱמֶת,
Therefore this too begins with the letter of truth,
וְהוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה וְקָפְצוּ עָלָיו הַיִּסּוּרִין,
and this is the quality of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who sought to dwell in tranquility and upon whom afflictions sprang;
לֹא לְנַגֵּד לִרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל הַיְשִׁיבָה בְּשַׁלְוָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה,
which occurred not to thwart his desire to dwell in peace through this,
כִּי כָּל רְצוֹנוֹתָיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וּ"רְצוֹן יְרֵאָיו יַעֲשֶׂה",
for all his desires were for the sake of Heaven, and "He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him",
רַק לְמַלֹּאות רְצוֹנוֹ וּמְבוּקָשׁוֹ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה.
but rather to fulfill his will and quest to dwell in true peace.

וְהַשַּׁלְוָה שֶׁלּוֹ הַיְינוּ חַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וּבְיֵצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁזָּכָה לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה1295 Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 5 — A measure of life without pain and without the evil inclination is given to the righteous in this world, a foretaste of the world to come; and these are they: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Jabez and Jethro, and their like. And why did Jacob merit such life in this world, of what the Holy One, blessed be He, will give the righteous in time to come? Because he sat in the study house from his childhood to his old age. Jacob our father was in well-being the seventeen years he was in Egypt, and the Holy One, blessed be He, reckoned it for him as though all his days had been in well-being, as it is stated: “And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.” Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 19): As the Sages said in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah on the verse "And Jacob lived" that he merited life without pain and without the evil inclination: not for nothing had Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility, nor did he ask for something that was not his — only its time had not yet come; in the end he did merit to dwell in tranquility, when he saw that his bed was whole, and he did not die at all. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): [Once Joseph rose to rule,] Jacob merited the dwelling in tranquility that he had first sought, in those seventeen years in Egypt, which were life without pain and without the evil inclination, as they said in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah; for the strength of the holiness within him was clarified also through his offspring, by the righteousness of Joseph, in whom, even in the place of "the nakedness of the land," the flame from his father's house — "the house of Jacob, a fire" — was not dimmed.׳);
And his peace meant a life without sorrow and without the evil inclination, which he merited, as written in Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 5);
וְהַיְינוּ בְּאוֹתָם שָׁנִים שֶׁיָּשַׁב בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עֲלֵיהֶם "וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב", שֶׁאָז הָיָה לוֹ שְׁלֵמוּת הַחַיּוּת.
namely during those years he dwelt in Egypt, concerning which it says "And Jacob lived," for then he possessed the fullness of vitality.
וְלַעֲשׂוֹת מְבוּקָשׁוֹ קָפַץ עָלָיו רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לְמִצְרַיִם.
And in order to realize his ultimate quest, the turmoil of Joseph sprang upon him, through which he arrived in Egypt.
וְסוֹפוֹ מְסַיֶּמֶת בְּ"זַרְעוֹ", לִזְכּוֹת לְזֶרַע אֱמֶת גַּם כֵּן;
And the end of the Megillah concludes with the word "zar'o" (his seed), to merit a seed of truth as well;
כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי, כִּי עַל יְדֵי מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק, שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ לְאַבֵּד כָּל זֵכֶר לָמוֹ,
as I have heard, that through the obliteration of Amalek, whose commandment is to erase all memory of them,
אָז בְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה", כְּשֶׁזֶּה נוֹפֵל זֶה קָם, נִתְוַסֵּף רִבּוּי בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
then in the principle of "one opposite the other," when this one falls that one rises, an increase is added to the souls of Israel,
וְזוֹכֶה לְזֶרַע מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לַהּ.
and whoever requires children merits offspring.

וּלְדַעְתִּי נִרְמַז זֶה בְּסִיּוּם הַמְּגִלָּה בְּמִלַּת "זַרְעוֹ1296 Esther 10:3 — “For Mordechai the Jew was second to King Achashverosh, and great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brethren — seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all their seed.” Rashi: "To the multitude of his brethren" — and not to all his brethren: this teaches that some of the Sanhedrin separated from him, because he had drawn close to the kingship and was neglecting his study. "To all his seed" refers back to "his people": to all the seed of his people. Malbim: Although he was viceroy over the whole kingdom and set in authority over the Jews in particular, he was still "acceptable to the multitude of his brethren," for in all his affairs he was "seeking the good of his people." He did not conduct himself toward them with force and a strong hand, but in peace and uprightness.",
And in my opinion, this is alluded to at the conclusion of the Megillah in the word "zar'o";
כִּי לְעוֹלָם הַמִּלָּה שֶׁבַּהַתְחָלָה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַדָּבָר מִצַּד הַהַתְחָלָה,
for always the word at the opening reveals the root of the matter from its start,
וְהַמִּלָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ סוֹף וְתַכְלִית הַמְּכֻוָּן בְּדָבָר זֶה.
while the concluding word reveals the root, conclusion, and ultimate purpose of that matter.
וְהַמְּכֻוָּן בִּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם;
And the intended purpose of wiping out Amalek is that the Divine Name become whole;
וְנוֹדַע כִּי שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁם הֵם הָאָבוֹת, וַאֲחֲרוֹנוֹת הֵם הַצֶּאֱצָאִים.
and it is known that the first two letters of the Name (Yud-Kei) correspond to the fathers, while the latter two (Vav-Kei) correspond to the offspring.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם הוּא שֶׁהָאָבוֹת זוֹכִים לִרְאוֹת צֶאֱצָאִים סְמוּכִים לָהֶם
And when the Name is whole, the parents merit to see offspring close beside them

[וְעַיֵּין זֹהַר פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳, עַיֵּין שָׁם1297 Zohar, Vayikra 7a — And when is a man called whole, after the pattern of above? At the hour when he is joined with his partner in oneness.],
and see Zohar, Parashat Vayikra 7a; examine it there,
וְזוֹכִין לָזֶה בִּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק.
and one merits this through the eradication of Amalek.
וְעַל כֵּן אֲדָר מַזָּלוֹ דָּגִים, הָרוֹמֵז עַל "וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב";
Therefore the zodiac sign of Adar is Pisces (fish), which hints at "and let them multiply like fish in the midst of the earth";
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי, כִּי חֹדֶשׁ זֶה מְסֻגָּל לְהוֹלִיד בּוֹ יוֹתֵר מִבִּשְׁאָר חֳדָשִׁים,
and likewise I heard that this month is especially propitious for childbearing more than other months,

עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ח1298 Rosh Hashanah 8a — R. Yochanan said: Both of them expounded the same verse, as it is stated: "The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are covered over with grain; they shout for joy, they also sing" (Psalms 65:14). R. Meir holds: When are the meadows clothed with flocks? At the time when the valleys are covered over with grain. And when are the valleys covered over with grain? In Adar. They conceive in Adar and give birth in Av, and so their New Year is Elul. Rashi: "The meadows are clothed with flocks" is a verse in Psalms: the ewes are "clothed", that is, they conceive; "the valleys are covered over with grain": the sown seed sprouts and is plainly visible; "they shout for joy, they also sing": in Nisan, when harvest time comes and the grain stands on its stalks, the wind blows and they knock against one another, and a sound is heard, so that they seem to be singing. The gestation of small cattle is five months; and "their New Year is Elul" because the division between their new and old [animals] at the renewal of the year falls close to the completion [of their births]. Tosafos (s.v. "the meadows are clothed with flocks"): The Targum renders it "the rams mount the flocks", which is a euphemism [for mating]. Rashi explains it in this way below (11a), on R. Yehoshua's statement that the world was created in Nisan, where it is said that that season is the time when cattle and beasts mate with one another; but here he did not explain it so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): This month corresponds to the power of desire, and its sign is the fish — "let them multiply like fish" — in which lies the power of increase, for the power of "be fruitful and multiply" was first stated of the fish. And it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar," and Israel are likened to a flock, for they too are exceedingly fruitful and multiply. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The month of Adar, whose sign is the fish, corresponds to Joseph, whose blessing is "let them multiply like fish," for in it lies the power of fruitfulness of that blessing, which is in Adar — as it says in Rosh Hashanah, "the flocks conceive in Adar," and Israel are everywhere likened to a flock. It is called Adar from adir, "mighty," denoting strength and might, whose essence is the subduing of the inclination. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 5): Therefore it says in Rosh Hashanah, "When are the meadows clothed with flocks? In Adar; they conceive in Adar" — Israel are likened to a flock, and that is the time of their increase. I have received that this month is therefore auspicious for barren men and women to be remembered, because it is designated for the eradication of Amalek, and every withholding of childbirth among the seed of Israel comes only from the accusation of Amalek.׳ עַמּוּד א׳): בְּצֹאן מִתְעַבְּרוֹת בַּאֲדָר, וְכֵן בְּצֹאן יִשְׂרָאֵל.
based on what they taught in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (8a): sheep conceive in Adar, and so it is with the flock of Israel.
וְעַל יְדֵי הָרִבּוּי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֵּילָא בָּא הַמִּעוּט לְזֶרַע עֲמָלֵק,
And through the multiplication of Israel, the diminishment of the seed of Amalek automatically follows,
דִּכְשֶׁזֶּה קָם זֶה נוֹפֵל;
for when one rises, the other falls;
וְעַל כֵּן חֹדֶשׁ זֶה מְסֻגָּל לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק וּלְאַבֵּד כָּל זֵכֶר לָמוֹ.
and therefore this month is auspicious for wiping out Amalek and erasing all remembrance of them.
וְהָמָן חָשַׁב אַדְּרַבָּה לְהֵיפֶךְ: כִּי אָז יֹאבַד, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כָּל זֵכֶר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
And Haman thought, on the contrary, the exact opposite: that then, God forbid, every remembrance of Israel would be lost,
מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ הַמַּרְאֶה לוֹ כֵּן;
from the power of his illusion that displayed this to him;
וְדִמְיוֹן זֶה גָּרַם אַדְּרַבָּה לְרִבּוּי,
yet this very illusion, on the contrary, brought about multiplication,

עַל דֶּרֶךְ "כַּאֲשֶׁר יְעַנּוּ אֹתוֹ", וְחָשְׁבוּ לְמַעֲטָם, "כֵּן יִרְבֶּה" וְגוֹמֵר1299 Exodus 1:12 — “But as they afflicted them, so did they increase and so did they spread out; and they were disgusted because of the Children of Israel.” Rashi: "And as they afflicted them" — in whatever measure they set their heart to afflict, so the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, was set to multiply them and spread them out; "so they multiplied" means so they did multiply and so they did spread. "And they were disgusted" — they loathed their own lives; and our Rabbis expounded that [the Israelites] were like thorns in their eyes..
in the manner of "As they afflicted them"—and thought to diminish them—"so they multiplied" and so forth.
כִּי כֵן הוּא מִדַּת הָרִבּוּי שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
For such is the nature of Israel's increase:
לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ דַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּמְיוֹן הַמַּרְאֶה הֵיפֶךְ מִקּוֹדֶם.
to be drawn down specifically through the illusion that shows the opposite beforehand.

כְּמוֹ צוּר חֻצָּבוּ, אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּאָמַר לוֹ: "צֵא מֵאִצְטַגְנִינוּת שֶׁלְּךָ" וְכוּלֵי1300 Shabbat 156a — Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: From where do we know that there is no constellation governing Israel? For it is said, “And He brought him outside.” Avraham said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the Universe, the steward of my house shall inherit me. He said to him: No — but one who shall issue from your own body. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, I have looked into my astrology and I am not fit to father a son. He said to him: Go out from your astrology, for there is no constellation governing Israel. Rashi: "Astrology" — the science of the constellations. "Go out from your astrology" — this is what is written, "And He brought him outside": outside his astrology. Maharsha: According to its plain sense, He brought him out of his tent to see the stars, as Rashi explains on the Torah; but this is difficult, for since he saw the stars in a vision, there was no need to write that He brought him outside to show him the stars, as in a vision He could show them to him inside his tent as well. Therefore they expounded that He brought him outside his astrology, in which he had looked [and found] that he was not fit to father a son. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 156a): When he says there is no constellation for Israel because it is written of Avraham, "And He brought him outside," this does not mean that there is no constellation for Israel at all; rather, Avraham's stature was above the constellations — "And He brought him outside," that is, his stature is over the constellations [and even so, it is impossible that the constellation should not act on him]. The upshot is that when Israel are in the truth of their stature and sin does not accuse, as was Avraham, the Holy One, blessed be He, performs a miracle for them as He did for Avraham, turning back the constellation so that it does no harm to Israel. (שַׁבָּת קנ״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳),
Just like the rock from which they were hewn, our father Abraham, peace be upon him, to whom Hashem said: "Go forth from your astrology..." and so forth (Shabbat 156b),
וְהוּא הוֹרָאַת הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם,
which was the indication of illusion beneath the heavens,
דְּכָל הוֹרָאַת הָאִצְטַגְנִינוּת הוּא מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם.
for every astrological forecast belongs to the realm of this world's illusion beneath the heavens.
וְכָל עֵסֶק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּבִנְיַן אֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
And the entire spiritual labor of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, and the construction of the Jewish nation
הוּא לָצֵאת מֵהַדִּמְיוֹן,
is to transcend illusion,
שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַבְלֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁתַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, דְּהַכֹּל הֶבֶל וְדִמְיוֹן וְרַק עַד אַרְגִּיעָה.
which comprises all the vanities of this world under the sun, where all is vanity, illusion, and only fleeting.
וְשֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְבַקֵּשׁ "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר תִּכּוֹן לָעַד";
And the root of Israel is to seek "the lip of truth that shall be established forever";
וְדָבָר זֶה נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and this matter is concealed in this world,

שֶׁכָּךְ הָיָה בְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא" (שָׁם ע״ז1301 Shabbat 77b — R. Zeira found Rav Yehuda standing at the door of his father-in-law's house, and saw that he was in a cheerful frame of mind, such that had he asked him about anything in the world he would have told him. He said to him: Why do the goats walk at the head of the flock and the ewes after them? He said to him: It is as in the creation of the world — first darkness and afterward light. Rashi: "All the hollows of the world": that is, the things that happen throughout the space of the world. "First darkness": goats are generally black, and ewes generally white. Maharsha: Although the natural philosophers gave reasons for how each thing is formed, and the Talmud too has a few such ("why is the whole ear hard and the lobe soft"), these reasons are forced in their plain sense, so they must be meant as a parable on matters of Torah: Greece is likened to a goat ("and the he-goat grew exceedingly great", Daniel 8:8) and Israel to a sheep ("Israel is a scattered sheep", Jeremiah 50:17), and he asked why in the Second Temple the goats — the kings of Greece, Alexander of Macedon and those after him — reigned first, and only afterward the sheep, the kings of Israel. He answered that this was already alluded to in the creation of the world: first darkness — "and darkness was upon the face of the deep", which Bereshit Rabbah expounds of Greece, who darkened Israel's eyes — and afterward light, the Hasmonean kingdom, who came to reign through the miracle of the Chanukah lights. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 77b): The goats derive from the power of the attribute of judgment, which is the attribute of night; and night came before day because the attribute of judgment, by the very strength of that attribute, hastens to go forth into actuality. So too the goats walk at the head of the flock because of the swiftness of action they receive from the attribute of judgment — and this is what he answered him: as at the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvos 1): With respect to night, which is darkness, cessation and darkness come before day, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness...": for one who stands in darkness, darkness comes first and afterward light, and so there were two thousand years of chaos and afterward two thousand of Torah. But for one who stands in the day, day comes first and afterward night, to rest from his toil; and so once the Torah was given there was light for the world, and light comes before darkness. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 61): Esau was the firstborn in birth, which is the emergence into actuality, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness": on the side of the refuse the left is the right and comes first, and the this-world of Esau, in which darkness prevails, comes first. But in formation [yetzirah], which is the hidden world, the thought of creation and the conception of the world, the right comes first. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 8): The creation of the world was "first darkness and afterward light": first comes the portion of Bereishis, in the knowledge of the vessels, and afterward the attainment of the light of Abraham our father through knowledge, in the manner of "the advantage of light over darkness." Such too is the order of man's attainment of the light of the Blessed One, like the creation of the world: first the six days of work and afterward Shabbos; but for man's own action the light must come first and afterward the making of the vessel. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): This light [of the soul's root] can be attained in this world only through repentance, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light." Thus for certain righteous men, such as King David in the trial of Bathsheba, the Blessed One arranged a deed of the wicked in order to establish the yoke of repentance, for this cannot come about except through a preceding darkness. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): [In the Oral Torah and the innovation of laws not yet clarified] it is impossible to stand at all without a prior stumbling, as at the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," for so is the light attained by created beings: specifically out of darkness and concealment. Therefore Esau was formed before Jacob, being the preceding darkness that leads to the attainment of the light of Torah afterward. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 21): On "Why do the goats go first... as at the creation of the world, first darkness and afterward light," Rashi explains that goats are ordinarily black. So Teves, whose sign is the kid, is the aspect of darkness, and specifically then [the Hasmoneans] brought about their miracle through their self-sacrifice, to shine out of the darkness with greater excellence, as the Zohar says, "there is no light except that which comes out of darkness"; and this is like the creation of the world. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): Since it is of the working of the Blessed One that it be so, "first darkness and afterward light," for the advantage of light is recognized only from darkness, [the forces of evil] therefore begin to act first, and from this the light shines forth, as in "He made darkness His hiding place," for there He is hidden. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 10): Such is the way of the Blessed One in the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light"; and so [the Sages] said that He would create worlds and destroy them, these being the worlds of chaos, until the world of rectification emerged. So it is in everything: all the incarnations of the Messiah that have already been in the world are akin to "creating worlds and destroying them," and specifically through those destructions the world of rectification is built, by raising up the lights of the broken vessels. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 174): Since in natural things the Blessed One established this order, "first darkness and afterward light," it is certainly the essence of His will, as [the Sages said], "In the place where penitents stand...". Although, Heaven forbid, one may not say "I will sin and repent" and do so by choice, it nonetheless happens of itself, for "there is no righteous man on earth..."; and such is the order: "the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light," far beyond one who did not walk in darkness. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 7): From the standpoint of this world's imagination it seemed at first that everything belonged to Esau, for such is the creation of the world, "first darkness and afterward light," as [the Sages] said at the beginning of Berakhos, which is why the evening Shema was placed first. For the Shema, the recognition of [God's] unity, was the essence of the creation of the world, and first one must recognize it out of darkness and concealment, for that was the whole matter of creation. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Shabbos): This is as it is written, "The Lord my God illuminates my darkness": after a person recognizes his sin and is pained over it, he merits that the Blessed One shines for him a rectification for it. Through the darkness, the remorse and pain he felt over the deed, he merits the light that reveals its rectification; and this is "first darkness and afterward light." Beis Yaakov (Vayeitzei 71): The Blessed One set the light in this world surrounded and encompassed by darkness, to leave man room to distinguish himself, that he remove the darkness and shine even within it. Therefore, when the Blessed One shines His bright light, He will shine it only for one who on his part walked in the light and did His will; He created the darkness only for the sake of one who desires the light, that for his sake He will illuminate the darkness too. Tiferes Yosef (Shavuos 7): It is written, "who forms light and creates darkness," yet at the creation of the world "there was evening and there was morning," first darkness and afterward light, so here too it should have said "creates darkness" first. The explanation: the first light was not yet within creation's capacity to receive, and light that creation cannot receive is called darkness from creation's standpoint; therefore it says "forms light and creates darkness," for from creation's standpoint it begins with day, since in the first evening creation had no grasp at all. Sod Yesharim (Shabbos HaGadol 6): As my father and teacher explained, the whole purpose of the darkness that the Blessed One set first is only that the light afterward be the more explicit; therefore "it was evening" is said first and then "it was morning." So too with Abraham our father: all the concealment he had at first, until he said, "Shall you say the palace has no master?", was the darkness that came first, only so that the Blessed One would afterward shine to him with greater clarity, "I am the master of the palace." עַמּוּד ב׳),
for such was the creation of the world: "first darkness and then light" (ibid. 77b),
שֶׁאֵין הָאוֹר נִגְלֶה מִיָּד,
in that the light is not revealed immediately,
רַק מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהַהֶעְלֵם נִגְלֶה הָאוֹר לִמְבַקְשָׁיו, וְהֵם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rather from within darkness and concealment the light becomes revealed to those who seek it, namely the children of Israel.
אֲבָל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִשְׁאָרִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ,
The nations of the world, however, remain in darkness,
אֲשֶׁר "יְכַסֶּה אֶרֶץ וַעֲרָפֶל לְאֻמִּים",
which "shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples,"
וְרַק "עָלַיִךְ יִזְרַח" וְגוֹמֵר,
and only "upon you shall Hashem shine..." and so forth,
דְּ"כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ ה' אוֹר לִי".
for "though I sit in darkness, Hashem is a light unto me."

items.h:
Seif 2 — The Ten Plagues and the Erasure of Amalek
Egypt's tenfold separation refined Israel and teaches that evil disappears when cut off from its divine life-source.

p: וּבִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהִיא תְּחִלַּת בִּנְיַן הָאֻמָּה,
And at the Exodus from Egypt, which was the beginning of the building of the nation,
וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה נֶחֱלָק לְעֶשֶׂר,
and it is known that every complete spiritual structure is divided into ten levels,
וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְהִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹתֵיהֶם,
and they needed to attain perfection in their ten attributes,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת נִבְדָּל מֵהָעַמִּים.
so that they would be entirely a seed of truth, separated from the nations.
הָיוּ הַבֵּרוּר בְּעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת שֶׁבָּאוּ עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים,
The clarification and refinement took place through the ten plagues that came upon the Egyptians,
וּבְכָל מַכָּה הִפְלִיא ה' בֵּין מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and with each plague Hashem distinguished between Egypt and the children of Israel.
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ קַמָּאֵי,
And it is known what the early masters wrote,
דִּבְבִיאַת הַמַּכּוֹת הָיָה פַּחַד גַּם לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that upon the arrival of the plagues there was fear also for the children of Israel,
דְּנִתְיָרְאוּ שֶׁמָּא יִהְיֶה גַּם עֲלֵיהֶם;
for they feared lest the plagues fall upon them as well;
וְכָךְ הָיָה רָאוּי כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן הַכּוֹזֵב,
and so it appeared fitting according to false worldly illusion,
וְשֶׁהֵם יֵצְאוּ מֵהַדִּמְיוֹן וְיִדְבְּקוּ בֶּאֱמֶת,
until they would emerge from that illusion and cleave to the absolute truth,
וְאָז יַכִּירוּ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת עִם הַמַּכּוֹת כְּלָל.
and then they would recognize the truth that they had no connection to the plagues whatsoever.
וּמַכַּת חֹשֶׁךְ הוּא הַתְּשִׁיעִי נֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד,
And the plague of darkness was the ninth, corresponding to the attribute of Yesod,
שֶׁשָּׁם עִיקַר זֻהֲמַת מִצְרַיִם, עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ;
where lay the primary filth and defilement of Egypt, "the nakedness of the land";
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמִדָּה זוֹ הַחֹשֶׁךְ יְכַסֶּה אֶרֶץ שָׁם,
therefore in this attribute darkness covered the earth there,
וּלְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם,
while for all the children of Israel there was light in their dwellings,
כִּי הֵם הָיוּ גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת,
because they were strictly fenced against sexual immorality,

וּשְׁמוֹ מֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם נֶגֶד הַמִּצְרִים לְעֵדוּת הַשֵּׁם יוּ"ד הֵ"א (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד, אוֹת יב1302 Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12:1 — At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "My sister, My bride, a locked garden." What is "a locked garden"? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: My garden is locked, and shall it be disgraced? R. Pinchas said: At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, summoned the angel appointed over conception and said to him: Go out and form them with all the features of their fathers. R. Huna in the name of R. Idi: a heh at the beginning of the word and a yod at its end — Yah testifies concerning them that they are indeed the sons of their fathers.),
and His Name testified for them against the Egyptians through the testimony of the Divine Name Yah (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12),
שֶׁהֵם שְׁתַּיִם רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הַמּוֹרוֹת עַל הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
which are the first two letters pointing to the concealed realms, as is known.
כִּי מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה הָיָה טַעֲנָה,
For from the perspective of what was outwardly revealed there was an accusation,
וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מוֹנִין אוֹתָם,
and the nations of the world taunted them;
וּכְפִי גּוֹדֶל שִׁקּוּעָם בְּמִצְרַיִם,
and according to the depth of their immersion within Egypt,

עַד שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי", כְּעֻבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר קז1303 Midrash Tehillim 107:4 — "From the lands He gathered them." Just as a bird lies in the hand of the fowler — if he wishes he kills it, and if he wishes he keeps it alive — so were Israel sunk in the hand of the Egyptians. R. Abbahu son of R. Acha said in the name of our master: Israel lay within Egypt like a fetus lying within the womb of an animal; and just as the shepherd puts his hand into her womb and draws it out, so did the Holy One, blessed be He, do, as it is said, "to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation" (Deuteronomy 4:34). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 20): Egypt, to whom Israel were slaves in complete servitude (and what a slave acquires, his master acquires), had all the holiness of Israel swallowed up within it, as the Sages said on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation" that they were like a fetus in its mother's womb; and a fetus is reckoned as its mother's thigh, so great was the power of Egypt's connection to the holiness of Israel. Therefore the Torah did not write the prohibition of the Egyptian and the Edomite, only the permission of the third generation, and in the words "you shall not abhor." Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 14): The Exodus is called a birth in Ezekiel, "and as for your birth, on the day you were born," and so it is said of "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb. And the Sages said that the song of Egypt is in the feminine, unlike that of the future, when there will be the birth of a male, for then they will be redeemed through repentance; whereas the Exodus was the birth of a female, which has nothing of its own. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Because some root of Israel was hidden in Haman, his downfall came in Nisan, on Pesach, the time prepared for Israel's going out from the straits of the husks, when the root of Jewishness goes out from every place in which it is sunk. For on Pesach, as it were, He took out "a nation from the midst of a nation," which the Sages expounded "like a fetus in its mother's womb" — that even purity that has been swallowed up is expelled and comes out; and then Mordechai was given the house of Haman and absorbed all the good, and the evil perished of itself. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 3): Remembering the Exodus is a segulah for being remembered with children, for by recalling that miracle one arouses the power of remembrance and brings about the remembrance of the barren as well; for the Exodus too was in the mystery of birth, as the Sages said on "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus slipping out of its mother's womb, and as is known from the Arizal that the Egyptian exile was in the mystery of gestation. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 7): The seed of Jacob, the root of truth in the world, was swallowed up within [Egypt], as it is said on "a nation from the midst of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb: that filth so surrounded them that they had no revealed existence of their own. And "he swallowed wealth and shall vomit it up" at the Exodus, when they were chosen as a unique people through the removal of the darkness of Egypt's filth that surrounded them. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares, from the Tanchuma 15): On the side of nature it is said "for My name is within him [bekirbo]," "within" meaning hidden and not perceptible to the eye, as the Sages said on "a nation from the midst [mikerev] of a nation," like a fetus in its mother's womb: it is hidden, yet the fetus is nonetheless recognized, for through understanding one knows there is a fetus in her womb, though it is not actually visible to the eye. This is from the side of wisdom, whereas prophecy is the complete seeing of the name of the Blessed One. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): As long as Israel were still in the Egyptian exile (and the Sages said on "a nation from the midst of a nation" that they were truly within them, wholly surrounded by them, like a fetus, which is its mother's thigh and has no life of its own), [Moses] had to be in Midian. Only after they left Egypt and were chosen as a distinct people was this clarified; but while they were in Egypt like a fetus in its mother's womb, the name "seed of Abraham" still applied to all who were of his seed. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Va'eschanan): "Or has God ventured to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation": Israel are so beloved before the Blessed One that even when they do deeds like those of the idolaters, the deeds of Israel are nonetheless good — just as Moses our teacher would not accept the mirrors of the women until the Blessed One answered him that in Israel there is great holiness in this. This is what is called "a nation from the midst of a nation," that the deeds of Israel are good, as the Midrash says: Israel were placed within Egypt like a fetus placed within the womb of an animal, and just as the shepherd puts his hand into her womb and draws it out, so did the Holy One, blessed be He. Sod Yesharim (Parashas Zachor 11): In Egypt Israel were in the aspect of a fetus, as the Midrash says, "like a fetus placed within the womb of an animal ... so did the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, 'to come and take Him a nation from the midst of a nation'": that is, the Blessed One so surrounded them in Egypt that they were raised above the bounds of this world and returned there to the level of a fetus, as it is written, "when His lamp shone over my head." And "just as the shepherd puts his hand within her womb" means that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them the one commandment of circumcision, which is two: the cutting, signifying the abiding recognition that they stem from the root of the Blessed One's will, and the uncovering, alluding to all the fences by which Israel restrain themselves.),
to the extent that they were termed "a nation from the midst of a nation," like an embryo in its mother's womb (Midrash Tehillim 107),
הָיָה נִרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ גַּם הֵם מְזֹהָמִים, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹהֶם.
it appeared as if they too were defiled, Heaven forbid, just like them.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת שָׁם דַּוְקָא נִתְבָּרְרָה טָהֳרַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
In truth, however, precisely there the purity of the children of Israel was clarified,
וְזָכוּ לִפְסִיקַת הַזֻּהֲמָא לְגַמְרֵי
and they merited the complete cessation of defilement
עַל יְדֵי הַהֲכָנָה בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם דַּוְקָא,
specifically through the preparation within the Egyptian exile,
שֶׁהָיָה הַחֲשׁוֹכָא דִּבְרֵישָׁא,
which constituted the "darkness at first,"
וּמִזֶּה זָכוּ לִנְהוֹרָא בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם אַחַר כָּךְ,
and from this they merited the radiant light in their dwellings afterward,
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל הוֹלֵךְ, הָיָה הָאוֹר מְמַשְׁמֵשׁ וּבָא עִמּוֹ.
and wherever a Jew went, the light moved and accompanied him.
וְהוּא כְּטַעַם: בַּחֹשֶׁךְ וְעֹמֶק הַשִּׁקּוּעַ ה' אוֹר לָהֶם,
And it is in the sense of: in the dark and in the depth of sinking down, Hashem is light to them,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַחֹשֶׁךְ לְהַחְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם כְּלָל.
and it is impossible for darkness to darken them at all.
וּמַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת הוּא שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים "בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי",
And the plague of the firstborn relates to Israel being called "My firstborn son,"
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ הַמִּיתָה וְהַבִּטּוּל יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and from this a seemingly greater danger of death and nullification extended over the children of Israel,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הֻזְהֲרוּ שֶׁלֹּא לָצֵאת מִפֶּתַח בֵּיתָם,
for they were warned not to go out from the entrance of their house,
וְהֻצְרְכוּ לְדַם פֶּסַח לְהָגֵן בַּעֲדָם,
and required the blood of the Passover offering to shield them,
נִרְאֶה שֶׁהָיָה מָקוֹם לַמַּשְׁחִית לִשְׁלוֹט, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם בָּהֶם.
so that it appeared as though there was room for the destroyer to rule, Heaven forbid, in truth over them as well.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה, אִם מִצְרַיִם חָטְאוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לְהוֹצִיא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And at first glance: if the Egyptians sinned because they refused to release the children of Israel,
יִשְׂרָאֵל מַה חָטְאוּ?
what was Israel's sin?
וְגַם אוֹתָהּ מַכָּה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
Furthermore, that plague was executed by the Blessed Name Himself,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אֲנִי וְלֹא מַלְאָךְ" וְכוּלֵי "וְהִכֵּיתִי" וְכוּלֵי1304 Exodus 12:12; Pesach Haggadah — “And I shall pass through the land of Egypt on that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and upon all the gods of Egypt I shall execute judgments — I am the Lord.” And the Haggadah expounds this verse: “I and not an angel … I and not a seraph … I and not a messenger … I am He and no other.”,
as the Sages expounded: "I and not an angel... and I will smite...,"

וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ "כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּתַּן רְשׁוּת לַמַּשְׁחִית" וְכוּלֵי1305 Bava Kamma 60a — Rav Yosef taught: What is meant by “And none of you shall go out from the door of his house until morning”? Once license has been given to the destroyer, it does not distinguish between the righteous and the wicked. Maharsha: Rashi on the Torah drew from this verse that night as such is the domain of the destroying forces, and Nachmanides objected: is a man then forbidden to leave his house every night? But the Mekhilta plainly supports Rashi, and two things follow from our passage — that in a time of plague one should not go out, since license has been given to the destroyer; and that, since the verse says "until morning" although the plague of the firstborn lasted only until midnight, night itself is the destroyers' domain, so that one should always set out and come home by daylight. Maharal (Gevurot Hashem 37): Once license has been given to the destroyer he no longer distinguishes between the righteous and the wicked — so it is in Bava Kamma, chapter HaKones; but within the house there was nothing to fear, for of that it is said "and He will not permit the destroyer to come into your houses," the destroyer having no license to enter there. And although the Holy One, blessed be He, was Himself striking Egypt, once He is striking, license to destroy is thereby given to every destroying power, for they are all drawn after Him; on other nights the harmful powers have no such license as on this night, and therefore "let no man go out.".
and the principle of "once permission is granted to the destroyer to harm..." does not seem to apply.
אֲבָל עִנְיַן מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
However, the inner matter of the plague of the firstborn being carried out by the Blessed Name Himself is:
אַף דְּמִפִּי עֶלְיוֹן לֹא תֵצֵא הָרָעוֹת,
even though from the mouth of the Most High evil does not emerge,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּאֵין זֶה רָעָתָם אֶלָּא טוֹבָתָם.
you are forced to conclude that this was not intrinsic evil, but ultimate goodness.
כִּי עִנְיַן מִיתָתָם הָיָה עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הִתְגַּלּוּת מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל דְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
For the reality of their death was brought about through the intense revelation of the "great terror" of the Shechinah's disclosure,
נָפַל פַּחַד עָצוּם עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים.
when an immense dread fell upon the Egyptians.
וְהַבְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם — רֵאשִׁית וְעִיקַר הָאוֹן וְהַכֹּחַ שֶׁל הָאֻמָּה,
And the firstborn among them—the firstfruit and primary vigor and strength of the nation,
דְּעַל כֵּן קֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה הַהַקְרָבָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת,
wherefore prior to the Giving of the Torah sacrificial service was performed by the firstborn,
שֶׁהֵם הַנִּבְחָרִים שֶׁבָּאֻמָּה,
who are the elite of the nation—
עֲלֵיהֶם הָיָה הַפַּחַד בְּיֶתֶר תֹּקֶף,
upon them the dread fell with supreme intensity,
עַד שֶׁיָּצְאָה נִשְׁמָתָם מִגּוֹדֶל הַפַּחַד.
until their souls departed from the magnitude of that terror.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר שֶׁהֻקְדְּשׁוּ מֵאָז,
And this is the matter of the sanctity of the firstling of a donkey consecrated from that time,

נֶגֶד מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לַחֲמוֹר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צו1306 Bereshit Rabbah 96:5 — Another interpretation: Jacob said, [I ask this] so that the Egyptians should not use me as their means of redemption. They bow down to the lamb, and I am likened to a lamb, as it is said, "Israel is a scattered lamb"; and of Egypt it is written, "whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys"; and it is written, "and the firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb." Hence, "Do not bury me in Egypt.");
corresponding to the Egyptians who were compared to a donkey, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah 96);
כִּי מַכָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת קְדֻשָּׁה,
for their plague was struck through the felt impact of holiness,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם טְמֵאִים בְּעֶצֶם,
only that they were intrinsically impure,
עַל כֵּן אֵין שַׁיָּךְ בָּהֶם קְדֻשָּׁה בְּעֶצֶם כְּלָל,
therefore intrinsic holiness could not take hold within them at all,
רַק קְדֻשָּׁתָם לִפְדּוֹתָם בְּשֶׂה אוֹ לְעָרְפָם.
and their only sanctification is to redeem them with a lamb or break their neck.
וּבְמִצְרַיִם הָיָה שְׁנֵיהֶם: הֵם נֶעֶרְפוּ,
And in Egypt both occurred: the Egyptians had their necks broken in death,
וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה נִכְנַס בְּשֵׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
while the holiness entered the lamb of Israel,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי לִי כָל בְּכוֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" וְגוֹמֵר "בְּיוֹם הַכֹּתִי" וְגוֹמֵר1307 Numbers 8:17 — “For every firstborn among the Children of Israel is Mine, among man and among beast; on the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt I sanctified them for Myself.” Rashi: The firstborn were Mine by strict right, for I shielded them when I struck the firstborn of Egypt and took them for Myself — until they went astray in the matter of the Golden Calf; and now "I have taken the Levites" in their stead. Sod Yesharim (First Night of Pesach 8): After the clarification at the Exodus, when the Blessed One distinguished between the firstborn of Egypt and the firstborn of Israel, He showed, as it is written, "For every firstborn among the Children of Israel is Mine," that even those actions of Israel which outwardly appear to lack settled thought — for "firstborn" denotes a force that appears as wantonness without knowledge — are bound to the root of His will, the Blessed One testifying that "every firstborn among the Children of Israel is Mine." From this branched out the questions of the four sons.;
as it is written: "For every firstborn among the children of Israel is Mine... on the day I smote..." and so forth;
וְלֹא שֶׁהָיוּ פִּדְיוֹנָם,
not that the Israelite firstborn were a mere redemption payment for them,
רַק שֶׁהֵם קָדְשׁוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּאוֹתוֹ פֶּרֶק שֶׁהָיָה גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
but that they too were sanctified at that precise moment of the Shechinah's revelation,
וְנִתְגַּלֵּית קְדֻשָּׁה גַּם לָהֶם;
and holiness was revealed to them as well;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם קְדוֹשִׁים בְּעֶצֶם, וְיָכְלוּ לִסְבּוֹל,
except that Israel is intrinsically holy, and they were capable of enduring the divine light,
וְלֹא יָצְאָה חַיּוּתָם;
so their life-force did not depart;
אַדְּרַבָּה, נִתְדַּבְּקוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים, לִהְיוֹת שַׁיָּךְ לוֹ.
on the contrary, through this they cleaved to the living God, belonging wholly to Him.

וּכְטַעַם: "הֲשָׁמַע עָם קוֹל" וְגוֹמֵר "כַּאֲשֶׁר" וְגוֹמֵר "וַיֶּחִי1308 Deuteronomy 4:33 — “Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?”",
And it is like the principle of: "Did a people ever hear the voice..." and so forth "as you have heard, and live?"
כִּי עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַשָּׂגָה כִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל ה' מִסְתַּלֵּק הַחַיּוּת,
for through the intensity of an apprehension such as hearing Hashem's voice, physical life departs,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וָחָי",
in the manner of "for man shall not see Me and live,"

אֲבָל בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתָן רוֹאִין (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ פִּסְקָא קג)1309 Sifrei Bamidbar 103 — R. Dosa says: What is the meaning of "for no man shall see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20)? While he is alive he does not see, but he does see at the hour of death. And so it says: "Before Him shall bow all who go down to the dust, and he who cannot keep his own soul alive" (Psalms 22:30). Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): When it is revealed that everything comes from the root in the Blessed One, the screen that sins made between Israel and their Father in heaven is removed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is shown to them before their eyes, even though "no man shall see Me and live" — for the Sages said that "at the hour of their death they see," since then the screen of this world is removed. So too, with the revelation of [Isaac's plea] "half upon You," the screen of this world will be removed. וּמִסְתַּלֵּק הַחַיּוּת.
though at the moment of their passing mortals behold the Divine (Sifrei, Behaalotecha 103) and bodily life departs.
וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁחַיּוּתָם הוּא גַּם כֵּן חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל,
Yet the children of Israel, whose soul-vitality is an actual portion of God from Above,
הֵם יוּכְלוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ וְלִחְיוֹת,
are able to hear and yet live,
וְכֵן בְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה דְּמִצְרַיִם.
and so it was during the revelation of the Shechinah in Egypt.
אֲבָל יָדוּעַ לְמַאן דְּעָיְילֵי וְנָפְקֵי,
Nevertheless, it is well known to those who enter and emerge from esoteric wisdom,
כִּי דָּבָר זֶה כְּפִי מַדְרֵגַת הָאָדָם,
that this capacity corresponds strictly to a person's spiritual level,
וְצָרִיךְ לִכָּנֵס בְּהַדְרָגָה מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה;
and one must ascend gradually from one rung to the next;
אֲבָל אִם יַשִּׂיג הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ, יוּכַל לָצֵאת נַפְשׁוֹ,
for if one attains an apprehension beyond his rung, his soul may depart,

כְּעִנְיַן (חֲגִיגָה יד1310 Chagigah 14b — The Sages taught: Four entered the orchard, and these are they — Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, Acher, and R. Akiva. Ben Azzai glanced and died; of him Scripture says, "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones." Ben Zoma glanced and was stricken; of him Scripture says, "Have you found honey? Eat only your fill, lest you be sated with it and vomit it." Acher cut down the shoots. R. Akiva came out in peace. Rashi: "Entered the orchard" — they ascended to the firmament by means of a [Divine] Name. "Glanced" — toward the Divine Presence; and "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones" means that his death was grievous before Him, since he died young, yet it was impossible that he should not die, for it is said, "for man shall not see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20). "Was stricken" — his mind was deranged. Tosafos (s.v. "they entered the orchard"): By means of a [Divine] Name — and they did not actually ascend on high; rather it appeared to them as though they had ascended. So too the Arukh explains. Maharsha: The Arukh calls it an "orchard" after the Garden of Eden that is hidden away for the righteous: so too that place in Aravot, where the souls of the righteous are bound up — and it is the shoots of this orchard that Acher cut down. He then cites an ancient book: Ben Azzai's soul clung in true attachment to the supernal things, and when he glanced at the shining light it was parted from the body and never returned to its place — a great level, and therefore Scripture says of him, "Precious in the eyes of the Lord." Ben Zoma was not as complete in his attainments and in settled mind as Ben Azzai, and having glanced at a light brighter than his mind could bear, his matters became confounded and his understanding deranged; while Acher, seeing that the merits of Israel were in [Metatron's] hand, thought that there were two authorities, and is called one who "cut down the shoots" because he cut apart things that are one and separated them from each other. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 16): The Sages' statement in Chagigah, "Ben Azzai glanced and died, and of him Scripture says, 'Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones,'" accords with Yevamos (63b): Ben Azzai expounded well but did not practise well, for he never married and did not perform the body of the deed; his soul desired Torah, which is "the sight of the eyes," and so he only "glanced," whereas R. Akiva entered in peace and came out, for he succeeded up to the completion of the deed. Since Ben Azzai contented himself with seeing alone, of him it is said "Precious in the eyes of the Lord": the eyes of the Blessed One, as it were, gazed upon him in return, for seeing without deed is stronger there — as the Sages said on "no man shall see Me and live," that at the time of death they do see — so that it was precious and praiseworthy in the eyes of the Lord precisely at the level of "the sight of the eyes." עַמּוּד ב): בֶּן עַזַּאי הֵצִיץ וָמֵת מִתֹּקֶף הַהַשָּׂגָה.
as in the case of (Chagigah 14b): Ben Azzai peered and died from the sheer intensity of the perception.
וְכֵן מִיתַת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא הָיָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה;
So too was the death of Nadav and Avihu;

וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד יָצְאָה נִשְׁמָתָם (שַׁבָּת פח1311 Shabbat 88b — R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: With every single utterance that went forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it is said, "My soul went forth when He spoke." And since their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will in time to come revive the dead, and revived them, as it is said, "A bounteous rain didst Thou pour down, O God; Thine inheritance, when it was weary, Thou didst establish."
