Rashi: "A bounteous rain" — this verse in the Book of Psalms is written with reference to the Giving of the Torah. Maharsha: R. Yehoshua ben Levi seems to contradict himself, for he also says that they retreated twelve mil and that the world was filled with fragrance to restore their spirits, which implies that they did not die; but there were different groups according to their natures — some were weakened by the terror of the voices and were helped by the spices, others, weaker still, died, and others retreated. He asks how they received the second utterance, rather than how they lived afterwards, to teach the greater novelty that they died and revived ten times, between each utterance, deriving it from the plural in "a rain of bounties," which follows "the earth trembled," through which they died. Dew is called "bounteous rain" because it comes to the world as a free gift and is never withheld, whereas rain comes only through merit. Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 31): At the level of the Blessed One's existence no other existence can stand at all; how then could Israel be joined to His speech openly, face to face, as though in partnership with the First Cause? Therefore their souls departed and they could not endure; they were sustained only because at that hour they cleaved to Him at the supreme level from which life comes to the dead — the place from which life comes to the world. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:2): When a person gives up his soul in actual deed, to the point of the soul's expiry, he still cannot come to actual extinction, for the light of the King's countenance that shone toward him is the source of life, and through that very self-sacrifice it immediately pours forth a new spirit of life, as is written of the stand at Mount Sinai, that the dew of revival revived them. This comes through cleaving to the pillar of Torah and cleaving in divine service, that is, "with all your soul." עַמּוּד ב),
and at the Giving of the Torah, likewise, with a single divine Utterance their souls departed (Shabbat 88b),
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ מוּכָנִים כֻּלָּם לְמַדְרֵגַת נְבוּאָה,
because not all of them were spiritually prepared for that rung of prophecy,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוֹרִיד טַל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁפַע חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה;
except that He brought down the dew of resurrection—a fresh flow of vitality whereby they became a new creation;
וְכֵן בְּכָל הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָה.
and so it is with every perception transcending one's rung.
וְהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזּוֹכֶה בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא לְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵמוּת, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And the baal teshuvah who merits in a single hour, in an instant, ultimate perfection, as is known,
גַּם כֵּן כְּשֶׁקּוֹנֶה עוֹלָמוֹ בְּשָׁעָה אַחַת תֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ,
likewise, when he acquires his eternal world in a single hour, his soul may depart,

כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדַיָּא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז1312 Avodah Zarah 17a — He said: The matter depends on nothing but myself. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A Divine voice went forth and said: R. Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come. R. Yehuda HaNasi wept and said: There is one who acquires his world in many years, and there is one who acquires his world in a single hour. Maharsha: R. Yehuda HaNasi's further statement, that penitents are not only accepted but are even called "Rabbi," refers to the Divine voice here, which proclaimed him "R. Elazar ben Durdaya." Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 17a, on his death): He died by the very force of his repentance: having cleaved to harlotry so utterly that it was reckoned like heresy, he had become as another man, all refuse, like wind that has no substance, and for such a one repentance is impossible while he lives, but only through death, since in the world after death there is neither heresy nor immorality. Therefore, when he repented, he received death so that his repentance might take effect. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 17a, s.v. "It was said of R. Elazar ben Durdaya"): The name by which he was called indicates his essence. Durdaya denotes the lees of wine, its refuse: a wicked man in whom some good remains is called "vinegar," for vinegar is not wholly spoiled, but one wholly spoiled, who sinned with his body in harlotry, is called "lees"; while Elazar is the power in a man for repentance, for the Blessed One helps a person, as they said, "one who comes to purify himself is helped." So the name suited him well: he was wholly refuse like the lees, yet within the lees lay a power ready for repentance with the help of the Blessed One — and thus his name pointed both to the sin and to the repentance. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 17a, s.v. "the matter depends on nothing but myself"): For repentance is a return to the Blessed One Himself, who is the root of all; therefore repentance must come from the man’s own essence, and not from others [such as the mountains, the heavens and the stars he had asked to seek mercy for him]. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:52): When a person uproots that root of evil and turns it back to good through true repentance, his soul's rectification is complete, as with R. Elazar ben Durdaya, over whom Rebbi wept, "There is one who acquires his world in a single hour," and who is even called "Rabbi" — a title belonging to one who has disciples — because he so worked upon his own particular root that the evil root was entirely uprooted, and thoughts of repentance were thereby awakened throughout the world in all who had sinned in that root. Even Rebbi's weeping came from his arousal: he had seemed to be in despair, with no one to plead for him, and in his weeping he was roused to beg mercy for himself and not to despair, until the sound of his weeping moved Rebbi to weep as well and roused him to see that one must not despair, for "there is one who acquires his world in a single hour," even after sinning for many years. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim 6): Although R. Elazar ben Durdaya did no commandment or good deed afterward and studied no Torah, a heavenly voice declared him destined for the life of the World to Come, because all his willful sins became merits for him, so that he had good deeds by which to merit it — and all because his repentance was "with all your heart and with all your soul." Hence Rebbi wept and said, "There is one who acquires his world in a single hour," adding that penitents are even called "Rabbi"; and though only one who teaches others is so called, this itself was the lesson he taught Israel: that if they repent with all their heart and soul, all their sins become merits. עַמּוּד א).
like Rabbi Elazar ben Dordia in Avodah Zarah (17a).
וְיָדוּעַ דִּבִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הִשִּׂיגוּ בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא שֶׁלֹּא בְּהַדְרָגָה,
And it is known that at the Exodus from Egypt they attained their level in a single moment without gradual ascent,
רַק בְּדִלּוּג וְקִפּוּץ עַל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת וּבְחִפָּזוֹן;
but rather by leaping and bounding over spiritual rungs in haste;
וְעַל כֵּן הֻצְרְכוּ לְהֲגַנַּת דַּם פֶּסַח עַל הַמַּשְׁקוֹף וּמְזוּזוֹת,
therefore they required the protection of the blood of the Passover offering upon the lintel and doorposts,
כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ;
for the blood is the life-soul;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מַקְרִיב נַפְשׁוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and when a person offers his very soul to the Blessed Name,
זֶהוּ דִּינָא לְמִצְרַיִם וְרַחֲמֵי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
this manifests as judgment to Egypt and mercy to Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (בֹּא לו עַמּוּד א),
as it is written in the Zohar (Bo 36a),
כִּי עַל הַפֶּתַח פֵּרֵשׁ שָׁם: פֶּתַח הַגּוּף זוֹ מִילָה,
for concerning "upon the entrance" the Zohar explains there: the entrance of the body is circumcision,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן הַגּוּף וְלֵידַת אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי,
which is the inception of bodily construction and the birth of the Jewish person,
לִהְיוֹת מָסוּר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן.
to be dedicated to the Blessed Name from birth, from the womb.
וְדָבָר זֶה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הוּא סִלּוּק חַיּוּת,
This total surrender, for the nations of the world, constitutes the departure of life-force,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִמְסֹר עַצְמָם לְגַמְרֵי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
for it is impossible for them to surrender themselves entirely to the Blessed Name;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פח1313 Shabbat 88a-b — A certain heretic saw Rava engrossed in his studies, his fingers beneath his foot and pressed so hard that they oozed blood. He said to him: You rash people, who put your mouths before your ears — you still stand in your rashness! First you should have listened; if you could bear it, you would accept, and if not, you would not accept. Rashi: ["His fingers":] the fingers of his hands. ["And he was pressing them":] he was crushing them under his legs and did not notice, from his absorption. ["A rash people":] hasty. ["Who put your mouths before your ears":] before you had heard how hard it is and whether you could stand up to it, you took it upon yourselves to fulfill it. ["We, who walk in wholeheartedness":] we walked with Him in simplicity of heart, as those who act out of love, and relied on Him not to burden us with something we could not withstand. Maharsha: ["The integrity of the upright shall guide them":] Besides Rashi's explanation, one may explain it in the manner of "In the way a person wishes to go, he is led" and "One who comes to purify himself is helped": the upright, who wish to walk the straight path even though it is hard for them to do, are guided with help from Heaven; and conversely, "the crookedness of the treacherous," who walk a crooked and not a straight path, "shall destroy them," for "one who comes to defile himself, [the way] is opened for him." Maharal (Tiferes Yisrael, ch. 29): The heretic held that this was out of order — by right a person should first hear a thing and afterwards know to do it — and so he said that Israel's putting "we will do" before "we will hear" came from their rashness, that they are disorderly in their actions. Rava answered him that the matter is the reverse of what he thought: it is the ways of those who walk in guile that depart from order, but Israel walk in their integrity, and the action of whoever is wholehearted never departs from the proper order — and by the proper order the doing should come first, for that is what man was created for. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Mishlei): To be easily enticed toward the good is a fine trait for which Israel were praised: they are drawn after the Blessed One with great haste, without deliberation or delay, as the heretic said to Rava, "Rash people, who put your mouths before your ears." Beis Yaakov (Vayishlach 20): Rava's reply to the Sadducee who called Israel "rash people, who put your mouths before your ears" and said they should first have listened to see whether they were able, namely "We who walk in wholeheartedness, of us it is written, 'The integrity of the upright shall guide them,'" means that we are wholehearted in the will of the Blessed One, [confident] that He will surely help us to complete it for the good; and this is what is called "whose strength is in You." Sod Yesharim (Seventh Day of Pesach 14): At times a person must set aside his human form [of reasoning] to fulfill the will of the Blessed One, like a horse ridden by its master, as in the heretic's charge against Rava and Rava's reply: Israel, who at their root cleave to knowledge, are taught by that knowledge that at times they should set aside their power of choice to fulfill the will of the Blessed One. But the nations, who branch from the supernal princes that stand in awe without knowledge, have no bond with their prince and act without knowledge or choice, like a horse of the Other Side; and even when they sometimes yield before the Blessed One, it is only so as to spread out afterwards with great force, as Balaam did. עַמּוּד א): "בְּרֵישָׁא אִיבַּעְיָא לְכוּ לְמִשְׁמַע אִי מָצֵיתוּ" וְכוּלֵי,
and as the gentile mocked in Shabbat (88a): "First you should have listened to hear whether you were able...," and so forth,
כִּי לֹא יָכְלוּ לְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמָם עוֹל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר
because they could not accept upon themselves the yoke of the Blessed Name in whatever He commands
רַק אַחַר שֶׁיִּשְׁמְעוּ אִם הוּא בִּיכָלְתָּם.
except after hearing whether it lay within their power.
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהֶרְאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׁמָעֵאל "לֹא תִנְאָף" וּלֶאֱדוֹם "לֹא תִרְצַח",
Therefore when the Blessed Name presented "Do not commit adultery" to Ishmael and "Do not murder" to Edom,
וְכַדּוֹמֶה כָּל אֻמָּה בַּמֶּה שֶׁהֵם מְשֻׁקָּעִים שֶׁכָּל חַיּוּתָם תָּלוּי בָּזֶה,
and similarly to each nation in that wherein they were steeped and their entire vitality depended,

לֹא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קצב עַמּוּד ב1314 Zohar 3:192b — He called Samael, and he came before Him, and He said to him: Do you want My Torah? He said: What is written in it? He said to him: "You shall not murder." He said: Master of the world, if You give it to me, all my dominion is taken from me, for my dominion is over killing, and there would be no wars. ... He then called Rahab and said to him: Do you want My Torah? He said: What is written in it? He said: "You shall not commit adultery." He said: Woe, if the Holy One, blessed be He, bequeaths me this evil inheritance, by which all my dominion would be removed — for I took the blessing of the waters, the blessing of the fish of the sea, "Be fruitful and multiply."),
they refused to accept the Torah (Zohar, Part III, 192b),
כִּי אִם יַנִּיחוּ זֶה, יַנִּיחוּ חַיּוּתָם לְגַמְרֵי,
for were they to abandon that trait, they would relinquish their very vitality completely,
כִּי כָּל חַיּוּתָם הוּא מִתַּאֲוָה זוֹ.
since their entire life-force stems from that appetite.
וְעַל כֵּן הָעָרְלָה נִקְרָא עַל שְׁמָם,
Therefore the prepuce (orlah) is named after them,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִהְיוֹת נִמּוֹלִים כְּלָל,
for it is impossible for them to become circumcised in soul at all;
כִּי הַמִּילָה הוּא חוֹתַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁהַיְּהוּדִי כּוֹרֵת עִם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
because circumcision is the seal of the covenant that the Jew cuts with the Blessed Name,
לִהְיוֹת נֶאֱמָן לֵאלֹהָיו בִּמְסִירַת כָּל כֹּחוֹת גּוּפוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ אֵלָיו לְגַמְרֵי מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן,
to remain faithful to his God through the total surrender of all bodily and psychic faculties to Him from birth, from the womb,
שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַדַּעַת וְהַהֲבָנָה וְהַכָּרַת הַשֵּׂכֶל,
transcending intellectual reason, comprehension, and human cognition,
רַק שֶׁבְּטִבְעוֹ וְתוֹלַדְתּוֹ הוּא כֵּן.
proceeding strictly as his inborn, innate spiritual nature.

דְּעַל כֵּן אֲפִלּוּ עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ מוּלִים (נְדָרִים לא1315 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along. עַמּוּד ב),
Wherefore even uncircumcised Jews are halachically called circumcised (Nedarim 31b);
וְהַיְנוּ אֲפִלּוּ מוּמָר לַעֲרָלוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית
meaning even an apostate regarding uncircumcision who fails to guard the covenant
וּמְטַמֵּא עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי טֻמְאוֹת,
and defiles himself with every variety of impurity,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִנָּתֵק שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ,
it is impossible to sever the status and name of Israel from him,
שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בְּתוֹלַדְתּוֹ מוֹרָשָׁה מֵהָאָבוֹת,
which is the innate power of Jewishness inborn in him as an inheritance from the Patriarchs,
וּמִיָּד כְּשֶׁיִּרְצֶה לָשׁוּב, כֹּחוֹ יָפֶה לִמְסֹר כָּל כֹּחוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ לְגַמְרֵי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the moment he desires to return, he possesses full spiritual power to surrender all faculties of his soul entirely to the Blessed Name.
וְכַנּוֹדָע בְּדוֹרוֹת הַשְּׁמָד, אֲפִלּוּ הַרְבֵּה מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מָסְרוּ עַצְמָם עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם,
And as was known in generations of persecution, even many of the transgressors of Israel surrendered their lives for the sanctification of the Divine Name,

וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סה)1316 Bereshit Rabbah 65:22 — Yakum of Tzerorot was the nephew of R. Yose ben Yoezer of Tzeredah. He rode by on a horse on the Sabbath as his uncle was going out to be hanged, and said to him: See the horse my master has mounted me upon, and see the horse your Master has mounted you upon. He answered him: If it is thus for those who anger Him, how much more so for those who do His will. ... The words entered him like a serpent's venom, and he went and carried out upon himself the four death penalties of the court. R. Yose ben Yoezer dozed off and saw his bier flying through the air, and said: In one brief hour this man has gone before me into the Garden of Eden. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 6): Like Tzadok and Boethus, Yakum of Tzerorot, the nephew of Yose ben Yoezer, was at first seduced and betrayed the holiness of Israel, saying to Yose ben Yoezer, "See the horse my master has mounted me upon" — for he was riding a horse on the Sabbath — "and see the horse your Master has mounted you upon," the beam on which he was to be hanged; this may have resembled Tzadok's heresy against the Oral Torah, since riding on the Sabbath is only a rabbinic prohibition. Nevertheless the words of Yose ben Yoezer entered his heart, and he carried out upon himself the four death penalties of the court and in a brief hour preceded Yose into the Garden of Eden. This is "the scent of his garments," expounded as "the scent of his traitors": from the scent of their earlier betrayal they rose to greater eminence, for the inwardness of their hearts was revealed — that at the root Israel are bound to holiness, even the lightest of the light, as these had been before. גַּבֵּי יָקוּם אִישׁ צְרוֹרוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
and likewise in Bereishit Rabbah (end of parashah 65) regarding Yakum of Tzerorot and similar figures.
וְזֶהוּ רְשִׁימַת הַדָּם עַל הַפֶּתַח,
And this was the inscription of the blood upon the entrance:

דְּאַף דִּ"בְּרֵישׁ כָּל מַרְעִין אֲנָא דָם" (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא נח1317 Bava Batra 58b — He saw that it was written there: "At the head of all death am I, blood; at the head of all life am I, wine." [He said:] If so, one who falls from a roof and dies, or falls from a palm tree and dies — did blood kill him? And further, one who is bound to die — do they give him wine to drink and he lives? Rather, this is what should be written: At the head of all illness am I, blood; at the head of all healing am I, wine; and in a place where there is no wine, there drugs are required. Rashbam: The inscription meant that a man dies only of an excess of blood which he failed to let at its proper season, and that wine sustains all who drink it; "one who is bound to die" means one already in his death throes. According to the corrected wording, all a man's illnesses arise from blood that grows excessive in him, and wine stands at the head of all remedies because one who drinks it as he should will not come to illness at all — and where wine is not to be had, illnesses abound and drugs must be sought for healing. Maharsha: Even on the corrected wording one might object that a man who falls from a roof and is injured was not made ill by blood. It seems, then, that the corrected version speaks not of bodily illness but of the illnesses of the soul — "for the blood is the soul" — since most evil traits, anger and envy and hatred and the like, depend upon an excess of blood; and wine is the head of all healing of the soul, as "wine gladdens the heart of man," or else it alludes to the wisdom and inner sense of the Torah, which is likened to wine. "And in a place where there is no wine" — where that keenness of wisdom is wanting — "there drugs [simmanin] are required," that is, mnemonic signs, for those who are not sharp acquire their learning by signs that recall it to them. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 11): All the illness of Egypt came upon them through Pharaoh's arrogance in saying "Who is the Lord?"; and "At the head of all illness am I, blood," for the blood begets haughtiness of spirit: the soul is the blood, and eating and drinking add to the blood and so add to pride and to every kind of illness. Only after one has prayed "for one's blood" — prayer being essentially submission and lowliness of heart, recognizing that one has nothing of one's own — does one quiet the turbulence of the blood and become a channel for drawing the Lord's blessing into all one's food and drink. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Large Aleph Small Aleph 5): The name Adam opens with aleph, alluding to the unity of the Blessed One, which is the purpose of man's creation, and ends with dam (blood). Likewise Bava Basra puts first "At the head of all illness am I, blood," for this is the end of every man, and "the living shall lay it to heart": the wise man, "whose eyes are in his head," should set the end as the beginning and proclaim the unity of the Blessed One, like R. Akiva, whose soul departed with "One." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 1): The seat of the nefesh, of the world of Action, is the liver — "for the blood is the soul," and "the essence of the blood is the liver" — and it is mostly evil. The blood is the husk of Esau, who the Midrash says hates the blood of man in his body; it corresponds to the husk of anger, as "the liver grows angry," and it is the root of all the husks, as they said, "At the head of all illness am I, blood." Only in Israel is there a holy nefesh, for there is an anger of the Sages that is good on every side. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Malachei HaShares 4): The portion of the blood is the nefesh, which is "at the head of all illness": whereas the neshamah is wholly the Lord's, the nefesh is blended and kneaded with the material body and therefore inclines especially after it. "And at the head of all healing am I, wine": wine is the Oral Torah, the drink that issues from the vine, which is Israel, flowing from the heart of the Sages of Israel and coming forth from their minds; it is at the head of healing for all the illnesses that come from the bad blood, for it guides all the parts of action to be conducted according to the will of the Lord. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 1): The whitening of the face [in shame] comes when the red drains away — that is, the blood, on account of which sin comes, for "the blood is the soul," the animal soul in man from which sin issues, of which the plain sense of "a soul that sins" speaks; so too Bava Basra says, "At the head of all illness am I, blood." Therefore, when the sin is mentioned while the past is not yet rectified, his blood is absorbed within him. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 244): David attained only the portion of the nefesh, and there lies the root of sin, as it says "a soul (nefesh) that sins" and "the blood is the soul," and "At the head of all illness am I, blood," for in the blood is the root of the soul's sickness toward every kind of craving, of lust and of murder. Therefore all his self-mortifications were to slay the evil inclination by fasting, because of the heavy stone in his heart. עַמּוּד ב),
that although "at the head of all sicknesses am I, the blood" (Bava Batra 58b),
שֶׁהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית שֶׁמִּכֹּחָהּ כָּל מִינֵי רָע שֶׁבַּגּוּף,
referring to the animal soul from whose energy stems every bodily evil,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם מוֹסְרִים וּמַקְרִיבִים זֶה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
nevertheless they surrender and sacrifice even this to the Blessed Name.
וְזֶהוּ הָעֵצָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְקַבֵּל גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה וְלֹא תֵצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ,
And this is the sacred counsel whereby one can receive the revelation of the Shechinah and not have his soul expire;
אַדְּרַבָּה, יַמְשִׁיךְ חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ וְתוֹסֶפֶת חַיּוּת עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵקוּת בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,
on the contrary, he draws down fresh vitality and an increase of life through cleaving to the living God,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַקְרָבַת כָּל כֹּחוֹת וְחַיּוּת נַפְשׁוֹ הַטִּבְעִיִּים הַמֻּשְׁרָשִׁים בּוֹ, כֻּלָּם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which occurs through dedicating all natural faculties and soul-vitality rooted within him, all of them, to the Blessed Name.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם,
For this is the root of the holiness of the Congregation of Israel, and it is the root of their vitality;
דְּכָל חַיּוּת אִישׁ הַיְּהוּדִי הוּא רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר מַכִּיר זֶה בְּבֵרוּר גָּמוּר
for the entire vitality of a Jewish person exists only when he recognizes with absolute clarity
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ עַצְמוֹ, רַק כָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמְסָרָם אֵלָיו.
that he possesses no independent power of his own, but all his faculties stem from the Blessed Name and are surrendered to Him.
וְזֶהוּ הַיְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לְאֻמָּה שְׁלֵמָה מְיֻחֶדֶת לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And this is the Exodus from Egypt, through which Israel became a complete nation uniquely consecrated to the Blessed Name,
וּלְהָאֻמּוֹת זֶהוּ מִיתָתָם;
while for the nations, such total surrender is their death;
וּמִצְרַיִם בְּיִחוּד הֵם הַקְּלִפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת הִתְגַּלּוּת אֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
and Egypt specifically was the husk encasing the manifestation of the Jewish nation as an independent people,
דְּעַל כֵּן שִׁעְבְּדוּם וְרָצוּ לְעַכֵּב הִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה.
wherefore they enslaved them and sought to obstruct this manifestation.
וְדַוְקָא שָׁם נִבְנוּ לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
Yet precisely there they were forged into a nation in their own right,
וְ"כַאֲשֶׁר יְעַנּוּ... כֵּן יִרְבֶּה".
and "as they afflicted them... so did they multiply."
וּבְגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה, שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת שֹׁרֶשׁ מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַחַיּוּת שֶׁל אֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
And through the revelation of the Shechinah, which is the disclosure of the root attribute of Knesset Yisrael and the vitality of the Jewish people,
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹכָם,
which comes from the Blessed Name dwelling in their midst,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְרַם מִמֵּילָא מִיתָה לִבְכוֹרֵי מִצְרַיִם,
there was automatically caused the death of the firstborn of Egypt,
דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם הוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִגִּלּוּי זֶה.
for the root of their vitality is the direct opposite of this holy disclosure.
וְהֻבְטְחוּ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁלֹּא יוֹסִיפוּ לִרְאוֹתָם עַד עוֹלָם,
And they were promised at the splitting of the Red Sea that they would never see Egypt again forever,
הַיְנוּ שֶׁכְּבָר נִבְחֲרוּ וְנִקְבְּעוּ לִכְנֵסִיָּה מְיֻחֶדֶת וְעַם מְיֻחָד,
meaning that they had already been chosen and permanently established as a distinct congregation and a unique people,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִרְאוֹת עוֹד עִנְיַן מִצְרַיִם,
and it became impossible for them ever again to experience the state of Egypt,
שֶׁהוּא הַקְּלִפָּה הַמַּעֲלֶמֶת הִתְגַּלּוּת עַם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי.
which is the husk that totally obscures the visible identity of the people of Israel.
דְּזֶה לֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם,
For this total concealment shall never happen again for all eternity,
דִּבְכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת לֹא נִתְעָרְבוּ בֵּין הַגּוֹיִם כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם: "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי",
for throughout all the exiles they never merged among the nations as they had in Egypt, as "a nation within a nation,"
וְכָל רוֹאֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּם לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, מְצֻיָּן וּמֻבְדָּל.
and all who behold them recognize them as a distinct nation, marked and set apart.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּסְרָה קְלִפָּה זוֹ הַמַּעֲלֶמֶת גִּלּוּי הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
And when this husk concealing the revelation of "truth to Jacob" was removed,
נִתְיָרְאוּ כָּל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מֵהֶם,
all the nations of the world were filled with dread before them,
דְּ"רָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם ה' נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ וְיָרְאוּ מִמֶּךָּ".
as "all peoples of the earth saw that the Name of Hashem is called upon you, and they feared you."
עַד שֶׁבָּא עֲמָלֵק וְקֵרְרָהּ בִּפְנֵיהֶם,
Until Amalek came and cooled that dread before them,
כִּי הוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
for he is "the first of the nations,"
שֹׁרֶשׁ הַדִּמְיוֹן הַחוֹשֵׁב וּמְדַמֶּה הַדִּמְיוֹן לֶאֱמֶת,
the root of delusion that conceptualizes and equates fantasy with truth,
וְהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם דְּעֵשָׂו, לוֹמַר: "טָהוֹר אֲנִי".
and he is the root of Esau's stretching forth split hooves to say: "I am kosher and pure."
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּלְחָם עִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
Therefore he was the first to wage war against the children of Israel after the Exodus from Egypt,
שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for as the inception of the construction of Knesset Yisrael was revealed,

נִתְגַּלָּה גַּם כֵּן זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה הַתְחָלַת הָאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הַמִּתְדַּמֵּית לְאֵשֶׁת חַיִל כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קמח עַמּוּד ב1318 Zohar 2:148b — And we have learned: everywhere this serpent follows after the mystery of the woman of valor, and the woman of harlotry seeks to array herself in her likeness, but cannot. The woman of valor — her mark and her letter is the letter heh, and so it befits her. The woman of harlotry — her mark and her letter has that same form, yet she is not fitted to be so; her letter is kuf, arrayed in the arrangement of the letter heh — like an ape alongside human beings, which goes after people though it is not fitted to do so. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:45): The woman of harlotry was created with the letter kuf, as the Zohar (Terumah) says; yet this is one of the holy letters, of the very essence of the Blessed One, for He wished there to be the resemblance of "an ape before a man," as Bava Basra says, "Man before the Shechinah is like an ape before a man" — the Shechinah being the mystery of the woman of valor, and man her likeness, so that from the root of man's creation spread the creation of the woman of harlotry in the likeness of the woman of valor, but intending for herself. Yet until the thing issues into action it is a creation of the Blessed One, who willed this force to exist and willed man, by his free choice, to restrain himself from acting against His will; therefore, before it acted, [the serpent] was "more cunning than all," resembling the woman of valor "like an ape before a man." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 1): The woman of harlotry is she who wishes to resemble the woman of valor "like an ape before a man," as the holy Zohar says; this is the outspread split hoof of the pig that was in Esau, who wished to resemble Jacob until Isaac erred regarding him.).
there was likewise revealed, "this opposite that," the inception of the harlot mimicking the woman of valor like an ape mimicking a human being (Zohar, Part II, 148b).
וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹת הַדִּמְיוֹן אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיסָם לִקְדֻשָּׁה,
The outspread branches of imaginative forces can be brought into holiness,
כִּי כָּל כֹּחַ פְּרָטִי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית,
for every specific faculty on its own is one of the powers of the animal soul,
וְהַיְּהוּדִי שֶׁמּוֹסֵר כָּל נַפְשׁוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתָן הַכֹּחוֹת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the Jew who dedicates his entire soul to the Blessed Name utilizes those faculties in holiness according to the will of the Blessed Name.
וְאוֹתָן מַצָּעוֹת שֶׁהִצִּיעָה בְּאִסּוּר בְּגַיּוּת,
And those very couches and garments she arranged in forbidden immorality during gentiledom,

אֶפְשָׁר לְהַצִּיעָן בְּהֶתֵּר בְּיַהֲדוּת1319 Menachot 44a — There was once a man who was scrupulous in the commandment of tzitzit. He heard of a certain harlot in the coastal cities who took four hundred gold pieces as her fee. He sent her the four hundred gold pieces and she set him a time. When his time came he went and sat at her door. Her maidservant went in and said to her: That man who sent you four hundred gold pieces has come and is sitting at the door. She said: Let him come in. He came in. She had set out for him seven beds, six of silver and one of gold, and between each of them a ladder of silver, and the topmost of gold. She went up and sat upon the topmost, and he went up to sit facing her. The four fringes of his garment came and struck him across the face. He slipped down and sat upon the ground, and she too came down and sat upon the ground. She said to him: By the Capitol of Rome, I shall not let you go until you tell me what blemish you have found in me. He said to her: By the Temple service, I have seen no blemish in you, for there is none as fair as you in all the world — but there is one commandment that the Lord our God has commanded us, and tzitzit is its name, and concerning it “I am the Lord your God” is written twice: I am He who is destined to exact punishment, and I am He who is destined to give reward. Now they appeared to me as four witnesses. She said to him: I shall not let you go until you tell me your name, and the name of your city, and the name of your teacher, and the name of the study hall in which you learn Torah. He wrote it and placed it in her hand. She arose and divided all her property — a third to the government, a third to the poor, and a third she took in her hand, apart from those bedcoverings — and she came to the study hall of R. Chiya. She said to him: My master, instruct that they make me a convert. He said to her: My daughter, have you perhaps set your eyes upon one of the students? She brought out the writing she held and gave it to him. He said to her: Go and take possession of your purchase. Those same coverings that she had spread for him forbidden, she now spread for him permitted. This was his reward in this world; and as for the World to Come, I do not know how much. Rashi: "By the Capitol of Rome" — she swore by the life of the king, who is the guardian prince of Rome; another reading: by an idol. "She brought out the writing she held" — and told him all that had happened, that she was converting for the sake of Heaven, because she had learned of the great miracle of the weight of the commandments, that his four fringes struck him across the face. "Those same coverings" — she had not sold them but brought them with her, and they were his reward in this world. Tosafos (s.v. "to the study hall of R. Chiya"): This is not [the well-known] R. Chiya, for R. Natan, who was more eminent than Rabbi — as they said, "It was youthfulness in me, and I was insolent toward Natan the Babylonian" (Bava Batra 131a) — would not have adduced a proof from R. Chiya; and in the Tosefta the reading is "to the study hall of R. Meir." Maharsha: "I am the Lord" means, as they expound everywhere, that I am faithful to exact punishment and to pay reward; and "your God" is added here because this commandment itself testifies to that, since in our garments we differ from all the nations, that we are His people and He is our God. Exacting punishment is put first because at the first "I am the Lord your God" the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned — I am the Lord who distinguished in Egypt between the drop of a firstborn and that of one who was not a firstborn, and I am He who will exact punishment from one who hangs indigo on his garment and says it is sky-blue. That is why he said the four fringes appeared to him as four witnesses: they are witnesses from a man's four sides that He is our God. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Menachos 44a): This man was pursuing his desire to the point of spending a great sum upon it, four hundred gold pieces — and four hundred is tav, beyond which there is no number in the alphabet — and that she was in the coastal cities shows that he put himself to the trouble of a long journey, and all of it for harlotry; the seven beds are seven grades of adornment that bring a man to desire. The four fringes came as witnesses, for a witness is nothing other than one who brings out into the open the thing he testifies to, and by the fringes a man is brought out into act. And against harlotry in particular the fringes bear witness, for they show that a man cleaves to the commandments of God, and harlotry is the opposite of this. (מְנָחוֹת מד עַמּוּד א).
can be arranged in permissible sanctity within Judaism (Menachot 44a).
אֲבָל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַדִּמְיוֹן, שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְדַּמּוּת הַדִּמְיוֹן לֶאֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק,
However, the very core of illusion—which is the mimicry claiming illusion is absolute truth, the core of Amalek—
זֶה אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה אֶלָּא לִמְחוֹתוֹ;
for this there is no rectification except to utterly wipe it out;
וּבָזֶה נַעֲשָׂה אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם הַדִּמְיוֹן אֱמֶת,
and through this, among the children of Israel, even the imagination is transformed into truth,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁ"נַהֲפֹךְ הוּא".
which occurs through the principle of "it was reversed."
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּיֵשׁ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי מִתּוּק לַיֵּצֶר: לְאִכְפַּיָּא וּלְאַהְפָּכָא.
As is known, there are two modes of sweetening the inclination: subjugating it (itkafya) and transforming it (ithapkha).
וּלְאִכְפַּיָּא הַיְנוּ שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בַּמְּצִיאוּת עֲדַיִן,
Subjugation means that it still remains in existence,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת אִסּוּר,
only that one does not obey it to commit a sin,
וְכוֹפֵהוּ לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָע לַעֲצַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַיֵּצֶר טוֹב.
and compels it to submit to the counsel of the Torah and the good inclination.
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר גַּם לֶעָתִיד,
And this is the power of the inclination that will endure in the future,

רַק דְּנִקְרָא לָבָן דְּאִתְלַבַּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלז עַמּוּד א1320 Zohar 1:137a — "The sister of Laban the Aramean" (Genesis 25:20) — the sister of the evil inclination, the deceiver. As we have learned: at first, while it is befouled with sins in this world, it is called Lot; but in the time to come, when it will not be befouled as before, but like one who bathes and immerses away his defilement, they call it Lavan, the white one. In any case, the evil inclination is not abolished from the world. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): I heard that Shittim denotes folly [shtut], which will be healed in the future — "a spring shall come forth from the house of the Lord and water the valley of Shittim" — that is, after the slaughter of the evil inclination, which is called Laban because it is whitened, as written in Midrash HaNe'elam, and as the Sages said on the verse "a heart of flesh," that it will be only a heart to bring forth flesh. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 9): The evil inclination was created to serve man in permitted needs that aid the service of the Blessed One — that is, once a person subdues it so that he rules over it and his heart is in his control; then the evil inclination is called Laban, for it has been whitened, as they said in Midrash HaNe'elam of the time to come, that it will not be entirely abolished but only whitened. This is like what they said on "I will give you a heart of flesh" — a heart to bring forth flesh — and this is its servitude to the form of man in all the bad traits within the inclination's power, which also have some needed use.),
only that it is termed "white" because it has been purified, as taught in Midrash HaNe'elam (Zohar, Part I, 137a),
שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְבַטְּלוֹ לְגַמְרֵי.
since it does not need to be eliminated completely.
אֲבָל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע וְעִקָּרוֹ יְבֻטַּל לְגַמְרֵי לֶעָתִיד,
However, the root of the evil inclination and its core will be abolished completely in the future,
וְזֶהוּ הַחֵלֶק מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְאַהְפָּכָא,
and this is the dimension regarding which our striving in this world is to transform it,
שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂה מִמֶּנּוּ טוֹב,
so that good shall be made from it,
וְיִתְבַּטֵּל הָרַע לְגַמְרֵי מֵהָעוֹלָם מְעַט מְעַט,
and evil will be eliminated entirely from the world step by step,
עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעוּ לִזְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
until they reach the slaughtering of the evil inclination in the time to come,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּשֶׁיִּמָּחֶה זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי.
which will occur when the seed of Amalek is blotted out from the world completely.
דְּהַכֹּל אֶחָד, כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע בָּעוֹלָם
For all is one: since from Amalek stems the root of the evil inclination in the world,
הַנִּמְשָׁךְ גַּם לְלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which extends also into the hearts of the children of Israel,
שֶׁצְּרִיכִים לִמְחוֹתוֹ וְלִהְיוֹת "נַהֲפֹךְ",
which they must wipe out and bring about the reversal,
שֶׁיִּשְׁלְטוּ הַיְּהוּדִים הֵמָּה בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם —
so that the Jews themselves rule over their enemies—
הֵם שׂוֹנְאֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּיַהֲדוּת,
meaning the spiritual enemies of Jewish soulhood,
שֶׁהוּא מְסִירַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which consists of the total surrender of the soul to the Blessed Name.
וַעֲמָלֵק שׂוֹנֵא זֶה,
And Amalek despises this surrender,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ1321 Bereshit Rabbah 63:13 — “For I shall make you blood, and blood shall pursue you” — if you have not hated blood, then blood shall pursue you. And Esav hated blood. R. Shmuel bar Nachman said: This is the blood of the firstborn service and of the offerings. R. Levi said: This is the blood of circumcision. (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג) עַל פָּסוּק "דָּם שָׂנֵאתָ":
as they expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 63) on the verse "you hated blood":
דַּם הַפֶּסַח וְדַם הַמִּילָה,
referring to the blood of the Passover offering and the blood of circumcision,
דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם מְיֻחָדִים בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
both of which are unique to the children of Israel alone,
הַמְבַטְּלִים כָּל כֹּחוֹת נַפְשָׁם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
who nullify all faculties of their souls to the Blessed Name.
וַעֲמָלֵק, שֶׁהוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם", הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַשִּׂנְאָה לְכֹחַ זֶה,
And Amalek, who is "the first of the nations," is the wellspring of hatred against this power,
כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַדִּמְיוֹן — שֶׁהוּא הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹן אֱמֶת —
for the root of illusion—which is the fantasy that illusion is truth—
מְדַמֶּה שֶׁזֶּה אֱמֶת שֶׁ"הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִבְנֵי אָדָם" לִהְיוֹת כֹּחוֹת נִפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
imagines it to be true that "the earth He gave to the children of men" to exist as independent entities separate from the Blessed Name.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם,
And this is the mystical lack wherein the Divine Name is not whole,
דְּהַיְנוּ יִחוּד עוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים עִם הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
namely the unification of the upper realms with the lower realms,
כִּי כָל חֵפֶץ עֲמָלֵק לְהַפְרִיד הָאָרֶץ וּמְלֹאָהּ וְכֹחוֹת הַנִּבְרָאִים כֻּלָּם מֵהַבּוֹרֵא.
for the entire desire of Amalek is to sever the earth and all that fills it and all created forces from the Creator.
וְעַל כֵּן חָשַׁב לְאַבֵּד הַיְּהוּדִים,
Therefore he conspired to destroy the Jews,
שֶׁהֵם הַמּוֹרִידִים שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
who draw down the Shechinah into the lower realms,
וּמְחַבְּרִים הַבּוֹרֵא עִם הַנִּבְרָאִים וּמְיַחֲדִים הַכֹּל;
and join the Creator with the creations and unify all;
וְהוּא שׂוֹנֵא יִחוּד זֶה שֶׁל בִּטּוּל הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית גַּם כֵּן בִּמְקוֹרָהּ,
and he hates this unification through which even the animal soul is nullified in its supernal Source,
לִהְיוֹת יִחוּד גָּמוּר גַּם מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם.
so that complete oneness prevails after the creation of the world just as it was before the world was created.
דְּבָזֶה אֵין מָקוֹם לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ וְהִתְפָּאֲרוּתוֹ
For under this oneness there is no place for his expansion and self-aggrandizement
בִּכְבוֹד עָשְׁרוֹ וְרֹב בָּנָיו וַאֲשֶׁר גִּדְּלוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ,
in the glory of his riches, the multitude of his sons, and how the king elevated him,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל הָאָדָם הַגַּשְׁמִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִצַּד גּוּפָנִיּוּתוֹ:
which represents the whole striving of corporeal man in this world from his bodily perspective:
כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וּמַאֲוַיָּיו לִזְכּוֹת לְעֹשֶׁר,
all his striving and longings are to attain wealth,
שֶׁבָּזֶה יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ לְכָל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת,
through which he can achieve all kinds of desires,
וּלְכָבוֹד, וּבִכְלָלוֹ גַּם הֲסָרַת הַקִּנְאָה, כִּי כְּלוּם מִתְקַנֵּא גָּדוֹל בְּקָטָן;
and honor, including the elimination of envy, for an elite person does not envy the lowly;
וּלְבָנִים, שֶׁבָּזֶה חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הַנִּצְחִיּוּת גַּם כֵּן וְהַקִּיּוּם בַּמִּין,
and children, through which he imagines he secures eternity and continuity of species,
אַחַר שֶׁיָּמוּת עֲדַיִן יִשָּׁאֵר גִּזְעוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
so that after he dies his branch will still endure in this world.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵמוּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִבְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
And this is the pinnacle of worldly perfection for the people of this world.
וְהַהִתְפָּאֲרוּת בִּשְׁלֵמוּת זֶה הוּא רַק לַמְשֻׁקָּע בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנִפְרָד לְגַמְרֵי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And boasting in such worldly perfection belongs only to one immersed in this world and totally severed from the Blessed Name,
כְּגוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת אֲשֶׁר הֵם יִתְהַלְלוּ:
like the gentile nations who glory in themselves:
"הֶחָכָם בְּחָכְמָתוֹ", שֶׁזָּכָה לְכָבוֹד אֲשֶׁר חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ;
"the wise man in his wisdom," boasting in the honor sages inherit;
וְ"הַגִּבּוֹר בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ", שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְנֵי הַנְּעוּרִים אֲשֶׁר הֵם "כְּחִצִּים בְּיַד גִּבּוֹר" וּכְאִישׁ גְּבוּרָתוֹ;
and "the mighty man in his might," boasting in youthful sons who are "like arrows in the hand of a warrior";
וְ"הֶעָשִׁיר בְּעָשְׁרוֹ".
and "the rich man in his riches."
אֲבָל הַנָּבִיא אָמַר שֶׁלֹּא יִתְהַלְלוּ בָּזֶה,
Yet the prophet declared that one must not glory in these,
כִּי אִם "בְּהַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדֹעַ אוֹתִי",
but only in "understanding and knowing Me,"
דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁמַּכִּיר דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
which means recognizing that everything is from the Blessed Name:
כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ וְעָשְׁרוֹ וּכְבוֹדוֹ וְרֹב בָּנָיו,
all of one's wisdom, strength, wealth, honor, and multitude of children,
הַכֹּל לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לָתֵת לוֹ,
all exist solely because the Blessed Name willed to bestow them upon him,
וְלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם,
and he has nothing whatsoever of his own,
וְכָךְ יוּכַל לָתֵת לְאַחֵר כְּמוֹ לוֹ;
and just as He gave to him, He could give to another;
וּבַמֶּה יִתְהַלֵּל?
and in what then shall he boast?
רַק הוּא תְּהִלָּתוֹ מַה שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
His sole praise is this: that he acknowledges that everything comes from the Blessed Name.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא שְׁלִיטַת הַיְּהוּדִים בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם,
And through this realization comes the dominion of the Jews over their enemies,
וּשְׁלִיטַת מָרְדֳּכַי עַל בֵּית הָמָן,
and the dominion of Mordechai over the house of Haman,
וְנִתַּן לוֹ כָּל הַכָּבוֹד וְהָעֹשֶׁר,
whereby all honor and wealth were granted to him,
וְכֵן מִסְּתָמָא גַּם לְרֹב בָּנִים,
and so too, presumably, an abundance of children,
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר: "דֹּבֵר שָׁלוֹם לְכָל זַרְעוֹ", כִּי זָכָה לְזֶרַע רַב גַּם כֵּן.
which is why Scripture states: "speaking peace to all his seed," for he was blessed with abundant offspring as well.

כִּי "בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנֵי לָאו בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא" (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח1322 Moed Katan 28a — Rava said: Length of life, children, and sustenance do not depend on merit but on fortune. For Rabbah and R. Chisda were both righteous sages: this one would pray and rain would come, and that one would pray and rain would come. R. Chisda lived ninety-two years, Rabbah lived forty. In R. Chisda's house there were sixty wedding feasts; in Rabbah's house, sixty bereavements. Tosafos (s.v. "rather, it depends upon fortune"): They asked in Tosafot: but we said at the end of Shabbat that "Israel is not subject to a constellation"! One may answer that sometimes a man's lot is changed, as in the cases there, and sometimes it is not changed — as is said in Taanit concerning R. Elazar ben Pedat, to whom it was said: Would it please you that I destroy the world, so that perhaps you might be created anew at an hour of sustenance? Tosafos (s.v. "sixty wedding feasts"): Some explain that the number is not meant exactly. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. "it depends upon fortune"): Tosafot's answer — and in Tosafot at Shabbat it is more explicit — is that "Israel is not subject to a constellation" means that by great merit one's fortune is changed. And so it is proved from our own passage, for Rava asked for Rav Huna's wisdom and Rav Chisda's wealth, which are matters fixed by the decree at birth, since the angel sets up the drop and asks whether it shall be wise or foolish, rich or poor; perforce one must say that by an abundance of pleading for mercy from Heaven, as Rava did, the decree and the constellation under which a man was born can be annulled. Maharal (Derech Chaim 4:9): If we see one who is not a wholly righteous man, and he is a poor Torah scholar, this too has its cause: his ill fortune brings it about, for "life, children and sustenance do not depend upon merit." And even of a wholly righteous man one may say the same, that his ill fortune is the cause — as we find with R. Elazar ben Pedat in Taanit, whose fortune was so exceedingly bad that he had no sustenance at all. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:98): Although children, life and sustenance "do not depend on merit but on mazal" — one's hidden root — the whole Torah is full of reward and punishment in these three, for through merit the mazal changes, as one's deeds incline the hidden root. Yet sometimes both men are completely righteous, as with Rabbah and R. Chisda — which Rosh Hashanah attributes to Rabbah's descent from the house of Eli — and in truth this is what is called mazal: a hidden root drawn from one's forebears, though he himself did nothing. Effort still helped, but because of his mazal Rabbah needed more effort, while less sufficed for R. Chisda. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): Children, life and sustenance comprise all of a person's needs in this world, where there is no reward for a commandment, and so they are decreed at the beginning of formation — "wise or foolish, strong or weak, rich or poor" — whereas "righteous or wicked," which is merit, is not. Yet the Torah promises all three as reward, for insofar as they bear on Torah and the commandments — long life to multiply Torah, children to serve God, a ready livelihood — they certainly depend on merit, which can change the mazal; what depends on mazal, decreed at formation, is given even where it does not aid the service of God. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 15): Children, life and sustenance, which "do not depend on merit but on mazal," cannot be attained through prayer; hence they said that sustenance and matching a couple are as hard as the splitting of the Sea. Although we petition for sustenance in every prayer, that is for one born in an hour of sustenance or who prays at a time of favor; but for one not so born, like R. Elazar ben Pedas, it depends on the supernal mazal in Atika, and prayer no longer avails — only Torah and calling to Him in truth, which is above mazal. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Balak 6): The root of all blessings is life, children and sustenance, which "do not depend on merit but on mazal"; the Zohar teaches that this is the attribute of Atika, which is "upon the Lord," as in "Hannah prayed upon the Lord" and "cast your burden upon the Lord" — the tip of the yod above the letters of the Name, alluding to Ayin [Nothingness]. When one merits the primordial light, the dew of Atika, one merits these three. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 1): The souls of converts too were at Mount Sinai, as the Sages said, "their mazal was there" — and mazal is a person's root, as I have written elsewhere on "a person has a mazal" and on children, life and sustenance, which "depend on mazal." Beis Yaakov (Vayechi 45): Of sustenance the Sages said that it "does not depend on merit" — that is, not on the service a person performs with knowledge and clarity when his mind is clear and settled — "but on mazal": holiness must be engraved in his heart so permanently that it does not budge even when his knowledge and clarity are diminished. This is called mazal because service flows from him of itself, even without his awareness; sustenance must be drawn from a place above merit, from the supernal will called mazal. עַמּוּד א),
For "children, life, and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal" (Moed Katan 28a),
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמַזָּלָא הַיְנוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ בִּמְקוֹרָהּ,
and it is known that mazal denotes the soul's supernal root in its transcendent source,
הַמַּזִּיל וּמַטִּיף חַיּוּת לְכָל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ;
which drips and channels vitality to all outward extensions of the soul;
וְ"אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל", יָדוּעַ הַפֵּרוּשׁ: שֶׁהָ"אַיִן" הוּא מַזָּלָם,
and regarding "there is no mazal for Israel," the well-known esoteric meaning is: the divine "Ayin" (Nothingness) is their mazal,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁשֹּׁרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם וְכֹחַ נַפְשָׁם הוּא שֶׁהֵם אַיִן וְאֶפֶס מִגַּרְמַיְהוּ,
meaning that the root of their vitality and soul-strength is that they are nothing and naught on their own,
רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ;
receiving only that which the Blessed Name bestows;
וְזֶהוּ הַמַּזִּיל וְהַמַּטִּיף לָהֶם הַשֶּׁפַע דְּבָנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנֵי.
and this Divine Nothingness is what drips and channels to them the bounty of children, life, and sustenance.
אֲבָל מִצַּד פְּרִידָתָם בְּיֵשׁוּת, כְּאִלּוּ הֵם יֵשׁ וְדָבָר נִפְרָד,
However, from the perspective of falling into egoistic separateness (yeshut), as if they were independent entities,
אֵין לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת וְשֶׁפַע דְּבָנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנֵי כְּלָל,
they possess no authentic existence or flow of children, life, and sustenance at all,
כִּי אֵינָם תַּחַת הַמַּזָּל דְּיֵשׁוּת שֶׁהוּא תַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם, מֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַכּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
because they are not placed beneath the cosmic mazal of worldly selfhood under the heavens—the rule of stars and constellations,
שֶׁהוּא הַמַּזָּל דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
which is the mazal governing the nations,
שֶׁהֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שֶׁפַע בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנֵי דְּיֵשׁוּת שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמַּזָּל שֶׁתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם.
who receive an egocentric flow of children, life, and sustenance through planetary determinism beneath the sky.
וַעֲמָלֵק, שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם,
And Amalek, who is "the first of the nations,"
הוּא הַמַּזָּלָא דְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
is the cosmic root-mazal of the nations of the world,
שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ הַשֶּׁפַע דְּבָנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנֵי לְכָל הָאֻמּוֹת;
through whom the egocentric flow of children, life, and sustenance is drawn to all gentile peoples;
וּכְשֶׁיִּמָּחֶה זַרְעוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם, יִתְבַּטֵּל כָּל הַשֶּׁפַע מֵאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
and when his seed is wiped out from the world, all that unholy bounty will be cut off from the nations,
וְיִהְיוּ גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
and they will become "dragged-along converts" in the future to come.
כִּי כָּל שֶׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן וְשֶׁפַע דְּהַאי עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא,
For all their bounty derives merely from illusion and the flow of this realm of falsehood,
שֶׁהוּא רַק "עַד אַרְגִּיעָה".
which endures only "for a fleeting moment."
וְהוּא חָשַׁב שֶׁזֶּה אֱמֶת;
And Haman imagined that this temporary vanity was absolute reality;
וּבְעֵת תַּכְלִית תָּקְפּוֹ וּגְדֻלָּתוֹ,
and at the very pinnacle of his power and grandeur,
שֶׁחָשַׁב לִתְלוֹת מָרְדֳּכַי וְ"לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר" וְכוּלֵי,
when he planned to hang Mordechai and assumed: "Whom would the king delight to honor more than myself...",
דְּעַתָּה יִגְדַּל כְּבוֹדוֹ עוֹד יוֹתֵר שֶׁיַּרְכִּיבוּהוּ בָּרְחוֹב וְגוֹמֵר,
presuming that his honor would now swell further by being paraded through the city street,
נַהֲפֹךְ הוּא,
the exact reverse occurred,
וְנִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ תַּכְלִית שִׁפְלוּתוֹ,
and there was exposed to him the ultimate depths of his degradation,
וְסוֹפוֹ לִתְלוֹתוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
culminating in him being hanged upon that very gallows.
וְרָאָה כִּי כָל כְּבוֹדוֹ דִּמְיוֹן,
And he saw that his entire honor was an illusion,
וּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ אֱמֶת — זֶה שֶׁקֶר גָּמוּר;
and his conviction that his illusion was truth was complete falsehood;
כִּי הָאֱמֶת שֶׁ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ" וְ"אַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם",
for the absolute truth is that "there is none else besides Him" and "You give life to them all,"
שֶׁאֵין חַיּוּת לְשׁוּם בְּרִיָּה וְדָבָר שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם אֶלָּא מֵחַיּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
in that there is no vitality in any creature or thing in the world other than His blessed life-force,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַפְרִיד כְּלָל הַנִּבְרָאִים מֵהַבּוֹרֵא,
and it is entirely impossible to separate the creations from the Creator,
דְּאָז לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל.
for then they would have no existence whatsoever.
וְהוּא נִמְחֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
And he is utterly wiped out from the world
כַּאֲשֶׁר פּוֹסֵק קַבָּלַת חַיּוּתוֹ מִבּוֹרְאוֹ.
when the reception of his sustained life-force from his Creator is brought to an end.

items.h:
Seif 3 — Holiness Hidden from the World's Eyes
Purim reveals divine rule within concealment and shows that Israel's covenantal holiness remains true despite outward appearances.

p: אֲבָל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעְלַם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּמְשָׁל לַלַּיְלָה וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה בַּלְּבָבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַכִּיר בְּבֵרוּר גָּמוּר
But this matter is concealed in this world, which is compared to night; and when it was revealed in the hearts of the children of Israel to recognize with absolute clarity
דְּגַם כׇּל הַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בְּכׇל מָשָׁלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אָז
that all the conduct of this world as well is from Him, blessed be He, and His kingship rules over all, as it was then,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה (יא.)1323 Megillah 11a — R. Yochanan introduced this passage with a verse from here: "He has remembered His mercy and His faithfulness toward the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God." When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordekhai and Esther. Rashi: "When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordecai" — because the matter became known to all the nations, for letters went out through the whole world. Maharsha: Many of that generation were liable to destruction for having enjoyed Ahasuerus's feast, and were spared only on account of Mordecai and the righteous of his company; hence the verse says "He has remembered His mercy" — for those who were not worthy of redemption — "and His faithfulness" — for those who were worthy. And because the redemption came through a woman, Esther, it says "toward the house of Israel," as in "Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob" — these are the women. "All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God" — because this deliverance reached the whole world, since, as the Gemara says further on, Ahasuerus reigned over the entire world. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Pesichah): This Megillah testifies to the renowned salvation that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed — not like the other miracles He did for them while Israel were in their own land and not under the hand of the nations, when the miracle was not revealed to the nations. But in the days of Ahasuerus, who ruled over the whole world, the salvation was wrought among the nations: when he decreed that Israel be destroyed and killed it was written throughout the land, and when the Holy One, blessed be He, saved them it became known to the whole world, and so "all the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God." Moreover, "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20), and when He saved them from Haman, of the seed of Amalek, it was as though He had saved them from all the nations; therefore all the ends of the earth saw it, for it was a great wonder in their eyes. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 4): "All the ends of the earth saw" does not refer to the nations of the world, for they did not see the salvation of our God, since it was clothed close to the way of nature, and the many who became Jews did so only out of fear of the Jews and of Mordechai. Rather, "all the ends of the earth" refers to Israel, who were then in the utmost lowliness and concealment, to the very ends of the earth, and precisely through this they saw the salvation of our God from within that very concealment. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 256): When Esther absorbed the trait of modesty, the salvation came in revelation, as in "When did all the ends of the earth see...? In the days of Mordechai and Esther." He had heard that "Megillah" denotes revelation, for then it was revealed that the way of nature too is the Blessed One's guidance, since the salvation came by way of nature and it was revealed to all that it was His doing — and this is the seeing of "all the ends of the earth." Salvation by way of nature is modesty and clothing rather than an open miracle, yet it is truly a greater revelation, even to the ends of the earth, for the recognition that nature too is from the Blessed One is the more manifest recognition. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Megillah): The miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, such as the Exodus and the splitting of the Sea, were beyond nature and are called "wonder"; the language of "seeing" does not fit them, for after the miracle the world remained as before, and only "hearing" applies. But in the miracle of Mordechai and Esther, which appeared to follow the course of nature, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed that all the ways of nature by which the world is conducted are likewise only for Israel's good, and to this the language of "seeing" applies, for it is evident to the eye at every moment. Tiferes Yosef (Purim 1): His honored grandfather and teacher explained: "the salvation of our God" denotes a salvation that endures forever, for with the Blessed One nothing is incidental; as He endures for all eternity, so His salvation endures for all eternity, akin to "Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation." Sod Yesharim (Purim 39): That is, they then saw plainly that all the concealment that had passed over them, and the salvation that followed, were all arranged in the Torah, and nothing new had been added to the Torah's order — as the Sages hinted, that the prophets neither took from nor added to what is written in the Torah except for the reading of the Megillah. Beforehand it had seemed that something new was being added, but once the Blessed One opened the salvation they recognized that it had all along been so arranged in the words of Torah, only it had been hidden from them through the concealment of Amalek. Sha'ar HaEmunah (Entrance to the Gate 14): The miracle of Purim was hidden, everything occurring by way of nature, and only after the miracle was revealed did they perceive how all the details combined into one miracle. This is "When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordechai and Esther": they reflected at the end and saw all the events together, and then they saw that the Blessed One guides all the nations even where they do not understand, though at the time His guidance appeared to follow the course of nature. אֵימָתַי רָאוּ כׇל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי וְעַד שֶׁרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים מֵעֵין דֻּגְמָא דִּלְעָתִיד.

as it is written in Megillah (11a), 'When did all the ends of the earth see...' and so forth? In the days of Mordechai; to the point that 'many of the peoples of the land became Jews,' a semblance of what will be in the future.
אָז כְּמוֹ דִּלְעָתִיד בְּשׁוּב הַשֵּׁם וְגוֹמֵר הָיִינוּ כְּחוֹלְמִים יִהְיֶה כׇּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כַּחֲלוֹם וְדִמְיוֹן בְּעָלְמָא כָּךְ רָאוּ אָז
Then, just as in the future, when 'Hashem returns...' and so forth, 'we will be like dreamers,' all the affairs of this world will be like a mere dream and illusion; so too they saw then
שֶׁכׇּל הַגְּזֵרָה וְהַפַּחַד שֶׁהָיָה עַל הַיְּהוּדִים מִקֹּדֶם הָיָה רַק חֲלוֹם וְדִמְיוֹן אֶלָּא שֶׁדִּמְיוֹן זֶה הוֹעִיל לְהָשִׁיב לְבָבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם
that the entire decree and fear that had previously been upon the Jews was only a dream and illusion. Yet this illusion served to return the hearts of the children of Israel to their Father

שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׂם יָד1324 Megillah 14a — "And the king removed his ring." R. Abba bar Kahana said: The removal of the ring was greater than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses who prophesied to Israel — for none of them turned them back to the good, whereas the removal of the ring turned them back to the good. Rashi (s.v. “returned them to the good way”): For they decreed fasts upon them for repentance, as it is written, “fasting, and weeping, and wailing; sackcloth and ashes were spread for many” (Esther 4:3). Maharsha: The king’s decree is made to depend upon the removal of the ring, for by it they were handed over to Haman, as the verse says, “the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you.” And in the Midrash: Ahasuerus hated Israel more [than Haman did] — the way of the world is that the buyer gives a pledge to the seller, yet here it is written, “And the king removed his ring.” That is the point here: the removal of the ring, in which they saw how great Ahasuerus’s hatred was, is what returned them to the good way, for they repented with their whole heart. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 3:10): The prophets prophesied of chastisement from the Holy One, blessed be He, so that it might not come upon them, and since He has compassion on His creatures, they were not so greatly afraid. But the removal of the ring showed that the king was removing this matter from himself and placing it in the hand of a man: as long as it is in a king's hand — and it is the Holy One, blessed be He, who establishes kings, so that they are like His messengers — they too do not wish to destroy everything; but when it is handed over to a commoner, him they fear. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 6): The essential salvation of Israel comes when they are saved in the very thing whose lack brought on the trouble, so that the healing grows from the blows themselves — as the Megillah says, "Greater was the removal of the ring...," for it returned them to the good, and in Perek Chelek this is taken as the model: "He sets over them a king as harsh as Haman." For in Haman's days they returned in complete repentance and accepted the whole Torah upon themselves and their descendants out of love; that was the essential salvation brought about through the decree, and with it the decree was annulled of itself. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): In the days of Haman Israel were returned to the good by something the forty-eight prophets had not achieved, as the Sages said, "Greater was the removal of the ring...": since "the king" in the Megillah means the King of the world, it was He who, as it were, removed the ring of His dominion for a short while and handed it to Haman, as though Haman were the ruler doing as he pleased. This was holiness clothing itself in Haman's sackcloth, because Israel were asleep from the mitzvos and could be roused only in this way, while the true intent was the opposite: to exalt Israel and to destroy Haman, the seed of Amalek and all Israel's enemies.) גְּדוֹלָה הֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת מֵאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה נְבִיאִים.
in Heaven, as it is written there (14a): 'Greater was the removal of the ring than forty-eight prophets.'

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צז:)1325 Sanhedrin 97b — R. Eliezer says: If Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. R. Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, are they not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, sets over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel repent, and He turns them back to the good. Maharsha: R. Eliezer's "if Israel repent" means a willed repentance, of their own accord, whereas R. Yehoshua holds that when the time of redemption comes, the Holy One, blessed be He, sets over them a king whose decrees are harsh and restores them to the good so that they repent — a compelled repentance. He rejects Rashi's reading that in R. Yehoshua's view they are redeemed without any repentance at all, for if so, why would R. Yehoshua speak of a king like Haman who restores them to the good? Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 97b): R. Eliezer does not mean that without repentance there will be no redemption and the matter will remain in doubt, for there is no doubt about the redemption of Israel; rather, exile is an accidental thing — in itself, for by the order of the world the Israelite nation ought to be in its land and not under the dominion of others, and if exile depends on sin, sin too is not essential but accidental, and what is accidental has no permanence — and God, blessed be He, will remove from them the sickness of the soul as He removes sickness of the body, as it is written, "And the Lord will circumcise your heart," so that it is impossible that they will not repent. R. Yehoshua did not hold that it depends specifically on Israel's repentance, as though the redemption lay in Israel's hands: Israel must indeed repent and then they will be redeemed, but if God, blessed be He, wishes to redeem Israel and they do not repent, He sets over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's and restores them to the good. In the end, according to all, it is impossible that the exile be permanent. Rav Tzadok (Kometz HaMinchah, part II 37): Answering Abraham's "Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it," He said "Know surely" and told him of the [subjugation to the] kingdoms, for the Land is merited through sufferings, which sweeten the flesh, the bodily part of man that corresponds to deeds. Only through this is there hope for the complete end, as they said, "He sets up a king as harsh as Haman," and then there will be an inheritance and possession without interruption. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 8): Of the future redemption it is said, "As in the days of your going out of Egypt I will show him wonders": when it comes "in its time" and they are not worthy, then even though the Holy One, blessed be He, will set up a king as harsh as Haman so that they repent, that repentance comes from an arousal from Above, and on this the nations have a claim, that had He aroused them from Above they too would have been aroused. Such a redemption "in its time," like the Exodus, comes from an arousal from Above: a sudden redemption without prior merit or effort, whose light is not yet grasped in this world before it appears. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 12): The King of the world, as it were, removed the ring of His rule and handed it to Haman, holiness clothing itself in Haman's sackcloth, since Israel were asleep to the commandments and could be roused only in this way, while the true intent was the reverse: to exalt Israel and destroy Haman, the seed of Amalek and all Israel's enemies. So too in the future, if, Heaven forbid, they should need a king as harsh as Haman, the Blessed One will clothe Himself within him, for "the king's heart is in the hand of the Lord," and through that clothing in the garment of Esau [Israel's enemies] will be wiped out from the world. אַלֶּעָתִיד מַעֲמִיד מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן וְהֵם שָׁבִים בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְדִיֵּק כְּהָמָן דְּכֵיוָן דְּהַכַּוָּנָה
And likewise they said in Sanhedrin (97b): in the future He will establish a king as harsh as Haman, and they will return in repentance. It says specifically 'as Haman,' because since the intention
רַק לַהֲשִׁיבָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה כׇּל קַשְׁיוּתוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דִּמְיוֹן כּוֹזֵב בְּעָלְמָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּהַמָּן מֵאַחַר שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת אֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל לָזֶה.
is only to return them in repentance, all his harshness is nothing but a false illusion, just as it was with Haman, since in truth the Blessed Name has no desire for this at all.
וְנִמְצָא הַדִּמְיוֹן גָּרַם לְבִטּוּל הַדִּמְיוֹן וְהִתְגַּלּוּת הָאֱמֶת וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁב הַדִּמְיוֹן לִהְיוֹת אֱמֶת לֹא שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹן עַצְמוֹ אֱמֶת
Thus the illusion itself caused the nullification of illusion and the revelation of truth; and through this, illusion returned to become truth—not that the illusion itself is truth
כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא דְּזֶה שֶׁקֶר רַק שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהִתְהַפְּכוּת נַעֲשֶׂה מִמֶּנּוּ הֲכָנָה לַטּוֹב אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלְטוּ הַיְּהוּדִים וְגוֹמֵר וְהוּא
as it stands, for that is falsehood; rather, through its reversal it became a preparation for the good, 'that the Jews should rule...' and so forth. This comes
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָאֱמֶת וְיִשְׁלְטוּ עַל הַדִּמְיוֹן הַמַּעְלִים הָאֱמֶת וּלְפִי
through the truth being revealed to them by this, so that they rule over the illusion that conceals the truth. And because
שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ לְאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל כַּיָּדוּעַ הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַלְבָּשָׁה חֵלֶק בְּחֵלֶק
the rule of man over man to his harm—over the worthless man, as is known—is always by way of one part being clothed in the corresponding part,
וְאֵבֶר בְּאֵבֶר זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כִּקְלִפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי כַּיָּדוּעַ וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא חוֹזֵר לִשְׁלֹט בּוֹ הוּא דֻּגְמַת שַׁלִּיטָתוֹ
