and limb in limb, this opposite that, like a shell surrounding the fruit, as is known; when the other returns to rule over him, it is in the very pattern of his former rule,
כִּי הוּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מַמָּשׁ עַל כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁב לְאַבֵּד כִּי זֶהוּ כֹּחַ הָרַע דַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁרוֹצֶה לַהֲרֹג
for he stands exactly opposite him. Therefore, just as he plotted to destroy—for this is the evil power of Amalek, which seeks to kill
וּלְאַבֵּד אַחַר כָּךְ נֶהְפַּךְ שֶׁהַיְּהוּדִים הָרְגוּ וְאָבְדוּ בָּהֶם.
and destroy—afterward it was reversed, and the Jews killed and destroyed among them.
וְזֶהוּ הַפּוּר שֶׁהוּא הוֹרָאַת הַדִּמְיוֹן דְּהַיְנוּ הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁל הַדִּמְיוֹן וְהָרָאשִׁית שֶׁלּוֹ טֶרֶם שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה לַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק הָרָאשִׁית
This is the pur, which signifies the imaginative faculty: the source and beginning of imagination before it comes forth into actuality. This is the root of Amalek, the first
דְּגוֹיִם שֶׁהֵם כְּלָלוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדִּמְיוֹנִי וְהוּא הַמַּזָּל שֶׁל רוֹמְמוּת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן.
of the nations, who comprise this imaginary world; and it is the mazal of the elevation of the nations over Israel according to appearances.
נֶהְפַּךְ לְפוּרֵינוּ לִהְיוֹת אַדְּרַבָּא אָז רוֹמְמוּת קֶרֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כִּי נִמְחָה זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק
It was transformed into our Pur, so that, on the contrary, then the horn of Israel was raised over the nations, for the seed of Amalek was blotted out,
וְנַעֲשָׂה מֵהַיֵּשׁ אֵין וְהָאִין הוּא הַמַּזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and being was turned into nothingness; and that nothingness is Israel's mazal.
וּפוּר זֶה עַצְמוֹ אַדְּרַבָּא הִזִּיל וְהִטִּיף שֶׁפַע לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי הוּא הַגּוֹרָל אֲשֶׁר מֵהַשֵּׁם כָּל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ וְהוּא אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד.
Indeed, this very pur, on the contrary, poured and dripped an influx of blessing to Israel, for it is the lot whose every judgment is from Hashem, and He alone is the God of Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּן כְּלָל קִיּוּם הַבְּרִיאָה דְּשֵׁשֶׁת אַלְפֵי שְׁנִין הַכֹּל בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל
Just as the entirety of Creation during the six days of Creation was for the sake of Israel, so too the entire continuance of Creation through the six thousand years is all for the sake of Israel,

וְכׇל מַה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה וְנִפְעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַכֹּל לְצֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת1326 Yevamot 63a — R. Elazar said: What is meant by “And through you shall all the families of the earth be blessed”? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Avraham: I have two goodly branches to graft onto you — Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite. “All the families of the earth” — even the families that dwell on the earth are blessed only for Israel’s sake. “All the nations of the earth” — even the ships that go from Gaul to Spain are blessed only for Israel’s sake. Rashi: "Two branches [berakhot]": as in "one who layers [mavrikh] a vine" (Kilayim 7:1). "Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite": from them came forth kings and prophets. Naamah was the mother of Rehoboam, and from her came Asa, Jehoshaphat and Hezekiah, who were completely righteous, and the prophet Isaiah — for the master said: Amoz and Amaziah were brothers (Megillah 10b). Tosafos (s.v. "even the ships that go from Gaul to Spain"): He expounds this from "all," which comes to include even those that stand on land only a little. Maharsha: Other verses like this one, such as "and in your seed shall [the nations] bless themselves [ve-hitbarkhu]," mean that a man will say to his son, "May you be like Abraham," "like Ephraim and Manasseh"; but here Scripture changed to the passive "ve-nivrekhu," [an act done] by another — that the Holy One, blessed be He, will make of them two grafts within you, or that they will be blessed from Heaven. And since he first expounds the word as grafting and then as actual blessing ("even the families that dwell on the earth are blessed only …"), the latter is a separate teaching drawn from the "all" of "all the families," just as they expounded "all the nations," as Tosafot wrote. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Yevamos 63a): Only these two are called "goodly branches," though many good converts joined Israel: Israel in themselves are complete, like one man, so other converts are an addition to them, and every addition impairs completeness — hence "converts are as hard for Israel as a sore" — but these two are no addition; like a grafted branch that brings forth new fruit, they brought a new existence into the world, and such newness could come only from the nations, above all from Ammon and Moab, the most remote from Israel, from whom the Messiah was to be born. "Even the families that dwell on the earth": Israel are the heart and essence of the world, and as the heart sustains every limb of the body, so everything is blessed for Israel's sake — even those who dwell within the earth, and even the ships that dwell at sea and not on land. For Israel are like the heart of the tree, receiving the blessing first from the Root, the Blessed Name, and through them every branch is blessed. (סג.) אֲפִלּוּ סְפִינָה הַבָּאָה מְגַלְּיָא וְכוּלֵי.
and everything that is done and effected in the world is all for Israel's need, as it is written in Yevamot (63a): even a ship coming from Gaul, and so forth.
וְעַל כֵּן הִפִּיל פּוּר מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם וּמֵחֹדֶשׁ לְחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה שׁוּם חֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם לְקַבֵּל פּוּר לְהָרַע לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
Therefore he cast the pur from day to day and from month to month, for no month or day wished to accept a pur to bring harm upon Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתַּרְגּוּם כִּי הַזְּמַן גַּם כֵּן נִבְרָא מִכְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְצֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
as is written in the Targum; for time too was created as part of Creation, and it too exists for Israel's sake,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם וְאֵיךְ יְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ לְהָרַע בּוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן לְאַבְּדָן מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
as it is written, 'This month shall be for you.' How, then, could it accept upon itself to harm Israel through it, and all the more so to destroy them from the world entirely,
חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כִּי אִם כֵּן יְאַבֵּד כׇּל הַבְּרִיאָה וִיאַבֵּד גַּם הַזְּמַן וְהַיּוֹם וְהַחֹדֶשׁ עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן עַד
Heaven forbid? For if so, it would destroy all Creation, and would destroy time, the day, and the month itself from the world as well—until
שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְחֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁבּוֹ נָפַל הַפּוּר וְשָׂמַח לְפִי שֶׁבּוֹ מֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
he reached the month of Adar, upon which the pur fell, and he rejoiced because Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, died in it.
הָעִנְיָן כִּי כׇּל חֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ בּוֹ אוֹר מְיֻחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּפִי הָאוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ בּוֹ
The matter is that every month possesses a unique light of its own, according to the letters through which it was created,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה דִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר פְּשׁוּטוֹת נֶגֶד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְנִיסָן בָּאוֹת הֵא הָרוֹמֵז לַשְּׁכִינָה כִּי בּוֹ הַתְחָלַת גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים.

as is written in Sefer Yetzirah: the twelve simple letters correspond to the twelve months; and Nisan was created with the letter heh, which alludes to the Shechinah, for in it begins the revelation of the Shechinah below.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַמְכֻוָּן דַּחֲדָשִׁים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ כְּמוֹתָהּ.
Therefore it is the head of the months, for this is the ultimate purpose of the months that Israel counts by the moon, since they are destined to be renewed like it.
בְּכׇל חֹדֶשׁ הַשָּׂגַת הִתְגַּלּוּת מְיֻחָד מַה שֶׁכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבֶּלֶת מִדּוֹדָה כַּלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֶּלֶת מֵהַחַמָּה כַּנּוֹדָע.
In every month there is the attainment of a distinct revelation that Knesset Yisrael receives from her Beloved, like the moon receiving from the sun, as is known.

וּבְנִיסָן הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת גָּמוּר לְהָאִיר גַּם בְּחֶשְׁכַת לַיְלָה וְרָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם וְכוּלֵי1327 Yalkut Shimoni, Beshalach 244 — “This is my God.” R. Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel and Yeshayahu did not see? For it is said, “And by the hand of the prophets I was imagined,” and it is written, “The heavens opened and I saw.” To what may the matter be compared? To a king of flesh and blood who entered a province, with a circle of guards about him, and warriors at his right and at his left, and troops before him and behind him — and all were asking, Which one is the king? Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): At the splitting of the Red Sea there came the revelation of "seeing" — "a maidservant saw at the sea" — which Israel afterwards attained as a possession [of their own] at the giving of the Torah. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 32): At the Exodus and at the giving of the Torah there was the "light of the King's countenance", the recognition of His presence: "a maidservant saw at the sea", they pointed with the finger, "This is my God", and they received the Torah from heaven in a revelation of Godliness "eye to eye." Even after the salvation of Purim there was no such light; though in the days of Achashverosh they accepted [the Torah] anew out of love and with greater endearment, it was not through a revelation of Godliness but from within concealment and darkness. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:35): Ma'aseh Merkavah is a union so complete that there is only One; hence the Sages said "a maidservant saw at the sea": with the destruction of all Egypt, the hidden root of evil, the hidden root of good was clarified — that its root is from the Blessed One alone — and this is the ultimate unification, when it becomes clear to the eye. Then she saw the whole Ma'aseh Merkavah of Yechezkel: how the Blessed One rides upon all of creation, which is merely a throne and chariot for Him, nothing apart from Him or a thing in itself. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on completing the Talmud 2): The Talmud opens in Berakhos with the Shema, prayer and blessings — speech before the Blessed One and clear recognition of His truth — in the sense of "a maidservant saw at the sea": when a Jew first begins to draw near to words of Torah, the Blessed One opens a great light for him. Yet the Blessed One has great depths, light above light, beside which this is darkness, and He wishes to raise a person ever higher; so as soon as one moves on from the beginning, that light becomes habitual to him and turns back into darkness and faith. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): One who truly cleaves to the Blessed One merits complete redemption from all the imaginings of this world, until he is freed from the evil inclination. This was the redemption from Egypt in Nisan, when they went out suddenly from the power of imagination and the immense immersion they had been sunk in there, in utter darkness, into a great light — until "a maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel did not see." Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): Holy "seeing" comes from fear, the level of Yitzchak ("and Yitzchak shows them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes"); its clarification began with Yitzchak's birth and ran four hundred years until the Exodus, when "a maidservant saw at the sea", as the Sages said — for then the seeing was completed in full. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah 1): At the sea and at Sinai there was a revelation of Atika [the Ancient One]: the splitting of the Red Sea depends on Atika, as the Zohar says, and the Mechilta says, "a maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel did not see"; so too at the giving of the Torah, "face to face the Lord spoke with you", and the Zohar says Israel saw there what Yechezkel did not see — that is, the revelation of Atika. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 189): There are two apprehensions of Godliness: from creation (Ma'aseh Bereishis), the "seeing" of the Patriarchs, and from His governance (Ma'aseh Merkavah, how the Blessed One rides upon His creatures), the "knowledge" of Moshe Rabbeinu. The generation of the wilderness, called "the generation of knowledge" — "a maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel did not see", that is, Ma'aseh Merkavah — for they were all prepared for knowledge and for the level of da'as of Moshe Rabbeinu, the leader who comprised them all. Mei HaShiloach (vol. II, Bava Metzia): On the Gemara's conclusion that sight alone does not acquire: one might have thought it does, and so it was at the Exodus, where Israel attained by sight — "a maidservant saw at the sea" — and thought that by this seeing they had acquired the light fully. But when they then went three days without finding water, that is, without longing or desire, they recognized that they had no full acquisition yet; only at the giving of the Torah did they merit it completely, for what a person attains by sight he can later acquire fully through effort, but it takes time. Sod Yesharim (Purim 15): After the great revelation of light Israel had before — as the Sages said, "a maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel did not see" — when that brightness was hidden from them, a question and doubt arose in their hearts about their very bond [with Him]: if we are truly bound to the Root above, why is this light hidden from us? For at the sea the Blessed One had illumined for them a very lofty level, above prayer and service. בִּרְאִיָּה גְּמוּרָה עַל יְדֵי
In Nisan there is a complete revelation that illuminates even the darkness of night: 'a maidservant at the sea saw...' and so forth, with complete vision, through
שֶׁמֵּאִיר כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה וּלְכׇל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר גָּמוּר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם.
the entire night being illuminated; and for all the children of Israel there was complete light in their dwellings.
וְנוֹדַע דְּיִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר הוּא מִן הַחוֹשֵׂךְ דְּכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא אוֹר בָּהִיר בַּשְּׁחָקִים אֵין רְבוּתָא כָּל כָּךְ
It is known that the advantage of light comes from darkness. When there is brilliant light in the skies, there is not such great distinction,
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ חֹשֶׁךְ וּמֵאִיר אָז נִכָּר הַיִּתְרוֹן וּשְׁלֵמוֹת הָאוֹר עַל זֶה תַּכְלִית בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וְאַחַר כָּךְ דַּיְקָא נְהוֹרָא.
but when there is darkness and then light shines, the advantage and perfection of the light become recognizable. For this purpose Creation was made: first darkness, and only afterward light.
וְזֶהוּ כׇּל הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הַחֲדָשִׁים מֵרֵאשִׁית הַשָּׁנָה בְּנִיסָן שֶׁהוּא הַגִּלּוּי הַגָּמוּר אֲבָל בִּרְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא עַד
This is the entire progression of the months, from the beginning of the year in Nisan, which is complete revelation, but only as a vision, until
שֶׁיִּקְבַּע בְּקִנְיָן גָּמוּר בְּאַחֲרִית הַשָּׁנָה לְהַכִּיר הַגִּלּוּי גַּם מִתּוֹךְ תֹּקֶף הַהֶעְלֵם.
it becomes fixed as a complete acquisition at the end of the year—to recognize the revelation even from within the very intensity of concealment.

וְזֶהוּ בַּאֲדָר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בָּאוֹת קוֹף הָרוֹמֵז לִקְדֻשָּׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (קד.)1328 Shabbat 104a — Kuf — holy; resh — wicked. Why is the face of the kuf turned away from the resh? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I cannot look upon the wicked. And why is the crown of the kuf turned toward the resh? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If he repents, I will tie a crown for him like My own. And why is the leg of the kuf suspended? So that if he repents he may enter. Rashi: "Why is the face of the kuf turned away from the resh" is a euphemism: [in fact] the back of the resh is toward the kuf, [signifying] that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish to look at the face of the wicked. The crown of the kuf is a small zayin-like stroke made at the end of the kuf's roof; its leg is "suspended" in that it does not join its roof. Maharsha (s.v. "Kuf — holy"): Kuf equals in numerical value Makom ["Place"], for He is the Place of the world; and "the face of the kuf is turned away from the resh" is a euphemism, as Rashi explains. The kuf is not placed so as truly to turn its face from the resh — which would better suit not looking upon the wicked — because it would then stand at the left of the resh, which is not fitting, since His right hand is extended to receive penitents. Hence the leg of the kuf is suspended toward the resh, "so that if he repents he may enter," for this is only on the right side. קוֹף קָדוֹשׁ דְּהוּא בִּמְקוֹם גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה
This occurs in Adar, which was created with the letter kuf, alluding to holiness, as it is written in Shabbat (104a), 'kuf—holy,' which is at the place of the boundary against sexual immorality,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד)1329 Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 2:4 — R. Yudah ben Pazi said: Why did Scripture place the section of forbidden relations next to the section of holiness [“You shall be holy,” Leviticus 19]? To teach you that whoever separates himself from forbidden relations is called holy. So the Shunammite says to her husband: "Behold now, I know that he is a holy man of God" (II Kings 4:9). … R. Avin said: Because he never looked at her. And the Rabbis said: Because he never saw a drop of seminal emission in his life. Pnei Moshe (s.v. "he is a holy man of God"): "He is a holy man," and so forth — this is in the Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 10. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaPerishus 1): Separation from forbidden relations is itself holiness, for by it a man separates himself from the corporeal and draws near to the separate, holy rank. Every forbidden union is a bodily matter, in which a man inclines after the body; and holiness is nothing other than being separate from bodily things and attaining the rank of the upper beings, who are holy in that they are without body. Therefore wherever you find a fence against immorality, there you find the term "holy" written beside it — meaning that you shall be holy and near to the upper beings, who are holy..
as is written in the Jerusalem Talmud, Yevamot (chapter 2, halakhah 4).
כִּי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הוּא הַיִּחוּד שֶׁאָדָם מְיַחֵד וּמוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ וְכׇל כֹּחוֹתָיו לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דֻּגְמַת קִדּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא נִקְנֵית בָּזֶה לְבַעְלָהּ לִהְיוֹת מֻתֶּרֶת לוֹ.

For holiness is the unification whereby a person sets apart and gives over himself and all his powers to the Blessed Name, like the betrothal of a woman, through which she is acquired to her husband and becomes permitted to him.
וְזֶה נִמְצָא רַק בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּמְצָא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה הַיְנוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אַף עַל פִּי
This is found only where there is a boundary against sexual immorality—namely, among Israel. Although the worshippers of stars and constellations

שֶׁגָּדְרוּ עַצְמָם בַּעֲרָיוֹת מֵימוֹת הַמַּבּוּל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הָעׇרְלָה נִקְרָא אֶלָּא עַל שְׁמָם (נְדָרִים לא:)1330 Nedarim 31b — One who vows that benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to him is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews and prohibited from the circumcised of the nations of the world. One who vows that benefit from the circumcised is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from uncircumcised Jews and permitted to benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world — for uncircumcision is ascribed only to the nations of the world, as it is stated: "For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart"; and it says: "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be"; and it says: "Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph." Rashi: "And he is forbidden with respect to the circumcised of the nations of the world" — because they are included in the category of the uncircumcised. "Uncircumcised Jews" are included in the category of the circumcised — such as one whose brothers died on account of circumcision [and who was therefore left uncircumcised]. Maharsha (s.v. "as it is stated... and it says... and it says"): From the first verse, "For all the nations are uncircumcised," one learns only that when a man vows against "the uncircumcised" in the plural, the circumcised of the nations are also included; but had he vowed in the singular against "this uncircumcised man," one might have said that if that man is in fact circumcised he is not called uncircumcised — and therefore it brings "And this uncircumcised Philistine shall be," for David did not know whether he was circumcised. And lest you say that only the men of the nations fall under the name of uncircumcision but not their daughters, it brings "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph," that the daughters too are disgraced by that name after their fathers. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:18): Because of the flaws in the covenant among Israel, it seems to the nations that they are alike in the yesod, the foundation of the whole structure, and hence alike in everything — but this is only imagination, as stated in Nedarim, "one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel." Therefore Balaam, whose prophecy was founded on Israel's flaws in the covenant, testified that they are not like all the nations, who truly are so. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 15): Circumcision is the root of Jewishness, as the Sages said that the foreskin is called only after the nations of the world; a Jew, "though he has sinned, is Israel" through circumcision, the covenant of the Blessed One's seal between us, marking that we belong to Him — and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. This is "walk before Me," the level of Israel's wholeness, whereby even one who does not walk with the Blessed One at all and defies His word is also walking in His ways, only without intending to. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 20): Jacob our father merited a complete bed because he never saw an emission, and therefore none of his seed is banished, and "though he has sinned, he is Israel": he is called circumcised even if wholly uncircumcised, for the foreskin is called only after the nations, as the Sages said in Nedarim. This is from the power of Jacob's root of holiness present in all his seed after him, from their beginning in holiness — from birth and from the womb they are circumcised to His Name — and all the sins and flaws of the covenant come only from the thorns surrounding the myrtle, concealing it in this world. Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): To bring so precious a soul as Isaac into the world, the very holiness of circumcision first had to be revealed in the world through Abraham our father, and "the foreskin is called only after the nations" — that is, the root of Jewishness had to be revealed first. Therefore immediately after Abraham was circumcised the angels came to announce Isaac's birth, for he was now ready and able to beget him. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14): Shabbos, circumcision and the sanctification of the month are called "the statutes of Your will" because they are engraved as a sign in the very souls of Israel, by which they are set apart from the nations. The holiness of circumcision, too, is a sign for Israel alone, as stated in Nedarim, that one who vows [not to benefit] from the circumcised is forbidden with the uncircumcised of Israel. Rav Tzadok (Sichas Sheidim 1): The division [into Jewish and gentile spirits] applies only to the shedin, as in Nedarim, that the foreskin is called only after the nations: the whole difference between Israel and the nations lies only in the sign of the covenant, which is the difference between one body and another, brought about by human action — through his effort a change is made in the body, in the yesod, so that this yesod is falsehood and that one is truth and holy. This comes about by uncovering the garment of foreskin and husk that covers it, for that is the essence of truth, when the fruit is revealed from the husk that covers and darkens it. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Your people are all righteous" — all, even the transgressors of Israel and the utterly wicked — for the name tzaddik means one who guards the covenant, like Joseph, and the Sages said in Nedarim that the foreskin is called only after the nations and even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised. The essential distinction between Israel and the nations lies in the sign of the covenant, which is why the foreskin is named after the nations — meaning the holiness of the root of one's birth: in deed the two may be equal, but this one's root is good; therefore even the transgressors of Israel are included in "the remnant of Joseph" and are "all righteous," while even the pious of the nations have no part in this. Sod Yesharim (Purim 13): With circumcision it seems that man repairs a deficiency the Blessed One created in him — but would the Blessed One create a deficiency? Rather, the holiness of the covenant of circumcision is permanently fixed in every Jewish soul even if he was not circumcised, as the Gemara rules: the nations, even when circumcised, are called uncircumcised, and a Jew, even when uncircumcised, is called circumcised. Yet one cannot recognize this fixed holiness unless he first circumcises himself; so there must first be a concealment in which it seems he is repairing a deficiency through his own work, and once he is circumcised it is revealed retroactively that the holiness of the covenant was fixed in him all along..
restrained themselves from sexual immorality from the days of the Flood, nevertheless the foreskin is called specifically by their name (Nedarim 31b).
כִּי הַמִּילָה הוּא הַחוֹתָם שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל גֶּדֶר הָעֶרְוָה שֶׁגַּם אֵבֶר זֶה מְיֻחָד לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דִּבְאֵבֶר זֶה הוּא תֹּקֶף הַתַּאֲוָה
For circumcision is the seal of the Blessed Name upon the boundary against sexual immorality, showing that this organ too is designated for the Blessed Name, precisely where desire is most intense,

וְהַכַּוָּנָה לְגַרְמֵיהּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה בָּאָדָם מֵחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאֵילָךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ)1331 Vayikra Rabbah 14:5 — R. Acha said: Even the most pious of the pious — it is impossible that he should not have in him one side of iniquity. David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the worlds, did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? He intended only his own pleasure. Know that it is so: once they had done what they needed, this one turned his face one way and that one turned her face the other, and it was You who brought in every single drop. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:10): The meaning of "the counsel of the serpent" is learned from Jesse, who is counted among the four who died through it, and of whom the Sages said, on "in iniquity was I formed," "even the most pious of the pious…". In Elijah, who did not die, even the serpent's counsel was rectified, and he, the angel of the covenant, testifies concerning birth that it is not, Heaven forbid, in iniquity, but that all are holy from the womb. Rav Tzadok (Es HaOchel 12): Death still comes through the counsel of the serpent, that is, the filth the serpent cast [into Eve], and that filth is the desire for lewdness, about which the Sages said of Jesse, one of the four who died through the serpent's counsel, "even the most pious of the pious…". Only Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their filth cease, and then they were truly free of the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 19): The seminal drop is drawn from the brain, but because it comes with the desire of this world, as the Sages said, "even the most pious of the pious…", it imparts impurity; yet the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth the pure from the impure, for a child is formed from it. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 16): The beginning [of a fall] is in matters of desire, where everyone is in any case somewhat lax about complete holiness like that of Jacob our father, who intended only to raise offspring and was aroused only for the sake of the mitzvah and of Heaven; not every person merits this, as the Sages said on "in iniquity," "even the most pious of the pious…". This comes from laxity in the service of the Blessed One and in bringing the holiness of the words of Torah into one's heart, for one whose thought cleaves to the love of Torah will let no desire for anything else enter him. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): On "in iniquity was I formed," with "iniquity" written full, the Midrash says that even the most pious of the pious intends only his own pleasure; this is Jesse, the father of David, and this is the counsel of the serpent, a deficiency in the birth of everyone born of woman, of the offspring of Eve, against which no effort avails, even for the most pious of the pious. Only, as the Sages said, "Who purifies you? The Holy One, blessed be He": the purification from this is His, for He testifies that this desire of Israel is clean and pure. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 5): The impurity of childbirth applies even when a woman bears a righteous one, even the Messiah, and its reason is the Midrash on "Behold, in iniquity was I formed": R. Acha says, "even the most pious of the pious… did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? Surely he intended only his own pleasure." This was said of Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, and the serpent's counsel is what the serpent instilled in man, that he should feel his own pleasure; from this sprang the impurity of the menstruant and the seven-day impurity of childbirth. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent, was clarified through the birth of David, who applied to himself "Behold, in iniquity was I formed," which the Sages expounded from "iniquity" being written full: "even the most pious of the pious…". As is known from the Arizal, wherever letters of the Divine Name are added they indicate added holiness, and vav is the letter of truth; for desire is called falsehood, being a pleasure of the moment, whereas the desire of Israel, who cleave to the living God, endures as they do, for all their powers cleave to holiness. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 147): Only the Unique One of the world can bring forth the pure from the impure, for in this desire lies the source of the deficiencies that come from the serpent, as the Sages said on "in iniquity" [written full], and that is Jesse, who died through the counsel of the serpent. Man's root is in truth impure, as it is written, "in iniquity was I formed," yet there is holiness and purity in it as well; Balaam, being of an evil root, did not believe this, for he did not know that there could be holiness here too. דַּאֲפִלּוּ חָסִיד
together with the self-directed intent that has existed in man from the sin of Adam the first and onward, as it is written in Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of Parashat Tazria: even the most pious
שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי וְהוּא יִשַׁי שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ דְּזֶהוּ עֵטָיו שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן דעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ בְּכׇל זַרְעוֹ כֵּן.
of the pious, and so forth—namely Yishai, who died through the serpent's counsel. This is the serpent's counsel and Adam's sin, through which this tendency was drawn into all his descendants.

וְהַתִּקּוּן הוּא הַמִּילָה דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח:)1332 Sanhedrin 38b — R. Yitzchak said: Adam the first man drew his foreskin forward. Here it is written, "But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant" (Hosea 6:7), and there it is written, "He has broken My covenant" (Genesis 17:14). Maharsha: We do not find that Adam was commanded concerning circumcision; rather, he was born circumcised, as is stated in the Midrashim, and afterwards he drew his foreskin forward. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Sanhedrin 38b): The foreskin is a covering, a closing-off and a separation, as the word is used everywhere. Adam held that the lower world runs by its own nature, as the Holy One, blessed be He, created it, and so man ought to be uncircumcised, as He created him — the opposite of circumcision, which is on the eighth day because seven corresponds to the seven days of Creation, the world of nature, while circumcision is above nature (and so it was given to Abraham, for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, worked miracles beyond nature). Adam thus removed himself from the One who acts upon and rules over nature and submitted himself to nature, saying that the world follows its course; therefore R. Yitzchak does not say that he refused to be circumcised but that he drew his foreskin — taking himself out of the domain of the Holy One, blessed be He, and making a partition between himself and his Creator, though without turning to serve foreign gods. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 4): "Adam the first man drew his foreskin forward" means that he became so after the blemish of the serpent's filth; and since this happened on the day of creation, within the six days of creation, the foreskin was drawn upon him by nature and all his descendants are born uncircumcised. Before the blemish, however, he was created circumcised, and had there been no blemish all would be born circumcised; hence Moses, in whom Adam's blemish was rectified, was born circumcised. אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מָשׁוּךְ בְּעׇרְלָתוֹ הָיָה דְּנוֹצֵר מָהוּל אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא נִמְשַׁךְ.
Its rectification is circumcision. Therefore they said (Sanhedrin 38b) that Adam the first drew his foreskin: he had been created circumcised, but through the sin it was drawn forth.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא מָל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶת עַצְמוֹ קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁקִּיֵּם כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד
Therefore our father Abraham, peace be upon him, did not circumcise himself before he was commanded, even though he observed the entire Torah before
שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה כִּי לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי אִי אֶפְשָׁר עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁאָז יְבֻלַּע בֶּאֱמֶת הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח
it was given; for complete rectification is impossible until the time of the End, when death will truly be swallowed up forever.

אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶעָלִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים וְלֹא רָצָה שֶׁיְּתֻקַּן תֵּכֶף לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כׇּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף1333 Avodah Zarah 5a — R. Yose said: The son of David will not come until all the souls in the store-chamber are exhausted. Rashi: There is a chamber called guf, and from the beginning of creation all the souls destined to be born were formed and placed there. Rashi: There is a store-chamber whose name is guf, and from the beginning of creation all the souls destined to be born were formed and placed there. He reads the proof-verse accordingly: "For I will not contend for ever" — after the time of the redemption — "neither will I be always wroth" from redeeming, "for the spirit from before Me" — the souls in the store-chamber — "shall be delayed [ya'atof]," that is, it is they that hold back the redemption, the word used as in "the later-born [ha-atufim] were Laban's" [Genesis 30:42]. Tosafos (s.v. "The son of David will not come until all the souls in the store-chamber are exhausted"): One might object that they would in any case be exhausted through the gentiles, who beget children. R. Elchanan answers that the souls of Israel and the souls of the gentiles are not in one store-chamber; and as for the statement that in the days of the Messiah a woman will give birth every day (Shabbat 30b), one may say that there will then be a new store-chamber and new souls. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Avodah Zarah 5a): It is a place whose name is guf ["body"], because the souls that come from there have no very exalted level, just as the body has no exalted level, for the head is higher in rank. But of the King Messiah it is written, "He shall be exalted and lifted up and be very high" [Isaiah 52:13]: the souls that will exist then are not called levels of the body, but the supreme level that will belong to the time of the Messiah. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, Large Aleph Small Aleph 7): As it says in Yevamos, "the son of David will not come until all the souls in the guf are exhausted" — explained to mean the body of Adam HaRishon, as Shemos Rabbah says that there are souls hanging from his hair and his nose. The totality of Israel's souls, together bearing the name of a collective "Adam", is what completes the revelation of [God's] unity in its truth and fullness. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 13): From the giving of the Torah onward the souls of Israel were set apart from those of the nations, issuing from a special storehouse in holiness; and whoever has a hold by birth in this storehouse of souls must necessarily be clarified for good in the end, as the Sages said, "the son of David will not come until all the souls in the guf are exhausted." Beis Yaakov (Chayei Sarah 2): The soul was given to a person to illuminate the body, and what it illuminates is called neshamah [soul]; of this the Sages said, "until all the souls in the guf [body] are exhausted." What remains body, which the person had not the power to make into neshamah, enters the grave to be hidden in the dust like anything sown in the earth, until the days draw near when the Blessed One will clarify that too, and it will sprout from the earth..
But in this world the Holy One, blessed be He, concealed the way to the Tree of Life and did not desire that it be completely rectified immediately, until all the souls in the body are exhausted.
וְאִם כֵּן הַמִּילָה מֵעַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם אֶלָּא כְּעַרְבִי וְגִבְעוֹנִי מָהוּל דמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא עָרֵל וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר
If so, circumcising oneself on one's own is nothing; it is like an Arab or a Gibeonite who is circumcised yet is nevertheless called uncircumcised. It is impossible
כְּלָל לִהְיוֹת בָּזֶה אֵין מְצֻוֶּה וְעוֹשֶׂה דְּכֹל שֶׁאֵין מְצֻוֶּה אֵין כָּאן עֲשִׂיָּה גַּם כֵּן דַּהֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בּוֹ כַּוָּנָה
for the category here to be 'one who is not commanded yet performs,' because wherever there is no command, there is no deed here either; for in truth, in this world there still remains an intention
לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁלְּאוֹתָם שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לָמוּל הַיְנוּ שֶׁהוּא חָתַם שְׁמוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם
for one's own benefit. But regarding those whom the Blessed Name commanded to circumcise—meaning that He placed the seal of His Name upon them—
דְּהֵם בֶּאֱמֶת עֹמֶק אֲמִתּוּת כַּוָּנַת הֲנָאַת עַצְמָם גַּם כֵּן הוּא רַק לַשָּׁמַיִם כִּי חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עַמּוֹ.
the deepest truth of even their intention for their own benefit is in fact only for Heaven, for 'Hashem's portion is His people.'

וְעַיֵּן עוֹד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם וּכְרוּת עִמּוֹ וְכוּלֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָחַז עִמּוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה אַרְבָּעִים וְתֵשַׁע)1334 Bereshit Rabbah 49:2 — He said before Him: And who will circumcise me? He said: You yourself. Immediately Abraham took a knife and took hold of his foreskin and came to cut, and he was afraid, for he was old. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He put forth His hand and held it together with him, and Abraham cut, as it is said: "You are the Lord God, who chose Abram, and made the covenant with him." It is not written here "and made the covenant to him," but "with him" — this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, was holding on to him.
See further what they said regarding Abraham, 'and He cut the covenant with him...' and so forth—that the Blessed Name held together with him (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 49),

וּמָצָא עַצְמוֹ מָהוּל (שָׁם סוֹף פֶּרֶק מז)1335 Bereshit Rabbah 47:9 — "Abraham was circumcised" — R. Abba bar Kahana said: He felt it and suffered pain, so that the Holy One, blessed be He, might double his reward. R. Levi said: "Abraham circumcised himself" is not written here, but "was circumcised" — he examined himself and found himself [already] circumcised. לֹא שֶׁהוּא מָל אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ פָּעַל זֶה.
and that he found himself circumcised (there, end of chapter 47), not that he circumcised himself as though his own effort had effected it.
וְזֶה טַעַם דְּאֵין בָּזֶה עִנְיַן הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם כְּבִשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת וְעַל כֵּן נִמּוֹל בְּעוֹדוֹ תִּינוֹק שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלוּם
This is why circumcision does not involve human effort as do other mitzvot, and therefore one is circumcised while still an infant who knows nothing,
כִּי אֵין בָּזֶה הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ רַק שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶחְתִּימוּ בְּחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מֻגְדָּר מֵעֶרְוָה וַאֲפִלּוּ שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית עַיִן אֵינוֹ כֵּן.
for his own effort is not involved; rather, the Blessed Name stamped him with His seal, that in his essence he is bounded against sexual immorality, even if outwardly it does not appear so.
וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בְּהִפּוּךְ אֲפִלּוּ הַמּוּלִים רָצָה לוֹמַר הַמַּרְאִים עַצְמָן בְּפֹעַל בְּתַכְלִית הַהַגְדָּרָה בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ כֵּן
The worshippers of stars and constellations are the reverse: even those who are circumcised—meaning those who outwardly display the utmost restraint—in truth are not so,
וּכְמוֹ בִּלְעָם שֶׁהָיָה נָבִיא אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אַדְּרַבָּא פָּרַץ גָּדֵר עֶרְוָה.
as with Balaam, prophet of the nations, who on the contrary breached the boundary of sexual immorality.

וַעֲמָלֵק חָתַךְ מִילוֹתֵיהֶן וְאָמַר טֹל מַה שֶׁבָּחַרְתָּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא ט)1336 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 9 — R. Yudan bar Gadya said: ["Return sevenfold into the bosom of our neighbors" —] remember what he did to us in the circumcision, which is set in a man's bosom. And this accords with what R. Chama bar Shikla, R. Yehoshua ben Levi, and R. Yochanan said: What did the house of Amalek do? They would cut off the circumcised flesh of Israel and fling it heavenward, saying, "In this You chose — take for Yourself what You chose." That is the meaning of "their taunt with which they have taunted You, O Lord." כִּי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קוֹרְאִים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׂוֹנֵא זִמָּה
Amalek cut off their circumcisions and said, 'Take what You chose' (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tetzei 9), for the nations call the Blessed Name 'One who hates immorality,'

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צג.)1337 Sanhedrin 93a — They went to the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar. Ahab said to her: Thus says the Lord — submit to Zedekiah. And Zedekiah said: Thus says the Lord — submit to Ahab. She went and told her father. He said to her: The God of these people hates lewdness. When they come to you, send them to me. Rashi: "Submit" — that is, have relations [with him]. Maharsha: "Because they have committed villainy in Israel and have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives" — "what did they do? They went to Nebuchadnezzar's daughter": this implies that Nebuchadnezzar roasted them because they had committed villainy and adultery in Israel. That is, through Nebuchadnezzar's daughter he heard from them that a married woman in Israel was permitted in their eyes, and for this he roasted them in the fire. גַּבֵּי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר וְגַבֵּי בִּלְעָם (שָׁם קו.)1338 Sanhedrin 106a — [Balaam] said to them: The God of these people hates lewdness, and they crave linen garments. Come, and I will give you counsel: make them enclosures of hangings and seat harlots in them, an old woman outside and a young woman within, and let them sell them linen garments. Rashi: "Enclosures of hangings" — tents of hangings, such as are set up in marketplaces. "From the Mountain of Snow" — that is, Senir. Maharsha: They craved linen garments because flax was already plentiful in Egypt, as it is written, "those who work in combed flax" (Isaiah 19:9), and Israel had grown accustomed to them; during the forty years in the wilderness they went without them, and so they longed to buy them wherever they could find them. וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּזֶהוּ מַה שֶׁבָּחַר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַמּוּלִים
as is written in Sanhedrin (93a) concerning Nebuchadnezzar and concerning Balaam (there, 106a), and they thought this was why He chose circumcised Israel,

לְפִי שֶׁהֵם מִלִּים וְגוֹדְרִים עַצְמָן וּכְשֶׁרָאָה אוֹתָם הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִים דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁאֵינָן כֵּן וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא שָׁם)1339 Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 9 — "How he happened upon you by the way" (Deuteronomy 25:18) — R. Yehuda says: "He happened upon you" means he defiled you, as you say, "who is not clean by reason of what happens by night" (Deuteronomy 23:11). עַל פָּסוּק אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ

because they are circumcised and restrain themselves. When he saw those who had grown weak—meaning those who were not so, as they said in Midrash Tanchuma, cited above, on the verse 'who happened upon you'—
שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בַּעֲלֵי קְרָיִין שֶׁהֱבִיאָן בַּנִּסָּיוֹן וְלֹא עָמְדוּ בּוֹ עַל כֵּן אָמַר טֹל מַה שֶׁבָּחַרְתָּ כִּי הִנֵּה כְּכׇל הַגּוֹיִם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל.

that they had become subject to seminal emissions, for he brought them to temptation and they did not withstand it, he therefore said, 'Take what You chose,' for behold, the house of Israel is like all the nations.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ הַפֵּירוּשׁ עַל וִהְיִיתֶם לִי סְגֻלָּה מִכׇּל הָעַמִּים
But in truth, 'Jacob did Yah choose for Himself, Israel for His treasure.' As is known, the meaning of 'you shall be to Me a treasure from among all the peoples'
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר כְּמוֹ סְגֻלָּה שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא טַעַם נִגְלֶה רַק כָּךְ הַדָּבָר מְסֻגָּל בִּסְגֻלָּה כָּךְ
is like a segulah, whose effect has no revealed reason; the thing simply has this special property. So too,
מַה שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכׇּל הָעַמִּים הוּא בְּלֹא טַעַם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל.
the fact that the children of Israel belong to Him, blessed be He, from among all the peoples has no reason that is revealed in this world at all.
דַּהֲגַם דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִין לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְאוֹהֵב אֶת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הֵפֶךְ הַזִּמָּה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׂוֹנֵא
Although both may appear equal to the eye in this world, 'I love Jacob,' who is the opposite of the immorality that the Blessed Name hates,
וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא זִמָּה אַף דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אֵינוֹ כֵּן מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַכִּיר
and 'Esau I hated,' for he is full of immorality—even if outwardly this is not so. Nevertheless the Blessed Name recognizes
שֶׁרָשַׁם הַנֶּעֱלָם מֵעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָרוֹאֶה לָעֵינַיִם.
their hidden roots, concealed from human eyes in this world, which sees only what is before the eyes.
וְהַמִּילָה הוּא עֵדוּת עַל הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנֶּעֱלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּשׇׁרְשָׁם גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וּקְדוֹשִׁים

Circumcision is testimony to the root of the children of Israel that is concealed in this world: at their root they are bounded against sexual immorality, and 'Your people are all righteous' and holy,
וּמַה שֶׁאֵין נִרְאֶה כֵּן הוּא רַק מִצַּד דִּמְיוֹן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּהַיְנוּ כְּחוֹלְמִים:
and whatever does not appear so is only from the illusion of this world—that is, 'we are like dreamers.'

items.h:
Seif 4 — Adar, Joseph, and the Sanctity of the Covenant
Adar belongs to Joseph's guarded covenant, where even bodily desire can become wholly holy and Amalek's accusation collapses.

p: וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד זַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית שֶׁגָּדַר עַצְמוֹ מֵעֶרְוָה וְשָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדֻשָּׁה.
This is the holiness of the month of Adar, corresponding to the seed of Joseph, guardians of the covenant—he who fenced himself away from sexual immorality; and there you find holiness.
עַל כֵּן נִבְרָא בָּאוֹת קוֹף וְאֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיָדָם כִּי כׇּל טַעֲנָתוֹ הוּא נֶגֶד קְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ
Therefore it was created with the letter kuf, and Amalek falls only into their hands, for his entire claim is directed against this holiness,
דְּעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר וַיְזַנֵּב וְגוֹמֵר כַּיָּדוּעַ וְעַל כֵּן בּוֹ נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and therefore it says, 'he struck those at your rear,' and so forth, as is known. Therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was born in this month,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד שֶׁפֵּרַשׁ לְגַמְרֵי מִן הָאִשָּׁה וּבוֹ מֵת גַּם כֵּן
for he is the root of the holiness of the children of Israel, to the point that he separated completely from his wife; and in this month he also died,
כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גָּלוּי לְכׇל בְּפֹעַל גָּמוּר וְהָאֱמֶת הִיא נֶעְלֶמֶת.
because the holiness of the children of Israel has still not been revealed to everyone in complete actuality, and the truth remains concealed.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד אוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ דִּבְכׇל דְּבַר אֱמֶת יֵשׁ דִּמְיוֹן כְּנֶגְדּוֹ זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה
This too comes from that month, from the imaginative aspect within it; for corresponding to every true thing there is an imitation, this opposite that.
וְגַם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְגֶדֶר עֶרְוָה יֵשׁ קְדוֹשִׁים בֶּאֱמֶת וְזֶהוּ אֵצֶל כְּלַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכׇל גּוֹי
Thus even in holiness and the boundary against sexual immorality there are those who are truly holy—this is found in the collective children of Israel, 'He did not do so for any nation'—
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁכְּפִי דִּמְיוֹן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה מֻגְדָּר וְקָדוֹשׁ וְזֶה יֵשׁ גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כַּיָּדוּעַ
and there are those who, according to the illusion of this world, appear restrained and holy; this too is found among the nations, as is known,
שֶׁמָּצוּי אֶצְלָם גַּם כֵּן הַפְּרוּשִׁים מֵעֲרָיוֹת לְגַמְרֵי וְיַחְשְׁבוּם לִקְדוֹשִׁים.
for among them too are found those who abstain entirely from sexual immorality and are considered holy.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא דִּמְיוֹן כּוֹזֵב וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲפִלּוּ הַפָּרוּץ פִּרְצָתוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא
In truth, however, it is a false appearance. Just as among Israel even one who is morally breached has a breach that is only like thorns surrounding a myrtle,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.)1340 Sanhedrin 44a — "Israel has sinned" (Joshua 7:11). R. Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is still Israel. R. Abba said: This is what people say — a myrtle that stands among briars, its name is still myrtle, and myrtle is what they call it. Rashi: "Israel has sinned" — since it does not say "the people has sinned," [we learn that] the name of their holiness is still upon them. "Thorns" (chilfei) — in Old French, orties [nettles]. Maharsha: Even though he sinned and transgressed the entire Torah, as [the Gemara states] below, he is not like a gentile; and so it has been written that even one who is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah is an Israelite in all his laws. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Chalomos 25): The Sages said in Song of Songs Rabbah that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel; therefore they said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, for the root in the depths of the heart is never severed from the Blessed One, and he is called "a myrtle standing among thorns." Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The Blessed One rules over the depths of Israel's hearts, and they cannot turn from Him in the depths of their hearts at all, for their root cleaves to the living God and they are not separate from Him, with a choice to separate and become like the nations of the lands. Of this it says, "What comes into your mind shall not be," for "even though he has sinned, he is Israel"; and this is the meaning of the mountain overturned upon them like a barrel at the giving of the Torah: that they would accept it perforce. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:50): Because the world cannot exist without Israel, the Sages said that even though he has sinned he is Israel, "a myrtle standing among thorns": the very human form of the Israelite is nothing but the recognition of the Blessed One, and his sins are only a matter of "standing among thorns," like a rose among the thorns that prick it, the thorns to which the Sages likened the idolaters, as it is written, "and the peoples shall be ... thorns cut down." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): [The nations' wish that Israel become one people with them] is utterly impossible, for even an Israelite who has converted out, that is, who has piled one sin upon another, is Israel even though he has sinned, and the Sages likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns. For the body of an Israelite is distinct from birth from the body of an idolater, and even a day-old infant can be recognized, by one able to discern, as holy flesh. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 4): The root of the evil inclination lies in the nations, who are so in their essence, their root being from evil; not so Israel, whom the Sages likened to a myrtle standing among thorns, for their sins issue only from the thorns surrounding the rose. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 12): Why did the Gemara expound so much to Achan's discredit, attributing to him sins not explicit in Scripture, when even of those who have no share in the World to Come the Sages said not to expound to their discredit, since they are of Jacob's seed, save Balaam? Rather, since "Israel has sinned" is written of him, to teach that "even though he has sinned, he is Israel," the Sages came to show that whoever is of Israel, even if he has multiplied transgressions until his sins reach the heavens, is still Israel and is called "myrtle," only that he stands among thorns. That is, in truth "our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough": by standing among the thorns, which hold the root of evil, the leaven in the dough spreads into the heart of Israel too. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): "Even though he has sinned, he is Israel": the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him even if he multiplies sins to the heights, and as is said there of Achan, who transgressed all five books of the Torah, sin can never reach so far as to uproot the very essence of Jewishness, the holiness at the root of every Jew inherited from the forefathers and Jacob our father; however he multiplies sins, it is all from the "leaven in the dough" and the subjugation to the kingdoms that surround the root of Jewishness. Therefore they likened him to a myrtle standing among thorns: the sins are only in the thorns surrounding the myrtle, but the essence of the myrtle has not changed. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 52): In truth none of the sins of Israel are of their essence; the Sages likened them to a myrtle standing among thorns. Hence the sufferings that come through sin are the thorn pricking it, but when the thorns around it are burned the rose remains whole, and indeed a rose among thorns is the more precious. וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק שֶׁשִּׁזַּפְתַּנִי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ דְּבִרְחִיצָה מוּעֶטֶת מִתְלַבְּנִים.
as is written in Sanhedrin (44a), and as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on the verse 'the sun has darkened me': with a little washing they become white,
כֵּן בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לְהֵפֶךְ הֵם שְׁחֹרִים מִמְּעֵי אִמָּם וּמַה שֶׁמִּתְלַבְּנִים וּמַרְאִים עַצְמָם קְדוֹשִׁים הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן

so with the worshippers of stars and constellations it is the reverse: they are dark from their mother's womb, and whatever whitening they display, presenting themselves as holy, is only outward appearance;
וּבִרְחִיצָה מוּעֶטֶת מִתְגַּלֶּה שַׁחֲרוּתָם הָעַצְמִי וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן גַּם זֶה נִרְאֶה קְדֻשָּׁה ובָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כׇּל זְמַן
with a little washing their intrinsic darkness is revealed. Nevertheless, from the standpoint of appearance even this seems like holiness; and in this world, as long
שֶׁלֹּא בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לֹא נִגְלֶה עֲדַיִן קְדֻשָּׁה הָאֲמִתּוּת עַל כֵּן בּוֹ מֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as death has not been swallowed up, true holiness has not yet been fully revealed. Therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, died in this month,
וְגַם בְּאוֹתוֹ קָדוֹשׁ פָּגְעָה מִדַּת הַדִּין וְכׇל מִיתָה הוּא רַק מִצַּד חֶסְרוֹן הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הַגְּמוּרָה
and even that holy man was touched by the Attribute of Judgment; for every death comes only from a deficiency in complete holiness.
וְאֶצְלוֹ לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם חֶסְרוֹן קְדֻשָּׁה כְּלָל עַל כֵּן לֹא יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת קְבֻרָתוֹ וּמֵת
Yet in him there was no deficiency of holiness at all. Therefore no man knew his burial place, and he died

רַק עַל פִּי הַשֵּׁם בִּנְשִׁיקָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יז.)1341 Bava Batra 17a — Our Rabbis taught: Six there were over whom the angel of death had no dominion, and these are they: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses, Aaron and Miriam. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob — for it is written of them "with everything," "of everything," "everything." Moses, Aaron and Miriam — for it is written of them that they died "by the mouth of the Lord" [that is, by a kiss]. Rashi: "Over whom the angel of death had no dominion" — rather, they died by a kiss, at the mouth of the Divine Presence. "With everything," "of everything," "everything" means that they lacked no honor; and we find this honor in Moses and Aaron, of whom it is said "by the mouth of the Lord" — so that had the patriarchs died at the hand of the angel, they would have been found lacking in honor. שֶׁהוּא אַדְּרַבָּא מִצַּד תֹּקֶף הַקְּדֻשָּׁה.
only by the mouth of Hashem, with a kiss (Bava Batra 17a), which on the contrary came from the very intensity of holiness.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּזֶה גָּרַם חִסָּרוֹן לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בִּקְדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֶצְלָם לֹא הָיָה מֻרְגָּשׁ בְּפֹעַל קְדֻשָּׁה כָּל כָּךְ
Rather, through this he caused an apparent deficiency in the holiness of the children of Israel, for in them holiness was not yet tangibly felt in actuality to such a degree,
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה נֶחְשָׁב הַחִסָּרוֹן בּוֹ כִּי פַּרְנָס הוּא הַדּוֹר.
and from this aspect the deficiency was reckoned to him, for the leader is the generation.
וְזֶהוּ הַחֵטְא דְּמֵי מְרִיבָה יַעַן לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי וִיקַדֵּשׁ בָּם כִּי הַשֵּׁם צִלֵּךְ
This was the sin of the waters of Meribah: 'because you did not believe in Me to sanctify Me'; and yet 'He was sanctified through them,' for 'Hashem is your shadow.'
וּבִקְדֻשַּׁת הָאָדָם גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְעֻמָּתוֹ נִקְדַּשׁ בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַיְנוּ עַל יְדֵי קְדֻשַּׁת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
Through the holiness of the person, the Blessed Name correspondingly becomes sanctified within the children of Israel—namely through the holiness of the children of Israel.
דְּיָדוּעַ מַיִם רוֹמֵז לְתַאֲוָה וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מְרֻחָק לְגַמְרֵי מִכׇּל מִינֵי תַּאֲוָה וְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
It is known that water alludes to desire, while Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was completely removed from every kind of desire and craving of this world,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר מֵאַיִן לִי בָּשָׂר דְּזֶה אֵין שַׁיָּכוּת לוֹ לְמַדְרֵגָתוֹ רַק לְהַמְטִיר לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
as he said, 'From where have I meat?' Such a thing had no relation to his level; his way was rather to rain down bread from heaven,
וְהוֹלִיכָם בַּמִּדְבָּר הַמְנֻגָּב מִכׇּל טוֹבָה וְהוֹצִיא מַיִם מָצוֹר הַחַלָּמִישׁ הַמְנֻגָּב לְגַמְרֵי.
to lead them through the wilderness, stripped of every worldly good, and to bring water forth from the flinty rock, utterly dry.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר אֶל הַסֶּלַע וְנָתַן מֵימָיו הַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם לוֹ יֵשׁ מַיִם כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא הַתַּאֲוָה
But the Blessed Name told him to speak to the rock and 'it shall give its waters'—meaning that even it has waters, for in truth the Blessed Name created desire,
וְאֵינוֹ לְבַטָּלָה רַק כְּשֶׁלֹּא יַחְמֹד וְיִתְאַוֶּה לְמַה שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ.
and it was not created in vain, provided a person does not covet and desire what does not belong to him.
וְאֵין לְךָ בְּרִיָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵשֶׁק וְתַאֲוָה לְאֵיזֶה דָּבָר הַשַּׁיָּךְ לוֹ וְזֶהוּ מֵימָיו הַשַּׁיָּכִים לוֹ.
There is no creature that lacks a longing and desire for some matter that belongs to it; these are 'its waters,' the waters appropriate to it.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר לְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁם יִהְיֶה הַנְּתִינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַתְאוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי
Through speech for the sake of the Name, the giving too would be for the sake of Heaven. This is the holiness of the desires of the children of Israel: although
שֶׁגַּם בָּהֶם יֵשׁ תַּאֲוָה אֲמִתּוּת תַּאֲוָתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכׇל תַּאֲוָתָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
they too possess desire, the true desire of Israel is for the Blessed Name, and all their desires are for the sake of Heaven.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִכָּה בְּסֶלַע הַכָּאָה רוֹמֵז לְיִסּוּרִין וּבְיִטּוֹשׁ קֻשְׁיוֹת הַגּוּף שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁקַע בְּתַאֲוֹתָיו
Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, struck the rock. Striking alludes to affliction and the battering of the body's hardness, so that it not sink into its desires,
כִּי הוּא חָפֵץ לְהַרְחִיק בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתַּאֲוַת גַּם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן כִּי חָשַׁב
for he wished to distance the children of Israel from desire even in outward appearance, because he thought
מַה שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן תַּאֲוָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן הֵפֶךְ הַקְּדֻשָּׁה וְזֶה גָּרַם חִסָּרוֹן בִּקְדֻשָּׁה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that whatever looks like desire is itself the opposite of holiness. This caused a deficiency in the sanctification of the Blessed Name,
שֶׁהוּא תָּלוּי בִּקְדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל כֵּן נִגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה וִיקַדֵּשׁ בָּם בְּמִיתָתָם דְּבָזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה
which depends upon the holiness of the children of Israel. Therefore death was decreed upon them, and 'He was sanctified through them' in their death; through this the holiness
שֶׁבְּתַאֲוַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּמֵחֲמָתוֹ נֶעֶנְשׁוּ וְנוֹסָף הִתְגַּלּוּת קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
within the desires of the children of Israel—because of which they were punished—was revealed, and the revelation of His holiness, blessed be He, was increased.

כִּי זֶהוּ קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים שֶׁגַּם כׇּל תַּאֲוֹתֵיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (נִדָּה לֹא.)1342 Niddah 31a — R. Abbahu expounded: What is meant by that which is written, "Who has counted the dust of Jacob, or numbered the stock [rova] of Israel"? It teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and counts the couplings of Israel, [awaiting] when the drop will come from which the righteous man is to be formed. And on account of this matter the eye of the wicked Balaam was blinded. He said: Shall He who is pure and holy, and whose ministers are pure and holy, gaze upon such a thing? Immediately his eye was blinded, as it is written: "The saying of the man whose eye is shut." Rashi: “Their couplings” — the times of their marital union. Tosafos (s.v. “whose eye is shut”): “Shut” [shetum] is a term of uncovering and opening, as the Targum renders it “who sees well,” and so it is used in the language of the Mishna in tractate Avoda Zara. Here the Gemara infers that his eye was blinded from the fact that “whose eye is shut” is written in the singular; and what is written elsewhere, “and whose eyes are open,” refers to how he was at first. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot, s.v. “and on account of this the eye of Balaam was blinded”): This is not explicit in that verse, and one must also consider how it can be said that his eye was blinded “immediately,” when several of Balaam's prophecies intervene. It seems that they relied on the exposition of the preceding verse, “And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel dwelling tribe by tribe” — that he sought to cast an evil eye upon them and diminish them, once he had seen that the Holy One, blessed be He, counts their couplings. Because he wished to set his eye upon them for evil, one eye was at once blinded, as is written thereafter “whose eye is shut”; and since “eye” is written in the singular, whereas above it says “he lifted up his eyes,” we learn that one of the two was blinded. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Niddah 31a): “And the number of the coupling of Israel” means the beginning from which their seed is drawn, for that very beginning is with the Holy One, blessed be He, on account of the eminence of the seed, which is drawn from the brain and has a deeply inward power — and all the more the holy seed, which is pure and holy. Balaam's eye was blinded because the seed of Israel is drawn from an inward power and there is no shame of nakedness in it, for nothing is called nakedness except where there is uncovering, as it is written “the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover”; but what is inward is no nakedness at all. Because he himself was a man of lewdness the matter was a wonder to him, and because he entered to gaze upon what it was not fitting for him to gaze upon, his eye was blinded. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): As the Sages said, "Sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you," so that this laughter be in holiness; and over this matter the eye of that wicked one was blinded, who said, "He who is holy and whose ministers are holy — shall He gaze upon such a thing?" For one whose mind is [rooted in] scheming and the harlot cannot understand that holiness could have any connection with this at all. Rav Tzadok (Ohr Zarua LaTzaddik, The Egyptian Exile 1): Impurity everywhere denotes desire, and the purification from it is that the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies — as the Sages said on the verse "and numbered the stock [rova] of Israel," "Over this matter the eye of that wicked one was blinded": the Holy One, blessed be He, testifies that this desire of Israel is clean and pure, and they are called "holy flesh," whereas the Egyptians, their opposite, are called in Scripture "the flesh of donkeys." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman's eye was evil in this, for he did not believe that any holiness is found in bodily pleasures such as eating and drinking. So too the Sages said, "Over this matter the eye of the wicked Bilam was blinded: he said, He who is pure and holy and whose ministers are pure and holy — shall He gaze upon such a thing?" — that is, he did not believe that holiness could exist in this matter, since, as is known, this desire too derives from the blemish of the serpent, who cast filth into Eve. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): Over this matter the eye of that wicked one, who said "and numbered the stock [rova] of Israel," was blinded: he saw that all their desires too are in holiness and beloved to the Blessed One, and so he gave counsel to make them stumble with the daughters of Midian. For only among the children of Israel, where he and she alike are of holy seed and cleave to holiness, are all their deeds "the work of the righteous for life"; but when one cleaves to the daughter of a foreign god, who is from the side of death, her offspring is like her, and this is not called "the stock of Israel" at all. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 147): Bilam, being of an evil root, did not believe in this and said, "He who is pure and holy…," for he did not know at all that there could be holiness in this too, "a pure thing out of an impure." Bilam's root was lacking, with no good or purity in it, and therefore he could not understand this; only the children of Israel, who cleave to the One Unique in the world, [understand it]. Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 6): Through this the eye of that wicked one was blinded, who said, "He who is holy and whose ministers are holy — shall He gaze upon this secret?" For the nations, who have no connection to the words of Torah, regard the sense of touch as an utter disgrace, as the Greek philosopher said, and holiness for them lies only in complete separation, since they cannot attain holiness in bodily matters, which for them are full of filth and lewdness. Not so Jacob our father, who said "Give me my wife" — something even the most frivolous would not say — and felt no disgrace in it, for he intended only to raise offspring.
For this is His holiness: when Israel are holy, so that even all their desires are for the sake of Heaven, as is written (Niddah 31a),
וּמִסְפַּר רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע אָמַר מִי שֶׁהוּא קָדוֹשׁ וּמְשָׁרְתָיו קְדוֹשִׁים יִסְתַּכֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁהוּא לֹא יָדַע אֶפְשָׁרוּת קְדֻשָּׁה בְּדָבָר זֶה.

'and the number of the seed of Israel.' That wicked man said: He who is holy, and whose servants are holy, should look at this matter—he could not conceive the possibility of holiness in such a thing.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכֹּל קְדֻשָּׁה:
But in truth, among the children of Israel everything is holiness.

items.h:
Seif 5 — Moshe's Death, Birth, and the Peace of Purim
Haman misread Moshe's death as concealment, but Adar turns hidden holiness into deeper revelation and peace.

p: וְהָמָן כְּשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁבּוֹ מֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שָׂמַח חָשַׁב דְּבֶאֱמֶת אָז הוּא הֶעְלֵם הַקְּדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
When Haman saw that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, died in this month, he rejoiced, thinking that this was truly a time when the holiness of the children of Israel was concealed.
וְלֹא יָדַע דְּהֶעְלֵם זֶה הוּא אַדְּרַבָּא תּוֹסָפוֹת גָּדוֹל בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת קְדֻשָּׁתָם.
He did not know that this concealment is, on the contrary, a great addition to the revelation of their holiness.
וְלֹא יָדַע דְּבוֹ נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה וּבוֹ אַדְּרַבָּא הִתְגַּלּוּת קְדֻשָּׁה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגַם מִיתָתוֹ הוּא תֹּקֶף גִּלּוּי גַּם בְּהֶעְלֵם.
He did not know that Moses was also born in it, so that on the contrary it contains the revelation of Israel's holiness; and even his death is an intense revelation within concealment.
וְזֶהוּ כׇּל קְדֻשַּׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר לְהַרְאוֹת קְדֻשַּׁת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם בְּתוֹךְ תֹּקֶף הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהַהֶעְלֵם דְּעַל כֵּן חַיָּב לִבְסוּמֵי עַד

This is the entire holiness of the month of Adar: to display the holiness of the children of Israel even within the most intense darkness and concealment. Therefore one is obligated to become intoxicated until

דְּלָא יָדַע (מְגִלָּה ז:)1343 Megillah 7b — Rava said: A man is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until he no longer knows the difference between "cursed is Haman" and "blessed is Mordecai." Rashi: "To become intoxicated" means to become drunk with wine. Tosafos (s.v. "that he does not know the difference between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai'"): In the Jerusalem Talmud [the formula runs]: "Cursed is Zeresh, blessed is Esther; cursed are all the wicked, blessed are all the Jews." Maharsha: There is a righteous man who suffers in this world — one not wholly righteous, who receives his punishment here — and a wicked man who prospers here — one not wholly wicked, so that he may be driven out of the World to Come; but the wholly righteous man is granted both tables, as Mordecai was granted all his greatness in this world too, and the wholly wicked man, like Haman of the seed of Amalek and Esau, loses even this world. "Until he does not know" therefore means that he no longer sets his heart to discern the vast distance between "cursed is Haman," who was wholly wicked and lost both worlds, and "blessed is Mordecai," who was wholly righteous and was granted both worlds. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Even in drunkenness "until he does not know," when he has no understanding to act from, the depths of [a Jew's] heart are steeped in love of Israel. This is the whole clarification of Purim — that Israel's sins and their seeming like all the nations are only external: even when one is intoxicated "until he does not know between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai,'" not recognizing openly the difference between Israel and the nations, they bear no likeness at all and are utterly distinct in the depths of their hearts. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Purim 3): Haman's eye was evil toward Israel's festivals, for he did not believe there could be any holiness in bodily enjoyment such as eating and drinking. Hence "a person is obliged to become intoxicated on Purim until...": precisely through drunkenness with wine, without conscious understanding, the inner holiness of Israel is made clear — that even their enjoyment of food and drink is in holiness — after the manner of "wine enters, the secret comes out." וּבְלֹא דַּעַת [שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם סוֹד הַדַּעַת כַּנּוֹדָע] נִכָּר גַּם כֵּן הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים.

he does not know (Megillah 7b); and even without knowledge for the death of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who embodies the mystery of da'at, is this lack of knowledge, the distinction between Israel and the nations is still recognizable.

וַהֲגַם דְּקָם רַבָּה וְשַׁחֲטֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא לְמָחָר הַחֲיֵהוּ1344 Megillah 7b — Rabbah and R. Zeira held a Purim feast together, and they became drunk. Rabbah arose and slaughtered R. Zeira. The next day he prayed for mercy and revived him. The following year he said to him: Let the master come and we will hold the Purim feast together. He said to him: Not at every hour does a miracle happen. Maharsha: It is astonishing to take this literally. Rather, it means something like slaughter: Rabbah plied him with wine and pressed him to drink beyond measure, until he fell ill and was near to death — and it is put in the language of slaughter because drinking wine is spoken of by the throat, the place of slaughter, as it is said, “let him fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine.” And he prayed for him that he not die of this illness, until he was healed and lived; for in Scripture and in the Talmud we find “living” used in the sense of healing. Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 17): Even when [Jews] outwardly appear to do the opposite, as in "Rabba arose and slaughtered R. Zeira," it was no murder at all but only in appearance, for he prayed for mercy and revived him. The story was not written in the Gemara for nothing, but to show that even what appears in Israel as its opposite, like outright murder, is only external and not real; indeed his essential intent was the reverse — love of companions and feasting together. וְהָרְצִיחָה שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן וּמִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן וְלֹא כִּרְצִיחָה דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.

And although Rabbah arose and slaughtered Rabbi Zeira, and on the next day revived him, his killing was only in outward appearance and from the side of imagination, not like the killing of the worshippers of stars and constellations.
כִּי אֵין אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רְצִיחָה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל, וּשְׁתִיַּת יַיִן עַצְמוֹ הִיא הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְמַאן
For among the children of Israel there is no true murder at all. Drinking wine itself is the desire involved in the sin of Adam the first, according to the one

דְּאָמַר עֲנָבִים סָחֲטָה לוֹ וְכֵן חָטָא נֹחַ וַיִּשְׁכָּר1345 Genesis 9:21 — “And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself within his tent.” Rashi: "And he uncovered himself" is the reflexive form. "His tent" is written אהלה, an allusion to the ten tribes, who were called after Samaria — which was called Oholah — and who were exiled on account of wine, as it is said, "who drink wine in bowls." Rav Tzadok (Machshavos Charutz 9): By Torah law [the Seder night] has only a commandment of eating; the Sages added drinking, with wine — as in the view that [the forbidden fruit] was grapes she pressed for him — for in wine the force of desire is greater. In this the father of the second world after Adam [Noah] stumbled, though he was "a perfectly righteous man"; so too the ten tribes were exiled because of wine, which confounds and confuses the mind. וְחָטָא דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים הַשֹּׁתִים בְּמִזְרְקֵי יַיִן וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת1346 Shabbat 147b — R. Chelbo said: The wine of Perugaita and the waters of Diomset cut off the ten tribes from Israel. Rashi: Perugaita is the name of a province whose wine was excellent, and Diomset is the name of a river whose waters are salty; they were given to pleasure and occupied with it, and did not occupy themselves with Torah, and so went out to evil ways. Maharsha: This is partly explicit in Scripture: "who drink wine in bowls … therefore now they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles" (Amos 6:6–7) — for they drank it for pleasure, as explained in chapter Bameh Ishah [Shabbat 62b]. Maharal (Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbos 147b): The physical is opposed to what is separate [from matter], and when a person is drawn after physical desire he distances himself from the separate level; the ten tribes, who inclined after bodily desire, were thus cut off from Israel. He names two things, wine and water, corresponding to soul and body — the waters delight and pamper the body, while wine gladdens the heart, as it says, "wine that gladdens the heart of man" (Psalms 104:15). The level of Israel is evenness and uprightness, the middle way, and when the ten tribes were drawn after the waters of Diomset and the wine of Perugaita, pampering body and soul alike, they veered from that level, and so these two things cut them off from Israel. (קמז:)
who says that she squeezed grapes for him; Noah likewise sinned and became drunk, and the ten tribes sinned as those 'who drink wine from bowls,' as is written in Shabbat (147b),

וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה)1347 Vayikra Rabbah 5:3 — "That drink wine in bowls" (Amos 6:6) ... And from where did they drink the wine? R. Abbahu said in the name of R. Chanina: From Prugita, for their wine seduced the body to licentiousness. And the Rabbis said in the name of R. Chanina: From Pelugta, for on account of their wine the ten tribes were seduced and exiled. מֵחַמְרָא דִּפְרוֹגִיתָא.
and in Vayikra Rabbah (chapter 5), concerning the wine of Phrygia.
אֲבָל בְּפוּרִים חַיָּב לִבְסוּמֵי וְהַשְּׁתִיָּה כַּדָּת שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשּׁוֹתֶה וּמִשְׂתַּכֵּר וְזֶה בִּכְלַל אֲשֶׁר שָׂנֵא הַשֵּׁם

But on Purim one is obligated to become intoxicated, and the drinking is in accordance with the law of Torah. Although he drinks and becomes drunk, and this is generally among the things that Hashem hates,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים קיג:)1348 Pesachim 113b — There are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, loves: one who does not grow angry; one who does not become drunk; and one who does not stand upon his own rights. And there are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates: one who says one thing with his mouth and another in his heart; one who knows testimony concerning his fellow and does not testify for him; and one who sees a licentious matter in his fellow and testifies against him alone. Maharsha: These three traits all bear upon a man's dealings with his fellow; he means that whoever is beloved below is beloved above as well. He speaks in the same way of the three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates — one who says one thing with his mouth [and another in his heart], and the rest — which likewise bear upon a man's dealings with his fellow; and he teaches us that whoever is not pleasing to his fellow creatures is not pleasing to the Omnipresent. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaKa'as 1): In these three they hinted at matters of the deepest wisdom, for one who has all three is fit to be loved, since by these traits he resembles the Creator of all, and like loves like. One who does not grow angry is not acted upon as a bodily thing is acted upon; one who becomes drunk is wholly bodily, for once a man is drunk his intellect has left him; and one who does not stand upon his own rights has no fixed boundary, since a thing that has a boundary never departs from it — and a boundary is a limit, which belongs to bodies.
