In each of these he bears a likeness to the Holy One, blessed be He, who is separate from matter, and therefore He loves him. Maharal (Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTochacha 1): These words are most puzzling: why should the Holy One, blessed be He, hate precisely these three? But know that He brought the whole world from nothing into being according to the intelligible design that is with Him, that He brought everything into actuality and left nothing unrealized, and that He brought it all forth in truth and by the justice that was required. Now one who says one thing with his mouth and another in his heart brings his speech into actuality otherwise than it is in his own soul; one who knows testimony for his fellow and does not testify fails to bring into actuality what ought to be brought forth; and one who testifies alone brings into actuality a thing that there was no obligation to bring forth — so that each of them stands against the very measures by which the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world. Mei HaShiloach (vol. I, Noach): The ark accords with what the Gemara says: "Three the Holy One, blessed be He, loves: one who does not grow angry, one who does not become drunk, and one who passes over his traits" — not growing angry means showing no anger in deed; not becoming drunk means having a settled mind, recognizing and believing in the Creator of the world; and passing over one's traits means removing the anger from one's heart too, so that no resentment against one's fellow remains there. Thus "an ark of gopher wood" means shutting anger away and not showing it, for sulfur [gafris] signifies anger; "with compartments" means not becoming drunk but being of settled mind, as one with many rooms must know each room's place and use; and "cover it with pitch [kofer]" means passing over one's traits, atoning [techaper] from the depth of the heart. Beis Yaakov (Noach 19): The verse specifies three things [gopher wood, compartments, and pitch], and my father, of blessed memory, explained in Mei HaShiloach that they are counsels for every person to hide from evil by holding fast to these three matters, which allude to the saying, "Three the Holy One, blessed be He, loves: one who does not grow angry, does not become drunk, and passes over his traits." שְׁלֹשָׁה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹהֲבָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִשְׂתַּכֵּר וּמִכְּלַל הֵן נִשְׁמַע לָאו לְכׇל לֵץ הַיַּיִן הֹמֶה שֵׁכָר.

as is written (Pesachim 113b): three the Holy One, blessed be He, loves, including one who does not become intoxicated; and from the affirmative the negative is understood, for 'wine is a scoffer, strong drink is boisterous.'
אֲבָל בְּפוּרִים אֵין רַע דְּזֶהוּ עִקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת הַפּוּרִים שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁכׇּל הַתְאוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְהַכֹּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

Yet on Purim there is no evil in this, for the essential holiness of Purim is the clarification that all the desires of the children of Israel are in holiness, and everything is directed to the Blessed Name,

וְכׇל מַה שֶׁעָשׂוּ נֶגֶד זֶה לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים וּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן וְלֹא עֵינָהּ מִלִּבּוֹ1349 Megillah 12a — [R. Shimon ben Yochai said that the Jews of that generation were liable to destruction because they had prostrated themselves to the image.] They said to him: But is there favoritism in the matter [that they were nevertheless delivered]? He said to them: They did it only for appearance's sake, and so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only for appearance's sake. And this is what is written: "For He does not afflict from His heart" (Lamentations 3:33). Rashi: "But is there favoritism in the matter?" — that is, how then did they merit a miracle? "They did it only for appearance's sake" — out of fear. Maharsha: That is, they acted so only from fear of being killed, as is set out in the book of Daniel, and did not intend in their hearts to serve the idol; so too the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with them only outwardly, frightening them that they deserved destruction so that they should take alarm and repent on that account. And this is the sense of "For He does not afflict from His heart": when a man commits a transgression with his heart not in it, the Holy One, blessed be He, "grieves the children of men" only in order that he should repent and be delivered from the trouble. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 33): Though the Jews were only joining gentiles at a single feast, the Gemara calls this "serving idols in purity," and this was the accusation: that they took pleasure in the feast of that wicked man, which is a trace of idolatry, and likewise that they bowed to the image — though it was only a [royal] statue and they did it only for appearance's sake, it is nevertheless a trace of idolatry, and "round about Him it storms greatly" [He is exacting with those near Him]. Because they then purified themselves in this matter until they had slaughtered the inclination to idolatry entirely, the Blessed One wished to establish a feast for them, to show that even in their drunkenness they need fear nothing, their hearts being already whole with Him. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, festival discourses 16): The acceptance of the Torah in the days of Ahasuerus, though out of love, was in concealment, for in what was revealed there were claims against them, as the Sages said that "they did it only for appearance's sake" — that is, only in the outward, revealed deed, while the inwardness of their heart is for God. This was the redemption of that time, which made clear concerning Israel's sins that even when they sin, the inwardness of their heart is for Heaven. Rav Tzadok (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 255): The Megillah opens with the feast because the decree sprouted from it, as the Sages said, "because they took pleasure"; and although the Gemara concludes that it was because they bowed to the image, they were not punished for that at the time, since in truth they did it only for appearance's sake, and "the Lord sees into the heart" — there was sin only from the human side, for "man sees what is before the eyes." As long as they conduct themselves with a generous eye, the Blessed One too has a generous eye toward them, bestowing on them by His measure of "seeing into the heart"; but on account of "they took pleasure" — the incitement of the power of the narrow eye — the Blessed One too said, "Mine is mine and yours is yours," judging by what is before the eyes..
and whatever they did contrary to this was only outwardly and for appearance, not from the depth of the heart.
וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְבָנִים כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֹאשׁ אֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית לֹא זָכָה לְבָנִים
Therefore through this they merit children. Our father Abraham, peace be upon him, the head of the Israelite nation, did not merit children
שֶׁיִּקָּרֵא לוֹ זֶרַע בָּהֶם אֶלָּא אַחַר שֶׁנִּמּוֹל כִּי הַמִּילָה הוּא הִשְׁתַּנּוּת עֶצֶם הַגּוּף שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה גּוּף אַחֵר
who would be called his seed until after he was circumcised; for circumcision is a transformation of the very body, so that it becomes another body,
וְאָז יוּכַל לְהוֹלִיד בְּדוֹמֶה לוֹ כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה עַצְמִיּוּתוֹ לִהְיוֹת כָּךְ.
and then he can beget one like himself, since his essential nature has been transformed accordingly.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָאָדָם מוֹלִיד אָדָם וּבְהֵמָה מוֹלִיד בְּהֵמָה כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹלִיד יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת מוֹלִיד עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים
Just as a human begets a human and an animal begets an animal, so Israel begets Israel, and worshippers of stars and constellations beget worshippers of stars
וּמַזָּלוֹת וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לָצֵאת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כִּי מִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן הֵם נִפְרָדִים וְשׁוֹנִים זֶה מִזֶּה.

and constellations. It is impossible for a worshipper of stars and constellations to issue from Israel, or Israel from them, because from birth and from the womb they are separated and distinct from one another.
וְלֹא רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוֹלִיד בָּנִים אֶלָּא הַרְאוּיָם לִקָּרֵא בְּנֵי אֵל חַי וְזֶרַע אֱמֶת וּבִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָם כׇּל מִי
The Blessed Name did not desire him to beget children except those fit to be called 'children of the living God' and 'seed of truth.' And among the children of Israel themselves, whoever
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ קְדֻשָּׁה וְהַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה יוֹתֵר זוֹכֶה לְרִבּוּי בָּנִים יוֹתֵר
possesses greater holiness and a stronger boundary against sexual immorality merits a greater multiplication of children,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְנֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבּוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא (בְּרָכוֹת ז סוֹף עַמּוּד א)1350 Berakhot 7a — As it is stated: "The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer... And the sons of Eliezer: Rechavia the chief... and the sons of Rechavia were very many" (I Chronicles 23:15-17). And Rav Yosef taught: "Very many" — more than six hundred thousand; this is derived by the verbal analogy of "many" and "many." It is written here, "they were very many," and it is written there, "And the children of Israel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied" (Exodus 1:7). Maharsha: The Gemara cites the verse in Deuteronomy rather than the one spoken at the time of the calf, "and I will destroy them and make of you a great nation," because there the promise is not stated as a condition that they outnumber Israel, that is, exceed six hundred thousand, whereas in Deuteronomy it is: "Let Me alone and I will destroy them… and I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they." The point is that although the word spoken for evil, "and I will destroy them," was annulled when Moses prayed for mercy, the stipulation concerning his descendants for good was nevertheless fulfilled, as it is written, "they were very many." Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on the Book of Joshua 27): Through blessing in words of Torah comes blessing in fruitfulness as well, the expansion of one's boundary in sons and daughters being also the expansion of one's boundary in students; and Moses our teacher, who was the teacher of all Israel, likewise merited the expansion of his boundary in sons and daughters, as the Sages said that [his descendants] increased beyond six hundred thousand. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 11): After [Moses] circumcised Eliezer his son and brought him into holiness, from him came Rechavia the chief, from whom came six hundred thousand, as it says, "they increased beyond six hundred thousand." The number six hundred thousand means that they encompass all the words of Torah, which contain six hundred thousand letters and parts of letters, corresponding to which there are in Israel six hundred thousand souls receiving the Torah. וּבְזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר עַם רַב אַתָּה.
as is written that the descendants of Moses multiplied to more than six hundred thousand (Berakhot 7a, end), and of Joseph's seed it is said, 'You are a numerous people.'
וּבִכְלַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים בִּקְבִיעוּת
Likewise, concerning Israel as a whole in the days of King Solomon, peace be upon him, and the building of the Temple, when the Shechinah was revealed below in permanence,
שֶׁהָיוּ אָז בְּתַכְלִית תֹּקֶף הַקְּדֻשָּׁה נֶאֱמַר יְהוּדָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל רַבִּים כַּחוֹל.
when they were at the greatest intensity of holiness, it is said: 'Judah and Israel were numerous as the sand.'
כִּי הָרִבּוּי דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַקְּדֻשָּׁה וְהַגְדָּרַת הָעֶרְוָה דַּוְקָא שֶׁהוּא לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גּוֹרֵם מִעוּט הָרִבּוּי
For the multiplication of the children of Israel is drawn specifically from holiness and the boundary against sexual immorality, which outwardly would seem to reduce multiplication,
אֲבָל אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַדְּרַבָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה כֵּן יִרְבֶּה.
but among the children of Israel, on the contrary, through this 'so shall they multiply.'
כִּי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הוּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד
For holiness is that one has only a heart of flesh, as will be in the future,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)1351 Zohar 1:137b — R. Acha said: So it is — the Holy One, blessed be He, will arouse [the evil inclination] only for that matter for which union is needed, and not at every hour, so that it be with a person constantly as it is now, when it is always present and people sin through it; only for that one union, and the arousal will be an arousal of the Holy One, blessed be He. This is what is written: "And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 36:26). What is "a heart of flesh"? R. Yehudah said: A heart to bring forth flesh, and for nothing else. Rav Tzadok (Takanas HaShavin 6): The root of the yetzer — the intensity of the heart's longing — is not for evil, and this yetzer will not be abolished even in the future: as [the Midrash HaNe'elam] says, it will be called "Lavan" because it will be whitened and have no dross in it, only "a heart to bring forth flesh", as the Sages said on the verse "and I will give you a heart of flesh." Rav Tzadok (Yisrael Kedoshim 5): Though "good of heart" denotes desire filling the heart, the desire of Israel is the Holy One, blessed be He, and even when they engage in matters of desire their intent is for the sake of Heaven; they have no heart of stone, only a heart of flesh — "a heart to bring forth flesh", as the Sages said in the Pesikta on this verse. Thus the "goodness of heart" of a righteous man like Boaz is to beget precious souls, while that of the nations is the mere fulfillment of desire. עַל פָּסוּק וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן לָהֶם כֵּן.
as our Sages of blessed memory said (Zohar, Part I, 137b) on the verse 'I will give you a heart of flesh'; and the Blessed Name grants them this.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּזֹּהַר כְּתַב יָד עַל פָּסוּק מִי יָלַד לִי אֶת אֵלֶּה הוּבָא בְּסֵפֶר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת
Our Sages of blessed memory also said in a manuscript Zohar on the verse 'Who bore me these?'—cited in Sefer Chasdei Avot—
דְּאֵין שׁוּם טִפָּה מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַטָּלָה וְהַכֹּל נַעֲשִׂים נְפָשׁוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
that no drop from the children of Israel goes to waste; all eventually become holy souls in the future.
וְזֶהוּ רַק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכׇל גּוֹי שֶׁהֵם כַּוָּנָתָם הָאֲמִתִּית הָעַצְמִיּוֹת הוּא רַק לְתַאֲוַת עַצְמָם לְבַד
This is only among the children of Israel, 'He did not do so for any nation,' for among them the true, essential intention is only toward their own desire,
וַאֲפִלּוּ מִתְכַּוֵּן לְהוֹלִיד בֵּן אֵין זֶה כַּוָּנָתוֹ הָאֲמִתִּית כְּלָל.
and even when one intends to beget a son, this is not his true underlying intention at all.
וְאָמַר חָכָם פִּילוֹסוֹפִי מֵחַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם רֹב הַבָּנִים רָקָב הַמָּמוֹן הֲרֵי כׇּל חׇכְמָתָם לִמְאֹס בְּרִבּוּי בָּנִים
A philosophical sage among the sages of the nations said, 'Many children are the decay of wealth.' Thus their whole wisdom is to reject having many children,
שֶׁאֵין מַאֲמִינִים דְּמַאן דְּיָהֵיב חַיֵּי יָהֵיב מְזוֹנֵי וְהַבּוֹרֵא נְפָשׁוֹת רַבּוֹת בּוֹרֵא פַּרְנָסָתָן לְהַחֲיוֹת בָּהֶן.
for they do not believe that He who gives life also gives sustenance, and that the Creator who creates many souls creates their livelihood by which to sustain them.

וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי עִם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה סוֹף פֶּרֶק כ)1352 Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 20:2 — Each and every one comes into the world by the reward of another man. The Holy One, blessed be He, brought Persia and Media into the world only as the reward of Cyrus, who wept and sighed when the nations destroyed the Temple. And the Holy One, blessed be He, brought Haman into the world only as the reward of Agag, who wept and sighed while he sat bound in the prison house and said, "Woe is me, perhaps my seed will be lost from the world forever." Therefore it is said, "And My people shall never be ashamed" [Joel 2:27]. עַל אַגַּג שֶׁנֶּאֱנָח
I also heard an explanation of what is written in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, end of chapter 20) concerning Agag, who groaned
שֶׁיִּכְלֶה זַרְעוֹ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לְהוֹלִיד הַיְנוּ מַה שֶׁבְּנֵי בָּנָיו לָמְדוּ תּוֹרָה כִּי אֲנָחָה זוֹ אֵינָהּ אֵצֶל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
that his seed would be eradicated, and through this merited to beget—meaning, that descendants of his descendants studied Torah—for such a groan is not characteristic of the nations,
שֶׁאֵין דּוֹאֲגִין כְּלָל עַל הַשְׁאָרַת בָּנִים לְאַחַר מוֹתוֹ.
who do not worry at all about leaving children after their death.

רַק הוּא מִצַּד שׇׁרְשׁוֹ מֵעֵשָׂו שֶׁנִּקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (יח.)1353 Kiddushin 18a — R. Chiya bar Avin said that R. Yochanan said: By Torah law a gentile inherits from his father, as it is written, "For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance." But perhaps an apostate Jew is different? Rather, from here: "For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance." Rav Tzadok (Poked Akarim 4): Isaac taught Torah only to his sons, and even among them there was one who was unworthy, except that he is called an "apostate Israelite" in Kiddushin, for he had a root of Jewishness from birth — his head is buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Isaac's bosom — and therefore he too had some hold on words of Torah; yet in the end he too was waste. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 4): [Isaac, the first to be circumcised at eight days, was the one in whom holiness began to take root in all his offspring;] and his wish to draw Esau near was because Esau had free choice, being called an "apostate Israelite," so that the matter stood in the balance whether he could enter into the holiness of Israel. שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ יַהֲדוּת מֵאֲבוֹתָיו וְזוֹ אֲנָחָה
Rather, it came from his root in Esau, who is called an apostate Israelite in Kiddushin (18a), for he retained a root of Jewishness from his forefathers; this was a groan
שֶׁל יַהֲדוּת וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לִהְיוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ הַשְׁאָרָה בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל.
of Jewishness. Therefore he merited to leave some continuation among Israel.
וְכֵן הַמָּן שֶׁנִּתְפָּאֵר בְּרוֹב בָּנָיו נִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַטּוֹב הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ קְצָת שֹׁרֶשׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה הִתְפָּאֲרוּת וְטוֹבָה.

Similarly, Haman's boasting in the multitude of his children appears also to have come from a little of the hidden good within him, a root connected to the children of Israel, recognizing that there is something praiseworthy and good in this.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָחַז לְשׁוֹן אֲבוֹתָיו דְּעָשׂוּ אָמַר יֵשׁ לִי רַב וְיַעֲקֹב אָמַר יֵשׁ לִי כֹּל
Nevertheless, he used the language of his fathers: Esau said, 'I have much,' while Jacob said, 'I have everything.'
וְכֵן הָמָן אָמַר רֹב בָּנָיו וְאֵצֶל מָרְדְּכַי נֶאֱמַר לְכׇל זַרְעוֹ.
So too Haman said 'the multitude of his sons,' whereas of Mordechai it is said, 'to all his seed.'
כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִדַּת הִסְתַּפְּקוּת כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הוּא אֶצְלוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כׇּל מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי
For one who possesses the trait of contentment regards whatever he has as though he has everything; unlike one
שֶׁהוֹמָה וּמֵהַמַּה בְּתַאֲוַת אֲפִלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד אוֹמֵר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רַב אֲבָל לֹא כׇּל
who clamors and yearns with desire: even if he has very much, he says he has much, but not everything,

כִּי אֵין אָדָם מֵת וַחֲצִי תַּאֲוָתוֹ בְּיָדוֹ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א)1354 Kohelet Rabbah 1:13 — "It is an evil matter that God has given to the sons of man to be occupied with" — R. Bon says: This is the vexation of money. R. Yudan said in the name of R. Aivu: No man departs from the world with even half his desire in his hand; rather, if he has one hundred he wants to make them two hundred, and if he has two hundred he wants to make them four hundred. Rav Tzadok (Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:106): The chief force of the evil inclination lies in desire; [Aza] "grew strong" in that the power of desire spread even then, and therefore he was cast into the depths up to his neck — he is in utter darkness and has no attainment that can expand, in the sense of "no man dies with half his desire in his hand." External wisdom, by contrast, has more expansion, for it sees some light. Rav Tzadok (Likutei Ma'amarim, on Samson 16): In evil [as in the letters of falsehood] the kuf comes before the resh, for it has no fulfillment, and "no man dies with half his desire in his hand." Though the Sages said of Torah too, "one who loves mitzvos is never sated with mitzvos", that means he wants more, yet he also has satiety, sufficiency and joy in his portion — "let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice", even while still seeking — whereas in desire one is forever hungry and lacking: "satisfy it, and it hungers." Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 6): In this world there is no satiety — "he who loves silver will not be sated with silver", and "no man leaves the world with half his desire in his hand." But "Naftali, sated with favor" means that the Blessed One bestows favor upon him, and thereby he is sated; so the Sifre teaches that Naftali rejoiced in his portion. Sha'ar HaEmunah (Entrance to the Gate 23): So too the distress of discontent grows in whoever is greater than his fellow, as the Sages said, "no man dies with half his desire in his hand; whoever has a hundred wants two hundred" — and the craving and envy of two hundred is not like the craving for thousands, sevenfold; the turmoil of longing for vast wealth, which overwhelms a man and drives him out of his mind, is many times greater than that of longing for a small thing. וְכֵן רִבּוּי הַבָּנִים שֶׁנִּתְפָּאֵר שָׁב אֶצְלוֹ לְתַאֲוָה
for no person dies with even half his desire in his hand (Kohelet Rabbah, chapter 1). So too, the multitude of children in which Haman boasted became for him an object of lust,
וְחָמְדָה כְּכׇל חֶמְדַּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כִּי לֹא כִּוֵּן לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְכׇל מַה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לֹא הָיָה מַסְפִּיק לוֹ עֲדַיִן.
and craving like every craving of this world, because he did not intend it for the sake of Heaven, and whatever he possessed was still not enough for him.

וְעַל כֵּן סוֹפוֹ עֲשָׂרָה נֶהֶרְגוּ וַעֲשָׂרָה נִתְלוּ וַעֲשָׂרָה מְחַזְּרִים עַל הַפְּתָחִים (מְגִלָּה טו:)1355 Megillah 15b — "And Haman recounted to them the glory of his riches and the multitude of his sons." And how many were "the multitude of his sons"? Rav said: Thirty. Ten died, ten were hanged, and ten went about begging at the doors. And the Rabbis say: Those who went about begging at the doors were seventy, as it is written: "Those who were sated have hired themselves out for bread" — do not read it "sated" but "seventy." Rashi (s.v. "Those who were sated have hired themselves out for bread"): Jonathan rendered this verse as speaking of Haman's sons. Maharsha (Chidushei Agadot): Scripture itself names only the ten who were hanged; what then is remarkable in "the multitude of his sons," since we find many in Scripture who had ten sons, and thirty and forty? Hence they expounded that "the multitude of his sons" means more than the ten who were hanged, and since Scripture left their number unstated we learn the unstated from the stated — they too were ten. And since Scripture likewise leaves unstated what became of them, whether they died or went about begging at the doors, we must say that both happened, each to the number of ten, so that there were thirty in all. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 5:12): "The multitude of his sons" was thirty, for thirty is complete multiplicity: plurality begins at three, and thirty is three counted in tens. They were divided into three because the multitude he had was answered by its opposite, complete privation, in all its kinds: death, which is natural; hanging, by the hand of man, which is wholly unnatural; and going about begging at the doors — the loss of livelihood — which lies between the two, so that every kind of privation ruled over Haman. The Rabbis, however, hold that ten beggars cannot be set against ten dead, for poverty is not the equal of death but is reckoned only as a seventh of it; seventy sons all begging at the doors are therefore reckoned as the death of ten. וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ בַּמֶּה לְהִתְפָּאֵר רַק כְּמוֹ רֶגַע.
Therefore his end was that ten were killed, ten were hanged, and ten went begging from door to door (Megillah 15b); he had nothing in which to boast except for a brief moment.
וּמַה שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר מִמֶּנּוּ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁלָּמְדוּ תּוֹרָה וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב הִתְפָּאֲרוּתוֹ זוֹ בִּמְגִלָּה
As for what remained from him forever—descendants of his descendants who studied Torah—therefore this boasting of his was written in the Megillah,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה דָּבָר רֵיק לְגַמְרֵי זֶה לֹא נִקְרָא בֶּאֱמֶת עַל שְׁמוֹ כִּי גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד וְאֵין לוֹ עוֹד יַחַס אָבוֹת.
for it was not entirely empty; yet this cannot truly be called by his name, because a convert who converts is like a newborn child and no longer has paternal lineage.
וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהֵפֶךְ כִּי מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמָרְדְּכַי לְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְבַת נִרְאֶה דְּלָא הָיָה לוֹ בָּנִים כְּלָל
With the children of Israel it is the reverse. From what is written of Mordechai, 'he took her as a daughter,' it appears that he had no children at all,
וְעַל כֵּן לָקַח יְתוֹמָה לְגַדֵּל שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לוֹ לַבַּת לִקָּרֵא שְׁמוֹ עָלֶיהָ.
and therefore he took an orphan girl to raise so that she would be as a daughter to him, with his name called upon her.
כִּי כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁזֶּה קָם זֶה נוֹפֵל וְאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה נָפַל אָז זֶה קָם
For whenever this one rises, that one falls; and after this one fell, the other rose,
וְזָכָה לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן דּוֹבֵר שָׁלוֹם לְכׇל זַרְעוֹ וְיָדוּעַ דְּשָׁלוֹם רוֹמֵז לְמִדַּת הַיְּסוֹד שְׁלוֹם בַּיִת וְדוֹבֵר לְשׁוֹן הַנְהָגָה
and he merited also to be 'speaking peace to all his seed.' It is known that peace alludes to the attribute of Yesod, domestic peace; and 'speaking' is language of governance,
כְּמוֹ יְדַבֵּר עַמִּים שֶׁהִנְהִיג וְהִכְנִיס מִדַּת הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּכׇל זַרְעוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ וּזְרוֹעֵי זֶרַע לְמֵנַם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּבְשֶׁלִּימוֹת.
as in 'he shall rule peoples': he led and instilled the attribute of peace throughout all his seed, so that they would be holy seed, sowers of seed in holiness and perfection.

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה רָצִי לְרֹב אֶחָיו וְלֹא לְכׇל אֶחָיו שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ מִמֶּנּוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין (מְגִלָּה טז:)1356 Megillah 16b — "For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the majority of his brethren" (Esther 10:3). "By the majority of his brethren" — and not by all his brethren. This teaches that some of the Sanhedrin parted from him. Rashi: They parted from him because he neglected words of Torah and entered public office. Maharsha: "His brethren" are his colleagues, who were of the number of the Men of the Great Assembly. Maharal (Ohr Chadash, Esther 10:3): Some of the Sanhedrin applied to him "Do not lust after the table of kings," as though royalty stood above the crown of Torah, whereas the crown of Torah is above the crown of kings; and though all that Mordecai did was only to save the lives of Israel, Torah study is greater than saving lives, for saving a life keeps the soul from death, while Torah study gives eternal existence even in the World to Come. Therefore, even if his intention was to save lives, he ought not to have done this, for the Torah is above all — and so some of the Sanhedrin parted from him. Yet the majority did not part from him, for saving lives too brings the life of the World to Come, as "better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come." וְאִם כֵּן
Although he was 'accepted by most of his brethren' and not by all his brethren, since members of the Sanhedrin separated from him (Megillah 16b), and if so,
כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה לֹא הָיָה בִּכְלַל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמַּרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם עַל זֶה אָמַר
outwardly he would not seem to be included among the Torah scholars who increase peace in the world; concerning this it says
כִּי מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה דּוֹבֵר שָׁלוֹם לְכׇל זַרְעוֹ וְרַב שָׁלוֹם בָּנֶיךָ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לָאֵל תִּקְרָא אֶלָּא בּוֹנֶיךָ
that nevertheless he was 'speaking peace to all his seed.' 'Great is the peace of your children' need not be reread as 'your builders';
רַק בָּנֶיךָ כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ כִּי זֶהוּ עִקַּר הַשָּׁלוֹם וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וּרְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
rather, 'your children' can be understood literally, for this is the essence of peace, as it is written, 'May you see children to your children—peace upon Israel.'

items.h:
Seif 6 — The False Peace of the Wicked and Purim's Abundant Peace
Haman's temporary peace becomes the path to destruction, while Purim reveals the higher peace that seals all blessing.

p: וּתְחִלָּה נִתַּן זֶה לְהָמָן כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן דְּעַד אַרְגִיעָה וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר
At first, this was granted to Haman according to the illusion of 'for but a moment,' as they said in the Zohar,
וַיִּקְרָא ט׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א כַּד בְּעָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְאִתְפְּרָעָא מִרְשִׁיעָיָא וּלְאוֹבְדָא לְהוּ יָהֵיב לְהוּ שָׁלוֹם עַיֵּן שָׁם.
Vayikra 9a: 'When the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to exact payment from the wicked and destroy them, He gives them peace'; see there.
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין שָׁלוֹם אָמַר הַשֵּׁם לָרְשָׁעִים הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּתַּן לָהֶם כְּדֵי לְהַאֲבִידָם הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין שָׁלוֹם מֵאַחַר
And although 'there is no peace, says Hashem, for the wicked,' the peace given to them in order to destroy them is in truth no peace at all, since
שֶׁהַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַתַּכְלִית וְהַמְכֻוָּן וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַגָּאוֹן הוּא לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גַּם הוּא מִכְּלַל הַשֶּׁבֶר.
everything follows its ultimate end and intended purpose; and since pride comes before destruction, that pride itself is part of the destruction.
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה דְּנַהֲפֹךְ הוּא אָז לְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִתַּן שָׁלוֹם אֲמִתִּי וּפוּרִים בְּגֵימַטְרִיָּא שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשֵׁשׁ וְחָסֵר הַמֵּם הַסְּתוּמָה הָרוֹמֵז
When it was revealed that the matter had been reversed, true peace was then given to Israel. 'Purim' has the numerical value three hundred thirty-six, lacking the closed mem that alludes
עַל הַסְּתִימָה וְהַהַעֲלָמָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
to closure and concealment in this world.

וְהוּא סוֹף כׇּל הַנִּסִּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (כט.)1357 Yoma 29a — R. Assi said: Why was Esther likened to the dawn? To tell you: just as the dawn is the end of all the night, so Esther is the last of all the miracles. Rashi: [Esther is likened to the "hind of the dawn" of Psalm 22 because] in Tractate Megillah (15b) it is said that Esther recited this psalm: when she reached the chamber of idols the Divine Presence departed from her, and she said, "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" Maharsha: At first glance, since troubles are everywhere likened to night and redemption to day, it should rather have likened Esther to evening: just as evening is the end of the whole day, so Esther is the end of all the miracles, which are likened to day. But it refers to the fact that the celebrated miracles of this world began at midnight, as the liturgical poet composed, "Then You performed most miracles at night," concluding with "The Agagite nursed hatred and wrote decrees at night"; so Esther is the end of all the miracles of this world that were performed at night, even though miracles are likened to day. Maharal (Or Chadash, Introduction): Miracles belong to the night, for the day is set apart for the natural order; thus the plague of the firstborn was at night, while the going-out from Egypt, which was itself in the order of the world, was by day. The dawn, the end of the night that is set apart for miracles, is close to the day and reckoned neither as day nor as night; so too the miracle of Esther was a hidden miracle, not a revealed one, and is therefore not likened to the night, to which miracles belong, yet since it was a miracle after all, neither is it likened to the day, in which nature governs, but to the dawn, which is close both to the day and to the night. וְסוֹף כׇּל קְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קָבָעֵי לָהּ
It is the end of all the miracles, as is written in Yoma (29a), and the end of all the sanctities of time that the children of Israel establish,
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשִׁי [לְאַפּוֹקֵי שַׁבָּת דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיְמָא] אֵין אַחֲרָיו עוֹד קְדֻשַּׁת זְמַן עַד רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן שֶׁהוּא רִאשׁוֹן לְחׇדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה וְהַתְחָלַת סֵדֶר חָדָשׁ.

for Israel sanctifies them excluding Shabbat, which is fixed and enduring. After it there is no further sanctity of time until Rosh Chodesh Nisan, which is first of the months of the year and begins a new order.
כְּמוֹ שָׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא חוֹתֵם כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת בְּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים וּבִתְפִלַּת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
It is like peace, which seals all blessings in the Priestly Blessing and in the Amidah.
וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ט׳ דְּכׇל הַבְּרָכוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְנֶחָמוֹת חוֹתְמִין בּוֹ כִּי הוּא הַסּוֹף וְהַתַּכְלִית הַמְכֻוָּן מִכׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת לְיַחֵד

And in Vayikra Rabbah, at the end of chapter 9, it says that all blessings, good tidings, and consolations conclude with peace, because it is the final end and intended purpose of all blessing: to unite
כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם דּוֹדָהּ וְאָז יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם הַכֹּל שָׁלוֹם.
Knesset Yisrael with her Beloved; then there will be peace—everything will be peace.
וְשָׁם דְּכׇל הַבְּרָכוֹת כְּלוּלוֹת בְּשָׁלוֹם וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף עֻקְצִין דְּרַק הוּא הַכְּלִי הַמַּחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה.
There it also says that all blessings are included in peace; and likewise they said at the end of Uktzin that peace alone is the vessel that holds blessing.

וְכֵן הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים כְּלִי מַחְזִיק בְּרָכָה וְכוֹלֵל כׇּל מִינֵי בְּרָכוֹת דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן כא)1358 Tikkunei Zohar 57b:10 — Purim is named after the Day of Atonement [Yom HaKippurim], for they are destined to take delight in it, and to turn it from affliction into delight.
So too, the holiness of the days of Purim is a vessel that holds blessing and includes every kind of blessing. Therefore the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21) said

עַל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר כִּפּוּרִים כְּמוֹ פּוּרִים וְיָדוּעַ מִי נִתְלֶה בְּמִי קָטָן בַּגָּדוֹל (תַּעֲנִית ז.)1359 Taanit 7a — Rava said: [The day of rain is greater] even than the day on which the Torah was given, as it is said, “My teaching shall drop as the rain.” Which is suspended upon which? You must say: the lesser is suspended upon the greater. Rashi (s.v. "as the rain, my teaching"): [Scripture] likened teaching to rain. Maharsha: This is explained as above, [where the comparison concerns the good each brings to the world — the Torah to souls, rain to bodies]: the good of rain is for bodies, for the righteous and the wicked alike, whereas the good of the Torah is for the righteous alone, who through it gain merit for their souls. Rav Tzadok (Divrei Soferim 38): The ultimate knowledge — that we do not know — is the grasp of the depth of His wisdom, which cannot be known at all; one cannot come to it through contemplation and understanding, and this knowing comes only through the absence of understanding. This is also the secret of intoxication on Purim "until he does not know": for of Yom HaKippurim they said in the Tikkunim that it is "like Purim," and "which is suspended upon which? The lesser upon the greater"; that is, Yom HaKippurim is the world of Binah [understanding]. Rav Tzadok (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis 9): Following what the holy Rebbe of Kotzk said, everything they said of the virtues of the day of rain — that it is greater than the resurrection of the dead, [equal to] the day the Torah was given, greater than the day the Torah was given, "which is suspended upon which, etc." — refers to Shemini Atzeres. This accords with the Tikkunim, that it is the "wellspring of the Torah," namely meriting the light of the Oral Torah, to understand one thing from another as it is contained in the Written Torah; and this is called "rain," which is seen to come down from heaven, unlike dew, to which the Oral Torah is likened, since it seems to the Sages that they innovate it in their hearts from their own intellect, while in truth it is the words of the living God appearing in their hearts like dew, which is not seen to come down from heaven.
of Yom HaKippurim that it means 'a day like Purim'; and it is known that the lesser is compared to the greater (Taanit 7a),
כִּי פּוּרִים הוּא יְמֵי רָצוֹן הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כִּי הוּא רַב שָׁלוֹם הָאֲמִתִּי חוֹתֵם כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת.
for Purim is a time of Divine favor far greater than Yom Kippur, because it is the true 'abundant peace,' the seal of all blessings.
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר:
There is no place here to elaborate further.

items.h:
Seif 7 — Conclusion
The sefer concludes after tracing how divine light, Torah, and Israel's holiness remain present even within concealment.

p: סְלִיק סֵפֶר
The book is concluded.
